summary: Collagen supplements are growing in popularity for potential health benefits beyond skin care. Collagen, which makes up 30% of the body's protein, decreases naturally with age. The main types found in supplements are I, II, and III, sourced from marine, bovine, porcine, or chicken origins. Hydrolysed collagen is considered most effective due to its easy absorption. Research suggests benefits including improved skin elasticity, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails and bones, joint pain relief, and muscle support. Recommended dosages range from 2.5 grams daily for skin and joint health to 15 grams for muscle mass improvement. Experts advise using third-party tested products for at least 12 weeks for noticeable results, though research remains ongoing. A balanced diet with protein, vitamin C, and bone broth also supports natural collagen production.

XYZprinting's MfgPro220 xPF 3D printer, powered by Nexa3D's LSPc technology, will be demonstrated at Rapid + TCT 2018 in Fort Worth from April 24-28. The $19,950 printer features a 16-liter build volume, cognitive software, and cloud controls for mass production. XYZprinting also announced a three-way partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D for digital dentistry, and an investment agreement to manufacture Nexa3D printers. The MfgPro220 xPF uses structured light matrix technology to achieve speeds of 1Z cm per minute. XYZprinting, backed by New Kinpo Group, is expanding from desktop to industrial additive manufacturing.

Sensient Technologies Corporation (NYSE:SXT) reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating Zacks' estimate of $0.78. The company had a net margin of 9.13% and return on equity of 16.73%. Its stock opened at $78.53 with a market cap of $3.48 billion, PE ratio of 27.90, and beta of 0.92. The 12-month range was $54.49-$83.38. Sensient announced a $0.30 quarterly dividend payable March 1st to shareholders of record February 7th, with an ex-dividend date of February 3rd, representing a 1.53% yield and 42.70% payout ratio. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84.00 with an "overweight" rating, while Zacks upgraded the stock from "sell" to "hold." The company manufactures colors, flavors, and fragrances for food, beverage, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and other specialty applications.

This technical report is a medRxiv preprint posted January 3, 2024, titled "Phase angle clusters in bioimpedance: An alternative to body mass index." The document contains sections on Introduction, Objective, Methodology, Cluster Analysis, Discussion, and Conclusion. It is licensed under CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 and has not been peer-reviewed. The research explores using phase angle clusters from bioimpedance measurements as an alternative to body mass index.

This MIT lecture on Discrete Stochastic Processes covers: the challenge of finding appropriate probability models for real-world problems versus solving well-posed mathematical problems; the distinction between probability as a mathematical theory and its application to uncertain real-world situations; Kolmogorov's 1933 axioms of probability (sample spaces, events, probability measures); discrete stochastic processes as sequences of random variables over time; key processes to be studied including counting/Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov chains, and random walks/martingales; applications across communication systems, networks, queuing, risk management, and catastrophe prevention; the definition of random variables as functions from sample points to real values; and the importance of distribution functions for handling discrete, continuous, and mixed random variables. The professor emphasizes that model selection is critical, as poor models—despite correct mathematics—have led to financial crises, and urges students to think carefully about probability models when making important decisions.

Each download creates a new mesh node, helping achieve the critical mass needed for the network to function. IBM uses digital signatures for security, and the technology can support messaging beyond emergency alerts.

President James Buchanan vetoed the Morrill Land-Grant College Act, which would have donated 6,060,000 acres of public lands to states for establishing agricultural and mechanical colleges. He objected on six grounds: (1) it would deprive the Treasury of needed revenue from land sales during a period of financial difficulty; (2) it would blur the constitutional separation between federal and state governments by making states dependent on federal resources; (3) it would harm new states by encouraging land speculation; (4) the federal government lacked constitutional authority to enforce proper use of the funds; (5) it would injure existing colleges by creating federally-funded competitors; and (6) Congress lacked constitutional power to make such donations, as "dispose of" in Article IV, Section 3 meant selling land for value, not giving it away, and public lands could only be used for enumerated federal purposes, not state education.

In November 2016, Bell Academy received a grant from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi through the Mississippi Alliance for Health, Physical Education, Recreation and Dance. Physical education teacher Joyce Aycock used the funds to build a new indoor P.E. building behind the school, constructed with help from parent and community volunteers. Students Taylor Anderson and Jade Cole noted the new building allows for more physical activities and reduces noise disruptions compared to their previous open-area indoor space or outdoor concrete location. Aycock expressed gratitude for community support and anticipation for the official ribbon cutting at 9:30 a.m. Friday.

The game originally launched on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC in October 2017. The Switch version requires a microSD card for storage. The Drive concept is a two-receiver combination featuring a 10-12 yard basic route and a 3-4 yard shallow crossing route from the same side, creating a natural triangle read for quarterbacks. It stresses linebacker-level coverage and works well against man coverage and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 3 due to outnumbered underneath defenders. The quarterback progression moves from go route to shallow cross to basic route to check-down. Variations include pairing with bunch formations to create natural picks against man coverage, and attaching it to the backside of other pass concepts as a quick blitz answer and reliable outlet.

This document describes the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate and Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for AMD SEV-SNP technology. VCEK certificates are X.509v3 certificates containing a unique ECDSA private key per AMD chip and TCB version, with custom extensions describing TCB elements. The certificate chain consists of the AMD Root Key (ARK) as root CA and AMD SEV Key (ASK) as intermediate CA. The KDS provides HTTPS endpoints at kdsintf.amd.com to retrieve VCEK certificates, certificate chains (ARK/ASK), and CRLs. VCEK certificates are generated on request with 7-year validity (backdated 1 day), while ARK/ASK certificates are valid for 25 years. The API supports pre-fetching certificates for future SPL values to enable seamless firmware upgrades. Product names are determined via CPUID instruction, with different hwID lengths for Family 19h (64 bytes) and Family 1Ah (8 bytes) processors.

Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie headline the squad, with McKennie returning for the first time since March. New call-ups include Tanner Tessmann, Aidan Morris, and Patrick Agyemang. They acknowledge defensive breakdowns and frustration scoring goals, emphasizing the need to refocus on defensive play. They mention Arturs Irbe's strong goaltending and how small mistakes against Detroit's offense prove costly. The present invention describes a vehicle radar sensing system using two-dimensional multiple input multiple output (MIMO) processing. The system includes a radar sensor with multiple transmitting and receiving antennas arranged in a two-dimensional array (such as 12 transmitting antennas in three rows of four and 16 receiving antennas in four columns of four), creating 192 virtual receivers. A control applies 2D MIMO processing to the antenna outputs to achieve an enhanced two-dimensional virtual aperture, providing improved angular accuracy and resolution in both horizontal and vertical directions simultaneously. This enables detection of objects exterior to the vehicle for driver assistance applications including autonomous driving, parking assistance, blind spot detection, and collision mitigation systems.

Jennifer Thompson mistakenly identified Ronald Cotton as her rapist, leading to his wrongful conviction. Eleven years later, DNA testing proved Bobby Poole was the actual perpetrator. Thompson and Cotton became best friends after his exoneration, and now both work with Healing Justice to help others affected by wrongful convictions. Thompson notes that traumatic memories can be unintentionally altered during questioning.

Russia's central bank cut its key interest rate to 9.25 percent from 9.75 percent on Friday, a deeper cut than expected. The bank forecast annual consumer price growth will fall to 4 percent by end-2017 and remain there through 2019, while maintaining plans for gradual cuts in Q2 and Q3. Governor Elvira Nabiullina had previously indicated possible 25-50 basis point reductions. The rouble briefly weakened to 57.19 against the dollar before recovering to 57.04. Despite inflation slowing to 4.2-4.3 percent in late April from nearly 17 percent two years prior, the bank cited ongoing concerns about inflation and global market volatility, with its baseline scenario assuming oil prices falling to $40 per barrel by year-end. The next rate-setting meeting is scheduled for June 16.

Missing this payment could provoke public anger and force a continuing resolution. Other potential catalysts include TSA disruptions, WIC benefit expirations on Oct. 13, and Thanksgiving travel impacts. Despite these pressures, analysts note the shutdown could extend longer, with prediction markets indicating a 71% probability of continuing past Oct. 14. President Trump has threatened to make temporary layoffs permanent if no agreement is reached.

This work presents the fabrication and characterization of hybrid NbN/Si-SiGe microwave quantum circuits, specifically CPW resonators capacitively coupled to a common feedline on 100 nm NbN films sputtered on Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ wafers. The fabrication process involves NbN reactive DC sputtering, e-beam lithography patterning, and a novel deep etching step through the heterostructure stack to the SiGe buffer layer to reduce intrinsic loss by shifting substrate-vacuum interfaces away from high electric field regions. TEM and STEM analysis confirmed the wafer heterostructure quality, including a 7 nm Si quantum well, though oxygenation was detected in the Si cap layer. Two samples (S1 and S2) with identical geometrical parameters (8 μm width, 5 μm gap, 100 nm NbN thickness) were characterized through four cooldown cycles over two years, demonstrating long-term stability. Fundamental resonance frequencies were measured at ~5.04 and ~5.57 GHz for S1, and ~5.08 and ~5.60 GHz for S2 at 50 mK. Internal quality factors (Qᵢ) for S1 reached approximately 860 in the single photon regime, increasing to 1064 at higher powers, with Qᵢ saturation observed in ultra-low power regimes indicating TLS-related losses. The dominant loss mechanism was identified as scattering from structural imperfections and the low surface resistivity of the Si/SiGe wafer, rather than TLS losses. Temperature-dependent measurements revealed quasiparticle losses above ~900 mK. The calculated relaxation time of ~14 ns indicates further improvements are needed for scalable transmon qubits. This CMOS-compatible platform combining NbN superconducting circuits with Si/SiGe quantum wells provides a pathway toward integrating superconducting, semiconductor, and topological qubits in large-scale quantum computing systems.

Ghana's gold mining companies, including Newmont, Gold Fields and AngloGold Ashanti, support new government certification tests for export values, according to the Chamber of Mines. The tests, administered by the Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC), aim to tighten sector control and ensure proper taxation. PMMC officials now have permanent access to gold rooms during pours to take samples and participate in pre-shipment processes. Ghana, Africa's second largest gold producer, earned $5.78 billion from gold exports in 2017. President Akufo-Addo's government initiated the policy following concerns about $5 billion in unaccounted revenues to the United Arab Emirates, which industry observers attribute to smuggled artisanal gold. The government maintains a ban on small-scale mining imposed last year.

President Carter's farewell address expresses gratitude to his administration and the American people for his four years in office. He describes the presidency as both powerful and constrained, emphasizing that presidential leadership requires public support and consent. Carter identifies three major global challenges: nuclear weapons proliferation, environmental stewardship, and human rights. He warns that nuclear war poses catastrophic risks requiring international control efforts, stresses the need to address resource depletion and pollution, and affirms human rights as foundational to American identity and foreign policy. Carter pledges support for the incoming president and commits to continuing his work as a private citizen for the nation's founding values.

Building a diverse workforce requires understanding that subconscious biases affect hiring decisions, as studies show gender and racial biases in callback rates. Employers should use behavior-based rather than personality-based language in job postings, remove names from resumes before review, and use skills-based challenges early in the process. While gut instincts matter, interviewers should analyze whether unease stems from prejudice rather than legitimate concerns.

High-dosage tutoring improves academic outcomes and builds the next generation of educators, according to Teach For America's Ignite Fellowship. The program, which has trained over 5,500 virtual tutors across 40+ communities, found that middle school math students improved up to 2.5 times faster than expected, while elementary readers improved up to three times faster. Key lessons include: structured training and support are essential; technology should expand rather than replace relationships; and tutoring serves as an effective teacher pipeline—nearly tripling applications to teaching programs, especially among men, people of color, and non-education majors. Since its launch, 550 Ignite fellows have joined Teach For America's teaching corps.

China's foreign exchange regulator stated that capital outflow pressure eased in 2016 and yuan exchange rate flexibility will increase in 2017. Authorities have implemented measures to curb capital flight while attracting foreign investment. The 2016 current account surplus was $196.4 billion (1.8% of GDP), down from 10% in 2007, with a $26.3 billion capital and financial account surplus. This paper analyzes the "free option problem" in Ethereum's enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation (ePBS), where builders can unilaterally withhold blobs after block commitment to prevent unfavorable blocks from becoming canonical. Under ePBS, builders receive an 8-second option window between proposer commitment and blob deadline, allowing them to condition reveal decisions on late-arriving external information like CEX price movements. The option value and exercise probability increase with volatility, liquidity, and CEX-DEX MEV share. Empirically, exercise probability averages 0.82% but spikes to 5.5% during high volatility, accounting for 80% of missed blocks on those days. Smaller builders with CEX-DEX-dominated flow show higher exercise rates (up to 23.44%) versus large builders (0.66-0.75%). Two mitigations are proposed: shortening the option window (reducing exercise probability 33-77%) and imposing penalties (0.075 ETH penalty reduces exercise 75%). A dynamic penalty mechanism using online gradient descent achieves comparable results with lower average penalties. Both mitigations trade off against scalability and builder competition.

After experiencing childhood homelessness, he became an educator and JV basketball coach who uses life lessons from the sport to mentor students. This experience shifted his focus from building a rec center to founding the Gibson Foundation, which mentors young African-American inner-city men through speakers, college tours, and basketball. Inspired by his high school principal who saw greatness in him, Gibson now helps youth see their own potential.

This passage discusses microtubule (MT) dynamics in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and their role in drug resistance. Treatment options for mCRPC remain limited, with approximately one-third of tumors being primarily refractory to tubulin inhibitors like docetaxel and cabazitaxel. The androgen receptor (AR) and its splice variants, particularly ARv7, are associated with taxane resistance through differential MT interactions—ARv7 increases MT dynamicity and polymerization rates compared to AR wild-type. The authors describe a computational method using EB1/EB3 comet tracking to analyze MT dynamics in living cells, which can identify patterns associated with drug sensitivity or resistance. They developed patient-derived organoid cultures from prostate tumor tissues, optimizing conditions using Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor to select for tumor cells. The study links MT dynamics regulation to proteins including pVHL, GSK3β, and Op18, showing that both faster and slower than normal MT turnover rates indicate drug resistance. The authors propose correlating MT dynamics signatures with gene expression data to predict patient responses to tubulin inhibitors and identify therapeutic targets to overcome resistance. They also discuss strategies involving NAD+, ferroptosis induction, and immune cell activation to treat resistant disease.

A sports team discussed adjustments to their game plan in a positive meeting, acknowledging they need to improve their speed and skating despite playing physically. Their goaltender has performed well in recent games, keeping them competitive even when the team hasn't played its best. Players emphasized the mental aspect of late-season play, noting that individual preparation and focus on personal responsibilities will help the team come together and perform better with home crowd support.

An email from Steven Kean to Bernadette Hawkins dated February 28, 2001, forwards news articles about California's energy crisis. Topics include: opposition to Enron's proposed Lake Elsinore hydroelectric plant and power lines; Republican Party struggles to politicize the crisis while avoiding blame for deregulation; Governor Davis's tentative $2.7 billion deal to buy Edison's transmission grid; first day without power alerts since January 13; increasing state costs for electricity purchases approaching $3 billion; PG&E disputes over ratepayer reimbursements; Assemblyman Lowenthal returning utility campaign contributions; concerns about political control of energy systems; proposed rate discounts for residents near power plants; missed deadlines for utility bailout agreements; potential GOP gubernatorial challengers; PUC ruling potentially shifting debt costs to taxpayers; and agreement by small generators to cut prices by half.

This article examines special education teacher preparation in Hungary, providing context through the country's demographics, government, and economy. Hungary has a declining population of 9.7 million and operates under a multiparty parliamentary democracy. Its economy shifted from agriculture to industry and services, with current low unemployment under "Orbanomics."

Hungary's education system dates to 1868, with compulsory schooling from ages 6-16. School admission is competitive, with entrance exams and selective criteria. Teacher preparation varies by level: preschool/primary teachers complete bachelor's degrees with limited practical training, while secondary teachers undergo 5-6 years of training. A 2013 reform increased pedagogical-psychological emphasis.

Hungary established Europe's first deaf school in 1802 and a special education teacher college in 1906. Currently, 60% of special needs students learn in inclusive environments, though many still attend specialized schools. Special education teachers complete four-year university programs in one of eight disability specializations, followed by a two-year compulsory traineeship.

Key legislation includes the 1993 Act III providing disability allowances and the 2011 Act CXC guaranteeing free education and expanding compulsory schooling to age 3. Current challenges include difficult autism diagnosis procedures, inaccessible school buildings, limited inclusion practices, low teacher salaries (lowest in OECD), and high teacher attrition. The authors recommend improving early diagnosis referral systems, building accessibility, inclusion training for general education teachers, and increasing teacher wages and retention.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian in 1905, consist of upper and lower bands based on the high and low of the last N bars. Originally designed as a trend-following indicator for commodities and currencies, they perform poorly for stocks in this capacity due to changed market conditions. However, when inverted as a mean reversion strategy for stocks, they show positive results. Backtesting from 1960-2021 on the S&P 500 yielded a 4.57% CAGR for trend-following versus 7.15% buy-and-hold, while the mean reversion approach achieved 9.16% CAGR with lower drawdowns. Though visually similar to Bollinger Bands, they may produce different backtest results. The channels remain effective for commodities and currencies as trend indicators and for stocks as mean reversion tools.

Three stocks—Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), and Western Digital (WDC)—are rallying after last week's market decline. NVDA bounced from its 50-day trendline after strong earnings, with traders viewing it as technical value and expecting new highs. MU is rebounding from an oversold RSI reading but faces chart resistance at $84; its 50-day moving average has turned bearish, suggesting the rally may be short-lived.

President Trump suggested some furloughed federal workers may not receive back pay during the ongoing government shutdown, stating "it depends on who we're talking about." His remarks followed circulation of a draft White House memo arguing that unpaid leave employees aren't guaranteed retroactive pay, which conflicts with recent administration guidance and a 2019 law Trump signed guaranteeing back pay. The administration claims Congress must specifically appropriate those funds. Trump also warned of permanent layoffs if the shutdown continues, while Democrats demand Affordable Care Act tax credit extensions in any funding resolution. The American Federation of Government Employees criticized the back pay stance as a "misinterpretation of the law" and political bargaining tactic.

Canadian lumber producer shares fell after BMO Capital Markets downgraded the sector due to concerns about U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar, and ongoing litigation. BMO downgraded West Fraser Timber, Interfor Corp, and Canfor Corp to "market perform," noting little progress in lumber dispute negotiations. The downgrade preceded Wednesday's NAFTA renegotiation talks, with Canada's foreign minister stating lumber discussions would proceed in parallel. West Fraser shares dropped 4.7%, Interfor fell 6.7%, and Canfor declined 2.4%. BMO analysts said continued tariffs and currency pressure would hurt earnings estimates, though long-term prospects appear more positive.

President Reagan delivered a speech at the University of Virginia honoring Thomas Jefferson's legacy of popular government, free inquiry, and balanced institutions. He drew parallels between Jefferson's era and contemporary politics, noting similarities in partisan attacks. Reagan highlighted global democratic progress, citing Freedom House statistics showing increased freedom worldwide, and discussed diplomatic achievements with the Soviet Union including arms reduction treaties and regional conflict resolutions. He emphasized three points for continued progress: maintaining skepticism in Soviet relations ("trust but verify"), rejecting inevitability theories about Soviet change, and urging cooperation between the Executive and Congress in foreign policy, citing Jefferson's own views on presidential authority in foreign affairs.

In a subsequent Q&A session, Reagan addressed topics including: his cautious approach to granting most-favored-nation status to the Soviet Union pending verification of reforms; Middle East peace efforts requiring direct negotiations between principals; continued resistance to terrorism with no recognition of sponsoring states; advice to youth about voting participation; economic accomplishments including tax cuts that increased revenue, job creation, and regulatory reduction; and future plans involving public speaking and potential book writing.

Japan's economy grew at an annualised rate of 4% in Q2, exceeding 2.5% expectations, driven by consumer spending and capital expenditure. Private consumption rose 0.9% as spending increased on cars, appliances, and dining out. Strong domestic demand offset a drop in exports. The expansion marks Japan's longest in a decade, supported by rising exports of smartphones and memory chips, plus Tokyo 2020 Olympics investment. The growth may help Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's Abenomics reforms aimed at combating deflation and slow growth since the 1990s bubble.

Select Security, ranked No. 32 on the SDM 100, acquired Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group in Charlotte, N.C., adding nearly 1,000 customers and key staff. The purchase includes a new downtown Charlotte branch for consolidating western North Carolina operations. Founded in 2003, Select Security serves nearly 30,000 customers across nine states with integrated security, fire alarms, video surveillance, access control, home security, life safety, and home automation systems.

Scientists at Newcastle University have 3D printed the first human corneas using a bio-ink made from stem cells, alginate, and collagen. The technique, which takes under 10 minutes, could address the global shortage of corneas for transplant, with 10 million people needing surgery to prevent corneal blindness and nearly 5 million suffering total blindness from corneal damage. The printed corneas can be customized to match patient specifications using eye scan data. Further testing is needed before clinical use, which remains several years away.

Texas beaches are regularly tested for fecal bacteria, which enters ocean water through storm runoff after heavy rain. Galveston County issued a brief advisory Thursday near 57th Street that was lifted Friday after water samples cleared. Health officials advise avoiding water during advisories to prevent illness, though bacteria typically clears within 48 hours. The county tests 52 locations regularly and posts advisories on TexasBeachWatch.com, GCHD.org, and seawall signs.

A 70-mile wide radar signature over Colorado, initially mistaken for birds by National Weather Service scientists, was identified as swarms of migrating Painted Lady butterflies. The unusual north-to-south movement pattern prompted meteorologist Paul Schlatter to seek public help on Twitter, where users correctly identified the phenomenon. The three-inch butterflies, often confused with monarchs, have descended on the Denver area recently and typically migrate to northern Mexico and the US southwest during colder months, following wind patterns to glide hundreds of miles daily.

This study presents a reproducible, data-driven method for prioritising AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities to expedite lung cancer diagnosis. Conducted across seven Greater Manchester trusts, it analysed two cohorts: 1,282 confirmed lung cancer patients (retrospective) and 13,802 primary care CXRs with AI running in shadow mode (prospective). Using the Annalise AI system detecting 124 findings, three prioritisation strategies were developed. Strategy 3, combining empirical prevalence ratios with clinical judgement, selected 32 findings and achieved optimal performance: 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% negative predictive value. The approach addresses NHS radiology workforce shortages and reporting delays while maintaining patient safety through shadow mode deployment. Limitations include lack of external validation and reliance on assumed cancer prevalence for cohort 2. The methodology offers a scalable framework for AI integration into radiology workflows.

The Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, released monthly by the US Department of Labor on the first Friday at 8:30 am Eastern time, tracks new jobs created in non-agricultural US businesses. It is a key economic indicator that causes significant market volatility and influences Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. The report affects all financial markets: bonds are most impacted (strong job growth typically depresses bond prices due to potential rate hikes), stocks tend to rise on positive data, forex traders favor USD on high readings, and commodities like gold and oil are affected through USD strength. Backtests on SPY showed a 0.09% average gain from open to close on NFP days, while TLT bonds averaged -0.02%. However, subsequent days showed poor performance for both. The article concludes that NFP trading strategies based on macro numbers generally lack reliable predictive edges.

The ICRC launched a nationwide public awareness campaign in Islamabad titled "Pehlay Zindagi: Give Way to Ambulances—Give Way to Life" to encourage citizens to give way to ambulances. The campaign, running until December 2017, includes awareness activities for motorists, a dedicated website, and a pledge application. It is part of the ICRC's global Health Care in Danger project addressing violence against health personnel and services. Supported by over 30 partner organizations, the campaign uses television, radio, and social media to urge citizens to respect ambulances. Participants who take the pledge become members of "Friends for Life," a virtual platform promoting social obligations. The campaign also aims to sensitize people to issues faced by ambulance staff. This is the second edition of the campaign, following the 2016 "Rasta Dein" campaign, which achieved a 16% impact measured through observational studies. The ICRC and partners will assess this year's impact through similar studies and recognize that sustained efforts over several years are needed for lasting change.

This lecture explores pseudorandom graphs through the lens of eigenvalues, focusing on n,d,lambda graphs where n is vertices, d is degree, and lambda bounds non-trivial eigenvalues. The expander mixing lemma shows smaller lambda yields more pseudorandomness. The Paley graph serves as a key deterministic example: constructed from cyclic groups mod p with quadratic residues, its eigenvalues are explicitly computable via Gauss sums, showing all non-trivial eigenvalues equal ±√p/2, making it pseudorandom. For Cayley graphs specifically, discrepancy (DISC) and eigenvalue conditions are equivalent—a result proven using Grothendieck's inequality, which bounds semidefinite relaxations of bilinear optimization problems. The Alon-Boppana bound establishes that for d-regular graphs, lambda cannot be smaller than 2√(d-1) - o(1), with two proofs presented: one constructing explicit test vectors via distance-weighted neighborhoods, another using trace methods and Catalan numbers counting closed walks on infinite d-regular trees. This bound is tight, achieved by Ramanujan graphs.

The Mariners-Tigers ALDS Game 3 in Detroit, originally scheduled for 4:08 p.m. ET, was delayed due to rain. The Tigers announced a new expected start time of 7 p.m. ET, creating a three-hour delay, though MLB on Fox reported aiming for 7:30 p.m. Fans waited in stands and concourses as rain continued. The game was moved to FS2 due to overlap with Blue Jays-Yankees Game 3 on FS1, and also airs on MLB Network and Fox One App. MLB rain delays have no maximum length, with umpires waiting 30-75 minutes minimum before calling games.

The Bridgeton National Bank sued Ellas Q. Hepner to recover $1,400 on a promissory note. Hepner claimed the note was obtained through fraud by the Kil-Tone Company, which promised not to negotiate it unless stock purchased with it was resold at profit. He argued that Hitchner, the bank's cashier who was also Kil-Tone's treasurer, knew of this fraud, making the bank liable. The trial court excluded this testimony, ruling Hitchner's knowledge was not attributable to the bank. The New Jersey Supreme Court upheld this decision, citing precedent that an agent's knowledge is chargeable to the principal only if the principal would have received such notice when acting directly. The court found no basis to presume the bank's board would have been informed of the fraud, and discharged the rule for a new trial.

Apple Inc. filed its Q1 2023 Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022, reporting total net sales of $117.154 billion, down 5% from $123.945 billion in Q1 2022. Lower interest rates globally and in the US may drive a housing sector rebound over one to four years. Recent lumber tariffs favor domestic manufacturers, though trade deals could alter this. Current leverage appears lower than 2007, supporting diversified housing stock exposure. The author has five years of investment experience, an MBA in Macroeconomics and Portfolio Management, and uses a top-down macro approach combined with bottom-up company analysis. No positions are held in mentioned companies.

Rite-Hite introduced the Uni-Dox Inflatable Shelter for loading docks servicing various truck and trailer configurations. In a 1918 New York Supreme Court appellate decision, the conviction of Solomon Montlake for grand larceny was reversed and a new trial granted due to erroneous jury instructions on alibi defense. The court held that: (1) a trial judge may discharge a jury before submission for substantial reasons arising during trial, with remedy by plea of former jeopardy rather than habeas corpus; (2) after submission, discharge is limited to Code of Criminal Procedure section 428 circumstances; (3) here, dismissal was proper due to prosecutorial misconduct in accusing defense counsel of criminality; (4) cross-examination about unpaid rent improperly disparaged a witness without showing moral turpitude; and (5) the alibi instruction erroneously required defendants to prove they "could not have been" at the crime scene, improperly shifting burden and requiring exclusion of bare possibility, rather than permitting acquittal if alibi evidence raised reasonable doubt about presence.

This passage details technical specifications for SD Memory Card commands and operations. APP_CMD (CMD55) enables application-specific commands (ACMDs), with specific rules for command interpretation based on APP_CMD bit status in responses. CMD6 (Switch Function) supports six function groups including Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit, with Mode 0 for checking functions and Mode 1 for setting them. The specification covers High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec), Command System extensions, CMD8 for interface initialization, and differences between SDSC and SDHC/SDXC card capacity types regarding memory addressing. It defines timeout conditions for read, write, and erase operations, CRC protection mechanisms, command classes, and response types (R1-R7). The document extensively covers Speed Class specifications for SDSC, SDHC, and SDXC cards, including Allocation Units, Recording Units, performance parameters (Pw, Pm, Pr), FAT update procedures, and CMD20 Speed Class Control command for optimizing card operations during stream recording.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Q3 FY2019 Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. The company reported revenue of $3.181 billion, up 21% year-over-year, with net income of $1.230 billion ($1.97 per diluted share), up 47% from the prior year. A 2023 study analyzing U.S. mortality data from 1999-2020 found that Black people experienced 1.8 million excess deaths and over 80 million excess years of potential life lost (YPLL) compared to White people. After declining from 1999 to the early 2010s, racial mortality disparities plateaued and then reversed dramatically in 2020 due to COVID-19, eliminating two decades of progress. Heart disease caused the most excess deaths, while perinatal conditions showed the highest YPLL rates. The greatest disparities occurred among infants, with Black-White mortality rate ratios exceeding 2.3 for those under one year. The authors propose excess deaths and YPLL as national accountability metrics to track health equity progress.

One police officer and two Barrio 18 gang gunmen were killed, and eight officers wounded, during a clash in a poor San Salvador neighborhood where police were searching for illegal weapons. One deceased gunman was identified as a Barrio 18 leader suspected in over a dozen murders. The wounded officers sustained superficial bullet wounds; four were released and four remain hospitalized. The passage explains the Simple Moving Average (SMA) as a technical analysis tool used to identify market trends by averaging closing prices over a specified period. SMAs smooth price data to help traders make buy/sell decisions, with shorter periods suited for short-term trading and longer periods for long-term strategies. Backtests show that short-term SMAs work best for mean reversion (buying when price crosses below), while long-term SMAs favor trend-following (buying when price crosses above). The 200-day SMA is highlighted as effective, with lower drawdown than buy-and-hold. SMAs lag more than Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) due to equal weighting of prices. SMAs can be misleading with seasonal/cyclical stocks and in range-bound markets. They can also be applied to non-price data like volume. The optimal SMA period varies by asset and requires backtesting.

Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 partners, have left Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft for Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, joining offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. This patent application describes multi-carrier communication systems, particularly focusing on carrier aggregation (CA), dual connectivity (DC), and scheduling mechanisms in 5G NR networks. The document covers: OFDM subcarrier configurations and radio resource structures; timing advance groups (TAGs) including primary and secondary TAGs with associated random access procedures; multi-connectivity architectures with master and secondary gNBs; tight interworking between 5G RAN and LTE RAN with various deployment scenarios; gNB functional split options between central units (CU) and distributed units (DU); bandwidth part (BWP) configurations including activation/deactivation mechanisms and timer-based switching to default BWPs; logical channel prioritization procedures considering multiple TTIs/numerologies; and control resource set (CORESET) configurations for PDCCH monitoring. The application also addresses LAA (Licensed Assisted Access) operations with listen-before-talk procedures for unlicensed spectrum, and various protocol structures for MCG bearers, SCG bearers, and split bearers.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units of high-titer convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). The primary endpoint—proportion alive and free of mechanical ventilation at day 15—showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% vs. 84.1%, p=0.976). No differences were found in mortality, day 30 outcomes, or any secondary endpoints. Safety profiles were similar, with transfusion-related side effects in 5.9% of the intervention group. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not improve clinical outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

This study prospectively examined surgical diagnoses and outcomes of intestinal obstruction among 228 adults (75% male, median age 34) at three regional referral hospitals in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania from December 2021 to July 2022. Adhesions were the commonest surgical diagnosis (98 cases, OR 5.7), followed by hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20). The crude mortality rate was 5.3% (12 deaths), with 76% discharged home, 9% developing surgical site infections, and 5.3% having unknown outcomes. No significant differences in surgical outcomes were found between hospitals. The predominance of adhesions over hernias as a cause of obstruction differs from typical developing country patterns and may reflect referral bias or changing epidemiology.

Averaging down is a trading strategy where investors buy more shares of a stock after its price falls, lowering their average purchase price. The article examines when this approach works best, noting it suits long-term investors who understand the company, but poses risks for short-term traders who cannot distinguish temporary declines from serious problems. A backtest on SPY (S&P 500 ETF) compared two strategies: one without averaging down versus one splitting equity into two 50% positions. Results showed averaging down produced similar returns but smoother performance with reduced drawdowns and more efficient capital use. The strategy works best in mean-reverting markets like stocks, though backtesting and margin of safety are essential. The article provides a formula for calculating breakeven price: [(N1 × purchase price) + (N2 × second purchase price)] / (N1 + N2).

The Personalized Medicine Conference, held annually in South San Francisco since 2008, addresses genomic health themes through presentations by scientific leaders in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Co-founded by SF State Professor Michael A. Goldman and three Genentech alumni, the conference is hosted by San Francisco State University's Department of Biology in partnership with the university, its alumni, and the City of South San Francisco.

On June 2, 2017, Personalized Medicine 10.0 will commemorate a decade of conferences with the theme "Has It Changed Your Life?" The event will review past topics, assess previous predictions, and examine future directions in personalized medicine. Topics include bioinformatics, oncology, epigenetics, rare disease genomics, sequencing technologies, the microbiome, gene therapy, and genome editing.

Opening keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker, founder of the Nicholas Volker One In A Billion Foundation, will discuss how genetic sequencing saved her son's life. She emphasizes the need for improved provider training in using and interpreting these tools and for insurance coverage of sequencing and related care.

The conference features numerous distinguished speakers from academia, industry, and government. Registration is open to students, researchers, executives, health professionals, and community members, with information available through Eventbrite, the conference website, or direct email contact.

Therapeutic antibodies require developability properties like thermostability and low hydrophobicity beyond target binding. While diffusion generative models aid antibody design, they typically require iterative wet-lab refinement. Bayesian optimization suits this low-data, expensive-evaluation setting but faces challenges in surrogate model and acquisition function selection. Prior work has not incorporated structural information, whose benefits for antibody-specific versus binding properties remain unclear when binding poses are unknown. This work investigates how to integrate structural information into Bayesian optimization surrogate models, identifies tasks where it aids optimization, compares antibody-specific versus general protein structural models, and assesses whether structural information is necessary. The authors also propose a novel protein language model "soft constraint" for incorporating sequence-only prior information.

Cleveland Police shared a photo of Steve Stephens' vehicle on April 16, 2017, asking the public to call 9-1-1 if spotted. This study compares a chest radiograph-based biological aging clock (CXR-Age) with first-generation (Horvath Age) and second-generation (DNAm PhenoAge) epigenetic clocks using 2,097 participants from the Project Baseline Health Study. CXR-Age showed moderate correlation with chronological age (r=0.50) versus high correlation for epigenetic clocks (r≈0.94-0.95). CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge accelerations were independently associated with coronary artery calcium scores, reduced pulmonary function (particularly DLCO), and worse frailty/disability measures, with CXR-Age associations remaining significant in adults as young as 45. No significant correlation existed between CXR-Age and epigenetic clock accelerations, suggesting they capture different aging aspects. Proteomic analysis identified CDH13 and ApoD as significantly associated with CXR-Age acceleration, and 13 proteins with DNAm PhenoAge, with CDH13 shared between both. CXRs with highest age acceleration showed various lung abnormalities. The findings suggest CXR-Age could enable opportunistic biological age screening using routine clinical imaging to inform medical decisions currently based on chronological age.

This study presents PhenoID, a natural language processing pipeline for extracting and normalizing dysmorphology physical examination findings to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms from electronic health records. The two-module system uses transformer-based architecture: an extractor identifies spans of abnormal findings while ignoring normal ones, and a normalizer maps these to HPO term IDs. The authors created a manually annotated corpus of 3,826 observations from 1,655 individuals, with 935 unique HPO terms annotated. PhenoID achieved state-of-the-art performance with 0.717 F1 score on normalization, outperforming six competing systems including txt2hpo, Doc2HPO, NeuralCR, PhenoTagger, and PhenoBERT. Analysis revealed that with perfect span extraction, the normalizer alone achieved 0.82 F1, indicating extraction is the primary performance limitation. Common normalization errors stemmed from HPO ontology imperfections, descriptive clinical language rather than standardized terms, and attention mechanism misplacement. The system successfully handled disjoint and overlapping terms, and correctly ignored 98.4% of negated findings.

SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch on Monday carrying Hewlett Packard Enterprise's "Spaceborne Computer" to the International Space Station. The supercomputer, capable of one trillion calculations per second, is designed to process data in space rather than transmitting it all to Earth, addressing bandwidth limitations from high-definition satellite imagery. Unlike previous space computers that required extensive "hardening" protection, this uses commercial hardware with special software to detect radiation dangers and make adjustments. NASA scientist Julie Robinson noted successful operation could benefit private sector applications like crop monitoring and oil exploration. HPE engineer Mark Fernandez expects initial power-up confirmation on September 4, followed by 2.5 hours of functionality tests, then a year-long operational trial. Success could enable more powerful computers for future Mars missions, where communication delays pose significant challenges for astronaut safety.

Limiting nutrients that drug-resistant pathogens need more than drug-sensitive ones can prevent resistance from emerging by exploiting competition between strains. Penn State researchers demonstrated this with malaria-infected mice: when a key nutrient was restricted alongside traditional drug treatment, resistant strains failed to emerge, whereas 40% of mice developed resistance when given the nutrient. The approach works because resistant pathogens typically compete poorly against sensitive strains when drugs aren't present; limiting resources amplifies this disadvantage. This ecological strategy could extend existing drugs' effectiveness and be integrated into new drug development, though further research is needed to identify target nutrients and optimal interventions for diseases like tuberculosis and malaria.

London-St. Thomas unemployment rose to 5.5% in September while labour force participation dropped by 3,000 people. A King's University College study found about half of working adults in the area hold precarious jobs without security or benefits, with young people and minorities most affected. This patent application describes methods and apparatus for real-time automatic classification of objects represented by 3D point clouds, particularly for long-range objects. The invention uses a multi-stage classification approach: first computing spin image and covariance matrix classification statistics to estimate object class, then using iterative closest point (ICP) comparison against model point clouds only for the top two candidate classes when the first two classifiers disagree. The system employs chirped LIDAR with heterodyne or homodyne detection to generate point clouds, extracts surface normals to define translational and rotational invariant coordinate systems, and computes feature variables for classification. The method enables near real-time object classification for applications including collision avoidance and target identification.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces significant advancements across multiple areas. The GeForce RTX 50 Series features FP4 data format support in new Tensor Cores, reducing memory requirements by over half compared to FP16 while maintaining quality through advanced quantization, enabling large AI models like FLUX.dev to run on more GPUs with 2x performance gains.

For ray tracing, Blackwell's Fourth-Generation RT Cores deliver double the ray-triangle intersection throughput, introduce Mega Geometry technology with Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) for efficient handling of complex geometry, and add hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for rendering hair and fine geometry. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reordering efficiency.

The AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V scheduler, offloads GPU context management from the CPU to reduce latency and improve multitasking. Video capabilities expand with hardware encode/decode for 4:2:2 chroma sampling and a ninth-generation NVENC encoder improving AV1/HEVC quality by 5%. DisplayPort 2.1b support enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating with multiple new levels, accelerated frequency switching 1000x faster than previous architectures, and 10x faster entry into deep sleep states. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to 3 additional frames per rendered frame) using transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, replacing CNN architectures for improved temporal stability and detail.

Neural shaders enable new techniques including RTX Neural Materials for film-quality asset rendering, Neural Texture Compression for up to 7:1 VRAM savings, Neural Radiance Cache for efficient global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces for AI-enhanced facial rendering.

The architecture spans multiple GPUs: GB202 (flagship, 92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores), GB203 (high-end, 45.6B transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores), and GB205 (performance segment, 31B transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores), powering products from RTX 5090 down through RTX 5070.

Children worldwide receive their first cell phones at varying ages. In Germany, about 51% of children ages 6 to 13 own mobile phones, with smartphones less common than in the US. Across Europe, approximately 46% of children 9 to 16 own smartphones, with usage restrictions varying by country. In the US, 45% of children 10 to 12 have smartphones with service plans, and 42% of children 8 and younger own tablets. In South Korea, 72% of children ages 11 to 12 own smartphones. Taiwan shows rising ownership from 45% at age 11 to 71% at age 15. Turkish parents disagree on optimal ages, with 59.8% favoring ages 12 to 17. In South Africa, 81% of secondary students own or have access to mobile phones. Ghana and Malawi show lower ownership rates, though increasing from 2007 to 2014. In Australia, the median age for first phone ownership is 8 years. The American Academy of Pediatrics states no "right" age exists, recommending limited screen time for young children and parental monitoring of media use.

The passage describes the development of a new embedded atom method (EAM) potential for the ternary tungsten-hydrogen-helium (W-H-He) system to simulate radiation damage in fusion reactor materials. Tungsten is a candidate plasma-facing component material due to its high melting point and thermal conductivity, but suffers from microstructural changes under irradiation, including gas bubble formation and material embrittlement. The authors extend an existing W-H potential by Mason et al. to include helium interactions, using a generalized Finnis-Sinclair formulation that allows negative electron density values. The fitting process employs a global minimization algorithm optimizing against DFT data for defect formation energies, binding energies, and relaxation volumes. Key features include: a W-He pair potential with weak interactions based on quantum mechanical studies; a helium embedding function with repulsive response to electron density; a revised He-He potential incorporating high-pressure DFT data for hexagonal close-packed helium; and H-He interactions fitted to vacuum dimer binding energies. The potential aims to accurately describe vacancy-gas and void-gas interactions, as well as defect relaxation volumes contributing to irradiation-induced swelling, addressing limitations in existing W-H-He potentials.

The Renewable Energy Alaska Project is training residents from five Southeast Alaska diesel-powered villages as energy assessors to help reduce high electric bills. For $25, these "energy leaders" conduct household assessments identifying simple improvements like LED bulbs and insulated coffee pots that can reduce bills by about 10%. The program, running through July 31, partners with tribes to make energy assessments more accessible, as professional audits cost thousands. While small fixes don't address diesel dependence, they provide immediate financial relief for communities still years away from alternative energy sources like tidal power.

National Australia Bank executive Andrew Hagger called the practice of financial advisers falsely witnessing superannuation beneficiary documents "sloppy and unprofessional." The banking royal commission has revealed widespread misconduct in financial planning divisions of major banks and AMP, despite years of whistleblower testimony, media reporting, and parliamentary inquiries on issues including trailing commissions, conflicted advice, and fees for no service. A notable case involved Joe Hockey's mother-in-law, who lost significant savings after a CBA planner invested her money in high-risk products, with the bank initially offering inadequate compensation.

Commercial property owners in Southern Nevada have been paying unapproved trash fees charged by Republic Services, the sole waste-management company for Clark County and the cities of Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, and Henderson. The Las Vegas City Council plans to introduce an ordinance Wednesday to codify these fees, including commercial container delivery ($65.10), removal ($65.10), and exchange ($100.15) fees, plus an industrial dry run fee ($107.42). Local ordinances require city councils and county commissioners to approve such fees, but elected officials across the region were unaware of the situation. Republic Services claims it reports supplemental service fees annually to municipalities, who they say approve them through that process. Officials from North Las Vegas and Las Vegas declined to comment, while Henderson acknowledged the fees "possibly" violate their ordinance. Clark County stated Republic does not need commissioner approval for these commercial fees.

This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate causal relationships between gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM). Using GWAS summary data from European populations, the researchers identified six gut microbial taxa causally associated with FM: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales (protective); and genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 (risk factors). They also identified 82 plasma metabolites associated with FM, with key pathways including caffeine metabolism, α-linolenic acid metabolism, and GLP-1/incretin regulation. Mediation analysis revealed that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine mediate the relationship between Enterobacteriaceae/Enterobacteriales and FM. The study suggests dietary interventions—limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 intake, adopting low glycemic index diets, and reducing oxalate consumption—as potential strategies to alleviate FM symptoms. Limitations include lack of demographic data for subgroup analysis and European-only ancestry limiting generalizability.

Guinness is partnering with former Arsenal footballer Thierry Henry for its Made of Black program in Nigeria and across Africa. Henry will highlight individuals demonstrating the Made of Black spirit. The campaign, launched in August 2014 on MTV Base, celebrates African attitude and mindset. This season, Guinness will host Fanzone activations with live football and music experiences and continue sponsoring EPL broadcasts through DStv.

This patent application describes implantable medical devices, particularly cochlear implants and other hearing prostheses, with improved MRI compatibility. The devices feature a magnet surrounded by an elastomeric body (such as silicone) with rigid plates sandwiching the magnet. When subjected to external magnetic fields (e.g., from MRI machines of 0.2T to 3T or higher), the magnet rotates and pushes the plates apart, which tensions the elastomeric material to create a restoring force that limits further rotation. The magnet can freely revolve within a container to align with external magnets while resisting rotation in other planes. The device includes a slit in the elastomeric housing to enable insertion or removal of the magnet apparatus. Various embodiments utilize different plate configurations, spring mechanisms, and materials to achieve the desired force-displacement characteristics for resisting torque while maintaining functionality.

TCI Fund Management reduced its valuation of Zodiac Aerospace shares to 7-10 euros after the French company posted a first-half loss, down from its previous 10 euro valuation. The activist hedge fund is pressuring Safran to abandon its acquisition bid, stating offers above 10 euros would destroy value, citing Zodiac's reported first-half 2017 loss and unrealistic margin forecasts.

Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell stated that demand for AI computing power is "tremendous" and that while "at some point there'll be too many" AI data centers, there are no signs of oversupply yet. Dell's stock rose over 3% after the company raised its long-term revenue growth target to 7-9% (from 3-4%) and diluted earnings per share growth to 15% (from 8%). The company plans to ship $20 billion worth of AI servers in fiscal 2026, double the previous year's sales. Dell's server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter.

This 1942 tripartite agreement between Belgium, the United Kingdom, and the United States governs commodity purchases from the Congo during World War II. Key provisions include: minimum purchase quantities with flexibility for additional purchases (Article 2); price agreements between governments (Article 3); standard payment methods with provisions for unshipped goods (Article 4); equal customs treatment for Congo and British colonial products (Article 5); Allied supply deliveries to Congo (Article 6); prohibition of transactions aiding enemy powers (Article 7); coordinated export licensing for economic warfare (Article 8); and immediate effect upon signature (Article 9). U.S. State Department comments address: agreement revision upon Belgian liberation; price information requests; foreign exchange considerations; payment for unshipped commodities; shipping arrangements; uncompleted transactions from prior agreements; options on entire Congo output; and proposed development articles to increase production of needed materials like pyrethrum.

This article presents three bullish candlestick patterns that showed positive results in backtests: the Bearish Engulfing Pattern, Three Outside Down Pattern, and Bullish Harami. Tests were conducted on the S&P 500 (SPY) from 1993 to October 2021 using a simple exit rule when the close exceeded the previous day's high. The Bearish Engulfing Pattern produced 296 trades with 5% CAGR and 71% win ratio. The Three Outside Down Pattern yielded 112 trades with 2.3% CAGR and 78% win ratio. The Bullish Harami generated 306 trades with 3.1% CAGR and 76% win ratio. The authors note that while most candlestick patterns fail quantitative tests, these three demonstrated reasonable predictive value, though they caution that results could be improved with additional variables.

The Turkish government issued detention warrants for 133 former public servants on Thursday over alleged links to the Gülen movement, based on their alleged use of the ByLock messaging app. The warrants, issued by the Ankara Chief Prosecutor's Office, cover 101 Finance Ministry and 32 Labor Ministry personnel across 11 provinces, with only four still on active duty. Additional detentions occurred nationwide: 14 women in a Uşak-based investigation, 18 teachers in Aksaray and Ankara, 19 military personnel in a Trabzon-based operation including two cadets previously dismissed, and others in Kozan and Bitlis-based investigations. Turkish authorities claim ByLock was used by Gülen followers; tens of thousands have been arrested or dismissed since the July 15, 2016 coup attempt. The Justice Ministry reported 50,510 arrests and 169,013 legal proceedings on coup charges, with over 150,000 judges, teachers, police and civil servants suspended or dismissed. Fethullah Gülen denied involvement in the coup and called for an international investigation.

NVIDIA's Titan V graphics card has demonstrated strong performance in leaked benchmarks, outperforming the Titan Xp and GTX 1080 Ti in synthetic tests despite lower clockspeeds. Sunderland manager David Moyes urged his players to create more scoring chances for striker Jermain Defoe after the forward returned to the England national team. Defoe has scored 14 of Sunderland's 24 league goals this season. Moyes stressed that other players must also perform as the team faces relegation, sitting seven points from safety with 10 games remaining. Sunderland have won once in their last 11 league matches and face Watford, Leicester City, and Manchester United in the next eight days.

The RSI & ADX Trading Strategy combines three technical indicators—RSI, ADX, and IBS—for short-term trading. RSI (Relative Strength Index), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, measures momentum with values between 0-100; above 70 indicates overbought conditions, below 30 indicates oversold conditions. ADX (Average Directional Movement Index), also by Wilder from 1978, measures trend strength without indicating direction, using DMI+ and DMI- components; backtesting suggests 5-10 day periods with 30-40 threshold values work best. IBS (Internal Bar Strength) is a mean-reversion indicator oscillating between 0-1, where low values signal buying and high values signal selling.

Individual backtests show: IBS on QQQ yielded 12.1% CAGR with 32% risk-adjusted return; RSI on SPY yielded 7.5% CAGR with 18% risk-adjusted return; ADX on SPY yielded 6.5% CAGR with 10.3% risk-adjusted return. Combining two indicators on SPY produced 56% risk-adjusted return with only 14% market exposure, profiting in 2022 and 2008 with only 2018 losing (-5.5%). The combined strategy on QQQ averaged 1.3% gain per trade with no losing years since 2000.

A closed Erie public school reopened as Erie Federal Credit Union's new corporate headquarters and 9th branch after an 18-month renovation. The 42,000-square-foot facility offers full banking services, a community room for meetings and potential polling place, and incorporates preserved school history including original lettering and foundation blocks. The project used local designers and contractors, returns the property to tax rolls, and accommodates future growth.

Beluga whales Qila and Aurora died from an unidentified toxin at the Vancouver Aquarium in November 2016. Researchers collected sufficient DNA from the mother and daughter to sequence the complete beluga genome, which they believe is one of the most complete mammalian genomes mapped. This will help scientists understand beluga adaptation to rapidly changing environments and aid conservation efforts. The study was published in the journal Genes.

Citadel Securities hired Anthony Cronin from Societe Generale to lead European Treasuries trading, expanding its market-making coverage across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. The firm aims to become a top global dealer in dollar rates products, having grown its Treasury counterparties to over 450 since 2016 and increased trading volume nearly fourfold. It plans to add Treasury Inflation Protected Securities and strips this year, with the goal of eventually becoming a Federal Reserve primary dealer. The firm also hired Michele How for fixed-income sales in January and has about 100 Treasury clients across 17 Asian and European countries.

Recent riots in France's immigrant-heavy suburbs, sparked by allegations of police brutality, may boost Marine Le Pen's presidential campaign. The National Front leader, who runs on an anti-immigrant, tough-on-crime platform, has gained support as her main conservative rival François Fillon faces scandal. Over 50 violent incidents occurred in approximately 30 towns near Paris in one night, with nearly 250 arrests made. Unlike 2005 riots, no firearms have been used against police. The author, who incorrectly predicted Brexit and Trump's victories, considers Le Pen's win unlikely but possible.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures market momentum by calculating the difference between two exponential moving averages (3 and 10 days standard) of the Accumulation/Distribution Line. It oscillates around zero, with positive values indicating buying pressure and negative values indicating selling pressure. The indicator generates signals through divergences and zero-line crosses. Quantified tests of ten trading strategies on the S&P 500 found limited profitability: a basic zero-cross strategy yielded 2.4% CAGR, a mean-reversion approach produced 287 trades with 0.54% average return and 37% max drawdown, and RSI-combination strategies resulted in 216 trades with 0.3% average return and 17-18% drawdowns. The article concludes the indicator lacks significant predictive value in tested strategies, though it may gauge buying/selling pressure.

The team has faced frustration throughout the playoffs, particularly after losing home games they felt they could have won. Players Zach Parise and Andy Greene discuss needing to capitalize on scoring chances, with Parise noting they've hit posts and had opportunities but failed to convert. University of Kansas researcher Brock Ternes found that well ownership correlates with increased water use during droughts, contrary to common assumptions about conservation. Surveying 864 Kansans, Ternes discovered that private well owners—who are more aware of their water supplies than municipal water users—actually irrigate more during droughts to protect crops, while relying on precipitation during non-drought years. His research on the High Plains Aquifer, which faces depletion in portions of southwestern Kansas within 25 years, suggests that groundwater stewardship requires selective timing for extractions rather than uniform reduction. Ternes argues that well owners should be studied as a distinct social group with unique drought responses, and will present these findings at the American Sociological Association's 2017 meeting in Montreal.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS) that controls autonomous vehicle operations safely using AI and machine learning techniques. The system receives sensor data to generate and maintain an internal 3D map of the vehicle's environment and state. Based on this map, goals, and safety considerations, it generates a plan of action comprising sequences of planned actions. The system uses various AI techniques including convolutional neural networks for object detection and reinforcement learning for action planning. Key safety features include: evaluating "what-if" scenarios through simulations of possible future situations by modifying internal map parameters; dynamically controlling sensor behavior (data content, timing, format); generating confidence scores to assess AI model prediction reliability; providing users with information about planned actions and their reasons; and implementing a safety indicator with interruptible commands for reinforcement learning models. The system comprises subsystems including sensors interface, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information subsystems. The internal map uses a multi-layered graph data structure for efficient storage and querying.

Leon Cooperman believes the stock market has reached the late stage of a bull market that Warren Buffett warned about, where excessive valuations and crowd behavior driven by momentum rather than fundamentals create bubble risks. This patent application describes methods and apparatus for ACK/NACK feedback in wireless networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station sends a user equipment (UE) information indicating PDCCH monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether ACK/NACK feedback across TRPs is allowed, rules for ACK/NACK feedback bundling when allowed, and a DAI definition indicating whether DAIs from multiple TRPs are independent or joint. The UE receives this configuration, determines ACK/NACK codebook size based on PDCCH monitoring occasions and DCIs from multiple TRPs, and transmits either joint ACK/NACK feedback in a PUCCH based on the bundling rules or multiple individual ACK/NACK feedbacks to separate TRPs. Two DAI approaches are described: joint DAI counting grants across all TRPs and carriers (requiring tight coordination), and independent DAI counting grants per TRP (allowing loose coordination with UE performing additional calculations to combine DAIs for bundled feedback).

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Mercer County provided unassembled bicycles to seven children awaiting mentors, who partnered with local law enforcement officers and community members to build them. Each team will build a second bicycle for donation through Capital K-9. Materials were funded by an I am Trenton Community Foundation grant.

C-BerryTrans is a C++ code licensed under GNU GPL 3.0 that computes anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) directly from WIEN2k DFT outputs without Wannier function interpolation. The code calculates Berry curvature (Ω) using the Kubo formula from eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements, then integrates Ω over the Brillouin zone with Fermi-Dirac weighting for AHC or entropy function weighting for ANC. Key features include parallelization over k-points via OpenMP, binary file storage for efficient data handling, and post-processing capability to compute AHC/ANC across temperature and chemical potential ranges after initial Ω calculation. The code requires SOC-enabled calculations and provides modules for k-list generation, Ω computation, and visualization. It has been validated on Fe, Pd, Fe3Al, and Co2FeAl.

The passage proposes a new hybrid framework combining the method of moments (MoM) with the generalized scattering matrix (GSM) for analyzing multiscale electromagnetic problems involving antennas embedded in large structures like radomes, reflectors, or biological tissues. Unlike previous MoM-T-matrix approaches that represent large bodies via spherical-wave expansion, this method inverts the roles: the electrically large environment is solved by MoM while the antenna is described by its compact GSM representation. This reduces unknowns, enables modular reuse of antenna data, and leverages recent GSM advances including Wigner translation theorems and array synthesis. The framework can evolve into specialized variants: a GSM-PO hybrid for large reflectors capturing higher-order interactions, and a GSM-T-matrix hybrid for structures amenable to spherical-wave expansion. The formulation derives coupled equations for equivalent currents on penetrable structures using PMCHWT integral equations with RWG basis functions, where antenna fields are expressed as vector spherical wave expansions and coupled to the MoM system through the GSM's source-scattering representation.

The Single/Double Offense uses double and down screens to free shooters, requiring defenders to disrupt both screen types. NBA teams prefer "Show and Recover" over switching to avoid post mismatches. Phase 1 involves dictating shooter direction away from preferred sides. Phase 2's "Show & Recover" has screeners' defenders step out to force shooters wide while chasers go under screens, then recover to deny post entries. Phase 3 defends single screens similarly. "All Out SOS Disruption" initiates action by trapping wing shooters, forcing freelancing. This uses aggressive on-ball pressure, sideline pushpoints, inverted big defenders, sequential switches, contact switches, snuggle denials, and triangle "I" positions for help defense and trap coverage. Rotations must occur as the ball leaves passers' hands.

This lecture covers the Weierstrass M-test for uniform convergence of function series, its application to power series, and the Weierstrass Approximation Theorem. The M-test states that if functions f_j on a set S are dominated by summable non-negative numbers M_j, then their partial sums converge uniformly. This is applied to show power series converge uniformly on any closed interval strictly inside their radius of convergence, enabling term-by-term differentiation and integration. The radius of convergence remains unchanged under differentiation. The lecture concludes with the Weierstrass Approximation Theorem: any continuous function on [0,1] can be uniformly approximated by polynomials, proved using an approximation to the identity constructed from polynomials q_n(x) = c_n(1-x²)^n that concentrate mass at the origin.

Louisville officials advise residents against setting off fireworks in neighborhoods on Independence Day due to particle pollution from smoke, which can worsen air quality, aggravate respiratory conditions, and sometimes exceed federal limits. The Air Pollution Control District issues annual advisories, noting that airborne and exploding fireworks are illegal in city limits. Cumulative use of smaller fireworks citywide can create more pollution than the city's official show. The last federal limit exceedance occurred in 2015.
