The framework aligns with five curriculum design categories and represents academic society involvement in curriculum development through a four-step process: assessing current learner situations, interpreting gaps relative to social changes, developing curriculum standards, and revising the national curriculum.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on March 6, 2019, reporting two compensatory actions approved by its Compensation Committee. On March 6, 2019, the Committee approved a new form of global performance-based restricted stock unit notice and agreement under the 2007 Equity Incentive Plan. On March 8, 2019, the Committee adopted the Fiscal Year 2020 Variable Compensation Plan, which allows eligible executive officers to earn variable cash payments based on corporate revenue performance goals. The plan requires participants to remain employed through the payment date. Target award opportunities for base operating plan achievement range from $250,000 to $1,100,000 for named executive officers, representing 29% to 110% of fiscal year 2020 base salary.

Robert Cyrus Garrison was convicted of First Degree Rape in Tulsa County and sentenced to 30 years. The Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals found that the trial court's instruction about good time credits, as required by 57 O.S.Supp.1969, § 138, was unconstitutional based on precedent in *Williams v. State*. While the court declined to reverse the conviction, it held the instruction was prejudicial to sentencing and modified the sentence from 30 years to 15 years.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 13, 2019, announcing two executive appointments. Zachary Kirkhorn, 34, was appointed Chief Financial Officer, succeeding Deepak Ahuja. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in March 2010 and most recently served as Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations. He will receive $12 million in stock options and $4 million in restricted stock units vesting over four years. Vaibhav Taneja, 41, was appointed Chief Accounting Officer, having served as Corporate Controller since May 2018. He previously worked at SolarCity and PricewaterhouseCoopers. Taneja will receive $6 million in stock options and $2 million in restricted stock units vesting over four years.

The Port Hardy Secondary School Senior Girls soccer team qualified for the BC Single A High School Provincials in Penticton by finishing second at the Island Championships in Duncan. After winning their opening match 6-1 against Duncan Christian School, they lost 5-4 to top-ranked Glenlyon Norfolk. They defeated second-ranked St. Andrews 3-1 in overtime to secure their provincial berth, then lost 4-3 to Glenlyon Norfolk in the final—being the only team to score against them in the tournament. The provincials will take place May 31 to June 3. Players expressed excitement about traveling and competing, while coaches emphasized team belief and representing the school well.

A state audit found former Duquesne School District superintendent Barbara McDonnell and four employees used district funds as a "personal piggy bank," authorizing $41,000 in no-interest personal loans without board approval. McDonnell received $22,000, including $1,000 for "the holidays and my daughter." The audit also cited questionable accounting for $1.3 million in transportation reimbursements and at least $180,000 in state overpayments. While the employees repaid the loans through payroll deductions, State Auditor General Eugene DePasquale referred the matter to the State Ethics Commission.

This 1920 Republican presidential nomination acceptance speech emphasizes party government over personal rule, constitutional restoration after wartime executive overreach, and rejection of the League of Nations to preserve American independence. The speaker pledges reduced armaments, an association of nations based on justice rather than force, and domestic policies including railway privatization, agricultural support through cooperatives, deflation to restore the dollar's value, tax reduction, protective tariffs, immigration restrictions, law enforcement including Prohibition, veterans' benefits, and women's suffrage ratification.

The Maine Lobstering Union (Lobster 207), formed in 2013 as both a union local of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers and a cooperative business, represented approximately 550 self-employed Maine lobstermen by 2017. The organizing effort, led by IAM special representative Dave "Sully" Sullivan and organizer Joel Pitcher, emerged after lobster prices hit a 20-year low of $1.80/lb in 2012, threatening the livelihoods of independent fishermen who lacked collective bargaining power due to anti-trust restrictions.

Lobster 207 achieved political victories first, including passing legislation protecting lobstermen on military duty, partnering with environmental groups to defeat harmful dredging projects, and defeating a Right to Work bill. The group then established economic power by incorporating as a statewide marketing cooperative, which exempted members from anti-trust laws and allowed collective price-setting. In February 2017, Lobster 207 purchased the Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound's wholesale operations for $4 million, financed through the union-affiliated Bank of Labor, other IAM locals, and seller financing. The acquisition gave members profit-sharing opportunities, group purchasing power, and vertical integration into the lobster supply chain. By 2016, average prices lobstermen received had risen 52% to the highest level since 2006.

Warren Buffett is reportedly considering Berkshire Hathaway's largest acquisition since 2022, with plans to purchase Occidental Petroleum's petrochemical unit OxyChem for approximately $10 billion. The deal could finalize within days. Berkshire currently holds a 28.2% stake in Occidental worth over $11 billion. Buffett, 95, is stepping down as CEO at year-end 2025 but will remain chairman, with successor Greg Abel taking over. Occidental's shares fell 1.8% following the report. Berkshire holds a record $344 billion in cash.

Christian Pulisic scored and assisted in a 4-0 U.S. victory over Panama in World Cup qualifying, with Jozy Altidore scoring twice and Bobby Wood adding a goal. The win moved the U.S. into third place in the region with 12 points, two ahead of Panama, putting them in position to qualify with a win or likely a draw against Trinidad and Tobago. Pulisic, playing his first match since turning 19, was moved to central midfield by coach Bruce Arena and sparked the attack from the start. His opening goal completed a 112-yard move, and he had been involved in 11 of the Americans' 14 goals in the hexagonal round.

Captain George O. Baker, a 58-year-old master mariner from Dartmouth with experience since 1848, testified about whaling in the Ochotsk and Japan seas. He stated the whaling season runs from mid-August to mid-October, with September being the best month. He would expect 6-10 whales per season, yielding about 10,000 pounds of bone and 900 barrels of oil. He considered returning to whaling grounds after October 1 impractical due to rugged weather with northerly and easterly winds. The document includes a certification by Secretary of State John Hay dated September 1, 1900.

The passage compares Trump's policies to grievances in the Declaration of Independence. Trump's disregard for rule of law and checks and balances contradicts Founding principles. His deferral to military advice violates civilian control of armed forces, which the Founders valued. The Founders supported immigration for economic growth, while Trump blames immigrants for wage stagnation—though economists attribute this to union decline. The Founders also valued judicial independence, which Trump has undermined through attacks on the Mueller investigation, Department of Justice, and judges.

This MIT lecture discusses capabilities as an alternative approach to privilege separation in operating systems. The professor begins by introducing the "confused deputy problem," where a Fortran compiler with elevated privileges could be tricked into overwriting sensitive system files because it implicitly combined user privileges with its own elevated permissions. This illustrates the problem of "ambient authority," where access control decisions depend on implicit process credentials rather than explicit authorization.

The lecture then explores capabilities, which are unforgeable tokens granting specific access rights to objects. Unlike Unix's permission model, capabilities require explicit possession to access resources, eliminating ambient authority. The professor uses Unix file descriptors as a practical example of capabilities—integers referencing kernel-managed tables that cannot be forged by user processes.

The Capsicum system for FreeBSD is presented as a capability-based sandboxing mechanism. It introduces `cap_enter()` to restrict processes to capability mode, where only existing file descriptors can be used, eliminating global namespaces like the filesystem root. Kernel modifications include `openat()` for directory-relative access, process descriptors (`pdfork`), and restricted network access. The `libcapsicum` library provides `lch_start()` for clean sandbox initialization and named file descriptor passing.

Applications like tcpdump and gzip were modified to use Capsicum, though this often requires restructuring code to separate privileged and unprivileged components. The professor compares Capsicum to virtual machine sandboxing, noting Capsicum's finer-grained sharing and lower overhead, though it requires developer awareness. Limitations include the difficulty of knowing all required capabilities beforehand, addressed partially by the Casper helper daemon for dynamic requests. Security guarantees depend on correct developer usage, proper capability masks, and kernel correctness.

The Magic Formula is a stock selection strategy popularized by Joel Greenblatt that ranks companies based on two metrics: return on invested capital (ROIC) and earnings yield (EY). The strategy aims to identify undervalued companies with strong financials by selecting stocks that rank highest in both metrics.

Historical backtests show mixed results. Greenblatt's original 1988-2004 study found annual returns of 30.8% for top-ranked stocks versus 12.4% for the S&P 500. However, more recent data shows significant underperformance from 2014 onward. International studies in Nordic countries demonstrated outperformance, though critics note returns may concentrate in small-cap stocks and exclude transaction costs.

The strategy faces criticism for its simplicity, lack of qualitative factors, sector concentration risks, and reliance on historical data. Risks include potential underperformance compared to growth stocks in certain market environments and mechanical selection ignoring management quality. Proponents cite its simplicity, ease of implementation, and long-term track record as advantages.

German tuner Alpha-N Performance modified a BMW M4 Coupe for Nürburgring time attack, achieving 560 horsepower through bespoke engine software and borrowing gearbox software from the M4 GTS. Upgrades include Öhlins coilover suspension, 20-inch OZ Racing wheels, carbon fiber hood and rear wing, custom front bumper, and Recaro bucket seats. The modified M4 lapped the Nürburgring in 7:20, beating the M4 GTS's 7:28 time. Pricing is available upon request.

National Weather Service zone forecast for Vermont and Northern New York issued March 19, 2018, covering Eastern Clinton, Western Clinton, Northern St. Lawrence, Southwestern St. Lawrence, Southeastern St. Lawrence, Northern Franklin, Southern Franklin, Eastern Essex, and Western Essex zones. Forecasts include sunny to partly sunny conditions with highs ranging from lower 20s to mid 30s and lows from near zero to mid 20s through Sunday. Northwest to west winds 10-15 mph early, becoming light and variable or northeast later. Sunday brings 30 percent chance of snow showers to most zones.

Roundhill Investments relaunched its meme stock ETF under the ticker MEME, which previously closed in 2023 after launching near the 2021 Nasdaq peak. The ETF fell over 96% during its first run, and analysts warn the relaunch may signal market exuberance. The new fund holds stocks like MicroStrategy and quantum computing companies, falling over 2% on its first trading day.

The lecture explains two techniques for designing infinite impulse response (IIR) digital filters: impulse invariance and bilinear transformation. Both methods map analog Butterworth filters to digital filters. Analog Butterworth filters are defined by magnitude squared function 1/(1+(jω/jω_c)^(2N)), with cutoff frequency ω_c and order N determining the frequency response shape.

The example designs a digital lowpass filter with passband below 0.2π and stopband above 0.3π, requiring less than 1dB passband ripple and at least 15dB stopband attenuation. For impulse invariance, analog specifications are obtained by Ω=ω/T, yielding N≈5.89 and ω_cT≈0.7047. Rounding up to N=6 and meeting passband specifications exactly compensates for aliasing effects. The parameter T proves irrelevant as it cancels out in the final design.

For bilinear transformation, critical frequencies are pre-warped using arctangent, yielding N≈5.3. Again rounding to N=6, the design meets stopband specifications exactly since aliasing is not an issue. The bilinear transformation produces better high-frequency attenuation than impulse invariance due to frequency compression. Both methods can be extended to bandpass, bandstop, and highpass filters through frequency transformations.

MDC-T president Thokozani Khupe defended her breakaway faction's leadership elections, criticizing male rivals as "cowardly" for attacking women leaders. Khupe was elected leader at a Saturday congress in Bulawayo, with Obert Gutu as vice president, Nixon Nyikadzino as secretary-general, and Abedinico Bhebhe as national chair. The election of Linda Masarira as spokesperson angered some members who claimed she was imposed, though Khupe's spokesperson Witness Dube insisted Masarira met constitutional requirements and highlighted the party's 50-50 gender representation. Khupe accused Nelson Chamisa of hijacking the party after Morgan Tsvangirai's death; Chamisa has sought a court interdict to stop Khupe from using MDC trademarks. A Bulawayo High Court judgment was reserved, while the Constitutional Court deemed Khupe's case urgent. The trademark dispute is significant as the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission requires such conflicts be resolved before nomination day.

Walmart announced a new education benefit allowing US employees to earn associate's or bachelor's degrees in business or supply chain management for $1 per day, with the company covering remaining tuition, fees, and books. The program, available to all part-time, full-time, and salaried workers after 90 days of employment, is offered through Guild Education in partnership with three online universities. Workers can earn college credits for paid job training. Walmart expects 68,000 of its 1.4 million eligible employees to participate over five years. The program replaces a previous 15% tuition discount and follows Walmart's February wage increase to $11 per hour. Other companies including McDonald's, Starbucks, and hotel chains have also expanded tuition benefits amid competitive labor markets.

Elite defensive ends are prioritized in football as the primary way to disrupt modern pass-heavy offenses. They line up on the edge of the defensive line, responsible for stopping the run and pressuring quarterbacks through sacks, hurries, and batted passes. The position requires a rare combination of size (typically 6'3"-6'7", 270-290 lbs), strength, quickness, and athleticism. Notable players include Reggie White (198 career sacks), Bruce Smith (NFL all-time sack leader), and Dwight Freeney. As offenses spread formations and release more receivers, defensive ends increasingly face one-on-one matchups against tackles, making their pass-rushing ability critical to defensive success without requiring frequent blitzes.

A 1917 memorandum outlines research being prepared for peace conference negotiations, covering: fisheries and natural resources; demographic and cultural data on populations; economic geography including trade routes and barriers; military geography and strategic frontiers; international law; and economic studies of participating nations' strengths and weaknesses. Material is being assembled on European strategic frontiers, economic intercourse restrictions, financial positions, shipping, industrial needs, and Russo-German commercial relations. The Executive Committee will edit submissions into brief, readable form with issue briefs. Costs cover only essential paid workers and supplies. A separate letter from Walter Lippmann to Colonel House regarding reconstruction is incomplete. The document also assesses Allied military situation against the Berlin-Baghdad project, noting German territorial gains but successful Allied captures of Baghdad, Palestine, and Arabia that have neutralized German threats to India, Suez, and the Red Sea.

A father in Indiana purchased $10,000 worth of bitcoin at $4,000 per coin to help pay for his daughter's wedding; the cryptocurrency's value quadrupled to over $16,000, now covering the entire event. The family uses a BitPay card to convert bitcoin for vendor payments. While some financial experts warn of bitcoin's volatility and risks, calling it a gamble or bubble, others see growing mainstream confidence in it as a store of value and praise its underlying blockchain technology.

Utah County hired former federal public defender Kathryn N. Nester to represent Tyler James Robinson, 22, who is accused of fatally shooting conservative activist Charlie Kirk on September 10, 2025, at Utah Valley University. Robinson could face the death penalty. The defense contract is expected to cost $750,000 over one year, while the prosecutor's office will receive about $600,000. Commissioner Skyler Beltran stated commissioners had no choice but to approve over $1 million in expenses that taxpayers will cover. Nester previously served as executive director of Federal Defenders of San Diego and federal public defender for Utah, and also represented Kouri Richins, a grief author accused of killing her husband.

A hockey player reflects on his team's improved performance after losing the first two games, noting that their fourth and third lines secured wins at home. He emphasizes the need for the top lines to maintain defensive play, create more scoring chances without taking risks, and play smart defensively by moving the puck up the boards. He credits their early road success with building confidence and notes the team is now playing with better energy and puck movement, similar to their earlier playoff form.

DNA research by AncestryDNA reveals Britons have an average of 16,000 relatives up to eighth cousins, far more than the six most people estimate. The North West has the largest families at 20,000 relatives, while the South East, South West and East Anglia fall below average. The average adult knows only 1% of their family. Seven million customers have used home-testing kits. The figures were released for DNA Day, marking the 1953 discovery of DNA's double helix structure.

The TLV321x devices feature an internal Power-on-Reset (POR) circuit that activates for up to 32µs after crossing 1.65V during power-up, holding the output low until the supply reaches minimum voltage. The basic comparator compares VIN to VREF, with output logic invertible by swapping inputs. Propagation delay varies with overdrive voltage, with smaller overdrives causing longer delays. The devices have 1.8mV internal hysteresis, but external hysteresis can be added via positive feedback networks—requiring three resistors for inverting configurations and two resistors plus VREF for non-inverting configurations. A low-side current sensing application uses an amplifier with a comparator, requiring 0.1µF bypass capacitors near supply pins to prevent ringing and false triggers. Layout recommendations include minimizing input-output coupling, using controlled impedance traces for long distances, and placing series resistors close to the device.

President Wilson addresses Congress on the state of the Union, emphasizing faith in democracy and right over might as America's guiding principle. He argues this faith won World War I and must now guide domestic and foreign policy. He urges Congress to pass a budget bill to establish systematic financial management, noting improved national finances with reduced debt and expenditures. He recommends tax simplification, particularly income and profits taxes, and calls for adequate care and vocational training for disabled veterans. Wilson also requests legislation on dyestuffs manufacturing, agricultural improvement, cold storage regulation, and federal licensing for interstate corporations. He proposes a supervised loan to Armenia and recommends granting independence to the Philippines, which has demonstrated stable self-government.

This document specifies the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD's Secure Encrypted Virtualization technologies (SEV-ES and SEV-SNP), which protect guest register state from hypervisor access by encrypting it during world switches. The GHCB is a 4KB shared memory area enabling controlled communication between guest and hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), where guests selectively expose register state. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap, SEV-SNP support, and various enhancements including APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL execution, page state changes, and trusted I/O. The document details GHCB layout, MSR protocol functions for version negotiation and CPUID requests, GPA registration requirements for SEV-SNP guests, NAE event handling procedures, and specific protocols for I/O, MMIO, MSR access, and AP management. Key structures include the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area for message sequence numbers and the EFI Confidential Computing Blob for firmware-to-OS communication.

LASIK is a common, pain-free eye surgery to correct vision and eliminate the need for glasses or contact lenses. The procedure offers immediate results, with most patients able to resume normal activities within 24 hours without bandages or stitches. It also reduces long-term expenses by eliminating costs for eye check-ups, prescription updates, and replacement eyewear.

This passage documents diplomatic and military developments during World War I, focusing on Latin American, Asian, and African countries' changing relations with Germany and the Allied powers. Key events include: the sinking of Argentine and Peruvian ships by German submarines; multiple Latin American nations severing relations with or declaring war on Germany and Austria-Hungary between September 1917 and December 1917, including Costa Rica, Peru, Uruguay, Brazil, Ecuador, Panama, and Cuba; the revocation of Brazilian and Uruguayan neutrality; American fleet visits to South American ports; negotiations over seized German ships; China's and Siam's declarations of war against Germany; Liberia's severance of relations and subsequent declaration of war; British maritime restrictions affecting neutral trade; and various neutral duties and responsibilities of the United States regarding recruitment, armed merchant ships, and treatment of German vessels in American ports prior to U.S. war entry.

Amendment 3 (4 May 2021) documents post-hoc statistical analysis changes. Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed for eligibility; 489 were randomized to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163), with 10 not randomized. Day 15 visits were completed for 434 patients; 55 missed due to loss to follow-up (14), death (14), hospital discharge (18), and other reasons (9). Day 30 visits were completed for 423 patients; 66 missed due to loss to follow-up (31), death (27), hospital discharge (5), and other reasons (3). Protocol deviations are summarized in Appendix 8.9.

A total solar eclipse will cross the United States on August 21, visible from Oregon to South Carolina, with partial visibility elsewhere in North America. The moon will block the sun for up to 90 minutes, creating umbral shadows (total eclipse) and penumbral shadows (partial eclipse). Salem, Oregon will see it first; Charleston, South Carolina last. This is the first coast-to-coast total solar eclipse in 99 years. Hotels are booking up as enthusiasts prepare for the event.

The Zipper offense is a basketball strategy that uses down screens on the ball side to free shooters, create point guard isolation drives, and establish strong post-ups. Originating with the 1960s Celtics, it remains common in NBA playbooks. The offense begins with a dribble clear entry to the wing, with shooters breaking high off down screens set by posts. The point guard can drive, pass to shooters, or feed posting screeners. Key phases include point isolation with various counters for defensive responses, proper down screen execution with reads for trailing or overplaying defenders, post isolation options, ball reversal with weakside down screens, and offensive rebounding advantages. The offense flows into multiple continuity options including motion, single/double, flex, triangle post, and side screen actions. Variations include Curl, Blocks, Back, and sideline out-of-bounds entries. Success requires coordinated execution between ballhandler, screener, and receiver through proper footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication.

The paper studies "transportation"—lifting theorems about typeability in the Edinburgh Logical Framework (LF) across different schematically defined typing contexts. The authors address when one context can replace another without affecting formula validity, extending subordination relations from individual typing judgements to properties relating varied judgements and families of contexts. They formalize this using the logic L_LF, introducing context schema subsumption to determine when universal quantification under one context schema implies validity under another. The work culminates in a sound proof rule implemented in the Adelfa proof assistant, enabling theorem transportation in dependently typed lambda calculi with higher-order abstract syntax.

W.K. Neuman petitioned for certiorari challenging a circuit court order that upheld the Tampa Board of Adjustment's denial of a variance to complete a fence/wall at his residence. The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, found no departure from essential legal requirements and denied certiorari on April 8, 1983.

Amazon launched Chime, a unified communications service combining voice, video, chat and online meetings, entering a crowded market with competitors including Adobe, Cisco, Google, Microsoft, AT&T, Verizon and numerous pure-play vendors. Chime supports up to 100 participants in group conferences with features like screen sharing, personalized URLs, recording and cross-platform switching between devices. It offers native apps for Android, iOS, Mac OS and Windows, plus API integration with Google Calendar and Outlook.

Coaches must address soccer tackling context—including general concepts, rules, and referee interpretations—before teaching tackle types. Legal tackling dispossesses opponents without violating Law 12, with the tackler responsible for safety. Tackles may occur anywhere, but fouls risk free kicks, bookings, or penalty kicks. Tackle selection depends on player positions, ball location, and circumstances. A proper defensive process includes marking, staying goal-side, intercepting, delaying, and tackling when directed. Law 12 defines fouls as careless, reckless, or using excessive force, with escalating sanctions. Legal contact is shoulder-to-shoulder with at least one foot on the ground and no excessive force. Illegal contact includes improper charges, kicks, pushes, strikes, tackles, or trips. Proper tackles require legal contact, clear ball attempts, ground contact, and injury avoidance. Referees evaluate proximity, legitimacy, force, and angle, with tackles from behind and mid-shin+ contact particularly scrutinized. Guidelines include knowing teammates, avoiding studs-up or two-footed lunges, using proper technique, and recovering quickly. Coaches should drill varied locations, address fatigue, teach "what not to do," use "Tackle" for communication, and avoid mismatched skill levels in practice.

Researchers developed MeTro, a highly elastic surgical glue made from natural elastic protein that seals wounds in 60 seconds when treated with UV light. Created by biomedical engineers from the University of Sydney and the United States, the adhesive can replace stitches or staples for wounds in organs that expand and contract, such as lungs, arteries, and hearts. It contains a degradable enzyme adjustable to wound-healing timeframes and has been successfully tested on rodents and pigs. Clinical trials on humans are the next step.

A 1944-1945 U.S. State Department memorandum outlines proposed discussions between President Roosevelt and British Colonial Secretary Colonel Oliver Stanley regarding postwar colonial policy. Key topics include: differentiation between international trust territories and colonies (U.S. favors international trusteeship, Britain prefers national administration); ultimate goals for dependent peoples (U.S. favors independence with option to remain in empire, Britain favors self-government within empire); international accountability for colonial administration (U.S. seeks universal accountability, Britain accepts limited accountability tied to control); adoption of standards declarations (U.S. favors general declaration, Britain opposes); and regional advisory commissions (both favor advisory commissions, details unresolved). The discussions were intended to be exploratory rather than definitive, focusing on the Anglo-American Caribbean Commission while allowing informal conversation on broader colonial questions.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

12-year-old Charlotte Olson of Vorhees, New Jersey collected 1,303 books for the Read and Reach Out program, exceeding her goal of 1,000. She gathered donations through word of mouth, social media, and collection boxes at local businesses, ultimately receiving over 2,000 books and raising $250. The books were delivered to Cooper University Health System's Children's Regional Hospital, where pediatricians distribute them to young patients to promote early literacy. Charlotte, who participates in the National American Miss Pre-teen New Jersey pageant, aspires to become an emergency room doctor.

President Franklin Pierce delivers his final State of the Union address, defending his administration's policies on slavery, Kansas, and foreign affairs. He asserts constitutional equality of states and citizens, condemns sectional parties, and criticizes abolitionists as revolutionary agitators. He defends the Kansas-Nebraska Act's repeal of the Missouri Compromise line, arguing Congress lacked constitutional power to restrict slavery in territories. He reports restored order in Kansas through military intervention without bloodshed. Financially, he notes reduced national debt and urges customs revenue reduction. He describes satisfactory foreign relations, including treaties with Britain and ongoing negotiations regarding Central America, maritime rights, and claims against Mexico and New Granada. He concludes expressing gratitude for national peace and prosperity.

Bruce Bochy will not return as Texas Rangers manager after a three-year tenure that included the franchise's first World Series championship in 2023, followed by two non-winning seasons. The team and Bochy mutually agreed to end his managerial role, though he was offered a front office advisory position. Bochy, 70, is baseball's winningest active manager with 2,252 career wins (sixth all-time) and four World Series titles. The Rangers finished 81-81, their first .500 record ever. Potential replacement Skip Schumaker, a senior adviser with Texas, is among candidates. The Giants also fired manager Bob Melvin, and the Twins fired Rocco Baldelli.

U.S. Treasury yields fell sharply on April 13, 2017, after President Trump expressed desire for low interest rates and stated the dollar was "getting too strong." The dollar initially slumped but later recovered. The flattening yield curve hurt European bank stocks, while Asian stocks rose on strong Chinese trade data and Trump's reversal on labeling China a currency manipulator. Trump also indicated he might re-nominate Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen. European markets declined ahead of the Good Friday holiday, with investor unease also focused on the French presidential election. Oil prices and gold remained relatively stable.

Cover 3 defense remains prominent for stopping big plays and the run, using 4 underneath droppers and 3 deep defenders with a middle-of-field-closed structure. Offenses attack its weaknesses in the seams and flats through quick game throws, RPOs, and flood concepts. Strategies include slant/flat combinations, reading flat defenders, 4 verticals to exploit seams, and sail concepts to overload zones. Specific plays like Dagger, Boot TB Flat, Square Out-Seam, Y-Cross, and Post-Wheel demonstrate these approaches with examples from college offenses.

The NR7 trading strategy is a narrow-range volatility strategy developed by Tony Crabel in 1990 that enters on low volatility days. The original strategy lacks a defined exit, so the authors created their own version with one entry parameter and one exit criterion, testing it on SPY since 1993. Results showed a 7.8% CAGR, 0.27% average gain per trade, 899 trades, and 25% max drawdown—deemed reasonable but not worth trading due to low average gains for multi-day holds. Optimization of lookback periods found no improvement in average gains. Adding one undisclosed parameter improved results to 0.46% average gain, 13% drawdown, and significantly fewer trades. The improved strategy has a high win rate, with 67% of trades occurring when close is higher than previous day, meaning it doesn't buy on weakness like mean reversion strategies. This makes NR7 complementary to mean reversion strategies for portfolio diversification. The strategy relies on accurate high-low data, with Yahoo Finance used but caution advised. Code is available for Silver members.

This case study examines the 2008 global financial crisis, focusing on perspectives from MIT professors Andrew Lo and Simon Johnson. The crisis was triggered by the collapse of the U.S. housing market, where high-risk lending practices and securitization of mortgages created systemic risk. Lo attributed the crisis to human behavioral factors—greed during prosperity and fear during collapse—while Johnson blamed a banking "oligarchy" that took excessive risks with implicit government backing. Contributing factors included deregulation (particularly the repeal of Glass-Steagall), unregulated derivatives like credit default swaps, close Wall Street-Washington ties, and global capital seeking higher returns. The U.S. government responded with TARP funds, stress tests, and the Public Private Investment Program. Johnson advocated for temporary nationalization and breaking up large banks, while Lo recommended more effective regulation, greater transparency, a Capital Markets Safety Board, risk-based accounting, improved corporate governance with quants in management, and campaign finance reform.

The speaker addresses Americans about entering World War I, stating the nation was unprepared militarily and mentally. The primary reason for entering the war is defending national rights, with broader goals of making the world safe for civilization and America safe for Americans. The speech emphasizes testing democratic government's capacity for self-defense, liberating American life, and committing to human freedom and justice. The speaker declares America will continue fighting regardless of potential Allied failures, aiming to eliminate disloyalty and establish true American citizenship.

SIG Plc named Ernst & Young as its external auditor after the UK's Financial Reporting Council began investigating Deloitte's audit of the building products group. The FRC probe focuses on SIG's 2015 and 2016 financial statements regarding cash and supplier rebates. The investigation follows a whistleblowing allegation of profit overstatement that led to staff suspensions. SIG reported 0.6% revenue growth for the first half of 2019, with stronger European demand offsetting UK weakness, and maintained full-year profit expectations under CEO Meinie Oldersma, who has led a turnaround including exiting 11 businesses.

Canada's S&P/TSX composite index rose for a seventh consecutive day to a record high of 15,801.06, led by financial services gains following strong economic data from Canada and the U.S. U.S. stocks opened little changed, with the Dow up slightly, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen testified that delaying rate hikes would be unwise, though she did not specify timing and expressed uncertainty about Trump administration policies. Strong U.S. retail sales and consumer price data were reported. Oil prices fell below $56 per barrel after an API report showed U.S. crude inventories rose by 9.9 million barrels, raising doubts about OPEC supply cuts tightening global supply despite record OPEC compliance.

A two-week drink and drug driving crackdown in North Wales has resulted in nearly 100 arrests—55 for drink-driving and 40 for drug-driving—as part of the All Wales Summer Anti Drink and Drug Driving campaign launched June 14. North Wales Police Inspector Dave Cust stated that despite warnings, motorists continue to offend, risking 12-month disqualifications, heavy fines, and job losses. Officers have increased patrols and use intelligence-led operations and new technology to detect offenders. Police encourage the public to report suspected drink or drug drivers via 101, Crimestoppers, or 999 in emergencies.

Alexei Ponikarovsky discusses his team's upcoming must-win game, noting they've played close games despite being down in the series. He mentions offensive struggles, shot-blocking by opponents, and the need to get more pucks and rebounds past the opposing goaltender, who covers the bottom of the net well. He references a previous series against the Rangers where they overcame two shutouts to win, emphasizing the importance of staying positive and persistent.

Cambridgeshire Short Mat Bowls held its annual ladies versus men triples match after the AGM, with six rounds over 10 ends. CMB BC defeated March Town 3-2 in the Ivan Henson Memorial Trophy final, winning singles and fours while losing pairs and triples, with overall shots of 66-62. This paper presents a non-LTE (NLTE) abundance analysis of neodymium (Nd) in metal-poor FGK stars. The authors construct a novel Nd I/Nd II model atom using experimental data from VALD, NIST, and linemake, calibrated with solar and meteoritic abundances. They test the model on the Sun and the r-process enhanced star HD222925, finding NLTE corrections up to ~0.2 dex that increase abundances relative to LTE. The authors then derive NLTE abundances for a sample of metal-poor stars and create a 6-dimensional grid of NLTE corrections covering stellar parameters typical of FGK stars (4000–6500 K, log g 0.5–4.5, [Fe/H] −3.0 to −1.0). Key findings include: NLTE corrections range from −0.3 to +0.5 dex depending on stellar parameters and spectral line properties; optical lines show positive corrections increasing for lower Teff, log g, and [Fe/H], while H-band lines show negative corrections; blue low-excitation lines in cool, metal-poor giants have the largest positive corrections; and corrections generally decrease toward zero at higher Nd abundances. The authors recommend adopting NLTE corrections for r-process abundance analyses, particularly for metal-poor giants, and using moderate-to-high excitation potential lines when possible.

Doug Ford held his first major rally as Ontario Progressive Conservative leader in Toronto on March 19, 2018, telling nearly 2,000 supporters he plans to "take back this province" and build a majority government by attracting voters dissatisfied with Liberal Premier Kathleen Wynne. Ford criticized the government's financial management, promised to cut taxes and hydro rates, bring back manufacturing jobs, make Ontario more business-friendly, and develop northern Ontario's natural resources. He appeared onstage with former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen. Supporters cited his personality, relatability, and fiscal policies as reasons for their backing.

He also praises backup goalie John as a valuable late-season addition who brings experience and peace of mind, despite initial awkwardness from previously competing against him. Harvey gave up three home runs in four innings and plans to see a doctor for physical issues following rib-removal surgery. The Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) is a 4KB decrypted memory region enabling communication between SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. Its format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area through offset 0x3ff, though only required fields are populated to minimize guest state exposure. Version 2 introduced hypervisor feature advertisement, SEV-SNP support, XSS MSR values, restricted APIC emulation, and multi-VMPL capabilities. Subsequent revisions added VLEK GUID definitions (2.02), APIC ID list retrieval and page state change notifications (2.03), and SEV-TIO trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and hardware debug documentation (2.04).

The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 for requests/responses, supporting operations including feature negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, VMPL execution, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register GHCB GPA before first use, with options to query preferred addresses. The protocol limits guest state exposure by returning only necessary information.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events handle intercepted operations through VMGEXIT, with standardized processing for exceptions, I/O, MSR access, MMIO, page state changes, firmware requests, AP creation, doorbell pages, IPI, timers, and VMPL switching. SEV-SNP adds extended guest requests with certificate GUIDs and TIO device attestation. Restricted Injection limits hypervisor interrupts to #HV doorbell notifications, with shared pages containing pending event and EOI assist fields.

SMP booting requires special handling: SEV-ES uses AP reset hold with initial measured register states, while SEV-SNP supports AP creation via VMSA pages. The SEV-SNP Secrets Page communicates message sequence numbers and AP jump table addresses between firmware and OS. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported when available; nested virtualization and SMM are not supported.

He pledges to build a unified nation of justice and opportunity, reform education, Social Security, and Medicare, reduce taxes, strengthen defenses, and confront weapons of mass destruction. In July 2020, the NHL and NHLPA negotiated a return-to-play plan for the COVID-19 interrupted 2019-20 season and extended the collective bargaining agreement through 2025-26. The 2013 CBA had established a 50% revenue sharing arrangement between players and owners, with "claw back" provisions if player compensation exceeded this threshold. In *Johnson v. The State* (1908), James Johnson was convicted of murdering his father and sentenced to life imprisonment. The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed the conviction, rejecting four grounds for a new trial: (1) that jurors previously stricken from the first trial (which was reversed on legal error) were improperly included on the second jury list; (2) that evidence of Johnson's knowledge of his father's life insurance and his request for help obtaining the money shortly after the homicide was improperly admitted; (3) that the trial court's instruction—that Johnson admitted a killing occurred and it was murder, but denied his own guilt—was erroneous; and (4) miscellaneous other grounds. The court held that Johnson's own statement to the jury, in which he referred to the homicide as "murder" and his father's being "killed," supported the challenged jury instruction, and that the insurance evidence was admissible to show motive and Johnson's state of mind.

Scientists have created hybrid embryos using frozen northern white rhino sperm and southern white rhino eggs, a step toward preventing the sub-species' extinction. Only two female northern white rhinos remain alive; researchers plan to harvest their eggs and use preserved sperm to create "pure" embryos for implantation in southern white rhino surrogates. A second method using frozen skin cells to generate eggs is also being developed. Some conservationists criticize the effort as too late and too expensive, arguing resources should focus on other endangered rhino species. Scientists hope to harvest eggs from the surviving females in Kenya by year's end, though health risks to the animals remain a concern.

Teb Lokey forwarded a Texas Monthly article about Enron's rise and fall to six Enron colleagues on October 25, 2001. This volume documents the intellectual foundations of Ronald Reagan's foreign policy from 1981–1988, focusing on the collective mindset of administration officials rather than specific diplomatic decisions. It draws from speeches, press releases, interviews, Congressional testimony, and internal records to illustrate policy perspectives and themes, including resetting U.S. foreign policy after Vietnam, Watergate, and Iran; promoting U.S. values globally; developing bipartisan activism; and building U.S.-Soviet restraint and reciprocity. The documents emphasize perspectives from President Reagan, Vice President Bush, Secretaries of State Haig and Shultz, National Security Advisors, Secretary of Defense Weinberger, and UN Ambassador Kirkpatrick. The declassification review, conducted 2018–2022 under Executive Order 13526, resulted in minor excisions in only 3 documents. The Foreign Relations series is overseen by the Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation, with editorial notes providing background, cross-references, and supplementary information.

This study investigated serum cardiac Troponin T (cTnT) as a biomarker for respiratory dysfunction in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Using two hospital-based cohorts (297 patients in Bonn, 49 in Essen), researchers found that cTnT levels correlated strongly and negatively with pulmonary function test parameters including forced vital capacity, slow vital capacity, forced expiratory volume, and peak expiratory flow. Approximately 65% of ALS patients had elevated cTnT levels, which originated from degenerating respiratory skeletal muscles rather than cardiac injury. Unlike neurofilament light chain (NfL), which reflects neuroaxonal damage but showed no correlation with respiratory function, cTnT demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy for detecting clinically significant respiratory impairment thresholds. The optimal cTnT cut-off values for identifying impaired respiration ranged from 14.00 to 17.80 ng/l. These findings establish cTnT as an independent biomarker that complements NfL measurements and provides quantifiable information about respiratory capacity in ALS patients, with potential utility for guiding interventions like non-invasive ventilation.

This study prospectively investigated the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on health-related quality of life (HRQOL) among 318 head and neck cancer (HNC) survivors from the NET-QUBIC cohort, comparing those who completed 36-month assessments before versus during the pandemic. Overall, the pandemic did not significantly affect HRQOL changes between 24 and 36 months post-treatment. However, subgroup analyses revealed differential effects: females showed worsened physical activity; multimodality-treated survivors showed worsened appetite loss; those with comorbidity showed worsened swallowing; survivors with lifetime major depressive disorder showed worsened fear of recurrence; and those with high BMI showed worsened emotional loneliness. Conversely, survivors living alone showed decreased painkiller use, and those with disease progression showed decreased financial problems. The study's longitudinal design was a key strength, though results cannot be generalized to patients diagnosed during the pandemic.

Text2MBL is a framework that translates textual descriptions into BIM-based modular building layouts (MBLs) through fine-grained, action-level code. Modular construction uses standardized 3D volumetric units manufactured off-site and assembled on-site, introducing challenges in layout design due to constraints imposed by modular systems. Text-based input methods allow users to express design intentions, but extending these to MBL design is complex due to the "module" concept. Text2MBL addresses the gap between conceptual design and BIM-compatible output by hierarchically structuring MBLs into four classes: Modules, Unit, Room, and Utils. The framework was implemented in Autodesk Revit using C#, with large language models fine-tuned to learn text-to-BIM mappings. Evaluation criteria include executable validity, semantic fidelity, and geometric consistency. The dataset comprises 198 unique MBL designs with paired textual descriptions and executable BIM code.

This article explains common football pass routes used from high school to professional levels, organized through the football route tree system coaches use to teach receivers. Quick routes include the hitch (5-6 yard pivot toward quarterback), slant (45-degree break inside), quick out (90-degree break to sideline at 5 yards), stick (sit in zone or break away from middle), flat (horizontal 2-3 yards), whip (fake in-breaking then turn out), and option routes (receiver chooses path based on defense). Deep routes covered include the go/fly (straight deep), seam (vertical between linebackers and safeties), corner (45-degree break to sideline at 10-12 yards), post (break toward goal posts at 10-12 yards), and post-corner (fake post then break outside). Intermediate routes include the square out (90-degree break to sideline at 10-12 yards), dig (sharp break to middle at 10-15 yards), curl (break back toward quarterback at 10-12 yards), comeback (break back toward sideline), drag (horizontal crossing 6-8 yards), and shallow cross (2-3 yards deep across field). The article notes that route trees vary by team and were historically used for play-calling.

A study using a Markov state transition model found that Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection screening and tuberculosis preventive treatment for formerly incarcerated individuals in Brazil is highly cost-effective. The optimal strategy—tuberculin skin test with 3-month isoniazid and rifapentine—cost $242 per disability-adjusted life year averted, averting 31 TB cases and 4.1 TB deaths per 1,000 individuals. Younger age, longer incarceration, and more recent prison release were associated with greater health benefits, though all subgroups showed cost-effectiveness. The intervention remained cost-effective even with elevated reinfection rates up to 50 times general population levels.

This passage describes the electronic edition of "Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1945 Volume I," published by the U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian in May 2018. Ralph Perkins and others. Finally, it notes that for 1945–1949, Foreign Relations provides selected public documents indicating U.S. foreign policy scope and goals, with country-specific items noted in respective compilations.

This patent application describes wireless communication systems, particularly 5G NR technology, covering: network architecture with core networks, radio access networks, and wireless devices; protocol stacks including PHY, MAC, RLC, PDCP, SDAP, RRC, and NAS layers; channel mappings and physical layer processes; RRC states (IDLE, INACTIVE, CONNECTED); OFDM transmission structures with multiple numerologies; bandwidth part adaptation; carrier aggregation with primary and secondary cells; random access procedures (contention-based, contention-free, two-step); synchronization signal blocks and beam management; reference signals including CSI-RS, SRS, DM-RS, and PT-RS; and wireless device and base station components including RF front ends, data processing systems, and memory. The Supreme Court deferred action on the Trump administration's request to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, scheduling oral arguments for January 2026. This study investigates how collagen fiber architecture influences mechanical behavior in arterial tissues with wall thickness variations. Using multiphoton microscopy, researchers identified two distinct fiber patterns: abrupt terminations near pathological features (e.g., microcalcifications in cerebral aneurysms) versus continuous fibers spanning thickness gradients (e.g., around atherosclerotic plaques). They developed 3D representative volume element models with discrete fiber networks to compare these architectures under uniaxial loading.

Results showed that continuous fiber networks substantially reduced stretch disparities between thick (200 μm) and thin (100 μm) regions from 20% to 0.68%, and lowered maximum von Mises stress from 2.49 MPa to 0.664 MPa. Continuous fibers enabled load transfer across thickness gradients and created higher local fiber density in thin regions (51.9% vs. 26.0%), enhancing mechanical support. Fiber tortuosity (recruitment stretch) modulated this behavior: before fiber engagement, geometry dominated; after recruitment, fiber architecture governed the response.

The findings challenge the classical view that wall thickness primarily determines stress fields, demonstrating that microstructural fiber organization plays a dominant role. For tissues with confirmed fiber continuity, constant-thickness models may provide accurate predictions even without precise local thickness measurements. This has implications for computational modeling of vascular pathologies and rupture risk assessment using standard clinical imaging.

This document outlines a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for clinical study ZEA-DNK-02170, detailing rules for handling missing dates, calculation formulas for derived variables, SAS programming QC requirements, and comprehensive specifications for tables, figures, and listings. LG's SJ9500 Super UHD TV uses Nano Cell quantum dot technology to deliver the company's best 4K LCD picture quality, with more accurate colors, deeper blacks, and 95% color retention at wide viewing angles. Asteroid 2025 TF, measuring 1-3 meters in diameter, passed 428 km above Antarctica on October 1, 2025—similar to the International Space Station's altitude. The Catalina Sky Survey detected it hours after the flyby, and ESA astronomers later confirmed its trajectory with high precision. Small asteroids like this pose no planetary threat, typically breaking apart in the atmosphere as fireballs. Larger objects—20 meters or more—can cause local damage, while those hundreds of meters wide risk regional or global consequences. International programs like ESA's Planetary Defence Office and NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office monitor near-Earth objects to predict potential impacts years in advance.

This patent application is a continuation of prior applications concerning a comprehensive eye solution for functional impairment due to facial paralysis, disclosing apparatus and methods for transcutaneous facial nerve stimulation to artificially elicit eye blink. The passage provides background on facial nerve anatomy and Bell's palsy, the physiology of eye blink and dry eye syndrome, and electrical stimulation technologies including TENS, EMS, and various electrode types such as skin, electronic skin, EEG, and implantable electrodes. It further details wireless communication protocols including Bluetooth, ZigBee, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, cellular networks, and NFC; Internet and networking technologies such as TCP/IP; and mobile platforms and messaging services including smartphones, SMS, MMS, instant messaging, Facebook Messenger, Twitter, and WhatsApp.

Reports of Tong Hâk followers marching on Seoul circulated months ago and resurfaced two weeks prior. Foreign representatives were warned of tens of thousands approaching with anti-foreigner aims, but no authority confirmed this; officials dismissed it as rumor. Gunboats departed after diplomats declined to act on vague reports. On March 29, about forty Tong Hâk members knelt at the palace gate with a petition seeking reversal of founder Ch'e Cheng-woo's execution for heresy in 1859 and permission to practice their religion, which blends Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism and emphasizes reverence for God and love for man. Their leader Pak Siung-ho denied hostility to foreigners. The movement's bold emergence suggests significant backing, with hundreds or thousands possibly in Seoul under the pretext of crown prince birthday examinations. Some join due to anti-Catholic sentiment, believing priests protect converts from magistrate exactions.

The PENTAD Timing Model by Nelson Freeburg is an active trading strategy for the US stock market that uses four stock indices and one advance/decline line to generate buy/sell signals. Nelson Freeburg, editor of Formula Research since 1991, developed this complex weekly-based model using two technical indicators: moving average envelopes (trading ranges with upper buy zones and lower sell zones) and moving average slope (an oscillator measuring trend momentum). The model operates as a voting machine requiring unanimous "yes" votes to enter the market and exits when at least two votes are "against." Unlike passive strategies, it allows traders to avoid being in the market 100% of the time. The article describes backtesting results including equity curves, drawdowns, monthly/annual returns, and performance statistics compared to the S&P 500 Total Return index.

The Facebook-Cambridge Analytica scandal increased public awareness of data surveillance risks, prompting investigations, stock drops, and a "Delete Facebook" movement. While users technically consented to Facebook's data collection through terms of service, the incident illustrates harms from massive data collection. The core issue extends beyond unauthorized access to a new form of "choice architecture"—personalized, microtargeted influence based on comprehensive individual profiles. Unlike traditional choice architecture that exploits general human cognitive biases, personalized versions target unique individual characteristics, blurring lines between persuasion and coercion. Examples include Google's Jigsaw countering ISIS recruitment and Facebook targeting emotionally vulnerable youth. While potentially beneficial (increasing voter turnout, promoting healthy habits), unchecked personalized choice architecture threatens democratic processes and personal autonomy, requiring systematic solutions across social, economic, technical, legal, and ethical domains rather than individual platform boycotts.

The Mortgage Collaborative, an independent mortgage cooperative, announced a partnership with Strategic Compliance Partners, a national compliance solutions provider. This Statistical Analysis Plan outlines data handling and analysis procedures for a clinical trial comparing dasiglucagon and GlucaGen®. Plasma samples for pharmacokinetic (PK) analysis are collected at specific intervals with defined allowable time deviations; concentrations below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) are set to zero or ignored based on timing relative to maximum concentration, and missing post-dose values are not replaced. This patent application describes Polkadot, a scalable heterogeneous multi-chain framework enabling shared security, interoperability, and scalability among multiple blockchains. The system uses a relay-chain with validator nodes that validate candidate blocks from parachains (parallelized chains), employing a Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus process. Four key roles exist: validators (seal blocks, require high bond), nominators (stake-holders contributing to validator bonds), collators (produce parachain blocks), and fishermen (independent bounty hunters detecting misbehavior). The relay-chain provides pooled security, allowing parachains to maintain arbitrary state-transition functions while communicating through trust-free interchain transactions routed via Merkle-based queuing mechanisms. The system separates consensus from execution, using Nominated Proof-of-Stake for validator selection with economic incentives and punishment mechanisms for misbehavior. Interoperability with Ethereum and Bitcoin is achieved through "break-in" and "break-out" contracts with threshold signatures or multi-signature schemes.

This randomized controlled trial investigated whether radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) combined with a specific rehabilitation program (RP) is more effective than sham-rESWT plus RP for treating acute hamstring muscle complex injury type 3b in athletes. Forty semi-professional athletes aged 18-35 years were randomized, with 36 included in the modified intent-to-treat analysis after excluding 4 patients with type 3a injuries. The RP consisted of three phases: acute (3-4 days), subacute/regeneration, and functional, with return to sport criteria including absence of pain, flexibility testing, strength testing, and medical clearance. The rESWT group received up to nine sessions using a Swiss DolorClast device. The primary outcome was time to return to sport. Results showed the rESWT + RP group had significantly shorter mean time to return to sport (25.4 ± 3.5 days) compared to sham-rESWT + RP (28.3 ± 4.5 days; p=0.037). Patient satisfaction and re-injury rates at six months did not differ significantly between groups. The study concluded that adding rESWT to this specific rehabilitation program reduces time to return to sport without increasing re-injury risk, though larger studies are needed for definitive evidence.

The lecture covers the theorem of irrelevance in detection theory, which states that for signals transmitted in J degrees of freedom, only those J received components matter; out-of-band noise and other signals are irrelevant. This reduces the problem to finite-dimensional vectors regardless of modulation scheme. For independent signals, signal-by-signal detection equals joint maximum likelihood detection; for dependent signals (e.g., coded systems), joint detection performs better. The lecture then examines orthogonal, simplex, and biorthogonal codes, noting that error probability calculations become complex for dimensions above two. A bound on error probability for orthogonal codes shows exponential decrease with bits sent when energy per bit exceeds the Shannon limit. The lecture transitions to wireless communication, contrasting it with wired systems due to time-varying channels, interference, and mobility. Cellular networks are described as appendages to wireline networks, with base stations connected to Mobile Telephone Switching Offices. Key problems include base station selection, mobile location, and multi-access channels (reverse) versus broadcast channels (forward). Physical modeling must account for carrier frequency effects, Doppler shift, and fading channels that vary with time and frequency.

This patent application describes a display apparatus with a flexible vibration module that uses the display panel as a vibration plate to generate sound. Multiple embodiments describe various configurations: equal-sized alternating strips, varying widths to optimize high or low-frequency sound, progressively decreasing organic portion sizes from center to edges to reduce stress concentration, and circular or triangular ceramic patterns for 2D/3D shaping. A bimorph structure with two stacked composite layers can enhance sound pressure. For stereo sound, two vibration modules can be separated by partition members creating air gaps that prevent sound interference between left and right channels. This study reports the first instance where precision therapies (targeted treatments and immunotherapy) have surpassed traditional cytotoxic treatments in routine community-based care for advanced cancer patients, leading to improved overall survival. This research article examines distance education experiences of visually impaired students in professional music education in Turkey during COVID-19. Tracing Turkey's distance education evolution from 1924 through four periods—conceptual, mail-based, radio-television, and internet-based—the study identifies persistent challenges in transmitting music's essential elements of sound and rhythm synchronously online. Using qualitative case study methodology, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with seven visually impaired music students representing 80% of such students nationally, enrolled across various universities and departments including music education, musicology, and Turkish music.

Findings indicate institutions predominantly utilized synchronous methods, with students primarily relying on computers for access. Most participants found course documents insufficient or completely inaccessible, noting materials failed to accommodate special needs, requiring dependence on parental support or large-print capabilities. Assessment practices varied: while some received individual arrangements such as video submissions or oral exams, others faced difficulties with standardized written examinations. Students identified temporal and spatial flexibility as primary strengths, with one noting improved social acceptance compared to physical classrooms. However, they reported significant weaknesses including technical deficiencies (sound synchronization problems, poor audio quality preventing simultaneous performance), decreased productivity, and instructor technological incompetence.

Participant suggestions included extended lesson durations, software converting written documents to audio, improved technical infrastructure beyond university systems, screen-reader compatible interfaces, and automatic system adjustments for disabilities. The study concludes that distance education during the pandemic largely ignored visually impaired students' needs, requiring implementation of accessible technologies (screen readers, Braille printers, speech recognition), customized educational materials, and comprehensive support systems to ensure equal opportunity.
