Anderson led after two rounds but fell on her final landing. Zoi Sadowski Synnott won bronze, New Zealand's first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years. The competition was moved from Friday to Thursday due to wind concerns, with officials seeking to avoid the conditions that plagued the earlier slopestyle event. Big Air features riders sprinting down a 50-meter ramp, performing aerial tricks with two of three attempts counting toward their total score.

This patent application describes flexible cable assemblies for connecting electrical circuitry in quantum computing systems, particularly cryogenic dilution refrigerators housing quantum processor units (QPUs) with superconducting circuits. The flex cables comprise electrically insulating strips (e.g., polyimide, Kapton) containing metal striplines sandwiched between metallic grounding planes, with electromagnetic shielding provided by vias connecting the ground planes. The cables terminate in mechanically stiff circuit boards that may integrate electronic components such as filters, attenuators, amplifiers, and connectors.

The assemblies address scalability challenges for large qubit arrays by providing high-density parallel signal lines with improved thermal conductivity profiles compared to coaxial cables. Configurations include single or multiple stripline layers, fanout regions at rigid board connections for mechanical integrity, and composite materials with conductive particles (e.g., copper, iron) for high-frequency absorption (10 GHz to 1 THz). The systems connect multiple isothermal plates in cryostats ranging from room temperature to millikelvin ranges, utilizing materials suited for different temperature stages, including superconducting metals (Nb, TiNb, Al) at lower temperatures and non-superconducting metals (stainless steel, brass) at higher stages.

Electrical connections employ various methods including solder bumps (e.g., indium), wire bonds, flip-chip assemblies, cavity flip-chip connections, and compliant joints using spring contacts (e.g., BeCu) for non-permanent connections. Rigid boards may include regions of electromagnetically absorptive material aligned with windows in the flex cable ground planes for signal conditioning. The technology enables continuous cable runs from room temperature to the QPU while managing thermal loads, reducing assembly complexity, and allowing integration of signal conditioning elements directly on the flex cable or rigid boards.

A Teagasc survey of 314 male farmers in southeast Ireland found 20% had never consulted a doctor. Farmers showed higher mortality rates from cardiovascular disease and cancers than other occupations. While 57% visited a doctor in the past year (below the 65% national male average), 39% reported ill health, mainly lower back pain, arthritis, and anxiety. Full-time farmers reported more back pain. The study noted farmers often prioritize work over health. Smoking rates were 20% (below the 24% national average), while 88% drank alcohol regularly. Weekly drinking was 22% (below 60% national average), but weekly binge drinking matched the national average at 22%. Farmers under 45 smoked and drank more; those over 45 reported more arthritis, with rheumatoid arthritis at 13%—three times the national average.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill law firm on the same day that state ethics regulators agreed to drop ethics charges against him in exchange for his resignation from the bench and agreement never to hold judicial office again. The New York State Commission on Judicial Conduct had alleged Nock acted rudely toward court staff and threatened retaliation against commission staff and witnesses. Nock denied all allegations but agreed to resign after the commission denied motions to dismiss. Anderson Kill stated Nock disclosed the allegations before hiring and that no wrongdoing was found. Nock's lawyer Malcolm S. Taub said Nock "vehemently" denies the demeanor allegations and respected commission staff, adding that Nock had already planned to leave the bench due to mandatory retirement at age 70 and family considerations.

This study analyzes data from the phase 3 LIVE-AIR trial to evaluate baseline C-reactive protein (CRP) as a biomarker for guiding lenzilumab treatment in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. GM-CSF is an early upstream mediator of hyperinflammatory immune response following SARS-CoV-2 infection, and lenzilumab (a GM-CSF neutralizing antibody) previously showed improved survival without invasive mechanical ventilation (SWOV) versus placebo. In this analysis, baseline CRP<150 mg/L was the strongest predictor of SWOV, with 78% of the study population showing greatest clinical benefit from lenzilumab (HR: 2.54; 95%CI: 1.46-4.41; p=0.0009). Elevated baseline CRP was the most predictive feature for progression to IMV or death (OR: 0.15; 95%CI: 0.07-0.29; p<0.001). Patients with CRP>150 mg/L experienced COVID-19-associated hyperinflammation and were at imminent risk of respiratory escalation or death. The findings suggest CRP may guide therapeutic intervention timing, with GM-CSF neutralization most effective before CRP exceeds 150 mg/L.

This is the biggest game due to the long journey with teammates. They feel calm but expect nerves and are excited to enjoy the moment. An injured teammate's return means much. Fans and the city are supportive.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison for the 2014 murder of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. Judge Stephen Everett noted her "utter lack of remorse" after she maintained her innocence and claimed Markel would be "appalled" at the lack of justice in her trial. Adelson was convicted of participating in a murder-for-hire plot with her son Charlie Adelson, who enlisted his girlfriend to hire hit men. The motive was reportedly the family's desire to move Markel's ex-wife Wendi Adelson to South Florida with their children. Harvey Adelson, Donna's husband, also asserted her innocence, stating "you're sending an innocent woman to prison."

The White House withdrew Kathleen Hartnett White's nomination to chair the Council on Environmental Quality. White, a climate change skeptic with fossil fuel industry ties, was announced in October 2017 but her nomination stalled in the Senate. She had compared climate scientists to ideologues, defended statements that particulate pollution is harmless, praised fossil fuels for improving living conditions, and called carbon dioxide a nutrient for plants. She previously worked under Energy Secretary Rick Perry in Texas and was a senior fellow at a conservative think-tank funded by fossil fuel companies. Senator Tom Carper supported the withdrawal and urged nomination of a qualified environmental champion.

Christopher K. Merker's research on public pension fund governance found significant performance variability among 35 plans from 2008-2012, with top performers annualizing 15% returns while bottom performers lost 4.2%. His Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ) showed that top-quintile governance scores produced nearly double the returns of bottom-quintile funds, with each FEQ improvement unit correlating to 0.36% higher performance. Key governance factors affecting returns included institutional knowledge consistency, meeting frequency (monthly outperformed quarterly), retired board member percentage, and staff delegation. Surprisingly, investment expenses showed no statistical significance. The research demonstrates that governance practices directly influence investment choices and outcomes, and that governance quality can be measured.

Turing GPUs enable real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores, overcoming previous limitations where single GPUs could not achieve real-time ray tracing for games. Earlier GPU architectures, including Volta, could produce realistic ray-traced scenes but not in real-time on a single GPU, forcing games to use rasterization techniques. NVIDIA's research, hardware, and software teams collaborated for nearly a decade to develop this technology.

A cross-sectional study of 217 female TV studies students at NTA TV College, Nigeria found relatively low levels of good contraceptive knowledge (55.3%), attitude (47.5%), and practice (50.7%). About 74% had ever had sex. Main information sources were friends (35.2%) and internet (34.3%); commonest contraceptives used were condoms (43.5%) and oral pills (36.5%). Fear of side effects was the primary reason for non-use. Significant predictors included: young adult age for good knowledge (aOR: 2.633); diploma status, off-campus residence, and good knowledge for good attitude (aOR: 2.369, 2.134, 3.798 respectively); and state indigenous ethnicity and sexual experience for good practice (aOR: 2.369, 24.482 respectively). The study concludes that improved advocacy, policies, and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services are urgently needed.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings Corporation reported fiscal year 2017 financial results showing significant growth. Total revenues increased 88.4% to $46.50 million from $24.68 million in 2016. Net income rose 343.9% to $15.27 million from $3.44 million. Total loans facilitated through the platform grew 59.9% to $1,308.7 million from $818.5 million. The company had 8,047 borrowers and 69,232 investors participating in 23,263 loans during 2017, compared to 1,067 borrowers, 39,999 investors and 8,739 loans in 2016. Operating income increased 301.6% to $17.95 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.21 compared to $0.05 in 2016. As of December 31, 2017, cash and cash equivalents were $12.68 million, up from $8.56 million at year-end 2016.

Chrissy Teigen, 32, discussed her pregnancy skincare routine to prevent stretch marks in an interview with Refinery29. The model, who is due to give birth to her second child in June, explained that she comes from a "stretch mark-prone family" and has had stretch marks on her thighs since before her pregnancies. To prevent stretch marks on her belly, she spends 10-15 minutes nightly applying multiple products, including Aquaphor on her elbows, coconut oil all over her body, and Lumière de Vie Concentrate on her belly. Her husband John Legend and daughter Luna assist with the routine. Teigen noted that despite her prevention efforts, she believes stretch marks are common, stating that every supermodel she has worked with has had at least one.

Research from the University of Essex and University College London found that girls who start using social media at age 10 with an hour or more daily show lower well-being by age 15. The study of 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10-15, published in BMC Public Health, found girls use social media more than boys and experience greater well-being declines during adolescence. Happiness scores dropped nearly three points for girls versus two points for boys. No association between social media use and well-being was found among boys; researchers suggest gaming time may be a factor instead. The link may be underestimated as data was self-reported and only covered school days.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated January 26, 2001, contains news clippings about Enron and energy-related topics. Key articles include: "California Dimming" from The Times of India discussing California's power crisis and deregulation failures; a Pittsburgh Post-Gazette piece noting Enron stock rose $2.25 to $82 after projecting 2001 profits would exceed analyst predictions; a Boston Globe op-ed mentioning Enron as a major Bush campaign contributor profiting from California's energy shortfall; a Business Standard editorial about U.S. Ambassador Richard Celeste offering to mediate between Maharashtra's chief minister and Enron over a payment dispute; a San Francisco Chronicle article on Democrats discussing Bush's Enron ties; a Wall Street Journal piece on wind energy's comeback in California, noting Enron's deployment of about 200 new windmills; an update that India's Maharashtra State Electricity Board may miss a $34.3 million payment to Enron's Dabhol Power unit; and a Houston Chronicle column about employee discontent with Enron's new "rank and yank" performance review system.

A coach discusses managing his hockey team through injuries and suspensions, particularly losing Chris Pronger, requiring multiple players to step up and absorb increased minutes. He addresses penalty discipline, noting some calls are questionable while others like careless stick use are truly undisciplined. Chris Kunitz is a game-time decision. The coach emphasizes utilizing all available personnel without holding back for future games, while never risking player health. He reflects on an earlier game where emotional overpreparation led to penalties and being out of sync, but the team regrouped at intermission, established their forecheck, and received key individual performances. He praises Teemu Selanne's leadership and skill plays, including setting up Dustin Penner's goal. The coach acknowledges the team must match their opponent's intensity and skill, and while enjoying their current series lead, stresses that the next game will be the toughest to win.

President returns House bill No. 6242 without signature, objecting to appropriations for local rather than national purposes, which he views as unconstitutional. While supporting some provisions for general welfare, he criticizes the bill's $18.7 million total as excessive compared to previous years' growth from $4 million (1870) to $11.4 million (1881). He warns that local appropriations create escalating demands and demoralizing effects on government. He suggests halving the amount and granting the Secretary of War discretion to allocate funds constitutionally.

A domestic violence support group meets Tuesdays at noon; call 541-400-0186 for details. AARP Tax Aide offers free tax preparation at Hood River Library (Mondays), Hood River Adult Center (Thursdays), and The Dalles Mid-Columbia Senior Center (Fridays/Saturdays); Spanish assistance available. Pakistan Volleyball Federation Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob called on the federal government to build a well-facilitated Sports Complex in Abbottabad, citing its moderate summer weather as ideal for national training camps from May to September. He criticized the Rs1200 million Narowal Sports Complex as underutilized due to its remote location, and noted that Islamabad's Pakistan Sports Complex lacks air-conditioning, causing problems for athletes during heat waves. Yaqoob stated that an Abbottabad facility would enable Pakistan to host international events in summer and suggested expanding boarding facilities at the Islamabad complex. Regarding Asian Games preparations, he said his federation requested an early camp from the Pakistan Sports Board, noting that only 2.5 months remain before the August 18-September 2 event in Indonesia, insufficient compared to the four months needed and years-long camps held by other nations. He confirmed Pakistan's Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi would arrive Thursday to oversee junior, youth, and senior team camps in Peshawar, after PSB recently halted established camps due to financial issues. The PSB will meet federations and the Pakistan Olympic Association on June 6 to finalize Asian Games preparations.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. The controllers use fixed frequency, peak current mode control with slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation when duty cycles exceed 50%, implemented through a voltage ramp subtracted from the error amplifier output. Frequency compensation options include Type 2A and Type 2B for the transconductance error amplifier. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C junction temperature with restart at 160°C. A design example details a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices with 5V output, demonstrating component selection for timing, feedback, dead time, leading edge blanking, soft-start, transformer design, switching FETs, output filtering, current sensing, hiccup mode, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noise coupling, separating analog and power grounds, and proper placement of bypass and compensation components.

Chicago granted landmark status to the former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters, which was then sold for $10 million to 3L Real Estate. The 46-year-old building, former home of Ebony and Jet magazines, will be converted into a 150-unit luxury apartment complex with a $20 million investment. Rents will range from $1,200 to $2,700. The developer plans to preserve the Ebony and Jet signs and begin reconstruction in 2018, with completion expected in 2019. The building was previously sold by Linda Johnson Rice to Columbia College in 2010, which resold it in 2016. Mayor Rahm Emanuel called the building a "decades-long epicenter of Black history and culture."

The Federal Government announced plans for multiple developmental projects in Nigeria's South-East region, beginning with the foundation laying of Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu stated the project aligns with President Buhari's commitment to informal science learning for sustainable development and economic diversification through science, technology, and innovation. The government signed an MoU with the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Culture for the centre. Onu emphasized that science and technology are essential for national development, noting Africa lags behind developed nations in this area. Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged support for the project's completion.

MIT 2.830J Control of Manufacturing Processes lecture introduces the course structure and key concepts. Professor Duane Boning explains the video recording policy for the Singapore-linked class, notes that materials are accessed through the Stellar website, and outlines prerequisites: manufacturing process experience and basic probability/statistics. Two textbooks are required: May and Spanos' semiconductor process control book and Montgomery's statistical quality control text. Grading comprises 40% from eight weekly problem sets, 40% from two quizzes, and 20% from a team project involving process diagnosis, improvement, or optimization using real data. Professor David Hardt joins to discuss manufacturing examples. The course focuses on managing variation and quality in manufacturing processes, covering statistical process control, design of experiments, and feedback control strategies.

CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) is an online advertising company offering affiliate programs since 1998. It connects advertisers with publishers, providing tracking, management, payment options, and promotional tools. Joining requires a website or social media profile with US/Canadian audience. Users create an account, complete a network profile, apply to programs, and share affiliate links to earn commissions. CJ offers programs across most niches with strong reporting tools. Payment methods include direct deposit, check, and Payoneer, with payouts within 20 days for accounts meeting minimum thresholds ($50 US, $100 international). This study translated and cross-culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised (WFQ-R) into Arabic (WFQ-Ar) for Saudi Arabian adults. Following Beaton's five-stage guidelines, researchers conducted forward and back translations, expert committee review, and pilot testing with 30 participants before validating with 290 Arabic speakers. The WFQ-Ar demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.93), test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.94), and construct validity with single-factor structure explaining 55.79% of variance. Minor adaptations included rewording one item and changing abbreviations to full words. The 10-item questionnaire measures foot preference on a spectrum from left-footed to right-footed, providing clinicians and researchers in Arabic-speaking countries with a validated multi-item tool for assessing footedness in rehabilitation and research contexts.

CoreWeave stock rose up to 8% after announcing new serverless AI tools for developers to train and monitor models, complementing its GPU rental business. The reinforcement learning service automatically adjusts computing power and reduces costs by 40% compared to local Nvidia H100 GPUs. The launch follows CoreWeave's $1 billion acquisition of Weights and Biases five months ago. CEO Michael Intrator stated the company will not revise its $9 billion bid for Core Scientific despite shareholder opposition.

Seasonal trading involves recognizing regular price patterns at specific times. For silver, January and July are historically the best months (positive 69.5% and 63.6% of the time), while June and September are worst (31.8% and 54.4%). A backtested strategy since 2001 holds silver only in December-February and July-August, outperforming buy-and-hold by 3.9% annually with 26.93% risk-adjusted return versus 7.33%, and reducing maximum drawdown from -71.65% to -23.34%. Silver's seasonality likely stems from industrial users placing orders at the start of financial years.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference with buffer. It supports internal (4.096V, enabled by default) or external voltage references, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit in RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference requires a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor and can drive external loads only with an op amp buffer. Thermal stress from soldering can degrade reference accuracy; multiple reflows should be minimized. The device features temperature compensation with drift performance specified across -40°C to +125°C.

For external reference mode, apply 4.096V at REFIO (configured as input) with INTREF_DIS=1, using the internal buffer to drive the ADC reference pin. The REFCAP output requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors. The internal buffer has 0.5ppm/°C typical drift (2ppm/°C maximum).

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar/unipolar ranges, outputting straight-binary format. Alarm features include programmable input thresholds (with hysteresis) and fixed AVDD thresholds (4.7V low, 5.3V high), accessible via ALARM pin, register reads, or appended data flags.

The multiSPI interface supports various data transfer protocols: standard SPI (CPOL/CPHA configurable), dual SDO mode, and source-synchronous modes. Configuration uses nine registers including DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (reset/power control with write protection), SDI_CTL_REG (SPI mode), SDO_CTL_REG (output configuration), DATAOUT_CTL_REG (data formatting), RANGE_SEL_REG (reference/input range), and alarm registers.

Three functional states exist: RESET (RST pin low), ACQ (signal acquisition), and CONV (conversion). Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge, requiring 32 SCLK cycles for optimal operation. Commands support byte/half-word read/write operations with specific addressing.

Power supplies AVDD (analog) and DVDD (digital) operate independently. Decoupling requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors per supply. Low-power modes include NAP (reduced power during ACQ) and power-down (deep sleep with register retention). PCB layout requires analog/digital partitioning, clean power routing, and proper reference decoupling without vias between pins and capacitors.

India faces selection challenges for the 2016 T20I series against England due to multiple injuries to key players. The squad, to be picked in early January 2017, will be crucial preparation for the ICC Champions Trophy in June. Probable selections include KL Rahul and Shikhar Dhawan as openers, with Rishabh Pant possibly chosen over Mandeep Singh. Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni are certain middle-order picks, alongside Manish Pandey, Karun Nair, and likely Suresh Raina. With Ashwin and Jadeja rested and other spinners injured, Kuldeep Yadav and Shahbaz Nadeem may debut. Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar are expected to lead the pace attack.

This patent application describes methods for encoding a single video bitstream that can be decoded by both SDR and HDR systems. The encoder receives an HDR master and reference SDR master, finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values to SDR values matching the reference SDR master when displayed, and generates metadata identifying this transform. In one embodiment, SDR values are encoded into the bitstream with metadata for HDR systems to convert back to HDR values. In an alternate embodiment, HDR values are encoded with metadata for SDR systems to convert to SDR values. The color volume transform can be a tone mapping function, scaling factor, or lookup tables, determined by minimizing differences between candidate SDR values and reference SDR values when emulated SDR display operations are applied.

The city contracted LIHI for $75,000 to operate Camp Second Chance, a city-sanctioned encampment at 9701 Myers Way S. in West Seattle, for four months through December 2017. The contract, signed November 21, 2017, requires LIHI to provide case-management services and specifies that the camp is self-managed without camper veto power, requires camper-provided security with at least one person at the gate at all times, and prohibits residents under 18. The 2018 contract was not yet finalized. The camp's renewal for a second year at the Myers Way Parcels site was under discussion, though it had already operated there for a year and a half, becoming city-sanctioned in February 2017.

A judge issued a temporary restraining order halting the Trump administration's federal worker layoffs sparked by the government shutdown. The lawsuit, filed by AFSCME and AFGE, alleges the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to justify staff cuts. Between 4,132 and 4,232 federal workers were marked for layoffs across multiple agencies including Commerce, Education, Energy, HHS, HUD, Homeland Security, and Treasury. OMB head Russell Vought indicated total layoffs could reach about 10,000. The Treasury and HHS Departments saw the largest cuts with over 1,000 employees each targeted for termination. Around 700 CDC workers mistakenly received layoff notices but were later told they could remain. Hundreds of thousands of federal workers remain furloughed, with many cutting spending and seeking financial assistance. The administration can appeal the decision.

Ella Ravenscroft, a 20-year-old model from Salford, is warning about sunbed dangers after having four moles removed due to changes in shape and color following two years of using sunbeds once or twice weekly. The Miss Teen Galaxy England 2016 winner shared before-and-after photos on Facebook to raise awareness, noting studies show sunbed use increases melanoma risk by 16-20%. Almost 500 people are diagnosed with melanoma annually in Greater Manchester, with around a fifth dying from the disease. Cancer Research UK advises monitoring moles for changes in size, shape, color, or texture, and seeking medical attention for any unusual skin changes, as early detection significantly improves outcomes.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation announced the 1Million Project, a 5-year initiative to connect 1 million low-income high school students lacking home internet access. Launching August 15, the program will provide 180,000 students across 32 states with free devices (smartphones, tablets, or hotspots) and 3GB of monthly LTE data for up to four years. Participating districts include New York City, Miami-Dade, Los Angeles, Chicago, and others. A January pilot with 3,750 students showed 86% reported improved attitudes toward learning and homework completion. Sprint will donate approximately $2.16 billion in services and support over five years, with device vendors contributing the majority of first-year equipment.

Gulf stock markets mostly declined on Wednesday, led by Qatar's 2.3% drop as major banks QNB and QIB fell sharply on profit-taking after recent gains from MSCI weighting increases. Dubai slipped 0.5% below levels before last week's visa announcement, though DXB Entertainments rose 4.1%. Saudi Arabia edged up 0.1% as Al Tayyar gained on early loan repayment news. Egypt fell 1.4%, while Abu Dhabi, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman also declined modestly.

Hexane is a hydrocarbon solvent found in plants and gasoline, produced from crude oil. It exists as n-hexane and other isomers, with two market types: pure hexane (laboratory use) and solvent-based hexane (industrial applications). Solvent-based hexane extracts vegetable oils from crops and serves as a cleaning agent in multiple industries. It appears in consumer products like glues and rubber. Hexane poses health hazards including neurological symptoms; OSHA sets a 500 ppm exposure limit. Benefits include removing unwanted tastes and odors in edible oils. Asia Pacific, particularly China, dominates global production and consumption. North American and European markets are expected to grow due to automotive rubber demand. Manufacturers are relocating production to Asia Pacific for lower labor costs.

Josie Goodenow, California Garden Clubs Inc. Bee Chairman, will present "All About Bees" at the Laguna Beach Garden Club on Friday, October 13. The event begins with a social at 9:30 a.m., followed by the meeting at 10 a.m. The program covers differences between native bees (Blue Orchard Mason Bee) and European honeybees, and methods to increase bee populations. Goodenow has served as bee chairperson since 2014 and has presented programs statewide. The public is welcome free for first visits. The club meets monthly September through May at Laguna Presbyterian Church, with a "Garden Boutique" available. Free parking is available in the Laguna Canyon Rd lot.

A Pennsylvania couple, Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were charged with endangering the welfare of their two children after leaving them home alone for three days. Police found the 10- and 11-year-old children in a deplorable home with trash on the floor and a temperature of 58 degrees. Sciortino was in Florida during this time, while Licciardello occasionally dropped off food. Sciortino claimed she didn't realize it was illegal and "didn't think it was really that bad." The children had missed 16 and 26 days of school respectively. Both parents received $10,000 unsecured bail and were released; the children are staying with family friends.

This study evaluated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis using CAPP-Seq in 24 advanced lung cancer patients with suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD). CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were significantly higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA (median 32.7% vs 1.8%). For LMD diagnosis, CSF-tDNA sensitivity was 91.7% compared to 81.8% for cytology. CSF-tDNA detection was strongly prognostic for overall survival (HR=7.1). Resistance mutations like EGFR T790M and MET amplification were common in peripheral blood but rare in time-matched CSF, indicating spatial heterogeneity in resistance mechanisms. In 12 patients receiving osimertinib for refractory LMD, those with CNS progression showed increased CSF-tDNA VAFs at follow-up, and post-osimertinib CSF-tDNA VAF was strongly prognostic for CNS progression (HR=6.2). The authors conclude CSF-tDNA detection is feasible and may improve LMD diagnosis sensitivity, enable better prognostication, and inform therapeutic strategies accounting for spatial heterogeneity in resistance mechanisms.

Jon Klemm is an underrated defenseman. Greg de Vries had a great year, establishing himself as a solid NHL defenseman who plays physical, skates well, has a good shot, and moves the puck. Skoula is an up-and-coming defenseman with speed, strength, size, poise, and a great shot. The speaker also references a talented forward who ranks highly in goals, assists, and points, and has been one of the league's best forwards in recent years.

NHS Digital data shows 719 people were admitted to hospitals in Devon, Cornwall and Isles of Scilly with eating disorders in 2016-17, including two children under 10. Girls and women comprised 94% of cases, with anorexia being most common at 45%. Admissions have more than doubled since 2010-11, though experts note this may reflect increased awareness or bed availability rather than rising prevalence, and could indicate insufficient outpatient care. Charities emphasize the need for early intervention and meeting government waiting time targets for community care.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 14, 2021, reporting its entry into an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley to issue $5.0 billion in unsecured notes: $1.25 billion each of 0.309% notes due 2023, 0.584% notes due 2024, 1.550% notes due 2028, and 2.000% notes due 2031. Net proceeds of approximately $4.98 billion will be used for general corporate purposes, including potential debt repayment. The notes are governed by a 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank as trustee and include provisions for redemption, change of control repurchase obligations, and covenants limiting liens and sale-leaseback transactions.

Poor medication adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, with non-adherence rates exceeding 50%. Person-centered care (PCC) has been proposed to improve adherence through better physician-patient communication, though empirical evidence is limited. This multicenter, cross-sectional study of Japanese hemodialysis patients examined relationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and tested whether trust mediates the PCC-adherence relationship. Participants were recruited from six medical facilities between April 2022 and February 2023. Medication adherence was measured using the Japanese ASK-12 scale, which assesses inconvenience/forgetfulness, treatment beliefs, and behavior.

Victor Tony Jones, sentenced to death in 1993 for a 1990 double murder, faces execution on Tuesday at 6 p.m. EDT and has asked the Supreme Court to block it. The Court has denied all execution stay requests this year, with 33 executions already in 2025—the highest in approximately a decade. This surge follows President Trump's January executive order ending the Biden administration's federal execution moratorium. Florida has conducted 13 of this year's executions, surpassing its previous record of eight in 2014. The Court typically denies stay requests without explanation, though it ruled in favor of death row inmates in three cases during the 2024-25 term. An upcoming case will address how courts determine intellectual disability in capital defendants. By the time that case is heard, 2025 executions may reach 43, the most since 2012.

Archive360 announced it is a finalist in two 2017 DBTA Readers' Choice Awards categories: Archive2Azure for "Best Cloud Storage Solution" and FastCollect for PSTs for "Best Data Storage Solution." The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's dismissal of Lewis Williamson's appeal regarding the Town of Surf City's closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive. The court rejected Williamson's argument that the town's intent to construct storage and bathroom facilities on the closed portion rendered the closing improper, distinguishing this case from Wooten v. Town of Topsail Beach because Surf City owned adjacent property and thus acquired vested rights in the closed street portion. Intraday trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day, including stocks, futures, or forex. Stroke disrupts motor control, causing upper extremity weakness and coordination deficits that impair daily activities. Surface EMG can measure post-stroke muscle changes, including excessive co-contraction of antagonist muscles and altered muscle synergies. Traditional low-density EMG cannot capture small hand muscle activity, while high-density EMG (HD-EMG) offers better resolution but is typically cumbersome. This study used an easy-to-use HD-EMG wearable sleeve to characterize forearm muscle coordination across functional movements in seven chronic stroke survivors (60±5 years) and seven able-bodied individuals (27±1 years). Participants performed cued hand, wrist, and forearm movements while EMG was recorded. The study evaluated isolated control through co-contraction index and muscle correlation metrics, plus sub-muscle coupling via muscle synergy analysis. The work demonstrates feasibility of combining HD-EMG features to assess functional movement ability in stroke, potentially improving rehabilitation and clinical care.

Researchers used four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) to visualize polar nanodomains in cryogenic SrTiO₃. Below the antiferrodistortive transition temperature (~105 K), local polar textures emerge with ~20 nm correlation lengths and periodic spatial ordering at ~25 nm length scales. Upon cooling below ~40 K into the quantum paraelectric regime, these polar nanodomains fragment into smaller, more disordered clusters with reduced correlation lengths (~14 nm) and suppressed periodic ordering. This re-entrant disordering demonstrates that quantum paraelectricity involves evolving polar nanodomains rather than complete absence of polarization.

This Court of Claims decision awards damages to Ralph Hartwell Brubaker, administrator of Berenice M. Brubaker's estate, for four State appropriations of approximately 365 acres near Massena, New York for the St. Lawrence River Project. The court applied *United States v. This patent application describes a display device with a substrate, pixel electrode, opposing electrode, encapsulation portion with alternating organic and inorganic layers, and a planarization layer on top. The planarization layer covers the edge portion of the encapsulation portion, with its edge side surface forming a larger angle (at least 70 degrees) with the substrate surface than the encapsulation portion's edge side surface. This structure maximizes the flattened upper surface area for forming patterns such as touch sensors, reducing dead space and parasitic capacitance while maintaining moisture protection. The touch sensor includes touch electrodes and wiring positioned on the planarization layer, with the edge side surface of the planarization layer being substantially flat or curved.

The passage details defensive strategies against the UCLA basketball offense, focusing on two approaches: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. The NBA method involves showing on high post rubs to force cutters inside, recovering to deny passes, and packing in weakside defenders. A majority of Supreme Court justices appear inclined to allow Rep. Michael Bost to challenge an Illinois law permitting mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to 14 days later, reversing lower courts that found he lacked standing. While Justice Kagan proposed a test requiring candidates to show a "substantial risk" of electoral disadvantage, she rejected requiring proof that a law might cause electoral defeat. This study investigates electrical resistivity in Al-Mg-Si alloys using SEM-based microscale four-point probe measurements. Researchers directly measured resistivity contributions from grain interiors and individual precipitates (Si and Mg2Si), finding that grain interior resistivity depends on heat treatment rather than composition. Si and Mg2Si precipitates contribute equally to resistivity. Bulk resistivity scales linearly with solute content, with coefficients dependent on heat treatment. The technique enables resolving bulk resistivity into microstructural components, demonstrating that precipitate volume fraction—not identity—drives resistivity increases in these alloys.

Y-Cross is a versatile drop-back passing concept used across football offenses, functioning as a weak-side flood play designed for deep shots and intermediate completions. The core involves a post route, crossing route (typically run by a TE or slot receiver), and a running back stretching the flat, with various backside route combinations available. It performs well against man coverage and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 3 due to the post safety occupying the middle of the field. The quarterback's progression follows: 1) Post, 2) Deep Crosser, 3) RB Check-down or Dig. Variations include post-wheel combinations and curl-flat tags to adapt against different defenses and personnel.

Bitcoin hit a six-week high on April 24, rising 4.4% to $9,340.88, following news that major financial institutions including Goldman Sachs and Barclays are exploring cryptocurrency trading. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education research from 2020 to 2024, using citation analysis of 35 articles from the Dimensions database. Key findings show a significant increase in publications and citations in 2024, with 15 articles receiving 234 citations (averaging 15.62 per article). The United States led in contributions with 9 documents and 103 citations, followed by China with 5 documents. The most cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson (55 citations each). The International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education was the most cited journal (55 citations), and Carnegie Mellon University the most cited institution. The most cited article was "Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education" (55 citations). The analysis reveals growing interest in AI's role in personalized learning, advanced analytics, and instructional automation in STEM education, while highlighting challenges including ethical concerns, AI literacy needs, and student engagement issues. The study provides insights for researchers, educators, and policymakers on integrating AI in STEM education.

The Trump administration's proposal to require a $100,000 fee for H-1B visas could threaten thousands of jobs at U.S. colleges and universities, which employed over 16,000 workers on approved H-1B visas as of June 30—about 5 percent of fiscal year 2025's total. The program allows employers to hire foreign workers with specialized knowledge and bachelor's degrees when domestic applicants are unavailable. Nearly half of college H-1B visas were concentrated at just 50 institutions, mostly research universities and medical centers. While the fee doesn't apply to current visa holders, it's unclear if universities will be exempt for new applications; the directive allows exemptions for national interest hires. Higher education advocates argue academic and medical hires serve national interest, but if applied broadly, the fee would likely impede colleges' ability to fill key positions, as many institutions with the most approved visas are public and may lack funds.

Benjamin Franklin's advice on prevention applies to natural disasters, which create lasting health hazards including contaminated water, toxic chemical releases, mold, disease-carrying mosquitoes, unstable structures, and mental stress. European scientists have established October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day to raise awareness of microscopic ocean algae that regulate Earth's climate. Coccolithophores capture atmospheric carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and form calcium carbonate plates that sink to the ocean floor, creating geological records of climate history. Five research institutions—Ruđer Bošković Institute (Croatia), Lyell Centre at Heriot-Watt University (UK), NORCE Norwegian Research Centre, MARE at University of Lisbon (Portugal), and the International Nannoplankton Association—lead this initiative. These organisms generate over 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate annually, but climate change threatens their survival. Researchers study their carbon storage mechanisms, viral interactions, bacterial relationships, aerosol fertilization effects, and fossil records to understand ocean carbon cycles and predict responses to environmental changes.

On June 28, 2021, NVIDIA Corporation completed a corporate structure simplification by domesticating a foreign subsidiary to repatriate non-U.S. intellectual property economic rights to the United States. This study analyzed prodromal symptoms and drug prescriptions before diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) using UK primary care data from the THIN database (20,214 AD, 28,222 PD, 4,682 DLB cases) with replication in UK Biobank. All three conditions showed increased rates of constipation, urinary disorders, hypotension, anxiety, depression, and sleep disorders 5-15 years before diagnosis, with DLB showing the strongest associations. Memory problems predominated before AD, tremor before PD, and hallucinations/confusion before DLB. Lower prescriptions of antihypertensives and antidiabetics were observed before all three diagnoses. Notably, statin prescriptions were lower before PD compared to AD/DLB, but higher in PD patients who later developed dementia. Benzodiazepines and beta-blockers were more prescribed before PD/DLB than AD. These findings highlight long prodromal phases and potential differential roles of cardiovascular medications in neurodegenerative disease risk.

A study reviewed 18 Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) from Eastern Mediterranean Region countries submitted between 2016-2021 to assess reporting on health-related Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets and indicators. While all VNRs established SDG monitoring mechanisms and 11 reported on all 17 SDGs, only 8 explicitly mentioned 2030 country targets. Data availability for SDG3 ranged from 48% to 93% among reporting countries, with 14 VNRs citing limited data availability as a key challenge. Reporting comprehensiveness varied by indicator type and country income level, with maternal, neonatal, and under-5 mortality rates most commonly reported. Indicators derived from disease surveillance and civil registration systems were reported more frequently than those from routine health information systems or national surveys. Only Qatar reported trends across all SDG3 indicators. The study concludes that strengthening health information systems, particularly civil registration and vital statistics systems and population-based surveys, is essential for improving data availability to achieve health-related SDGs.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, featuring an internal 4.096V reference (enabled by default, selectable via INTREF_DIS bit) and an integrated high-bandwidth ADC driver. The device supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar/unipolar ranges, outputting straight-binary format. It includes programmable alarm functions for input voltage (user-set thresholds with hysteresis) and AVDD supply (fixed 4.7V/5.3V thresholds), accessible via ALARM pin or registers.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI protocols (SPI-00-S default) and source-synchronous modes, with single or dual SDO-x bus width options. Communication uses 32-bit data transfer frames initiated by CONVST/CS, with commands for register read/write operations. Nine configuration registers control device operation including reference selection, input range, data output formatting, and power modes.

The device operates in three states: RESET (RST pin controlled, configurable as application or power-on reset), ACQ (signal acquisition with optional NAP mode), and CONV (conversion using internal clock). Low-power modes include NAP (reduced power between conversions) and power-down (deep sleep with retained registers).

For layout, separate analog/digital sections, use 10µF/1µF AVDD decoupling, 10µF REFCAP capacitance with <0.2Ω ESR, and 4.7µF REFIO decoupling when using internal reference. The internal reference exhibits thermal hysteresis from solder reflow; minimize exposure by soldering in final reflow pass.

Princeton scientists developed Diag2Diag, an AI tool that generates synthetic plasma data from existing sensor inputs to fill gaps left by incomplete diagnostics in fusion research. The system, created with international collaborators including PPPL, Chung-Ang University, Columbia University, and Seoul National University, produces detailed predictions for regions like the plasma edge where traditional sensors fail. By reducing hardware needs, Diag2Diag could make future fusion reactors more compact, affordable, and reliable. The AI also provided evidence supporting the magnetic island theory for suppressing edge-localized modes, dangerous plasma disruptions. The technology may extend to spacecraft and robotic surgery applications.

The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal regarding a 2007 non-prosecution agreement between Jeffrey Epstein and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida. The 5-Day Low of The Range Strategy uses two criteria: IBS below 0.25 and close lower than the previous 5 days' lowest low. From January 1993 to present, it produced 309 winners from 517 trades with 0.46% average return per trade, exceeding the 0.11% average for any 5-day period. The strategy has a 60% win ratio with larger average winners than losers. Profitability peaks at 3-7 days, yielding 10.76% annualized return with only 510 days in market versus 2,826 days for buy and hold. Short selling adaptation using 0.75 or 0.9 criteria on today's range generated approximately 10% returns but with more difficulty. The strategy has underperformed recently.

The Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test is the first FDA emergency use authorized saliva-based RT-PCR point-of-care (POC) device. Unlike central laboratory RT-PCR tests with long turnaround times and nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) requirements, or early POC platforms requiring healthcare worker-collected NPS samples with additional handling steps, the Sal6830™ allows patients to self-collect saliva directly into a sealed cartridge, eliminating operator exposure and sample mix-up risks.

A study at two US health clinics evaluated whether six non-laboratory trained healthcare workers could use the Sal6830™ accurately. Blinded sample testing showed 100% concordance with expected results (23/24 positive, 24/24 negative; one invalid). In a prospective clinical trial with 119 participants comparing Sal6830™ to the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV test, Sal6830™ demonstrated 87.2% positive percent agreement, 97.2% negative percent agreement, and 93.3% overall agreement. Differences were attributed to Sal6830™ detecting only intact virions versus Cepheid detecting viral debris.

Usability questionnaires from nine healthcare workers showed high confidence (4.9/5), ease of use (4.6/5), and no need for technical support. The study concluded that non-laboratory trained healthcare workers can operate the Sal6830™ accurately without training, offering RT-PCR accuracy with simplified patient self-collection.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) is a neural shader that caches and approximates radiance information to enable real-time global illumination and dynamic lighting. It takes path-traced rays after one bounce as input and infers final lighting values for multiple bounces using tiny neural networks trained on live game data. This reduces GPU computational load by avoiding full ray tracing while improving indirect lighting quality through inferred bounces on a limited ray budget. NRC adapts to game scenarios by training during gameplay.

The Washington State Court of Appeals Division Three reversed and remanded a Superior Court judgment in State v. Douglas John Nelson, case No. 31760-9-III, decided July 3, 2014. The original judgment was entered June 10, 2013, in Spokane County Superior Court case No. 12-1-00619-0, with Judge James M. Triplet presiding. This patent application describes a voice-directed inspection system that enables multiple inspectors to simultaneously inspect business assets using portable devices with headsets. The system comprises: inspection assistance devices (portable computers with headsets) that request assignments, receive inspection plan sections, provide audible commands, and send completion updates; site computers that distribute inspection plan sections to multiple devices and aggregate results; and host computers that store and receive inspection plans. The system divides large inspection plans into non-interfering sections based on physically distinct asset parts, allowing parallel work by multiple inspectors. Inspectors interact hands-free through speech recognition and synthesis, with real-time updates sent to the site computer. The system includes an inspection plan editor for creating and modifying voice instructions with configurable parameters, text-to-speech conversion, and speech recognition adaptation.

The Supreme Court's *Bruen* decision established a two-step test for Second Amendment challenges: first, whether the plain text covers the conduct; second, whether the regulation aligns with historical firearm traditions. Critics, including Justice Breyer and lower court judges, argue this imposes impractical historical burdens on courts. The author contends this criticism misframes the issue—judges are lawyers, not historians, and legal adjudication inherently requires answering historical questions. Originalists argue legal evidence is durable and judges possess tools to resolve uncertainty, including burden-shifting and precedent. While *Bruen*'s first step is now largely settled, step two requires examining historical traditions, though limited regulation in the early republic constrains available traditions. The author rejects replacing historical analysis with means-ends scrutiny, noting *Bruen* explicitly rejected judicial lawmaking.

A speaker expresses joy over winning the Stanley Cup, acknowledging Buffalo's strong performance and young team. A professor teaches poker strategy, emphasizing "decision mentality"—focusing on expected results rather than actual outcomes. He explains three levels of reasoning: Level 1 (specific hand vs. specific hand), Level 2 (hand vs. opponent's range/exploitative play), and Level 3 (range vs. range/optimal play/Nash equilibrium). He discusses key concepts including effective stack size, position (relative to the button), equity, and pot odds. For tournament play with antes, he recommends raising to 2.25 big blinds when opening, and going all-in with 12 big blinds or less. He provides conservative starting hand ranges by position, from 6% under the gun to 55% on the button, noting that experienced players weigh stack size and position more heavily than cards. He demonstrates equity calculations using PokerStove and explains that bluffing (betting with weak hands to induce folds) and value betting (betting with strong hands to induce calls) are fundamental to poker strategy.

In the UK, nearly half of women with ovarian cancer are diagnosed as emergency cases, with only one-third identified at early stages when treatment is most effective. According to Jo Stanford of Ovarian Cancer Action, late diagnosis stems from difficulties obtaining timely appointments and being dismissed by healthcare providers. The four main symptoms are: persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary urgency or frequency, and persistent pelvic or abdominal pain. Other signs include lower back pain, digestive issues, postmenopausal bleeding, and unusual fatigue. There is no screening test for ovarian cancer—a CA-125 blood test can only assist diagnosis, not confirm it. Ovarian Cancer Action offers a free online symptom checker and downloadable symptoms diary to help women track patterns and advocate for themselves. Early detection yields a 95% survival rate versus 16% at stage four. Stanford emphasizes that symptom awareness can save lives and encourages everyone to support women in seeking medical help promptly.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, causing catastrophic damage including destruction of the electricity grid, infrastructure failures, and over $82 billion in damages. The hurricane destroyed approximately 80% of crop value, representing $780 million in agricultural losses. This study addresses limitations in previous research on excess mortality by developing a semiparametric Poisson regression model that accounts for population displacement, intra-annual variability, and multiple causes of death including non-communicable diseases. The model captures varying durations of mortality effects across different causes and enables estimation of excess deaths by comparing expected deaths during post-emergency periods versus pre-emergency baselines, using penalized likelihood maximization with restricted maximum likelihood for smoothing parameters.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran, and Garry Cullum won class titles at the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series final at KartSport Hamilton. Cullum secured his record fourth title in KZ2 Restricted. Hendrik Bessembinder's 2017 study found that only 43% of U.S. stocks outperformed Treasury Bills between 1926 and 2015, with just 86 of 26,000 stocks generating half of all returns. The opposing team then returns the ball via throw-in to the team that originally had possession. Similarly, if the referee stops play for an injury, the team receiving the dropped ball should pass it back to opponents who had possession. Neither team should exploit this courtesy.

The Teachers' Union of Ireland has advised teachers against becoming Facebook friends with students, warning that it narrows professional distance and risks compromising teachers. General secretary John MacGabhann also cautioned members about making hasty or angry comments on social media, noting some had endangered their employment. He urged circumspection before posting and avoiding involvement in online disputes. Additionally, he criticised employers for using technology to place staff on effective 24/7 availability, advising members they have no obligation to respond to unreasonable out-of-hours contact and should switch off devices instead.

VentureWire newsletter dated May 17, 2001, covering venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include: Tahoe Networks launching with $38 million first round; Startups.com changing its business model to market intelligence, renaming to Startups, Inc., and cutting 30% of staff; Hermes Pensions Management investing $965 million for BTPS in private companies and funds; and OffRoad Capital splitting into two divisions and laying off 50% of employees. The speaker, upon assuming executive duties under the Federal Constitution, outlines governing principles: respecting constitutional limits on executive power; pursuing peaceful foreign relations; honoring states' rights; practicing strict economic management to reduce national debt; favoring agriculture, commerce, and manufactures equally; supporting internal improvements and education; maintaining subordination of military to civil power while strengthening the navy and militia; implementing just policies toward Native Americans; reforming government patronage and appointments; and selecting capable, diligent officials while seeking guidance from predecessors, coordinate government branches, and divine providence.

This study examines how TRNC Presidents' discourses have shaped education policies and national identity construction. Following the 1974 Cyprus Peace Operation and 1983 TRNC declaration, education was restructured around Turkish models with emphasis on national identity. The Turkish Cypriot Education Council drove reforms in teacher training, curriculum, and infrastructure. History textbooks long presented Turkish-centered narratives emphasizing conflict with Greek Cypriots, though post-2004 reforms attempted more reconciliatory approaches. Presidential statements show shifting priorities: Denktaş focused on national identity and Turkey integration; Talat emphasized EU harmonization; Eroğlu stressed technical education; Akıncı promoted multiculturalism and peace; Tatar returned to national identity themes. Key policy elements include Turkish-medium instruction, educational cooperation with Turkey, higher education internationalization, and debates over secular versus religious education. The study recommends multi-perspective history curricula, long-term strategic planning independent of political ideology, and balancing cooperation with Turkey against local educational autonomy.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that India's accession to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has increased the group's political profile and capacity to stabilize Central and South Asia, including resolving the Afghanistan crisis. He praised India's independent foreign policy while noting unsatisfactory bilateral trade volumes, targeting $30 billion by 2025. Lavrov criticized the US military strategy in Afghanistan, citing failed NATO efforts against extremism and quadrupled heroin production since 9/11. He denied Russian support for the Taliban, stating contacts were solely for extraction operations and pressuring negotiations under UN criteria. Lavrov regretted US rejection of the Moscow Process in favor of the Six Plus One group, emphasizing that Afghan resolution requires inclusive participation from all stakeholders.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben'Ary claims the Department of Justice leadership prioritizes punishing perceived Trump enemies over public safety. Ben'Ary was terminated during a terrorism prosecution involving the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly falsely suggested on social media that he was an ally of former Biden administration official Lisa Monaco. The letter warned that removing career officials from U.S. attorney's offices and the FBI makes America less safe.

A speaker emphasizes preparing for an opponent playing desperately for survival, stressing the importance of starting strong to avoid a difficult game, while acknowledging both teams want opposite outcomes—one to end the series, the other to extend it.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell will receive the Promise Hero Award from America's Promise Alliance for his literacy advocacy. Mitchell overcame his own reading struggles in college by starting with children's books and teaching himself to read better. He launched Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative promoting book ownership and reading benefits to underserved students. Mitchell graduated from the University of Georgia in 2015, was drafted by the Patriots in 2016, and wrote "The Magician's Hat." He aims to inspire children to read, emphasizing that increased access to printed material improves reading achievement for low-income children.

Yandex announced it will report Q2 2018 financial results on July 26, 2018, with a conference call at 8:00 a.m. ET. The call can be accessed via phone with passcode 4056605 or webcast, with replays available until August 2, 2018. Yandex is a NASDAQ-listed technology company founded in 1997 that builds machine learning-powered products including search, transportation, and navigation services.

This paper describes a one-day digital accessibility workshop designed for 73 software professionals and CS educators in India, held around Global Accessibility Awareness Day. The workshop addressed India's critical gap in accessibility training despite having the world's largest computing student population and software workforce. Using a three-phase model (preparation, execution, post-workshop reflection), the workshop featured five instructional modules covering accessibility basics, design, development, testing/reporting, and teaching accessibility, plus hands-on thematic booths. Evaluation through pre/post surveys showed 100% of participants would recommend the workshop, 90% found it highly effective and engaging, and 52% reported significant attitude shifts. Key findings revealed higher accessibility expertise in industry than academia, with participants requesting future content on advanced practices, AI applications, neurodiverse design, organizational strategies, and real-world case studies. The authors recommend pre-workshop materials, role-customized content, peer learning opportunities, and continued engagement to sustain impact.

The article analyzes whether the Supreme Court will uphold or modify *Humphrey's Executor v. FTC* (1935), which established that Congress can insulate certain agency heads from presidential removal. The case concerns President Trump's firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter. The Court seems likely to uphold the firing without fully overturning *Humphrey's Executor*, instead applying the framework from *Seila Law LLC v. CFPB* (2020), which requires examining whether modern agencies actually exercise executive, legislative, or judicial functions. The modern FTC differs significantly from the 1935 version, with expanded enforcement powers and decreased claim to nonpartisan expertise. The Court's order reframing the question suggests a "mend it, don't end it" approach that may preserve *Humphrey's Executor* for agencies like the Federal Reserve while limiting its application to agencies primarily wielding executive power.

DA Leader Mmusi Maimane delivered a parliamentary speech criticizing President Zuma's ANC government as "the enemy of the people," citing the Esidimeni tragedy where 94 mentally ill patients died, militarization of Parliament during SONA, and corruption allegations against Zuma. Maimane argued Zuma's "Radical Economic Transformation" masks elite self-enrichment through deals like the nuclear build and MPRDA Bill, while failing six million unemployed youth—the "Lost Generation." Alexa can help with cleaning tasks through several features: the Cleaning Buddy skill for scheduling, voice-activated ordering of supplies from Amazon, controlling robot vacuums like Neato and Roomba with voice commands, and laundry assistance through the Laundrapp service (available in select US cities) or stain removal skills like Good Housekeeping and Stains Be Gone.

This study investigates defects introduced by electropolishing (EP) on highly polished niobium surfaces for superconducting radio frequency (SRF) applications. Using white light interferometry and atomic force microscopy, researchers characterized sharp intergranular sloped steps that develop during EP, with slope angles up to ~50° and step heights up to 70 nm. These defects cause magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression, limiting achievable peak magnetic fields in SRF cavities. The study also examines how topography affects impurity diffusion, finding that large slope angles and step heights reduce impurity concentration at defect bottoms where vortex penetration preferentially occurs. The results indicate that EP produces smoother surfaces than buffered chemical polishing, with intergranular step heights comparable to the London penetration depth and impurity diffusion lengths, which helps preserve impurity uniformity during surface treatments like low-temperature baking. The findings suggest that achieving gradients above 35 MV/m requires polishing processes that produce surfaces smoother than conventional EP.

MIT scientists developed an enhanced prime editing system that reduces gene editing errors by 60 times. The refined method, called vPE, combines mutated Cas9 proteins with improved RNA template stabilization to lower mistake rates from roughly one in seven edits to one in 101 for common editing types, and from one in 122 to one in 543 for more precise modes. Prime editing uses a modified Cas9 enzyme to make single-strand DNA cuts rather than double-strand cuts, inserting corrected sequences via an RNA template. The team identified Cas9 mutations that make old DNA strands less stable, preventing reattachment errors when new sequences are incorporated. The researchers, led by Vikash Chauhan with senior authors Phillip Sharp and Robert Langer, aim to improve delivery to specific tissues and hope other labs will adopt the approach for research and therapeutic applications.

British police are investigating after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious from an unknown substance in Amesbury, eight miles from Salisbury where ex-spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter were poisoned in March. Counterterrorism officers are assisting local police. The pair remain in critical condition at Salisbury District Hospital, where they were initially thought to have taken contaminated drugs. Police have cordoned off locations they visited but say there is no wider risk, and it remains unclear if a crime was committed.

In a bankruptcy adversary proceeding, D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak's discharge under four sections of the Bankruptcy Code. The plaintiff alleged fraudulent transfer or concealment of property, failure to preserve financial records, false oaths, and failure to explain asset losses. The court found that while Fasolak made transfers to his wife and contained inaccuracies in his bankruptcy filings, the evidence did not establish fraudulent intent. The court noted Fasolak's age, retirement, and withdrawal from financial affairs as explanations. The plaintiff failed to identify specific missing records or prove Fasolak owned particular unexplained assets. The court entered final judgment for Fasolak and granted his Chapter 7 discharge.

Horse polo originated in Persia over 2,000 years ago, spread through Asia, and reached England via India before coming to the U.S., where it became popular in the 18th century. The Milwaukee Polo Club, located in Hartland, Wisconsin, traces its roots to 1923 and has occupied its current location for over 20 years. Despite its reputation as "The Sport of Kings," the club promotes itself as accessible "blue collar" polo with $5 admission, welcoming diverse participants including students, nurses, bartenders, and retirees. Matches consist of six seven-minute chukkers lasting about two hours, with a halftime divot stomp where fans interact with horses and players. Games are weather-dependent for safety. The club emphasizes proper horse care, limiting work to prevent overexertion and treating horses as teammates rather than equipment. The summer season began June 18; contact information and details are available through their website or phone numbers.

The speaker emphasizes living in the present and focusing on preparation rather than momentum. Digital laggards focus on optimizing existing initiatives with short-term, transactional training and risk-averse cultures marked by low trust. Digital leaders embrace learning mindsets, though cultural transformation requires sustained effort; some industries face regulatory constraints that discourage risk-taking. A pharmaceutical case study shows how localized experimentation environments can foster innovation within regulated industries.

Digital leaders prioritize transparency in data and decision-making, making data widely available across teams while implementing proper governance controls. They believe good ideas can come from anywhere and use standardized APIs (88% vs. 27% of laggards). Digital laggards restrict data access on a "need-to-know" basis, hoard data as power, and favor "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions.

Digital leaders embrace measurement to inform objectives and track progress, using detailed metrics that give teams flexibility and autonomy. A retail case study demonstrates how real-time sales reporting enables nimble, data-driven decisions. Digital laggards set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and focus on process adherence rather than outcomes.

Digital leaders create structured, transparent goals aligned to strategy through combined top-down and bottom-up processes, fostering vertical and horizontal organizational alignment. Digital laggards fail to connect goals clearly to strategy, causing misalignment. Data culture serves as a central coordinating function for digital leaders, while laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior.

Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Successful transformation requires establishing beliefs around learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement, then reflecting these in values and daily practices.

This inaugural address celebrates the centennial of American constitutional government, tracing the nation's evolution from the weak Articles of Confederation to a strengthened Union following the Civil War. The speaker emphasizes that the Constitution's supremacy was established through war, that emancipation fulfilled the promise of 1776, and that African Americans' elevation to citizenship requires equal ballot access protected by law. ATR Trailing Stop is a technical indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder that helps traders set dynamic stop-loss levels based on price volatility. It uses the Average True Range (ATR) to calculate trailing stops, typically multiplying ATR by a multiplier of 3.5, then subtracting from the previous close for long positions or adding for short positions. The indicator adjusts stop levels according to market volatility, helping traders protect profits, minimize losses, and determine exit points. It can also signal potential trend reversals when prices breach trailing stop levels, and can be applied to stocks and other financial instruments. ATR bands help identify breakouts and gauge volatility intensity. While useful for risk management, ATR Trailing Stop has limitations: it doesn't account for past performance or price movements, and traders should supplement it with other analyses. The cross point—where price intersects with trailing stop levels—indicates potential market dynamic changes.

Harvard University President Drew Faust announced she will step down on June 30, 2018, after 11 years as the university's first female president. The historian, who previously served as dean of the Radcliffe Institute, plans to take a sabbatical and return to scholarship. Faust is credited with restoring trust after a period of campus strife, fostering academic collaboration, expanding financial aid, and leading a fundraising campaign that raised $8 billion. Her tenure also included controversies over efforts to restrict all-male social clubs, demands for greater diversity, suspension of the men's soccer team over a sexual "scouting report," and a 2 percent endowment loss in 2016. A search committee will be formed to find her replacement.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice, retiring after leading since 2019, urges lawmakers to ensure students receive 180 actual instructional days rather than allowing professional development days and virtual instruction to count toward that total. Alphabet will pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump's lawsuit over his post-January 6, 2021 ban from YouTube, with $22 million going to Trump and $2.5 million to co-plaintiffs. Peter Lynch, a renowned retired money manager, led Fidelity's Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, achieving 29.2% annual returns—more than double the S&P 500. He popularized "invest in what you know" and "ten baggers," emphasizing fundamental analysis over market prediction. Lynch began as a golf caddy for executives, including Fidelity's George Sullivan, which led to a 1966 internship and eventual fund leadership. He grew Magellan from $20 million to $14 billion across 1,200 companies. His strategy involved categorizing companies into six types: slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, turnaround, and asset plays. He favored simple, overlooked businesses with clear models, allocating 30-40% to growth stocks while maintaining diversified holdings. Lynch reviewed portfolios quarterly, selling when price movements outpaced fundamentals and buying when strong companies dipped. He believed amateur investors could outperform institutions by researching companies they understood.

Scientists are calling for cheetahs to be listed as Endangered based on a comprehensive assessment of populations in southern Africa supported by the National Geographic Society. This study forecasts Aedes invasive mosquito abundance in the Basque Country, Spain, a non-endemic region experiencing increased imported cases of mosquito-borne diseases and expanding Aedes albopictus and Aedes japonicus populations. Using ovitrap egg count data from 2016-2023 across Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia provinces, researchers applied machine learning and statistical models (Random Forest, Generalized Linear Model, SARIMAX, Conditional Inference Trees) to predict mosquito abundance based on climate variables including temperature, humidity, and precipitation.

Key findings indicate temperature shows the strongest correlation with egg counts, while precipitation has minimal influence. Incorporating lagged variables significantly improved model performance. Random Forest performed best on training data, while GLM generalized better to test data. The 2023 test data for Bizkaia showed unusually high egg counts, challenging model predictions. Forecasts for 2024 suggest reduced mosquito abundance compared to 2023. The study emphasizes that continuous entomological surveillance and egg abundance monitoring are essential for accurate forecasting and effective public health interventions in non-endemic regions with maritime climates.

A UK study published in Thorax found that CT lung cancer screening increases smoking cessation rates among high-risk participants. Researchers sent information packs to nearly 2.5 million British residents aged 50-75, identifying 8,729 high-risk individuals. Of those screened, 10% quit after two weeks and 15% after two years, compared to 5% in the unscreened group. The study confirms that clean screening results do not reduce motivation to quit. Researchers note that participants were self-selected and may have already been considering quitting, but those who quit showed marginal tendencies toward distress about smoking. The findings suggest CT screening offers a "teachable moment" for smoking cessation and supports integrating screening with anti-smoking interventions.

The Geminid meteor shower peaks Wednesday night, potentially offering up to 50 meteors per hour between midnight and 4 a.m. Thursday. Viewing conditions will be favorable due to a smaller crescent moon, unlike last year's obstructing supermoon. The meteors, which radiate from the Gemini constellation, originate from debris of asteroid Phaethon and are known for being longer-lasting and brighter than other annual showers. No telescope is needed; rural areas with limited light pollution offer optimal viewing. Some clouds may appear late Wednesday but are not expected to be widespread.

The U.S. Geological Survey awarded $4.9 million to Caltech and six other institutions for developing an earthquake-warning system on the West Coast, plus $1 million for sensor equipment for the ShakeAlert system. The program had faced potential budget cuts earlier this year but received $10.2 million after legislative outcry. The USGS estimated in 2014 that completing the system requires $38.3 million in capital investment and $16.1 million annually to operate.
