Turing GPUs enable real-time ray tracing through RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, performing these operations autonomously while freeing SMs for other work. RT Cores process BVH traversal and intersection testing that would otherwise require thousands of software instructions per ray, making ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs.

NVIDIA NGX provides AI-based graphics enhancement through deep neural networks utilizing Turing Tensor Cores, including features like Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for improved image quality and performance, InPainting for content replacement, AI Slow-Mo for frame interpolation, and AI Super Rez for resolution upscaling.

Mesh Shading introduces Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders using cooperative thread models to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks and enable rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects in real time. Task Shaders dynamically generate work while Mesh Shaders produce triangles for rasterization.

Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows dynamic adjustment of shading rates per 16x16 pixel regions, enabling Content Adaptive Shading (reducing rates in slowly changing color regions), Motion Adaptive Shading (reducing rates for moving objects), and Foveated Rendering (reducing rates in peripheral vision areas).

Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance sampling by computing shading values in texture space, enabling temporal stability and reuse of shaded texels across frames, particularly beneficial for VR rendering efficiency.

Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per pass (32 at API level), efficiently rendering scenes from multiple viewpoints by fetching and shading geometry once, expanding upon Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection functionality.

Turing GPUs include USB Type-C and VirtualLink support for simplified VR connectivity, and feature RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and integer operations for hybrid rendering performance measurement.

The TU104 GPU contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 GPU, used in GeForce RTX 2070, contains three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, without NVLink or SLI support.

Most patients (95.9%) underwent on-pump surgery; 84.1% were male with mean age 61.4 years. Common complications included hydrothorax (12.0%), arrhythmia (10.7%), and psychosis (4.9%). Five patients died (1.7%). Key findings: elderly patients had higher risks of arrhythmia, psychosis, and stroke; diabetes mellitus and its complications extended ICU and total hospitalization; low BMI patients were at higher hydrothorax risk; prolonged aortic cross-clamp time and CPB time increased complications; patients with preoperative progressive angina and post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis had more complications. However, no statistical significance was found between the number of shunts or ITAs used and complication rates. The number of complications correlated with age, CPB time, aortic cross-clamp time, and hospitalization duration, but not with patient survival status.

Coach Sutter discusses lineup decisions, praising players like Tanner, Tyler, and Kopitar for their two-way play, tenacity, and consistency. He emphasizes team maturity, preparation, and leadership over individual stardom, noting the team remains young despite playoff experience. Sutter defends Slava's performance, attributes past criticism of team speed to puck movement, and avoids discussing elimination scenarios until games conclude. He confirms his top goalie will likely play next game.

A hockey player reflects on winning the Stanley Cup, emphasizing the team's ability to handle adversity, strong home performance, and key contributions from players like John who stepped up defensively. He notes the challenges of injuries, travel fatigue, and integrating new players after losing leaders like Bobby Holik. He acknowledges the opposing team's goaltender deserved the Conn Smythe Trophy, expresses satisfaction with winning but not being fully satisfied given past disappointments, and hopes to build toward potential dynasty status while recognizing it's too early to make that claim.

A creditor's action against assignees for an accounting and distribution of funds is not "an action for money received" under Code section 179 permitting arrest of defendants in fiduciary capacities. The court held that such actions contemplate more than simple money recovery, requiring judicial determination of amounts chargeable to assignees and distribution among creditors. The plaintiff assignee's arrest under execution was unauthorized, and the $100 false imprisonment judgment against the attorneys who issued it was affirmed.

Only 40% of U.S. households report good or excellent savings progress. America Saves Week, held annually since 2007, promotes savings behavior through participating financial institutions, government agencies, employers, and organizations. America Saves Week 2017 runs February 27 to March 4 with daily themes like family savings and tax-time saving. Participants receive toolkits, badges, and resources. Military Saves Week 2017 runs concurrently for servicemembers and families.

In 2011, St. Olaf student Erik Brust founded JonnyPops to honor his late cousin Jonathan Jeffrey, with whom he had conceived the idea for a natural, fruity frozen treat. Brust recruited classmate Connor Wray to develop recipes using real cream, fruit, cane sugar, and salt. After campus taste-tests, JonnyPops launched at Twin Cities farmers markets and vendors in 2012. By 2013, distribution expanded to multiple states, and both co-founders were named to Forbes' 30 Under 30. After graduating in 2014, they took the company full-time, launching grocery retail with 50 Minnesota stores. JonnyPops now has 10,000 distribution points nationwide and recently introduced a Delights line with five chocolate-based flavors. The company maintains a social mission called Better Pop for a Better World, printing day-brightening messages on sticks and partnering with retailers to raise funds for addiction treatment organizations.

The speaker expresses gratitude for reelection and acknowledges predecessors' greater contributions to the Revolution. He outlines principles for his administration, reviews the recent war with Britain, and describes defensive measures including coastal fortifications and naval expansion. He discusses neutrality in the Spanish-American colonial conflict, the suppression of piracy in Florida, and the importance of acquiring Florida through treaty with Spain. He notes commercial treaties with Britain and ongoing negotiations with France, as well as naval forces maintained in the Mediterranean and Pacific. He addresses the nation's prosperous financial condition, diminished revenue from price depression, and the potential need for internal taxes. He advocates for reforming Indian policy through land cessions, individual land rights, and education funding. He affirms neutrality toward European conflicts while defending maritime rights, praises the American elective system of government, and celebrates territorial expansion including the Mississippi River, Louisiana, and the Floridas.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated the company will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite a new $100,000 fee that could cost Nvidia an estimated $147.3 million for 2025 visa approvals. Huang called legal immigration "essential" in an internal memo, noting that Nvidia's success "would not be possible without immigration." The fee applies only to new applicants, not renewals. Huang, who was born in Taiwan, previously supported Trump's H-1B changes but later said the $100,000 fee "probably sets the bar a little too high."

Investment analysts issued price target changes for multiple companies on Friday, October 6th. BNP Paribas set targets for Covestro AG (€64.00, sell), Basf Se (€96.00, buy), Evonik Industries AG (€29.00, neutral), Linde AG (€175.00, neutral), Lanxess AG (€65.00, neutral), and Wacker Chemie AG (€110.00, neutral). Cowen and Company raised AdvanSix's target to $46.00 (outperform). Royal Bank of Canada lowered Ascena Retail Group's target to $2.50 (sector perform) and raised Constellation Brands' to $226.00 (outperform). Oppenheimer Holdings set targets for Costco Wholesale ($185.00, buy), Netflix ($215.00, outperform), and Yum China Holdings ($45.00, outperform). Stifel Nicolaus raised Deckers Outdoor to $80.00 (buy) and Constellation Brands to $235.00 (buy). Benchmark Co. raised New Oriental Education to $100.00 (buy). HC Wainwright set Inovio Pharmaceuticals at $13.00 (buy). Morgan Stanley set Eli Lilly at $86.00 (hold). UBS AG set Mallinckrodt PLC at $70.00 (buy). Craig Hallum raised Plug Power to $4.00 (buy). Mizuho lowered Rite Aid to $2.25 (neutral). Needham & Company raised 2U to $66.00 (buy).

This review protocol aims to evaluate SARS-CoV-2 infectivity in immunosuppressed transplant patients by examining the relationship between PCR cycle threshold values or other viral burden measures and viral culture results. The study will search LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and WHO COVID-19 databases for studies from November 2019 to December 2021 reporting serial PCR data with viral culture from solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. Four researchers will independently screen studies, with inclusion requiring respiratory samples and viral culture data; post-mortem only, non-respiratory only, and studies without viral culture will be excluded. Data extraction and quality assessment using five criteria will be performed, with narrative synthesis planned rather than meta-analysis due to laboratory practice variations. The review is funded by NIHR and University of Calgary, with multiple authors declaring various grants and competing interests related to COVID-19 research, vaccine development, and healthcare organizations.

A president has died for the fourth time in U.S. history, and his constitutional successor assumes office. The speaker pledges to continue the predecessor's policies promoting prosperity, economy, and friendly foreign relations. With no urgent legislative demands, the new executive will rely on constitutional discretion, divine guidance, and the American people's virtue and intelligence to fulfill these responsibilities.

Lincolnshire County Council approved a new care leavers strategy. The council supports vulnerable young people leaving care through measures including council tax discounts of up to 100% for 18-21 year-olds, university cost assistance, and driving licence funding. Support now extends to age 25 following central government changes. The leaving care services budget is approximately £1.2 million, with 300 young people currently receiving services. Corporate Parenting Manager Andrew Morris emphasized the council's legal responsibility to act as parents to care leavers, helping those from disadvantaged backgrounds get a good start in life. Support is available through the council or Barnardos.

A 245-million-year-old fossil of Dinocephalosaurus, a long-necked marine reptile from the Triassic Period discovered in southwestern China, reveals the first known instance of live birth in archosauromorphs—a vertebrate group including birds, crocodilians, dinosaurs, and pterosaurs. The pregnant fossil contained a developing embryo in curled posture facing forward, confirming viviparity rather than egg-laying. This adaptation allowed the fully marine creature to avoid land predators. The 13-foot reptile had a 5.5-foot neck, paddle-like flippers, and fish-catching teeth. Unlike temperature-dependent sex determination in some reptiles, Dinocephalosaurus used genetic sex determination like mammals and birds.

Farmers State Bank of Craig sued Samuel J. Lydick on a $3,000 promissory note. Lydick claimed fraud and failure of consideration, alleging bank officer Everett J. Martin conspired to deceive him into purchasing worthless stock. The trial court directed a verdict for the bank on Lydick's cross-petition and submitted to the jury whether the bank was a holder in due course and whether Martin made fraudulent representations. The jury found for the bank and for Martin. The appellate court affirmed, holding: (1) the court properly withdrew issues lacking sufficient evidence; (2) the evidence sustained the verdict; (3) jury instructions were proper; and (4) under Nebraska precedent, a payee receiving a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice of infirmity from a holder (not maker or drawer) is a holder in due course, precluding defenses of fraud and failure of consideration between the maker and prior holder.

James Schenck, CEO of PenFed Credit Union, was named Large Business Philanthropist of the Year at the 20th annual Volunteer Alexandria Business Philanthropy Summit. Schenck accepted the award on behalf of PenFed's 2,500 employees, emphasizing the organization's "People Helping People" philosophy. Recent charitable donations by PenFed and its philanthropic arm, the PenFed Foundation, include $300,000 to Serve our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America, and $15,000 to Bunker Labs. The PenFed Foundation, headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia, has provided over $30 million in financial support since 2001. Schenck volunteers as CEO of the PenFed Foundation without compensation and serves on multiple boards. He was elected National Credit Union Hero of the Year in 2017 and named one of the 100 most influential veterans by HillVets in 2015. PenFed Credit Union, established in 1935, is America's second-largest federal credit union with over 1.6 million members worldwide and $23 billion in assets.

Amazon Prime Day returns October 7-8, with early deals already available on WIRED-tested products. The publication's Reviews team, with hundreds of years of combined experience, only covers deals on gear they've hand-tested. New deals added September 30, 2025 include Amazon devices, laptops, fitness trackers, and smart bird feeders. Notable deals include: Apple iPad (2025, A16) for $299 ($149 off); Apple MacBook Air (M4, 2025) for $799 ($200 off); Arlo Pro 5S Security Camera for $100 ($80 off); Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024) for $300 ($100 off); and Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) for $70 ($20 off). The Ultrahuman Ring Air is also featured, though FTC rules will ban US sales after October 21.

China has spent roughly 20 years modernizing its military to match its growing global economic and diplomatic influence, defend regional interests like South China Sea territorial claims and sea lanes, support initiatives such as AIIB and OBOR, and counter US military presence in the Indo-Pacific. These efforts have transformed the PLA into a markedly more capable and assertive force, though the ultimate outcome remains uncertain.

New sanctions on North Korea have further frozen its rarely traded defaulted debt, which investors once hoped would benefit from economic opening. The $1 billion in syndicated loans, in default since the 1980s and repackaged by BNP in 1997, stopped trading around 2013 due to earlier sanctions. Prices had risen briefly in 2011 on hopes for reform under Kim Jong-un. Fresh UN sanctions banning key exports and escalating tensions between Trump and Kim have made trading even less viable. Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund holds $15.5 million in zero-coupon bonds maturing 2020, last valued at $830,000 in 2013 after acquiring them for over $3.1 million. Experts estimate total debt including arrears at around $3 billion, with interest arrears 4-5 times principal, and see no near-term resolution. North Korea joins Cuba and Iran as frontier markets becoming less accessible to investors seeking high returns.

Latin American stocks rebounded on Monday as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased, with Mexico's IPC index rising 1.1% and Brazil's Bovespa hitting its highest level since May. Currency markets remained subdued as investors awaited NAFTA negotiations and Brazil's fiscal goal revision.

Materials characterization requires multiple techniques for complex materials. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy are complementary bulk techniques—XRD probes long-range periodic structure while XAFS measures short-range local structure element-specifically. Researchers use synchrotron facilities for enhanced resolution and sensitivity, but facility access is limited and conventional homogeneous mapping approaches are inefficient for inhomogeneous samples.

This work presents a modular AI-driven framework for multi-modal synchrotron experiments. An ensemble of AI agents performs real-time data processing, analysis, and Bayesian optimization-based decision-making to guide measurements, with human-controlled adjudicators maintaining researcher autonomy. The framework was demonstrated through synchronous XRD and XAFS mapping of Al-Ni-Pt combinatorial libraries across two beamlines at NSLS-II, achieving inter-beamline coordination and autonomous operation. A digital twin validated that AI-driven mapping surpasses conventional grid approaches, achieving higher accuracy with fewer measurements by prioritizing phase boundaries and heterogeneous regions.

Let’s Grow Kids, a Vermont child care advocacy organization, officially ended operations on October 3, 2025, after a planned 10-year run. Founded in 2015 by Rick Davis with Aly Richards as CEO, the group raised over $70 million in private philanthropy and grew to 40 staff members. Its efforts helped establish Vermont as the first state with a near-universal child care system through Act 76, signed in 2023. The sunset strategy was central to its success, enabling faster operations, increased philanthropic investment, and stronger accountability. The organization planned its wind-down years in advance, transitioning implementation work to permanent organizations focused on financing, workforce, data, and advocacy. Former staff moved to key roles in state agencies and related nonprofits. A remaining 501(c)(4) group, the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network, will handle political work to protect Act 76 funding. While 80-90% of Vermont families with children in child care now qualify for subsidies, the system is not yet fully universal. Other states have sought to replicate Vermont's model, with Richards emphasizing that the time-limited structure and robust data collection were critical to passing and sustaining the legislation.

A social media argument between Jennifer Bartell's daughter and Albany Pierce escalated to a planned meeting that never happened, leading Pierce, her boyfriend Joshua Bowen, her mother Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson to Bartell's home on March 14 in Portsmouth, Virginia. Bowen allegedly shot Bartell several times after a fight broke out; he claimed she appeared armed, though investigators found no firearms at the scene. All four have been arrested, with Bowen charged with shooting and the others with accessory after the fact. Neighbors expressed shock but relief that the shooting was targeted, not random.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana "Nevermind" album cover featuring a naked baby underwater is not child pornography, dismissing a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who was photographed at 4 months old. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found that while Elden was nude, no other factors met the legal standard for child pornography, comparing the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

A Florida Museum of Natural History study found that lice parasitizing primates and humans have hosted their bacterial endosymbionts continuously for 20-25 million years, contradicting previous theories of multiple replacements. These bacteria, which supply essential vitamins lice cannot obtain from blood, have coevolved with their hosts since great apes and old world monkeys shared a common ancestor. Researchers sequenced symbiont genomes from human, chimpanzee, gorilla, and red colobus monkey lice, finding extremely small genomes (530,000-570,000 base pairs) with extensive remodeling that clustered vitamin-synthesis genes together. The study provides insights into bacterial genome evolution and primate evolutionary history.

A University of Bern study using deep learning on over 50,000 European satellite images found that Martian dust devils and winds can reach speeds up to 160 km/h—much faster than previously believed. The research, led by Dr. Valentin Bickel using data from CaSSIS and HRSC cameras, indicates these stronger winds likely lift significantly more dust into Mars's atmosphere than earlier estimates. The findings, based on two decades of global data, will help improve atmospheric modeling and risk assessment for future Mars missions.

This study investigated whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) patterns of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) could predict ADHD symptom course in 54 newly diagnosed adult patients over approximately three years. Participants underwent baseline fMRI scans and clinical evaluation using the Wender-Reimherr Interview (WRI), with follow-up assessment at t2. At follow-up, 34 patients continued stimulant medication while 20 had discontinued treatment.

Key findings showed that lower NAc connectivity to the right paracingulate gyrus (part of the default mode network) correlated with higher baseline symptom severity. Lower NAc connectivity to the right anterior insula predicted better long-term symptom improvement. Medication status revealed divergent patterns: treated patients showed higher NAc-posterior insula connectivity associated with improvement, while non-responders showed the opposite pattern where higher connectivity predicted worse outcomes.

The study suggests FC patterns between the reward system and default mode/salience networks may serve as potential biological markers for ADHD prognosis and stimulant medication response, though limitations include small sample size and need for replication in larger studies.

The Utah Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control overcharged business customers $1,161 on seven special-order items due to a computer entry error during a required price markup change from 86% to 88% in July. The error caused a $186 loss to the department in nine sales while overcharging customers in 28 sales. The DABC will issue refunds and has implemented software to flag incorrect markup percentages. The audit also found the department failed to transfer $4.6 million in required revenue to state school lunch and public safety programs in November 2017, which was later corrected.

The Aedes aegypti mosquito, known for spreading Zika, also transmitted yellow fever in a 1793 Philadelphia epidemic that killed approximately 5,000 people. Physicians then, including Benjamin Rush, failed to identify mosquitoes as the vector, attempting ineffective treatments like bloodletting and quarantine. The mosquito transmission mechanism was discovered over a century later, leading to improved sanitation and the last North American outbreak in 1905. Today, yellow fever is resurging in Brazil with 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths since December 2016, threatening to spread to major cities. Prevention methods mirror historical advice: eliminating standing water and avoiding mosquitoes. An effective yellow fever vaccine exists since 1939, and researchers at Penn are developing similar DNA and mRNA-based vaccines for Zika, with clinical trials underway. WHO recommends yellow fever vaccination for travelers to affected Brazilian regions.

Rachael Caplan, 29, has Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), a rare neurological disease causing constant, severe nerve pain throughout her body. Once athletic with a law degree, she is now bedridden in her parents' Thornhill home, unable to go downstairs or outside since August 2016. CRPS affects over 9,000 Canadians annually, beginning as an apparent autoimmune disease before progressing to nerve injury. Symptoms include intense burning pain, swelling, temperature changes, and system breakdown. Caplan's symptoms started seven years ago from a hip injury, intensifying after acupuncture; diagnosis took 18 months. Early treatment (within 3-6 months) has 80-90% success, but delayed diagnosis often leads to permanent disability. Her friends launched the #AceThisFire social media campaign, where participants hold hands in ice water to simulate CRPS pain, garnering over 20,000 views. Recently, green light therapy has helped her sleep up to nine hours nightly. Caplan remains hopeful for remission and works to raise awareness for quicker diagnoses and better treatments.

Gulf Island Fabrication (GIFI) trades at a significant discount to book value due to troubled offshore markets and operational problems, including a $24.3 million Q4 loss. The company builds offshore platforms, vessels, and steel structures through three divisions. Its offshore support vessel market faces massive oversupply, with 196+ OSVs competing for 21 active floater rigs. Positive factors include minimal debt, a diverse backlog shifting away from offshore, and potential asset sales: its Texas South Yard has a $55 million purchase option, with the North Yard also for sale. Combined book value of these facilities is ~$100 million, versus a market cap of ~$120 million. The company may secure new contracts, including a large SeaOne Caribbean project and an offshore wind MOU with EEW. Shares have dropped 40% in two months, with technical support at $7.

This article introduces QoCGM, an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) data analysis. QoCGM addresses gaps in existing analytical tools by incorporating newer clinically relevant metrics, analyzing nocturnal versus diurnal glucose patterns, detecting hypoglycemic events, and assessing day-to-day glucose variations. The tool processes preprocessed CGM data from CSV files through two stages: preprocessing with duplicate removal and missing data interpolation using PCHIP, followed by metric derivation. QoCGM calculates six categories of metrics: basic descriptive statistics, time-in-range metrics, glycemic risk indicators, glycemic variability metrics, glycemic control indicators, and entropy/complexity measures. A case study of 324 insulin-treated type 2 diabetes patients demonstrated that metrics like day-to-day standard deviation of TIR, multiscale complexity index, mobility, and distance traveled per minute capture unique independent information with low correlation to other metrics. The authors conclude that QoCGM facilitates standardized CGM analysis across research populations to identify clinically relevant metrics.

Post-WWI negotiations will focus on European recuperation, with Allied control of essential materials giving them negotiating power. Germany faces revolutionary discontent from demobilization regardless of speed. German imperialism is divided between two schools: Kühlmann's group favors "accommodation" with western nations to secure overseas supplies and dominate the Near East, while the Fatherland Party insists on military retention of Belgium to guarantee access to world markets. Belgium has become central to German policy due to its commercial value, strategic position against England and France, and potential for drawing Flemish regions into German influence.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch its fall menu on August 28, featuring returning pumpkin spice items and new maple pecan flavors, including a maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. The company aims to gain a sales advantage by releasing seasonal beverages earlier than competitors McDonald's and Starbucks, which have not announced 2018 launch dates. Dunkin' has reported seven consecutive quarters of better-than-expected earnings, partly attributed to unique and limited-time menu offerings such as Wake-Up Wraps, pretzel croissant breakfast sandwiches, cold brew coffee, and fruited ice tea.

Sarasota County v. Department of Administration, No. 77-159 (Fla. 2d DCA Oct. 5, 1977): The District Court of Appeal denied Sarasota County's petition for writ of certiorari seeking review of a declaratory statement by the Department of Administration. The County wanted a proposed crude oil splitter in neighboring Manatee County classified as a development of regional impact under Chapter 380, Florida's Environmental Land and Water Management Act of 1972. The court held the County lacked standing to invoke Chapter 380's procedures because it was neither a regional planning agency, appropriate local government, state planning agency, nor developer. The majority declined to reach the merits, noting the County could pursue relief through its regional planning agency or under the Florida Environmental Protection Act. Judge Scheb dissented, arguing the County had standing and the Department's declaratory statement incorrectly restricted the state land planning agency's authority to determine whether unlisted projects qualify as developments of regional impact.

A coach discusses giving a player a day off, acknowledges second-period struggles in Boston games, praises two players for playing better than their point totals indicate despite being shut out, emphasizes a one-game-at-a-time mentality, and notes the physical demands of competing for a trophy while expressing confidence in the team's readiness.

ICICI Bank's mortgage loan portfolio reached Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player in the segment, with a target to grow to Rs 2 trillion by FY20 at 15% annual growth. The mortgage book comprises half of its Rs 3 trillion retail loan portfolio, which represents 52% of total assets. Growth is driven by tier II and III towns under PM's Awas Yojna, with average ticket size slightly above Rs 30 lakh. The bank is expanding digitisation, including 2,000 fully online approved housing projects and a repository of 30,000 approved projects across 40 cities. It plans to increase loan processing centres by 50% from 1,050. The bank has been under probe since March for alleged wrongdoings in loans to Videocon group by former MD Chanda Kochhar.

SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have substantially reduced COVID-19 cases, hospitalisations, and deaths, though variant emergence has reduced effectiveness against infection while efficacy against severe outcomes remains more durable. Omicron and its subvariants now dominate globally, causing repeated infections due to waning immunity. Two Omicron-specific bivalent vaccines are available, showing higher immunogenicity than original vaccines.

Researchers developed a model to estimate vaccine efficacy from immunogenicity data by fitting to national-level vaccine effectiveness estimates from England for three vaccines (AZD1222, BNT162b2, mRNA-1273) against Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2 variants. The model uses a biphasic exponential decay function for immunity levels and a logistic relationship between immunity and protection against mild disease, hospitalisation, and death.

Results show higher immune levels are required for protection against mild disease than severe endpoints. The model estimates a 6.5-fold reduction in immunity against Omicron versus Delta. mRNA-1273 generated highest immunity levels, followed by BNT162b2 and AZD1222. Effectiveness against Omicron hospitalisation 180 days post-boost was 49.5% for AZD1222, 69.8% for mRNA-1273, and 63.7% for BNT162b2, declining further after one year.

Using immunogenicity data, the Moderna bivalent vaccine showed 1.61-fold higher neutralising antibody titres against BA.1 versus the original vaccine. While short-term protection was similar, the bivalent vaccine maintained substantially higher efficacy over one year (77.9% vs 60.0% against hospitalisation). The study demonstrates challenges in predicting vaccine effectiveness from immunogenicity data alone due to complex immune responses beyond neutralising antibodies.

New research by Tweak Mattress found that the average Brit wakes up three times nightly, with one in ten waking 7-10 times. The top ten reasons for disrupted sleep are: needing the toilet (47%), partner snoring (41%), being edged out of bed by partner (25%), back pain or aches (19%), bad dreams (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), partner talking or making noises in sleep (10%), phone light disturbing sleep (10%), anxiety (6%), and partner watching TV or reading (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart explains that sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene (pre-bed routines) and sleep cycles, with environmental factors affecting whether people return to sleep after naturally stirring during lighter REM sleep.

Larry Connors' R3 strategy, from his 2009 book "High Probability ETF Trading," is a mean-reversion strategy using 2-day RSI. Key rules include: close above 200-day moving average, three consecutive days of 2-day RSI drops (first from below 60), and entry when 2-day RSI falls below 10, exiting above 70. Backtesting on 25 ETFs from 2000-2020 showed 992 trades, 75% win rate, 0.68% average gain, 2.08 profit factor, 6.47% CAGR, and -16% maximum drawdown during August 2011. Applied to SPY/QQQ portfolio (50% each), profit factor was 3.37 with 2.69% CAGR. The strategy still performs after 12 years, though about 50% of ETFs performed worse in recent years, and it works best on equity markets.

N62.4 billion in 91-day and 182-day Treasury bills and N168.1 billion in OMO maturities are expected this week, with rollovers offsetting the Treasury bills. Financial system liquidity remained negative last week due to CBN's OMO sales and forex auctions, pushing OBB and overnight rates to 105.0% and 107.8% midweek before closing at 55.8% and 59.3% Friday. The Federal Executive Council approved dollar-backed Treasury instruments with extended 2-3 year maturities to restructure debt, reduce borrowing costs, and increase private sector lending. The CBN's Importers' and Exporters' forex window attracted $4 billion since April, with exchange rates converging across markets. The bond market was bearish with yields flat at 16.8%, while corporate Eurobond performance was mixed. The 2018-2020 MTEF targets 3.5% GDP growth in 2018, with oil benchmark at $45 and N305/$ exchange rate.

Six Texas public university systems are reviewing curricula, syllabi, and course descriptions after conservative politicians targeted faculty teaching about gender identity. The reviews follow an incident at Texas A&M University-Commerce where administrators were demoted and the president pushed out over a lesson on gender identity in a children's literature class. Texas A&M president Mark Welsh ordered an audit extended system-wide by the Board of Regents. The University of North Texas system set a January 1 deadline for reviews, while the University of Texas system is reviewing gender identity courses for November Board discussion. System leaders cited a March executive order stating there are only two sexes, though no laws prohibit teaching about transgender identity. The University of Houston and Texas Woman's University are also conducting reviews. Faculty face risks from publicly accessible syllabi through platforms like Simple Syllabus and Texas House Bill 2504, which requires public access to syllabi. One University of Houston lecturer was targeted by a conservative news site after they found his courses through Simple Syllabus keyword searches.
The Eighth Circuit denied Earl Ringo's petition for rehearing en banc and petition for rehearing by the panel; Judge Bye would have granted the en banc petition. Judge Benton did not participate.

This study found that COVID-19 mRNA vaccine boosters aggravate insulin resistance in pre-diabetic and diabetic patients. In a clinical trial of 155 adults, booster shots significantly elevated HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglyceride, and TyG indices in pre-diabetic and diabetic subjects, with 61.1% showing impaired insulin sensitivity and 66.7% showing increased cardiovascular risk. HOMA-IR positively correlated with immune response markers. Mouse studies confirmed that multiple vaccine doses impaired glucose tolerance and insulin signaling. Metformin alleviated vaccine-induced insulin resistance in mice without affecting vaccine efficacy. The authors suggest SARS-CoV-2 spike protein may contribute to insulin resistance through TLR4 and ER binding, and recommend glucose monitoring for at-risk individuals post-vaccination.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is a website active since 2009 that covers dinosaur-related content through paleoart, scientific reports, and reviews of books, toys, films, TV shows, and museum exhibits. The site features factual reports from scientists, diverse artistic styles recreating prehistoric life, and notably snarky reviews of vintage children's books that critique zoological inaccuracies with humor. It posts weekly with monthly dinosaur news round-ups, offering extensive archived content. The name references Gabriel García Márquez's novel and a Chasmosaur dinosaur, and the site includes a mascot on its homepage.

Olivia Munn, 45, was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer at 43 despite clear mammograms and no symptoms. A two-minute online lifetime risk assessment revealed she had a 37% risk, prompting her to get an MRI that detected the cancer. Her mother also took the assessment and was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer. Munn advocates for the assessment to become standard care, noting that women with 20% or higher risk should seek earlier screening.

Hugh Jackman, 48, revealed on social media that he is undergoing another treatment for basal cell carcinoma, the most common form of skin cancer. The Sydney-born actor, who has been treated for this condition at least four times previously since his first diagnosis in November 2013, credited frequent body checks and his doctors for his positive prognosis. Despite the recent diagnosis, Jackman's professional schedule remains unaffected, with "Logan" scheduled for March release and "The Greatest Showman on Earth" slated for later this year.

Doug Ford launched his Progressive Conservative election campaign with an energetic rally at the Toronto Congress Centre, featuring enthusiastic supporters, music, and appearances by former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney, and Tanya Granic Allen. Ford criticized Premier Kathleen Wynne and Liberal record debt and spending, promising prosperity for all Ontarians. Kory Teneycke will serve as campaign manager and Jeff Silverstein as communications manager. Supporters expressed confidence while acknowledging the campaign will be challenging, with volunteers and family members including nephew Michael Ford, who honored his late uncle Rob Ford, present to show support.

Stan Lee, 95-year-old comic book creator, was hospitalized due to shortness of breath and irregular heartbeat but has been released and is recovering well. The hospitalization was precautionary, and Lee reports feeling great. His latest public appearance was at the "Black Panther" premiere on January 30, 2018.

Valeant Pharmaceuticals, CEO J. Michael Pearson, and Pershing Square Capital Management with William Ackman entered a litigation management agreement regarding a putative class action in California federal court. The agreement terminates November 1, 2017 if no settlement is executed. Pershing Square, which owns 7.8% of Valeant's common stock, agreed to forbear from related actions. Legal fees for Allergan litigation will be split 50/50 between Valeant and Pershing Square for the first $10 million. The parties also executed mutual releases.

A hockey player discusses preparing for the Stanley Cup Final, emphasizing drawing on past experience, maintaining routines, and relying on team play rather than individual pressure. He mentions optional morning skates, mixed emotions of excitement and focus, and not looking too far ahead. He reflects on childhood hockey memories, the pain of watching from the bench due to a knee injury in a previous final, and the difficulty of playing against skilled opponents while injured. He acknowledges the sacrifices of family, coaches, and teammates, highlighting veteran players like Billy Guerin and Gonch who had waited years for a championship. He addresses crowd reactions to injuries and expresses appreciation for Pittsburgh fans' loyalty through difficult years, noting four road series wins and selling out home games for three consecutive years.

This study examined 101 cardiomyopathy patients (43 dilated cardiomyopathy, 58 other cardiomyopathies) and 101 healthy controls to assess relationships between inflammatory markers, oxidative stress, and disease severity. This document outlines the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial comparing dasiglucagon, placebo, and GlucaGen® in patients with type 1 diabetes. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes), analyzed using a stratified log-rank test with 90% power. The study plans to randomize 20 patients to dasiglucagon, 10 to placebo, and 10 to GlucaGen®. Efficacy analyses will use the Full Analysis Set (FAS) with a hierarchical testing procedure for primary and secondary endpoints. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic parameters will be analyzed using non-compartmental methods. Safety analyses will cover adverse events, local tolerability, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity. Meb Faber's Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model Strategy is a simple momentum-based approach investing equally in stocks, bonds, and gold when their monthly 3-bar moving average exceeds the 10-bar moving average. Originally published in 2015 based on Ned Davis Research, the strategy returned 13% annually from 1971 to 2015. Updated backtests using ETFs (GLD, SPY, TLT) from 2006 show 8.9% annual returns with only 18% maximum drawdown, demonstrating defensive characteristics during recessions. Performance weakened to 5.3% annually after 2015, though 2022 showed small losses while stocks declined significantly. The strategy is not curve-fitted, as nearby parameter settings produce similar results. With 1.5x leverage, returns increase to 13.1% with 26% drawdown. The authors emphasize simplicity, patience, and long-term evaluation over ten-year periods.

Soccer passing directions terminology describes the path a ball takes from a passer to a receiver, typically when facing the attacking goal. Clockwise directions include: Forward (ahead, deep, downfield, down the line, long, parallel, short, straight, upfield); Angled Right (corner, diagonal, line, post); Right (centering, flat, lateral, square, wide); Back and Right (angled, diagonal, reverse); Back (behind, straight back); Back and Left (angled, diagonal, reverse); Left (centering, flat, lateral, square, wide); and Angled Left (corner, diagonal, line, post). Additional terms cover angles, back heels, center, posts, horizontal/vertical axes, interfaces, outlets, possession passes, and switching fields.

Phlogopite (KMg3(AlSi3O10)(OH)2), a dark mica mineral with monoclinic layered structure, has low resistance to ionizing radiation and applications in insulation, construction, and radiation-related fields. This study uses the XTANT-3 code, combining tight-binding molecular dynamics, transport Monte Carlo, and Boltzmann collision integral methods, to simulate phlogopite's response to 92 eV photon irradiation. Simulations reveal competing nonthermal and nonadiabatic effects: electron-phonon coupling increases damage thresholds by cooling electrons and preventing nonthermal damage. At ~0.17 eV/atom, hydrogen migration occurs first, matching experimental results (~1000 kGy). At ~0.4 eV/atom, Mg becomes liquid-like while other sublattices remain stable. Complete disorder occurs at ~0.5 eV/atom, bandgap collapse and metallic state at ~0.9 eV/atom, and subpicosecond nonthermal heating at ~2 eV/atom, with selective acceleration of K and O atoms. These findings demonstrate rich transient states in irradiated phlogopite and validate simulation methods for complex materials.

This MIT lecture discusses two major real estate development case studies: Winthrop Center in Boston and 425 Park Avenue in New York City.

The building had 0% pre-leasing at construction start, faced near-collapse when HSBC withdrew financing due to COVID-19 in March 2020, and was salvaged by a Kuwait-based fund. The project ultimately achieved only a 1% cost premium due to experienced execution. Cornell Tech served as an instrumental precedent, with Cornell University taking equity to de-risk that earlier Passive House project. The city of Boston and Massachusetts emerged as major beneficiaries, as the project helped educate regulators and informed BERDO 2.0 and stringent building energy codes incorporating Passive House elements.

Located in prime Park Avenue versus competitors at Hudson Yards and Ground Zero, the developer considered options including enhanced ventilation/filtration ($12.3M initial cost, $3.9M annual operating increase), WELL certification, or Fitwel. The pro forma assumed 5-10% rent premiums based on cognitive studies showing productivity, health insurance, turnover, and absenteeism benefits, though students questioned these assumptions as optimistic given limited 2012 market awareness of indoor air quality. The developer targeted early adopter tenants like Citadel (200,000 sq ft anchor), using HR and CFO engagement strategies rather than traditional facilities managers. The building achieved record NYC rents (~$300/sq ft penthouse) but faced 2020 financial distress due to construction delays from the structural retention, wiping out Japanese LP equity before Blackstone salvaged the project. This lecture covers utility from beliefs and learning biases. People derive anticipatory utility from positive beliefs about the future, which affects information acquisition—individuals may avoid negative information (like Huntington's disease testing) to maintain positive feelings. When people cannot manipulate beliefs, information preferences depend on whether utility from beliefs is concave (information-averse) or convex (information-loving). However, when belief manipulation is possible, people tend toward overoptimism unless: (1) beliefs affect future outcomes requiring action, (2) overoptimism distorts economic decisions, or (3) potential disappointment from unmet expectations reduces utility.

Evidence shows widespread overoptimism: people rate positive future events as more likely for themselves than others, and negative events as less likely. Most drivers and professors consider themselves above average, though MIT students show under-confidence, possibly due to frequent feedback and biased perceptions of "average." Ego utility—feeling good about oneself—also drives inflated self-views. Positive illusions may promote mental health, with "depressive realism" suggesting accurate expectations harm wellbeing.

Factors affecting positive biases include personal importance of traits, availability of objective information (reducing bias), ambiguity of feedback (increasing bias), perceived control, and expertise with good feedback. Lab experiments show asymmetric information processing: people readily accept positive feedback but discount negative feedback, and remember positive signals better over time. Real-world evidence includes overconfident investors trading excessively and losing money, and overconfident managers making value-destroying mergers.

The lecture then addresses Bayesian learning difficulties. While people correctly update beliefs directionally, they struggle with magnitude. Three systematic deviations are: (1) gambler's fallacy—believing independent outcomes "balance out," (2) hot-hand fallacy—over-inferring streaks in unknown distributions, both explained by belief in the "law of small numbers," and (3) base-rate neglect—ignoring prior probabilities when given new information. These biases affect important decisions like judicial rulings and medical test interpretation.

Heuristics like representativeness (using similarity for probability) and availability (using recall ease) speed decisions but cause errors. Understanding why people hold wrong beliefs—attention limits, wrong theories, motivated beliefs, or learning failures—has different policy implications: salience helps for attention problems, but correcting motivated beliefs may reduce wellbeing if people prefer self-deception.

Topological insulator lasers combine topological insulator physics with laser technology to create more efficient, stable devices. Traditional lasers suffer from defects and instability at higher powers, producing unwanted colors and distorted beam profiles. Topological insulators have protected surface states where electrons flow without scattering off defects because changing direction requires spin-flipping, which is energetically difficult. Researchers created analogous photonic systems using rings of optical waveguides arranged so light travels only at edges and cannot scatter without changing color. The protected state light is amplified while unprotected light is scattered away. Experiments showed these lasers remain efficient and stable even with defects or increased power, maintaining single-color output unlike conventional lasers. Such lasers are valuable for applications including 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

This passage documents medical problems reported in clinical trials of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines (BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA). In Phase 1, some participants had temporary lymphocyte count drops 1-3 days after dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, which normalized by 6-8 days. Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, pain) and systemic events (fever, tiredness, headache, chills, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle/joint pain) were common but generally mild/moderate and short-lived. Most medical problems were mild/moderate; fewer than 1% of participants in Phase 2/3 left due to medical problems. Serious medical problems were rare (less than 1%), with researchers believing most were unrelated to the vaccine. In Phase 2/3, 85 participants who received BNT162b2 at study start died, 62 who initially received placebo then later BNT162b2 died, and 23 who received only placebo died—researchers did not attribute deaths to the vaccine. No deaths occurred in Phase 1 or among BNT162b2SA-naïve participants in Phase 3.

This lecture covers neutral particle diagnostics for measuring ion distribution functions in fusion plasmas like tokamaks. Since core ions are confined and fully ionized, direct measurement is impossible. Instead, diagnostics rely on neutrals created in the core through charge exchange—either with edge neutrals or neutral beam injection—that escape to external detectors.

Neutral transport faces re-ionization challenges from electron impact, ion impact, and resonant charge exchange. For typical reactor conditions (10 keV, 10²⁰ m⁻³), neutrals have mean free paths of only ~10 cm, requiring relatively low density for detection.

Passive diagnostics use edge fueling: edge neutrals penetrate inward, charge exchange with core ions, and the resulting core neutrals escape to detectors. A stripping cell re-ionizes them, then magnetic fields energy-separate particles for distribution function measurement. This technique is line-integrated and works best when filtering out cold edge neutral contributions.

Active diagnostics use neutral beams for localization. Charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) makes fully stripped impurities visible by giving them electrons, enabling impurity density, flow velocity, and temperature measurements. Beam emission spectroscopy (BES) measures density fluctuations via collisional excitation of beam neutrals. The motional Stark effect (MSE) uses the electric field (V×B) seen by fast beam neutrals to split spectral lines, enabling magnetic field angle and poloidal field measurements for current profile reconstruction.

In late 2004, Walt Bernstein, Toyota's director of production control at TMMGA, confronted ChassisCo plant manager David McDonald about severe quality and production problems with rear suspension cradles for the Suprima crossover. Despite ChassisCo's Athens plant having dramatically increased automation (from 13 to 102 robots), workforce (quality staff grew from 18 to 90), and responsibilities (sourcing 85 parts versus receiving pre-kitted components), production rates remained at only 60% of target 14 months after launch.

The crisis stemmed from multiple factors: Toyota had granted ChassisCo significantly more responsibility for the 2003 Suprima launch based on successful prior performance, but underestimated capability gaps in project management, supplier oversight, and "tuning" processes. ChassisCo's internal decentralization in 2000 had dispersed experienced personnel, while concurrent global launches stretched engineering resources thin. The company lacked systems for tracking parts, stage-gate processes, and defect feedback mechanisms. Aggressive cost targets led to accepting low bids from unqualified suppliers and inadequate logistics planning. Toyota's delayed recognition of second-tier supplier problems and engineering team rotation further compounded issues.

By November 2004, defect rates had quintupled, welding process audits scored 13%, and the plant risked a downward spiral of burnout and quality failures, prompting Bernstein to seek breakthrough solutions beyond standard Toyota Production System interventions.

Radiotheranostics enables personalized cancer treatment through agents that bind to biological targets for simultaneous diagnosis and therapy. Current radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs) use standardized regimens despite interindividual variability in pharmacokinetics, tumor burden, and radiobiological sensitivity. Computational nuclear oncology (CNO) proposes theranostic digital twins (TDTs) using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models, which incorporate patient physiology and drug characteristics to estimate absorbed doses and clinical responses. PBPK models comprise computational, anatomical-physiological, and radiopharmaceutical frameworks, and can be developed through bottom-up, top-down, or middle-out approaches. Verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ) are essential for clinical translation. Verification ensures correct model implementation; validation confirms reliable description of patient biokinetics through goodness-of-fit assessment, model selection, sensitivity analysis, and prediction evaluation; uncertainty quantification characterizes precision and accuracy of predictions. TDTs extend PBPK models through bi-directional feedback between physical patients and virtual representations, enabling real-time data integration and adaptive treatment planning. However, TDTs present unique VVUQ challenges due to dynamic, continuously updated inputs. While PBPK models are established in pharmaceuticals, regulatory standards for radiopharmaceutical applications remain undefined, necessitating fit-for-purpose VVUQ frameworks to support clinical translation.

This paper proposes a theory-driven framework for evaluating and advancing large language models' (LLMs) persuasive capabilities, grounded in Bayesian persuasion theory. The authors conceptualize LLMs' persuasion as strategic information revelation between a Sender (persuader) and Receiver (decision-maker), both implemented as LLMs. They construct evaluation environments using repurposed human persuasion datasets and validate their design with a 45-participant human study. Experiments with frontier models show that stronger models like DeepSeek-R1 achieve higher persuasion gains and exhibit more sophisticated behaviors such as adaptive information revelation. The authors also demonstrate that reinforcement learning can train even small LLMs (Llama3.2-3B-Instruct) to achieve persuasion capabilities comparable to larger models, with improvements transferring across different Receiver architectures. Key contributions include: (1) a principled measurement framework based on persuasion gains and conditional mutual information of signals, (2) concrete benchmark environments for strategic persuasion, and (3) empirical evidence that LLM persuasive capabilities can be improved at scale via reinforcement learning.

The "Clock" is a simple, teachable basketball zone offense combining freelance passing with rotation rules, effective against person-to-person and zone defenses. The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces real-time ray tracing, AI acceleration, and hybrid rendering. The flagship TU102 GPU features six Graphics Processing Clusters, 36 Texture Processing Clusters, and 72 Streaming Multiprocessors, with each SM containing 64 CUDA Cores, eight Tensor Cores, and one RT Core for ray tracing acceleration. Turing implements concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, unified memory architecture, and GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling rates. The architecture includes second-generation NVLink for multi-GPU connectivity, Variable Rate Shading for optimized rendering, Texture Space Shading for decoupled visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass. Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision for AI inference, enabling features like Deep Learning Super-Sampling. The TU104 and TU106 GPUs scale down the TU102 architecture for different market segments, with TU104 used in products like the GeForce RTX 2080 and Tesla T4, while TU106 powers the GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink support.

Jordan Cowman of Baker & McKenzie's Global Labour, Employment & Employee Benefits Practice Group sent the October 15, 2001 Global Employment Law Alert to Sam Barganier. The Alert provides updates on employment law developments worldwide, organized into six regional sections: Global, Asia Pacific, Europe & CIS, Africa/Middle East, South America, and North America. Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 31, 2016, reporting that its subsidiaries Tesla Finance LLC and Tesla 2014 Warehouse SPV LLC entered into a $300 million Loan and Security Agreement with Deutsche Bank AG to support Tesla's direct vehicle leasing program. The Warehouse Agreement has a draw period ending August 31, 2017, with full repayment due September 20, 2018. Borrowings bear interest at approximately 2.0% based on LIBOR plus margin. NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame using fifth-generation Tensor Cores and enhanced Flip Metering for improved frame pacing. DLSS 4 transitions from CNN to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, delivering better temporal stability, reduced ghosting, and enhanced detail. Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting technologies like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (3x memory savings), Neural Radiance Cache for global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI. The architecture comprises GB202 (flagship, 92.2B transistors), GB203 (high-end, 45.6B transistors), and GB205 (performance, 31B transistors) GPUs, powering the GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 respectively.

This patent application describes a variable multiplexer system for vehicle communication bus compatibility. Modern vehicles use standardized data link connectors (e.g., 16-pin OBD ports) for CAN bus communication, but pinout configurations vary by manufacturer. The disclosed external device includes a programmable variable multiplexer that can be electronically configured to match different vehicle pinout configurations, eliminating the need for multiple cables. The device determines the correct pinout configuration through two methods: querying a remote computing system using a vehicle identifier (e.g., VIN) from a vehicle data index, or analyzing communication bus data through a listening mode that compares received signals against known configurations and uses checksum validation. The system includes components for connection detection, pinout determination, and multiplexer configuration.

The passage defines equality as a moral and social ideal shaped by historical discussions, with modern interpretations including equality of opportunity, political, racial, social, economic, and gender equality. Equality of opportunity refers to providing all individuals fair chances to access advantageous positions regardless of origin. Education is described as a continuous process that develops individuals' skills and socializes them according to societal rules. Equality of opportunity in education emerged in 18th-century Prussia and involves providing equal access to educational services without discrimination. Five factors affect educational equality: economic, geographical, political, individual, and social factors. In Turkey, the Ministry of National Education shapes education policies, with equal opportunity challenges including inadequate schools, economic difficulties, insufficient equipment, and cultural barriers. The conclusion emphasizes that equal educational opportunity requires child-centered approaches, measuring abilities independently of family background, improving education quality and access, ensuring teacher quality, and making all schools equally qualified through scientific planning.

Bad Bunny's selection as Super Bowl LX halftime show headliner has sparked backlash from MAGA influencers and right-wing figures who criticize his Spanish-language music, anti-Trump stance, and activism against ICE raids. Patterns enable reusable components in software development, with distributed systems requiring specific design approaches. Single-node patterns using container groups (pods) include the sidecar pattern (augmenting applications), ambassador pattern (brokering external communications), and adapter pattern (standardizing interfaces). Multi-node patterns address distributed system challenges through microservices architectures, replicated load-balanced services for stateless applications, and sharded services for stateful applications with large data requirements. Sharded services use functions to route requests to appropriate shards, with considerations for caching, replication, and key selection based on request characteristics.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces significant advancements across multiple areas. The SM architecture unifies INT32 and FP32 cores, doubling integer operation throughput for many instructions. Texture units increased from 512 (RTX 4090) to 680 (RTX 5090), with bilinear-filtered texel rates reaching 1636.76 Gigatexels/sec. GDDR7 memory uses PAM3 signaling, delivering 1.792 TB/sec bandwidth (RTX 5090) with built-in ECC and EDR support.

Fifth-generation Tensor Cores add FP4 and FP6 support, enabling models like FLUX.dev to run with less than 10GB VRAM versus 23GB at FP16. Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and introduce Mega Geometry with Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) for efficient LOD management. New Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) provide hardware-accelerated hair rendering. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 improves efficiency with twice-as-fast reorder logic.

The AI Management Processor (AMP) offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU using a dedicated RISC-V processor. Video capabilities expand with 4:2:2 chroma format support, ninth-generation NVENC with 5% quality improvements, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. Max-Q power efficiency features advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and 10x faster sleep state entry.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to 3 additional frames per rendered frame) and transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability and detail. Neural shaders enable RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM savings), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The GB202 flagship GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors with 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores. GB203 (45.6 billion transistors) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 (31 billion transistors) targets the performance segment with the RTX 5070.

Enron faces financial turmoil as its stock price plummeted from over $80 to $19.79, with shares dropping more than 40% in one week. The Reverse Action Offense, developed by Hall of Fame Coach Pete Newell in the late 1950s, features guard-around continuity with precise execution and footwork. Its signature element is the weakside wing's rub cut off a post screen to the basket. The offense includes strong post-up options, two-player guard isolation, and counters against defensive overplay. Basic continuity involves entry passes to wings, guard-around cuts to corners, rub cuts off post screens, and reversal passes. Success requires patience, proper footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication between passer, screener, and receiver. Multiple entry options exist including weakside, strongside, dribble clear, and back door entries. The offense incorporates sideline triangle action, post isolation, and various counters based on defensive positioning such as over-the-top cuts, baseline cuts, screener pops, and dives. Guard-around action creates two-player games with reads for drives, pull-up jumpers, and rolls. Post play includes options against high-side, baseline-side, behind, fronting, and double-team defenses. Back cuts counter overplays, with special end-of-period options like weakside screen-and-roll, double screens, and back screen lobs.

A defensive wall in soccer is a shoulder-to-shoulder formation of defenders positioned approximately 10 yards from a free kick to block half the goal, giving the goalkeeper more reaction time to cover the remaining area. The goalkeeper decides when to build a wall based on ball location and distance from goal, typically calling for 2-5+ players. The "Anchor" or first player positions on an imaginary line from the near post to the ball, then adjusts based on goalkeeper or designated "Wall Setter" directions. Walls become important around age 12 when players develop accurate shooting skills. Under Law 13, defenders must stay 10 yards back until the ball is kicked, though referees aren't required to allow time for wall construction. Attackers must remain 1 meter from walls of three or more defenders. Quick free kicks bypass wall setup, while ceremonial free kicks allow referees to mark distances with vanishing spray. For indirect free kicks within 10 yards of goal, defenders stand on the goal line between posts.

This email from Nikita Varma dated November 19, 2001, contains newsclips from November 14-18, 2001, regarding the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) crisis. Key developments include: Indian financial institutions led by IDBI setting a $700 million reserve price for DPC's sale to prospective bidders Tata Power and BSES, who initially offered only $400 million; both companies beginning due diligence after signing confidentiality agreements; the Singapore meeting discussing incentives including reduced tariffs, MAT exemption, mega power status, and separation of LNG facilities from the power project; bidders demanding distribution rights for 1,500 MW power in Maharashtra; MSEB refusing to attend the November 19 DPC board meeting in Houston following a Bombay High Court order restraining DPC from issuing final termination notices; the court also restraining the government from encashing DPC guarantees; and ongoing arbitration proceedings in London scheduled for November 24 regarding MSEB's non-payment of Rs 102 crore December bill. The newsclips also cover Enron's accounting scandal and Arthur Andersen's audit failures, as well as the Oman government bailing out the LNG Laxmi tanker project by acquiring 50% equity in Greenfield Shipping Company after ANZ Investment Bank declared an event of default.

The reverse play in football deceives defenses by running the ball in one direction before handing it to a player moving the opposite way. A traditional reverse involves the quarterback handing off to a running back or wide receiver, who then tosses it to another receiver crossing in the opposite direction. Success depends on proper disguise and offensive linemen forming a "seal" to block pursuing defenders. Variations include the fake reverse, where the quarterback keeps the ball after faking handoffs; the reverse screen, where the ball returns to the quarterback who throws to the original ball carrier behind a wall of blockers; and the reverse pass, where the quarterback becomes a receiving option after handing off.

Green Bay Packers cornerback Damarious Randall is having a strong offseason, with coach Mike McCarthy praising his performance at the nickel position. Randall is attempting to rebound from an injury-plagued and inconsistent second season, which was complicated by Sam Shields' season-ending injury. The Packers added cornerback depth with Davon House and Kevin King, but Randall's return to form remains important. The passage examines technology trends in industrial development and manufacturing, focusing on data visualization, digital twins, and high-performance computing (HPC). Data visualization and engineering workstations as a service enable collaborative design through cloud-based access to common data pools. Digital twins allow detailed digital mapping of processes, plants, and products for monitoring, analysis, and simulation, supporting new business models like "Product as a Service."

Most enterprises (87%) prefer external HPC infrastructures, with only 6% operating on-premises datacenters.

Charles W. Parker, administrator of Melvin Douglas's estate, appealed a district court ruling that Farmway Credit Union could exhaust its security interest in Douglas's personal property after his death without filing a claim in estate proceedings or foreclosing in district court. Douglas had defaulted on $111,290.17 owed to Farmway, secured by farm machinery, crops, livestock, and real estate. Before Douglas's death, he and his wife orally agreed with Farmway to sell the collateral at public sale; his heirs continued this agreement after his death. The administrator, appointed May 17, 1984, took no action to stop Farmway's sale of equipment, wheat harvest, or cattle sale before filing for declaratory judgment on July 5, 1984. The district court granted Farmway summary judgment on August 14, 1984, finding no conflict between the administrator's possession rights under K.S.A. 59-1401 and Farmway's self-help repossession rights under K.S.A. 84-9-503. The appellate court affirmed, holding that Farmway's contractual right to exhaust security was unaffected by Douglas's death, citing *In re Estate of Dahn* (1970), and that summary judgment was proper given uncontroverted facts with no need for further discovery.

The Counter play is a football run scheme that creates the illusion of Power in one direction before blocking for the runner to go the opposite way, with the backside Guard pulling to kick out an edge defender and the Fullback inserting to block an Inside Linebacker. Its main strength is exploiting over-aggressive defenses that pursue the fake, while its weakness is slower development that leaves it vulnerable to defensive penetration and spill techniques. The passage details specific assignments for Counter Trey against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, covering all offensive positions, and describes two variations: Singleback GT Counter (where the backside Tackle replaces the Fullback as the insert blocker) and Gun Split GT Counter Triple Option (which adds triple option reads for athletic quarterbacks).

This paper develops a mathematical framework for investigating cubic-tetragonal (C-T) phase coexistence in ferroelectric materials using high-resolution X-ray diffraction. The authors extend the Wechsler-Lieberman-Read (WLR) crystallographic theory and "adaptive state" (AS) concept to model mismatch-free connections between coexisting cubic and tetragonal phases through periodic assemblages of tetragonal domains, without requiring domain miniaturization.

The framework catalogs 24 variants of C-AS-T coexistence, deriving analytical expressions for orientation relationships between real and reciprocal lattices, habit plane indices, and predicted Bragg peak splittings in 3D reciprocal space. The model assumes large enough tetragonal domains to diffract independently while maintaining orientation relationships imposed by phase coexistence.

Experimental validation using high-resolution reciprocal space mapping of PMN-35PT single crystals at the C-T phase transition (approximately 435 K) demonstrates strong agreement between predicted and observed Bragg peak separations. The results support the formation of AS-like states without domain miniaturization, with estimated domain sizes of several hundred nanometers based on peak widths. The methodology enables analysis of multi-length-scale phenomena in bulk ferroelectric materials using non-destructive synchrotron X-ray diffraction techniques.

BA.2.86 (Pirola), a SARS-CoV-2 lineage first detected in Denmark in July 2023, harbors over 30 spike protein mutations relative to BA.2, including 13 in the N-terminal domain (NTD), 14 in the receptor-binding domain (RBD), and 7 in the S1/S2 and S2 domains. Its descendant JN.1 is becoming globally dominant. Using a reverse mutational scanning approach with 33 reversion mutants on the BA.2.86 background, researchers tested serum from 30 healthcare workers before and after BNT162b2 XBB.1.5 vaccination. Before vaccination, BA.2.86 and JN.1 showed 40-fold and 80-fold reduced neutralization, respectively, compared to wild-type. After vaccination, neutralization improved substantially for both. Key mutations contributing to immune escape were identified: ins16MPLF, K356T, N460K, V483Δ, A484K, F486P, and S621P. After XBB.1.5 vaccination, removing the MPLF insertion at position 16, reinserting Y144, and reversions K544E, S621P, and K484A improved neutralization to BA.2 levels. The study demonstrates that reverse mutational scanning can identify immune escape epitopes in polyclonal responses and shows the XBB.1.5 vaccine effectively boosts neutralization against BA.2.86 and JN.1.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed a judgment confirming a local improvement assessment roll for the City of South Bend. This study investigated 90 UAE elementary mathematics teachers' perspectives on distance education (DE) during COVID-19. Conducted in spring 2021 using a quantitative questionnaire, it examined teachers' views on instructing mathematics through DE, challenges faced, and future preferences.

Results showed teachers held generally positive perceptions about their ability to use digital technologies and adapt lessons for online teaching, though they doubted DE's suitability for elementary students over face-to-face instruction. Key obstacles included increased preparation time, stress, and concerns about student motivation and achievement. While 87.8% reported adequate administrative support and 85.6% received sufficient training, 76.7% still preferred face-to-face teaching in the future.

The study found no significant differences in perceptions based on educational level, gender, or years of experience, though graduate-level teachers reported fewer obstacles. Teachers noted that online instruction required more effort than traditional methods, including converting content to digital formats. Despite challenges, 64.4% enjoyed teaching mathematics online.

The research concludes that while teachers developed confidence with digital tools during the pandemic, successful DE implementation requires comprehensive professional development, robust support systems, and strategies to enhance student engagement. The authors recommend exploring hybrid models and further research on student perspectives and long-term DE impacts.

This document defines the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP virtualization technologies, which protect guest register state from hypervisors by encrypting it during world switches. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted memory area that mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, enabling standardized communication between guest OS and hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement, SEV-SNP support, XSS MSR values, and restricted APIC emulation. Subsequent revisions add APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page state change notifications, VLEK certificate GUID, expanded error handling, and EFI protocol documentation. The protocol standardizes minimum guest state exposure, NMI handling, SMP booting, and various VMGEXIT operations including I/O protection, MSR access, MMIO, SNP guest requests, AP creation, and termination requests.

MITOCW lecture on Langmuir probes by Jack Hare covering sheath theory, probe operation, and measurement techniques. Langmuir probes are simple metal conductors inserted into plasma to measure potential and current. When immersed in plasma, electrons strike the probe faster than ions due to mass differences, making the probe negatively charged until reaching floating potential (Vf), distinct from plasma potential (Vp). The current-voltage characteristic shows electron saturation current, ion saturation current, and three operational regimes. Sheath theory, using the Debye length as the characteristic scale, links probe surface measurements to bulk plasma properties. Under cold ion approximation, the ion saturation current depends on electron temperature and ion mass, while electron current follows a Boltzmann distribution. Practical single probe operation near floating potential uses the slope of ln(I - Iis) versus V0 to determine electron temperature, then ion saturation current for density. Double probes bias two probes relative to each other, limiting current to ion saturation for safety. Triple probes add a floating probe to measure three points on the IV curve simultaneously, enabling fast time resolution without voltage sweeping. Magnetic fields and collisions complicate sheath theory by altering particle orbits and requiring modified flux calculations.

The Denver Broncos ended a 37-game streak without a 100-yard rusher during their 28-3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football, evening their record at 2-2. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July (+7.8% YTD), with US large-cap stocks ranking third monthly but mid-table year-to-date. Frontier Markets led monthly returns.
