A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found over 25% of U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support, significantly affecting job satisfaction. Two-thirds reported shortages of teaching assistants, aides, or paraprofessionals, while 62% cited insufficient mental health resources or special educators. Teachers with adequate resources showed 77% job satisfaction versus 44% without. Equipment gaps included classroom furniture (24%), laptops/computers (25%), and printing supplies (35%). One-third found material ordering processes difficult. Wealthier and low-income schools reported similar furniture shortages, but low-income schools faced greater technology deficits. Teachers valued collaborative planning and peer observation for professional development, though only one-third had observation opportunities. The survey included 6,202 teachers from October 2024 to May 2025.

This study presents the Patient Report Template (PRT), a structured clinical decision support tool designed to improve nursing handoffs and reduce EHR documentation burden. The PRT integrates established handoff methods (SBAR, I PASS the BATON) with nine sections: Patient Profile, Review of Systems, Situation, Safety, Background, Actions, Timing, Ownership, and Next. A survey of 106 University of Iowa Health Care nurses evaluated the PRT's perceived usefulness and attitudes toward AI integration. Nurses rated most PRT components as useful, with Patient Profile (highest: Name 4.42, Code Status 4.38), Safety (Allergies 4.36), and Actions (Signs to Elevate 4.17) scoring highest. Lower ratings occurred for Level of Uncertainty (3.25), Family History (3.36), and Rationale (3.71). Nurses reported low comfort (mean 2.38) and trust (mean 2.50) with AI, but moderate expected utility (mean 3.0). Respondents were diverse across departments (Pediatrics 18%, Obstetrics/Gynecology 10%, Internal Medicine 9%), experience levels (54% with 0-10 years), and age groups (44% Young Adult, 46% Adult). The study identifies a pathway for further usability and accuracy testing of AI-integrated clinical reports.

The turn of the month trading strategy involves going long at the close on the fifth last trading day of the month and exiting at the close of the third trading day of the next month, resulting in approximately 33% market exposure. The strategy extends the traditional end-of-month effect (also called the Ultimo Effect) to include the first three days of the new month. Backtesting since 1960 shows strong performance in the S&P 500 with a 7.1% CAGR and lower drawdowns than buy-and-hold. The effect has been tested across multiple markets and sectors including emerging markets, healthcare, gold mining stocks, high yield funds, real estate, consumer staples, Brazil, Japan, Bitcoin, commodities, utilities, energy, technology, and Indian stocks, with varying results. The last calendar day of the month performs better than the last trading day. The strategy's persistence is attributed to structural forces such as capital inflows from savers and fund rebalancing. Python and Amibroker code for implementation is referenced but not fully provided.

Logging systems vary widely in format and output method, creating challenges for containerized applications that typically expect stdout logging. The adapter pattern addresses this by using separate containers to redirect file logs to stdout and transform heterogeneous formats into unified structured representations for log aggregators. This approach is preferable to modifying third-party application containers, as it avoids maintenance burdens and enables reuse across different applications.

A peer quarterly financial comparison of eight major oil companies (Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Royal Dutch Shell, BP, Statoil, Total, ENI, and ConocoPhillips) indicates they can sustain profitable margins at roughly $50/bbl. Aggregate revenues bottomed in 2016 and are rising due to higher oil prices and increased production. Oil production grew 5.3% from 2Q 2015 to 2Q 2017, while natural gas production increased 9.7%. Margins and return on sales have improved significantly, with Chevron and Statoil showing the most dramatic improvement. Capital spending decreased 32% from 2Q 2015 to 2Q 2016 and 14% in 2Q 2017, lifting net operating cash flows. Global oil supply and demand are rebalancing as inventory levels decline. The author expects positive trends to continue through 2018.

The Imperial and Royal Government, through diplomatic channels, transmits Germany's response to the Allied rejection of its December 12 peace proposal. Germany protests the Allies' characterization of the proposal as insincere, defending its motives and accusing its adversaries of hypocrisy regarding self-determination and international law violations. The passage introduces PATCH (PA–TC–H), a network growth model combining preferential attachment, triadic closure, and homophily to study visibility inequalities in social networks. The model extends the Barabási-Albert framework by allowing different mechanisms for global versus triadic closure links. Key findings show that homophily drives network segregation and inequity between majority and minority groups, while preferential attachment increases degree inequality. Triadic closure moderates segregation and inequity only when unbiased; when biased by homophily or preferential attachment, it can exacerbate inequalities. Applying likelihood-free inference to three empirical scientific networks (APS collaborations, APS citations, DBLP collaborations), the study finds that observed gender inequalities are best explained by a model where both global and triadic closure links are biased by preferential attachment and moderate gender homophily. The results suggest that mitigating network inequalities requires simultaneously addressing all three mechanisms, as isolating one can produce unintended consequences.

The DAT bus line is high when idle. Data blocks begin with start bits (1-4 bits LOW), contain payload data with optional error correction, and end with end bits (1-4 bits HIGH). Transmission is clock-synchronous, with 1-4 bit CRC protection. Power interruption during reads does not destroy data, though write/erase operations are vulnerable. Read commands are rejected if BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR occurs. Block reads use 512-byte maximum blocks; smaller blocks must fit within 512-byte boundaries. CMD16 sets block length up to 512 bytes. CMD17 reads a single block; CMD18 reads multiple consecutive blocks until CMD12 stops transmission. When reading the last user area block with CMD18, OUT_OF_RANGE errors should be ignored. Block misalignment is detected at the first misaligned block if accumulated partial block lengths are not block-aligned.

Researchers have identified microscopic structures that explain why dandelion seeds selectively detach with upward wind gusts but resist downward forces. The seeds connect to the parent plant via an off-center tether surrounded by a horseshoe-shaped barrier that is lower on one side. When wind pushes seeds toward this opening, they release easily; when pushed the opposite direction, the taller barrier helps them hold on. Measurements showed releasing upslanting seeds requires ten times less force than downward plucking. This structural quirk, reported September 10, allows dandelions to maximize chances of seeds catching favorable upward air currents rather than doomed downward flights.

Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease (MAFLD), formerly non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, affects 32.4% globally and is the commonest liver disease. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a major MAFLD risk factor, with 55.5% prevalence among T2D patients worldwide versus 32.4% in the general population. T2D patients with MAFLD face doubled risk of advanced liver disease, elevated cardiovascular disease risk, and nearly tripled chronic kidney disease risk, plus higher liver-related mortality. Clinical guidelines recommend diabetes screening for MAFLD, but African evidence is limited—only four studies contributed to the estimated 30.4% prevalence among African T2D patients as of 2018. With African diabetes cases projected to increase 134% by 2024, comprehensive research is urgently needed.

This systematic review and meta-analysis, registered on PROSPERO (CRD42023491271) and following PRISMA guidelines, aimed to determine MAFLD prevalence and its association with glycemic control (HbA1c) in African T2D patients. The search covered PubMed, Medline, Embase, Scopus, Global Health, Web of Science, African Index Medicus, and African Journals Online through December 6, 2023, plus reference lists. Inclusion criteria were: observational studies, T2D patients, African countries, calculable MAFLD prevalence, adults ≥18 years, and English publication. Studies with unclear MAFLD diagnostic methods were excluded.

Two independent reviewers conducted screening and data extraction, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Quality assessment used the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for prevalence studies. Data analysis included logit transformation of prevalence data, DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis, and pooling of correlation coefficients for MAFLD-HbA1c association, with heterogeneity assessed via I² statistic and publication bias via Egger's test.

From 659 references, 232 articles were screened after duplicate removal, yielding 29 full-text reviews and 10 included studies. These comprised nine cross-sectional and one case-control study from 2011-2023 across six African countries (Nigeria n=3, Ethiopia n=2, Morocco n=2, Egypt, Ghana, and Sudan n=1 each). The 1,667 total T2D participants had mean age above 50 years, diabetes duration 4-10 years, majority overweight/obese (BMI >25 kg/m²), and poor glycemic control (HbA1c >7%). MAFLD diagnosis was primarily by ultrasonography.

Drug addiction poses a serious public health threat, with over 100,000 overdose deaths in 2022, primarily from opioids. Treatment dropout rates average 30% across substances and reach 91% for opioid addiction. Self-report measures, commonly used to assess addiction severity, suffer from reporting biases and social desirability effects. Objective cognitive-behavioral measures targeting drug-biased processing—such as picture-viewing choice tasks and verbal fluency tasks—may better predict clinical outcomes. This study tested whether these drug-bias markers outperform traditional measures in predicting 4-month treatment adherence in 59 inpatients with opioid use disorder (iOUD), compared to 29 healthy controls. Participants received comprehensive residential treatment including relapse prevention, anger management, and Seeking Safety therapy.

This study used 7 tesla magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) to examine brain metabolite levels in people with psychotic psychopathology (PwPP; n=64), first-degree biological relatives (n=42), and healthy controls (n=43). Participants were scanned in mid-occipital and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex volumes of interest. Among six metabolites examined a priori, N-acetyl-aspartate (NAA) was significantly lower in occipital cortex in both PwPP and relatives versus controls, while N-acetyl-aspartylglutamate (NAAG) was lower in prefrontal cortex in PwPP versus controls and relatives. Post hoc analyses revealed significantly higher glucose levels in prefrontal cortex in PwPP versus controls, with relatives showing intermediate values. Hierarchical clustering showed glucose levels clustered with psychiatric symptoms and visual task performance measures. A subset of participants completed repeat scans; metabolite measurements showed fair to excellent reliability across time. The findings suggest metabolic dysfunction in psychosis, with higher brain glucose and lower NAA potentially reflecting reduced glucose utilization, and lower NAA in relatives indicating possible genetic liability effects.

The TLV321x and TLV322x are families of 5V single, dual, and quad channel high-speed comparators with 40ns propagation delay and 40μA quiescent current per channel. Both families include rail-to-rail inputs extending 200mV beyond supply rails, 1.8mV internal hysteresis, Power-on Reset (POR) circuitry, and operate from 1.8V to 5.5V across -40°C to 125°C. Applications include current sensing and zero-cross detection.

The Z-transform is introduced as a generalization of the discrete-time Fourier transform to address convergence issues. The Fourier transform converges only for absolutely summable sequences, where the sum of absolute values is finite. The Z-transform multiplies sequences by a decaying exponential r^(-n) to achieve convergence, defined as X(z) = Σx[n]z^(-n) where z = re^(jω). It equals the Fourier transform when |z| = 1 (the unit circle).

Key properties include: the region of convergence (ROC) is bounded by poles and never contains them; finite-length sequences have ROC as the entire z-plane (possibly excluding 0 or ∞); right-sided sequences have ROC outside the outermost pole; left-sided sequences have ROC inside the innermost pole; and two-sided sequences have ROC between two poles. A stable system has ROC including the unit circle; a causal system has ROC outside the outermost pole. The Z-transform of exponential sequences yields rational functions (ratios of polynomials), characterized by poles and zeros in the z-plane.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the INS's reinstatement of Alejandro Mendez Suarez's 1996 deportation order under 8 U.S.C. § 1231(a)(5). Mendez, a Mexican citizen, was deported in 1996 after using counterfeit documents, illegally reentered in 1999, and was arrested in Colorado in 2002. The court held: (1) the district court properly transferred his habeas petition to the court of appeals under 28 U.S.C. § 1631; (2) the INS was not required to consider bond violations or pending criminal charges when reinstating the order; (3) § 1231(a)(5) applied without retroactivity concerns because his unlawful reentry occurred after IIRIRA's effective date; (4) he was ineligible for LIFE Act adjustment of status due to prior misrepresentation; and (5) any due process violation in reinstatement procedures caused no prejudice as he conceded key facts establishing proper reinstatement. The court lacked jurisdiction to review the underlying 1996 deportation order.

Ashby Fields Primary School in Daventry is consulting on closing early at 1:15pm on Fridays to improve teachers' work-life balance. The proposal would reduce weekly hours from 27.5 to 25.5. Parent Kelly Holmes opposes the plan, citing limited paid spaces at the on-site childcare and concerns about lost education time. The school cites national teacher recruitment and retention problems due to 60-hour work weeks. Governors will review parent feedback on April 25 before deciding whether to formally propose the change to the InMat Trust Board.

This study estimates the direct healthcare economic burden of mental health disorders associated with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in the United States. PCOS affects 5-15% of reproductive-aged women and is associated with increased risks of anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder. The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining relationships between PCOS and mental health disorders, then calculated related economic costs.

From 25 included studies, meta-analyses found women with PCOS had significantly higher prevalence of anxiety (PR: 1.42), depression (PR: 1.65), and eating disorders (PR: 1.48) compared to controls, though postpartum depression was not significantly associated. Excess annual healthcare costs in 2021 USD were estimated at $1.94 billion for anxiety, $1.68 billion for depression, and $644 million for eating disorders, totaling over $4.26 billion annually. Combined with prior estimates, total PCOS economic burden exceeds $15 billion annually, with mental health disorders accounting for approximately 28%. The authors note PCOS is globally prevalent with at least 125 million affected women worldwide, suggesting enormous worldwide economic impact, and call for improved detection, clinical awareness, and increased research investment.

A Chinese math problem given to 11-year-old students asking "If a ship had 26 sheep and 10 goats onboard, how old is the ship's captain?" has gone viral for being intentionally unsolvable. The Shunqing Education Department confirmed there was no answer, stating the purpose was to encourage creative thinking rather than standardized responses. Students provided various answers, including one claiming the captain was 36 and narcissistic, while adults attempted solutions based on Chinese boating license requirements. President Theodore Roosevelt proclaims September 19, 1901, as a national day of mourning and prayer following the assassination of President William McKinley, urging Americans to gather in worship to honor McKinley's memory and submit to God's will.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated May 16, 2001, contains news clippings about Enron and energy-related topics. Resource Generation (RG) is a 20-year-old nonprofit that works with approximately 500 wealthy millennials (ages 18-35, in America's top 10% by wealth) to encourage them to give money to groups fighting social, economic, and racial injustice. The organization uses "money stories" to help members openly discuss their wealth, understand its origins and connection to inequality, and redirect it to grassroots movements. RG emphasizes that those most affected by injustice should decide how money is spent, distinguishing its approach from traditional philanthropy, which it views as allowing continued wealth accumulation. Members report significantly increased giving after joining: for example, Adam Roberts increased annual donations from under $200 to over $50,000, and Hanna Mahon shifted her family foundation's giving to $1 million annually for social justice organizations led by people of color. RG operates amid stark U.S. wealth inequality, with the top 1% seeing sevenfold wealth growth from 1963-2016 while the bottom 10% went from zero wealth to $1,000 in debt, and with an estimated $30 trillion in baby boomer inheritances approaching.

Since 1976, Druze education in Israel has operated as an autonomous system separate from Arab education, established to preserve Druze heritage and foster Israeli-Druze identity and state loyalty. The Israeli Ministry of Education’s Unit for Druze Education and Culture developed unique curricula emphasizing Druze heritage while maintaining standard core subjects. A study examining this separation’s effects on student achievements conducted semi-structured interviews with nine Druze principals, supervisors, and trainee principals. The research found that Druze students currently achieve approximately 89% eligibility for matriculation certificates, surpassing the Arab and Bedouin sectors. Interviewees attributed these high achievements primarily to investment in quality teaching staff, sociocultural modernization—particularly regarding women’s education—and a strong community desire to excel. Opinions were divided regarding the separation’s direct impact: some viewed it as enabling focused resources and professional guidance that accelerated development, while others argued that achievements stemmed from internal societal changes rather than separation, which some criticized as a state tool for “reeducating” the community. Despite high matriculation rates, the study identified a significant gap in academic preparedness for higher education, with principals noting insufficient school resources to adequately prepare students for university integration and success.

The government urges public trust in its handling of a bird flu outbreak in San Luis, Pampanga, assuring swift control through Agriculture and Health department coordination. Agriculture Secretary Manny Piñol states the H5 virus is not transmissible to humans, though samples are being tested for H5N6; results expected in 12 days. A Luzon-wide fowl shipment ban is precautionary. Health Assistant Secretary Eric Tayag emphasizes safety measures, noting human infection is remote and properly cooked chicken is safe. Epidemiologists monitor farm workers for symptoms.

This study evaluated COVID-19 testing and isolation strategies for winter 2022/2023 in France, Belgium, and Italy using survey data from 4,594 participants and mathematical modeling. Survey results showed high adherence to testing if symptomatic (91-97%) and isolation if symptomatic (88-96%), but lower willingness for additional booster doses in France (72.5% of elderly) compared to Belgium (93.9%) and Italy (86.4%). Modeling predicted that current protocols would reduce community transmission by 17-18% in France and Belgium, and 24% in Italy, though none would reduce the effective reproductive number below 1. The Italian protocol's longer isolation period increased effectiveness but at higher social cost. Simpler guidelines like Belgium's fixed-duration isolation without exit tests would reduce testing resources by 30% while maintaining similar effectiveness. Introducing costs for tests (up to 20 Euros) would reduce adherence and protocol effectiveness by approximately 60%. Achieving high booster coverage remains essential for controlling the winter wave.

Two Motley Fool contributors debate Alcoa's investment potential. Rich Duprey argues Alcoa is a buy due to expected growth in bauxite production, new supply contracts worth nearly $600 million, and potential to double EBITDA to $2.2 million. An email from Miyung Buster dated March 19, 2001, distributed to numerous Enron and external recipients, containing summaries of news articles about California's energy crisis. Vienna topped Mercer's quality of life survey for the ninth consecutive year while Baghdad ranked last among 231 cities. Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017, reporting total revenues of $2.70 billion, up from $1.15 billion in Q1 2016. A professor discusses corporate sustainability strategy with students, focusing on Porter's framework for strategic CSR. The lecture covers why common CSR justifications—moral obligation, license to operate, reputation, and sustainability—are insufficient for driving lasting organizational change. Porter advocates instead for integrating social impact into core business strategy through three categories: generic social impacts (basic compliance), value chain social impacts (mitigating operational risks), and social dimensions of competitive context (strategic opportunities). The professor emphasizes that companies must say "no" to peripheral issues and focus resources where they can create competitive advantage, using examples like Whole Foods, Siemens, and Toyota. Key implementation challenges include measuring environmental performance, connecting metrics to business operations, setting credible targets with incentives, and working with suppliers—typically starting with tier one and expanding based on where impacts lie. The discussion highlights that most emissions occur outside company boundaries, making supply chain engagement critical, though depth of engagement should align with strategic priorities and business impacts.

Erik Demaine introduces a class on geometric folding algorithms, covering the mathematics and algorithms behind folding and unfolding geometric objects. The course examines three main structures: linkages (one-dimensional objects like robotic arms), paper (two-dimensional origami), and polyhedra (three-dimensional objects). Two fundamental question types are foldability (determining how given structures fold) and design (creating folding structures to achieve specific goals). Results fall into three categories: universality (everything can be folded), decision algorithms (distinguishing foldable from unfoldable), and hardness results (computationally intractable problems).

Applications include robotics, computer graphics, manufacturing, medical devices, aerospace, biology, sculpture, and architecture. The field combines historical problems dating back centuries with recent advances from the last 12 years. The class structure includes mandatory lectures, problem sets, and a project component with optional open problem sessions.

Key results discussed: For linkages, 2D chains have universal foldability while 2D trees and 3D chains do not; locked configurations exist in 3D chains and 2D trees. For paper, flat foldability is NP-hard, but universal design results exist for creating any shape. For polyhedra, edge unfolding of convex polyhedra remains unsolved since Dürer (1525), while general unfolding is always possible for convex shapes. Hinged dissections, a recent addition, show that any equal-area polygons can be folded from one chain of polygons.

Sugar output in Tamil Nadu, India's fourth largest sugar producer, is expected to fall by over a third to 600,000 tonnes in 2017/18 due to severe drought. Production dropped from 1.36 million tonnes in 2015/16 to around 1 million tonnes in 2016/17. Drought-affected farmers from southern India protested in New Delhi, some putting rats in their mouths and carrying skulls of farmers who died by suicide, urging Prime Minister Modi to help. Uneven monsoon distribution left southern India dry despite average national rainfall. Tamil Nadu's cotton production is also expected to fall 21 percent to 550,000 bales in 2016/17.

A Yale-led research team has created a dataset tracking city populations from 3700 B.C. to present by digitizing historical records, extending far beyond the U.N.'s 1950 starting point. The data, visualized in a Metrocosm animation beginning with Eridu (c. 3000 B.C.), shows global urbanization growing from 34% in 1960 to 54% today, with a projected 75% by 2030. This MIT computer security course lecture introduces the class structure, covering policy, threat models, and mechanisms for building secure systems. The professor explains that security involves achieving goals despite adversaries, breaking it down into three components: policy (what the system should enforce, such as confidentiality, integrity, and availability), threat model (assumptions about attackers), and mechanism (software/hardware implementations). Security is difficult because it requires preventing all possible attacks—a "negative goal"—rather than just enabling specific functionality.

The lecture provides examples of failures in each component: policy failures include account recovery questions that weaken security and interconnected systems with cascading vulnerabilities (such as the Mat Honan hack involving Amazon, Apple, and Gmail); threat model failures include assuming users pick strong passwords or that cryptographic keys remain secure over decades; mechanism failures include iCloud's missing rate limiting on password attempts, Citibank's missing access control checks, Android's SecureRandom bug exposing Bitcoin private keys, SSL certificate encoding mismatches, and buffer overflow vulnerabilities demonstrated through live coding. The professor concludes that minimizing the trusted computing base—reducing the amount of code that must be correct for security—is a key defense against mechanism bugs.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018 with the SEC. Keith Whittington argues professors should self-censor to preserve academic freedom, but this misguided approach would undermine the right rather than protect it. Demanding discretion destroys rather than defends academic freedom.

Topological quasiparticles in condensed-matter physics have shifted from magnetic to polar textures in ferroelectric crystals. This study investigates barium zirconate titanate (Ba(ZrxTi1−x)O3, BZT), where Zr substitution stabilizes the rhombohedral phase above room temperature. Using molecular dynamics simulations with first-principles parameterized effective Hamiltonians, researchers found that in a 12.5% Zr superlattice with chemically doubled unit cells, topological textures split into alternating −2 antiskyrmions and +4 skyrmions—composed of six −1/3 and six +2/3 topological quarks respectively. Random Zr substitution (0–12.5%) also sustains nontrivial topological textures, though with distorted, "skyrmion-glass" like configurations. Thermal stability testing revealed critical temperatures up to nearly 100 K depending on concentration and diameter, with a non-monotonic trend: initial Zr substitution reduces stability (minimum at 6–8%), partially recovering toward 12.5%. At room temperature (293 K), the 12.5% superlattice maintains rhombohedral symmetry, and local electric fields (~350 kV/cm) can write and stabilize +4 skyrmions, though retention is volatile without sustained bias. Random compositions fail to retain single domains under identical conditions due to disorder-assisted nucleation. The study establishes BZT as a platform for engineered ferroelectric topology, with potential applications in multi-state memory and neuromorphic computing.

This study investigates WSe2/CrI3 van der Waals heterostructures using the QSGŴ computational method to understand proximity-generated magnetic effects on excitons. The researchers find that these heterostructures exhibit type I band alignment with both band edges residing on WSe2, preserving A and B excitons while generating novel interlayer excitonic states. These interlayer excitons appear systematically between A and B excitons with enhanced brightness (~20× that of intralayer CrI3 Frenkel excitons) and binding energies of ~400 meV. Magnetic splittings of A and B excitons range from tens of GHz to ~1000 GHz depending on configuration, with largest splittings in ferromagnetic trilayers. The interlayer excitons combine bright, dipolar character from TMDs with on-site magnetic character from vdW magnets, making them promising for photonic and spintronic applications. The work establishes that magnetic splittings are highly sensitive to band alignments between TMD and magnet layers, varying with interlayer spacing, strain, and phonon coupling.

The reproduction number (R), widely used to measure pathogen propagation, has a major shortcoming: it does not account for time-varying testing volumes. The authors introduce the acceleration index (ε), which measures the proportional responsiveness of cases to tests as an elasticity. The acceleration index nests the reproduction number as a special case; R only tracks case growth rates while ε corrects for test variation by measuring the ratio of case growth to test growth. When test intensity exceeds infectivity intensity, R overestimates viral spread; when test intensity is lower, R underestimates it. Empirical analysis of French COVID-19 data (May 2020–October 2022) shows R significantly underestimated viral spread compared to ε, particularly during the Omicron wave. Similar patterns appear in five other countries. The authors recommend public health authorities use ε alone or R combined with test and infectivity intensities to accurately track viral acceleration, with ε being more parsimonious and practical.

Bill Ackman's Pershing Square US long portfolio increased marginally from $5.96B to $6.01B in Q2 2017, maintaining 7 heavily concentrated positions. Simone Askew became the first black woman to serve as first captain of the Corps of Cadets at the U.S. Military Academy, the highest position in the cadet chain of command. Askew's mother described her as a natural leader.

Syrian rebels faced a Wednesday deadline to accept Russian-brokered surrender terms in southern Syria or face renewed military attack. Russia rejected rebel proposals for ceasefire, army withdrawal, and population transfers, instead demanding army return to pre-2011 positions with Russian military police coordination. Over 30 towns had already returned to regime control, expanding Assad's hold on Daraa province to 60 percent. The offensive displaced 270,000-330,000 people, with Jordan and Israel refusing border entry despite rights group demands. An NHL official discussed Las Vegas's successful expansion franchise, noting the commissioner's early faith in the market despite economic challenges and building issues. NVIDIA Corporation's Q2 FY2020 Form 10-Q filing reports financial results for the quarter and six months ended July 28, 2019. This study examined Ethiopian education policy intentions and secondary school principals' and teachers' conceptualizations of curriculum differentiation (CD). Two national policy documents (ETP 2023, GECF 2020) conceptualize CD as tracking through fields of study, streams, and school types, while the 2012 Guidelines for CD and IEP emphasize differentiating curriculum components (content, instruction, assessment, learning environment) in inclusive classrooms. Data from two school principals and 17 teachers revealed five conceptualization themes: CD as gifted programs, student placement into subjects/streams/schools, special curriculum for student groups, identification and accommodation of gifts/talents, and curricular planning/teaching strategies. Principals' and teachers' conceptualizations varied from lacking awareness to aligning with policy intentions, with incoherent policy guidance and limited practitioner engagement contributing to diverse understandings. The study found misalignment between policy intentions and CD practices, as school-type differentiation (regular, special day, boarding) does not correspond to variations in subject types and difficulty levels.

Former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe was fired on March 16, two days before his planned retirement at age 50, potentially delaying his pension benefits for at least five years. McCabe, a 21-year FBI veteran, was dismissed following an internal investigation into his approval of unauthorized media disclosures related to the Hillary Clinton email probe in 2016. Under the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS), he was estimated to receive approximately $60,000 annually. His firing may prevent him from accessing pension payments and health insurance until age 57. Some lawmakers have offered temporary Capitol Hill positions to help him qualify, though experts dispute whether this would work. McCabe may file an appeal.

The St. Louis Blues have nine core players signed through at least the next three seasons at a total cap cost of $47.425 million, including Vladimir Tarasenko ($7.5M through 2022-23), Alex Pietrangelo ($6.5M through 2019-20), and Jake Allen ($4.35M through 2020-21). ISDA Press Report dated June 4, 2001, covering financial industry news. The Macon Mosquito Abatement District in central Illinois has established a lab in Decatur that enables rapid West Nile virus testing in under 24 hours, down from a week previously. The district has set up 500-mosquito capacity traps at 19 locations to monitor the virus, which appeared unusually early in Illinois this year with the first human case in mid-May. Testing involves sorting mosquitoes and a 90-minute wait before machine analysis. No human cases have been reported in Macon County, though a positive mosquito batch was found in June. The CDC is investigating the early case. Last year, Illinois had 90 human cases and eight deaths.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon sailed on a whaling voyage December 7, 1891. On September 10, 1892, while whaling in the Okhotsk Sea, the vessel was arrested and seized by an Imperial Russian naval officer, despite the captain having previously requested permission to fish in Russian bays and received no indication that Russia claimed jurisdiction over the entire sea. The crew was forced to navigate the Russian vessel to Vladivostok, where the bark was detained until October 1, 1892. The arresting officer claimed the Okhotsk Sea was a closed sea, though the Russian government did not support this claim in subsequent diplomatic correspondence. The U.S. legation at St. Petersburg was notified by telegram, and after diplomatic exchange, the bark was released.

No. 15 Florida defeated Auburn 114-95 on February 14, 2017, in Auburn, Alabama. Canyon Barry led Florida with a season-high 30 points, and the Gators set a new team scoring record, surpassing their previous high of 106 points. The game was tied 50-50 at halftime before Florida opened the second half with a 13-3 run. Florida shot 56% from the field and made 11 of 19 three-pointers. Florida improved to 21-5 overall and 11-2 in the Southeastern Conference, extending their winning streak to seven games. Auburn fell to 16-10 and 5-8 in conference play. An Islamic State car bomb killed 24 people and wounded 67 in Baghdad's Sadr City district on January 2, 2017, targeting Shi'ite Muslims. The group also cut a key road north to Mosul, their last major stronghold, where U.S.-backed Iraqi forces face fierce resistance. Since the Mosul offensive began October 17, elite forces have retaken a quarter of the city. Islamic State attacks elsewhere killed 29 in Baghdad on Saturday, seven policemen near Najaf on Sunday, and at least 16 pro-government fighters near Baiji, where they seized weapons and checkpoints. Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi, meeting with French President Francois Hollande, vowed to end terrorism; Hollande stated French soldiers in Iraq help prevent attacks at home.

This study examines the relationship between parental education level and child cognitive ability using data from the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS), which sampled approximately 20,000 students from grades seven and nine across 28 county-level regions in 2013-2014. The research employs multiple linear regression analysis with parental years of education as core explanatory variables and child cognitive ability (measured by 3PL test scores) as the dependent variable, controlling for personal, family, and school characteristics.

Key findings indicate: (1) a significant positive correlation exists between parental education and child cognitive ability, with each additional year of parental education associated with a 0.019-point increase in child cognitive scores; (2) educational expectations and parent-child interaction serve as mediating factors; (3) parental education impacts girls' cognitive ability more than boys', and urban parents' education has greater effects than rural parents'; and (4) the impact of parental education diminishes as child cognitive ability increases. The study aims to inform policies addressing cognitive ability disparities and socioeconomic "Matthew effects."

This MIT lecture covers financing sustainable real estate at the portfolio level, focusing on REITs and green bonds. REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) are publicly traded companies that invest in income-generating commercial real estate, offering tax advantages if they distribute 90% of income and invest 75% of assets in real estate. Compared to direct real estate investment, REITs provide greater geographic diversification, liquidity, and lower capital requirements, though with less investor control. While the US originated modern REITs, other countries have adopted variations—China's infrastructure-focused REITs emerged recently due to fiscal pressures rather than tax incentives.

Research indicates institutional investors, particularly European and Canadian pension funds, drive REITs' ESG commitments through capital allocation decisions. Studies show greener REITs with higher shares of certified green buildings demonstrate better returns and lower risk. Current research distinguishes between "green talking" (ESG pledges) and "green doing" (actual investments) to assess market responses.

Green bonds represent the debt side, with governments and corporations issuing fixed-income instruments specifically for environmental projects. Green bonds can lower issuers' capital costs when market demand is high. REITs like Boston Properties issue green bonds, and government-sponsored enterprises like Fannie Mae securitize green mortgages into green bonds.

Benchmarking tools like GRESB (Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark) provide portfolio-level ESG ratings similar to LEED for individual buildings. Research correlates higher GRESB scores with better financial performance and lower borrowing costs, though rating inconsistencies across agencies create "ESG confusion" requiring methodological improvements.

This passage describes two stackless assembler procedures for processor initialization and cleanup. The first procedure initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region, divides it among processor cores, maps them to global address space, and sets MTRRs. It handles protected mode and real mode differently, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance, and returns status codes indicating success, stack reentry warning, or unknown processor family errors. The second procedure removes the pre-memory stack when main memory becomes available, disables CAR mode, flushes cache lines, and should only be invoked by the BSP. Both procedures destroy specific registers and require the host environment to use them exclusively for stack management. The passage also documents AmdCreateStruct, a helper procedure that creates storage space for AGESA parameter blocks using three allocation methods: PreMemHeap (Cache-as-RAM), PostMemDram (main memory), or ByHost (caller-managed).

This document details the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104 GPUs. Key features include: 2x FP32 processing throughput via redesigned Streaming Multiprocessors; second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection performance and new hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur; third-generation Tensor Cores supporting structured sparsity for 2x throughput, plus new TF32 and BF16 data types; GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling for up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth; PCIe Gen 4 support; and third-generation NVLink. The architecture delivers up to 1.7x faster raster graphics and 2x faster ray tracing than Turing. Specific products include GeForce RTX 3090/3080/3070, RTX A6000 workstation GPU, and A40 data center GPU. Additional features covered include RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading/decompression, HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K support, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, seventh-generation NVENC, and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology for safer memory overclocking.

Scott Hughes introduces a general relativity course, describing required and recommended textbooks including Carroll's "Spacetime and Geometry" (primary), Schutz's "A First Course in General Relativity" (supplement), Misner-Thorne-Wheeler's "Gravitation" (reference), and Wald's "General Relativity" (mathematical). Assessment consists of 11 problem sets with no exams. The course structure covers mathematical foundations in the first half (leading to Einstein field equations) and applications (cosmology, black holes, gravitational waves) in the second half.

Hughes then introduces core geometric concepts: spacetime as a manifold of events with a metric, where a manifold is a set of points with connectedness properties, an event is a point in spacetime (when/where something happens), and the metric defines distances between events. He establishes an inertial reference frame as a lattice of synchronized clocks and measuring rods moving freely (no forces, no rotation), with uniform ticking and orthogonal orientation. Clock synchronization uses Einstein's procedure: light bounced between clocks, with reflection time equaling the average of emission and reception times, exploiting the invariant speed of light.

He introduces natural units where c=1 (length unit = distance light travels in time unit). Spacetime vectors are defined as four-component objects transforming via Lorentz transformations between inertial frames, with displacement vectors as the prototype. Notation includes Greek indices (0-3) for spacetime, Latin indices for spatial components, over-arrows for four-vectors, and Einstein summation convention with upstairs/downstairs index positions. The distinction between geometric objects (independent of coordinates) and their component representations (observer-dependent) is emphasized.

This study investigates the reliability of deep learning models for predicting mammographic density from low-dose mammograms (approximately 10% of standard dose) compared to standard-dose images. Using the ALDRAM dataset of 147 women aged 30-45 with prior unilateral breast cancer, researchers trained ResNet-18 models on standard and simulated low-dose images from the PROCAS dataset (15,290 mammograms). Results show high correlation between standard and low-dose predictions (Spearman rank correlation 0.964-0.973 for individual views, 0.980 when averaged). Variability factors analyzed include: view type (CC/MLO), model differences, image size, breast area, density level, age, and dose ratio. Key findings indicate that averaging predictions across views and multiple models reduces variation; higher breast density and smaller breast area correlate with greater prediction differences between standard and low-dose images; age and dose ratio show no significant effect. Low-dose predictions tend to be slightly lower than standard-dose equivalents, particularly for smaller, denser breasts. The study concludes that low-dose mammography combined with deep learning can enable breast cancer risk assessment in younger women, though systematic differences require correction for clinical implementation.

Ultra-processed foods (UPF) comprise up to 60% of calories consumed in developed nations and are linked to non-communicable diseases. Researchers developed Food Processing Score (FPro), a machine learning-based continuous index (0-1) that translates nutritional content into degree of processing, trained on NOVA classifications. GroceryDB analyzed over 50,000 products from Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods, finding most inventory is ultra-processed with store differences: Whole Foods offers more minimally-processed items, Target the most ultra-processed. Higher processing generally correlates with cheaper calories (8.7% price decrease per 10% FPro increase), though this varies by category. Ingredient Processing Score (IgFPro) ranks individual ingredients' contribution to ultra-processing, identifying markers like corn syrup and palm oil. The continuous FPro enables precise substitution strategies and public health interventions, addressing limitations of categorical classification systems.

Tecomaria capensis (Cape Honeysuckle) is a scrambling shrub or small tree up to 6 m in the Bignoniaceae family, with opposite compound leaves and year-round orange-red trumpet-shaped flowers. Native to southern and eastern South Africa, it grows in thickets and forest margins across five provinces. Listed as Least Concern by SANBI, it is browsed by game and stock, visited by pollinators, and hosts hawkmoth larvae. Traditionally used medicinally for fever, pain, and other ailments, its wood is carved into protective necklets (isixhoxho) for nursing mothers. It requires well-drained soil, regular watering until established, and winter pruning to encourage growth.

VirtualLink simplifies VR headset connectivity through a single USB-C connector, enabling VR on small form factor devices. NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe interfaces for SLI GPU-to-GPU data transfers in Turing TU102 and TU104 GPUs, providing 25-50 GB/sec peak bandwidth per direction and supporting advanced display topologies, though only two-way SLI is supported. Turing GPUs introduce RT Cores for real-time ray tracing, enabling physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Hybrid rendering combines ray tracing and rasterization for optimal performance. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, making ray tracing 10x faster than Pascal GPUs. NVIDIA NGX provides AI-based graphics enhancement through Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) enables dynamic shading rate control for Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per pass for efficient VR rendering. Turing GPUs include USB Type-C and VirtualLink support, with TU104 used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000, and TU106 used in GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink or SLI support.

From November 1961 to October 1962, the Special Group (Augmented) oversaw Operation Mongoose, a covert program to overthrow Castro's regime in Cuba, with Brigadier General Lansdale coordinating CIA, State, and Defense Department activities. President Kennedy established the Special Group (Counter-Insurgency) in January 1962, and President Johnson later assigned counterinsurgency coordination to the Secretary of State in 1966. The "Special Group 5412" was renamed the "303 Committee" in June 1964, with Bundy as chairman. The 303 Committee approved 163 covert actions during Kennedy's administration and 142 during Johnson's through February 1967, though only 14% of CIA projects were reviewed. In 1970, President Nixon established the 40 Committee, adding the Attorney General and requiring annual reviews, though formal meetings declined over time. The 40 Committee reviewed about 25% of CIA covert action projects. The Hughes-Ryan amendment in 1974 required explicit presidential approval via signed findings and expanded congressional oversight.

The lecture discusses the economics of spam and cyberattacks, contrasting economically-motivated attacks with ideological ones (like Stuxnet). For profit-driven attacks, the speaker examines how understanding financial incentives can help disrupt operations.

Key examples include Chinese "text message cars" that harvest mobile numbers and send 200,000 spam messages daily—costing ~$1,600 for equipment while generating ~$1,600 daily profit, with fines under $5,000 and rare enforcement. Chinese mobile carriers reportedly profit from this spam through revenue-sharing schemes.

The lecture outlines the spam ecosystem's three components: advertising (getting users to click), click support (DNS/web infrastructure), and realization (payment processing). Spammers use botnets ($0.01-$0.10 per infected host), bulletproof hosting, fast-flux DNS, and CAPTCHA-solving services (~$0.001 per CAPTCHA via cheap labor or Mechanical Turk).

Despite low conversion rates (28 purchases from 350 million emails), spam remains profitable due to minimal costs. The realization phase reveals a financial choke point: only ~30 acquiring banks handle spam transactions, and spammers must properly classify transactions and deliver goods to avoid chargeback fines exceeding 1%.

Following research publication, Visa implemented stricter policies labeling pharmaceutical sales as high-risk and explicitly forbidding illegal drug/trademark sales. The lecture concludes with "hackbacks"—private companies (Microsoft, banks) conducting offensive operations against attackers, using creative legal justifications like trademark infringement.

While self-driving technology has been promoted as a way to reduce traffic deaths caused by human error, the accident highlights ongoing safety concerns. In *United States v. Tyler* (2016), the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania denied defendant Willie Tyler's motions to dismiss his retrial on obstruction of justice charges. Tyler was originally convicted in 2000 for witness tampering by murder and intimidation related to the 1992 killing of Doreen Proctor, who was to testify against his brother. After his convictions were vacated on appeal due to legal errors regarding the interpretation of 18 U.S.C. § 1512, Tyler argued retrial was barred by the Sixth Amendment's Confrontation Clause, the Fifth Amendment's Double Jeopardy Clause, and the Due Process Clause. The court rejected all three claims: (1) a hearsay statement from Proctor was admissible to show she would have communicated with federal law enforcement, not for its truth; (2) retrial was permitted because the vacatur was based on legal error, not insufficient evidence; and (3) the government did not engage in outrageous conduct warranting dismissal.

Four western North Carolina school districts damaged by Hurricane Helene in September 2024 have made varying progress one year later. Henderson County's Atkinson Elementary reopened in December 2024 after relocating to a Boys & Girls Club and installing new flood-resistant flooring. McDowell County's Old Fort Elementary students merged with Pleasant Gardens Elementary for the 2024-25 school year and returned to their repaired building on August 25, 2025, with reinforced creek walls and elevated HVAC units. Watauga County's Valle Crucis School, which flooded 70%, had students distributed across three community locations; its new building construction was delayed due to workforce shortages, with middle schoolers now at Caldwell Community College. Yancey County's Micaville Elementary closed permanently after record rainfall; its students relocated to Burnsville and Blue Ridge Elementary schools, with expansions completed or underway. All districts emphasized the importance of preexisting community partnerships, communication plans for future emergencies, and ongoing infrastructure and drainage improvements.

Professor Hong introduces a quantum field theory course, explaining its goal to develop concepts and techniques for quantum dynamics of fields. He notes that quantum field theory describes three of the four fundamental interactions and has become a universal language for theoretical physics. The course is the first of a three-semester sequence, focusing on fundamental concepts.

He addresses quantum field theory's reputation for difficulty, arguing it stems from conceptual challenges rather than calculations. He offers three pieces of advice: recognize it as quantum mechanics with infinite degrees of freedom, understand that formalisms were designed to solve concrete physical problems, and build intuition through worked examples.

The lecture then covers classical field theory, emphasizing the principle of locality formulated by Faraday around 1830, which states that effects propagate from point to neighboring point rather than acting at a distance. Fields are the mathematical device realizing this principle. He discusses scalar, vector, tensor, and spinor fields, and introduces the action principle for classical fields, showing how locality constrains the Lagrangian to involve only single-point values and their derivatives. He derives the general equation of motion through variational principles, then restricts discussion to translationally and Lorentz invariant theories, providing examples including Maxwell theory, Einstein gravity, and scalar field theories, with the Klein-Gordon equation as the simplest case.

This paper introduces a quantum algorithmic framework for generalized linear model (GLM) sparsification that achieves quadratic speedups over classical algorithms for a broad class of regression problems. The framework constructs ε-approximate sparsifiers—small weighted subsets that preserve objective values—for loss functions satisfying L-auto-Lipschitz and lower θ-homogeneous properties, including linear, ridge, Lasso, Huber, ℓp, and γp regression. The quantum algorithm runs in time rÕ(pr√mn/ε + poly(n)) · log(smax/smin)), compared to classical rÕ(mr) time, yielding speedups when m ≫ n. The approach combines quantum leverage score approximation, multiscale leverage score overestimates, and quantum importance sampling techniques.

Digital Foundry's analysis of Monster Hunter World on Xbox One and PlayStation consoles reveals technical shortcomings across all versions. Both console families share strengths including well-modeled monsters, detailed textures, excellent character models, and rich environments, but suffer from reduced visual contrast, weak HDR effects, clipping, collision detection issues, and poor motion blur.

Base PS4 runs at 1080p with uncapped frame rates frequently dipping below 30 fps, while base Xbox One performs worse at 864p with lower frame rates. On enhanced consoles, Resolution mode shows PS4 Pro at 1800p via checkerboard rendering versus Xbox One X at 1728p native, with smoother edges on One X but missing distant visual assets and inferior performance. Frame-rate mode locks both at 1080p with 30-60 fps ranges, One X averaging higher. Graphics mode maintains 1080p with extended LODs, finally showing missing One X assets, but One X significantly outperforms Pro.

Digital Foundry concludes MHW is technically disappointing, inadequately optimized for both enhanced consoles, with the One X build particularly problematic despite the console's superior hardware.

The Flex offense uses baseline and down screens in a "Pick the Picker" continuous action that burdens defenses with two simultaneous screen types. The basic continuity involves O1 passing to O2 while O5 steps to the corner; O3 uses O5's baseline screen as O1 down-screens for O5, giving O2 options to shoot, feed O3, pass to O4, or hit O5 popping out. Ball reversal continues the pattern with alternating screens. Variations include corner post isolation, bump-back shots against cheating defenders, back cuts against overplay, weakside lobs, and entries like high post rub, shuffle cuts, and dribble clear. A "Pop" variation uses weakside double screens allowing receivers three cutting options. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation and hustle rather than size, with players needing to box out defenders and pursue second efforts.

The speaker addresses Americans on national conditions, finding much that is satisfying and encouraging. The U.S. leads global readjustment after the Great War, with returning confidence, revived business, and emerging prosperity. America has contributed resources and counsel to European relief and dispute settlement.

These successes came through sustained effort and sacrifice across generations. To continue, the nation must learn from history, recognizing that human nature and essential human relationships remain constant. The speech traces American development from independence through territorial expansion, the Monroe Doctrine, and entry into the Great War, emphasizing enlarged freedom and strengthened independence throughout.

To remain distinctively American requires embracing legitimate desires of civilized people for conscientious living, not being narrowed by slogans. America maintains peaceful intentions but needs balanced, modern military forces as instruments of security, not menace. The nation seeks honorable peace protecting citizens' rights everywhere, promoting peace through friendliness, mutual understanding, and forbearance rather than competitive armaments. America has committed to naval limitation and should lead in this new direction.

International conferences and arbitration treaties advance peace; the U.S. should adhere to the Permanent Court of International Justice without bartering sovereignty. America avoids Old World political entanglements but assists Western Hemisphere nations and responds to human suffering globally. Permanent peace requires addressing economic pressures and cultivating brotherly love in human hearts—only spiritual nature triumphs over parchment and sword.

Political detachment allows America to assist others while demanding justice for itself. Domestic success enables international success. The party system, though imperfect, best expresses popular will; responsible party government requires coherence and loyalty to platform principles. The recent election mandate rejected public ownership of railroads and utilities, affirmed constitutional guarantees and judicial integrity, and demanded economy in public expenditure with tax reduction and reform.

Economy saves people, not money, by reducing burdens on workers. Tax reform should encourage business, avoid extremely high rates, and create conditions for universal success. Property rights derive from personal rights; waste denies divine sanction and causes moral decay. Restrictive immigration and protective tariffs have produced plentiful employment, high wages, and contentment. Agriculture revives slowly.

Maintaining existing advantages matters more than securing new ones. The three-branch system, federalism, and constitutional wisdom require constant vigilance. Citizens must obey laws they help make; lawbreakers display ignorance and savagery, not superior intelligence. Congress represents people and states, collaborates with the President, and deserves cooperation.

America has not fully practiced its principles but overwhelmingly expresses determination to proceed rightly. The nation should be less sectional, replacing false prejudice with enlightened pride. Liberty requires toleration; minds must remain free. America stands as an example of domestic and international tranquility, seeking peace and prosperity, promoting enterprise, education, and justice, desiring divine rather than human allegiance, seeking only to merit God's favor.
