Canada's main stock index fell from a record high Thursday, along with other North American markets, due to escalating trade war fears after the U.S. proposed new tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods. The TSX retreat was partly attributed to profit-taking after Wednesday's peak. Energy stocks declined 2.11% amid expectations of OPEC increasing production, while mining stocks also fell. Cannabis stocks rose following Canada's marijuana legalization date announcement. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed lower. The Canadian dollar slipped to 75.13 cents US. Crude oil fell to $65.54 per barrel, gold dropped to $1,270.50 per ounce, and natural gas rose slightly to $2.98 per mmBTU.

This study analyzed 24,849 soft-tissue sarcoma (STS) patients from the SEER database (2000-2018) to determine mortality rates and predict survival probabilities using nomograms. Six sarcoma types were examined: liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, spindle cell sarcoma, giant cell sarcoma, and myxofibrosarcoma. Key findings showed myxofibrosarcoma had the highest survival rate (75%) while spindle cell sarcoma had the lowest (37%). Surgery reduced mortality by 74%, chemotherapy by 33%, and radiation by 24%. Increasing age, male sex, non-white race, advanced stage, and higher tumor grade negatively affected survival. The study developed all-cause mortality nomograms predicting 5- and 10-year survival probabilities based on patient characteristics and treatment combinations, with surgery showing the greatest survival benefit (above 90% at 5 and 10 years) compared to no treatment (45% and 25%). Limitations included missing clinicopathological factors, histological subtypes, recurrence data, and radiotherapy details in the SEER database.

BART is expanding its rapid response team by five members and launching a mobile bio-hazard reporting option following increased complaints about drug needles on trains, including an incident where a woman was pricked by a syringe. The 19-member team will be stationed at MacArthur and Lake Merritt stations to address urgent cleaning needs. San Francisco distributes approximately 400,000 needles monthly, with an estimated 154,000 unaccounted for each month, though the health department reports no known disease transmissions from accidental needle pricks.

The Supreme Court struck respondent Mascio's answer in a mandamus case because it was filed one day late, violating Rule XIV(1)(C) which prohibits untimely filings. The answer was due March 19, 1998, but was filed March 20, 1998.

Queensland's cyclone season remains active with potential for wild weather before Easter. Modelling shows two deep low pressure systems may form off the coast by next Tuesday: one tropical low near Thursday Island expected to intensify while moving west across the Gulf of Carpentaria, and a second system over the Solomon Sea forecast to shift into the north-eastern Coral Sea. The Bureau of Meteorology notes uncertainty in system evolution but expects a weak Coral Sea low to remain offshore. Sea temperatures exceed cyclone-feeding thresholds in multiple locations. The Sunshine Coast faces increasing showers, with 90% chance of rain Wednesday and 80% chance Thursday-Friday, plus south-easterly winds reaching 30km/h.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 2, 2017, reporting its fourth fiscal quarter 2017 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and data sheet (Exhibit 99.2) as attachments. The document was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This MIT 14.271 lecture introduces industrial organization (IO) as a field combining theory and empirics, with Glenn Ellison as the primary lecturer. The course covers 12 topics over two lectures each—typically theory on Wednesdays and empirical work on Mondays.

The lecture begins with monopoly pricing fundamentals: a monopolist maximizes profit by setting marginal revenue equal to marginal cost, yielding the Lerner index (price minus marginal cost over price) equal to negative one over the elasticity of demand. This shows pricing depends on demand elasticity, not demand levels.

Several monopoly inefficiencies are discussed: deadweight loss from underproduction, productive inefficiency from lack of competitive pressure, quality distortions, rent-seeking costs, and equity concerns from consumer-to-firm transfers.

For multiproduct pricing, the analysis extends to account for diversion ratios between goods. With substitutes, markups exceed the single-product Lerner index; with complements, prices may fall below cost (as with printers/ink or newspapers/ads).

On product quality, a monopolist chooses quality based on the marginal consumer's willingness to pay, not the average consumer—potentially leading to underprovision relative to social optimum.

For durable goods, a monopolist with commitment power should set a single monopoly price and never reduce it. Without commitment, the Coase conjecture suggests prices may converge to marginal cost as pricing frequency increases, though real-world factors (reputation, new customer inflows, rental options, best-price guarantees, capacity constraints) typically prevent this extreme outcome.

The lecture concludes introducing information design: firms may strategically provide or withhold product information to maximize profits. Full information enables monopoly pricing; no information can extract more surplus by making consumers homogeneous; partial information (as through intermediaries like Amazon or Yelp) can sometimes benefit both consumers and firms by shifting the pricing equilibrium.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on August 24, 2022, announcing financial results for the quarter ended July 31, 2022. The filing includes a press release and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress, which are furnished but not deemed "filed" for SEC purposes.

This MIT lecture discusses natural sandwich structures and efficient mechanical designs in nature. The professor explains that many monocotyledon plant leaves, such as iris and cattail (bull rush), exhibit sandwich construction with dense sclerenchyma fibers as faces and parenchyma cells as a foam-like core, enabling lightweight stiffness. Experimental analysis of iris leaves confirmed they behave mechanically like sandwich beams, with calculated and measured stiffness values in the same order of magnitude despite some approximations.

Other natural sandwich examples include: sea kelp with honeycomb cores providing buoyancy; bird skulls with foam or trabecular bone cores between face plates, making them lightweight for flight; cuttlefish bones with gas-filled chambers for buoyancy control; and horseshoe crab and Galapagos tortoise shells.

The lecture also covers palm stems, which maintain constant diameter while growing taller by depositing additional cell wall layers as they age, creating a radial density gradient. Analysis of Paul Rich's data shows this gradient makes palm stems 2.5 times stiffer than uniform density would allow, with strength distribution closely matching stress distribution. Bamboo exhibits similar radial density gradients. The professor concludes by announcing a review session before the upcoming test.

Rep. Trey Gowdy, a senior House Republican and Trump supporter, stated there is no evidence the FBI planted a "spy" on Trump's 2016 campaign, contradicting Trump's repeated claims. After being briefed by the Justice Department and FBI, Gowdy said the FBI acted appropriately and that informants are standard law enforcement practice. Gowdy, who led investigations into Hillary Clinton's Benghazi role, announced his retirement from Congress in January. Trump has labeled the informant reports "spygate" and called it potentially one of the biggest political scandals in U.S. history. His legal team has requested classified information about the FBI investigation's origins to prepare him for an interview with special counsel Robert Mueller.

This paper examines Temperature Scaling (TS) for calibrating CNNs in brain tumor classification from MRI scans under five synthetic noise types: Gaussian, Poisson, Salt & Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform. A lightweight CNN was trained on a composite dataset from three public repositories and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, NLL, and ECE. Results show TS consistently reduces NLL and ECE across all noise conditions while preserving classification accuracy. Optimal temperature values ranged from 1.175 to 1.581 depending on noise type and severity. Extended experiments with ResNet50 confirmed TS benefits apply to deeper architectures, improving FP and FN rates without affecting accuracy. The study concludes TS is an effective, computationally efficient calibration method for medical imaging applications requiring reliable confidence estimates.

The lecture completes Cantor's theorem proof that any set A has strictly smaller cardinality than its power set, using a diagonalization argument involving a constructed set B that leads to contradiction. The instructor then transitions to defining real numbers R as the unique ordered field containing Q with the least upper bound property. Key definitions covered include: ordered sets (with comparison and transitivity properties), upper/lower bounds, supremum (least upper bound), and infimum (greatest lower bound). Examples demonstrate that Z has the least upper bound property while Q does not, illustrated by the set of rationals whose squares are less than 2 having no supremum in Q. The lecture begins proving that if such a supremum existed in Q, it would satisfy x² = 2, establishing one inequality (x² ≥ 2) before time runs out.

This study examines how two middle grades teacher candidates (TCs) viewed, experienced, and used translanguaging with multilingual learners during a year-long Professional Development School (PDS) experience, and how their ESL-focused coursework prepared them for this practice. Despite positive asset-based views of translanguaging and feeling theoretically prepared with instructional "tools," both TCs struggled to implement translanguaging in practice due to limited experience with multilingual learners, lack of modeling by cooperating teachers (CTs), and personal discomfort—particularly for the monolingual TC. The study reveals a persistent theory-practice gap, as TCs rarely observed CTs using students' native languages or employing translanguaging strategies beyond translation. Findings suggest teacher education programs must provide TCs with opportunities to see translanguaging modeled in classrooms and recommend professional development for CTs to create linguistically inclusive spaces where translanguaging is actively embraced.

Australia's business investment grew just 0.4% in the first quarter, below the expected 1%, with construction (down 1.3%) dragging down results due to a 16% fall in new factory builds. Equipment, plant and machinery investment rose 2.5%. The second estimate for next financial year's capital expenditure is $87.7 billion, below forecasts and only modestly higher than last year. Capital Economics' Paul Dales noted risks to the business investment outlook and called non-mining investment particularly disappointing.

George Herbert and two friends chased down a bike thief in Bristol on Sunday evening, recovering a white mountain bike. The thief abandoned the bike and fled. Herbert is now trying to find the original owner, with police attempting to match the bike to theft reports. He posted on the Bristol Cyclists Facebook page seeking help, noting bolt croppers fell from the thief's rucksack. Herbert is not posting photos of the bike, requiring the owner to provide a matching description or photo to claim it. This follows a similar incident last month where Jenni Morton-Humphreys recovered her stolen bike from an online seller after a tip from another cyclist.

A speaker describes a different post-game feeling compared to last year, noting the team had an extra day to spend with families and a good practice. They mention previous issues with finding focus at the start of games during the regular season, but state this is no longer a problem now that playoffs have begun. Another person responds that it was a perfect answer.

On February 6, 2024, Ford CFO John Lawler prepared to present 2023 financial results showing Ford Model e, the company's separately reported EV segment, lost $4.7 billion—up from $0.9 billion in 2021 and $2.1 billion in 2022. Ford's unique segment reporting among legacy automakers contrasted with competitors who include EVs in internal combustion operations.

Ford's EV history dates to Henry Ford's 1914 battery experiments, but projects were repeatedly shelved, including the 2009-2018 Focus Electric. Despite false starts, Ford committed $4.5 billion (2016-2020), increasing to $11.5 billion (through 2022), $30 billion (through 2025), and $50 billion (through 2026), targeting 50% EV production by 2030. The 2021 launches of Mustang Mach-E, F-150 Lightning, and E-Transit made Ford the No. 2 U.S. EV seller with 275,000 orders by year-end. However, momentum faded by October 2023, when Ford delayed $12 billion in EV investment amid cooling demand.

Lawler noted that U.S. GAAP requires R&D expensing as incurred, while IFRS permits development cost capitalization after establishing technical and commercial feasibility. Ford's 2023 R&D expense of $8.2 billion exceeded its $5.5 billion consolidated profit before interest and taxes, with growing EV allocation. International competitors capitalized portions of development costs, creating accounting disparities evident in 2023 financial data from Volkswagen, Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Honda, and Subaru.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2020 reports Q3 fiscal year 2021 revenue of $4.73 billion, up 57% year-over-year, with net income of $1.34 billion. The company completed the $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies on April 27, 2020, contributing 13% of Q3 revenue. NVIDIA entered into a $40 billion agreement to acquire Arm Limited on September 13, 2020, paying $2 billion at signing with expected closing in Q1 2022. The company changed its reportable segments to Graphics and Compute & Networking. Graphics revenue was $2.79 billion (up 25% YoY) and Compute & Networking was $1.94 billion (up 146% YoY). Gaming revenue reached $2.27 billion (up 37% YoY), while Data Center revenue was $1.90 billion (up 162% YoY). The company issued $5 billion in notes in March 2020 and had $10.14 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at quarter end.

RDRAND and RDSEED instructions read values from a cryptographic co-processor via memory-mapped I/O, which is slower than software-based PRNGs. For latency-sensitive applications, a hybrid approach using hardware-generated seeds with a PRNG can improve performance while maintaining security. The AMD Secure RNG library abstracts low-level hardware access for AMD Zen processors, providing an easy-to-use API for applications like cryptographic key generation.

HCPEA, a nonprofit trade association representing major private equity firms in healthcare with over $1 trillion in assets under management, has named Terry Woodward as its new President. Woodward, who co-founded Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan's healthcare private equity practice in 2009 and has served as an HCPEA director since 2014, will lead the organization as it prepares to hold its inaugural Healthcare Forum in June in Park City, Utah. The association's members collectively manage one of the world's largest portfolios of privately-held healthcare businesses across multiple segments including services, products, diagnostics, distribution, pharmaceuticals and IT.

Cboe Global Markets launched bitcoin futures trading on December 10, 2017, marking the first government-regulated exchange approval for a bitcoin-backed security. Most initial bets favored price increases. Bitcoin rose about 8% to over $15,700 within 10 minutes of trading beginning, later exceeding $16,000, with January futures contracts above $18,000. The move allows mainstream investors to speculate on bitcoin prices without owning the currency and enables betting against its value. Some economists warn of a bubble, while industry insiders predict continued growth. Bitcoin had risen roughly 1,500% since the start of 2017.

North American cannabis stocks declined sharply this week, with the North American Marijuana Index falling 27.2 percent and the U.S. Marijuana Index down 18.1 percent. Canadian stocks led losses following over $1.2 billion in deal offerings from licensed producers and concerns about Aphria's purchase of Nuuvera. The Horizons Marijuana Life Sciences Index ETF lost 29.61 percent, while the ETFMG Alternative Harvest ETF shed 19.2 percent. Major decliners included Aurora Cannabis (down 36.8 percent), THC Biomed (down 38.25 percent), and Canopy Growth (down 31.9 percent). Company news included MassRoots completing a $4.75 million raise, DOJA Cannabis and Tokyo Smoke merging to form Hiku Brands, Jane West launching a $1.07 million crowdfunding campaign, and iAnthus Capital acquiring Citiva Medical for approximately $18 million. New cannabis indices launched include the Canadian Cannabis LP Index and the Green Market Report Index.

Billionaire real estate investor Jeff Greene predicts higher interest rates and fiscal policy will end the eight-year stock market rally. Greene argues that the Federal Reserve's near-zero interest rates and $4.5 trillion balance sheet have been more stimulative to markets than tax cuts could be. The 10-year Treasury yield has fallen from 5.027% a decade ago to around 2.230%, helping the Dow and S&P 500 roughly triple since March 2009. Greene believes Washington's newfound legislative activity could slow the economy by pushing rates higher, though he expects rates to rise slowly due to lackluster growth. Wall Street has reacted calmly to Trump's pro-growth agenda of tax cuts, infrastructure spending, and deregulation, though market momentum has faded since March 1 amid legislative delays.

Divergence trading strategy identifies potential market reversals by comparing price action with oscillator indicators like RSI, MACD, or Stochastic. Divergence occurs when price and indicator movements are out of phase, signaling weakening momentum. Two main types exist: classical divergence (against the trend, indicating potential reversals) and hidden divergence (with the trend, indicating trend continuation). A backtest on S&P 500 (SPY) using simple rules showed profit factors above 1.75 for 2-20 day settings, with strong Sharpe ratios and low drawdowns. Examples include bullish divergences on Nasdaq 100 and TSLA (March 2020) and bearish divergences on S&P 500 (February 2020) and Nasdaq 100 (December 2018). Volume analysis can confirm signals, while common mistakes include overtrading, ignoring risk management, and relying solely on divergence without confirmation. The strategy requires backtesting to determine optimal indicators for specific markets.

The UAE announced its first nuclear reactor at the Barakah plant will come online in late 2019 or early 2020, a further delay from previous schedules. Construction of the first of four reactors at the $20 billion plant is complete. The second reactor is 93% complete, the third 83%, and the fourth 72%. When fully operational, the four reactors will produce 5,600 megawatts, about 25% of UAE's electricity needs. The plant is being built by a consortium led by Korea Electric Power Corporation. The UAE aims for 50% clean energy by 2050. Saudi Arabia plans up to 16 nuclear reactors, though projects have not materialized.

The passage provides PCB layout guidelines for power traces and ground planes in switching regulator designs. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per Ampere), with critical components placed close together to reduce EMI, inductance, and voltage errors. Ground connections should use ground planes on both PCB sides when possible, with multilayer boards using ground planes to separate power and signal planes. Vias should handle 200 mA each for inter-plane connections. Switching current loops should curl in the same direction to prevent magnetic field reversal and reduce radiated EMI. For high-current output drivers, a dedicated power ground section is required for high di/dt currents, with VCC and VREF bypassed separately to power and signal ground planes using low ESR/ESL ceramic capacitors. The document also includes sections on documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD precautions, and mechanical packaging information with disclaimers about data accuracy and liability limitations.

President Andrew Johnson issued a May 29, 1865 proclamation appointing William W. Holden as provisional governor of North Carolina following the Civil War. Citing constitutional authority, Johnson directed Holden to convene a convention of loyal delegates to amend the state constitution and restore North Carolina to the Union. The proclamation required electors and delegates to take an amnesty oath and meet pre-1861 voter qualifications. Johnson also ordered federal military, treasury, postal, judicial, naval, and interior officials to assist in establishing civil government and enforcing federal laws in North Carolina.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of Charles A. Meeker's civil rights complaint against multiple defendants involved in a child abuse investigation that resulted in custody of his four daughters being transferred to New Mexico Human Services. The district court dismissed the case based on failure to properly serve four defendants, res judicata from prior unsuccessful suits, and failure to state a claim against guardian ad litem Deborah Grout. The appellate court held that a guardian ad litem, like a public defender, does not act "under color of state law" for § 1983 purposes because they owe undivided loyalty to the minor rather than the state and must exercise independent professional judgment. The court also ruled that Meeker could not represent his minor daughters pro se under Fed.R.Civ.P. 17(c) and 28 U.S.C. § 1654.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court's grant of summary judgment for Bank of St. Louis and two employees in a malicious prosecution case brought by Harvey F. Euge. Euge sought $400,000 in damages after the bank's actions led to his indictment and conviction for obtaining money by a bogus check, later reversed by the Missouri Supreme Court. The court held that Euge's discharge on appeal did not eliminate probable cause for prosecution, as his conviction created a presumption of probable cause that he failed to overcome. The undisputed facts—Euge's use of a fictitious name to open an account and his deposit of a check later returned for insufficient funds—established probable cause as a matter of law, making summary judgment proper.

The authors propose video object segmentation-aware audio generation, a new task enabling precise control over audio synthesis by conditioning on visual segmentation masks. They develop SAGANet, which extends the MMAudio model with a segmentation-aware control module combining global and localized visual information through gated cross-attention. The method trains only a fraction of parameters on the curated Segmented Music Solos dataset (5,395 training samples of solo instrument performances with segmentation masks), yet generalizes to multi-source scenes. Experiments show SAGANet outperforms the base model in semantic alignment (IB-score: 40.87 vs 35.94) and temporal synchronization (DeSync: 0.31 vs 0.95), with LoRA fine-tuning further improving results.

Britain's FTSE 100 rose 0.6% to 7,353.89 points on Monday, recovering from a three-month low, with financials and miners leading gains. Banks rose 0.8% and miners gained 1.7% as tensions between the U.S. and North Korea eased. Energy stocks lagged as oil prices retreated. TUI hit a record high, up 4.8%, following a Credit Suisse upgrade, while Experian and G4S fell 1.5% and 1.1% respectively after Morgan Stanley downgrades. Mid caps rose 0.8%.

A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander, Major-General Qassem Soleimani, said the Guards were ready to implement a policy preventing regional oil exports if Iranian oil sales were banned by the United States. President Hassan Rouhani had appeared to threaten disrupting oil shipments from neighbouring countries if Washington forced countries to stop buying Iranian oil. Iranian officials have previously threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz. The United States withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal in May and demanded countries halt Iranian oil imports by November 4. Iran's Opec governor, Hossein Kazempour Ardebili, said Trump's pressure would drive oil prices higher and hurt the US economy. The European Union vowed to keep the 2015 deal alive. Rouhani, in Vienna to salvage the deal, said Iran would remain if other signatories guaranteed its benefits. Foreign ministers from China, France, Germany, Britain and Russia will meet Iranian officials in Vienna on Friday to discuss preserving the accord.

Tom Petty's cause of death has been deferred pending further tests following his autopsy. The 66-year-old musician died last week at UCLA hospital in Santa Monica, California, after his family removed life support following cardiac arrest and confirmation of no brain activity. He was surrounded by family, friends, and bandmates. Tributes followed, including from Kings of Leon's Nathan Followill, who cited Petty as a major inspiration. Petty rose to fame in 1976 with the Heartbreakers and later joined the supergroup The Traveling Wilburys.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis's estate, sued David Lewis to recover $505.58 withdrawn from his deceased mother's bank account after her death on August 4, 1929, and to collect rent for estate property he allegedly occupied. David Lewis admitted withdrawing the funds but claimed he was entitled to them as repayment for loans totaling $936 he made to his mother between 1926 and 1928. The trial court dismissed the suit, but the Court of Appeal reversed, ruling that David Lewis was merely a creditor of the estate and could not satisfy his own claim by taking succession assets. The court awarded the bank $505.58 with interest but found the rent claim unproven.

This work presents a method for robots to model, reason about, and explain differences between competing plans. The approach addresses two research questions: how robots can model what differentiates plans to determine which is better, and how they can explain these differences through narrative.

The authors first develop a novel ontological model extending OCRA that formalizes plan comparison through three qualities: cost, expected makespan, and number of tasks. The model defines relations between plan qualities (better/worse/equivalent) and between plans themselves (cheaper/faster/shorter/better). Logical rules enable inference of which plan is superior when all qualities favor one option.

Second, they introduce ACXON (Algorithm for Contrastive eXplanatory Ontology-based Narratives), which retrieves divergent knowledge between plan pairs and constructs textual contrastive narratives. The algorithm operates at three specificity levels, using casting, clustering, ordering, and grouping rules to generate natural language explanations.

Evaluation against baseline AXON across three planning domains shows ACXON reduces knowledge tuples by 40-70% and communication time by similar percentages, though readability remains comparable. The authors also propose a modification to constrain knowledge retrieval to specific aspects (e.g., only qualities), enabling shorter, potentially personalized explanations.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, down eight percent from 3,157 in 2016. Cases included two kittens beaten to death by their owner, Aaron Barker, who was jailed for 20 weeks, and 40 animals kept in stacked cages without basic necessities. Dogs accounted for most complaints (1,702), followed by cats (737) and horses (281). Nationally, 141,760 complaints were investigated. The RSPCA urged the public to report concerns via their 24-hour helpline.

The article examines how Treasury liquidity patterns explain the stock market adage "Sell in May and come back in November." Analysis of US Treasury cash balances from 2006-2017 shows consistent annual peaks in January, May, and November. The May spike occurs when the government pays tax refunds, primarily to wealthy individuals who tend to invest in stocks, bonds, and real estate, causing a market rise. The November spike results from Fed Treasury buybacks, with ex-bondholders reinvesting in stocks. The February and November patterns relate to Fed open market operations. Recent tax law changes may make 2018-2019 particularly strong for the May effect. The author concludes that liquidity spikes, not seasons or holidays, drive this market pattern, with May being the most consistent due to tax refund flows.

A Karolinska Institutet study of 27,500 UK Biobank participants found that poor sleep is associated with brains appearing older than chronological age. Using MRI scans and machine learning, researchers estimated brain age based on over 1,000 phenotypes and scored sleep quality across five factors. Each 1-point decrease in healthy sleep score widened the brain age gap by about six months, with poor sleepers showing brains appearing one year older on average. Inflammation explained just over ten percent of this link. Other possible mechanisms include impaired brain waste clearance and negative cardiovascular effects. Limitations include healthier-than-average participants and self-reported sleep data.

The Indian tax authority has issued retrospective tax demands exceeding Rs 6,000 crore to banks for allegedly providing free services to account-holders maintaining minimum balances. The demand assumes charges imposed on non-compliant customers represent the value of these services. Banks are expected to challenge the demands; if upheld, costs would likely pass to customers. Critics argue the demand ignores that such charges serve as deterrents rather than service fees, and that it perpetuates "tax terror" despite government promises to address irrational tax demands.

Weak gravitational lensing from surveys like KiDS, DES, and HSC has become a competitive cosmological probe, achieving percent-level measurements of the structure growth parameter S₈. Current precision is limited by two dominant effects: intrinsic alignment (IA) of galaxies and baryonic feedback. This paper focuses on IA, which can bias cosmological parameters by 4-5σ if unaccounted for. Various IA models exist, including NLA, δ-NLA, TT, and TATT, with observations showing strong color-dependence in galaxy alignments. The authors present a novel pipeline to infuse NLA, extended-NLA, and TT models into N-body simulations, introducing the extended-TT model and coupling tidal fields with HOD galaxies to probe non-linear galaxy bias effects. Using the SkySim5000 simulation, they validate models against two-point shear correlation functions and study IA impacts on non-Gaussian statistics, addressing limitations for next-generation surveys like LSST and Euclid.

President Clinton delivered remarks at the signing of the Oslo Accords between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization. He acknowledged U.S. and Russian cosponsorship of the peace process, honored previous diplomatic efforts by Presidents Carter and Bush, and praised Norwegian mediation. Clinton emphasized the historic nature of the agreement between Prime Minister Rabin and Chairman Arafat, which established interim Palestinian self-government. He pledged U.S. support for implementation, warned against enemies of peace, and called for reconciliation between peoples, citing religious texts and historical cooperation. The speech concluded with a commitment to future generations and wishes for peace in Hebrew, Arabic, and English.

A 14-year-old girl was arrested by Kingston Police after a violent outburst at her grandmother's home when a phone didn't work. The girl threw a tantrum, damaging property, then grabbed a baseball bat and smashed a window before fleeing. She was apprehended after a foot chase, charged with mischief, and released to her mother with conditions and a court date.

Oil prices fell below US$56 a barrel after an API report showed U.S. crude inventories rose by 9.9 million barrels, signaling ample supply despite OPEC's record compliance with production cuts. Brent crude dropped to US$55.62 and U.S. crude to US$52.84. Rising U.S. stocks and revived output have limited price gains from OPEC and Russia's 1.8 million barrel daily cuts. A strong U.S. dollar, following signals of faster interest rate rises from Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen, also pressured oil prices. While Saudi Arabia exceeded its cut commitment, Iraq's 40% compliance rate concerns group cohesion, and non-OPEC producers have delivered smaller reductions.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) is a collaborative partnership founded in 2011 by four regional restoration company leaders—Rich Piltch of ARS, Damon Gersh of Maxons Restoration, Ras Fenger of Disaster One, and Andy Goldberg of RestoreCore—to compete with national players like Belfor by providing national service solutions for large insurance and property management companies. By fall 2013, RA had 21 member organizations with $300 million in combined revenue. RA operates as an LLC with equal shareholders, a nine-person board, and membership requirements including $5 million annual revenue, commercial focus, and adherence to "Go-Giver" principles of giving without expecting return. Members pay $5,000 annual dues plus $12,000 for marketing, and referral fees of 5-10% on referred projects. RA faces strategic questions about governance, communication systems, service standards, referral fees, internal competition, and marketing as it scales, particularly after securing a three-year national contract with Forest City Enterprises.

This paper introduces a unified method for deriving codensity presentations of monads through duality and density. The core insight is that codensity monads can be understood as "density + duality": when a functor F decomposes into a dual equivalence E, the opposite of a dense functor G, and a contravariant right adjoint R generating a monad T, then T is the codensity monad of F (Theorem 3.2). This framework simplifies proofs by reducing codensity questions to better-understood density properties.

The authors apply this method to derive both known and new codensity presentations across multiple domains: ultrafilter and filter monads on sets and topological spaces (Theorems 4.1–4.4), double dualization monads including Isbell duality (Theorems 4.5–4.7), Vietoris-type monads on Stone spaces and topological spaces (Theorems 5.1–5.2, 5.4), and probability monads including the expectation, Giry, Radon, and Kantorovich monads (Theorems 6.4, 6.8, 6.11). In each case, the approach yields shorter, more transparent proofs by leveraging standard categorical dualities and density results.

This eulogy honors Henry Clay, born April 12, 1777, who died in 1852 after nearly fifty years of public service. Born the same year America declared independence, Clay became one of the nation's most influential statesmen, serving as Speaker of the House, Senator, Secretary of State, and presidential candidate. His unmatched eloquence, excellent judgment, and indomitable will made him the most prominent politician of his era, though he never won the presidency. Clay played decisive roles in major national crises: promoting the War of 1812, crafting the Missouri Compromise of 1821, opposing nullification, and developing compromise measures on slavery. He consistently advocated for the Union above sectional interests and supported gradual emancipation through the American Colonization Society, which he led for many years. His death prompted national mourning transcending party lines, with even political opponents acknowledging his greatness as a champion of liberty and union.

The passage presents a collection of quotations critical of taxation, banking, corporations, and government systems, attributed to various figures including Robert Kiyosaki, Stefan Molyneux, Bob Dylan, Robert Reich, David Icke, and others, some unknown. The quotes characterize taxation as theft, describe banking as debt-based control, criticize corporate tax breaks, and suggest education controls perception.

On January 30, 2017, Microsoft Corporation entered into an Underwriting Agreement with multiple underwriters for the issuance and sale of $17 billion in senior unsecured notes across seven series with maturity dates ranging from 2020 to 2057 and interest rates from 1.850% to 4.500%. The notes will be issued under an indenture dated May 18, 2009, as supplemented by a Twelfth Supplemental Indenture dated February 6, 2017, with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. Interest will be payable semi-annually on February 6 and August 6, beginning August 6, 2017. The company filed a prospectus supplement dated January 30, 2017, in connection with the offering.

A visiting Harvard Law School professor, Carlos Portugal Gouvêa, was arrested on October 1 for firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during Yom Kippur services. He told police he was hunting rats. Gouvêa was placed on administrative leave and charged with illegally discharging a pellet gun, disturbing the peace, disorderly conduct, and property damage. Police and synagogue officials do not believe antisemitism was a factor. His lawyer called it a misunderstanding of an innocent situation.

Jacob Hackin of Shelly Row, Castle, became the first person in Cambridge prosecuted for leaving dog mess in a park after failing to pay a fixed penalty notice issued by a council enforcement officer who spotted him not clearing up at Midsummer Common. At Cambridge magistrates' court on January 19, Hackin pleaded guilty and was fined £75, plus £125 in costs and a £30 victim surcharge, having called himself "stupid" for not paying the initial penalty. Between April 2015 and March 2016, the council issued 15 fixed penalty notices for dog fouling, with 93% paid within 14 days; proceeds fund street and park maintenance. Executive councillor Anna Smith stated that dog owners must clean up after their pets, bins are widely available, and this prosecution demonstrates such behavior won't be tolerated.

Former CIA officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is on trial in Virginia for allegedly selling top-secret information to China for $25,000. Prosecutors say he was caught with undeclared cash at O'Hare Airport in April 2017, and that text messages on a Chinese-provided phone show he sought payment for secrets, including information about human assets. Defense attorneys claim Mallory was loyal and planned to expose Chinese intelligence operations by feeding them false documents, having notified CIA contacts in February 2017. The trial is rare as espionage cases typically end in plea deals; Mallory faces possible life imprisonment under a statute last used in 2003.

Kelly Keefe will become ERC's first female president on January 1, succeeding Pat Perry after nearly 20 years. Perry will remain as chairman, focusing on NorthCoast 99, ERChealth, and client relations. Keefe, ERC's vice president of training, consulting, and coaching services for almost 13 years, previously worked at Deloitte for eight years. She aims to continue ERC's positive impact regionally and nationally.

This patent application describes a virtual object machine learning system that generates synthetic training data using 3D models to classify highly dynamic subjects. The system addresses the difficulty of training machine learning schemes on real-world subjects like dogs or human hands that vary in pose, texture, and lighting. The system comprises multiple engines: an interface engine receives images for classification; a model engine manages 3D models with rigging structures and trackable key points; a gesture engine arranges models into different poses; a model texture engine applies varied textures; an environment engine controls lighting and backgrounds using spherical HDR images; a render engine generates training images; and a machine learning engine trains classification models. The system can be integrated into messaging applications to analyze images and provide features like gesture-based annotations. The training data generation involves nested loops iterating through models, gestures, textures, and environment variables to create large labeled datasets without manual tagging.

"Upgrade" is a 2018 science fiction horror action film directed by Leigh Whannell. Logan Marshall-Green stars as Grey Trace, a mechanic who becomes paralyzed after a brutal attack that kills his wife. He receives an experimental implant called STEM that restores his mobility with machine-like precision, enabling him to seek revenge. The film explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity's relationship with technology, and the dangers of unchecked technological advancement. While praised for its action sequences, believable near-future setting, and philosophical depth, critics noted its predictable mystery plot and felt it could have benefited from additional runtime for greater dramatic development. Produced by Jason Blum's BH Tilt, the film succeeds across multiple genres despite its micro-budget constraints.

The President communicates to Congress correspondence regarding the Hawaiian Islands and recent events in China. The Hawaiian Islands, strategically located in the Pacific, serve as an important refitting station for American and European vessels, with American ships comprising five-sixths of annual visitors. The President declares U.S. support for Hawaiian independence and recommends funding for a consul to protect American interests there. Regarding China, the President notes the recent treaty between Britain and China opening four new ports to British commerce, and recommends appropriating funds for a commissioner to reside in China to protect American commercial interests and citizens, as no U.S. agent is currently present.

Sen. John McCain criticized President Trump for releasing the GOP-Nunes memo, stating that undermining the rule of law serves Russian interests. McCain, who chairs the Senate Armed Forces Committee, urged officials to stop viewing special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation through a political lens. He acknowledged Russian interference in the 2016 election and expressed concern that it fueled political discord. McCain characterized the memo's release as partisan attacks on the FBI and Department of Justice that benefit only Putin. The memo, spearheaded by House Intelligence Committee Chairman Devin Nunes, alleges FBI surveillance abuse during its investigation of former Trump adviser Carter Page. Democrats called for the release of their own memo on the matter.

A real estate broker (Freeman) sued a purchaser (Polstein) for commission after making active efforts to purchase property for him, but another broker secured an acceptable offer first. The court reversed the judgment for the plaintiff, ruling that: (1) charging a purchaser with commission requires proof of a special contract, which was absent; (2) the broker failed to bring about the sale; and (3) the complaint should have been dismissed based on the plaintiff's own testimony.

Thabane Sigadla, 24, from KwaDabeka, was sentenced to 38 years imprisonment for carjacking, possession of an unlicensed firearm, and possession of ammunition. He hijacked vehicles in KwaDabeka in October 2016 and New Germany in 2017, and was arrested in June 2017 while driving a stolen Mercedes Benz in Claremont Road. The Pinetown Regional Court found him guilty on all counts on 25 June 2018.

Azerbaijan's Health Ministry spokesperson Safaya Ahmadova rejected a US State Department recommendation advising Americans against undergoing surgery in Azerbaijan, stating it reflects US policy toward citizens rather than Azerbaijan's healthcare quality. She noted that foreign patients receive high-level treatment in Azerbaijan and disputed US claims about tuberculosis spread, citing declining figures confirmed by the Global Fund.

AI-Noether is a formal abductive reasoning system that reconciles derived hypotheses with canonical scientific knowledge when both are expressible as polynomial equations. Given background theory axioms and a hypothesized formula, it generates new axioms that replace or augment existing theory to explain the hypothesis. The system uses three steps: Encode (forming solution sets as geometric varieties), Decompose (breaking varieties into irreducible components via primary decomposition), and Reason (testing whether adding component generators allows derivation of the hypothesis). Tested on physical theories including Kepler's Third Law, the system successfully recovered single missing axioms in all cases and multiple missing axioms in 25-60% of cases, with runtimes averaging 0.1-11.1 seconds. The approach addresses limitations of existing AI scientific discovery tools by enabling automated theory modification when data contradicts incomplete or incorrect background theory.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists led by Dr Henry Leung have developed a method to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. The process uses water and Cupriavidus necator bacteria to break down coffee waste over 7-10 days, producing a biopolymer called PHA. The team improved extraction purity from 30% to over 50% by switching to eco-friendly solvents and genetically modifying the bacteria. From 100g of coffee waste, they now yield 1-3g of pure PHA. The team, which began experiments in 2013, seeks industrial partners to commercialise the process within 3-5 years. PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than traditional PVC plastic.

Patient advocacy groups asked the U.K.'s antitrust regulator to investigate large drugmakers and their lobbying organization for alleged coordinated efforts to drive up medicine prices. The Trump administration backed off threatened 100% pharma tariffs. A government shutdown is set to furlough over 32,000 HHS workers and hamper CDC and CMS communication. Other news includes: a whistleblower suit over UnitedHealth's artery disease test; MoonLake's failed autoimmune drug; Lilly's head scientist discussing its GLP-1 pill and Alzheimer's strategy; Amgen reporting its cholesterol shot prevented heart problems; and Uniqure's Huntington's therapy winning recognition in biotech.

The Iowa Supreme Court reversed a district court decision that had allowed Gary G. Kehde to recover unemployment benefits. The court held that Kehde's failure to apply for a rehearing before seeking judicial review did not deprive the district court of jurisdiction, but that the Department of Job Service correctly refused to give effect to Kehde's former employer's withdrawal of its protest after a hearing and decision had already occurred. The court also held that Kehde's possession of a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises constituted misconduct under Iowa law, disqualifying him from benefits, regardless of whether he knew of the specific company rule, because he knowingly violated criminal law and employer expectations of lawful, safe conduct.

A regulation American football field measures 120 yards long by 53.3 yards wide (360 feet by 160 feet), covering approximately 1.32 acres. The playing area between end zones is 100 yards long, with each end zone 10 yards deep. Key markings include goal lines 100 yards apart, yard lines marked every yard with solid lines every five yards, hash marks that vary by level (NFL: 18 feet 6 inches apart; college: 40 feet; high school: 53 feet 4 inches), and sideline numbers positioned at varying distances (NFL: 12 yards; college: 9 yards; high school: 6 yards from sidelines). Sidelines are 6 feet wide, and coaches are typically restricted to between the 25-yard lines.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials have become excessively complex, increasing duration, costs, and burden on participants and staff. ICH guideline E19 encourages reducing irrelevant data collection, but little progress has been made. Merck developed "Lean Design," a method to simplify trials by rebuilding schedules of assessment (SoA) from "Ground Zero" with only essential elements, using principles to evaluate each addition's biological plausibility and necessity. The Faro Smart Design Tool quantifies impacts on hours, costs, and complexity in real-time.

Six protocols across therapeutic areas underwent Lean Design workshops. Recommendations included fewer assessments, modified timing, subsampling for large trials, and excluding routine clinical care data. Changes could reduce participant hours by 4-47 per trial and costs substantially (e.g., $120 million potential savings in one cardiovascular trial). Most teams adopted some changes, though late-stage development limited adoption. Merck has since launched company-wide implementation, training leaders across therapeutic areas. The approach requires leadership support, cross-functional buy-in, and early application in protocol development for maximum benefit.

The IMF praised Ghana's "Ghana beyond Aid" vision and President Akufo-Addo's first-year economic performance as inspirational for Africa. Abebe Selasie, IMF Deputy Director for Africa, encouraged Ghana to "keep on track" at the inaugural "Governor Speaks" series. Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta, who delivered the first address on this new IMF platform, outlined the agenda's goal of achieving self-sufficiency within a generation through domestic resource mobilization and investment in job-creating sectors. He affirmed the government's commitment to maintaining recent high growth levels. Ofori-Atta led Ghana's delegation to the 2018 IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings, which concluded on April 22.

WebRTC VPN bugs have leaked real IP addresses since 2015, though most VPN providers now prevent this. A March 2018 test of 124 VPNs found 20 (16.13%) still leaked IPs via WebRTC. Leaking providers include Astrill, BlackVPN, ChillGlobal, Hola!VPN, Hoxx VPN, and Windscribe Addons. VPNs that protect against WebRTC leaks include ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, and others. Users can test for leaks at expressvpn.com/webrtc-leak-test, ip.voidsec.com, or ipleak.net, and disable WebRTC manually or via browser add-ons. Most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer.

MoviePass has signed a marketing and revenue agreement with an unnamed independent movie distribution company, under which it will promote specific films and earn revenue based on incremental ticket sales increases. The service is demonstrating measurable impact on box office numbers, accounting for 13.21% of Roman J. Israel, Esq.'s opening weekend and 10% of Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri's, with percentages often increasing in second weeks as subscribers catch up on older releases. MoviePass's parent company, Helios and Matheson Analytics, plans to use subscriber data to target advertisements, similar to Facebook and Google's model.

This application describes an improved non-occluding intravascular blood pump designed to reduce hemolysis and blood clotting. The pump comprises a cylindrical shroud with inlet and outlet, a centrally disposed motor sharing a central axis with the shroud, an impeller rotated by the motor, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud. Key design features to minimize hemolysis include: a trumpeted shroud with larger inlet than outlet; raked-back impeller blade leading edges; extended inlet length and bare hub length; matched pillar angle to outlet blade angle; matched flare angles for impeller base and stator tip; optimized clearance between shroud and impeller blades; and controlled wrap angle. The device is designed as a minimally invasive axial flow pump for NYHA Class III-IVa heart failure patients. Through iterative optimization across three project phases using transient CFD simulations and experimental validation, the final prototype (P_31) achieved a 78% improvement in Normalized Index of Hemolysis at 20,000 rpm compared to earlier designs, with maximum shear stress reduced by 150-200 Pa and average impeller surface shear below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm.

MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges council members reassured residents that local recyclables are still being valued, despite a global recycling crisis caused by China's new strict import standards that reject contaminated materials. The MRC belongs to Tricentris, a non-profit managing 33% of Quebec's recyclables, which has invested in research to diversify markets and improve material quality. The MRC has created an online sorting tool at tricycle-mrcvs.ca, and residents can subscribe to the Tricentris Express newsletter for updates.

This 1943 customs case established that the proper dutiable value of Christmas tree ornaments exported from Germany in August 1938 was the per se unit invoice price plus 3½% social assessments, plus costs of packing, containers, and other expenses incident to placing merchandise ready for shipment to the United States. The decision incorporated facts from a prior Woolworth Co. case, finding the ornaments were freely offered for sale in Germany's Sonneberg-Lauscha district. The appeal was dismissed regarding other merchandise.

Asteroid 2025 TF, measuring 1–3 meters in diameter, passed 428 km above Antarctica on October 1, 2025—similar to the International Space Station's altitude. Detected hours after the flyby by the Catalina Sky Survey, it posed no danger. ESA astronomers later confirmed its trajectory with high precision using the Las Cumbres Observatory. Small asteroids like this enter Earth's atmosphere several times yearly, typically breaking apart harmlessly. Objects around 20 meters can cause local damage, while larger ones pose regional or global risks. International monitoring efforts, including ESA's Planetary Defence Office and NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office, track near-Earth objects to predict potential impacts and improve detection systems.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate radiation damage in pure niobium at PKA energies of 1–75 keV and 300 K, comparing four interatomic potentials: EAM, FS-1, FS-2, and SNAP. All potentials capture general cascade features but differ in defect production, clustering, and morphology. At low energies, defect behavior follows trends based on stiffness-to-range ratio, threshold displacement energy, and defect formation energies; at higher energies with subcascade formation, these parameters alone become insufficient. FS-2 produces extended 1/2⟨111⟩ dislocation loops matching experimental observations; FS-1 and SNAP generate more compact C15-like rings and disordered clusters; EAM forms a balanced mix of loops and rings. SNAP produces C15-like rings up to nine atoms that may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ and ⟨100⟩ dislocation loops. Vacancy clustering dominates over interstitial clustering across all potentials. The findings reveal how interatomic potential choice significantly influences defect morphology in irradiated niobium.

A player discusses the advantages of being up in a playoff series, noting it builds confidence and forces opponents to adjust. He considers the four or five day break sufficient, preferring games to practice, and appreciates time to enjoy their San Jose win. He mentions a key teammate is day-to-day with injury, and identifies an opposing player as big, strong, and skilled who will be a tough matchup, emphasizing his team needs to reach its potential.

Live Nation is offering $20 "all-in" tickets to over 2,000 summer concerts from April 30 to May 8 for National Concert Week. The promotion includes over 1.5 million tickets across genres including comedy, country, hip-hop, Latin, metal, rock, and pop. Featured performers include Alan Jackson, Bon Jovi, Kevin Hart, Keith Urban, and Shakira. Tickets are available at livenation.com.

Horsell Lodge near Woking, Surrey, offers specialised residential and dementia care from short-term respite to long-term solutions. Staff collaborate with residents, families, and advocates to create bespoke care plans based on each person's unique history. Residents are encouraged to bring personal possessions for their rooms. The provider advises verifying care home suitability before decisions and notes that service descriptions come from the care home itself, accepting no responsibility for inaccuracies. Contact details for reporting missing or incorrect information are available on their About us page.

Google's $399 Pixel Watch 4 offers satellite emergency communications, multi-day battery life, and outdoor features comparable to the $799 Apple Watch Ultra 3. Both watches last through weekend camping trips, with the Pixel Watch charging faster and fitting more comfortably. The Pixel Watch 4 provides emergency-only satellite calls in the US, while the Ultra 3 allows regular texting in multiple countries. The Pixel Watch excels at sleep tracking through Fitbit and offers easier offline Google Maps integration, though it lacks the Ultra 3's dive computer capabilities, automatic water lock, and hypertension notifications.

Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) often lack high-quality phenotype data due to measurement costs and incomplete participation. Machine learning (ML)-assisted GWAS, which imputes missing phenotypes, has gained popularity but risks pervasive false-positive associations. This study demonstrates that conventional ML-assisted GWAS methods have an 81% replication failure rate for type 2 diabetes, as imputed phenotypes capture indirect associations through predictor variables rather than true genetic effects. The authors introduce POP-GWAS, a statistical framework that uses three sets of GWAS summary statistics—observed phenotype in labeled data, imputed phenotype in labeled data, and imputed phenotype in unlabeled data—to provide unbiased estimates with well-calibrated type-I error while maintaining greater statistical power than conventional GWAS. POP-GWAS requires no assumptions about imputation quality, algorithms, or missingness patterns. Applied to bone mineral density across 14 skeletal sites in UK Biobank, POP-GWAS identified 39% more loci than conventional methods (188 versus 135), including 89 novel associations, and revealed site-specific genetic architecture including head-specific effects at the LGR5 locus.

A Federal High Court in Katsina ordered former Governor Ibrahim Shema remanded in EFCC custody until April 27 on money laundering charges involving alleged misappropriation of N5.7 billion SURE-P funds. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 counts of fraud. The defense filed a bail application, but the prosecution objected, arguing the court lacked jurisdiction before a plea was entered and calling the application premature. Justice Babagana Ashigar remanded Shema to EFCC custody pending a hearing on the written bail application on April 27.

The passage describes a method for designing Boger fluids—dilute viscoelastic polymer solutions with nearly constant viscosity across shear rates—with independently controlled rheological properties. Using polyisobutylene (PIB) dissolved in polybutene/mineral oil mixtures, the authors experimentally determined scaling relationships between fluid design parameters (polymer concentration c, molecular weight M, solvent viscosity ηs) and viscoelastic properties (shear modulus G0, relaxation time τ, first normal stress difference coefficient ψ1). They found that G0 ∝ c^1.00 M^-0.93 ηs^0.01, τ ∝ c^0.10 M^1.54 ηs^0.84, and ψ1 ∝ c^1.41 M^1.86 ηs^1.61, differing from theoretical Zimm model predictions. These empirical relationships were compiled into an invertible design matrix enabling precise fabrication of fluids with target G0, τ, and ψ1 values. The approach was validated by creating fluids with independently varied G0 (while holding τ constant), varied τ (while holding G0 constant), and varied ηs (while holding ψ1 constant), demonstrating successful decoupling of viscous and elastic effects. The method provides a practical framework for tailoring viscoelastic fluids for flow experiments and can be extended to other polymer-solvent systems.

Jason Day will face Louis Oosthuizen, Jason Dufner, and James Hahn in the group stage of the World Golf Championships-Match Play in Texas. Fellow Australian Marc Leishman will play Branden Grace, Bubba Watson, and Julian Suri. Cameron Smith, ranked world No.50, faces Hideki Matsuyama, Patrick Cantlay, and Yusaku Miyazato, needing a strong finish to secure a Masters invitation. An all-Australian final is possible with Day and Leishman on opposite sides of the draw, while Smith could face Day in the semi-finals. The passage lists all 16 groups for the tournament.

Week 6 Idaho high school football saw top-ranked teams maintain their positions, with Bishop Kelly and Eagle surviving close games to stay undefeated. Significant movement occurred at the bottom of the rankings, with Minico (4-1) and Ririe (6-0) entering the top 25. Notable results included Bishop Kelly's 22-20 win over Columbia, Rocky Mountain's 41-7 victory over Centennial, Eagle's 21-14 win over Mountain View, and Timberline's 50-19 rout of Capital. Other undefeated teams including Lakeland (6-0), Sugar-Salem, and Owyhee (5-0) continued strong starts. Middleton and Capital dropped out of the rankings after losses.

The Supreme Court justices return for their 2025-26 term, gathering for the annual "long conference" to review cert petitions accumulated during summer recess. Justice Clarence Thomas recently questioned the use of stare decisis, stating it should not replace critical thinking. Former Justice Anthony Kennedy expressed concern about increasing partisanship and antagonistic discourse in court opinions. The court issued emergency orders allowing the Trump administration to withhold billions in foreign-aid funding and invited review of executive orders on birthright citizenship and Venezuelan protected status. Order lists, typically released Mondays at 9:30 a.m., document actions from private conferences, with long conference lists being particularly significant as they add new cases to the merits docket. Research shows emergency docket decisions correlate with political outcomes, with conservative-resulting cases decided 76% faster than liberal ones in 2024.

Enron transformed from a struggling pipeline company in 1985 into a Wall Street darling trading energy commodities, with stock rising 1,700% over sixteen years. Under Jeff Skilling's leadership, the company created aggressive trading markets for natural gas, electricity, and eventually bandwidth, weather, and other commodities. Skilling cultivated a cutthroat culture hiring elite graduates with no loyalty to traditional energy industry values, implementing a "rank and yank" performance system and offering unlimited bonuses. The company used mark-to-market accounting to book immediate profits and abandoned projects when margins declined. After becoming CEO in February 2001, Skilling faced California energy crisis criticism, a failing telecommunications division, and declining stock prices. He resigned abruptly in August 2001 after six months, leaving Ken Lay to return as CEO and promise a return to core energy businesses.

Euro zone stocks hit their highest in more than a year on January 2, 2017, after manufacturing activity data showed the fastest growth in over five years. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.5% to its highest since December 2015, with Italy's FTSE MIB up 1.5%, Germany's DAX up 0.9%, and France's CAC up 0.5%. The euro fell 0.4% below US$1.05 due to a strengthening dollar, which analysts attributed to expectations of U.S. Federal Reserve rate hikes and Trump administration fiscal expansion. Trading was thin as major Asian, British, Swiss, U.S., and Canadian markets were closed for the New Year holiday. An Istanbul nightclub attack claimed by Islamic State killed 39 people and had limited market impact, though the Turkish lira fell 0.5%. China's manufacturing expanded for a fifth month in December but slowed more than expected. Bitcoin rose above US$1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

The NBA unveiled its full 2017-18 season schedule on Monday, following the earlier release of the Christmas Day and first-week national TV schedules. The schedule includes numerous nationally televised games on TNT, ESPN, ABC, and NBA TV throughout the season from October through April, featuring matchups such as Boston at Cleveland and Houston at Golden State on opening night (Oct. 17), and a Christmas Day slate including Cleveland at Golden State and Houston at Oklahoma City.

This passage describes a Bengali transliteration system where Bengali numerals ০-৯ correspond to 0-9, and special symbols like ্ (Hasant/Viram), ় (Nukta), ঽ (Avagrah), ৺ (Isshar), ৹ (Bengali ana sign), ৲ (Bengali Rupee sign), ৳ (Taka sign), । (Devanagari danda), ॥ (Devanagari double danda), ₹ (Indian Rupee sign), and 卐 (Swastika sign) are assigned keyboard shortcuts using "~". Symbols &, ~, *, :, ^, |, and ' require "~" to type literally. English punctuation and brackets translate directly. Ligatures render automatically; ZWJ (^) creates half-formed consonants, ZWNJ (^^) creates dead consonants, and ZWJ separates combined vowels (ai, au) into individual vowels without appearing in output.

The retail apparel industry faces significant challenges from e-commerce, overexpansion, and trade policy uncertainty. Francesca's Holdings Corp. (FRAN), despite its small size with $488 million in sales and $320 million market cap, demonstrates financial strength with $48 million in cash, no debt, and $57.6 million in free cash flow. The company operates 670+ stores targeting 18-35 year old women, with plans to expand to 900 stores. First quarter 2017 results showed 1% sales growth to $107.7 million but 5% comparable store sales decline and reduced earnings. FY18 guidance projects $518-537 million in sales and $1.07-1.17 diluted EPS. FRAN's valuation metrics are mixed: lowest P/E ratio (8.4) among profitable peers but high price-to-book. The company shows solid profitability with positive ROIC and economic value added, and is repurchasing shares. The author projects share price growth to $14.50-$17.00 within 1-3 years and $27.00-$29.00 within 3-5 years.

Oil prices fell after Israel and Hamas agreed to a Gaza ceasefire deal, calming markets. U.S. stocks saw modest moves near record highs, with the S&P 500 up 0.1% and the Nasdaq little changed. Gold held near its record at $4,054.50 per ounce. PepsiCo shares rose slightly after reporting third-quarter earnings that beat forecasts despite weaker North American demand. Delta Air Lines shares jumped 5.8% after topping profit expectations and forecasting strong full-year results, lifting other airline stocks. Novo Nordisk announced a $4.7 billion acquisition of Akero Therapeutics, sending Akero shares up 18%. European shares were mixed, while most Asian stocks rose, with Japan's Nikkei 225 gaining 1.8%. Trading has been muted recently due to limited major economic reports affecting Federal Reserve interest rate expectations.

Callinex Mines Inc. filed a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) technical report on SEDAR for its Nash Creek and Superjack Projects in New Brunswick, Canada. The 2018 PEA outlines a 10-year, 3,900 tpd open-pit mining operation with a pre-tax IRR of 34.1% and pre-tax NPV of C$230 million. The projects benefit from proximity to infrastructure including highways, transmission lines, and Glencore's Brunswick Smelter. Callinex plans to begin drilling within 10 days to identify satellite deposits. The PEA is preliminary and includes Inferred Mineral Resources considered too speculative for reserve classification. J.J. O'Donnell, P.Geo, approved the technical information.

This study conducted a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using the METRO method to identify genes associated with general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in European American (EA) and African American (AA) populations. Using gene expression data from 1,032 AA and 801 EA participants from the GENOA study and GWAS summary statistics, researchers identified 266 genes for general cognitive function, 23 for WMH, 69 for AD (EA GWAS), and 2 for AD (AA GWAS) after fine-mapping with FOCUS. Key findings include 82, 12, and 45 novel genes not previously identified in original GWAS for general cognitive function, WMH, and AD respectively. The gene ICA1L was identified in both WMH and AD analyses, suggesting it may contribute to overlapping AD and vascular dementia neuropathology. Genes were enriched in pathways related to innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. This represents the first TWAS using expression mapping in multiple ancestries for these traits, with potential implications for identifying pharmaceutical targets for dementia treatment.

Pay for private college presidents continued rising in 2015, with 58 earning over $1 million, up from 39 in 2014, and average compensation reaching $570,000, a 9% increase, according to a Chronicle of Higher Education survey cited by The New York Times. This compared to 3-4% annual wage growth for average American workers. Four Ohio presidents ranked in the top 100: Daniel Curran of University of Dayton was highest-paid in the state at over $2.4 million (No. 8), followed by Barbara Snyder of Case Western Reserve University at $1,152,836 (No. 41), Grant H. Cornwell of The College of Wooster at $911,651, and Marvin Krislov of Oberlin College at $829,913.

The African Union Commission's Department of Trade and Industry organized the First African Union Start Up Fest to address youth entrepreneurship and startup development in Africa. The symposium aimed to assess startup capacity needs, facilitate policy-maker and private sector interaction, establish foundations for an African Association of Start-ups, and build political support for startup development. Speakers emphasized SMEs' role in competitiveness, youth entrepreneurship as a solution to unemployment, and leveraging digital economy opportunities. Key outcomes included planning a follow-up event at the 2018 Transform Africa Summit in Rwanda to discuss creating an African Association of Community Innovation Hub, with the African Union Commission collaborating with i4Policy and participants to draft the agenda.

Offsites can focus on alignment, communication, coordination, or celebration rather than innovation. For breakthroughs, create environments that disrupt routines and foster connections around a shared purpose. Yarrow Kraner's HATCH experiences exemplify this through five BRAVE elements: Environment uses unfamiliar settings and limited connectivity to open people to new ideas; Values center on inclusivity and collaboration to improve the world; Attitude organizes people, programs, and flow accordingly, with careful curation of diverse participants and balanced programming including talks, exercises, activities, and prototype sessions.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Q1 2022 10-Q report with the SEC, covering the quarterly period ended March 31, 2022. The company reported total revenues of $18.8 billion, up from $10.4 billion in Q1 2021, with net income of $3.3 billion compared to $464 million in the prior year period. Automotive revenues totaled $16.9 billion, while energy generation and storage contributed $616 million and services and other contributed $1.3 billion.

Total assets grew to $66.0 billion from $62.1 billion at year-end 2021, with cash and cash equivalents of $17.5 billion. Total liabilities were $30.6 billion, and stockholders' equity increased to $34.1 billion from $30.2 billion. The company had 1.04 billion shares outstanding as of April 19, 2022.

Tesla operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. The company continues to face supply chain constraints, including semiconductor shortages and logistics challenges related to COVID-19 impacts, as well as inflationary pressures affecting costs.

During Q1 2022, $29 million of 2022 Convertible Notes and $23 million of 2024 Convertible Notes were converted and settled. The 2022 Notes were fully settled in March 2022. The company early repaid $380 million of Solar Asset and Loan-backed Notes, recording an $11 million extinguishment charge.

Three operational milestones under the 2018 CEO Performance Award were achieved in Q1 2022, resulting in $11 million of catch-up stock-based compensation expense. Total stock-based compensation was $418 million for the quarter.

Tesla maintains various legal proceedings, including ongoing litigation related to the 2018 SolarCity acquisition, the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and a securities class action concerning potential going-private statements from 2018. The company is also defending against race discrimination claims brought by the California DFEH and a former employee.

Enron-related news from June 7, 2001 includes: Enron and Exelon's Commonwealth Edison signed a Chicago power supply agreement; Enron Broadband invested $30 million in AP Engines; lenders extended talks to save Enron's $3 billion Dabhol Power project in India; Enron leased additional London office space; Indian Prime Minister Vajpayee expressed confidence in resolving the Dabhol dispute; Enron planned to challenge an Indian regulator's arbitration order; and Chicago proposed purchasing 60% of city electricity from Enron. Other energy news included Pacific Hydro's wind farm expansion and California regulators considering ending direct access to alternative power suppliers.

This study examines hybrid immunity from combined COVID-19 vaccination and natural infection, finding that longer intervals between exposures improve antibody responses. Two cohorts were analyzed: one with individuals recovered from COVID-19 before vaccination, and another with vaccinated individuals experiencing breakthrough infections, with exposure intervals ranging from 35-404 days. Results show hybrid immunity produces 3.6-fold higher spike-specific antibody levels and significantly improved neutralizing titers against all SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to vaccination alone, with the greatest improvements against vaccine-resistant variants like Beta and Omicron. Neutralizing titers increased up to 17.6-fold by day 400 post-exposure, with longer intervals correlating with better variant cross-neutralization. The study suggests primary immune responses continue developing for over a year after first exposure, and that delayed vaccination still provides substantial benefits against emerging variants.

Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones addressed his lack of effort on Trevor Lawrence's game-winning touchdown run against the Jacksonville Jaguars, calling it a "teaching point" and "learning lesson." Jones explained he thought the play was over when Lawrence stumbled, causing him to stop pursuing. He denied deactivating his social media accounts to avoid criticism, stating they were deactivated before the game, and said he welcomes constructive criticism as "fuel." DPI (UK), an aluminium frames and lightboxes manufacturer based in Castle Donington, has received a £12,200 grant from Collaborate, a Leicester business scheme funded by the European Regional Development Fund. The three-year-old company, founded by Sandra Wiggins and Paul Tomlinson, will use the funding to purchase an automated saw enabling larger in-house production, faster contract completion, and eventual job creation. Andrew W. Lo introduces MIT's 15.401 Finance Theory course for first-year MBA students, emphasizing finance as the core language of business applicable across all management decisions. He defines finance as mathematics plus money, illustrating its range through three examples: James Simons (quantitative hedge fund manager using advanced mathematics), Warren Buffett (value investor using basic arithmetic), and Jack Welch (GE CEO using financial principles for corporate decisions). The course covers four economic components—households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets—focusing on two fundamental challenges: asset valuation and asset management. Lo explains that time and risk distinguish finance from basic economics, and introduces six core principles including "no free lunch" and self-interested behavior. The course structure includes valuation (discounting, pricing securities), risk analysis, and corporate finance applications, with grades based on participation (10%), a case study (10%), midterm (25%), and cumulative final (55%). Exams draw primarily from provided problem sets, as Lo stresses that learning finance requires active problem-solving rather than passive listening.

President Trump called the House-passed health care bill "mean" during a closed-door lunch with Republican senators, confusing conservatives like Rep. Dave Brat who said Trump had pressured them to pass it. Trump previously praised the bill as "a great plan" at a Rose Garden ceremony. ARDD issued a report on Jordan's legal response to the Syrian refugee crisis, commending governmental agencies and UNHCR for rapid support. This patent application describes a hardware database privacy device that enables differentially private queries on sensitive databases. The system receives client queries with specified privacy parameters (ε,δ), modifies operations to satisfy differential privacy definitions, and returns perturbed results. The privacy system includes specialized engines for count, median, mean, variance, IQR, batch/stochastic gradient descent, random forest, histogram, model testing, and synthetic database queries. Each engine applies appropriate noise mechanisms (Laplacian, Gaussian, or Cauchy distributions) based on global, local, or smooth sensitivity calculations to protect individual record privacy while maintaining analytical utility. The system balances privacy protection with information release through privacy budgets and supports various machine learning models including linear regression, logistic regression, SVMs, and random forests.

Moody's Investor Service stated that despite risks to achieving the 3.3 percent fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019, the Indian government may still meet its target by cutting capital spending. The Indian basket of crude oil rose from $66 to around $75 per barrel.
Greater noctule bats use high-tech sensors to capture birds mid-flight at night, with one bat found in a mist net containing passerine feather and blood in its mouth.
