TyreWatch predictive tyre management launched on 16 May at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus. The system monitors tyre pressure and temperature via wheel rim sensors, sending data to a central server for analysis using cellular and satellite communications. Fleet managers access real-time data through a secure web portal and receive push notifications, while drivers see only a dash-mounted warning light. The AI recommends corrective actions based on identified trends—maintenance alerts for slow pressure loss or critical alerts for rapid changes. Post-operation monitoring continues every 15 minutes to detect overnight punctures. The open architecture integrates with existing vehicle technology and supports third-party telematics providers. Testing showed 95% prevention of tyre-related breakdowns. TyreWatch was developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium, which received £1.2 million from Innovate UK.

The "horns" or double mid screen alignment is an effective basketball strategy to isolate a star ballhandler against a Box & One defense. The double screens allow the star to go either direction, making it difficult for the "Chaser" to defend. After passing the screen, the star can drive to create an outnumbered situation. If unable to drive, options include feeding a rolling screener or kicking out to corner shooters. Variations include screen-and-pop actions where one screener pops out while the other rolls. Single/Double continuity can be initiated by reversing the ball to the top. Successful execution requires proper defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. The Box & One defense uses four players in a zone box with one "Chaser" denying the star player the ball. Game strategies include scouting opponents, educating players on anticipated defensive reads, varying alignments, and attacking weakest defenders.

Japanese government bonds firmed on April 28 after a two-year auction saw strong demand, with investors awaiting Bank of Japan bond-purchasing details for May. The 10-year JGB yield held at 0.015 percent, while two-year yields fell to minus 0.210 percent. The Ministry of Finance's 2.2 trillion yen two-year bond sale drew bids 5.51 times the amount offered, up from 3.82 times previously. The BOJ, which trimmed shorter-dated JGB purchases in April, has reduced market liquidity through its massive asset purchase program. BOJ Governor Haruhiko Kuroda stated the bank's main target is now interest rates rather than bond-buying pace, and that yield targets can be achieved with less buying. The BOJ kept policy unchanged Thursday but offered its most optimistic economic assessment in nine years. March core consumer prices rose slower than expected but increased for a third straight month.

President John Quincy Adams addresses Congress, expressing gratitude for national blessings including healthful seasons, peace, and preserved liberties. Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh announced plans to introduce skill development courses in educational institutions during interactions with students at two women's colleges in Srinagar. A former Walmart employee in Tacoma, Washington, who was fired for allegedly attempting to steal a safe, returned to the store claiming he forgot it there. Loss prevention staff opened the safe and found heroin and Xanax inside. When the 24-year-old arrived and confirmed the container held his "medication," employees called 911. This study examines adrenal vessels from adrenalectomy specimens to identify morphologic similarities between normal adrenal veins, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM). The human adrenal central vein contains unique longitudinal asymmetrical smooth muscle bundles that develop over age. Analysis of 30 cases (2018-2022) of normal tissue, cortical adenomas, and pheochromocytomas revealed that normal adrenal veins exhibit features indistinguishable from arterial FMD, including gapping muscular media and disorganized elastic layers. Adrenal cortical adenomas displayed SAM features including hyalinized arterial walls with CD68-positive macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and medial degeneration. Pheochromocytomas showed thin-walled arteries with muscular wall reduction, myxoid/fibrinoid degeneration, and intimal fibroplasia. Asymmetrical muscle bundles were present in all normal adult adrenal tissues but uncommon in tumors, while SAM was commonly observed in both neoplasm types. Hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis were the most common complications. No FMD-like lesions were identified in arteries outside the adrenal gland or in fetal autopsy cases. The findings support unifying FMD and SAM into a spectrum of a single entity and suggest pathogenic mechanisms involving abnormalities of adrenal hormone actions or receptor signaling affecting vascular smooth muscle.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison for the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law, plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation. Despite her claims of innocence and lack of evidence, Judge Stephen Everett cited her "utter lack of remorse." Adelson was convicted of plotting the murder-for-hire with her son Charlie Adelson, who used a girlfriend to hire two hit men. Prosecutors said the motive was moving Markel's ex-wife Wendi Adelson to South Florida with their children. Donna's husband Harvey also maintained her innocence, calling her "an innocent woman."

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2021, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021, via a press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The company is incorporated in Washington, with headquarters in Redmond, and its common stock (MSFT) trades on NASDAQ, along with 3.125% Notes due 2028 and 2.625% Notes due 2033. Cloud-based High-Performance Computing (HPC) architectures are becoming dominant in manufacturing, with public cloud expected to be the most important architecture, followed by hybrid models that combine on-premises infrastructure with cloud scalability. Unlike traditional in-house HPC—which faces limitations in expansion, requires high CAPEX investment, and lacks flexibility for adjusting to new usage scenarios—cloud-based HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) offers OPEX-based cost structures, on-demand scalability, and access to cutting-edge technologies without upfront investment. IDC research indicates that 81% of industrial HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models, while benefits include improved agility for product development, enablement of digital twins and predictive maintenance services, enhanced global collaboration, and greater security and resilience. However, cloud HPC still requires skilled IT personnel for configuration and operation. IDC recommends manufacturing enterprises evaluate operating models based on specific utilization, budget, and flexibility needs; adopt scalable solutions focusing on security and energy efficiency; create holistic data strategies ensuring a single source of truth; and leverage external expertise for implementation.

Two pieces of ammunition were found in a bathroom at Litchfield High School in Illinois on Wednesday at 8:40 a.m., prompting a soft lockdown of the high school and middle school. Students were dismissed to parents around 10:00 a.m. Multiple police officers responded to the scene. Wednesday was the last day of classes, with early dismissal scheduled before noon.

The Yankees exemplify baseball's shift from starting pitching to bullpen emphasis, evidenced by Aroldis Chapman's large closer contract. Following a tradition begun under Joe Torre, the team continues prioritizing relievers like Chapman and Betances for 2017. While this trend changes the game's presentation, it raises questions about the value of high-priced starters, as 2015 starters averaged only 87 pitches per game and quality starts have declined. Hall of Famer John Smoltz advocates pitching more to build strength, contrasting with current practices. A new study funded by Boeing and published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences suggests passengers can reduce their risk of catching colds or flu by sitting in window seats and remaining seated. Researchers from Emory University and Georgia Tech observed 10 flights and found that while 80 percent of aisle seat passengers moved during flights, only 43 percent of window seat passengers did. Mathematical modeling indicated that if an infectious passenger sat in an aisle seat, on average only one other person out of approximately 150 would be infected, with the 11 closest passengers facing the highest risk. However, the study had limitations: researchers observed only one person coughing and found none of the 18 viruses tested for. Independent researchers noted that the small sample size makes generalizations difficult, though they acknowledged the research provides novel insights into disease transmission on aircraft.

The SuperTrend indicator, created by Oliver Seban, is a trend-following tool that signals trend direction, continuation, and changes. A backtest on the S&P 500 over 60 years using weekly timeframes with default parameters (ATR period 10, multiplier 3) showed a 65.79% win rate, 67% accuracy, and max drawdown of 24.6% versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold. The indicator appears as a line on price charts—green when price is above (uptrend), red when below (downtrend)—reversing when price crosses the previous period's value. It calculates using median price and ATR to create upper and lower bands, following one band at a time with constraints preventing the lower band from decreasing or upper from increasing. Best suited for trending instruments and long-term investments, it works on multiple timeframes but requires backtesting for optimization. The indicator is lagging, can be combined with RSI, moving averages, or Bollinger Bands, and adapts to volatility by widening or tightening. Limitations include false signals in choppy markets.

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of the 3-person AI policy nonprofit Encode, accused OpenAI of using intimidation tactics to undermine California's SB 53 AI safety law and targeting critics through subpoenas. Calvin claimed OpenAI used its lawsuit against Elon Musk as pretext to imply Musk secretly funded Encode and other critics. President Hoover transmits his 1932 State of the Union message to Congress, reporting that the nation remains at peace with effective national defense, reduced industrial conflict, and public health at record levels. He notes widespread economic hardship from the continuing worldwide depression, citing emergency measures that prevented disaster and began showing improvement by July 1932. Hoover presents data showing declining mortality rates and improving business indicators from August to October 1932. He recommends three priorities for recovery: balancing the federal budget through over $830 million in spending cuts, immediate reorganization of the banking system, and international economic cooperation. His budget proposes limiting public works to existing commitments ($442.8 million vs. $717.3 million current year), continuing government employee furloughs, adding an 11% temporary salary reduction for earnings above $1,000, and eliminating certain veterans' payments while protecting war-disabled veterans. He advocates extending manufacturers' excise taxes uniformly and reorganizing over 50 executive agencies. Hoover emphasizes that banking reform is essential, noting 4,665 bank failures since 1930 with $3.3 billion in deposits lost, contrasting this with no bank failures in Britain or Canada. He supports world disarmament, a World Economic Conference, and maintaining war debt payments while offering methods to address exchange difficulties. Concluding, Hoover stresses American individualism, limited government participation in economic life, and the spiritual foundations of national ideals.

Case Western Reserve University research published in The Journal of Family Violence estimates the federal government spends $55 billion annually addressing effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. The study found exposed children experience higher health-care costs, crime rates, and lower productivity as adults, with lifetime economic costs per person reaching nearly $50,000—including $11,042 in medical costs, $13,922 in crime-related costs, and $25,531 in productivity losses. Researchers noted this first-of-its-kind economic analysis can help policymakers justify preventive and therapeutic interventions.

In D.L. Cromwell Investments, Inc. v. NASD Regulation, Inc., plaintiffs—targets of a federal grand jury investigation—sought an injunction to prevent NASD Regulation from compelling testimony regarding Pallet Management Systems, Inc., punishing invocation of Fifth Amendment privileges, and misusing grand jury materials. The court suggested NASD improve physical and administrative separation between CPAG and DOE to avoid future questions about independence.

The Shepherd Express criticizes We Energies, a regulated monopoly with rates set by the Public Service Commission (PSC) to provide over 10% return on assets, for high utility costs and executive pay. In Hogg's Estate, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court held that the word "grandchildren" in a will unambiguously included all grandchildren, including those of afterborn children, despite the testator having only four named children when executing the will in 1855. The majority, led by Bok, J., affirmed the auditing judge's decision, rejecting the argument that only grandchildren of named children should inherit. The court cited precedents establishing that general terms like "children" and "grandchildren" include all members of the class unless expressly excluded, and that "per stirpes" governs distribution shares without indicating discrimination between ancestral lines. Steakne, J., dissenting with Sinkler, J., argued the testator's intent was clearly limited to grandchildren of his four named children, and that including grandchildren of afterborn children—whose parents already received intestate shares—produced an unjust distribution contrary to the testator's scheme. The exceptions were dismissed and the account confirmed.

This document is a legal agreement and technical specification from AMD (2018–2025) defining the SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol. The agreement restricts use of the specification to reviewing for product design and providing feedback, grants no intellectual property rights, disclaims all warranties, and imposes export control obligations. The technical content standardizes a 4KB decrypted memory area for guest-hypervisor communication during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), where encrypted guest register state must be selectively shared. Key protocol elements include: GHCB MSR protocol for version negotiation and page registration; hypervisor feature advertisement via bitmap; VMGEXIT instruction handling with defined exit codes for I/O, MSR access, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, AP creation, and restricted injection features; SMP booting mechanisms including AP Jump Table and AP Creation NAE events; and support for SEV-TIO trusted devices and Secure AVIC. The specification documents multiple protocol versions (1, 2 with revisions 2.01–2.04) with incremental features like multi-VMPL support, timer/IPI restricted injection, and VLEK certificate retrieval.

The Dogs of the Dow (DOD) is a stock-picking strategy that invests in the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks from the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), rebalanced annually. The COVIDFast assay is an RNA extraction-free RT-qPCR test for SARS-CoV-2 detection using either anterior nares swab (SwabFAST) or saliva (SalivaFAST) samples. The method bypasses the laborious nucleic acid extraction step that creates bottlenecks in conventional PCR testing by using optimized buffers—viral transport buffer (VTB) for swabs and TCEP-containing buffer for saliva—combined with proteinase K digestion. The system uses standardized 2 mL bar-coded cryovials with externally threaded screw caps for both sample types, enabling automated high-throughput processing with compatible decappers and electronic pipetting equipment. Analytical validation showed equivalent performance between extraction-free and extraction-based methods, with a limit of detection of 4 copies/µL for both specimen types. Clinical validation demonstrated 100% positive and negative percent agreement for swabs and 98.8%/99.4% for saliva compared to extraction-based methods. Real-world deployment of 409,883 tests showed 8.10% overall positivity, with SwabFAST comprising 83.62% of tests despite both options being available. The extraction-free approach reduces costs, contamination risk, and turnaround time to 24 hours for over 5,000 samples daily.

The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index reported a 6.3% annual gain in February 2018, up from 6.1% the previous month. Coach Quenneville discusses his team's playoff experience, resilience, and preparation. In Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co., the Michigan Supreme Court reversed a judgment for the plaintiff in an action on an accident insurance policy. The court held that while letters from the defendant and its agents were admissible to show waiver of proof of death requirements, the insurance company's denial of liability for death benefits—recalling proof blanks and offering only to consider disability claims—excused the plaintiff from making proof of death but did not waive or estop the time limitation for bringing suit. The plaintiff failed to sue within the 14-month contractual period after the June 1918 denial, and her efforts to gather proofs with an agent's encouragement did not extend the deadline. The court distinguished between waiver of proof requirements and waiver of suit limitations, granting a new trial only on the disability indemnity claim.

This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework, DNN-Transformer-AE, for corporate tax risk supervision. The model integrates three modules: a Deep Neural Network for static enterprise features, a Transformer for temporal financial data, and an Autoencoder for anomaly detection. This study investigates the orbital degree of freedom (ODF) in magnon-phonon coupled systems, addressing a gap in understanding how orbital angular momentum (OAM) transfers between these bosonic quasiparticles. The authors demonstrate that ODF in magnon-polarons originates from two mechanisms: global system rotation and quantum geometry of wavefunctions. Using a 2D honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order as a model system, they show that magnetoelastic coupling breaks parity-time symmetry, enabling phonons to acquire finite OAM through hybridization with magnons. This quantum geometric OAM, described by the quasi-quantum geometric tensor, persists even without lattice rotation. The study predicts measurable transverse voltages from accumulated electric polarization when temperature or strain gradients excite magnon-polarons, with the orbital contribution dominating over spin effects at low magnetic fields. The findings establish theoretical foundations for phonon orbitronics and demonstrate that magnon-phonon coupling enhances electrical control over magnetization and phononic transport.

The International Monetary Fund advised Saudi Arabia to pace economic reforms to avoid harming growth while praising efforts to reduce oil dependency. The kingdom, facing $200 billion in deficits over three years and a forecast $53 billion shortfall this year, targets budget balance by 2019 under its Fiscal Balance Programme, though the IMF recommends 2022. Planned austerity measures include five-percent value-added tax and fuel price hikes, expected to raise $67.7 billion by 2020.

The Value Area trading strategy uses volume profile (market profile) to identify price ranges where 70% of trading activity occurred during a specific period, helping traders find support/resistance levels and potential entry/exit points. The 70% threshold approximates one standard deviation from the mean. Common applications include intraday and daily timeframes across futures, stock, and forex markets. Traders generate signals by watching for breakouts, reversals, or pullbacks from these levels, often using candlestick patterns and momentum oscillators for confirmation. Advantages include clear identification of market-valued price levels; disadvantages include false signals and changing value areas over time. Risk management requires stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification. The strategy can be difficult to backtest due to varying rules and settings.

This study investigates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) using first-principles calculations and statistical mechanics. The researchers parameterized an embedded cluster expansion (eCE) model to efficiently predict formation energies across the composition space, then extended a coarse-graining method to compute finite-temperature equilibrium vacancy concentrations within the canonical ensemble.

Key findings include: (1) Adding group 4 elements (Ti, Zr, Hf) to refractory MPEAs significantly enhances vacancy concentrations by 10-100× compared to alloys containing only groups 5 and 6 elements; (2) Equilibrium vacancy concentrations strongly depend on short-range order and bonding energies—elements forming strong bonds decrease vacancy concentrations while unfavorable bonding increases them; (3) The rigorous coarse-graining method outperforms special quasi-random structure (SQS) approaches, which underestimate vacancy concentrations by factors of 3-7 due to inadequate treatment of chemical potentials and finite-temperature ordering effects; (4) Approximately 50-60% group 4 element concentration is needed to achieve vacancy concentrations of 10⁻⁴–10⁻⁵ at 1500°C for sufficient vacancy-mediated diffusion. The methodology enables efficient exploration of high-dimensional composition spaces to identify alloy chemistries with tailored kinetic properties.

Astronomers are preparing extensive scientific observations for the upcoming total solar eclipse across the United States, the best in nearly a century. Scientists will use ground-based telescopes, the International Space Station, 11 satellites, three aircraft, and over 70 high-altitude balloons to study the sun's corona, Earth's weather, space weather, and effects on animals and plants. The federal government is spending approximately $7.7 million on eclipse research. Citizen scientists can participate through projects like Citizen CATE, which provides special telescopes to volunteers, the iNaturalist app for tracking animal and plant reactions, and UC Berkeley's Eclipse Megamovie 2017. Eclipses remain uniquely valuable for solar research because the moon blocks the sun's brightness more effectively than artificial methods, allowing study of the corona where space weather originates. Past eclipse observations led to the discovery of helium in 1868 and provided crucial evidence for Einstein's theory of general relativity in 1919.

In *Waterhouse v. Gibson*, the court held that a conveyance by extent (execution levy) follows the same construction rules as a conveyance by deed. Buildings on land pass with the land in both cases, regardless of whether their foundations are sunk below the surface. Parol evidence is inadmissible to show buildings were excluded from an extent when the official returns contain no such exception. The court rejected defendants' evidence that the creditor's attorney intended to exclude the buildings, noting that exceptions for tenant-erected trade buildings do not apply to owner-erected structures. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff.

A Danish study found children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis face higher risks of developing rheumatoid arthritis (nearly three times), thyroid disease (2.2 times), and epilepsy (1.6 times). The research analyzed over 2,100 children of women with the disease and 1.3 million children of women without it, born over 25 years. Published in Arthritis Care & Research, the findings suggest doctors should monitor child development for these conditions when mothers have rheumatoid arthritis during pregnancy.
