President-elect Trump criticized a photo of himself on CNN's book "Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything," calling it the "worst cover photo of me" in a January 2, 2017 tweet. The photo shows Trump pointing. CNN released a 2017 commemorative version with a different cover photo. The tweet generated social media responses, with some users calling Trump vain for focusing on the photo while others posted unflattering images of him. The incident follows other instances where Trump has taken issue with photos used in news articles or book covers.

The Bank of Japan will not rush to exit ultra-loose monetary policy due to risks of sharp yen appreciation and stubbornly low inflation, despite solid economic growth. While the BOJ does not officially target the yen, preventing abrupt yen rises remains a priority to support the export-reliant economy. Any yield target hike next year would be modest and one-off, not the start of a full rate hike cycle. Political pressure, an impending leadership change when Governor Kuroda's term ends in April, and Abe's focus on stock prices further complicate normalization efforts. The BOJ is already slowing government bond purchases but its balance sheet continues rising rapidly. Analysts warn that delaying normalization leaves limited tools to fight future economic shocks.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars defendants from directly appealing contested post-judgment restitution orders entered pursuant to plea agreements that contemplated restitution with capped amounts. Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI, agreeing to pay restitution up to $53,653.45. After the court later ordered $40,933.45 in restitution, Hoffman's direct appeal was dismissed. The court ruled that such restitution orders constitute part of the "sentence" under § 13-4033(B), and appellate review must be sought through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. The decision interpreted the 1992 amendment's legislative intent to reduce appellate burdens, rejected arguments that § 13-4033(A)(3) authorized direct appeals, and disapproved two prior cases that had assumed jurisdiction over similar appeals without analyzing § 13-4033(B).

This study describes a blood-based liquid biopsy test for non-invasive detection of glial malignancy (GLI-M) using circulating glial cells (CGCs). The test enriches CGCs from peripheral blood using a proprietary medium that selectively induces apoptosis in non-malignant cells, followed by immunocytochemistry profiling for GFAP and OLIG2 markers. Analytical validation demonstrated 92.5-95% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 95.3-96.9% accuracy. Clinical validation across multiple studies showed >99% sensitivity and 100% specificity for differentiating GLI-M from benign brain tumors (BBT), with 100% concordance in orthogonal FISH verification for EGFR amplification. The 5 mL blood test provides a minimally invasive alternative to surgical biopsy for patients presenting with intracranial space-occupying lesions, enabling faster diagnosis while reducing procedural risks. Limitations include inability to detect rare subtypes like CNS lymphoma and gliosarcoma, and no differentiation of tumor grade or subtype.

The author describes living with panic disorder (PD), which affects 2-3% of Americans, and shares techniques for managing panic attacks. Panic attacks differ from anxiety: they are sudden bursts of intense fear lasting under 30 minutes, often without triggers in PD. Common symptoms include rapid heartbeat, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, and fear of dying. Recommended coping strategies include: learning the physiological signs to reduce fear; writing facts and mantras on index cards; visualizing panic as a passing wave; using smartphone games for distraction; and practicing slow, deep breathing daily to prepare for attacks.

This study used 2019 NSECE Household Survey data to identify five distinct child care and early education (CCEE) search types through latent class analysis, based on up to two information sources families reported using. The five search types were: (1) CCR&R or friends/family, (2) internet search or social media, (3) known providers or friends/family, (4) social media or friends/family, and (5) friends/family or internet search. The analytic sample comprised 1,190 households with children under age 6 who conducted a recent search considering multiple providers. Search types varied significantly by whether families sought information on types of care, whether the child had a condition affecting care provision, and geographic region. Search Types 1 and 3 were more likely used for children with such conditions. Search Type 5 was more common in the Northeast, while Search Type 3 was more prevalent in the West. The study found limited variation by other family and child characteristics.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU features 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100), and 108 SMs with third-generation Tensor Cores delivering 16x higher mixed-precision performance than FP32. Key innovations include Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, Compute Data Compression (up to 4x bandwidth improvement), and third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. The architecture introduces asynchronous copy operations, L2 cache residency controls, and hardware-accelerated barriers in CUDA 11. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, and includes five NVDEC units and a 5-core NVJPG decode engine. The DGX A100 system delivers 5 PFLOPS in a 6U form factor, using eight A100 GPUs interconnected via NVSwitch with 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth.

This MIT lecture covers web security vulnerabilities and defenses. The professor demonstrates the Shellshock bug, where attackers exploit CGI servers that set Bash environment variables from HTTP headers, allowing arbitrary code execution. He also demonstrates cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, showing how malformed HTML can bypass browser filters to execute attacker-controlled JavaScript.

The lecture discusses XSS defenses including: browser-based filters (imperfect due to complex HTML/CSS/JavaScript grammars), HTTP-only cookies (prevents JavaScript cookie access but not CSRF attacks), privilege separation (hosting untrusted content on separate domains like googleusercontent.com), content sanitization (encoding special characters, though complex grammars limit effectiveness), using less expressive markup languages like Markdown, and Content Security Policy (CSP) which restricts content sources and prevents inline JavaScript and eval().

The lecture covers SQL injection attacks where unsanitized user input in database queries allows attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands. It discusses stateless authentication using Message Authentication Codes (MACs) as an alternative to cookies, with AWS as an example, though key storage and revocation remain challenges. DOM storage and client-side certificates are mentioned as other alternatives.

Protocol vulnerabilities include URL parsing inconsistencies between browser components (like Flash vs. browsers), and the "GIFAR" attack where malicious JAR files are embedded in valid GIF images to bypass upload restrictions and execute Java via XSS. The lecture concludes with covert channel attacks using timing: CSS-based sniffing (detecting visited links via color), cache-based attacks (timing cached vs. non-cached resources), DNS-based attacks (timing DNS resolution), and rendering attacks (timing page rendering), demonstrating how browser features intended to help users can be exploited for information leakage.

Eagles wide receiver A.J. Brown expressed frustration Wednesday about his limited production this season, having exceeded 30 receiving yards only once despite being the team's top receiving threat. UK scientists found that bumblebee queens exposed to neonicotinoid pesticides were 26% less likely to lay eggs, potentially causing population decline. The study, published in Nature Ecology and Evolution, used thiamethoxam levels similar to those near treated canola fields. Lead researcher Nigel Raine noted uncertainty about how this compares to other threats like nutrition loss and parasites. The findings may support EU efforts to make permanent a 2013 temporary moratorium on neonicotinoid use, though pesticide companies and some farmers oppose restrictions, citing reduced canola yields and increased alternative pesticide spraying.

Swarthmore students, typically aged 18-22, often take themselves too seriously despite the low-stakes nature of college. While academic and personal excellence matter, students should embrace self-deprecating humor when making mistakes—whether academic errors, social embarrassments, or daily mishaps. The campus environment is uniquely intense and idiosyncratic, but mistakes rarely have life-altering consequences. Students should also extend grace to others, assuming good intent when someone misspeaks or causes offense, seeking clarification before judgment. Laughter serves as a valuable coping mechanism and defense against the pressures of campus life.

The speaker discusses solutions for problem set 8, noting some problems are new and untested. Problem 8.2 requires background not yet covered, while 8.3 involves BCJR algorithm decoding that may be deferred. The lecture then covers Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes, explaining how the m-fold tensor product of a 2×2 matrix generates these codes. The Hadamard transform over binary field F2 is self-inverse. Reed-Muller codes are generated by rows of the universal matrix with specific weights. Graphical realizations using simple constraint nodes (equality and zero-sum) are constructed recursively, though these contain cycles. For the 8,4,4 code, reductions yield a simple realization with 12 constraints. Agglomeration produces cycle-free trellis realizations with higher complexity. The speaker then introduces the sum-product algorithm for a posteriori probability (APP) decoding on cycle-free graphs, which becomes iterative and approximate on graphs with cycles. APP decoding computes probability distributions for variables given received sequences, useful for feeding soft decisions between component decoders in concatenated codes. The algorithm uses past-future decomposition and sum-product update rules, completing in finite time on cycle-free graphs.

This study proposes a brain-predicted disease duration (DD) gap as a neuroimaging biomarker for multiple sclerosis (MS) severity and progression, complementing the established brain-age gap (BAG) metric. Using deep learning on structural MRI scans from 4,392 patients across 15 European centers, researchers trained models to predict chronological age and disease duration in people with MS (PwMS). The DD gap—measuring deviation from typical disease trajectory—showed low correlation with BAG (r=0.06), indicating relative independence between ageing-like and disease-specific processes. The DD gap explained additional variance in physical disability (EDSS) beyond BAG alone (ΔR²=0.012 cross-sectionally, ΔR²=0.064 longitudinally), and its annualized change correlated with disability worsening (r=0.50). In contrast, an alternative MS-specific brain-age model showed higher correlation with BAG (r=0.35) and failed to significantly improve disability prediction. Interpretability analyses revealed that DD predictions were sensitive to lesion presence, while BAG was not. The study demonstrates that complementing brain-age models with disease-specific metrics enables more comprehensive assessment of brain damage in PwMS.

The Situation Calculus is a logical framework for specifying and reasoning about dynamical systems in artificial intelligence. The frame problem—providing axioms for what changes and what remains unchanged during action execution—was addressed by Reiter's successor state axioms for Markovian systems, where action preconditions and effects depend only on the current situation. Gabaldon extended this to non-Markovian systems, allowing dependence on past situations, applicable to domains like database transactions and smart contracts. Scherl and Levesque extended Reiter's solution to knowledge-producing actions. This paper uses non-Markovian Situation Calculus to model a taxonomy of obligations, building on prior work embedding deontic logic via an accessibility relation fluent O(s′, s) representing "s′ is deontically accessible from s."

Five years after archaeologists confirmed Richard III's remains were found beneath a Leicester car park, four people share how the discovery changed their lives. Dominic Smee, who has the same spinal condition as the king, became his body double for a documentary, overcoming low self-esteem to become a confident public speaker. Michael Ibsen, a descendant who provided DNA confirming the identity, found himself in a media frenzy and was asked to make the coffin. Mike Mistry, the car park attendant who unwittingly painted an "R" marking the burial spot, lost his job but remains connected to the site's legacy. Musician Ian Churchward transformed his hobby into a career, producing six albums of Ricardian folk-rock music.

The TPS7H500x-SP series consists of radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. The TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP feature configurable maximum duty cycles via the DCL pin (100% when connected to VLDO, 75% when floating, or 50% when connected to AVSS), while the TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% maximum duty cycle. The controllers include programmable features such as dead time, leading edge blank time, soft-start, hiccup mode operation with cycle-by-cycle current limiting, external fault protection, and slope compensation. Peak current mode control is implemented using the CS_ILIM pin with a 150 mV offset and 1.05 V overcurrent threshold. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart at 160°C. The devices support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz for GaN-based designs and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter demonstrates component selection including transformer turns ratio of 2.5, 40 μH primary inductance, 170 V GaN FETs for primary switches, 80 V GaN FETs for synchronous rectifiers, and 2.3 mF output capacitance for radiation-induced single event transient mitigation. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds, and routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes.

Junior County, a top-five shooting guard in the 2026 class, has committed to UConn men's basketball. The 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy (Utah) is ranked No. 43 overall and No. 4 at his position in the SC Next 100. County chose UConn over other finalists after his official visit last weekend, citing his relationship with coach Dan Hurley and the program's intensity as key factors. VentureWire newsletter dated November 14, 2000, covering private company business news. Beijing ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising, and feng shui advice by Wednesday to cool its housing market. The targeted websites, including Lianjia and I Love My Home, cannot promise investment returns, assist with residence permits or school enrollment, spread rumors, or offer financing advice. Authorities aim to address soaring home prices, rising household debt, credit risks, and affordability concerns. These measures follow March restrictions that raised down payment requirements and limited mortgage terms.

Researchers from OIST and collaborators traced fungal origins to 1.4-0.9 billion years ago using fossil evidence and horizontal gene transfer analysis, finding fungi diversified hundreds of millions of years before land plants. These ancient fungi partnered with algae, recycled nutrients, broke down rock, and created primitive soils, acting as ecosystem engineers that prepared Earth's surface for terrestrial life.

The passage argues that U.S. strategic superiority prevented war during the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, but subsequent defense policies ignored Soviet aggressive intent and military buildup. By 1980, the Soviet Union had surpassed America in most strategic military categories. The Carter Administration's response to Soviet actions was characterized as weak, inconsistent, and vacillating, damaging American credibility. The author contends that weakness provokes aggression, citing World War II as precedent, and advocates restoring military strength, consulting allies, combating terrorism, and maintaining principled leadership to achieve peace.

This email from Ann M. Schmidt contains news clippings about Enron from October 19-20, 2001. United Airlines took subtle jabs at rivals Delta and American during its Thursday earnings call, positioning itself as a premium carrier. United highlighted its uncrowded lounges, contrasting with Delta's overcrowded Sky Clubs, and touted seatback entertainment on 64% of its fleet—over 146,000 seats across 765 planes—while American largely refuses to install screens domestically, opting for tablet holders instead. China's top official in Hong Kong, Zhang Xiaoming, warned that Beijing will not tolerate activities threatening national sovereignty, challenging central government authority, or using Hong Kong to destabilize the mainland. The statement follows rising tensions over Beijing's tightening controls on the semi-autonomous territory, including the ousting of pro-independence lawmakers. Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule in 1997 with guaranteed autonomy and freedoms for 50 years, but critics say these are eroding. Concerns include Beijing's suppression of dissent, the 2015 disappearance of five booksellers who later appeared in mainland detention, and the potential election of hardliner Regina Ip as the city's next leader after unpopular incumbent Leung Chun-ying announced he would not seek re-election.

MusConv is an online software program that enables users to transfer playlists from Spotify to Amazon Music. Users select their source, choose the playlist, and pick Amazon Music as the destination before clicking 'Transfer'. The software is available in three subscription tiers: Basic offers unlimited songs and playlists per session, CSV export, and 2 years of free updates; Professional adds batch importing and 3 years of updates; Ultimate includes Apple Music support, priority support, lifetime updates, and duplicate track deletion.

An athlete discusses their pre-game preparation routine, including wearing a hoodie and headphones to focus and block out distractions. National Health Center Week is being celebrated by Caring Health Center in Springfield and over 1,200 community health centers nationwide. Monday featured Elected Officials Day with local, state representatives and community leaders discussing health center missions and honoring healthcare recipients. The observance ends August 19.

A whistleblower claims Ohio's Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT), which closed in January 2018, used ActivTrak software to intentionally inflate attendance figures for state funding. The former technology employee reported to state officials and the auditor that school officials ordered staff to manipulate student data. The state previously demanded ECOT return $60 million for overpayments in 2015-2016 and assessed another $19 million penalty for 2016-2017. State officials met with the whistleblower in December about his August 2017 concerns. ECOT's former lobbyist dismissed the allegations, while Democratic candidates called for criminal investigation. The state auditor incorporated the claims into an unreleased financial audit.

President Clinton delivered his final Oval Office address, expressing gratitude for serving two terms and highlighting achievements including 22 million new jobs, lowest unemployment in 30 years, welfare reform, crime reduction, and environmental protections. He urged three priorities for the future: maintaining fiscal responsibility to eliminate national debt, continuing global leadership to address terrorism and poverty while expanding trade benefits, and uniting America's diverse population around shared values. He wished success to incoming President George W. Bush and affirmed his continued service as a citizen.

This paper examines blockchain technology programs in US higher education to address the enterprise knowledge gap in implementing blockchain solutions. The authors analyzed 361 blockchain courses from 151 AACSB-accredited universities (28% of 533 schools), finding most courses are undergraduate-level (72%) and concentrated in Computer Science (70 courses) and Information Systems (67) departments, with Business fields overall offering the most courses (216). Course categories span Fundamentals & Overview (140 courses), Digital Assets & Cryptocurrencies (71), Technical Development (66), Business Implications (33), Law and Compliance (29), Supply Chain and Governance (12), and Interplay with Other Technologies (6). The study reveals blockchain education increasingly intersects with AI, IoT, and other emerging technologies, and emphasizes that successful blockchain integration requires not only technical skills but also social, methodological, and personal competences across multiple enterprise functions including management, finance, supply chain, IT, and law.

Seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg created "Heart Cents" to raise money for heart patients after his grandfather died of heart disease. He placed collection buckets in Savannah and Richmond Hill, raising over $200 for St. Joseph's Hospital. A donor family matched his funds, bringing the total to $422. Later, another anonymous donation added $250, for a final total of $672.14. The money helps cover transportation and co-pays for heart patients. Joseph plans to continue fundraising year-round to honor his grandfather.

The passage describes SPI communication protocols for the ADS868xW series ADC devices. A valid write operation requires minimum 32 SCLKs per data transfer frame. Read protocols fall into three categories: legacy SPI-compatible with single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible with dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) protocol.

On power-up or reset, the device defaults to SPI-00-S protocol. Alternative SPI protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S) are selected by programming SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in SDI_CTL_REG, with SDO_MODE[1:0] set to 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. The RVS output remains low during SPI-compatible data transfers.

For dual SDO-x operation, SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] bits in SDO_CTL_REG must be set to 11b, enabling the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin as SDO-1. Dual mode launches two bits per SCLK edge, requiring half the SCLK cycles compared to single mode for the same data output.

This patent disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring devices and methods that combine data from multiple measurement sites to generate single measurements of physiological parameters. Conventional pulse oximeters process data from single sites independently, while this disclosure enables combining raw or minimally processed sensor data from multiple sites—such as cephalic sites (nose, earlobe) and peripheral sites (finger)—into a single algorithm. The system uses optical sensors with multiple light emitters and photodetectors arranged in three-dimensional configurations conforming to patient anatomy, providing diverse light path lengths and topology information for improved measurement robustness and sensor positioning validation. The signal processor combines interface outputs from multiple sensors to generate measurements of parameters including oxygen saturation, pulse rate, perfusion index, and various hemoglobin levels.

This patent application describes a surgical robotic wrist design with torque sensing capabilities. The invention addresses limitations of prior surgical robot wrists, particularly the inability to measure forces from multiple directions and kinematic singularities that require high-speed joint operation.

The disclosed wrist comprises distal, intermediate, and basal segments with three articulations: first and second articulations permitting rotation about parallel axes, and a third articulation (universal joint) permitting rotation about two transverse axes. Torque sensors are positioned to sense torque about these transverse axes, enabling measurement of forces applied from multiple directions to the surgical instrument. Optional additional torque sensors may sense torque about the first and second axes.

The wrist can be implemented at the end of a robot arm or at the end of a surgical instrument. When at the arm's end, the instrument shaft extends along the first axis, allowing the wrist to orient the end effector without lateral displacement of the shaft. The design eliminates kinematic singularities, enables compact arm construction, and facilitates force feedback to surgeons through haptic technology.

Nobel Prizes honor scientific discoveries but overlook much of science. The article discusses how one person's idea for a prize came to define scientific genius, noting that in 2023, biochemist Katalin Karikó became one of few women to win a Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine. Karikó initially thought the award notification call was a joke.

Southern California house prices rose significantly in the 12 months ending May 2018, with Los Angeles County up 8.3%, the Inland Empire up 8.2%, and Orange County up 6.2%, according to CoreLogic data released July 3. Nationally, prices increased 7.1%, while California saw an 8.9% rise. The price gains are attributed to a lean supply of homes for sale, particularly for entry-level properties. Many homeowners are reluctant to sell due to low existing mortgage rates (half below 3.75%) compared to current higher rates. A CoreLogic survey found 15% of homeowners hope to buy within a year versus 11% wanting to sell, with 28% of renters looking to buy. CoreLogic data compares individual home sale prices over time, while median price reports showed Southern California increases of 7.4-7.7%.

This book aims to regularize distributed systems design by identifying common patterns, similar to how patterns improved algorithmic development and object-oriented programming. While focused on distributed systems, the first section covers single-node patterns using containers as foundational building blocks. Multiple motivations exist for splitting single-node applications into container groups: resource isolation allows different priorities and requirements for components (e.g., user-facing services versus background tasks); team scaling benefits from small, focused, reusable modules owned by small teams; and separation of concerns enables easier testing, updating, and deployment with fewer dependencies. The following chapters present patterns for modular container groups, assuming tight dependencies where containers can be coscheduled on a single machine and optionally share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and memory—called a "pod" in Kubernetes.

Kesha publicly supported Taylor Swift on Twitter after a judge dismissed DJ David Mueller's lawsuit against Swift, who had accused him of groping her in 2014. Swift's $1 countersuit for assault and battery remains pending. Kesha referenced Swift's previous financial support—$250,000 donated in 2016 during Kesha's legal battle with Dr. Luke, whom she accused of abuse. Other celebrities including Lena Dunham and Nelly Furtado also expressed support for Swift. Kesha recently released her album "Rainbow," which reached No. 1 on iTunes.

A "Combo" defense combines person-to-person and zone defense to counter spread offenses like North Carolina's Four Corner style. Three outside defenders play aggressive pass denial while two inside defenders provide backside zone support. The on-ball defender forces the ball handler to the sideline, while inside defenders zone the baseline. After a pass, the original defender denies return passes, and the defense aims to force non-ball handlers to handle the ball. On middle dribble penetration, the inside defender steps up to trap with help from the on-ball defender. If a dribbler picks up the ball, defenders jam the handler and close out on other players to force turnovers. Against good ball-handling corner shooters, switch to a 1-3-1 trap defense.

Mikel Obi assured the Super Eagles will perform their best in their June 2, 2018 friendly match against England at Wembley Stadium, two weeks before Nigeria's World Cup opener against Croatia. Nigeria will also play the Czech Republic before the tournament, where they face Iceland and Argentina in Group D. England will play Tunisia, Panama and Belgium in Group G. Match tickets range from £35 to £70.

This passage documents AMD AGESA firmware interface procedures for processor initialization, memory configuration, and system management. Key components include stackless assembler routines for pre-memory initialization (AmdEnableStack, AmdDisableStack), structure management utilities (AmdCreateStruct, AmdReleaseStruct), and boot sequence entry points (AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate). The procedures handle processor core identification, memory training, PCIe configuration, graphics initialization, and ACPI table generation. Required host environment call-outs include memory allocation (AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaLocateBuffer), system reset (AgesaReset), SPD reading (AgesaReadSpd), and AP task dispatching (AgesaRunFcnOnAllAps, AmdLateRunApTask). S3 suspend/resume support is provided through AmdInitRtb, AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3FinalRestore. Platform customization occurs through build configuration settings and optional hooks for memory timing adjustments, voltage control, and device-specific handling.

United Distributors, Inc. sued Airco Appliance & Hardware, Inc., Henry R. Burke, and Alfred R. Willis to recover on a note, with Willis contesting liability based on a guarantee he signed. Willis claimed the guarantee's consideration failed because he never became a 50% stockholder as planned, and alternatively pleaded revocation and estoppel. The trial court dismissed the suit against Willis, and the Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed. The court found that Willis's sole motive for signing the guarantee was to become a stockholder, and when this failed and plaintiff was notified, the contract became ineffective under Civil Code Articles 1825-1827. The guarantee was retained by plaintiff's credit manager without Willis's knowledge, while other documents were returned and destroyed. The note in question was for $3,107.82, given a year after Willis withdrew from the venture.

Johnson & Johnson reported mixed Q1 results with sales slightly below consensus but adjusted EPS meeting estimates. The company raised 2017 guidance to $75.4-$76.1 billion in sales and $7.00-$7.15 adjusted EPS, incorporating the Actelion acquisition. Key drug Remicade sales declined 6% year-on-year to $1.67 billion. The stock trades at approximately $125 with a 19x forward P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA, considered neither bargain nor expensive. Shares rose 1.1% pre-market before falling below $125. Growth challenges persist in baby care, oral care, and wound care units. The author finds the stock unattractive for value investors, citing subdued growth prospects and operational concerns, despite solid fundamentals and attractive long-term debt securities.

ConocoPhillips agreed to sell its San Juan Basin assets to a Hilcorp Energy affiliate for $2.7 billion cash, with potential for $300 million in additional payments tied to natural gas prices over six years. The assets contain 0.6 billion barrels of oil equivalent in proved reserves, 78% natural gas. The sale follows a larger $13.3 billion Canadian asset sale to Cenovus earlier in the month. Combined, the sales will reduce Conoco's 2017 production by 25.4% and operating cash flows by $0.3 billion. The San Juan Basin assets are currently valued at $5.9 billion on Conoco's books, resulting in a non-cash impairment. Management plans to use proceeds for "general corporate purposes," likely including share buybacks, rather than specified debt reduction. The author views the transaction favorably if cash is allocated appropriately, noting the price of $5 per boe reflects the gas-heavy reserve mix.

The passage outlines tasks for a post-war peace conference, including assessing strength/weakness of various states, establishing economic arrangements, and safeguarding minorities across multiple regions. It details how an Inquiry can assist through data collection, problem presentation, and trained personnel. The Inquiry cannot address certain tasks including prisoner exchange, devastated area restoration, armament limitation, aircraft regulation, resource allocation, commercial treaties, current relations, and record-keeping. The document also contains confidential correspondence between Dr. S.E. Mezes and Secretary of State Robert Lansing regarding a proposed "Pan American Treaty" for mutual guarantee of sovereignty and territorial integrity among American republics.

The passage describes patent figures showing graphical user interface designs for display screens. FIG. 1 shows the claimed design; FIGS. 2-4 show alternative embodiments; and FIG. 5 shows an electronic device with the FIG. 1 interface applied. Broken lines indicate unclaimed elements including display screens and electronic devices.

VIX futures are financial derivatives introduced in 2004 that allow trading based on the VIX Index, which measures 30-day implied volatility in U.S. equities. Trading occurs on the Cboe Futures Exchange with regular hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. CT and extended sessions. Two contract types exist: full (index value × $1,000) and mini (one-tenth size). Contracts expire monthly via financial settlement. Key price factors include stock market cycle phases and contango/backwardation effects from spot VIX mean reversion. The all-time high was 80.850 (March 2020), with spot VIX reaching 89.53 (October 2008) and all-time low of 8.56 (November 2017). Primary risks stem from leveraged positions magnifying losses. VIX futures differ from CFDs in having exchange trading and expiration dates. Traders use VIX futures for hedging, diversification, and speculation, though backtesting showed limited direct trading value compared to using spot VIX for equity timing strategies.

Researchers developed a simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography method to capture nanoscale 3D maps of structure, chemical composition, and valence states in battery cathode materials. Applied to LiNi₁/₃Co₁/₃Mn₁/₃O₂ (NCM111) cathodes, the study revealed that chemical composition evolved uniformly throughout primary particles during electrochemical cycling, while valence state changes and transition metal inhomogeneity were strongly surface-localized and depth-dependent. After 200 cycles, oxygen content dropped sharply (from ~66% to 61%), and 33.7% of particle volume transformed to rock-salt structure. Valence states showed pronounced depth gradients: Mn⁴⁺ and Co³⁺ fractions increased with depth in pristine particles, but this reversed after 200 cycles with emergence of Mn²⁺ and Co²⁺. Transition metal segregation was twice as pronounced at surfaces compared to interiors. The findings indicate that degradation involves coupled structural phase transitions, ion migration, and dissolution-driven segregation, with 3D valence state distribution and chemical inhomogeneity serving as both degradation signatures and active contributors to cathode stability.

Brayan Rocchio hit a solo home run in the eighth inning off a 99.9 mph fastball from Tigers reliever Troy Melton, sparking a five-run rally that gave the Cleveland Guardians a 2-1 lead and forced a decisive Game 3 in the AL Wild Card Series. The Tigers stranded a playoff-record 15 baserunners in the loss. Rocchio, who spent six weeks in Triple-A earlier this season after struggling, has mirrored his team's rags-to-riches trajectory. The Guardians overcame afternoon shadows and a strong wind blowing in from right field to win despite having only two hits through seven innings. Both teams face elimination in Thursday's Game 3.

Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. appealed a trial court ruling that denied its claim for sales and use tax refunds on drilling equipment purchases. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment, holding that the taxpayer failed to qualify for exemption under IC 6-2-1-39(b)(6) for "manufacturing machinery, tools and equipment" used in "extraction of tangible personal property." The court interpreted "manufacturing" to require resale of extracted property, whereas Mumma's customers used water for personal, farm, or business consumption without resale. The exemption was designed to prevent tax pyramiding on wholesale transactions, not to cover extraction for end-use consumption.

The Elliott Wave theory, developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott in the 1920s-1930s after studying 75 years of stock data, is a technical analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. The theory classifies waves into impulse waves (five sub-waves moving with the trend) and corrective waves (three sub-waves moving against the trend). Used primarily by technical traders in stocks, forex, and commodities, the theory helps identify potential price direction and trading opportunities. However, it faces significant criticism for being highly subjective, difficult to backtest, and lacking clearly defined entry/exit rules. Traders often combine it with other indicators like moving averages and momentum oscillators. No single timeframe is optimal; selection depends on trading style.

The Supreme Court debated whether restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act (MVRA) constitutes criminal punishment, which would trigger the Constitution's ex post facto clause. The case involves Holsey Ellingburg, whose offense predated the MVRA's enactment. Unusually, both Ellingburg's counsel and the government agreed the statute could not be applied to increase his punishment, leaving only a court-appointed attorney to defend the sentence. Justice Alito emphasized civil aspects of the statute, such as victims enforcing restitution as judgment liens, while Justices Kagan and Jackson focused on restitution's placement within criminal sentencing and its penal nature. The author predicts the Court will likely reject applying the MVRA to Ellingburg early in the year.

This passage discusses microtubule (MT) dynamics in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and their relationship to drug resistance. Key findings include: AR splice variants (particularly ARv7) correlate with taxane resistance through altered MT dynamics; ARv7-expressing cells show 40% faster EB1 comet speeds (24.6 μm/min) compared to AR-wild type cells (16.2 μm/min). The authors developed computational methods to track EB1 comets for analyzing MT polymerization rates. Patient-derived organoids from 16 PC patients were established, with tumor cells selected by reducing Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor concentration. GSK3β and pVHL regulate MT dynamics—pVHL loss increases MT turnover rates, while GSK3β phosphorylation of pVHL at Ser-68 inactivates its MT stabilization function. Both faster and slower than normal MT turnover rates indicate drug resistance. The authors propose correlating MT dynamics signatures with gene expression data to predict drug susceptibility and identify therapeutic targets.

Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE:VZ) saw traders buy shares on weakness during Friday trading, with a net money flow of $56.85 million into the stock, ranking 11th highest among tracked companies. The stock closed down $0.37 at $48.81. Recent analyst ratings include TheStreet upgrading to "b-" and Vetr raising to "buy" with a $47.44 target, while Barclays lowered its target to $47.00 with an "equal weight" rating. The stock has an average "Hold" rating and $52.86 target price. Unusually large options trading occurred Thursday with 87,567 call options purchased, up 524% from typical volume. Q2 2017 earnings met estimates at $0.96 EPS with revenue of $30.55 billion, up 0.1% year-over-year. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.59, payable November 1st, representing a 4.84% yield. EVP Craig L. Silliman sold 610 shares in August, with insiders selling 1,830 shares total last quarter. Institutional investors own 62.24% of shares, with several hedge funds recently adding new positions.

NVIDIA RTX IO is a technology suite enabling rapid GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets, accelerating I/O performance up to 100x compared to hard drives. It works with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to offload CPU decompression work to RTX GPUs, improving frame rates and enabling near-instantaneous game loading. The NVIDIA A40 GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X AI training throughput compared to Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000. It features 48GB GPU memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4 interface, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software. Ampere architecture GPUs support 8K displays at 60Hz and 4K at 120Hz, include HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, and feature fifth-generation NVDEC supporting AV1 hardware decode and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware-accelerated video encoding. The GA10x architecture provides up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, with second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores. The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates GA102 GPU with 24GB GDDR6X memory, while RTX 3070 uses GA104 GPU with GDDR6. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology in GDDR6X memory detects transmission errors and retries failed transactions. The RTX A6000 features GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6 memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

The Eleventh Circuit affirmed Alexis Perez's 51-month prison sentence for conspiracy to commit mail fraud. The court rejected his claim that he deserved a three-level reduction under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy, finding that he and co-conspirators had taken "crucial steps" toward completing the offense when law enforcement intervened. The court also rejected his claim for a minor-role reduction under § 3B1.2, finding the record supported the district court's determination that he played an "important" role in planning and preparation. Though Perez had signed a sentence appeal waiver, the court declined to enforce it because the district court failed to specifically question him about it at the plea hearing. The court noted Perez could not adopt arguments from codefendants' appeals because his case was not consolidated with theirs and he filed no motion for adoption.

Price action trading is a technical analysis method that uses price movement patterns to determine trade entry and exit points without relying heavily on indicators. Day trading price action strategies involve analyzing intraday price charts for patterns including reversal patterns (head and shoulders), continuation patterns, harmonic patterns, and candlestick patterns. Traders may use pure price action or combine it with indicators like moving averages, VIX, or RSI. Backtesting price action strategies is challenging due to coding difficulties and cognitive biases, but essential for verifying effectiveness. An example strategy using consecutive lower lows and highs on WTI crude oil futures showed poor historical performance until 2021. Successful day trading price action strategies require quantification through backtesting, out-of-sample testing, and diversification across markets and strategies.

Credit card debt and auto loans increased household bills for millions in 2016. To pay off debt, reduce credit card use, create a spending plan, build an emergency fund, and pay as much as possible toward debt monthly. Cut unnecessary spending, prioritize high-interest debts first, and reallocate freed funds to remaining balances. Make gradual lifestyle changes to avoid overwhelming yourself.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network that exploited transsexuals recruited through fake "Miss Trans" competitions in Venezuela, promising winners a new life in Spain. Over 20 victims were freed from overcrowded apartments in Barcelona and Palma de Mallorca where they were forced into prostitution and drug dealing to pay off 15,000 euro debts. The network confiscated travel documents upon arrival and required 24-hour availability to clients. Fourteen people were arrested; the network earned up to 1 million euros over five years.

Google Doodle honored German physicist Max Born on his 135th birthday. Born made major contributions to quantum mechanics, including the Born Rule, a probability-based theory for predicting particle locations that earned him the 1954 Nobel Prize. Born was born December 11, 1882, in Breslau, Germany, to an academic family. He taught at the University of Göttingen for 12 years, where notable scientists including Werner Heisenberg and J. Robert Oppenheimer studied under him. Born maintained a 40-year friendship with Albert Einstein despite their scientific disagreements about randomness versus causality in physics. Forced to emigrate to England in 1933 when Hitler expelled Jewish academics, Born died January 5, 1970, at age 87 from heart disease.

The Regulatory Sandbox in Education bill allows district and charter schools to create innovation plans and apply for state board rule waivers; permits LEAs to use restricted funding and accept private funds for innovative programs; requires charter authorizers to amend charter agreements; mandates state board reporting on innovation plans, funding use, and denied waivers; and permits plan termination under certain circumstances. The State Board must report annually to the Education Interim Committee by November 30. Due to no current applications or approved plans, recommendations include creating website resources, developing optional application forms, and actively promoting the program.

UK economic outlook faces growing concerns as slowing pay growth combines with rising inflation to squeeze households. Employment rose 109,000 in the three months to April, reaching a record 74.8% rate, with strong hiring continuing into May. However, regular earnings grew only 1.7% annually—the weakest since January 2015—while consumer prices rose 2.9%, causing real pay to fall. Consumer spending is under strain, potentially dragging on future growth. Business uncertainty following the election shock may undermine confidence, leaving exports and investment as key growth drivers. Input cost inflation moderated in May, suggesting consumer price inflation may peak later this year. Wage growth shows no signs of improvement despite higher employment, and the labour market may weaken further. Bank of England interest rates will likely remain on hold until economic prospects improve.

The passage describes the AGESA software interface for AMD platform initialization in UEFI BIOS environments. It details the bridge-dispatcher model where host BIOS code calls AGESA functions through a binary image interface, with call-outs for host services. The document covers initialization phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTB), build methods (binary modules vs. source integration), and key procedures including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, and S3 resume functions. It specifies stack requirements, configuration structures, memory initialization parameters, and required host environment call-outs for buffer allocation. Platform solutions use customizable option files, with specific support for x86-64 and AArch64 architectures.

U.S. Minister Schoenfeld met with Finnish Foreign Minister Witting on January 21, 1942, to clarify American public attitudes toward Finland, correcting Witting's impression that U.S. sentiment was more favorable than it was. Witting defended Finland's strategic aims, including control of the Karelian and Onega Isthmuses, citing Russian aggression via the Murmansk railroad. Schoenfeld questioned the logic of Finland's security based on strategic lines versus political foundations. Witting compared German and British treatment of small nations unfavorably, claiming Germans merely acted first in Norway, Holland, and Belgium. Witting cited Procopé's reports of State Department views favoring postwar Anglo-Russian control of small European nations and German industrial disarmament. Schoenfeld concluded Witting recognized Finland's limited autonomy amid overwhelming forces. In a separate January 1942 communication, Secretary of State Hull informed Finnish Minister Procopé that American citizens serving in Finnish diplomatic posts must comply with U.S. travel reporting requirements or face severance from official duties, extending and modifying previous instructions.

On December 21, 2015, Apple Inc.'s Board of Directors amended its Amended and Restated Bylaws to implement proxy access. The new Section 5.15 allows shareholders or groups of up to twenty shareholders owning at least three percent of outstanding common stock continuously for at least three years to nominate director candidates comprising up to twenty percent of the Board for inclusion in annual meeting proxy materials. The Bylaws also updated Section 5.14's Advance Notice provisions and made ministerial changes to Sections 2.4, 5.4, and 10.6. The amended Bylaws are attached as Exhibit 3.2.

NEMA South East coordinator Walson Ibarakumo warned of impending floods in Enugu, Anambra, and Ebonyi States based on NIHSA and NiMET forecasts, attributing the heavy rainfall and storms to climate change. He advised residents to change their energy use attitudes and prepare early for potential disasters. Highly probable flood areas include Enugu South and East; Aguata, Idemili North, and Ogbaru in Anambra; and multiple areas in Ebonyi. Probable areas include Oji River, Udi, and Uzo Uwani in Enugu, and several local government areas in Anambra.

DBS Banking Group notes challenging conditions for Indian government bonds due to renewed supply pressure and rising developed market yields, though the worst of the sell-off may have passed. The bank favors shorter-term bonds as India's CPI has eased, reducing rate hike urgency, while remaining neutral-to-negative on longer-term bonds. India's 10-year real yields appear high regionally at 3.2 percent. The Indian rupee has depreciated 2 percent year-to-date against the US dollar, with the BSE Sensex falling 3.3 percent, both ranking second worst in Asia ex-Japan. India's current account deficit more than doubled to 1.9 percent of GDP, with the savings-investment gap projected to widen to 2-2.2 percent in fiscal year 2019. DBS expects the rupee to depreciate toward 67 this year due to financing requirements and vulnerability to rising US rates.

Al-Qaida-linked militants in Syria shot down a Russian Su-25 fighter jet in Idlib province on Saturday and killed its pilot after he ejected and resisted capture. The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed the downing, attributing it to a portable ground-to-air missile. The incident occurred near Sarqeb, where Syrian troops backed by Russian airstrikes have been advancing. Separately, Turkish forces reported three soldiers killed in clashes with Syrian Kurdish militia in Afrin, bringing total Turkish casualties to eight since Operation Olive Branch began on January 20. Turkey's presidential spokesman stated Turkey will not tolerate Kurdish militia presence along its border and called for U.S. disengagement from the YPG.

NVIDIA Corporation's 2015 Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 25, 2015, filed with the SEC. The company, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, is a large accelerated filer with approximately 549.8 million shares outstanding as of March 6, 2015. NVIDIA operates in visual computing through two reporting segments: GPU and Tegra Processor, serving four markets: Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing & Cloud, and Automotive. GPU brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, and GRID; Tegra powers DRIVE and SHIELD platforms. The company employs a fabless manufacturing strategy using suppliers like TSMC and Samsung. For fiscal year 2015, revenue was $4.68 billion with net income of $631 million. Research and development expenses totaled $1.36 billion. The company returned $1.0 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends. NVIDIA faces risks including intense competition from AMD and Intel, dependence on third-party manufacturing, customer concentration, and ongoing litigation with Qualcomm and Samsung. The company holds $4.62 billion in cash and marketable securities and has $1.5 billion in convertible senior notes due 2018.

Strong relationships with adult and peer mentors help young people thrive academically. Mentoring occurs through school programs, afterschool activities, community organizations, and naturally formed relationships with teachers, family friends, and community leaders. The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted student engagement, leaving students months behind academically and disconnected from caring adults.

Multiple meta-analyses demonstrate that mentoring programs significantly improve academic outcomes including attendance, grades, test scores, and classroom behavior. Specific programs like Big Brothers Big Sisters School-Based Mentoring, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, and Check and Connect show measurable improvements in academic performance, attendance, and graduation rates. After-school programs such as Quantum Opportunities and Pathways to Education also yield positive results.

Natural mentoring relationships with teachers and school personnel prove particularly effective, with teacher mentors predicting higher educational attainment. These relationships especially benefit students of color by building positive racial regard and reducing stereotype threat.

However, mentoring relationships are inequitably distributed, with youth of color, low-income youth, and those with less-educated parents receiving less support. Expanding access requires private and public investment at all government levels.

Xiaomi Redmi 5 goes on sale in India today at 12 pm on Amazon India, Mi.com, and Mi Home stores, starting at Rs 7,999. The budget smartphone comes in three variants: 2GB+16GB (Rs 7,999), 3GB+32GB (Rs 8,999), and 4GB+64GB (Rs 10,999). It features a 5.7-inch HD+ 18:9 display, metal unibody design, Snapdragon 450 processor, 3300 mAh battery, 12MP rear camera, 5MP front camera with selfie flash, and runs Android Nougat 7.1.2 with MIUI 9. Available in Black, Gold, Lake Blue, and Rose Gold, with 128GB expandable storage via hybrid dual-SIM slot. Xiaomi claims over 4 lakh units will be available.

President Franklin Pierce transmits a State Department report to the Senate explaining his refusal to submit for ratification the 1853 Tehuantepec transit convention with Mexico. His objections include: the convention binds the U.S. to guarantee a private company's contract with Mexico indefinitely, requiring protection of construction personnel and capital investment throughout the contract's duration; withdrawal requires one year's notice even if regulations violate the convention's spirit; and the obligations would be comprehensive and embarrassing given Mexico's instability. Additionally, ratification would violate the 1850 Clayton-Bulwer Treaty with Great Britain, which covers any interoceanic communication across the Isthmus of Tehuantepec. Pierce concludes that after careful consideration, he cannot ask for Senate ratification.

This study examined SARS-CoV-2 antibody responses in 11 nursing home residents in Georgia from October 2020 to April 2021. Participants were enrolled after testing positive for COVID-19 and followed through nine visits with blood and nasal specimen collection. Ten of 11 participants received two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine 71–105 days post-diagnosis.

Post-infection, 90% of participants developed detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, with median time to detection of 13 days for Pan-Ig/IgG and 16 days for IgA. Pan-Ig and IgG remained elevated while IgM and IgA declined by 30–50 days. One unvaccinated participant maintained antibodies for 150 days.

An outside day is a two-bar price pattern where the current day's bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar, with open and close falling outside the prior day's range. It indicates rising volatility and stronger conviction from buyers or sellers. The pattern has four configurations based on bar directions; only opposite-direction combinations qualify as outside reversals.

Outside days can function as continuation or reversal patterns depending on context. A bullish outside day suggests trend continuation in upswings, while bearish versions suggest continuation in downswings. Outside reversals occur when the second bar opposes the first bar's direction and prevailing trend.

Backtesting outside day strategies on SPY showed average gains near zero for basic outside days, negative 0.07% when combined with higher closes, and positive 0.06% with lower closes—none producing tradable results. The authors found limited practical value for day trading outside day patterns despite their popularity among price action traders.

William Green delivers his final lecture on stochastic methods, covering Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo, and molecular dynamics. He explains that multidimensional integrals often take the form of probability density times a function, where the weighting factor w is easier to work with than explicit probability distributions. Metropolis Monte Carlo requires careful step size selection—too large causes repeated rejections, too small prevents adequate sampling. Step sizes can be adjusted adaptively to maintain acceptance ratios around 0.2-0.8.

Kinetic Monte Carlo addresses problems where probability distributions evolve over time and are too large to enumerate explicitly, such as catalytic surface reactions with 10^60 possible states. The Gillespie algorithm generates trajectories using random numbers for waiting times and event selection. Computational efficiency requires computing averages on-the-fly rather than storing trajectories, and sampling initial conditions from Poisson distributions. Common approximations include eliminating fast processes (like diffusion) or slow processes (like coking) that fall outside relevant time scales.

Molecular dynamics solves Newton's equations using the velocity Verlet algorithm, often with thermostats for thermal bath coupling. It serves as an alternative to Metropolis Monte Carlo for equilibrium properties but is time-accurate, limiting simulations to nanoseconds. This makes it unsuitable for millisecond-scale processes but ideal for picosecond phenomena like exciton transfer. Proper tool selection depends on matching the method to the problem's time scales and whether time-dependent or equilibrium properties are needed.

This MIT lecture covers model-free optimal control methods, focusing on actor-critic algorithms that combine policy gradient and value function approaches. Policy gradient methods scale well to high dimensions and guarantee convergence but suffer from high variance and local optima. Value function methods are more efficient and reuse data through temporal difference learning but lack convergence guarantees and can diverge with function approximation. Actor-critic algorithms address these trade-offs by representing both policy and value function simultaneously, using the critic's value estimates to reduce variance in policy updates while maintaining convergence guarantees. The lecturer presents his thesis work on "Toddler," a walking robot that learned stable locomotion in 10-20 minutes using an actor-critic approach with linear function approximation, demonstrating robust adaptation to disturbances and terrain changes without requiring an accurate system model.

SOS Switching Concepts

Switching is integral to the SOS Pressure Defense system, with "Screen-Over-Switch" as basic terminology. Automatic switching eliminates hesitation and reduces fouls while disrupting offensive flow and forcing turnovers.

**Contact Switching Rules (in order of importance):**
- More effective at denying passing lanes than "Show and Recover" or "Slide Thru" methods
- Eliminates defender hesitation, denying quick catches and open jump shots
- Disrupts screening offensive flow, causing offensive bewilderment
- Results in fewer fouls than other screening defense methods
- Denies first passing lanes, forcing turnovers and increasing transition baskets

**SOS Switching Techniques:**
Defenders call "Screen," hedge "Over" one stride to block the offensive player's path, then call "Switch" as defenders exchange assignments.

**Off-Ball Switching:**
- **Down Screen:** Defender bumps screener, hedges outside, executes contact switch forcing cutter wide; both assume SNUGGLE denial positions

The passage describes the development and application of TOPIC (TOpology-constrained Prediction of Inorganic Crystals), a crystal structure prediction algorithm designed to discover novel oxide solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) with oxygen-corner-sharing (CS) frameworks. TOPIC addresses limitations of existing methods by constraining searches to CS bond topologies, significantly reducing computational cost while enabling exploration of complex quaternary oxide systems with over 100 atoms per unit cell.

The algorithm generates candidate structures through a three-step process: creating cation sublattices, forming cation-oxygen frameworks under CS constraints, and placing Li atoms via Monte Carlo simulations. Validation against known materials including LLZO, LiTi2(PO4)3, and LiTa2PO8 demonstrates TOPIC's accuracy, with successful reproduction of known structures and discovery of new polymorphs.

Using TOPIC with machine-learning interatomic potentials, the authors screened quaternary oxide compositions containing elements like Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, P, Si, and Al. They identified lithium content ratio (Li atoms divided by non-Li metal atoms) as a key descriptor: CS frameworks are more stable at Li ratios ≤1.0, and these structures exhibit significantly higher ionic conductivity than non-CS alternatives. Comprehensive screening of 45 compositions yielded 92 candidates with predicted room-temperature conductivities exceeding 0.1 mS cm−1, with 15 validated through DFT calculations. Notable discoveries include Li4Hf2Si3O12 with 14.09 mS cm−1 conductivity and several novel structural prototypes. The study establishes design principles linking Li content to conductivity through structural distortion effects and conduction pathway dimensionality.

A prospective study of 157 hospitalized acute decompensated heart failure patients evaluated whether bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) could predict clinical outcomes. Among patients, 45.9% had chronic kidney disease (CKD) and 70.7% had heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). CKD patients showed higher OH and OH/ECW at admission but no association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or heart failure hospitalization (HHF). HFrEF patients demonstrated greater OH/ECW reduction with diuresis compared to non-HFrEF patients (P = 0.036), yet this did not improve clinical outcomes. Across all subgroups, BIS parameters were not significant predictors of MACE or HHF during 10.7-month follow-up. The lecture introduces wireless communication, contrasting it with wired communication where only white Gaussian noise is the main concern. In wireless systems, fading occurs due to multiple signal paths with different propagation delays and Doppler shifts. When a receiver moves, it experiences frequency shifts; multiple paths create interference patterns causing rapid signal strength variations called multipath or fast fading. The professor explains that single Doppler shifts can be tracked and compensated, but multiple Doppler shifts from different paths create beats that cannot be easily eliminated. Ray tracing models approximate channels as sums of attenuated, delayed paths. The system becomes a linear time-varying filter where the impulse response changes slowly compared to the delay variations. At baseband, Doppler shifts appear as phase rotations, and the Doppler spread—the range of Doppler shifts across paths—determines how frequently channel measurements must be updated for effective communication.

The lecture covers combinatorial bounds and algorithms for folding polygons into convex polyhedra using gluing trees. For general gluings, there are exponential upper and lower bounds of 2^Θ(n), with an open problem of whether polynomial-time decision is possible. Edge-to-edge gluings (where whole edges glue to whole edges) admit polynomial-time decision algorithms, though enumeration remains exponential. For polygons with bounded sharpness—where all reflex angles are bounded away from 360° by a constant—both the number of gluings and enumeration time become polynomial.

The lecture defines combinatorial types of gluings through abstract gluing trees with specified junctions. A key proof shows at most n+4 leaves exist (vertices or fold points), yielding exponential tree bounds. A lower bound construction uses spiky stars with angles carefully chosen to allow exponentially many valid gluings. For bounded sharpness, constant curvature per leaf limits leaves to a constant, giving polynomial bounds.

Dynamic programming algorithms are presented: for edge-to-edge gluings, O(n³) decision and exponential enumeration; for general gluings, exponential enumeration with intervals handling vertex-edge gluings. The lecture concludes with examples, showing 85 gluings (23 distinct polyhedra) for a Latin cross and illustrating rolling belts for convex polygons like triangles and squares.

This passage describes the interrupt shadow mechanism and #HV doorbell page configuration for SEV-ES guests, including host and guest behaviors for interrupt delivery and acknowledgment. Guests execute HLT with interrupts disabled; hosts re-enter guests if interrupts are pending. Doorbell page configuration uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0014 with GET, SET, and QUERY functions. Guests acknowledge interrupts via atomic exchange with zero, validate vectors, and handle EOI through NoEoiRequired exchange or APIC register writes. ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for astronomical time series that combines global self-attention with local depthwise convolutions and gating mechanisms to improve representation learning for stellar light curves. The architecture addresses limitations of existing transformer models by better capturing short-lived local phenomena and regulating noisy measurements. Each encoder block contains three sublayers: multi-head self-attention, a depthwise convolutional sublayer with Gated Linear Units, and a gated feed-forward network. Inputs combine magnitudes, uncertainties, and sinusoidal time embeddings through learned projection. The model uses masked reconstruction for self-supervised pretraining, masking 30% of probed positions, replacing 10% with random values, and leaving 10% unchanged. ASTROCO-S (5.9M parameters) and ASTROCO-L (15.2M parameters) both outperform Astromer baselines on the MACHO R-band dataset in reconstruction error and classification scores, with the smaller model achieving better results using less training time and hardware than prior work.

SOS disruptions apply full-court pressure to extend passing lanes and pull offenses from their operating areas, with tactics including wing pass denials, post split switches, and weakside two-game disruptions. All-out SOS disruption initiates trapping on the first pass to force offenses into freelance situations, employing first-pass traps with specific rotations for pass-outs to the wing, corner, or skip passes, maintaining SOS rules and trap rotations throughout.

Girlfriends' shop in Liberal is preparing for Liberal High School's prom on April 22. Employee Kenna McNeil reports approximately 100 orders received so far for corsages, boutonnieres, and other accessories, with preparation beginning around March 1 due to flower shipments from Arkansas. The shop also serves other area schools including Southwestern Heights, Forgan High School, and Hugoton. This paper presents twelve shared tasks organized by NFDI4DS, a German consortium supporting research data lifecycle in Data Science and AI. Seven completed tasks include: SOMD 2025 (software mention detection from scholarly articles), SciVQA (scientific visual question answering), ClimateCheck (fact-checking climate change social media posts), FoRC2025 (field of research classification), LLMs4Subjects (automated subject tagging for library catalogs), LLMs4OL-2024 (ontology learning using LLMs), and Scholarly QALD (question answering over scholarly knowledge graphs). Four tasks under development cover: dataset and ML model mention detection, GitHub README to knowledge graph conversion, clinical uncertainty quantification for decision-making (CURED), and algorithm generalizability benchmarking (Algorithm2Domain). Vietnamese fishermen clashed with police in Nghe An province while attempting to file lawsuits demanding compensation from Taiwanese firm Formosa for a 2016 toxic waste dump that caused mass fish deaths. Despite Formosa paying $500 million to Vietnam's government, fishermen say they received no compensation. Catholic priest Pham Xuan Ke reported police beat protesters, hospitalizing many, though local authorities agreed to receive the lawsuits. Several people were briefly detained. This follows a September attempt by other fishermen to sue for greater compensation, which courts dismissed. The April 2016 incident killed tonnes of fish, including rare offshore species, destroying coastal fishing communities' livelihoods and sparking nationwide protests.

Hollywood's summer movie season begins early with "Avengers: Infinity War," as the industry seeks to recover from a 3% year-to-date box office decline and last summer's worst performance in over a decade. Major franchise releases include "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," "Deadpool 2," "Solo: A Star Wars Story," and "The Incredibles 2." Digital leaders use detailed metrics to set realistic, ambitious goals and encourage employees to collect relevant data to inform objectives and measure progress. Leading organizations expect continuous tracking of project and individual performance goals, using data-driven metrics and 360-degree reviews. On May 17, the Colchester-Milton Rotary Club volunteered with Dealer.com and Vermont Gas to plant saplings at Pine Island Farm in Colchester, organized by Burlington's Intervale Center. The passage reviews credit card offers from Motley Fool Money, focusing on the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card and Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card. The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU delivers significant performance improvements for HPC and AI workloads through multiple architectural innovations. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support IEEE-compliant FP64 computations with 2.5x the performance of Tesla V100, and introduce TF32 precision that delivers up to 20x speedup over FP32 on V100 with minimal code changes. The A100 implements Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that doubles compute throughput for deep neural networks by skipping zero values, with virtually no accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

Memory subsystem improvements include 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) with 2.3x bandwidth increase, and combined 192 KB L1 data cache/shared memory per SM. The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, enabling multi-tenant use cases with quality-of-service guarantees.

Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (2x V100) with improved error detection. PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth to 31.5 GB/sec. Additional features include hardware JPEG decode (NVJPG), five NVDEC units for video decode, optical flow acceleration, and improved atomic operation throughput.

CUDA 11 enables programming support for these features, including task graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous copy operations bypassing register files, asynchronous barriers for improved synchronization, and L2 cache residency controls for persistent data. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS in a 6U form factor for scalable AI infrastructure.

This study examines global rankings of top five higher education institutions (HEIs) in ten Asian countries (Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, Philippines, Russia, Thailand, Vietnam) from 2015-2025 using Times Higher Education World University Rankings data. Odell Beckham Jr. has accepted a six-game NFL suspension for violating the league's PED policy.
