This lecture discusses renormalization in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) and summing Sudakov logarithms, using b to s gamma as an example. The professor explains that Wilson coefficients contain ultraviolet divergences requiring counterterms, which at one loop show unusual 1/epsilon squared divergences. The anomalous dimension contains both a regular piece and a cusp anomalous dimension with a log(mu/omega) term, where omega equals mb due to kinematics. The cusp term dominates renormalization group evolution and produces Sudakov double logarithms when integrated, yielding a Sudakov exponential for the Wilson coefficient. With QCD's running coupling, this becomes a more complex function of alpha_s ratios.

The lecture then examines when momentum labels in Wilson coefficients are fixed by external kinematics versus when they involve loop momenta. In multi-collinear processes with one building block per direction, labels are fixed and renormalization is simple. However, when multiple fields share the same collinear direction, as in the operator chi_n^dagger(w1) chi_n(w2), one momentum combination remains unfixed, leading to integral equations in the anomalous dimension. This structure reproduces classical evolution equations: the Altarelli-Parisi/DGLAP equation for parton distribution functions and the Brodsky-Lepage equation.

The professor introduces deep inelastic scattering (DIS) in the Breit frame, where the incoming proton is collinear and the virtual photon is hard. The hadronic tensor decomposes into two structures T1 and T2, each with corresponding operators in SCET. The lowest-dimension operators involve quark and gluon fields with Wilson lines, giving rise to quark and gluon PDFs. The quark PDF operator chi_n^dagger(0) chi_n(omega) emerges from forward matrix elements with a delta function constraint w1=w2, while the sum w1+w2 corresponds to the momentum fraction variable.

The passage discusses patterns for distributed systems development using container technology, focusing on single-node and multi-node patterns. Single-node patterns include the sidecar pattern (augmenting application containers), ambassador pattern (brokering external communications), and adapter pattern (standardizing interfaces). Multi-node patterns cover replicated load-balanced services, session tracking, caching layers, SSL termination, and sharded services. The text emphasizes modularity, reusability, and separation of concerns through containerization, with practical Kubernetes deployment examples throughout.

This study examined whether increased physical education (PE) hours with cognitively demanding activities improves attention in 75 middle school students (ages 11–12). Class 6 (experimental group) had four weekly PE hours; Class 7 (experimental group) had two. Control groups maintained standard schedules. Attention was measured using the Bells Test, assessing processing speed (bells identified in 30 seconds) and sustained attention (bells identified in 120 seconds).

Results showed significant improvements in processing speed for both experimental groups (p < 0.001), with greater gains in Class 6. Sustained attention improved significantly only in Class 6 (p = 0.012). Control groups showed no changes. The findings suggest that higher PE dosage (four versus two hours) enhances short-term attention more than long-term attention, and that cognitively engaging motor activities may amplify cognitive benefits. Limitations include contextual factors affecting attention and limited generalizability to other age groups.

The UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status (SMS), marking the first use of powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act to target a major tech company. This follows a 10-month investigation and allows the regulator to impose changes including offering users rival search engine options, fair ranking principles, increased data portability, and requiring permission to use publishers' content in AI Overviews. Google Search holds over 90% of UK general search queries, with UK firms spending over £10 billion on its advertising in 2024. Google responded that proposed interventions could inhibit innovation and harm businesses. The regulations will affect Google Search's News tab, Top Stories carousel, and Google Discover, but not Google News or Gemini. Implementation may take months, with the CMA having flexibility to adjust interventions as developments occur.

This patent describes methods and hardware for efficiently implementing Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) using programmable lookup tables for activation functions. The key innovation involves calibrating the hardware by monitoring input values to determine an expected range, then generating lookup data optimized for that specific range rather than the full possible range. This improves accuracy and efficiency by concentrating lookup table entries on values actually encountered during operation.

The hardware includes activation modules with programmable lookup tables that can switch between two data sets, allowing concurrent loading of new activation functions while processing continues. The system supports multiple interpolation methods (linear, quadratic) and can handle out-of-range inputs through clamping or extrapolation. A separate ReLU path provides power savings when simple activation functions suffice.

The configuration process uses calibration data to monitor inputs, determines value ranges through histograms or min/max tracking, calculates optimal lookup data, and loads this into the hardware. This enables area-efficient, flexible DNN implementation adaptable to changing network definitions while minimizing power consumption and silicon area.

The Rockwood School District in Missouri outperformed national reading scores by keeping students in grade-level cohorts rather than grouping by ability. Their approach combines whole-class instruction in phonics and comprehension with flexible, needs-based small groups for reteaching or enrichment. Students engage in daily independent and partner reading, receive targeted interventions from reading specialists, and use movement-based learning techniques. Research shows ability grouping can trap struggling students in lower tracks with limited vocabulary and comprehension strategies. Rockwood's 2024-25 data showed kindergarteners outperforming national proficiency averages by over 17 percentage points in some areas, with first and second graders also exceeding national averages. The district emphasizes that strong Tier I instruction for all students, rather than separation by ability, prevents gaps from emerging and builds both skills and confidence.

A study published in Science found that 75% of honey samples from nearly 200 global sites contained neonicotinoid pesticides, with 45% containing multiple compounds. North America had the highest contamination rate at 86%, followed by Asia at 80% and Europe at 79%. Researchers noted this worldwide exposure may harm pollinators, as neonicotinoids can impair bee brain function and colony growth.

This review examines new models in higher education, focusing on quality assurance, online teaching, leadership, and scholarly communication. Studies by Ramírez-Hurtado et al. (2021) and Elumalai et al. (2021) assess online teaching service quality and e-learning factors during COVID-19, emphasizing technological infrastructure, instructor competence, and student engagement. Karsono et al. (2022) explore leadership spirituality's impact on educational quality in Indonesia, while Anastasiadou and Taraza (2020) address resistance to change as a barrier to quality improvement. Additional studies cover topics including university rankings (Kayyali, 2020-2023), interoperability in e-learning systems (Naim and Alahmari, 2020), student loyalty (Del Río-Rama et al., 2021), e-learning acceptance frameworks (Khodadad Hoseiny et al., 2023), stakeholder alignment (Cavallone et al., 2022), and institutional responses to the pandemic (Dagiene et al., 2022). Platinum futures are standardized contracts traded on the CME Globex platform, representing 50 troy ounces of platinum settled by physical delivery. Two backtested trading strategies are presented: a monthly mean reversion strategy trading both long and short positions (473 trades, 64% win rate, 1.7 profit factor, uncorrelated to stock market) and a seasonal strategy trading on specific days with volume requirements (60 trades, 75% win rate, 2.3 profit factor). The contract tick size is $5.00, with minimum fluctuation of $0.10 per troy ounce. Key risks include leverage-amplified losses and supply concentration in South Africa and Russia.

High-dosage tutoring delivers academic gains and can serve as a teacher pipeline, according to Teach For America's Ignite Fellowship. The program has reached over 40 communities, trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors, and produced compelling academic results: middle school math students grew up to 2.5 times expected rates, and elementary readers grew up to three times faster. Key lessons include that training and support must be non-negotiable, technology should expand rather than replace relationships, and tutoring can spark teaching careers. Research shows tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of applying to teacher programs, particularly among men, people of color, and non-education majors. Since launching, 550 Ignite fellows have joined Teach For America's teaching corps, with 280 new teachers entering classrooms this year alone.

President Grover Cleveland vetoed House bill No. 7864, which proposed adding a literacy test to immigration restrictions. The bill would have excluded immigrants over 16 who could not read and write English or another language, with limited exceptions for family reunification. Cleveland argued this represented a radical departure from America's traditional welcoming immigration policy, which had successfully built the nation through assimilation of millions of immigrants. He rejected claims that recent immigration quality was poor or that immigrants caused unemployment, noting economic conditions were temporary. He found the literacy test ineffective for identifying desirable citizens, as literacy doesn't prevent agitation while illiteracy doesn't cause disorder. Cleveland criticized the bill's family reunification provisions as indefinite and inadequate, particularly for excluding siblings and creating impractical support requirements. He also opposed provisions criminalizing employment of certain aliens, calling them illiberal, un-American, and potentially provoking retaliation against American workers abroad. He concluded the bill was unnecessarily harsh, oppressively constructed, and would harm citizens.

New Orleans' Lower Ninth Ward, devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005, faces ongoing challenges from displacement, gentrification, and extreme weather. The cup and handle pattern is a bullish continuation chart formation resembling a cup with a handle, consisting of a rounded bottom "cup" forming after a price rally and a "handle" trading range on its right side. Popularized by William O'Neil in his 1988 book, the pattern signals consolidation followed by breakout. Key criteria include: occurring in an uptrend, 30-50% cup depth retracement, handle not dipping below half the cup's depth, and volume decreasing during cup formation then increasing on breakout. An inverted version exists for downtrends. Backtests show mixed results—Ali Akhtari's 2016-2018 S&P 500 test underperformed the index, while Thomas Bulkowski's older research showed 26% failure rate (10% if waiting for upside breakout) with 38% average gain. Traders should confirm patterns with volume, set stop-losses below the handle, and consider broader market context.

This lecture discusses Szemerédi's graph regularity lemma and its application to the induced graph removal lemma. The standard graph removal lemma states that for any graph H and epsilon > 0, there exists delta such that if an n-vertex graph has fewer than delta n^|V(H)| copies of H, it can be made H-free by removing fewer than epsilon n² edges. The induced removal lemma is a variant where induced copies of H are considered, requiring both edge additions and deletions (edit distance) to make the graph induced H-free.

The proof strategy for the standard removal lemma involves three steps: partition using regularity lemma, cleaning (removing low-density and irregular pairs), and counting. However, this fails for the induced version because irregular pairs cannot simply be removed—adding edges creates uncertainty about what was removed.

The strong regularity lemma addresses this by producing two partitions P and Q where Q refines P, P is epsilon_0-regular, Q is extremely regular (epsilon_|P|-regular), and their energy difference is small. The proof applies Szemerédi's regularity lemma repeatedly until energy increases by less than epsilon_0. This yields bounds involving the "wowzer" function (iterated tower function).

A corollary provides an equitable partition with subsets W_i that are pairwise regular with no irregular pairs, and whose densities approximate those of the ambient parts. Using this, the induced removal lemma is proved: partition, clean based on densities between W_i's, and apply counting lemma to show few induced copies would imply many exist.

The lecture also covers the infinite removal lemma (for infinite families of patterns) and property testing: hereditary properties are testable using oblivious testers, as follows from the infinite removal lemma.

Higher-order Feynman diagrams contain loop corrections that lead to divergent integrals when calculated to infinity, causing infinite results for physical quantities like cross-sections. The solution involves introducing a cutoff scale and renormalizing physical parameters—masses and couplings—by separating them into bare values plus scale-dependent corrections. These couplings "run" with energy, as shown in plots of inverse coupling versus logarithm of energy for electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions. Introducing new particles at high energy scales changes this running behavior, suggesting a potential unified theory where all three couplings converge at a specific scale.

Boston has been the leading global hub for life sciences for over a decade, with unmatched lab space and substantial funding from both venture capital and federal sources. This article compares lump sum investing and dollar-cost averaging strategies. Dollar-cost averaging involves investing fixed amounts at regular intervals to smooth out market volatility, while lump sum investing deploys capital immediately to capitalize on long-term market growth. The article backtests a lump sum buy & hold strategy using five diversified ETFs across three crisis intervals. Results indicate lump sum investing historically provides higher probability of success over long-term horizons, with earlier investments yielding greater returns. Financial crisis impacts become insignificant over extended periods. The strategy involves investing a significant amount in a diversified portfolio and holding long-term regardless of short-term fluctuations.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated June 5, 2001, contains a compilation of news articles about Enron and California's energy crisis. The articles cover: natural gas price manipulation allegations in California involving El Paso Corporation and Southern California Gas; FERC's new price mitigation plan for electricity; a PBS Frontline documentary "Blackout" examining deregulation and Enron's role; California Senate subpoenas to eight power generators including Enron; Enron's troubled Dabhol power project in India where creditors met to salvage the $2.9 billion venture; Marathon replacing Enron in a $25 billion Saudi gas project; and a Connecticut dispute over using conservation funds for Enron-backed fuel cell technology.

NeoWorld is a neural network framework for generating infinite, interactive virtual worlds from a single image. Inspired by the 1964 novel Simulacron-3, it uses a hybrid object-centric scene structure that begins with lightweight 2D representations and progressively unfolds into detailed 3D models based on user exploration or natural language commands. The system combines panoptic segmentation, Gaussian splatting with compact instance-aware features, and image-to-3D reconstruction to balance computational efficiency with immersive realism. Key innovations include: (1) object-centric Gaussian layers with efficient codebook-based attribute binding, (2) progressive 2.5D-to-3D unfolding prioritized by object proximity or user prompts, and (3) LLM-driven user interaction for object manipulation and physics-based animation. Experiments show NeoWorld outperforms prior 2D and 2.5D methods in 3D consistency, scene quality, and interactive capabilities, while maintaining reasonable efficiency. Limitations include error propagation across cascaded modules and failures in alignment, LLM interpretation, reconstruction under occlusion, and segmentation.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address delays in delivering performance-based bonuses to public school teachers, a problem since 2012-2013. Teachers have not received bonuses for 2016-2017, the first time delays extended into the following fiscal year. DepEd blamed failed biddings and delayed clearance processing, while teachers' groups cited existing funding allocations.

Former Zimbabwean president Robert Mugabe returned from medical treatment in Singapore to face allegations linking him to a June 24 bomb attack in Bulawayo that killed two people and injured over 40, including Vice President Kembo Mohadi. President Emmerson Mnangagwa accused Mugabe's allies, known as Generation 40 (G40), of involvement based on a "hunch without evidence." Relations between the Mugabes and Mnangagwa's government deteriorated sharply after the attack. Mnangagwa stated he could not trust Grace Mugabe, who had attacked him previously. Mugabe's nephew Patrick Zhuwao warned British Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa might use the bombing to target perceived enemies. Mugabe, who calls Mnangagwa's government illegitimate, has reportedly aligned with opposition leader Nelson Chamisa ahead of July 30 elections. Mnangagwa rose to power through a November 2017 military intervention that forced Mugabe to resign after 37 years in office.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. It features input clamp protection allowing ±18V swing, programmable gain amplifiers with configurable input ranges and antialiasing filters, and wide common-mode voltage rejection up to ±12V. The device outputs 20-bit data in straight-binary or two's-complement formats, supports differential or single-ended clock inputs, and includes synchronization capabilities for multi-device operation. It offers internal or external reference options, 2-lane/4-lane SDR/DDR data interfaces with source-synchronous timing, data output randomization, and simple/moving average modes for SNR improvement. Test patterns aid debugging. Power-down and reset functions initialize registers to defaults. Configuration uses SPI with daisy-chain support across three register banks. Speed-boost mode enables 8MSPS sampling for selected channel pairs. For ATE applications, it achieves 0.0015% TUE post-calibration and 99.95% settling in 7.5µs in wide-bandwidth mode. Three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) require proper decoupling and layout practices avoiding digital-analog signal crossing.

On February 2, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. for the issuance of $6.5 billion in notes: $500 million in Floating Rate Notes due 2020, $1.25 billion in 1.55% Notes due 2020, $1.25 billion in 2.15% Notes due 2022, $1.5 billion in 2.50% Notes due 2025, and $2 billion in 3.45% Notes due 2045. The notes are senior unsecured obligations issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013, with floating rate interest payable quarterly and fixed rate interest payable semi-annually beginning August 9, 2015.

Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, caused 1.6 million deaths in 2021, with COVID-19 disrupting diagnosis and treatment access. Extrapulmonary TB (EPTB), affecting sites like lymph nodes and pleura, comprises 16% of cases but remains understudied. Standard treatment uses four first-line drugs: rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

Researchers developed a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model—the first to include pleura and lymph node compartments and simulate all four first-line drugs simultaneously. The model uses ordinary differential equations with physiological parameters, tissue:plasma partition coefficients calculated via the Rodgers and Rowland method, and pharmacokinetic parameters estimated from plasma and lung concentration data.

Model validation showed good agreement with independent plasma concentration data. Simulations revealed that rifampicin and isoniazid generally achieve concentrations above critical thresholds across tissues, while ethambutol fails in brain, kidney, bone, and skin, and pyrazinamide falls below critical concentrations in all compartments. The model over-predicts rifampicin pleural concentrations, possibly due to unaccounted fibrosis effects. Isoniazid shows marked differences between slow and fast acetylators, suggesting potential for dosage customization.

Limitations include assumptions of no drug-drug interactions, no rifampicin autoinduction, and a consolidated lymph node compartment. The model provides a foundation for optimizing EPTB treatment regimens and guiding future clinical studies.

Researchers from Taiwan and South Korea established the K-T collaborative EVT registry by harmonizing data from two national stroke registries (TREAT-AIS and CRCS-K), creating a unified dataset of 9,941 patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke. The Taiwanese cohort was older with more vascular risk factors and severe strokes, while Korean patients had faster treatment times. Successful recanalization rates were similar between countries, but functional independence at 90 days was lower in Taiwan (34.7% vs. 41.1%) and mortality was higher in Korea (14.2% vs. 6.2%). Age strongly influenced outcomes, with patients ≥80 years showing significantly lower functional recovery (18.1% vs. 46.9%) and higher mortality (19.7% vs. 10.5%), particularly between ages 75-85, though symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage rates did not differ by age. Pre-stroke functional independence and bridging thrombolysis predicted better outcomes in elderly patients. The study highlights the value of multinational registries for understanding real-world EVT performance in underrepresented East Asian populations and supports individualized treatment selection beyond chronological age.

Dr. Maria Pane became a neonatologist after discovering her passion during medical school. She treats critically ill newborns at GBMC and involves parents in rounds to keep them informed. She participates annually in the Father's Day 5K fundraiser for the neonatal intensive care unit and values her team's collaborative approach.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Q2 2022 Form 10-Q with the SEC, reporting financial results for the period ended June 30, 2022. The company reported net sales of $121.2 billion for Q2 2022, up 7% from $113.1 billion in Q2 2021. Net income was a loss of $2.0 billion in Q2 2022 compared to net income of $7.8 billion in Q2 2021. For the six months ended June 30, 2022, net sales were $237.7 billion with a net loss of $5.9 billion.

Key financial data includes: cash and cash equivalents of $37.5 billion as of June 30, 2022; total assets of $419.7 billion; long-term debt of $58.1 billion; and stockholders' equity of $131.4 billion. Operating cash flow was $9.0 billion for Q2 2022 and $6.2 billion for the six-month period.

Segment results showed North America net sales of $74.4 billion with operating loss of $627 million; International net sales of $27.1 billion with operating loss of $1.8 billion; and AWS net sales of $19.7 billion with operating income of $5.7 billion.

Notable events included: a 20-for-1 stock split effective May 27, 2022; acquisition of MGM Holdings Inc. for approximately $6.1 billion in March 2022; agreement to acquire 1Life Healthcare, Inc. for approximately $3.9 billion in July 2022; and a change in estimated useful lives of servers and networking equipment effective January 1, 2022, which reduced depreciation expense by $928 million in Q2 2022.

The company reported significant losses from its equity investment in Rivian Automotive, Inc., with marketable equity securities valuation losses of $4.3 billion in Q2 2022 and $12.6 billion for the six-month period. As of June 30, 2022, the fair value of the Rivian investment was $4.1 billion, down from $15.6 billion at December 31, 2021.

This lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs), a proof system where a verifier can check validity by reading only a few random bits of a polynomially longer proof. The lecture constructs a PCP for 3SAT using the GKR protocol, achieving polylog n query complexity and randomness complexity with completeness 1 and soundness 1/2. The construction works by "unrolling" GKR's interactive proof into a static proof: the prover computes low-degree extensions of all circuit layers and includes all possible sumcheck protocol transcripts for every layer, every point, and every possible verifier randomness. Despite exponential-looking size, the PCP remains polynomial because GKR's "memoryless" property allows efficient packing—each layer's sumcheck tree has only polynomial size due to careful parameter setting where H^m = s and F is polylogarithmic. The verifier simulates GKR by querying this oracle, checking consistency across layers. The lecture also transitions from information-theoretic proofs to computational soundness (arguments), noting that relaxing soundness to computationally bounded provers enables more constructions.

This study examines how pupil dilation (mydriasis) affects image quality and AI performance in diabetic retinopathy screening using portable fundus cameras. Researchers analyzed 597 paired retinal images from 327 patients, comparing mydriatic and non-mydriatic conditions. Mydriatic images showed significantly higher gradability (82.1% vs. 55.6%, P<0.001). Factors reducing non-mydriatic image quality included systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race. An AI model (ResNet-200d) trained on the mBRSET dataset achieved 82.91% accuracy, F1 score 0.83, and AUC 0.94 for mydriatic images versus 79.23% accuracy, F1 score 0.79, and AUC 0.93 for non-mydriatic images. The mydriatic group had fewer false positives (13.9% vs. 17.8%) but slightly more false negatives (3.2% vs. 3.0%). While mydriasis improves AI diagnostic performance, non-mydriatic imaging remains pragmatic for resource-limited settings despite lower quality. Limitations include single-camera use, selection bias from paired-image analysis, and non-specialized operators.

A Stephens County jury convicted Robert Pearl Bryson of multiple sex offenses against two children and failure to register as a sex offender. On appeal, Bryson challenged the sufficiency of evidence, various trial court rulings, and claimed ineffective assistance of counsel. The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed all convictions, finding: sufficient evidence supported the aggravated sodomy and child molestation charges based on victim testimony; evidence showed Bryson left Georgia for over a year without notifying authorities of his address change, satisfying the failure to register charge; his motions to quash were untimely or meritless; the trial court properly denied counsel's withdrawal motion filed four days before trial; severance was not required as the charges were connected and evidence cross-admissible; the no contest plea was properly admitted for registration purposes; and Bryson waived his ineffective assistance claim by refusing to pursue it at the motion for new trial hearing despite the trial court's warning.

Image registration is a non-linear inverse problem that seeks to find a coordinate transform to deform a moving image to match a fixed image by minimizing an objective function combining dissimilarity and regularization terms. Current approaches face memory and computational bottlenecks when handling ultra-high resolution images, which can require solving billions of parameters compared to ~20 million for clinical scans.

This paper proposes Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a framework that scales image registration to arbitrarily large problem sizes. The authors identify three key memory bottlenecks: deformable interpolation and warp composition, cross-correlation loss, and mutual information loss. They develop fused CUDA kernels that reduce memory overhead from O(N) to O(1) for grid sampling and mutual information computation, and achieve up to 76.5% memory reduction for localized normalized cross-correlation.

For distributed scaling, they introduce Grid Parallel for boundary-synchronized image sharding and a Ring Sampler that enables distributed interpolation without allgather operations. The framework demonstrates registration of a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo human brain FLASH volume with 11.8 billion transform parameters in one minute using 8 GPUs—570× larger than standard clinical data. FFDP accelerates traditional pipelines by up to 7.48× with 59% less memory and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14× with 24% less memory.

This paper develops a multidimensional framework for data-driven AI innovation, examining the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA) within digital business platforms. The research addresses the gap in systematic empirical analysis of AI management by creating a taxonomy framework with five maturity levels of human-machine interaction: Human Led/Initial Analytics, Human Led Machine Supported/Advanced Analytics I, Machine Led Human Supported/Advanced Analytics II, Machine Led Human Governed/Advanced Analytics III, and Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV. The framework includes an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain comprising four key activities: AI Awareness/Big Data Acquisition, Measurement of AI/Big Data Curation, AI Reporting and Interpretation/Big Data Storage, and AI Decision-making/Big Data Usage. The study uses a methodology combining conceptual-to-empirical and empirical-to-conceptual approaches, drawing on literature review and expert interviews with Russian National Technology Initiative members. The framework aims to help organizations evaluate current business transformation initiatives, identify automation opportunities across tasks, activities, and processes, and communicate AI value through changing human-machine interactions while considering legal, ethical, and societal norms.

This document is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, dated March 2006. It lists 17 errata (numbered 100-116) describing hardware bugs and their workarounds. Issues include: SSMI events may not be synchronous if IRQ occurs simultaneously; PIO access to CD-ROM with UDMA bus master active fails; most wake event inputs don't work from ACPI S3 state; RTC CMOS RAM accesses incorrectly under specific conditions; I/Os to LPC devices fail during block and demand mode legacy DMA; USB controller clock gating doesn't work; ATAPI packet commands after bus master enable fail on certain CD-ROM firmware; keyboard controller AuxOutputFull bit behaves incorrectly; tACK bits don't affect UDMA timing; ATAC can hang with non-DWORD aligned PRD addresses; LPC aborts on certain sync patterns; SMB controller NEGACK status bit behaves incorrectly; GLPCI retry counter doesn't distinguish between accesses; GPIO High Bank Feature Bit writes fail after suspend; SMBus hold time is too short; LOWBAT_FLAG missing after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X not deasserting if delay exceeds PM_SED delay. Each entry includes description, implications, and resolution or workaround.

The Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy's second manslaughter conviction for a 1976 highway collision that killed three people. The court rejected Gandy's claims that: (1) the verdict was against the overwhelming weight of evidence, finding sufficient proof he was intoxicated and driving in the wrong lane; (2) the trial court improperly refused his proposed jury instruction on intoxication factors; (3) sketches of the accident scene were improperly admitted, ruling they merely illustrated witnesses' observations rather than reconstructing the collision; and (4) the jury was denied food during deliberations, noting the short duration and lack of precedent. The court held that culpable negligence was established by Gandy's intoxicated driving into oncoming traffic on a straight road with unobstructed visibility.

This study develops a meta-population SIR model linking Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) to SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics in Norway, Sweden, and Germany. The model treats GCMR settings (Retail and recreation, Grocery and pharmacy, Transit stations, Workplaces) as having additive effects on transmissibility, while temperature and virus variants (Alpha, Delta) have multiplicative effects. For Sweden, 60% of infections were attributed to GCMR-captured settings versus 39% for Norway. Transit stations and Workplaces showed highest baseline contribution to transmission in Norway and Sweden, while Retail and recreation was most important in German regions. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by ~40%, and Delta variant approximately doubled transmissibility. The model demonstrates GCMR utility for real-time pandemic assessment but requires strong assumptions and complex parameterization.

President Reagan accepts the Republican nomination for reelection, contrasting his administration's record of economic growth, tax cuts, and military strength against Democratic policies of higher taxes, inflation, and government expansion. He highlights achievements including 6.5 million new jobs, reduced inflation, restored military readiness, and the Grenada rescue mission. Reagan criticizes Democratic opposition to balanced budgets, line-item vetoes, and crime legislation, while pledging continued tax reduction, economic growth, and nuclear arms negotiations with the Soviet Union. He frames the election as a choice between "up or down"—individual freedom versus government control—and concludes with patriotic imagery from the Olympic torch relay and Statue of Liberty.

EUR/USD is climbing to around 1.1840 due to lack of direction in the US dollar, advancing for a fourth consecutive session from last week's lows near 1.1690/85. Friday's US inflation figures triggered a dollar pullback, supporting the pair's recovery. Market participants await ECB and FOMC minutes later this week for clarity on QE tapering and balance sheet reduction. Current levels show the pair at 1.1826, with resistance at 1.1846, 1.1894, and 1.1911, and support at 1.1722, 1.1687, and 1.1611.

The document contains technical specifications for Texas Instruments integrated circuits (ADS8681W, ADS8685W, ADS8689W), including ESD handling precautions, revision history noting status changes from Advance Information to Production Data, mechanical and packaging information with orderable details, and disclaimers regarding technical data usage and liability limitations.

This email from Ann Schmidt to Jeff Dasovich dated July 10, 2001, contains news clippings about Enron and California's energy crisis. Key stories include: California electricity cost data showing diverse suppliers charged high prices, not just Texas firms targeted by Governor Davis; Duke Energy refusing to release certain bidding data to a Senate committee investigating price gouging; a federal judge proposing hundreds of millions in refunds for California's electricity overcharges, far below the $8.9 billion demanded; Neil McGregor, CEO of Enron's Indian Dabhol Power unit, resigning after contract expiration amid a payment dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board; Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay meeting Indian officials to resolve the $2.9 billion Dabhol project issues, stating more work is needed but expressing commitment to India; Tropic Networks announcing $60 million financing with Enron Broadband Services as an investor; and analysts maintaining "buy" ratings on Enron stock despite multiple challenges including the California crisis, India project troubles, and failed deals.

Grief is a unique emotional reaction to loss, varying by individual and circumstance. It can result from death, life changes, or anticipated losses. Common experiences include numbness, denial, yearning, guilt, anger, sadness, and disrupted sleep. The process is non-linear, with emotions fluctuating. Factors affecting grief include personality, life experience, and circumstances of loss. Older individuals may struggle more if they perceive limited time ahead. While intense grief eventually lessens, the deceased remains missed. Support from friends, family, or professionals can help.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with two data averaging modes: simple average (reduces output data rate by factor of 2) and moving average (no rate change). It features test patterns for debugging, including fixed pattern, digital ramp, and alternating test pattern modes for two channel groups (CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]). The device supports speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for one channel pair while other channels idle. Reset occurs via logic 0 on RESET pin or writing to address 0x00; power-down via logic 0 on PWDN pin or writing to address 0xC0. Initialization requires a sequence of register writes with free-running sampling clock. SPI configuration uses three register banks with 16-bit registers addressable via 8-bit addresses; register writes require two 24-bit frames (bank selection then data), while reads require four frames. Daisy-chain topology allows multiple devices with shared CS/SCLK, requiring N×24 SCLKs per frame where N equals device count. Key registers include: 0x00 (SPI mode, read enable), 0x01 (daisy-chain length), 0x03 (bank selection), 0x0D (data format, averaging enable), 0x13/0x18 (test patterns), 0x37 (speed-boost mode), and 0xC0 (channel power-down). For ATE applications, the device achieves 0.0015% TUE post-calibration at 25°C±5°C and offers two bandwidth modes: low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) for fast multiplexed signal settling.

The New England Patriots had one of their worst offensive performances during the Tom Brady era against the Miami Dolphins on Monday night, gaining only two yards in the first quarter and going 0-11 on third downs. Despite trailing by seven in the final minute, they had a chance to force overtime with an onside kick recovery. However, kicker Stephen Gostkowski's onside kick attempt was described by ESPN commentator Jon Gruden as "the most bizarre onside kick I've ever seen." The Dolphins recovered and won the game.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell at Vanderbilt University reported in Nature Materials a tenfold improvement in hyperlens imaging capability by using isotopically purified boron nitride crystals. The advance reduces optical losses and extends polariton lifetime three-fold, potentially enabling resolution of 30-nanometer objects—small enough to view viruses on living cells. Unlike electron or atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses can image living organisms in natural environments using low-energy infrared light, which also provides spectroscopic material identification. The technology has applications in biological science, communications, and nanoscale optics. Further improvements are theoretically possible with larger crystals.

Beating the offside trap requires strikers to remain in onside positions when the ball is passed, recognizing when defenders move up rather than retreat. Attackers must adjust through tactics including: dribbling through without passing, timing through passes properly, making horizontal or checking runs, passing short or back to buy time, executing deep-lying or bending runs, delaying runs, and using designated non-runners. Success leaves strikers one-on-one with the goalkeeper and often discourages future trap use.

Ocean acidification from absorbed carbon dioxide damages coral reefs and oyster hatcheries, but research on periwinkle sea snails shows some calcifying organisms may adapt. When exposed to predicted 2100 ocean conditions (pH 7.85), periwinkles maintained shell production by creating less-dense inner shells and developing less-soluble, more resistant shells despite metabolic decline, suggesting potential adaptive capacity for some calcifying organisms.

The District Court of Humacao's judgment in People v. Roldán (No. 2032, decided June 26, 1923) was reversed and the defendant acquitted based on the same reasoning as People v. Soldán (No. 2037), as both cases involved identical issues, evidence, and errors. Chief Justice Del Toro and Justices Aldrey and Hutchison concurred; Justice Wolf did not participate.

China blacklisted Canadian technology research firm TechInsights, adding it to the "unreliable entity list" after the firm published analysis of Huawei's advanced AI chips. The ban prohibits Chinese organizations from collaborating with or supplying data to TechInsights, cutting off a significant market for its semiconductor research services. TechInsights is known for reverse engineering and chip teardown analyses used by governments and corporations to track export compliance and assess rival technology sectors. Analysts say the move reflects China's tightening control over tech information flows and escalating global semiconductor tensions, warning foreign firms against investigating Chinese chip manufacturing. The blacklisting highlights growing fragility in international technology research collaboration as geopolitical competition increases.

Netflix shares declined slightly last week following a Barron's cover story suggesting the stock could lose over half its value. The article cited Disney's planned content withdrawal by 2019, Facebook's new video service, Amazon Prime competition, Netflix's cash burn, and unconventional accounting as risks. However, Netflix has grown its subscriber base from 23.6 million to over 104 million since Amazon launched Prime Video in 2011, demonstrating resilience against competition. The company has successfully raised U.S. prices 25% since 2014 and recently increased prices in Australia and Canada without losing subscribers. Netflix's large subscriber base creates cost advantages and attracts content creators, forming a competitive moat. The author argues that bearish valuation scenarios have historically proven wrong as Netflix exceeded growth expectations.

A study published in Pediatrics found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window-blind related injuries, with entanglement in cords causing nearly 80% of hospitalizations and 94% of 271 deaths. Most incidents occurred at home when children were unsupervised for brief periods. Researchers and safety advocates are calling for mandatory standards requiring cordless or inaccessible cord blinds, noting that voluntary standards since 1996 have been insufficient. The Window Covering Manufacturers Association proposed revised voluntary standards in 2017 requiring stock products to be cordless, with expected compliance by late 2018. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission supports mandatory rulemaking and recommends cordless coverings in homes with children.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Evercreech, was remanded in custody after admitting multiple assaults at Taunton Crown Court. The attacks included punching a woman in the face and leaving a man unconscious in a pub toilet. Kerr, who has previous convictions dating to 2008, showed no remorse, telling a probation worker one victim "deserved what was coming to him." His defense requested psychiatric reports for sentencing, but Judge David Ticehurst adjourned the case until October 13.

Peterborough City Council has brought 31% of long-term empty homes back into use last year and 663 over five years, generating £3 million in government bonuses. The council faces severe funding cuts, with government grants reduced 80% from £55 million to £10 million over eight years, and warns this may not sustain vital services. Two Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago show early success in reducing littering and unauthorised cycling. A new mental health service called CHUMS launches this week to support children and young people with mild-moderate issues.

Cookbook author and chef Shannon Bard announced Wednesday that Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she owned with her husband Tom, has permanently closed. Bard cited changing family priorities as their children reach their final years of high school and first year of college, noting their children had sacrificed for their restaurant industry dreams. The Bards opened Zapoteca six years ago and still operate two Kennebunk restaurants (Toroso and Salud), a cooking school, and a catering company. Bard published "The Gourmet Mexican Kitchen" in 2015 and made television appearances on Food Network shows including "Beat Bobby Flay." She cooked at the James Beard House in 2014.

This passage describes a clinical study (DAWN - Donated Antibodies Working agaiNst COVID-19) evaluating convalescent plasma therapy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees and conducted per Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with informed consent required. The global COVID-19 toll is noted (149+ million cases, 3+ million deaths). Current treatments show limited benefit: dexamethasone and tocilizumab help in hyperinflammatory phase, while remdesivir shows minimal benefit. Convalescent plasma trials show mixed results, possibly due to timing, volume, or antibody levels. The study hypothesizes that high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma given early reduces mechanical ventilation needs. Primary objective: evaluate efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus supportive care versus supportive care alone. Secondary objective: assess clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization outcomes.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures the average US Equity market exposure reported by its members through weekly surveys. The indicator uses a two-week moving average of responses, with high readings suggesting bullish sentiment and low readings indicating bearish sentiment. While often used as a contrarian indicator, backtests revealed poor performance compared to alternatives like the VIX. The index is not predictive and only reflects past adjustments by active managers.

Lubrizol Corp. is expanding its engineered polymers thermoplastics polyurethane (TPU) business with an US$80 million investment across North America, Europe, and Asia due to increased demand. New capacity in North America will come onstream later this year. In Songjiang, China, a new compounding line and extrusion lines were inaugurated, marking the fourth major expansion there since the early 2000s, with further Asian investment planned for 2019. In Europe, production capabilities for elastomers, aliphatics, and adhesives are being extended, with another major expansion planned for 2019. Headquartered in Wickliffe, Ohio, Lubrizol operates manufacturing facilities in 17 countries and reported 2016 revenues of US$6.5 billion.

Australian boxer Jeff Horn faces Gary Corcoran in a WBO welterweight title defense in Brisbane, with promoter Bob Arum stating a victory could lead to major 2018 fights including a potential bout with Terence Crawford. Horn, unbeaten in 18 fights, seeks to prove his controversial win over Manny Pacquiao was legitimate. The buildup featured tensions over head-butting accusations and biting threats, with both camps exchanging symbolic gestures at press events. Corcoran, ranked 10th by the WBO and fighting outside Britain/Ireland for the first time, remains confident despite being the underdog.

President Trump announced a deal with Pfizer to lower drug prices for Medicaid and patients, with Pfizer also agreeing to launch new medicines at prices matching other countries. In exchange, Pfizer may avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs if it continues U.S. manufacturing investment. Policy experts question the deal's actual impact on affordability, noting Medicaid enrollees already pay minimal out-of-pocket costs and that existing laws require drugmakers to offer Medicaid their lowest U.S. prices. Sanofi confirmed it is under European Commission investigation for potential anticompetitive activity.

Manchester City faces Burnley at Etihad Stadium on January 2, with kickoff at 10:00 AM ET, broadcast on NBC. City aims to continue winning to challenge Chelsea for the title, while Burnley seeks points to avoid relegation. Sergio Aguero returns for City after missing the Hull City match. Kevin de Bruyne and David Silva are key to breaking down Burnley's defense. Burnley relies on Andre Gray and Sam Vokes for goals but has struggled away from home. Guardiola emphasizes winning midfield battles and defending set pieces, where Burnley excels. City needs an early goal to prevent Burnley from gaining momentum.

This study investigated neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS) using EEG recordings of 19 adults with TS and 19 matched controls during median nerve electrical stimulation. Neural noise was operationalized as increased trial-by-trial variability in response magnitude and timing. Results showed no between-group differences in timing, temporal variability, or topography of early/mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) components, though the P100 SEP component was significantly increased in TS and correlated with tic severity. Trial-by-trial variability was substantially higher in TS throughout trials but normalized following stimulation. The TS group exhibited flatter 1/f noise slopes at beta/gamma frequencies, indicating increased asynchronous neural activity. Inter-trial phase coherence increased post-stimulation for both groups, though with delayed synchronization in TS. These findings suggest that trial-by-trial recruitment of sensorimotor neural populations is less stable at rest in TS, likely due to dysfunctional striatal-thalamic efferents, but normalizes with stimulation.

Facebook released a detailed 8,000-word rule book for its community standards, replacing a brief public version with previously internal guidelines. The company aims to increase transparency amid criticism over hate speech, terrorism promotion, and cooperation with repressive governments. New policies allow appeals for individual content removals and provide specific reasons for takedowns. Facebook uses 7,500 moderators and automated software to enforce rules, with standards updated biweekly at Content Standards Forums. The document covers prohibited content including cannibalism videos (with medical exceptions), non-medical drug use admissions, cursing at minors, and hacked content without newsworthiness. Content violating local laws is blocked in specific countries but not globally.

On June 20, 2017, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of $1 billion in 3.000% Notes due 2027, pursuant to an Underwriting Agreement dated June 13, 2017 with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Merrill Lynch as underwriters. The Notes, issued under a 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company as trustee, will pay semi-annual interest on June 20 and December 20, maturing on June 20, 2027. They constitute senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple's other unsecured debt.

A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive force allegations for punching Jon "Chris" Erwin seven times during a 2011 arrest outside a restaurant. The jury unanimously found Hudson's force reasonable after two days of testimony. The incident, captured on video and widely shared on social media, occurred when Hudson attempted to arrest Erwin for disorderly conduct at a private party. Hudson testified that Erwin refused orders, put hands on him, and resisted arrest. Erwin, who sustained facial injuries, maintained he was not resisting and sought to highlight police accountability. The city of Little Rock and the restaurant had settled with Erwin before trial, leaving Hudson personally liable for any damages. Former police chief Stuart Thomas testified that repeated face punches were permissible when necessary and reasonable. Witnesses gave conflicting accounts of whether Erwin was intoxicated or threatening. Hudson expressed vindication; Erwin stated his goal was removing bad officers.

Finnish press largely ignored U.S. official statements on the war. Finns grew irritated with German troops perceived as ineffective, yet remained dependent on Germany for military supplies and food. German influence persisted through press censorship, including suppression of parts of the Pope's Christmas message. The Social Democratic Party showed increasing restiveness, submitting a memorial to the Prime Minister on January 3 highlighting war hardships and food maldistribution. The gap between Socialists and Conservatives widened, raising concerns in Berlin about potential socialist peace movements. Popular discontent grew despite official exhortations for resolve, with civilians and soldiers questioning holding distant Soviet Karelia. Continued moderate Soviet activity risked wearing down Finnish resistance through economic and popular strain. Soviet official Vyshinski denied knowledge of rumored Soviet-Finnish government conversations. U.S. official Higgs met with Finnish representative Toivola, expressing concern over Finnish press attacks on the United States and censorship of U.S. Legation communications, warning these actions could damage Finnish interests with American and British supporters. Toivola agreed and planned to urge Helsinki toward more careful consideration, acknowledging press neutrality was impossible regarding Germany due to dependence, while Higgs suggested German inspiration behind anti-U.S. attacks.

This paper addresses process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) through ontology design patterns (ODPs). The authors identify three core requirements for MSE process modeling: process structure, data and resources, and project goals with participant roles. They survey existing ontologies including P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, General Process Ontology, and PMDcore, evaluating their alignment with these requirements. A baseline automated method using semantic similarity techniques and the ROBOT extraction framework is proposed for identifying ODPs. Evaluation results show P-PLAN performs best for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore supports all three categories. The method demonstrates promise but has limitations including annotation quality bias and isolated ontology processing. Future work aims to expand subdomain coverage, integrate cross-ontology mappings, and develop a community platform for pattern publication.

FSU linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital and moved to Brooks Rehabilitation in Jacksonville after being shot in the back of the head on August 31 in a case of mistaken identity. Pritchard is alert, responsive, and able to communicate. Four people were arrested in connection with the shooting. The FSU team cheered Pritchard as he left the hospital. His father, Earl Pritchard, thanked supporters including coach Mike Norvell, hospital staff, and law enforcement.

Old Forge High School students Christian Killino, Iain Kerrigan and Kole Barbetti organized a Math-a-thon that raised $3,864 for St. Jude's Research Hospital. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary on June 4; new board members include Diane Fox as vice president, Melissa Rickard as president-elect, Diane Popovich as treasurer, Pat Kandrovy as secretary and Mary Lou Davis as assistant treasurer. The nonprofit organization presented over $250,000 to the hospital during the previous president's term and has two major fundraisers scheduled. Hannah Perry Burgess, fifth-generation beekeeper and owner of the Beekeeper's Daughter, presented a program on honey bees and conservation at the Scranton City Chapter of the DAR meeting.

GoDaddy is terminating its domain hosting of neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer after the site published an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. The article called Heyer "fat" and "childless" and said "most people are glad she is dead." GoDaddy cited concerns that the post could incite additional violence. The Daily Stormer initially claimed it had been hacked and would shut down, but contributor Andrew Auernheimer admitted this was a prank. Publisher Andrew Anglin said he was trying to regain control of the site. The Daily Stormer, founded in 2013, is known for orchestrating harassment campaigns through its "Troll Army" and has previously been banned by PayPal and other services.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak linked to an Eid al-Adha barbecue in Cardiff. Twenty-two cases were identified among 43 attendees (51% attack rate). A cohort study of 36 people and nested case-control study using Firth logistic regression found consumption of the traditional raw liver dish "marrara" was the most likely infection vehicle (aOR: 49.99, 95%CI 1.71-1461.54, p=0.02). Food samples from two local butchers with a common supplier yielded identical whole genome sequences to human isolates. The outbreak highlighted severe illness (54% sought emergency care, 27% admitted overnight) likely due to high infective dose from raw liver. Cases were part of a larger 5 SNP cluster dating to 2018 across Wales and England. Public Health Wales developed culturally sensitive food safety messaging through community engagement, now used annually for World Food Safety Day and Eid al-Adha. The investigation identified a new outbreak vehicle and recommends future investigations consider culturally relevant foods beyond standard questionnaires.

An appeals court ruled the federal government cannot legally stop interstate trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S., finding the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lacked authority under the Lacey Act to restrict such shipments. The 2012-2015 bans on importing and transporting certain constrictor species across state lines remain in effect for imports, and state laws like Florida's pet python prohibition are unaffected. The North Carolina-based United States Association of Reptile Keepers sued in 2013 to overturn the ban, arguing most exotic snakes are domestically bred and can only survive wild in limited areas. The court cited grammar guides to interpret the act's wording as only authorizing restrictions on trade between the continental U.S. and territories, not within the 49 contiguous states.

A hockey coach discusses his team's performance in a playoff series against New Jersey, noting that the pace slowed in the second period after Holik's missed opportunity, which suited his team better. He explains they used three centers (Nieuwendyk, Modano) and four sets of wingers, doubling shifts for different centers in each half of periods. The coach describes the game as becoming purely about emotion and enthusiasm rather than technical strategy, comparing it to previous experiences in an Edmonton series. He states his team finally started hanging onto the puck and making plays, gaining confidence, but acknowledges they still need to outplay New Jersey in more areas to win, as the Devils remain slightly in control. The team stayed overnight after the game to maintain schedule consistency. He mentions players were so focused they were oblivious to surroundings, and that both goaltenders (Brodeur and Belfour) played exceptionally well.

The passage argues that declining birth rates and family disintegration threaten national survival, calling willful sterility a sin leading to "national death." It then addresses Congress on two policy matters: developing American shipping through legislation benefiting seaboard states like Maine, Louisiana, and Washington, with fallback provisions for South American mail lines if broader measures fail; and reforming currency laws to address seasonal fluctuations, high call money rates, and credit uncertainty that harm commerce. The speaker endorses a Treasury Department plan allowing national banks to issue taxed notes proportional to their capital to address monetary stringency without disturbing existing bond arrangements or creating bank profits.

Fad diets are not a healthy or sustainable way to lose weight, according to dietician Bonnie Taub-Dix. She advocates for a non-diet approach focused on reconnecting with food and establishing a healthy relationship with one's body. Taub-Dix emphasizes moderation and notes that fat is an important dietary component, even for weight loss. This approach promotes long-term healthy habits rather than deprivation.

Gold Coast Titans signed veteran fullback Michael Gordon to a two-year NRL deal after he was released from his Sydney Roosters contract. The 34-year-old will fill the void left by Jarryd Hayne's departure and is expected to assume goal kicking duties. Gordon, a former NSW representative who grew up in northern NSW, expressed excitement about returning home. Roosters coach Trent Robinson praised Gordon's contributions and wished him well.

Morgan McSweeney, a biotech scientist known as "Dr. Noc" on social media, discusses his approach to science communication in a STAT podcast interview. With 4 million followers across platforms and a Ph.D. in pharmaceutical sciences and immunology, McSweeney creates "edutainment" content—combining education with an engaging, digestible format for general audiences. He initially felt embarrassed about social media science communication but gained confidence as his reach grew, with casual videos attracting far more views than his published research. His content often addresses misinformation through reaction videos and explains scientific concepts in actionable ways, such as how dietary fiber affects cardiovascular health. McSweeney deliberately targets confused but open-minded viewers rather than preaching to supporters or arguing with committed opponents, finding that nuanced, less emotionally charged content better informs people despite reducing algorithmic reach. He emphasizes that audiences crave detail and transparency about scientific uncertainty rather than simplified directives. Personal elements, like mentioning his wife, build trust more effectively than credentials alone. McSweeney maintains his biotech day job separately from his content creation and believes institutions like the WHO struggle to produce engaging material due to resource limitations, bureaucratic review processes, and the genuine difficulty of developing video-making skills. He handles hostility by blocking rather than engaging and advocates for more diverse science communicators so audiences can find trusted voices that resonate with them.

The Coppock Curve Strategy is a long-term momentum indicator created by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 for the Episcopal Church. It uses a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month rate-of-change indicators to identify significant market swings, primarily in stocks. Trading signals occur when the curve crosses above zero (entry) or below zero (exit). Backtesting on monthly S&P 500 charts since 1960 produced only 12 trades over 63 years, with all being profitable, approximately 80% and 65% gains on two example trades lasting about six years each. The strategy reduces drawdown and market exposure time compared to buy-and-hold, with better risk-adjusted returns, though the small number of trades limits statistical significance. The ROC values of 11 and 14 were derived from Coppock's research on mourning recovery periods.

Nick Foles, the Philadelphia Eagles' backup quarterback turned Super Bowl LII starter, faces an uncertain future despite potentially leading the team to its first championship since 1960. While a Super Bowl win would make him a permanent fan favorite, starter Carson Wentz remains the franchise's long-term quarterback upon recovering from his torn ACL. Foles' contract allows free agency after 2018, and a Super Bowl victory could increase trade interest from quarterback-needy teams, though his quiet demeanor suggests he won't demand a move. Eagles executive Howie Roseman must weigh keeping Foles as a reliable backup against maximizing his trade value, with third-stringer Nate Sudfeld also developing behind him.

President Reagan addresses the 100th Congress in 1987, the Constitution's bicentennial year, congratulating members and Speaker Jim Wright. He highlights economic achievements including low inflation, reduced interest rates, and 13 million new jobs. Reagan takes full responsibility for the Iran-Contra affair's failure while defending its goals. He urges Congress to support defense spending, noting Soviet military investments and global expansion, and opposes cuts to security assistance. He reaffirms commitment to the Monroe Doctrine regarding Central America, specifically opposing the Sandinista regime in Nicaragua, and insists SDI will proceed despite Soviet opposition. Domestically, he calls for a balanced budget amendment, line-item veto, welfare reform, catastrophic illness coverage for elderly, enhanced competitiveness through education and research, and allowing voluntary prayer in schools. He concludes by emphasizing "We the people" as the Constitution's distinguishing principle, expressing optimism for America's future.

The passage describes the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors, covering system MMU features, L4 peripheral memory maps, DDR DMM TILER extended addressing with 4 GB of additional range for rotated/mirrored frame buffer access, package pin assignments, and boot configuration terminal functions. Boot mode pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot configuration and GPMC peripheral functions, sampled at reset to determine boot settings before functioning as GPMC data/address pins.

Players discuss needing better effort and teamwork, acknowledging they weren't fully engaged in most games except one they won. They emphasize not getting outworked, playing for teammates, and fixing defensive focus. Issues include poor shot selection, passing instead of shooting, and lack of synchronization, with powerplay struggles against Pittsburgh's offensive weapons.

The UND campus senate's executive committee will discuss a draft resolution from NDSU Faculty Senate at its Wednesday meeting to determine if the wider body would support it. The resolution declares a "crisis of confidence" in the North Dakota University System due to budget cuts, consolidation efforts, and perceived lack of support from state leadership. It calls for improved advocacy through "supportive collaborations" and a Higher Education Summit with stakeholders including the governor. UND Senate Chair Dana Harsell noted that changing circumstances could make the resolution irrelevant, and the NDSU Faculty Senate had not planned to send it beyond the 11 system campuses.

The author wrote this book to address the challenge of building distributed systems from scratch, which wastes time and produces less polished results. Containers and container orchestrators now enable reusable components and shared patterns for distributed systems. The book aims to provide practitioners with a shared language and standard library to build better systems more efficiently, making distributed system development more approachable through repeatable, generic patterns.

This is an Energy Central Research Report Watch email newsletter from February 20, 2002, sent to khyatt@enron.com. The email promotes recently published research reports on the power industry, including European utility profiles, home energy improvement loans and audits, country-specific utility industry reports, company profiles, and various InfoGrid reports. Reports are available for purchase ranging from $50 to $4,995, with options for online access or hard copy delivery. Contact Mark Johnson at 800-459-2233 for orders or inquiries. The email includes unsubscribe instructions and is copyrighted by CyberTech, Inc.

This MIT lecture on sustainable real estate finance covers how capital flows through green buildings from tenants to owners to developers, and how sustainable finance principles apply to real estate assets. The instructor explains portfolio theory showing how green buildings, as a fourth asset class, shift the efficient frontier northwest due to lower risk and higher returns from regulatory advantages and tenant preferences. The lecture details mortgage markets, where climate risk increases default risk for properties in flood or wildfire zones, while green mortgages offer lower interest rates and higher loan-to-value ratios because energy-efficient homes have lower default risk—especially for low-income households who benefit most from reduced utility costs. The instructor also describes innovative financing where banks lend additional upfront capital for renovations based on expected post-improvement property value increases. The session concludes with an introduction to private equity's growing ESG integration in investment decisions.

National Weather Service Lubbock issued zone forecasts for the South Plains area of Texas on March 18, 2018. A wind advisory was in effect until 7 AM CDT Monday for all zones. Sunday night featured windy conditions with west winds 15-35 mph, areas of blowing dust, and lows in the 40s-50s. Monday remained windy with northwest winds 20-35 mph and highs in the 60s. Monday night brought colder temperatures with lows in the 30s. Tuesday through Thursday showed warming trends with sunny to mostly sunny skies, reaching highs in the 80s by Thursday. Friday through Sunday maintained mostly sunny conditions with highs in the 70s-90s and lows in the 40s-50s. Some zones reported a 20% chance of thunderstorms Saturday night.

Patrick Kane discusses lineup combinations, noting Toews, Sharp, and Hossa on one line with Handzus and Bickell. He mentions Ryan Suter's long shifts and reach as a defensive challenge, emphasizing using speed against players like Chara. Kane reflects positively on playing overseas before the season started. He acknowledges the difficulty of watching Vancouver win the Cup after Chicago's 2010 victory, making them no longer defending champions. He notes increased attention and ticket requests during the Finals, calling it a special opportunity. Kane praises Boston's defensive performance against Pittsburgh, particularly Rask's goaltending, while acknowledging Toronto and others had some success against them. He feels he and teammates from 2010 have become more well-rounded players, especially defensively. Kane describes learning to handle recognition in Chicago, appreciating the passionate fanbase. He emphasizes back-checking as a team requirement, citing Hossa as the hardest worker. Kane states he performs better with the puck, focusing on making plays rather than worrying about scoring statistics.

Treasury market bears recovered some losses on Wednesday after Italian government instability triggered safe-haven buying of U.S. government debt, forcing traders to close short positions. CME Group data showed open interest in Treasury futures plunged over 400,000 contracts on Tuesday, with 2-year note futures dropping 266,000 contracts and 10-year futures falling 137,000 as trading volume hit records. The 10-year Treasury yield had fallen to 2.759 percent on Tuesday before rising to 2.855 percent Wednesday. Tuesday's rally produced a 0.952 percent total return, the largest since July 2011. A J.P. Morgan survey showed clients were least bearish on Treasuries since April 2017. Analysts warn bearish bets remain vulnerable to European political developments, including Italy's government formation and a possible Spanish no-confidence vote.

Havant Borough Council in Hampshire has banned bouncy castles and other inflatables on its land following the death of three-year-old Ava-May Littleboy, who suffered a fatal head injury when thrown from an inflatable trampoline that exploded at Gorleston Beach, Norfolk on Sunday. The ban will remain until the cause of the explosion is identified and risks can be properly managed.

Michael Leighton discusses his career, including his daughter's birth before a game, working with Jeff Reese to change his goaltending style, and his nervousness before playoff games. He mentions facing skilled opponents, his approach against opposing goalies like Niemi, his unexpected opportunity with the Flyers after being with Carolina, his stomach and groin surgery the previous summer, and the difficulty of building rivalry hatred against an unfamiliar opponent.

Gold prices exceeded $4,000 per ounce on Tuesday due to expectations of Federal Reserve monetary policy easing, driven by weak U.S. retail and manufacturing data. The rally reflects investor demand for safety amid global uncertainty, with anticipated rate cuts by early 2026 making non-yielding assets more attractive. Central banks, particularly in Asia and the Middle East, continue net buying, while geopolitical tensions and fiscal pressures further support gold's appeal. Analysts note potential short-term corrections if Fed signals shift hawkishly, but sustained high prices could reshape 2025 asset allocation toward precious metals.

Wikipedia's Italian and Spanish sites blocked all articles on July 3, 2018, to protest proposed EU copyright law changes. The protest targeted Articles 11 and 13 of the EU Copyright Directive, which would require content filtering systems and create a "link tax." The European Parliament was scheduled to vote on July 5, 2018. Italian Wikipedia editors warned the directive would harm internet openness and put Wikipedia at risk. English Wikipedia displayed a protest banner instead of blocking content. Critics, including Jimmy Wales and the EFF, criticized the legislation's vague wording and potential to restrict online freedom, while supporters like German MEP Axel Voss argued it would correct copyright imbalances.

The Twin Rivers Council of the Boy Scouts is enrolling girls in Cub Scouts immediately, ahead of the national fall 2018 launch. The council aims to involve girls and families by spring so they can attend summer camping programs. Mark Switzer, the Scout Executive, expressed enthusiasm about daughters participating alongside sons. The council hopes to enroll 125 girls in grades K-3 by March 31st. Interested families can find packs through the "Be a Scout" website or by calling 518-869-6436. The program modification addresses families' time constraints and desire for shared activities.

Audi's Q8 flagship SUV will feature an aggressive hexagonal grille, vertical slats, and scowling headlamps similar to its 2017 Detroit Auto Show concept. Expected to debut in Shanghai in early June, the Q8 shares Volkswagen Group's MLB platform with the Audi Q7, Bentley Bentayga, and Lamborghini Urus. Its slope-backed design includes a full-band taillight treatment. While the concept had a plug-in hybrid powertrain with 443 horsepower, the production model's powertrain remains unconfirmed, though a 48-volt mild hybrid system is likely.

Earth Day, established in 1970, has evolved from practical environmental action into what the author describes as a "pagan rite" driven by "Big Environment"—powerful organizations that prioritize environmental concerns above all else. The author criticizes local environmental group Protect South Portland for passing the Clear Skies Ordinance, which banned Canadian oil sands and cost taxpayers millions in legal defense while damaging the oil industry. The author also attacks wind power projects supported by Senator Angus King, arguing turbines ruin Maine's wilderness landscape without providing meaningful energy output. The author accuses environmental groups of manufacturing fear to raise funds, comparing them to televangelists exploiting the fearful. Despite acknowledging legitimate 1970s environmental achievements, the author suggests Earth Day should return to practical activities like litter cleanup rather than serving "Big Environment's political and financial benefit."

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July, up 7.8% year-to-date, though August began with a 1.6% decline. Market momentum remains intact but short-term technicals show warning signs, with volatility and credit spreads seeing seasonal increases. Investors are increasing tech stock allocations while US electricity demand hit record highs. Netflix stock fell after Elon Musk urged followers to cancel subscriptions. The US government shutdown continues after a GOP funding bill failed in the Senate. ADP reported the largest private payroll drop in 2.5 years, increasing expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts. Frontier Markets led July returns, while US large-cap stocks placed third.

SpaceX launched an unmanned Falcon 9 rocket from Florida's Kennedy Space Center at 12:31 p.m. Monday, carrying 6,400 pounds of cargo to the International Space Station, including research experiments, 20 mice, and ice cream for the crew. The Dragon capsule is scheduled to arrive Wednesday. NASA packed vanilla, chocolate, and birthday cake ice cream cups plus candy bars using extra freezer space. U.S. astronaut Peggy Whitson, in orbit since November, is among the six crew members. SpaceX will attempt to land the booster at Cape Canaveral.

Legislators met in Finance Committee on 3 July to consider a government request for $20 million in supplementary budget funding, with half from reserves and half from the Environment Protection Fund. The Health Ministry requested $8 million for rising indigent and Seafarers health costs. Bodden Town West MLA Chris Saunders and Health Minister Dwayne Seymour discussed moving toward a national health insurance system and reviewing free healthcare for children. The funding was approved, with Saunders abstaining from the EPF withdrawal vote.

A blitz is a defensive football play where five or more defenders rush into the offensive backfield to attack the quarterback, compared to the typical four rushers. While this creates pressure and potential sacks, it leaves fewer defenders to cover receivers. Types include conventional blitzes, zone blitzes (where a linebacker rushes while a lineman drops into coverage), safety blitzes, cornerback blitzes, zero blitzes (no deep safety), and run blitzes. Offenses can counter with quick passes to open receivers (often running backs), mobile quarterbacks who can evade rushers, or max protection schemes with additional blockers.
