The defensive coordinator typically calls these plays to outsmart the offense and get the ball back quickly.

AnimationXpress compiled five romantic VFX moments from Indian cinema for Valentine's Day. In *Baahubali* (Makuta), effects created emerald butterflies, waterfalls, and moonlight chases for the "Dheevara" song. *Befikre* (yFX) fabricated a cliff-kissing scene with ocean views. *Shivaay* (NY VFXWAALA) produced a dreamlike tent sequence amid snow-covered mountains. *Sanam Re* (Pixel D) added snow to green scenery for silhouette love scenes. *Prem Ratan Dhan Payo* (NY VFXWAALA) created an enormous fortress and enabled double roles for Salman Khan and Sonam Kapoor.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended October 30, 2016. The company reported revenue of $2.004 billion for Q3 FY2017, up 54% year-over-year, with net income of $542 million ($0.83 per diluted share). For the nine-month period, revenue was $4.737 billion with net income of $1.012 billion. The GPU business generated $1.697 billion in Q3 revenue (up 53% YoY), while the Tegra Processor business contributed $241 million (up 87% YoY). Growth was driven by gaming, datacenter, professional visualization, and automotive markets. The company issued $2 billion in long-term notes (2.20% due 2021 and 3.20% due 2026) and had $6.67 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. NVIDIA returned $694 million to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends during the first nine months of FY2017, with plans to return $1.25 billion in FY2018. The board authorized an additional $2 billion for stock repurchases through December 2020.

The passage explains market sentiment indicators, focusing on the AAII (American Association of Individual Investors) sentiment index. Market sentiment measures the aggregate mood of investors—bullish, neutral, or bearish. The AAII index surveys members weekly on their 6-month market outlook. Backtests show that very bearish AAII readings (bull-bear spread below -20) yielded average gains of 1.03% over four weeks, while very bullish readings (spread above 40) produced negative average returns of -0.33%. The logic suggests extreme sentiment indicates potential reversals: when most participants are already positioned bullishly, fewer buyers remain to drive prices higher, and vice versa for bearish extremes. However, the authors conclude that while the AAII indicator shows expected patterns, better indicators exist for short-term trading.

Antarctic krill eject more food waste when consuming plastic-contaminated food. These tiny crustaceans influence the global carbon cycle through their feces and compact food masses that sink to the seafloor, though plastic's effects on this process remain unclear.

Coach Sutter discusses playoff strategy, emphasizing the value of top offensive players, time and score management, and the importance of veterans guiding younger players. He notes the team has maintained emotional stability for two months and handles breaks between series well. Sutter highlights nutrition, hydration, and travel routines as important factors. He addresses a player's dual role as physical presence and goal-scorer, stating confidence isn't an issue for the team. He observes the finals series has been very close with minimal gaps between games, praises opposing goalie Brodeur's performance, and stresses that small details during shifts can determine outcomes.

Romania's library system includes the National Library, public libraries, educational libraries, and specialized libraries, administratively subordinated to the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Culture, and local authorities. Academic LIS education began after 1999, with only four universities surviving from an initial seven. Three training pathways exist for librarians: bachelor's in LIS, bachelor's in another field plus post-graduation LIS program, or bachelor's in another field with competences assessed through occupational standards. The 2012 Occupational Standard "Librarian (Higher Education)" developed by the National Library of Romania defines professional competences including communication, IT, learning, social/civic, entrepreneurial, and cultural skills, plus specific activities like collection management, automation, and scientific research. Lifelong learning faces challenges from low salaries, low educational investment, and negative stereotypes about the profession, with few libraries complying with the legal requirement to allocate 5% of personnel expenses for training.

Residents of Greensboro's Cottage Grove community report declining housing conditions at Avalon Trace Apartments, including boarded windows, trash dumping, sewage leaks, inadequate heating, roaches, and mold. Mold has been linked to asthma cases in children. Collaborative Cottage Grove received a $250,000 BUILD Health Challenge grant, with Greensboro Housing Coalition, Cone Health, and UNCG's Center for Housing and Community Studies partnering to map asthma hot spots and connect residents to services. Cone Health is matching the grant with $250,000 in cash and in-kind services. The Guilford County Department of Public Health also participates, operating a mobile farmers market and diabetes prevention program.

China's July power generation reached a record 604.7 billion kWh, up 8.6% year-on-year, driven by thermal power output. January-July generation totaled 3.57 trillion kWh, up 6.8%. Thermal power rose 10.5% in July to 433.4 billion kWh, while solar grew fastest at 26.7% to 5.6 billion kWh. Nuclear increased 16.5%, wind 11.6%, and hydro edged up 0.2%.

Student journalists at The Miami Hurricane describe their work and advocate for protecting student newsrooms nationwide. They note that many peer publications face defunding or loss of editorial independence when absorbed into school communications programs. The authors argue that student newspapers need physical spaces, funding, and freedom from institutional control to practice journalism ethically and learn professional skills. They emphasize that threats to student journalism harm all students by limiting education about independent press functions. The piece supports the #SaveStudentNewsrooms movement started by the Independent Florida Alligator and encourages readers to engage with student journalism and oppose budget cuts threatening its survival.

This passage introduces a theoretical framework combining Bayesian persuasion with behavioral framing effects, where a sender communicates with a receiver through both signals and natural language framing. The authors propose three optimization variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing-recommendation. Their theoretical analysis shows that framing-only optimization is computationally hard and sensitive to errors, while joint optimization is more tractable with continuous utility and a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme. The authors implement a practical hill-climbing method using LLMs as belief oracles, demonstrating effectiveness through case studies involving real estate and advertising, with human validation showing directional correctness.

The Imperial Government defends its actions in Belgium, stating Belgium violated its neutrality by military cooperation with Britain and France, and that Germany had offered guarantees of Belgian territory and independence in exchange for passage. Germany claims responsibility for Belgium's fate lies with its government and allied powers, and protests charges against its conduct of war there. Germany states its adversaries declined peace overtures, making them responsible for continued bloodshed, while the four allied powers vow to continue fighting for honorable peace.

The Persian Minister expresses support for President Wilson's December 18, 1916 peace note, noting Persia's neutrality was violated by belligerent fighting on its territory, and requests U.S. assistance in maintaining Persian integrity at any future peace conference.

The U.S. Ambassador in Turkey reports the German Ambassador acknowledged potential justification for deporting Greeks as a war measure but had tried to prevent it due to expected hardship and loss of life. The German Ambassador admitted German influence with Turkish officials was minimal, with Turks often taking contrary action. The U.S. Ambassador warned that Greek massacres following Armenian ones would cause neutral indignation and hold Germany responsible, and suggested pressure on Berlin or Washington might be effective.

The adapter pattern modifies application container interfaces to conform to predefined standards, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, and other services across heterogeneous applications. Unlike modifying application containers directly, adapters provide modular, reusable solutions that decouple concerns and facilitate sharing. Examples include Prometheus exporters for monitoring, Fluentd for log normalization, and custom health check containers for databases. The pattern extends to distributed systems through microservices architectures, which offer reliability and agility benefits but introduce debugging complexity. Stateless replicated services with load balancing provide redundancy and horizontal scaling, while sharded services handle stateful data too large for single machines. Scatter/gather patterns parallelize computation across nodes for improved latency. Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) enables event-driven processing ideal for lightweight, stateless transformations but faces limitations with long-running processes, memory-intensive operations, and sustained high-volume workloads.

Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker underwent left wrist surgery on Monday but could play against the Kansas City Chiefs. Coach Liam Coen listed him as day-to-day. Walker was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's 26-21 victory over San Francisco and did not return. The 2022 No. 1 overall pick has two sacks, 12 tackles, and one pass breakup this season, having missed only two career games as a rookie.
A new study confirms that pasteurization completely inactivates the H5N1 bird flu virus in milk, though inactive viral proteins may remain.

A hockey player discusses his team's confidence and balanced scoring heading into a playoff series against the defending Stanley Cup champions, emphasizing their veteran experience, need to shoot frequently against goalie Hasek, and his own improved playoff performance.

A hockey team reflects on a shutout loss in the Stanley Cup Finals, acknowledging missed scoring chances, power play disadvantages, and self-inflicted mistakes rather than being outplayed. Players emphasize needing to capitalize on opportunities, hit the net more consistently, and maintain discipline, while expressing frustration with officiating and the missed chance to take a series lead. The team remains focused on self-improvement heading into a best-of-three series conclusion.

Department of Education officials met with a negotiated rule-making committee in Washington, D.C., and maintained they will not change their proposed definition of professional programs, which currently limits the category to 10 specific degrees including law, medicine, and theology. This stance means dozens of health-care graduate programs like clinical psychology and occupational therapy would face a $20,500 annual cap on federal student loans rather than the higher $50,000 annual/$200,000 total cap for professional programs. Committee members submitted an alternative definition that will be discussed Wednesday, with negotiations continuing through November before a vote. The department aims to curb excessive graduate student borrowing under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which must be implemented by July 1, 2026. Critics warn the limited list could reduce enrollment in critical fields, push students toward private loans with fewer protections, and decimate pipelines for mental health professionals.

ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE) mission received NASA approval in April 2016, moving it from design to implementation phase. The $114.4 million probe, scheduled to launch in 2022 and reach Jupiter by 2030, will spend three years studying the gas giant and three of its largest moons—Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa—to assess their habitability. NASA is contributing a UV spectrograph and components for two main instruments to JUICE's 10-instrument suite. The mission is ESA's first large-class project under its Cosmic Vision 2015-2025 program, with a critical design review planned within a year of approval.

Drake University's Student Activities Board (SAB) coordinates Painted Street for the Drake Relays. Co-chairs Karoline Sandusky and Meghan Mulligan select 54 organization squares based on creativity and theme incorporation, not first-come or rotation. Organizations submit designs within a week after Blitz Day's theme announcement. Small groups like DAAC self-fund paint and equipment, while the University provides paint for the paint fight. SAB President Anna Jensen, who previously served as Relays co-chair, finds painting over old squares emotional.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff at BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% went to Democrats in 2023-2024, up from a 6-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio in 2017-2020. The study by Notre Dame professor Derek Muller examined the nation's 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms. Total contributions were approximately $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups versus $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton (99.7%), Fried Frank (99.4%), and Mintz Levin (99.1%) had the highest Democratic contribution percentages, while Nelson Mullins (66.4%), Lewis Brisbois (77.3%), and Ogletree Deakins (81.5%) had the lowest.

The passage accuses Washington, DC lawmaker Trayon White of blaming Jews for weather conditions and claims anti-Semitism is tolerated within the Democrat Party. It lists nine Democrat lawmakers with alleged connections to Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, citing his anti-Semitic statements. The named Democrats are: former President Barack Obama, DNC Deputy Chairman Keith Ellison, Representatives Maxine Waters, Barbara Lee, Danny Davis, André Carson, James Clyburn, Al Green, and Gregory Meeks. The passage describes various interactions between these politicians and Farrakhan, including meetings, speeches, and praise, and alleges media cover-ups of these associations.

Olusola Simeon, 25, was convicted by a Magistrate court in Osogbo, Osun State for assaulting his girlfriend Fadunsi Alaba on July 2, 2018. Simeon pleaded guilty to beating Alaba when she came to live with him after six years of dating, angered that she discovered his wife and children at home. Magistrate Mrs Awodele Modupe Adedoyin remanded him to Ilesha prison and adjourned sentencing to August 3.

The lecture covers numerical methods for solving the second-order wave equation, presenting two formulations: as a second-order equation and as a first-order symmetric system with eigenvalues c and -c, indicating two-way wave propagation. The professor introduces semidiscrete methods (method of lines) where space is discretized but time remains continuous, analyzing solutions through exponential growth factors. For the fully discrete case using the leapfrog method, stability analysis yields a quadratic equation for the growth factor g, showing that stability requires the Courant number r = cΔt/Δx to be less than 1—the CFL condition. The lecture concludes with a preview of staggered grids, important in electromagnetism.

Wally Adams, 29, of Grande Prairie was arrested in Calgary on August 3 for possession of child pornography and making it available. RCMP executed a search warrant in Grande Prairie on August 2 following information from the National Child Exploitation Coordination Centre. Adams was released and will appear in court on September 27. The investigation continues.

San Juan High School's baseball coaches in Citrus Heights are warning schools and businesses about a fraudulent fundraising scheme where someone posing as part of the team solicited sponsorships from local businesses. An auto repair shop lost approximately $1,400 to a company called "Athletic Sports," which has no website and uses a UPS store postal box as its address. The team has filed a police report and posted the fraudulent flyer on social media to alert others, while urging businesses to verify donations directly with schools before contributing.

George McPhee discusses building the Vegas Golden Knights, emphasizing team-first mentality, strong leadership, and selecting quality people during the expansion draft. He reflects on emotional community events, coaching philosophy focused on patience and relatability, and the team's unexpected success without setting specific win goals. McPhee compares their playoff run to previous experiences, notes the salary cap era created unique expansion opportunities, and expresses excitement about reaching the Stanley Cup Finals without predetermined expectations.

The TSX rose 0.08% to 15,564.28, boosted by CN Rail up 1.2% despite lower quarterly profit, Restaurant Brands International up 3.7% on better-than-expected earnings, and materials stocks including Barrick Gold and Teck Resources up 3% each. Gold prices steadied after three days of losses. Seven of ten sectors gained. Mitel Networks rose 10.1% on a $2 billion sale announcement, while Prairiesky Royal fell 6.5% as the largest decliner. TSX volume was 15.44 million shares.

This study demonstrates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controlled method for defect engineering in monolayer MoS₂. CVD-grown samples were exposed to varying irradiation times (30s, 60s, 120s), with characterization through Raman, PL, XPS, KPFM, and first-principles calculations. Results showed increased chalcogen vacancy density with irradiation time, evidenced by Raman peak shifts and enhanced LO(M) mode intensity. XPS revealed Mo-O bonding indicating oxygen incorporation at vacancy sites, while KPFM showed increased work function (4.8 eV to 5.24 eV) confirming p-type doping. Temperature-dependent PL at 85K revealed defect-bound emissions (D peaks) at 200-300 meV below the A exciton, with intensity increasing and A exciton decreasing with irradiation. Power-dependent PL showed defect emission saturation, confirming bound exciton nature. Valley polarization decreased from 62% to 38% with defect density due to enhanced intervalley scattering. First-principles calculations confirmed that oxygen interactions at sulfur vacancies create acceptor states near the valence band, explaining the observed p-type behavior and defect emissions. The study establishes high-energy electron irradiation as a precise, controllable approach for introducing functional defects in 2D TMDs for optoelectronic and quantum device applications.

The article examines a gold trading strategy that activates when prices are near all-time highs. Gold prices are influenced by supply and demand, US Dollar fluctuations, investor behavior, central bank reserves, and jewelry demand. From 1955 to 2022, gold set 80 monthly all-time highs, averaging 1.25 per year, though it experienced a 14-year gap without new highs between 1981 and 2005. The backtested strategy, using monthly closing prices from the World Bank's Commodities Markets Database, showed decent performance with reduced drawdowns and only one-third market exposure time compared to buy-and-hold, helping identify gold bull regimes.

Japanese and Chinese military forces are massing in Korea following mutual troop deployments that allegedly violated an 1885 convention requiring prior written notice. Over 4,000 Japanese troops occupy Seoul and strategic positions, while China has sent additional forces to Chemulpo. Japan refuses to withdraw until China guarantees non-interference in Korean affairs; China refuses withdrawal until Japan does. Foreign representatives at Seoul proposed simultaneous withdrawal, but both governments declined. Japan has demanded governmental reforms in Korea as a condition for troop withdrawal. The Chinese Empress has reportedly diverted birthday celebration funds to military purposes. Conflict appears imminent.

Tencent added DC's Batman to Arena of Valor as an Assassin-class character with batrang and forearm blades, joining Wonder Woman, The Flash, The Joker, and Superman. The update includes a Death Match mode with five teams of two players on a colosseum map, where points above heroes mark high-value targets, and matches last eight minutes. Valor TV allows live match viewing, schedule checks, and competition recordings. The update also optimizes lobby menus, friends lists, and messaging systems.

The Wing-T offense is a football strategy developed by Coach Harold "Tubby" Raymond at the University of Delaware from 1966 to 2001. It uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to exploit aggressive defenses by making plays look similar. The offense requires at least two capable running backs, including a fullback who can run inside and catch passes, an athletic quarterback with good footwork, and smaller, quicker offensive linemen skilled at pulling and trapping.

Strengths include slowing down more talented defenses through deception, having established answers for defensive adjustments, and being uncommon in modern football. The main weakness is limited traditional dropback passing, though many teams incorporate spread formations.

Common formations include the Wing (100/900), Wing-Slot (Red/Doubles 100), and Unbalanced. Key running plays are the Buck Sweep, Down play (Belly G), and Trap. Common pass plays include the Waggle, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass.

While rare in major college football, the Wing-T remains popular at the high school level. Coaches like Gus Malzahn have combined Wing-T principles with spread offenses successfully.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end and precision reference, supporting nine configuration registers and multiSPI interface protocols. The device operates in ACQ (signal acquisition), CONV (conversion), and RESET states, with transitions controlled by CONVST/CS and RST signals. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge, with 32-bit optimal frames required for valid commands; frames can be short (invalid writes, partial reads), optimal, or long (last 32 bits used). Supported protocols include four SPI-compatible modes (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) for configuration, with single or dual SDO-x options, plus source-synchronous (SRC) protocols using internal or external clocks. Key registers control device ID, reset/power (NAP and power-down modes), SDI/SDO protocols, data output formatting, input range selection, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis. The device features two power supplies (AVDD/DVDD), programmable alarms for input and AVDD, and requires specific decoupling capacitors for optimal performance.

Vishay Intertechnology (NYSE:VSH) shares rose 2.08% recently, closing at $19.65. Analysts project a 52-week price target of $20, with a high of $22 and low of $18 based on 4 opinions. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 3.75 from 4 analysts, ranking 138th out of 265 industries. Recommendations include 1 Buy, 3 Hold, 1 Underperform, and 1 Sell. The ATR-14 is 0.55, weekly volatility is 2.47%, monthly volatility is 2.50%, and RSI is 53.51. Market capitalization is $2.83 billion with 144.15 million outstanding shares; average trading volume is 1.5 million shares.

Scale AI laid off over a dozen contractors in its Dallas office from the NPO team, which handled generalist AI tasks like improving chatbot writing. The company attributed the cuts to an industry shift toward expert-driven data labeling work. Affected workers received four weeks of severance and healthcare through October, and were invited to join Scale's gig-work platform Outlier. Scale AI stated the cuts affect a small fraction of its workforce and don't impact customer delivery, while continuing to expand expert-level programs. The move follows previous downsizing, including September cuts to generalist AI tutors and twelve Red Team members.

Immunogenicity will be analyzed descriptively by treatment group without statistical tests. ADA incidence will be calculated from evaluable patients, defined as those with at least one post-dose sample appropriate for ADA testing. The numerator includes treatment-induced ADA patients (baseline-negative becoming positive) and treatment-boosted ADA patients (baseline-positive with ≥5-fold titer increase), divided by total evaluable patients. Baseline-positive patients without post-dose samples are excluded from evaluable patients. Unscheduled dosing visit results must be included for ADA-positive patients.

The passage provides board layout guidelines for the ADS9803, including avoiding crossing digital lines with analog signal paths, using 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors near power-supply pins without vias, and placing reference decoupling capacitors close to REFIO and REFM pins. It also describes TI's support resources, documentation update notifications, trademark information, ESD handling precautions, and disclaimers regarding technical data and liability limitations.

Corning Incorporated, a specialty chemicals and materials company founded in 1851, manages innovation through its Growth and Strategy Council (GSC), established in 2001 and centralized under CEO Wendell Weeks in 2002. The GSC, comprising the CEO, COO, and CTO plus key executives, meets several times monthly to oversee high-potential innovation projects in Stages 2-4, make resource allocation decisions, and maintain balanced investment across existing and developing businesses. This structure emerged after the 2000-2002 telecommunications crash, which reduced revenues from $6.3 billion to $3.1 billion and stock from $100 to $1.50, teaching Corning lessons about risk management and strategic balance. By 2008, Corning had recovered with four business segments (Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, Life Sciences), $5.86 billion revenue, and 10% RD&E spending. The GSC complements the Corning Technology Council (handling early-stage projects) and operates through honest dialogue, zero-based budgeting, and "patient money" philosophy—investing for long-term payback. Challenges include scaling the process as Corning targets doubling innovation rate to 2-4 businesses per decade, managing larger meetings, and adapting to diverse new business models.

The article presents a trading strategy for the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ) using Donchian Channels with short-term settings and an Exponential Moving Average filter. The strategy takes only long positions when price breaks above the Donchian Channel while above the EMA. Optimization testing found settings of Donchian Channel length 3 and EMA 200 produced robust results, outperforming buy-and-hold with lower volatility. The strategy showed 87 trades from September 2016 to present. Testing on a 2-hour timeframe also showed promising results, though the authors caution that short-term trading is difficult and recommend out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period before live trading due to limited data and curve fitting risks.

A player reflects on a tough loss, acknowledging the team needs to improve in areas like limiting turnovers and making smarter plays on the bluelines. Despite being the better team early and giving themselves a chance to win, they failed to come through in the third period and made it too easy on their opponents.

Three defendants were sentenced for the 2015 death of 15-year-old Zaevion Dobson, a football player who shielded friends from gunfire. Christopher Drone Bassett received life plus 35 years for first-degree murder. Richard Gregory Williams III was sentenced to 143 years and Kipling Deshawn Colbert to 109 years for facilitating the murder; their sentences include time for unrelated charges.

The S&P Financial Services sector comprises S&P 500 companies classified under GICS Financial Services, including banks, investment houses, insurance firms, and fintech companies. The sector is tracked by ETFs such as VFH and XLF. Five major stocks by market capitalization include Berkshire Hathaway, JP Morgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs. The sector collapsed 85% during the 2008/09 financial crisis but has since stabilized with tighter regulations. A backtested XLF trading strategy shows 198 trades, 1.05% average gain, 73% win rate, 21% max drawdown, and 2.25 profit factor. The sector exhibits high volatility and strong correlation to overall markets like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.

The Fabry-Perot cavity is a widely used optical device with applications in quantum electrodynamics, quantum information science, sensing, and timekeeping. Traditional mirrors made with super-polishing techniques are large and unsuitable for compact systems. Recent microfabrication techniques have produced smaller alternatives, but with trade-offs in performance metrics like finesse, quality factor, and mode volume.

This work presents a simple fabrication method using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors to create state-of-the-art visible microcavities. The process involves thermal smoothing of silicon wafers, deposition of SiO2/Ta2O5 dielectric coatings, and backside etching to create suspended mirrors that naturally buckle due to compressive strain. The resulting mirrors achieve surface roughness below 50 pm and rotational symmetry.

Characterization using a swept-ring-down method at 780.24 nm demonstrated finesse up to 0.89 × 10^6 and quality factor up to 2.3 × 10^9. Finesse decreases with cavity length due to diffractive losses, while quality factor initially increases before plateauing. The surface roughness is estimated below 90 pm, comparable to state-of-the-art visible dielectric coatings.

The fabrication enables compact, assembled cavities as small as 2 mm³, integrable into fibers or photonic chips. Demonstrated assemblies include a 45 µm cavity with finesse 0.616 × 10^6 and a 1 mm cavity with finesse 0.263 × 10^6. These microcavities are suitable for quantum networking applications with neutral atoms and trapped ions, as well as classical applications including filters, transfer cavities, and laser stabilization.

Amazon is developing a domestic robot codenamed "Vesta" through its Lab126 division, overseen by Gregg Zehr. The project, which originated a few years ago, has accelerated hiring this year for positions like robotics engineers and sensors engineers. Amazon hopes to test the robots in employees' homes by year-end and potentially launch to consumers in 2019. The Vesta robot may function as a mobile Alexa with advanced cameras and computer vision capabilities for home navigation, led by former Apple executive Max Paley. This project differs from Amazon Robotics, which handles warehouse automation. While domestic robots have historically struggled commercially, advances in computer vision, AI, and voice activation may improve feasibility. Amazon may subsidize costs for Prime subscribers. The consumer robot market is projected to reach $15 billion annually by 2023.

SAN MIGUEL Pure Foods Company, Inc. (SMPFC) has postponed its planned follow-on offering (FOO) of P100-150 billion to the third or fourth quarter to allow investors time to absorb multiple stock rights offerings in the market and due to stock market volatility. The FOO is needed to increase SMFBI's public float from 4.3% to the required 15% minimum following SMPFC's merger with Ginebra San Miguel, Inc. and San Miguel Brewery, Inc. SMPFC plans P56-60 billion in capital expenditures over three years and reported 16% net income growth to P6.9 billion in 2017 on 5% revenue growth to P117 billion.

This disclosure describes computer-implemented methods, systems, and program products for digital twin simulations that allow selective bypassing of input parameters. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical asset that tracks real-time changes through sensor and IoT data. The disclosed system captures real-time data feeds to create digital twin models, maintains multiple time-stamped versions reflecting the asset's evolution, and enables configurable simulations. Users can select specific model versions, create hybrid models combining components from different versions, bypass selected components during simulation, and input overriding values for non-simulated portions. The system includes a creation engine for model generation, a data collection engine for aggregating sensor data, version management for tracking changes, a simulation engine for executing configurable simulations with component bypass and substitution capabilities, and a reporting engine for results distribution. The architecture supports containerized deployment and cloud computing environments.

Nigeria is experiencing a consumer revolution with large shopping malls opening across the country, particularly in Lagos, creating jobs and generating tax revenue. Analysts attribute this growth to demand for one-stop shopping, convenience, brand consciousness, and busy lifestyles. Shoprite and Spar are among retailers expanding their presence. Emmanuel Efuntayo of Ibukun Efuntayo & Co stated that over five upscale malls have opened recently, signaling positive investor confidence and providing direct employment to thousands of Nigerians.

Exeter City manager Paul Tisdale praised his team's performance in their 1-0 defeat to Luton Town, despite having six defensive players missing and fielding 20-year-old Jordan Storey for his first league start. Exeter lost to a deflected Harry Cornick goal, with a late Liam McAlinden equaliser disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper. Tisdale credited Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson for developing Storey from seventh-choice centre-back to starter, and expressed confidence ahead of their next match against Wycombe Wanderers.

The device boot state is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset de-assertion, with values latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[15:11] controls GPMC CS0 data bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing. BTMODE[4:0] sets boot mode order per Table 5-1, executing primary through fourth boot modes sequentially until success. BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and must be pulled down. BTMODE[9:8] selects Ethernet PHY mode when EMAC bootmode is active. BTMODE[10] selects GPMC pin muxing options for XIP bootmodes.

Messaging apps are evolving from simple communication tools into comprehensive ecosystems of products and services. WeChat in China already offers services like food ordering, transportation, games, and dating. WhatsApp, with 94% reach in India, is following a similar path, having introduced voice/video calls and now expanding into payments. Content consumption has risen dramatically with cheap data availability, making chat platforms key distribution channels. WhatsApp previously failed with "stories" but may succeed with professionally produced content. Hike, backed by Airtel, started payments earlier and could compete by bundling with Airtel TV and Wynk content. Gaming represents another engagement opportunity, with Gamepind as an early example. India's internet is consolidating into an oligopoly of global-backed giants, with chat platforms becoming a critical battleground for the next decade.

This patent application describes a security appliance with a local touch screen interface for network management during attacks. Traditional network security devices are managed remotely via network connections, which become unavailable during denial of service attacks. The disclosed appliance incorporates a local input/output interface (such as a multi-touch display) that provides command and control without network login. During attacks, local interface commands receive priority access to processing resources and memory, enabling mitigating actions like port shutdowns, source blacklisting, or filter rule modifications without requiring manual reboot or network disconnection. The system uses geoprocessing-based analysis with minimum bounding rectangles and R-tree indexing for faster packet filtering compared to traditional B-tree searches. Rules are distributed to appliances based on threat likelihood, with mandatory rules for known attacks sent to all devices and potential rules randomly distributed to subsets. New devices are quarantined until physically authorized through the local interface, preventing compromised devices from modifying security settings remotely.

Apple Inc. held its Annual Meeting of Shareholders on March 10, 2015. Shareholders elected seven directors, ratified Ernst & Young LLP as the independent accounting firm, approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation, and approved an amendment to increase the Employee Stock Purchase Plan by 50 million shares. Two shareholder proposals, "Risk Report" and "Proxy Access for Shareholders," were not approved. The amended Employee Stock Purchase Plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Environment and Climate Change Canada announced Friday that none of over a dozen reviewed phthalates pose human health risks, with only one needing further environmental study. Phthalates are chemicals used in plastics and numerous commercial products. Environmental Defence criticized the findings, noting the EU has concluded at least four phthalates are health risks, and highlighted Canada's regulatory approach requiring proof of harm rather than proof of safety. The House of Commons environment committee recommended modernizing the Canadian Environmental Protection Act last June, including adopting Europe's safety-first approach. Environment Minister Catherine McKenna said the government is considering recommendations and will develop a plan by June 2018.

High-stakes standardized testing constrains school choice by forcing curriculum alignment to single assessments. Studies show educators narrow instruction and use more test-like problems in response. Wisconsin and Texas require private school choice students to take state exams aligned with Common Core, while Oklahoma and other states mandate ACT/SAT for graduation or scholarships, forcing schools to prioritize test priorities over their own. These tests show declining standards: SAT reading passages shortened to "tweet" length, AP Literature top scores spiked 240% while national reading declined, and SAT math rigor dropped 71 points from 2008–2023. Universities that tried test-optional admissions reversed course, finding value in standardized testing. The solution is testing choice—allowing schools and students to select from multiple assessments. The Classic Learning Test (CLT) offers an alternative grounded in classic literature and philosophy, with scores correlating 0.89 with SAT scores. Arkansas and Florida already allow multiple tests for school choice programs; Florida accepts CLT for university admissions. States should provide assessment menus for all school choice participants and ensure all tests qualify for college admissions and scholarships to achieve true education freedom.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments on October 7 in a case challenging Colorado's 2019 ban on conversion therapy for minors. Therapist Kaley Chiles argues the ban violates her free speech rights, claiming it regulates speech rather than conduct and should face strict scrutiny. Colorado defends the law as regulating unsafe and ineffective medical treatment, arguing it should receive rational basis review. The 10th Circuit upheld the law, ruling it regulates conduct that incidentally involves speech. The federal government supports Chiles, urging the Court to apply strict scrutiny and return the case to lower courts. Colorado maintains the ban is narrowly tailored to protect minors from harmful practices and warns that ruling for Chiles could destabilize healthcare regulation.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians analysis concludes that expanding palliative care services across Canada would improve patient care while reducing health care costs. The report cites studies showing hospital-based palliative care saves $7,000-$8,000 per patient compared to usual acute care, with outpatient services reducing costs by about 30%. Home-based palliative care and residential hospice transfers also demonstrate significant cost savings. With nearly one in six Canadians aged 65+ and an estimated quarter of health care costs spent in patients' final year of life, the CSPCP recommends governments implement a mix of palliative care programs.

AMP chairman David Murray criticized ASX corporate governance principles for causing deteriorating governance standards in the financial sector, arguing they evolved from broad guidelines into prescriptive "one-size-fits-all" regulations that institutions follow without question, creating a "trust deficit" that requires fundamental reform.

Gardaí in Louth have appealed for information about the murder of 18-year-old Cameron Reilly, whose body was found in Dunleer on Saturday with neck injuries. He had been socialising with up to 20 people on Friday night. Officers are searching for his iPhone 8 Plus with a black and lime green cover, believing it may contain messages from attackers. Superintendent Andrew Watters stated the investigation's focus is establishing the truth for Cameron's family, not on alcohol or drug consumption. Separately, gardaí in west Dublin seized a semi-automatic shotgun and prevented a likely gangland attack, arresting a 31-year-old man and 53-year-old woman. Follow-up searches recovered €1m worth of drugs including 6kgs of heroin and 2kgs of cocaine, plus cash.

The Johnston Press South Business Awards returned for a seventh year at Brighton's Grand Hotel, presented by Nick Wallis. Guardian Angel Carers from Chichester won both Large Business of the Year and Overall Business of the Year. Other winners included Olive and Vine (Place to Eat or Drink), Brandon Relph (Young Achiever), Southsea Bathing Hut (Retailer of the Year), and Talks at Six (Outstanding Contribution to the Community). Additional awards covered categories such as customer service, innovation, green business, hospitality, manufacturing, and lifetime achievement.

The Supreme Court of Georgia affirmed the judgment in favor of defendants in a negligence case involving an automobile collision at a street intersection. The court held that: (1) the trial court properly instructed the jury regarding plaintiff's allegations of negligence, including failure to sound a horn; (2) no error occurred in failing to charge on right-of-way rules where not specifically pled; (3) no error in failing to instruct on speed reduction where not alleged; (4) a specific charge on statutory violations did not preclude consideration of other negligence allegations; (5) the comparative negligence charge was proper where evidence showed both parties negligent; (6) any error regarding damages was harmless given the verdict for defendants; and (7) the verdict was authorized by conflicting evidence.

The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced FORM X to simplify foreign exchange documentation for Small and Medium Enterprises and retail businesses needing $10,000 or less. CBN spokesman Isaac Okorafor stated the form requires basic documents including a supporting application letter, beneficiary invoice, and bank wire transfer, aiming to ease documentation challenges and ensure adequate forex supply for genuine transactions.

The passage describes techniques for enhanced trick-play modes in streaming video, where a media guidance application maintains both a normal buffer window of continuous video content and a trick-play window containing only selected frames (typically key frames at spaced intervals) for portions outside the normal buffer. During trick-play operations, the application plays using only these buffered selected frames without requiring full video segments, enabling faster-than-real-time playback with frequent frame updates. The system uses frame address information from metadata to locate specific frames, monitors streaming performance metrics to optimize frame selection and stream quality, and can expand the normal buffer by re-using trick-play frames. A trick-play optimizer component manages frame selection based on playback rate, performance metrics, and anticipated trick-play duration, while a proxy server can generate necessary metadata for conventional streaming servers.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with around 56,000 new cases annually. Self-examination involves checking breasts and armpits regularly, ideally every 2-4 weeks, looking for lumps, swelling, skin changes, or nipple abnormalities. Lumps vary in size and texture, sometimes pea-like, other times hard and irregular. Risk factors include age, family history, HRT use, and lifestyle factors. Men can also develop breast cancer, typically between ages 60-70. Early detection through screening and self-checks improves survival rates, which have nearly doubled in 40 years, with over 75% of women surviving 10 years post-diagnosis.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 17, 2019, reporting the appointment of Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer, effective June 17, 2019. Robertson, 50, previously held finance and accounting roles at Western Digital Corporation and SanDisk Corporation. He replaces Michael Byron, who became Vice President of Finance, Merger & Acquisition Integration and Financial Systems. Robertson's at-will employment terms include: $650,000 annual base salary; $600,000 sign-on bonus (repayable if employment ends before one year); 15,000 RSUs vesting over four years; eligibility for the employee stock purchase plan; and comprehensive benefits. Robertson also entered into NVIDIA's standard indemnity agreement.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months for stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach with a flick knife during an argument over a spilt drink at the Newmarket Tavern in Plymouth. Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing a knife in public, and cannabis possession. He was also in breach of an eight-month suspended sentence for a 2015 affray. The judge noted Haydon's "appalling record" for violence and weapons, and said the offence was aggravated by alcohol and drug use. The victim was treated for a 2cm puncture wound and kept overnight; witnesses refused to give statements, leading to a less serious charge than the facts suggested.

SPYR, Inc. announced it will give shareholders of record as of May 19, 2017, a 1-for-1 dividend in shares of a new spin-off company created to divest its restaurant division. The new company will file with the SEC to become a separate publicly traded entity and will focus on licensing/franchising the Eat at Joe's® name and manufacturing/distributing branded foods. The publisher, Stock Market Media Group, disclosed it is compensated by SPYR with $5,000 monthly and 250,000 restricted shares for publishing SPYR-related content.

Scientists discovered a 167-million-year-old Jurassic lizard named *Breugnathair elgolensis* on Scotland's Isle of Skye. The fossil, described in an October 1 study, combines snake-like jaws and hook-like teeth with a lizard's short body and limbs. Researchers placed it in a newly defined group of predatory squamates called Parviraptoridae. The unusual mix of features suggests either that snake ancestors differed from expectations or that snake-like traits evolved independently. The specimen, discovered in 2016, was studied for nearly a decade using CT scans and x-rays. Researchers could not determine if it represents a lizard-like snake ancestor or a stem-squamate that independently developed snake-like features.

The A100 GPU features 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7x larger than the Tesla V100, improving performance for HPC and AI workloads by enabling faster data access than HBM2 memory. The cache is shared across GPCs and SMs, divided into two partitions for higher bandwidth and lower latency, delivering 2.3x L2 bandwidth over V100. Each partition contains 40 L2 cache slices, with eight 512 KB slices per memory controller. The A100 L2 read bandwidth is 5120 Bytes/clk versus V100's 2048 Bytes/clk. The NVIDIA Ampere architecture adds L2 cache residency controls for programmers and Compute Data Compression, providing up to 4x improvement in DRAM and L2 read/write bandwidth.

The passage describes technical specifications for Texas Instruments MSPM0 G-Series microcontrollers (MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, MSPM0G1518), covering peripherals, application guidelines, and development support.

**Peripherals:**
- **RTC_B**: Real-time clock with 32kHz input, providing time/calendar counters (seconds to year), customizable alarms, interval wake-up interrupts, crystal calibration (±240ppm), and temperature compensation.
- **IWDT_B**: Independent watchdog timer with 32kHz clock, eight selectable periods (2ms to 2hr), generating POR reset on timeout.
- **WWDT**: Windowed watchdog with eight periods, sleep mode auto-stop, and interval timer mode.
- **Timers (TIMx)**: General-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) timers with 16/32-bit counters, prescalers, PWM, QEI/Hall sensor support, synchronization, and cross-trigger capabilities.

**Application Guidelines:**
- Decoupling capacitors (10µF + 0.1µF) near VDD/VSS pins
- NRST pullup (47kΩ) with pulldown capacitor (10nF)
- 100kΩ 0.1% resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction (optional)
- 0.47µF tank capacitor for VCORE
- Pullup resistors required for 5V-tolerant open drain I/O

**Development Support:**
- Serial wire debug (SWD) interface
- Boot strap loader (BSL) with UART/I2C, password-protected, invocable via pin, unprogrammed reset vector, or software command
- Factory constants memory region for device capabilities and trim data
- Tools: LaunchPad kits, MSPM0 SDK, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, CCS, IAR, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm toolchain

Chicago faces a major security challenge with three large events: Sunday's marathon (1.7 million spectators), Monday's Cubs playoff game (45,000 fans), and Monday Night Football (60,000+ fans). Concerns intensified after the Las Vegas massacre and reports that gunman Stephen Paddock had booked rooms overlooking Lollapalooza in Grant Park. Security consultant Arnette Heintze advised coordination with high-rise building employees to watch for suspicious behavior. University of Chicago's Robert Pape noted copycat attacks are rare due to heightened alertness and said layered security measures like bag checks are effective. Following the 2013 Boston Marathon bombings, Chicago implemented random backpack checks and restricted access to start/finish lines. Mayor Rahm Emanuel expressed full confidence in security, noting police will deploy 1,000 additional officers and more undercover officers for the marathon. Alicia Tate-Nadeau of emergency management confirmed meetings with downtown building security and a "robust plan" addressing threats from elevated positions. Several marathon runners expressed concern but planned to compete.
AI models Evo 1 and Evo 2 generated multiple bacteriophage genomes from scratch, with some lab-grown viruses outperforming a well-studied strain in killing bacteria.

Saudi Aramco plans to change its crude oil pricing formula for Asian customers starting October, replacing the Platts-assessed Oman-Dubai average with a 50:50 blend of DME Oman futures and Platts Dubai cash prices. This marks the first benchmark change for Saudi official selling prices since the mid-1980s. The move, discussed internally for years, could boost liquidity for DME Oman futures trading. Saudi Aramco's monthly prices influence other Middle East producers affecting over 12 million barrels per day of Asian-bound crude; Kuwait indicated it may follow after observing market feedback.

DoorDash unveiled Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall autonomous delivery robot with cameras, sensors, and a cute design featuring pixelated eyes and a Pac-Man-like opening. The robot operates on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes as part of DoorDash's "hybrid" delivery model combining humans, drones, and autonomous vehicles. The company also partners with Coco Robotics, which uses smaller sidewalk robots with teleoperations teams assisting behind the scenes. The delivery robot industry saw peak enthusiasm during the pandemic but cooled as companies like Amazon and FedEx abandoned projects due to technical challenges navigating unpredictable sidewalk environments. Current strategies focus on limited contexts like suburbs and college campuses where conditions are more controlled. Concerns exist about robots occupying limited bike lane space and regulatory complications. Labor impacts may shift work rather than eliminate it, as robots struggle with tasks like stairs, gates, and building entry that humans handle easily.

A U.S. official welcomes Native American chiefs to the seat of government, expressing friendship and a desire for peace between their nations. He addresses their proposal to sell lands on the Tombigbee and Mississippi rivers to pay merchant debts, agreeing to purchase Mississippi lands for boat establishments but deferring boundary details to future negotiators. He rejects any debt for lands sold to the English, citing custom of immediate payment and witness testimony. He encourages the chiefs to adopt agriculture and industry, noting previous gifts were not payment for land. He directs other matters to the Secretary at War, offers travel arrangements for their visit, and expresses relief at their safe arrival after a navigation error to Savannah.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed the Unemployment Appeals Commission's denial of unemployment benefits to Genel Altimeaux, finding the appeals referee's determination that Altimeaux voluntarily quit was not based on competent, substantial evidence. The court held that Milliken's testimony from the first hearing—where Altimeaux was not present and could not cross-examine—was incompetent under Florida law. Testimony from the second hearing, including that of supervisor Tranowski who never heard Altimeaux quit and Altimeaux's own denial of quitting, did not support a voluntary quit finding. The court directed reinstatement of Altimeaux's unemployment award.

Parents are questioning Township High School District 113's principal hiring process for Highland Park High School, specifically why only two parents serve on the 18-member stakeholder interview committee. Parent Amy Small cited concerns about transparency and differences between Highland Park and Deerfield High Schools. Superintendent Christopher Dignam is using Ray and Associates to screen candidates to replace departing Principal Tom Koulentes, with finalists to be interviewed April 25. Dignam stated the process mirrors the one used for Deerfield High School last year. Board member Julie Gordon noted parents who applied for the committee were unclear why they weren't selected.

The Pin and Pull is a football run play that creates favorable down block angles while getting blockers into space as lead blockers for outside runs. Its strengths include getting extra blockers to the point of attack on perimeter runs, versatility in blocking assignments, and allowing the tailback to run from the C-gap to the sideline. Its weaknesses are the requirement for guards who can pull effectively and a speed-based tailback rather than a power back. Unlike the Buck Sweep, which requires a simultaneous inside run threat, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. The passage details specific blocking assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts for all offensive positions, plus two variations: Pin and Pull Toss and TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss.

Greater noctule bats hunt migrating songbirds by ascending to high altitudes, then diving down to capture prey in mid-air, according to research published October 9, 2025. Scientists from Aarhus University and Doñana Biological Station used biologgers with accelerometers, magnetometers, altimeters, and microphones to track the bats' movements and sounds. The devices recorded feeding buzzes as bats approached birds, followed by distress calls and chewing sounds during 23-minute in-flight meals. Two hunting events above 1,200 meters were documented, with one successful capture of a robin. The high-frequency sounds are inaudible to birds, which only detect the bats at close range. Researchers also found physical evidence including bats with blood-stained lips, feathers in mouths, and passerine wings falling from captured bats.

Former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Brock University research found rosemary extract inhibits lung cancer cell growth by blocking the Akt signalling pathway and enhancing apoptosis. While results suggest anti-tumour potential, Tsiani cautioned against dietary recommendations until specific active components—possibly carnosic acid or rosmarinic acid—are identified through further research.

This paper introduces COTUTOR, a generative AI model for personalized programming education that integrates knowledge tracing, convex optimization, and signal processing. Unlike existing LLM-based educational tools that lack interpretable student models, COTUTOR uses Bayesian Knowledge Tracing with convex optimization to enable transparent, globally optimal tracking of learning states while requiring fewer computational resources. The system collects multimodal learning signals (submissions, participation logs, queries) through an iterative flywheel mechanism that continuously refines student models and generates optimized resource recommendations. Implemented as an AI copilot integrated with Online Judge platforms, COTUTOR was evaluated through benchmarking and classroom studies, demonstrating superior performance in knowledge modeling and learning outcomes compared to baseline methods including traditional BKT and Deep Knowledge Tracing.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon stated that while AI itself is real and transformative, some asset prices are in "bubble territory." He distinguished between AI (which his bank has successfully applied to specific functions like fraud prevention) and generative AI (which he placed in a separate category due to uncertain returns). Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at age 91, created a unique collection of chimpanzee skeletons from Tanzania's Gombe National Park that allowed researchers to study how individual life experiences influence skeletal features. Starting in 1960, she and her team retrieved chimp bodies, cleaned the bones, and documented each individual's known sex, age, weight, and life history. This collection offered a new perspective for scientists studying ancient hominid fossils, who typically lack such detailed information about the individuals they examine. Goodall explained her motivation with characteristic humility: "When you're working in the field, you shouldn't waste anything." The skeletons, including that of famous matriarch Flo, revealed insights about bone loss patterns and reproductive biology that differed from humans, continuing to yield scientific discoveries decades after collection.

This patent application describes multi-camera imaging systems for detecting faint objects using arrays of economical, low-performance cameras. The systems combine images from multiple cameras to achieve signal-to-noise ratio improvements of at least √N times that of individual cameras, where N is the number of cameras combined. Three array configurations are disclosed: common field arrays (cameras sharing overlapping fields of view), hybrid field arrays (multiple camera arrays with partially overlapping common fields), and adaptive field arrays (reconfigurable cameras that switch between wide-field detection and focused common-field imaging). The systems enable detection of dim space objects, geosynchronous satellite tracking, and uncorrelated target identification through image co-registration, combination, and processing techniques including streak detection and orbit determination. Benefits include reduced costs compared to high-performance single telescopes, increased bit depth for advanced deconvolution, cosmic ray artifact reduction, and scalability through modular camera addition.

Researchers from the University of Washington and partner companies conducted the first large-scale experiment using poplar trees with probiotic bacteria to clean up TCE-contaminated groundwater at a Superfund site in California. The study, published August 11 in Environmental Science & Technology, found that trees inoculated with a specific microbe strain showed greater growth, higher survival rates, and significantly reduced TCE levels after three years compared to untreated trees. Groundwater downstream also showed lower toxin levels. TCE, a common industrial pollutant and known carcinogen present at over 1,000 priority cleanup sites, is typically expensive to remediate through traditional engineering methods. The probiotic approach, which uses naturally selected microbes to protect trees from toxicity while accelerating pollutant degradation, offers a lower-cost, sustainable alternative for cleaning contaminated sites.

American agencies intercepted the calls during routine intelligence collection and investigations into Russian election interference but have not seen proof of collusion. Zircon undergoes a structural transition at high pressure to form reidite, a scheelite-structured phase. This study investigated trace element behavior during shock loading of natural zircon monocrystals to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa under laboratory conditions. Samples from Australia's Mud Tank deposit were shock-compressed using aluminum projectiles, with temperature calculations accounting for porosity effects. At 13.6 GPa, zircon retained its structure with pronounced texturing and fracturing. At 51.3 GPa, complete transformation to reidite occurred with lattice parameters a = 4.722(2) Å, c = 10.524(5) Å. The reidite showed mosaic structure with residual zircon near fractures. Cathodoluminescence revealed intense REE³⁺ luminescence in 2–10 μm speckles, particularly Dy³⁺ at 577 nm, indicating segregation on planar defects. This rapid segregation—occurring in seconds rather than days—suggests reconstructive phase transition mechanisms cause local charge imbalances that expel substituting trivalent elements to interstitial positions, where high mobility promotes defect segregation. The findings demonstrate that trace element redistribution can occur without prolonged post-shock annealing, with implications for geochronological studies using zircon.

This patent application is a continuation of prior applications for ladar transmitters. It addresses needs for improved computer vision technology for applications including autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and mapping, noting limitations of conventional ladar systems regarding cost, size, power, and flash ladar shortcomings. The disclosure presents several embodiments: a field splitter/inverter positioned optically downstream from scanning mirrors to split and invert the scan pattern, converting fast center/slow edge scan characteristics to slow center/fast edges to optimize gaze time on central regions; a technique for inducing periodic phase drift in Lissajous scan patterns to reduce scan gaps and blindspots in desired regions while preserving periodicity; and a compact beam scanner assembly featuring an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging mirror positioned between first and second scannable mirrors with a lens upstream, enabling equally-sized closely-positioned mirrors and reduced distortions. The application details various configurations including W-shaped and triangular prism field inverters, overlapped splitting, hinged adjustable mirror pitch angles, and mathematical formulas for phase drift implementation and CPA angle calculations for the ECR assembly.

A new analysis of the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic found that just 3 percent of patients caused more than 60 percent of infections. Researchers calculated that each Ebola patient infected an average of 2.39 others, but transmission was uneven—many infected no one, while superspreaders infected many. People who stayed home rather than seeking hospital care drove most spread. Age was a key predictor of superspreading, with the very young and very old attracting more caregivers. Superspreaders also played major roles in SARS and MERS outbreaks. Ebola was eventually stopped through public health efforts focusing on safe burials and quick hospitalization.

This patent application describes Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) transmission schemes for small data transmission in 5G New Radio (NR), enabling User Equipment (UE) to transmit data while remaining in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE states without full state transitions. The application details configured grant Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) resources broadcast via system information blocks, incorporating NOMA parameters like DM-RS ports, multiple access signatures, and interleavers. Key technical innovations include UE-specific reference bits constructed from device identities and multiple access identities, jointly encoded with information bits using systematic LDPC encoding, which serve as preambles or demodulation reference signals to mitigate sequence collisions. The described methods reduce signaling overhead, latency, and power consumption compared to conventional LTE approaches requiring RRC connection establishment, with specific procedures outlined for idle state (using NAS security context) and inactive state (using stored AS security context) transmissions.

The Tax Court granted summary judgment for the Commissioner in a case reviewing an Appeals officer's determination to proceed with levy collection of unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes. Petitioner Robert Poindexter, a songwriter, challenged the assessments' accuracy, claiming his returns contained false information due to disputes with record companies over royalties. The Court rejected the Commissioner's argument that self-reported taxes cannot be challenged under section 6330(c)(2)(B), citing Montgomery v. Commissioner. However, the Court found Poindexter failed to meet Rule 331's requirement for specific factual allegations showing error in the assessments—he did not identify incorrect income, deduction, or credit items, nor provide evidence of proper royalty amounts. The Court also found no factual basis for his other procedural claims. Since Poindexter declined to file amended returns and requested IRS assistance unavailable under the Code, the Appeals officer's determination was sustained.

Acting CDC Director Jim O'Neill approved recommendations allowing anyone over 6 months to receive updated Covid-19 shots after provider consultation, and that children under 4 receive MMR and chickenpox vaccines separately rather than combined. The approvals enable states to order updated Covid vaccines for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program, which roughly 50% of U.S. children rely on. The recommendations, issued over two weeks prior, had been delayed, creating access disparities. A new routine childhood vaccine schedule is expected, marking early Trump administration changes to U.S. vaccine review and recommendation processes.

Agents Mutual, owner of OnTheMarket.com, plans to float on London's AIM and raise £50 million to challenge rivals Rightmove and Zoopla. On The Market is currently Britain's third largest online property site. The funds will support marketing, sales, customer relations, and technology, including a national TV and media campaign. The company abandoned its mutual status earlier this year and signed long-term listing agreements with major estate agencies. Analyst George Salmon noted that while the strategy is sensible, toppling Rightmove remains a significant challenge. On The Market previously won a competition case upholding its rule restricting estate agents to listing on only one additional rival site.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a father was allegedly assaulted at Coed Bach Park in Pontarddulais, Swansea on 29 June. The victim was spat at, punched to the floor, and kicked while his children watched, after suggesting a moped rider take more care around children. Inspector Emma Fox described the attack as "particularly nasty and unprovoked." Police have issued descriptions of two male attackers and a woman who was with them.

In *Pelitsie v. National Surety Corporation of New York* (1956), the Wisconsin Supreme Court reversed a trial court judgment in favor of the plaintiff insured, holding that the plaintiff failed to substantially comply with a record-keeping clause in burglary insurance policies. The clause required records enabling the insurer to "accurately determine" the loss amount. Plaintiff maintained a check-cashing fund, recording only nightly totals of cash and checks on a scratch-pad without separately listing check details. After a burglary, plaintiff could only recover $182 of approximately $600-$800 in stolen checks by personal memory. The court ruled that for negotiable instruments like checks, minimum records must include sufficient detail to permit subrogation claims against drawers, and plaintiff's aggregate totals were insufficient as they required supplementation from memory.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed a Tax Court judgment holding Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Company liable for income tax deficiencies for 1975 and 1976. The Delaware corporation, which manufactured jewelry in American Samoa, had excluded from gross income all revenue from sales to its parent company under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a), which allows income exclusion for domestic corporations doing business in U.S. possessions. The court ruled that because payment checks were deposited into the taxpayer's account in Honolulu, the funds were "received within the United States" under § 931(b), making them taxable despite the general exclusion rule. The court rejected the taxpayer's argument that receipt should depend on the corporation's primary physical presence rather than the location of physical receipt.

This work investigates the application of steady-state variance reduction techniques (VRTs) to time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations, focusing on their interactions with population control techniques (PCTs). The study examines global VRTs including Implicit Capture (IC), CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen (CL) weight windows, alongside PCTs including uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC).

Key findings demonstrate that weight-based combing conflicts severely with weight window methods, causing memory exhaustion due to excessive splitting when particle weights are reset at census. Conversely, uniform combing preserves weight distributions and combines effectively with CL weight windows, achieving significant efficiency improvements. IC unexpectedly underperforms with UC across all test problems. Time-dependent weight windows outperform static implementations by adapting to evolving flux distributions.

Testing was conducted using Shift (with DENOVO coupling for adjoint methods) and MC/DC (with full time-dependent capabilities including delayed neutrons and moving geometries). Three benchmark problems were evaluated: a pulsed slab in Shift, the AZURV1 supercritical infinite medium in MC/DC, and a 1D reactor SCRAM simulation with moving surfaces.

Results confirm that proper selection of VRT-PCT combinations substantially impacts simulation efficiency, with CL weight windows plus uniform combing providing optimal performance. The study validates that steady-state global VRTs can be adapted for time-dependent problems, with time-dependent modifications yielding additional gains.

U.S. language education faces declining enrollment, threatening programs like German and French. This article proposes fostering "imagined communities"—connections formed through imagination with target language speakers—to reframe language learning around ACTFL's principle that "language connects." A yearlong study in eighth-grade German classrooms used task-based instruction where students imagined moving abroad, completing authentic activities like finding apartments, shopping, and navigating transit systems using real materials. Implementation requires creating plausible scenarios, designing relevant activities, providing autonomy and just-in-time instruction, and ensuring authenticity. Results showed students reported deeper cultural engagement, increased connection to target language speakers, and continued study beyond requirements. This approach works across K-16 levels without extra funding, needing only instructor planning time and creativity.

A federal humanities advocate and a Native nonprofit are each contributing about $2 million to fund Native American language education programs in tribal communities. The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute aim to revitalize approximately 150 Native languages spoken in the U.S. Lawrence Kaplan of the Alaska Native Language Center said Alaska Natives deeply value their languages, which are endangered. First Nations CEO Michael Roberts noted funding will be competitive, with about 15 programs funded annually. Priority will go to immersion programs or those in pre-immersion stages with active community involvement.

This email from Henry Means to Sharonda Stephens dated May 3, 2001, contains a compilation of news articles mentioning Enron. The articles cover: a town meeting in Pompano Beach, Florida regarding an Enron power plant proposal; debate over whether California should boycott high-priced electricity, with Enron noted as one of several profitable power wholesalers; Indian banks appealing to their government to resolve Enron's payment dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board over the Dabhol power project; Democratic National Committee criticism of Bush administration energy policy ties to Enron and other energy donors; Innogy beginning European power trading including in markets where Enron operates; Mosaic Group's Paradigm unit contracting with New Power (formed by Enron) for customer acquisition; European telecom companies' improving credit outlook with Enron trading related bankruptcy derivatives; growing corporate use of credit derivatives with Enron Credit marketing such products; Allegheny Energy's $667 million purchase of three Midwest power plants from Enron; Salomon Smith Barney cutting power profitability forecasts while noting Enron among trading-focused energy merchants; Fitch affirming Northern Border Partners ratings with Enron holding a 10% stake; Enron's Indian unit agreeing to meet with a government renegotiation panel but denying this constitutes an offer to renegotiate; postponement of that meeting; EnergieKontor securing a 200 MW wind turbine deal with Enron Wind for Spain and Germany projects; and Scottish Power considering refining its focus including potential interest in Enron's Portland General unit.

This patent application describes methods, polypeptides, nucleic acids, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids and related compounds. The disclosure focuses on novel geranyl pyrophosphate:olivetolic acid geranyltransferase (GOT) polypeptides, particularly the CsPT4 polypeptide and its truncated version (CsPT4t), which catalyze production of cannabigerolic acid (CBGA) from GPP and olivetolic acid at least ten times more efficiently than previously identified Cannabis polypeptides. The genetically modified host cells may contain heterologous nucleic acids encoding various enzymes involved in cannabinoid biosynthesis, including TKS, OAC, CBDA synthase, THCA synthase, and enzymes for precursor synthesis from the mevalonate pathway and acyl-CoA generation pathways. Host cells can be eukaryotic (particularly yeast such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae) or prokaryotic. The methods enable production of natural and non-natural cannabinoids, cannabinoid precursors, and derivatives through microbial fermentation using simple feedstocks like sugars and carboxylic acids, offering advantages over agricultural production including faster production cycles, climate independence, and higher purity.

U.S. Rep. Garret Graves attributes the shooting of Congressman Steve Scalise and three others to the nation's divisive political climate, criticizing inflammatory rhetoric from media, bloggers, and government officials. Scalise was shot by James T. Hodgkinson, a former Bernie Sanders volunteer with anti-Republican views, though police haven't stated a motive. Sanders condemned the violence. A player felt energized throughout a game despite heavy special teams play, attributing team success to four balanced scoring lines. Both teams played well on penalty kill, being aggressive and blocking shots. The ice was chippy due to heat in the building. The player scored by shooting high on the goalie after a teammate created an open lane. The team maintained composure between periods, believing persistence would create scoring opportunities, which eventually paid off.

A New York Times survey of 65 federal judges found majority dissatisfaction with the Supreme Court's emergency docket decisions in Trump-related cases since his second term. Only 12 of 65 judges found the emergency docket use appropriate, 12 said lower courts receive sufficient guidance, and just 2 of 54 believed it improved public perception of the judiciary. Judges anonymously criticized orders as "mystical," "overly blunt," and "incredibly demoralizing." Survey respondents included 28 Republican and 37 Democratic appointees. At least 7 of about 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, with nearly all benefiting Trump. The New York Times noted respondents may not represent the full judiciary, while the Volokh Conspiracy suggested potential sampling bias toward dissatisfied judges.

This is an email from Energy Central Direct dated January 15, 2002, sent to Paul D. Thomas at Enron, containing daily energy industry news. The newsletter covers multiple topics including: National Grid's imminent approval to acquire Niagara Mohawk; UBS sharing profits from Enron's energy trading unit; Treasury Secretary Paul O'Neill downplaying calls with Enron's Ken Lay; potential end of utility stranded cost bonds; Thomas M. Ray III named president of KWI North America; Los Angeles potentially recovering $62 million from Southern California Edison; Texas electricity deregulation progress; various Enron-related developments including Senate hearings, document destruction by Arthur Andersen, and political contributions; international energy news from Australia, UK, Spain, Brazil, and other countries; utility stock price gainers; and renewable energy projects.
