Nigeria launched its National Cancer Control Plan 2018-2022 on April 13, 2018, with BVGH presenting its Africa Access Initiative (AAI) partnership to address rising cancer cases. AAI, led by BVGH with partners including AORTIC, IFPMA/Access Accelerated, Pfizer, and Takeda, aims to expand cancer medicine access, improve healthcare infrastructure, and build clinical capacity in Africa. In its first phase, AAI works with Nigeria and four other African countries (Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Kenya, and Rwanda) that have prioritized cancer control. BVGH President Jennifer Dent announced completed needs assessments of eight Nigerian hospitals and eight more underway to design sustainable cancer treatment access, with future efforts guided by the NCCP.

The court affirmed the Unemployment Insurance Appeal Board's decision disqualifying Michael Moss from receiving unemployment benefits. Moss, a warehouse worker, resigned in lieu of discharge after pulling a box cutter on his supervisor. The court found substantial evidence supported the Board's ruling that this violent behavior constituted disqualifying misconduct, noting that claimant's denial presented a credibility issue for the Board to resolve.

President Trump granted a full pardon to Scooter Libby, convicted in 2007 of perjury and obstruction of justice, following an FBI raid on his personal attorney Michael Cohen's home and office. Critics accused Trump of signaling to Russia investigation targets that they would be protected. The Constitution grants presidents broad pardon power, but its limits remain untested, including whether self-pardons or corruptly motivated pardons would be valid. Historical precedents include George H.W. Bush's Iran-Contra pardons and Nixon's consideration of self-pardon. Congressman Adam Schiff introduced legislation requiring disclosure of connections between pardoned individuals and presidential interests, while New York's Attorney General seeks to close a "double jeopardy loophole" to allow state prosecution of federally pardoned individuals. Legal experts note that pardoned individuals lose Fifth Amendment protections and must testify truthfully, potentially advancing rather than hindering investigations.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy from Overweight to Neutral, calling it a "show me" story, while raising the price target from $75 to $78. Analysts believe the stock has already seen multiple uplifts from stable returns and improved capital discipline under CEO Joe Gorder, but further gains may take time due to industry cyclicality. JPMorgan views 2016 as below mid-cycle but not a trough, caused by capacity additions outpacing demand. The firm estimates Valero's total return potential at 6 percent versus 7 percent for the group.

Large Language Models (LLMs) used in agent-based modeling for social simulation exhibit two distinct behavioral archetypes when facing social dilemmas: "Adaptive Egoists" (o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B) default to self-interest but become more altruistic when exposed to social norms via a message board, while "Altruistic Optimizers" (Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek series) inherently prioritize collective welfare regardless of social interaction. The study proposes a Schelling-variant urban migration model with over 200 agents to evaluate these tendencies, finding that model selection for social simulation constitutes a theoretical choice about whether to simulate bounded rationality with emergent norms or idealized pro-social actors.

This study investigated the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in 1,918 ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) using the MIMIC-IV database. ICH accounts for 20%-30% of strokes and has mortality rates up to 50%. Patients were grouped into four RHR quartiles (Q1: 40.4-70.2; Q2: 70.2-78.5; Q3: 78.5-88.2; Q4: 88.2-147.9 bpm). Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed higher ACM in Q3 and Q4. Multivariate Cox regression revealed RHR >78.5 bpm was significantly associated with 50-100% higher ACM risk. Restricted cubic splines identified 90.3 bpm as a threshold: RHR below this was protective, while RHR above was associated with increased ACM risk. Subgroup analyses found age >60 years showed stronger RHR-ACM associations. Mediation analysis showed age had a negative mediating effect. The study concludes RHR >90.3 bpm is an independent risk factor for ACM in ICH patients, suggesting heart rate control as a potential management strategy.

This MIT lecture by Siqi Zheng covers quantitative methods to measure benefits of green buildings and cities. The core methodology discussed is the hedonic pricing model, which decomposes housing prices into components representing willingness to pay for various attributes (rooms, location, green certification, parks, etc.) plus a residual for unobserved factors. This revealed preference approach uses regression analysis on real estate transaction data rather than stated preference surveys.

The lecture emphasizes challenges in causal inference, particularly the "apples-to-oranges" comparison problem where green buildings differ systematically from non-green buildings in unobserved ways (quality, location, age, tenant type). Endogeneity issues include omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias. Techniques to achieve valid causal inference include randomized controlled trials, matching methods (especially geographic matching), regression discontinuity, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences.

Applications extend beyond green buildings to green cities, measuring premiums for subways, schools, parks, and clean air. Examples include Bryant Park's private-public partnership restoration in New York, where nearby property owners invested expecting appreciation, and High Line Park, which illustrates both amenity value creation and environmental gentrification concerns as higher-income residents displace original communities.

Purdue University ended its GEAR UP program after the Trump administration canceled its $34.9 million federal grant, which had been awarded to run through 2031. The program provided college-prep programming for over 13,000 low-income Indiana students. The U.S. Department of Education terminated the grant on September 12, citing that the application violated department policy and civil rights law due to plans for DEI training and culturally responsive teaching. Purdue did not appeal the termination, and the program shut down on Tuesday. The Education Department has canceled at least nine GEAR UP grants.

Edinburgh has experienced significantly more haar than usual this spring. Normally, westerly winds from the Atlantic dominate Scotland's weather, carried by an active jet stream fueled by temperature contrasts across the ocean. However, in spring these contrasts typically lessen as land heats while water stays cool, weakening the jet stream. This spring, temperature contrasts across the Atlantic have been particularly weak, resulting in a much weaker jet stream with less influence on UK weather. Consequently, persistent easterly winds have become more common, making the east of Scotland prone to haar while the west experiences better weather.

The Volkswagen ID Buzz, inspired by the Microbus, shares underpinnings with other ID models, improving its production chances, though it may not arrive until around 2025. The regular ID targets Golf buyers in Europe, while the ID Crozz, with dual-motor all-wheel drive and 302HP, suits American consumers concerned about EV performance in snow and rough terrain.

DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG upgraded from the Vienna Stock Exchange's "Third Market" to the mid market segment on 23 April 2018, becoming subject to stricter transparency and quality requirements. The Austrian government plans to allow bearer shares of Austrian companies to trade on the Third Market again, with the Vienna Stock Exchange preparing a new offer for companies.

The Supreme Court declined to review multiple cases on October 6, 2025, including challenges involving gun laws, an American Indian sacred site, Ghislaine Maxwell's prosecution, and police dog drug searches. The justices invited the U.S. solicitor general to file briefs on three cases concerning nuclear safety regulations, trademark law, and arbitration under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act. Justice Samuel Alito recused himself from a case involving Laura Loomer's lawsuit against social media platforms. Justice Neil Gorsuch, joined by Justice Clarence Thomas, dissented from the denial of rehearing in a case challenging the transfer of sacred Native American land in Arizona.

The Turtle Trading Strategy is a trend-following approach developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in 1983 to test whether trading could be learned. Dennis trained 14 novice traders ("Turtles") for two weeks and funded their accounts; many became successful, proving trading skills can be taught.

The original rules emphasized three elements: volatility-based position sizing using the ATR indicator, pyramiding to add to winning trades while maintaining low risk-to-reward ratios, and strict stop-loss orders for exits. Traders entered on 20-day breakouts, added positions at 55-day breakouts, and exited on 20-day breakdowns. They traded diverse markets including bonds, commodities, currencies, and futures.

The strategy remains effective today, though modified with technical indicators. Performance has declined since the 1980s but still generates returns, as shown by the Barclay CTA Index and funds like Swedish Lynx. Backtests from 2007 onward of four variations (momentum, dual moving average, ATR channel, Bollinger Band breakout) demonstrated continued profitability despite increased whipsaws and lower win rates. The strategy requires patience due to long drawdown periods and works best in strongly trending markets.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, featuring a second-order 500kHz antialiasing low-pass filter, programmable gain amplifier, and ADC driver. It supports internal (4.096V) or external reference operation, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference requires a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor and is factory-trimmed with temperature compensation; thermal stress from soldering can cause voltage shifts. An external reference can be used with the internal buffer, requiring 10µF and 1µF capacitors on REFCAP.

The device offers input and AVDD alarm functions with programmable thresholds and hysteresis, outputting alarm flags via dedicated pin or appended data. It supports single-ended and differential inputs with straight-binary output format.

The multiSPI interface enables flexible communication through standard SPI or source-synchronous protocols, with single or dual SDO modes. Daisy-chain topology allows multiple devices sharing CONVST/CS and SCLK lines. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by CONVST/CS and RST pins, with NAP and power-down modes for power saving.

Nine configuration registers control device operation, including protocol selection, data output formatting, input range, and alarm thresholds. Data transfer frames require minimum 32 SCLK cycles for valid commands, with read operations returning conversion data or register contents with optional flags appended.

The BC Coroners Service reported 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in British Columbia in 2017, a 43% increase from 2016's 993 deaths. Deaths declined in the last four months of 2017 compared to earlier months. Approximately 81% of deaths involved fentanyl, up from 67% in 2016. Vancouver Coastal Health had the highest death rate at 35.9 per 100,000, while Fraser Health had the highest number of fentanyl-related deaths at 377. Over half of victims were aged 30-49, 90% were aged 19-59, and approximately 80% were male. Deaths spiked following income assistance payments. Officials emphasized the need for continued evidence-based prevention strategies including naloxone distribution and drug-checking services.

This study investigates dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSC) using natural dyes from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) as alternatives to synthetic ruthenium-based dyes. MP contains anthocyanins with strong UV-blue absorption, while GJL contains chlorophyll with red-region absorption. Various MP:GJL volume ratios (3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, 1:3) were tested to optimize photovoltaic performance.

The fabrication process involved preparing ITO-coated glass substrates, depositing TiO₂ films via spin coating, extracting dyes through ethanol-based stirring at 70°C, preparing iodide/iodine electrolyte, and creating graphite counter electrodes. Devices were assembled in sandwich configurations with dye-adsorbed TiO₂ photoanodes.

UV-Vis analysis showed complementary absorption: MP-rich solutions appeared reddish with anthocyanin peaks at 440-460 nm and 530-550 nm, while GJL-rich solutions showed yellow-brown hues with chlorophyll peaks at 610 and 665 nm. Mixed dyes exhibited both spectral features without chemical alteration, broadening the light-harvesting window.

Morphological analysis revealed MP-rich films suffered cracking and poor continuity, while balanced ratios (1:1, 1:2, 1:3) showed homogeneous, crack-free surfaces. FESEM confirmed the 1:1 mixed dye produced uniform nanoporous structures with minimal defects.

Photovoltaic testing demonstrated the 1:3 MP:GJL ratio achieved maximum efficiency (3.50%), compared to pure MP (2.75%) and pure GJL (2.12%). This synergistic enhancement resulted from complementary light absorption and improved charge collection. However, stability testing over 10 cycles showed GJL-rich compositions retained performance better than the 1:1 mixture, which collapsed rapidly. The study concludes that optimizing natural dye mixtures requires balancing initial efficiency with long-term stability.

Luca Speight, 18, received two awards at an Isle of Wight College ceremony: the 'Outstanding Achievement Award' and 'Isle of Wight College Student of the Year 2018'. He was recognized for his determination to succeed despite spending three months away due to a life-threatening illness that required hospitalization, induced coma, major surgery, and ongoing treatment. Luca caught up on missed work, excelled at his placement, and volunteered at college events. He credited his tutors, course mates, family, and friends for their support.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, a town of 1,500 residents, is preparing for the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse—the first to cross the continental U.S. in 99 years—as if facing a natural disaster. Located where "totality" will first appear, the town expects thousands of visitors. Hotels and campgrounds are sold out, and officials estimate crowds from thousands to hundreds of thousands. Preparations include renting portable restrooms, buying garbage cans and protective glasses, staffing three fire stations instead of one, and advising residents to stock supplies. Major concerns include traffic gridlock on single-lane Highway 101, which could block emergency vehicles, and harbor congestion from boaters. The Coast Guard will monitor water traffic, and local charter boats are offering $100 eclipse-viewing cruises.

Figma shares rose 7% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman demonstrated ChatGPT integration with Figma at the company's DevDay conference. The integration allows ChatGPT's 800 million monthly users to request Figma by name to convert sketches into diagrams, with Figma also suggested contextually by the assistant. NVIDIA RTX IO is a GPU-based technology that accelerates game asset loading and decompression by up to 100x compared to traditional storage methods, offloading CPU work to RTX GPUs via Microsoft's DirectStorage API. This enables faster frame rates, near-instant loading, and reduced game install sizes.

The NVIDIA A40 GPU, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and 5-10x AI training throughput compared to Turing-based GPUs. It features 48GB of scalable GPU memory, PCIe Gen4, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software for data center virtualization.

Ampere architecture GPUs support 8K60 and 4K120 displays via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1. They include fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decoding for AV1, HEVC, VP9, and other codecs, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding that matches x264 Medium quality.

The GA10x architecture provides up to 2x performance improvements in shading, ray tracing, and AI through second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory up to 936 GB/sec.

The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6 memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink, offering significant performance gains in rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads compared to the previous generation RTX 6000.

A Wisconsin man, Benjamin David Sherwood, was sentenced to 11 years in prison for traveling to Houston to engage in sexual contact with a 4-year-old girl. Chief District Judge Lee H. Rosenthal also ordered lifetime supervision. Sherwood pleaded guilty in August to interstate travel for illicit contact with a child and enticing a minor. The case began in 2015 when a Homeland Security agent posted an online ad for a fictional 2-year-old; Sherwood responded, admitting attraction only to children. In May 2017, he traveled to Houston with gifts and sexual items, where agents arrested him. He will register as a sex offender with restricted access to children and the Internet.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018, filed with the SEC, reports total revenue of $26.8 billion (three months) and $80.3 billion (nine months), with net income of $7.4 billion and $7.7 billion, respectively. The company adopted new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases effective July 1, 2017, requiring restatement of prior period results. Revenue recognition changes primarily affected Windows 10 and commercial software subscriptions, resulting in earlier recognition of license revenue. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act enacted December 22, 2017, resulted in a provisional net charge of $13.8 billion, including a $17.8 billion transition tax on deferred foreign income partially offset by $4.0 billion benefit from deferred tax remeasurement. Total assets were $245.5 billion, with $132.3 billion in cash and short-term investments. Long-term debt totaled $76.9 billion. The company had $30.3 billion remaining under its $40 billion share repurchase program. Contracted not recognized revenue was $61 billion.

Portland Thorns captain Christine Sinclair stated that anything less than a championship would be disappointing, motivated by last season's semifinal loss to the Western New York Flash. The Thorns finished second this season and will host Orlando Pride in the first playoff semifinal, while first-place North Carolina Courage hosts Chicago Red Stars in the other. The winners meet Oct. 14 for the final. Portland has never lost to Orlando (3-0-1), though Pride gained strength from Alex Morgan's return and Marta's play. Courage's Lynn Williams led with nine goals, while Chicago's Christen Press scored 11. Sky Blue's Sam Kerr won the Golden Boot with a league-record 17 goals. BMW launched the 1 Series sedan exclusively in China in July 2016 through its partnership with Brilliance Automotive Ltd. The company is considering bringing the vehicle to India, though no decision has been made. The sedan, based on the UKL1 platform and featuring front-wheel drive, measures 4,456mm long with a 2,670mm wheelbase. The Oroville Dam's spillways may face less severe testing than feared despite 7.5 inches of rain expected over 10 days. This rainfall is significantly less than the 13.6 inches that caused damage in February, and will be more spread out with colder temperatures producing snow rather than runoff. Inflow is expected to be roughly one-quarter of previous peaks. Upstream dams are holding back water to reduce pressure, and reservoir levels are dropping about 4 inches hourly, creating a potential 40-foot buffer before Friday's first major rain. However, meteorologist Jan Null warns that a sudden warm spell melting the record snowpack poses a serious future risk.

Hong Liu reviews the LSZ theorem, which relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions by taking the on-shell limit and stripping external propagators. He explains sign conventions arising from Fourier transforms of initial and final states, and discusses truncating external propagators and considering only connected diagrams. Liu then transitions to fermions, introducing the Dirac equation as Dirac's 1928 attempt to fix problems with the Klein-Gordon equation. Though motivated by relativistic quantum mechanics, the Dirac equation is properly understood as field theory. Liu derives the equation by requiring Lorentz covariance with first-order time derivatives, leading to 4×4 matrices (alpha and beta) and a four-component spinor. Squaring the equation and matching to the Klein-Gordon form yields anticommutation relations: alpha_i alpha_j + alpha_j alpha_i = 2δ_ij and beta alpha_i + alpha_i beta = 0, with alpha_i and beta Hermitian. These define a Clifford algebra, with gamma matrices introduced as gamma^0 = iβ and gamma^i = iβα^i, giving the compact form (γ^μ∂_μ - m)ψ = 0. Liu notes that for massless particles, 2×2 Pauli matrices suffice, showing massive particles have more degrees of freedom. Different gamma matrix representations are equivalent under similarity transformations, with specific forms useful for different regimes.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Q1 2017 Form 10-Q with the SEC, reporting financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2017. The company reported net sales of $35.7 billion, up 23% year-over-year, with net income of $724 million. Operating income was $1.0 billion, down from $1.1 billion in Q1 2016. The company operates in three segments: North America ($21.0 billion sales, $596 million operating income), International ($11.1 billion sales, $481 million operating loss), and AWS ($3.7 billion sales, $890 million operating income). Cash and cash equivalents were $15.4 billion as of March 31, 2017, down from $19.3 billion at year-end 2016. The company has $8.8 billion in long-term debt outstanding and $45.9 billion in total contractual commitments. Amazon faces ongoing tax disputes with the IRS and French Tax Administration, and in March 2017 signed an agreement to acquire Souq Group Ltd. for $580 million.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards to resume patrols at Phuket's beaches by April 1, 2018, following a March 21 meeting. The Phuket Provincial Administration Organisation (PPAO) had previously hired lifeguards for 10 beaches covering 12 beaches across three districts. The governor instructed local administrative offices to manage beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu districts, while a procurement-selected company would handle Thalang district. Offices lacking budgets could request PPAO support, though this contradicted the governor's December 12 order removing PPAO involvement. The NNT report provided no explanation for this apparent reversal.

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt will fund a project through Schmidt Sciences to deploy uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) in the Southern Ocean around Antarctica. The $45 million, five-year initiative aims to collect data on why this ocean absorbs disproportionate amounts of CO2 despite its small size. The drone boats can operate in extreme winter conditions and remote areas inaccessible to crewed vessels or commercial shipping routes. The project uses machine learning to optimize data collection and will make findings publicly available. The funding comes as federal climate research faces significant cuts, with NOAA's budget targeted for 30% reduction and NSF's for 57%.

This document describes AMD AGESA firmware procedures for processor initialization and system configuration. Key procedures include: AMD_ENABLE_STACK, a stackless assembler routine that initializes processor and cache systems before main memory is available, using register passing and creating UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instances; AMD_DISABLE_STACK, which returns the system to a non-stack-enabled state when main memory becomes available; and AmdCreateStruct, which allocates and initializes parameter block storage using methods like PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost. Additional service procedures provide data eye results for DIMMs, APIC addresses, available pre-memory cache sizes, PCI base addresses, and processor/memory identification. Most procedures require an established stack environment and operational HyperTransport links. AARCH64 APUs with Platform Security Processors handle DRAM initialization differently and do not use early stack macros.

Lab experiments show that jostling microbubbles of air and methane in water can create tiny electrical sparks, offering a new possible explanation for will-o'-the-wisps—bluish lights historically reported above swamps and cemeteries. Researchers led by Yu Xia and Richard Zare at Stanford University designed a 3-D printed nozzle to create tiny bubbles mimicking swamp gas seepage. When bubbles were made small and crowded enough, high-speed cameras captured visible microlightning zaps between differently charged bubbles. While some scientists find the finding intriguing, others note limitations: the experiments were underwater rather than in air, and will-o'-the-wisps are rarely reported today despite unchanged conditions. The research advances understanding of triboelectricity—electric charge from friction or contact—and may have applications in driving chemical reactions or breaking down pollutants.

Multiple devices in a daisy-chain topology share CONVST/CS and SCLK connections from a host controller, with SDO-0 of each device connected to SDI of the next. Devices use identical configuration register values and operate with single SDO-0 output using SPI-compatible protocols. All devices sample analog inputs on CONVST/CS rising edge and begin data transfer on its falling edge. Devices shift out MSB on SCLK launch edges and shift in SDI data as LSB on capture edges. The host receives data from device N first, proceeding in MSB-first order. Optimal data transfer requires 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices; shorter frames cause configuration errors.

Solawave's 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is currently on sale for over $100 during Prime Day. The device targets specific facial areas, vibrates, radiates warmth, and requires three minutes of manual use per session. It uses a single 630-nm red-light wavelength. WIRED staffers reported positive results with skin tightening, particularly around the eyes. Solawave's Red Light Therapy Face Mask is also on sale for $227 ($122 off), though WIRED recommends other masks with better features.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on February 10, 2016, reporting three corporate actions: (1) election of Wendell P. Weeks as director and Audit Committee member, including a 1,365-share restricted stock unit award; (2) approval of a two-year leave of absence for Senior Vice President Diego Piacentini beginning August 2016, with suspension of RSU forfeiture, and assignment of his international consumer business responsibilities to Russ Grandinetti; and (3) Board authorization of a $5 billion stock repurchase program, replacing the previous $2 billion authorization from 2010.

This message to Congress addresses conservation of national resources, including waterways, reclamation of arid lands, forest preservation, and public land reclassification. The public domain has decreased from over 1 billion acres in 1860 to 731 million acres today, plus 368 million acres in Alaska. Early land statutes led to fraud and irresponsible private ownership. The speaker recommends validating executive withdrawals of coal lands and water-power sites, classifying lands by value, separating mineral rights from surface ownership, and leasing coal and minerals with anti-monopoly provisions. Water-power sites should be leased for up to fifty years with graduated rentals to prevent monopoly. Soil conservation is paramount, requiring scientific attention to improve productivity. The Reclamation Act has enabled over 30 projects, but inadequate funding has left settlers in distress; the speaker recommends issuing up to $30 million in bonds to complete projects. Forest reserves of 190 million acres are under Agriculture Department control, with reforestation proposed at stream sources. Inland waterway improvements are urged, specifically completing 54 dams on the Ohio River for 9-foot depth at $63 million cost, and similar improvements on the Mississippi and Missouri rivers. The speaker urges prompt action on these recommendations without awaiting pending investigations.

NVIDIA RTX IO accelerates data transfer from storage to GPU for large datasets, CAD models, and VR applications by integrating with Microsoft's DirectStorage API. It enables GPU-based lossless decompression, reducing CPU load and doubling I/O performance.

The NVIDIA A40 GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X AI training throughput compared to Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000. It features 48GB GPU memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), PCIe Gen4, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software for virtualized workstations.

Ampere architecture GPUs support 8K60 and 4K120 displays via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1. They include fifth-generation NVDEC for hardware-accelerated video decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 codecs, and seventh-generation NVENC for encoding up to 8K HEVC.

GA10x Ampere provides up to 2X performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI through second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity. It introduces GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, achieving 936 GB/sec bandwidth in RTX 3090.

The RTX A6000 features 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, with NVLink support for 96GB combined memory. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology in GDDR6X detects transmission errors and retries failed transactions, enabling safer overclocking by identifying performance plateaus before crashes occur.

This document specifies the SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD processors. The GHCB enables secure communication between encrypted guests and hypervisors through a 4KB shared memory area, protecting guest register state from hypervisor access during world switches.

Key components include: the GHCB MSR protocol for early communication before GHCB page establishment; hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap; NAE (Non-Automatic Exit) events for controlled state sharing; and versioned protocol updates (Version 2, Revisions 2.01-2.04) adding SEV-SNP support, multi-VMPL levels, trusted I/O (SEV-TIO), Secure AVIC, and enhanced certificate retrieval.

The specification details GHCB layout mirroring VMCB save state, registration requirements for SEV-SNP guests, SMP booting challenges with encrypted state, AP creation mechanisms, NMI handling protocols, and Restricted Injection features using #HV doorbell pages for event notification when direct interrupt injection is disabled.

The passage examines the relationship between consumer confidence indices and stock market returns through backtesting. The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index and the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) measure economic optimism through monthly surveys. Backtests using OECD consumer confidence data from 1993 show that investing in the S&P 500 only when consumer confidence exceeds its 12-month moving average yielded an 8.4% CAGR with 23% max drawdown, versus 10.4% CAGR and 55% drawdown for buy-and-hold, though the strategy was invested only 55% of the time. Conversely, investing only when confidence fell below the moving average produced just 1.58% annual returns. The CCI surveys 5,000 households monthly on current conditions and expectations; changes exceeding 5% indicate economic momentum shifts. High confidence typically precedes increased consumer spending and bullish markets, while low confidence signals reduced spending and economic contraction.

Natalie Grabow, 80, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship in Hawaii, completing the course in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds. She began competing in triathlons at age 60, one year after learning to swim. Grabow, a grandmother of four from Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, qualified for her first Kona championship at 61. She prepares for months before races, working out approximately two hours daily, and maintains a healthy diet without restrictions. Grabow was greeted at the finish line by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld, who set the record at 78. She plans to continue competing in triathlons for as long as possible.

The NVIDIA A40 GPU, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is designed for data center visual computing workloads. It delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X AI training throughput compared to the previous generation Quadro RTX 6000. The A40 features PCIe Gen4, 48GB of scalable GPU memory via NVLink, three DisplayPort outputs, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and Quadro Sync. It is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform for accelerated data center workloads. The GA10x architecture also introduces second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, GDDR6X memory, and hardware-accelerated AV1 decode. The NVIDIA RTX A6000, also based on GA102, offers 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48GB GDDR6 memory, and professional certifications for workstation applications.

Lenovo officially unveiled the ThinkPad 25, a limited edition retro laptop based on the T470 model, at an event in Yokohama, Japan. The design draws inspiration from the 1992 ThinkPad 700C, featuring a rubberized coating, red TrackPoint, classic seven-row keyboard with blue enter button, dedicated volume button, colorful logo, and status LEDs. Modern hardware includes a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Intel Core i7-7500U, GeForce 940MX GPU, 16GB DDR4, 512GB NVMe SSD, Thunderbolt 3, 720p webcam, fingerprint scanner, and 18-hour battery life. The laptop contrasts sharply with the 700C's Intel 486 25MHz CPU, 4-8MB RAM, 120MB HDD, and 640x480 10.4-inch LCD. Available in limited quantities in select countries starting at $1,899, below the 700C's original $2,375 price.

Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations use Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD) methods to calculate thermal conductivity. Both require heat flux (HF) calculations: NEMD measures energy exchange between thermostats, while GK averages atomic velocities and forces. Interfacial thermal conductance uses instantaneous heat current Q1→2, which can be spectrally decomposed (SDHC) to analyze phonon contributions. LAMMPS, a widely used MD code, originally used HF formulas valid only for pair potentials, leading to incorrect results for many-body potentials. While corrections exist for specific systems (molecular systems, carbon with Tersoff potential, some machine learning potentials), implementations for arbitrary many-body potentials were lacking, particularly for control surface calculations and SDHC. This work extends and implements Torii et al.'s exact formulas in LAMMPS for HF calculations in control volumes and control surfaces, and for SDHC, for arbitrary many-body potentials. The paper presents theoretical background, comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials, and SDHC results for graphene and MoS2.

COPD, a leading cause of death in the United States, presents with chronic coughing and shortness of breath. According to pulmonologist Dr. Jordan Taillon, smoking is the almost exclusive cause. Diagnosis involves assessing smoking history and pulmonary function tests measuring breathing capacity. Treatments include inhalers, oxygen, or pulmonary rehabilitation, which can reduce daily exacerbations but cannot reverse lung damage. The only way to prevent COPD or stop its progression is to quit smoking.

This study evaluates distance education in Turkish sports higher education during COVID-19 through qualitative interviews with 14 lecturers. Distance education, originating from 1728 correspondence courses, evolved through postal services to modern online platforms. Key elements include physical separation of teacher and student, institutional framework, technical tools, two-way communication, and occasional meetings.

Research identified four themes: positive aspects (independence from time/space, resource access, technology use, socioeconomic benefits); negative aspects (socialization loss, communication problems, motivation issues, technology/access barriers, ineffective applied lessons); challenges (infrastructure problems, ineffective communication, assessment difficulties); and management issues (poor crisis management, excessive administrative control, insufficient training).

Main findings show that while distance education offers flexibility and pandemic safety, sports education faces unique difficulties because applied courses cannot be conducted effectively online. Participants reported student motivation problems, unequal access to equipment/internet, communication barriers, and inadequate assessment systems. Process management was criticized for unclear decision-making chains and lack of preparation. The study recommends field-specific distance education designs, improved infrastructure, better data security measures, and further research on effectiveness across different departments.

This study investigates the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in Mn₃Sn(01̄10)/MgO(110)/Mn₃Sn magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) using first-principles calculations. The Mn₃Sn electrode is a noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse 120° magnetic structure that breaks time-reversal symmetry, enabling a finite TMR effect through momentum-dependent spin splitting. The researchers constructed the MTJ with a thick MgO barrier to ensure realistic tunneling transport, finding a TMR ratio exceeding 1000%. Analysis reveals the TMR effect arises from the x-component spin polarization of Mn₃Sn (aligned with the cluster octupole moment's easy axis) combined with electron filtering by the MgO barrier, whose complex band structure provides lowest decay rates around k∥∼0. The Mn₃Sn(01̄10) orientation was selected for its experimental demonstration of electrical switching via spin-orbit torque. This work establishes Mn₃Sn as a promising material for antiferromagnetic spintronic devices with advantages including reduced stray fields and faster switching speeds compared to ferromagnetic alternatives.

Jeff Bezos has proposed space-based data centres as a future solution to Earth's strained digital infrastructure, citing benefits like reduced land and energy constraints and resilience against terrestrial disruptions. The concept addresses growing demand for cloud and AI computing, though significant challenges remain including radiation shielding, cooling in vacuum, communication latency, and high launch costs. Other aerospace and technology companies are also exploring orbital and lunar infrastructure, encouraged by declining launch costs and hardware advances. While economically unviable currently, proponents suggest early investment could become profitable as data demand grows exponentially. The proposal reflects intensifying competition for computing power pushing the sector beyond traditional boundaries.

Owl eyes are immobile, tubular structures that provide binocular vision for focusing on prey. A study in the Journal of Neuroscience tested whether barn owls, despite having simpler brains than primates, can group moving visual elements to distinguish objects from backgrounds—a task previously studied only in primates. Researchers showed barn owls screens of moving black dots and tracked their head movements and brain activity. The owls successfully identified target dots moving differently from background dots, performing better when contrasting directions were uniform. Activity in the ocular tectum, a basic visual processing area, varied with dot movement, indicating this brain region handles the task. The findings suggest this visual processing ability is more fundamental than previously thought.

Strong US job creation and wage growth data increased expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, causing the dollar and bond yields to rise while stocks fell. The economy added 200,000 jobs last month, with wage growth reaching 2.9 percent—the largest 12-month increase in over nine years. The 10-year US Treasury yield hit a four-year high of 2.84 percent.

Gold prices edged lower on Friday as the dollar rose 0.2% against the euro ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls data due at 1330 GMT, which is expected to show 180,000 jobs added in January. Stronger data could increase expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes, negatively impacting non-yielding gold. Silver fell 0.7% to $17.11, platinum dropped 1.4% to $991.60, and palladium rose 0.6% to $1,042.72 but remains on track for its biggest weekly drop since September, down 4.8%.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired on the last day of school after five years in the role and 30 years in the district. He cited raising the graduation rate from 60% to 83% and expanding magnet school seats by over 10,000 as key achievements. Skorkowsky noted the district's $60 million budget shortfall and urged the new superintendent, Dr. Jesus Jara, and the school board to advocate for education funding in the 2019 legislative session, specifically questioning how marijuana tax revenue is distributed across counties. He also highlighted school safety improvements like single-entry doorways and called for more mental health professionals on campuses. Skorkowsky advised Jara to engage with the community and listen to concerns. The two will work together for several weeks before Skorkowsky departs without definite future plans.

Lifeline Fiji's program director Jeremiah Merekula states that suicide remains taboo in Fiji, with 124 suicides and 107 attempted suicides recorded in 2015, and 102 suicides and 104 attempted suicides in 2016. From 2011 to March 2017, 627 suicides and 694 attempted suicides were recorded nationally, with 56 suicides and 97 attempted suicides among children. Merekula attributes high rates to lack of help-seeking behavior, community support structures, and awareness of emotional wellbeing. Lifeline Fiji operates a 24/7 toll-free helpline (132454) and works with schools and parents to promote early intervention and awareness.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security's Chris Young warned security professionals about "data landmines"—corrupted data used to manipulate decision-making, citing the 2016 presidential election as an example. He also identified home networks with IoT devices as a new attack surface threatening corporate networks. Microsoft President Brad Smith called for the tech community to act as "a digital Switzerland," proposing digital Geneva Conventions principles including defensive-only operations, collaboration, civilian protection, and no attacks on infrastructure. Smith advocated for an international cyber agency to monitor nation-state attacks, urged governments to sign cyber conflict agreements, and emphasized private sector leadership in cybersecurity, noting that nation-state attacks increasingly target private assets.

This patent application describes a geographically-based graphical user interface (map GUI) for social media applications that enables real-time location sharing and destination prediction. The system receives location information from a user's client device, determines their current trajectory, accesses historical location data, and predicts a presumed destination by correlating current and historical data. The predicted destination is displayed to friends via icons on a map GUI. The system includes client devices running location sharing applications, a location sharing server system with API and application servers, and databases storing message data, entity graphs, and location information. The prediction component analyzes habitual places and trajectory patterns to compute destination probabilities, and can estimate arrival times. Users can control location sharing permissions through audience options (Best Friends, Friends, Custom) and interact with friends directly from the map interface through chat and other features.

The MSPM0G MCUs feature an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU (32kHz-80MHz) with pre-fetch/cache, SysTick, MPU, and NVIC. Five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) optimize power consumption across two power domains (PD1 for CPU/high-performance peripherals, PD0 for low-power peripherals). The PMU provides brown-out reset and core regulation. Clock sources include internal/external oscillators (32kHz-80MHz) and PLL. Peripherals include 12-channel DMA, event manager, up to 128KB SRAM with ECC/parity protection, dual-bank flash (up to 512KB), 93 GPIOs with wake capability, two 12-bit ADCs (4Msps), temperature sensor, VREF, three comparators, 12-bit DAC, security features (AES-128/256, TRNG, CRC), math accelerator, multiple UART/I2C/SPI/CAN-FD interfaces, RTC, watchdog timers, and flexible timers with PWM. Development tools include LaunchPad kits, SDK, SysConfig, and multiple IDE/compiler options.

Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open a micropub called the Radyr Tap in Station Road, Radyr, which has been without a pub since 2003. The plans follow a Twitter campaign by resident Jamie Grundy. The micropub would occupy a former dry cleaners unit and serve local beers, wines, spirits, and takeaway drinks, plus artisan snacks. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council decides.

MIT became the first of nine invited universities to publicly reject the Trump administration's "Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education," which would mandate campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding treatment. MIT president Sally Kornbluth stated the compact would restrict institutional independence and freedom of expression, and that its premise conflicted with MIT's values. Eight other universities received invitations, with most providing vague responses while Texas officials expressed enthusiasm. Some state officials, including California's governor and Virginia Democrats, threatened funding cuts if institutions signed. Academic organizations and some lawmakers praised MIT's rejection, while former Trump administration officials suggested potential retaliation.

Spiritual healer Komar Uddin, 68, denies raping a 19-year-old woman during a religious ritual at her Leicester home in February 2015, where he allegedly claimed to drive out an evil spirit while her family remained downstairs. The woman testified that Uddin rubbed holy oil on her, announced she was pregnant, and offered to make the baby "go away" for £200. DNA evidence linked Uddin to the victim. After arrest and bail in 2015, he fled to Germany and was extradited last November. The defence claims the woman initiated sexual contact and lied, which she denied. The trial continues.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos from Nikolas Cruz, the suspect in the February 14 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, that killed 17 people and injured 17 others. In the videos, Cruz, 19, announces his plan to become "the next school shooter of 2018," stating his intent to kill at least 20 people with an AR-15 and saying "you're all going to die." He describes logistics including taking Uber to campus, and expresses loneliness, anger, and hatred toward others. The videos were found on Cruz's cellphone after the attack. Cruz is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 counts of attempted murder; his lawyers have offered a guilty plea in exchange for life without parole, but prosecutors are seeking the death penalty. The Broward State Attorney's Office released the videos under Florida public records law after turning them over to defense attorneys as part of pretrial discovery. Cruz's attorneys opposed the release, stating it would further harm victims' families and the community. Cruz had previously attended a school for children with emotional disabilities, and his late mother had called 911 on him nearly 20 times; he also had a history of killing animals and posting images online.

The passage calls for expanding naval officer training at Annapolis and facilitating retirement of impaired senior officers to address a critical shortage straining junior officers. It emphasizes maintaining naval preparedness to prevent foreign conflicts, warning that refusal to do so invites disaster. The Post-Office Department saw record revenue growth of over $10 million, with rural free-delivery service proving highly successful—showing 10% yearly increases versus 2% in non-served areas, covering one-third of available U.S. territory with 10,748 additional routes requested. The passage also supports nationally-aided irrigation in the West, scientific forest protection, and immediate legislation to stop "senseless slaughter" of game animals on forest reserves, particularly criticizing elk killing for antlers or tusks.

Michael T. Klare argues that Donald Trump is attempting to dismantle the post-WWII liberal world order and replace it with a new global system based on energy preferences rather than political ideology or civilization. Trump's foreign policy aims to create an alliance of fossil-fuel states led by the U.S., Russia, and Saudi Arabia, while isolating renewable-energy powers like Germany and China. Evidence includes his revitalization of U.S.-Saudi relations with a $110 billion arms deal and energy cooperation, his weakening of NATO and the EU, his withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement, and his efforts to lift sanctions on Russia. These three petro-powers control approximately 38% of global oil output and 41% of natural gas output, with their broader network controlling nearly 60% of world petroleum production. Despite obstacles like Russia-Saudi differences over Syria and Iran, Trump continues pursuing this petroleum-based trilateral alliance through diplomatic, military, and energy sector coordination.

Scientists have found that blocking a protein called Ant2 reprograms T cells' energy metabolism, making them more resilient, faster, and more effective at attacking tumors. The research, led by Hebrew University PhD student Omri Yosef and Prof. Michael Berger in collaboration with international colleagues, shows this metabolic rewiring can be achieved through both genetic modifications and drugs. The findings suggest potential for new cancer immunotherapy treatments that enhance the body's own immune response.

Facebook took over two hours to remove live video of a shooting death in Cleveland due to its reliance on user flagging. Separately, US immigrant rights activist Hugo Castro went missing in Mexico after posting a Facebook Live plea for help while being chased. In political news, Democrats are watching Georgia's 6th Congressional District special election, where candidate Jon Ossoff has raised $8.3 million in an attempt to flip a long-held Republican seat.

This study surveyed 304 Belgian medical students across four universities to assess their knowledge, attitudes, and exposure to global surgery. Despite 16.9 million annual deaths from conditions requiring surgical care and five billion people lacking access to safe surgical care, global surgery remains neglected in medical education. Only 24.7% of students had prior exposure to global surgery, primarily through social media, while 75.3% wanted more exposure, preferring optional teaching, events, and clinical internships. Knowledge was poor: only 23.9% correctly identified that five billion people lack surgical access, and 21.7% knew that 150 million additional procedures are needed annually. While 95% agreed global surgery is relevant and 70% supported more compulsory teaching, master's students showed less interest than bachelor's students. Obstacles to pursuing global surgery careers included personal responsibilities (42.8%), language barriers (42.1%), lack of established career paths (39.1%), financial constraints (34.5%), and lack of mentorship (33.6%). The authors recommend integrating pre-clinical global surgery seminars and equitable bilateral international internships into formal medical curricula to address workforce needs.

Paul Ehrlich's 1968 book "The Population Bomb" framed overpopulation as a crisis of poor, non-European nations, but this perspective has been criticized as potentially racist. While global urban population is projected to reach 66% by 2050, cities actually reduce birth rates—urban women in Kenya, India, and elsewhere have fewer children than rural counterparts. However, cities create a "consumption bomb": though housing half the world's population, they consume three-quarters of global materials and depend heavily on external resources for water, food, and materials.

A 2018 test of 124 VPN and proxy providers found that 20 (16.13%) leaked users' IP addresses via WebRTC, while 101 kept IPs hidden. Leaking providers included Astrill, Hola!VPN, Windscribe Addons, and others. Recommended VPNs that prevent WebRTC leaks include ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, and VyprVPN. Users can test for leaks using sites like ipleak.net or disable WebRTC manually in browsers, as most enable it by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer.

This section provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W devices, including status codes, material types, RoHS compliance, lead finish options, MSL ratings, and part marking details. Global equity markets declined Monday as U.S. 10-year bond yields approached 3 percent, a level investors view as a tipping point for alternatives to equities. Caterpillar Inc.'s board voted to maintain the quarterly dividend at $0.77 per share, payable May 20 to shareholders of record April 24, marking seven consecutive quarters of flat dividends despite a 23-year history of increases. The company offers a 3.25% yield, above S&P-500 and Treasury averages. Goldman Sachs added Caterpillar to its 'conviction buy' list with a $120 price target, citing increased mining capital spending. Caterpillar shares rose ~20% in nine months, partly due to Trump's pro-energy policies and proposed $1 trillion infrastructure spending. However, the author advises caution: Caterpillar trades at 29x current earnings, faces a federal tax investigation, declining revenues and earnings for four years, and reduced cash flows. The company's 2017 guidance predicts further revenue and profit declines, making dividend growth unlikely.

The passage introduces EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework that uses PCME++ and ECHO-CLIP to address two challenges in estimating echocardiogram variables from ECGs: signal complexity and scarce labeled data. Traditional cross-modal contrastive learning uses deterministic embeddings with one-to-one mappings, which limits capturing ECG temporal variability. The proposed probabilistic approach enables many-to-many mappings by modeling embeddings as distributions with mean and variance, better representing uncertainty. ECHO-CLIP, trained on ECHO-text pairs, serves as a teacher to guide ECG representation learning without requiring large-scale annotated ECG-ECHO datasets. The three main contributions are: (1) a probabilistic multimodal ECG model capturing structural and functional insights, (2) a knowledge distillation approach reducing dependency on large annotated datasets, and (3) experimental evidence of uncertainty-aware downstream task evaluation.

Henry L. Stimson advised against raising territorial adjustments or trusteeships for discussion until the Pacific war advanced further and Russia joined, warning that excluding Pacific areas of interest would provoke distrust. The Cairo Declaration of December 1, 1943, stated the Allies sought no territorial gain and aimed to strip Japan of Pacific islands seized since 1914. At a January 26, 1945 meeting in Washington, Under Secretary Grew discussed upcoming Mexico City conference plans, emphasizing study of international organization and strengthening the Inter-American System. He noted ten American republics had commented on Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, welcomed further exchanges, and stressed that preserving peace required drastic measures including preparedness to use force.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on April 20, 2022, reporting its first quarter 2022 financial results, which were released via a company website posting. The filing, signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn, includes the quarterly update as Exhibit 99.1 and is furnished under Item 2.02, not deemed "filed" for Section 18 purposes.

Chris King, 57, who became the first person in the UK to receive both hands in a transplant operation at Leeds General Infirmary in July 2016 after losing his hands in a work accident, made his first visit to Headingley Carnegie Stadium to watch Leeds Rhinos defeat Widnes Vikings 42-22. The rugby league fan was applauded at half-time when he went onto the pitch to draw the winning ticket for the golden gamble draw, describing the experience as "absolutely exhilarating."

The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rejected Crocs Inc.'s design patent after a five-year legal battle against competitor USA Dawgs, finding another company filed a similar patent first. Crocs plans to appeal. The ruling compounds existing struggles, as the company announced plans to close 160 stores over two years and reported a 3.3 percent revenue drop in the most recent quarter.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of academic publications on Digital Accessibility in Education from 2013-2024, using data from Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC databases. The research found significant growth in publications, particularly post-2020, with 502 total publications on digital accessibility in 2024 (339 specifically in education) compared to 12 in 2013. Scopus hosted the majority of publications (1,199 for digital accessibility; 782 for education), followed by Web of Science and ERIC. Journal articles were the predominant publication type (468), with conference papers second (274). Research areas were most concentrated in Digital Accessibility and Inclusion (438 publications), Education and Social Sciences (385), and Computer Science (340). English dominated with 873 publications, while other languages remained minimal. Higher education was the most studied educational level (469 publications). Geographically, the USA led with 236 publications, followed by the UK (104) and Spain (74). Citation analysis identified Chen Weiqin as the most cited author (58 citations) and Gorriz (2023) as the most cited document (74 citations). The USA and UK showed the highest citation counts among countries, though Norway demonstrated the strongest international collaboration links. The study concludes that digital accessibility research has grown substantially, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic, but notes limited international collaboration and calls for strengthened legal frameworks and increased focus on computer literacy for students with disabilities.

Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) is emerging as an alternative cytogenomic technique for hematologic malignancies, offering comprehensive detection of structural rearrangements and copy number variants at 5kbp resolution. This study presents a streamlined analysis workflow using Bionano Access and VIA software for myeloid neoplasms, tested on 10 retrospective samples analyzed 5-6 times each by independent teams. The workflow involves quality control, automated variant calling, technologist review with custom views and classifications, and director review with final reporting. Results showed 100% concordance with standard of care (karyotype/FISH) for reported variants, with OGM additionally detecting novel findings in 5 of 6 positive cases. Technologist review times averaged 25-47 minutes depending on case complexity, representing approximately 50% time reduction compared to Bionano Access alone. The study demonstrates that OGM with VIA provides efficient, reproducible, high-resolution cytogenomic analysis capable of consolidating multiple legacy techniques into a single assay.

Mark Ryan, headteacher of St. Patrick's Catholic Primary School in Thornaby, was falsely accused of taking a two-week term-time holiday after an inaccurate Gazette report. In fact, he took three days of sanctioned leave to attend a close family friend's wedding abroad, approved by governors as an "exceptional circumstance" under school policy. The article also incorrectly claimed he had threatened to fine a parent for term-time holidays, though he never spoke to her. Ryan, who has worked at the school for 22 years with only one other absence request, received strong support from governors, staff, parents, and the community. Governor chair Gary Wilson and parish priest Father Michael Keogh defended Ryan's commitment to the school.

The Shippers Group celebrated the grand opening of its new 540,000 square foot distribution facility in Austell, Georgia on September 15th with a DC Chamber Ribbon Cutting. The facility provides warehousing, transportation, packaging and e-commerce fulfillment services. Founded in 1901 as a cotton warehousing company, the Dallas-based firm has expanded to eleven locations nationwide since 1970 and recently rebranded from Shippers Warehouse to reflect its broader logistics services. The new multi-client facility brings the company's total Georgia warehouse space to 1.5 million square feet.

The New York Mets are overhauling their coaching staff after missing the playoffs despite having MLB's most expensive roster at $429 million in payroll and luxury tax. Manager Carlos Mendoza will return, but pitching coach Jeremy Hefner, hitting coaches Jeremy Barnes and Eric Chavez, third base coach Mike Sarbaugh, bench coach John Gibbons (resigned), and catching coach Glenn Sherlock (retiring) will not. The team collapsed from 45-24 in June to 38-55 in the final 93 games, with pitching and defense as primary issues. Assistant pitching coach Desi Druschel and bullpen coach José Rosado may interview elsewhere, while first base coach Antoan Richardson, strategy coach Danny Barnes, and coaching assistant Rafael Fernandez are invited to return.

Apple Inc. has been the world's most valuable public company and came within $50 billion of a $1 trillion market cap in early June. Amazon is rapidly closing the gap, with the spread between the two companies narrowing from 50 percent to about 10 percent since the beginning of 2018. As of Friday's market close, the difference was approximately $85 billion. Amazon's stock value has increased by $260 billion in 2018 alone.

World stocks declined Tuesday after U.S. 10-year Treasury yields exceeded 3% for the first time since January 2014, while oil prices rose above $75 per barrel. The pan-European FTSEurofirst 300 fell 0.23% and MSCI's global gauge shed 0.16%. U.S. stocks dropped despite strong earnings from Verizon and Caterpillar, with the Dow down 0.19%, S&P 500 down 0.24%, and Nasdaq down 0.73%. Alphabet fell 4.93% on cost concerns. Brent crude reached its highest since November 2014 due to OPEC cuts, strong demand, and potential Iran sanctions.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model strategy, created by Yale Hirsch, is an active market timing approach that uses entry and exit signals to reduce risk exposure compared to passive strategies. The strategy was backtested over 16 years using a diversified portfolio of five asset classes—stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities—with equal weights. Specific ETFs were selected for each category based on diversification, liquidity, and performance history. Results showed significantly lower drawdowns (-27.27%) compared to buy-and-hold strategies (-47.77%). Yale Hirsch, founder of the Hirsch Organization and creator of the Stock Trader's Almanac, pioneered seasonal market analysis and introduced concepts like the "Presidential Election Year Cycle" and "Best Six Consecutive Months."

The speaker defends Republican calls for American military superiority, criticizing Secretary of State Muskie and the Carter Administration for neglecting defense spending while the Soviet Union expands globally through proxies in Africa, Afghanistan, and Central America. The speaker argues that peace requires strength, not unilateral disarmament, citing post-WWII security and the Korean War as examples where military weakness or ambiguity invited aggression. The Vietnam War is reframed as a "noble cause" whose veterans deserve respect, with lessons that America must provide troops the means to win. The speaker warns against "peace at any price" and the "Vietnam Syndrome," emphasizing that credible military strength prevents challenges and preserves freedom.

Home Capital Group Inc is negotiating with a syndicate of banks including Royal Bank of Canada, Bank of Montreal, and Toronto-Dominion Bank to secure approximately $2 billion in loans to replace an emergency credit line from April. International banks including Credit Suisse and Goldman Sachs are also in discussions. The mortgage lender has experienced severe deposit withdrawals—95% from high-interest savings accounts since March 27—following the termination of its former CEO and accusations by Ontario's securities regulator of misleading investors. Home Capital is seeking interest rates 2-3% above cost of funds, though this is uncertain. The company and involved banks declined to comment.

This paper examines the normative assumptions underlying educational disparities research through luck egalitarianism, a political philosophy theory holding that inequalities caused by factors beyond individual control (brute luck) are unjust. While luck egalitarianism justifies correcting educational disparities based on social background, Elizabeth Anderson's critiques—the harshness objection and humiliation objection—reveal problems with pursuing fairness alone. The harshness objection notes that luck egalitarianism can leave individuals in severe conditions due to their own choices; the humiliation objection highlights how compensation policies may undermine dignity and impose stigma. To address these issues, the paper proposes three additional values: fresh start (allowing individuals to restart despite past choices), sufficiency (guaranteeing minimum thresholds of welfare), and respect (avoiding humiliation in redistribution). The author argues that empirical research on educational disparities should incorporate these values alongside fairness, examining longitudinal opportunities for renewal, threshold-based educational standards, and classroom experiences of humiliation.

The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-5 in Game 1 of their NL Division Series on October 6, 2017. Justin Turner homered and drove in five runs, tying a Dodgers postseason record. Clayton Kershaw won despite giving up four home runs, becoming the first pitcher in team history to do so in a postseason game. The Dodgers scored four runs in the first inning against starter Taijuan Walker, who lasted only one inning. Game 2 features Rich Hill against Robbie Ray.

Social media algorithm changes make influencers valuable for expanding reach. Social influencers are credible users with large followings whose endorsements provide significant value. Local influencers for pizzerias include food bloggers, dedicated food enthusiasts, community leaders, and local celebrities. Five actionable steps are suggested for finding them.

A bankruptcy trustee sued to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances under 11 U.S.C.A. § 548(a). Defendants moved to dismiss, arguing the plaintiff lacked standing and that recovered assets wouldn't benefit creditors equally. The court denied the motion, finding that under the confirmed Modified Plan of Reorganization, impaired unsecured creditors received stock or stock purchase rights in the successor-in-interest, so recovering fraudulent transfers would indirectly increase the value of their distributions by strengthening the successor-in-interest's financial health. The court held that 11 U.S.C.A. § 1123(b)(3) expressly permits a plan to provide for retention and enforcement of claims by a trustee or representative, and distinguished cases where recovery would benefit only third parties rather than creditors.

In *Hardin v. White*, the Iowa Supreme Court affirmed a decree enjoining an execution sale of real estate. The court held that an injunction bond need not be double the judgment amount when seeking only to restrain sale of specific property under a general execution, rather than to defeat or postpone collection of the judgment itself. The court also held that where a judgment creditor causes real estate to be sold upon execution issued for only part of his judgment, he cannot later sell the debtor's right of redemption upon another execution for the remainder, even if the second execution was issued under a different decree, when both decrees cover the same underlying debt and the creditor is entitled to only one satisfaction. The court distinguished *Barnes v. Cavanagh*, noting that successive sales under different judgments are permissible only when based on different claims, not when the same indebtedness is involved.

The IMF released a report on China's financial system stability, recommending that regulators prioritize financial stability over growth objectives. The report noted that pursuit of regional growth targets and job preservation has led to surging debt, particularly at local government levels. The IMF advised forming a financial stability sub-committee and increasing staff for the banking watchdog. Stress tests on 33 banks showed potential capital shortfalls equal to 2.5% of GDP under severely adverse scenarios, with nonperforming loans rising to 9.1%. The IMF warned that rapid development of wealth management products and new financial instruments poses systemic risks. China's central bank responded that the stress tests don't reflect the whole picture and that China has strong ability to fend off financial risks.

A young, inexperienced person expresses confusion about distinguishing good from evil and fear of becoming a victim of violence. They describe extreme bullying in schools, where students don't report incidents due to fear and adults often dismiss concerns. Bullies sometimes extend harassment to social media, with some believing they're "helping" victims or acting from their own unhappiness. The writer suggests addressing bullying through changes at home and school, urging readers to make a difference for future generations.

Chrissy Teigen discussed her anxiety and postpartum depression (PPD) in a Marie Claire interview, describing symptoms like feeling shaky and self-conscious. She was diagnosed with both conditions after her daughter Luna's birth in 2016, experiencing PPD for four months. Anxiety affects 40 million American adults, while PPD impacts one in seven to nine mothers. Teigen takes antidepressants and hopes to expand her family despite concerns about recurring PPD. The passage includes mental health resources and praises Teigen for using her platform to reduce stigma.

Islamic Finance has thrived despite 2016's economic shocks, with the industry expanding rapidly due to growing demand for Sharia-compliant services. Islamic banks now grow at 19.7% annually, with capital at $3 trillion expected to reach $4 trillion by the early 2020s. Over 300 Islamic banks operate globally, gaining popularity in non-Muslim countries like the UK, Luxembourg, Hong Kong, South Africa, and the US. More than half of Islamic banks are investing $5-20 million in digital banking initiatives. The World Finance Islamic Finance Awards recognize innovation and excellence in the sector, with winners featured in the latest issue of World Finance.

An email from Miyung Buster dated March 19, 2001, shares news articles covering California's energy crisis. Topics include: a San Diego panel easing air pollution restrictions on the Cabrillo power plant to prevent blackouts; FERC identifying $55 million in potential February overcharges by electricity suppliers, with state leaders criticizing the amount as insufficient; OPEC's decision to cut oil production by 4%, prompting Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to call for increased U.S. domestic production; various groups using the energy crisis to advance agendas including auto makers seeking to avoid electric car mandates and manufacturers challenging overtime rules; creditors threatening to force Southern California Edison into bankruptcy over unpaid debts; PG&E reorganizing its "Block 50" blackout exemption list affecting hundreds of thousands of customers; and a commentary criticizing political rhetoric about "out-of-state profiteers" as misguided parochialism.

The author returned to school part-time six years ago to study journalism, building on an associate arts degree from the 1990s. Despite uncertainty about career goals, they remained open to possibilities while adapting to the field's digital transformation. They rediscovered their love of learning, overcoming earlier academic struggles caused by junior high bullying. In their 40s, they took financial risks and succeeded in challenging coursework like statistics, while actively participating in campus activities including student media, honors society, cultural events, and notable lectures. After graduating, they chose to continue as a digital storytelling graduate student and research assistant, finding personal healing and fulfillment in completing what they started decades earlier.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic disorder causing abnormal, sickle-shaped hemoglobin cells that carry oxygen poorly, leading to reduced healthy red blood cells and blocked blood vessels. Most common in sub-Saharan African, South/Central American, Middle Eastern, and Mediterranean populations, it affects approximately 100,000 people in the United States. Symptoms include sickle cell crises (severe pain episodes), acute chest syndrome, anemia, jaundice, and organ damage. Smoking increases complications. Diagnosis requires a simple blood test, with newborn screening standard in the U.S. Treatment involves regular vaccinations, screenings, pain management, medications to increase fetal hemoglobin, blood transfusions, and potentially stem cell transplantation. Lifestyle recommendations include smoking cessation, balanced diet, limited alcohol, adequate rest, and regular exercise to support heart health and reduce symptom episodes.

Coach Quenneville discusses various aspects of a hockey playoff series, including player injuries (Toews' upper body status uncertain, Bergeron limited), lineup decisions, and team performance. He praises Corey's goaltending, notes the physical intensity of the series, and emphasizes the importance of faceoffs, special teams, and balanced scoring across all lines. Quenneville mentions adapting to opponents' strategies, maintaining focus, and capitalizing on home-ice advantage while managing player fatigue through a long playoff run.

A coach praises his hockey team's will to win, preparation, and determination, crediting veteran leadership and a businesslike approach. He highlights Sidney Crosby's exceptional drive, off-ice habits, and leadership by example, noting his ability to set the tone early in games. He commends Jake Guentzel's hockey sense, poise, and playoff performance, and expresses confidence in goaltender Matt Murray's timely saves. The coach states Game 3 was their best in the series, believes the team is improving with each game, and values the extra rest between games for higher quality play. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs, aided by AMD gains. AppLovin shares plummeted following a Bloomberg report that the SEC is investigating the mobile advertising company over its data-collection practices, specifically whether it violated agreements on targeted advertising.
