The company recently joined the S&P 500, replacing MarketAxess Holdings, despite short-seller opposition. Muddy Waters Research alleged in May that AppLovin systematically violates app store terms by extracting proprietary IDs to deliver ads without user consent.

Thousands of cases of "Budget $aver Cherry Pineapple Monster Pops" and "Sugar Free Twin Pops" are being recalled due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination. The products were distributed to 15 states including Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Maine, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. Listeria can cause serious or fatal infections in vulnerable populations and miscarriages or stillbirths in pregnant women.

Research from the University of Exeter indicates that traditional "inefficient" fishing methods—specifically sail-driven boats and hand-hauled dredges—are sustaining oyster stocks in Cornwall's Fal fishery, Europe's only remaining sail-driven commercial fishing fleet. The study found that motorizing the fleet would increase fishing activity nine-fold, threatening the fishery's survival. While oyster stocks have declined due to disease, mechanization poses the greatest threat. The native European flat oyster is now threatened by pollution, overfishing, and non-native species. Researchers used GPS tracking to demonstrate sail dredging's inefficiency compared to modern methods, concluding that traditional practices provide important insights for sustainable fishery management.

A Gallup poll found only 44 percent of Americans believe Donald Trump can prevent major scandals, compared to 74 percent for Obama in 2009 and 77 percent for Bush in 2001. Trump scored lower than his three predecessors across all categories, with deficits ranging from 15 to 32 percentage points. Gallup attributes this partly to historically low public trust in government. The poll surveyed 1,028 adults December 7-11 with a 4 percent margin of error.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 30, 2017. The company reported net sales of $88.3 billion, up 13% from $78.4 billion in the prior year quarter, with net income of $20.1 billion compared to $17.9 billion. iPhone net sales increased 13% to $61.6 billion despite a 1% decline in unit sales, attributed to higher average selling prices. Services revenue grew 18% to $8.5 billion. The company spent $10.1 billion on share repurchases and paid $3.3 billion in dividends. Total assets were $406.8 billion, with $266.6 billion in liabilities and $140.2 billion in shareholders' equity. The U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act enacted December 22, 2017 lowered the federal tax rate from 35% to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax, resulting in a provisional $2.6 billion tax impact. The company had $111.0 billion in term debt outstanding and $12.0 billion in commercial paper.

The article discusses building a "Get Rich Portfolio" focused on stock investments, citing Jeremy Siegel's research showing stocks as the most productive asset class over 220 years. FOX 17 News, a Tribune station in West Michigan, seeks a Weather/Multimedia Journalist with at least two years of commercial TV weather forecasting experience. The role requires delivering on-air and digital forecasts, producing weather graphics, covering breaking news, shooting/editing/writing content for all platforms, and engaging audiences through social media. Candidates must demonstrate strong time management, digital/social media, editing, and shooting skills, plus proof of social media/digital journalism abilities. Medium market experience preferred. Apply at www.tribunemedia.com with demo reel link included. Tribune Media operates 42 local TV stations, WGN America, Tribune Studios, Tribune Digital Ventures, and other media properties.

A player reflects on a tough overtime loss, noting missed opportunities and the opponent's late success. They describe the third period as their most successful, with pucks to the net creating scrambles, but acknowledge the pain of the defeat. They call it a good learning experience about what it takes to win, and express hope that going through difficult experiences as a group has brought them closer together.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese candlestick charting technique imported to the West in the 1990s, popularized by Dan Valcu in 2004, designed to smooth price movements and highlight trends by using averaged values rather than actual prices. The method calculates haClose as the average of open, high, low, and close; haOpen as an exponential moving average of previous haClose; and haHigh/haLow as maximum/minimum of actual prices and haOpen. Because Heikin Ashi uses derived values, it cannot be traded directly and acts as a lagging indicator.

The article presents a profitable trend-following strategy using monthly S&P 500 data from 1960 onward: buy when haClose crosses above haOpen, sell when haClose crosses below haOpen. This strategy yielded a 49.4% win ratio with favorable asymmetric profit/loss distribution. An alternative mean-reversion strategy using ADX filtering with two consecutive red candles showed 5.27% CAGR on S&P 500 but only 5% market exposure, with better results on consumer staples (XLP). The authors note Heikin Ashi works best on longer timeframes and propose customizable parameters to filter noise by adjusting the haOpen calculation period.

On October 22, 2001, Enron Corporation announced that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information regarding certain related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron's stock plunged 21% to $20.65 following the disclosure. The partnerships, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, engaged in transactions with Enron that resulted in a $35 million charge and reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion after Enron repurchased 55 million shares. Multiple shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging breach of fiduciary duty and securities fraud. Enron stated that its board approved the arrangements, which were disclosed in SEC filings, and pledged full cooperation with the SEC inquiry. Analysts expressed concerns about potential costs of dismantling affiliated companies, estimated at up to $3 billion, and possible dilution of common shareholders. The stock had declined 75% year-to-date amid previous concerns about failed investments and the August resignation of CEO Jeff Skilling.

On October 22, 2001, Enron Corp. disclosed that the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow, causing Enron shares to plunge over 20% to $20.65. Fabinho has indicated his desire to leave Monaco, stating "the club knows my will" following Monaco's 4-1 win over Dijon. Trinidad and Tobago won the men's 4x400 metres relay at the 2017 World Athletics Championships in London, ending the United States' streak of six consecutive world titles. Lalonde Gordon overtook Fred Kerley on the final leg to secure Trinidad's first world title in this event with a time of 2:58.12, the fastest of the year. The U.S. took silver and Britain won bronze. Jamaica, Bahamas and Botswana failed to qualify for the final.

FHA loans require lenders to consider both spouses' debts when married couples apply, even if only one spouse is on the mortgage. This joint liability approach differs from conventional loans like Fannie Mae loans. The spouse's debts are factored into the debt-to-income ratio, potentially reducing borrowing power. This requirement applies only to legally married couples, not single or engaged individuals. Married applicants with one spouse having poor credit may benefit from switching to conventional loans, which require only 1.5% more down payment but lack this spousal debt requirement. Unmarried couples aware of a partner's financial issues should consider purchasing before marrying.

A 2013 YouTube video shows actress Allison Mack, recently arrested for alleged involvement in NXIVM sex trafficking, praising JNess, a NXIVM-affiliated women's group. In the video, Mack discusses her desired legacy and names Lena Dunham and Miranda July as personal heroes.

A 16-year-old Iowa girl with severe depression visited a Waterloo salon with matted hair, requesting it be shaved off. Stylist Kayley Olson refused, spending 13 hours over two days untangling and restyling it instead. The teenager, who had stopped brushing her hair due to depression, felt worthless and couldn't face the pain of combing it out. Olson shared the experience on Facebook, which was shared over 75,000 times, to raise awareness about mental health. The girl was pleased with the result and said she would smile for her school pictures.

The Side Screen is a motion offense using continuous "On Ball" side screens that burden defenses through quick-hitting options and full-court ball reversal. Entries include High Post Rub, Dribble Clear, and Pass & Clear. Basic actions feature wing drives over screens with options to turn the corner, pull up, return pass to the post, or kick out to shooters. Continuity involves back cuts, screen-and-roll sequences, and dribble hand-offs. Defensive counters include Post Slips against "Show & Recover," Outside Mismatch and Post Mismatch against switches, and String Out against double teams, creating 2-1-2 alignment with high post and baseline cutting options.

This MIT lecture covers nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, focusing on India and Pakistan as a potential nuclear flashpoint. The professor introduces three lectures on current nuclear issues, emphasizing that nuclear exchange would cause catastrophic destruction and global cooling effects lasting 5-10 years from even limited regional nuclear war.

Vipin Narang, MIT political science professor, discusses nuclear proliferation in South Asia. He explains basic deterrence theory—preserving status quo by threatening unacceptable costs to adversaries—distinguishing between deterrence by punishment (retaliation) versus deterrence by denial (preventing objectives). Nuclear weapons fundamentally altered deterrence by enabling city destruction with minimal risk to the attacker.

Narang details how Pakistan's nuclear program was triggered by its 1971 conventional defeat by India, predating India's 1974 "peaceful nuclear explosion." Pakistan pursued uranium enrichment through AQ Khan, who stole URENCO centrifuge designs, and later received Chinese assistance including HEU and warhead designs. India weaponized its program only after Pakistan's 1987 claims of nuclear capability, testing in May 1998.

The two countries developed opposing doctrines: India adopted assured retaliation with no-first-use policy and civilian control, while Pakistan pursued asymmetric escalation with first-use doctrine and military control, deploying tactical nuclear weapons like the NASR missile to deter Indian conventional superiority.

Narang analyzes three crises—Kargil (1999), the 2001-2002 parliament attack standoff, and Mumbai (2008)—showing how Pakistan's nuclear shield enabled bolder proxy attacks while deterring Indian conventional retaliation, creating strategic instability distinct from Cold War dynamics.

Kieran Trippier called England's penalty shootout victory over Colombia "the best feeling of my career" after converting the team's fourth penalty. The 27-year-old Tottenham wing-back has been a key performer throughout the World Cup and praised the team's spirit and belief. England's win, sealed by Eric Dier's final kick after Jordan Pickford saved Carlos Bacca's attempt, marked only their second success in eight penalty deciders. Dele Alli, who played through injury before being substituted, called Pickford's save "great" and described him as "a phenomenal keeper" and "top-class."

A three-year study of 195 Ugandan health facilities found that smaller, rural, and for-profit health facilities struggle to sustain HIV treatment services despite free antiretrovirals and donor support. Barriers include staff shortages, reporting burdens, and ARV supply issues. Current funding favors large hospitals, while for-profit facilities face misaligned incentives between donor requirements and their business models. Patients also prefer larger hospitals for better services. The study recommends mentoring programs, government service purchase agreements, salary support, and increased government funding to expand treatment coverage beyond established hospitals.

The passage specifies mechanical, visual, and electrical requirements for a socket. Mechanical requirements include: a latch mechanism to lock the lever when closed, support tabs to cradle the lever, actuation/de-actuation force under 3.6 kgf, pin displacement under 1.0 mm during actuation, and durability for 50 cycles. Visual inspection requires 1X magnification, with prohibitions on missing, malformed, damaged, or misaligned solder balls; missing or damaged contacts; missing gold plating on mating surfaces; cracks or flashing on cover and base; damaged or missing securing tabs; gaps between cover and base; and damaged, malformed, or missing lever latches or actuation levers. Electrical requirements include: 1.5 A current rating per contact with under 30°C temperature rise; initial and final low level circuit resistance not exceeding 25 mΩ per contact; mated partial self-inductance under 4 nH; mated-loop inductance and partial-loop inductance matrix of 3 nH ± 10% at 500 MHz and 2 GHz; mated capacitance and capacitance matrix under 1 pF at 500 MHz and 2 GHz; differential impedance of 100 Ω ± 10% with 150 ps rise time if using Time Domain Method; propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus 3 ps measurement error for single-ended and differential signals; crosstalk measurement; minimum 650 Vac dielectric withstanding voltage; and minimum 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

This passage provides an FAQ and overview of corn futures trading, covering contract specifications, trading strategies, and market factors. Corn futures are standardized contracts traded on CME Globex for 5,000 bushels (full) or 1,000 bushels (mini), settled by physical delivery. Trading occurs Sundays to Fridays, 5:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. CT. The all-time high was $8.3125 (2012) and all-time low was $1.007 (1960). Key price drivers include weather, USDA reports, and Chinese demand. Seasonal patterns show stronger performance in January-February and October-December versus summer months. The text describes two backtested seasonal strategies, noting commodities' difficulty and high volatility, with one strategy showing 70% maximum drawdown and another averaging 1.13% per trade over 175 trades. Alternatives include CFDs and the Teucrium Corn Fund (CORN) ETF. Major risks involve adverse price movements and leverage-related losses.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments on October 6 in a case determining whether state "affidavit of merit" statutes for medical malpractice claims apply in federal court. The case involves Harold Berk, a Florida resident who sued a Delaware doctor and hospital in federal court without providing the required doctor's affidavit of negligence that Delaware state law mandates. Under the Erie doctrine, federal courts typically follow state substantive law but federal procedural rules. Lower courts ruled the Delaware statute is "substantive," but Berk argues it conflicts with Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 8 and 9. The defendants counter that the statute creates no direct conflict and serves to limit malpractice litigation costs. A group of civil procedure professors filed an amicus brief arguing that applying state procedural requirements in federal court would cause administrative chaos.

The AIRSS (Ab-initio Random Structure Search) code generates random structures near local minima using chemically informed parameters. MINSEP defines minimum atomic separations between species, while TARGVOL specifies target volume. Constraints are satisfied through two-stage optimization: first removing atomic overlaps, then optimizing lattice and ionic degrees of freedom using a truncated Lennard-Jones model with fixed volume.

President Andrew Jackson addresses Congress regarding South Carolina's nullification ordinance, which declares federal tariff laws void within the state and prohibits their enforcement after February 1, 1833. He describes South Carolina's military preparations, including volunteer enlistments and militia organization, as evidence of hostile intent to obstruct federal revenue collection. Jackson argues that nullification violates the constitutional compact, threatens the Union's integrity, and subverts the supremacy of federal laws. He recommends congressional measures to ensure revenue collection, including relocating custom houses to secure locations, authorizing military protection for federal officers, and enabling removal of state court cases to federal jurisdiction. Jackson asserts that South Carolina has bypassed constitutional remedies and that the federal government must maintain law supremacy while remaining open to modifying tariffs through proper channels.

A player praised an opponent's puck-handling skills and power play effectiveness, noting their ability to find open players and score. He felt his team was too deep in the lanes, needed better positioning, and acknowledged momentum swings throughout the game. He mentioned surprise at a late penalty call, noted his team carried play in the second period but faced a strong push early in the third, and observed that referees were stricter in this game compared to previous ones. He concluded that special teams were the difference, with the opponent's power play proving decisive.

This study reports results from over 18,000 plasma samples from over 15,000 hospitalized patients tested with the Karius Test, a commercially available microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing assay. The test identifies and quantifies mcfDNA from over 1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. Median turnaround time was 26 hours with 96% valid results. Of valid tests, 58% detected at least one microbe, identifying 701 unique taxa. The top 50 taxa accounted for 69% of all detections and included commensal organisms common in immunocompromised patients. The test detected diagnostically challenging pathogens including Legionella, Nocardia, Mycobacterium species, dimorphic fungi, and zoonotic bacteria that are difficult to identify with standard methods. Detection rates were lower than in well-defined clinical use cases, supporting the need for diagnostic stewardship. Limitations included lack of orthogonal testing data and incomplete clinical context. The authors conclude that plasma mcfDNA sequencing enables unbiased, noninvasive pathogen detection with potential to enhance diagnosis of difficult-to-identify infections, particularly in immunocompromised patients, though further studies are needed to optimize clinical utility.

Coach Julien assessed his team's performance in a recent game, acknowledging they battled hard to force overtime but played below their best, citing poor decision-making, subpar puck movement, and defensive coverage issues. He praised specific players including Patrice Bergeron for his consistent two-way play, Johnny Boychuk for his tying goal and defensive reliability, and Jagr for his playmaking. Julien emphasized the importance of staying focused on the present game rather than looking ahead, noted that momentum is irrelevant, and highlighted the value of veteran leadership and players embracing varied roles. He also discussed power play dynamics and the need for smarter decisions against Chicago's shot-blocking defense.

NVIDIA Corporation's Q1 FY2020 10-Q filing for the period ended April 28, 2019, reports revenue of $2.22 billion, down 31% year-over-year, with net income of $394 million ($0.64 per diluted share), down 68% from the prior year. GPU business revenue declined 27% to $2.02 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue fell 55% to $198 million. Gaming revenue dropped 39% to $1.055 billion, Data Center revenue decreased 10% to $634 million, and OEM/Other revenue fell 74% to $99 million due to absence of cryptocurrency mining processor sales. Gross margin was 58.4%, down 610 basis points year-over-year. Operating expenses rose 21% to $938 million. The company held $7.80 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. NVIDIA entered into a $6.9 billion agreement to acquire Mellanox Technologies, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals, with a potential $350 million termination fee. The company plans to return $3.0 billion to shareholders by fiscal year-end, including $97 million in Q1 dividends and $700 million in prior share repurchases. As of April 28, 2019, 609 million shares were outstanding and $7.24 billion remained authorized for future repurchases through December 2022.

This study developed a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combining VGG-16 and Inception v3 to classify thyroid nodules as benign or malignant from ultrasound images. The model was trained on the Thyroid Digital Image Database (TDID), which uses the TI-RADS classification system where TR2/TR3 indicate benign and TR4/TR5 indicate malignant nodules. Due to limited data (68 training images, 8 testing images), image augmentation and early stopping were employed to prevent overfitting, and class weights were applied to address the 4:1 ratio of malignant to benign cases. The model achieved 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929, demonstrating that deep learning can effectively assist in thyroid cancer diagnosis from ultrasound images, potentially reducing reliance on invasive Fine Needle Aspiration procedures. Limitations include the small dataset size; larger clinical datasets could improve model performance.

Rahul Gandhi has been elected unopposed as president of India's Congress party, succeeding his mother Sonia Gandhi. The elevation of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty scion prepares him to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2019 national polls. Gandhi has faced skepticism about his leadership since Congress's heavy 2014 defeat, while Modi remains highly popular despite criticism over slowing economic growth and tax implementation. The announcement coincides with Gujarat state polls that Congress hopes will offer the party a chance at revival.

Hiscox's 2016 DNA of Entrepreneur report surveyed over 4,000 small businesses across six countries, including over 1,000 in the U.S. The study found that flexibility (68%), control (61%), and remote work (57%) motivated American entrepreneurs more than money (37%). Despite prioritizing flexibility, 22% took no vacation. U.S. businesses showed strong performance: 70% reported revenue growth, 68% profit growth, and 73% gained new customers. Top growing sectors included financial services, hospitality, and technology/media/telecom. The U.S. led surveyed countries in hiring optimism, with 23% planning to increase headcount. However, 61% lacked succession plans, and funding challenges persisted—17% found bank financing harder to obtain, with 23% using personal credit cards and others turning to venture capital (11%) or peer-to-peer lending (15%). Only 34% felt government policies supported entrepreneurs, down from 37%, with 31% citing political instability as negative. Oregon's Bend metro ranked first among small business locations, with Business Oregon offering alternative financing programs including direct loans and guarantees.

The passage examines the relationship between rising interest rates and S&P 500 performance through backtesting. While finance theory suggests an inverse relationship between interest rates and stock prices, the correlation has become more positive since the 2000s. A simple trading strategy using the S&P 500 based on whether its SMA is above or below the 10-year yield produced poor compounded returns when investing during rising rates. Conversely, a strategy investing when interest rates are falling showed dramatically improved CAGR with similar drawdowns, though performance was stronger before the 1990s than during the quantitative easing era of the 2000s and 2010s. The conclusion holds that holding stocks when interest rates are falling remains more profitable than buying when rates are rising.

President Barack Obama announced he will deliver a farewell address on January 10, 2017, in Chicago to reflect on his presidency and thank supporters. The speech follows the tradition of George Washington's 1796 farewell address. Obama campaigned for Hillary Clinton and has worked to ensure a smooth transition to successor Donald Trump, who takes office January 20 and has pledged to undo many Obama policies. Obama leaves office without a clear successor as Democratic figurehead.

Apple Watch Series 3 with LTE will launch in Denmark, Sweden, and India on May 4, with deliveries starting a week later. Three will support the device in Denmark and Sweden, while Reliance Jio and Airtel will support it in India. Official pricing remains unannounced.

IFC Films promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Boxer oversees theatrical, non-theatrical, and Canadian distribution for IFC Films, Sundance Selects, and IFC Midnight titles, and previously worked at Artisan Entertainment. Schwartz creates promotional campaigns and previously served as publicity director at Oscilloscope Laboratories. The promotions were announced by co-presidents Jonathan Sehring and Lisa Schwartz. IFC Films recently released "Personal Shopper," "Wakefield," and "Chuck."

Marquez Charter Elementary reopened as a temporary campus nearly nine months after the Palisades fire destroyed most of the school, making it the first public school to return among those damaged by the January fires. The school, which declined from 310 to 130 students, now operates from portable structures with 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library, and play areas. The temporary campus and full rebuild will cost approximately $202.6 million, with completion expected by 2028. Two other affected schools—Palisades Charter Elementary and Palisades Charter High School—will also be rebuilt, with total costs around $600 million funded by a construction bond. Pasadena Unified School District, which saw eight schools affected by the Eaton fire, has installed portable structures at five campuses but lacks a rebuild timeline and faces funding challenges without bond support.

The MMA Manifesto ranks middleweight fighters twice weekly, with Michael Bisping (39 points) ranked first as UFC Middleweight Champion, followed by Luke Rockhold (35 points), Yoel Romero (34 points), and tied Chris Weidman and Ronaldo 'Jacare' Souza (25 points each). Rankings exclude suspended or inactive fighters without scheduled fights. The voting panel includes Jeff Fox, Ryan MacDonald, Ricky Leone, and Daniel Vreeland. Kelvin Gastelum enters at #10, replacing Derek Brunson. Rankings continue through #10 with fighters' records, recent performance, and next fights listed where applicable.

This bibliometric study analyzes 402 articles on open education from the Web of Science database to map key trends and inform policy. Open education encompasses OER, MOOCs, open textbooks, and open-access journals, aiming to democratize education through accessibility and affordability. Despite rapid global expansion, research remains fragmented, with gaps in comprehensive analysis of the entire open education ecosystem.

The study employs co-citation analysis to examine past and current trends and co-word analysis to identify future directions. Co-citation analysis revealed five clusters: evolving open education (transition from OER to OEP), OER's role in education, adoption of open education, educational paradigms of MOOCs, and implementation of OEP. Co-word analysis identified five emerging themes: blended learning in open education, openness in the COVID-19 era, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia.

Key findings show publication growth since 2016, with 3,041 citations and an H-index of 27. The analysis highlights persistent challenges including digital divides (only 10% of sub-Saharan African schools have internet access versus 90% in Western Europe/North America), faculty resistance, and lack of institutional support. Future research should address scalability, quality assurance, sustainability of open practices, and strategies to overcome adoption barriers.

The OHL trading strategy is an intraday approach using open, high, and low price levels in the first minutes of a session to determine trade entries. A buy signal occurs when open equals low, suggesting bullish sentiment; a sell signal occurs when open equals high, indicating bearish sentiment. Backtests on S&P 500 and WTI crude oil showed small average gains (0.04-0.12%), with improved results when today's open exceeded yesterday's close. The strategy works best on 1-5 minute timeframes and can be combined with CPR levels for filtering.

This paper introduces a novel neural solver combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to address three key challenges in applying PINNs to complex, multi-patch computer-aided design (CAD) geometries: enforcing solution continuity across patch interfaces, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and handling geometry parts with significant size and shape variations. The method develops neural network-based ansatz functions operating on IGA reference domains, using pushforward mappings to obtain physical domain solutions. These ansatz functions satisfy Dirichlet boundary conditions through custom output layers, ensure differentiability within patches, and maintain solution continuity across interfaces via interface-specific terms. Training employs the variational PINN framework minimizing discretized energy functionals. The approach is demonstrated on two engineering applications: a 2D magnetostatics quadrupole magnet model and a 3D nonlinear solid mechanics mechanical holder model with hyperelastic material, contact boundary conditions, and parametric dependencies.

Owen Sound Foodland will become one of 87 new Ontario grocery stores authorized to sell beer and cider starting in April, bringing the provincial total to 370 stores. The Foodland, located in Georgian Bluffs, is the first grocery store in the immediate Owen Sound area to receive this authorization. The new 34,000-square-foot store, opening March 22 on the former Towers/Zellers site, will expand fresh food departments, catering, delivery services, and health options while maintaining traditional departments. Employee count will increase from 100 to approximately 160.

ADAPT (Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer) is a coordinate-based Transformer alternative to graph-based MLFFs for predicting per-atom forces and energies in defect computations. Unlike GNNs, ADAPT computes attention over all possible atom interactions without graphs or inductive biases, using tokenized atoms with 12-dimensional feature vectors. Trained on DFT defect data in silicon, ADAPT achieves state-of-the-art performance with training costs two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures, outperforming pretrained universal MLFFs like MACE and MatterSim.

Almost 88% of Ireland's publicly-quoted companies met or beat market earnings expectations recently, according to a Merrion Capital review of 33 companies. Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil, and IFG Group missed expectations. Companies averaged 8% earnings per share growth despite sterling's slump against the euro. The Iseq index hit a 15-month high of 6,750.78 points, 6% above pre-Brexit referendum levels. Irish Continental Group is the top performing stock in the Iseq 10 index this year, with shares up 17% since December. Origin Enterprises, Glanbia, Kerry Group, and FBD are also top performers. Aryzta has fared worst, with shares down 27.2%.

This study examines Turkish parents' experiences with emergency distance education during COVID-19. Following school closures in March 2020, Turkey implemented distance education through platforms like EBA, television broadcasts, and academic support systems. The research surveyed 2,371 parents using quota sampling across Turkey's 12 statistical regions.

Findings show 57.7% of parents viewed distance education positively, primarily for maintaining educational continuity and protecting health, while 42.3% considered it inefficient and inadequate. Parents' main criticisms included system inadequacy (41%), learning difficulties (17.8%), insufficient class time (17.4%), and technical problems (8.6%). Only 13.6% arranged private tutoring for their children. WhatsApp dominated parent-teacher communication (91.1%).

Key parental concerns centered on students' adaptation difficulties, lack of self-discipline, time management problems, and reduced social interaction. Economic inequality emerged as the primary obstacle, with many families lacking adequate internet access, devices, or suitable learning spaces. Parents strongly opposed replacing face-to-face education entirely (86.5% disagreement) but supported using distance education as a supplementary tool.

Recommendations include addressing technological infrastructure gaps, providing economic incentives for disadvantaged families, enriching EBA content, and strengthening digital literacy policies for all citizens.

The Detroit Tigers, currently using a closer by committee approach, are linked to free agent closer Robert Suarez, who is expected to opt out of his contract this offseason. Suarez posted a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, 0.904 WHIP, and 40 saves in 70 appearances this season. Analysts suggest Suarez would be a strong fit to pair with starter Tarik Skubal and provide a definitive closer solution for Detroit.

This is a weekly email from the Haas School of Business at UC Berkeley dated November 2, 2000, listing 17 job openings for Haas alumni. Six of 49 employees will transfer to the council, with remaining staff continuing under the Ministry of Culture. A 2010 amendment already excluded it as a government body. President Tsai Ing-wen made its scrapping a priority in October 2016. The Executive Yuan can order closure before legislative abolition of its authorizing act. DPP Legislator Tsai Yi-yu opposed merging part into the Mainland Affairs Council, fearing it would subordinate Mongolia to China. KMT Legislator Lin Te-fu called it a move toward de jure independence. New Power Party's Hsu Yung-ming urged swift abolition, calling the commission "non-functional."

Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho has urged midfielder Marouane Fellaini to sign a new contract immediately following a knee injury sustained during the Tottenham match. Fellaini, who has rejected a new deal, faces up to two months out and will miss upcoming fixtures including Huddersfield and potentially both Champions League matches against Sevilla. The 30-year-old Belgian has already missed 20 games through injury this season.

Renewable energy generation fluctuates due to natural resource variability, creating grid management challenges as coal plants are phased out. Prof. Mahesh Bandi of OIST used turbulence theory and experimental data to explain wind power fluctuations in a Physical Review Letters paper. While Kolmogorov's 1941 wind speed spectrum was assumed to apply to wind power due to the cubic relationship between power and speed, Bandi showed the spectra match for different reasons: Kolmogorov's work involved spatial measurements, while turbine power is measured temporally. Turbulence consists of nested eddies—large low-frequency eddies containing smaller high-frequency ones. Turbines within the same eddies fluctuate together, and even geographically dispersed plants show correlated low-frequency fluctuations when sharing long time-scale eddies, though high-frequency fluctuations average out. This reveals a natural limit to "geographic smoothing" previously underestimated by scientists. Bandi confirmed this limit using data from 20 Texas wind plants and 224 Irish wind farms. The findings have implications for reserve energy calculations, carbon emissions from backup plants, and optimal regional renewable energy mix policies.

Merger arbitrage is a trading strategy that profits from price differences between a target company's stock price and acquisition offer price during mergers. The strategy involves buying target company shares at market price, anticipating convergence with the offer price upon deal completion.

Backtesting results show mixed profitability. The IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF (since 2010) returned 2.73% CAGR versus 18.52% for the S&P 500, with roughly half the volatility (7.83 vs. 17.27). The Merger Fund (since 2013) returned 4.46% CAGR versus 17.37% for the S&P 500, with significantly lower volatility (3.81 vs. 17.29).

A Verdad Research study of 835 deals (2000-2020) found an 89% success rate for deal closures, with successful deals averaging 2.0% returns and failed deals losing 2.8%, producing a blended 1.5% average return. The study used a quantitative approach: long positions in targets five days post-announcement, with short positions in stock-paying acquirers.

Merger arbitrage is market-neutral with lower volatility than broader markets, but requires careful deal analysis, regulatory assessment, and risk management. Success demands understanding deal terms, monitoring progress, and reacting swiftly to new information.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO) exhibit color-neutral photochromism under ambient conditions, losing ~50% transmittance without pronounced absorption bands, making them promising for smart windows. REHO films are typically produced via magnetron sputtering, with photochromism being a bulk effect that strengthens with film thickness and shorter illumination wavelengths. While earlier models proposed single-phase oxyhydride structures, recent evidence shows multiphase composition with O-rich and H-rich regions, where hydrogen migration drives photochromism.

This study investigates photodarkening kinetics in YHO films using optical transmittance measurements. The time-dependent transmittance shows non-trivial behavior that cannot be described by simple zero-, first-, or second-order reaction kinetics. EELS analysis reveals higher free hydrogen concentration in photochromic films (plasmon peak at 14.4 eV) compared to opaque films (15.9 eV), suggesting mobile hydrogen facilitates the effect.

A two-phase exponential decay model successfully fits the data: a fast initial decay (k₁=0.016 s⁻¹, 2-3 minutes) attributed to local structural changes or loosely bound hydrogen loss, and a slow decay (k₂=0.001 s⁻¹) attributed to hydrogen migration/diffusion and associated lattice contraction. This model provides excellent fitting quality and enables straightforward comparison of photochromic film performance for device optimization.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 26, 2022, reporting its financial results for the quarter and year ended December 31, 2021. The company released its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update on its website, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

The federal government shut down at midnight Wednesday after Congress failed to pass a funding extension. Most education programs will continue uninterrupted in the short term, with Title I and special education funds available as expected. However, districts relying on Impact Aid near military installations or national parks could face cash flow problems, affecting roughly 1,100 districts serving eight million students. A prolonged shutdown could impact Head Start and school nutrition programs. The Trump administration, which seeks to downsize government, has directed agencies to consider additional mass layoffs. Head Start grantees serving 6,500 children expect funding Wednesday, with more at risk November 1 if the shutdown continues. School nutrition programs have federal reimbursements for September and October, and SNAP benefits should continue for at least a week. Civil rights investigations and regulatory work at the Education Department would halt, and states and districts cannot reach staff with questions about grants or programs.

Chicago wheat prices rose 0.9% to $4.54-3/4 a bushel on Tuesday, recovering partially from a 7.8% three-day decline, the largest since April 2013. Corn increased 0.1% to $3.75-1/2 a bushel, ending a four-session losing streak, while soybeans gained 0.2% to $10.25 a bushel. The gains followed beneficial rain and snow in the drought-stricken southern U.S. Plains, which aids hard red winter wheat emerging from dormancy. U.S. Department of Agriculture data showed Kansas winter wheat ratings declined to 11% good-to-excellent condition. Most Ukrainian winter grain crops remain in good or satisfactory condition. Australia offered the lowest wheat price at $306/tonne in Iraq's tender. CME Group's new Black Sea grain futures show active trading. Oil prices slipped Monday amid Wall Street declines and supply concerns, while Asian shares fell Tuesday due to technology stock selloffs.

William Asa Hutchinson III, son of Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson, was arrested on charges of driving while intoxicated, speeding and violation of implied consent. The 42-year-old was booked into Washington County jail early Monday and released on $1,626 bond. He is scheduled to appear in West Fork District Court Wednesday, with another hearing set for July 19. The arrest came less than a year after a judge dismissed a previous DWI conviction against him due to citation errors. Hutchinson was also arrested in May 2016 in Alabama on drug possession charges and received a pretrial diversion.

U.S. billionaire investor Paul Kazarian, owner of Japonica Partners and a major Greek bond holder, has opened his first European office in Lisbon, citing Portugal's corporate sector as ripe for investment. Kazarian praised Socialist governments in both Portugal and Greece for their recovery policies following the euro zone debt crisis, noting Portugal's strong growth since exiting its bailout in 2014. He expressed surprise at their outperformance of prior administrations despite lacking business backgrounds. Japonica, which became a large Greek debt holder in 2013, is now exploring Portuguese investment opportunities in real estate and technology, with Kazarian seeing potential to help companies expand globally beyond Portuguese-speaking markets. The Lisbon office will also examine broader European investments.

This study examines degradation mechanisms in commercial NMC/graphite lithium-ion batteries cycled at high C-rates (1C–3C) using Nuclear Reaction Analysis (Li-NRA) combined with XRD, SEM, and EDS. High C-rate cycling accelerates capacity fade and increases internal resistance, with 3C cycling causing ~60% capacity loss and 0.34 Ω resistance. Structural analysis reveals c-axis lattice contraction in the cathode (14.27878 Å to 14.27442 Å) and interlayer expansion in the graphite anode (6.71906 Å to 6.72132 Å). Li-NRA quantifies lithium distribution, showing 19.7% lithium loss in the cathode and 115.96% lithium increase in the anode due to plating and SEI formation. The non-destructive Li-NRA technique enables direct measurement of mobile lithium with depth resolution, providing critical insights into lithium inventory loss and electrode degradation under high-stress cycling conditions.

The Education Department announced it will rewrite two Obama-era student loan forgiveness rules: Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment. Secretary DeVos called the regulations "overly burdensome and confusing," while critics warned the changes would harm students and taxpayers. Eight states and D.C. filed a motion to retain the rules. The department will hold hearings in July and fulfill nearly 16,000 pending claims under current rules.

Nigeria's T-bills market traded bullish with demand focused on shorter maturities, as system liquidity remained buoyant from N300bn bond maturity inflows. The CBN raised N49.60bn at its May 30 PMA, which was over-subscribed at N103.40bn, mainly from non-competitive bidders. OBB and OVN rates fell to 1.75% and 2.50% respectively as liquidity rose to approximately N600bn positive. The interbank rate held stable at N305.95/$, while CBN external reserves declined to $47.65bn. The I&E FX Window rate depreciated to N362.02/$, a 10-month high, though cash and transfer rates rose to N362.50/$ and N366.00/$ following CBN retail interventions. Sovereign bonds declined, with the 2047s down approximately 1.30 points to 99.70.

Kawann "KK" Short's nickname comes from his first name plus an extra K due to his size. The Panthers signed him to a five-year, $80 million deal, ending year-long negotiations. This reflects GM Dave Gettleman's "hog mollies" philosophy and represents a penultimate major offseason move for a franchise seeking its first championship for its 80-year-old owner. Gettleman rejects "championship windows," emphasizing winning now. Other win-now moves include signing Julius Peppers, adding 36-year-old safety Mike Adams, re-signing Captain Munnerlyn, and giving Matt Kalil a $55 million deal. The defense's projected starters average 29.45 years old. Concerns remain about Cam Newton's health after shoulder surgery and multiple recent injuries; the offense will "evolve" with less zone-read. The Panthers let Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown leave, replacing them with Russell Shepard and Charles Johnson. With Short signed, Carolina should draft an offensive playmaker at No. 8, targeting Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey, or O.J. Howard.

The annual Battle of Alberta chess tournament will be held at the University of Calgary on February 18–19, 2017, hosted by the U of C Chess Club. Between 30 and 40 players from across the province will compete, including 6 to 8 from the U of C. The tournament follows World Chess Federation rules. The U of C Chess Club, founded in 2015 by Riley Workman and Chinmoy Ayachit, holds weekly meet-ups open to all skill levels. Registration is $10 for students and $15 for non-students.

This patent application describes systems and methods utilizing cache coherent switch on chip technology with Compute Express Link (CXL) protocol. The cache coherent switch on chip enables low-latency memory access, coherent caching between devices, and resource sharing without CPU bottlenecks. It supports multi-host access, component disaggregation, and server composability through CXL-connected resources including accelerators, memory, storage, and networking components. The system includes fabric managers for resource allocation, virtual hierarchies for cache prioritization, and bridges for legacy device support. It enables memory pooling across servers, cache coherency resolution within the switch, and CXL-over-Ethernet communication for distributed resource sharing. The technology incorporates compression, security, erasure coding, and prefetching capabilities, with configurable frame formats and software stacks for various network protocols.

Sugar futures are derivative contracts traded on ICE and CME exchanges, representing agreements to deliver or receive 112,000 pounds of sugar at a future date. ICE contracts (symbol SB) settle via physical delivery, while CME contracts (symbol YO) are financially settled. Trading hours differ by exchange, with both using March, May, July, and October contract cycles. Minimum price fluctuation is 0.0001 per pound ($11.20 per contract). Sugar prices are influenced by government subsidies, tariffs, ethanol demand, oil prices, Brazilian currency, and weather. Seasonality shows stronger performance in February, June, July, November, and December. The all-time high was 66.00 cents/pound (November 1974) and all-time low was 2.63 cents/pound (June 1985). Trading requires a futures broker; CFD alternatives exist for speculation without delivery concerns. Major risks include adverse price movements amplified by leverage. Backtesting of trend-following strategies on sugar showed limited success, with commodities generally considered difficult to trade.

Prime Day offers mixed value for MacBook buyers. The 13-inch M4 MacBook Air at $800 (down $200) is the best deal, with 16 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. The M5 MacBook Air is rumored but likely not worth waiting for, as Apple typically discontinues older models. The five-year-old M1 MacBook Air at $600 remains a solid budget option, though a new entry-level MacBook may replace it. MacBook Pro discounts are weaker at 10% off, and with M5 models potentially launching soon, waiting may be prudent for power users seeking maximum performance.

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case involving William Case, a Montana man shot by police after they entered his home without a warrant in 2021. Case's former girlfriend had reported he threatened suicide and harm to officers. Police saw a suspected suicide note and empty holster through a window before entering; an officer shot Case after mistaking an object at his waist for a gun. Case argued evidence from the warrantless entry should be suppressed, but state courts held warrantless entry is permissible when reasonable and non-investigatory. The justices appeared skeptical of Case's proposed "probable cause" standard for emergency entries, with several questioning applying criminal investigation standards to welfare checks. Most justices seemed inclined to adopt or affirm an "objectively reasonable basis" standard for believing someone needs emergency help, though they debated whether to remand the case to state court or apply the standard themselves. A decision is expected by June or July.

Kano Pillars drew 1-1 with Niger Tornadoes in a rescheduled 2017/2018 Nigeria Professional Football League week 12 match at Sani Abacha Stadium. Andrew Ikefe scored for Tornadoes in the 19th minute, while Junior Lokosa converted a penalty in the 81st minute for Pillars, bringing his season tally to 11 goals.
