The Kiss of Death is a sell signal for the S&P 500 that triggers when the index drops from an all-time high, falls below its monthly 21-EMA, bounces back above it, then drops below its recent low. Historically rare, it occurred in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008, preceding major bear markets, though the September 2022 signal proved false. A backtest from 1967 using trading rules of selling on the signal and buying when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA showed improved performance over buy-and-hold, with higher CAGR and roughly halved maximum drawdown, despite occasional false signals.

Fair Isaac, creator of the FICO score, unveiled a new pricing model allowing mortgage lenders to bypass credit bureaus and obtain credit scores directly from the company. The announcement caused Fair Isaac's stock to surge more than 20%, its largest increase since November 2022. Shares of credit bureaus Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax fell 4-10% as investors anticipated reduced roles for these agencies. The new model offers lenders choice between two pricing options and eliminates credit bureau mark-ups on FICO scores. Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte praised the move as a "creative solution" to help consumers, while encouraging credit bureaus to take similar competitive actions.

MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs operating up to 32MHz, with 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, and supply voltages from 1.62V to 3.6V. Features include a high-speed internal oscillator, 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, 12-bit ADC, comparator, temperature sensor, multiple timers, and communication peripherals supporting UART, SPI, I2C, LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus, and PMBus protocols. The MSPM0 family enables customers to select devices matching their analog and digital integration needs while reducing energy consumption.

Pekkala assured the author that most Finnish people supported the democracies and that conviction was growing for Finland to make separate peace with the Soviet Union, views shared by Mannerheim, the Social Democratic Party, Swedish Party, and Progressives, though not the Agrarian Party. The author planned to meet Foreign Minister Witting to discuss concerns about Finland's relations with the US and potential withdrawal from the war. Witting received the memorandum but noted Finland's 93% dependence on German imports, compared Finland's position to Iceland's regarding Allied troops, and showed little willingness to break from Germany due to fear of starvation. Meanwhile, the Minister in Sweden reported Finland's military situation was deteriorating rapidly, warning that continued Russian offensives could lead to Swedish internal political crisis, potential German collaboration, and government endangerment. Soviet Minister Kollontay privately expressed concern about Swedish reaction to Russian advances and believed only a simple cessation of fighting could bring peace.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 11, 2016, correcting an immaterial error in its 2015 Annual Report on Form 10-K that overstated the net book value of the Supercharger network. The correct net book value as of December 31, 2015 was $166.6 million. The error was limited to Item 7 and did not impact the consolidated financial statements.

Scientists have developed a molecular sensor that releases a thyme-like flavor when it detects influenza virus, potentially enabling at-home flu screening through chewing gum or lozenges before symptoms appear. The sensor uses a neuraminidase substrate with attached thymol molecules that viruses release, producing a detectable taste. Lab tests showed thymol release within 30 minutes in saliva from flu-infected individuals, with no cellular harm. Human clinical trials are planned for approximately two years. The technology, patented with the European Patent Office, was funded by the Federal Ministry of Research and Education.

Four candidates for Baltimore County executive—Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin, Johnny Olszewski Jr., and Al Redmer Jr.—addressed real estate professionals, pledging to encourage smart growth and improve development approvals. None supported impact fees, with Brochin suggesting school capacity limits instead and others citing existing development or timing concerns. All criticized the cumbersome approval process, with some open to waiving certain requirements. On rezoning, candidates called for more predictability and consistency with the master plan, with differing views on decision-making authority. While most candidates emphasized partnership with developers, Brochin repeated his pledge to "end pay-to-play politics." The forum was the first of several scheduled events before the June 26 primary to succeed County Executive Kevin Kamenetz.

Nominations are open for the 12th Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards, with a deadline of noon on March 13. The black-tie ceremony will be held on April 27 at the Royal Hall, a restored Edwardian theatre, marking the venue's first time hosting the event. There are 10 award categories spanning rural businesses, tourism, family-run businesses, employers, company sizes, websites, and individual honors. Main sponsor is Verity Frearson estate agents. Previous winner Zara Jackson of Network Scientific noted the award boosted her business's credibility and recruitment.

Former tenured professor Robert Oscar Lopez, who resigned from California State University, Northridge after opposing same-sex adoption, now argues academic freedom is neither a virtue nor a reality. He claims tenure protects only select faculty with favorable views while leaving adjuncts vulnerable, and describes higher education as a "diabolical machine" producing dysfunctional citizens through inflated tuition and ideological indoctrination. The author agrees academic freedom is impossible in practice, citing inconsistent application against conservatives versus leftists, and advocates cutting college funding while promoting trade schools and apprenticeships. The proposed alternative governing principle for education is whether teachings represent Truth or lies.

The first trading day of the month effect refers to the S&P 500's tendency to perform significantly better on the first trading day of each month compared to other days, with an average gain of 0.24% versus 0.04% on average days. While the basic strategy is too unstable to trade profitably, especially post-2008, improved versions using filters have shown better results: one version yields 0.35% average gain per trade with 3% CAGR since 1993, while another buying on the close of the first trading day averages 1.1% per trade. The effect is likely caused by capital inflows from savers, pension funds, and automatic 401(k) contributions. February and July show the strongest first-day performance.

This passage introduces bilateral trade as an economic model where a seller and buyer with private valuations trade a good, focusing on a broker's profit maximization problem under dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality constraints. Unlike prior work on efficiency maximization, this study examines profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade through online learning, with the goal of minimizing regret against the best mechanism in hindsight.

The authors present two key results: First, for the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated valuations, they provide a polynomial-time algorithm achieving Õ(√T) regret, which is nearly tight given their Ω(√T) lower bound. Second, for the adversarial setting, they prove that no learning algorithm can achieve sublinear regret against even a 2/3+ε fraction of optimal profit, establishing a separation between stochastic and adversarial models. They also apply their techniques to reduce regret for the joint ads problem from O(T^(3/4)) to Õ(√T).

The analysis faces challenges from the non-parametric action space and irregular profit functions, requiring novel approaches beyond standard discretization methods.

The passage describes multiple views of a cooling fan design: front and top perspective, rear and bottom perspective, front elevation, rear elevation, left and right side elevations, top and bottom plan views, and an alternative position perspective view. Broken lines indicate portions not part of the claimed design.

Mediation analysis examines how interventions affect outcomes through mediator variables, with structural equation modeling (SEM) serving as the standard approach for latent mediators. However, SEM requires the unrealistic assumption of no unmeasured confounding. Rank-preserving models (RPMs) offer a robust alternative by allowing omitted covariates that don't interact with treatment or mediator, but they haven't been extended to latent variables. The authors introduce Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), which integrates RPM with factor score regression to enable robust mediation analysis with measurement error and omitted confounders. RAPSEM estimates controlled direct effects and controlled mediation effects within a potential outcomes framework, modeling all variables except treatment as latent factors with a measurement model and structural model.

The speaker discusses their team's confidence during a playoff game, noting they felt comfortable and eventually capitalized on their chances. They express happiness for their goalie, who had been through a difficult year, and emphasize his experience and maturity. The team has created another opportunity for themselves, similar to their previous series against San Jose. The speaker highlights the team's growth together, mentioning players like Ryan, Gator, Georges, and Stevie, and praises a key player as the face of the organization who works extremely hard and serves as an example for younger players. They describe his incredible skill level and ability to win games despite playing hurt. The speaker analyzes the opponent's power play strategy, noting they pressure hard and have active sticks, but expresses confidence in their own power play personnel. They joke about Ryan Smyth's unorthodox scoring ability, praising his work ethic and competitiveness. The team's solid game plan and coaching adjustments throughout the playoffs are credited for their success, including a more structured approach to shorthanded situations. They mention handling adversity after a controversial non-goal, maintaining focus and refocusing quickly. The speaker believes they haven't played their best yet and that raising their level slightly will allow them to take over the series. They conclude by noting the special tradition of playing for their team and the desire to have their names alongside past greats from the 1980s.

A player reflects on their team's success, attributing it to having fun while working hard. They praise a fearless teammate who blocks shots despite injury risk and leads by example through consistent effort. They note the shift from rest to playoff excitement with media presence. They also agree that a smooth, non-flashy defenseman deserves recognition as a top player.

A cross-sectional study in Denan district, southeastern Ethiopia found 9.63% sero-prevalence of visceral leishmaniasis (VL) among 187 asymptomatic pastoralists. Risk factors included age 19-36, damp floors, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelters. Only 53% had heard of VL, 42% knew sand flies transmit it, and 36% believed it preventable. Twelve sand fly species were identified, with P. orientalis (11.4% of captures) as the probable VL vector. Most sand flies were captured from termite mounds and forest habitats. Poor knowledge and outdoor sleeping practices pose significant challenges for VL control in this new endemic focus.

This study investigates whether transformers can learn to infer transitive relations from training examples, equivalent to learning connectivity in directed graphs. The authors hypothesize that transformers more easily learn connectivity on low-dimensional grid graphs (where nodes embed into R^k such that path existence is determined by non-negative embedding differences) compared to disconnected chain graphs (which lack such simple embeddings).

Experiments show transformers achieve near-perfect accuracy on grid graphs but struggle to generalize on disconnected chain graphs. Scaling model size improves performance for grid graphs but not for disconnected chain graphs. Scaling graph size maintains consistent performance for grid graphs while improving performance for larger disconnected chain graphs with fixed chain counts. Higher-dimensional grid graphs show degraded performance, though increasing nodes helps more than increasing model size. Similarly, more chains in disconnected graphs hurt performance, with graph scaling benefiting more than model scaling.

The key finding is that data scaling benefits transformers more than model scaling for complex graph structures (higher-dimensional grids or many-chain disconnected graphs), while transformers excel at learning low-dimensional embeddings that enable connectivity inference.

Hawkin's Bazaar, a gift and gadget shop on New George Street in Plymouth, will close permanently on February 4 after four years at that location. The store is holding a closing down sale with discounts of 50-75 percent. The business previously operated in the West End for six years. The Plymouth Herald contacted the company for comment but received no response.

Cincinnati handed No. 14 Iowa State its first loss of the season, winning 31-23 with a 17-point first quarter and recovering a late onside kick to seal the victory. The Bearcats (4-1, 2-0 Big 12) earned their first home win against a ranked opponent since December 2021, while Iowa State (5-1, 2-1) rallied from a 31-7 deficit but fell short. Iowa State was missing 16 injured players, including key defensive backs and their top two kickers.

In State v. Roy Allen Whisnant (1967), the North Carolina Supreme Court granted a new trial after finding that the trial court erred by forcing the defendant to trial the day after he changed his plea from guilty to not guilty. The indigent defendant, charged with assault with a deadly weapon, had requested continuances to obtain witnesses from West Virginia and Florida and to allow his court-appointed counsel time to prepare, but both requests were denied. The court held that the defendant was not given reasonable time to prepare his defense, violating his right to present his case fairly. The court also noted that jurors who had heard his guilty plea were likely prejudiced when he was tried the next day.

MADSEN Cycles manufactures bucket bikes designed to carry up to four children plus cargo, featuring a large rear bucket with removable bench seats and seat belts. The company offers numerous accessories including rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and middle bucket seats to enhance comfort, security, and functionality. Based in Utah, MADSEN Cycles produces brightly colored, customized bicycles aimed at helping families ride together in style.

Jerome "Jay" Powell becomes Federal Reserve chair on Monday, succeeding Janet Yellen. Powell, a Republican former investment banker and likely the wealthiest Fed chair ever, takes over during a period of economic stability following a decade of turmoil. His main challenge will be calibrating interest rate increases as the US economy experiences late-cycle growth, synchronized global expansion, and new fiscal stimulus from corporate tax reform. Yellen leaves with unemployment at a 17-year low of 4.1 percent, quiet inflation, and nearly four years of uninterrupted growth, having gradually raised rates five times. The Fed indicated three more hikes are likely in 2018, though policymakers debated the pace due to uncertain inflation and tax cut impacts. Powell's first press conference and expected rate increase will occur in March. Economists note that combining massive fiscal policy with solid growth and limited labor availability is unprecedented, creating uncertainty about wage and price inflation.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on October 7 in Barrett's case, which applies double jeopardy principles to federal firearm offenses under Sections 924(c) and 924(j). Barrett was convicted in 2013 for his role in an armed robbery where a victim was shot to death. Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm to advance a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense, while Section 924(j) applies when such use causes death. The central question is whether Section 924(j) creates a separate crime with separate punishment from Section 924(c). The Court will use the Blockburger test, which compares whether each offense requires proof of a fact the other does not. While the government and Barrett agree separate sentences are not permitted for the same conduct, the Court appointed amicus John Bash to defend the Second Circuit's judgment allowing separate convictions and sentences. The case will determine whether Congress clearly intended to authorize separate punishments under both provisions.

Formative assessment in vocational education requires active teacher-student participation, immediate feedback, and self-evaluation, though it demands additional teacher preparation. Competence-based education connects classroom learning to workplace skills, emphasizing performance standards over academic testing. Authentic assessment prioritizes workplace-relevant contexts over reliability, using tools like rubrics and professional development to ensure consistency. A comprehensive assessment program must address all levels of vocational knowledge through varied methods including written tests, technical skills assessments, and workplace evaluations. Effective VET assessment balances theoretical knowledge with practical competence to prepare students for professional success.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to Reisdorf Brothers, Inc. on Patrick and Linda George's Clean Water Act (CWA) and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) claims, and its dismissal of state law claims without prejudice. The court held the Georges failed to raise triable issues of fact regarding ongoing or intermittent pollutant discharges required for CWA liability, as their evidence showed only a single discrete incident or was speculative. For RCRA, the plaintiffs failed to allege or prove violations of relevant regulations defining "open dump." The court also affirmed the district court's refusal to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over state law claims and its denial of attorney's fees to Reisdorf, finding no abuse of discretion as the plaintiffs' claims had some arguable basis and were litigated in good faith.

This study used multi-state modeling of longitudinal data from the PREVEND cohort to examine age- and sex-specific transitions between KDIGO kidney disease risk stages and their association with new-onset heart failure. Among 8,569 participants followed for a median 12.6 years, forward transition rates between risk stages increased exponentially with age and were higher in men than women, while women had higher backward transition rates from intermediate to low risk stage. Kidney disease progression was rapid, with progression to intermediate risk occurring mostly between ages 60-70 and to high/very high risk after age 70. Higher KDIGO risk stages were associated with increased heart failure risk, with relative risks attenuating with age (e.g., high/very high vs. low risk: RR 6.1 at age 60 to 2.0 at age 80) but absolute rate differences increasing with age. The study found substantial misclassification of risk stages when using creatinine-based eGFR, with lower misclassification rates using cystatin C-based eGFR. The authors conclude that slowing KDIGO risk stage progression may reduce heart failure incidence in middle-aged populations.

The Pittsburgh Penguins defeated the Washington Capitals 7-4 on Friday night, extending their winning streak to four games. Phil Kessel scored twice with an assist, while Evgeni Malkin added two goals and two assists. Sidney Crosby extended his scoring streak to 11 games with two assists. The Penguins pulled within four points of first-place Washington in the Metropolitan Division. Alex Ovechkin scored twice for Washington, reaching 32 goals for the season. Pittsburgh went 3 for 4 on the power play, while Washington went 0 for 3. The Capitals host Las Vegas next, while the Penguins play at New Jersey.

The passage discusses methods to access Australian financial markets for portfolio diversification, including ETFs, ADRs, direct stock purchases through international brokers, and CFDs. It focuses on backtested trading strategies using the EWA ETF as a proxy for Australian stocks, finding that mean reversion strategies perform poorly due to Australia's commodity exposure, while seasonal strategies like the Santa Claus effect show 92% win rates since 1996. The ASX is Australia's primary exchange, open 10am-4pm AEDT (11pm-5am GMT). US investors can access Australian markets through various ETFs including EWA for equities and FXA for currency exposure.

This study developed a valid and reliable scale to measure prospective teachers' attitudes toward values education through distance education. Following DeVellis's (2017) scale development steps, researchers created a 36-item instrument with two factors: "Necessity and Usefulness" (21 items) and "Feasibility" (15 items). Data from 341 prospective teachers at Gazi University underwent exploratory factor analysis, revealing the two-factor structure explained 63.286% of total variance. The scale demonstrated high reliability, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients of .969 for Factor 1 and .961 for Factor 2. However, Tukey's Test for Nonadditivity indicated the scale lacks additivity, requiring separate evaluation of each factor rather than a total score. Item-total correlations ranged from .656 to .841, and all items showed significant discriminative power. The study addresses a gap in literature, as no prior scales examined attitudes specifically toward values education through distance education. Limitations include gender imbalance (77.3% female participants) and single-university sampling, suggesting need for confirmatory factor analysis with broader populations.

Sandeep Kohli forwarded news articles from Indian press dated April 27, 2001 to Stinson Gibner and Vince Kaminski regarding the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) crisis. The DPC board authorized managing director Neil McGregor and Enron India MD K Wade Cline to issue a termination notice to Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) for the power purchase agreement, passed 6-1 with IDBI opposing. International lenders supported termination while domestic lenders led by IDBI opposed it. MSEB paid Rs 134 crore under protest toward March bills. The Centre's potential liability if terminated was estimated at Rs 2,840 crore including one year's electricity bill and $300 million termination fee. Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh expressed dismay, stating the state wanted renegotiation not termination, and planned to form a committee to renegotiate the agreement.

Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock purchased 1,000 tracer rounds before the October 1, 2017 massacre that killed 58 people and injured nearly 500. The .308-caliber and .223-caliber tracer ammunition was bought from a private seller at a Phoenix gun show. It remains unclear whether Paddock used the illuminated bullets, which help shooters track bullet paths in darkness but can reveal their position. His extensive preparations included reserving an upper-floor room overlooking the Route 91 Harvest music festival, stockpiling 23 firearms (12 modified for automatic fire), and installing surveillance cameras. Authorities also discovered he had booked rooms overlooking Chicago's Lollapalooza festival in August and Las Vegas's Life Is Beautiful festival in September. Investigators found 1,600 rounds of ammunition, fertilizer, and 50 pounds of Tannerite explosive material in his car, and are examining whether he planned additional attacks including a possible car bombing. Paddock's girlfriend told FBI agents she observed no warning signs of violence; he had sent her to the Philippines before the attack. The 64-year-old died by suicide as police approached his Mandalay Bay hotel room.

Defending talented post players requires team-based strategies including active hands from the passer defender, helpside support, and post traps. Individual techniques involve beating the post to the block, pushing off the block when behind, and front guarding with backside support. Influencing the ball away from the post's preferred side limits their effectiveness. Additional disruptions include full-court pressing to extend the court, using a 2-3 zone with adjustments for double/triple teams, and employing a Diamond & One combination defense with a chaser fronting the post.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Q2 2017 Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended June 30, 2017. The company reported consolidated net sales of $37.955 billion (up 25% year-over-year) and net income of $197 million for Q2 2017, compared to $857 million in Q2 2016. Operating income decreased to $628 million from $1.285 billion in the prior year period. For the six months ended June 30, 2017, net sales were $73.669 billion with net income of $921 million.

The company operates three segments: North America (59% of sales), International (30%), and AWS (11%). AWS showed strong growth with 42% year-over-year sales increase to $4.1 billion in Q2, generating $916 million in operating income. International segment reported an operating loss of $724 million in Q2 2017, widening from $135 million in Q2 2016.

Key financial position items as of June 30, 2017: total assets of $87.781 billion, cash and cash equivalents of $13.203 billion, total long-term debt of $7.769 billion face value, and stockholders' equity of $23.214 billion. Cash provided by operating activities was $3.829 billion in Q2 2017.

Significant commitments include $13.7 billion agreement to acquire Whole Foods Market, Inc., to be funded with debt financing and cash on hand. The company also faces various tax contingencies and legal proceedings, including a $600 million valuation allowance recorded against deferred tax assets in Luxembourg and ongoing IRS and European Commission tax examinations.

Justice Babatunde Quadri of the Federal High Court, Abuja admitted EFCC documents as evidence on March 30, 2018 against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, charged with concealing $300,000 while attempting to fly to Dubai. The offence violates Section 2 (3) (5) of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, 2011, which requires declaring cash over $10,000 to Nigerian Customs. EFCC counsel P. K. Latona presented witness Hassan Mohammed Misau, an AFF detective, who testified that Nigerian Customs arrested Li at Nnamdi Azikwe International Airport on March 15, 2018. Misau stated EFCC investigators received handover notes, customs statements, boarding passes, passport, mobile phone, and the $300,000, with the defendant transferred to EFCC custody on March 16, 2018.

Live updates from a Texas high school football game between Aledo Bearcats and Ryan Raiders in Denton, Texas. Aledo leads 2-0 after Ryan was called for intentional grounding in their own end zone, resulting in a safety. Aledo is ranked in The Sporting News High School Football Top 25 and No. 16 in Massey Ratings. Ryan is unranked but could enter rankings with a win. The article also promotes The Sporting News Preseason All-American Teams and includes author Kendall Webb's credentials.

Elizabeth C. Charles, Ph.D., identifies sources for documenting U.S.-Soviet foreign relations from January 1983 to March 1985. Key sources include White House Staff and Office Files at the Reagan Library, particularly Executive Secretariat files containing NSC and NSPG meeting files, NSDDs, and files of national security advisors. Department of State records include multiple Executive Secretariat S/S Lot Files and collections from officials like Lawrence Eagleburger and Kenneth Dam. The Central Foreign Policy File contains embassy cable traffic. The passage also provides a historical note on U.S. covert actions, tracing their management from the Truman presidency, beginning with NSC 4–A in December 1947, which authorized CIA peacetime covert operations, followed by NSC 10/2 in June 1948, which expanded these to broader "covert" operations with defined secrecy parameters.

Children of obese parents have doubled obesity risk by age two, with both maternal and paternal BMI influencing offspring weight through distinct biological mechanisms. Egg and sperm carry non-coding RNAs and mitochondrial factors that respond to parental nutrition and shape embryonic metabolism. Obese mothers have defective egg mitochondria that alter offspring energy metabolism, while obese fathers show altered sperm non-coding RNAs linked to offspring fatness. However, embryos are adaptable: lifestyle interventions like exercise and improved nutrition can restore egg and sperm quality in mice, and similar effects are expected in humans. Research supports pre-conception health interventions for both parents to reduce community obesity rates.

VentureWire, dated October 19, 2000, reports private company business news including major venture capital fund closings: St. Paul Venture Capital's $1.3 billion sixth fund, Constellation Ventures' $350 million second fund, and New Edge Networks' $140 million third round. Idealab! postponed its IPO citing market volatility. The issue details numerous funding rounds for technology firms including Alopa Networks ($15.1 million), Egenera ($20 million), Propel ($38.3 million), and Revit Technology ($30 million). Other sections cover new product launches, M&A activity including NetObjects' $51 million acquisition of MyComputer, new board appointments, personnel changes, and upcoming industry events.

This manual provides troubleshooting for SanDisk MP3 players, including issues with unplayable files (likely due to DRM restrictions), firmware updates, CD ripping, file conversion, MTP/MSC transfer modes, podcast compatibility, and missing ID3 tags. It also covers technical support contact information, a 1-year limited warranty with repair/replacement/refund options, software license terms restricting modification and reverse engineering, and disposal instructions requiring proper electronic waste handling.

The speaker notes that Ozzie played well and made great saves, though the opposing team had more scoring chances than their low shot total suggested. After taking the lead, the speaker's team didn't play as well in the second period, allowing the opposition to gain momentum and carry the play. The first game of the series involved a feeling-out process typical when playing teams from other conferences, with action picking up in the second period.

Novo Nordisk announced it will acquire Akero Therapeutics, developer of a MASH liver disease drug, for up to $5.2 billion. Other biotech news includes: Amgen's cholesterol shot prevented heart problems in a broad population; Colorado set a first-in-the-nation payment limit on an Amgen drug; former FDA vaccine regulator Peter Marks joined Eli Lilly; Expedition Therapeutics raised $165 million; and a billionaire-backed VC firm launched led by a former Flagship associate.

Football has become offense-driven, with accurate passing leading to success at college and professional levels. Cornerbacks are crucial defensive players whose primary job is covering wide receivers in man or zone coverage. In man coverage, they mirror receivers' routes in one-on-one situations, starting at a disadvantage since receivers know their routes while cornerbacks must react. The position is named for protecting the outside "corners" of the field near boundaries. Cornerbacks are part of the defensive backs unit, with teams typically fielding two and sometimes three in nickel packages. Great cornerbacks are called "lockdown corners." Required skills include speed, agility, and the ability to transition from backpedaling to sprinting while tracking receivers. They also contribute as run defenders on outside plays. Notable cornerbacks include Deion Sanders, considered the greatest ever; Charles Woodson, the only defensive Heisman winner; and Darrell Revis, whose "Revis Island" nickname described his ability to shut down receivers alone. Eighteen cornerbacks are in the Hall of Fame. The position is vital because without strong cornerback play, quarterbacks exploit replacements immediately, while elite corners allow defensive schemes to focus resources elsewhere.

Defending soccer goal kicks involves strategic positioning and pressing to either win possession immediately or deny easy build-up play. Goal kicks occur when the ball crosses the defenders' end line last touched by an attacker, taken from within the six-yard Goal Area. Opponents must remain outside the 18-yard Penalty Area until the kick is taken, though play continues if they haven't retreated in time; touching the ball before it's in play results in a retake. The ball is live once kicked and visibly moves.

Three main defensive tactics exist: positioning defenders to cover receivers using man-to-man and zone coverage, aggressively moving to win the ball first with immediate transition to attack if successful, and pressing to keep the ball in the opponents' half if not won. Specific positioning includes center striker at the top of the Penalty Area, wing strikers marking wing backs, center midfielder at the center mark, wide midfielders covering sideline receivers, and backs supporting defensive positioning.

For youth players (10 and under), build-out lines allow defenders to retreat before pressure, encouraging playing out from the back. The simplest approach involves kicking to a dribbler who advances upfield. For ages 11 and above, progression includes multiple target options based on defensive coverage. Adult play utilizes all options, with goalkeepers typically taking kicks to maintain attacking numbers. Goal kicks are direct restarts where goals can be scored without intermediate touches, and players must remain aware of field conditions and ball location at all times.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who has missed the past two games with a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 3, was spotted doing rehab work outside on Wednesday for the first time since his injury. While there is still doubt about his immediate return, Cowboys executive Stephen Jones indicated Lamb could be back within the next two weeks, and he has not been placed on injured reserve. The team will release its first injury report later Wednesday, with Lamb expected to be limited at best.

David Jones has ended its two-year partnership with model Jesinta Franklin, replacing her with Victoria's Secret model Victoria Lee as ambassador. The retailer stated they are "taking another direction" but expressed gratitude for Franklin's dedication. Franklin, who won Miss Universe Australia in 2010 and is married to AFL star Buddy Franklin, was known for her intensive training for runway shows. The status of fellow ambassador Jessica Gomes with the retailer remains unclear.

Zameer Ghumra, a 38-year-old pharmacist from Leicester, was jailed for six years for showing a beheading video to children and attempting to radicalise them to support Islamic State. He told primary school-age boys they had a duty to kill people who insulted Islam. Nottingham Crown Court convicted him of disseminating terrorist propaganda between January 2013 and September 2014. Judge Gregory Dickinson QC called it a determined effort to turn children into terrorists, noting the absence of remorse. One child developed post-traumatic stress disorder; the other suffered sleep difficulties and fear of snipers.

Larry Connors' 3-day high/low method, published in "High Probability ETF Trading" (2009), is a quantified ETF trading strategy that buys when an ETF makes lower highs and lower lows for three consecutive days, with criteria including closing above the 200-day moving average and below the 5-day moving average. Connors emphasizes "quantify, quantify, quantify" and targets high win-ratios (at least 65%) to avoid behavioral mistakes, trading only ETFs because they rarely go to zero. Original tests on 20 popular ETFs through 2008 showed strong results, but 13 of 20 ETFs performed worse in subsequent backtesting. When tested as a portfolio with 25 ETFs (max 5 positions, 20% allocation each), the strategy still showed promise despite some deterioration, with the worst drawdown occurring during the July 2011 EU debt crisis. Connors did not originally test the strategy as a portfolio, which presents challenges due to correlated signals during market panics.

NewMarket Corp. is a specialty chemical company focused on petroleum-based fuel and lubricant additives through its Afton Chemical business. The company faces growth challenges from improving vehicle efficiency and longer oil change intervals in developed markets, but is expanding in emerging markets like Asia through a new Singapore facility and acquisitions such as Aditivos Mexicanos. NewMarket generates strong EBITDA margins and cash flow, and spends 5-8% of sales on R&D. The author projects 3% long-term revenue growth driven by emerging market vehicle volumes, but believes the stock is not undervalued at current prices trading above 12x EV/EBITDA, with valuation already pricing in high-single digit free cash flow growth.

Nippon Express Co. admitted an employee falsified inspection stamps on government-stockpiled rice stored for the farm ministry, which had been entrusted by Mitsubishi Corp. The misconduct affected 251 container bags total, with 15 bags shipped for livestock feed and the remainder to be incinerated; no health damage was reported. Mitsubishi received a business improvement order in May and submitted preventive measures. The incident follows other quality data falsifications at major Japanese manufacturers including Kobe Steel, Nissan, Subaru, and Hitachi Chemical. Japan regularly stockpiles about 1 million tons of rice for emergencies.

This passage is a maritime shipping contract for the vessel "Cape Horn Pigeon" from 1893, certified in 1900. Articles 5-10 specify: expenses from misconduct are charged to responsible individuals; the master may displace incompetent crew with adjusted pay; sick or deceased crew's representatives receive prorated shares; crew must account for entrusted items and handle cargo safely; compliant crew receive payment in San Francisco for whale oil at 20 cents/gallon, sperm oil at 40 cents/gallon, and whalebone at $1.25/lb (or $1.50/lb if Arctic fleet catch exceeds 200 whales). Signatories pledge voluntary agreement, timely reporting aboard, and prohibition of spirits except for medical use, with forfeiture of entire share for violations. The document includes certifications by Deputy Collector M. Webber and Secretary of State John Hay.

Seeking Alpha's transcripts team manages transcript-related projects, publishing thousands of quarterly earnings calls. EON Resources Inc. published a slide deck for an event. A chart displays time data from September 25-30, 2025, with values ranging from 0.4121 to 0.5074.

The Bifrost subsea cable, a 20,000-kilometre system connecting Singapore and the U.S. West Coast, is ready for commercial operations. Developed by a Keppel-led consortium with Meta and Telin Indonesia, the $760 million project links Singapore to Guam and California with branches to Jakarta, Manado, Davao, and Oregon. It will deliver over 260 terabits per second with 165ms latency, about 10ms faster than existing trans-Pacific systems. Keppel invested roughly $350 million for five of twelve fibre pairs. This study examines how 147 engineering and technical management students at a Hungarian university evaluate their education within the Education 4.0 framework and their preparedness for the changing job market. Industry 4.0 and COVID-19 have accelerated digital transformation in education, creating demand for new skills including critical thinking, problem-solving, self-management, and digital literacy. Education 4.0 emphasizes personalized learning, interdisciplinary approaches, and practical elements aligned with industry needs.

The research found that both student groups prioritized problem-solving as the most important skill, but differed in other areas: engineering students valued technical knowledge and specialization, while technical management students emphasized decision-making and analytical skills. For international experiences, both groups prioritized foreign language skills, though engineering students valued research opportunities while management students focused on networking. Students generally believed individual talents and professional devotion mattered more than university knowledge for career success. Significant differences between faculties emerged regarding expectations of higher education's contribution to analytical skills, teamwork, and self-awareness.

The study confirms that universities must adapt curricula to integrate both hard and soft skills, promote multidisciplinary collaboration, and address students' varying needs across disciplines to meet Industry 4.0 demands.

Irrfan Khan revealed he has a Neuro-Endocrine tumor and is receiving treatment in London. He shared an inspiring Rainer Maria Rilke poem on Instagram reflecting on his condition. Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 partners, have moved from Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft to Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, joining offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. This conceptual survey examines how Michel Foucault's theory of panopticism illuminates the relationship between slavery and pedagogy, particularly through surveillance as extraction, capitalist imperative, and technology of power. The author introduces "surveillance pedagogy" to describe how digital surveillance in education echoes historical practices of racial chattel slavery, where human experiences were extracted, textualized, and commodified. Ancient Greek pedagogues were typically enslaved people, and this master/slave binary persisted in American education through "fugitive pedagogy"—African American educators' subversive practices against racial surveillance. Contemporary data-driven pedagogy and surveillance capitalism, exemplified by platforms like Google Classroom, continue these extractive patterns by digitizing student data for behavioral conditioning and profit. The study argues that recognizing these continuities between slavery's surveillance practices and modern educational technology is essential for understanding current power asymmetries in teaching and learning.

The passage introduces BALLAST (Bayesian Active Learning with Lookahead Amendment for Sea-drifter Trajectories), a novel methodology for placing Lagrangian ocean drifters using active learning. Unlike existing placement strategies that rely on space-filling designs or expert opinions, BALLAST uses an information-theoretic utility function to iteratively select optimal observation points that maximize knowledge about time-dependent ocean currents. The method employs a spatio-temporal vector-output Gaussian process surrogate with a temporal Helmholtz kernel, and applies the stochastic partial differential equation approach for efficient implementation. The expected information gain policy selects placement locations by optimizing the reduction in entropy between prior and posterior distributions of the vector field. The authors' contributions include introducing active learning concepts to Lagrangian observer placement literature, proposing BALLAST with its lookahead amendment accounting for Lagrangian observations, and developing a new GP posterior sampling method combining standard regression with the SPDE approach.

This study examined the relationship between long-term blood pressure variability and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) in 1,284 participants from the Kailuan cohort. High systolic blood pressure variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and perivascular spaces. High diastolic blood pressure variability was associated with lacunae. High pulse pressure variability showed the strongest risk effects on moderate/severe cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. These associations were modified by age and hypertension status: in adults under 60, only high pulse pressure variability was significantly associated with severe cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces, while systolic and pulse pressure variability effects were only significant in participants with hypertension. The study concludes that long-term blood pressure variability is an independent risk factor for cSVD, particularly in combination with hypertension, and that pulse pressure variability warrants attention in young adults.

MIT professor Gary Gensler discusses payment systems and blockchain technology in this lecture marking Bitcoin's 10th anniversary. Key pain points in traditional payment systems include multiple intermediaries with parallel ledgers, high costs (estimated at 0.5-1% of world GDP), delayed settlement especially for merchants, lack of financial inclusion, fraud, privacy concerns, and cyber attacks. Blockchain offers potential benefits through lower verification and networking costs, but faces challenges including scalability, high transaction costs, speed, interoperability, error resolution difficulties, and governance issues. The class debates whether blockchain is necessary for innovation or if traditional systems can improve without it, with a MasterCard representative arguing existing systems can accomplish blockchain's promises. Cross-border payment solutions using cryptocurrency as a bridge currency are explored, with Ripple's xRapid cited as an example, though liquidity and volatility remain concerns. Few blockchain payment companies have achieved significant adoption despite many white papers, and incumbents like Visa and MasterCard hold hundreds of blockchain-related patents, possibly as barriers to entry.

The password protection feature allows a host to lock a card using a password stored in 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, with optional Force Erase Password registers if Card Ownership Protection is supported. Cards automatically lock after power-on if PWD_LEN is non-zero. The lock/unlock command operates only in transfer state, requires card selection, and uses a single block write command structure containing password mode, PWD, and lock/unlock information.

In a 1996 New Jersey Superior Court case, Judge Menza ruled that an employee's sick pay and wages received for personal days and family illness days are not collateral sources subject to deduction from lost wage awards under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97. The court followed the reasoning of *Bruwelheide v. Garvey*, a Minnesota case with a similar statute, holding that such benefits are earned compensation rather than duplicate recovery. Because the plaintiff exhausted her accumulated benefits due to the defendant's negligence—surrendering future use of those benefits including potential cash-out at retirement—deducting them would improperly reduce her recovery. The court concluded that sick pay and similar employment benefits are not within the contemplation of the collateral source statute.

This paper examines exclusion of disabled and marginalized students in Ontario's K-12 education system, arguing that current "special education" practices invite students without ensuring they belong. The historical overview traces special education from 1860s residential schools through 1960s integration efforts, noting persistent segregation rationalized by deficit-based views of disability. Racialized students face compounded barriers, with overrepresentation in behavioral and intellectual disability categories and underrepresentation in gifted programs. The Individual Education Plan (IEP) process, while intended to support inclusion, relies on school-based disability identification that uses deficit models and offers five placement options ranging from regular class with indirect support to full special education classes. The Policy on Accessible Education for Students with Disabilities (2018) claims to guarantee equal treatment but lacks accountability mechanisms and provides limited implementation guidance. Teacher preparation programs contain minimal disability content, and educators face constraints including reduced funding, larger classes, and curricular demands that hinder inclusive practices. Recommendations include enhancing teacher training in universal design for learning, developing policies supporting educators with disabilities, ensuring student and teacher involvement in policy development, and adopting intersectional approaches that address how race and disability interact.

This study developed and validated a two-week Critical Multicultural Education (CME) learning module for pre-service English language teachers in Türkiye. The module was created through a four-stage process: researcher brainstorming sessions, critical friend review, small group implementation with 15 participants, and larger group validation with 86 participants followed by in-depth interviews with 10 participants. Findings showed the module provided personal benefits including positive attitudes toward diversity and perspectives on social issues, and professional benefits such as pedagogical insights on CME, awareness of educational ideologies and political positions, and guidance on implementing CME in practice. Challenges included limited time, dense content, and insufficient information on taking critical action. The study addresses a research gap in non-Western contexts regarding CME integration into English language teacher education, demonstrating that even a short module can raise awareness and initiate attitude changes toward critical multicultural education, though longer durations are recommended for deeper engagement.

Pakistan's higher education (HE) enrollment grew from 2% to 12.6% between 2003-2021 following 2002 reforms establishing the Higher Education Commission (HEC). However, access remains inequitable: universities concentrate in low-poverty urban areas (70% of universities serve 40% of population in low-poverty zones versus 1 university for 5.6% in extreme poverty zones), private institutions charge fees 5-10× higher than public universities, and rural populations face geographic and financial barriers. Female enrollment improved nationally (36% to 47% by 2014) but persists at only 0.02% in extreme poverty zones versus 32% in low-poverty areas. Regional disparities show Islamabad (0.97% population) has 14% enrollment while Baluchistan (5.7% population) has 3%. The study recommends targeted scholarships, rural public university expansion, regulated private sector access, and community colleges to achieve equitable 15% enrollment by 2025.

Digital leaders cultivate data-driven cultures through four key practices: adopting growth mindsets that encourage experimentation and long-term learning, providing transparent data access across teams, using clear metrics to track progress, and aligning the organization through shared data-driven goals. They balance measurement with flexibility, allowing teams autonomy in achieving goals.

Digital laggards contrast sharply by prioritizing short-term optimization, restricting data access, relying on "culture of genius" decision-making, and setting aspirational goals without data grounding. They discourage risk-taking, hoard data as power, and focus on process adherence over objective measurement.

A pharmaceutical case study demonstrates how localized experimentation environments can foster innovation even within regulated industries, while a retail case study shows real-time data enabling faster decision-making. This lecture introduces linearized general relativity as a method for solving Einstein's field equations in weak gravity, where spacetime is nearly flat. The metric is expressed as flat spacetime plus a small perturbation h_αβ. Key concepts include: nearly Lorentz coordinates where Lorentz transformations leave the background unchanged while the perturbation transforms as a tensor; raising and lowering indices using the flat metric η_αβ; the inverse metric being η^αβ - h^αβ to linear order; and infinitesimal coordinate transformations (gauge transformations) that shift h_μν by symmetrized derivatives of ξ_ν, analogous to electromagnetic gauge transformations.

The Riemann tensor in linearized theory becomes second derivatives of h, and is gauge-invariant. The Einstein tensor simplifies when using the trace-reversed perturbation h̄_αβ = h_αβ - ½η_αβh. By choosing Lorentz gauge (∂^μh̄_μν = 0), the field equations reduce to □h̄_αβ = -16πT_αβ, a wave equation analogous to electrodynamics.

For a static, non-relativistic perfect fluid source, time derivatives vanish and T_00 ≈ ρ dominates. This yields h̄_00 = -4Φ_N (Newtonian potential), giving the Newtonian limit metric with g_00 = -(1+2Φ_N) and g_ij = δ_ij(1-2Φ_N). The lecture notes that rotating bodies produce additional "gravito-magnetic" corrections, with the next lecture covering dynamic sources and gravitational radiation.

This 2025 study by Merola examines online learning's potential to improve access and quality in Mexican higher education through qualitative interviews with 32 stakeholders (leaders, professors, and students) across six universities. Distance learning enrollments grew 150% from 2013-2023, reaching 22% of tertiary students, with private institutions dominating this sector (69% of distance learners).

Findings reveal that while online learning expands access for non-traditional students, significant barriers persist: economic constraints limiting technology access, poor rural internet infrastructure, and unequal institutional resources creating digital divides. Quality concerns include faculty unfamiliarity with digital platforms, lower student engagement, collaboration difficulties, and increased academic dishonesty. Stakeholders consistently viewed online learning as complementary to—not replacing—in-person education, particularly for hands-on subjects and vulnerable populations including neurodivergent, rural, indigenous, and low-resource students.

The study concludes that without substantial infrastructure investment and targeted support, online learning risks exacerbating rather than reducing educational inequalities in Mexico.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. The controllers feature soft-start functionality controlled by an external capacitor, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when SS pin voltage reaches 1 V. Three oscillator modes are available: internal oscillator (RT resistor sets frequency, SYNC outputs clock at 2× frequency), external synchronization (RT floating, external clock applied to SYNC at 2× desired frequency), and primary-secondary mode (two controllers synchronized via SYNC connection). Primary switching outputs include single (OUTA) or dual (OUTA/OUTB) options, with ~150 mA peak current capability requiring external gate drivers. Synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) are available on select variants, activating after soft-start completes. Programmable dead times (TDSP/TDPS) and leading edge blank time are set via external resistors; pulse skipping mode activates when COMP voltage is below 0.3 V and previous duty cycle was under 25%. Duty cycle limits are configurable (50%, 75%, or 100%) through DCL pin connections. Current sensing uses CS_ILIM pin with 1.05 V overcurrent threshold triggering hiccup mode, where CHICC capacitor controls delay and restart timing. Additional features include external fault protection (FAULT pin), slope compensation (RSC resistor), Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V input and support buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds, and routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes.

The lecture covers black holes in general relativity, beginning with the Schwarzschild solution and its coordinate singularity at r = 2GM. The speaker explains that while this surface appears problematic in Schwarzschild coordinates, it is merely a coordinate artifact—objects cross it in finite proper time but never reach it in coordinate time. The surface represents infinite gravitational redshift, where emitted light loses all energy as observed from afar.

To resolve this, the lecture introduces alternative coordinates: tortoise coordinates (r*) stretch the radial axis to keep light cones at 45 degrees; Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates (using v = t + r* or u = t − r*) simplify null geodesics; and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates eliminate the coordinate singularity entirely, revealing that r = 2GM is an event horizon—a boundary beyond which no information can escape.

The lecture then presents three additional black hole solutions: Reissner-Nordström (charged, with horizon at r = GM ± √(G²M² − Gq²)), Kerr (rotating, with horizon at r = GM ± √(G²M² − a²)), and Kerr-Newman (charged and rotating). The No-Hair theorem states that all stationary black holes in 3+1 dimensions are completely characterized by mass, spin, and charge—any other structure radiates away during formation.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a source-synchronous data interface providing output data and capture clock on DCLKOUT. The device features a data output randomizer using XOR operations with either the LSB or PRBS bit to minimize ground bounce interference. Two data averaging modes (simple and moving) improve SNR. Test patterns including fixed, digital ramp, and alternating patterns aid interface debugging. The device is reset via logic 0 on RESET pin or register write, and powered down via logic 0 on PWDN pin or register write. Initialization requires a sequence of register writes after power-up or reset with a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode enables 8MSPS sampling for a selected channel pair. SPI register access uses three banks with 16-bit registers addressable via 8-bit addresses; daisy-chain topology supports multiple devices with configurable chain length. Key registers control SPI mode, bank selection, data format, averaging, XOR randomization, test patterns, speed-boost mode, analog input bandwidth, power-down, and output lane configuration. The device suits ATE applications with 0.0015% TUE post-calibration and offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes. Three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) require proper decoupling and layout avoiding digital-analog signal crossing.

Nominal techniques formalize syntax with binders, but many pragmatic formalizations rebuild infrastructure for each new development. This paper proposes a formalization of constructive nominal sets in Rocq using typeclasses and generalized rewriting, achieving shorter proofs. The work covers core nominal theory concepts including permutation types, support, freshness, name abstraction, and supported functions, along with the Freshness Theorem and Freshness Condition for Binders. The development uses finite permutations represented as swap lists, defines constructive freshness via some/any principles, and implements name abstraction as a dedicated record type to avoid typeclass search issues. Future work aims toward α-structural principles for reasoning modulo α-equivalence.

The DISCARD operation de-allocates blocks and treats their contents as "don't care," with data readability depending on card implementation. It requires CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 (with argument 00000001h) in sequence, and hosts must check the DISCARD_SUPPORT bit (b313) in SD_STATUS. Out-of-sequence commands trigger ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET, while out-of-range addresses cause OUT_OF_RANGE errors. DISCARD is only supported for SDHC/SDXC cards, not SPI, and indicates progress via DAT0 held low with a 250ms busy timeout.

This passage describes AMD AGESA firmware procedures for processor initialization and memory management. Two main stack-related procedures are detailed: one that initializes a pre-memory stack using register passing (destroying EAX, ECX, EDX, EDI, ESI, and optionally DS/ES in 16-bit mode), checks protected mode status, sets up UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF, and returns status codes for success, reentry warnings, or unknown processor family errors; and another that removes the pre-memory stack, preserves EBX for return addressing, flushes cache lines, and disables CAR mode when main memory becomes available. Additional helper procedures include AmdCreateStruct for allocating parameter block storage through PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost methods, with associated status codes and dependencies on proper stack establishment; and a data eye retrieval function for DIMM analysis requiring operational HyperTransport links and returning 31×32-bit bitmaps normalized to trained centers.

The speaker outlines principles for his presidential administration, emphasizing the pacification of the country and protection of constitutional rights for all citizens. He addresses conditions in the Southern States, stressing the need for local self-government that equally protects both races and adheres faithfully to the Constitution. He acknowledges a moral obligation to protect emancipated citizens' rights, advocates for universal education as the basis of suffrage, and calls for the material development of the South. The speaker demands thorough civil service reform to eliminate partisan patronage and recommends a constitutional amendment for a six-year presidential term without reelection. Regarding the economy, he notes the continuing depression since 1873 and supports the resumption of specie payments. On foreign policy, he advocates noninterference and arbitration of disputes. He references the resolution of the recent electoral controversy by a tribunal as a lawful settlement of conflict and calls for national unity based on justice and peace.

Linda Farr, 68, received a 20-month suspended prison sentence for gross negligence manslaughter of her 86-year-old mother Doreen Shufflebotham, who died in September 2016 after sitting in a chair for 8-12 months. Shufflebotham suffered multiple health conditions including a fractured femur, sepsis, and meningitis. Neighbors described Farr as reclusive and reported fly infestations following the death. President Obama delivered his farewell address in Chicago, thanking Americans for making him a better President and person. He reflected on his early work there with church groups and his belief that change comes from ordinary people engaging in democracy. He highlighted achievements including economic recovery, healthcare expansion, marriage equality, and killing Osama bin Laden, while acknowledging uneven progress and remaining challenges.

Obama identified four threats to American democracy: economic inequality and lack of opportunity, persistent racial divisions, political polarization and rejection of facts, and taking democracy for granted. He urged citizens to bridge divides, participate in civic life, and protect democratic institutions. He expressed optimism in the younger generation and concluded by asking Americans to believe in their own ability to bring about change, ending with his campaign slogan: "Yes, we can."

A New Zealand man, Nigel Rothsay, discovered in December that he does not own the house he purchased in 2012 due to an administrative error where lot numbers were mixed up during the property transfer. Police discovered the mistake when placing a restraining order on his neighbour's house for suspected methamphetamine dealing. Conveyancing business First Property Legal denied wrongdoing and blamed either real estate agent Harcourts or seller's agent Public Trust. The situation remains unresolved as multiple parties are involved.

Recent advances in reasoning language models (RLMs) have created a landscape of models with varying sizes, domains, and reasoning budgets. While always selecting the most capable and expensive configuration is suboptimal—since simpler queries can be solved by cheaper models and strong RLMs may "over-think"—practitioners face challenges in selecting the right configuration for each query. This paper proposes RADAR (Reasoning—Ability and Difficulty-Aware Routing), a framework that selects optimal {RLM, reasoning budget} configurations in real-time (~7ms latency) based on user-specified performance-cost tradeoffs. RADAR uses item response theory (IRT) to jointly estimate query difficulties and RLM abilities, formulates routing as multi-objective optimization with linear or Chebyshev scalarization, and employs adaptive testing to rapidly integrate new RLM configurations. Experiments on 8-9 challenging benchmarks demonstrate RADAR's superior performance-cost tradeoffs, achieving 90% of OpenAI o4-mini's performance at 1.31-10% of its cost, with strong generalization to out-of-domain and long-context queries.

A Campaign for Black Male Achievement report shows Milwaukee's score for supporting black and Latino males rose from 63 to 71 since 2015, ranking 13th among 50 cities measured. The report cites creation of the MPS Department of Black and Latino Male Achievement and website MyBlackStory.us as progress indicators. Despite increased engagement through initiatives like the Black Male Achievement Advisory Council and Milwaukee Fatherhood Initiative, officials acknowledge this has not yet improved graduation rates (49% for African-American males, 57% for Latino males) or reduced crime. The Department has identified five strategies including improving school climate, positive media campaigns, expanding manhood academies, and hiring more male teachers of color to address disparities.

Meteorologists are monitoring an outflow boundary moving slowly southeastward for scattered storm development this evening, along with storms forming over southeastern Missouri from Gulf moisture. An MCV to the north and northwest may trigger a severe storm bow that could affect part of the Tri-State with scattered severe gusts, though peak intensity duration is uncertain as it moves from better mid-level flow.

Reckitt Benckiser's shares have fallen at least 15% from 52-week highs across all markets, with its P/E ratio of 22.79 below industry and S&P 500 averages. The decline stems from a South Korean dehumidifier controversy that caused over 92 deaths and 530 injuries, and the $17.9 billion acquisition of struggling Mead Johnson. Despite these challenges, the company maintains strong financials with profitable established brands, manageable debt following a $4.2 billion food business sale, and a 2.37% dividend yield. The Mead Johnson acquisition strengthens its position in developing markets, particularly China. The author suggests current discounted prices present a buying opportunity.

A "Hands Across the Sand" protest was held at Laguna's Main Beach on February 3 against the Trump administration's proposal to expand offshore oil and gas drilling. The plan would allow leasing of 47 coastal areas from 2019 to 2024, including seven in the Pacific Ocean off California, Washington, and Oregon. It would be the first new offshore drilling leases in California since 1984. The protest included environmental groups, ocean enthusiasts, and concerned citizens, with participants gathering on the beach and paddle boarders joining in the water.

Baylor NAACP created the hashtag #myblackhistory for African-American students to share diverse perspectives on their experiences and what being black means to them. Press and publicity chair Maryse Bombito films students answering questions about what they love about being black and posts the videos on the Baylor NAACP Twitter page. Bombito wanted to celebrate present experiences that will become history, not just past events. The group also celebrated the NAACP's 108th founders day with a viewing of "A Raisin in the Sun." President Reginald Singletary expressed appreciation for the organization's longevity and its platform for continuing justice work. Baylor NAACP will support upcoming multicultural events including a Black Heritage Banquet with Malcolm X's daughter, the Coalition of Black Ambassadors' All For One Soiree, and an Asian Student Association fashion show.

The Area Agency on Aging and Preble County Council on Aging are offering Healthy U, a six-week workshop for people with chronic diseases to learn skills for managing symptoms and improving quality of life. The program covers topics including chronic pain, nutrition, exercise, medication use, emotions, and communication with doctors and family. Workshops will be held Tuesdays, March 6 through April 10, from 9:30 a.m. to noon at 800 East St. Clair Street in Eaton. Advance registration is required by calling 937-456-4947 or emailing hsteele@prebleseniorcenter.org or scopes@prebleseniorcenter.org.

A police constable facing rape charges in Gwanda allegedly hanged himself at Gungwe Police Base where he was deployed. Constable Godknows Dube, 36, was found hanging from a tree by a colleague around 6AM on Wednesday, approximately two hours after leaving his girlfriend's place. He had been scheduled to appear in court on October 26. No suicide note was found, but sources suspect pressure from the rape allegations motivated the act. Dube allegedly used a rope taken from a flag post at Gungwe Primary School, where his girlfriend is a student teacher. National Police Spokesperson Senior Commissioner Charity Charamba stated she had not yet received a report. The incident follows two other police suicides in the past year: a married officer in Masvingo who hanged himself after his girlfriend left him, and a senior officer at Bulawayo's Westgate Police Station who shot himself.

Two insurers disputed priority of coverage for a workplace injury settlement. The Third Circuit affirmed the District Court's ruling that Vigilant Insurance's policy had priority over Travelers' policy, based on an unambiguous endorsement in Travelers' policy explicitly subordinating its coverage to other insurers when an additional insured is involved.

Male cichlids exposed to predator alarm substances grow faster and delay conspicuous breeding coloration to reduce predation risk, developing larger eyes and longer dorsal fin spines for protection. At peak sexual maturity, however, they display full colors regardless of risk to attract mates. University of Bonn researchers studying *Pelvicachromis taeniatus* found only males exhibited this plasticity, as they defend exposed territories while females remain in breeding caves. The study appears in *The American Naturalist*.

Investors prefer UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti's strategy over Barclays' Jes Staley, reflected in UBS trading at 1.3 times tangible book value versus Barclays' 0.7 times. First-quarter results show both banks lagged U.S. peers in capital markets, with Barclays hurt more by fixed income declines. However, adjusting for one-time items, Barclays' return on tangible equity of 9% neared UBS's 10.9%, with core operations matching its rival. Simultaneous erasure of multiple write blocks enhances data throughput. Identification uses CMD32 (start) and CMD33 (end) commands, followed by CMD38 (ERASE). CMD38 arguments 00000001h or 000000002h may prevent execution if DISCARD or FULE is supported. Out-of-sequence commands trigger ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET status bits. Write-protected sectors within erase ranges remain intact, setting WP_ERASE_SKIP. Address fields use byte units, with lower bits below WRITE_BL_LEN ignored. Erase progress is indicated by DAT0 held low; hosts may deselect cards during long operations. Post-erase data values ('0' or '1') vary by vendor.

H. W. Robinson & Co. v. United States, decided December 23, 1946, was a customs reappraisement case involving merchandise entered at New York on May 27, 1946. The court ruled that export value under section 402(d) of the Tariff Act of 1930 was the proper basis for valuation, equaling appraised values minus additions made by the importer due to advances by the appraiser in similar cases.

Antonia Martinez's cousin is moving from New York City to Nevada to escape winter cold that causes her depression. This "thing" is seasonal affective disorder (SAD), a recurring depression tied to seasons. Winter SAD is most common; summer SAD is rare. SAD affects 1-10% globally, more women and young adults, with 10 million Americans suffering. Though clinically defined in the 1980s, seasonal illness was described since ancient times. Scientists believe reduced sunlight disrupts serotonin and melatonin levels, though some question SAD's existence. Symptoms include fatigue, cravings, weight gain, and social withdrawal in winter; insomnia and anxiety in summer. Untreated SAD can worsen to eating disorders or suicidal thoughts. Treatments include light therapy, medication, and psychotherapy. Prevention involves exercise, outdoor time, social activity, proper sleep, balanced diet, stress reduction, full-spectrum lighting, plants, and color.

The Arms Index (TRIN) is a market sentiment indicator created by Richard W. Arms in 1967 that gauges market strength by comparing advancing/declining stocks (AD Ratio) to advancing/declining volume (AD Volume). Readings of 1.0 indicate market balance; below 1.0 suggests bullish conditions with greater volume in advancing stocks, while above 1.0 indicates bearish bias. Extreme readings above 3.0 signal oversold conditions and potential bullish reversals, while below 0.50 indicates overbought conditions. The AD Volume Line measures market breadth through net volume changes. Backtests show TRIN performs best combined with other indicators, with one modified strategy achieving 0.66% average gain per trade, 77% win rate, and 2.4 profit factor.

This paper proposes PAST (Pilot-and-Adaptive Stable Trading), a framework for edge-assisted UAV networks with spatio-temporal dynamism (STD-EUNs). PAST addresses three key challenges: high overhead and failure risk from online trading, leveraging pre-signed agreements and overbooking for market efficiency, and adaptive updates under uncertainty. The framework consists of two stages: PilotAO establishes futures trading agreements with overbooking via stable matching before transactions, while AdaptAO uses deep reinforcement learning to dynamically refine agreements and overbooking rates during execution. PilotAO ensures stability, individual rationality, and weak Pareto optimality through many-to-many matching between UAVs (buyers) and edge servers (sellers), accounting for risks of unsatisfactory utility and overbooking-induced breaches. AdaptAO models the adjustment process as a Markov Decision Process with states capturing resource demands, UAV locations, utilities, interactions, and reputation values, using double deep Q-networks to optimize renewal decisions. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate PAST reduces running time, number of interactions, and practical task completion time compared to conventional spot trading and futures trading without adaptation, while improving social welfare, task completion rates, and resource utilization.

Netflix is raising its standard plan from $9.99 to $10.99 monthly and its premium plan from $11.99 to $13.99. Current customers will be notified in mid-October, while new signups see updated prices immediately. This marks Netflix's first price increase since 2014. While 2018 headlines highlight record U.S. meat consumption, the dietary mix has shifted dramatically from beef to chicken over recent decades. Per capita beef consumption peaked in the 1970s and has declined by one-third, while chicken consumption has more than doubled. This transition reduces environmental pressure, as beef production requires seven times more land and emits seven times more greenhouse gases than chicken per gram of protein. The shift stems from health concerns, convenience, increased chicken production, and lower prices. Although beef consumption has rebounded since 2014 due to economic recovery and lower feed prices, it remains far below peak levels. However, U.S. beef consumption still exceeds the world average fourfold, and researchers emphasize that further reductions in beef consumption and shifts toward plant-based foods in high-consuming countries are essential to meet climate targets and sustainability goals.

This MIT lecture covers empirical research on price discrimination, contrasting theoretical models with real-world evidence. Early studies examined whether price discrimination actually occurs, with Borenstein finding evidence of discrimination in leaded vs. unleaded gasoline pricing and Shepard documenting second-degree discrimination in self-serve versus full-serve gas stations.

The lecture then examines racial and gender discrimination in retail car prices. Early audit studies by Ayres and Siegelman found substantial discrimination (5-10% price differences), while Goldberg's Consumer Expenditure Survey analysis found no differences. A more comprehensive study by Scott Morton, Zettelmeyer, and Silva-Risso using detailed JD Power transaction data (671,000 car purchases) found discrimination exists but at smaller magnitudes: Black buyers paid ~1.5% more, Hispanic buyers ~1.1% more, women ~0.2% more. The study found that online purchasing through Autobytel largely eliminated these demographic effects, suggesting discrimination stems from differences in search costs and bargaining sophistication rather than animus.

Two papers examine online price discrimination's welfare effects. Shiller's study of Netflix using web browsing data found demographic targeting increased profits only 0.3%, while web browsing-based targeting increased profits 13% with minimal consumer surplus loss. Dubé and Misra's ZipRecruiter experiment, featuring randomized pricing, found optimal uniform pricing should be $327 (vs. $99 charged), while personalized pricing could increase profits 8.2% but would reduce consumer surplus 25% and lower total welfare. ZipRecruiter ultimately adopted $249 uniform pricing rather than implementing discrimination, suggesting firms may avoid discrimination due to reputational concerns despite modest profit gains.
