This study presents the first transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) comparing virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH, N=194) to HIV-negative individuals (N=361), using whole blood RNA sequencing to identify gene expression changes associated with chronic HIV disease and ART. The researchers identified 566 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 274 up-regulated and 292 down-regulated in PLWH. These DEGs showed significant enrichment for immune system processes and cancer-related pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, p53, and TGF-β signaling. Cell-type deconvolution revealed altered proportions of CD8+ T cells, follicular helper T cells, naïve CD4+ T cells, resting CD4+ memory T cells, and resting mast cells in PLWH. Approximately 40% of HIV-associated DEGs were classified as ART-affected based on comparison with pre/post-ART gene expression data, with most showing inverse expression changes relative to HIV-negative samples, suggesting ART shifts gene expression toward but does not fully restore the uninfected state. Partitioned heritability analysis showed no enrichment for cancer or HIV acquisition traits, but significant enrichment for inflammatory diseases including Crohn's disease, asthma, rheumatoid arthritis, primary biliary cirrhosis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis. Colocalization analysis identified 26 eGenes with shared genetic signals across 17 immune-related traits. Drug target analysis identified 111 DEGs as targets for approved drugs or clinical trial compounds, including 11 pathways in cancer DEGs, highlighting potential therapeutic targets for co-occurring conditions in PLWH.

This study examined lipid profiles in 108 Thai university students with simple dysmood disorder (SDMD) or first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD) versus healthy controls, excluding participants with metabolic syndrome. Results showed decreased lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) activity and elevated free cholesterol and apolipoprotein E (ApoE) in SDMD and FE-SDMD patients compared to controls, with no significant changes in HDL-cholesterol, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport (RCT), ApoB, or triglycerides. LCAT effects on depression severity and suicidal behaviors were mediated through free cholesterol and brooding. Even without subclinical metabolic syndrome, SDMD and FE-SDMD patients showed decreased LCAT and elevated free cholesterol. Interactions between SDMD diagnosis and subclinical metabolic syndrome stages led to reduced HDL-cholesterol and RCT and increased ApoB/ApoA ratio. The authors conclude that SDMD and FE-SDMD represent pre-proatherogenic states and recommend lipid screening for these biomarkers to identify at-risk individuals for preventive intervention.

A professor introduces games to measure social preferences in an economics class. The first is the Dictator game, where a "dictator" decides how much of an endowment (candy, apples, or money ranging from $5-$20) to share with a randomly selected receiver. The professor implements some choices publicly to demonstrate how publicity affects decisions. Variations include allowing communication between players and making selections more private.

The second game is the Ultimatum game, where a proposer offers a split and a responder can accept or reject—if rejected, neither receives anything. The professor explains the "strategy method," where players specify contingent plans for all possible scenarios, allowing more efficient data collection from multiple participants while only paying out for one randomly selected pair.

The third game is the Trust game: an investor sends money that gets multiplied (by 3), then the responder decides how much to return. The professor notes that communication between players can influence outcomes, and that these classroom demonstrations are "sloppy" compared to rigorous experimental economics standards. Students are invited to share observations anonymously on a forum for discussion in the next class.

The flea flicker is a football trick play designed to look like a run, where the quarterback hands off the ball then receives it back to throw downfield. It exploits defensive aggression against the run, leaving defenders out of position when the play shifts to a pass. Illinois coach Bob Zuppke invented it in 1910, naming it for the quick flicking motion of a dog shaking off fleas. The quarterback can be penalized for intentional grounding on this play since he relinquished possession earlier. A 2022 Michigan example shows its effectiveness even with minimal defensive hesitation. Variations include the reverse flea flicker, combining it with a reverse play, and the fake flea flicker, where the running back pretends to toss back but keeps the ball.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, featuring internal overvoltage protection (±20V when powered, ±15V when unpowered), programmable gain amplifier with nine input ranges, second-order antialiasing filter (500kHz cutoff), and integrated reference (4.096V internal or external). The device supports multiSPI interface with various data transfer protocols including legacy SPI and source-synchronous modes, daisy-chain topology for multiple devices, and programmable alarm functions for input voltage and AVDD monitoring. Configuration is managed through nine registers controlling reset, power modes (NAP and power-down), data protocols, input ranges, and alarm thresholds. The device operates with separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, requiring proper decoupling capacitors for optimal performance.

This MIT lecture on numerical linear algebra focuses on solving sparse matrix systems through elimination, emphasizing that reordering unknowns significantly affects fill-in—where zeros become non-zeros during elimination. The professor explains fill-in using both symbolic and graphical representations, showing how elimination creates new edges between nodes previously connected to the pivot node. Key reordering strategies discussed include: red-black ordering (numbering nodes by checkerboard colors), minimum degree algorithms (selecting nodes with fewest connections at each step), and nested dissection using graph separators (dividing graphs recursively with small separator sets). The lecture notes that while bandwidth reduction seems intuitive, it can increase fill-in, and that MATLAB's backslash uses approximate minimum degree (AMD) ordering. For large 3D problems, nested dissection may outperform minimum degree methods. The professor encourages experimental comparison using MATLAB's nnz command to count non-zeros in L and U factors.

Contractor's Sand and Gravel, Inc. v. Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission, 2000 WL 3884 (D.C. Cir. Jan. 7, 2000): The D.C. Circuit held that while the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission had jurisdiction to review an Administrative Law Judge's Equal Access to Justice Act fee award, the Commission erred in finding the Secretary of Labor's position "substantially justified." The Secretary had cited CSG for using frame grounding of electrical equipment, claiming this method was prohibited, though no regulation actually forbade it. The court found the Secretary's position lacked reasonable basis in law or fact, noting the Secretary persisted in prosecuting violations of non-existent regulations rather than pursuing rulemaking, and had failed to conduct any testing to determine actual compliance. The court reversed the Commission's decision vacating the fee award and remanded for determination of fees for the appellate proceedings.

Philosophy of education is marginalized in mainstream educational research, which prioritizes empirical, quantitative, and qualitative methods while relegating philosophical work to peripheral status. Students and colleagues often question whether philosophy constitutes "real" research, viewing it as subjective and lacking rigor compared to data-driven approaches. Economic precarity and competitive academic pressures further discourage students from pursuing philosophy of education, as it offers limited funding opportunities, low citation impact, and scarce job prospects. The field faces internal debates about its identity, methods, and relevance, compounded by a nostalgic "golden years" narrative that obscures historical struggles and diversity. The author argues for abandoning self-serving imaginaries and embracing philosophy of education's distinctive pluralism, critical reflexivity, and conceptual depth as strengths, while challenging the assumption that educational research must be empirical.

On the organization's seat, he dismissed Switzerland as ineligible due to neutrality and showed interest in the Pays de Gex idea. He accepted some Latin American proposals on political independence and territorial integrity but opposed strengthening the Assembly and Court at the Council's expense. He criticized small nations' demands against permanent member voting on their own disputes as "unrealistic." The conversation ended with a request for written analysis of Council voting procedures under the President's formula.

Cancer cells transfer mitochondria to neighboring fibroblasts through threadlike nanotubes, reprogramming them to support tumor growth. Researchers at ETH Zurich identified the protein MIRO2 as crucial for this process, which causes fibroblasts to grow faster and activate cancer-linked genes. Cancer cells can also transfer mitochondria to immune cells, weakening their cancer-fighting abilities. The findings, published August 28, 2025, suggest potential therapeutic targets but raise questions about triggers and mechanisms.

A player states there is little carryover from previous seasons regarding rivalries or heated matchups against Philadelphia. The team hasn't focused on chatter about an opposing player potentially returning, expressing respect but uncertainty about his effectiveness. They remain focused on their own play, noting that while home crowds provide some advantage, they need to maintain their performance. Despite losing the first two games despite playing well, they are confident they can win at least one away game as they had planned.

This inaugural address emphasizes the mutual covenant between president and people in upholding the Constitution and laws. It notes the 26th presidential term, national growth in territory, population, and wealth since 1789, and improvements in living standards and education. The speech defends protective tariffs, linking their sectional nature historically to slavery, and argues for manufacturing development in the South to unify the nation. It rejects special executive policies for any section, insists on uniform law enforcement, and warns against nullification by individuals or communities. The address calls for stricter naturalization laws, continued non-interference in European affairs while protecting American interests abroad, civil service reform, reduction of Treasury surpluses, naval expansion, admission of Dakota, Montana, and Washington as states, and election law reform to secure ballot integrity. It concludes by urging patriotism over partisanship and expressing confidence in the nation's future.

Penn State's White Building has been undergoing renovations since summer 2016, with completion expected by end of March. Updates include a renovated main lobby, two new registration desks, a new stairwell and elevator, and updated main entrance exterior and pathway. Post-renovation, the building will have one entrance and exit. The purpose is to improve building flow, enable efficient traffic monitoring, comply with Penn State policy, improve safety, and track usage trends. The renovations follow extensive work on the IM Building. Despite construction detours, gym membership and usage have not decreased. No plans exist to renovate the White Building fitness center.

The global visceral pain market is projected to reach USD 14.22 billion by 2024, driven by an aging population, rising disease prevalence, and increased awareness. North America held the majority share in 2016 due to high healthcare expenditure and prevalence of Crohn's disease and irritable bowel syndrome, while Asia Pacific is expected to grow fastest at 6.2% CAGR. Analgesics dominated therapeutics with 60.4% market share, and Crohn's disease was the largest indication segment at 41.4%. Key players include Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Takeda, Allergan, and AstraZeneca, which are focusing on R&D and collaborations. The market is segmented by therapeutics (analgesics, narcotics, NSAIDs, pain modifiers, tricyclic antidepressants, tricyclic anticonvulsants), indications (interstitial cystitis, Crohn's, irritable bowel, chronic prostatitis), and region (North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, Rest of World).

Superannuation tax changes taking effect in July are expected to increase self-managed super funds (SMSFs), with over two million Australians projected to have SMSFs within 15 years. Key changes include a $1.6 million transfer balance cap, removal of tax exemptions for transition-to-retirement pensions, reduced annual concessional contributions cap to $25,000, reduced non-concessional cap to $100,000, 30% tax on concessional contributions for higher earners, and expanded tax-deductible contributions. Demographics show 35% of younger Australians and more women are establishing SMSFs, while the previously dominant group of males over 54 is declining. Business owners remain the largest sector by super fund value.

AI effectiveness depends on training data quality, making regulated financial institutions' extensive data repositories valuable for AI development. Financial sector AI adoption has surged, with top 10 banks increasing AI mentions in annual reports by 340% from 2019 to 2023. However, AI incidents in finance are underreported compared to sectors like aviation and healthcare due to confidential regulatory reporting, market stability concerns, and intellectual property protection. Existing global AI incident databases lack financial sector coverage because they rely on public sources and cannot access proprietary regulatory reports or handle specialized financial data requirements.

The authors propose a regulatory-grade database where regulators report standardized AI incident data without compromising market-sensitive information. This framework uses percentage-based metrics and omits temporal specifics to enable cross-jurisdictional risk analysis while protecting confidential business information. The database design includes 15 mandatory fields across four categories: Market Context, Volume Metrics, Price Impact, and AI-Specific Information, reporting only "Significant Incidents" causing >5% price deviation or >20% volume anomaly.

Two use cases demonstrate utility: systemic risk monitoring showing AI system type affects trading behavior more than geography, and market manipulation detection revealing five distinct trading zones through clustering analysis. The framework addresses algorithmic opacity, enables pattern analysis while preserving confidentiality, and bridges traditional market oversight with emerging AI governance needs.

The Ministry of Finance issued an order amending Rule 80 of the Compendium of Rules on Advances to Government Servants, retaining and modifying provisions for advances to families of government servants who die while in service. The advance amount is capped at Rs. 25,000. The order takes effect from its issue date and does not reopen already sanctioned cases. Indian Audit and Accounts Department cases were issued in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Ministries and Departments must inform attached and subordinate offices of the amendments.

Hockey players Jason Garrison and J.T. Brown discuss their team's resilience through injuries and playoff grind. They emphasize staying confident, avoiding back-to-back poor performances, and maintaining focus internally rather than on outside criticism. Garrison describes a broken play where Fil positioned himself well for a goal. Both express urgency about avoiding elimination and the need to rebound from losses with anger and full effort.

Version 2 of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification introduces hypervisor feature advertisement, initial SEV-SNP support, and various enhancements including XSS MSR value addition, restricted APIC emulation, and shared area requirements. Subsequent revisions add 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers, new error codes for VMGEXIT processing, GUID definitions for VLEK, expanded SW_EXITINFO2 error handling, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL level support, page state change notifications, SEV-TIO for trusted PCIe devices, Secure AVIC, and hardware debug support documentation.

The specification defines a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap for hypervisor capability advertisement, GHCB MSR protocol functions for version negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, page state changes, and VMPL execution. GHCB GPA registration is mandatory for SEV-SNP guests, with support for preferred GPA queries and hypervisor validation.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, page state changes, SNP Guest Requests, SNP Extended Guest Requests, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page management, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Requests, Secure AVIC backing page management, and termination requests. Each NAE event specifies required guest-to-hypervisor and hypervisor-to-guest state transfers through GHCB fields.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests identify support through CPUID properties, with SMP booting requiring special handling due to encrypted register states. The AP Jump Table facilitates environment transitions, while the SNP AP Creation feature enables vCPU hotplug. Restricted Injection limits host interrupt delivery to #HV doorbell notifications, with defined PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for interrupt management. Nested virtualization and SMM are unsupported.

Sweden's unemployment rate held steady at 7.3% in July 2017, but significant disparities persist between native-born Swedes (3.9% unemployment) and those born abroad (21.8%). A record 76,561 foreigners were registered in Arbetsförmedlingen's Introduction Programme, up from 59,362 the previous year, largely due to cleared backlogs from 2015's asylum surge. Long-term unemployment rose from 142,499 to 145,896, with Introduction Programme participants comprising most of this increase. Arbetsförmedlingen has requested additional government funding of 600 million kronor for 2018 and 900 million for 2019.

Derivatives are financial contracts deriving value from underlying assets like commodities, stocks, currencies, or indices. Common types include futures, options, forwards, swaps, and CFDs. Derivatives serve purposes of hedging risk, speculation, or accessing hard-to-trade markets. Futures obligate parties to buy/sell assets at predetermined prices on future dates. Options provide rights (not obligations) to buy (calls) or sell (puts) assets at strike prices by expiration dates. Forwards are privately negotiated future asset trades. Swaps exchange cash flows between parties. CFDs are broker-trader contracts exchanging price differences of underlying assets.

Derivatives trading dates to ancient Greece, with documented olive contracts. Modern derivatives trading emerged in the 1980s. While institutions often hedge risks, retail traders typically speculate. Success rates are low due to market volatility, cognitive biases, and the zero-sum nature where gains equal others' losses. The 2007-2008 financial crisis demonstrated risks from poorly structured derivatives like mortgage-backed securities.

Trading strategies vary by instrument. Futures strategies include specific approaches, while options strategies involve combinations of calls and puts. General strategies across markets include trend-following, mean reversion, and arbitrage. Risk management emphasizes conservative leverage, backtesting plans, and understanding instruments before trading. Interactive Brokers is recommended for retail derivative traders. Key advice includes never trading without understanding, always backtesting, and prioritizing survival over maximizing opportunities.

This paper compares pretrained large language models (LLMs) with small proprietary Transformer models for financial transaction understanding at JPMorgan Chase. The task involves standardizing messy point-of-sale transaction data to identify merchant IDs, processing over 50 million daily transactions with millisecond latency requirements. Previous rule-based and string similarity methods covered only 80% of transactions, leaving 20% unmanaged and costing millions annually in inquiry calls.

The study evaluates three Transformer architectures—Encoder-Only, Decoder-Only, and Encoder-Decoder—comparing pretrained LLMs (SentenceBERT, Llama3-8B, Flan-T5) against proprietary models built from scratch. Experiments on three data types (Rulebased, ESD, Rawcleansed) using weighted accuracy metrics show that proprietary models achieve comparable or better accuracy with far fewer parameters: the proprietary Decoder-Only model reached 72.07% accuracy with 1.7M parameters versus Llama3's 72.89% with 8B parameters, while being 7.7x faster at inference (95ms vs 735ms).

Key findings indicate that larger models are not always better. Optimal configurations vary by architecture: Encoder-Only models perform best with WordPiece tokenization and 1000 vocabulary size, while Decoder-Only and Encoder-Decoder models prefer BPE with 500 vocabulary. Embedding dimensions and layer counts show diminishing returns, with each architecture having distinct optimal sizes.

The proprietary Decoder-Only model was deployed for Rawcleansed data, increasing transaction coverage from 80% to 94% and generating approximately $13.2 million in annual cost savings through reduced inquiry calls. The paper concludes that domain-specific proprietary models can outperform general-purpose LLMs in specialized financial applications when balancing accuracy, speed, and cost.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 21, 2015, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2015. The report includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer. The filing states that the information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and shall not be incorporated by reference into other filings unless expressly set forth.

IHE news editor Katherine Knott and editor in chief Sara Custer discuss White House and Congressional developments affecting higher education, including funding cuts to minority-serving institutions, restrictions on international students, student borrowing rule making, and the "Compact for Academic Excellence." Knott previews upcoming federal policy coverage. The passage also lists article titles on U.S. rankings decline, an accreditor dropping DEI standards, hidden student costs, September budget cuts, and academic staff freedom.

Sunderland manager David Moyes named his team to face Liverpool, with injuries forcing changes: Lamine Kone and Victor Anichebe were out, Donald Love replaced suspended Billy Jones at right-back, and Jack Rodwell returned to midfield. The bench notably included academy players George Honeyman, Josh Maja, Elliot Embleton and Michael Ledger, with only 34 combined Premier League appearances between them. Wahbi Khazri was the most experienced substitute with 24 appearances. Moyes faces limited January transfer funds and aims to strengthen his squad quickly.

GOG's 2017 Piñata Madness event offers random games for $3 each, with prizes valued between $6-$45. Each piñata guarantees a game the buyer doesn't already own, with confirmed titles including Heroes of Might and Magic V, Pillars of Eternity, and Shadow Warrior 2. New games may be added during the event, which runs until August 21, with piñatas automatically opening by August 28 if unopened. The event represents an expansion of the loot box model from in-game items to full game purchases, raising concerns about gambling in gaming.

The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point to 1%–1.25%, the third increase in six months, and announced plans to gradually reduce its $4.5 trillion bond holdings later this year. Despite sluggish economic growth and inflation below its 2% target, the Fed maintains confidence in the economy's durability, with unemployment at a 16-year low of 4.3%. The Fed foresees one additional rate hike this year but gave no timeline. Political uncertainty in Washington and three pending Fed board appointments, expected to shift policy toward a more "hawkish" stance, may influence future rate decisions. Fed Chair Janet Yellen's term ends in February, with Trump sending mixed signals about her reappointment.

Chess, originating in India approximately 1,500 years ago, is a strategic board game defined by researchers as requiring tactical skill, decision-making, and planning. Studies indicate chess improves students' planning ability, critical thinking, concentration, logical thinking, creativity, and mathematical achievement. Chess-playing students demonstrate better school adaptation, academic success, and optimistic attitudes toward education compared to those preferring other activities. The game provides immediate feedback, develops meta-cognitive skills, and enables skill transfer to academic subjects like mathematics and reading. Research suggests chess benefits both gifted students and those with learning disabilities, though some studies question whether observed improvements result from the Pygmalion effect or instructor effort rather than chess itself. Methodological limitations in existing research, including lack of random assignment and active control groups, complicate definitive conclusions about chess's educational impact. Chess expertise develops through knowledge acquisition, experience, and analytical thinking, though the relationship between intelligence and chess skill remains debated. Ideal chess education begins at ages four to five, with classroom integration supporting cognitive development, social skills, and personal growth.

The Horns offense is a basketball set using two high post screeners to create driving options for the ball handler in either direction while clearing baseline help defense. The 1-4 high alignment works well against pressure defenses. The basic option involves point guard dribble penetration off a high post screen, with choices including driving to the basket, pull-up jumpers, return passes to rolling screeners, or kick-outs to wing shooters. When initial action fails, the offense transitions to post isolation or ball reversal with side screens. Success depends on execution, coordination, proper footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication between ballhandler and screener. The offense includes multiple counters for defensive strategies like trailing, sagging, switching, trapping, and showing/recovering. Variations include High Post Rub, Flex, Twin Side Screens, Loop, Picket Fence, and Hand Back Lob. Installation requires breakdown drills and scrimmaging, with emphasis on individual skill development. Game strategy involves scouting opponents, recognizing defensive adjustments, and using multiple alignments to prevent defensive focus.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces accelerated frequency switching for power efficiency and 10x faster sleep state entry than Ada. DLSS 4 features Multi Frame Generation (generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame with 40% faster AI, 30% less VRAM), enhanced Flip Metering, and transformer-based models replacing CNNs for improved temporal stability, detail, and reduced ghosting in Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA.

Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, allowing Tensor Core access in any shader type. Key neural shader applications include: RTX Neural Materials (film-quality assets at game frame rates), Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression), Neural Radiance Cache (real-time global illumination approximation), RTX Skin (real-time subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI face rendering).

The architecture comprises three GPUs: GB202 (flagship, 92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, powers RTX 5090), GB203 (high-end, 45.6B transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, powers RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (performance segment, 31B transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, powers RTX 5070).

A California law allowing courts to issue temporary Gun Violence Restraining Orders resulted in 190 orders in 2016-17. The law permits law enforcement or family members to petition judges to remove weapons from individuals deemed dangerous, following a 21-day cooling-off period with possible one-year extension. Most orders (173 of 190) were not extended beyond 21 days. Law enforcement initiated the vast majority of requests, with only five family-initiated orders in five Southern California counties. Police failed to serve 31 orders. State Senator Nancy Skinner authored the law after the 2014 Isla Vista shooting, and Florida Senator Marco Rubio introduced similar national legislation following the Parkland shooting.

Taco Cabana is offering free breakfast tacos through a "Random Acts of Tacos" promotion with delivery app Favor today from 9-11am. Users in Dallas's delivery zone can request two free tacos via the app banner. Supplies are limited and first-come, first-served. Those who miss out can visit a local Taco Cabana Friday morning for a limited-supply coupon for a free breakfast taco on their next visit.

AMD's Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables non-persistent runtime firmware updates without BIOS reflash or system reset, improving stability and reducing maintenance downtime. SFS patches priority runtime concerns in AMD-provided binary firmware components like ASP firmware and modules, but excludes x86 code (SMM, AGESA, UEFI) and run-once code. Updates are temporary and must be reapplied after reboot.

SFS uses three version identifiers: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), Security Patch Level (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL). AMD cryptographically signs all packages; customers may optionally co-sign to maintain control over deployed updates. The ASP verifies signatures before applying updates.

Application requires a customer SFS Deployment Agent using the PSP/ASP driver, with specific memory alignment requirements. Commands include GET_FW_VERSIONS for version checking and UPDATE_FW for patch application. Package names follow a standardized format tied to AGESA releases.

Security features include AMD's root of trust for detection, optional OEM/ODM co-signing for root of trust for update, and ROM Armor protection. SEV/SNP updates have special handling requirements. Updates run parallel to x86 operations with minimal performance impact, though some operations like SEV firmware updates may require brief VM pauses.

Pharmaceutical dosage form testing systems verify drug efficacy and bioavailability through standard QC tests including weight variation, content uniformity, hardness, friability, disintegration, and dissolution. The global market is expected to grow significantly due to regulatory requirements from organizations like the U.S. FDA and technological advancements, though high costs and skilled personnel shortages may restrain growth. North America leads the market, followed by Europe, while APCEJ and China represent emerging lucrative markets. Key players include SOTAX AG, ABC Laboratories, Almac, and others.

Future Market Insights projects the global surface protection films market will grow from US$ 1,196.2 Mn in 2017 to US$ 2,081.6 Mn by 2027 at a 5.7% CAGR. The 50–100 microns thickness segment holds 38% market share with 6.2% CAGR. PE dominates base materials with over 40% share and 5.8% CAGR, while PET has the highest CAGR at 6.3%. Construction & interior leads end use with over 50% share, projected to reach 56% by 2027. Western Europe holds the largest regional share at 30.4%, followed by APEJ at 22.6%. Mature markets (Western Europe and North America) are expected to exceed US$ 1 Bn combined by 2027. Key players include Chargeurs S.A., Nitto Denko Corp, Tredegar Corporation, and others.

President John Quincy Adams addresses the Senate regarding U.S. participation in the Congress of American Nations at Panama, invited by Colombia, Mexico, and Central America. He seeks Senate approval for nominations and appropriations, though he considers the measure within executive constitutional competency. The U.S. aims to promote liberal commercial principles, maritime neutrality doctrines (free ships make free goods, reasonable blockade restrictions), prevention of future European colonization in the Americas, and religious liberty among newly independent southern nations. The U.S. will not participate in belligerent deliberations or alliances. Adams nominates Richard C. Anderson, John Sergeant as envoys, and William B. Rochester as secretary to advance reciprocity and fraternal friendship with southern republics.

Hollywood Bowl Group's shares rose nearly 8% following strong full-year results: revenue up 9%, like-for-like sales up 3.5%, net cash from operations up 16%, and adjusted underlying earnings after tax up 30%. The company declared its first meaningful full-year dividend (1.9% yield) plus a special dividend (total 3.5% yield). The UK bowling operator opened three new centres and plans further expansion. The author prefers Hollywood Bowl's reliable cash flow over UK Oil & Gas Investments' speculative drilling programme.

Researchers document a significant "Voice Reasoning Gap" (VRG) in voice-interactive AI systems, where models optimized for low-latency streaming show substantially lower performance on complex reasoning tasks compared to text-based counterparts. Using their VERA benchmark, they find voice models average 42% lower accuracy, with gaps exceeding 68% on complex domains like mathematics. The gap persists even with extended thinking time, perfect audio conditions, or decoupled cascade architectures, suggesting a fundamental architectural tension between real-time streaming requirements and the iterative computation needed for deep reasoning. Analysis of 2,931 episodes reveals distinct failure signatures: native streaming models produce fluent but incorrect responses, while decoupled systems suffer grounding and consistency errors. The researchers conclude that bridging the VRG will require novel architectures that explicitly separate reasoning from real-time narration.

Reuters interviewed ARSA fighters and Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh camps following August 25 attacks on Myanmar police posts. New recruits described minimal training, homemade weapons, and WhatsApp coordination; many joined just months earlier expecting AK-47s but fought with knives and sticks. Despite UN condemnation of Myanmar's counteroffensive as ethnic cleansing and their own displacement, most fighters remain committed to continuing the insurgency. ARSA, which emerged in 2016, seeks rights for the stateless Rohingya minority; Myanmar labels it an Islamist extremist group. Analysts warn desperation in camps could fuel further radicalization, with transnational Islamist groups potentially exploiting the situation. Refugee opinion is divided, with some supporting ARSA while others blame the violence for their losses. WhatsApp groups administered from Saudi Arabia and Malaysia helped coordinate and build support. The Myanmar military's ferocious response surprised fighters, who were ordered to disband within weeks.

The Seattle Seahawks defeated the San Francisco 49ers 25-23, rallying from an 11-point deficit. Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson threw for 258 yards and a touchdown before being replaced in the fourth quarter by coach Pete Carroll to rest key players for the playoffs. The win made Seattle the NFC's third seed; they will host Detroit next week. The loss ended a 2-14 season for San Francisco, matching a franchise record for losses. Hours after the game, 49ers coach Chip Kelly and general manager Trent Baalke were fired.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon on October 24-25, 2001, following an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow ran that cost the company $35 million and triggered a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. CEO Kenneth Lay stated the change was necessary to restore investor confidence. Enron's stock fell 17% to $16.41 on October 24, down 50% from the previous week and 80% year-to-date. Multiple analysts downgraded the stock, with Prudential Securities issuing a rare "sell" recommendation. The partnerships LJM Cayman and LJM2, which Fastow managed while serving as CFO, involved potential conflicts of interest and complex off-balance-sheet transactions. McMahon had previously voiced concerns about these arrangements as treasurer before being reassigned in 1999. The SEC launched an informal inquiry, and shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging insider trading and misleading disclosures.

Confirmation hearings for Ronny Jackson, President Trump's nominee for Veterans Affairs secretary, have been postponed amid allegations of professional misconduct. Jackson, the current White House physician, faces accusations of creating a hostile work environment, improperly dispensing medication including Ambien, and being repeatedly drunk on duty while traveling with the president. Trump met with Jackson and publicly expressed support, calling him "one of the finest people," while privately the White House plans to fight the allegations. Questions about Jackson's qualifications to lead the government's second-largest agency existed before these allegations emerged. Some Republicans say they need more time to review the nomination, while critics claim the White House failed to properly vet Jackson.

Gavin, president of Delta College since 2021, will resign in January to lead a national coalition defending equity in higher education. He informed the Board of Trustees last week, stating he felt compelled to take the role despite not seeking a new job. The coalition's priorities and funding will be announced soon. Gavin has been a prominent defender of DEI work in higher education during the second Trump administration, with participation in Education for All increasing as college leaders sought guidance on protecting programs. Delta College trustees will begin selecting his successor in coming weeks.

NVIDIA's Ampere GA102 GPU architecture, part of the GA10x class released in 2020, delivers significant performance improvements over the previous Turing architecture. GA102 powers consumer cards like the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080, as well as professional GPUs including the RTX A6000 and A40 data center GPU.

Key architectural advancements include: 2x FP32 processing throughput by enabling FP32 operations on both datapaths in each SM partition; second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection performance and new hardware-accelerated motion blur support; third-generation Tensor Cores with structured sparsity support for up to 2x throughput and new TF32/BF16 data types; and GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling achieving up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth.

The full GA102 GPU contains 28.3 billion transistors on a 628.4 mm² die, with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores. Other features include third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs), PCIe Gen 4, and RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression. The architecture emphasizes performance per watt, with Ampere GPUs up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at equivalent performance levels.

President Donald Trump attended the opening of the Mississippi Civil Rights Museum in Jackson last Saturday, an event that drew controversy due to his past statements on race. Jackson Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba, who took office in 2017, criticized Trump's policies while emphasizing the museum's significance as recognition of struggle. Several civil rights leaders had threatened to boycott due to Trump's response to Charlottesville. Trump spoke at a smaller, scripted event rather than the main ceremony. Lumumba aims to make Jackson "the most radical city" through people's assemblies, a model of participatory democracy rooted in Black self-determination movements that his father, former Mayor Chokwe Lumumba, helped establish.

The Southern Poverty Law Center released a campus guide titled "The Alt-Right on Campus: What Students Need to Know" to help students respond to alt-right speakers on college campuses. The guide, distributed to over 2,000 schools, advises against giving speakers a "spectacle" or engaging in heated confrontations, instead recommending peaceful protests, educational outreach, and enlisting support from targeted groups. It identifies key alt-right figures like Milo Yiannopoulos and Richard Spencer as white nationalists rebranding white supremacist ideology. The SPLC developed the guide because students and administrators were unprepared for the rise of alt-right campus appearances since 2012, when the first "White Students Union" was founded. The guide's most crucial advice is to avoid direct engagement or violence with speakers.

The TLV32xx comparator family features rail-to-rail inputs (200mV beyond supply rails), 1.8mV internal hysteresis, and two output options: push-pull (sourcing/sinking) and open-drain (sinking-only, 0V–5.5V pull-up). Unused inputs must not be tied together but to voltages with ≥50mV differential. Inputs and outputs have ESD clamps; current must be limited to ≤10mA. The TLV321x includes power-on reset (32µs delay, output held low). Applications include low-side current sensing with amplifier, requiring proper bypassing and PCB layout to prevent oscillations. External hysteresis can be added via resistor networks for inverting or non-inverting configurations.

Randall Margraves, father of three daughters sexually abused by Larry Nassar, attempted to attack the former sports doctor in a Michigan courtroom after Judge Janice Cunningham denied his request for five minutes alone with Nassar. Margraves was tackled by deputies and removed from court, later apologizing for losing control. The judge declined to punish him, acknowledging a father's anguish but stating that "assault with assault" is unacceptable. The incident occurred during Nassar's third sentencing hearing for assaults at Twistars gymnastics club; he already faces life in prison for multiple convictions. Over 200 accusers have spoken in court, including Margraves' daughters Lauren, who told Nassar her parents' guilt "will never go away." Assistant Attorney General Angela Povilaitis urged families to "use your words," not violence. Margraves said he snapped when Nassar shook his head denying the abuse, and insisted he is "no hero."

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a habeas case involving federal prisoner Michael Bowe, who seeks to challenge his firearm conviction through a successive habeas petition. The case presents two procedural questions: whether the Court has jurisdiction to hear Bowe's challenge despite Section 2244(b)(3)(E) barring appeals of authorization denials, and whether Section 2244(b)(1)—which applies to state inmates—was erroneously applied to Bowe as a federal inmate. Bowe's lawyer argued that a dismissal under Section 2244(b)(1) is not a "grant or denial of an authorization" under Section 2244(b)(3)(E), citing a precedent involving threshold questions about successive habeas procedures. The federal government countered that Section 2244(b)(3)(E) clearly limits jurisdiction, and that a dismissal constitutes a denial. The justices questioned both sides on statutory interpretation and potential anomalies in applying the provisions, with particular focus on whether the jurisdictional bar clearly applies to federal prisoners.

This lecture introduces data structures for memory hierarchies, focusing on two models: the external memory model (I/O model) and the cache-oblivious model. The external memory model considers two levels—cache (fast, size M) and disk (slow, infinite)—with data transferred in blocks of size B. Key results include: scanning costs ⌈N/B⌉ memory transfers; B-trees achieve O(log_{B+1} N) search time, which is optimal; sorting can be done in O((N/B) log_{M/B}(N/B)) time; permuting costs the minimum of N and the sorting bound; and buffer trees provide dynamic sorting with amortized O((1/B) log_{M/B}(N/B)) per operation.

The cache-oblivious model (1999, MIT) differs by having algorithms unaware of B and M, with automatic cache management assumed to be optimal. Cache-oblivious algorithms work simultaneously for all B and M, adapting to multi-level hierarchies automatically. Results include: scanning remains O(N/B); search, insert, and delete achieve O(log_{B+1} N); sorting matches the external memory bound; permuting cannot achieve the min of N and sorting bound simultaneously; and priority queues achieve O((1/B) log_{M/B}(N/B)) with the "tall cache" assumption (M = Ω(B^{1+ε})).

The main construction is cache-oblivious B-trees using van Emde Boas layout: recursively split a binary tree at the middle level, lay out subtrees recursively, and concatenate. This gives O(log_B N) memory transfers for search. For dynamic operations, the structure combines van Emde Boas layout with ordered file maintenance (a black box achieving O(log² N) amortized updates with O(log² N/B) memory transfers). Updates propagate changes up the tree in post-order, analyzed by considering levels straddling B. Using indirection with Θ(log N)-sized blocks at the bottom reduces update cost to O(log_B N), matching B-tree performance without knowing B.

Python is an open-source, high-level programming language widely used for algorithmic trading, data analysis, and backtesting. It enables traders to automate trading strategies, analyze large datasets, and execute trades based on predefined rules. Popular backtesting frameworks include PyAlgoTrade, Backtrader, Fastquant, Zipline, and LEAN (QuantConnect), each with distinct features. Backtesting involves testing strategies on historical data to assess potential performance, though it doesn't guarantee future success. While Python offers benefits like readability, extensive libraries, and community support, some argue traders may be better served using dedicated trading software rather than coding from scratch, as strategy quality matters more than coding skill.

A hockey player discusses his team's series-opening victory, emphasizing the importance of the upcoming second game. He praises a new teammate as positive, intense, and a natural scorer who fits well in the locker room. The Kentucky Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and affirmed the Daviess Circuit Court's decision in a workers' compensation case involving David Eugene Bunch. The court clarified that under KRS 342.120(4), the test for determining liability of the Special Fund is not whether an employee is working, but rather the degree of occupational disability evidenced immediately before the subsequent injury. The court rejected the Court of Appeals' interpretation that "dormant" means non-disabling and "active" means disabling, instead reaffirming the test from *Griffin v. Booth Memorial Hospital* (1971). The Workers' Compensation Board had properly excluded 55% of Bunch's disability as attributable to his condition prior to his 1977 work-related injury, finding only 15% compensable by the employer and 30% by the Special Fund for arousal of a dormant condition.

Electronic Arts will go private in a $55 billion leveraged buyout, the largest in history, backed by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners. CEO Andrew Wilson, who joined in 2000 and became CEO in 2013, will remain in his role. While the deal removes Wall Street pressure, Wilson may face demands from new private owners. Shareholders will receive a 25% premium. The move follows a difficult year for EA, including a 17% stock drop in January after cutting its fiscal outlook due to challenges with "EA Sports FC." Analysts note EA's reliance on dated franchises and struggles in mobile gaming. Going private may allow Wilson to focus on innovation through generative AI and expand esports presence with Saudi partners.

Colorado Boy Scout Troop 1532, formed in 2014 by Dr. P.J. Parmar, is composed almost entirely of refugees from Burma, Rwanda, Nepal, and other countries. The troop helps refugee children adjust to American culture while providing a safe space where they can be authentic. Due to parents working long hours and transportation challenges, the troop gathers primarily for camping trips rather than regular meetings. Activities include hiking, fishing, and preparing culturally diverse foods like fish head stew and Chatpate alongside traditional s'mores. The troop faces unique challenges including maintaining adult leadership, membership retention, and behavioral issues, but leaders emphasize teaching discipline and respect. The group serves as a model for attracting refugee youth to scouting nationwide.

The SNB and ECB are exploring linking their instant payment systems (SIC and TIPS) to enable faster cross-border transfers between Switzerland and the eurozone. The exploratory phase runs through 2026, examining technical, economic, legal, and operational feasibility. If implemented, the linkage could reduce reliance on slower, costlier correspondent banking and improve cross-border payment efficiency. Challenges include harmonizing liquidity management, cybersecurity, and regulatory alignment. The project aligns with G20 goals for more efficient global payments and could set a precedent for connecting central bank instant payment systems worldwide.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments on October 14 in a case involving Michael Bowe, a federal inmate challenging his Section 924(c) firearm conviction. Bowe was sentenced to 24 years in 2008 for conspiracy to commit Hobbs Act robbery, attempted robbery, and a firearm offense. Following Supreme Court decisions in 2019 and 2022 that narrowed the definition of "crime of violence," Bowe filed successive habeas petitions seeking to vacate his firearm conviction. The case presents two legal issues: whether 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E) bars Supreme Court review of rulings on successive habeas petitions for federal inmates, and whether 18 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1) applies only to state inmates. The government concedes that Section 2244(b)(1) applies only to state inmates but argues other doctrines could limit repetitive filings. The court appointed Kasdin Mitchell to defend the 11th Circuit's contrary position.

This patent application describes near-eye-display technology using scanning MicroLED arrays for VR/AR/MR systems. High short interest is empirically bad for future stock returns, according to research from Nasdaq and the CFA Institute covering periods from 1973-2020. Stocks with the highest short interest (around 20%) significantly underperform those with low short interest (under 2%). While short squeezes like GameStop in 2021 can cause dramatic price spikes, they are rare outliers rather than norms. Short interest represents the percentage of outstanding shares sold short, while the short-interest ratio measures days needed to cover positions. FINRA requires biweekly short position reporting, making data available through platforms like Seeking Alpha and NYSE subscription files. Short selling is generally difficult due to unlimited risk and long-term market upward trends, though it can serve roles in pairs trading and risk mitigation. Predicting short squeezes remains challenging despite their profit potential.

Multi-agent systems are increasingly important in complex domains, but Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) relies on a limiting single-reward assumption. Real-world agents face multiple conflicting objectives, and while Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) addresses this for single agents, it fails in multi-agent settings where optimal trade-offs depend on other agents' strategies. This strategic coupling problem requires unifying game theory with multi-objective optimization. The paper introduces Multi-Objective Markov Games (MOMG) and Pareto-Nash Equilibrium (PNE) as a solution concept, proving PNE existence in finite MOMGs. It establishes equivalence between PNEs and Nash Equilibria of linearly scalarized games, enabling use of existing solvers. The authors also develop computationally efficient alternatives (WPNE, PCE) and a decentralized online learning algorithm converging to PCE.

This lecture by Zhengzhong Jin covers SNARGs for Batch NP, also known as Batch Arguments (BARGs). A BARG allows a prover to convince a verifier that multiple statements (x₁ to xₖ) in an NP language L are all true using a single succinct proof π, where proof size is smaller than the total witness length. The lecture explains completeness and soundness requirements, noting that BARGs serve as building blocks for SNARGs for all of P.

The construction uses a simplified Kilian's protocol with PCPs, where k PCP proofs are arranged in a matrix. Each column is hashed using a somewhere statistically binding (SSB) hash function constructed from FHE. The SSB hash binds to a specific row i*, allowing extraction of that row's PCP. Correlation-intractable hash functions make the protocol non-interactive. The proof size is poly(λ, |C|, log k), with verification time depending on k·|x| plus terms for log k, circuit size, and security parameter. The verifier can be decomposed into preprocessing (depending on instances) and online phases (independent of k).

This article examines a "Stay Rich Portfolio" designed for wealth preservation after achieving financial independence. The portfolio aims to minimize drawdowns, protect against inflation, and provide steady returns without requiring active management. Analysis of historical data from 1926-2019 shows all asset classes experience significant drawdowns over time, with US and foreign stocks offering the best risk/reward ratios despite higher volatility, while T-bills provide poor long-term protection. The proposed moderately conservative portfolio combines multiple asset classes—US stocks (VTI, VNQ), foreign stocks (VEU), corporate bonds (LQD), TIPS (TIP), and commodities (DBC)—weighted approximately 75% US and 25% international. This diversification across asset classes helps reduce maximum drawdowns compared to single-asset investments, though drawdowns remain unavoidable for long-term results. The article emphasizes that wealth preservation requires different strategies than wealth building, and that short-term market volatility does not equate to permanent capital loss for quality assets.

This MIT lecture on general relativity covers mathematical tools for physics on curved manifolds and introduces geodesics. The professor recaps previous material on tensor calculus: naive derivatives fail to produce tensors, requiring covariant derivatives that preserve tensorial character under transport operations. The covariant derivative emerges from demanding metric compatibility (derivative of metric equals zero). The Lie derivative, involving commutators of vector fields, provides another transport operation with similar correction terms but opposite signs compared to the covariant derivative.

Tensor densities are introduced as quantities transforming like tensors but with additional Jacobian determinant factors. The Levi-Civita symbol is a tensor density of weight 1, while the metric determinant is a tensor density of weight -2. Multiplying tensor densities by appropriate powers of |g|^(1/2) converts them to proper tensors. This construction yields covariant volume elements, exemplified by dV = r² sinθ dr dθ dφ in spherical coordinates.

A "party trick" using the metric determinant simplifies computing contracted Christoffel symbols: Γ^μ_μα = (1/2) g^μβ ∂_α g_μβ = ∂_α ln|g|^(1/2). This follows from linear algebra identities for determinants. This shortcut proves valuable for calculating divergences and expressing Gauss's theorem on curved manifolds, though it fails for general tensors except antisymmetric ones.

The lecture transitions to geodesics—trajectories of test bodies (point masses with no charge, spin, or spatial extent) in curved spacetime. In freely-falling frames, such bodies follow straight lines; covariantly, this means parallel transporting their tangent vectors. This yields the geodesic equation: d²x^μ/dλ² + Γ^μ_αβ (dx^α/dλ)(dx^β/dλ) = 0. Non-affine parameterizations introduce a right-hand side term κu^μ, but reparameterization can always restore affine form where the tangent vector's magnitude remains constant. Proper time serves as the natural affine parameter for timelike trajectories.

An alternative derivation via variational principles shows geodesics extremize proper time between events—actually maximizing it due to relativity's metric signature. The professor notes planned but unaddressed topics: null geodesics for light and using Killing vectors to derive conserved quantities from spacetime symmetries.

This systematic review examines empirical studies on Large Language Models (LLMs) in education, focusing on risks across technical, pedagogical, and societal domains. The authors analyzed 70 papers from 2023–2025, identifying three main application areas: operational effectiveness (feedback generation, data processing, domain knowledge assessment), personalized applications (grading, content generation, predictions), and interactive learning tools (student engagement, cognitive impact, academic performance).

Key technical risks include toxic content, misinformation, bias amplification, hallucinations, and privacy violations. Pedagogical risks encompass cognitive load reduction, memory erosion, diminished critical thinking, metacognitive disengagement, over-reliance, and compromised academic integrity. Societal risks involve the AI divide, data colonialism, environmental harm, and regulatory gaps.

The review finds that GPT models dominate empirical studies, with most research employing comparative evaluation methodologies. The authors propose the LLM-Risk Adapted Learning Model (IMO), mapping how risks emerge across Interaction, Monitoring, and Outcome stages of learning. Mitigation strategies target educators (human monitoring, training, student guidance), developers (robust training, improved detection, learner-centered design), students (verification, responsible use, AI literacy), and governments (data governance, stakeholder collaboration).

The authors emphasize that technical optimization alone is insufficient; LLM-based educational tools must support learner autonomy, competence, and relatedness while ensuring transparency, equity, and accessibility. They call for longitudinal studies, cross-cultural research, and design-oriented investigations embedding mitigation strategies into everyday LLM interactions.

A Commodity Trading Advisor (CTA) is an individual or organization providing personalized advice and services for trading futures contracts, commodity options, and forex contracts or swaps. CTAs manage client accounts directly or run hedge funds using managed futures strategies, investing across global markets including foreign exchange, energies, metals, interest rates, equity indices, and commodities. They are compensated through management fees and incentive fees based on profits exceeding hurdle rates.

CTAs must register with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and become National Futures Association members. While some use discretionary strategies, many employ systematic approaches using algorithmic trading models based on technical analysis, trend following, momentum indicators, and economic data. Systematic CTAs rely solely on algorithm-generated signals without human intervention.

The CTA industry manages approximately $350 billion in funds and managed accounts. Trend following is the predominant strategy, aiming to identify medium to long-term trends through signal generation and exposure sizing. Momentum strategies are also common, often implemented across multiple asset classes using cross-sectional approaches like winners-minus-losers portfolios.

CTAs differ from hedge funds by being limited to derivatives contracts rather than broader securities. Most CTAs now operate as Managed Futures Strategies structured as hedge funds. Effective CTA strategies prioritize having multiple uncorrelated strategies that complement each other to reduce volatility, rather than maximizing individual performance. Simple, systematic approaches with proper risk management are valued over complexity.

The passage argues that new Soviet leader Andropov has personal incentives to pursue arms control agreements due to military/economic pressures and political competition from Chernenko. This paper proposes a meta-learning framework using Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to improve variational data assimilation (4D-Var) by approximating the inverse Hessian operator. The FNO-CG method combines FNO predictions with the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm, using the FNO output as an effective initialization for CG. Experiments on a linear advection equation demonstrate that FNO-CG reduces average relative error by 62% and iteration count by 17% compared to standard CG, with greater improvements in ill-conditioned problems. The approach eliminates the need for separate observation terms in training and shows FNOs can approximate operators beyond PDE solvers. Future work aims to extend this to nonlinear PDEs and chaotic systems.

This article explains the low volatility stock strategy, which involves investing in stocks with lower price fluctuations than the overall market. Low volatility stocks, typically found in sectors like consumer staples, utilities, and healthcare, have a beta below 1 and are considered less risky investments that may provide more consistent returns. Research by Kenneth French from 1964-2015 shows low volatility stocks outperform high volatility stocks over time, with the three lowest volatility deciles never showing negative 10-year returns. Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway confirms this hypothesis, achieving the highest Sharpe Ratio of US stocks listed 30+ years through leverage and focus on cheap, safe, quality stocks. The low volatility anomaly exists in international markets as well. Implementation methods include investing in low volatility ETFs like SPLV, analyzing historical price data, diversifying across sectors, and regularly rebalancing. Strategies to enhance returns include combining with other factors, using leverage, and tactical allocation. However, the strategy requires a long time horizon and carries risks including periods of underperformance and potentially lower short-term returns.

Defensive tackles play a critical role in modern football despite the game's emphasis on passing. Material properties are determined by quantum mechanical equations, commonly approximated by Density Functional Theory (DFT), though its high computational cost limits applications to large systems. Machine learning force fields have emerged as scalable alternatives, with performance depending on atomic representation methods. Current approaches include hand-engineered descriptors, graph neural networks with pairwise interactions, angular embedding methods, and equivariant/invariant GNNs. However, real-space encoders struggle to capture long-term atomic interactions, often mapping distinct crystal structures to identical representations.

This work introduces PRDNet, a multimodal framework integrating graph embeddings with a learned pseudo-particle diffraction module that generates synthetic diffraction patterns invariant to crystallographic symmetries. Reciprocal-space encoding provides a unique, compact representation of crystal structures by capturing complete real-space information without approximation. The pseudo-particle representation serves as a learned probe more effective than conventional physical probes (X-rays, electrons, neutrons) at differentiating atoms in varying chemical environments. The model satisfies geometric constraints including rotation, reflection, and translation invariance. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in crystal property prediction tasks.

The paper introduces Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), a framework for creating incentive-robust LLM summaries that align source incentives with user needs. Unlike standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation approaches that focus only on technical accuracy, TTS addresses how LLM summarization reshapes content creator incentives and creates vulnerabilities to strategic manipulation.

TTS operates through a two-pass pipeline: first, it scores sources using leave-one-out claim generation and multi-task peer prediction to reward informative corroboration; second, it filters low-scoring sources before generating the final summary. This design prevents sources from influencing their own evaluation while structurally aligning truthful reporting with maximum visibility.

Theoretical analysis proves that TTS achieves informed truthfulness (truthful reporting weakly dominates all strategies and strictly dominates uninformed ones) with finite-sample guarantees, and strong truthfulness against significant deviations for sufficiently large claim sets. Empirical evaluation on Natural Questions and ClashEval datasets shows TTS substantially outperforms baselines in answer accuracy (70.7% vs. 22.7-34.0% on NQ; 74.3% vs. 3.3-14.0% on ClashEval) while maintaining robustness against adversarial content, prompt injection, and coordinated uninformative behavior.

In *Magdalena Grafing v. Catharine Heilmann*, the New York court affirmed that savings bank deposits made "in trust for" a beneficiary, even where the depositor retained the passbook and drew interest during his life, create a valid inter vivos trust rather than a testamentary disposition. The court held that the beneficiary's interest vested at the time of deposit, that partial payment of principal to the beneficiary evidenced recognition of her title (not a loan), and that any conditions requiring the beneficiary to pay others did not affect her rights to the fund. The executors' appeal was dismissed.

The 123 pattern reversal strategy is a three-swing price formation indicating potential trend reversals. It forms when price fails to make expected higher highs in uptrends or lower lows in downtrends, with two versions: bearish reversal from uptrends and bullish reversal from downtrends. A 123 bottom is the bullish variant forming in downtrends. Trading rules include entry at point 2 breakout, stop loss below/above point 3, and profit targets measured from pattern structure. Backtests on gold (GLD) showed promising results for bullish reversals, with weaker performance for bearish reversals. The strategy applies to stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin, though stock shorting requires caution.

This patent application describes techniques for cooperative monitoring networks that enable multiple security/monitoring systems to collaborate in detecting, tracking, and responding to events across neighborhoods or communities. The system evaluates detected events against predefined rules to dynamically form cooperative networks between nearby monitoring systems, allowing shared data and coordinated responses. Key components include monitoring system control units with various sensors (motion, environmental, health), cameras, network modules, user devices with surveillance applications, monitoring application servers, and central alarm station servers. The system can track moving entities (intruders, missing persons) across multiple properties by sequentially adding/removing monitoring systems from the network based on location and timing data. It distinguishes between property-specific events (isolated to one system) and cooperative events (affecting multiple systems), with different response protocols for each. Applications include neighborhood security, medical emergencies, mobile device panic alerts, and detecting widespread malfunctions like RF jamming or false alarms from environmental factors.

Hajime, an IoT malware discovered six months ago, has infected approximately 100,000 devices globally and rivals the notorious Mirai malware. Hajime targets ARM-based IoT devices, while Mirai variants affect multiple platforms including ARM, MIPS, and x86. Security researchers have not observed Hajime launching DDoS attacks, and its creators remain unknown. The malware continues to spread 24/7, potentially for future cybercrime or possibly as a research project or vigilante effort against Mirai. Both malware strains exploit poorly secured IoT devices through credential attacks, and experts predict they will persist until vulnerable devices are patched or retired.

MIT finance professor Andrew Lo discusses alternatives to Net Present Value (NPV) for capital budgeting: payback period, discounted payback, Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and profitability index. While NPV remains the recommended method, these alternatives persist in practice due to cultural inertia and their focus on career risk—managers' concern for job security over shareholder value.

Payback period measures years needed to recover initial investment but ignores time value of money, scale, and post-payback cash flows. Discounted payback addresses the time value issue but retains other flaws. Profitability index (present value divided by initial investment) resembles NPV but ignores scale, potentially favoring small high-return projects over larger value creators.

IRR, equivalent to bond yield-to-maturity, finds the break-even discount rate. It fails when cash flows change signs multiple times, producing no solution or multiple solutions, and ignores scale. IRR works only with single upfront investment and strictly positive subsequent cash flows—conditions met in bonds and private equity, explaining its prevalence there.

Survey data shows payback period used by over 80% of large US firms, IRR by 65%, with NPV gaining popularity. Lo notes that while financial analysis provides tools for project evaluation, real-world decisions require incorporating political, social, cultural, and implementation factors beyond pure economics.

This study examined associations between maternal and child gut microbiomes and neurodevelopment in 116 mother-child pairs from the VDAART cohort. Using multinomial regression with reference frames to address data compositionality, researchers found that the maternal gut microbiome showed stronger predictive power (average Q2 ~ 0.21 at class level) for first-year neurodevelopment (ASQ-Y1) than infant (months 3-6) or child gut microbiomes. Predictive power diminished by year two and disappeared by year three. Similar taxa in maternal and infant microbiomes showed different associations with neurodevelopment—for example, Fusobacteriia correlated with high fine motor skills in mothers but low skills in infants. The findings suggest prenatal maternal microbiome influences may be more critical than postnatal vertical transmission for early neurodevelopment, though sample size limitations and need for mechanistic validation are noted.

Scientists observed that 14 of 16 dwarf galaxies orbiting Centaurus A move in a common plane, contradicting the lambda cold dark matter model's prediction of random, spherical distribution. This marks the first such observation outside the Local Group. Study author Marcel Pawlowski suggests considering alternative models, while other astrophysicists like Mike Boylan-Kolchin argue the standard model should not be abandoned, proposing the planar orbits may be a statistical fluke or explained by larger-scale dark matter filaments. Soccer offensive corner kick options expand as players develop strength and accuracy. All offensive corner kicks require a designed play, designated target, and proper service kick. Common types include: Far Post Corner (traditional kick to the far post area using lofted instep drives, with inswingers bending toward goal and outswingers bending away); Near Post Corner (accurate waist-high service to exploit undefended near post); Medium Corner (to areas in front of goal like the 6-, 12-, or 18-corner); Top-of-the-Arc Corner (grounded kick to pull back from defenders); Short Corner (10-yard pass to draw defenders away); Skip Header Corner (flat header flicked across goal); and Direct Score Corner ("Olympico," a curved kick attempting direct goal). Coaches select plays based on player abilities, with takers chosen for passing skill and receivers for heading ability. Teaching progresses from no defenders to full game conditions. Additional tactical considerations include floated-ball corners, wind adjustments, goalkeeper challenges, and proper timing of runs.

This study investigates lubricin glycosylation patterns in osteoarthritis (OA) using a developed Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA). Researchers validated FILA through spike-recovery tests, dilution linearity, and benchmarking against mass spectrometry, finding good agreement between methods. Analysis of matched plasma and synovial fluid (SF) from 19 OA patients revealed that SF lubricin levels were 1-3 orders of magnitude higher than plasma, with distinctly different glycosylation patterns—plasma lubricin showed higher sialylation and lower Tn-antigen content. Comparing 183 OA patients and 38 controls, only SNA-detected glycoforms (sialyl-Tn-antigen with 6-linked sialic acid) showed significantly decreased levels in OA plasma (p=0.0023). BMI positively correlated with sialylation (MAA, SNA, Gal-3), while age showed negative correlation with sialylation (MAA, SNA) and positive correlation with Tn-antigen (MGL). The findings suggest plasma and SF lubricin originate from different tissues, with plasma lubricin likely hepatic-derived, and indicate that metabolic factors and aging influence lubricin glycosylation more than OA pathology itself.

This study examined pneumococcal carriage among community-dwelling older adults to evaluate adult-to-adult transmission. From 2020-2022, 121 individuals aged 60+ from 61 households provided saliva samples every two weeks for six visits. Pneumococcus was detected using qPCR targeting the piaB gene, with 4.8% of samples positive and 22.3% of individuals colonized at least once. Carriage prevalence was substantially higher among those with contact with children (10.4%) versus no contact (2.4%), with highest rates among those contacting children aged 24-59 months (17.8%) or having daily/frequent contact (15.7%). The mean duration of colonization was 17.7 days. While some households had both members colonized, no clear evidence of adult-adult transmission was found; instead, contact with young children was the primary risk factor for acquisition. The study suggests adult pneumococcal vaccination primarily benefits those exposed to children rather than reducing transmission among adults.

The "Double Stack" offense counters the Triangle & Two defense by positioning two posts at mid-post with shooters behind them, creating space and head starts for open shots. This passage details the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD secure encrypted virtualization. It covers the GHCB/VMGEXIT mechanism where guests handle #VC exceptions to communicate with hypervisors via a shared GHCB page, including examples of the protocol flow. The document specifies requirements for SEV-ES guests to determine encryption bit positions before establishing GHCB communication, secrets page usage for SEV-SNP guests, and EFI protocol support for confidential computing blobs.

The passage extensively documents Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events that guests handle through VMGEXIT, including standard processing methods and specific NAE types: IOIO_PROT for port I/O, MSR_PROT for MSR access, VMMCALL for hypercalls, #NPF/MMIO for memory-mapped I/O, Page State Change for memory management, SNP Guest Request for firmware communication, SNP Extended Guest Request for certificates, AP Creation for vCPU management, #HV doorbell page registration, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List retrieval, SNP Run VMPL for privilege level changes, SNP TIO Guest Request for trusted devices, Secure AVIC backing page management, and Termination Request.

Additional sections cover guest identification of SEV-ES support via CPUID, SMP booting challenges and solutions including AP jump tables and the SNP AP Creation feature, NMI handling protocols, debug register virtualization, and SEV-SNP Restricted Injection with #HV doorbell page semantics for interrupt delivery between hypervisor and guest.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1,162 subjects with atrial fibrillation to receive either standard of care (SOC) or an additional educational program, with 1,160 treated with apixaban. At 24 weeks, adherence was 91.64% (Primary SOC) and 91.88% (Additional Educational Program), with no significant difference between groups (p=0.8117). Persistence was also comparable (91.7% vs. 91.3%). At 48 weeks, adherence and persistence remained similar across all groups, with no significant differences. Adherence declined significantly between Week 12-24 and Week 24-48 compared to earlier periods in both groups. Only 28.1% and 26.5% of subjects were fully adherent at 24 weeks, dropping to approximately 14.5-14.9% at 48 weeks. Predictive factors for non-adherence included lower MMSE scores, alcohol consumption, and permanent atrial fibrillation. Safety outcomes were similar between groups, with bleeding events reported in 6.5% (Primary SOC) and 9.0% (Additional Educational Program) at 24 weeks, and 24 deaths total. The additional educational program did not improve adherence or persistence compared to standard care.

A phase 2 clinical trial presented at the 59th ASH Annual Meeting showed that adding Abatacept (Orencia) to standard GvHD prevention reduced severe acute graft-versus-host disease from 32% to 3% in patients receiving mismatched unrelated donor stem cell transplants. Patients receiving abatacept had improved disease-free and overall survival compared to controls. At 100 days post-transplant, grade III-IV acute GvHD occurred in 3% of abatacept patients versus 32% receiving standard treatment. At one year, overall survival was 85% for abatacept patients versus 57-68% for controls. The drug works by blocking activation of effector T cells that cause GvHD while preserving beneficial regulatory T cells. A second cohort of 140 patients with matched unrelated donor transplants completed enrollment in November 2017, with data expected within six months.
