This study examined whether the 2021 CKD-EPI equation (which removed race adjustment) reduced diagnostic disparities for Black patients with chronic kidney disease compared to the 2009 equation. Using electronic health records from over 8 million patients, researchers found significant discordance in CKD staging between the two equations, particularly for Black patients. Nearly 50% of Black patients classified as stage 3a using the 2021 equation were not diagnosed with CKD using the 2009 equation. The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier in 24% of Black patients versus 0.7% of non-Black patients. Multivariate analysis showed Black patients were 126 times more likely to have increased disease staging with the 2021 equation. The study concludes that removing race from GFR estimation improves early identification of CKD in Black patients, potentially enabling earlier treatment and better outcomes.

The device requires minimal maintenance—patients recharge the battery by leaning on a charging pad for 15-20 minutes and use a wireless controller to adjust impulses. Edmonton blogger Barry Kent Winters, 62, was charged June 1 with wilfully promoting hatred under the Criminal Code, an extremely rare charge with only three instances in Alberta in the last six years. The $7 billion Strategic National Stockpile, a federal repository of medical supplies for bioterrorism, nuclear attacks, and disease outbreaks, is being transferred from CDC oversight to the Department of Health and Human Services' Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR). The stockpile, created in 1999, contains antibiotics, vaccines, antivirals, and other supplies stored in at least six secret warehouses nationwide, with enough smallpox vaccine for every American.

This study investigated associations between COVID-19 vaccines and audiovestibular conditions (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo) using two Australian datasets from February 2021 to March 2023: SAEFVIC spontaneous reports and POLAR general practice records analyzed via self-controlled case series (SCCS) methodology.

Results showed increased relative incidence of vertigo following mRNA vaccines (relative incidence: 1.40, 95%CI 1.26-1.56) and increased tinnitus following both adenovirus vector (2.25, 95%CI 1.45-3.50) and mRNA vaccines (1.53, 95%CI 1.25-1.87) in the 42-day post-vaccination window. No increased hearing loss risk was found. Spontaneous reports showed higher rates for adenovirus vector vaccines overall, particularly after dose 1. The SCCS analysis found no sex differences, contrary to spontaneous reports showing higher female reporting. COVID-19 infection status was unknown and may confound results. The multi-dataset approach helped minimize individual biases inherent to each data source.

This lecture explains the Higgs mechanism, which gives masses to gauge bosons (W and Z) and fermions. The problem is that adding mass terms directly to the Lagrangian breaks gauge invariance. The solution is spontaneous symmetry breaking: using a complex scalar field with a "Mexican hat" potential (where μ² < 0), the vacuum expectation value v breaks symmetry. This generates mass terms proportional to coupling strength times v. The Goldstone boson (massless) is "eaten" by the gauge boson's longitudinal polarization, becoming its mass. In the Standard Model's SU(2) × U(1) gauge group, the Higgs field is an SU(2) doublet with four components. After spontaneous symmetry breaking, three Goldstone bosons give mass to W⁺, W⁻, and Z bosons, while the photon remains massless. The remaining scalar is the Higgs boson, predicted in the 1960s–70s and discovered in 2012.

The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, unanimously affirmed Vu Ngo's conviction for three counts of first-degree robbery. The court declined to review Ngo's claim of unlawful peremptory challenge discrimination as it was not preserved for review. The court ruled that Ngo's initial police encounter at a hospital emergency room was not an unlawful detention, and even assuming partial detention for investigation purposes, it did not constitute a forcible seizure. Police developed reasonable suspicion to continue detaining Ngo for a showup identification after another officer arrived investigating a nearby robbery and homicide.

This study investigated enlarged perivascular spaces (PVS) in 467 people with various epilepsy subtypes and 473 healthy controls using T1-weighted MRI and the PINGU deep-learning algorithm. All epilepsy subtypes showed significantly higher PVS volume fractions in the basal ganglia compared to controls (101-140% increase, effect sizes 0.95-1.37), with no difference in white matter PVS. The temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis group exhibited asymmetrical PVS distribution, larger on the contralateral side. No association was found between PVS burden and illness duration. The findings suggest enlarged basal ganglia PVS is common across epilepsy types, though whether this is a cause or consequence of seizures requires longitudinal study.

On June 16, 2016, David M. Shannon, 60, Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary of NVIDIA Corporation, announced his retirement effective end of calendar year 2016. Shannon joined NVIDIA in August 2002 and oversees legal and human resources functions. Senior Vice President and General Counsel Brian E. Cabrera, 51, will lead the legal team upon Shannon's retirement; NVIDIA will recruit a new human resources leader.

Redundancy management improves reliability in safety-critical systems like avionics and nuclear control. This work presents a correct-by-construction fault-tolerant voter unit for N-modular redundant measurement systems, formally verified using the Rocq theorem prover. The voter selects reliable inputs from redundant units that may have transient or permanent faults, using a noise-resilient voting algorithm with multi-cycle history. The design includes configurable parameters (noise threshold, persistence limit, maximum simultaneous faults) and satisfies 16 formal requirements covering fault identification, permanent fault isolation, and output generation. The voter maintains soundness and completeness properties for fault detection, avoids frequent prime unit switching, and handles boundary cases through validity states (valid, unidentifiable, not valid). The Rocq implementation carries embedded proofs of invariants, with extracted OCaml code of 362 lines executing in ~3ms per cycle.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolution, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) on May 29, 2018. The ANN was adopted by the Nigerian Intervention Movement (NIM), of which YesWeFit is a part. Ikubese, who left the National Conscience Party two weeks prior over alleged over-taxation, will run for president under ANN. He urged other young aspirants and his supporters to join the party, calling it a "third force" for Nigeria's recovery and progress.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which facilitates moving memory pages between physical tiers while maintaining guest physical addresses. TMPM enables migration of pages during concurrent DMA operations and migration of SNP-protected guest pages that hypervisors cannot otherwise access.

The system requires IOMMU enablement and uses a ring buffer command interface. Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for hypervisor pages with DMA coordination, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages using a Pre-Migration state. Commands support batching up to 128 pages for efficiency.

Initialization involves checking ENGINE_READY, configuring the ring buffer with 1-255 contiguous 4KB pages, and setting PAGEMIGRATION_EN in IOMMU registers. The interface provides interrupts for completion, errors, queue empty, and threshold conditions. Firmware can be reloaded via BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol when operations are paused.

Performance optimizations include using 16+ page commands, with 128 pages achieving maximum bandwidth, and avoiding per-command interrupts. Restrictions include 4KB-aligned addresses, no migration of IOMMU data structures or ring buffer pages, and prevention of concurrent IOMMU host PTE modifications during TMPM operations.

Doctors emphasize the need for greater awareness about eye cancer after noting most cases in India are detected at late stages, making treatment complex. Ocular oncologist Bikramjit Pal highlighted that eye cancer, while uncommon, can cause blindness or death if not caught early. He cited scarce specialized treatment facilities and only 10-11 trained ocular oncologists nationwide. Pal identified Retinoblastoma as the most common childhood eye cancer, affecting 1 in 20,000 children under five, which is treatable if detected early but potentially fatal if delayed.

This study examines how online informal education contributes to personalized learning in design education. It distinguishes between formal, non-formal, informal, and random education, highlighting how digitalization has transformed learning through virtual environments, multimedia tools, and global collaborative networks. The research analyzes two case studies—a synchronous workshop on computational design by Driven by Volumes and a course on sustainability through computational design by Rethinking the Future—to assess their structural and cognitive components. Findings indicate that online workshops and courses provide applied, multidisciplinary learning with discussion environments and open access, but face limitations including individual material requirements, competitive dynamics, unequal certification recognition, and lack of integration into formal transcripts. The study concludes that while informal online education fosters personalization, collaboration, and efficient skill acquisition, its exclusion from mandatory curricula and economic accessibility barriers create contradictions with universal education principles.

This study develops and evaluates an integrated environmental education model based on the theory of multiple intelligences for students in expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Province, Thailand. The research involved 364 junior high school students, 44 teachers, and 3 school directors across 22 schools. A SWOT analysis identified community environmental issues including soil, water, and air pollution from agricultural chemicals, as well as waste pollution from indiscriminate disposal. Students showed lowest awareness (3.79) and participation (3.90) in environmental education, while teachers demonstrated excellent overall environmental learning levels (4.48). The developed integration model achieved efficiency criteria of 81.51/82.11, with high content validity (4.60) and construct validity (3.97). Post-study achievement scores increased significantly from 5.90 to 24.63, and students reported high satisfaction (3.83) with the integrated model. The study recommends promoting environmental education awareness through holistic, practical learning systems that connect classroom knowledge with real-world applications.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench of India's Supreme Court ruled that re-promulgation of ordinances constitutes fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. The majority judgment, authored by Justice DY Chandrachud, held that placing ordinances before the legislature is mandatory, though Justice Madan B Lokur disagreed and the Chief Justice left the question open. The Court determined that presidential and gubernatorial satisfaction under Articles 123 and 213 when issuing ordinances is subject to judicial review. The case arose from Bihar government ordinances appointing school teachers who were not regularized. The Court ruled that rights and obligations surviving a lapsed ordinance must be determined by construction, and held that salaries already paid to teachers need not be recovered.

Solar energy has become the cheapest power source globally, with costs as low as £0.02 per unit in sunny countries, according to a University of Surrey study. Global solar capacity reached 1.5 terawatts in 2024, double 2020 levels. Lithium-ion battery prices fell 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems cost-competitive with gas plants. However, grid congestion and integration pose significant challenges, requiring smart grids, AI forecasting, and regional interconnections. Innovations like perovskite solar cells could increase output by 50%, while sustained policy support remains essential for accelerating the clean energy transition.

An 1893 anonymous notice by Mr. Kung-i of Pai-ling Shan attacks foreign religious teachings as false and corrupting, accusing missionaries of deception, hypocrisy, and exploitation, and threatening violent attack on the 7th of the third moon if they do not depart. A separate 1894 dispatch reports that Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned their king to compel Tong Hâk members to return to orthodoxy or be exterminated; the king responded that the government would handle the matter while admonishing petitioners to study their own principles.

A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and voltage reference (VREF). When VIN is below VREF, output is low; VIN must rise above threshold VIN1 to switch high. When VIN exceeds VREF, output is high; VIN must drop below VIN2 to return low. Hysteresis equals VIN1 minus VIN2.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 26, 2015, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014, with the press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

A bull market signal strategy uses 18 consecutive closes above the 200-day SMA in a bear market as a buy signal, selling when the S&P 500 drops 20% from its all-time high. Backtested from 1927, it generated 12 signals with a 7.24% CAGR, 15.26% standard deviation, and 60% maximum drawdown (25% excluding 1929). The S&P 500 averaged 9.54% gains six months and 21.84% one year after the signal. Compared to the Golden Cross strategy, this model produces fewer false signals (12 versus 49) while being invested 30% more time. The last signal triggered on February 15, 2023.

St. George, Utah welcomed an 11-person delegation from its sister city Ibigawa, Japan in October 2017, continuing a nearly 30-year cultural exchange tradition. The visit included four runners competing in the St. George Marathon, with Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita ranked among the top 20 elite runners in their respective categories. The delegation was welcomed by Mayor Jon Pike and other officials at multiple events, including a reception, city council meeting, and international luncheon where Pike and Ibigawa Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji exchanged ceremonial gifts. The visitors stayed with local host families and toured area attractions including Zion National Park. St. George planned to send a return delegation to compete in Ibigawa's marathon the following month.

Ola and Uber drivers in Delhi-NCR threatened a one-day strike on Tuesday over low fares and 25% commission charges, demanding rates increase from Rs 6 to Rs 20 per km. The Delhi High Court issued a permanent injunction against two taxi-driver unions from disrupting services. The Sarvodaya Drivers' Association, claiming to represent 1.25 lakh app-based taxis, organized a protest march to the Chief Minister's residence and warned of indefinite strike if demands are unmet. While some tourist taxi and autorickshaw groups supported the strike, Delhi Autorickshaw Sangh and Delhi Pradesh Taxi Union declined participation.

Rain Bird's WPX is a 9V battery-operated irrigation controller designed for locations without mains power or where cable installation is impractical. IP 68 rated and fully submersible, it suits wet or muddy valve box installations. Available in 1, 2, 4, or 6 zone models, it features LCD screen programming, Contractor Rapid Programming™ for quick setup, and automatic zone-stacking. Battery life extends approximately one year with one 9V battery or two years with two. Contact: +44 7575 626600, www.rainbird.eu.

A hockey player describes scoring a goal on a set play with Teemu Selanne, with Brad May as his winger, during a line change at the end of a shift. He notes the goal wasn't as emotional as expected, and the team focused on staying disciplined after a strong second period to finish the game.

A study in Nature Ecology & Evolution found that birds and mammals adapt to temperature changes 2-3 times faster than reptiles and amphibians, based on analysis of 300 million data points across 11,500 species over 270 million years. Endotherms' ability to regulate body temperature and control their offspring's development temperature aids their adaptability. However, researchers caution that current climate change occurs too rapidly for these historical patterns to apply, and other factors like pollution, hunting, and habitat loss pose greater immediate threats. Species are currently disappearing up to 10,000 times faster than normal, with about 25% of mammals and 12% of birds threatened with extinction.

The passage describes SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication protocols, including VMPL level transitions, SEV-TIO trusted device binding, SNP TIO Guest Request NAE events with specific register usage for PCI ID, MMIO ranges, and TDISP status, Secure AVIC backing page management, termination requests, AP booting challenges and solutions using AP jump tables, SNP AP Creation NAE events for vCPU hotplug support, NMI handling conventions, debug register virtualization, and #HV doorbell page mechanisms for interrupt delivery with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields governing host-guest signaling and EOI optimization.

Kuwait will complete cleanup of a crude oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, according to Oil Minister Essam al-Marzouq, who stated no new oil patches have been found. The cause and magnitude of the spill near Ras al-Zour—where Kuwait is building a major refinery—remain undisclosed. Khajfi Joint Operations, which operates in the Kuwait-Saudi Neutral Zone, denied media reports that a tanker caused the spill, stating its facilities were safe and that it activated emergency protocols and planned aerial surveys. The Khafji oilfield has been shut since October 2014 for environmental reasons, while Wafra has been closed since May 2015 due to operating difficulties.

This patent application describes an augmented reality system for image-guided surgery using head-mounted displays worn by healthcare professionals. The system includes tracking devices on the head-mounted devices that monitor patient markers and tool markers to align computer-generated images with actual patient anatomy, typically requiring misalignment of no more than 2-3 mm. When the primary tracking device loses line of sight with markers, the system incorporates data from additional tracking devices—either from another healthcare professional's head-mounted device or from a stationary room-mounted device—to maintain accurate image alignment. The patient marker uses an array of elements providing unique appearances at different locations and orientations, enabling single-camera tracking without triangulation. The system can display virtual tool and anatomy images overlaid on actual patient anatomy, show another healthcare professional's view when line of sight is blocked, or continue displaying from the last known position using inertial measurement units when markers are obscured.

Investors who had been optimistic about economic strength and corporate profits are now concerned that rising wages may signal higher inflation, potentially causing central banks to end the era of cheap money that has fueled the nine-year stock market boom. This shift in sentiment led to a major stock sell-off and surging Treasury yields.

Market corrections (10-20% drops) occur annually on average, with 80% not becoming bear markets (>20% drops). Historically, corrections average 13.5% declines lasting 54 days. Bear markets average 33% drops, lasting about one year, but markets rose in 75% of years from 1980-2015 despite regular declines. Warren Buffett and Jack Bogle emphasize staying invested through volatility, as impatience transfers wealth to patient investors.

The TPS7H500x-SP series controllers feature single or dual primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) with ~150 mA peak current capability, requiring external gate drivers. OUTB and SRB are only active when DCL is connected to AVSS for 50% duty cycle limit, valid for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. Synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) activate when SS exceeds 1V. Dead times (TDSP/TDPS) and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors (10 kΩ–300 kΩ) on PS, SP, and LEB pins; TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50 ns dead time and blank time. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP < 0.3V and previous duty cycle < 25%, maintaining volt-second balance. Duty cycle limits are configurable: 50% (DCL=AVSS), 75% (floating), or 100% (DCL=VLDO). Peak current mode control uses CS_ILIM compared to COMP/2 with 150 mV offset; overcurrent at 1.05 V triggers hiccup mode with programmable delay via CHICC (minimum 3.3 nF). FAULT pin enables external protection with 0.6 V threshold and 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width. Slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation via RSC resistor. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C, resuming at 160°C. The controllers operate from 4–14 V with 0.1 µF minimum bypass capacitance, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge up to 2 MHz.

The speaker advocates for government supervision rather than ownership of businesses, arguing that combination of capital and labor is necessary but requires rigorous regulation to prevent public harm. Current laws prohibiting all combinations are ineffective and create unintended negative consequences; instead, railroad agreements should be permitted with Interstate Commerce Commission approval and public disclosure. On taxation, the speaker supports federal graduated inheritance and income taxes, emphasizing that wealthy individuals owe special obligations to the state, while insisting that such taxes must be implemented with absolute fairness and moderation toward both rich and poor.

Apple Inc. filed its Q2 2018 Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended March 31, 2018. The company reported net sales of $61.1 billion (up 16% year-over-year) and net income of $13.8 billion for the quarter. Key financial highlights include: iPhone net sales of $38.0 billion (62% of total), Services revenue of $9.2 billion (up 31%), and gross margin of 38.3%. The company had $45.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $267.2 billion in total cash and marketable securities. Apple repurchased $32.9 billion in common stock and paid $6.5 billion in dividends during the six-month period. The company adopted new accounting standards for share-based compensation and recorded a $2.6 billion provisional tax expense related to the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered the federal rate from 35% to 21%. Apple faces ongoing litigation including a $503 million patent infringement verdict from VirnetX and a €13 billion European Commission state aid decision regarding Ireland. The company announced a new $100 billion share repurchase authorization in May 2018.
Two teens arrested and a third is at large after a pursuit in Frankston. A 17-year-old girl and 18-year-old man fled a stolen car in Bayswater; he was hospitalized after a police dog bite.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated May 18, 2001, contains news summaries about Enron and energy markets. Key stories include: California's long-term power contracts losing value as forward prices decline, with the state potentially facing $6.5 billion in losses; options market activity showing investors selling options amid flat market expectations, including bullish Enron options trades; and Saudi Arabia selecting international oil companies for three major natural gas projects worth $25 billion, with Exxon Mobil and Shell winning major roles and Enron receiving a stake in the Red Sea project alongside Occidental Petroleum. The Saudi deals mark the first major foreign investment in the kingdom's energy sector since nationalization in the 1970s.

This case study details the collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX and its founder Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF). FTX, founded in 2019, became the world's second-largest crypto exchange by early 2022, valued at $32 billion. The company collapsed in November 2022 after a leaked balance sheet revealed that Alameda Research (SBF's trading firm) held 40% of its assets in FTT tokens (FTX's self-created cryptocurrency), triggering a run on FTX as customers withdrew $6 billion in 72 hours. FTX filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022, revealing an $8.9 billion shortfall in customer funds.

SBF and key executives—Gary Wang, Caroline Ellison, and Nishad Singh—were charged with fraud for diverting billions in customer funds to Alameda for venture investments, real estate, and political donations. Singh, who wrote code enabling the diversion and inflated FTX's 2021 revenues by $50 million, pled guilty in February 2023. Wang and Ellison also pled guilty and cooperated with prosecutors; SBF pled not guilty.

The case examines regulatory gaps, with the SEC and CFTC disputing jurisdiction over crypto, and failures by investors and auditors (Prager Metis and Armanino) to demand adequate governance. FTX operated with no independent board, no CFO, and no accounting department. The collapse raised questions about accountability across investors, auditors, regulators, and celebrity endorsers.

Penn State University has banned the student-led Outing Club from organizing outdoor trips starting next semester, citing safety risks from remote environments with limited emergency access. The 1920-founded club and two other outdoor groups—the Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Nittany Divers SCUBA Club—were not consulted during a two-month risk review. While the university emphasizes student safety and will continue offering costlier university-operated trips, student leaders criticize the lack of dialogue and note the difference between paid guides and peer-led experiences.

Android 8.0 Oreo, released in August, includes Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, which allows videos to play in a floating window while using other apps. Unlike Android 7.0's split-screen multi-window, PiP works at the OS level across supported apps. Supported apps include Google Chrome, Duo, Play Movies & TV, Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube (requires YouTube Red), and VLC. To use PiP with YouTube without Red, open YouTube in Chrome's desktop mode, play a video in full-screen, then press the home button. The video becomes a movable floating window that can be paused, closed, or returned to full-screen. If PiP doesn't work, enable it in Settings > Apps & notifications > Advanced > Special app access > Picture-in-picture.

In *Thomas Henderson v. Alex. Beaton*, the Supreme Court of Texas held that an 1839 instrument from Mastín Latham to William F. Henderson constituted an absolute deed conveying an undivided half interest in land, not an executory contract. The court rejected defenses of stale demand and statutes of limitation (three, five, and ten years), noting the absence of tax payment evidence for the five-year claim, lack of privity for the ten-year claim, and that possession was held under Latham's title rather than under defendants' chain of title. The judgment for defendants was reversed and the cause remanded.
Gifts to the Annual Fund support democracy, the rule of law, independent courts, and access to justice. Donors receive stickers and magnets.

President Madison reports to Congress that diplomatic efforts to end European trade restrictions have failed, with Britain rejecting a proposal to rescind its orders in council and France not responding. The embargo therefore remains in effect, though it has protected American shipping and allowed time for defensive preparations. Congress must now decide on further measures. Relations with Spain are paused due to internal crisis; harmony continues with Barbary powers except for an incident with Algiers; peace is maintained with Indian tribes, with some groups seeking closer ties. Coastal defenses and gunboat construction are underway, military recruitment is progressing, and domestic arms production is being expanded. The suspension of foreign trade has spurred internal manufacturing. Treasury receipts totaled nearly $18 million, allowing debt reduction and leaving $14 million on hand. Madison concludes by expressing gratitude and confidence in the nation's future.

Ukraine has partnered with Bitfury Group to implement blockchain technology for government data in what is described as likely the largest such project globally. Following a memorandum of understanding, a pilot project launching late this year will cover state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy, eventually expanding to all government electronic data. This initiative exceeds smaller blockchain programs in countries such as Sweden, Estonia, and Georgia.

Investors face five key themes this week. The Bank of England holds its "Super Thursday" with no rate change expected, though markets will focus on inflation and growth outlook amid sterling's surge to $1.43. Australian and New Zealand central banks meet as housing markets cool and currencies strengthen, while China releases monthly economic data. The U.S. December trade deficit is expected to widen to $51.7 billion on record imports, with another government shutdown looming as funding expires Thursday. Corporate earnings reveal a growth gap between European and U.S. equities, with European stocks trading at a 9 percent discount to U.S. peers. Finally, emerging market central banks meet, with Russia expected to cut rates while Mexico and Romania may hike.

Joseph McGreal, a former Orland Park police officer, sued the Village of Orland Park and three police officials, claiming his 2010 firing violated his First Amendment rights and constituted intentional infliction of emotional distress. McGreal alleged he was terminated for presenting cost-saving alternatives at a November 2009 village board meeting that protected lower-level officers. The defendants argued McGreal was fired for legitimate misconduct, including lying under oath, insubordination, and reckless driving. The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court's summary judgment dismissal, finding McGreal provided no admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his protected speech or that their alternative explanations were pretextual. The court also rejected his emotional distress claim, noting McGreal himself characterized his distress as "garden variety," insufficient under Illinois law.

HoopTactics provides proven baseline, sideline, and full court out of bounds plays designed to create high percentage shots with multiple options, flowing into continuity if unavailable. Full court situations require preparation for pressure defense with 5-on-4 advantage, utilizing best players and shooters while scouting tendencies. End-of-game strategies include advancing for timeouts or safely inbounding with free throw shooters on court.

Kyle Freeland pitched effectively into the sixth inning and doubled to help the Colorado Rockies defeat the San Francisco Giants 11-4. Every Rockies starter recorded at least one hit, including David Dahl's first career pinch-hit home run. The Giants lost two pitchers to injury: starter Jeff Samardzija left with shoulder tightness after one inning, and rookie Dereck Rodriguez, making his major league debut, was removed after being struck by a line drive. Evan Longoria hit two home runs for San Francisco. Colorado took advantage of three Giants errors to score unearned runs.

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old high school senior from Rome, Georgia, will donate a kidney to her grandfather, Sam Senseney, 63, after being found to be a perfect match. Senseney has been on dialysis for six years while waiting for a transplant, with 2,000 others ahead of him on Georgia's kidney transplant list. Maddie spent two years raising $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund and advocating for organ donation through the Miss Georgia Outstanding Teen Pageant. Though initially told she was too young to donate, she convinced doctors to approve the surgery, which is expected to take place within the next month. Maddie will miss three weeks of her senior year for the procedure.

This patent application describes embodiments for Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) selection in 5G systems supporting network slicing. It defines three network slice isolation levels: fully isolated (no shared network functions), partly isolated with shared Radio Access Network (RAN), and partly isolated with shared RAN and AMF. During registration, a User Equipment (UE) sends a Requested Network Slice Selection Assistance Information (NSSAI) and network slice isolation information (indicating isolation type/level) to the (R)AN. For fully isolated slices, a Network Repository Function (NRF) selects the AMF. For partly isolated slices with RAN shared, a Network Slice Selection Function (NSSF) selects the AMF. For partly isolated slices with RAN and AMF shared, Unified Data Management (UDM) selects the AMF. Selection is based on requested/subscribed NSSAI, network slice isolation information, UE identifiers, Data Network Names (DNN), and subscription data obtained from the UDM, enabling the UE to register and establish PDU sessions via the appropriate network slice instance.

Astronomers from Trinity College Dublin used the James Webb Space Telescope to observe fierce auroras, storms, and unchanging sand-like clouds on the rogue planet SIMP-0136. The planet, which exceeds 1,500°C and lacks a host star, showed strong auroral activity heating its upper atmosphere and temperature variations smaller than 5°C linked to storm activity. The silicate-based cloud coverage remained constant across the surface. This research, led by Dr. Evert Nasedkin and published by the 'Exo-Aimsir' group, represents the first direct measurement of atmospheric property changes on an extrasolar object. The findings advance understanding of alien atmospheres and exoplanet weather processes.

In an 1908 California appellate case, E.F. Joy (assignee of creditor W.W. Montague & Co.) sought to set aside deeds of gift from Louis Helbing to his wife Louise, executed in May 1893 when Helbing was solvent but unrecorded until December 1895. Between September-December 1895, Helbing obtained approximately $1,000 credit from Montague & Co. by representing himself as owner of the conveyed property, and continued exercising acts of ownership including insuring property in his own name and filing insurance claims. The trial court found no fraudulent intent, noting the wife lacked knowledge of her husband's representations. The appellate court affirmed, holding that (1) intent to defraud creditors is determined from all facts and circumstances, (2) the two-year recording delay was suspicious but insufficient alone to prove fraud, (3) the burden to prove fraudulent intent rested on plaintiff, and (4) exclusion of testimony about events four years post-deed (concealed goods and wife's 1897 ownership claim) was harmless error as it bore no connection to the deed's execution.

Tropical Storm Nate, the 15th Atlantic system this year, threatens to hit the U.S. Gulf Coast as a hurricane this weekend after killing 22 people in Latin America. Louisiana declared a state of emergency and ordered coastal evacuations. Gov. John Bel Edwards mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops and urged residents to prepare by Saturday evening. Forecasters project Nate will strengthen over the Caribbean and make landfall as a Category 1 hurricane. This year's hurricane season is the most active in over a decade, with September setting a record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy. Nate caused 15 deaths in Nicaragua and 7 in Costa Rica, where 5,000 residents fled to emergency shelters.

The article examines a pair trading strategy between SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (Treasury bonds) following significant opposite-direction moves. Triggered by the June 18, 2021 market event where SPY rose 1.43% and TLT fell 1.67%, the strategy tests going long SPY and short TLT when both ETFs move beyond 1.25 times their 50-day average high-minus-low on the same day. Backtesting from 2003 to June 2021 yielded erratic results with a 1.93% CAGR, 60% win rate, and 0.18% average gain per trade. Adjusting holding periods (optimal at 3 days) or movement thresholds failed to improve performance significantly, leading to the conclusion that the strategy is not tradeable.

This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed factors causing delayed discharge (length of stay [LOS] >15 days) from a 23-bedded Complex Discharge Unit (CDU) at St James's Hospital, Dublin, during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020–February 2021). Of 390 patients admitted, 83.6% were over 65 years old, 59.7% were female, and 48.2% had more than four comorbidities. The median LOS was 19.4 days. Using Kaplan-Meier and stratified Cox regression analyses, the study found that patient-centred needs (including cognitive dysfunction, psychosocial needs, and carer involvement) and complications arising from primary diagnoses or multimorbidity were significant factors prolonging LOS. Patients aged 65–75 years, females, and those with greater than four multimorbidities were more likely to experience prolonged LOS. However, healthcare-associated infections, frailty or falls necessitating integrated rehabilitation, and community services were not significant contributing factors to delays exceeding 15 days. The analysis concluded that addressing complexities arising from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs is imperative for reducing LOS and improving outcomes.

OpenAI is preparing to launch a stand-alone social app for its video generation AI model, Sora 2. The app features a vertical video feed with swipe-to-scroll navigation, similar to TikTok, with all content being AI-generated. It includes a "For You" recommendation page and options to like, comment, or remix videos.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) is an investment strategy allocating 90% to low-cost S&P 500 index ETFs and 10% to government bonds, inspired by Buffett's 2013 letter to Berkshire Hathaway investors. The approach emphasizes passive investing, long-term growth, reduced risk, and lower fees compared to actively managed funds. The S&P 500 component provides exposure to 500 large U.S. companies with historically strong returns, while government bonds offer stability against market volatility. Three backtests compared different bond maturities: SHY (short-term), IEI (intermediate), and TLT (long-term). Results showed longer maturities yielded better compensation for added risk, with TLT performing nearly on par with 100% SPY allocation. The strategy suits beginners due to its simplicity, and implementation options include lump-sum investing or dollar-cost averaging. Risks include market volatility and interest rate changes, while tax implications depend on individual circumstances.

Bank of England research suggests a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could strengthen monetary policy transmission to the real economy. While not currently planning to issue one, the Bank has extensively studied CBDC design, including how interest-paying digital currencies could give the central bank greater monetary control. Commercial banks would need to respond faster to rate changes to retain deposits. A CBDC could also improve quantitative easing by allowing direct asset purchases from non-banks without banking intermediaries. Sweden's Riksbank is actively considering its own digital currency.

In People v Schaub, the Michigan Court of Appeals reversed a circuit court order reinstating a child abandonment charge against Lawrence Schaub, who sold his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for $60,000. The court held that while sufficient evidence existed to show intent to wholly abandon, the prosecution failed to prove "exposure" under MCL 750.135. Following Shannon v People (1858), the court ruled that exposure requires placing a child in circumstances creating reasonable apprehension of personal injury hazard; here, the child was transferred directly to a caregiver and never left without care. Judge O'Connell dissented, arguing that selling a child to a total stranger creates sufficient risk of injury to constitute exposure, making it a jury question. The majority noted the Legislature subsequently enacted MCL 750.136c specifically prohibiting child selling.

American citizens in Cuba, particularly in rural central and eastern districts, face destitution due to displacement from farms and lack of work or money. Local authorities cannot assist them. Consul-General Lee reports 600-800 Americans without support. The President recommends Congress appropriate at least $50,000 for immediate relief under the Secretary of State, with discretion to also fund transportation for citizens wishing to return to the United States.

The editor acknowledges assistance from staff at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, Library of Congress, CIA, and Office of the Historian, plus permissions from the Haig and Kirkpatrick estates. Walmart plans to expand drone deliveries to most areas where it operates, according to senior vice president Greg Cathey. The company has been testing drones for over five years and has surpassed 300,000 deliveries. Walmart is expanding its partnership with Alphabet's Wing to 100 stores across five cities, plus Northwest Arkansas, with plans to add "a lot" more locations. Cathey cited the evolving regulatory environment as enabling business viability. While widespread drone delivery remains years away due to technical, regulatory, and infrastructure challenges, Walmart's plans signal that major companies now see a clear path to scale. The retailer has also partnered with Zipline and previously worked with DroneUp. Wing is one of few companies FAA-approved for beyond-visual-line-of-sight delivery in Dallas.

The Golden Cross Trading Strategy uses the 50-day and 200-day moving averages to generate buy and sell signals. A Golden Cross occurs when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average, signaling a buy; a cross below signals a sell. Backtesting on the S&P 500 since 1960 showed 33 trades with 79% winners, averaging 15.8% gain per trade and 6.8% annual return. While this underperforms buy-and-hold's 7.2% annual return, the strategy was only invested 70% of the time, yielding a 9.6% risk-adjusted return and a lower maximum drawdown of 33% compared to buy-and-hold's 56%. The strategy aims to capture long-term uptrends while reducing losses in bear markets.

A cross-sectional study of 424 HIV patients at Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda found 13% non-adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART). Significant factors associated with non-adherence included: age under 31 years (AoR 15.462), lack of tertiary education (AoR 8.232), experiencing stigma (AoR 2.148), perceiving ART as ineffective (AoR 9.333), and failure to integrate ART into daily routines (AoR 11.180). Setting alarms as reminders showed no significant association with adherence. The study used stratified random sampling from March-April 2024, with data analyzed via SPSS using Fisher exact tests and logistic regression. Rwanda provides free universal ART access, with 94% of HIV-positive individuals aware of their status and 91% achieving viral suppression as of 2022. The 13% non-adherence rate compares favorably to rates of 22.9% in Ethiopia, 30.4% in Nigeria, 25% in Uganda, and 28% in South Africa.

In a 1989 case, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Indiana granted summary judgment for prison officials in a § 1983 action brought by inmate Richard Milan. The court ruled that Milan failed to establish a constitutionally protected liberty interest in visitation privileges under the Due Process Clause, applying Supreme Court precedent from *Hewitt v. Helms* and *Kentucky Department of Corrections v. Thompson*. While prison officials failed to provide written notice of the denial as required by administrative procedure, this procedural defect alone did not create a substantive constitutional violation. The court also denied Milan's cross-motion for summary judgment.

E-learning governance provides strategic direction, ensures objectives are achieved, manages risks, and allocates resources for organizational e-learning initiatives. This paper defines e-learning as networked ICT use to enhance learning, and e-learning ecosystems as learning communities united by learning management systems. The authors propose an e-learning governance framework comprising four elements: structures (roles, responsibilities, committees), processes (strategic planning, regulations, resource management), communications and relational mechanisms (stakeholder collaboration, cross-functional communication), and pedagogies and instructional designs. They adopt Darking's six characteristics and dimensions of digital ecosystem governance: constitution and balance of interests, culture of communication, credibility/attunement/trust, organization and synchronization, licensing and regulation, and technological dimension. Information security governance is emphasized as critical due to ICT dependency, requiring security policies, counter-measures, monitoring, and risk management. Trust in services, business activities, and knowledge is essential, alongside a knowledge base addressing privacy, e-signatures, security, and jurisdiction.

This study estimates the COVID-19 burden of disease in the Republic of Ireland from March 1, 2020, to February 28, 2021, using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs). The research combines Years of Life Lost (YLL) from mortality and Years Lived with Disability (YLD) from five health states: asymptomatic, moderate, severe, critical, and post-acute consequences. Data was sourced from public Irish health databases, with mortality data from the Central Statistics Office and case data from data.gov.ie. YLL calculations used 2019 Global Burden of Disease standard life tables and Irish population estimates. YLD calculations applied disability weights and durations from established burden of disease frameworks, with assumptions for asymptomatic cases and post-acute consequences based on seroprevalence studies and literature estimates. The study received ethical approval from University College Cork.

Explainable AI research aims to enhance transparency and trust in AI decision-making by developing methods to understand pre-trained language model mechanisms. Improved interpretability enables more efficient resource use and helps identify safety risks like adversarial attacks and ethical breaches. Key challenges include lack of unified evaluation frameworks, computational inefficiency scaling with model size, and bridging gaps between techniques and real-world applications. The authors propose a framework for editing concept activation vectors (CAVs) that controls model behavior by training classifiers on activation vectors to detect target concepts, then dynamically applying these CAVs during inference to enhance or suppress specific concepts while maintaining text fluency and managing multiple concept adjustments through optimization.

This patent application describes systems and methods for managing snapshots in a cloud-integrated storage appliance to reduce stable data eviction. The storage appliance caches snapshots from data sources before migrating them to cloud storage, maintaining snapshot metadata in key-value stores while evicting snapshot data files based on policies like least recently used. In forever incremental backup strategies, stable data blocks (unchanged across multiple snapshots) risk eviction, causing restore delays. The solution involves creating synthetic baseline snapshots and refreshing eviction state data. Two approaches are presented: expanding ownership of valid snapshot metadata records to the most recent snapshot, and maintaining a reverse incremental synthetic baseline that transfers invalidated data to a pre-baseline snapshot while refreshing the synthetic baseline with new data. The system uses local snapshot identifiers as key prefixes in key-value stores for inode records, directory records, and data map records, enabling efficient metadata manipulation without expensive data transfers.

Police are investigating a video showing officers using a stun gun on Dailene Rosario, a pregnant 17-year-old, in a Bronx apartment building. The incident occurred Friday night when officers responding to an unrelated call encountered Rosario interfering with them during a fight involving her ex-boyfriend. The video shows onlookers shouting that she was pregnant as officers shocked her. Rosario, reportedly 14 weeks pregnant, faces charges of resisting arrest, harassment, and disorderly conduct. A coach discusses his team's goaltending situation, noting that Martin was initially blamed for losses when the team struggled offensively, but remained a "great soldier" ready to play. The coach emphasizes the importance of depth, shot-blocking, and playing multiple lines in playoff hockey, noting Anton's emergence as a top defenseman and leader in shot-blocking. He reflects on his difficult decision to leave his previous team, feeling proud of the young players he helped develop.

In *Rebecca T. Shumye v. Samuel D. Felleke* (N.D. Cal. Apr. 4, 2008), the Court granted in part and denied in part Defendant’s motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiff’s motion. Plaintiff, a citizen of Ethiopia, sued her former spouse and Form I-864 sponsor to enforce his obligation to maintain her annual income at 125% of the federal poverty level. The Court held that Form I-864 creates an enforceable contract and that income must be analyzed annually, not in the aggregate. The Court ruled that the $49,000 divorce settlement and student loans do not constitute income, but student grants and housing subsidies do. The Court granted summary judgment for Defendant for years 2000, 2001, 2002, 2004, and 2005 based on Plaintiff’s concession that her income exceeded the threshold. The Court denied summary judgment for Defendant for 2003, 2006, and 2007, finding he failed to establish through undisputed evidence that Plaintiff’s income exceeded the threshold. The Court denied Plaintiff’s motion because she failed to meet her burden of establishing by undisputed facts that Defendant breached his obligations in those years.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2016, reporting net income of $857 million for Q2 2016 compared to $92 million in Q2 2015, and $1.37 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2016 compared to $35 million in the prior year period. Amazon faces ongoing legal proceedings including patent infringement claims and tax disputes with the IRS and French Tax Administration. The company also disclosed voluntary reports to U.S. authorities regarding sales to individuals and entities in Iran that may have violated sanctions laws.

This study examines time-delayed feedback in multi-agent learning for normal-form games. While optimistic algorithms like Optimistic Follow the Regularized Leader (OFTRL) achieve $O(1)$ regret and convergence to Nash equilibrium without delays, the authors demonstrate that any time delay causes OFTRL to suffer $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ regret and divergence from equilibrium in Matching Pennies games (Theorems 6-7). To address this, they propose Weighted OFTRL (WOFTRL), which applies an optimistic weight $n$ to predictions. Analysis shows that the optimistic weight and time delay $m$ cancel each other out. When the weight exceeds the delay ($n = m + 1$), WOFTRL achieves $O(1)$ regret (Corollary 11) and best-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium in poly-matrix zero-sum games (Corollary 13). Experimental results validate these findings, showing $O(1)$ regret and convergence when $n > m$, and $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ regret and divergence when $n \leq m$.

Molina Healthcare is a government-sponsored health insurance company specializing in Medicaid and dual-eligible populations, trading at a discount (~8–9× earnings). Despite risks from policy changes, acquisitions, and medical cost inflation, state-level dynamics and contract discipline mitigate concerns. The author, who holds a long position in MOH, views it as a structurally profitable value opportunity for defensive investors. The passage includes stock chart data (September 26–October 1, 2025, price range $189.83–$195.105) and unrelated article headlines.

President Carter delivered a commencement address at Notre Dame University, thanking the university for his honorary degree and expressing kinship with graduates. He praised Father Hesburgh's 25-year commitment to human rights and honored three religious leaders receiving honorary degrees for their human rights advocacy in Rhodesia, Brazil, and South Korea.

Carter outlined a new American foreign policy based on five principles: reaffirming human rights as fundamental; reinforcing bonds among democracies; engaging the Soviet Union to halt the nuclear arms race; pursuing Middle East peace; and reducing nuclear proliferation and conventional weapons spread. He emphasized moving beyond the "inordinate fear of communism" that previously led America to support dictators, and rejected adopting adversaries' flawed tactics.

He noted historical shifts since 1945, including decolonization and the emergence of nearly 100 new nations, arguing that traditional war and peace issues can no longer be separated from global questions of justice, equity, and human rights. Carter expressed confidence in democracy's effectiveness, citing recent successes in India, Portugal, Spain, and Greece, and called for cooperation with developing nations through expanded trade and aid to address immediate problems of hunger, disease, illiteracy, and repression.

Children of obese parents show higher rates of developmental delays by age 3, with maternal obesity linked to fine motor skill deficits, paternal obesity to social competence issues, and dual parental obesity to problem-solving difficulties. The mechanism is unknown but may involve inflammation or gene expression changes. The study of over 5,000 US women appears in Pediatrics.

VentureWire's September 28, 2000 issue reports private company business news. Top stories include Warburg Pincus closing a $2.5 billion international private equity fund, Primus Venture Partners raising $200 million for its fifth fund, Gear.com's president resigning and laying off 22 employees, Goldman Sachs launching a $250 million investment venture called GSVentures, Hyperchip raising $67 million in Series C funding, and Sally Ride resigning as president of Space.com. The issue also covers numerous funding rounds for technology and internet companies, an IPO withdrawal by Asia Online citing market conditions, mergers and acquisitions including Zoho acquiring NCL and Band-X acquiring TeleGeography, new board appointments and executive hires at various firms, and two new venture capital funds launched by technology executives.

Drew Doughty stated he struggled early in the season but improved by midseason and entered the playoffs with confidence. He noted the team developed strong chemistry with consistent line pairings and overcame adversity by defeating the top three Western Conference teams while losing only two games. He acknowledged feeling pressure from his contract early but moved past it by focusing on playing carefree hockey. Doughty described the finals opponent as similarly defensive-minded with elite goaltending, noting both teams had subpar regular seasons before improving. He praised his goaltender's critical saves and humble personality, adding that the goalie avoids media attention. Doughty expressed excitement for the finals, mentioning increased fan recognition in Los Angeles after years of obscurity, though noting diehard fans always existed. He highlighted hockey's growing popularity in the city.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture introduces third-generation Tensor Cores with Sparsity features and TF32 precision, second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection performance and motion blur acceleration, and GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling for up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth. The architecture doubles FP32 throughput, improves power efficiency by up to 1.9x over Turing, and supports PCIe Gen 4, third-generation NVLink, and RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading. Key products include the GeForce RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070 for gaming, and the RTX A6000 and A40 for professional visualization and data center applications. The GA10x SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, one RT Core, and 128 KB L1/Shared Memory. Display capabilities include 8K60 and 4K120 support via HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC. Hardware-accelerated video decoding supports AV1, HEVC, VP9, and other formats, while NVENC enables high-quality streaming up to 8K HEVC.

Scientists report that Isle Royale National Park's moose population, estimated at 1,600, could double in three to four years due to only two remaining wolves. The wolf population has declined from 24 in 2009 due to severe inbreeding. Without predator control, moose are overeating balsam fir trees, which could lead to starvation. The National Park Service prefers relocating 20 to 30 wolves to restore balance but has not committed; a decision is expected this fall.

A coach discusses his hockey team's versatility in winning games through different strategies, including quick-strike offense, defensive play, special teams, and counterattacks. He emphasizes learning from film sessions, making adjustments, and maintaining a short memory after games. He praises players like "Kuny" for team-first versatility and "Tanger" for contributing as an injured player through coaching insights. The coach highlights the importance of execution, taking what the game presents, and staying motivated during the Stanley Cup Finals. A coach discusses his team's playoff performance, praising Mike's hard work and defensive play, noting that Carter and Gagne are getting scoring chances despite low point production. He credits Craig Berube for penalty kill coaching and emphasizes player execution. The coach highlights team confidence, fast-paced hockey against Chicago, and Jeff's recovery from injury. He notes the second line's offensive generation, the importance of focus during playoffs with an end date in sight, and denies fatigue as a factor for either team given the high quality of play.

The Eagle Creek fire has burned over 48,000 acres since September 2, severely damaging the Oneonta Gorge and other areas in the Columbia River Gorge. About 7,300 acres suffered severe burns and 14,600 acres moderate burns. Officials are particularly concerned about visitor safety near Oneonta Gorge and Multnomah Falls Lodge, where fences will be installed and hazardous trees removed. Trailheads and trails in Oneonta Gorge remain closed, with some areas potentially closed until September 2018.

Peter Blackmore's August 2000 report to Compaq executives highlights strong momentum across global operations despite supply challenges causing a non-linear quarter. A K-5 Honor Choir at NRH International Leadership of Texas in North Richland Hills has written original music that is being used across the United States. This manual provides instructions for using the SanDisk Sansa c200 MP3 player. Microsoft Research Asia's Societal AI team presents a whitepaper outlining ten research questions for responsible AI integration into society. The passage distinguishes between investing and speculation based on Benjamin Graham's definition: true investing requires both capital protection and adequate return, not just buying securities. The author shares a personal example of buying Ask Jeeves stock based on expected price momentum, which Graham would classify as speculation rather than investment because it ignored principal safety. To protect capital, investors should buy stocks at significant discounts to intrinsic value—larger margins of safety provide bigger buffers against business deterioration and assessment errors. Financially solid companies with clean balance sheets, low debt-to-equity ratios, and strong current assets are preferred. The author notes that buying unloved companies with large margins of safety often leads to profits as price-value gaps close, particularly with "net net" stocks trading below reasonable business value. Ultimately, being an investor depends on the selection process, not the assets purchased.

Location tracking in electronic devices raises privacy concerns. Kurt Peterson, owner of Experimac in Pueblo, advises users to disable location services through device settings—on iPhones via Privacy > Location Services, on Androids and smartwatches similarly, and on MacBooks through System Preferences > Security and Privacy. Users can turn off all location services or disable them per app. Peterson notes that apps pose greater privacy risks than device hacking, citing Strava as an example where followers can see user locations. He warns that visiting the App Store automatically re-enables Location Services, and the only way to fully avoid tracking is to power devices off.

A hockey player discusses his team's playoff series, noting both teams have strong defense and goaltending, making one-goal games common. He mentions their improved home record this year compared to past seasons when they started on the road. Despite losing two overtime games, he remains confident, emphasizing the team played well, created chances, and needs to stay positive heading home for upcoming games. He dismisses fatigue as a factor and frames overtime as simply another period, expressing frustration but not demoralization.

The Stack Zone Offense is a basketball strategy based on the overload principle, creating matchup problems for zone defenses through specific player alignments and movements. It features precise spacing, multiple entries, and "Crunch Time" specials for late-game situations. The offense assigns distinct roles: Point Guard directs the offense, Shooting Guard is the top three-point shooter, Small Forward handles baseline shooting and rebounding, Power Forward operates from high and low post positions, and Post focuses on inside rebounding. The system progresses through phases including Basic Overload Reads, Pass & Cut Action, High Post Roll, and Ball Reversal, with continuity options and special entries like Flop, Exchange, and Triple Stack alignments. Offensive rebounding is emphasized, with missed shots treated as potential passes for put-backs. The offense was developed with contributions from Mike Frink and Tom Newell.

Offensive set pieces from free kicks in soccer restart play after fouls, requiring adherence to Law 13 and strategic planning based on distance, angle, and whether kicks are direct or indirect. Direct free kicks allow immediate goals; indirect kicks require the ball to touch another player first. This document provides a user-level description of AGESA™ software procedures and interfaces for host environment wrapper implementers, requiring BIOS programming knowledge. The release package includes binaries, build control files, wrapper examples, and tools. Source files follow UEFI C Coding Standards with descriptive long filenames and standardized headers.

Build customization occurs through <Plat>Options.c files, with technology code compiled as libraries linked with platform-specific defaults tables.

Execution requires 32-bit protected mode flat addressing with identity-mapped paging if enabled. The interface includes standard headers with function identifiers, image base pointers, PCIe base addresses, callout pointers, and heap status.

Following the Las Vegas shooting, WUWF examined local preparedness for mass casualty incidents. The largest recent event in Pensacola was a 2014 jail explosion that killed two and injured scores, requiring treatment of 184 victims across five hospitals. Escambia County Public Safety Director Mike Weaver explained that mass casualty responses involve coordinated triage, hospital communication, and surge plans including canceling elective surgeries. Pensacola has two Level II trauma centers, with the nearest Level I center in Mobile. Weaver noted that incident severity is relative to community resources—three patients can overwhelm a small town. Local officials conduct regular training including hurricane, airport, active shooter, and Incident Command System exercises. Weaver expressed confidence in the area's ability to respond despite the inevitable challenges.

In *Hunter and Others v. Bales*, the Supreme Court affirmed a decree for specific performance of a land sale contract. The case involved two conflicting theories about whether Thompson had a valid oral contract with Moore's agent before Moore sold the same land to Hunter. Following appellate practice, the Court adopted the theory sustaining the lower court's finding that Thompson had prior equity. The Court held that a vendor who makes a valid sale in contravention of a prior verbal contract elects to treat that contract as void, but the intermediate purchaser with notice may be bound. In suits for specific performance, plaintiffs need only offer to bring purchase money into court upon decree, not actually tender it, and are not chargeable with interest after tender unless they used the money.

Ronald Reagan criticizes President Carter's foreign policy as weak and contradictory, arguing that failure to respond decisively to the Iran hostage crisis and the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan has emboldened enemies and increased the risk of nuclear confrontation. He calls for America to become strong, reliable, and predictable through a coherent grand strategy for the 1980s. Priorities include rebuilding military strength through a sustained long-term effort, maintaining nuclear deterrent capabilities, achieving naval superiority, and restoring the capacity to project force to the Persian Gulf region. Reagan blames the Democratic-controlled Congress and Carter Administration policies for allowing Soviet advancement in weaponry and warns against declaring defense doctrines without possessing sufficient military power.

Cars.com's 2018 American-Made Index ranks vehicles by U.S. manufacturing location, percentage of American parts, and support for American factory jobs. Jeep Cherokee tops the list, assembled in Belvidere, Illinois. Honda has four vehicles in the top 10 (Odyssey, Ridgeline, Pilot, and Acura MDX), while Ford has three (Taurus, Explorer, F-150). The index reveals that foreign automakers sometimes use more American-made components than domestic manufacturers, complicating the definition of "American-made" amid potential tariffs on imported vehicles.

This study compared a hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow against a multiplex PCR panel for detecting respiratory pathogens in 29 nasopharyngeal samples from patients with suspected acute upper respiratory infections. The PCR panel detected 15 microorganisms (4 bacteria, 11 viruses), while the mNGS approach identified 44 microorganisms (27 bacteria, 2 fungi, 15 viruses), including 29 additional pathogens not covered by PCR. Both methods showed 98.33% positive percent agreement for shared targets. The mNGS workflow classified detected organisms into three phenotypic groups based on pathogenic potential: normal flora/colonizers (31%), frequently disease-associated (34%), and pathogenic (34%). Notably, mNGS exclusively detected SARS-CoV-2, Coxsackievirus A, and Human rhinovirus C—organisms with significant lower respiratory trafficking potential. The hybridization capture-based approach offers advantages over target-agnostic mNGS by focusing on clinically relevant microbes, reducing cost, and enabling deployment in resource-limited settings with lower-throughput sequencing instruments.

The Florida Department of Transportation unveiled plans to build a connector between the Sawgrass Expressway and I-95 along Southwest 10th Street in Deerfield Beach, a project opposed by neighbors since the 1980s. Two options were presented at a public meeting: one splitting Southwest 10th Street with the connector running between, and another with the connector running north of the street. The project, which includes depressed and covered roadways to address rush hour congestion, would not begin for at least three years. Local opposition remains strong, with concerns about property values and living near a major highway similar to I-595.

Nigeria faces a healthcare crisis as doctors emigrate en masse to the UK, US, and other countries. NOIPolls found the UK hires at least 12 Nigerian doctors weekly, while 88% of remaining doctors plan to leave. The physician-patient ratio has worsened from 1:4,000 to 1:5,000, far exceeding WHO's 1:600 recommendation, causing fatalities, longer waits, and medical errors. With 182 million people, Nigeria needs 303,000 doctors but has only 35,000 practicing. Primary reasons for departure include high taxes (98%), low work satisfaction (92%), poor salaries (91%), and knowledge gaps abroad (47%).

This study introduces an architecture for digitally structured information exchange between industrial enterprises, focusing on technical information in the lifecycle domain of process industry. Current practices rely on manual, labor-intensive methods like spreadsheets due to insufficient standards and lack of scalable digital communication media. The proposed solution uses an open consortium to establish common business practices and information formats, with mediators delivering information between enterprises via multi-sided platforms. A prototype was implemented demonstrating equipment information exchange between suppliers and plant operators for maintenance and renewal projects. The architecture aims to reduce transaction costs by enabling single-integration connectivity through adapters that map proprietary enterprise systems to common formats. Key challenges include forming a governance model for the open consortium and creating affordable solutions for low-volume partners.

In *Asa B. Meech, and others v. The City of Buffalo*, the court held that a municipal corporation with power to make public improvements may voluntarily increase a contract price when circumstances equitably justify it, unless prohibited by charter. The City of Buffalo contracted with Randolph to build a sewer for $1,058.63, but unforeseen quicksand made completion impossible at that price. The common council increased the contract price by $588.13 and ordered a supplementary assessment on benefited property owners. Plaintiffs sued to restrain collection of the second assessment. The court affirmed the city's power to make the additional assessment under charter provisions allowing "further assessment" when an assessment proves insufficient to defray improvement expenses. The court found the first assessment insufficient due to unforeseen circumstances, making the supplementary assessment valid. The new contract with Randolph, made to secure completion, was supported by adequate consideration and was not a gratuity.

This study examines how peer mentoring develops 21st-century skills in Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students during a movement education course at a Turkish university. Three peer mentors and 25 first-year students participated in a 14-week course using storytelling and gamification. Data from field notes, recordings, social media, and reflections revealed three themes: peer groups excluded non-contributing members while mentors divided responsibilities to complete tasks; mentors enhanced accountability and teaching awareness through content creation; and narrative-based learning connected course content to daily life, improving retention. The study concludes that peer mentoring provides realistic teaching experiences and develops skills like communication, cooperation, and accountability, recommending its integration throughout undergraduate programs.

The Korean Diet (K-diet) is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods including fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods like kimchi. It features smaller portions than Western diets and includes foods such as rice, barley, various vegetables, fermented soybean products, and broth-based dishes. The diet minimizes processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Benefits include high fiber, low calories and saturated fats, improved gut health from probiotics, and potential weight loss when combined with physical activity. Drawbacks include high sodium content from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium due to limited dairy, and high carbohydrates from rice and noodles that require portion control. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free needs.

College football Power Rankings analyze offensive strengths and weaknesses for Top 25 teams after Week 6. Ohio State's defense dominates but rushing needs improvement. Miami wins despite late offensive lulls. Oregon's Dante Moore excels with strong freshman running backs. Ole Miss needs more explosive runs. Texas A&M's Reed develops with dominant defense. Oklahoma's run game struggles without injured Mateer. Indiana's high-powered offense faces questions against pressure. Texas Tech remains undefeated with room to improve. The Citi Simplicity® Card offers 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases, with no late fees, penalty rates, or annual fee. It requires good to excellent credit (670-850). Balance transfers must be completed within 4 months, with a 3% fee (minimum $5) during the intro period, rising to 5% afterward. Google launched three experimental photography apps for Android and iOS: Storyboard (Android) converts videos into comic layouts with 1.6 trillion possible combinations; Selfissimo! (both platforms) automatically captures black-and-white selfies when users stop moving; and Scrubbies (iOS) allows users to manipulate video playback speed and direction to create loops. These apps utilize technologies including object recognition, person segmentation, and stylization algorithms. Google notes the apps are based on active research and performance may vary, with public feedback intended to guide future development.

The passage details grievances against Russia for forcibly impressing American crew members from the Cape Horn Pigeon into service on a Russian vessel, violating their natural rights and national pride. The men were left without adequate food, shelter, or legal counsel at Vladivostok. The text argues for full indemnity including interest on damages, citing numerous precedents from international arbitration cases where interest was awarded at rates of 5-12 percent. Pumpkin is a nutritious fruit from the Cucurbitaceae family, rich in fiber, iron, vitamins, and minerals. One cup of cooked pumpkin contains 52 calories, 3 grams of fiber, and 565 mg of potassium—more than a large banana. It is also high in carotenoids including beta-carotene (5.4 mg), alpha-carotene (7 mg), and lutein & zeaxanthin (2.5 mg), which offer anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory benefits. Five health benefits of pumpkin include: reducing cardiovascular disease risk through potassium and phytonutrients; supporting immunity via carotenoids; protecting eye health by reducing cataract and macular degeneration risks; promoting brain health and cognition; and lowering blood pressure through favorable potassium-to-sodium ratios. Pumpkin can be incorporated into various dishes including soups, smoothies, lasagna, and muffins.

This paper presents a computational systematic review of social science research on large language models (LLMs), using unsupervised machine learning to induce a taxonomy from 270 studies and validating it against expert coding. The analysis reveals three stable, interpretable clusters: LLM as Social Minds (mind-attribution, theory of mind, moral reasoning), LLM Societies (multi-agent interactions, cooperation, institutional design), and LLM–Human Interactions (trust, perception, productivity, educational integration). The machine-derived structure shows strong alignment with expert classifications (NMI = 0.811, ARI = 0.867, Macro-F1 = 0.954). The authors argue this tripartite framework enables cumulative research by clarifying cross-level relationships, standardizing constructs, and identifying where improved measurement and theory can advance the field. They emphasize treating these as levels of analysis rather than mutually exclusive camps, with implications for evidentiary standards and institutional design.

Lincoln County defeated Laughlin in their Homecoming volleyball game last Thursday, winning 3-1. The Lady Lynx won the first two sets but lost mental focus when close to finishing in four sets, allowing Laughlin to win the third set. Coach Chantel Holt noted her team needs to work on maintaining concentration and choosing to win. Lincoln regained control in the final set, keeping Laughlin under 10 points. Holt made frequent substitutions to build team camaraderie and showcase roster depth. The Lady Lynx play Calvary at home today at 3 and 4 p.m.

WiseGuyReports published a 2017 market research report on the global Smart Service Robots market, forecasting through 2022. The report uses SWOT analysis and profiles key manufacturers including SoftBank, Honda, Kawada (Japan); PROTRYLY VISION GROUP, Ubtech Robotics, Suzhou Pangolin Robot, SIASUN Robot, QIHAN Technology/Sanbot (China); ROBOTIS, Hanson Robotics, Dongbu Robot (Korea); Engineered Arts (UK); and Willow Garage (US). This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which facilitates page migration operations as an extension to SEV and SNP. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and allows software to migrate pages between memory tiers while maintaining guest physical addresses. Key capabilities include migrating pages during concurrent DMA operations and migrating SNP-protected guest pages that HV/OS cannot otherwise access. The engine uses a ring buffer command interface with commands like PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, supporting up to 128 pages per command. Performance is optimized with 128-page commands and proper interrupt pacing. Restrictions include 4KB-aligned addresses only, and certain data structures cannot be migrated. Firmware can be reloaded via BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol when operations are paused.

The San Francisco 49ers have ruled out quarterback Brock Purdy, wide receiver Ricky Pearsall, and wide receiver Jauan Jennings for their Thursday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams due to injuries. Purdy has been dealing with toe soreness, Pearsall injured his right knee, and Jennings suffered rib injuries. Mac Jones will start at quarterback, making his third start this season.
