This passage examines a knowledge exchange project between University College London's Institute of Education and Diversity Role Models, an LGBTQ+ anti-bullying charity, which supported student teachers in England to develop trans-inclusive citizenship education practices from October 2023 to June 2024. The project addressed rising hostility toward transgender communities and controversial draft government guidance that sought to restrict discussion of gender identity in schools. Student teachers learned to "actualize" LGBTQ+ identities by placing them in real-life contexts, though they noted greater difficulty addressing transgender compared to lesbian and gay identities due to media debates and policy uncertainty. Key pedagogical approaches included using personal stories to build empathy, grounding lessons in the Equality Act 2010 and human rights frameworks, and implementing whole-school strategies like restorative behavior management and bystander training. The project highlighted how citizenship education's focus on rights-based learning can support trans inclusion when combined with specialist training and partnership with civil society organizations. International frameworks including the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and Yogyakarta Principles+10 were identified as additional resources for advancing trans-inclusive education.

King Salman held talks with Turkish President Erdogan in Riyadh on Tuesday, reviewing bilateral relations and regional developments. Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Naif, Deputy Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Salman, and other high-ranking officials attended. Erdogan received an official reception including national anthems and guard of honor inspection. Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Naif also held separate talks with Erdogan focusing on regional peace, security, and counterterrorism efforts, attended by Foreign Minister Adel Al-Jubeir and other senior officials.

The President urges Congress to reduce tariff duties on Cuban imports before the session adjourns, citing moral obligations and national interest. Cuba's Constitution establishes closer relations with the U.S. than any other power, and the President argues for reciprocity to support Cuba's material well-being and prevent financial ruin. The proposal aligns with President McKinley's earlier messages and the existing tariff law's provision for up to 20% reductions for specific countries. The President dismisses concerns about harm to American industries, noting similar fears about Hawaii proved unfounded, and emphasizes that controlling Cuba's growing market benefits U.S. producers. He frames the request as completing America's honorable record of supporting Cuban independence following the Spanish-American War.

Table 6 documents medical problems occurring in at least 1% of participants between Dose 3 and one month after Dose 3 of 5 or 10 µg BNT162b2 booster doses in Phase 3, among those who previously received two 30 µg doses. Table 7 shows medical problems between Dose 3 and one month after Dose 3 of 30 µg BNT162b2 booster in Phase 2/3. Table 8 shows medical problems between Dose 4 or 5 and one month after for additional 30 µg BNT162b2 boosters in Phase 2/3. In Phase 1, between Dose 1 and 6 months after Dose 2 of BNT162b2 or placebo, 2 of 48 participants (4%) had serious medical problems: one case of inflamed appendix in the 20-µg group and one case of inflamed nerves in the 30-µg group. Health authorities in Taiwan are warning residents to avoid raw or undercooked eggs due to rising avian flu threats. Eggs must be cooked to at least 70 degrees Celsius to destroy the bacteria. Common foods containing raw eggs include hot pot dipping sauces, soft-boiled eggs, eggs Benedict, mayonnaise, and tiramisu. Residents should wash hands with soap after handling eggshells and avoid touching their face. Additional recommendations include maintaining hygiene, thoroughly cooking poultry, wearing surgical masks, and seeking medical attention if fever develops.

Malaysia's central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell Malaysian government securities from May 2, expanding from only licensed and investment banks previously. Non-bank entities may also net forward hedge up to 100% of underlying assets and manage 25% additional foreign exchange exposure. The measures aim to boost bond market liquidity and encourage onshore ringgit trade. The central bank is considering allowing short selling of shariah-compliant MGII bonds and will issue a concept paper for industry feedback by April 28. Residents may hedge up to 6 million ringgit per bank without documentary evidence in pound sterling, euro and yen from May 2, adding to existing dollar/ringgit and yuan/ringgit options. A new financial markets code of conduct will replace the 1994 version. The ringgit hit a near 19-year low in January but has recovered 1.5% this year.

The Supreme Court, General Term, Fifth Department, reversed a judgment in favor of plaintiff Charles Jones and granted a new trial in his indemnity action against defendant Orin S. Bacon, executor of James McKechnie. The court held that the trial court erred in admitting evidence that McKechnie and plaintiff's son-in-law Sherman Kingsbury had speculated in hops and that McKechnie refused a profitable offer for the hops that would have paid off Kingsbury's notes. This evidence was foreign to the issues, served only to excite jury sympathy for plaintiff and Kingsbury, and was prejudicial to the defendant. The plaintiff alleged McKechnie promised to indemnify him for endorsing Kingsbury's promissory notes totaling $47,000, but the only surviving witness to the alleged agreements besides plaintiff was Kingsbury, his son-in-law, whose testimony was subject to suspicion.

Kinlochleven has received three new defibrillators through local fundraising efforts and donations from charity Lucky 2B Here and residents Marcus and Martine Spence. The equipment was presented to the community first responders group, with additional support including cabinets and life support training. Multiple local groups and individuals contributed to fundraising efforts. The defibrillators will be placed outside the Co-op and GP's surgery. The first responders group has raised £2,900 of its £3,500 target, with donations accepted at local venues and online.

Magda Enriquez, a Sandinista revolutionary and Nicaraguan Council of State member representing the Nicaraguan Women's Association AMNLAE, secretly joined the Sandinistas in 1976 after discovering that malnutrition caused mental retardation in children she worked with. The 1978 poisoning of peasant children during a land sit-in led her to request military training. Formerly married to an American professor, she divorced after her husband demanded she choose between him and the Revolution. Now a trained soldier, peasant organiser, and mother of six (including one adopted child), she balances government work with family life through community solidarity and party-assigned childcare support. Her 14-year-old son joined the militia two years under age. Enriquez has helped lay groundwork for Nicaragua's first elections and challenges American government narratives about her country.

Harry Kane led England to a 4-3 penalty shootout victory over Colombia in the World Cup Round of 16, scoring from the spot in regular time and again in the shootout. Yerry Mina had equalized late for Colombia. England will face Sweden in the quarter-final on Saturday, with Kane urging full focus on that match. Kane leads the tournament scoring with six goals, two ahead of Romelu Lukaku and Cristiano Ronaldo. Teammate Kieran Trippier praised the team's spirit. However, Colombia's Radamel Falcao accused American referee Mark Geiger of bias toward England, citing his English-only communication and disputed calls. Diego Maradona called the result "a monumental theft."

Between weeks 24-48, adverse events were reported by 33.8% of Primary SOC subjects, 40.8% of Secondary SOC, and 38.6% of Continued Additional Educational Program subjects. Serious AEs occurred in 11.8%, 13.5%, and 14.0% respectively. Bleeding events were reported by 4.1%, 4.0%, and 3.2% of subjects, with fatal bleeding in 2 subjects total. Overall, 24 deaths occurred: 11 before week 24 and 13 after. No pregnancies were reported. Laboratory data showed no concerning hepatic or renal signals. The AEGEAN study found high adherence and persistence with apixaban for atrial fibrillation through 48 weeks, with no added benefit from proactive education.

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars, a program recognizing students in the top 10 percent of the state's graduating seniors based on ACT/SAT scores, unweighted GPA, and class size. Named students include Basem Al-Tarshan, Philip Andrango, Michael Ardovitch, and 82 others.

This article examines the risk of financial ruin for retirees and FIRE (Financial Independent Retire Early) individuals, emphasizing fragility due to sequence of returns risk, withdrawal rates, and lack of diversification. An example illustrates a couple who retired in 2000 with $1 million, withdrew $50,000 annually, and went broke by 2017 due to poor market timing and the 2008 financial crisis. Monte Carlo simulations by Mark Spitznagel show 10% chance of under 3% CAGR over 25 years. The 4% rule, established by William Bengen in 1994, may be insufficient for FIRE's longer timeframe; even 3-4% rates risk ruin without recovery. Edward Thorp recommends 2% withdrawal for perpetual endowments. Mitigation strategies include conservative withdrawal rates, diversification across asset classes, and frugality.

An Appleton couple, Andrea and Luke Benrud, are sharing their story nationally to promote CPR training after Luke used skills from a Red Cross class to save Andrea's life when she collapsed from a rare, undetected heart defect. Featured in People Magazine, the couple and their family are all CPR trained and hope their experience encourages others to learn life-saving skills.

Body camera footage shows Grand Rapids Police Officer Kevin Penn pressing his AR-15 rifle muzzle against a suspect's head during an August 19 arrest. The incident occurred after officers responded to an armed robbery call and mistakenly detained a drunk man who refused to cooperate. After Sgt. Neil Gomez tased the suspect, Penn dug the rifle muzzle into the man's head while verbally tormenting him. Another officer pushed the rifle away. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker announced on October 3 that Penn will not face criminal charges, stating the action was not approved police procedure but did not rise to a criminal offense under the specific facts. The suspect was arrested for resisting arrest and released; he did not file a complaint, likely due to intoxication. Penn was allowed to resign after other officers reported his conduct.

The European Central Bank is expected to maintain its stimulus programme and keep interest rates at historic lows on Thursday, due to threats to economic growth and sluggish inflation in the eurozone. Analysts predict the ECB will stick to its September expiry date for its 30-billion-euro monthly bond-buying scheme. Downside risks have re-emerged, including a stronger euro, US trade tariffs, and stalled eurozone reform talks. Despite strong 2017 growth of 2.3 per cent, recent indicators show slowing momentum, with inflation at 1.3 per cent in March—below the ECB's 2.0 per cent target. Both the ECB and IMF forecast 2.4 per cent growth for 2018.

Jonathan Erick Miles, 33, of Lancaster Township faces multiple charges including manufacturing and possessing controlled substances, drug paraphernalia, and endangering the welfare of children after police found two marijuana plants in his home during an April 9 search. He was allegedly under the influence while caring for his daughter alone. He was arraigned and released on $20,000 unsecured bail. Three other individuals were also charged in separate incidents: Glen VanDerSchaaf, 75, of East Petersburg for indecent assault; Tyran Gregory Ellis, 38, of Manheim Township for corruption of minors involving an 11-year-old; and Gilberto Isaac-Suarez, 50, for burglary, assault, terroristic threats and related charges following a domestic dispute involving a metal pipe.

Companies use exhibitions and events to enhance brand image and interact with customers, requiring experienced hosts and trade show models. Traditional recruitment agencies are expensive with limited databases. Professionate, an online event staffing agency, offers a global platform connecting companies with temporary event staff. Companies can access thousands of candidate profiles with ratings and reviews, while candidates can upload profiles and browse vacancies directly. The service operates worldwide, including Dubai.

This study examined sex differences in the correlation between self-reported PCL-5 and clinician-administered CAPS-5 PTSD assessments in 100 participants (56 males, 44 females). While CAPS-5 scores showed no sex differences, females exhibited stronger PCL-5/CAPS-5 correlation (Rho=0.907) than males (Rho=0.655). Males showed significant deviation from ideal regression lines and higher misclassification rates (26.8% vs. 11.4%). Civilian trauma showed stronger correlations than military trauma for both sexes. Findings suggest PCL-5 may be less reliable for males and military populations, warranting cautious interpretation and additional assessment tools.

The U.N. warns that Yemen's two-year war may deprive a generation of children of education, with up to 4.5 million children at risk of not finishing the school year. Over 166,000 teachers (73% of the total) have not received salaries since October 2016 due to a crisis that began when the government moved the central bank from Houthi-controlled Sanaa. Children out of school face increased risks of child marriage or military recruitment. Public sector employees in northern Yemen report seven months of unpaid salaries, causing severe hardship.

A Channel 4 documentary titled "The Super Orgasm" follows five women who claim to experience up to 100 orgasms in one sexual encounter. The documentary includes experiments measuring arousal, brain activity, and blood flow, but experts criticize the research as unscientific due to small sample size and lack of controls. Researchers found that women with multiple orgasms show sustained alpha waves and increased blood flow to over 30 brain areas. Experts like Cynthia Graham and Nan Wise dispute the term "super orgasm," noting it differs little from multiple orgasms and is uncommon. They warn against setting it as a standard, emphasizing that orgasm experiences vary widely among women.

This lecture covers continuity of functions, presenting a three-part theorem: (1) if c is not a cluster point of set S, then any function f is automatically continuous at c; (2) if c is a cluster point, f is continuous at c if and only if the limit of f(x) as x approaches c equals f(c); and (3) f is continuous at c if and only if for every sequence xₙ converging to c, the sequence f(xₙ) converges to f(c). The proof of part 1 uses the fact that non-cluster points have no nearby points in S to compare. Parts 2 and 3 connect continuity to limits and sequential convergence, with the sequential characterization proved using epsilon-delta arguments and contradiction.

The lecture then applies these results: sine is proven continuous directly using trigonometric identities and the inequality |sin x| ≤ |x|, while cosine's continuity follows from the sequential theorem using cos(x) = sin(x + π/2). An example of a function discontinuous everywhere is given: f(x) = 1 if x is irrational, 0 if rational, proven using density of rationals and irrationals.

Further theorems show continuity is preserved under addition, multiplication, division (where defined), and composition of functions. By induction, all polynomials are continuous, as are compositions like 1/(3 + sin⁴x). The lecture concludes with preview of upcoming topics: the min/max theorem and intermediate value theorem for continuous functions on closed bounded intervals.

The FDA approved a second generic version of the abortion pill mifepristone. Amgen reported that its cholesterol-lowering drug Repatha reduced heart disease risks in a 12,000-patient trial. The passage also mentions a new NIH office aimed at reducing animal testing and various other biotech news items.

Cover 3 is a zone defense with 4 underneath players and 3 deep players, commonly used at all football levels by coaches like Nick Saban and Pete Carroll. The defense features a free safety covering the deep middle third, two cornerbacks covering outside deep thirds, and 4 underneath defenders (3 linebackers and strong safety) covering Hook, Curl, and Flat zones. Cover 3 adds a third deep defender compared to Cover 2, allowing an extra safety closer to the line to stop the run. Strengths include balanced coverage against deep and intermediate routes and run-pass flexibility. Weaknesses include vulnerability in the flats, seam routes between deep zones, and perimeter runs. Variations include flipping safety responsibilities, Fire Zone (adding a 4th rusher), Cover 3 Buzz (safety playing hook-to-curl), and pattern reading coverage like Rip/Liz.

The President transmits to the House of Representatives a report from the Secretary of State with documents regarding the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo with Mexico, including instructions to U.S. commissioners that were previously withheld for public interest reasons. The commissioners were directed to obtain Mexican ratification of the Senate-amended treaty without modification, using personal conferences rather than diplomatic notes to explain amendments. Mexico ratified the treaty on May 25, 1848, based solely on the Secretary of State's explanatory letter, before any conferences with U.S. commissioners occurred. The President explains that a subsequent protocol containing clarifications about three treaty articles—regarding rights of ceded territory inhabitants, land grants, and payment transferability—did not modify the treaty and was not submitted to the Mexican Congress, making it non-binding. The treaty was proclaimed U.S. law on July 4, 1848, and by then peace was restored, troops withdrawn, and obligations partially executed, rendering unilateral abrogation impossible without formal war declaration.

In re BEECHWOOD, District Court, D. New Jersey, Jan. 12, 1942. American Surety Company filed an involuntary bankruptcy petition against John Jacob Beechwood, who claimed immunity as a farmer under the Bankruptcy Act. A jury found him insolvent and that he committed acts of bankruptcy. The court addressed whether Beechwood qualified as a farmer under 11 U.S.C.A. § 1, Par. 17, which requires an individual to be personally engaged in farming with the principal part of income derived from such operations, measured at the time of the act of bankruptcy.

Beechwood was a New York lawyer employed full-time by Fidelity and Casualty Company at $7,200 annually, plus $2,000-$3,000 from private legal work. He lived on a New Jersey farm where agricultural activities occurred, but these were secondary to his employment. On September 20, 1940, he conveyed the farm to his wife—an act of bankruptcy—while still employed. He resigned September 23, 1940, retroactive to September 16.

The court distinguished Supreme Court precedent in First National Bank & Trust Co. v. Beach, noting Beechwood failed to meet the criterion of personally deriving principal income from farming. On September 20 and October 10, 1940, he remained a lawyer and businessman seeking to mitigate losses from his fraud, not personally engaged in farming as his principal occupation. The court held that extending farmer immunity to Beechwood would improperly allow business professionals to use rural residences to evade creditors. His farmer defense failed; order of adjudication as bankrupt entered.

The New York Times reported that U.S. officials said Trump campaign adviser Paul Manafort was picked up on intercepted calls involving Russian intelligence officials. Manafort denied knowingly speaking to Russian intelligence officers. The report follows Michael Flynn's resignation as national security adviser over calls with Russia's ambassador regarding U.S. sanctions. Rep. Elijah Cummings expressed alarm and noted difficulty obtaining information from Republican committee leadership. White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer maintained no campaign contacts with Russians occurred.

S. E. Mezes reports progress from a Thursday meeting of The Inquiry and distributes a memorandum outlining research tasks for an upcoming peace conference. The document details eight practical tasks including establishing boundaries, setting up governments, estimating state viability, creating economic arrangements, safeguarding minorities, ensuring economic equality, rewriting international law, and considering diplomatic history. It then maps these tasks across nineteen regions, specifying which tasks "will have to be" versus "may have to be" undertaken for each area, with Russia, Poland, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, and Turkey requiring the most extensive work. The memorandum also covers topics such as data on war-breeding areas, national aspirations, governmental arrangements for international areas, laws of war, reparations, and internationalized trade routes.

Amazon is planning new layoffs, with sources indicating up to 15% of its human resources staff (PXT team) may be cut, alongside potential reductions in other divisions. The cuts align with CEO Andy Jassy's strategy to reduce costs while investing over $100 billion in AI infrastructure. Jassy previously oversaw 27,000 layoffs in 2022-2023 and has warned employees that AI adoption will reduce corporate workforce needs. The PXT division employs over 10,000 people globally. Amazon declined to comment on the reports. The company simultaneously announced seasonal hiring of 250,000 warehouse workers for the holidays. Amazon's stock is down slightly this year but up 15% from 12 months prior.

This inaugural address affirms American democratic principles and the ongoing work to realize equality for all citizens. The speaker emphasizes that while freedom requires collective action, prosperity must rest on a rising middle class, and security programs strengthen rather than weaken national character. The speech addresses climate change, sustainable energy, ending perpetual war, and maintaining global alliances while supporting democracy worldwide. It calls for completing the nation's journey through equal pay, LGBTQ rights, voting access, immigration reform, and protecting children from harm. The address concludes by urging citizens to act in their time with common purpose to advance freedom.

A study in the Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases found that Bt toxins in GMO crops may cause blood abnormalities including anemia and leukemia in mammals. Brazilian researchers tested Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, and Cry2A toxins on mice, finding they damaged red blood cells and suppressed bone marrow proliferation. Contrary to previous beliefs, the toxins activated without alkaline conditions and showed increased effects after 72 hours. The lowest tested dose (27 mg/kg of Cry1Ab) caused hypochromic anemia. The authors concluded that Bt toxins may pose hematological risks to vertebrates and that further safety studies are needed before deeming them safe for mammals. The article criticizes industry-funded research and calls for GMO labeling or bans.

In December 2017, multiple manufacturer incentives were available for fuel-efficient vehicles. Kia offered a $5,000 factory discount on the 2017 Optima Hybrid in Western states ($4,000 elsewhere) or 0-percent APR financing over 60 months with $3,000 less bonus cash. The 2017 Optima Plug-In Hybrid leased for $249/month over 36 months with $1,999 down, plus federal and California incentives totaling $6,419. The 2017 Hyundai Sonata Plug-In Hybrid leased at $289/month with $1,699 due at signing in California. The 2017 Chevrolet Volt leased for $273/month over 39 months with $500 due at signing, qualifying for a $7,500 federal tax credit. The 2017 Kia Soul EV offered $18,100 off the "EV+" version or a $159/month lease over 36 months with $1,999 down, plus $7,500 federal and $2,500 California rebates. The 2017 Chevrolet Bolt EV leased for $303/month over 36 months, or $292/month for the 2017 model. The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox Diesel offered $4,000 off nationwide. The 2017 Toyota Yaris iA had $2,000 off in Southern California, priced around $15,000.

H H Martyn & Co, established in Cheltenham in 1888 by Herbert Henry Martyn, closed in 1971. The firm employed over 1,000 people by 1910 and became Gloucestershire's largest employer, excelling in diverse craftsmanship including ironwork, stone carving, ship fitting, and aircraft manufacturing. Notable commissions included gates for Marble Arch, interiors for Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle, fittings for over 100 ocean liners including the Titanic, and the birth of the Gloster Aircraft Company. The company also produced the Speaker's Chair in the House of Commons, the Cenotaph, and sculptures by Henry Moore. Despite its concentration of skilled craftsmanship, recession and the decline of British shipbuilding led Maples of London to close the firm in 1971.

A market research report on the Global Meat Starter Culture Market analyzes past and current trends to forecast future market values, covering manufacturers including Chr. Hansen, Danisco, Kerry, and others. The report examines market drivers, constraints, PEST and Porter's Five Forces analysis, and segmentation by product type (Maturation Starters, Surface Starters) and application (Meat, Poultry, Seafood, Others). It provides historical, current, and projected revenues by sector and region, including United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World from 2018 to 2025. The report includes SWOT analysis, investment feasibility, and regional market data on price, profit, capacity, production, supply, demand, and growth rates.

In 1826, Captain Thomas ap Catesby Jones negotiated the first formal treaty between Hawaii and a foreign power with King Kamehameha II, though it was never ratified by the U.S. In 1829, Captain Finch delivered a presidential letter urging peace and lawful conduct between Americans and Hawaiians. U.S. naval vessels continued visiting Hawaii, with Commodore Downs successfully interceding for Catholic converts in 1831. French demands in 1839, backed by threats from Commander Laplace, resulted in a treaty protecting Catholics. British consul Charlton's complaints led to Lord George Paulet seizing Hawaii in February 1843 and extracting a cession deed from King Kamehameha III. A British commission administered the government until Commodore Kearney protested in July 1843. Rear-Admiral Thomas arrived, disavowed the seizure, and restored Hawaiian sovereignty on July 31, 1843.

On September 9, 2020, Amazon.com, Inc.'s Board of Directors elected General (Ret.) Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee. Gen. Alexander is Co-CEO, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, Inc., which he founded in 2014. He previously served as Commander of U.S. Cyber Command (2010-2014) and Director of the National Security Agency (2005-2014). Upon election, he received a restricted stock unit award for 288 shares vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2021, and entered into a standard director indemnification agreement.

The passage introduces a recursive bipartitioning framework for community detection in networks that addresses two limitations of existing methods: the need to pre-specify the number of communities and the inability to capture hierarchical structures. The framework consists of a bipartitioning algorithm and a stopping rule based on Bayes factors, and can incorporate various model-based methods including stochastic block models, edge exchangeable models, and latent space models. The authors establish theoretical consistency results for the recursive bipartitioning method under the stochastic block model using Erdős-Renyi modularity, and describe Gibbs sampling algorithms for inference in each model class.

Progress Software Corporation held its Q3 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025, with Michael Micciche (Senior Vice President of Investor Relations), President and CEO Yogesh Gupta, and CFO Anthony Folger participating. The call included a safe harbor statement regarding forward-looking information and noted that financial figures referenced are non-GAAP measures unless otherwise indicated.

A study published in Nature found that exoplanet WASP-121b, a gas giant 880 light-years from Earth, has a stratosphere where temperature increases with altitude—similar to Earth and other solar system planets. Researchers detected this using Hubble's infrared spectrograph to observe water molecule signatures during the planet's transit. WASP-121b is a "hot Jupiter" orbiting its star every 1.3 days with atmospheric temperatures reaching 4,500°F. Scientists hope future observatories like the James Webb Space Telescope will enable study of smaller, cooler, potentially Earth-like exoplanets.

Winthrop University received $1.1 million of a $20 million National Science Foundation grant for research on complex materials, announced September 19. The five-year award, part of the MADE in SC initiative managed by EPSCoR, will fund 36 summer student research experiences, capital equipment purchases, and faculty research development. Five faculty members will lead research on electronic, optical, and biomaterials, including nanoparticle synthesis, supercapacitors, and photocatalysis for hydrogen energy production. The project also includes two-week summer teacher workshops for regional high school outreach. Winthrop was selected based on research quality among 10 participating South Carolina institutions competing nationally for the highly competitive grant.

The NHS Constitution, or Patient Charter, establishes patients' legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities. Rights include free care at point of use (with exceptions), equal access regardless of protected characteristics, waiting time standards, qualified staff in safe settings, NICE-recommended treatments, informed consent, privacy, choice of GP, involvement in decisions, duty of candour, and complaints procedures. Patient responsibilities involve self-care, respecting staff, following treatment plans, and participating in public health programmes. The Charter emphasizes partnership between patients and the NHS, empowering patients while requiring mutual contribution to maintain the service.

Coach Sutter discussed the team's emotional series against Chicago, noting the quick turnaround and schedule disruptions affected performance. He acknowledged five or six players were in their first Stanley Cup Final, which may have caused early issues. He praised Kyle's energy and role, emphasized that chasing leads is unsustainable, and highlighted Mike Richards' winning mentality and adaptability. Sutter addressed Jonathan's focus, a young player's development potential, and the small-town atmosphere in Manhattan Beach. He dismissed concerns about venue effects, explained defensive lineup changes, and noted he adjusted lines partway through the first period when multiple players struggled.

The Average True Range (ATR) is a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr., commonly used for stop-loss placement and position sizing rather than generating trading signals. This article demonstrates calculating ATR in Python using pandas_ta, then backtests a simple strategy on S&P 500 (SPY): buying when ATR exceeds its 14-day moving average and selling when it falls below. The backtest shows the strategy performs better when adjusted for risk but has similar drawdown to buy and hold. The authors suggest pairing ATR with other indicators may improve results.

A University of Bristol-led study found that chloroplasts split from their closest cyanobacterial ancestor over 2.1 billion years ago in low salinity environments, with the symbiotic relationship between chloroplast and eukaryotic host forming 200 million years later. Marine algae diversified around 800–750 million years ago, suggesting algae first evolved in freshwater before colonizing marine environments. The findings, published in PNAS (2017), have significant implications for understanding the carbon cycle and early life on Earth.

The Daily Stormer, a neo-Nazi website founded by Andrew Anglin in 2013, was removed from GoDaddy's domain registration service on August 13, 2017, after publishing an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed at the Charlottesville Unite The Right rally. GoDaddy cited terms of service violations regarding incitement of violence. The site briefly moved to Google Domains, which also terminated its registration within hours for similar violations. The Daily Stormer's web host remains obscured through Cloudflare, which has faced criticism for providing complainants' personal information to Anglin. The site also faced a claimed Anonymous hack and ongoing legal issues, including a lawsuit by the Southern Poverty Law Center for harassment of a Jewish family in Montana, with Anglin's whereabouts currently unknown.

NASA will broadcast a six-hour spacewalk on August 17 starting at 10:00am EDT, featuring Russian cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy of Expedition 52. The spacewalk begins at approximately 10:45am EDT from the Pirs airlock. Tasks include deploying five nanosatellites—one with a 3D-printed casing for material testing and another commemorating Sputnik 1's 60th anniversary and Konstantin Tsiolkovsky's 160th birth anniversary—collecting residue samples from the ISS exterior, and installing new handrails and struts. This is the only planned spacewalk for Expedition 52 and among the longest this year, though shorter than the record 7-hour, 4-minute spacewalk by Peggy Whitson on March 24, who has accumulated over 50 hours of spacewalking time.

This study estimated direct costs of managing measles in children at Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda. In 2018, 570 measles patients were admitted; 267 charts were sampled. Median age was 1 year, 63% were under 1 year, and 11% died. Severe pneumonia was the most common complication (39.5%). Average direct health care costs were $33.13 per patient (blood tests $11.73, radiology $3.48, treatment $21.98), with overhead costs of $81.37, totaling $114.50. Higher costs were associated with male gender, comorbidities, longer hospital stays (>15 days), and death. The study concludes that measles treatment costs substantially exceed vaccination costs ($0.86), supporting promotion of immunization.

Anne-Marie D'Amico, an Invesco employee, was identified as one of 10 people killed in a deliberate van attack on Yonge Street in Toronto at approximately 1:30pm ET on Monday. Fifteen others were injured. Suspect Alex Minassian, 25, was arrested after confronting police and is due in court. Police continue investigating the motive and identifying victims while appealing for witnesses.

This patent application describes a recommendation model training method and apparatus for big data applications. The method addresses challenges in training recommendation systems with massive data volumes, including overfitting, high computational costs, and data imbalance between positive and negative samples.

The core innovation involves calculating sampling probabilities for negative samples using a preset algorithm based on three rules: (1) sampling probability is negatively correlated with the score difference between positive and negative samples, (2) sampling probability is negatively correlated with the vector distance between positive and negative sample eigenvectors, and (3) sampling probability is positively correlated with the variation in ranking indicators when positive and negative sample rankings are exchanged. Higher sampling probabilities are assigned to negative samples that have greater impact on model training.

The method includes selecting positive samples for a training set, calculating sampling probabilities for negative samples, selecting negative samples based on these probabilities, and training the recommendation model. The trained model generates estimated scores for ranking objects and can be used iteratively to improve subsequent training. The apparatus includes sampling units and a training unit implementing these functions. Testing on HUAWEI APPGALLERY data showed improved performance over random sampling, dynamic negative sampling, and optimized logistic regression sampling methods.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and TSMC 7nm process, delivers significant AI and HPC performance improvements over previous generations. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary) with structured sparsity doubling throughput, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into up to seven isolated instances, third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s bandwidth, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, 40 MB L2 cache, and enhanced error detection and fault isolation. The A100 SM includes 192 KB combined L1/shared memory, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, and simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution. CUDA 11 adds support for task graphs, asynchronous operations, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering 5 petaFLOPS performance for scalable AI infrastructure.

The passage details the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It covers MSR protocol functions including CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, page state changes, VMPL execution, hypervisor feature support, and termination requests. The document specifies GHCB negotiation procedures between guests and hypervisors, NAE (Non-Automatic Exit) events for handling intercepted instructions, and SNP-specific features like AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, and restricted injection. It also describes SMP booting challenges under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, NMI handling, debug register virtualization, and the #HV doorbell page structure for interrupt delivery when restricted injection is enabled.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA Corporation, SoftBank Group Capital Limited, and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated the Share Purchase Agreement dated September 13, 2020, for NVIDIA's acquisition of Arm Limited due to significant regulatory challenges. SoftBank will retain the $1.25 billion prepaid by NVIDIA, while NVIDIA retains its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA will record a $1.36 billion charge in Q1 fiscal year 2023, including the $1.25 billion prepayment.

The "High/Low" zone offense is effective at all levels, combining outside three-player passing with interior high/low rotation. It creates matchup problems through constant interior movement and generates open outside shots when defenses collapse. The offense features simple continuity with entries from point to wing, post rolls, high post flashes, and ball reversals. Key entries include Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns. Special situational plays like Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas provide quick-hitting options late in shot clocks or after timeouts.

MITOCW lecture on business plan financials by Charlie Tillett, former CFO and $10K Contest participant. Covers creating financial projections using an Excel template, understanding business models through percentage-based income statements, venture capital expectations (3-5x returns over 5-7 years), equity dilution across funding rounds, and cash flow management. Tillett emphasizes building bottom-up sales projections, benchmarking against industry peers, and maintaining 10-20% R&D and 5-15% G&A as percentages of revenue. Discusses founder vesting (typically 4 years), employee equity ranges, and the importance of experienced financial leadership before taking venture capital.

This paper presents a knowledge graph-based approach to support criminal investigations analyzing Instant Messaging App (IMA) data. The solution combines speech-to-text transcription (using Whisper), entity extraction via a Named Entity rEcognition and Linking (NEEL) pipeline, and semantic search interfaces to help investigators explore large volumes of chat data and audio messages. Developed in collaboration with Italian prosecutors and law enforcement through an official consultant contract, the system was tested on two real investigations involving over 1,000 chats and hundreds of thousands of messages. The approach stores data as a property graph in Neo4j for visualization and querying, and provides faceted search through a DAVE web application. Investigators found the graph visualizations and semantic search capabilities helpful, particularly for reducing the manual effort required to analyze audio content. Current limitations include the need for domain-specific fine-tuning of NLP components and the requirement for technical expertise to use graph query interfaces. Future work aims to improve the NEEL pipeline, develop conversational search interfaces, and extend multimedia enrichment to images and videos.

AQTWM, Inc. (Aqua Terra) announced it filed a preliminary prospectus for an initial public offering of common shares with Canadian securities commissions, excluding Québec. The offering will be underwritten by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity, and RBC Capital Markets. Share quantity and price are undetermined. The Prospectus is available on SEDAR but not yet final. The release is not for U.S. distribution; securities are unregistered under U.S. law with no U.S. public offering planned. Aqua Terra provides oilfield water management and disposal services in Canada (Montney, Viking, Conventional Heavy Oil, Saskatchewan Bakken regions) and the U.S. (Permian, North Dakota Bakken, Eagle Ford regions).

This MIT lecture covers coding for bandwidth-limited channels, focusing on lattice constellations, shaping, and trellis codes. The professor explains that while binary codes work well for power-limited channels, bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels require non-binary, multi-level codes using Euclidean distance metrics.

Key topics include: the union-bound estimate for probability of error per n dimensions, which separates coding gain (from lattice structure) from shaping gain (from region geometry); shaping techniques where n-spheres provide maximum theoretical gain of 1.53 dB as dimensionality increases; and lattice constructions including Barnes-Wall lattices (D4, E8, Lambda-16) with their coding gains and nearest neighbor problems.

The lecture details trellis-coded modulation developed by Ungerboeck in 1982, using set partitioning and convolutional codes to achieve coding gains. A four-state rate-1/2 code yields 3 dB gain, while more complex codes reach 5-6 dB. Four-dimensional constellations (Wei codes) reduce redundancy requirements, achieving 4.2 dB with practical complexity.

Advanced techniques mentioned include multi-level coding and bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM), which approaches capacity using existing binary coding chips. The professor concludes that while traditional AWGN coding has matured near Shannon limits, research continues in iterative decoding convergence, graph theory, and network/multi-user applications.

Major drugmakers are scrambling to negotiate price-lowering deals with the Trump administration following Pfizer's agreement, while concerns arise about a December pharmaceutical summit hosted by BlinkRx—an online drug delivery company with Donald Trump Jr. as a board member—potentially favoring Trump family ties. Sarepta faces a setback as a New York panel recommends pausing Medicaid coverage for its Duchenne drug, and Colorado becomes the first state to set a payment limit on an Amgen drug. Other developments include Medicare gaining expanded drug price negotiation authority, former FDA vaccine regulator Peter Marks joining Eli Lilly, and the Trump administration backing off threatened 100% pharmaceutical tariffs.

The speaker presents his thesis research on manufacturing microfluidic devices using polymers, focusing on hot embossing of thermoplastic layers. Polymers are preferred over silicon or glass due to lower cost, transparency for biological observation, and mechanical toughness for field use. The hot embossing process involves heating polymer above its glass transition temperature, applying load to fill stamp cavities, then cooling below transition temperature before removing the load. Key parameters include temperature, load, and timing.

The speaker distinguishes micro hot embossing (thicker workpieces) from thermal nano imprint lithography (sub-micron layers on silicon wafers), which enables sub-micron feature transfer without light wavelength limitations. Stamp creation methods include deep reactive ion etching for micro-scale features and electron beam lithography for nano-scale features.

Research challenges include pattern-dependent non-uniformity, de-molding issues from differential thermal contraction, and dimensional stability. The speaker describes developing simplified viscoelastic models using springs and dashpots to efficiently simulate embossing outcomes, validated through experiments with PMMA and cyclic olefin polymers (ZEONOR, TOPAS). Results show temperature, force, and hold time significantly affect cavity filling, with material anisotropy observed in TOPAS. Optimal de-molding near glass transition temperature can minimize defects but requires precise temperature control.

University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no evidence he posed a threat or violated policy. Dixon, a teaching associate professor of Asian and Middle Eastern studies, was placed on leave following allegations related to his activism at counterprotests and past membership in Redneck Revolt. The university consulted with security offices and law enforcement before clearing him.

The gold-silver ratio strategy involves trading precious metals based on their price relationship, calculated by dividing gold price by silver price. The article backtested several approaches: buying gold when RSI exceeds 75 (which showed erratic results), shorting silver under the same conditions, and a pair trade buying gold while shorting silver. None proved robust. Historically, governments fixed the ratio (12:1 in Rome, 15:1 in early US), but it now floats freely, averaging 47:1 in the 20th century and ranging 50-70:1 recently, with extremes of 35:1 (2011) and 114.77 (2020). Traders typically use mean-reversion strategies, buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, or vice versa when low. The authors found no consistently profitable strategies using this ratio for metals or equities.

Hetzner, South Africa's largest specialist hosting company, has established a direct 10Gbps peering connection at NAP Africa in Isando, Johannesburg, joining Africa's largest active peering community. This follows their earlier connection at NAP Africa in Cape Town and JINX peering a year ago. Over 65% of Hetzner's local traffic now routes through these exchange points rather than costly transit links, with the company contributing over 4Gbps of traffic weekly. Hetzner advocates for settlement-free peering to reduce connectivity costs, lower latency, and increase network resilience. The company peers with major South African network operators and maintains a carrier-neutral data centre in Samrand with redundant 10Gbps connections and access to four international cable systems.

A letter from Deborah Jones, Rain gardens coordinator for Cougar Creek Streamkeepers, opposes a development permit application for highrise buildings at 7592 119A St. and 7551, 7565, 7595 and 7597 120 St. in North Delta. The proposal for 35 storeys conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan's six-storey limit and fails to meet policies on tree preservation, urban forest canopy, watershed-based stormwater management, and rainwater infiltration. The parking garage would occupy the entire lot, preventing groundwater recharge despite 7-8 million litres of annual rainfall. Jones argues the project does not qualify for tax exemptions under the Scott Road Revitalization Bylaw's "low environmental impact" requirement. She warns approving this would encourage developer pressure to upzone other properties, increase land speculation, and notes highrise condos often become speculative investments rather than housing. She suggests rejection unless the developer provides significant environmental mitigation, including at least 15% open permeable space for trees and infiltration, and proposes requiring all multi-family developments to set aside 15% permeable land.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification outlines technical requirements for AMD firmware updates. For attestation, OS or system management software requests evidence via side-band (SPDM) or in-band (DPE) interfaces, with SFS providing measurements to attestation managers; AMD will not modify firmware protected by certain attestation schemes. Update packages must verify proper firmware versions exist before updating to prevent version mismatches, and partial package application is prohibited to avoid forced resets. Update packages are non-persistent across reboots and can be applied during OS boot, after system boot, or during operation.

SFS commands require 2MB memory alignment for TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, with specific address offsets for GET_FW_VERSIONS and UPDATE_FW commands. A customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent creates command buffers, appends co-signing headers and signatures if used, and communicates requests via the TEE mailbox interface. The ASP process involves protecting DRAM from x86 access, verifying customer and AMD signatures, loading and executing patches, and returning status.

The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command retrieves firmware and patch level information using two contiguous pages, with output initialized to C7h. The UPDATE_FW command loads, verifies, and executes SFS packages after full validation. Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run parallel to x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; most require no OS quiescing, though SEV/SEV-ES VMs must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP VMs can continue operation.

Apple Inc. filed its Q3 2018 Form 10-Q with the SEC for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2018. The company reported net sales of $53.3 billion for Q3 2018 (up 17% year-over-year) and $202.7 billion for the nine-month period. Net income was $11.5 billion for Q3 and $45.4 billion for nine months. Key drivers included higher iPhone, Services, and Other Products sales, with Services revenue growing 31% to $9.5 billion in Q3. iPhone net sales increased 20% to $29.9 billion despite flat unit sales, due to higher average selling prices. The company repurchased $20 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends during Q3. Apple adopted new accounting standards for share-based compensation and income taxes, including adjustments related to the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered the federal tax rate to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax. The company faces ongoing litigation including VirnetX patent infringement cases ($503 million verdict in April 2018) and a dispute with Qualcomm over royalty payments. As of June 30, 2018, Apple held $243.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, with total assets of $349.2 billion and long-term debt of $97.1 billion.

This paper presents a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) framework called EqDiff-CT for synthesizing CT images from CBCT scans in head and neck radiotherapy. The method uses a time-conditioned, group-equivariant U-Net denoiser with self-attention blocks, trained with a non-adversarial hybrid objective combining MSE and SSIM losses on predicted noise. Evaluations on the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset demonstrate superior performance over baseline diffusion and CycleGAN models in SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE metrics, while preserving clinically relevant anatomical structures.

A speaker discusses their hockey team's performance and preparation for upcoming games against Dallas, acknowledging mistakes made while recognizing Dallas's strong record after first-game losses. They emphasize focusing on current preparation rather than dwelling on past games, noting Dallas's tendency to become more aggressive and physical after slow starts. The speaker stresses the importance of limiting time and space for Dallas's skilled players including Modano, Hull, and Nieuwendyk. They highlight the significance of Game 2 for both teams, with Dallas seeking to split on the road and their own team wanting to build a 2-0 lead. The speaker evaluates individual player performances, noting one player's improved defensive responsibility and another's struggles with turnovers from trying to do too much. They acknowledge their team played poorly with poor puck decisions and insufficient forechecking penetration, yet remained close against the Stanley Cup champions. A disputed offside goal by Hull is mentioned but dismissed as not the reason for losing. The speaker concludes that despite creating adversity for themselves, the series is tied 1-1 and there is no need to panic.

A CDC report shows mosquito, tick, and flea-borne illnesses have tripled in the U.S. since 2004. Venice faces particular risk due to still waters in the Venice Canals and Ballona Wetlands. West Nile Virus, which incubates in birds and spreads to humans through mosquito bites, is endemic in Los Angeles County, with 300 human cases reported in 2015. While 80% of infected people show no symptoms, severe cases can cause neuroinvasive disease with tremors, coma, and paralysis. The Los Angeles County West Vector & Vector-Borne Disease Control District manages standing water to prevent breeding. Residents are advised to use insect repellent containing 5-30% DEET or alternatives like picaridin when outdoors between dusk and dawn, and to eliminate standing water in yards.

Weston Public Library is hosting events for the August 21 solar eclipse, when Weston will see approximately 70% coverage. The library will distribute free solar viewers starting August 14, host a pinhole projector workshop for ages 5+ on August 15, and live stream NASA coverage with treats on August 21.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 by WIRED, are currently discounted to $128 on Amazon. These gaming earbuds feature portability, compatibility with Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, PC, and smartphones, low-latency 2.4GHz audio via USB-C dongle, Bluetooth connectivity, 10-hour battery life (40 hours with case), active noise-canceling, game-specific equalizer settings via mobile app, physical button controls, and comfort for everyday use.

Metal complex (MC) crystals, composed of metal ions coordinated with organic or inorganic ligands, have been studied for over a century. Recently, melt-quenched MC glasses, including metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses, coordination polymer (CP) glasses, and metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) glasses, have attracted attention due to their bulk nature and enhanced processability. However, their preparation is constrained by ligand decomposition or molecular sublimation upon heating.

This work synthesized two Zn-based MIOC crystals—MIOC-4 (ZnCl2HIm2) and MIOC-7 (ZnCl2HbIm2)—by introducing chloride into ZIFs. MIOC-4 has a monoclinic phase with stacked hydrogen-bonded layers, while MIOC-7 has a triclinic phase with interdigitated layers featuring π-π interactions. Melting points were 440 K and 508 K, respectively, with glass transition temperatures of 282 K and 359 K. Mixed-ligand synthesis created binary MIOC mixed-crystals with reduced melting points and tunable glass-transition temperatures.

In-situ XRD revealed that melting begins with slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded structures, followed by rapid disordering upon hydrogen bond breaking. FT-IR, Raman, NMR, and high-energy XRD analyses showed that vitrification preserves short-range Zn-ligand correlations while disrupting medium- and long-range intermolecular order. The ligand-tuning approach was extended to Co/Cu metal nodes and SCN- anions, confirming its universality.

MIOC-7 glass exhibited enhanced photoluminescence compared to its crystalline form, with internal quantum yield increasing from 1.2% to 3.4%. The glass showed excitation-dependent emission with red-shift behavior attributed to frozen molecular conformations in the rigid hydrogen-bonded network, demonstrating potential for anti-counterfeiting applications.

James Harden became the first NBA player to record a 60-point triple-double, leading the short-handed Houston Rockets to a 114-107 victory over the Orlando Magic. Harden finished with 60 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists, breaking Calvin Murphy's 1978 Rockets single-game scoring record. The Rockets played without Chris Paul, Trevor Ariza, and lost Eric Gordon to injury early in the game. Harden scored 18 points in the fourth quarter, including a record-breaking 3-pointer and subsequent free throw. The game was tied at 107 with under four minutes remaining before Harden scored six straight points to seal the win. Hezonja and Speights each scored 17 points for Orlando. The Magic host the Lakers next, while the Rockets visit San Antonio.

This patent application describes a networked exercise system, particularly a treadmill, designed for streaming and on-demand exercise classes. The system addresses limitations of existing home and gym equipment by incorporating features for competition, social interaction, and gamification. The treadmill includes dual rotary controls on separate arms for controlling different functions (such as speed and incline), each with tactile, visual, and audible feedback mechanisms. The system enables real-time interaction between users and instructors through video, audio, and data sharing, supports unlimited remote participants in live or recorded classes, and provides comprehensive performance tracking and display interfaces for class selection, metrics, and leaderboards.

The Socket 940 specifications define its physical dimensions, materials, and electrical characteristics. The socket cover and base are made from black and natural/ivory Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) with UL 94 V-0 flammability rating. The package-seating plane is 4.00 ± 0.20 mm from the PCB mounting surface with flatness better than 0.25 mm. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm. Markings include "SOCKET 940," directional indicators, orientation symbols, UL symbols, and lot traceability numbers. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with 1.27 µm nickel and 0.76 µm gold plating. SMT solder balls are 63/37 tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, with 0.20 mm co-planarity. A stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation with forces under 3.6 kgf. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 cycles. Electrical specifications include 1.5 A current rating, initial and final LLCR under 25 mΩ, inductance under 4 nH, capacitance under 1 pF, 100 Ω ± 10% differential impedance, propagation delay skew under 10 ps, minimum 650 Vac dielectric withstanding voltage, and minimum 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

This passage outlines strategies for teaching and implementing an early offense and press break in basketball. Key principles include precise execution, coaching players rather than systems, and using the "Whole-Part-Whole" teaching method with progressive breakdown drills from one-on-one to five-player scenarios. Coaching objectives focus on developing poise against presses, proper outlet passing, quick ball advancement, and flowing into early offense. The method emphasizes starting with visual demonstrations, walking through options, using progressive drills, and practicing at game speed against motivated defense. Recommended drills include "Wolf," "Michigan," and continuous 3-on-2 with trail. Game strategies include playing tenacious defense, breaking on every possession, and scouting opponents. The passage concludes by noting that defensive pressure can disrupt early offense flow and catch teams unprepared.

The speaker discusses a goalie's mental resilience after facing adversity, comparing two centers who excel at faceoffs and two-way play, noting similarities between teams in defensive style and physicality, emphasizing disciplined play between whistles, team-first identity, and the necessity of using two goalies during playoffs.

A Kentucky high school valedictorian used a bullhorn to deliver his graduation speech outside after the Catholic diocese barred him from speaking at commencement, citing late submission and content inconsistent with church teaching. Christian Bales, who is gay, spoke about student activism and youth power, referencing Florida students' gun reform efforts. Student council president Katherine Frantz also gave her speech by bullhorn. Bales said the diocese's attempt to silence him backfired, giving him a national platform instead of a 300-person audience. His mother agreed the opposition amplified his voice.

The Trump administration's goal of hiring hundreds of new federal prosecutors is proceeding slowly. LinkedIn data shows hiring of assistant US attorneys dropped by more than half from January through August compared to the same period in the previous four years. The slowdown stems from budget pressures, hiring freezes, pay raises making recruitment more expensive, and turmoil at the Justice Department including sagging morale and concerns about ethically questionable casework. Despite the administration's call to add over 400 attorneys, factors like public skepticism of law enforcement, rising wages, and the DOGE initiative causing departures have hindered progress. Some US Attorneys' Offices are now making hiring pushes, and the department maintains high standards—over a third of new hires attended Top 14 law schools. Former prosecutors offer mixed advice to young lawyers about pursuing government work, with some citing ongoing controversies and potential White House meddling as concerns.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture introduces significant advancements across multiple areas. The GPU enhances Async Compute functionality, allowing RT Core and graphics/compute workloads to process concurrently, with new software controls for workload prioritization. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing rates and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit that accelerates ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing architecture. Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce Sparsity for up to 2x speedup, support new data types including TF32 and BF16, and enable 8K DLSS gaming. GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling achieves up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth, a 52% improvement over previous generations. NVIDIA RTX IO offloads storage decompression from CPU to GPU, improving I/O performance by up to 100x. The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and 5-10x AI throughput compared to Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000. Display support includes 8K60 and 4K120 via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode support, while seventh-generation NVENC enables high-quality encoding up to 8K HEVC. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology helps users identify optimal memory overclocking limits without crashes.

The ADX (Average Directional Movement Index) indicator, developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, measures trend strength but not direction. It consists of three components: ADX (trend strength), DI+ (uptrend momentum), and DI- (downtrend momentum). The indicator ranges from 0-100, with readings above 20 indicating trending markets and below 15 indicating non-trending markets.

Backtesting on the S&P 500 showed mixed standalone results. A DI+/DI- crossover strategy using 10-day periods produced a 5.4% CAGR with 1.71 profit factor. An ADX breakout strategy (35-day DMs, 15-day ADX) yielded only 3.03% CAGR versus 9.9% buy-and-hold, though with smaller drawdowns (13.76% vs 55%).

The ADX proved more valuable as a filter for other strategies. When combined with an unspecified mean-reverting indicator, adding an ADX filter (5-10 days, 30-40 threshold) improved the profit factor from 2.15 to 2.6% while reducing market exposure from 24% to 7%. On Nasdaq (QQQ), this combined approach achieved 12.5% CAGR with 8% exposure.

The article concludes that while the ADX works reasonably well alone, it adds greater value when combined with other indicators, and recommends proper backtesting to develop profitable strategies.

A hockey player discusses game strategy, including power play execution, defensive coverage, overtime momentum, and penalty kill challenges. He praises teammates' abilities, acknowledges fan support, and expresses confidence in the team's depth despite key player absences.

A study by Stanford, Harvard, and Census Bureau researchers found that in 99% of U.S. neighborhoods, black boys earn less in adulthood than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds, challenging the belief that class outweighs race in predicting economic outcomes. The study analyzed data from 20 million children and parents, tracking outcomes across racial groups. Black and Native American children showed the lowest upward economic mobility rates, while whites and Asians ranked highest. Even among the wealthiest families, black children grew up to earn 12.4% less than white children from similar households. About 11% of white children from the bottom income fifth rose to the top, compared to 2.5% of black children. The income gap is driven primarily by earnings differences between black and white men; black women actually earn slightly more than white women when parental income is controlled. A few neighborhoods showed parity, including some D.C. suburbs with low racial bias and high percentages of present black fathers. Researchers suggest historical factors may explain persistent disparities for African-Americans and Native Americans.

Clinton pledged a new American Embassy in Berlin and affirmed continued U.S. military presence in Europe. He called for "civil courage to build" a democratic, prosperous Europe without borders, rejecting divisive rhetoric about race, ethnicity, or religion. Clinton walked through the Brandenburg Gate with Chancellor Kohl, declaring it a gateway to a united Europe "united in peace, united in freedom, united in progress."

President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Pfizer to lower U.S. drug prices, including selling existing drugs to Medicaid patients at the lowest price offered in other developed nations through a website called TrumpRx.gov. Virtual education offers benefits including schedule flexibility, individualized learning, credit recovery, accommodations for special needs, parental engagement, and preparation for post-secondary education. Challenges include internet access issues, need for independent motivation, delayed feedback, isolation, difficulties accommodating special needs, and maintaining student engagement.

A study of Indiana school districts during 2020-21 found COVID-19 concerns were the primary factor driving virtual program implementation (79.2% of superintendents) and maintenance (84.8% of program directors). Credit recovery was the second most important factor. Key benefits identified were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner flexibility. Primary challenges were student engagement, curriculum quality, and professional development for staff.

Interviews with 11 administrators revealed three themes: pandemic impacts on school corporations (financial concerns, technology plan changes), teachers (stress, inadequate training), and students (social-emotional needs, parental support requirements, engagement issues). The study suggests virtual education growth will likely continue beyond the pandemic due to school choice demands and personalization needs.

This paper studies the existence of satisficing paths in multi-agent reinforcement learning from a topological perspective. The authors introduce the novel concept of grouped satisficing paths, which extends the classical "win-stay, lose-shift" principle from individual players to player groups. They establish sufficient conditions for the existence of finite-length grouped satisficing paths from any initial joint strategy to an equilibrium: convex and compact strategy sets, continuous and partially analytic payoff functions, and existence of equilibria in all sub-games. The main results include Theorem 1, which provides conditions for reducing games to sub-games under grouped satisficing dynamics, and Theorem 2, which establishes the existence theorem. Four corollaries apply these results to continuous games, N-player games, and finite-state Markov games (both stationary and k-step), proving that satisficing paths exist in these practical settings. The paper concludes with open problems regarding necessary conditions, extensions to ϵ > 0, and neighborhood restrictions on strategy selection.

The lecture covers two main topics: protein folding and interlocked chains. For protein folding, the professor discusses the HP (hydrophobic-polar) model, a simplified lattice-based model where hydrophobic (H) and hydrophilic (P) amino acids are represented as nodes on a chain folded on a square grid. The goal is to maximize adjacent H-H bonds. Finding optimal foldings is NP-hard in both 2D and 3D. A 1/3-approximation algorithm exists that works by pairing even-parity H nodes on one side with odd-parity H nodes on the other. Unique optimal foldings exist for certain chain lengths in closed and open chains.

For interlocked chains, the lecture examines when multiple open or closed chains in 3D cannot be separated. Key results include: two 2-chains (hairpins) always separate, as do 2-chain/3-chain and 3-chain/3-chain pairs; but 3-chain/4-chain pairs can interlock. The minimum cuts needed to unlock a chain (Lubiw's problem) is between n/4 and (4n-3)/2. Topological arguments using spheres and linking numbers prove interlocking. Applications include building rigid structures for PSPACE-completeness proofs in motion planning.

E-mini futures are electronically traded contracts that are one-fifth the size of standard futures contracts, created by the CME in 1997 to make futures markets accessible to individual investors with less capital. They are available on various indexes, commodities, and currencies, with the S&P 500 E-Mini being the most actively traded.

To trade e-mini S&P 500 futures, traders need approximately $13,000-$15,000 in their account, though the CME maintenance margin requirement is $10,000. Costs typically range from $0.50-$2.50 per contract plus fees. E-minis offer leverage and 24-hour trading but carry significant risks due to volatility and the zero-sum nature of derivatives markets.

A backtested Rubber Band strategy on the @ES contract from 2000-2021 showed 163 trades with 79% win rate and 2.0 profit factor, though 2022 out-of-sample results were weaker (0.18% average gain vs. -15% S&P 500 decline). This study examines digital transformation leadership in education through bibliometric analysis, focusing on Thailand's transition to Education 4.0 and Digital Thailand 4.0. The research identifies five critical components of digital educator competency: comprehension, utilization, leadership, integration of digital technology, and ethical considerations. Six leadership components address rapid technological change and national policies. The analysis covers 2019-2025, emphasizing COVID-19's acceleration of digital disruption. Key findings highlight five pillars of digital transformation leadership: Digital Literacy (access and utilization skills), Digital Readiness (organizational preparedness), Digital Culture (technology-embracing organizational change), Digital Mindset (design thinking and innovation acceptance), and Digital Leadership (vision-setting and adaptability). The study concludes that successful transformation requires K-S-A (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities) development, collaborative digital teams, and cultural transformation led by top-level management with clear vision.

This research examines Songyang Academy's educational philosophy and its relationship to general education. Founded in 484 AD, Songyang Academy is one of China's four major academies with over 1,500 years of history, experiencing rises and falls across multiple dynasties. The study uses documentary and field research methods, including literature collection, local chronicles, and interviews.

The academy's educational philosophy emphasizes moral education as core, cultivating personality through "the way of adulthood," and the unity of knowledge and action. It advocates learning for practical use with the goal of "cultivating oneself, managing the family, governing the country, and pacifying the world." The academy practiced non-discriminatory education, attracting students regardless of region or status, and employed teaching methods emphasizing autonomous learning, mutual questioning, and debate.

Songyang Academy's educational concepts align with modern general education principles, which emphasize all-round development of morality, intelligence, physical fitness, and aesthetics rather than narrow vocational training. The academy's focus on combining moral education with teaching, autonomous learning, and the integration of knowledge and practice provides valuable experience for contemporary general education development. The research concludes that reviving and adapting these traditional educational concepts can contribute to cultivating well-rounded modern talents.

Kobe University researchers discovered that orchid seeds germinate exclusively near decaying logs by forming partnerships with wood-decaying fungi, which provide carbon the dust-sized seeds lack. This finding reveals a hidden carbon pathway from deadwood to plants in forest ecosystems and explains how some orchid species evolved to depend entirely on fungi for nutrition throughout their lives.

This study examined 30 elementary inclusion teachers in Liloan District, Philippines to assess their attitudes toward inclusive education and develop an intervention plan. Using descriptive correlational design and Modified STATIC survey, findings showed teachers held positive philosophical attitudes (mean 4.03) and professional views (4.08), but neutral stances on logistical concerns (3.23) and advantages/disadvantages (3.50). Most teachers were female (93%), married (83%), aged 34-43, with graduate-level units (77%), yet had limited experience with special needs learners (90% had 1-5 years) and minimal training (80% had 1-2 sessions). No significant relationships existed between demographics and attitudes. Teachers recognized inclusion's social benefits but expressed concerns about resources, class sizes, and practical implementation. The study concluded that while philosophical foundations were strong, sustained professional development, smaller classes, stronger support systems, and targeted resources are needed to translate positive attitudes into sustainable practices as inclusion reforms expand.

Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School reopened on February 28, 2018, with heavy security including about 50 uniformed officers, therapy dogs, and grief counselors, two weeks after 17 students and teachers were killed in a shooting. A study found that over half of 21st-century FDA-approved drugs are linked to NIH research that would have been at risk under a 40% budget cut. The paper "What if NIH had been 40% smaller?" examined grants in the bottom 40% of funding priority from 1980-2007 and their connection to drugs approved from 2000-2023. Of 557 approved drugs, 40 directly cited NIH extramural funding, with 14 citing at-risk grants including Cerdelga for Gaucher disease. Fifty-nine percent of approved drugs cited at least one NIH-supported publication, and 65 had "highly linked" research with over 25% NIH-funded citations, including Tarceva for lung cancer. Drugs linked to at-risk research showed higher FDA priority review rates (60% vs. 41%) and greater market value than unlinked drugs. Researchers noted these findings likely underestimate total impacts, as they only captured direct connections to new active ingredient drugs and not indirect research pathways.

The Supreme Court, Bronx County, dismissed Brian O'Loughlin's defamation action against the Patrolmen's Benevolent Association and its president Phil Caruso, and this dismissal was unanimously affirmed on appeal. The dispute concerned a letter in which Caruso called O'Loughlin and eight other officers "a disgrace" with "no feelings" for requesting refunds of a $20 memorial contribution. The court held that Caruso's statements were non-actionable expressions of pure opinion under the standard from *Steinhilber v Alphonse*, as they were indefinite, ambiguous, and could not be characterized as true or false. The context and readership of the PBA magazine indicated Caruso was expressing personal opinion about the officers' unwillingness to support the organization's project, not stating verifiable facts.

Vertical farming grows crops in controlled, soilless, stacked environments using methods like hydroponics and aeroponics. Growth drivers include food quality, population increase, reduced water/soil dependency, and new technologies. Barriers include high urban investment costs, energy consumption, and focus on high-value crops. North America leads the market; Asia-Pacific is fastest-growing. Key players include Aerofarms, Philips, and Sky Greens. The global market is projected to reach USD 6 billion by 2022 with 21% CAGR. The market is segmented by component (hardware, software, services), type (hydroponic, aeroponic, aquaponic), crop type, and region.

Rising global population drives increased cereal production and pesticide usage, particularly herbicides. The grain and cereal crop protection market includes insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, with herbicides dominating due to low cost and R&D investments. Crop rotation protects crops and maintains soil nutrients, though chemical crop protection harms the environment, human health, and soil productivity. Geographically, North America leads the market, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, with Asia Pacific expected to grow fastest. Demand is boosted by population growth, food consumption, and health awareness in developing countries like India, China, and Japan. The market features numerous local, regional, and international vendors competing on price, quality, innovation, and distribution.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff at BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% went to Democrats in 2023-2024, up from a 6-1 ratio in 2017-2020. WiseGuyReports published a market research report on November 14, 2017 forecasting the US data center UPS market to grow at a CAGR of 4.01% from 2016-2020.
