New York's Board of Regents voted unanimously to allow special-education students to earn high school diplomas through occupational assessments rather than minimum scores on Regents exams in English and math. The emergency measure, proposed by Education Commissioner MaryEllen Elia, applies to students graduating as early as January. Parents lobbied for the change, arguing their children's futures depended on it. Currently, special-education students could earn local diplomas with lower exam scores or obtain CDOS certificates, which employers often don't recognize as valid. Under the new plan, students meeting CDOS requirements can earn local diplomas if their superintendent determines academic proficiency. Students graduating in 2017-19 receive additional flexibility. In 2016, over 15,000 students with disabilities statewide failed to earn diplomas after four years. Some analysts expressed concerns about reviving separate academic tracks and the rushed policy process.

Turkey secures €974 million loan from international lenders for a central Anatolian highway project to improve connectivity, trade access, and regional economic development. The District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District, affirmed the Agency for Health Care Administration's final order dismissing Riverwood Nursing Center's untimely request for an administrative hearing. Glenwood Nursing Center appealed AHCA's dismissal of its June 15, 2010 hearing request, arguing equitable tolling based on AHCA counsel's post-deadline agreement to accept late filings, and that its April 16, 2010 letter to CMS challenging state law deficiencies constituted a timely request that its June filing amended. The court rejected both arguments: equitable tolling did not apply because Glenwood knew the deadline and no pre-deadline extension was agreed to, distinguishing Foley v. Dep't of Health and following Watson v. Brevard County Clerk; and the April letter to CMS was insufficient as a matter of law to invoke Chapter 120 rights because it was not filed with AHCA's agency clerk as required by statute and administrative rule. The court affirmed AHCA's order revoking Glenwood's nursing home license and imposing a $25,000 fine.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz.

The controllers feature hiccup mode operation where cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, with a CHICC capacitor controlling delay and restart timing. External fault protection is available through the FAULT pin, which triggers shutdown above 0.6 V for 0.4–1.4 µs. Slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle, set via an RSC resistor. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B schemes with transconductance error amplifier.

A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices demonstrates component selection: 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 25 ns dead time with 20.5 kΩ resistors, 49.9 kΩ RLEB for 50 ns leading edge blanking, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5:1 transformer turns ratio with 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary GaN FETs, 0.47 µH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance for SET mitigation, 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, and 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF.

Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt/dv/dt loops, keeping feedback traces away from noise sources, and placing bypass capacitors close to pins. The controllers operate from 4–14 V input with 0.1 µF minimum bypass capacitance.

RTX Neural Faces is a real-time generative AI technology that addresses the challenge of rendering realistic human faces in games. Faith-based organisations are increasingly supporting the NHS, with over 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers working on health and social care initiatives, according to the Cinnamon Network. This IDC White Paper examines how high-performance computing (HPC) serves as a transformative technology for manufacturing industries in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Columbiana defeated Lisbon 49-47 in a high school girls basketball game after scoring twice in the final 23 seconds. This paper proposes iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning method for zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in PDE dynamics forecasting. The authors identify two-level PDE invariance—operator invariance and compositionality invariance—and design a mixture of operator experts architecture with frequency-enriched invariant learning objective to capture this invariance. Experiments on five PDE systems and real-world SST data demonstrate iMOOE's superior zero-shot OOD performance compared to existing methods, with 40.21% improvement on nMSE and 30.78% on fRMSE. The method also shows compatibility with diverse neural operator backbones.

The lecture covers quantum gases, focusing on Bose and Fermi gases with interactions and their superfluid properties. The professor reviews the Bogoliubov approximation for homogeneous Bose gases, where replacing condensate operators with c-numbers transforms the Hamiltonian into a bilinear form describing non-interacting quasiparticles with linear dispersion at low momenta. Experimental observation of sound propagation in Bose-Einstein condensates using laser-induced density perturbations is discussed, along with quantum depletion—showing cold atomic gases have ~1% depletion versus ~90% in liquid helium. The dynamic structure factor and stimulated Raman spectroscopy methods for measuring quasiparticle dispersion are explained.

For inhomogeneous systems in harmonic traps, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation describes the macroscopic wave function, with interactions flattening density profiles and creating a healing length scale where kinetic and interaction energies balance. The Thomas-Fermi approximation neglecting kinetic energy yields inverted parabola density profiles. Vortices in rotating condensates are discussed, with multiple singly-charged vortices forming lattices due to energy minimization, unlike doubly-charged vortices which are unstable.

The lecture then covers optical lattices, introducing the Bose-Hubbard model with tunneling parameter j and on-site interaction U. In the tight-binding limit, Wannier functions localize particles at lattice sites. The superfluid-to-Mott insulator transition is analyzed using mean-field theory: when U >> j, the system is an insulator with fixed particle number per site; when j >> U, it becomes superfluid with delocalized Bloch waves. A decoupling approximation treating tunneling perturbatively from the insulating side reveals the transition occurs when a psi-squared term in the energy changes sign, creating a phase diagram with Mott lobes at integer fillings separated by superfluid regions. Experimental signatures include interference patterns in time-of-flight imaging for superfluids versus structureless expansion for insulators, and quantum gas microscopy showing site-resolved atom distributions.

Crude sulfate turpentine is a flammable byproduct of the Kraft process used in fragrances, flavors, cosmetics, food & beverages, and as a paint solvent. This study presents a pragmatic randomized controlled trial protocol evaluating Ambient AI, a generative AI tool for clinical documentation, within a Learning Health System (LHS) framework at University of Wisconsin Hospitals and Clinics. The authors developed a Pragmatic Trial Operations (PTOps) playbook with five core components—governance, user experience, technical strategies, documentation sustainment, and analytics—to align research and operational priorities. The alpha phase (June-October 2024) involved 20 providers and 8,527 encounters, using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles to refine workflows and address issues including diagnostic coding accuracy, which dropped from 79% to 35% post-intervention before recovering after template modifications. The beta phase implements a 24-week stepped-wedge trial with 66 providers across eight specialties. Key innovations include automated ICD-10 code extraction using a large language model (mean Jaccard score 0.54), real-time dashboard monitoring, and difference-in-differences analysis to detect performance drift from software updates. The governance structure integrated executive sponsors with multidisciplinary teams, enabling iterative improvements while maintaining research rigor.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture introduces significant performance improvements over the previous Turing generation, including up to 2x faster traditional raster graphics and ray tracing performance. API misuses in software systems can cause runtime errors, performance issues, or incorrect output. While most research has focused on statically typed languages, Python's dynamic typing and growing use in data science introduce unique challenges. Data-centric libraries—those with extensive data processing needs like NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn—exhibit data-dependent misuses where API behavior depends on input data characteristics.

The paper presents DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach that combines API directives from documentation with dynamic variable information to detect and fix API misuses in data science libraries. Through five research questions, the authors evaluate: which prompt information is most effective (RQ1), whether few-shot prompting improves performance (RQ2), generalizability to deep learning libraries (RQ3), comparison to existing tools (RQ4), and an agentic version for real-world scenarios (RQ5).

Results show that combining API directives and variable information improves LLM performance by 7% F1-score for detection and 5% for fixing. DSCHECKER outperforms prior tools (46.15% vs. 16.49% recall) and works across different data-centric libraries. The agentic version, DSCHECKERagent, achieves 48.65% F1-score and 39.47% fix rate, demonstrating practical potential despite performance drops compared to the idealized setup.

This MIT lecture covers inverse and ill-posed problems, beginning with a geometric puzzle about rectangles: for any point connected to four corners, the sum of squares of distances to opposite corners are equal (a² + c² = b² + d²). The professor then discusses inverse problems where small input errors cause large output errors, giving examples including finding velocity from noisy position data, seismology (finding earth density from wave travel times), medical imaging (CT/MRI), scattering problems, and finding matrix coefficients from inputs/outputs. Integral equations of the first kind are noted as common mathematical formulations. The lecture explains Tikhonov regularization (adding αx² to least squares problems), showing that with noise level δ, choosing α = δ^(2/3) optimally balances error reduction. Applications include GPS velocity estimation and genomics, where identifying important genes requires estimating derivatives from limited high-dimensional samples.

Opioid misuse is a global epidemic with high mortality rates. The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is targeted by both abused opioids and treatment medications, but MOR agonists carry respiratory depression risks. Naloxone, an opioid antagonist, reverses opioid effects and is used with buprenorphine for opioid use disorder management. MORs are expressed throughout the central nervous system, peripheral organs, and immune system. While PET imaging with [11C]carfentanil has advanced MOR understanding, studies have been largely brain-limited due to instrumentation constraints. Long axial field-of-view PET technology now enables whole-body imaging. This study presents the first human whole-body neuroreceptor PET imaging using [11C]CFN, investigating extra-CNS reference regions. Healthy adults aged 18-45 underwent T1-weighted MRI and 90-minute dynamic PET scans on the PennPET Explorer after [11C]CFN injection, with brain volumes of interest analyzed using standardized atlases and reference tissue models.

Australian swimmer Mitch Larkin is considering adding the 400m individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials program after winning the event at the Queensland titles. Larkin says his disappointing year has left him hungry for redemption with three years until the next Olympics.

A California police chief says his department will review procedures after a homeless man fatally stabbed a restaurant patron in Ventura. This lecture covers the Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem in additive combinatorics. Additive energy E(A,B) counts quadruples (a₁,a₂,b₁,b₂) where a₁+b₁=a₂+b₂, measuring additive structure in Abelian groups. Sets with small doubling have large additive energy, but the converse fails—sets can have large energy yet large doubling if they contain structured and unstructured parts.

The Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem states that large additive energy implies a large subset with small doubling, with only polynomial loss in constants. A two-set version is presented: if A,B have size at most n and large energy, then large subsets A'⊆A, B'⊆B exist with small sumset A'+B'. The Ruzsa triangle inequality connects these versions.

The proof uses a graphical analog involving bipartite graphs with restricted sumsets. Key tools include the path of length 2 lemma (finding large subsets where most pairs have many common neighbors via dependent random choice) and the path of length 3 lemma (upgrading to subsets where every pair has many length-3 paths). These graph-theoretic results combine to show that restricted small sumsets imply complete small sumsets on large subsets, proving the theorem.

This IDC White Paper examines high-performance computing (HPC) in manufacturing, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. IT-based simulation, modeling, and analysis are key to optimizing processes and enabling innovation, with 75% of respondents citing increased innovation as the primary business goal. Advanced applications include virtual prototyping, digital twins, design optimization, and high-performance data analytics (used by 42%). Demand for high-performance calculations is growing rapidly—from 8% currently to nearly 50% in two years. Already, 81% view HPC as a game changer for innovation, with 25% using professional HPC infrastructures and 39% planning deployment.

Challenges include security concerns (72%), high energy consumption and sustainability (58%), inadequate computing power, availability issues, and lack of expertise (42%). Most enterprises (87%) prefer external HPC infrastructures, with only 6% operating on-premises datacenters. Cloud-based architectures—particularly public cloud (deemed most important) and hybrid cloud—offer scalability and flexibility advantages over traditional in-house setups, which face limitations in expansion and utilization efficiency.

Douglas Haig, 55, was charged with conspiracy to manufacture and sell armor-piercing ammunition without a license after allegedly selling reloaded bullets to Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock, who killed 58 people and wounded hundreds in the October 1, 2017 mass shooting from his Mandalay Bay hotel suite. Scientists at The Rockefeller University, led by A. James Hudspeth shortly before his death in August 2025, kept a tiny slice of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time. Using a custom-designed chamber that replicated the cochlea's living environment, they directly observed how hair cells amplify sound through ion channel activity and electromotility. The experiments provided direct evidence that a Hopf bifurcation—a mechanical instability tipping point—governs hearing in mammals, confirming this principle operates across the animal kingdom. The advance enables targeted pharmacological studies that could lead to treatments for hearing loss, for which no restorative drugs currently exist.

NVIDIA Ampere architecture adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 formats to Tensor Cores. BF16 uses 8-bit exponent, 7-bit mantissa, and 1 sign-bit, matching FP32 training results without hyper-parameter adjustment. Both FP16 and BF16 provide 16x more math throughput than FP32 in A100 GPUs. TF32 enables default tensor core acceleration for AI training, using 8-bit exponent, 10-bit mantissa, and 1 sign-bit, reading FP32 data and producing IEEE FP32 output. This patent describes memory arrays comprising vertically-alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells. Each memory cell includes a transistor with first and second source/drain regions having a horizontally-oriented channel region there-between, and a gate operatively proximate the channel region, plus a capacitor with first and second electrodes having a capacitor insulator there-between. The first capacitor electrode is electrically coupled to the first source/drain region. Multiple embodiments are described, including configurations where second capacitor electrodes are electrically coupled via an elevationally-extending capacitor-electrode structure, and where second source/drain regions are electrically coupled to an elevationally-extending sense-line structure. Some embodiments feature two gates directly above one another in individual memory cell tiers, while others include two memory cells stacked vertically within a single tier. The patent also details manufacturing methods involving selective etching and deposition processes to form these structures.

President Biden delivered a speech in Pittsburgh outlining his American Jobs Plan, a roughly $2 trillion infrastructure and economic investment proposal. He emphasized rebuilding the middle class through union support, modernizing transportation infrastructure including 20,000 miles of roads and 10,000 bridges, replacing all lead water pipes, expanding broadband access, investing in clean energy with 500,000 electric vehicle charging stations, improving power grids, and increasing federal R&D spending. The plan aims to create millions of jobs and compete globally, particularly with China. Biden proposed funding through raising the corporate tax rate from 21% to 28%, establishing a 21% global minimum tax on U.S. corporations, eliminating offshoring deductions, and strengthening IRS enforcement, while pledging no tax increases for those earning under $400,000. He called for bipartisan support, citing historical Republican infrastructure leadership, and framed the investment as necessary for America's future competitiveness and democratic credibility.

The passage describes pin attributes for device packages, explaining that each digital I/O maps to a Pin Control Management Register (PINCMx) for configuring pin functions via PINCM.PF control bits. The IOMUX supports only one IOMUX-managed digital function per pin simultaneously. For non-IOMUX managed functions like analog connections, PINCM.PF and PINCM.PC should be set to 0. However, non-IOMUX managed signals (analog inputs, WAKE inputs) can coexist with IOMUX-managed digital functions if no contention exists, requiring designer verification.

The XPIC has a bug where it delays clearing the IRR bit until one clock after the second interrupt acknowledge pulse instead of the first. When AEOI (bit 1 of ICW4) is enabled in the master PIC, this causes two interrupts to be sent to the CPU instead of one. AEOI can only be enabled on the master PIC and should only be used when nested multilevel interrupts are not needed. PCs require nested multilevel interrupt structures.

This patent application describes automated storage, retrieval and processing systems that use programmable motion devices to move objects between storage bins and destination bins. Traditional AS/RS systems bring totes to human workers who manually pick items; this invention automates the picking process using robotic arms with end effectors. The system includes gantry retrieval conveyance systems to move bins to processing locations, perception systems to identify grasp locations on objects, and machine learning to optimize grasp selection based on surface normals and fiducial features like barcodes. Multiple embodiments are described, including systems with separate or intermingled storage and destination bins, single or multiple processing stations, and multi-floor configurations.

A coach discusses his team's performance in a hockey game, noting they generated traffic and rebound opportunities but couldn't score a third goal. He praises their energy, puck control, and territorial dominance despite an unsettled start. He credits Matt for settling in as the game progressed and commends the team's handling of opponents' strengths below the goal line. He expresses trust in team leadership to maintain controlled emotion, highlights Sid's consistent impact regardless of matchups, and praises Sergei's valuable insights for the defense. He states he isn't superstitious, emphasizes staying disciplined and present, and expresses no concern about Geno's improving performance. He lauds Matt's on-ice performance and locker room leadership, viewing him as an extension of the coaching staff.

President Buchanan responds to a House resolution requesting reasons for assembling troops in Washington, D.C. He states 653 men were deployed as posse comitatus to maintain peace for the presidential inauguration. While a House committee found no proof of conspiracy to seize the capital, the House voted to remove the troops, which Buchanan cites as reason to keep them. He defends his decision as necessary precaution during a time of high excitement and alarm, emphasizing protection of public property, government archives, and the inauguration. He notes the troops' arrival quickly restored calm and security.

This FAQ article examines bear markets, focusing on the 2000–2003 dot-com crash. Bear markets feature high volatility and sharp rallies, with markets falling faster than they rise. The S&P 500 spent 70% of time above its 200-day moving average since 1960. Recovery from bear markets takes significantly longer than the decline itself—the Nasdaq took 15 years to recover from its 80% drop. Traders benefit from increased volatility as both long and short strategies perform well; investors gain opportunities to buy at lower prices. Bear markets occur roughly 20% of the time and serve to "clean out excesses" in the economy. Central bank interventions may delay but not prevent future recessions.

The Louisiana Supreme Court declined to consider Arthur Rhodes's supervisory writ as untimely filed. The court noted that Rhodes has exhausted his right to state post-conviction relief, as Louisiana law permits successive applications only under narrow exceptions in La. C.Cr.P. arts. 930.4 and 930.8, with 2013 amendments making procedural bars mandatory. The district court must record a minute entry consistent with this ruling.

β-Ga₂O₃, an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor with superior electronic properties, faces thermal management challenges due to its low thermal conductivity (k), which is further complicated by fabrication-induced strain gradients (η). This study investigates thermal transport in β-Ga₂O₃ under uniform strain (ε) and η using first-principles-based neuroevolution potentials combined with the Boltzmann transport equation.

The computational framework employs density functional theory to train machine learning potentials, achieving excellent agreement with experimental data for phonon dispersions and k values. Under uniform strain, k shows high anisotropic sensitivity, particularly to b-axis strain, with maximum changes of -26.8%/+22.9% in 10-nm films. This modulation occurs primarily through altered phonon lifetimes rather than frequency shifts.

Strain gradients produce more dramatic thermal suppression than equivalent uniform strains. For 10-nm films under uniaxial η (0.6%/nm), k reductions reach 31.8-36.6% across all crystallographic directions, exceeding corresponding ε effects. Biaxial η amplifies suppression further, achieving 41.6-43.3% reductions—approximately 1.5 times stronger than uniform strain and surpassing benchmark materials like silicon and BAs.

The enhanced suppression stems from two mechanisms: translational symmetry breaking activates forbidden scattering channels, while altered inter-mode frequency gaps expand the phonon scattering phase space. Gradient-induced scattering rates dominate across 0-10 THz, particularly affecting heat-carrying acoustic and low-lying optical phonons.

Critically, η decouples k suppression from thermal anisotropy modulation. Unlike ε, which varies anisotropy ratios by ~25%, η reduces k while maintaining stable anisotropy ratios (kb/ka changes minimally from 2.60 to 2.47 in 10-nm films). This stability ensures predictable thermal performance in flexible electronics where non-uniform strains are ubiquitous, establishing η as an essential consideration for accurate thermal modeling in ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor device design.

Startup fundraising requires understanding investor priorities to create an attractive offering. Key factors include demonstrating strong return on investment potential and equity flexibility, presenting yourself confidently while accepting feedback, building an experienced team, showing market traction through revenue or customer satisfaction, identifying market opportunities or disruptive potential, and providing a detailed business plan with realistic financial projections. Mental preparation and business acumen inspire investor confidence.

Hong Kong stocks ended slightly higher on Wednesday, with the Hang Seng index rising 0.2 percent and the China Enterprises Index gaining 0.1 percent. Gains in shipping firms and Tencent offset weakness in property shares. Tencent rose 0.6 percent after acquiring a 5 percent stake in Tesla. Banking stocks increased following modest profit growth reports from Bank of Communications and Agricultural Bank of China. Fosun International shares ended up 2 percent after announcing its CEO's departure and strong profit growth. The real estate sector fell 0.2 percent as additional Chinese cities imposed property curbs. Moody's warned that financial risks from a potential property downturn have increased due to record lending making banks more risk-prone.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 20, 2017, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2017 via an attached press release (Exhibit 99.1). The filing, signed by Corporate Vice President Frank H. Brod, states the information is furnished, not filed, under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act.

UCLA researchers Heather Christofk and William Lowry discovered that manipulating hair follicle stem cell metabolism can activate these normally quiescent cells to promote hair growth. The study, published in Nature Cell Biology, found that hair follicle stem cells process glucose into pyruvate, which can then become either energy or lactate. Increasing lactate production accelerates stem cell activation and hair growth. The team identified two drugs—RCGD423, which activates the JAK-Stat pathway, and UK5099, which blocks pyruvate from entering mitochondria—that promote lactate production and hair growth in mice. Both drugs have provisional patents filed by UCLA. The experimental drugs have not been tested in humans or FDA-approved.

Colgate-Palmolive's relative decline has paused, with Wall Street analysts turning bullish as profit growth returns. Argus set a $72 price target, representing a 12% increase, and the forward PE ratio has fallen below 20. Revenue and profit growth are expected to resume over the next two to three years. CL remains a dividend aristocrat, with 42 cents per share quarterly dividends yielding about 2.6%. However, the author maintains that CL stock remains dangerous due to its no-moat status. E-commerce has enabled smaller competitors to challenge large consumer goods companies' shelf space dominance, threatening growth potential. Despite loyal customers and stable dividends, the author believes 20 times earnings is too high a price for a no-moat business.

The DEBUGSS interfaces ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) to debug functions, supporting processor execution debugging, device state monitoring, and mailbox communication. Key features include SWD two-wire interface with on-chip resistors, configurable peripheral behavior during debug, mailbox for data transfer, and security features like SWD lockout. Device Factory Constants provide read-only capability data in a memory-mapped FACTORY region; DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008. Typical applications require 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors on VDD/VSS, 47kΩ pullup with 1000pF pulldown on NRST, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open drain IOs. TI offers development tools including LaunchPad kits, SDKs, cloud-based and offline tools, SysConfig, MSP Academy, and GUI Composer. Device nomenclature uses MSP prefix for production devices and X for experimental prototypes. The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information and updated multiple specifications.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker stated that India's 5.7% GDP growth, while criticized domestically as a slowdown, would be considered strong performance in Europe, where growth is around 2%. His comments came during the India-European Union Business Forum in New Delhi, amid criticism over India's growth slowing to a three-year low due to demonetisation and GST implementation. World Bank President Jim Yong Kim also characterized the slowdown as temporary. The remarks follow criticism from BJP leader Yashwant Sinha, who called the economy a "mess" in a recent article aimed at prompting government course correction.

Officials raised the AJC Peachtree Road Race alert level to Code Red - Dangerous shortly after 9 a.m., advising runners to slow down, follow course changes and official instructions, and consider stopping if necessary. The 49th running of the race, broadcast by 11Alive, is one of the nation's most recognized Independence Day traditions. Stormtrackers predict a dry morning with temperatures in the upper 80s. The 2018 race features a $70,000 prize purse awarded exclusively to American athletes, with $10,000 each for top male and female finishers, whose names are placed on the Peachtree Cup.

The lecture reviews digital communication's binary interface between source and destination, emphasizing standardization and layering benefits. The professor outlines source coding's three layers: sampling/expansion, quantization, and discrete coding. The course will study these sequentially, starting with discrete source coding—mapping symbol sequences into binary sequences with unique decodability.

Fixed-length codes map each of m symbols to binary strings of length l, requiring 2^l ≥ m, with optimal l = ⌈log₂m⌉. Generalized fixed-length codes use blocks of n symbols, yielding m^n combinations and approaching log₂m bits per symbol as n grows large.

Variable-length codes assign shorter codewords to probable symbols. Prefix-free codes—where no codeword is a prefix of another—are uniquely decodable and can be represented as binary trees. The Kraft inequality states that prefix-free codes exist with lengths l(x) if and only if Σ2^(-l(x)) ≤ 1. All uniquely decodable codes also satisfy this inequality.

The lecture introduces discrete memoryless sources: sequences of independent, identically distributed (IID) chance variables from a finite alphabet with arbitrary probability assignments. This simplified model provides foundation for studying more complex sources.

The shallow cross concept combines a basic route and shallow drag route from opposite directions to put linebackers in conflict against both man and zone coverage. It creates a triangle read for quarterbacks, offers quick answers against blitzes, and allows tight ends to find voids over the middle. The concept works well against man coverage, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 3 due to numerical disadvantages. Route landmarks include 10-12 yards for the basic route and 3-4 yards for the drag route. The quarterback progression reads: post, drag, basic, then running back checkdown. Two variations discussed are Bunch X Shallow Cross and Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel, which provide answers against 2-high and 1-high defenses respectively.

This MIT lecture on the economics of green buildings examines how market forces can drive sustainable real estate development through a "sandwich" model where end users and capital market investors push developers toward greener practices. The instructor uses Millennium Partners as a case study, tracing their evolution from non-sustainable luxury condos (Millennium Tower San Francisco, 2008; Millennium Place Boston, 2013) to increasingly green projects, culminating in the LEED Platinum/Passive House Winthrop Center (2023), demonstrating that developers respond rationally to changing market conditions and buyer preferences rather than pursuing sustainability from principle alone.

The lecture presents a three-stakeholder chain model—tenants, owners/investors, and developers—where tenant willingness to pay higher rent for green building benefits (health, productivity, lower energy costs) translates into higher net operating income and asset values for owners, ultimately incentivizing developers. Empirical evidence shows green buildings command average rent premiums of 6% (residential) and 5% (commercial), with occupancy and resale price premiums, though ranges vary widely (0-23% for rents, 0-43% for sales prices). Green buildings also offer lower operational costs, reduced risk profiles (policy, market, physical), and lower financing costs.

However, the instructor emphasizes market failures that impede green building adoption: information asymmetry (buyers cannot verify green claims), split incentives (misaligned costs/benefits between tenants and landlords), and externalities (social costs not captured in private transactions). Information problems particularly enable "greenwashing," where developers make unsubstantiated environmental claims. Certification systems like LEED address this by providing credible signals, though they have limitations. The lecture concludes that while market mechanisms can drive sustainability when properly aligned, understanding and addressing market failures through policy and certification remains essential.

A WIS News 10 special on the total solar eclipse will air at 7:30 p.m., covering safety and science information for viewers in Columbia, which lies in the path of totality. On August 21, the moon will cross in front of the sun from west to east across the U.S., with hundreds of thousands expected to visit the Midlands to experience complete darkness during the day.

The Brea Police Department has added a Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar to patrol The Tracks at Brea trail and the downtown entertainment district. The all-electric vehicle, introduced at the Centennial Parade and in use for about three weeks, has a top speed of 25 mph, 98-mile battery range, and cost approximately $21,000 funded by the Air Quality Management District. Lt. Darrin Devereux stated the vehicle allows quicker patrol of the linear trail compared to foot or bicycle, helping monitor amenities and prevent problems. The vehicle features a 69-inch wheelbase, 103-inch length, 800-pound capacity, two seats, off-road capabilities, and 6-8 hour charging time.

Higher education institutions have well-established learning assessment processes for credit-bearing courses but limited assessment for noncredit continuing education, which includes professional competency maintenance, career advancement training, and personal enrichment. This gap persists due to shorter course durations, varied learner motivations, and resource constraints. The authors, drawing from their experience at a public research institution, propose practical assessment methods: creating clear, measurable, SMART learning outcomes tailored to course length and learner background; using end-of-course surveys with self-rated learning achievement questions and retrospective pre-post designs; and implementing direct assessments through embedded quiz questions, observed performances, or submitted products evaluated with simple scoring systems. They recommend leveraging micro-credentials to motivate learners and align outcomes with assessments.

BG Group PLC agreed to purchase Enron Corp.'s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, acquiring stakes in the Tapti gas field, Panna/Mukta oil and gas fields, and the CB-OS/1 exploration license. The deal, valued at approximately $2.30 per barrel of oil equivalent, requires approval from Enron's partners and the Indian government, with BG's operatorship contingent on consensus among stakeholders including ONGC. Enron is simultaneously attempting to exit its 65% stake in the troubled Dabhol Power Project, where its Indian unit recently defaulted on a $24 million interest payment. The sale aligns with Enron's strategy to divest physical assets and focus on trading operations. BG aims to double gas production capacity by 2004 and leverage the acquisition to support its planned LNG terminal in Gujarat, targeting India's growing energy market.

The professor reviews eigenvalues and eigenvectors of Markov chains, explaining that for a block upper diagonal transition matrix with transient and recurrent components, the eigenvalues are simply the union of eigenvalues from each component. He then introduces Markov rewards, where each state has an associated reward, and discusses expected aggregate rewards over time, noting they consist of a transient component plus steady-state gain. The lecture covers first passage time problems, showing how to convert them into reward problems by creating a trapping state. Finally, the professor introduces dynamic programming, where a decision maker at each time step chooses among alternatives with different rewards and transition probabilities, and presents Bellman's algorithm: solving optimal policies by working backward from the final step, using the optimal "reward to go" at each stage.

This patent application describes methods and apparatuses for information transmission and reception in communication systems, particularly addressing maximum power exposure (MPE) concerns in millimeter wave 5G communications. A first communication node (e.g., user equipment) sends report information to a second communication node (e.g., base station), where the report includes first type power parameter information (such as maximum power reduction, power headroom, remaining/accumulated energy values, uplink duty cycle, alert identification, or power backoff) and/or uplink channel state information (such as reference signal information, antenna group information, path loss values, or quasi co-location information). This enables the base station to determine appropriate maximum power reduction and schedule the user equipment accordingly to minimize human body exposure while maintaining transmission efficiency. The application details various triggering conditions for reports, configurations for virtual power headroom reporting, and apparatus implementations including processors, storage, and communication modules for both user equipment and base stations.

The Power play is a popular gap run play in football where a backside guard pulls to block a linebacker, combined with a kick out block and multiple back blocks to create angles at the point of attack. Its strengths include creating numerical advantages through double teams and angles, allowing smaller offensive lines to succeed, and offering flexibility with vertical or horizontal blocking combinations. Its main weakness is vulnerability to backside pursuit and penetration through the open gap left by the pulling guard. The passage details specific blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, and describes two variations: Diamond Fullhouse (with an arcing fullback and crossing U-back) and Gun Same-Side Power RPO (a spread formation with run-pass option capabilities).

Bill Purswell v. The State (No. 10770, decided May 11, 1927, rehearing denied June 8, 1927): The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals affirmed Purswell's conviction for transporting intoxicating liquor, rejecting his claims that evidence was obtained through illegal search and seizure. The court held that (1) only the owner or possessor of premises may challenge an illegal search, not a guest; (2) warrantless arrest and search of a person is lawful when officers witness a felony being committed; (3) general objections to jury charges are insufficient; and (4) an unsupported affidavit alleging jury misconduct in considering defendant's failure to testify does not warrant reversal. Officers observed Purswell carrying a whiskey jug in a field near a social gathering, providing probable cause for arrest.

Dairylea Cooperative, Inc. appealed a Supreme Court order denying its application to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by New York's Attorney-General for a Grand Jury criminal investigation. The company argued the Attorney-General lacked authority to issue the subpoena and that its scope was unduly burdensome. The court rejected the authority challenge, finding that a proper request had been made by the Commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and Markets under Executive Law section 63(3), and affirmed the order.

This email from Tana Jones to Marie Heard, dated October 25, 2001, forwards a Texas Monthly article titled "How Enron Blew It" through multiple Enron employees. The article, written by Mimi Swartz, examines Enron's rise and fall, detailing how CEO Jeff Skilling transformed the company from a pipeline business into a trading powerhouse with a cutthroat, "rank and yank" corporate culture. The piece describes Enron's aggressive recruitment of Ivy League talent, its emphasis on short-term profits, and its use of mark-to-market accounting. It chronicles Skilling's abrupt resignation after six months as CEO, the company's falling stock price, failed ventures in telecommunications and water, and its role in California's energy crisis.

The South Dakota Board of Regents is preparing a plan to close the Capital University Center in Pierre, directing central office staff and officials from the state's two largest universities to present it at the October 3-5 meeting at Dakota State University. The decision follows a lengthy discussion about university centers in Pierre, Sioux Falls, and Rapid City during a three-day planning meeting. Regents John Bastian and Kevin Schieffer expressed urgency about addressing the center's future, with Schieffer stating he was tired of delaying action.

Firefly Aerospace's stock fell 20% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test flight at its Texas facility. The company stated all personnel were safe and safety protocols were followed. Firefly debuted on the Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but shares have since dropped more than 50%. The company makes rockets, space tugs, and lunar landers, and competes with SpaceX for NASA and government contracts. Firefly's sixth Alpha rocket failed in April, and the FAA recently approved continued testing.

The passage describes improved transmitting devices and methods for radio resource selection and sensing in LTE-based vehicular communication systems. It covers LTE evolution from 3G, its architecture with eNodeB and EPC components, and carrier aggregation supporting up to 100 MHz bandwidth. The document details Device-to-Device (D2D) communication, Proximity Services (ProSe), and V2X services including V2V, V2P, and V2I communication types. Two resource allocation modes are explained: Mode 1 (eNB-scheduled) and Mode 2 (UE-autonomous). The core improvement involves distinguishing primary subframes (fully sensed) from secondary subframes (partially sensed due to transmission conflicts) during autonomous resource selection, preferring resources in primary subframes to improve transmission reliability and reduce latency. The sensing procedure monitors scheduling assignments and measures received signal energy, with resource reservations indicated in scheduling assignments for periodic traffic like Cooperative Awareness Messages.

The Arctic is a dynamic, interconnected system where environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors interact, creating cascading effects across domains. Systems thinking—identifying components, understanding interactions, and recognizing long-term effects—offers an essential educational framework for Arctic security professionals, contrasting with traditional linear, siloed approaches. Key principles include seeing the whole, recognizing patterns, and identifying leverage points. The Systems Thinking Education Model comprises three components: core principles (interdisciplinary learning, interconnected analysis), leverage points (mental model shifts, improved information flows, governance adaptation, behavioral changes, technological integration), and learning/assessment strategies (scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis, competency-based metrics). Active learning methods such as concept mapping, simulations, wargaming, role-playing, and interactive case studies reinforce systems thinking. This approach bridges theory and practice, equipping professionals to anticipate unintended consequences and develop sustainable, adaptive security strategies. The framework is particularly suited for online graduate education, enabling flexible, interdisciplinary, experiential learning through digital simulations and collaborative exercises.

Enron Corp. faces severe financial crisis as its stock price plummeted over 50% in two weeks to seven-year lows around $13-14. Moody's downgraded Enron's senior unsecured debt to Baa2, two notches above junk status, with further downgrades possible. The company is negotiating with banks for $1-2 billion in new credit lines after drawing $3.3 billion last week, moves analysts view as desperation rather than strength. European energy firms are freezing or restricting trading with Enron due to credit concerns. The crisis stems from SEC investigations into off-balance-sheet partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, $1.2 billion in equity writedowns, and disclosure failures. Multiple shareholder lawsuits target executives over these transactions. Enron's asset-light business model faces scrutiny as trading profits shrink and talent retention becomes difficult with worthless stock options.

Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular materials—porous solids with low volume fractions of solid material. The course covers honeycombs, foams, trabecular bone, tissue engineering scaffolds, and natural materials like wood, cork, and bamboo. Students complete open-ended projects in pairs on cellular materials topics. The course examines processing methods, structural modeling, and mechanical properties (stiffness, strength) of cellular solids, with applications to sandwich panels, energy absorption, thermal insulation, and medical implants. Processing methods discussed include expansion and corrugation for honeycombs, and various techniques for polymer, metal, and ceramic foams, such as mechanical stirring, blowing agents, replication, and entrapped gas expansion.

Research indicates that soccer goals are scored at higher rates during specific approximately five-minute segments: match starts, periods after goals/penalty kicks (scored, saved, or missed), after dangerous fouls, before and after halftime, match endings, and extra time periods. These patterns stem from psychological factors including excitement, mental unpreparedness, complacency, emotional reactions, and time pressure. Coaches should address this phenomenon to prevent overconfidence when scoring and depression when conceding, commonly using the reminder "No letdown!" after any goal.

Municipal bonds remain an extremely safe asset class viewed as a flight to quality product, though Q3 2025 may mark a turning point in muni credit quality. The Federal Reserve lowered short-term interest rates in September amid slowing job growth and mixed inflation data. Many municipalities have received credit upgrades due to better-funded reserves, indicating improved budgeting or economic growth. The commentary, authored by David Kotok of Cumberland Advisors, notes that anticipated challenges are now present and highlighted by the government shutdown. Kotok co-founded Cumberland Advisors in 1973 and served as Chief Investment Officer until December 2024. The passage also lists various investment articles and municipal bond ETFs.

Ivy Chiu of RBC advises newcomers to Canada to build their network before job searching. Tips include: starting your search online before arrival, finding free career workshops through associations like ACCES Employment, pursuing internships and volunteer opportunities, updating credentials for the Canadian market, and building language proficiency through courses. Preparation helps manage the emotional challenges of job hunting in an unfamiliar market.

Treetops is a 1992 purpose-built care home near Keynsham town centre, providing dementia accommodation in three family-sized units with lounges, dining rooms, and communal areas. Residents and families contribute to care planning through a family support group, with each resident having a named carer and access to individual support and activities organized by staff. The home advises careful consideration before selecting care, notes that facility descriptions are provided by the home without responsibility for accuracy, and invites corrections via email.

Trump's meeting with Trudeau eased Canadian trade concerns, with Trump calling bilateral trade problems "much less severe" than with Mexico and promising tweaks rather than overhaul. USD/CAD fell to 1.3060 on the comments. The pound outperformed while the euro lagged. Upcoming events include Chinese CPI data (forecast at 2.4% YoY), PPI data (forecast at 6.5%), and a speech from BOJ's Kuroda. A short EURUSD trade closed with 130-pip gain. Yellen's semi-annual testimony is anticipated Tuesday, with inflation expectations in a NY Fed survey rising to 3%.

U.S. Supreme Court justices debated whether Delaware's procedural requirements for medical malpractice lawsuits—requiring an affidavit before filing and delaying defendant's response—should apply in federal court. Justices Kagan, Jackson, and Sotomayor expressed strong opposition, arguing these rules conflict with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure's notice pleading system and filing requirements. Defendants' counsel argued federal courts could apply parts of state statutes selectively, but Justice Gorsuch questioned this "Frankenstein" approach. Justices Roberts, Thomas, and Alito remained silent, making the outcome uncertain.

"An American Soccer Player's Creed" by CoachingAmericanSoccer.com outlines tactical and behavioral guidelines for soccer players, including maintaining ball awareness, communicating with teammates and coaches, avoiding fouls and retaliation, knowing the Laws of the Game, and demonstrating fair play and sportsmanship.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Conducted in accordance with Helsinki principles and ICH-GCP guidelines, it randomized participants 2:1 to standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone. The primary endpoint was percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Inclusion criteria required adults ≥18 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and radiographic infiltrates or SpO2 ≤94%; exclusion criteria included prior mechanical ventilation and grade 3 plasma allergies. Convalescent plasma (800-1000mL in 4 doses, first dose within 12 hours) with neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/160 was administered. Randomization was computer-generated with blinded trial statistician until database lock. Six patients were substituted after five withdrew consent and one failed screening. Study monitoring was conducted by the sponsor with regular site visits, data captured in RedCap, and analyses described in a statistical analysis plan finalized October 27, 2020.

This study evaluates the usability of e-business websites in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market ranked 46th globally in B2C e-commerce. The research assessed eight popular websites (four retail and four booking sites) using trained student evaluators divided into two groups. Participants completed questionnaires rating navigation, design, and content aspects on a 1-5 Likert scale. Findings revealed common weaknesses across both website categories: poor internal navigation, inconsistent Arabic-English language interfaces, layout and icon labeling issues, missing contact information, and absence of last update dates. While most ratings were positive, these specific usability problems could negatively impact user engagement and trust. The study recommends improvements through user-centered design approaches, participatory design methodologies, and better content management to enhance customer acquisition and retention in Saudi Arabia's growing e-commerce market.

Voters in Blair school district narrowly rejected a $250,000 transportation bond issue, falling short of the required 60% super-majority with 58.76% approval (111-80). The bond would have purchased three 72-passenger buses. Southwest Oklahoma voters also decided school board races in Caddo, Comanche, and Cotton counties, and municipal races in Altus and Walters.

Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins expects household debt relative to disposable income to gradually decline, citing slowing credit growth and rising labour income. The debt ratio stood at 170.4% in late 2017, slightly down from a peak of 170.5%. Wilkins notes Canadians have also gained higher net worth through asset purchases like housing. The ratio has risen steadily since 1990, when it was 90%. Governor Stephen Poloz stated high debt loads have likely made households 50% more sensitive to interest rate changes.

A hockey player discusses team strategy for scoring against a large goalie who plays deep in his net, emphasizing getting to the net and shooting high. He mentions having two days to regroup after a disappointing loss, including one practice day to prepare for tonight's game.

In a May 6, 1980 Wall Street Journal interview, Ronald Reagan criticized President Carter's handling of the Iran hostage crisis and expressed concern about Soviet influence in Iran, calling potential Iranian alignment with the Soviet Union "one of the most serious threats to the Middle East." On July 17, 1980, Reagan accepted the Republican presidential nomination in Detroit, pledging that protecting Americans from hostile foreign powers would be his top priority. He emphasized that peace requires strength, not weakness, and that freedom must be defended against those who would destroy it. In a separate address to veterans, Reagan defended military preparedness against accusations of militancy, citing Will Rogers' observation that strength deters aggression.

This passage provides detailed basketball strategies for attacking full-court pressure defenses. Key principles include spreading the floor, bypassing defenders, taking available court space, and using short crisp passes rather than dribbling. Offensive fundamentals emphasized are proper passing techniques, creating leads to get open, inbounding against pressure, and attacking outnumbered situations. The 2-1-2 alignment is recommended over set plays, with specific passing progressions: first look long, second short, third to middle. Players should receive the ball in triple-threat position with back to sideline, use jump stops, and avoid one-handed or lob passes. The "Whole-Part-Whole" teaching method breaks down press breaks into progressive drills from one-on-one to five-player scenarios. Coaching objectives focus on developing poise, quick ball advancement, and attacking double teams. Game strategies include scouting opponents, maintaining defensive balance with a trailer, and flowing directly into early offense when the press break doesn't produce a shot.

Spin defects in wide band-gap semiconductors, particularly nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, enable nanoscale quantum sensing. However, NV centers face challenges with diamond processing and surface proximity degradation. Boron vacancy (V⁻ᴮ) centers in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) offer advantages for near-surface sensing due to surface-stable defects and established fabrication methods.

This study demonstrates coherent control of ¹⁵N nuclear spins adjacent to V⁻ᴮ centers in isotopically enriched h¹⁰B¹⁵N crystals. Using electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR), researchers selectively addressed four nuclear spin states of three identical spin-1/2 nitrogen nuclei. Hyperfine coupling induces state-dependent mixing, creating distinct transition shifts (α, β, γ) that enable selective addressability. This mixing enhances the nuclear g-factor by approximately 116× compared to pure nuclear spin states.

Rabi oscillations showed coherence times exceeding 10 µs—two orders of magnitude longer than electron spin T₂. However, optical pumping caused unexpected rapid nuclear depolarization within 1 µs, tentatively attributed to the triplet optical excited ³E″ state. The narrow resonance linewidths, long coherence times, and fast nuclear spin control make this platform promising for quantum sensing applications, with hBN's 2D nature facilitating integration with van der Waals heterostructures.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed that Act 109 (the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The Commonwealth Department of Education had denied aid to the First School, arguing that Act 109 was entirely unconstitutional under *Lemon v. Kurtzman* (1971), not severable, impliedly repealed by subsequent legislation, and incapable of constitutional administration. The Court rejected all contentions: *Lemon I* struck down Act 109 only as applied to sectarian schools, not nonsectarian ones; Act 109 is severable under Pennsylvania's statutory construction principles and its own severability clause; subsequent legislation did not impliedly repeal Act 109; and determining whether schools are sectarian or nonsectarian does not create excessive entanglement under the Establishment Clause.

Amid Jake Browning's struggles with consistency, speculation has emerged that the Cincinnati Bengals could target former starter Andy Dalton as a potential solution. Dalton, now with the Panthers through 2026, started 13 games for current head coach Zac Taylor in 2019 and threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns in a 2024 Week 3 win over the Raiders. A trade would cost the Bengals approximately $3 million for the remainder of his contract. Browning has thrown for 506 yards with three touchdowns and five interceptions through three games while filling in for injured Joe Burrow.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended March 31, 2018 with the SEC. The company reported total revenues of $3.41 billion for Q1 2018, up from $2.70 billion in Q1 2017, with automotive sales comprising $2.56 billion. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $709.6 million ($4.19 per share), compared to $330.3 million ($2.04 per share) in the prior year period. Total assets were $27.27 billion, down from $28.66 billion at December 31, 2017, while total liabilities decreased to $21.55 billion from $23.02 billion. Cash and cash equivalents plus restricted cash totaled $3.22 billion, down from $3.96 billion at year-end 2017. Tesla adopted ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, on January 1, 2018 using the modified retrospective method, which changed revenue recognition timing for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees from operating leases to sales with right of return. The company had 169.8 million shares outstanding as of April 30, 2018.

Socket 940 specifications include: LCP base and cover with UL 94 V-0 rating; cover thickness ≤1.17 mm and flatness <0.25 mm; removable tape/plastic overlay for vacuum pick-and-place; molded markings including "SOCKET 940," directional designators, orientation symbol, UL symbol, and lot traceability number. Contact base metal is high-strength copper alloy with 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold overplating on mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 tin/lead, 0.76 mm diameter, with 0.20 mm co-planarity. Stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation with <3.6 kgf force; insertion/extraction forces ≤2 kgf open, ≥0.013 kgf/pin closed; pin displacement <1.0 mm. Durability: 50 cycles. Visual inspection requirements cover solder balls, contacts, cover/base integrity, and lever condition. Electrical specifications: 1.5 A current rating, <30°C temperature rise; initial and final LLCR ≤25 mΩ; inductance <4 nH single pin, 3 nH ±10% loop/matrix; capacitance <1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%; propagation delay skew <10 ps; dielectric withstanding voltage ≥650 Vac; insulation resistance ≥1000 MΩ.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016, reporting total revenues of $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million in Q2 2015, driven by increased vehicle deliveries including Model X. Gross margin was 21.6%, down from 22.3% year-over-year. The company posted a net loss of $293.2 million for Q2 2016 and $575.5 million for the six-month period. Total assets grew to $11.87 billion from $8.07 billion at year-end 2015, with cash and equivalents increasing to $3.25 billion. Tesla produced 18,345 vehicles in Q2 2016, targeting 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016 and 500,000 total vehicles in 2018. The company entered into a definitive agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation in July 2016, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. Tesla also completed a $1.7 billion public stock offering in May 2016 and had $678 million outstanding under its Credit Agreement as of June 30, 2016.

This ebook edition of "Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1906, Part I" was generated by the Office of the Historian at the U.S. Department of State on May 26, 2018. The ebook program, launched in 2018, provides portable, searchable versions of FRUS volumes established in 1861, accessible offline once downloaded. The President's 1906 annual message to Congress addresses national prosperity and urges completion of two pending bills: one prohibiting corporate campaign contributions, and another granting the government right of appeal in criminal cases on questions of law, citing recent conflicting court decisions on rebate conspiracy cases and a district judge's ruling against railway employees' labor protections.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD power supplies, with AVDD for internal circuits and DVDD for the digital interface. Decouple AVDD with minimum 10µF and 1µF capacitors near supply pins, and DVDD with minimum 10µF capacitor. The device offers NAP and power-down (PD) low-power modes: NAP mode requires writing 69h to register 05h, setting NAP_EN to 1b, and keeping CONVST/CS high; PD mode requires writing 69h to register 05h, setting PWRDN to 1b, and using CONVST/CS rising edge. For PCB layout, partition analog and digital sections, keep analog signals away from digital lines, use 1µF X7R capacitors for AVDD and DVDD decoupling without vias, use 1µF and 10µF capacitors for REFCAP (10µF ESR <0.2Ω), and minimum 4.7µF for REFIO if using internal reference. ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed from Advance Information to Production Data status.

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick took responsibility for his team's 38–10 loss to Clemson, citing defensive lapses that allowed 399 passing yards, offensive struggles with only 2-of-11 third down conversions, and three illegal formation penalties. Despite the blowout, Belichick praised his team's effort and refused to evaluate whether the program rebuild is steeper than expected, stating the team will "keep grinding."

Russia denies involvement in the Novichok poisoning of former spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter in Britain, with officials suggesting alternative culprits including Britain's own Porton Down facility. Britain claims evidence that Russia continued producing and stockpiling Novichok nerve agent despite destroying its declared chemical weapons stockpile in 1992. The author argues the West should impose stronger sanctions targeting Putin's cronies and their assets hidden abroad.

Topological quantum matters enable topologically protected boundary states with applications in quantum state transfer, gates, and devices. This work introduces a periodically modulated one-dimensional multi-chain system for non-Abelian quantum interference and entanglement generation via braiding of topological edge states. The platform uses time-dependent interchain symmetry and time-independent inversion symmetry to protect non-Abelian characteristics and adiabatic evolution.

In a double-coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain system, two pairs of topological edge states exhibit Abelian braiding. The time-dependent interchain symmetry enables branch switching, while inversion symmetry protects parity-conserved adiabatic evolution. Particles injected at one chain end transfer to both ends of another chain at tunable ratios determined by accumulated dynamical phase.

Extending to a triple-coupled SSH chain, three pairs of edge states demonstrate non-Abelian braiding with cyclic swapping properties. The braiding sequence determines particle transfer outcomes, exhibiting operation-sequence-dependent transport. With two particles, non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel interference generates spatially entangled NOON states, where the braiding sequence dictates which chain receives the entangled state. Photonic waveguide arrays provide a feasible experimental platform for these protocols.

Speedy, a leading equipment hire company that floated on the stock market in March 1999, faced significant challenges when Russell Down became chief executive in 2015 following a profit warning. Down found the company struggling with unreliable IT systems, declining revenue from neglected smaller customers, and a failed cost-cutting strategy that created equipment backlogs. Under his leadership, Speedy has transformed through customer-focused initiatives, cost control, and improved asset availability, resulting in a 58.8% profit surge to £10.8m and reduced net debt. Down has reinstated staff surveys, boosted engagement, and revived "the Speedy spirit." The company has recently acquired Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited to expand its powered access capabilities and now plans for sustainable profitable growth.

Clark County schools are individually deciding how to use weighted funding allocated by the Nevada Legislature for students learning English who also live in poverty. The program provides $1,200 per qualifying student, with Garside Junior High School receiving over $450,000. Unlike Zoom or Victory funding, which is used schoolwide, weighted funding targets specific students. Schools are now determining spending plans, with Garside considering expanded after-school tutoring and technology for English learners. The $36 million statewide allocation, with over $34 million going to Clark County, will be tracked separately and analyzed for impact on student achievement.

Mastitis is the most expensive disease in the dairy industry, costing over $400 per case and damaging cows' future milk production and comfort. While 96.9% of U.S. dairy facilities use antibiotics to treat clinical mastitis, antibiotics cannot restore damaged mammary tissue. Cornell University researchers Gerlinde Van de Walle and Daryl Nydam are developing alternative therapies using bovine mammary stem cell secretions. Their March 16 paper in Scientific Reports details how these secretions promote tissue healing, new blood vessel formation, cell migration, and protection from bacterial toxins. Some secreted factors are antimicrobial peptides that kill bacteria, potentially complementing existing antibiotics which work better against gram-positive bacteria. The researchers are the first to characterize bovine mammary stem cell secretions and plan to test the therapy in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai Motor Co. and Kia Motors Corp. have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system on a 14-kilometer road section in Hwaseong, South Korea, to advance autonomous driving technology. The system enables real-time information exchange between vehicles, roads, signals, and pedestrians, addressing limitations of onboard sensors in bad weather. The companies will research the system's effectiveness through year-end, aiming to deploy it for highway vehicle communication by 2020.

President transmits to the Senate a treaty of annexation concluded February 14, 1893, between Secretary of State John W. Foster and Hawaiian commissioners. The provisional treaty leaves future adjustments to the United States. The Administration had encouraged Hawaiian independence while it provided stability and protection for foreign interests. The monarchy was overthrown due to Queen Liliuokalani's reactionary policies, which endangered U.S. and foreign interests; restoration is deemed undesirable. Only two options remain: a U.S. protectorate or full annexation. The President favors annexation as promoting Hawaiian interests and securing U.S. interests, including preventing other powers from acquiring the islands. No foreign government has protested, and representatives acknowledged the provisional government. Prompt ratification is requested to maintain peace until Congress establishes permanent government legislation characterized by liberality and regard for rights.

Caitlin Bassett, 29, says the build-up to Saturday's Super Netball grand final between Sunshine Coast Lightning and Greater Western Sydney is unprecedented in her 12-year professional career. The international netball star has experienced sleepless nights during the fortnight wait but has tried to "soak it all up" with guidance from teammates Geva Mentor and Laura Langman, both previous title winners. Despite her experience, Bassett has never played in a national league grand final, having previously played for struggling West Coast. Lightning captain and goal keeper Mentor, 190cm, has prepared for the decider by training against 215cm Junior Levi from the Queensland men's team to ready herself for facing Giants' shooters, including 196cm Kristina Brice.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is a momentum oscillator measuring price gains and losses over a set period, typically ranging 0-100. Readings above 70 indicate overbought conditions, below 30 oversold. Research shows RSI works best on mean-reverting stocks with short time frames (2-6 days) and extreme thresholds (e.g., 15/85), requiring additional filters for optimal performance. Backtests on S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 demonstrated success rates around 71-91% with proper settings. Daily bars outperform intraday time frames. Variations include Connors RSI and Cutler's RSI. Combining RSI with other indicators, such as Internal Bar Strength, enhances effectiveness. RSI performs poorly on commodities, forex, and trending markets.

This passage provides instructional guidance for coaches on teaching offensive corner kicks in soccer to young players. It outlines a progressive teaching method: explaining Law 17 components (ball going over end-line by defender, placement in corner arc, 10-yard defender distance), demonstrating proper run-up and instep drive technique, introducing a three-position play (corner taker, receiver, cover man), rotating all players through positions, practicing both right-footed and left-footed kicks from both corner arcs, and finally assigning specific players and adding defenders. The passage emphasizes corner kicks as significant scoring opportunities despite their rarity at higher levels, and includes coaching tips about referee signals, waiting for acknowledgment, and advancing to longer lofted balls as players develop.

The Supreme Court case *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety* addresses whether the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA) authorizes money damages against government employees. Damon Landor, a Rastafarian prisoner, had his dreadlocks forcibly shaved by prison officials in violation of his religious rights; the Fifth Circuit ruled he could not seek monetary damages. The author argues this decision misinterprets RLUIPA, contradicts precedent under the similar Religious Freedom Restoration Act, and would gut the statute's effectiveness. The case challenges common narratives that religious freedom cases are polarized partisan battles, majority-serving, or merely conservative culture-war tactics. The author notes that religious liberty protections historically and currently benefit minority faiths—including Rastafarians, Muslims, Sikhs, and Native Americans—and that the Supreme Court often reaches unanimous or near-unanimous decisions upholding these rights across ideological lines.

San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights on Sunday around 12:30 p.m. The pursuit began on Fairmont Avenue and ended when the suspect crashed into fences at Central Elementary School and San Diego Fire-Rescue 17. The suspect, armed with a gun, fled on foot and was arrested near 41st Street and University Avenue. The school's main gates were damaged. No further information was available.

This retrospective study of 671 TBI patients (68.4% male, 31.6% female) found domestic accidents were the most frequent cause in both genders (37.5% of men, 57.5% of women). Men were affected at younger ages than women (44.4 vs. 49.5 years). Village residents had higher TBI risk than city dwellers. Men had longer hospitalizations than women. Alcohol-related injury affected 26.6% of men versus 8.0% of women. Surgical treatment was required in 34.4% of men versus 18.9% of women. The study concludes gender significantly influences TBI risk factors, incidence, and outcomes.

This passage documents U.S. foreign policy developments in late 1945 under President Truman, including statements on China policy, establishment of a Department of National Defense, and immigration of displaced persons. It details State Department organizational changes: Edward Stettinius Jr. resigned as Secretary of State on June 27, 1945, replaced by James F. Byrnes on July 2; Joseph C. Grew resigned as Under Secretary on August 16, replaced by Dean G. Acheson; and Patrick J. Hurley resigned as Ambassador to China on November 27, with General George C. Marshall appointed as personal envoy. Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize on December 10. The Department assumed new duties through Executive Orders 9608 (August 31) and 9621 (September 20), transferring international information functions from the Office of War Information and research/intelligence activities from the Office of Strategic Services to support foreign policy development.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces advanced power management with reduced latencies for entering and exiting power states, fine-grain power gating, and accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks 1000x faster than previous architectures. The architecture features DLSS 4 with Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame using transformer-based AI models for improved image quality, temporal stability, and reduced ghosting. Blackwell enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, allowing Tensor Cores to be accessed through any shader type for techniques including neural texture compression, neural materials, neural radiance cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The architecture spans multiple GPU variants: GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores), GB203 (high-end, 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores), and GB205 (performance segment, 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores), powering the GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 respectively.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a hydrotrope compound with hydrophilic and hydrophobic properties, available in powder and liquid forms. It increases solubility of organic matter, lowers cloud points, promotes ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity in aqueous products. Applications include wax cleaners, drilling fluids, detergents, metal processing, and oilfield uses. Raw material price volatility and health hazards from exposure pose market challenges. The liquid form and household segments dominated the 2015 market and are projected to continue leading. Industrial and institutional applications are expected to see moderate growth.

U.S. stocks fell about 2% on March 19, 2018, with the Dow dropping nearly 400 points, as Facebook led a technology sector selloff following reports that political consultancy Cambridge Analytica improperly accessed data on over 50 million users. Facebook shares plunged 7.1%, entering correction territory. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.09% and the S&P technology index dropped 2.5%, both facing their worst one-day declines since early February. Other FAANG stocks declined 1.7% to 7.2%. The S&P 500 fell 1.44% and the Dow slipped 1.23%, with all 11 major S&P sectors lower. The CBOE Volatility index rose sharply to 21.66. Market concerns also included potential global trade wars ahead of a G20 meeting and uncertainty about Federal Reserve rate hike expectations.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons will merge in January to form FBT Gibbons, a law firm with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. The merger gives Frost Brown Todd its first Northeast offices in New York and New Jersey. Robert Sartin will chair the merged firm, while Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will serve as co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd had $336.5 million in gross revenue compared to Gibbons' $115 million. Merger discussions began several years ago after Sartin met Gibbons leaders at a retreat hosted by the Zeughauser Group.

Stephen Hawking, the renowned theoretical physicist, has died at age 76. Despite being paralyzed by ALS for over 50 years, he made groundbreaking contributions to understanding black holes, space, and time. His 1988 book "A Brief History of Time" became an international bestseller, making him science's biggest celebrity since Einstein. As Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, he pursued a "unified theory" to reconcile relativity and quantum mechanics. He communicated through a voice synthesizer after a 1985 pneumonia attack left him unable to speak. Hawking appeared on television shows like "The Simpsons," and his life was portrayed in the 2014 film "The Theory of Everything." His children called him "a great scientist and an extraordinary man whose work and legacy will live on."

Multiple treaties between the United States and Hawaii failed between 1854 and 1870. An 1854 treaty proposing Hawaiian statehood and annuities failed after King Kamehameha III died and his successor opposed it.
