An 1855 reciprocity treaty failed Senate ratification due to competing priorities. A reciprocity treaty concluded in May 1867 was approved by the President but rejected by the Senate in June 1870. Secretary Seward instructed U.S. minister McCook in 1867 that annexation should be preferred over reciprocity if the two policies conflicted. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna in Hawaiian waters during 1867 delayed reciprocity treaty ratification by the Hawaiian legislature until July 1867.

The speaker takes the presidential oath, invoking divine wisdom to restore harmony among states and preserve free institutions. Having declined reelection, he seeks only to serve faithfully. He notes the recent calm following electoral passions and praises popular sovereignty for settling the slavery question in territories, deferring to the Supreme Court on timing disputes. He urges suppression of continued agitation as dangerous to the Union and emphasizes that no material calculation can value disunion, which would destroy national prosperity. He stresses preserving government from corruption, addressing the unprecedented surplus through constitutional appropriations including debt reduction and naval expansion, while modifying tariffs justly. He advocates reserving public lands for actual settlers at moderate prices. He supports strict construction of constitutional powers except for military roads under war-making power to defend Pacific states. In foreign policy, he advocates peace, commerce, direct diplomacy, non-interference, and no entangling alliances, noting territorial expansion only by purchase or voluntary union, with protected liberties for inhabitants.

On February 16, 2016, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, J.P. Morgan, and Merrill Lynch to issue $11.5 billion in notes: $1 billion in floating rate notes (due 2019 and 2021) and $10.5 billion in fixed rate notes (due 2018-2046 with rates of 1.300%-4.650%). The notes are senior unsecured obligations issued under a 2013 indenture, with floating rate interest paid quarterly and fixed rate interest paid semi-annually. Apple filed the related agreements as exhibits to this Form 8-K report dated February 23, 2016.

Synaptics announced plans to mass produce "Clear ID," an optical in-display fingerprint sensor embedded under smartphone screens. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition and works from any angle. The technology targets bezel-less OLED displays, as consumers prefer front-facing fingerprint authentication. While not the first to develop this technology, Synaptics aims to compete with major companies. The announcement comes as Apple shifted to facial recognition, though researchers have hacked such systems.

The Bemidji High School Lumberjacks (14-6) defeated Thief River Falls 77-45, led by Caden Rolfes with 18 points and Linaes Whiting with 17. Caleb Carlson added 14 points and eight rebounds, while Jeremy Beberg contributed 10 points and seven rebounds. Coach Travis Peterson called it one of their best games of the season for sustained effort and execution. The 32-point margin was a significant improvement from their 56-51 win over the Prowlers (9-12) three weeks prior. BHS will next play at 7:30 p.m. on February 18 at Fergus Falls against Section 8AAA's highest-ranked team.

This passage covers container design patterns and distributed system architectures. It begins with single-node patterns: sidecars (augmenting applications), ambassadors (brokering external communications for sharding, service discovery, and request splitting), and adapters (standardizing interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks). It then discusses multi-node patterns including replicated load-balanced services, sharded services (with consistent hashing and hot sharding), scatter/gather systems for parallel computation, and introduces function-as-a-service/serverless computing as an emerging architecture.

Florida State University President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs, to review campus naming policies and markers including statues. The panel was created following national movements to remove Confederate designations and FSU administrator meetings in August. The committee will seek community input on naming criteria and recommendations. The review comes after Students for a Democratic Society sought removal of the Francis Eppes statue, citing his slave ownership and Confederate support. The committee meets next week to plan public meetings and will launch a website.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an 8th-generation data center GPU built on the Ampere architecture, designed to accelerate AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary), Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology enabling partitioning into up to seven isolated GPU instances, and third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/s total bandwidth. The A100 delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessor V100: 2.5x for FP16/FP32 mixed-precision training, 10-20x for TF32 operations, and 20x for sparse INT8 inference. It includes 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, 40 MB L2 cache, and supports PCIe Gen 4. The GPU enables elastic computing through scale-up capabilities via NVLink/NVSwitch and scale-out via MIG. CUDA 11 introduces features like asynchronous copy, task graphs, and L2 cache residency controls to optimize performance. The A100 powers the DGX A100 system, delivering 5 petaFLOPS in a 6U form factor for enterprise AI infrastructure.

Federal aviation safety workers, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, are working without pay during a government shutdown, causing increased stress and reduced efficiency. While employees say air travel remains safe, they warn of potential delays and cancellations as the shutdown continues. Workers express anxiety about missed paychecks, halted projects, and fears that officials may use the shutdown to target unions or conduct mass firings. Some contractors supporting vital functions could still be furloughed. The FAA states it will slow air traffic when staffing constraints arise to maintain safety, and that air traffic controllers will be paid and exempt from reductions in force.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects nearly 3,000 participants for events including marathon, half marathon, 10K, and 5K runs. Walk-up registrations are available Friday 3-7 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m.-6 p.m. at the Sports Expo. The Boston Marathon-qualifying course runs along Okanagan Lake. New features include timed 5K and an adult beverage garden. Saturday events include a 9 a.m. Friendship Run, 10:30 a.m. 5K, and noon Kids 1K Fun Run with inflatables and activities. Sunday features marathon, half marathon, and 10K races starting 7:40-8:40 a.m. Special participants include Team "Special Addition" fundraising for lung transplant recipient Andrew Brownell, and Olympic race walker Mat Bilodeau. The event supports The Sunshine Foundation of Canada. Race package pickup occurs at City Park Friday through Sunday.

This patent application describes robotic and navigation-assisted surgical systems and methods for spinal procedures, particularly pedicle screw placement. The disclosure addresses limitations of existing techniques, including flexible K-wires that may bend or break, and robotic systems lacking tool advancement capabilities within bone.

The described system includes a manipulator with interchangeable end effectors, a screw with a coaxial sleeve, and navigation tracking. Three primary method aspects are presented: (1) advancing screw and sleeve together along a trajectory, then advancing the screw relative to the sleeve; (2) using a sleeve with a flexible distal feature that opens when the screw advances through it; and (3) incorporating a ratcheting tracking device for rotational marker adjustment.

The tool assembly features modular working tools (scalpels, drills, burs, dilators, tap markers) with standardized coupling interfaces, enabling rapid interchangeability without decoupling from the robotic arm. An elongate sleeve provides tissue retraction and working channel access, with deployable features to prevent tissue ingress and anti-skid elements for bone engagement. The system supports semimanual operations with haptic feedback constraints and includes tracking devices with magnetic coupling and ratcheting mechanisms for navigation relocalization during procedures involving vertebral movement, such as discectomy and cage placement.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 27, 2022, reporting its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The company is incorporated in California, headquartered in Cupertino, and trades on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol AAPL. The filing lists multiple debt securities with various maturity dates and interest rates.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural death cases involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala, with drug overdose not ruled out. Pravin Sundaram, 28, from Tamil Nadu, collapsed at a Vagator parking area after attending a rave party with friends and was declared dead at a private hospital. Abdul, a Kerala native, died at a hospital after being brought by an unknown person whom police are trying to trace. Both bodies were sent for autopsy with viscera preserved. Water Resource Minister and Siolim MLA called for stopping outdoor music parties, blaming them for increasing drug-related cases, and stated he spoke to the Superintendent of Police to halt drug-related activities.

A New York panel unanimously recommended pausing state Medicaid coverage of Sarepta Therapeutics' Elevidys for Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to safety concerns, pending FDA label updates and evaluation of a new risk-mitigation regimen. Coverage will continue case-by-case for eligible children under 21 through the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment benefit. Other states may follow the outcome.

The St. John's Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4 of the National Basketball League of Canada Central Division final, tying the best-of-seven series 2-2. The Lightning delivered a sloppy, unfocused performance, while the Edge played with intensity and energy. The Lightning built an early double-digit lead but collapsed afterward, allowing 50 points in the paint and missing 13 free throws. A confrontation between Lightning teammates Royce White and Ryan Anderson occurred at the end of the third quarter. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap adjusted his lineup, starting Alex Johnson, while Lightning coach Keith Vassell acknowledged failing to prepare his team adequately. Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams led the Edge with 28 points each, while White led the Lightning with 32 points. The NBL is investigating a complaint that a Lightning player used a homophobic slur during Game 3. Game 5 will be Thursday in St. John's, with Game 6 scheduled for Sunday in London regardless of the outcome.

A hockey player discusses his team's upcoming playoff game, emphasizing their focus on moving past the previous loss and concentrating on Wednesday's decisive match. He highlights their strong road performance throughout the season, the importance of forechecking, getting pucks deep, and playing tight defense. He praises his goaltender's consistent excellence, expresses excitement about a teammate's potential return, and stresses maintaining their simple, hard-nosed road game approach despite the high stakes of what he calls the biggest game of their careers.

Mothers of children with Down's syndrome created a viral Carpool Karaoke-style video for World Down's Syndrome Day, featuring the song "A Thousand Years" by Christina Perri. The video, which uses Makaton sign language, has been viewed over 600,000 times and received praise from James Corden and Perri. The group, called "DesignerGenes," was inspired by a SingingHands video. Coventry mother Becky Carless, whose son Archie has Down's syndrome, conceived the idea. The mothers filmed separately, and a father edited the clips together. The video aims to change perceptions of people with Down's syndrome.

This study examines Turkish teachers' experiences with distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on Turkish language courses and technological tools used. Using qualitative case study methodology, researchers interviewed 20 Turkish teachers in Diyarbakır's Hazro district. Findings indicate that while 45% of teachers believed education progressed despite challenges, 70% considered distance education insufficiently efficient, with no participants viewing it as fully productive. Target behaviors and achievements were only partially achieved due to infrastructure problems and lack of materials. Key student needs identified included reading books, dictionaries, and technological devices. Teachers primarily used phones (65%) and WhatsApp as communication tools. Essential teacher competencies included subject knowledge, technological proficiency, and activity-oriented instruction. Recommendations include resolving infrastructure issues, eliminating material shortages, strengthening the EBA platform, implementing hybrid education models, and developing professional development programs for teachers.

Topshop has recalled all till display stands nationwide after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick died from serious head injuries in an incident involving a display barrier at its Reading store on February 13, 2017. The boy was pronounced dead at Royal Berkshire Hospital following the accident at the Oracle shopping centre. Police and Reading Borough Council are investigating the death. Topshop expressed deep sadness and kept the Reading branch closed. The incident follows a 2013 death when a mirror killed a four-year-old boy at Bicester Village.

President Nixon's inaugural address emphasizes the historic opportunity for peace and unity both domestically and internationally. He acknowledges America's material prosperity but spiritual crisis, calling for reduced rhetoric and increased listening. He pledges to address inequality, environmental protection, and quality of life while recognizing government's limitations and the need for citizen partnership. Nixon commits to open diplomacy, peaceful competition with adversaries, and reducing arms burdens, while maintaining strength against weakness. He cites the Apollo 8 mission as symbolizing humanity's shared destiny on Earth, urging Americans to seize the "chalice of opportunity" through faith and purpose.

The FDA announced a crackdown on illegal sales of Juul e-cigarettes to minors on April 24, 2018, including nationwide undercover operations targeting stores and online retailers. The agency issued 40 warning letters for violations since March and contacted eBay to remove listings. The FDA also requested documents from Juul's manufacturer to understand youth appeal and plans similar requests to other companies. Juul products, which resemble USB drives and contain nicotine levels equal to a pack of cigarettes per cartridge, now hold over half the e-cigarette market. The Truth Initiative criticized the FDA for not removing youth-enticing flavors and evaluating products before market placement.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger, an Irish-born botanist and medical researcher, lives on a 160-acre property near Merrickville, Canada, with her husband Christian. After losing her family in a childhood car accident, she was raised by families who taught her ancient Irish knowledge of nature. She holds degrees in botany, medical biochemistry, and experimental surgery, and conducted cardiovascular research before dedicating herself to her garden, Carrigliath. She has written books and speaks globally about trees and the environment. Her latest project is the Canadian-made documentary "Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees," which addresses deforestation and climate change. She created the Bioplan, proposing that if every person plants one tree annually for six years, atmospheric carbon dioxide could drop from 400 to 300 parts per million. The film, based on her book "The Global Forest," has drawn record Canadian documentary audiences and is nominated for Paris Science Awards.

Cases of alleged forced conversion of Hindu girls to Islam in Pakistan's Sindh province have increased in recent years, causing alarm among Hindus, who comprise about 2% of Pakistan's population. The pattern typically involves young Hindu girls converting and marrying Muslim men, with families claiming abduction and coercion while religious institutions defend the conversions as voluntary. A 2016 bill outlawing forced conversions and conversions under age 18 was blocked after opposition from hardline religious groups. Without specific legislation, activists use underage marriage laws to challenge cases involving minors, though courts often rule in favor of the marriages. Mass conversions of Hindu families, particularly lower-caste individuals offered economic incentives, are also occurring. The trend has prompted some Hindus to relocate within Pakistan or migrate to India.

A speaker praises a coach's character and leadership, noting his honesty and high expectations. They discuss facing a strong defensive opponent with depth, acknowledging it as a familiar challenge requiring hard work. They express excitement about their team's chances, emphasizing shared dreams and the need to enjoy the moment despite difficulties ahead. They highlight Canadian hockey's passionate fan support, recalling an electric atmosphere in Edmonton. Regarding goaltenders, they acknowledge their athleticism and large equipment, making scoring difficult. They praise their own team's forward depth, noting younger lines often outperform and multiple lines can deliver key goals. They reflect on age as just numbers, feeling youthful despite being slightly older. They suggest a player (Giggy) would receive more recognition in a larger market like Toronto. The passage ends with a joke about lacking insurance.

A high school senior from Las Vegas describes how his first job transformed him from a disengaged student with poor grades to a high-achieving student with a 4.0 GPA. He was at risk of becoming one of 42,000 "disconnected" youth (NEETs) in southern Nevada—youth aged 16-24 not in education, employment, or training. NEET rates are rising, particularly among young men, with Nevada having the second-highest rate at 19%. Research shows youth employment programs improve academic performance, reduce delinquency, and enhance social-emotional development. However, opportunities remain scarce: only 5% of students access apprenticeships or internships, and African American youth face unemployment over 14%. The author advocates for government incentives for businesses to hire young people, citing successful tax credit programs in Louisiana and New Mexico, and creative solutions like Indiana's transportation grants and flexible school schedules.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 1, 2017, reporting its third fiscal quarter financial results ended July 1, 2017. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and data sheet (Exhibit 99.2), signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

A coach discusses his team's loss, attributing it to self-inflicted mistakes in the third period rather than opponent pressure. He emphasizes that these errors—puck support mistakes leading to odd-man rushes—are correctable and expresses confidence in his team's ability to recover. He contrasts this situation with past comebacks, noting the difference in goaltending quality. He praises opposing players like Malakhov and Zubov for their quiet, smart play, and acknowledges New Jersey's superior defensive commitment and speed. He reflects on the mental challenges of facing elimination, stressing that passion and leadership must come from within the dressing room. He critiques his own team's inconsistency in raising their defensive level when games intensify, and discusses tactical adjustments needed, including avoiding "home run" plays and maintaining short passing routines. He also comments on player identity, particularly for veterans like Carbonneau and Keane, and the importance of staying within their system rather than freelancing.

Saturday night television remains a competitive ratings battle between BBC1 and ITV, despite streaming alternatives. Family viewing makes early Saturday evening valuable, but new shows rarely succeed in this slot, with established programs like Strictly, The X Factor and Casualty dominating. Few entertainment shows launched in the past decade have matched the longevity of hits like Blind Date or Britain's Got Talent. While The X Factor's ratings decline, it still attracts young viewers for ITV, whereas Strictly captures broader audiences. No clear successors have emerged for when these aging formats eventually fail, leaving channel controllers to rely on instinct and hope when commissioning new programs.

Colony Northstar Inc (NYSE:CLNS) shares declined 2.3% in the most recent session, closing at $5.94. Analysts project a 52-week price target of $8.80 based on 5 opinions, with a high target of $10 and low of $6. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1 from 3 analysts, with 1 Buy, 3 Outperform, and 1 Hold rating. Its industry ABR rank is 202 out of 265. The ATR-14 is 0.3, weekly volatility is 2.44%, and monthly volatility is 3.81%. The RSI is 21.31, indicating oversold conditions. The company has a market capitalization of $3.32 billion with 558.38 million outstanding shares. Average trading volume is 8.14 million shares, with 11.19 million shares traded in the previous session.

Combination defenses are deployed to limit touches by outstanding offensive players or as surprise tactics, with timing and surprise being critical to their success. Common types include: Box & One (four players in a box zone, one "Chaser" denying a star player), Diamond & One (similar purpose but matches single guard fronts, effective against middle attacks but vulnerable in corners), and Triangle & Two (used against two scorers, for catching opponents off guard, or for clock management).

A study published in PAIN found that pre-existing depression, anxiety, substance use disorders, and psychoactive medication use increase the risk of long-term opioid use. Researchers examined 10.3 million patients with insurance claims for opioid prescriptions between 2004-2013, finding that 1.7% became long-term users, with risk increasing up to 9 times for those with prior opioid use disorders. Harmful outcomes of opioid use also predicted long-term use. The findings suggest mental health assessment should accompany long-term opioid therapy.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel agreed to establish asylum "transit camps" along three Austrian borders to save her governing coalition, following pressure from Interior Minister Horst Seehofer and the rising far-right AfD party in Bavaria. The deal requires migrants who applied for asylum in other EU countries to stay in transit centers while Germany negotiates their return; if unsuccessful, they would be sent back to Austria. However, Austria and Italy have rejected accepting returned refugees, threatening the EU's open-border system. The policy marks a shift from 2015, when Germany accepted over 1.4 million refugees, to now admitting about 10,000 monthly. The center-left SPD, part of Merkel's coalition, opposes the transit centers, which they had rejected in 2015. Several EU countries including the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, and Slovakia refuse to accept immigrants.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivers significant performance improvements for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads compared to the previous generation V100 GPU. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary), with TF32 providing 10x faster performance than V100 FP32 operations. The A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which can double throughput for deep learning inference by exploiting 2:4 structured sparsity patterns.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache—nearly 7x larger than V100. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology allows partitioning a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, improving utilization for cloud service providers. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, doubling V100's capability. The A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 and includes hardware features for improved error detection, isolation, and containment.

CUDA 11 introduces several optimizations including Task Graph acceleration, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch and Mellanox networking, delivering 5 petaFLOPS of AI performance in a single system.

A professor reviews binary detection theory, emphasizing Claude Shannon's approach of solving simplified "toy problems" first before adding complexity. The lecture covers Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) detection, where the receiver observes a value v and chooses the hypothesis (0 or 1) with higher a posteriori probability to minimize error probability. For binary antipodal signaling (±a) with Gaussian noise (variance n₀/2), the optimal detector compares the log-likelihood ratio (4av/n₀) against a threshold based on prior probabilities. The probability of error depends on the ratio of signal amplitude to noise standard deviation, expressed as Q(a/√(n₀/2)) or equivalently Q(√(2E_b/n₀)) when priors are equal. The professor extends this to vector signals, showing the inner product (v,a) serves as sufficient statistic, implemented via matched filtering, with decision regions forming perpendicular planes in signal space.

The NPD Group identified five trends shaping Britain's £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: (1) Click & collect through smartphones will transform consumer-operator interactions, requiring operational adjustments but offering higher sales and better customer data; (2) Investing in quality staff and training builds emotional brand connections, increasing customer satisfaction, loyalty, and profits; (3) Tiered, personalized loyalty schemes targeting valuable customers with VIP offers will replace traditional discount-based programs; (4) Operators must avoid over-promising and under-delivering to prevent customer disappointment and social media complaints; (5) Personalized recommendations through staff training and customer data help consumers make better choices and feel valued. Cyril Lavenant emphasized that success depends on innovation, staff development, and consistently delivering on brand promises.

Three chemists—Omar Yaghi of UC Berkeley, Susumu Kitagawa of Kyoto University, and Richard Robson of the University of Melbourne—were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks since the 1990s. These structures combine metal ions with carbon-based molecules to create porous materials capable of harvesting water or storing toxic gases, with over 100,000 frameworks created since their discovery.

William Koster et al. sued John Koedding to recover the value of a horse. The plaintiffs, horse dealers, sold a horse to the defendant who kept it briefly, returned it due to price disagreement, then requested it again and kept it several days before returning it; the horse died shortly after. The defendant claimed a thirty-day trial agreement, which the court rejected due to conflicting testimony. The defendant also argued the contract was void under the statute of frauds and that there was a breached warranty, but the court found there was delivery and acceptance, and no warranty breach was proven. The appellate court affirmed the judgment for the plaintiffs with costs.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Q3 2020 Form 10-Q with the SEC, reporting financial results for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2020. The company reported net sales of $96.1 billion for Q3 2020 (up 37% year-over-year) and $260.5 billion for the nine-month period (up 35%). Net income was $6.3 billion for Q3 2020 and $14.1 billion for the nine months, compared to $2.1 billion and $8.3 billion in the prior year periods.

The company operates through three segments: North America, International, and AWS. North America sales increased 39% to $59.4 billion in Q3 2020; International sales rose 37% to $25.2 billion; and AWS sales grew 29% to $11.6 billion. Operating income increased to $6.2 billion in Q3 2020 from $3.2 billion in Q3 2019.

COVID-19 related costs exceeded $2.5 billion in Q3 2020, totaling over $7.5 billion for the first three quarters. The company changed its server useful life estimate from three to four years effective January 1, 2020, reducing depreciation expense by $634 million in Q3 2020 and $2.1 billion for the nine-month period.

As of September 30, 2020, the company held $68.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Total assets were $282.2 billion, with stockholders' equity of $82.8 billion. Long-term debt was $32.9 billion, including $10.0 billion in senior notes issued in June 2020. The company had 501.8 million shares outstanding as of October 21, 2020.

This patent application describes systems and methods for creating arbitrarily-shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDF) in plasma processing using shaped-pulse bias. The invention addresses limitations of traditional RF bias in reactive ion etch (RIE) plasma processing, where typical two-peak IEDFs can cause feature wall bowing and reduced etch anisotropy. The disclosed shaped-pulse bias waveform includes a positive jump, negative jump (V_OUT), and negative voltage ramp to maintain nearly constant sheath voltage for up to 90% of each cycle, producing mono-energetic IEDFs. To create arbitrary IEDF shapes, the invention modulates the amplitude of the negative voltage jump in predetermined patterns, with relative pulse numbers determining ion fractions at specific energies. Alternative embodiments achieve wider IEDFs by overcompensating or undercompensating for ion current during the ramp phase, creating controlled energy spreads. The methods enable precise control of ion directionality, feature profiles, and selectivity for high-aspect-ratio etch applications.
The Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's denial of Paul Nagy's Rule 60(b) motion, finding no reversible error and dispensing with oral argument.

A Kazakh man died and another was hospitalized after a fire on the steppes caused by falling rocket debris from a Russian launch at Baikonur cosmodrome. The 15 km-wide blaze was triggered by parts of a Soyuz 2.1a rocket that successfully launched an ISS supply ship. Roscosmos attributed the death to difficult meteorological conditions and strong winds. The two victims were employed by Russian rocket-building firm NPO Mashinostroyeniya for debris-clearing work. The fire, reported around 40 km from Zhezkazgan, was extinguished by 2100 GMT Wednesday.

The NVIDIA GA102 GPU, fabricated on Samsung's 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors, features three compute resources: CUDA Cores for programmable shading, RT Cores for ray tracing acceleration, and Tensor Cores for AI operations. A full GA102 includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Key architectural improvements include 2x FP32 processing through dual-datapath SM design, second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection throughput and new motion blur acceleration, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting structured sparsity and new data types including TF32 and BF16. The GA10x architecture uses GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling achieving up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 interface, and third-generation NVLink supporting up to 96GB combined memory.

The RT Core adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for up to 8x faster motion blur rendering. Tensor Cores deliver up to 2.7x throughput gains with sparsity. GDDR6X uses four-level PAM4 signaling to double data rates. RTX IO enables GPU-based decompression, offloading CPU work for faster game loading.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU provides up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray tracing, and 5x AI performance over previous generation, with 48GB GDDR6 scalable to 96GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU offers 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48GB GDDR6. Display outputs support 8K60 via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC or HDMI 2.1. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode, while seventh-generation NVENC enables high-quality encoding up to 8K HEVC.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, team-oriented basketball style developed by Pete Carril that relies on constant motion, defensive reads, and counter actions rather than set plays. Its signature move is the back door cut. All five players must possess shooting, passing, dribbling, and court awareness skills, along with unselfishness and superior conditioning.

Key elements include: 12-15 foot spacing to spread defenses; adaptability against any defense; three phases of execution (entries, exchanges, post action); and multiple entry options including off guard rub, point rub, mid screen, dribble clear, zipper, and high post entries. The offense emphasizes ball control, patience, 15-20 passes per possession, and psychological pressure on opponents through its reputation as a "giant slayer" and low-possession tempo.

A hockey player discusses his team's recent victory, emphasizing it as a first step requiring more wins, with a shorthanded goal providing a significant boost. The team aims to return to Edmonton, where they play well at home, and maintain their current style to force additional games. He praises a teammate's scoring ability and confidence, noting the importance of playing four lines, skating well, and clogging the neutral zone. Despite the opponent having two remaining chances, a home win could force a decisive game. He credits another player's strong first period for setting the tone and disputes claims that the opponent outplayed them in the third period, citing shot statistics.

A coach reflects on a hockey game, noting his team's improved work ethic in the latter part of the second period and third period after being outmuscled earlier. He praises a key player who contributes in all situations, and highlights the team's strong third-period scoring ability, crediting the twins' line for wearing down the opponent's defense. He expresses happiness about Manny returning to the lineup, noting his faceoff skills and increased ice time. Regarding player injuries, he explains that game-time decisions are strategic to prevent opponents from exploiting weaknesses. He admits it took him three years to tell the Sedin twins apart, describing Danny as quieter and Henrik as more outspoken. He supports protecting players by withholding injury information, a common league practice. He plans to ease Manny back in, using him for faceoffs and defensive zone situations but not reuniting him with his former linemates. He acknowledges needing to reduce offensive zone penalties and hopes for a more effective power play.

This Iowa Supreme Court case, decided March 15, 1917 and modified April 13, 1920, affirmed the dismissal of a petition to recover on a foreign judgment and enjoin fraudulent conveyances. The court held that objections to witness competency must specifically state the grounds; a general objection that a witness is "incompetent and unqualified" is insufficient. Interested witnesses may testify against a deceased's administrator regarding property descriptions, values, reliance on representations, and property condition. An objection to testimony about "personal transactions" with the deceased does not necessarily cover "personal communications." The court also held that costs taxed to an administrator in official capacity will not be retaxed to individual capacity merely because the action was brought officiously. Three justices dissented, finding the objection sufficient to cover communications and that the testimony was inadmissible.

Volunteers in southern New South Wales and the ACT are conducting late winter surveys to track platypus populations, gathering baseline data on the near-threatened species. The fourth annual Upper Murrumbidgee River survey found no platypus sightings on this occasion, though a native water rat was spotted. Four years of data indicate stable platypus numbers at this site. Platypus populations have declined across eastern Australia and Tasmania due to habitat change, reduced river flows, exotic fish, and discarded waste. Survey organizers encourage year-round public sightings reports and advise watching for ripples, bubbles, and three distinct water shapes during early morning or late evening in August and September.

The lecture covers Wald's identity, sequential hypothesis testing, and martingales. Wald's identity relates stopping times in random walks to moment generating functions, showing that E[e^(rS_J - Jγ(r))] = 1 for stopping time J. This yields probability bounds for threshold crossings: P(S_J ≥ α) ≤ e^(-αr*) where r* is the second root of γ(r). In sequential hypothesis testing, the log-likelihood ratio forms a random walk with r* = 1 always. The MAP rule reduces to threshold tests on the likelihood ratio. Wald's equality (E[S_J] = E[J]E[X]) emerges as the first derivative of Wald's identity at r=0; the second derivative gives E[S_J²] = E[J]σ²_X when E[X]=0. For simple symmetric random walks with thresholds α and -β, E[J] = -αβ.

Martingales are sequences where E[Z_n | Z_{n-1},...,Z_1] = Z_{n-1}. Examples include zero-mean random walks, sums of conditionally zero-mean variables, and product martingales. A key counterexample: double-or-nothing betting has E[Z_n] = 1 for all n but lim Z_n = 0 almost surely, showing limits and expectations don't commute. Submartingales (E[Z_n | past] ≥ Z_{n-1}) and supermartingales (≤) are defined with reversed terminology. Jensen's inequality states that for convex h, h(E[Z]) ≤ E[h(Z)].

The passage lists ten AI tools for content creation in 2025: ChatGPT (writing assistance), Canva Magic Studio (visual design), RunwayML (video effects), Midjourney V6 (image generation), Synthesia (AI avatar videos), Descript (audio/video editing), ElevenLabs (voice synthesis), Tribescaler (viral content optimization), Clickable (ad creation), and CopyAI (copywriting). Each tool is described with its key capabilities and target users. The article notes that AI amplifies rather than replaces human creativity, and contains affiliate links.

Socket 940 specifications include molded markings for identification, orientation, and traceability. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with nickel and gold plating. SMT solder balls are tin-lead (63/37) with 0.76 mm diameter and 0.20 mm co-planarity requirement. A stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation with insertion/extraction forces under 2 kgf and actuation force under 3.6 kgf. The socket must endure 50 actuation cycles while maintaining electrical and mechanical integrity. Electrical specifications include 1.5 A current rating, 25 mΩ maximum contact resistance, under 4 nH inductance, under 1 pF capacitance, 100 Ω ± 10% differential impedance, under 10 ps propagation delay skew, 650 Vac dielectric withstanding voltage, and 1000 MΩ minimum insulation resistance.

Smartphone manufacturers face challenges achieving full-screen displays due to selfie cameras and sensors. While most use sizable bezels, Xiaomi moved components to the bottom, and Apple introduced the notch, which industry competitors copied. Vivo's Apex concept used an under-screen fingerprint sensor and pop-up camera, though this added cost and bulk. The author proposes transparent OLED panels as a better solution, where the selfie camera hides behind the screen and becomes visible only when needed via per-pixel opacity control. Samsung, LG, Panasonic, and Sharp have already demonstrated transparent OLED technology for televisions and smart windows, leaving competition open for smartphone implementation.

A study shows that adding four live ants to warmed cow's milk and burying it in an ant mound overnight creates yogurt through a traditional method once popular in Bulgaria and Turkey. The ants and their microbes acidify and thicken the milk, producing lactic and acetic acids, while formic acid from the ants and milk-digesting enzymes contribute to fermentation. Frozen or dehydrated ants are less effective than live ants, though live ants carry rare parasite risks.

A hockey player describes his unexpected opportunity to play in the Stanley Cup Finals after two and a half years in the organization's minor league system. He credits coach Burns for believing in him, veteran teammates for keeping him calm, and the team's depth for their success. He felt good upon waking and wasn't overthinking the game. He wanted to contribute in any way possible, not necessarily on the scoresheet. He praises a team leader who inspired him despite being injured, and describes the chaotic, exhilarating final moments of winning the championship.

The Clark County School District Board of Trustees voted Dr. Jesus Jara as superintendent on May 2, 2018, following a contentious 4-3 vote. Jara, deputy superintendent of Orange County Public Schools since 2012, was selected over internal candidate Dr. Mike Barton, who had strong support from principals, Trustee Linda Young, and the Clark County black caucus. The board was divided, with Young accusing the majority of splitting the community. After Barton's defeat and two hours of debate, Vice President Carolyn Edwards called for Jara's vote, which he won. Six finalists were interviewed April 27 from 77 applicants. Jara aims to start before June to work with outgoing superintendent Pat Skorkowsky.

This command moves SNP guest pages within system physical address space, serving as a faster replacement for SNP PAGE_MOVE. It requires 2M pages to be physically contiguous 4K pages and 2M-aligned, with no DMA support during migration. CPU access must be prevented, source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destination pages must be Pre-Migration. The 15-step firmware process includes validation checks, exclusive RMP access, TLB invalidation, data copying, and RMP updates. A completion command marks migration end and can trigger interrupts. Errors are reported in command status, migration list entries, PM_STATUS register, or via Machine Check Architecture; hardware errors during batch processing of up to 128 pages may render them unrecoverable.

The passage discusses gamification in academic education, defining it as the application of game mechanics to increase motivation and modify behaviors. It presents four projects conducted at the University of Wrocław: (1) "Kulturalny Wrocław," a location-based game where students solved cultural riddles across the city, rated highly for socialization and experiential learning; (2) a five-day career management seminar using a space mission narrative with point systems and badges, found effective but resource-intensive for instructors; (3) "Zostań przedsiębiorcą," an entrepreneurship game where teams completed quests to earn coins, praised for developing soft skills though weather-dependent; and (4) "Spell of the Black Magic Master," a LARP game for soft skills development, which achieved educational goals but suffered from complexity and lack of player preparation. The summary concludes that simpler, well-designed games with clear rules work best for curriculum integration, while complex games suit supplementary subsidized programs.

ASH, America's oldest anti-tobacco organization founded in 1967, advocates for zero tobacco deaths, arguing that smokers are victims of an industry that engineers addictive, deadly products. The organization cites the Danish Institute for Human Rights and the March adoption of the Cape Town Declaration on Human Rights and a Tobacco-Free World, endorsed by over 150 organizations, as evidence of growing recognition that tobacco production violates human rights. ASH aims to achieve a tobacco-free world as soon as possible.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney maths teacher, has gained celebrity status through his YouTube channel "Wootube," which has over 200,000 subscribers and 12 million views. In 2018, he was named Australia's Local Hero and became a finalist for the $1 million Global Teacher Prize. He now works as a "master teacher" for the NSW Department of Education, mentoring students and teachers across the state while maintaining his position at Cherrybrook Technology High School. Woo began filming lessons in 2012 for an ill student, leading to his channel's exponential growth. He is praised for making mathematics accessible and engaging, though his increased fame has drawn him away from family and his regular teaching duties.

In Rodes v. Yates (1912), the Kentucky court dismissed an appeal from an order that sustained a demurrer to an amended petition without further disposition of the action, holding that such an order is not final and therefore not appealable.

The IRS announced 2026 inflation-adjusted tax brackets and deductions, including standard deduction increases to $32,200 for married couples, $16,100 for single filers, and $24,150 for heads of household. The top 37% rate applies to incomes above $640,600 (individuals) and $768,700 (couples). The estate tax exemption rises to $15 million, with adjustments to EITC and child tax credit thresholds, plus a new $6,000 deduction for taxpayers aged 65+. These changes aim to prevent bracket creep and maintain real earnings value under the OBBBA framework.

The New Jersey Supreme Court affirmed denials of costs and counsel fees to defendants in two consolidated appeals under N.J.S. 2A:15-53 of the Anti-Injunction Act. In the arbitration case, the Court held the action—a declaratory judgment suit about arbitrability of a grievance—fell outside the Act's scope, as it was not a labor dispute involving coercive activity warranting injunctive relief. In the strike case, though within the Act's scope and reversed on appeal, the Court held mandatory fees apply only when a suit lacks merit; here, the reversal was for procedural deficiencies, not substantive entitlement, and plaintiff was not responsible for the delay. The Court affirmed both judgments but granted leave to reapply for statutory trial court costs in the strike case.

This manual describes the SanDisk Sansa Fuze MP3 player, a portable digital audio/video device with a 1.9" color screen, FM tuner, built-in microphone, and microSDHC expansion slot. It supports MP3, WMA, Audible, and video formats via conversion software. The player features a rechargeable battery lasting up to 24 hours for audio or 5 hours for video, a Hold Switch to prevent accidental operation, and controls including a Power Switch and thumbwheel for navigation and volume. Users can transfer media via drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player, and use Sansa Media Converter for photos and videos. The device plays music with options for repeat, shuffle, and equalizer settings; supports audiobooks with chapter navigation and playback speed control; plays converted videos with bookmark and brightness options; displays photos with slideshow capabilities; includes FM radio with 30 programmable presets and recording function; and offers voice recording via built-in microphone.

Meighan Wark, Huron County's Acting CAO, presented to Central Huron Council about renovating Clinton Library to achieve accreditation status. While 11 Huron County Library branches received five-year accreditation in 2015, Clinton Library failed due to accessibility issues and inadequate square footage. The county handles staff, materials, and services; municipalities manage buildings and utilities. Renovations would address accessibility standards requiring wider aisles and lower shelves, plus improve community services. Next steps involve agreeing on space needs based on population, then developing architectural plans. Provincial funding may be available for "shovel-ready" projects. The county would match municipal investment in interior improvements once commitments are made.

The Turing GPU architecture introduces significant advancements including a redesigned Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) with concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, Tensor Cores for AI acceleration, and RT Cores for real-time ray tracing. Key features include GDDR6 memory with 20% improved power efficiency, unified L1/shared memory architecture, and Variable Rate Shading for optimized rendering. Turing enables hybrid rendering combining rasterization, ray tracing, and AI through technologies like DLSS for image enhancement. The architecture supports NVLink for improved multi-GPU communication, VirtualLink for simplified VR connectivity, and advanced video encoding/decoding capabilities. Three GPU variants (TU102, TU104, TU106) target different market segments from high-end gaming to data center inference, with the Tesla T4 delivering up to 40x higher inference performance than CPU-based solutions.

Charlie Alliston, then 18, is on trial at the Old Bailey for manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving after hitting and killing Kim Briggs, a 44-year-old mother of two, while riding a fixed-wheel track bike with no front brake on Old Street, east London, in February 2016. Alliston was traveling at about 20mph when he collided with Mrs Briggs, who was crossing the road during her lunch break; she died a week later from catastrophic head injuries. Prosecutor Duncan Penny QC stated that riding such a bike without a front brake on public roads is illegal and dangerous, and reconstructions showed Alliston could have stopped in time with a proper brake. Alliston had removed front brakes from previous bikes and purchased the "Planet X" bike a month before the incident. Following the collision, Alliston posted online comments blaming Mrs Briggs, claiming she was distracted by her phone and stopped in his path, and asserting the crash was not his fault. He denies all charges.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico's final 19, to lead the Lobos to a 78-73 victory over Boise State. New Mexico (16-10, 9-5 Mountain West) used an 11-0 run late in the first half to take control. Chandler Hutchison scored a career-high 31 points for Boise State (16-8, 9-4), which never led. The win creates a tight Mountain West race, with Boise State, Colorado State, and Nevada tied atop the standings with four losses, while New Mexico trails by one loss. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each added 14 points for New Mexico. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game with a foot injury.

A Harvard poll found 65% of millennials aged 18-29 favor Democrats versus 33% for Republicans, with only 25% approving of Trump's job performance. Key findings show 14% believe America is headed in the right direction, 67% view internal forces as the greatest threat, and 61% support stricter gun laws—up from 49% in 2013.

This retrospective cohort study using the HCUP-NIS database (2017-2019) examined whether perinatal mood disorders are associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and cardiac events. Among over 2.2 million hospitalizations, 7.4% had mood disorders. Patients with mood disorders had higher incidence of PPCM (0.12% vs 0.05%, p<0.001) and composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%, p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.03-1.80), composite cardiac events (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37-1.81), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39-1.89), but not maternal death. The incidence of PPCM among patients with mood disorders was 1 in 827, higher than previously reported rates. The study identifies mood disorders as a modifiable risk factor for PPCM, suggesting opportunities for prevention and improved outcomes through mental health screening and optimization.

Preempt announced new technology integrations for its Behavioral Firewall at RSA 2017, enabling deeper context for network threat detection and expanded enforcement options. New data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory, and VPN gateways; enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator, and HP Aruba ClearPass. The solution combines User and Entity Behavioral Analytics with automated, adaptive response to stop threats in real-time.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates voltage ranges, and assigns Relative Card Addresses (RCA). Communication uses only the CMD line. CMD0 resets cards to Idle State, while cards in Inactive State remain unaffected. After power-on or CMD0, cards initialize with RCA=0x0000 and 400KHz clock frequency; default driver strength varies by signaling voltage. UHS-II Mode preserves RCA as Device ID. CMD8 verifies interface operating conditions by checking supplied voltage via the VHS field, using CRC and check pattern for validation. Cards echo back voltage and pattern if compatible, or remain idle if incompatible. CMD8 is mandatory before ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC cards and indicates host support for Physical Layer Version 2.00+.

Modern defensive schemes have evolved to combat spread offenses and RPOs, but this has created challenges with run fits that coaches must communicate clearly to players. Run fits stem from two core influences: front spacing (even or odd, determined by where the open gap/"bubble" is located) and coverage behind the run fit. Even spacing has the open gap at the B gap, while odd spacing moves it to the C gaps.

Three main spacing types exist based on box defenders versus 12/21 personnel: 7-man spacing ("out-gapped" or "light box") is minus one defender with middle-of-field-open coverage, using tools like two-gapping, stunts, "stack track and fallback" versus zone, and "spill-overlap" versus gap scheme. 8-man spacing ("gapped-out") has equal numbers with middle-of-field-closed coverage, using one-gap fits, "indicator fitting," and "lever-spill-lever." 9-man spacing ("maxed out" or "blitz fits") has an extra defender with cover 0, allowing aggressive gap play.

The 3-4 defense can use any spacing type. In 7-man spacing, it plays stack track fallback versus zone and spill-overlap versus power. In 8-man spacing, overhangs use "fill or freeze" rules based on running back location to determine run fit involvement. In 9-man spacing, the defense gains an additional overhang defender while maintaining similar fit concepts.

This MIT lecture explains light forces using the dressed atom picture, where laser-driven atoms are described as superpositions of bare ground and excited states rather than the naked states. The professor reviews how diagonalizing the two-level Hamiltonian yields dressed states with energies split by the generalized Rabi frequency, and how spontaneous emission connects these states with rates involving trigonometric factors of the mixing angle theta. In the strong-field limit, populations and coherences decouple, enabling simple rate equations.

The dressed atom picture provides physical insight into stimulated forces: atoms in the two dressed states experience opposite forces proportional to the gradient of their energy levels. For blue-detuned light, population concentrates in the upper dressed state yielding repulsion; for red detuned, the lower dressed state dominates giving attraction. On resonance, equal populations produce zero average force but fluctuating forces causing heating.

A key result is that non-adiabaticity—population lagging behind the changing laser field as atoms move—produces friction. For blue-detuned standing waves, this creates "blue molasses" cooling, opposite to the red-detuned Doppler cooling case. The lecture derives the friction coefficient and heating rate, showing the lowest achievable temperature equals the lattice depth, preventing localization in two-level systems without additional physics like Raman sideband cooling.

The professor also presents Sisyphus cooling: atoms climbing potential hills in blue-detuned standing waves preferentially emit at hilltops, dropping to valleys and repeating the climb, extracting kinetic energy. A perturbative treatment in the large-detuning limit recovers the full dressed-atom results simply.

Finally, the lecture connects the dipole force to four equivalent pictures: Optical Bloch Equations, dressed atoms, classical polarizability/harmonic oscillator physics, and geometric optics with index of refraction—showing how the same stimulated force physics applies from atoms to macroscopic objects trapped in optical tweezers.

This MIT lecture covers trajectory optimization methods for underactuated robotics, focusing on two main approaches: shooting methods and direct collocation. Shooting methods involve simulating the system forward with parameterized controls and adjusting parameters to optimize performance, using either adjoint methods (backpropagation through time) or real-time recurrent learning (RTRL) to compute gradients. RTRL propagates gradients forward but requires maintaining a larger matrix, while adjoint methods work backward with less memory but need a full forward pass first. Direct collocation methods parameterize both states and controls, adding dynamics constraints explicitly to leverage efficient constraint-handling in sequential quadratic programming solvers like SNOPT. This approach avoids numerical integration during optimization and allows better initialization to escape local minima. The lecturer demonstrates these methods on pendulum and acrobot swing-up problems, noting that while local minima exist, they are often acceptable in practice.

This study describes 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital in Kuwait between March 2020 and March 2022 on COVID-19 patients requiring prolonged intubation. Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years and mean BMI of 31.3, with diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%) as common comorbidities. Complications occurred in 23% of cases, with minor bleeding (14%) being most frequent. Nine tracheo-esophageal fistulae (2%) were detected. Mean time to weaning from sedation was 7.5 days and from mechanical ventilation was 12.9 days. Overall mortality was 63%, with hypertension and age over 65 significantly associated with increased death risk. The authors conclude percutaneous tracheostomy is safe for COVID-19 patients and should be performed after day 7 of intubation when possible.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. The device can be powered down via the RESET pin (logic 0) or by writing to register 0x00, or via the PWDN pin (logic 0) or by writing 11b to the PD_CH field at address 0xC0 in register bank 1. After reset or power-up, registers initialize to default values and require an initialization sequence of register writes, with a free-running sampling clock connected before execution.

The device supports speed-boost mode for up to 8MSPS sampling on a user-selected channel pair, with remaining channels idle. Register access uses three banks (0, 1, 2) selected via address 0x03 in bank 0; bank 0 is always accessible. Write access requires SPI_RD_EN = 0b; read access requires SPI_RD_EN = 1b and SPI_MODE = 1b. Multiple devices support daisy-chain topology with shared CS and SCLK, configured by setting DAISY_CHAIN_LEN.

Key registers include: 00h (SPI mode, read enable), 01h (daisy-chain length), 03h (bank selection), 04h and 92h (normal operation settings), 0Dh (data format, averaging), 13h/18h (test patterns), 37h (speed-boost channel/mode), C0h (bandwidth, power-down), C1h (reference, output lanes), and C4h/C5h (common-mode range, PGA initialization). Registers 44h-45h and 4Ah-4Bh store 21-bit gain error correction codes for ADCs A and B.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 achieves 0.0015% TUE at 25°C ±5°C post-calibration, with wide-bandwidth mode (700kHz) enabling 99.95% settling in 7.5µs. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, requiring 0.1µF bypass capacitors near each pin and careful layout avoiding digital-analog signal crossing.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sued Clifford Mitchell and Laureen Wilczynski for unpaid medical bills. The defendants raised special defenses under the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut's hospital bed funds statute, claiming the hospital failed to provide required notices of free care availability. They also filed counterclaims under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act (CUTPA). The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing no private right of action exists under these statutes. The court denied the motion, finding that: (1) defendants could raise Hill-Burton Act and hospital bed funds statute violations as defenses to collection actions; (2) private causes of action exist under both statutes; (3) CUTPA claims can proceed based on violations of statutes lacking explicit private remedies; and (4) the Hill-Burton Act does not preempt CUTPA.

This MIT lecture by Alan Oppenheim introduces the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm for computing the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT). The FFT is orders of magnitude more efficient than direct DFT computation, reducing complexity from O(N²) to O(N log N) when N is a power of 2. The algorithm works by recursively decomposing an N-point DFT into two N/2-point DFTs using even and odd indexed samples, then combining results with "butterfly" computations involving complex twiddle factors W_N^k. For N=8, this decomposition continues down to 2-point DFTs. A key simplification extracts the multiplication by W_N^r outside each butterfly, leaving addition/subtraction operations inside. The input sequence ends up in bit-reversed order while outputs are sequential. The FFT, first published by Cooley and Tukey in 1965, was a landmark development in digital signal processing, enabling practical spectral analysis and efficient convolution implementation.

This lecture introduces Szemerédi's graph regularity lemma, a powerful tool in graph theory developed in the 1970s. The lemma states that for any large, dense graph and any epsilon > 0, there exists a constant M depending only on epsilon such that the graph's vertex set can be partitioned into at most M parts where the graph appears "random-like" between most pairs of parts.

Key definitions include: edge density between vertex sets X and Y (number of edges divided by |X||Y|); an epsilon-regular pair (X,Y) where for all sufficiently large subsets A⊆X and B⊆Y, the edge density between A and B differs from that between X and Y by at most epsilon; and an epsilon-regular partition where the total size of pairs of parts that are not epsilon-regular is at most epsilon times the total number of vertex pairs.

The proof uses an "energy increment argument." Energy is defined as a weighted mean of squared edge densities between partition parts, always between 0 and 1. Starting from a trivial partition, if the current partition is not epsilon-regular, witnessing sets are found for irregular pairs and used to refine the partition simultaneously. This refinement guarantees an energy increase of at least epsilon^5. Since energy is bounded by 1, the process terminates in at most epsilon^{-5} steps, yielding an epsilon-regular partition with at most a tower of exponentials of height O(epsilon^{-5}) parts.

The bound is essentially optimal—Tim Gowers showed that some graphs require partitions with tower-type size in 1/epsilon. The proof can be modified to obtain equitable partitions (parts differing by at most one vertex) by adding a rebalancing step after each refinement, ensuring energy still increases sufficiently.

Digital piracy, enabled by digitalization and internet connectivity since Napster's 1999 launch, has caused significant revenue losses across industries despite technical and legal countermeasures. The International Chamber of Commerce estimated global digital piracy at $213 billion in 2015, projected to reach $384-$856 billion by 2020. Piracy persists due to consumer demand for free, convenient access to large content catalogs without geographical or device restrictions.

This study examines how firms can design business models to minimize piracy's negative impact, using Netflix and Spotify as case studies. Both companies employ subscription-based streaming models that compete with piracy by offering: free tiers or trials to attract users; intuitive interfaces and personalized recommendations; broad device accessibility with offline consumption; consistent quality; social features; and global availability. Their business models create virtuous cycles where growing userbases improve personalization and community features, increasing willingness to pay and enabling better content licensing agreements.

Key limitations include dependence on content owner negotiations, reduced price discrimination flexibility, and value capture by social media platforms. The analysis suggests effective anti-piracy responses require comprehensive service-oriented approaches rather than device-focused restrictions, with technological innovation enabling both piracy and its commercial alternatives.

This work extends Uustalu's characterization of monoid structures on non-indexed containers to indexed containers. The authors outline the monoidal structure on indexed containers corresponding to composition of their extents, generalize Uustalu's characterization to account for indexing by adjusting data and equations, and prove these structures correspond precisely to monad structures on indexed container functors. They demonstrate practical applications by describing the product of two indexed container monads, indexed variants of state and writer monads, and a free monad giving well-scoped λ-terms when applied to Fin. The development is formalized in Cubical Agda, chosen for its support of functional extensionality. The work relates to Gambino and Kock's study of polynomial monads and various Agda formalizations of container theory by other researchers.

This 1981 paperback book by Fred Puhn covers car handling, suspension system design, and chassis theory. The Fifth Circuit vacated Mariano Del Cid-Mendez's sentence for illegal reentry, rejecting his constitutional challenge to 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) as foreclosed by *Almendarez-Torres*, but finding that the district court's application of mandatory Sentencing Guidelines was not harmless error under *Booker*. This study examines the changing role of different age groups in transmitting Omicron variant SARS-CoV-2 during four epidemic waves in France (March-December 2022) using the relative risk (RR) statistic applied to ICU admission data. The RR statistic measures changes in age group proportions among cases before versus after epidemic peaks, with higher values indicating greater relative contribution to transmission during the ascent phase.

Results show children aged 10-19y had the highest RR during the Spring wave (RR=1.92), while children 0-9y led the Summer wave (RR=1.61). The Autumn wave again showed highest RR in 10-19y children (RR=1.64). By the Autumn-Winter wave, adults aged 30-39y showed the highest RR (1.47), followed by those over 80y (RR=1.27), suggesting accumulated immunity shifted transmission patterns from children to older adults.

The authors conclude that increasing booster vaccination coverage for all adults and possibly children could help limit future Omicron spread, with particular attention needed for preventing transmission among elderly populations, including in Long-Term Care facilities.

Southern Illinois defeated Evansville 73-61 in a men's basketball game on Saturday at the Ford Center. Ryan Taylor and Jaylon Brown each scored 19 points for Evansville (10-9, 1-5 MVC), while Mike Rodriguez led Southern Illinois (11-8, 4-2 MVC) with 20 points. An international team led by the University of Hawaiʻi's Harald Ebeling discovered the galaxy eMACSJ1341-QG-1, magnified 30 times by gravitational lensing from the massive galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441. This Hubble Space Telescope observation sets a record for magnification of a rare "quiescent" galaxy—one that has stopped forming stars. The extreme magnification allows detailed study of stellar populations and galaxy evolution, with follow-up observations underway in Chile and on Maunakea. The findings were published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Larry Connors' Multiple Days Up (MDU) and Multiple Days Down (MDD) strategy, from Chapter 6 of his 2009 book "High Probability Trading," is a mean reversion approach for ETFs. The strategy buys when an ETF drops 4 of the last 5 trading days (while remaining above its 200-day moving average and below its 5-day moving average) and sells when it closes above its 5-day moving average. Testing from 2000 to December 2020 on a portfolio of maximum five positions showed lower profit factors compared to Connors' other mean reversion strategies. Limiting trades to SPY and QQQ (50% equity each) yielded 287 trades, a 1.82 profit factor, 12% max drawdown, and 2.4% CAGR with only 7.7% market exposure. The short side performed poorly as a broad portfolio but showed 65% win ratio and 0.68% average gain when limited to SPY and QQQ, though most gains occurred in 2008. Results suggest the strategy can likely be improved through optimization and asset selection.

The discovery of a 2.5-pound, 6-inch-tall skull of Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch in eastern Utah suggests Pangea's split occurred 15 million years later than previously believed. The catlike, plant-eating creature was a hair-covered, egg-laying mammal relative. A Michigan State University study found that adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grazing systems can offset greenhouse gas emissions and act as a net carbon sink, while feedlot operations produce higher emissions due to fertilizer-based nitrogen. The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. Each device generates an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference divided to 0.613 V for error amplifier regulation within +0.7%/-1% tolerance. The controllers feature three oscillator modes: internal oscillator (100 kHz–2 MHz via RT resistor), external synchronization (200 kHz–4 MHz clock at SYNC pin), and primary-secondary synchronization. Output voltage is programmed via resistor divider to VSENSE pin. Soft-start timing is controlled by an external SS capacitor, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when SS exceeds 1 V. Programmable dead times (TDSP/TDPS) and leading edge blank time are set via PS, SP, and LEB resistors. Current sensing at CS_ILIM with 1.05-V threshold triggers cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup mode operation. Duty cycle limits are configurable (50%, 75%, or 100%) via DCL pin connection. The controllers include slope compensation (RSC resistor), Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, thermal shutdown at 175°C, and external fault protection via FAULT pin.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is an AMD firmware update mechanism that is disabled by default, requiring customers to opt-in and configure BIOS settings. Customers can optionally co-sign update packages using RSA keys (2048-bit or 4096-bit) to control which systems receive updates. During early boot, the customer BIOS passes signing keys to the AMD Security Processor (ASP), which authenticates packages against customer keys first, then AMD keys. The SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE command must be issued prior to BOOT_DONE and cannot be updated afterward.

SFS update packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions. SEV updates are automatically committed without rollback capability. For SNP-enabled systems, update pages must be HV-FIXED. Each package checks system patch levels and firmware versions before applying updates, ensuring dependencies are met. If any portion fails, the entire package aborts to prevent system desynchronization.

Update packages are non-persistent across reboots and can be applied during OS boot, after system boot, or during operation. The process requires 2MB-aligned memory, a TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, and communication through the TEE mailbox interface. The ASP verifies signatures, loads patches, updates patch levels, and returns status. Version information can be retrieved via GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO. Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run parallel to x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though some operations like SEV/ES VM updates require brief quiescing.

The Second Circuit affirmed the denial of Rodney Nicholson's habeas corpus petition. Nicholson, convicted of second-degree murder, claimed state courts violated due process by excluding Darnell Phelps's hearsay confession. The court found that even assuming Chambers v. Mississippi applies to retrial motions, Nicholson failed to show state courts "mechanistically" excluded reliable evidence. Phelps's confession lacked reliability: it contradicted his prior denial, could have been tailored to public forensics evidence, and was inconsistent with Nicholson's own statements. The court held no due process violation occurred and affirmed the district court's judgment.

The UC1825B-SP is a dual-output controller with a sawtooth oscillator, integrated push-pull drivers, and support for voltage and current mode topologies. Design parameters include RT (1 kΩ–100 kΩ), CT selection based on frequency and duty cycle, and a recommended DMAX above 70%. A 215 kHz switching frequency was chosen with RT = 10 kΩ and CT = 680 pF. Transformer design used a 2.2:1 turns ratio, 1.5 auxiliary winding ratio, 120 µH primary inductance, and 6% magnetizing current. The Bollinger Band Squeeze Trading Strategy involves entering trades in the direction of breakouts following periods of low volatility, identified when Bollinger Bands contract. Bollinger Bands measure volatility using a center line (moving average) and two bands representing standard deviations from that average; contracting bands indicate low volatility, while expanding bands indicate high volatility. Backtesting of this strategy showed poor performance across most assets, including stocks like Pepsi, where it underperformed buy-and-hold returns while requiring more active trading. The strategy was tested with multiple variations and assets without success. John Bollinger, born in 1950, developed Bollinger Bands in the 1980s and named them during a 1980s television interview; he is a financial analyst and author whose book "Bollinger on Bollinger Bands" has been translated into 11 languages. Common trading mistakes include lacking positive expectancy and failing to follow the strategy due to behavioral biases. The strategy differs from mean reversion approaches, featuring lower win rates and whipsaw risk. Asset-specific behavior varies, with stocks tending toward mean reversion while commodities do not, making universal strategy application unreliable.

The Second Circuit reversed a Board of Tax Appeals decision that had upheld the Commissioner's determination of an $89,841.75 income tax deficiency for 1931. The case involved whether preferred stock dividends distributed to common stockholders were exempt under Section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, which states "a stock dividend shall not be subject to tax." The majority held that the statutory language unambiguously exempted all stock dividends without qualification, following the Seventh Circuit's decision in Gowran v. Commissioner. The court rejected the argument that the 1928 stock dividend was taxable in 1928, noting the Commissioner did not appeal that ruling. Judge Hand dissented, arguing Congress intended to exempt only stock dividends not constitutionally taxable as income under Eisner v. Macomber, and that preferred stock dividends on common stock created substantially new rights constituting taxable income.
