Despite strong statistics, the Heat felt James was no longer fully committed, and Miami lost to the Spurs in five games. The report raises questions about whether James might similarly disengage if he reaches the 2018 Finals with Cleveland but doubts his team's chances against the Warriors.

Bitcoin rallied to within 1% of its all-time high, trading at $123,874, as investors sought safe haven assets during the third day of the U.S. government shutdown. The cryptocurrency has gained 12% this week. Standard Chartered analyst Geoff Kendrick noted Bitcoin now trades with "US government risks" and predicted it could reach $135,000. Gold also rose 0.5% to $3,876.55 per ounce, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite gained 0.5% and 0.27% respectively.

Executors of Horace M. Whitmore sued to enjoin San Francisco Savings Union and trustees from selling land under a deed of trust, arguing the creditor failed to present its claim within the statutory ten-month period after notice to creditors. The district court granted perpetual injunction, but the California Supreme Court reversed. The court held that failure to present a claim against an estate bars recovery from the estate but does not extinguish the debt itself or compel surrender of securities; equity cannot force a creditor to release valid security while the debt remains unpaid. Two justices dissented, arguing that failure to present a claim against trust-deed-secured property should abrogate the lien to allow proper estate administration.

Google and GoDaddy canceled website-hosting services for the neo-Nazi site Daily Stormer after it posted content ridiculing Heather Heyer, killed at a Charlottesville protest. Google cited policy violations for inciting violence; GoDaddy cited terms of service violations for promoting violence. YouTube terminated Daily Stormer's channel for hate speech, and Facebook removes links to the site unless posts condemn it. Daily Stormer briefly re-registered with Google via automation before Google canceled it again. Tucows denied hosting the site but confirmed Daily Stormer used its privacy service, which was terminated. Cloudflare, identified by GoDaddy as a possible host, denied hosting but provides masking services. The crackdowns follow violent Charlottesville clashes and could signal growing obstacles for extremist sites online. Progressive activist Amy Siskind's social media campaign helped spur action against Daily Stormer.

Matthew Phelps, 29, called 911 on September 1 claiming he killed his wife Lauren, 29, while in a medicated stupor after taking Coricidin cough medicine. Investigators found red-stained bedding and an empty box of the same cold medicine at their North Carolina home. Lauren was mortally wounded when police arrived and died at the hospital. Phelps, an aspiring preacher with no criminal record, faces first-degree murder charges and is held without bail. The couple had been married less than a year.

This patent application describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics, particularly augmented reality (AR) smart glasses. The technology addresses the need for high-resolution, high-brightness microLED displays with small pixel pitches (less than 5-6 μm) suitable for near-eye applications. The invention involves directly bonding monochromatic LED elements (red, green, blue) to processor elements (such as silicon CMOS backplanes) without adhesive using dielectric-to-dielectric and conductor-to-conductor bonding techniques. These bonded optical devices can be arranged in various configurations—parallel, perpendicular, or angled—to superimpose monochromatic images into full-color images via optical pathways including waveguides, mirrors, and combiner optics. The direct bonding enables fine pixel pitches below 5 microns or even 1 micron, with bonding interfaces featuring nitrogen and/or fluorine peaks. The systems incorporate isolation structures to limit crosstalk between pixels and can be implemented in AR glasses, heads-up displays, smart watches, and cell phones.

Transport Cabinet Secretary James Macharia attributed motorbike disorder in Kenyan cities to poor enforcement of existing regulations by bodies like NTSA. Appearing before the National Assembly Transport Committee, he stated that sufficient laws exist but lack implementation due to insufficient goodwill from mandated authorities. Macharia said the ministry is collaborating with county transport committees and the traffic department to accelerate regulation implementation. Ruiru MP Simon King'ara proposed creating a dedicated motorbike safety authority to replace NTSA, which he accused of being overwhelmed, and urged crackdown on implementation delays. While acknowledging the sector's revenue contribution, King'ara opposed banning riders from city centres, suggesting Rwanda's model as a benchmark. The statement comes amid ongoing conflicts between boda boda riders and county governments, including Nairobi's CBD ban.

The IRS is furloughing nearly half of its workforce—about 34,000 workers—due to a government shutdown, while 39,870 employees (53.6%) remain on the job. The agency-wide furlough began October 8, 2025, with most operations closed and affected employees placed in non-pay, non-duty status.

NVIDIA's GA10x SM Architecture improves upon Turing and Volta with third-generation Tensor Cores (one per partition, four total, each twice as powerful as Turing's), doubled FP32 throughput via dual datapaths per partition, and 33% larger combined L1 data cache/shared memory (128 KB per SM). The architecture features second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection testing, new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for motion blur acceleration, and concurrent RT/graphics or RT/compute processing. GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling (up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth), RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading/decompression, and supports 8K displays. The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and 5-10x AI throughput versus Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32/BFloat16 support and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x speedup. The RTX 3090 features 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10496 CUDA Cores. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology enables safer memory overclocking.

This study analyzes public financing instruments for European cleantech start-ups and SMEs under Horizon 2020, which had €80 billion in funding from 2014-2020. Common funding types include loans, equity, grants, and guarantees, with focus areas such as energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. The EIB and EIF are primary managing bodies, alongside EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission. The research benchmarks instruments across metrics including portfolio size, investment size, success rates, technology readiness levels, consortium requirements, and monitoring frequency. Many instruments also provide non-financial support like business coaching, IP protection, and R&D cooperation. Some target both SMEs and research institutions.

A speaker addresses a meeting in Washington, D.C. convened to aid victims of the Johnstown, Pennsylvania flood disaster. The speaker notes that Jacksonville, Florida—previously a recipient of charity—has contributed $2,000 to the relief effort. Following a dispatch from Pennsylvania's governor, the speaker proposes three committees: one to collect food for immediate shipment to Williamsport, where thousands are hungry and homeless; one to gather clothing and bedding; and one to raise money for long-term reconstruction. The speaker concludes by expressing hope that Washington will respond generously and discloses having personally subscribed to the relief fund on Saturday.

The Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge headquarters and Visitor Center will close on August 21st for the solar eclipse. Since the area is not in the total eclipse zone, the public is directed to Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge in Dover for viewing. Staff and volunteers will assist with parking and information; special glasses are required for safe viewing. The partial phase begins at 11:56 am CDT, with totality at 1:25 pm CDT lasting approximately 55 seconds. Solar viewing glasses ($3.00/pair), commemorative t-shirts, and bottled water will be sold as fundraisers. Visitors may bring picnics. Cross Creeks NWR, established in 1962, covers 8,862 acres along Lake Barkley and provides habitat for migratory birds. Contact 731-642-2091 for more information.

William Brock was convicted of molestation of a juvenile and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. The victim, a three-year-old girl, told her mother Brock had touched her private area; medical examination found vaginal trauma consistent with manual digital manipulation. The Louisiana Court of Appeal, Fourth Circuit, rejected Brock's claims of insufficient evidence and excessive sentence, affirming the conviction. The court found sufficient evidence of all elements: a lewd act occurred, Brock was the perpetrator, the act was intentional for sexual gratification, and it involved his position of control over the child. The court also upheld the sentence as proportionate, noting the trial court properly considered aggravating and mitigating factors under C.Cr.P. Art. 894.1.

This study examines education faculty students' attitudes toward the Research Methods in Education (RME) course at Bayburt University, Turkey. Using mixed methods with 190 quantitative and 10 qualitative participants, researchers developed a 21-item attitude scale with three dimensions: contribution to profession, confidence, and contribution to daily life. Findings showed no significant attitude differences by department, but fourth-year students had significantly more positive attitudes than first-year students. Qualitative results indicated 90% of students found the course necessary, with 50% reporting personal gains and 60% citing insufficient course duration. The study recommends offering RME in later years, extending course duration, and making it compulsory rather than elective.

Centrica's stock price fell 35% in the last year, giving it an 8.6% dividend yield that appeals to income investors. Volution, a ventilation products supplier, reported 11.6% revenue growth and 6.7% adjusted operating profit growth, with further acquisitions expected to boost performance. Its 2.2% dividend yield is covered 3.3 times by profit, suggesting potential for dividend growth. Centrica faces business model challenges and regulatory uncertainty but trades at a P/E ratio of around 10, indicating a possible margin of safety and 7% expected earnings growth.

President Bush held his final press conference, thanking the press corps for their professional relationship. He discussed remaining TARP funds, stating he would request the additional $350 billion only if President-elect Obama specifically asked. On Gaza, he supported Israel's right to defend itself while hoping for a sustainable cease-fire requiring Hamas to stop rocket attacks. He defended his record on Iraq, the economy, and tax cuts, acknowledging some disappointments including Abu Ghraib and missing WMD in Iraq. Bush admitted mistakes including the "Mission Accomplished" banner and Katrina response timing, but defended decisions based on available information. He rejected criticism that America's moral standing was damaged, defended interrogation policies as constitutional, and expressed hope for reduced partisan tone under Obama. He confirmed he would not discuss pardons and planned to step back from public life after leaving office.

This study examines culturally sensitive mentorship needs of occupational therapy students from historically underrepresented groups. A cross-sectional survey of 133 students found current mentorship programming insufficient for these students, who desired mentors demonstrating cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for workplace discrimination. BIPOC students rated mentor awareness of biases as significantly more important than white students. Hispanic/Latinx students reported lower satisfaction with mentors' cross-cultural effectiveness. Students valued personality, expertise, availability, and shared interests in mentors, with over one-third preferring similar ethnic/cultural backgrounds. They sought mentorship for clinical transitions, certification preparation, networking, and navigating discrimination. The authors recommend hybrid formal/informal mentorship models, cultural sensitivity training, diverse mentor recruitment, virtual platforms, and institutional DEIJA policy support. Limitations include single urban institution focus, cross-sectional design, and lack of data on program year and intersectional identities beyond race/ethnicity.

The Colorado Supreme Court granted a writ of prohibition against the Denver District Court in Kellner et al. v. District Court, decided February 16, 1953. Defendants, former Colorado residents who moved to Ventura, California for health reasons, were served with process in California under Rule 4(f)(1) R.C.P. Colo., which permits personal service outside the state only on Colorado residents. The trial court denied defendants' motion to quash service, finding they remained Colorado residents. The Supreme Court held that uncontroverted evidence—including California voter registration, automobile licenses, employment, and purchase of property—demonstrated defendants' bona fide intent to establish permanent California residence before the action commenced. Since plaintiffs failed to meet their burden of proving Colorado residence, service was invalid and the trial court lacked personal jurisdiction. The Court rejected arguments that this was merely a private dispute, ruling that a court proceeding without jurisdiction over the person is always a matter of great public importance warranting original jurisdiction.

European markets reached record highs driven by strong steel and banking sector performance, with the STOXX 600 gaining 0.5%. Steelmakers advanced on proposed EU tariff quota cuts, while banks rallied on stable yields and improved credit margins. BMW's profit forecast cut due to U.S. tariffs and weak China demand dragged on auto stocks. Gold surpassed $4,000 on Fed easing expectations. Other news includes: Bank of England AI bubble warning, Fifth Third's $10.9B Comerica acquisition, Santander UK CEO departure, AMD-OpenAI chip deal, Poland's $5.5B NATO fuel network investment, U.S. freezing $18B NYC infrastructure funds, Germany's Temu antitrust probe, OpenAI's $500B valuation, and World Bank raising China's 2025 growth forecast to 4.8%.

The Sensex and Nifty closed marginally lower on Tuesday. Five stocks hit new 52-week highs: AIA Engineering rose 2.02% after reporting 17.6% year-on-year profit growth and declaring an interim dividend; Alkem Laboratories closed 2.03% higher following 24.9% profit growth in Q3; KEC International reached Rs 170 but closed 3.85% lower; Exide Industries hit Rs 218 but closed 0.81% lower after receiving a buy rating with Rs 230 target; and Kalpataru Power Transmission reached Rs 299.85 with high trading volumes but closed 0.07% lower.

Royal Rumble 2017 at the Alamodome aims to sell over 60,000 tickets with confirmed appearances by Goldberg, Brock Lesnar, and John Cena. The Undertaker is expected to appear, while Shawn Michaels is rumored for a non-wrestling role in his hometown. Both legends will appear on Raw on January 9th. Confirmed matches include: AJ Styles (C) vs John Cena for the WWE Championship, Kevin Owens (C) vs Roman Reigns for the WWE Universal Championship with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage, and a 30-Man Royal Rumble Match featuring Goldberg and Lesnar as entrants.

Bath Rugby fans remain stranded in France three days after their team's 24-20 Champions Cup loss to Toulon, due to severe weather causing widespread flight cancellations from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam. While the team returned via chartered flight Sunday, supporters faced disrupted connections through Munich, Brussels, Madrid and Paris, with Eurostar delays and London train cancellations compounding problems. Some fans missed funerals and faced work and childcare complications. British Airways erroneously cancelled wrong flights and double-booked others, causing chaos at Nice airport. Several passengers experienced diversions to Bournemouth and Cardiff, with one flight sitting on the runway for four hours. Some fans extended stays positively, citing French hospitality and wine.

China tightened export restrictions on rare earths, requiring licenses for products containing 0.1% or more rare earths by value and for use of Chinese extraction, refining, or magnet recycling technology. The move comes ahead of an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Seoul. U.S. rare earth and critical mineral mining stocks surged Thursday amid speculation of increased White House investment in domestic supply chains. The Trump administration has already taken equity stakes in several miners this year, including MP Materials in July, to reduce U.S. dependence on Chinese imports. Rare earths are essential inputs for weapons, robotics, electric vehicles, and electronics. Analysts suggest China's restrictions strengthen its negotiating position with the U.S.

Two Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashes killed 346 people: Lion Air Flight 610 in October 2018 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 in March 2019. Both involved the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS), software designed to prevent stalls by automatically pushing the nose down when high angle-of-attack was detected. MCAS relied on a single sensor, lacked redundancy, and was modified during development to activate more aggressively without pilot knowledge. Boeing sought fast FAA certification and minimal pilot training to compete with Airbus's A320neo, compressing the development timeline. Internal communications revealed employee concerns about rushed work and safety compromises. The FAA approved Level B training (computer-based only) without simulator requirements. After the crashes, the 737 MAX was grounded for 21 months, Boeing lost over 1,000 orders, and investigations revealed failures in Boeing's design process and FAA oversight. CEO Dennis Muilenburg was fired, and the FAA later required simulator training. Boeing faced over $21 billion in direct costs and significant reputational damage.

Sergei Fedorov discusses his return to the Detroit Red Wings after a seven-month absence, detailing contract negotiations, his selection for the Russian Olympic team, and an offer from North Carolina that Detroit matched. He describes the emotional experience of reuniting with teammates and seeing Vladimir Konstantinov at the Stanley Cup celebration after Konstantinov's career-ending injuries, noting the team's inspirational motivation to win for him.

Constraint Programming (CP) faces adoption challenges due to the modeling bottleneck—translating real-world requirements into efficient CP models requires significant expertise. Constraint Acquisition (CA) aims to automate this process, but passive learning suffers from over-fitting with limited examples, while active learning can require excessive queries. This paper introduces a three-phase hybrid CA framework (HCAR) that addresses over-fitting in global constraints through a central Query-Driven Interactive Refinement phase. The framework begins with passive learning to generate candidate constraints from positive examples, then refines global constraints using machine learning-based confidence scoring and targeted oracle queries, with a Subset Exploration mechanism to recover valid substructures from rejected constraints. Finally, active learning completes the model. Key contributions include the three-phase architecture, the Subset Exploration mechanism, and Bayesian confidence updates with ML-informed priors. The framework handles AllDifferent, Sum, and Count constraints, and empirical validation demonstrates high accuracy with manageable query complexity.

This study examines research expectations for US mathematics education faculty, finding they vary by institution type (R1, R2, Other), department type (education vs. mathematics), and research time commitment. R1 faculty typically devote 40% time to research and publish ~2.25 papers yearly; R2 faculty publish ~1.5 papers; Other institutions expect ~1 paper. Research journal articles are most valued across all groups. R1 faculty face higher expectations for external funding and presentations, while R2 institutions more often codify expectations in writing. Mathematics departments value conference proceedings and funding more than education departments but expect fewer total publications. Higher research commitments correlate with more expected papers and greater emphasis on sole authorship. The authors recommend explicit documentation of expectations to benefit faculty, programs, and the field.

This study investigates the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE) and spin Edelstein effect (SEE) in gated monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). The authors employ a minimal 5×5 Hamiltonian model within the metal d orbital subspace, with parameters fitted to density functional theory calculations. They find that breaking mirror symmetry via a perpendicular electric field or substrate induces chiral spin/orbital textures, enabling both OEE and SEE. For electron-doped TMDs, the OEE dominates and is several times larger than the SEE, with susceptibilities reaching ~10⁻⁸–10⁻⁷ µB V⁻¹m—orders of magnitude larger than reported in other materials. For hole-doped TMDs, the Γ valley contribution becomes dominant once occupied, with both effects enhanced by small compressive strain that reduces the Γ–K energy separation. The study identifies TMDs as ideal platforms for investigating orbital Edelstein physics and potential spintronics applications.

Keltner Channels are a technical analysis tool developed by Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s, consisting of three lines: a middle line (typically a 20-period EMA) and upper/lower bands calculated using Average True Range (ATR) multipliers. Unlike Bollinger Bands, which use standard deviation, Keltner Channels use ATR for volatility measurement, making them less responsive to price changes. They function as leading indicators and can be used for mean reversion or momentum strategies. A backtest on S&P 500 showed 288 trades with 77% win rate, 6.3% CAGR, and 2.0 profit factor. Optimal settings vary by market, though 20-period EMA with 2.0 ATR multiplier is common. The tool does not repaint and can be customized for different trading styles and markets, but should not be used in isolation.

On December 12, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into a Termination Agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. to terminate 63,259,180.62 warrants issued under warrant transactions from November 2013. NVIDIA will deliver shares of common stock to Goldman based on daily volume-weighted average prices from December 13, 2016 to January 31, 2017. The shares are issued under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933 exemption.

Government shutdowns historically have minimal economic impact, but President Trump's threat to make some federal government furloughs permanent could create longer-lasting effects. A prolonged shutdown could also delay key economic data releases, including monthly jobs reports and inflation readings, potentially affecting Social Security cost-of-living adjustments and Federal Reserve policy decisions. While most analysts expect limited overall economic impact, furloughed employees and contractors face immediate financial instability.

The Netflix documentary "Unknown Number: The High School Catfish" follows students in Beal City, Michigan, as they investigate who is harassing junior high student Lauryn Licari with hateful, sexually graphic, and threatening text messages. Despite receiving 30-40 messages daily with intimate personal details, local investigations stalled for 18 months until the FBI became involved. A forensic phone examination ultimately revealed the perpetrator. The author, a criminal defense attorney, discusses cellphone dangers for teens and supports Oklahoma's new "bell to bell" no cellphone policy in schools, noting that excessive phone access creates opportunities for cybercrime and can make any student a potential suspect.

The Bank of England allocated £5.085 billion in its six-month indexed long-term repo operation, the highest amount since March 2020 and more than double last week's £2.352 billion. This reflects rising bank demand for central bank liquidity as the BoE shifts from excess reserves toward a framework where banks actively borrow funds. The move aims to normalize funding conditions while maintaining market stability, though six-month repo demand remains modest compared to short-term facilities, with a record £87.149 billion allotted in seven-day repos last week. The transition's success depends on sustained longer-term repo demand and the BoE's ability to balance liquidity provision with smooth gilt market functioning.

The Fabian Market Timing Model is a quantitative long-term trend-following strategy developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s. It uses intermarket signals between the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and utilities sector based on 39-week moving averages to generate buy and sell signals executed weekly. Backtesting shows lower volatility and maximum drawdown compared to buy-and-hold strategies, though returns approach buy-and-hold over the long term. Fabian emphasized mechanical adherence to trading rules over perfecting the model itself, stressing that discipline in following the system is more important than the strategy's specific mechanics.

A South Carolina House panel advanced a bill to address the state's $24 billion pension shortfall by raising employee contributions from 8.66% to 9% and employer contributions from 11.56% to 18.56% by 2023. Local government officials criticized the plan's 60% increase in their costs. The House Ways & Means Committee will debate the proposal Thursday. Separately, a bill recognizing out-of-state concealed weapons permits advanced to the House floor, and the Senate passed a measure creating Coastal Carolina University championship license plates, with proceeds funding academic scholarships.

Chelsea will face Barcelona in the Champions League last-16. Chelsea finished second in Group C, while Barcelona topped Group D with 14 points. First leg matches will be on February 13/14 or 20/21; second legs on March 6/7 or 13/14. The 2018 final will be at Kiev's Olimpiyskiy Stadium. Chelsea last played Barcelona in 2012, winning 3-2 on aggregate in the semi-final. Lionel Messi, with 363 goals in 397 appearances since 2004, is Barcelona's key player. First leg odds: Chelsea 9/4, draw 23/10, Barcelona 6/5.

Lorna Gibson discusses modeling osteoporosis using Voronoi honeycombs to represent trabecular bone structure. She describes obtaining whale vertebrae from Mass Fish and Wildlife for student experiments, noting their uniform trabecular bone makes them suitable for testing. Graduate student Matt Silva used finite element analysis on 2D Voronoi honeycombs with random seed points and minimum separation distances, finding elastic moduli matched analytical models but strengths were 60-80% of regular hexagonal honeycombs due to broader strain distributions, with a minimum strength around 5% relative density where elastic buckling and plastic yielding interact.

Further modeling examined bone loss through strut thinning versus strut removal. Thinning struts gradually reduces modulus and strength following analytical formulas, but removing struts causes dramatic property loss, reaching zero at the percolation threshold (30-35% density reduction in 2D, 50% in 3D). More realistic models perturbed square Voronoi arrays to match vertebral bone's vertical-horizontal orientation, showing similar behavior: thinning causes modest strength loss while strut removal creates severe fracture risk.

Gibson then covers metal foams as bone substitute materials, describing manufacturing methods including replica processes (polyurethane foam coated with tantalum or infiltrated with titanium hydride), fugitive phase processes, foaming agents, gas expansion, freeze casting, and selective laser sintering. These porous coatings on implants allow bone ingrowth, with potential for vertebral body replacements.

Finally, she discusses evolutionary studies using trabecular architecture to determine locomotion patterns. Analysis of 8-million-year-old Oreopithecus bambolii ilium fossils showed trabecular density patterns and architecture more similar to bipedal humans than quadrupedal primates, suggesting the species was bipedal. Bone mineralization evolved from calcium carbonate in early multicellular organisms to calcium phosphate in vertebrates approximately 450 million years ago.

This study by Rinholm, Solem, and Ulleberg explores dialogic pedagogy through two cases: a pre-service teacher education music course and an upper-primary mathematics class. The authors analyze how epistemological dialogue (subject knowledge development) and ontological dialogue (deeper personal engagement) interact in educational settings, using concepts of musicking, mathematizing, and Bildung. In the music case, a teacher's personal story about AIDS created existential resonance while teaching "Seasons of Love." In the mathematics case, a teacher's openness about uncertainty allowed students to discover fraction patterns collaboratively. Both teachers established didactic contracts valuing student participation, showed vulnerability, and facilitated genuine dialogue where learning became unpredictable and transformative. The study addresses how classroom practices can realize educational rhetoric about democratic citizenship, critical thinking, and participation, while acknowledging paradoxes in promoting autonomy through directed teaching.

President Wilson addresses the council on U.S. conditions for joining a league for peace after World War I. He states that America must participate in establishing new foundations for international peace, but only under specific conditions: the peace must be worth guaranteeing, not merely serving immediate national interests; it must include New World nations; and it must be secured by an organized major force greater than any single nation or alliance. Wilson emphasizes that mere agreements between belligerents are insufficient—peace requires "a community of power, not a balance of power." He interprets assurances from warring states as implying "a peace without victory," arguing that only peace between equals based on equality and mutual benefit can endure, not terms imposed through humiliation and duress.

A 19-year-old woman was sexually assaulted on a train to Taunton on April 8 when a man from a group of five passengers fell into her during a jolt and continued touching her inappropriately despite her shouting. Members of the public intervened before the group left at Bridgewater. British Transport Police are appealing for witnesses and information, with Det Con Amy Perry urging anyone with knowledge of the incident or the group to contact them.

This MIT lecture covers gravitational radiation, focusing on linearized Einstein equations and the properties of gravitational waves. The speaker recaps previous work decomposing space-time perturbations into gauge-invariant degrees of freedom, identifying two radiative degrees of freedom corresponding to gravitational wave polarizations.

The lecture examines how to detect gravitational waves through two methods: measuring light travel time between freely falling bodies and analyzing geodesic deviation. The latter reveals that gravitational waves produce tidal stretch-and-squeeze effects on a ring of test particles, with two fundamental polarizations called "plus" and "cross."

The speaker derives the quadrupole formula for computing gravitational radiation from a source, using far-field and slow-motion approximations. The transverse-traceless metric perturbation hij^TT equals (2G/r) times the second time derivative of the source's quadrupole moment, projected with tensors to enforce transverse and traceless conditions. This formula explains how observatories like LIGO measure gravitational waves through interference-based timing experiments.

Scientists have identified TRPM8 and TRPP3 receptors as therapeutic targets to increase brown adipose tissue (BAT) in humans, according to research published in The FASEB Journal. The study found that TRPM8 activation supports browning while TRPP3 is required for brown fat formation. These receptors, potentially activated by foods or drugs, could lead to treatments for obesity, diabetes, and metabolic disorders.

Whangarei District Council advises drivers using Kensington Park area to plan ahead for winter parking congestion, as no additional parking is planned. Enforcement includes warning fliers followed by tickets for violations such as blocking driveways, damaging verges, or obstructing footpaths. Suggested alternatives include car pooling, arriving earlier, drop-offs, and walking from distant parking.

The Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission has kept in abeyance the results of the 2016 Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination and withdrawn the notification for the main examination after discrepancies were detected in question papers and answer keys. The Commission will refer all materials to independent experts for evaluation. The April 23, 2017 results declared 6,925 candidates successful out of 36,681 who appeared, but new representations and RTI applications revealed further discrepancies despite earlier expert review. The main examination date will be notified after the independent experts submit their report, with concerns raised about potential litigation if successful candidates are excluded from revised results.

Lyminster Primary School in Littlehampton received a "requires improvement" rating from Ofsted following a May inspection, with findings published June 12. Inspector Marcia Goodwin noted positive changes under headteacher Steven McGinley, appointed in September 2016, but stated they had not yet had sufficient impact. The report praised good leadership, governance, and student conduct, while identifying inconsistent teaching quality and underachievement in last year's Year 6 SATs as concerns. McGinley expressed confidence the school would "rapidly bounce back" to a "good" rating, noting they were already meeting development targets.

Apple Inc. filed its Q2 2023 Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 1, 2023. The company reported net sales of $94.836 billion for the quarter (down 3% year-over-year) and $211.990 billion for the six-month period (down 4% year-over-year). Net income was $24.160 billion for the quarter and $54.158 billion for the six-month period. Products net sales declined due primarily to lower Mac sales, while Services net sales increased 5% year-over-year. The company repurchased $19.1 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends during the quarter. As of April 1, 2023, the company held $24.687 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $141.646 billion in total marketable securities. Total assets were $332.160 billion, with total liabilities of $270.002 billion and shareholders' equity of $62.158 billion. The company had $2.0 billion in commercial paper outstanding and $107.6 billion in term debt. On May 4, 2023, the Board authorized an additional $90 billion share repurchase program and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.23 to $0.24 per share.

Bluehole launched a "Snipe City" community event for PUBG on Xbox One, challenging players to collectively achieve 400,000 kills using M24 and Kar98 sniper rifles. Participants who play at least one round and earn 1 BP are eligible for rewards if the goal is met, including a Bloody Tank Top, Padded Jacket, and two Militia Crates. The event runs until July 10, with updates on July 6 and 9, and results announced July 11.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded State Bank Financial Corporation (NASDAQ:STBZ) from "sell" to "buy" with a $30.00 price target, suggesting 11.69% upside. Hovde Group downgraded the stock from "outperform" to "market perform," lowering its target to $24.50. The stock has an average "Hold" rating and $25.25 target price among seven analysts. Shares opened at $26.86 Thursday, with a market cap of $963.28 million, P/E ratio of 20.29, and beta of 0.86. The company reported Q3 EPS of $0.34, beating estimates by $0.03, with a 24.14% net margin and 8.97% return on equity. It pays a $0.56 annualized dividend (2.08% yield) with a 42.11% payout ratio. Insiders own 6.31% and institutional investors hold 81.81% of shares. Two directors recently sold shares totaling 6,073.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the divorce decree and custody award to the father, John Geesbreght, but reversed and remanded the property division. Mary Lee Geesbreght's jurisdictional challenge failed due to waiver and the court's finding that the children's domicile remained in Texas. The jury trial on custody contained no reversible error regarding supplemental jury instructions. The property division was reversed because the trial court erred by failing to consider "good will" value in John Geesbreght's stock in Emergency Medicine Consultants, a professional corporation, beyond its $16,000 book value. The court held this corporate good will had value apart from John's personal services, making the property award grossly inadequate and clearly erroneous.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for Q2 FY2019 ended July 29, 2018, reporting revenue of $3.123 billion (up 40% YoY), net income of $1.101 billion (up 89% YoY), and diluted EPS of $1.76. GPU business revenue was $2.656 billion (up 40% YoY), driven by gaming, datacenter, and professional visualization growth, while Tegra Processor revenue was $467 million (up 40% YoY). The company held $7.94 billion in cash and marketable securities, returned $837 million to shareholders through repurchases and dividends, and maintained $1.16 billion in remaining share repurchase authorization.

Asian shares fell on Tuesday as investors sold U.S. technology stocks amid fears of stricter regulation following reports that Facebook allowed improper data access. This study validates a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model for predicting Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression in community-dwelling, multiethnic older adults. The model, previously developed using clinic-based, non-Hispanic white patients with high socioeconomic status (Predictors 2), was tested on the Predictors 3 cohort of 273 community-dwelling participants from Washington Heights/Inwood, Manhattan, including Hispanic (77.5%), non-Hispanic white (9.2%), and non-Hispanic nonwhite (13.6%) individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD dementia.

The L-GoM model represents each patient's clinical status as weighted combinations of four latent disease subtypes, with Subtype 4 indicating greatest severity. Validation examined two outcomes: mortality and need for full-time care (FTC). Results showed accurate predictions for AD nonreverters (N=118) and MCI cases (N=123), with observed values falling within 95% confidence bands. However, the model failed for 32 AD reverters who reverted to non-dementia diagnoses, likely representing initial misdiagnosis. Among MCI cases, 40 converted to AD while 83 did not; the model accurately predicted survival for both groups combined.

Demographic analyses revealed significant differences in L-GoM scores: males and non-Hispanics had higher Subtype 1 scores, while Hispanics and APOE4+ carriers had higher Subtype 3 scores. The study demonstrates the model's applicability to diverse populations and its extension to MCI, though validation in additional minority groups is needed.

The Side Screen Offense is a two-player screen and roll isolation play widely used in the NBA. It can be initiated by a post stepping out to set an on-ball screen, triggered by point guard dribble-clearing or passing to the wing with a basket cut. NBA teams typically run it on the left side for right-handed players and right side for left-handed players to enable strong-hand dribble penetration to the middle.

Basic options include: driving over the top, pull-up jumper if defense goes under, return pass to the post on switches, or kick-out pass to shooters when help defense collapses.

Eight defensive reads and counters:
1. Defender chases over: turn corner and drive
2. Baseline defender helps: drop pass to post
3. Wing defender sags: kick-out for three
4. Defender goes under: pull-up jumper
5. Defender cheats over early: drive opposite
6. Defender fights through: crossover or behind-the-back dribble
7. Defense shows and recovers: screener pops out
8. Defense switches: post roll, isolation for mismatches, or screener slips screen if defenders anticipate switch

Additional counters include lob passes when screens are denied and 2-1-2 alignment against traps.

Entry variations include High Post Rub, Power/Motion, and Horns sets. Continuity options include Flex, Triangle Game, Single/Double Motion, Weakside Double Screen, and Baseline Down Screen.

Success requires execution, coordination, proper footwork, timing, non-verbal communication, and experience between ballhandler and screener.

This application is a continuation of multiple prior patents and claims benefit from numerous provisional patent applications related to hydraulic fracturing fluid ends. The passage describes a fluid end for hydraulic fracturing operations comprising multiple fluid end sections with horizontally positioned housings, each having a single horizontal bore rather than intersecting vertical and horizontal bores found in traditional designs. Each housing uses a fluid routing plug installed within the horizontal bore to route fluid, with upper and lower intake manifolds delivering fluid through first fluid passages and second fluid passages directing pressurized fluid to a discharge bore. The design eliminates common stress points, reduces manufacturing costs and time, allows use of lower strength materials, and enables individual section replacement. The fluid routing plug features tapered walls, beveled sealing surfaces, and seals positioned in housing grooves to prevent leakage while accommodating thermal expansion. Suction and discharge valves operate axially along the housing's longitudinal axis, with valve movement limited by corresponding guides.

Erik Demaine's MIT lecture covers fusion trees, a static data structure achieving O(log_w n) predecessor/successor queries on the word RAM model. The key innovation is using "bit tricks" and word-level parallelism to handle branching factor w^(1/5) per node despite only reading O(w) bits per operation.

Core techniques include: (1) sketching—compressing w-bit integers to fewer bits while preserving order among keys, implemented via integer multiplication with carefully chosen multipliers; (2) parallel comparison—comparing multiple sketches simultaneously using subtraction and masking; and (3) computing the leftmost 1-bit in constant time using recursive clustering and sketching.

The data structure, invented by Fredman and Willard in 1990, uses polynomial preprocessing time and linear space. Demaine notes variants including AC0 RAM versions (without multiplication), dynamic versions using exponential search trees or hashing, and the static version covered in the lecture.

This MIT lecture covers life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology for quantifying environmental impacts of products, using a hand dryer study as an example. LCA differs from corporate carbon footprinting by focusing on product-level rather than organizational-level analysis, enabling comparisons across supply chains. The lecture explains LCA's four stages: goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation. Key challenges discussed include setting system boundaries, making assumptions when data is unavailable, choosing functional units (e.g., "per pair of dried hands"), and handling uncertainty through sensitivity analyses. The hand dryer study compared Dyson Airblade, Xlerator, and paper towels, revealing how assumptions about manufacturing location, electricity grid, drying times, and product lifespans significantly affect results. The lecture notes that Dyson commissioned the study and provided proprietary data while competitors relied on public information, raising questions about objectivity. LCA originated with Coca-Cola in 1969 and evolved through ISO standards, with two main types: attributional (static snapshots) and consequential (modeling system changes). The methodology requires value judgments when selecting impact categories and weighting different environmental effects, making transparency about assumptions critical for credible results.

This study examined malaria and malnutrition risk factors among school-age children in Tanzania and evaluated whether intermittent preventive therapy (IPTsc) for malaria improves nutritional status. Using secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a 20-month randomized controlled trial, researchers analyzed 1,566 children aged 5-15 years randomized to three groups: dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ), or standard care.

At baseline, malaria prevalence was 27%, with 23% of children ≤10 years underweight, 21% stunted, and 28% thin. Children with malaria had 78% higher odds of stunting (AOR=1.78, 95%CI=[1.36,2.33], P<0.001), and low socioeconomic status was associated with 50% higher odds of being underweight (AOR=1.50, 95%CI=[1.13,2.01], P=0.006). However, during the intervention, changes in mean weight, height, and BMI over time did not significantly differ between treatment groups and controls. Age, sex, and female sex were significantly associated with growth parameters, but IPTsc did not improve nutritional status. The authors conclude that public health agencies should reinforce nutritional programs alongside malaria control, ensuring food availability in schools and providing sustainable nutritional education.

A "pulse" scenario—where warm water causes Antarctic and Greenland glaciers to collapse—could trigger 10-30 feet of sea-level rise in South Florida by 2100, far exceeding current 7-8 foot predictions. This feedback loop accelerates melting and could slow global ocean currents, leading to superstorms and faster atmospheric warming. Researchers emphasize that stopping global temperature rise is essential to prevent ice shelf collapse.

Andrew Johnson expresses being overwhelmed by assuming office following a tragic event, declines to outline specific future policies, and instead points to his past opposition to rebellion and advocacy for free government principles as assurance of his future conduct. He emphasizes his lifelong commitment to improving conditions for ordinary Americans, accepts responsibility for his actions while leaving outcomes to divine judgment, and requests support from his audience in guiding the government through current dangers.

Zebronics launched its portable "Buddy Speakers" for ₹1,699, featuring 630g weight, LED display with RGB lighting, 5W RMS output, 3-hour battery life, Bluetooth connectivity, FM radio, and USB/MicroSD/AUX options with 10-meter wireless range. Director Pradeep Doshi highlighted the speaker's compact design and audio performance.

Pre-apprenticeships are proposed as a solution to make construction apprenticeships more accessible, as current programs favor students who already possess skills and knowledge, excluding those needing extra support. These short-term programs provide career exposure, skill-building, mentorship, and industry credentials. However, pre-apprenticeships face underfunding, limiting their reach and data collection capabilities. Solutions include innovative financing for wraparound supports like transportation and childcare, better outcomes data collection to demonstrate effectiveness, and strategic partnerships among employers, unions, government, and philanthropy to unlock additional funding.

Researchers developed an AI tool called Waldo that scanned over 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use to detect harmful side effects, flagging more than 28,000 posts as potentially problematic. Verification of 250 flagged posts found 86 percent represented genuine adverse experiences. The tool outperformed ChatGPT in accuracy but not human reviewers. Researchers suggest such AI monitoring of social media could help public health workers identify harmful products, particularly where official reporting systems are lacking, though experts caution about ethical implementation and limitations in applying the tool to other substances.

This paper presents Robodoc, a medical chatbot prototype integrating multiple AI models through OpenAI APIs. The system combines a conversational interface with specialized diagnostic models: an X-ray model detecting viral/bacterial pneumonia, an OCT model identifying retinal conditions (Drusen, CNV, DME), and a diabetes detection model using TensorFlow.js. Google's Teachable Machine enabled rapid transfer learning for image models with minimal training data. The chatbot uses OpenAI's function calling to intelligently route user inputs—text or images—to appropriate diagnostic models, then generates human-friendly responses. Testing showed good integration with minor deviations, including some misclassification between pneumonia types and occasional errors in urgency assessment for retinal conditions. The architecture allows modular expansion through a "Lego approach" where new models can be added via API links. The author emphasizes this demonstrates how public APIs enable building complex medical AI systems without extensive infrastructure, offering an alternative UI/UX for bioinformatics tools while noting limitations around LLM unpredictability and the need for human oversight in medical applications.

Enterprises prefer external HPC solutions: 87% use or plan to use cloud providers, 74% use colocation datacenters, and 43% partner with scientific institutions. Only 6% currently maintain on-premises HPC infrastructure, though 28% plan to within two years. Scientific partnerships face limitations due to prioritization of research projects and long wait times for commercial needs.

Turing GPUs feature enhanced Tensor Cores with INT8, INT4, and FP16 precision modes for AI inferencing, enabling real-time deep learning in gaming through NVIDIA NGX features like DLSS. The architecture introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing for realistic lighting effects. Turing includes GDDR6 memory, larger L2 caches, and improved compression for 50% effective bandwidth gains over Pascal. New display capabilities include 8K/60Hz support, HDR processing, and VirtualLink USB-C for VR. The architecture offers Variable Rate Shading, Mesh Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering for optimized performance. Three GPU variants exist: TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (RTX 2080/Tesla T4), and TU106 (RTX 2070), with the Tesla T4 delivering up to 40x higher inference performance than CPUs. RTX-OPS provides a workload-based metric combining tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and integer operations for hybrid rendering scenarios.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington addressed the Wilson County Commission about an upcoming total solar eclipse, calling it the biggest public one-day event in U.S. history. Wilson County is positioned near the center of the 70-mile wide total eclipse path, where viewers will experience up to 2 minutes and 38 seconds of totality. Wellington noted that half the U.S. population is within a day's drive of the path, potentially doubling local populations. The commission also voted to allow retiring officers to retain their service weapons after 15 years of service, and approved funding for a school resource officer at Springdale Elementary School, which opens in August and will receive over 700 rezoned students.

This article identifies Williams %R as the best swing trading indicator based on backtests of six popular indicators, ranking them by risk-adjusted return rather than highest return. Swing trading involves holding positions from one day to a few weeks, with optimal indicator time frames of 1-15 days. Risk-adjusted return measures annual return divided by market exposure, compared against maximum drawdown. The six indicators tested were Williams %R, WilliamsVixFix, Bollinger Bands, Stochastics, Internal Bar Strength, and RSI. Williams %R performed best with slightly longer lookback periods (around 10 days), very low entry thresholds (-90), and minimal exit criteria (-80), producing low drawdowns and only two negative years since 1993. The article notes that mean reversion indicators work better on stocks than commodities, and that low drawdowns help prevent behavioral trading mistakes.

This patent application describes video encoding/decoding methods and apparatuses that improve prediction efficiency through several techniques. For inter-prediction, the invention uses weight prediction parameters (multiplication and addition parameters) to handle brightness changes between videos, with options to merge these parameters from neighbor blocks or estimate them from reconstructed pixels. Motion vector precision can be upwardly adjusted using adjacent reconstructed pixels. For intra-prediction, the invention corrects prediction samples using reconstructed pixel areas, determines candidate modes based on neighbor block frequency of use, and encodes mode differences between blocks. The methods also include dividing blocks into sub-blocks for individual prediction, with various techniques to reduce overhead information transmitted between encoding and decoding apparatuses.

Organized patriotism and national unity, replacing local and class divisions with loyalty to the whole country, are essential for national growth. Technical education ranks second to patriotism in fostering national success. The federal government cannot lead technical industrial education nationwide but should ensure schools in the District of Columbia provide commercial and industrial training. Current public school systems that focus only on literary education discourage students from industrial work, which should be combated. Technical education—from basic trades to advanced engineering—is crucial for developing skilled workers who can compete internationally against educated labor. The federal government can set examples through legislation for the District of Columbia regarding industrial training, child labor, and factory laws. Farmers are equally vital to national welfare; farming must become a technical and scientific profession with practical training opportunities, as intensive cultivation and better business organization replace outdated frontier farming methods.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reports revenue of $20.379 billion, down 12% from $23.201 billion in the prior year period, with net income of $4.620 billion compared to $4.540 billion. The company implemented a new segment structure: Productivity and Business Processes ($6.306 billion revenue), Intelligent Cloud ($5.892 billion, up 8%), and More Personal Computing ($9.381 billion, down 17%). Revenue decline was primarily due to lower phone revenue and a $1.3 billion Windows 10 revenue deferral, partially offset by Intelligent Cloud growth. Operating income was $5.793 billion, down 1%. The company had $99.355 billion in cash and short-term investments, repurchased $4.0 billion in common stock, and declared a $0.36 per share dividend. Windows 10 launched and reached 110 million devices, with commercial cloud annualized run rate exceeding $8.2 billion.

The leu remained steady as investors awaited the Romanian central bank's interest rate decision, while the forint and Czech crown firmed 0.2% after China's central bank moved to reverse yuan declines. The Romanian central bank has raised rates since January and manages its currency more closely than regional peers. Analysts are divided on whether it will hike rates to 2.75%, though monetary conditions have already tightened with the 3-month ROBOR rate rising to 3.17%. Hungary's central bank discussed inflation trends with analysts after abandoning its ultra-low rate stance, with the forint rebounding on speculation of more credible price stability policies. Central European currencies have declined this year due to dollar-driven capital flows, with the forint and zloty down about 5% and the Czech crown down 2%.

Local share prices rose with most Asian markets, partly due to weak US inflation data suggesting continued dovish Federal Reserve policy and easing US-North Korea tensions. Singapore's STI gained 0.9% to 3,308.69. Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 1.4%, South Korea's Kospi 0.6%, and China's Shanghai Composite 0.9%, despite disappointing Chinese economic data. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 1%. Last week's market losses were driven by Trump-North Korea tensions, though assurances from US officials have somewhat calmed nerves. Investors remain cautious ahead of North Korea's Liberation Day. OCBC and DBS led Singapore gains, while UOB declined. Property stocks CapitaLand and City Developments rose, as did Olam International after reporting 29% higher Q2 profit. Asian Pay Television Trust gained despite 29% lower quarterly profit.

U.S. stocks rose Monday after the Easter holiday, with technology, industrial, and consumer companies gaining after China reported 6.9 percent first-quarter economic growth. The S&P 500 climbed 0.5 percent, the Dow rose 0.6 percent, and the Nasdaq added 0.6 percent. Notable gainers included Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Netflix, and Alere, which accepted a reduced $5.3 billion buyout from Abbott Laboratories. Eli Lilly and Incyte fell after the FDA rejected their rheumatoid arthritis drug Olumiant. Snyder's-Lance dropped 18.6 percent on weak guidance and CEO retirement. Arconic rose 4.7 percent after CEO Klaus Kleinfeld resigned following undisclosed contact with Elliott Management. Straight Path Communications climbed 16.5 percent on potential competing buyout interest. Oil prices declined slightly, bond yields dipped to 2.23 percent, the dollar weakened against the yen, and the euro strengthened. Several major overseas markets remained closed for Easter.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode using the SYNC pin, where the primary device's clock output (at twice the switching frequency) serves as the secondary's clock input. The primary device has its RT pin populated while the secondary's RT pin floats. This mode supports two scenarios: synchronizing two independent converters to the same frequency with no other connections, or creating an interleaved converter with parallel phases requiring shared VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC connections. The secondary controller inverts the received clock signal, creating a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs.

This article demonstrates how to backtest a MACD trading strategy using Python. It covers downloading historical data from Yahoo Finance with the yfinance library, calculating the MACD indicator using pandas' ewm() function, generating trading signals based on histogram values, and plotting results with matplotlib. The strategy assigns 1 when histogram is positive and 0 otherwise, with positions entered the day after signals trigger. When backtested on Apple stock, the MACD strategy yielded 15.04% CAGR versus 19.07% for buy-and-hold, but was only invested 51.13% of the time. The article provides base code for readers to develop their own strategies.

Former Prime Minister Jean Chrétien spoke at a Liberal nomination meeting in Vaughan-Woodbridge, reflecting on unity following the Yonge St. van attack that killed 10 people and injured 14. Economic Development Minister Steven Del Duca urged attendees to donate blood and support Premier Kathleen Wynne's government ahead of the June 7 election. Outside, hundreds of LiUNA Local 183 members protested labour changes in the budget bill.

This paper introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only rectification module that maps camera-centered 3D human poses to a body-centered canonical frame. The system uses a hybrid GCN-Transformer encoder with cross-attention fusion to predict a global 6D rotation (converted to SO(3) via Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization) and an optional residual correction. Trained with self-supervised synthetic rotations, it reduces rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4° and MPJPE by ~27% on MM-Fi, with stable cross-subject and cross-environment generalization. On TotalCapture, canonicalized poses yield acceleration signals that better match IMU ground truth than geometric baselines, demonstrating improved kinematic fidelity for applications in health monitoring, sports science, and VR training.

New federal tax law changes to payroll withholding tables will result in extra money for about 90% of workers beginning in February, though amounts vary significantly based on income, family status, and pay frequency. A married couple with two children earning $90,000 annually could see approximately $61 extra per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single person earning $35,000 might see nearly $32 more. Key factors include the doubled child tax credit to $2,000 per qualifying child under 17 and higher income phase-out thresholds. Employers must implement new withholding tables by February 15. Workers may need to complete new W-4 forms when available to adjust withholding, as the higher standard deduction ($24,000 for married couples, $12,000 for singles) and eliminated deductions for home equity loan interest and capped state and local tax deductions may affect tax situations. Bonus check withholding rates have dropped from 25% to 22%.

Bill Norton, a four-star defensive lineman from Christian Brothers High School in Tennessee, committed to the University of Georgia on March 18, 2018. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound prospect, ranked 11th nationally at his position, chose Georgia over offers from Alabama, LSU, Ohio State, Notre Dame, and others. Norton announced his decision shortly after visiting Tennessee, where new coach Jeremy Pruitt had recently been hired. His high school coach noted Norton's athleticism and ability to find the football, adding that Georgia consistently viewed him as a defensive lineman while some other schools considered him for offense.

This study examines the intersection of wartime and online education in African higher education institutions through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus database publications from 2000-2024. While online education in Africa has grown since the 1990s through ICT development, the continent faces challenges including limited internet penetration (47%), inadequate infrastructure, and faculty unpreparedness for digital teaching. Despite over three-quarters of African nations experiencing warfare in the past three decades, the bibliometric analysis reveals a significant research gap: no African countries appear among publications on wartime and online education. Of 53 documents analyzed, most originate from the United States (21) and Ukraine (10), with only five publications specifically addressing war, education, and online learning—none from Africa. The study identifies two distinct keyword clusters: learning-focused (e-learning, online teaching) and warfare-focused (students, teachers, Ukraine, war). The findings highlight urgent need for research on wartime online learning in African contexts to address organizational sustainability and educational continuity during conflicts.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic Party operative known for political pranks targeting Richard Nixon, died at age 94 in Tucson, Arizona. Tuck's pranks included planting bogus fortune cookies, booking large venues with small crowds for Nixon speeches, posing as a fire marshal to underreport crowd sizes, and infiltrating a 1962 Chinatown rally with a critical sign in Chinese. His actions contributed to Nixon's paranoia, leading the 1968 campaign to destroy multilingual buttons fearing Tuck's interference. Tuck also worked on Robert F. Kennedy's 1968 campaign and ran unsuccessfully for California Senate in 1966. He maintained his Nixon animus into his 90s, proposing "Nixmas" to commemorate Nixon's resignation.

Mathieu Henderson concluded his four-year OHL career with a breakout season, finishing ninth among league defencemen with 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games for the Flint Firebirds. The 21-year-old Brantford native improved his defensive game significantly, raising his plus/minus from minus-45 to minus-seven, which he credited for opening up offensive opportunities. After the Firebirds' first-round playoff elimination, Henderson joined the ECHL's South Carolina Stingrays for three games before roster limitations ended his stint. He is currently undecided on his next step, considering professional hockey in North America or Europe, or university, while crediting his coaches and parents for their support throughout his career.

The lecture covers online markets, focusing on Google's search advertising auction mechanism. It begins with a review of VCG mechanisms, which implement utilitarian solutions in dominant strategies but are often computationally infeasible due to large message spaces. Google instead uses a generalized second-price auction where advertisers submit per-click bids, which are ranked by bid times quality score, and winners pay based on the next highest bid.

Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz modeled this as a clock auction showing it has an equilibrium with bid shading that surprisingly reproduces VCG payments, making it ex post stable and efficient. However, this model lacks consumer search behavior. Athey-Ellison's paper adds consumer search costs, showing reserve prices can signal quality and improve welfare by guiding search. Under uniform search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price, though Google has incentives to set higher prices that harm advertisers and consumers.

The lecture briefly mentions Anderson-Renault's work on endogenous pricing where firms set prices to deter further consumer search, creating multiple equilibria, and Armstrong-Zhou's analysis of information design in platform markets like Amazon, where limited information can intensify price competition.

The civil aviation ministry has requested a two-month postponement of GST implementation, citing airlines' need for more time to revamp systems for compliance. Airlines, including Air India, have raised concerns about modifying global ticket distribution systems and lack of clarity on taxation of aircraft parts movement, which could increase operational costs. Minister of State Jayant Sinha chaired a GST preparedness meeting with industry stakeholders. The finance ministry maintains GST will launch as scheduled on July 1, with Revenue Secretary Hasmukh Adhia dismissing delay rumours as false.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The IRS announced new federal income tax brackets for 2026 with higher income thresholds to adjust for inflation. The standard deduction will increase to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single taxpayers. Other changes include adjustments to long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemption, and earned income tax credit eligibility. The top tax rate of 37% will apply to individuals with taxable income above $640,600 and married couples filing jointly earning $768,700 or more. The announcements came a day after the IRS said it would furlough nearly half its workforce due to a government shutdown.

This document specifies the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization. It defines GHCB data structures, MSR protocol functions for initialization and communication, and Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events for hypervisor requests. Key components include GHCB GPA registration, protocol version negotiation, CPUID request handling, page state changes, AP management, SNP guest requests, and restricted injection with #HV doorbell pages for secure interrupt delivery. The specification covers SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest initialization, memory encryption bit handling, and hypervisor-guest communication mechanisms.

Egyptian archaeologists unveiled the tomb of Hetpet, a Fifth Dynasty priestess to Hathor, on the Giza plateau. The tomb features well-preserved wall paintings depicting hunting, fishing, offerings, musical performances, and rare scenes of monkeys—one eating fruit and another dancing before an orchestra. The discovery was made during excavation in Giza's western cemetery, which contains tombs of top Old Kingdom officials. A German expedition had previously found antiquities bearing Hetpet's name in 1909, now in Berlin's museum. Archaeologists plan continued excavation of the site.

SOS full court pressure scenarios force offensive teams to react to backcourt pressure, with "shadow" presses (Back shadow, Up shadow, Face shadow) featuring a second defender behind the on-ball defender, and "Blitz" presses providing more aggressive denial and trapping. These presses aim to create turnovers, rushed shots, player fatigue, and transition opportunities while disrupting offensive tempo and removing the ball from playmakers. Deployment depends on player personnel and game situation, typically used against inferior or slow teams, when behind, or as a change of pace. Success requires basic SOS defensive fundamentals including forcing the ball to side checkpoints and denying first passing lanes. All shadow presses end in Base Go Red, with pressure ending if the shadow player cannot position properly or if deep/middle outlet passes occur.

The UK and Ukraine are discussing future trade growth post-Brexit, including continuity of the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement's DCFTA, which facilitates over £1.7 billion in trade. The UK confirmed it will be treated as an EU member state for international agreements during the Implementation Period, ensuring no trade disruption. Both countries agreed to strengthen bilateral trade.

Amber Enterprises, a Gurugram-based appliance manufacturer, has received Sebi approval to raise approximately Rs 555 crore through an IPO. The company filed its draft prospectus on September 29 and received regulatory observations on December 5. The IPO includes a fresh issue of Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 105 crore by promoters Jasbir Singh and Daljit Singh. Proceeds will be used for loan repayment and general corporate purposes. Edelweiss Financial Services, IDFC Bank, SBI Capital Markets, and BNP Paribas are managing the offering.

This study examines perineuronal nets (PNNs) in the hippocampus of subjects with substance use disorder (SUD), major depressive disorder (MDD), and comorbid SUD/MDD. Researchers found increased PNN densities in CA1 and other hippocampal subregions of subjects with SUD, accompanied by increased parvalbumin and VAMP2 gene expression and decreased matrix metalloproteinase 9 and cathepsin S expression. Subjects with MDD showed decreased PNN densities in CA1, while comorbid SUD/MDD subjects showed mixed results. Rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration also displayed increased hippocampal PNNs. The findings suggest PNNs may stabilize reward memories in SUD and represent potential therapeutic targets for context-induced relapse, while highlighting the importance of considering comorbid MDD in SUD pathology.

This patent application describes systems and methods for detecting abnormalities in medical images using deep learning approaches. The invention addresses challenges in evaluating high-resolution, multi-modal medical images by providing automated localization and classification of abnormalities such as lesions, fractions, and bleeding.

Key embodiments include: (1) a multi-task network with jointly trained localization and classification networks using encoder-decoder and neural network architectures; (2) a multi-modality fusion network combining information from multiple imaging protocols (e.g., T2-weighted, DWI, ADC images); (3) a regression network for scoring lesions (e.g., PI-RADS scores for prostate cancer); and (4) an abnormality detection method using generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize normal tissue images for comparison with input images containing abnormalities.

The application also describes training methodologies using multi-site datasets to improve model generalizability, including curriculum learning strategies that progressively fine-tune models using datasets ordered by similarity, and deployment-stage optimization that selectively refines models using annotated data ranked by uncertainty.

A player reflects on a loss, noting little difference between this game and a previous one against Anaheim, emphasizing that his team failed to execute their game plan while their opponents succeeded, including capitalizing on a power play. He mentions a disputed goal reviewed in Toronto that was disallowed, stating the team must accept the decision and move on to focus on the next game.

President Trump tweeted criticism of the Russia investigation over Memorial Day weekend, claiming it devastated young aides who came to Washington with "stars in their eyes." Most departures from his White House, however, stemmed from internal infighting rather than the probe. Trump's lawyer Rudy Giuliani said on CNN that the president is "fine with" answering questions about potential obstruction but expressed personal discomfort with that aspect of the investigation. Giuliani also stated he no longer views the investigation as legitimate. Trump falsely called Mueller's team "13 Angry Democrats" and repeated claims that FBI informants amounted to "spying" on his campaign—claims Sen. Marco Rubio disputed, saying the FBI appropriately investigated suspicious individuals near the campaign. Trump also falsely accused The New York Times of using a "phony" source regarding North Korea summit logistics; the source was actually a senior administration official briefing reporters under White House-arranged anonymity rules.

A University of Virginia Health System recovery program for thoracic surgery patients reduced morphine use by 59-74%, shortened hospital stays by two days, and saved over $1.3 million in its first year. The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program, launched in 2016 with 139 patients, achieved these results without increasing complications or readmissions. The multidisciplinary approach emphasizes patient education, standardized care, and reduced opioid use. UVA has expanded ERAS to other surgical areas including colorectal, gynecologic, and orthopedic surgery. Findings were published in the Annals of Thoracic Surgery.

Two Lashkar-e-Jhangvi militants escaped from Karachi's Central Jail, prompting suspension of at least 12 prison officials including the superintendent. The militants, Shaikh Muhammad Mumtaz and Muhammad Ahmed Khan alias Muna, belonged to dangerous LeJ factions. DIG Prisons requested police register a case against suspended officials for negligence. IG Prisons Nusrat Mangan stated the escape occurred from a newly formed ATCs complex on the prison's outer perimeter with different security levels, and a committee was formed to investigate. Separately, a robber was killed in a police encounter in DHA Karachi after resisting during a car snatching attempt, while his accomplice fled. Police also arrested 15 outlaws in citywide raids, recovering weapons and narcotics.

The speaker views the upcoming Stanley Cup final game as just another game they need to win, emphasizing they will prepare to win without dwelling on past losses or the high stakes. They acknowledge the excitement but maintain focus on the task at hand, noting that no team has had a perfect playoff record.

French President Emmanuel Macron made his first official visit to Nigeria, meeting with President Muhammadu Buhari to discuss security cooperation including intelligence sharing for the G-5 Sahel force and the multinational joint task force against Boko Haram, as well as economic matters including a French reforestation and agricultural project in Ogun State expected to create 150,000 jobs. Macron stated France would help with terrorism but that Nigeria must address Fulani herdsmen violence, and emphasized African leaders should understand why youth join terrorist groups. Separately, a South African newspaper reported on child trafficking in Gabon, highlighting cases of two girls trafficked from Benin and Mali, with one found chained after forced marriage; Gabon is among nine West and Central African countries where the UN has documented long-standing child labor exploitation.

AMD shares surged following an AI chip deal with OpenAI. Gold rallied above $3,900/oz amid yen weakness and U.S. rate cut expectations. USD/JPY dropped over 2% after a weak NFP report and President Trump firing the Bureau of Labor Statistics CEO; it holds near key support ahead of ISM services PMI data. GBP/USD faces direction uncertainty ahead of the BoE decision, with markets anticipating a 25 basis-point rate cut despite elevated inflation. BTC/USD declined with U.S. equities, testing crucial support near 112,000; technical indicators show oversold rebounds but uncertainty persists. Fed officials are scheduled to speak throughout the week. Evercore's Emanuel suggested a bubble scenario could push the S&P 500 to 9,000 by 2026.

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation's annual study states UK families need £40,000 yearly for a decent standard of living, with each working parent of two children requiring £20,000 (up from £13,900 in 2008) and single people needing £18,400 (up from £13,400). The author critiques this calculation, noting only 30% of households earn above this threshold, making redistribution unviable. Proposed solutions include reducing childcare and housing costs through deregulation, raising personal tax allowances to £18,400, and pursuing economic growth through lower taxation and smaller government.

Culpeper defeated Courtland 2-1 in a baseball game decided by defensive errors. Courtland committed seven errors, including five in the final two innings, while Culpeper made routine plays consistently. Culpeper's winning run scored in the seventh inning on an error by Courtland third baseman Ethan Critz. Both starting pitchers delivered complete games with nine strikeouts and two hits allowed: Courtland's Alex Kobersteen walked none, while Culpeper's Jake Dudley walked three. Courtland's only run came on a steal of home by Addie Burrow. Courtland coach Tim Acors and first-year Culpeper coach Brandon Mack both emphasized the importance of making routine defensive plays.

The Department of Education will halt two Obama-era rules set to take effect July 1 that would have protected student borrowers and held for-profit colleges accountable. The department will instead create committees to review and improve the rules. One rule required for-profit colleges to demonstrate "gainful employment" for students to maintain federal aid; the other established how defrauded borrowers could apply for loan forgiveness.
