Education Secretary DeVos stated the rules missed "an opportunity to get it right." The department will maintain debt forgiveness for 16,000 borrowers with pending claims. Critics call the rules burdensome, while Democratic Attorneys General and senators oppose the delay.

VentureWire newsletter dated November 30, 2000, covering venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include: 724 Solutions acquiring Tantau Software for $375 million in stock; El Dorado Ventures raising a $250 million fund for early-stage IT investments; children's website MaMaMedia reducing staff to 15 employees amid financial struggles; and former Prodigy chair Samer Salameh becoming CEO of network services firm iVMG. The newsletter details numerous funding rounds, including INEA ($3M), Parachute ($10M), Spintopia ($2.85M), Medschool.com ($26M), Vectiv ($13M), DemandTec ($16M), Latinia ($5M), Clarendon Photonics ($16M), Tapestria ($25M for 20% stake), Firstdoor ($9M), E2O Communications ($38.5M), IDe ($12M), Whereoware ($21M), and RealTimeImage ($9M). Other news includes Ariba and Softbank joint venture Nihon Ariba KK bringing in 20 new investors for a 5% combined stake, ProSeed Capital making three international investments, and ProcureZone.com securing $3M from Mitsui. Product launches include EA Web Holdings' cardiac health sites and Xdrive rebranding to Xdrive Technologies. Blackboard acquired AT&T Campuswide Access Solutions and CEI SpecialTeams from iCollege. Multiple executive appointments and board changes are reported across various companies. VC fund news includes Hyperion Partners closing $73M of a $100M fund and Crosspoint Venture Partners delaying its $1 billion fund due to market conditions. Gabriel Venture Partners added a former Sun Microsystems executive, and Redleaf Group opened a Boston office. Corrections note the omission of Mike Kaplan from Three Arch Capital Partners' partner list.

Etisalat Nigeria has not yet reached an agreement with 13 local banks to restructure a $1.2 billion loan after missing a payment, according to an unauthorized company source. The source spoke at Etisalat's annual general meeting in Abu Dhabi, where CEO Saleh Al Abdooli declined to comment on the debt talks. Nigerian regulators agreed in March to pursue a default deal rather than receivership to avoid deterring investors and triggering a wider debt crisis. Sources indicate Etisalat may sell its stake in the Nigerian unit after a debt deal is finalized.

The offensive goal kick in soccer aims to retain possession and create attacks. Taken from the Goal Area after the ball crosses the end line off an attacker, the kick is live once kicked and visibly moves. Youth modifications include build-out lines for players 10 and under, requiring defenders to retreat before challenging. Younger players learn short passing sequences to targets; older youth progress to multiple receiving options including midfielders. Adults typically use goalkeepers for kicks, with varied short and deep targeting strategies. Goal kicks are direct restarts where goals can be scored without intermediate touches, though wind conditions can cause unusual outcomes.

Greece's central bank chief Yannis Stournaras urged Athens and its foreign lenders on February 13 to complete the country's bailout review by end of February, warning that further delays would rekindle uncertainty and undermine economic recovery. Months-long talks have stalled over disagreements on labour and energy reforms, fiscal targets, and IMF involvement. Stournaras told parliament that conditions could worsen and it may become too late, noting that household deposits reversed their upward trend in early 2017 and that prolonged uncertainty could hurt Greek banks' capital adequacy. Finance Minister Euclid Tsakalotos met with euro zone officials and IMF representatives last week to break the impasse, with euro zone finance ministers expected to discuss the issue in Brussels the following week. Greece's economy, which has been expanding after years of recession, is projected to grow 2.7 percent this year.

India's Finance Ministry endorsed Project Sashakat, a five-pronged strategy to resolve non-performing assets faster. The plan, headed by PNB's Sunil Mehta, involves independent asset management companies and steering committees for bad loans over Rs 500 crore. It addresses lender alignment through inter-creditor arrangements requiring 66% agreement, and aims to attract foreign capital. Steering committees will handle stressed accounts over Rs 50 crore within 90 days using templatised approaches. The committee suggested an asset trading platform but rejected creating a 'bad bank.' SMEs with loans up to Rs 50 crore will be resolved through template-based approaches. Banking sector gross NPAs reached 11.7% as of March 2018.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement to build a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho, allowing Qatari pilots to train with American military personnel using F-15 fighter jets. The announcement follows Qatar's gift of a Boeing 747 jet to the U.S. and reflects deepening ties between the Trump administration and Qatar.

Researchers have launched a six-year-designed experiment to study how supplemental monthly income affects brain and emotional development in babies and toddlers during their first three years, potentially reshaping understanding of poverty's effects on children.

This study describes clinical manifestations and outcomes of 165 scorpion sting patients admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea's western lowlands from June 2019 to May 2020. The case fatality rate was 4.8% (8 deaths). Most patients were from urban areas (57%), over 15 years old (61.2%), and worked as shepherds, farmers, or students. Black scorpions (38.8%) were most commonly identified, with stings occurring predominantly at night (62.4%), indoors (56.4%), and on feet (64.8%). Common symptoms included localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), and vomiting (33.9%). Using Abroug's classification, 43.6% had class III (severe) symptoms, 35.8% class II, and 20.6% class I. Children under 15 showed greater severity and fatality risk than adults. Most cases occurred during summer (93%), peaking in September-October. Treatment included local anesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, and for severe cases, nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom. The high class III rate was attributed to delayed hospital seeking due to local reliance on traditional remedies. The study recommends preventive education, improved healthcare access, and essential drug availability.

The random walk trading strategy is based on the theory that stock prices move unpredictably, making market timing futile. Popularized by Burton Malkiel's 1973 book "A Random Walk Down Wall Street," the strategy emphasizes diversification through broad market index funds rather than individual stock picking. The theory assumes a 50% probability of price movements in either direction, rendering technical and fundamental analysis ineffective. A 1988 Wall Street Journal experiment comparing professional investors to dart-throwing stock selection showed experts beat the market only half the time. Backtests of random entry strategies on S&P 500 stocks showed positive results due to market upward drift, while gold ETF backtests performed poorly. The strategy contrasts with the efficient market hypothesis—while both conclude outperforming the market is difficult, random walk assumes irrationality whereas EMH assumes market efficiency. Key proponents recommend passive, diversified investing over active trading.

The passage is a collection of financial news headlines and promotional content for StarCompliance, a regulatory technology company. Headlines cover mergers (Fifth Third acquiring Comerica for $10.9B), executive changes (Santander UK CEO stepping down), market developments (AMD stock surge, London IPO activity, Tesla deliveries), infrastructure investments (Poland's $5.5B NATO fuel network, Bifrost subsea cable), and regulatory actions (U.S. freezing NYC infrastructure funds). The main content promotes StarCompliance's employee compliance platform, emphasizing how technology transforms compliance from a defensive burden into a strategic advantage. The company highlights challenges facing multinational firms in balancing global consistency with local regulatory requirements amid accelerating regulatory change and rising enforcement penalties. StarCompliance's platform offers real-time monitoring, automated reporting, and unified oversight across jurisdictions for employee conflicts, incident tracking, and MNPI oversight. The company received Pan Finance's Most Innovative Employee Technology Platform USA award and has 25+ years of experience serving large financial institutions.

The United States consistently opposed foreign aggression in Hawaii and viewed annexation as a contingent necessity from an early date. Lord Palmerston acknowledged this possibility in 1850. In 1851, King Kamehameha III signed a contingent deed of cession to the U.S. Commissioner to be enacted if France attacked. In 1854, Secretary Marcy negotiated a draft annexation treaty that failed due to foreign influence and the king's death. In 1867, Secretary Seward instructed the Honolulu minister to favorably receive annexation overtures, and President Johnson anticipated eventual voluntary Hawaiian application for statehood. In 1871, President Grant solicited Senate views on annexation. In 1873, Secretary Fish directed the minister not to discourage annexation sentiment. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, U.S. policy focused on defending exclusive commercial rights and supporting the Hawaiian government. In 1881, Secretary Blaine stated the U.S. would seek an "American solution" if Hawaii could not maintain benevolent neutrality. The report was submitted by John W. Foster on February 15, 1893. The first U.S. official in Hawaii was John C. Jones, appointed on September 19, 1820, as "Agent of the United States for commerce and seamen," with Navy officers also occasionally reporting on American interests.

Official car fuel economy figures are unreliable due to outdated testing procedures with multiple loopholes. The New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), used since 1997, allows manufacturers to remove weight, disable features, use eco modes, and inflate tires to improve results. A new test (WLTP) began in September 2017. Which? conducts more realistic tests using WLTP with cold and hot cycles, motorway driving, air conditioning on, and no modifications. They also measure emissions and use portable devices to verify NOx levels on real roads. Which? has tested over 700 vehicles, revealing true fuel costs that can differ by over £800 annually between efficient and inefficient medium-sized cars.

Anthurium, also called "tongues of fire," is a South American plant with red, pink, or white heart-shaped blossoms that filters ammonia and xylene from indoor air. Its sap and leaves may cause allergies. The plant requires bright indirect light, humidity, temperatures of 18-21°C, and annual repotting in containers with drainage holes. Leaves need misting in winter to prevent dry air damage, with repotting frequency reduced to every two years as the plant matures.

This study examines how college teaching modalities (in-person, hybrid, online) during COVID-19 affected infection spread in surrounding communities. Using a quasi-experimental approach matching similar colleges with different modalities, the research finds that in-person reopening increased COVID-19 cases and deaths over time in neighboring areas. The study addresses limitations in prior research by accounting for endogeneity in colleges' modality choices and using varied reopening dates for identification, analyzing county-level outcomes rather than campus-level data.

The passage outlines strategic assets for negotiating peace with Germany after World War I, covering economic exclusion risks facing Austria-Hungary and Germany; opportunities in Bulgaria through satisfying territorial claims; military successes and Turkey's postwar weakness as leverage; German colonies and Pacific exclusion as bargaining material; Russian revolutionary radicalism as a threat to German interests; Vatican diplomacy as a potential asset; American military and economic resources ensuring ultimate victory; intangible factors including global peace desires, anti-diplomatic sentiment, league of nations hopes, and social revolution fears; and Germany's shifting geopolitical ambitions from southeast to east following Russia's collapse.

President Harry S. Truman announces Germany's unconditional surrender to the United Nations, marking victory in Europe while noting the ongoing war against Japan. He calls for sober reflection on the sacrifices made and emphasizes the need for continued work to complete the war and build lasting peace. Truman designates Sunday, May 13, 1945, as a national day of prayer for thanksgiving and remembrance of the fallen.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 2, 2022, reporting results from operations and financial condition under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The filing incorporated by reference a press release dated October 2, 2022, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on October 3, 2022.

Navient Cp Cmn (NASDAQ:NAVI) shares rose 2.27% in the most recent session, closing at $13.51. Wall Street analysts project a 52-week price target of $16.89 based on 9 opinions, with a high estimate of $22 and low of $13.5. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 2.75 from 8 recommendations, ranking 138th out of 265 industries. Analyst recommendations include 1 Buy, 3 Outperform, 5 Hold, 1 Underperform, and 0 Sell. The stock's ATR-14 is 0.41, weekly volatility is 2.72%, monthly volatility is 2.82%, and RSI is 51.03. Navient has a market capitalization of $3.55 billion with 263 million outstanding shares. Recent trading volume was 5.78 million shares, above the average of 2.8 million.

Viral genome sequencing has shifted from retrospective research to near-real-time analysis, informing public health responses during outbreaks like SARS-CoV-2. However, global sequencing capacity is highly concentrated: 90% of sequences come from just 10% of countries, creating challenges for monitoring variants in low-capacity regions. Traditional regression methods require large sample sizes and struggle with geographic heterogeneity, leading to unreliable early estimates of variant growth rates.

The authors developed a hierarchical Bayesian modeling approach that pools data across countries to estimate variant dynamics even with sparse sequencing. This method generates country-specific prevalence estimates, growth rates, and global fitness advantages while accounting for regional heterogeneity. Applied to SARS-CoV-2 variants BA.1 through BA.5, the model revealed substantial geographic variation in fitness advantages—for example, BA.5 showed higher relative fitness in the US and UK compared to India and South Africa. Retrospective validation using BA.5 emergence in Portugal demonstrated that the multicountry model produced more stable estimates and lower prediction error than single-country approaches, particularly early in variant emergence when data are limited. The method complements sequencing capacity investments by maximizing information extraction from available global data, with applications for real-time surveillance dashboards and subnational estimates.

President Johnson addresses the nation following a week of violence and tragedy, announcing the appointment of a special Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders chaired by Governor Otto Kerner with Mayor John Lindsay as Vice Chairman. The Commission will investigate the origins of recent urban disorders and recommend measures to prevent future disasters. Johnson condemns the looting, arson, and violence as criminal acts, not civil rights protests, stating they must be punished forcefully. He has directed new riot control training for National Guard units and emphasizes that lasting peace requires addressing conditions like poverty, discrimination, and unemployment through legislation including the Model Cities Act, Civil Rights Acts, Medicare, Medicaid, and education programs. He criticizes congressional rejection of urban funding requests, including $20 million for rat control in slums. Johnson calls for a national day of prayer on July 30 for order and reconciliation, urging Americans to reject violence and hatred while pursuing justice and equality through peaceful means and continued legislative action.

This paper studies Gorenstein-projective modules over the ring of dual integers Z[ε] = Z[T]/(T²). The authors classify these modules and establish equivalences between several categories: the stable category of Gorenstein-projective Z[ε]-modules modulo projectives, the stable category of submodules of finitely generated free Z[ε]-modules, the orbit category Dᵇ(Z)/[1] of the derived category of integers, and categories of perfect differential structures. The main result shows these five categories are equivalent, with the theorem also holding when replacing integers with any principal ideal domain. The paper further describes a chain of categories linked by dense functors from bounded complexes of free abelian groups through Gorenstein-projective modules to finite abelian groups, and constructs a commutative cube of categories using three types of dense functors.

Scotiabank's 1832 Asset Management LP will pay $950,000 in fines and costs to settle with the Ontario Securities Commission over improper spending on promotional activities for financial advisers from 2012 to 2017. The firm, manager of Dynamic mutual funds, provided excessive non-monetary benefits including NHL tickets, concerts, golf events, Apple iPad minis, keyboards, sunglasses, and expensive food and entertainment. The firm began compliance improvements last year and stated it takes regulatory responsibilities seriously.

WIRED's podcast "Uncanny Valley" features host Zoë Schiffer and senior culture editor Manisha Krishnan discussing five major stories. Federal workers received politically charged out-of-office templates blaming Democrats for the government shutdown, potentially violating the Hatch Act. Peter Thiel's lectures about an impending Antichrist figure who will unify humanity before the apocalypse are examined, noting the irony given his investments in surveillance technology. Tesla is encouraging drowsy drivers to use its "Full Self-Driving" feature despite safety concerns and a recent liability ruling. Scientists successfully created human eggs from skin cells to form embryos, offering potential infertility treatments but raising ethical questions. OpenAI launched Sora 2, a social video app using AI-generated content where users create digital avatars of themselves; it includes guardrails against nude content but has inconsistent copyright enforcement.

Vodafone Ghana CEO Yolanda Cuba assisted customer Andrew Kufuor, cousin of former President J. A. Kufuor, at company headquarters. Kufuor had come to thank SME Enterprise team member Eunice Ampomah-Manu for saving his life. During a routine customer call, Ampomah-Manu remained on the line for ten minutes as Kufuor suffered a medical attack, extracted his wife's number, and contacted her. Kufuor's wife rushed home and took him to a clinic. Cuba stated Vodafone's commitment to unmatched customer experience as a core business value.

Nick Kyrgios will face John Isner in the second singles rubber of Australia's Davis Cup quarter-final against the United States in Brisbane, with both players tied for third on the ATP ace leaderboard with 218 aces this season. The match follows Jordan Thompson versus Jack Sock. Australia and the U.S. have 60 Davis Cup titles combined, though neither has won since 2003 and 2007 respectively. Isner leads their head-to-head 2-1. Sock, ranked 15th, has never played Kyrgios. Thompson replaces Bernard Tomic for Australia.

IT technologies have expanded usage scenarios for industrial calculations, with over half of surveyed decision makers using simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping. Digital twins and IoT sensor data enable feedback loops for product development. High-performance computing (HPC) is becoming critical as demand grows from 8% currently to nearly 50% in two years. Eighty-one percent view HPC as a game changer for innovation, citing benefits including complex calculations, quality improvements, new usage scenarios, and increased agility. Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructures (87%) or colocation (74%) over on-premises solutions due to security concerns, costs, and energy consumption. Cloud-based HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) offers advantages in scalability, cost optimization, global collaboration, and access to modern technologies. Eighty-one percent of HPC users plan to implement HPC-based business models. IDC recommends virtual development, holistic data strategies, evaluation of HPC operating models, and leveraging external expertise.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 25, 2022, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021. The report includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. The filing states that the information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in an electric circuit in the 1980s. Their work with Josephson junctions showed quantum effects at a macroscopic scale, enabling the development of superconducting qubits used in quantum computers. The three researchers, affiliated with UC Berkeley, UC Santa Barbara, and Yale University, will share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

Enron's stock plunged over 18% to eight-year lows on October 30, 2001, following Moody's downgrade of its senior unsecured debt to two notches above junk status and the company's disclosure that it was seeking new credit lines. The energy trader, which had lost $15 billion in market capitalization over two weeks, faced ongoing SEC investigation into off-balance-sheet partnerships run by ousted CFO Andrew Fastow. Bond default insurance premiums doubled as investors sought protection amid credit concerns. Trading partners including AEP, Exelon and Northeast Utilities expressed caution but continued limited trading with Enron. Meanwhile, new CFO Jeff McMahon outlined ambitions to expand Enron's forest products trading unit, aiming to become one of North America's largest newsprint marketers through financial hedging tools, despite acknowledging hurdles in convincing publishers of product quality.

This technical document describes design considerations for the TPS7H500x-SP series of radiation-tolerant PWM controllers. Key sections cover synchronous rectifier FET selection (80-V rated GaN FETs with parallel Schottky diodes), RCD clamp circuit design using transformer leakage inductance and peak current parameters, output inductor calculation (0.47 μH selected for 40% ripple current), and output capacitance determination accounting for voltage ripple, load transients, and radiation-induced single event transients (2.3 mF total used). Additional filter design equations address ESR zero and resonant frequency placement. Current sensing uses a 7.5-Ω resistor with 1:100 current sense transformer for 35-A cycle-by-cycle limiting. Frequency compensation employs Type 2A with 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF components. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loop areas, separating analog and power grounds, routing sensitive traces away from noise sources, and proper bypass capacitor placement. The controllers operate from 4-14 V input with 0.1 μF minimum bypass capacitance. Revision history notes QMLP option releases for TPS7H5001-SP (August 2023) and TPS7H5002/3/4-SP (August 2024).

The MSPM0 G-Series microcontroller datasheet describes the device's power management unit (PMU), clock module (CKM), DMA controller, event manager, memory organization, flash memory, SRAM, GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, DAC, security features, TRNG, AES accelerator, keystore, CRC, math accelerator, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, low-frequency subsystem, RTC, watchdog timers, general-purpose and advanced timers, analog connections, debug interface, boot strap loader, and factory constants. Key specifications include: PMU with brown-out reset and multiple power modes; CKM with internal/external oscillators and PLL generating clocks up to 80MHz; DMA with 12 channels supporting various transfer sizes; dual 12-bit ADCs at 4Msps; up to 256kB/512kB flash with ECC and 100k cycle endurance on selectable 32kB sectors; up to 128kB SRAM with ECC protection on Bank 0; 93 GPIO pins; security features including AES-128/256, firewalls, and secure key storage; multiple communication interfaces including UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD; and comprehensive development tools and software support.

The Open Source Definition was published 20 years ago, with the term "open source" proposed by Christine Peterson on February 3, 1998, as a more commercially palatable alternative to Richard Stallman's "free software." Both terms emphasize making source code available under licenses favoring user freedom. Bruce Perens, who drafted the Debian Free Software Guidelines that became the OSD, dates its announcement to February 9, 1998. Open source has become central to the tech industry, with major companies like Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Microsoft depending on it. Microsoft notably shifted from its 2001 stance when Steve Ballmer called Linux "cancer" to now embracing open source. Tim Burke of Red Hat notes open source has evolved from cloning proprietary software to leading innovation.

German Ambassador Bernstorff informed U.S. officials that Germany would terminate its naval blockade if peace conference terms could be arranged, while German Foreign Secretary Zimmermann presented submarine warfare documents to Ambassador Gerard, expressing hope that President Wilson would remain neutral for two months while Germany attempted to force England to seek peace through submarine warfare. Zimmermann warned of an exhausted Europe vulnerable to Japan and other Asian powers if peace was not achieved, and conveyed Germany's peace terms including retention of Belgian infrastructure, French territory, limited Serbian restoration, and German indemnities. Meanwhile, Austria-Hungary's Foreign Minister requested U.S. consideration of their defensive war position, noting their acceptance of Wilson's "peace without victory" principle and urging Wilson to pressure the Entente to abandon dismemberment aims, while stating that submarine warfare modifications were technically impossible due to deployed vessels.

Energy storage, particularly batteries, has gained attention as a solution for increasing renewable energy use and reducing fossil fuel reliance. Storage systems take power from grids or local sources for later use. Costs include capital and running expenses, requiring benefits to exceed these for economic viability. Various technologies exist: lithium ion batteries work well at small scales but are expensive per unit; pumped hydro operates at large scales cheaply; flywheels provide short-term power dispatch and frequency stability; others include compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries, and hydrogen.

Lithium ion battery costs have fallen from US$1,200 to US$600 per kWh in five years. For home systems to break even, costs need to reach roughly A$1,000 per kWh fully installed, though current retail electricity rate structures may change. If flat rates replace variable rates, batteries would need to cost around A$300 per kWh. Network infrastructure savings from peak demand reduction only apply where electricity demand is growing; since 2009, overall demand has declined, limiting grid benefits.

Pumped hydro costs approximately A$100 per kWh and can store large amounts using water, with 1,500 megawatts already in Australia's National Electricity Market. Despite being cheaper and easier to control, distributed lithium ion batteries may prevail due to consumer behavior patterns, similar to rooftop solar's popularity over large-scale solar.

An Irish Times "Portrait Gallery" article features Nobel Prize-winning physicist Ernest Walton, described as a quiet, shy man who declined glamorous atomic physics jobs abroad to remain in Ireland. The piece downplays his 1930s achievement of splitting the atom at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab, noting it was "difficult for the layman to grasp." Jack McManus's photograph shows Walton working with a biro in a Trinity College Dublin lab, with a guarded expression. The author contrasts this understated coverage with modern hyped science reporting, particularly regarding CERN's Higgs boson announcements. Related photographs and a book, "The Times We Lived In" by Arminta Wallace (€19.99), are available for purchase.

Apple Inc. filed an amendment to its Restated Articles of Incorporation on August 3, 2020, increasing authorized common stock shares from 12,600,000,000 to 50,400,000,000 and implementing a 4-for-1 automatic stock split effective August 28, 2020.

Bitcoin futures began trading on Cboe Global Markets' exchange, offering a regulated way to bet on the cryptocurrency's price movements. The launch has received mixed reactions from financial institutions: Interactive Brokers will offer access with restrictions, while Charles Schwab, TD Ameritrade, JPMorgan Chase, and Citigroup are not participating immediately; Goldman Sachs plans to clear futures for certain clients. Analysts suggest futures may reduce long-term volatility and improve price discovery, but concerns remain about inaccurate pricing, systemic risk to clearing houses, and potential manipulation of the underlying spot market.

The Korean Diet (K-diet) is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods including vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods like kimchi. It features smaller portions than Western diets, with foods such as rice, barley, various vegetables, fermented soybean products, and broth-based dishes. The diet minimizes processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Benefits include high fiber, low calories, improved gut health from probiotics, and potential weight loss when combined with physical activity. Drawbacks include high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium due to limited dairy, and high carbohydrates from rice and noodles requiring portion control. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free needs.

CoachingAmericanSoccer.com provides general "Rules of the Road" for new soccer players and coaches, covering team tactics including positioning, ball work, and team functions. The guidelines complement position training and can be adapted to individual coaching styles.

This manual provides instructions for using the Sansa Fuze media player. It covers transferring music via drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player, converting and transferring photos/videos using Sansa Media Converter, and playing music, audiobooks, videos, and photos. The device supports MP3, WMA, secure WMA, and Audible formats. Additional features include FM radio with 30 presets, voice recording, and customizable settings such as wallpaper, backlight, power saver, and language. Content can be deleted directly on the player or via computer. The manual also includes troubleshooting tips, warranty information, and software license terms.

A speaker expresses concern for Mr. Horton's recovery and notes Aaron's absence from the playoffs. The team plans to move forward despite a tough loss, drawing on their experience of bouncing back from a blowout in Chicago. They had a strong first period but unlucky bounces and broken equipment led to easy goals for the opponent. The speaker states that all three series played have been hard fought and nothing unusual has occurred.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. It features a speed-boost mode enabling up to 8MSPS sampling for a selected channel pair while other channels remain idle. The device uses SPI for configuration with three register banks, supporting single-device and daisy-chain topologies. Daisy-chain mode requires setting DAISY_CHAIN_LEN and uses N × 24 SCLKs for register writes across N devices. Key registers control SPI mode, bank selection, data format, test patterns, speed-boost channel selection, gain error correction, analog input bandwidth, power-down, reference configuration, and common-mode range. For ATE applications, the ADS9803 achieves 0.0015% TUE post-calibration at 25°C ±5°C and offers wide-bandwidth mode (700kHz) for fast multiplexed signal settling. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, requiring careful decoupling capacitor placement and layout practices to minimize noise.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 28, 2021, reporting its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 25, 2021. The filing includes a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This study developed a predictive nomogram for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Researchers retrospectively analyzed 109 patients who underwent aneurysm treatment between 2013–2021, identifying three significant risk factors: age ≥65 years, surgical clipping (versus endovascular coiling), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3. The multivariate logistic regression model showed odds ratios of 3.94 for age, 4.36 for clipping, and 3.59 for HHS ≥3, with an area under the curve of 0.753. A nomogram was constructed assigning 1 point to each risk factor to estimate SDHC probability. The study found that posterior circulation aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, PNR) were not significant predictors in this cohort, possibly due to universal external ventricular drainage placement and higher rates of endovascular coiling. Limitations include retrospective design and limited sample size.

Nike reported surprise 1% revenue growth in its fiscal first quarter, beating expectations of a mid-single digit decline, though profits fell 31% and gross margin dropped to 42.2% as inventory clearance efforts continue. CEO Elliott Hill highlighted progress in wholesale, running, and North America, where sales rose 7% and 4% respectively, but acknowledged ongoing struggles in other areas, including a 9% revenue decline in China and 4% drop in direct sales. The company is executing a turnaround strategy focused on clearing old inventory, realigning corporate structure by sport rather than gender, and expanding female customers through initiatives like the NikeSKIMS partnership launched last week.

Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated knee during Monday night's win over the Jets. The injury occurred in the third quarter when his left leg twisted under him during a tackle. Hill was carted off with an air cast, smiling and waving to the crowd. He will remain hospitalized overnight for further tests. The 31-year-old had 67 receiving yards before the injury and leads the Dolphins with 198 receiving yards this season. With Hill out, Jaylen Waddle becomes the team's de facto No. 1 receiver, with second-year receiver Malik Washington potentially stepping into a larger role. Hill has 11,363 receiving yards since 2017, the most in the NFL over that span.

An international research team has obtained live specimens of Kuphus polythalamia, a giant sulfur-feeding shipworm found in a Philippine lagoon. Unlike wood-eating shipworms, this species burrows in mud and consumes hydrogen sulfide. Scientists hope to discover new antimicrobial substances by studying microbes in its gill. The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The animal's elephant tusk-like shells can reach 5 feet, though its life cycle and age remain unknown. Researchers had sought live specimens for 20 years.

The article presents a seasonal trading strategy for the German stock market using the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG). The strategy involves investing only during the fourth quarter (October-December) based on historical data showing EWG's strongest returns occur in this period. A backtest of this approach since EWG's inception demonstrated better performance than buy-and-hold. The DAX 40, Germany's main stock index of 40 blue-chip companies with $1,250 billion market capitalization, serves as the underlying market reference. For U.S. investors, EWG provides easier access to German stocks than direct DAX investment, though its 0.50% expense ratio is relatively high. The strategy's holding period is limited to the final three months of each year.

Climate change is threatening cutthroat trout in the northern Rocky Mountains by warming and reducing stream flows, allowing rainbow trout to invade their habitat. Rainbow trout and cutthroat trout are mating and producing less fit hybrid offspring, with no reversal possible. A study in Global Change Biology found widespread hybridization, especially where rainbow trout were historically introduced. Some states are removing rainbow trout to protect the native species, which biologists warn could otherwise face permanent extinction.

Former INEC official Christian Nwosu testified in Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into falsely admitting he received N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Dieziani Alison-Madueke. Nwosu claimed operative Usman Zakari threatened detention unless he wrote dictated statements, then escorted him to surrender N5 million cash and N4 million bank draft. Nwosu also alleged prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo ordered his continued detention and demanded he list property worth N30 million while threatening conviction if he didn't cooperate.

A nationwide study of over 1.1 million older adults found that long-term exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning, was associated with a 10% higher risk of Parkinson's disease. Researchers estimated outdoor TCE exposure using ZIP+4 codes and EPA air pollution data, finding highest concentrations in the Rust Belt and near certain industrial facilities. The study, published October 1, 2025, does not prove causation but adds to evidence that environmental pollutants may contribute to Parkinson's risk. Limitations include focus on Medicare-aged individuals and reliance on 2002 outdoor air data that may not reflect lifetime or indoor exposure.

State Street Corporation, the firm that commissioned the "Fearless Girl" statue promoting women in leadership, agreed to pay $5 million to settle claims that it discriminated against 305 female employees and 15 black vice presidents by paying them less than male and white counterparts in the same positions. The company denies the allegations but will pay approximately $4.5 million in back pay and $500,000 in interest. The 4-foot bronze statue was installed in March 2017 opposite the "Charging Bull" in New York City's financial district as a publicity stunt for State Street Global Advisors, which manages $2.5 trillion in assets, while also promoting a gender diversity index product.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit, bringing quantum effects to a scale once thought impossible.

A swimming advisory was issued for Little Beach in Port Stanley due to high bacteria levels, warning of gastrointestinal illness and infection risks. The advisory, posted Friday and still active Monday, does not close the beach—people may still swim at their own discretion. Cathie Walker of the Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit explained the difference between advisories and closures. Some visitors, including Terrie Vergiris who brought three children Monday, were unaware of the signs. Vergiris considered Little Beach safer than the main beach and had visited previously without issues. This was the first advisory issued this summer after prior testing. Advisories are posted at www.elginhealth.on.ca.

Sir John Deane's sixth form college held its fourth annual Evening of Jazz and Soul at the Macdonald Portal Hotel in Tarporley. The 35-member jazz collective, directed by Timothy Murphy, performed 1960s soul and classic swing music to a packed audience. Head of performing arts Alison Richards praised the performers, who had only been together for months. The college's next event is a classical music evening at Arley Hall on February 9, with tickets at £8 (£6 concessions).

Norwich children Evan (10) and Brynn (6) Meek made and distributed 220 bagged lunches to homeless people in Manhattan on August 6 after being inspired by their mother's concerns about NYC homelessness. NPD officer Thomas Miller, an eight-year veteran, left for the Syracuse Police Department on August 10; he and his K9 Nitro hosted community events, with a local bakery donating Nitro's food. Tracy A. Price, 31, of Norwich, was arrested August 16 on charges of torturing, injuring and neglecting a dog and was granted $750 bail.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden used machine learning and advanced simulations to reveal the hidden structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a promising halide perovskite solar material. Their findings, published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on August 14, 2025, identified the material's low-temperature phase and explained why formamidinium molecules become semi-stable during cooling. This breakthrough could enable durable, ultra-efficient, flexible solar cells thin enough to coat phones and buildings. The research combined simulations with experimental validation from the University of Birmingham and was funded by multiple Swedish and European organizations.

A 36-year-old New York man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, was arrested at the Coachella festival in Indio, California, after concertgoers used "Find my iPhone" to track him with over 100 stolen cellphones in his backpack. He faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges. Police advise attendees to keep valuables in front pockets, use elastic bands, carry dummy wallets, and distribute items to prevent theft.

Wafa Yahia, a 52-year-old Syrian grandmother and mother-in-law of Honolulu imam Ismail Elshikh, arrived in Honolulu Saturday night after receiving U.S. government approval several weeks ago. Elshikh is a plaintiff in Hawaii's lawsuit challenging President Trump's travel ban on people from six mostly Muslim countries, which argues the ban prevented Yahia from visiting. Her 28-hour journey began in Lebanon and went through San Francisco. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin stated that Yahia's visa approval does not affect the ongoing lawsuit, as the state continues to seek the ban's full overturn. A federal appeals court in Seattle will hear arguments later this month on the government's appeal of a July ruling allowing grandparents and other family members to enter. The Supreme Court previously permitted a scaled-back version of the ban to take effect, exempting applicants with "bona fide" U.S. relationships, with full arguments scheduled for October. Two of Elshikh's five children had never met Yahia, who last visited Hawaii in 2005. Elshikh credited the lawsuit for enabling his family's reunion while expressing sadness for others still affected by the ban.

Cuba held a military parade on January 2 to mark the 58th anniversary of the revolution that brought Fidel Castro to power, with tens of thousands marching at Revolution Square in Havana. Soldiers marched without equipment, unlike previous years. Participants carried banners and photos of Castro, despite his request against creating a cult of personality; Cuba's legislature had recently banned monuments and infrastructure named for him. The event occurred as Cuba faces economic challenges from Venezuela's crisis and uncertainty over US relations under President-elect Donald Trump, who has threatened to reverse diplomatic thaw. Student leader Jennifer Bello stated Cuba would not renounce its principles, calling normalization with the US a "long process."

A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found that general distraction is the best way to recover from a breakup, though it should be used sparingly. Distractions include new hobbies, education, or exercise. Another option is focusing on negative aspects of the past relationship to move on faster.

Pregnancy makes sleeping difficult due to physical changes and medical restrictions—back sleeping is unsafe after month five, and only left-side sleeping is recommended. The author, a stomach-sleeper, discovered the U-shaped Leachco pregnancy pillow through a Facebook post and purchased it for $65. The pillow provided immediate comfort, allowing side-sleeping with leg support and easy position changes without readjustment. The author used it constantly, even carrying it around the apartment. Downsides include its large size (challenging for smaller beds), scratchy original cover (replaceable), and messy blanket arrangement. The author plans to continue using it post-pregnancy and recommends it broadly.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 27, 2021, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2021. The report includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. The company's common stock and notes trade on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT.

Vale SA's stock conversion plan received 84.4% shareholder backing, exceeding the 54.09% minimum threshold, with 1.66 billion preferred shares converted to common stock. The company may accelerate its planned 2020 listing on Brazil's Novo Mercado to 2018. The conversion aims to attract Asian investors and mining specialists while limiting political involvement, though the government retains a golden share. Vale will absorb controlling entity Valepar SA as part of restructuring toward dispersed ownership. Common shares rose 2% to 31.40 reais, with year-to-date gains exceeding 26%.

COVID-19 emerged in Wuhan, China in January 2020 and was declared a pandemic by WHO in March 2020, causing global disruptions including in education. Over 1.5 billion students worldwide were affected by school closures, leading to widespread adoption of virtual education. In Turkey, the Education Informatics Network (EBA TV) was launched to provide remote learning.

This study examined primary school teachers' perspectives on virtual education for students with disabilities in inclusive settings during COVID-19. Using phenomenological design, researchers interviewed 10 general education teachers in Turkey's Marmara region. Findings revealed six main themes: teachers' virtual education methods, student attendance, inclusion and monitoring processes, following course activities and homework, teacher-parent cooperation, and solution suggestions.

Most students with disabilities participated regularly in virtual classes when supported by parents, though some faced barriers including family illiteracy, technology limitations, and preference for rehabilitation center education. Teachers reported challenges including large class sizes preventing individualized attention, lack of socialization, students turning cameras off, and insufficient family support. Successful cases involved daily parent communication and use of EBA tracking features.

Teachers applied varied solutions including hybrid models, flexible scheduling, video feedback, and psychological support for families. Suggested improvements included maintaining home discipline, providing device/internet support, ensuring continuous school access for students with disabilities, and coordinating with rehabilitation centers. The study emphasized parents' critical role as both caregivers and educators during virtual learning, recommending better stakeholder preparation, technological infrastructure, and disability-appropriate content for future emergency education situations.

This paper argues for adopting cooperative education (co-op) in Nigeria to address youth unemployment and skills mismatches. The UN defines youth as persons aged 15-24, and skills development encompasses both hard (technical) and soft (generic workplace) skills. Co-op is a form of experiential learning fully integrated into curricula, alternating academic terms with paid work terms.

Nigeria's youth unemployment has risen significantly, now exceeding most global regions except South Asia and MENA. Youth unemployment rates are at least double total unemployment rates, with higher rates among educated youth, urban residents, and females. The informal sector predominates, and 28% of Nigerian youth were not in employment, education, or training (NEET) in 2019.

Co-op originated in industrialized nations (UK, US, Canada, Australia) and exists in some Sub-Saharan African countries like South Africa and Namibia. Key dimensions include integrated curriculum, work-derived learning, and logistical coordination. Models include alternating, parallel, sandwich, and new American approaches. Benefits include higher graduate earnings, enhanced employability, employer input into curricula, and improved labor market outcomes.

Evidence from developed countries shows co-op graduates have higher employment rates, better field-of-study matches, lower overqualification rates, and 7% higher earnings. Practical implementation requires dedicated co-op units, quality assurance through accreditation bodies like WACE and CEWIL, student fees during work terms, and employer compensation.

Nigeria's existing programs (SIWES, SURE-P, N-SIP) lack full curriculum integration and close university-industry collaboration. The paper recommends federal government championed co-op, integrated with SIWES and N-Power, using the alternating model with multiple four-month work terms. This would require tax credits, grants, and public sector role modeling to encourage private participation.

This study analyzes the spatial dissemination of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 in England from November 2021 to January 2022 using 48,615 genomes and human mobility data. Researchers identified at least 6,455 independent introduction events, with early importations (6% of total) responsible for ~80% of infections. Travel restrictions on southern African countries were largely ineffective as importation sources shifted to the US. Greater London served as the central hub for initial spatial expansion, with viral spread following gravity model dynamics and human mobility patterns. The study found evidence of voluntary behavioral changes in response to local case numbers, with 11.97% reduction in trips per unit increase in weekly cases. The research highlights limitations of targeted travel restrictions and emphasizes the need for globally coordinated genomic surveillance systems.

The TLV321/2x comparators consume 40µA per channel with 40ns propagation delay. The TLV321x has push-pull output; TLV322x has open-drain output pullable to 5.5V. Input range extends 200mV beyond rails with 1.8mV internal hysteresis. Unused inputs require 50mV differential, not tied together. Push-pull outputs must not be shorted to opposite rails; open-drain needs 100µA–1mA pull-up. ESD clamps limit inputs to 0.2V beyond rails; series resistors recommended. Power-on reset holds output low for 32µs after 1.65V threshold. Applications include low-side current sensing with bypass capacitors critical for stability.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture delivers significant performance improvements over Turing, featuring 2x FP32 throughput, second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection performance and hardware-accelerated motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity support. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, and 128 KB L1/Shared Memory. The GA102 GPU includes 112 ROPs, 6144 KB L2 cache, and GDDR6X memory reaching 936 GB/sec bandwidth via PAM4 signaling. Key innovations include concurrent ray tracing and compute workloads, RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression, and support for 8K gaming with DLSS. The architecture introduces new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for AI workloads. Power efficiency improves up to 1.9x over Turing. The A40 data center GPU offers up to 5x AI throughput, 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink, and PCIe Gen4 support. Display capabilities include HDMI 2.1, 8K60/4K120 output, and AV1 hardware decode.

This is a fantasy football email report from Commissioner.COM dated November 22, 2001, sent to Paul Lucci at Enron. The email contains promotional offers for products including Anna Kournikova's 2002 calendar, Lara Croft Tomb Raider DVD, The Sporting News subscription, gas discounts, a Vegas vacation contest, satellite dish offers, fantasy football guides, and an Xbox giveaway at Taco Bell. The main content provides NFL player news and fantasy football recommendations for Week 11, including start/sit advice for numerous players across all positions, with specific team assignments noted for each player. The report also includes a dedicated section for "Luccis Losers" team player news.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on August 16, 2018, announcing its financial results for the quarter ended July 29, 2018. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress (Exhibit 99.2), which will be posted to the company's investor website. The information is furnished but not deemed "filed" under securities regulations.

The passage discusses Justice Amy Coney Barrett's defense of originalism in her book and examines its implications for the Supreme Court case *Robinson v. Callais*, which involves a constitutional challenge to Louisiana's majority-Black congressional district. The author argues that the *Shaw v. Reno* doctrine—which holds that race-predominant districting violates the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause—cannot be justified on originalist grounds, as neither the Fourteenth nor Fifteenth Amendment's original public meaning addressed such claims. The author contends that a consistent originalist should reject *Shaw* and defer to Congress's power under the Fifteenth Amendment to enforce voting rights, as amended in the 1982 Voting Rights Act, rather than using *Shaw* to limit that enforcement power.

The United States advanced to the Davis Cup quarterfinals after beating Serbia 3-0, with Ryan Harrison and Steve Johnson winning the decisive doubles match. Switzerland, without Roger Federer, was eliminated 3-0 by Kazakhstan. Belgium led Hungary 2-1, France led the Netherlands 2-1, Croatia led Canada 2-1, Spain led Britain 2-1, Germany led Australia 2-1, and Italy led Japan 2-1 in ongoing ties.

TI provides technical data, design resources, and other materials "as is" with all faults, disclaiming all warranties including merchantability, fitness for purpose, and non-infringement. Users are solely responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance with standards and requirements. Resources may change without notice and are permitted only for developing applications using described TI products; other use is prohibited. No additional intellectual property licenses are granted. Users must indemnify TI against claims arising from resource use. TI products remain subject to separate Terms of Sale, and these resources do not alter product warranties or disclaimers.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, created by AW Cohen in 1963, is a contrarian indicator that surveys over 100 market newsletters weekly to measure advisor sentiment as bullish, bearish, or expecting correction. Readings above 55% bullish indicate excessive optimism (negative), while below 35% indicates excessive pessimism (positive). Weekly figures above 70% suggest overbought conditions; below 30% suggest oversold. The index differs from AAII Sentiment Survey, which polls individual investors since 1987 rather than professional advisors. The index is available through Chartcraft's website by subscription.

Euclid, Ohio police are reviewing a viral cellphone video showing a white officer repeatedly punching a 25-year-old black man and hitting his head on pavement during a Saturday traffic stop. Police said the man ignored orders and resisted. The three-minute struggle ended with backup officers helping handcuff him. The officer is on paid leave. The NAACP is calling for a federal investigation. The man was examined at jail and released on bond for driving under suspension and resisting arrest. Police noted the incident was also recorded on a dashboard camera.

A pipe bomb strapped to a man exploded in a New York City subway passageway near the Port Authority bus terminal at 42nd Street and 8th Avenue around 7:30 a.m. Monday. The suspect and three others were injured, with non-life-threatening injuries. The suspect is in custody. The explosion triggered a massive emergency response, shutting down the area and disrupting subway and bus service. New Jersey Transit buses were diverted to Secaucus and Hoboken. President Trump was briefed on the incident.

Macmillan has released new editions of classic and new picture books for early years children. A 35th anniversary gift edition of Rod Campbell's "Dear Zoo" (£12.99) features gold foil and a slipcase. Catherine Rayner's "Solomon and Mortimer" (£6.99) follows two playful crocodiles. Paul Stickland's "Ten Terrible Dinosaurs" (£6.99), endorsed by the Natural History Museum, teaches counting through rhymes. Julia Donaldson and Rebecca Cobb's "The Everywhere Bear" (£11.99) tells of a lost school teddy's adventure. Morag Hood's "When Grandad Was a Penguin" (£11.99) features a grandfather acting strangely. Lane Smith's "A Perfect Day" (£11.99) shows how one bear's perfect day ruins others'.

The Rotary Club of Lakewood and Rocky River held its annual Speech, Music, and Visual Arts Contest awards ceremony on April 9 at Beck Center for the Arts, honoring students from five local high schools. Nicholas Cleary won the speech contest, while Angeliki Cintron took first place in music and Elyza Mihalski won visual arts. The article also covers community events including North Olmsted's Fan Walk brick sale, free meals at area churches, Lakewood City Schools' repeat Best Communities for Music Education award, a decorated traffic barrel in West Park, North Olmsted High School's musical, a special needs theater production at Beck Center, blood drives honoring Dr. Steve Meadows, a genealogy assistance event, a West Park neighborhood cleanup, and reminders about upcoming Earth Day and rummage sale events.

Department of Education employees had their automatic out-of-office email responses forcibly changed from neutral language to partisan messages blaming Senate Democrats for the government shutdown, without their consent. Some employees who changed the messages back to neutral language saw them reverted to the partisan version again. The Department of Labor also reportedly received similar partisan suggested language. Experts suggest this may violate the Hatch Act, which limits political activity by federal employees. The Department of Education's press line is now using the same partisan out-of-office message.

This policy brief argues that the "out-of-school children" (OOSC) indicator is inadequate for capturing educational access and exclusion, using Afghanistan as a case study. The OOSC indicator focuses solely on formal school enrollment, overlooking alternative pathways like madrasas, community-based education, and technology-based learning. It fails to account for geopolitical, cultural, and social realities driving exclusion, and privileges formal schooling while delegitimizing indigenous systems. The brief advocates replacing OOSC with an "out-of-education children" (OOEC) indicator that incorporates formal, informal, and non-formal educational pathways. This shift would broaden perspectives on educational challenges, foster culturally relevant solutions, and reimagine education as an interconnected ecosystem. Implementing OOEC requires changes to data systems, credentialing, collaboration among education actors, and resource allocation. The brief emphasizes that what gets measured determines what gets managed, and current narrow metrics limit policymakers' ability to address educational exclusion comprehensively.

SFS is an AMD firmware feature enabling runtime patching of high-priority system issues without rebooting. Patches are distributed as cryptographically signed "Seamless Firmware Servicing Update Packages" and tracked through three version numbers: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), Security Patch Level (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL). The AMD Security Processor verifies signatures before applying updates. Customers can optionally co-sign packages for additional control. SFS requires BIOS enablement via specific tokens and does not persist across reboots. Updates apply sequentially and validate firmware compatibility before execution. Memory alignment requirements and TEE command buffers structure the deployment process. Package naming follows AGESA release conventions.

The New York Supreme Court, Kings County, affirmed the judgment convicting Ronald Haynes of criminal possession of a weapon in the third degree based on his guilty plea. The court found no nonfrivolous issues for appeal and granted counsel's application to withdraw. The defendant's pro se arguments were precluded by his valid waiver of appeal rights.

U.S. passport application rules from 1902 require an oath of allegiance, physical description, and witness certificate. Native citizens need only basic information; those born abroad to U.S. citizen fathers must prove paternal citizenship; naturalized citizens must submit naturalization certificates with emigration and residence details. Unmarried women state marital status; married women provide husband's citizenship details. Children of naturalized citizens must submit parent's certificate. Residents of U.S. insular possessions need two witnesses to verify birth, residence, and loyalty. Passports expire in two years. One passport covers spouses, minor children, and servants. Professional titles are excluded. Applications may be rejected for unlawful purposes or noncompliance. Fees total $2.00.

Archaeologists in Mexico will excavate a sealed tunnel believed to lead to a hidden cenote beneath El Castillo pyramid at Chichen Itza. Cenotes—water-filled sinkholes—were central to Mayan spirituality as entrances to the underworld and sources of fresh water. The Maya practiced human sacrifice in these caverns to appease their rain god, Chac. The hidden cenote, discovered by scientist Rene Chavez Segura two years ago, may represent a fifth "axis mundi" direction. Previous exploration of nearby tunnels found them intentionally sealed with stone. Lead archaeologist Guillermo de Anda estimates three months to clear the tunnel. Research on remains from Chichen Itza's Sacred Cenote indicates about 80 percent of sacrificial victims were malnourished children aged 3 to 11, possibly already dead when deposited.
Lab tests show that jostling microbubbles of air and methane can create tiny lightning zaps, potentially explaining what ignites the methane gas believed to cause swamp will-o'-the-wisps.

The EU's Global Gateway plan has pledged €545 million ($636 million) for clean energy projects in Africa, including transmission lines in Côte d'Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydro energy in Lesotho, and mini-grids in Madagascar. The initiative aims to expand electricity access for nearly 600 million Africans while reducing fossil fuel dependence and creating an estimated 38 million green jobs by 2030. Global Gateway serves as Europe's alternative to China's Belt and Road Initiative, which has invested over $1.3 trillion globally and dominates Africa's critical mineral supply chains. China exported 15GW of solar panels to Africa in 2024-2025, a 60% increase, and secured $39 billion in African energy contracts in early 2025. The US also launched the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment in 2022. A key Western project is the Lobito Corridor railway connecting Zambian copper and DRC cobalt mines to Angola's Atlantic port, challenging China's control of metals essential for the green transition.
The New York Court of Appeals affirmed Enix Bussey's conviction on October 16, 1947, with no opinion issued. Seven judges concurred.

Patriarch Theophilos III announced the Greek Orthodox Church will appeal an Israeli court decision approving the sale of church property in East Jerusalem to Israeli settler organizations. The church has contested the deal for a decade, arguing it was illegally conducted by deposed Patriarch Irenaios. The Jerusalem District Court recently upheld the 99-year lease of three properties near Jaffa Gate to Ateret Cohanim. Theophilos called the ruling "politically motivated" and expressed concern over alleged Israeli legislative efforts to restrict Christian churches' property rights, urging world leaders to intervene.

The COVID-19 pandemic led Greece to implement distance education in preschools, though kindergarten teachers faced significant challenges due to inadequate digital infrastructure, limited teacher training, and unequal family access to technology. A 2020-2021 study of 82 kindergarten teachers in Epirus, Greece found that over 75% had little to no familiarity with distance education before the pandemic, and 91.5% had not previously incorporated it. While 65% preferred synchronous methods using state-provided Webex tools, teachers largely viewed distance education negatively: 90% believed it reduced psychomotor activities and required adult supervision, 86% found it less effective for social skills development, and 73% cited limited internet access as a barrier. Teachers with Level B ICT certification showed significantly higher familiarity with distance education, though years of service correlated with no difference in ICT literacy. Teachers considered distance education appropriate only for emergencies when physical attendance was impossible, citing young children's age as the primary obstacle to equitable implementation.

A "Take a Knee Chart" is a tool football coaches use to determine when their offense can safely kneel to run out the clock at the end of a game. The strategy involves lining up in "victory formation" to minimize turnovers, with the quarterback immediately kneeling after the snap—a run play that keeps the clock moving. Effective clock management is crucial for coaches, especially with the 40-second play clock now standard in high school and college football. Coaches must avoid clock-stopping mistakes like incomplete passes that could allow opponents time for a final scoring drive.

S&P Global Ratings downgraded Bridgeview, Illinois to BB-minus junk status on March 31, citing debt pressures from $135 million in bonds issued in 2005 for Toyota Park stadium. The rating agency placed the suburb on watch for further downgrade due to concerns about reduced market access and weak liquidity. Bridgeview's general obligation debt totals approximately $256 million, and the village is considering restructuring $24.5 million of variable-rate bonds. S&P noted the underperforming stadium has created an extremely high debt burden and very weak liquidity for the village of 17,000 residents.

The passage describes 24 photos from the 3rd Round of the Scripps National Spelling Bee held in Oxon Hill, Maryland, on May 30, 2018. The images show various spellers aged 9 to 15 from locations across the United States and South Korea, with pronouncer Brian Sietsema also pictured. Several spellers correctly spelled words including "bonspiel," "slickensides," "aspirator," "heliosis," "revivification," "sclerotic," and "deliverable," while others incorrectly spelled words including "giddily," "abandonedly," "finial," "frustraneous," "transude," "athleisure," and unnamed words. Reactions ranged from celebration to disappointment.

ML²B is the first benchmark for evaluating large language models on generating complete machine learning pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. It extends 30 Kaggle competitions into 13 languages, creating 390 evaluation instances across tabular, text, and image modalities in 12 domains. The benchmark includes human-reviewed task descriptions, standardized data cards to prevent information leakage, and 6 private competitions to address benchmark data leakage concerns. Evaluation of five LLMs across two execution frameworks reveals 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks, with English consistently performing best and low-resource languages showing higher failure rates. The modular submission format reduces preprocessing leakage, while static analysis identified potential data leakage in 5.9% of submissions. Hybrid architectures partially mitigate low-resource limitations but do not eliminate cross-lingual disparities.

This is Amazon.com, Inc.'s 2018 Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company, incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). For fiscal year 2018, Amazon reported consolidated net sales of $232.9 billion, operating income of $12.4 billion, and net income of $10.1 billion. Net sales grew 31% year-over-year, with North America sales at $141.4 billion, International at $65.9 billion, and AWS at $25.7 billion. The company employed approximately 647,500 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2018. Amazon identifies intense competition, international expansion risks, fulfillment network optimization, seasonality, and data security among its principal risk factors. The company holds $41.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of year-end 2018.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to generate buy and sell signals based on price crossings above or below the indicator. It identifies short-term market trends and can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, and cryptocurrencies. Backtesting shows the strategy performs well in trending assets like Bitcoin but fails in mean-reverting markets like stocks. Adding a 200-day moving average trend filter improves results. The strategy can be combined with other indicators such as RSI or Bollinger Bands for confirmation. Risk management techniques include stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification. Common mistakes to avoid include over-leveraging and emotional trading. The strategy is easy to implement but requires proper optimization and market selection to be effective.

Mark Palmer of Enron forwarded a class action lawsuit filed against electricity generators and traders including Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy North America. The lawsuit, filed by plaintiff Pamela R. Gordon in California Superior Court, alleges defendants manipulated California's wholesale electricity market from May 2000 by improperly using confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, exporting power to create artificial shortages, and scheduling outages to inflate prices. The suit claims violations of California antitrust laws, unfair trade practices, and seeks treble damages for overcharges estimated at $4 billion. The complaint references FERC and CPUC findings of "unjust and unreasonable" prices and notes similar suits against generators were expected.

GOLDWOOD is a premium plywood manufacturer in Yamunanagar, Haryana, known for quality products without compromise. The company emphasizes mutual trust, transparency, intellectual honesty, and on-time delivery. It prioritizes sustainable development alongside profits, focusing on quality manufacturing, people growth, and environmental safety. GOLDWOOD PLY offers products including Block Board, Flush Door, and Plywood across India.

The passage discusses the importance of enacting laws against corporate crimes that lack public excitement but face opposition from interested parties. It notes the government's shift from civil to criminal proceedings in trust and interstate commerce cases, citing successes in deterring offenders through fines and imprisonment. Judge Holt's opinion is quoted extensively, emphasizing the severity of rebate violations by railroad corporations—deliberate crimes committed by educated businessmen that threaten competitors and violate public trust. Holt argues such offenses are more heinous than common crimes, noting the difficulty of prosecution due to secrecy, and concludes that corporations should bear principal penalties when violations are flagrant.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony Friday, featuring Col. Roderik Cox as keynote speaker. The event included the National Remembrance Day Roll Call, where names of deceased MU student veterans were read. Speakers included student organization leaders and addressed Hollywood stereotypes of veterans, emphasizing that most are regular people pursuing education and careers. Robert Ross of the MU Veterans Center, which serves over 400 student veterans, expressed hope for future peace. The ceremony concluded with a reception at Bengal's Lair.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, enacted August 24, 2025, removes barriers to competition in the Philippine telecommunications market, enabling Virtual Network Operators to compete with market leader PLDT. The author argues this threatens PLDT's profitability, which is already declining, by introducing excess capital into a mature, highly penetrated industry. Despite PLDT's attractive valuation, the author recommends staying on the sidelines due to competitive threats.

Passports expire two years from issuance and can be renewed upon application. One passport covers a spouse, minor children, or servant when ages and allegiance are stated. Professional titles are excluded. A $1 fee is required, payable by currency or postal money order to the Department of State's disbursing clerk; drafts and checks are not accepted. The Department does not procure visa stamps from foreign governments. Blank application forms are available except to passport procurement businesses. Communications should be addressed to the Department of State, Passport Bureau, with return addresses included. The Secretary of State may reject applications for unlawful purposes or noncompliance. These rules were prescribed by President Theodore Roosevelt on July 19, 1902, under authority of Section 4075 of the Revised Statutes. Additional rules govern passport issuance in U.S. insular possessions: applications go to the chief executive or U.S. diplomatic/consular officers abroad; passports are denied to non-citizens and those with only declaration of intent; written affidavit applications require attestation by oath-administering officers with seals or authenticated certificates, two witnesses if signed by mark, and must include birth details, occupation, residence, and intent to return.

The International Nurses Association welcomed Joy Williams, BSN, RN, to their organization for publication in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare. Williams, a Louisiana-based Registered Nurse with over seven years of experience, began her career in 2009 as a Licensed Practical Nurse after graduating from Nunez Community College. She earned her Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Dillard University in 2016. She maintains memberships with the National Black Nurses Association and National Student Nurses Association, and credits her daughter Londen as her inspiration.

Small group differentiation is a pedagogical strategy that enhances learning outcomes and fosters inclusivity in diverse educational settings. The research, guided by Constructivism and Sociocultural Theory, examines differentiation across elementary and higher education from 2000-2023. Key findings show that effective differentiation requires flexibility in learning goals, ongoing assessment, respectful challenges, collaboration, and student autonomy. In elementary settings, teachers play more active roles with foundational content, while higher education emphasizes independence and self-directed learning with specialized, complex material. Challenges include time constraints, large class sizes, and inadequate teacher support. The study identifies limitations: lack of comparative data across settings, difficulty assessing relationships between small group instruction and learning outcomes, and absence of longitudinal studies tracking students from elementary through higher education. Future research should examine long-term effects of differentiation exposure and outcomes by learning style.

The Atlas of Human-AI Interaction is a computational framework that uses large language models to systematically extract and synthesize empirical findings from over 1,000 HCI papers, organizing them into structured [cause, relationship, effect] triplets to create a navigable knowledge graph. The system features three visualization modes: a 3D Graph View for exploring research themes and gaps, a Cause-Effect View for tracing directional relationships, and a Paper View for detailed study examination. Analysis identified 24 thematic clusters across human stakeholders, AI technologies, and concepts, with major research concentrations in educational contexts, explanation-trust relationships, and design applications. Network analysis revealed five concepts at significant structural holes—large language models, generative AI, trust dynamics, conversational interfaces, and autonomous agents—representing opportunities for cross-community synthesis. A user study with 20 expert researchers found the tool effective for landscape visualization, relationship discovery, and gap identification, though participants noted limitations in information depth, temporal analysis, and technical domain coverage. The work contributes open-source research infrastructure, a novel LLM-based synthesis methodology, structural analysis of the field, and expert-validated design principles for literature analysis tools.

The 4-3 defense, popularized by Tom Landry and modernized by Jimmy Johnson, consists of four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs. It features a 1 technique nose guard, two 5 technique defensive ends, and a critical 3 technique defensive tackle. The three linebackers include the big Sam, the versatile Mike, and the athletic Will. Strengths include strong run defense with seven players in the box and gap soundness. Weaknesses involve vulnerability to spread offenses that pull linebackers into coverage and personnel demands requiring athletic linebackers.
