Common blitzes include the Will Edge Blitz and Zone Blitz DE Drop. Coverages feature Tampa 2, where the Mike drops deep, and Cover 3. Notable users include the 2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 2006 Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic High School under Mike Bukovsky, who won multiple state championships.

Google launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for businesses offering secure, large-scale AI integration with advanced models, data governance, and compliance tools. Positioned between consumer and research offerings, it enables firms to deploy customized AI on Google Cloud with proprietary data fine-tuning and built-in controls. Google targets financial, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors, emphasizing transparency and accountability to compete with Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI. The platform integrates with Google Workspace and third-party software, reflecting Google's shift from AI development to enterprise deployment and monetization. Success depends on proving reliability and delivering measurable returns while balancing innovation, trust, and corporate integration.

Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio is a diversified investment strategy designed to perform across all economic environments through risk parity principles. It allocates heavily to bonds (40% long-term, 15% intermediate-term), with smaller positions in stocks (30%) and commodities (7.5% gold, 7.5% broad commodities). The portfolio prioritizes lower drawdowns over maximum returns, making it suitable for risk-averse investors, retirees, and FIRE practitioners. Backtests from 2007 show a 4.5% CAGR with 17% max drawdown versus S&P 500's 6.7% CAGR and 55% drawdown. The strategy outperformed during 2008/09, March 2020, and 2022 bear markets but underperformed during bull markets. Retail investors can replicate it using five ETFs, rebalancing 1-2 times annually in tax-deferred accounts. Leveraging 1.5x increases returns to 6.5% CAGR with 25% max drawdown. The portfolio's construction reflects Dalio's macro-based, top-down approach developed at Bridgewater Associates, the world's largest hedge fund.

A mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding $31 per month per child in child support, arguing the amount was too low and that support should not abate during the father's visitation periods. The court found the father, a law firm partner earning $16,930 in 1985 with likely future income increases, and the mother, a school librarian, had a visitation arrangement resembling joint custody where children were with the father about half the time. While agreeing that the father's expenses during visitation should factor into support calculations, the court concluded the trial court's amount was insufficient. Due to difficulty estimating the father's future income, standard formulas could not be readily applied. The judgment was modified to require the father to pay $65 per month for each child.

The theatrical production "Please, Continue (Hamlet)" by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat stages a real trial of Shakespeare's Hamlet for Polonius's murder using actual legal professionals and courtrooms. Since its 2011 Swiss premiere, it has played in 12 countries, adapting to each jurisdiction's legal system and requiring jury systems to function. The show incorporates elements from a real 2010 case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend's father, which Duyvendak obtained from a lawyer friend. Audience members serve as the jury and deliberate for 20 minutes. The creators, inspired by the Guantanamo trials' injustices, aim to demonstrate the complexity of justice systems and how perspectives on guilt shift when participants engage directly with legal processes.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of 270 articles on the metaverse in education from the Scopus database (2015–July 2024), using PRISMA methodology and VOSviewer visualization. The metaverse is defined as a three-dimensional virtual reality where avatars participate in everyday activities, merging real and virtual worlds. Research publications began in 2020, surged in 2022, and peaked in 2023. South Korea, China, and the United States are the most productive countries, with South Korea leading in citations. The most influential journals are *IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies* (most articles) and *Sustainability (Switzerland)* (most citations). The most cited article is Dwivedi et al.'s (2022) multidisciplinary perspective on metaverse challenges and opportunities. Prominent research themes include virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence, with emerging areas such as extended reality, blockchain, sustainability, and gamification. Two main research areas are identified: using the metaverse to create virtual educational environments and investigating user perceptions and attitudes. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) is frequently applied to study adoption factors, particularly perceived usefulness and ease of use. Gaps remain in longitudinal studies and cross-cultural comparative research.

The Appellate Division, Second Department affirmed an order in Jones v. Dow with $10 costs, with Judge Thomas dissenting on grounds that the ex parte order deprived the plaintiff of a statutory right to reply, and Judge Carr not voting.

Michigan State Police and Emergency Management are holding a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday during Severe Weather Awareness Week. Residents are urged to prepare by identifying shelter locations, conducting drills, monitoring weather broadcasts, and assembling 72-hour emergency kits. Tornadoes develop with 10-15 minutes warning on average and are most common in late spring and early summer. The drill will move to Thursday if severe weather occurs Wednesday.

This passage provides a comprehensive guide to basketball transition defense, emphasizing that good transition defense begins with good offense—taking care of the ball, making smart shots, and maintaining defensive balance. It outlines twelve essential principles including sprinting back with ball vision, maintaining numerical advantage, forcing extra passes, and defending outnumbered situations (2-on-1, 3-on-2, breakaways). The text details specific techniques for disrupting outlet passes, slowing ball handlers, and recovering after turnovers, blocked shots, and missed free throws. It stresses teaching methods like the "Whole-Part-Whole" approach and includes drills such as "Wolf" sprints and continuous three-on-two/two-on-one scenarios to build habits and conditioning.

The GHCB VALID_BITMAP field tracks which GHCB fields are valid for NAE events between guest and hypervisor. The guest sets bits for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2; the hypervisor sets bits for SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Both parties must reset VALID_BITMAP before each NAE event. Bit positions are calculated from field offsets: divide byte offset by 8 for qword offset, then divide by 8 for byte offset and mod 8 for bit position.

NAE events follow standard processing with exceptions documented separately. Software must disable interrupts and preemption when updating the GHCB and accessing it after VMGEXIT. For NMI handling, a separate GHCB is recommended. Hypervisor errors are communicated via non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0], with specific error codes for malformed input, unregistered GHCB, invalid scratch fields, missing required fields, and invalid NAE input.

Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT for IN/OUT instructions, MSR_PROT for RDMSR/WRMSR, VMMCALL for hypervisor-specific calls, #NPF/MMIO_ACCESS for memory-mapped I/O, Page State Change for SEV-ES/SNP guests, SNP Guest Request for firmware communication, SNP Extended Guest Request for certificate data, SNP AP Creation for vCPU management, #HV doorbell page for restricted injection notifications, #HV Send IPI for inter-processor interrupts, #HV Timer for emulated APIC timers, APIC ID List for discovering processor IDs, SNP Run VMPL for switching protection levels, SNP TIO Guest Request for trusted device binding, Secure AVIC for APIC state management, and Termination Request for guest-initiated shutdown.

SEV-ES guests identify support via CPUID: hypervisor present (ECX[31]), SEV support (EAX[1]), encryption bit position (EBX[5:0]), and physical address reduction (EBX[11:6]). SMP booting requires special handling since hypervisors cannot modify measured/encrypted registers; methods include memory-based reset vectors or predetermined CS/IP values. SEV-SNP adds AP Creation NAE for direct vCPU state management, enabling simpler AP booting and vCPU hotplug.

Restricted Injection limits host notifications to #HV exceptions via doorbell pages, with PendingEvent fields for interrupt vectors and non-maskable events, and NoEoiRequired for optimized end-of-interrupt handling. The hypervisor emulates APIC behavior, presenting interrupts by writing to PendingEvent and managing EOI cycles.

The Navy's Pier Pressure mobile application, part of the Keep What You've Earned campaign, helps Sailors make responsible drinking choices. Released for Alcohol Awareness Month in April 2017, the free app combines interactive gaming with tools including a calorie counter and integration with Uber and Lyft for safe rides home. The app has been played over 30,000 times and is available on iTunes and Google Play.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell over 400 points on April 24 due to concerns about rising interest rates and Caterpillar's indication that its first quarter would be its best for the year. The S&P 500 fell 1.3 percent and the Nasdaq composite dropped 1.7 percent, driven by declines in Facebook, Amazon, Alphabet and Netflix shares. Caterpillar stock initially rose on strong earnings but later fell 6.2 percent after its CFO's comments. 3M stock dropped 7 percent after lowering its profit forecast. Alphabet fell 5 percent despite reporting $9.4 billion in first-quarter net profit. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield exceeded 3 percent for the first time in four years, potentially prompting faster Federal Reserve tightening and higher borrowing costs.

Florence O. Summers sued Clennon C. Hemsell and Columbian Fuel Corporation for negligence causing the death of her husband J.W. Summers in a 1937 automobile collision. A jury awarded $30,890 in damages. The Court of Civil Appeals of Texas reversed the judgment due to multiple errors in the trial court's jury instructions. The court improperly fixed life expectancies at 34.5 years for the deceased husband and 20.2 years for his mother based on mortality tables, removing these fact questions from jury determination. The court also erred by allowing consideration of non-pecuniary damages such as loss of love, care, and fatherly advice, and by improperly suggesting specific damage items like college education expenses. Additionally, the trial court improperly allowed inflammatory argument by counsel criticizing opposing counsel for introducing admissible evidence. The case was remanded for a new trial.

Security researcher Michael Myng discovered a keylogger in Synaptics touchpad drivers affecting over 450 HP laptop and tablet models. The keylogger, disabled by default, was debug code inadvertently left in the drivers. HP confirmed the issue and released security patches in November. This marks the second keylogger issue for HP this year, following a similar discovery in Conexant audio drivers in May.

Police in China's Xinjiang region shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five people and injured 10 in Pishan County on Tuesday evening. Authorities called the attackers "thugs" and restored social order. The incident occurred in an area home to the Uighur ethnic minority, who are predominantly Muslim and speak Turkish. Beijing frequently accuses exiled Uighur separatist groups of planning attacks in the region, while some foreign-based Uighurs claim Beijing cracks down on the minority. The passage cites previous violence in the area, including a 2015 manhunt and a 2014 Kunming train station attack that killed 31 people, which state media called "China's 9/11."

Major League Soccer had four midweek matches with early and late kickoffs. Philadelphia's Borek Dockal, a 29-year-old Czech import, delivered two assists and a penalty in a Man of the Match performance, helping the Union extend their unbeaten run to four games. Ilsinho scored a highlight goal against Chicago, dribbling past Bastian Schweinsteiger. In another match, Josef Martinez scored after a slow cross while New England's Antonio Delamea Milnar defended poorly, though Teal Bunbury's late penalty earned the Revolution a 1-1 draw.

Johnny Juzang is making a case for a roster spot with the Minnesota Timberwolves after scoring 20 points in 14 minutes during a preseason game. The 24-year-old, on a non-guaranteed contract, has made 9-of-15 three-pointers this preseason and fits the team's need for outside shooting. Juzang, a former third-team All-American, has shot over 38% from three-point range over the past two seasons. The Timberwolves lost Nickeil Alexander-Walker this offseason and are evaluating young bench scorers including Rob Dillingham and Terrence Shannon Jr.

Researchers from Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic published a guideline in JAMA Internal Medicine to help physicians eliminate creatine kinase-myocardial band (CK-MB) testing for suspected heart attacks, as it adds no diagnostic value beyond cardiac troponin. Despite 2014 guidelines finding CK-MB redundant, 77% of U.S. labs still used it in 2013. The guideline, first in a series from the High Value Practice Academic Alliance, outlines four implementation steps: hospital education, removing CK-MB from order sets, creating IT alerts, and measuring outcomes. Heart disease kills 120,000 Americans annually; eliminating unnecessary CK-MB testing could reduce the $416 million yearly cost of heart attack blood tests.

This study uses hydrodynamical simulations combined with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer to assess the accuracy of observational methods for measuring infall velocities in prestellar cores. The authors simulate a collapsing Bonnor-Ebert sphere, post-process it with chemical and radiative transfer codes, and apply the Myers et al. (1996) method to derive infall velocities from synthetic line observations of CS, HCO+, and other molecular tracers. They find that measured infall velocities significantly underestimate the true mass-weighted values—often by factors of two to ten—because self-absorption features originate in outer regions where velocities are lower than the peak. The discrepancy arises from the method's reliance on constant-velocity slab models, which fail to capture realistic radially-varying velocity profiles. The authors suggest that non-thermal velocity dispersion from optically-thin lines may provide a better estimate of infall speed, though this requires further validation in turbulent environments. Consequently, mass accretion rates derived from these techniques likely underestimate true values substantially.

Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri, a 59-year-old Indian-origin surgeon, has been struck off the UK's medical register after a Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service hearing found him guilty of abusing his professional position by writing a love letter to a female patient he treated for a stomach complaint. The patient reported the letter to police and said she was distressed. Amaragiri, who did not attend the hearing, called the letter a "moment of madness," apologised to the patient and colleagues at Russells Hall Hospital, and intends to appeal the decision.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on March 11, 2021, reporting that Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking, effective March 11, 2021. Guillen will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including charging and servicing networks. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on March 12, 2021.

Sony launched a U.S. instant rebate and trade-in program through September 30, 2017, offering up to $300 off select full-frame cameras, up to $500 additional trade-in credit for interchangeable lens cameras, up to $200 on A7 cameras, and up to $100 on select lenses and accessories, with free shipping. Eligible items include Sony Alpha a7R II and a7S II cameras with various kits and storage options, plus several FE lenses including 16-35mm f/4, 24-240mm f/3.5-6.3, and 24-70mm f/4 models.

Compass Minerals International (CMP) is rated "Buy" due to attractive valuation and operational improvements in salt and plant nutrition segments, with rising revenue, volumes, and improved cash flow from cost-cutting. Despite higher net debt and leverage than peers, CMP trades at lower multiples with upside potential. Management projects 2025 top-line growth, though leverage risk prevents a "Strong Buy" rating. The author has no position in CMP and wrote the article independently.

The CANSLIM method, developed by William O'Neill of Investor's Business Daily, is a stock selection strategy based on seven criteria. Backtests show it has beaten the S&P 500 since 2003 with an 18% CAGR versus 9%, but with higher volatility and larger drawdowns. The method's small-cap exposure may explain some outperformance. The IBD 50 provides weekly lists of stocks meeting CANSLIM criteria. The Innovator IBD 50 ETF offers exposure to the strategy. CANSLIM focuses on stocks with strong fundamentals, positive earnings, growth, institutional sponsorship, and uptrends. It is primarily for long-term investing. Recent performance has underperformed the S&P 500. The method is difficult to backtest due to requiring both fundamental and technical data.

A hockey player discusses his team's recent win, crediting Rucchin's two goals and Jiggy's strong performance. He acknowledges he wasn't playing his best in previous finals but felt good contributing offensively. He believes his team controlled the game despite the opponent gaining some momentum, and emphasizes maintaining consistent preparation and routine for success. He leads by example rather than speaking much. He addresses a past hit from Scott, noting it was a patient play typical of Scott's style, and says he'll continue making the same plays. He admits the first two games in New Jersey were poor performances where the team lacked energy, but expects better play at home. He doesn't believe road matchups significantly affect outcomes, citing overall strong road playoff performance. He recalls watching the Stanley Cup as a child and stresses staying focused on preparation. He notes defensive tightening is needed despite scoring three goals on the road. He describes recovering quickly from a hard stick hit after medical clearance, with minimal reaction from teammates during the loud game. He avoids using "hate" to describe the rivalry, calling it intense competition with natural animosity in long playoff series. He fondly remembers a past comeback win with Rucchin's goal but considers it distant history.

Peter Crouch made a joke on Twitter about the height of the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge as they waved from hospital steps with their newborn third child. His wife Abbey Clancy responded with a brutal reply that amused many users. Crystal Palace football club also tweeted humorously about the royal birth, pretending the word "son" in a news headline was the baby's name.

Former NBA player and coach Mark Jackson and former NBA coach Jeff Van Gundy express concern about the Golden State Warriors' tendency to fall behind early in games before mounting dramatic comebacks. The Warriors led the NBA in third quarter scoring this season and overcame significant deficits against the Houston Rockets in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals, but failed to complete comebacks in Games 2, 4, and 5. Both analysts warn that relying on this pattern is risky, as eventually the team will be unable to recover.

Savvy investors are purchasing closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges at discounts to their NAVs. These schemes have lock-in periods of 3-5 years, forcing original investors to sell on exchanges where modest liquidity creates discounts. Buyers benefit as redemption occurs at full NAV at maturity. Examples include Reliance Close Ended Mutual Fund Series A trading at 10% discount and HDFC Equity Opportunities Funds at 6% discounts. Discount size depends on time to maturity and tax considerations, with shorter periods typically showing higher discounts. Experts recommend targeting schemes with over Rs 250 crore in assets under management for better trading activity.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous flying car prototype planned for testing by 2017 and short-haul availability by 2021. The helicopter-style vehicle aims to reduce urban road congestion and infrastructure costs while using clean technology. Other companies pursuing flying cars include Uber (VTOL aircraft network), Urban Aeronautics (Cormorant passenger drone), and AeroMobil (land-air vehicle). Tech investors such as Skype's co-founder and Google's Larry Page have also funded flying car startups.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben'Ary claims the Department of Justice leadership prioritized punishing perceived Trump enemies over public safety. Ben'Ary was terminated during a terrorism prosecution involving the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly falsely suggested on social media that he was an ally of former Biden administration official Lisa Monaco. The letter warned that removing career officials from U.S. attorney's offices and the FBI was making America less safe. Ben'Ary's firing came after interim U.S. Attorney Halligan replaced his predecessor, who had been pressured by Trump to indict former FBI director James Comey.

This patent application describes a light emitting diode (LED) device and its manufacturing method. The device includes a thin film transistor substrate with first and second diode electrodes, a passivation pattern between them, micro LEDs on the passivation pattern, and bridge patterns connecting the electrodes to the micro LEDs. Each micro LED has a cylindrical shape with a light emitting material surrounded by a protective layer, where sidewalls of the micro LEDs and passivation pattern form the same plane to create reliable electrical connections. The manufacturing method uses a single mask process with two etching steps—first a longer, more anisotropic etch, then a shorter, more isotropic etch with oxygen-containing gas—to align the micro LED sidewalls with the passivation pattern sidewalls, minimizing steps that could break bridge patterns and improving connection reliability.

MLB wild-card series coverage includes three winner-takes-all Game 3s, only the second time in baseball history. The Tigers left a franchise playoff-record 15 runners on base in Game 2 and are 3-for-38 with runners in scoring position over three potential elimination games. The Padres-Cubs matchup will feature Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon on short hooks, with bullpen depth likely deciding the outcome. The Yankees forced Game 3 against the Red Sox with a narrow win; Boston used six relievers in Game 2 after pulling starter Brayan Bello early, leaving their bullpen potentially overtaxed. Other news includes Brian Snitker not returning as Braves manager in 2026, Rockies GM Bill Schmidt dismissed after a 119-loss season, and Shohei Ohtani scheduled to start Game 1 of the NLDS for the Dodgers.

Aspen, Colorado is replacing its annual Fourth of July fireworks display with a 15-minute drone show featuring 50 drones due to wildfire risks from drought conditions. The show, organized by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association, will take place at Wagner Park starting at 21:15 local time. Colorado fire authorities have imposed strict fire restrictions across the state. The decision follows increased annual fire dangers, with officials seeking alternatives to end celebrations safely. The concept may have been inspired by a 2018 Winter Olympics drone show in Pyeongchang, though that event used 1,218 drones and was pre-recorded due to weather concerns.

The US national debt surpassed $21 trillion, growing by $73 billion in one day and $215 billion in February 2018. Over six months, debt increased by over $1 trillion despite no economic crisis. Debt growth (6%) significantly outpaced GDP growth (2.5% real, 4.4% with inflation), with debt expanding 36% faster than the economy proportionally. Over ten years, debt grew 123% (from $9.4 trillion to $21 trillion) while the economy grew only 36%. The author dismisses claims that debt "doesn't matter" because it's owed domestically, noting defaulting on Social Security, banks, or the Federal Reserve would cause catastrophic financial consequences.

Jio announced cashback and data offers for Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo under the Jio Galaxy Club, valid until September 30. Both phones offer Rs 2,750 instant cashback via 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each. Galaxy J2 2018 buyers (priced at Rs 8,190) get 100GB additional data through ten 10GB vouchers on Rs 198/299 plans, effectively reducing cost to Rs 5,440. Galaxy J7 Duo buyers (priced at Rs 16,990) receive double data on Rs 198/299 plans—4GB/day instead of 2GB, and 6GB/day instead of 3GB. The Galaxy J2 2018 features a 5-inch qHD display, Snapdragon 425 processor, 2GB RAM, 8MP/5MP cameras, and 2600mAh battery. The Galaxy J7 Duo has a 5.5-inch HD display, Exynos 7 processor, 4GB RAM, 13MP/5MP cameras, and 3000mAh battery.

New Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rules could force many payday lenders out of business by requiring them to verify borrowers' ability to repay within 30 days and limiting unauthorized account debits. The rules face Republican opposition in Congress. Payday loans typically carry APRs near 400%, and over 80% are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. The $39 billion industry serves 30-40 million customers annually; the CFPB estimates loan volume could drop by half. The rules take effect in 2019 but may be rolled back. Meanwhile, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency lifted restrictions on banks making small-dollar loans. A Pew poll found 70% of Americans favor more payday lender regulation.

This study identifies predictive biomarkers for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response in sarcomas by analyzing transcriptomic profiles from 67 patients across three clinical trials. Using RNA sequencing-based immune cell quantification, tumors were classified into "immune-hot" and "immune-cold" clusters. Immune-hot tumors showed significantly higher objective response rates (30% vs. 8.1%) and longer progression-free survival (3.65 vs. 1.7 months) compared to immune-cold tumors. Lasso regression models identified transposable element (TE) expression and the epigenetic regulator IKZF1 as predictive features of immune type. Six TE subfamilies (MER57F, MER45A, Tigger17a, MER61F, LTR104_Mam, HERVL74.int) and IKZF1 were significantly elevated in immune-hot tumors. Both TE score and IKZF1 expression correlated with immune pathway activation (cGAS-STING, type I/II interferon, antigen presentation) and prolonged progression-free survival. Conditional independence analysis suggested IKZF1 regulates TE expression, which determines immune type. These findings were validated in an independent cohort of 190 TCGA sarcoma samples, where high TE score and IKZF1 expression associated with improved overall survival. The study proposes TE score and IKZF1 as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI response in sarcomas.

A writing program at Seattle Children's helps parents of seriously ill children express their emotions through journaling. Meagan Holt, whose 3-year-old daughter Madeline has Zellweger Syndrome, uses the program to process her fears about her daughter's impending death. The Pediatric Advanced Care Team offers the sessions, which participants describe as empowering and calming. The program operates on donations.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 27, 2022, announcing its third quarter 2022 financial results. The filing includes two exhibits: a press release with the financial results announcement and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath store after 33 years due to lack of free parking, increased business rates, and persistent anti-social behaviour. Managing director Mike Semmens cited council street works that disrupted business, a bench placed outside the store near an off-licence that attracted drinking and disorder, and staff having to deal with fights, vandalism, and biohazards. Other local retailers acknowledged anti-social behaviour issues, particularly in summer. Neath Council defended its street improvements and noted the bench was removed a year ago, while stating they work with police to tackle anti-social behaviour. Regarding parking, Semmens criticized limited free options, while the council highlighted a new multi-storey car park with free parking after 3pm. On business rates, Semmens noted they rose substantially, though the Welsh Government stated relief schemes support nearly 15,000 small businesses. The company continues operating elsewhere and may seek another Neath site.

This study explores physics teachers' attitudes toward science education research (SSSE), addressing a research gap regarding experienced teachers' perspectives. Using a two-step mixed-methods approach—interviews with 13 teachers followed by a survey of 174 teachers—the study identifies four factors of science scepticism: relevance for individual teachers, feasibility of findings, general relevance for practice, and cooperation between research and practice. Latent profile analysis revealed four teacher profiles: The Sceptical Ones (14%), who reject research value entirely; The Uncertain Ones (27%), with neutral stances; The Undersupplied Ones (41%), who value research but criticize its applicability and cooperation; and The Research Advocates (18%), who support research but still question cooperation. Only frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership, with other professional variables (teaching experience, education type, school type, doctoral degree) showing no significant association. The study suggests that scepticism toward research-practice cooperation is widespread across all profiles, indicating a need for improved communication between researchers and practitioners and greater integration of research in teacher education.

The Baltimore Ravens traded pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman. Oweh, 26, had no sacks in five games this season after recording 10 last year, with his playing time dropping to 45% of defensive snaps. The Ravens free up approximately $8 million in cap space and address their struggling pass defense, which ranks 31st in the NFL. They also signed safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson to the practice squad. The Chargers gain a young edge rusher with the second-highest pressure rate on their team, addressing a bigger need than safety, where Derwin James Jr. has moved to nickel and veteran Tony Adams will likely replace Gilman as starting deep safety. The Ravens (1-4) have allowed the most points in the NFL at 35.4 per game.

African countries have been urged to use modern technology to address tax non-compliance. Secretary to the Treasury Ben Botolo made this call at the 18th Forum for Value Added Tax Administrators in Africa (VADA) in Lilongwe, Malawi. He emphasized that electronic fiscal devices are critical for optimizing tax revenue collection and noted that most African countries remain cash economies, making tax collection difficult. Botolo stated Malawi has made progress in electronic tax monitoring and that a Tax Administration Act is forthcoming. VADA Chairperson Henry Saka, also Uganda's Commissioner for Domestic Taxes, stressed the need to formalize regulatory strategies for business tax compliance. VADA provides technical support to 12 non-member countries; its 10 members include Malawi, Zambia, Uganda, Tanzania, and Rwanda. The forum enables member countries to share challenges and propose interventions for improving domestic revenue mobilization.

This MIT lecture reviews propagators in free scalar field theory, presenting two interpretations: as transition amplitudes between spacetime points and as correlation functions. The instructor explains retarded, advanced, and Feynman (time-ordered) Green's functions, detailing how contour integration around poles in the complex omega plane yields each type, with the epsilon prescription providing a convenient alternative to explicit contour deformation. The lecture notes that in free theory, n-point vacuum correlation functions factorize into products of two-point functions, and introduces composite operators and their associated singularities requiring renormalization.

The discussion then transitions to interacting theories, specifically adding a phi^4 term to the Lagrangian, noting that nonlinear terms produce interactions but that exact solutions become impossible. The S-matrix is introduced as the fundamental observable for scattering experiments, defined as the evolution operator between asymptotic free states at t = ±∞. Key properties include unitarity, momentum conservation (extracted via delta function), and symmetry constraints. The LSZ theorem is stated without proof, connecting scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting vacuum. The lecture concludes with a preview of the path integral approach for treating interactions perturbatively.

The President clarifies that his previous message to the Senate was not intended to deny Congress's constitutional power to legislate regarding the custody, safe-keeping, and disposition of public money and property. He admits without reserve the Legislature's authority to prescribe deposit locations and regulations for public property, and disclaims any Executive right to possess, dispose of, or interfere with public property except as authorized by law. He also disclaims authority to supervise persons entrusted with such property unless they are officers whose appointment falls under presidential responsibility. He requests this communication be entered with his original message on the Senate journals to prevent future misconstruction of his views.

The speaker discusses a hockey team's preparation for upcoming games, noting Philadelphia's better performance away from home in previous series. He emphasizes the need for players to stay focused despite home crowd distractions, citing a past loss at home. Several players have prior experience in similar situations. The speaker addresses goaltending, praising Mike's resilience and confidence after being pulled from a game, and his past performances against notable goalies like Grant Fuhr and Patrick Roy. He analyzes a specific play where a player made the right decision despite not scoring. The team has had success playing away from Detroit. Penalties and maintaining composure are concerns, with the team doing well not retaliating. The speaker reflects on past playoff lessons about one-goal games and trades involving a player who struggled in Hartford. Ice conditions should be manageable, and the team stays away the night before games. Defensive pairings, particularly Fetisov-Konstantinov and Murphy-Lidstrom, have worked well. He compares the current team to past versions that struggled against the Devils' defensive play, noting differences in scoring ability and experience. Kirk Maltby's move to left wing due to a surplus of right wingers is discussed, highlighting his defensive commitment and recent scoring success.

This application describes a sidelink positioning method and apparatus for communication systems. Existing positioning technologies based on network device-to-terminal device reference signal measurement require core network control and suffer from increasing positioning errors as distance increases. The proposed solution enables terminal devices to determine positions using sidelink signals for relative or absolute positioning, improving accuracy and reducing latency by avoiding core network transmission of measurement values.

The method involves: a first terminal device receives sidelink positioning configuration from a network device, sends a first sidelink positioning reference signal to a second terminal device, and determines its position based on measurement values and the second terminal device's position. The second terminal device measures the reference signal to obtain values including Rx-Tx time difference and angle of arrival. Configurations include time-frequency resources, sequence information, and reporting methods for Uu and PC5 interfaces. The solution supports terminals that do not sidelink reference signal measurement by having another terminal perform measurements.

The passage describes multiple views of two embodiments of an analytical instrument design, including perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views for each embodiment. Broken line portions are not part of the claimed design.

Retired lawyer Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his law schoolbooks from over 50 years ago, weighing sentimental attachment against practical uselessness. He recalls specific cases from his textbooks—including Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball, Hadley v. Baxendale, and a contract case involving a prostitute's carriage—before discarding most volumes, including property law texts on "fee simple" and "fee tail" ownership. He regrets learning one book now sells for over $1,000, but kept his 5-inch-thick tax law volume to use as a standing desk.

In June 2014, Hertz Global Holdings announced it would restate three years of financial results due to widespread accounting problems, causing its stock to drop 9%. The case examines Hertz's history from its 1918 founding through its 2006 IPO, its operations including the 2012 Dollar Thrifty acquisition, and its 2013 performance with record revenue and EBITDA. The analysis focuses on depreciation accounting for Hertz's rental fleet, which comprised over 50% of total assets. Hertz used straight-line depreciation based on estimated holding periods and residual values, with rates reviewed quarterly. The company purchased program cars with manufacturer repurchase guarantees and non-program cars subject to residual price risk. Analyst Abby Devins examined Hertz's revenue earning equipment balances and depreciation expenses from 2006-2013, comparing them to competitor Avis Budget Group, to assess whether depreciation issues contributed to Hertz's accounting restatement.

AI may augment human cognition, learning, and creativity, but risks include over-reliance on AI systems and limited internalization of learned skills. Mitigation involves selective task delegation, encouraging critical thinking, and redesigning education toward personalized, interactive assessment. AI also challenges traditional social structures built on knowledge scarcity and the middle class, potentially blurring job boundaries and enabling the gig economy through algorithmic management. This requires institutional reforms for labor protections. AI-driven global collaboration may shift toward dynamic, network-based partnerships. In social science research, LLMs offer synthetic data generation and automated analysis but raise concerns about bias, validity, and ethical use. Regulatory frameworks must balance innovation with risk mitigation through multi-stakeholder collaboration, forward-looking policies, and combined top-down and bottom-up governance approaches.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 25, 2018, announcing its third quarter 2018 financial results. The filing includes two exhibits: a press release with the financial results announcement and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This technical document describes the TLV32xx comparator family specifications and application guidelines. Unused inputs should not be tied together but connected to voltages within the input range with minimum 50mV differential. The family features 1.8mV internal hysteresis (VHYST) to reduce noise sensitivity, with output options including push-pull (TLV321x) and open-drain (TLV322x). Push-pull outputs can source and sink current but must never be shorted to opposite supply rails or connected to other outputs. Open-drain outputs allow logic level translation and OR'ing with pull-up resistors of 100µA–1mA recommended. ESD protection limits input voltages to 0.2V beyond rails, requiring series resistors for low-impedance sources. Power-on reset holds outputs low for up to 32µs after crossing 1.65V threshold. External hysteresis can be added through positive feedback networks for inverting (three-resistor) or non-inverting (two-resistor with reference) configurations. Applications include low-side current sensing with critical requirements for bypass capacitors, proper PCB layout, and minimized noise coupling between inputs and outputs.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike called for a US Visa Office in Port Harcourt during a visit by US Ambassador William Symington. Wike criticized the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) as a "fund raising commission for politicians," alleging it funded APC rerun elections in Rivers State and that its Managing Director was amassing wealth to contest the Akwa Ibom governorship election. He cited NDDC's failure to act on 2016 project proposals and its reneging on a Mother and Child Hospital agreement despite the state's N800 million counterpart payment. Wike also called for Ogoni land cleanup, noting the flag-off was politically motivated, and expressed interest in US partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization. The ambassador stated his focus was interacting with state residents.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on March 19, 2020, disclosing under Item 7.01 that it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Coach Vigneault discusses his team's recent loss, noting they need to bring their "A game" against a strong, structured opponent with skill, speed, and physicality. He mentions reviewing game footage, potential lineup adjustments including defenseman Johnny, and emphasizes compete level and execution. He praises goaltender Hank's performance, Rick's strong playoff play, and Ryan McDonagh's improving stamina and defensive excellence. Vigneault acknowledges the challenge ahead, stating the team must play to its strengths, particularly speed, to win.

A professor discusses nuclear war risks, comparing climate change's near-certain probability with nuclear war's low daily but catastrophic cumulative risk. He examines pathways to nuclear war: accidental US-Russia launch due to early warning malfunctions or cyber attacks, and India-Pakistan escalation from conventional conflict. The professor critiques nuclear deterrence theory, noting weapons failed to coerce Soviet behavior during the Cold War, and highlights risks from aggressive deployment postures like Pakistan's delegation to field commanders. He discusses the Non-Proliferation Treaty's tension between nonproliferation and disarmament obligations under Article VI, predicting conflict at upcoming reviews. Regarding Iran, he supports continuing interim agreements with rigorous inspections rather than demanding zero centrifuges. On abolition, he argues it's desirable but unlikely, emphasizing risk minimization over elimination. He criticizes Obama's mixed record: inspiring hopes but modernizing weapons, maintaining hair-trigger alerts, and failing to engage North Korea. He finds limited optimism in the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty monitoring system and arms control organizations, concluding the present situation remains stable only "with luck."

The passage advocates for creating a Secretary of Commerce Cabinet position to address growing corporate and labor issues. It supports a reciprocity treaty with Cuba, citing strategic and moral reasons, and notes a pending trade convention with Great Britain regarding Newfoundland. The text praises arbitration over warfare, highlighting the U.S. and Mexico as first users of The Hague Court. It mentions Hawaiian fire claims and emphasizes building an isthmian canal at Panama as a continuing national policy transcending administrations.

CPRE Bedfordshire has challenged Central Bedfordshire Council's claim that it needs 44,000-55,000 new homes over 20 years, stating that 60% would be for people moving into the area rather than current residents. A 2017 assessment identified an Objectively Assessed Need of 32,000 dwellings, with only 41% for existing residents. The council added 7,400 homes for Luton residents plus a 20% contingency. CPRE argues this over-development is unsustainable given existing infrastructure strain. CBC defends its position, stating it must follow government requirements to plan for predicted population growth, including migration trends, using a standard formula.

President Andrew Johnson transmits to the House of Representatives additional correspondence with General U.S. Grant regarding Grant's resignation as Secretary of War ad interim. The February 10, 1868 letter from Johnson accuses Grant of deception and insubordination, charging that Grant secretly intended to restore Edwin Stanton to office from the beginning and misled the President about his willingness to hold the position through judicial proceedings. Johnson includes statements from five Cabinet members—Gideon Welles, Hugh McCulloch, Alexander Randall, Orville Browning, and William Seward—who corroborate his account of their January 14, 1868 conversation. Grant's February 11 response denies insubordination, claiming he only sought clarification on interpreting presidential authorization for War Department orders, and notes that other cabinet secretaries continued recognizing Stanton's authority.

Grief specialists Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder offer strategies for navigating holiday grief: limit events, have exit plans, express emotions, share memories, practice self-care, create new traditions while keeping old ones. Travnicek, who lost two brothers to suicide, notes the Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group has operated for 20 years, currently meeting twice monthly at Smith Leroy Funeral Home starting January, 7-8:30 p.m.; registration at 519-537-3611. Additional programs include "Understanding Your Grief" beginning April 4 in Woodstock, and "Healing Journey Through Grief" February 1-March 22 in Ingersoll; registration at 519-485-1802.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 20, 2016, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2016. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer. The information is furnished but not deemed "filed" under the Securities Exchange Act.

Medical students face significant stressors including workload, sleep deprivation, and financial pressures, placing them at higher risk for psychological distress and burnout than peers in other disciplines. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these issues. This qualitative study examined 37 Year 4 medical students at Mohammed Bin Rashid University in Dubai, UAE, regarding their perceptions of a 6-hour curriculum-based resilience course grounded in constructivism experiential learning theory. Analysis of reflective essays revealed three themes: Awareness (understanding resilience concepts), Application (practical implementation through mindfulness, meditation, and self-care activities), and Appraisal (valuing the course for improving wellbeing, academic performance, and clinical skills). Students identified challenges including time constraints, skepticism about efficacy, and difficulty changing habits. The study supports integrating resilience training into medical curricula using experiential, self-directed learning approaches to foster sustainable mental health skills among future healthcare professionals.

North Carolina football coach Bill Belichick will not make structural changes despite the team's struggles, following a 38-10 loss to Clemson where UNC trailed 28-3 after the first quarter. The Tar Heels fell to 0-3 against Power 4 opponents, having been outscored 120-33 in those games. Belichick attributed the defeat to execution failures and accepted responsibility for coaching lapses, stating the team needs to "keep doing what we're doing but do them better." The loss came days after GM Mike Lombardi's letter to donors called this a "rebuilding" year due to talent shortages from past recruiting exits. Belichick downplayed the rebuild label but acknowledged to recruits that the program is "building." Some players, including receiver Shipp, rejected the rebuild narrative, emphasizing their focus on winning. Belichick said playing time will be based on performance, not age or long-term vision, as UNC prepares to face Cal.

This article describes an undergraduate course, "All Means All: Inclusive Teaching for Students with Disabilities," designed to integrate advocacy throughout special education teacher preparation. Rather than treating advocacy as a standalone lesson, the course weaves it through content, learning goals, and assignments. Key components include scaffolded reflection assignments, a jigsaw activity on special education law cases, an in-class debate on inclusive education, and a final TED Talk-style presentation with accompanying paper. The course emphasizes skills like argumentative writing, critical analysis, and persuasive communication. The authors argue that advocacy preparation is essential for special educators to challenge systemic inequities and influence policy, and recommend incorporating similar interactive, practice-based strategies across all special education coursework.

Community-based organizations and out-of-school-time programs—such as summer camps, mentoring programs, sports leagues, and after-school clubs—represent an untapped opportunity to expand youth mental health support. These spaces already foster trusted relationships and belonging among young people. With proper investment in training, resources, and partnerships, staff at these organizations can recognize signs of distress, respond appropriately, and refer youth to professional care when needed. Research indicates young people are increasingly open about mental health and want support in familiar community settings. However, many youth-serving staff currently lack adequate training and infrastructure to address mental health needs sustainably. Funders can help by supporting strategic planning, staff training, partnerships with mental health providers, and frontline worker well-being. Community-based organizations can complement school-based efforts to build a more cohesive mental health safety net for young people.

The lecture discusses regulating tech giants and platform economics, focusing on two-sided markets where platforms connect consumers with merchants/apps. The speaker critiques the Chicago School view that platforms naturally avoid discrimination because they benefit from rich ecosystems, identifying three flaws: platforms often cannot raise consumer prices due to zero lower bounds (optimal prices are negative but constrained to zero), contestability concerns where favoring in-house apps may deter future competition, and dual zero lower bounds creating supranormal profits. The Digital Markets Act addresses contestability and fairness through obligations like data portability and interoperability, though implementation challenges remain. The speaker analyzes optimal access pricing, showing that access charges set too low invite non-price foreclosure while charges too high squeeze third-party apps, with the theoretically optimal access charge equal to ancillary benefits (b).

Avoyelles Parish is projected to spend $8,123 per student in 2017-18, ranking second-lowest among Louisiana's 69 school districts. Its local contribution of $2,102 per student ranks 68th. The state average is $9,015 per student, down from $10,888 in 2015. Louisiana reduced education spending by 5.1% from 2008-2017, less than Florida's 26% cut. The Minimum Foundation Program allocates state funds using a formula that provides more to poorer districts, starting with a $3,961 base per student and adjusting for local tax capacity, special populations, and other factors. Most districts rely more heavily on state than local funds. The state Senate has requested a study to determine actual education costs and identify new funding mechanisms, due February 1, 2018.

President Ford's EO 11905 (February 1976) replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group (OAG) for covert action oversight, banned political assassinations, and prohibited domestic intelligence involvement. President Carter retained this structure but replaced the OAG with the NSC's Special Coordination Committee (SCC) in EO 11985 (May 1977), later formalized in EO 12036 (January 1978), which made the Attorney General and OMB Director full members. Carter also created the Special Activities Working Group (SAWG) as a lower-level review body, though it fell out of use by late 1979, replaced by an interagency group chaired by David Aaron. The Carter administration introduced "worldwide" or "generic" covert operations findings for lower-risk activities, with "Perspectives" documents providing specific tasking guidance drafted by CIA and cleared by State Department.

A Pittsburgh Steelers fan blog post previews Super Bowl LII between the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles, includes five prediction questions about the game and NFL offseason, and provides results from previous weekly prediction contests with a current leaderboard topped by Alan Tman.

This MIT lecture on Real Analysis (18.100A) covers foundational concepts for rigorous mathematical proofs. The course aims to develop proof-writing skills through analyzing real numbers, functions, and limits. The lecture introduces set theory notation and definitions including sets, elements, subsets, unions, intersections, set differences, complements, and disjoint sets. Key number systems are reviewed: natural numbers, integers, rationals, and reals, with the latter's rigorous definition being a course goal. DeMorgan's Laws are stated and the first law is proved as an example of rigorous proof structure. The well-ordering property of natural numbers is introduced as an axiom, used to prove the principle of mathematical induction. Induction is then applied to prove two theorems: a geometric series formula and Bernoulli's inequality.

1. Democrats want independent investigation of Trump-Russia ties after Flynn's exit; GOP rejects this.

New computer modeling reveals Uranus emits about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, solving the decades-old mystery of why the planet appeared to lack internal heat. The finding, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, indicates Uranus does generate some warmth, though far less than Neptune. Researchers developed an advanced model incorporating decades of atmospheric data to determine the planet's full energy budget. The discovery provides insights into Uranus' violent past and helps scientists understand similar-sized exoplanets.

Oclaro Inc (NASDAQ:OCLR) shares traded down 0.99% with a closing price of $9.04. Wall Street analysts project a 52-week price target of $9.27 based on 13 opinions, with a high target of $11.25 and low of $6.50. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 2.38 from 13 analysts, with 2 Buy, 3 Outperform, and 9 Hold ratings. The ATR-14 is 0.29, weekly volatility is 2.50%, and monthly volatility is 3.07%. The RSI is 55.48. The company has a market capitalization of $1.53 billion with 169.6 million outstanding shares, and average trading volume of 5.58 million shares.

This study developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict pulmonary restriction from spirometry data, comparing their performance to the current ERS/ATS guideline of using forced vital capacity lower limit of normal (FVC LLN) to exclude restriction. The random forest model achieved 88.3% negative predictive value (NPV) versus 72.7% for FVC LLN in the validation dataset. The ML models demonstrated improved equity, with the NPV ratio between non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White patients increasing from 62.2% (FVC LLN) to 82.1% (random forest). While the ML models were more accurate and equitable, they excluded restriction from fewer tests (56.7% vs 78.4%), potentially increasing the need for static lung volume measurements. The study used PFT data from two academic health systems, employed race-neutral reference equations, and made all code and models publicly available.

G. M. Cox sued District Judge George W. Burnham, claiming he lacked jurisdiction to grant a liquor permit to pharmacist P. H. Bell because the hearing occurred at a term subsequent to the one where the application was filed. The court rejected this argument, holding that Code section 2389's requirement that applications be tried at the first term "if the business of the court shall allow" is discretionary, not mandatory. An adjournment does not automatically dismiss such applications; they continue to the next term under general practice rules. The court presumed valid reasons existed for continuing the April 1901 term, and found the September 1902 hearing regular and non-evasive. Proceedings dismissed.

Tesla, Inc. filed its 2018 annual report (Form 10-K) with the SEC, reporting as a large accelerated filer with 172.7 million shares outstanding as of February 12, 2019. The company operates as a vertically integrated sustainable energy company designing, developing, manufacturing and selling high-performance fully electric vehicles (Model S, Model X, Model 3) and energy generation/storage systems. Tesla sells vehicles through company-owned stores and galleries, maintains service centers and Mobile Service technicians, and operates Supercharger and Destination Charging networks. The company manufactures vehicles in Fremont, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and at Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada, with Gigafactory Shanghai under construction. Energy storage products (Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2) and solar energy systems are manufactured at Gigafactory 1 and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York. Tesla faces risks including production ramp delays, supply chain constraints, competition, dependence on single-source suppliers (particularly Panasonic for battery cells), and the need to achieve cost reductions to reach profitability targets. The company had 48,817 full-time employees as of December 31, 2018.

Asian stocks were unstable on Wednesday and the Chinese yuan neared 11-month lows due to concerns over a potential Sino-U.S. trade war ahead of Friday's U.S. tariff deadline. MSCI's Asia-Pacific index rose 0.1% after hitting a nine-month low, while Japan's Nikkei fell 0.5%. Wall Street declined Tuesday with the S&P 500 down 0.49% and Nasdaq dropping 0.86%, pressured by technology shares. Facebook fell 2.3% amid a broadened federal probe, Tesla dropped 7.2% on production concerns, and Micron Technology fell 5.5% after a Chinese sales injunction against rival United Microelectronics. Japanese chip-related shares also declined. Investors fear $34 billion in U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods will take effect July 6, with matching Chinese retaliation. The yuan traded at 6.6715 per dollar, recovering slightly from Tuesday's 11-month low after China's central bank pledged stability. The Mexican peso surged 2.6% on reassuring comments from its newly elected president. Major currencies were steady amid trade worries, with the euro at $1.1658 and dollar at 110.56 yen. Oil prices rose on lower U.S. stockpiles data, with U.S. crude at $74.62 per barrel, while copper hit nine-month lows on growth concerns.

The Dugan Stock Scoring System evaluates Dividend Champions, Contenders, and Challengers (CCC) companies using metrics across four categories: Risk, Value, Past Performance, and Future Performance Expectations. For January 2017, the author applied ten filters to David Fish's "All CCC" list of 684 companies, including being in the top-scoring half (342 companies), minimum 2.25% yield, minimum $5B market cap, maximum 70% relative Graham number and payout ratio, minimum 5% recent dividend increase and estimated EPS growth, maximum 1.0 debt/equity ratio, and minimum Dugan Score of 50. A small bonus or penalty is applied based on broker sector weighting recommendations. These filters yielded 21 companies. The author holds positions in PRU, AIZ, MGA, BBY, HBAN, DOW, ADM, CSCO, and RAI.

The Care Quality Commission rated East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust as Requires Improvement overall, though Outstanding for caring. The March inspection found progress in safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act understanding and incident reporting, but ongoing failures to meet national response standards, low staff morale, and disengagement between frontline staff and senior management. The trust must improve emergency response times, ensure consistent procedures, review risk registers, and better support staff. Chief Executive Robert Morton acknowledged challenges, citing the trust's large geographic area and mobile workforce, while noting £11.5 million in additional funding for improvements.

Coach DeBoer discusses his team's situation, emphasizing they don't want to go down in the series but have been in similar spots before. He states they won't panic or make lineup changes just for the sake of it, despite having depth available. He notes they've had quality scoring chances that haven't gone in, crediting the opposing goaltender. DeBoer expresses confidence from past experiences overcoming similar frustrations, mentions travel and time change adjustments for the finals, and praises the officiating. He identifies several forwards on the verge of breaking out and acknowledges the need to score more than one goal. He questions a momentum-changing officiating call where the whistle didn't blow despite lost sight of the puck. DeBoer says he's not disappointed in his team's effort, noting they battled to the final buzzer, and emphasizes they need to handle their frustration correctly and find ways to score against a strong opposing goaltender.

Temple Grandin will present "Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior" at a breakfast event from 7-9 a.m. on Friday, Feb. 23 at the Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff. The event is sponsored by Shasta College Ag Leadership Club and UC Cooperative Extension. Grandin, a Colorado State University professor, is known for her work on animal behavior and livestock handling, including research on flight zone principles and cattle temperament. She has been featured in major media and authored several books, including "Animals in Translation." Breakfast costs $15. Contact Josh Davy at 527-3101 or jdavy@ucdavis.edu for information.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized free trade agreement to replace their 1997 agreement. The new Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement was signed by Canadian International Trade Minister Francois-Phillippe Champagne and Israeli Economy Minister Eli Cohen in Montreal. Key changes include eliminating duties on thousands of additional products and adding chapters on labor, environment, trade and gender, small businesses, and corporate social responsibility. Canada's top exports to Israel include industrial machinery and aircraft parts, while industrial machinery is Israel's top export to Canada. The agreement requires ratification by both parliaments and aims to double bilateral trade.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture enables real-time ray tracing in single-GPU systems through dedicated RT Cores, combined with NVIDIA RTX software and filtering algorithms. Microsoft simultaneously announced DirectML for AI and DirectX Raytracing (DXR) APIs in early 2018, allowing developers to deploy real-time AI and ray tracing in games. Turing also features advanced shading improvements and inherits Volta architecture enhancements to the CUDA platform, including independent thread scheduling and hardware-accelerated Multi Process Service. The flagship TU102 GPU powers the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000. Turing combines programmable shading, real-time ray tracing, and AI algorithms.

This meta-analysis of 13 studies from eight countries (2015-2024) found that AI-related technologies have a large positive effect on educational outcomes (effect size = 0.86, 95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001). Chatbots and generative AI showed the strongest effect (1.02), followed by online learning and virtual reality (0.79), and learning management systems with AI platforms (0.62). The study employed PRISMA guidelines and introduced novel algorithmic approaches including Naive Bayes-based algorithms, TF-IDF variants, BERT-based search algorithms, and a weighted hybrid model combining random and fixed effects (effect size = 0.88). Substantial heterogeneity (I² 54.03%-93.23%) and publication bias were observed across studies. The findings support implementing AI technologies in education, particularly chatbots and generative AI, while accounting for specific educational contexts and student needs.

Diet plays a crucial role in fighting infections and supporting immune function. Key food groups include: fruits and vegetables, which provide essential vitamins (A and C), minerals, and fiber that support beneficial gut bacteria and immune regulation; protein, necessary for immune cell production, energy, and tissue repair; herbs and spices like ginger and turmeric, which contain anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial compounds; green tea, rich in immune-boosting polyphenols; probiotics from fermented foods, which regulate gut health and nutrient absorption; and nuts and seeds, which supply minerals, fatty acids, and vitamin E for cell repair. Poor nutritional choices can slow recovery and worsen symptoms.

A Danish study found that children of older mothers had fewer behavioral, social, and emotional difficulties at ages seven and 11, though differences disappeared by age 15. Researchers attributed this to older mothers' "psychological maturity," resulting in less scolding and discipline, plus greater emotional stability and positive attitudes. The study used 4,741 mothers from the Danish Longitudinal Survey of Children. Despite psychosocial benefits, the lead researcher noted health risks of later pregnancy, including miscarriage, premature birth, and deformities.

A coach discusses his team's recent loss, noting poor passing and turnovers in the first half, ineffective power play execution, and overanxious forechecking. He mentions Fredrik underwent X-rays with results expected by day's end. The coach defends keeping certain forward lines together despite the loss, citing past playoff success. He addresses ice time imbalances affecting key players like Yzerman, Fedorov, and Shanahan due to special teams duties, and plans adjustments to create more balanced minutes. He emphasizes the need to get pucks deeper in the offensive zone and improve neutral zone entries for the next game, while acknowledging each game presents unique circumstances rather than following historical patterns.
Scientists created functional human egg cells from skin cells by fusing them with empty eggs and inducing meiosis, a step toward helping infertile people have children.

Niu Technologies experienced significant stock gains in 2025 driven by strong recent growth, but future growth is uncertain and may not sustain current valuations. The author maintains a neutral hold rating due to risks that expected growth may not materialize as priced into the stock. The company manufactures urban mobility solutions including electric bicycles and scooters. The author holds no positions in the company and received no compensation beyond Seeking Alpha.

This patent application describes CAR T cell therapies with enhanced efficacy through disruption of methylcytosine dioxygenase genes (Tet1, Tet2, Tet3). The invention provides engineered immune effector cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors where Tet gene expression/function has been reduced or eliminated, leading to decreased 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels and enhanced CAR T cell proliferation and function. The CARs comprise antigen-binding domains (including CD19 and numerous other tumor antigens), transmembrane domains, and intracellular signaling domains with primary and costimulatory components. Tet inhibition is achieved through gene editing systems (CRISPR/Cas9, zinc finger nucleases, TALENs, meganucleases), siRNA/shRNA, small molecules, or dominant negative proteins. The application includes methods for manufacturing these cells, treatment protocols for various cancers, and vectors encoding both CAR and Tet inhibitor sequences. Experimental data demonstrate that Tet2 disruption promotes Tscm cell expansion and enhances CAR T cell function.

"Russian math," an after-school program emphasizing deep understanding and reasoning over memorization, is growing rapidly across the United States, with 22,000 students at the Russian School of Mathematics alone. Founded 20 years ago by Russian immigrants Inessa Rifkin and others, the program draws from Soviet teaching traditions and now attracts diverse American families seeking advanced math education for their children. While some parents worry about creating an "arms race" of enrichment programs and potential inequities, others see it as opening doors for their children's futures. The trend poses challenges for public schools, including wider performance gaps among students and increased pressure on families, though it may also expand the pool of students comfortable with advanced mathematics.

This Mendelian randomization study found that genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) is significantly associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism. Hypertension was identified as a mediator in the causal pathway between PAT and several cardiovascular diseases. The study suggests PAT may serve as a potential therapeutic target for cardiovascular diseases, particularly in people with obesity who have greater PAT accumulation. The research used 11 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instrumental variables derived from genome-wide association studies of 28,161 participants. Limitations include European-only population data, potential sample overlap, and small case numbers for some outcomes.

The SEC has requested information from Enron regarding its financial dealings with partnerships recently run by CFO Andrew Fastow, causing Enron's stock to fall over 20% to $20.65. The inquiry focuses on related-party transactions, particularly LJM Cayman LP and LJM2 Co-Investment LP, which Fastow managed until July 2001. Enron disclosed a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from terminating these partnerships, contributing to a $618 million third-quarter loss. The SEC's Fort Worth office initiated the voluntary document request, indicating an informal inquiry from the enforcement arm rather than a formal investigation. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay stated the company would cooperate fully. Analysts expressed concerns about Enron's complex operations and potential dilution of shareholders if credit ratings and stock prices fall further. Fastow reportedly earned millions in fees from the partnerships, and internal documents revealed conflict-of-interest concerns raised by Treasurer Jeffrey McMahon to then-President Jeffrey Skilling in 1999. Multiple news sources reported on the SEC inquiry and related developments, including a class action lawsuit and concerns about other off-balance sheet financing vehicles like Whitewing and Marlin trusts.

Indian troops killed three youth—Umar Majid Sheikh, Adil Malik, and Irfan Sheikh—during a siege and search operation in Awneera, Shopian district. Troops blasted a mosque and four houses. Protests followed, with civilians injured by pellet firing; twelve were hospitalized locally and two with bullet wounds sent to Srinagar. Locals reported troops ransacked houses in multiple areas. Two Indian soldiers were killed and several injured in an earlier attack on forces in Awneera; three troops were injured in a separate attack in Hajin, Bandipora. Train services between Badgam-Srinagar and Islamabad-Banihal remained suspended for a second day. Joint resistance leaders Syed Ali Gilani, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, and Muhammad Yasin Malik opposed any attempt to undermine Kashmir's disputed status or change its demographics, accusing India of crushing the liberation movement. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq stated BJP and RSS were challenging Article 35A to remove Jammu and Kashmir's special status. Civilian Imtiyaz Ahmad Mir, injured in a Dalgate explosion, died at Soura hospital.

A professor at OAU, Richard Akindele, was dismissed after being found guilty of soliciting sex from a student. The passage commends OAU for swift action and urges other universities to emulate this example, implement measures to protect female students from sexual harassment, and punish offending lecturers. It also advises female students against luring lecturers into sexual immorality.

Tom Evans, father of terminally ill toddler Alfie Evans, announced that his son has been breathing unassisted for nine hours after life support was withdrawn at Alder Hey Children's Hospital. Initially, doctors reportedly refused to provide oxygen, but re-intervened after Evans argued the situation was becoming "unlawful." Alfie was subsequently given oxygen and water. Evans stated doctors are "gobsmacked" by his son's unexpected endurance but believes he will need life support support soon. Alfie's mother, Kate James, posted on Facebook that her son "has already proved these doctors wrong."

This email from Ann Schmidt dated June 4, 2001, contains news clippings about Enron. Key stories include: Bush adviser Karl Rove owning $100,000-$250,000 in Enron stock while helping shape energy policy; Saudi Arabia signing $25 billion agreements with nine oil companies including Enron for natural gas development; a satirical San Francisco Chronicle column criticizing Enron as emblematic of corporate greed; and multiple reports on Enron's troubled $2.9 billion Dabhol power project in India, where lenders met in Singapore to discuss the dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills. Other coverage includes Nigerian President Obasanjo criticizing Enron's "poor performance" on a Lagos power project, and Enron Japan's Joseph Hirl commenting on Japan's electricity deregulation.

A speaker discusses preparing for a playoff road game, emphasizing setting their own tone, expecting a desperate opponent, and using the day off for rest and practice adjustments. They note the importance of awareness of crowd influence, winning faceoffs for possession, patient execution, and playing more aggressively on their toes. They praise a teammate's versatility and hard work, acknowledge everyone is banged up this time of year, and value past experience in staying focused game-by-game. They also credit a former player coach for his passion, offensive insight, and relatability.

Researchers developed a metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow using HostEL for human background depletion and AmpRE for single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation to address limitations of conventional pathogen detection methods. The workflow was validated using spiked plasma samples and 42 clinical plasma samples, achieving 96% sensitivity and specificity in analytical validation and 93% agreement with qPCR results in clinical validation. The method detects bacteria, fungi, DNA viruses, and RNA viruses with low-depth sequencing on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq platforms, enabling results in 13-27 hours. HostEL uses magnetic bead-immobilized nucleases to enrich pathogen nucleic acids, while AmpRE combines DNA and RNA library preparation into one reaction. The workflow is incompatible with parasite detection.

Cruzin' for Life, a Santa Maria nonprofit founded in 2003, operates a retrofitted transport van that has served over 2,600 cancer patients in its first year, logging more than 34,000 miles across eight Central Coast communities. The van provides free rides to Mission Hope Cancer Center for patients like Sal Diaz, who previously struggled to find transportation for chemotherapy sessions. The organization raised $69,000 for the vehicle, including a $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy, and continues fundraising through events like its annual Valentine's Day crab feed. The wheelchair-accessible van is stocked with comfort items and is frequently at capacity, with officials considering a second vehicle given rising demand from approximately 700 new cancer diagnoses annually at Marian Regional Medical Center.

A woman declared dead by paramedics after a car crash in South Africa was found alive in a mortuary refrigerator hours later. The incident occurred on June 24 near Carletonville, where two other occupants died. Distress Alert, the ambulance service, confirmed all proper procedures were followed but has launched an investigation. The woman showed no signs of life when checked for breathing and pulse. She was taken to hospital after being discovered alive.

The 2025–26 NHL season marks Jim Montgomery's first full season as head coach of the St. Louis Blues. After leading the team to the playoffs mid-season, Montgomery aims to establish his structured systems and strong special teams to return the Blues to contention. The season opens October 9 at Enterprise Center, with seven of the first 11 games at home. Key early matchups include division rivals, with 26 Central Division games total. The schedule includes a February 5–25 break for the Winter Olympics, creating a compressed March and April. Montgomery faces challenges integrating veteran leadership with young talent, tightening defense, and finding effective line combinations. Success will depend on performance in high-stakes division games.

San Juan Mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called new Hurricane Maria death toll estimates "a day of collective mourning" after Harvard researchers estimated 4,645 "excess deaths" between September 20 and December 31, potentially more than 70 times Puerto Rico's official count of 64. The study, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, had a margin of error ranging from 793 to 8,498 deaths, with researchers suggesting the likely figure is about 5,000. Cruz, wearing a hat with "4,645," criticized the Trump administration for failing to acknowledge the tragedy, noting Trump compared Maria's death toll favorably to Hurricane Katrina during his visit.
