A backtest of NIFTY 50 found a positive end-of-month effect comparable to the US market's turn-of-the-month effect. Using Yahoo Finance data from 2007, the optimal strategy enters at the close of the fifth-to-last trading day and exits at the close of the second trading day of the new month. This produced a 10.5% CAGR with 26% maximum drawdown, outperforming buy-and-hold despite only 30% market exposure. Results remained reasonably robust when varying entry and exit dates slightly.

Celtic's 19-point lead over Rangers with a game in hand marks the largest gap between the clubs in 91 years, dating back to 1925-26 when John Logie Baird invented television. That season, Celtic won the title with 58 points (equivalent to 83 today) while Rangers finished sixth with 44 points (63 today), a 20-point margin. This study examines drama-based pedagogy in STEAM education through a literature review and pilot case study with 19 first-year university students in Hungary. The research investigated how students view dramatic activities in science and history classes and what they can achieve through such activities. Two drama activities were conducted: "The Life Cycle of a Butterfly" and "Indian Caste System." Findings showed that drama activities increased student creativity, facilitated group collaboration, developed problem-solving and thinking skills, and enhanced motivation and involvement. Students demonstrated diverse artistic interpretations, worked effectively in groups, and felt more connected to the topics. Challenges include time constraints, student participation issues, and lack of teacher training. The study acknowledges limitations due to the small, homogeneous sample of female students, suggesting results require further validation.

This patent application describes an autonomous vehicle with multiple independent control systems for safety redundancy. The primary system (AV control sub-system) handles normal autonomous operation using various sensors and processing resources. One or more auxiliary control units operate independently to detect specific predefined conditions or events and implement predetermined responses, either by bypassing the primary system or verifying its trajectory calculations. These auxiliary units use dedicated sensors, separate communication busses, and can directly control vehicle interfaces (braking, steering, etc.) when triggered. TrackR unveiled three new Bluetooth tracking products ahead of CES: the TrackR pixel, a cheaper colorful alternative to the aluminum TrackR bravo; the TrackR wallet 2.0, a credit card-thin tracker; and the TrackR atlas, a smart plug that maps home locations and works with Amazon Alexa. Lightning strikes randomly and is not attracted to metal or water. National Weather Service expert John Jensenius clarifies that metal objects, batteries, and tools do not attract lightning; height, pointy shape, and isolation are the dominant factors. The article debunks five myths: metal attracts lightning (false—height and shape matter); rubber tires protect car occupants (false—it's the metal roof and sides); sunny skies mean safety (false—lightning can strike 10 miles from storms); lightning never strikes the same place twice (false—tall, isolated objects are repeatedly struck); and trees offer safe shelter (false—their height makes them likely targets). Most lightning deaths during leisure activities occur on or near water, not on golf courses.

The "Power" Offense is an NBA basketball set offense designed to free up shooters through baseline and down screens. It begins with shooters crossing under the basket, then curling off down screens set by posts. The offense includes multiple reads and counters based on defensive reactions: curl for trailing defenders, basket curl for late trailers, fade for defenders going over screens, back cut for early screen cheats, screen-and-roll for switches, and slip screens for show-and-recover defenses. Automatic counters include fake cross, misdirection, back cut, direct post entry, and dribble drive entries. A "Single/Double" variation allows shooters to go either direction off baseline screens. Success requires execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, timing, and defensive recognition. Teaching follows the whole-part-whole method with breakdown drills. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, varying alignments, attacking weak defenders, and using Side Screens late in shot clocks.

Higher education institutions, hospitals, and private sector leaders opposed a Department of Homeland Security proposal to cap international student stays at four years, replacing the "duration of status" policy that allows students to remain until completing their studies. Commenters argued the rule would unnecessarily restrict already-monitored students, disrupt healthcare access for 17,000 J-1 visa physicians, harm research and industries relying on international talent, and create costly administrative burdens. A player discusses the difficulty of losing a long overtime game in the finals, acknowledging the need to regroup and bounce back for the next game. This qualitative study examines perspectives of 8 bilingual and 8 monolingual early childhood teachers in Ankara, Turkey, on bilingualism and bilingual education. Using phenomenological design and semi-structured interviews, researchers identified five themes: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children in monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and impact of bilingualism on children's development.

All teachers agreed bilingualism offers advantages for career prospects, self-confidence, and communication skills. However, views diverged on educational environments: bilingual teachers emphasized risks of language loss in monolingual schools, while monolingual teachers stressed Turkish proficiency needs. Both groups supported expanding bilingual schools but noted insufficient qualified personnel and resources as barriers. Teachers lacked comprehensive knowledge of bilingual program structures, though most believed all staff should be bilingual.

Key challenges identified included teachers' ineffective use of both languages, financial and human resource shortages, children's native language deficiencies, and family-related cultural conflicts. Teachers disagreed on social skills development, with monolingual teachers more concerned about community language mastery and bilingual teachers emphasizing multicultural advantages.

The study concludes that despite gaps in understanding program implementation, all teachers view bilingualism positively and advocate for more bilingual schools. Recommendations include targeted professional development, improved teacher qualifications, parental support programs, and policy development for scaling bilingual education in Turkey.

AI is transforming intellectual property law, raising unresolved questions about whether AI can be an inventor, hold patents, and what constitutes "obvious" inventions. Biotech patent lawyer DeAnn Smith anticipates future litigation will address these issues.

This review examines lung cancer screening biomarkers, analyzing 32 articles on U.S.-based clinical research from the past 10 years. Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death due to late diagnosis and inadequate screening. The study evaluated seven biomarker categories: volatile organic compounds (80% sensitivity, 80% specificity), circulating tumor DNA (80% sensitivity, 96% specificity), miRNA molecules (93-96% sensitivity, 23-33% specificity), methylation beads (34-93% sensitivity, 8-92% specificity), Ga-Alfatide II scans (86% sensitivity, 85% specificity), combined score (78% sensitivity, 50% specificity), and WT-IDH (63% sensitivity, 93% specificity). Circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT scans demonstrated the strongest combined sensitivity and specificity for screening. The review identifies primary prevention as understudied and emphasizes improving early detection through biomarker-targeted screening to reduce mortality.

This study compared three surveys of primary care physicians' EHR use and interoperability experiences: the 2021 National Electronic Health Records Survey (NEHRS), the 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. The CCQ had a 100% response rate (3,991 respondents), NEHRS had 18.2% (1,875 respondents), and UCSF had 3.6% (3,209 respondents). Respondents differed demographically: CCQ respondents were younger, more likely to work in health systems, and less likely to be in private practice compared to NEHRS and UCSF respondents. All surveys found low physician satisfaction with EHRs and limited interoperability, with approximately 20% reporting frequent access to external clinical information. However, responses varied significantly across surveys on specific measures. CCQ respondents reported better interoperability experiences and more after-hours documentation than NEHRS or UCSF respondents. Stratified analyses showed these differences persisted across age groups, EHR platforms, and practice types. The study suggests that supplementing NEHRS with mandatory certifying board surveys like the CCQ could improve data reliability and representativeness for health IT policymaking, though certifying boards are limited to single specialties.

A 12-month intensive dementia-specific exercise and rehabilitation programme (PrAISED) was evaluated in a randomised controlled trial of 365 participants with mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Despite good adherence and fidelity, the intervention showed no effect on activities of daily living, physical activity, quality of life, falls, cognition, or other health outcomes. A possible small reduction in falls rate and improvement in specific cognitive domains did not translate into functional gains. The study adds to evidence that exercise and rehabilitation therapies are unlikely to change the rate of functional decline in dementia, suggesting a need to redefine wellbeing outcomes and focus on supportive, adapted functioning rather than independence.

Russian cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct a spacewalk from the International Space Station on August 17, exiting the Pirs airlock at approximately 10:45 am EDT. Ryazanskiy will manually deploy five nanosatellites, including one testing 3-D printed materials in low-Earth orbit, one with multilingual greetings, and one commemorating Sputnik 1 and Konstantin Tsiolkovsky. The spacewalkers will also collect residue samples and install handrails and struts. This will be Yurchikhin's ninth spacewalk and Ryazanskiy's fourth, both wearing Russian Orlan spacesuits. The event marks the 202nd spacewalk for space station assembly and maintenance and the seventh this year.

Stenabolic (SR9009) is a synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand developed by Scripps Research Institute, not a SARM. It binds to and activates the Rev-Erb protein, affecting circadian rhythms, metabolism, and fat storage. Benefits include increased fat loss, enhanced endurance, and improved health markers: studies show it reduces plasma triglycerides by 12%, total cholesterol by 47%, plasma glucose by 19%, insulin by 35%, and proinflammatory cytokine IL-6 by 72%. It increases mitochondria count in muscles, boosting energy production and endurance—mice ran 50% longer on SR9009. It raises resting energy expenditure by 5% and improves glucose metabolism, creating effects similar to continuous exercise.

In Gittens v. Garlock Sealing Technologies, the U.S. District Court for the Western District of New York granted defendant's motion for summary judgment and dismissed plaintiff's ADA disability discrimination complaint with prejudice. Plaintiff Steven C. Gittens, Sr., proceeding pro se, failed to respond to defendant's summary judgment motion despite multiple court orders and warnings that non-response could result in dismissal. The court found dismissal warranted under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 41(b) for failure to prosecute, Rule 16(f) for failure to obey court scheduling orders, and Rule 56 for failure to show genuine issues of material fact. On the merits, the court held Gittens failed to establish a prima facie ADA claim because his 25-30 pound lifting restriction did not constitute a "disability" under the ADA—specifically, inability to perform a single particular job does not substantially limit the major life activity of working. The court noted that even if a prima facie case existed, defendant provided legitimate non-discriminatory reasons for reassignment that plaintiff failed to show were pretextual.

The passage argues for lawful justice over mob violence, emphasizing that education—particularly industrial education like that at Hampton and Tuskegee—elevates citizens above criminality and improves race relations. The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District announced plans to finalize high school boundary changes using three new focus groups. The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Indiana confirmed Jeffery Wayne Smith and Paulette Monee Smith's amended Chapter 13 plan with modifications. The debtors proposed paying Chrysler Financial Corporation in full ($20,800 plus 8% interest) for their 1997 Dodge Stratus while paying NBD Bank only the replacement value ($11,400) for their 1996 vehicle, and offering 10% to unsecured creditors. The Standing Chapter 13 Trustee objected, claiming unfair discrimination against NBD Bank, lack of good faith, and failure to apply all disposable income.

The court found the disparate treatment of Chrysler permissible under 11 U.S.C. § 1322 because the debtors purchased the vehicle five months before filing and made no payments due to a payroll deduction error. Paying Chrysler less than the full amount would create a "virtual windfall" for the debtors. The court also found the debtors acted in good faith and that Mrs. Smith's ERISA-qualified Profit Sharing Plan benefits were not disposable income until actually received in cash.

The court modified the plan to: (1) reduce Chrysler's interest rate from 8% to 3.9%; (2) require debtors to submit paycheck stubs every six months; (3) increase plan payments by any overtime exceeding projections; (4) increase monthly payments by $75 to $1,808.33; (5) require net proceeds from any Profit Sharing Plan cash distributions to go to creditors; and (6) cease voluntary retirement contributions.

Safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar across study groups. Before Week 24, adverse event rates were comparable between the Primary SOC group (51.2%) and Additional Educational Program group (52.0%), with similar rates of related AEs, serious AEs, and discontinuations due to AEs. Between Weeks 24-48, AE rates were 33.8% (Primary SOC), 40.8% (Secondary SOC), and 38.6% (Continued Additional Educational Program). Twenty-four deaths total were reported. No pregnancies occurred. The "Single/Double" offense is an effective method to attack the Triangle & Two defense by using screens to free up shooters. The offense involves shooters communicating to form single or double screens from either side, creating options like the Double Screen (fake one way, reverse off double screen), Single Screen Right (primary shooter uses double screen, secondary crosses to single), and Pop Out Left (primary uses single screen, secondary pops out). Additional options include Base Screen (posts screen defenders with opposite post flashing to ball) and Side Screen (post steps out for screen and roll with drop pass or kick out opportunities). Success requires proper execution of screens, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Game strategies include scouting opponents, varying alignments, and attacking weakest defenders. The Triangle & Two defense uses three players in a triangle zone while two "chasers" deny passes to specific opponents.

The passage examines Greek primary teachers' views on STEM education implementation in primary schools. A study of 114 teachers found they consider scientific thinking development very important (83%), particularly for everyday life problem-solving, inquiry engagement, and critical thinking. However, while 70-75% value practices like problem-solving, group work, and experimental predictions, only 7-19% report students actually develop these skills in classrooms. Teachers identify self-efficacy gaps in teaching science (20-30% effective) and mathematics (30-40% effective). Key advantages cited include experiential interdisciplinary learning (46%), real-life connections (38%), and teamwork development (29%). Main weaknesses involve inadequate teacher training (58%), insufficient infrastructure/equipment (42%), and time constraints (31%). For successful implementation, 71% request more training, 31% need infrastructure, and 11% want curriculum restructuring. Teachers unexpectedly highlighted STEM's potential to reduce educational inequalities by engaging diverse learners. The study concludes that Greece's STEM introduction lacked necessary prerequisites, leaving implementation to teachers' discretionary efforts despite their willingness and need for systemic support.

A report by the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs found that South Korea's birthrate began declining in the mid-1980s as more married women received higher education. The total fertility rate dropped from 2.1 in 1984 to 1.6 in 1987, coinciding with high school graduates surpassing middle school graduates among married women aged 15-49. By 2012, nearly 95% of married women had high school or university diplomas, up from 70% with elementary education in 1974. Married women's labor force participation also rose from 39% to 53% during this period. South Korea's fertility rate fell to 1.24 in 2015, among the world's lowest.

This document outlines the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial comparing dasiglucagon to placebo and GlucaGen® for plasma glucose recovery in hypoglycemic patients. Concomitant medications will be coded using WHODrug Global (March 2018) with ATC level 4 for listings and level 2 for summaries. The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods with stratified log-rank tests on the FAS, adjusting for age group and injection site. Secondary endpoints include recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests and ANOVA. Pharmacokinetic parameters will be calculated using non-compartmental analysis. Safety analyses cover adverse events (coded with MedDRA v21.0+), local tolerability, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity. No interim analyses are planned. Programming specifications include QC requirements and detailed table/figure/listing formats.

Amsterdam archaeologists discovered 700,000 discarded objects dating from Neolithic times to the present while excavating the Amstel riverbed for a new subway line. The "Below the Surface" project, costing 6 million Euros, yielded items including stone axes, coins, cellphones, and dentures that document the city's urban history. A selection of 10,000 objects will be displayed at the Rokin subway station when the North/South line opens July 22. A hockey goalie describes making key saves during playoff games, including a "soccer goalie save" after an initial stop. This lecture continues the proof of Freiman's theorem, focusing on Bogolyubov's lemma and the geometry of numbers. The speaker reviews Ruzsa's modeling lemma, which allows passing from a set of small doubling in the integers to a positive proportion subset of a small cyclic group while preserving additive structure via Freiman 8-isomorphism.

The main topic is Bogolyubov's lemma, which states that adding a set to itself multiple times "smooths" it and reveals large additive structure. In the finite field model F₂ⁿ, if A is an α-proportion subset, then 2A−2A contains a subspace of codimension less than 1/α². The proof uses Fourier analysis, showing that the convolution of indicator functions has positive support on the orthogonal complement of large Fourier coefficients.

For cyclic groups Z/nZ, subspaces are replaced by Bohr sets—sets where rx/n is close to an integer for all r in some set R. Bogolyubov's lemma in this setting states that 2A−2A contains a Bohr set of dimension at most 1/α² and width 1/4.

The lecture then covers geometry of numbers, defining lattices, their determinants, and successive minima with respect to convex bodies. Minkowski's second theorem relates the product of successive minima to the volume of the body and lattice determinant. This is applied to show that Bohr sets contain large proper generalized arithmetic progressions (GAPs): a Bohr set of dimension d and width ε contains a proper GAP of dimension at most d and size at least (ε/d)ᵈ fraction of the group.

The proof constructs a lattice from the Bohr set's defining parameters, applies Minkowski's theorem to find a large parallelepiped in this higher-dimensional space, and projects it down to Z/nZ. The speaker notes that finding this GAP in 2A−2A is progress toward Freiman's theorem, with remaining tools (Ruzsa's covering lemma) to be covered in the next lecture to complete the proof.

Japanese universities lagged behind in ICT use for education before COVID-19 due to traditional views of in-person education and structural factors like limited distance learning credits. The pandemic forced rapid adoption of online classes, prompting policy changes by MEXT, including relaxed credit limits for remote learning and projects like Scheem-D and Plus-DX to support digitalization. However, the Central Council for Education maintained credit limits in 2022 due to concerns about interaction quality, while proposing exceptions for universities with strong quality assurance.

Faculty faced challenges with emergency remote teaching, including technological anxiety and ineffective communication, though resource sharing emerged. Students struggled with increased assignment burdens and the "substantiation of the credit system," as Japanese undergraduates traditionally study less outside class due to heavy course loads and early job-hunting activities.

Lifelong learning digitalization progressed unevenly: university distance learning for degrees expanded pre-pandemic, while traditional non-degree programs like Kokaikoza remained largely undigitalized due to resource constraints. Newer vocational certificate programs saw greater digitalization, partly due to pandemic acceleration.

Challenges persist, including cultural resistance to educational change, personal information protection risks with government data-sharing initiatives like "My Number," and the need to address structural barriers to maximize digitalization benefits while safeguarding student data.

The ScottishPower Foundation has donated £95,220 to the Sussex Wildlife Trust for its 50-year celebrations at Woods Mill in Henfield. The funding will enable 1,300 additional people to participate in events, deliver ten wildlife identification courses, train 250 wildlife champions, and establish a young naturalists club. The money will also fund habitat improvements including reed bed restoration and enhanced path access. A camera has already been installed in a kestrel nesting box for public viewing. Woods Mill opened to the public on 8 June 1968. ScottishPower Foundation trustees visited the site this week, joining a pond-dipping session with local primary school students. The foundation has donated over £1 million to UK charitable projects this year.

NVIDIA's A100 GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, introduces significant performance improvements over the V100 through enhanced Tensor Cores, memory optimizations, and new hardware features. Third-generation Tensor Cores enable 4x more thread data sharing, reducing register file bandwidth and redundant data loads. A new asynchronous copy instruction bypasses L1 cache and register files, loading data directly from global memory to shared memory. The A100 features 1.7x larger shared memory allocation (164 KB), 1.7x faster HBM2 memory bandwidth (1555 GB/sec), 2.3x improved L2 cache read bandwidth, and a 7x larger 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls for optimized data caching.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability partitions each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, enabling multi-tenant cloud environments with quality-of-service guarantees. Third-generation NVLink doubles the data rate to 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair and increases total bandwidth to 600 GB/sec with 12 links. PCIe Gen 4 support provides 31.5 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth.

SMP booting requires special handling due to encrypted register states, with options including reset vector modifications, AP creation NAE events, or AP jump tables. Non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibit functional properties like piezoelectricity and ferroelectricity. Polar metals combine polar crystal structures with metallic conductivity, where electric fields are screened by itinerant electrons. The distortive polar metal (DPM) subclass involves centrosymmetry-lifting transformations, following the "weak coupling principle" where electronic structure is decoupled from polar distortions. Domain boundaries in DPMs exhibit "bound charge" and "charged" configurations (head-to-head and tail-to-tail), though these concepts differ from ferroelectrics due to metallic screening.

This study examines domain boundaries in metallic DPM Mn5Al8, which undergoes a martensitic cubic (γ-brass) to rhombohedral (γ2) transformation at ~880°C. The polar R3m structure and metallic behavior were confirmed through XRD, resistivity measurements, and DFT calculations. The transformation produces herringbone microstructures with {100}PC and {110}PC twin boundaries, visualized via EBSD and HAADF-STEM. 4D-STEM DPC revealed "bound charge" density maps showing H-H and T-T domain boundaries forming "interlocking Y patterns."

Variable surface reactivity was observed: low-voltage SEM showed bright contrast at H-H boundaries, while copper deposition and oxide formation preferentially occurred at H-H versus T-T boundaries. This suggests electron enrichment at H-H and depletion at T-T boundaries, affecting local work function and surface reactivity despite complete field screening in metals.

Chemical sorting of the ICSD identified ~134 metallic polar metals (5.1% of polar compounds), with ~20% being DPMs. Notable metallic DPMs include AuCuZn, CuNiAl, and β′-Mg2Al3. The study challenges the "weak coupling principle" in fully metallic DPMs and highlights the unexplored physics of domain boundaries in metallic polar metals.

Assembly seats span Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Meghalaya, Punjab, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal. The bypolls are significant for the BJP and opposition parties. Key contests include Kairana, where BJP faces RLD backed by BSP, SP, and Congress; and Maharashtra's Palghar and Bhandara-Gondia, contested by BJP, Shiv Sena, NCP, and Congress. Kairana fell vacant after BJP leader Hukum Singh's death; his daughter Mriganka Singh is the BJP candidate. Palghar, a reserved seat, was vacated by BJP MP Chintaman Wanga's death in January.

The passage describes nine figures of an under sink organizer with sliding storage basket, showing perspective, elevational, plan, and exploded views. Broken lines indicate unclaimed portions of the design.

This MIT lecture covers corporate carbon footprinting using a case study of WidgetCo, a chair manufacturer with facilities in Michigan and Shanghai. The professor explains how to calculate emissions using activity data multiplied by emissions factors, with common pitfalls including aggregation errors in transportation calculations. Key concepts include the three emission scopes: Scope 1 (direct emissions from owned sources), Scope 2 (indirect from purchased electricity), and Scope 3 (other indirect emissions). Organizational boundary decisions significantly impact results—using equity share versus control approaches can halve reported emissions for joint ventures. The lecture notes that most companies report only 25% of supply chain emissions as Scope 1 and 2, with Apple owning just 2% of its total value chain emissions. Disclosure decisions involve trade-offs between transparency and competitive positioning, as companies like FerretCo can appear more efficient simply by outsourcing manufacturing. The Greenhouse Gas Protocol provides standards, but comparability remains challenging due to boundary discretion. The session concludes by introducing life cycle assessment as the methodology for product-level carbon footprinting, to be covered in the next lecture.

The speaker analyzed his team's physical play and offensive success in a Stanley Cup Final game, noting unusual scoring luck against goaltender Belfour. He anticipates the opponent will respond angry and hungry tomorrow, requiring disciplined, physical play to maintain home ice advantage. He praised Jason's development as a leader since midseason, recalling his previous captaincy in Edmonton. The team created scoring chances through hard work rather than opponent errors. Players maintain strong competitive chemistry. The speaker emphasized that while winning the first game provides momentum, the series resets for the next game.

This study estimated noma incidence in northern Nigeria from 1999-2024 using retrospective data from 1,383 patients at the Noma Children's Hospital in Sokoto, the only dedicated noma facility in Nigeria. The estimated incidence was 114.5 cases per 100,000 population, with annual average and median incidence of 4.4 and 2.2 cases per 100,000. Incidence was highest among children under 10 years (399.9 cases per 100,000 for under 5 years; 226.2 for ages 5-9), and higher among males (120.7) than females (108.1). Sokoto state had the highest overall incidence (921.9), though Kebbi state showed highest incidence among young and middle-aged adults. Most patients presented with advanced disease: 59.7% had gangrene (stage 3), compared to 7.3% with oedema (stage 2) and 0.4% with acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (stage 1). The cheeks were the most commonly affected site. The study highlights the need for early detection programs, as earlier stages are reversible with cost-effective interventions.

Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge, fresh from winning his third London Marathon title, visited Tottenham Hotspur's training facility to meet Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama, coach Mauricio Pochettino, and other team members. Wanyama had earlier congratulated Kipchoge on Twitter for his London victory alongside Vivian Cheruiyot. Kipchoge was also recently crowned World Marathon Majors Champion and plans to attempt Dennis Kimetto's world record at September's Berlin Marathon.

This study investigates barriers to distance education in university mathematics courses using Q methodology with 13 Turkish faculty members who switched to online teaching after the February 2023 earthquake. Three factors emerged: student-related barriers (Factor 1, 6 participants), technology-related barriers (Factor 2, 5 participants), and pedagogical barriers (Factor 4, 2 participants). Notably, teacher-related barriers did not emerge as a distinct factor. Participants generally viewed distance education as unsuitable for standalone mathematics instruction, preferring blended or hybrid models. The most significant barriers across all factors were curriculum-pedagogy related (Z=1.64), followed by teacher-related (Z=1.05), technology (Z=0.90), and student barriers (Z=0.71). Key discriminative items included faculty feedback efforts, digital library access, and unreliable online assessment. Participants agreed most strongly that students show reluctance to participate in distance education classes.

This patent filing describes a secure, zero-knowledge data sharing system for cloud applications, particularly for healthcare. The system uses multi-layered encryption with a key hierarchy structure (KHS) to protect personal health information (PHI). Keys include derived keys (password-based and question-based), master encryption keys, and data encryption keys. Data is encrypted client-side before transmission, with servers storing only encrypted data without access to decryption keys. The system enables secure sharing between users (e.g., doctors and patients) through public-key infrastructure and shared data encryption keys (SDEKs) managed via shared data KHS (SD-KHS). Recipients decrypt shared data using their private keys, and modifications require owner approval. The architecture prevents cloud providers from accessing plaintext data, addressing liability and security concerns while enabling real-time communication without burdensome patient portal enrollment.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed Noe Martinez Paredes's 57-month sentence for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. His counsel filed an Anders brief stating no grounds for relief and moved to withdraw; the court granted the motion after independent review found no arguable grounds for appeal. Martinez Paredes, proceeding pro se, filed no supplemental brief.

The Senate approved on third reading Senate Bill No. 1738, the Philippine Identification System Act of 2018, with 17 affirmative votes and 2 negative votes. The bill institutionalizes a single national ID for citizens and foreign residents, assigning each individual a "PhilSys Number" to be incorporated across government identification systems, with the Philippine Statistics Authority serving as the registry. Senator Panfilo Lacson, the bill's sponsor, stated it would help deter criminality and terrorism through identity authentication while protecting privacy, as the PhilSys number would only be released under specific conditions including consent, public safety risks, court order, or personal request. The National ID system is expected to roll out in 2019 with a P2 billion budget allocation from the Department of Budget and Management.

Researchers have identified natural bacteria from grape plant leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a key compound causing smoke taint in wine after wildfire exposure. Two bacterial strains consumed guaiacol within 96 hours in lab conditions, though they did not grow on similar smoky compounds. The team identified the gene responsible for this degradation. This microbial approach could offer a more targeted alternative to current mitigation techniques like activated charcoal filtering, which can remove desirable wine components. The wine industry faces increasing challenges from prolonged wildfire seasons, with over $3 billion in losses in 2020 alone. Further research is needed to find bacteria capable of degrading other volatile phenols that contribute to smoke taint.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality has filed a DRHP for an IPO with Sebi, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 200 crore and an offer for sale of 61.79 lakh shares, constituting 14.22% of post-offer capital. The company operates 81 Barbeque Nation restaurants in India and one in Dubai. Net proceeds will fund new restaurants, loan repayment, and corporate purposes. The book-built offer allocates up to 50% to QIBs (with 5% reserved for mutual funds), at least 15% to non-institutional bidders, and at least 35% to retail investors, with 1.5 lakh shares reserved for employees.

Telstra CEO Andy Penn faces pressure at the upcoming investor day to deliver positive news amid a declining share price and an S&P Global credit downgrade. Analysts anticipate potential dividend cuts for 2019 and seek reassurance about earnings growth after NBN compensation payments end. However, recent analyst sentiment has slightly improved, with UBS upgrading its recommendation to buy and Morgan Stanley offering positive outlook commentary.

Six months after Abby Williams and Libby German were killed near the Monon High Bridge in Delphi, Indiana, no arrests have been made. First Sgt. Jerry Holeman of Indiana State Police, who manages the investigation, stated the case is not cold and that over 24,000 tips require follow-up. A suspect sketch released July 17 generated more than 3,000 additional tips. Police are testing DNA from the crime scene daily to identify whether it belongs to the suspect, victims, or family members. Holeman hopes to identify a person of interest and begin court proceedings by the one-year anniversary. Detectives are reviewing old evidence and tips to ensure nothing was missed.

Ajay Bodke of Prabhudas Lilladher advises retail investors not to worry about the 10% LTCG tax, as equities remain the only asset class delivering inflation-beating post-tax returns. He identifies key upside triggers for Indian markets: revival in corporate earnings, favorable macro-economic outlook compared to emerging economies, and range-bound crude oil prices at $60-70 per barrel. Bodke notes that DIIs have become a strong counterforce to FIIs, with monthly SIP inflows of Rs 5,000-6,000 crores proving sticky. He expects RBI may tighten monetary policy due to global central bank actions and fiscal concerns. While equities have historically delivered 4-6x returns every 10 years versus inferior gold returns, he recommends the under-penetrated insurance sector and retail-focused BFSI players for medium to long-term investment.

Montclair State University's mascot, Rocky the Red Hawk, celebrated his 16th birthday on October 5, 2017, with campus-wide festivities. Team Rocky distributed free bagels and candy from 8 a.m., followed by a party in the Student Center Ballrooms featuring free gifts, photo booths, cupcakes, and a prize wheel. The event included a donation box for a local food pantry, a speech from President Susan Cole, and raffle prizes including sweatshirts, a $100 gift card, and a parking pass. Students expressed appreciation for Rocky's role in bringing joy and unity to campus.

This study examines whether highly impactful medical journals lead in disseminating interdisciplinary research (IDR) compared to less impactful journals. Using correlation networks of Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) from PubMed articles published in 1999, 2010, and 2022, the authors compared journals in the top 10% of SCImago Journal Rank (SJR) against others. Key findings indicate that less impactful journals actually produce more interdisciplinary work, as measured by higher average node strength and network density. Cancer-related research emerged as the main driver of interdisciplinarity. Analysis of differences between impactful and less impactful networks revealed that while both journal types agree on areas of absolute prominence (stable core knowledge structures), their relative prominence differs substantially and evolves over time. The authors suggest that structural factors in evidence-to-guideline pipelines, including peer review biases and reporting standards favoring single-discipline studies, disadvantage IDR in high-impact journals.

Police bodycam footage shows Emily Weinman, 20, was slammed to the ground by Wildwood Police officers in New Jersey after refusing to provide her last name during a Memorial Day weekend beach stop. Weinman had passed a breathalyzer and the alcohol present was unopened, but officers attempted to write her up for obstruction. The footage captures officers threatening to "drop" her before taking her down, with Weinman screaming that she was being choked. An officer later stated he "slammed her on the ground" and claimed she kicked them, though this is not visible in the footage. Wildwood Mayor Ernie Troian had said the footage would vindicate police, but its release sparked online outrage over police brutality. The officers were reassigned to desk duty pending investigation. Weinman faces multiple charges including aggravated assault on an officer, resisting arrest, and minor in possession of alcohol.

The Legislative Analyst's Office criticized Gov. Jerry Brown's proposed 5 percent raise for California correctional officers, finding no evidence of recruitment or retention problems to justify the increase. The report notes that entry-level officer numbers have grown, mid-career retention is stable, private-sector opportunities are declining, and wages have exceeded inflation since 2001. The contract, which would cost an estimated $338 million over two years, could increase overtime costs by $6-20 million. The one-year agreement is simpler than previous multi-year contracts that reduced benefits.

Archaeologists identified remains of the Viking Great Heathen Army in a mass grave at St. Wystan's church in Repton, Derbyshire, dating to winter 874. The study in *Antiquity* used corrected carbon dating accounting for marine reservoir effects from a seafood-heavy diet, confirming earlier estimates were skewed. The burial site contained over 250 individuals, including women and children, with artifacts like swords and Thor's hammer pendants. Some graves showed unusual practices, including possible child sacrifices and a boar's tusk interpreted as a symbolic replacement for genitalia. The findings align with historical records of the army's defeat by Alfred the Great and subsequent peace agreement.

A nationwide manhunt is underway for Steve Stephens, a 37-year-old job counselor accused of posting Facebook video of himself killing 74-year-old Robert Godwin Sr., a random victim shot while collecting aluminum cans in Cleveland. Police cannot explain what triggered the killing; Stephens blamed a former girlfriend in the video, though she said he was good to her. Stephens' cellphone was last detected in Erie, Pennsylvania. Nine Philadelphia schools were locked down due to possible sightings. Stephens, who filed for bankruptcy in 2015 and had a gambling problem, worked with teens at a social services agency. Godwin's family held a vigil Monday evening.

Camp America offers UK students summer work opportunities at camps across the USA, with no specific qualifications required. Applications open early for over 8,000 places, with recruitment fairs in January and February. The £599 package includes flights, insurance, and 30 days of travel, plus $650-$1200 pocket money. A former camper described daily routines starting at 7am with activities like high ropes, drama, and swimming, noting the job is fast-paced with unbeatable perks. The experience provides CV benefits and career skills, with previous campers pursuing work with children, international roles, or Camp America management positions.

This lecture covers plasma diagnostics, specifically simplified equilibria for modeling ionization and excitation states in plasmas. The speaker discusses four main equilibria: complete thermodynamic equilibrium (rare, requires optically thick systems with all processes balanced), local thermodynamic equilibrium or LTE (optically thin, collisional processes dominate, described by Saha equilibrium), coronal or collisional-radiative equilibrium (optically thin, low density, collisional excitation balanced by radiative de-excitation), and non-LTE (requires solving all relevant processes case by case). The lecture then outlines the workflow for modeling spectroscopy: determine density and temperature, identify appropriate equilibrium, calculate ionization and excited states, compute line strengths, predict spectra, account for optical thickness and detector response, and compare with experimental data. Line ratio techniques can simplify temperature determination. The second half covers X-ray spectroscopy specifics, including K-shell and L-shell transitions, helium-like and lithium-like ions, and X-ray imaging methods. Pinhole imaging is limited by geometric and diffraction blur. Bent crystals enable monochromatic imaging. Detectors include film (high resolution, time-integrated), image plates (reusable with laser readout), time-gated cameras (expensive, lower resolution), and streak cameras (fast time resolution, one spatial dimension).

Researchers from Aarhus University, in cooperation with Arla, studied how on-farm reverse osmosis concentration affects milk quality. They found that reverse osmosis did not negatively affect total bacterial count, free fatty acid levels, or protein breakdown. Milk powder made from concentrated milk had equal quality and durability compared to ordinary milk, while cheese made from concentrated milk coagulated approximately ten minutes later. On-farm concentration could reduce water transport costs, but profitability depends on herd size, distance to dairy, and energy consumption. Farmers have shown interest, but dairies remain skeptical about finances and handling logistics.

Agriculture sector stocks surged up to 13% after the government raised the minimum support price for paddy by Rs 200 per quintal. Kohinoor Foods gained 12.96%, LT Foods 7.01%, and Chaman Lal Setia Exports 2.27%. Fertiliser stocks including Coromandel International and Deepak Fertilisers also rose. Analysts expect increased rural income and demand for consumption-oriented stocks due to higher MSP and monsoon progress. The cabinet approved MSP for 14 kharif crops for 2018-19.

Nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. SNP-protected guests use the SNP RestrictInjection feature, limiting hosts to #HV exception doorbells. While most host-guest communication uses architecture-specific formats (Virtio/VMBus), this document defines a common format for notifications integral to OS functionality, while allowing drivers flexibility for their own optimized communication paths.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of Florida's Southern District was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah, after conservative commentators published his past blog posts criticizing President Trump as "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist." Rosenzweig allegedly wrote the posts while at private law firm Kobre & Kim before joining the U.S. attorney's office in September 2020. He becomes one of dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump's Justice Department who were believed to be at odds with the president's agenda. The Department of Justice also fired three other Florida prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith, who recently criticized the targeting of political opponents and attacks on the rule of law. Days after Smith's remarks, Virginia U.S. Attorney Erik S. Siebert resigned after Trump pressured him to indict New York Attorney General Letitia James and former FBI Director James Comey.

The British Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs communicated to the U.S. Government that while Britain shared President Wilson's desire for lasting peace, they believed peace's durability depended on its terms. The note argued that pre-war conditions—including aggressive powers, unenforceable international laws, and mismatched national boundaries—had enabled the current conflict. The expulsion of Turkey from Europe was justified by changed circumstances: the "Union and Progress" regime was more barbarous and aggressive than before, controlled by Germany, and responsible for massacres in Armenia and Syria. However, territorial changes alone were insufficient; Germany's militarized political system and accumulated military equipment meant Europe would remain unsafe unless German militarism was addressed. The note concluded that international treaties and laws alone could not ensure security, as Germany had rejected arbitration while preparing for war, and had violated its treaty obligations to Belgium.

CompareCards reports that credit card issuers are offering generous 0% Intro APR deals, with promotional periods ranging from 12 to 21 months. The site, which receives compensation from listed companies but states this doesn't influence ratings, recommends several cards including Bank of America options with 15-month 0% APR periods, cash back rewards up to 6% in selected categories, and sign-up bonuses. Other featured cards include Capital One's Quicksilver (unlimited 1.5% cash back, $300 welcome bonus) and VentureOne (1.25 miles per dollar, $300 travel bonus), Citi cards with 18-month balance transfer offers and 2% cash back, and Discover cards with first-year cash back matching. The passage notes that low or zero percent APR cards can save consumers significant money, with variable rates tied to the Prime Rate and fixed rates remaining more stable.

A thermal alarm triggers Faulted Standby state, but the PMC cannot auto-recover because the alarm resides in the Work domain rather than Standby domain. The thermal alarm timer is blocked by the Work/Standby interface during Faulted Standby. Once exited, if THRM_ALRM# remains asserted, its timer restarts. Thermal alarm removes system power to cool it; after delay, the system repowers. Normally the alarm de-asserts and operation resumes. If the alarm persists past the delay, Standby is reforced, repeating until resolution.

The author draws parallels between dating and selecting a content marketing partner, offering five tips: find aligned interests, compare multiple providers, verify claims through references and results, define your specific needs beforehand, and start with a trial period before committing long-term.

Play action is a football pass play designed to look like a run, deceiving the defense into defending a fake run while the quarterback keeps the ball to pass downfield. It works best when a team has established a strong run game, causing defenders to commit to the line of scrimmage and leaving space behind them. The entire offense must sell the run fake—particularly the quarterback's handoff motion and the offensive line's initial run blocking. Effective times to call play action include short yardage and red zone situations when the defense expects a run. Common concepts include the Double Post, which sends two receivers deep on post routes, and Bubble Y Over, which uses short routes to draw defenders downfield while three receivers run deeper routes. Play action differs from Run Pass Option (RPO), where the quarterback decides after the snap whether to run or pass; play action is always a pass play.

Gold prices rose above $4,000/oz amid political and economic uncertainty, while mining stocks failed to follow gold's rally, suggesting early signs of a larger decline. The USD Index shows bullish inverse head-and-shoulders patterns, and stocks face bearish signals after breaking below support lines. Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded in 2007 by Bill Staby, developed the Wave O₂, a wave-driven desalination system targeting communities lacking affordable potable water. The company focused on South Africa's Ugu municipality, where residents paid $1.00/m³ for water due to weak electric grids requiring expensive diesel generators for desalination. By May 2012, the Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in funding site testing and permitting for a pilot.

RME considered three strategic approaches: (1) a wave energy converter (WEC) producing electricity to power standard desalination plants, which offered grant funding access but lower margins and competitive risks; (2) a hydraulic-powered system with higher water production margins and fewer competitors, requiring private investment; and (3) a vertically integrated "black box" solution owning both WEC and desalination plant, offering maximum control but requiring more capital and expertise.

The wave energy industry faced commercial challenges from environmental factors and lacked cost-competitiveness with fossil fuels. RME differentiated by targeting niche water markets rather than grid-scale electricity, estimating South Africa as a $1.4 billion opportunity. The Wave O₂ system, still in prototype, consisted of a submerged oscillating WEC, flow smoother/pressure intensifier, and standard reverse osmosis desalination plant, producing water at $1.00–$2.00/m³ compared to $3.00–$8.00/m³ for diesel-powered alternatives.

RME held 10 provisional patents and 3 PCTs, with financing primarily from U.S. government grants ($1.3M from Department of Energy, $37K from Department of Interior) plus $400K private investment and $50K from MassChallenge. The company sought $6 million for pilot completion, targeting impact investors given traditional VC disinterest in wave energy's long development timelines.

New York State Attorney General Schneiderman announced the arrest of Guilderland Town Judge Richard Sherwood and financial advisor Thomas Lagan for allegedly stealing over $4 million from family trusts they oversaw. The trusts were funded by Capital Region philanthropists Warren and Pauline Bruggeman and included provisions for Pauline's sisters, Anne Urban and Julia Rentz. Sherwood and Lagan provided estate planning services to the family since at least 2006. Both face felony charges including grand larceny, scheme to defraud, and criminal possession of stolen property. Multiple agencies collaborated on the investigation.

The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims' ruling that under the Public Safety Officers' Benefits Act, a beneficiary's death after the officer's death but before payment does not terminate eligibility for benefits. The court held that "surviving" in the statute means surviving the officer's death, not surviving until payment, rejecting the government's argument that beneficiaries must remain alive through the claims process. The majority found the statute unambiguous on this point, denying Chevron deference to the agency's contrary interpretation. Judge Prost dissented, arguing the statute is ambiguous regarding whether estates are eligible recipients and would have deferred to the agency's interpretation limiting payment to living payees.

A lorry driver from Boston was banned from driving for 20 months after pleading guilty to drink driving. Jaroslaw Buczkowski, 47, was caught driving at 70mph in 40mph zones on New Year's Day with a breath alcohol reading of 83 microgrammes, more than twice the legal limit. His defence stated he had gone to collect a frightened woman from a party. He was fined £350 plus £120 costs and offered a rehabilitation course to reduce his ban by 20 weeks.

Apple's stock is underperforming the S&P 500, falling 6% over two days in June 2017 while major indices hit new highs. The stock now behaves like a "growth cyclical." Forward EPS estimates for fiscal 2017-2019 have risen since May 31, while revenue estimates fell slightly. The author compares this to two previous corrections: a 45% drop in 2012-2013 and a 37% drop in 2015-2016, noting that Apple's recoveries are taking longer. Current fiscal 2018 estimates remain positive, but the stock's failure to sustain a breakout above its February 2015 high of $133-$134 is concerning. The author sold some Apple shares and warns that if high expectations for the iPhone "supercycle" aren't met, the stock could decline significantly. Apple comprises 3.65% of SPY, nearly 7% of the Nasdaq Composite, and 11.65% of QQQ. Potential positives include tax reform and cash repatriation, but the $765 billion market cap makes growth increasingly difficult. The author holds long positions in AAPL and QQQ.

The AEGEAN study evaluated apixaban treatment compliance and efficacy in patients with atrial fibrillation. Mean compliance exceeded 94-95% across all study groups at weeks 4, 12, 24, and 48, with no significant differences between standard of care (SOC) and additional educational program groups. Treatment adherence at 24 weeks was approximately 91.6-91.9% with no significant between-group differences, though adherence significantly declined from weeks 12-24 and 24-48 compared to earlier periods. Persistence at 24 weeks was approximately 91.5% and at 48 weeks was 85-88%, with no significant differences between groups. Only 26-28% of subjects maintained full adherence at 24 weeks, dropping to 14.5-14.9% at 48 weeks. Predictive factors for non-adherence included alcohol consumption, certain occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, and lower MMSE scores. Subgroup analyses showed significant interactions for atrial fibrillation type and sex regarding adherence from weeks 24-48. Safety outcomes were similar across groups, with 51-52% experiencing adverse events before week 24 and 34-41% between weeks 24-48. Major bleeding occurred in 0.3-1.1% of subjects, with 3 fatal bleeding events total. The study concluded that a proactive educational program provided no additional adherence or persistence benefits compared to standard care.

This study examines digital business models for digital startups in Industry 4.0, focusing on the Lean Canvas methodology. Industry 4.0 relies on information technology to enhance productivity and customer connectivity. Indonesian digital startups have grown rapidly but often lack profitable management due to poor business model exploitation. The business model serves as a bridge between technology, ideas, and customers, describing how companies create and distribute value. The Lean Canvas offers nine components: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships, and cost structure. The research uses descriptive qualitative methods with 120 respondents from digital startups, applying semi-structured interviews and purposive sampling with data triangulation. A case study of "Beautiful Memories," a wedding services digital startup, demonstrates the Lean Canvas application, addressing problems like limited service packages and difficulty finding vendors through solutions such as unbundled services and certified professional matching, with revenue from 10% commissions on transactions.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 25, 2022, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2022. The report includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and specifies that the information is furnished, not filed, under the Securities Exchange Act. The company is incorporated in Washington, with its headquarters in Redmond, and its common stock and notes trade on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT.

The US Department of Transportation issued an order to ban seven Chinese airlines from flying over Russia on US routes, forcing them to take longer, less efficient paths. The order aims to address competitive disparities faced by US airlines, which are barred from Russian airspace due to sanctions over the Ukraine invasion. Chinese carriers currently avoid added time and fuel costs by using Russian airspace. The order excludes cargo carriers and Cathay Pacific Airways. Airlines for America supported the move, while China's Foreign Ministry criticized it for hindering travel. Only two affected routes—China Eastern's New York-Shanghai and China Southern's New York-Guangzhou flights—used Russian airspace in October. US-China flights remain 28% below 2019 levels, with US carriers having cut some China routes while Chinese carriers were allowed increased flights in 2024. Security concerns also exist about US citizens on flights over Russia, following two Air India diversions to Russia in 2023 and 2024.

A hockey player discusses their team's Stanley Cup Final appearance, highlighting their depth, rest after the first round, and strong defensive play. They praise teammates Webby and Irvin, note the importance of five-man defense against Pittsburgh's Sidney Crosby, and acknowledge Pekks' key saves despite occasional odd-man rushes given up.

A Lodi man, Steven Ma, who struggled academically as a teenager and was once called "the stupidest student" by a teacher, credits his success to his 10th-grade geometry teacher Linda Brandt. Jeff Smith joined KBC Networks in March 2018 as Midwestern regional sales manager, bringing nearly 30 years of security industry experience. He will support system integrators and security distributors carrying KBC products across the central United States. Previously, Smith was national accounts manager at American FiberTek for the OT Systems product line. He began his career at Alarm Detection Systems Inc. in 2002, later joining Convergent Technologies, where he handled pre-sales engineering and manufacturer relationships. Spontaneous symmetry breaking in physics describes systems adopting lower symmetry than their underlying laws dictate, manifesting in phenomena like magnetism, superconductivity, and electronic nematic phases. While extensively studied in correlated systems like iron-based superconductors and Kagome materials, symmetry breaking in structurally simple 3D intermetallic compounds remains poorly understood. This study investigates CoSn₂, a battery-applicable compound, revealing unprecedented nematic electronic behavior below 25 K.

Resistivity measurements show a slope change at 25 K without corresponding anomalies in specific heat or magnetic susceptibility, ruling out structural or magnetic transitions. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction reveals extremely weak superlattice reflections at 22 K indicating a symmetry reduction from tetragonal I4/mcm to acentric monoclinic C2, with doubled a and c axes. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance confirms four-fold to two-fold symmetry breaking below 25 K.

Phonon calculations show dynamic stability, while electronic susceptibility calculations reveal instabilities at N and X points capable of breaking rotational symmetry. ARPES measurements display orbital-selective anisotropy: linear horizontal polarization preserves four-fold symmetry, while linear vertical polarization shows twofold symmetry, suggesting Co-dxy orbital-driven nematicity. The Fermi surface exhibits a nodal loop structure with Dirac-like crossings.

These findings establish CoSn₂ as a platform for studying electronically driven symmetry breaking in a nonmagnetic, weakly correlated nodal line semimetal, expanding nematic phenomena beyond strongly correlated systems.

Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative condition affecting the elderly, characterized by amyloid beta plaques and tau tangles, with symptoms progressing through preclinical, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and dementia stages. Diagnosis is challenging due to nonspecific symptoms and high misdiagnosis rates (12-23%). This work develops a causal Bayesian Network (BN) for improved AD diagnosis, combining knowledge and data to calculate probabilities of suspected and diagnosed AD. The BN uses medical idioms for interpretability, includes variables from validated diagnostic criteria (NIA-AA), and distinguishes between having AD versus being formally diagnosed. Risk factors include age, family history, traumatic brain injury, and pathogenic mutations (APP, PSEN1, PSEN2). Parameters are specified using NACC UDS data, literature, and expert judgment. Validation shows the model produces clinically consistent predictions, with scenarios demonstrating "explaining away" behavior and backward reasoning. Limitations include simplified modeling of non-AD conditions and reliance on diagnosed cases for parameter setting.

This is a Missouri Supreme Court case, Vansickle v. Brown, affirming a judgment in a malicious prosecution action. The court held: (1) evidence of an arresting officer's uncivil conduct is inadmissible against the defendant unless it shows defendant instigated it; (2) a later trespass judgment against the defendant was properly excluded as it didn't involve the highway's existence and post-dated the prosecution; (3) a second county court order was properly excluded as it didn't vacate the established road; (4) verbal county court instructions were admissible to show defendant's good faith, not road legality; (5) a defendant may testify about his good faith intentions; (6) probable cause requires both belief in guilt and reasonable grounds for that belief, overruling Hickman v. Griffin; (7) Hill v. Palm was reaffirmed; (8) waiving preliminary examination and entering recognizance constitutes prima facie evidence of probable cause; and (9) malicious prosecution requires both malice and want of probable cause—malice is not inferred solely from lack of probable cause. Judges Napton and Henry dissented on points 6 and 8 respectively.

This document describes the AMD Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which facilitates page migration operations for systems using Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) and Secure Nested Paging (SNP). TMPM enables migration of pages during concurrent DMA operations and migration of SNP-protected guest pages that hypervisors cannot otherwise access.

The TMPM engine communicates via a ring buffer interface with mailbox registers. Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (for hypervisor-owned pages with DMA support), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (for SNP guest pages), and PM_NOOP. Commands can process 1-128 pages per operation.

Key features include: IOMMU coordination for safe DMA migration, a Pre-Migration state for RMP entries, firmware reload capabilities (with version checking), and multiple interrupt sources for ring buffer management. Performance is optimized with 128-page commands and proper interrupt pacing.

System requirements include IOMMU enablement, 4KB page alignment for all SPAs, and specific page state requirements. Error handling covers command-level status codes, sub-statuses for retryable conditions, and MCA reporting for hardware errors.

Soccer position numbering originated in 1920s England with a back-to-front, right-to-left system (1-11) for a 2-3-5 formation. The 1950s "W-M" formation kept the same numbers but repositioned inside forwards and moved the center halfback into defense. By the 1960s, "Total Football" eliminated fixed number-position correspondence. In 2012, U.S. Soccer standardized a 4-3-3-based numbering system (1-goalkeeper, 2/3-outside backs, 4/5-center backs, 6/8/10-midfielders, 7/9/11-forwards) with defined position profiles. Modern terms include "False 9" (dropping center forward) and "Double-9s" (paired strikers).

This patent application describes a microservices architecture for cloud computing environments. The system enables dynamic discovery, provisioning, and chaining of microservices across diverse hardware and software resources without requiring application developers to know implementation details at design time.

Key components include: a Service Discovery Function (SDF) that maintains a catalog of available microservices; a standardized microservices API that provides uniform calls regardless of underlying implementation; and a microservices driver that translates generic API calls into optimized service calls for specific instances. Microservices can be implemented as local software, virtual machines, FPGAs, ASICs, GPUs, or other hardware accelerators.

When resources come online, they register capabilities with the SDF, including connection capabilities for direct communication with other microservice instances. Applications request functions through the microservices API, and the driver queries the SDF to identify and provision optimal instances, creating service chains where microservices forward messages directly to subsequent services without returning to the host application. This reduces latency and eliminates request-response overhead.

The architecture supports dynamic load balancing, autoscaling through instance spawning, and message forwarding via various mechanisms including shared memory, RDMA, PCIe, and fabric interconnects. An ontological language describes microservice capabilities, enabling discovery based on desired functionality rather than specific implementations.

The MOVE Index measures U.S. interest rate volatility through 1-month OTC options implied volatility, commonly called the "VIX of the bond market." Created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, it spiked to 199 in March 2023 amid Federal Reserve rate hikes and banking concerns, compared to its 2000-2023 average of around 85 and all-time high of 264 in October 2008.

Unlike the VIX with stocks, high MOVE Index readings do not signal good bond buying opportunities. A backtested trading strategy holding TLT when MOVE is below its historical mean (~86) and selling when above showed linear equity growth from 2002, with maximum drawdown roughly half of buy-and-hold. The strategy underperformed in 2008 but helped in 2022, demonstrating that avoiding high volatility periods reduces risk but does not generate superior returns.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The primary endpoint was percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. The study followed WHO master protocol guidelines, with IEC approval and informed consent obtained. Analysis sets included Full Analysis Set (FAS) and Per Protocol Set (PPS), with 91.9% of plasma group patients receiving all 4 units.

The COVID-19 pandemic forced higher education institutions worldwide to transition from face-to-face to online learning, revealing infrastructure challenges and limitations of existing platforms like Zoom, Google Classroom, and Microsoft Teams. Many universities lacked sufficient on-premise infrastructure and faced data protection concerns with public cloud solutions. Additionally, instructors and students struggled with adaptation, practical course delivery, exam security, and psychological distance in online environments.

This study presents UZEP, a cloud-based distance education platform developed using the Education as a Service (EaaS) model to address emergency distance education needs in higher education. UZEP integrates a learning management system, virtual classroom module (using BigBlueButton), online exam module, homework-project module, digital material sharing, announcement, survey, and reporting modules. The platform requires no local infrastructure, offers easy integration with university management systems, scales horizontally, and complies with personal data protection laws.

The system was tested by 12 Turkish universities during Fall 2020, serving 78,732 users with 13,180 virtual classrooms and 11,314 online exams. Evaluations by experts, administrators, lecturers, and students found UZEP easy to learn and use, with particularly high ratings for virtual classroom functionality. However, limitations were identified in social networking features, group work capabilities, and learning analytics compared to platforms like Moodle and Google Suite. This patent application describes apparatus and methods for measuring tissue viability around burns and other wounds using capacitive sensors that measure sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. The technology employs electrode arrays forming virtual capacitive sensors to measure tissue capacitance, which is converted to SEM values indicating tissue moisture levels. Lower SEM values indicate non-viable tissue (necrosis), while elevated SEM values indicate edema in damaged but potentially recoverable tissue. The apparatus includes visual indicators or projectors to mark boundaries between viable and non-viable tissue, aiding clinical treatment decisions. The system can determine burn depth by comparing measured capacitance or SEM values to reference data arrays. Various embodiments include flexible substrates with embedded electrodes and visual indicators, perforations for skin marking, and optical projection systems for mapping wound regions. The technology enables dynamic monitoring of wound progression and healing over time.

This patent application describes systems, methods, and instrumentalities for low latency MAC PDU assembly in 5G flexible radio access technology (5gFLEX). The WTRU monitors DCI, identifies downlink control channel resources, decodes DCI containing scheduling information, determines decoding parameters (CRC length, aggregation level, robustness level), and derives transmission/reception parameters (QoS level, spectrum operating mode, HARQ feedback parameters, MCS, resource blocks, power information, TTI duration) from these decoding parameters. The device features programmable high/low input alarms with independent thresholds and common hysteresis, plus fixed AVDD alarms (5.3V high, 4.7V low) for debugging. This study demonstrates that diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) combined with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps can effectively predict pTERT mutation status in glioblastoma (GBM) using a ResNet deep learning model, outperforming conventional structural MRI. The entire tumor volume as region of interest yielded optimal results. While age, necrosis volume, and tumor location showed significant associations with pTERT mutation, adding these clinical characteristics did not improve prediction performance beyond DWI data alone. The findings suggest DWI should be incorporated into clinical GBM management for noninvasive pTERT mutation prediction.

This scoping review protocol describes a study to map evidence on determinants and interventions for antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome (MS) in community-dwelling adults. Antipsychotics, while effective for severe mental illness, cause MS in 40%-80% of users, increasing cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes risks. Non-modifiable determinants (gender, ethnicity, age, family history) and modifiable determinants (diet, physical activity) exist, but their relative significance and targeting remain unclear. Previous non-pharmacological interventions show limited clinical efficacy and uncertain sustainability. The review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR checklist, searching multiple databases and grey literature for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies. Two reviewers will screen titles/abstracts independently, with 10% full-text screening checked. Data extraction will cover citations, population, interventions, outcomes, and study types, with narrative synthesis and stakeholder consultation. The aim is to identify knowledge gaps regarding determinants, interventions, and preferred delivery contexts to inform future research.

Cervical cancer, though preventable, remains the second most common cancer among women globally, with 85% of cases and 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) due to limited access to prevention tools. In 2020, WHO launched a 90/70/90 strategy to eliminate cervical cancer by 2030 through HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment. However, LMICs face significant gaps in precancer treatment due to high costs, weak infrastructure, provider shortages, and loss to follow-up. Self-administered topical therapies like 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) cream offer a potential solution, with U.S. trials showing 93% regression in CIN2 cases.

This study examined acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5FU among 12 women living with HIV in Kisumu, Kenya, following primary treatment for CIN2/3. Participants applied 5FU every other week for eight doses at home. All 12 completed questionnaires and in-depth interviews. Results showed high acceptability: all participants strongly agreed the cream was safe, were confident in correct use, and preferred 5FU over prior ablation/excision treatments. Participants valued reduced pain, privacy, convenience, and minimal disruption to daily life. Challenges included initial anxiety, measuring correct dosage, limited anatomy knowledge, and privacy concerns in single-room homes. Partner support for condom use and abstinence requirements was generally achieved but sometimes difficult. The study concludes that self-administered 5FU is highly acceptable among African women and could help address treatment gaps in LMICs, though larger efficacy trials are needed.

Preflop hand equities discussed: bigger pair vs smaller pair (~80/20), pair vs zero overcards (~93%), dominating hands (~70/30), two overcards vs pair (~50/50), and highest card scenarios (~60/40). Suitness matters more when behind.

Key preflop strategy: go all-in with <12 big blinds (BB) with antes, <10 BB without. Small blind all-in ranges can be wider than button due to position irrelevance when all-in. Nash equilibrium for 15 BB small blind vs big blind: shove ~66.8% of hands, call ~38.5%. Position matters more than stack size for shoving frequency. Small pairs and suited connectors play better as all-ins with shallow stacks; big card hands prefer fewer players behind. Calling all-ins requires ~30% equity easily achievable with most hands. Re-raise to 2.5x original raise; go all-in if committing >25% of stack. Add 1 BB per limper to raise size. Avoid small raises that give opponents free options.

The device has an active-high alarm output on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured for alarm functionality by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] bits to 01b. Two alarm types exist: input alarm (monitors ADC input against user-programmable thresholds) and AVDD alarm (monitors analog supply voltage against 4.7V low and 5.3V high thresholds). Both alarms are enabled by default and can be selectively disabled via RST_PWRCTL_REG register bits. Each alarm has active and tripped flags read in ALARM_REG; active flags clear at conversion end while tripped flags clear only after register read. Alarm flags update at each conversion end and can be read via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to data output.
