This lecture covers empirical models of demand, focusing on supply-side modeling, the BLP random coefficient model, and applications to testing market conduct.

The supply side of static competition models involves firms maximizing profits across owned products, with quantities derived from demand models. An ownership matrix tracks which products each firm owns, enabling construction of an omega matrix from price derivatives. First-order conditions allow recovery of marginal costs through matrix inversion, though this makes the model untestable without additional assumptions. Alternatively, specifying functional forms for marginal costs (e.g., based on input prices) enables joint estimation of demand and supply, with supply-side restrictions improving demand parameter precision and serving as overidentifying restrictions to test conduct models.

The BLP paper (1971-1990 US automobile data) demonstrates the random coefficient model's advantages. Simple logit inversions (OLS/IV) show price coefficients become more negative with instruments, reducing implausible inelastic demand. Random coefficients capture heterogeneous substitution patterns—luxury car buyers show low price sensitivity and substitute within quality tiers, while economy buyers face higher elasticity and greater outside option diversion. Miles-per-dollar preferences vary significantly across consumers. Supply-side restrictions improve estimation precision.

Nevo's cereal market paper tests collusion versus competitive conduct. Using city-quarter market data with product fixed effects and demographic-interacted random coefficients, he compares model-implied markups to observed accounting margins (31-46%). The BLP model rejects joint profit maximization across 25 brands, while simpler logit models fail to do so, demonstrating the importance of realistic substitution patterns for conduct testing.

The common ownership hypothesis suggests institutional investors holding competing firms' shares may soften competition. Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson apply this to cereals, developing GMM-based conduct tests using demand-side instruments as excluded restrictions. Despite documented increases in institutional ownership (BlackRock, Vanguard holdings), they reject common ownership models in favor of own-profit maximization, contributing to broader skepticism about this hypothesis due to lacking implementation mechanisms.

The Ichimoku trading strategy is a technical analysis system developed by Japanese journalist Goichi Hosoda in the late 1930s. The strategy generates signals through crossovers and cloud breakouts, but backtesting shows it typically underperforms risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns despite reducing drawdowns and market exposure time. Traders should backtest any Ichimoku-based strategy before implementation, as signal accuracy varies and requires proper risk management to be effective.

The Rhode Island Supreme Court affirmed Andrew A. Bucci's conviction for giving legal advice to Robert Oliva while suspended from practicing law. Bucci was initially found guilty in District Court and fined $500, exceeding the statutory maximum of $250. After a trial de novo in Superior Court, he was sentenced to six months imprisonment. The court rejected Bucci's three arguments: that there was a variance between the charge and proof (the recorded conversations showed extensive legal advice on criminal litigation matters); that pecuniary benefit was a required element (the statute contains no such requirement); and that the harsher sentence violated due process (under *Colten v. Kentucky*, greater sentences after trial de novo are permitted in two-tier systems). The court declined to address the sentencing challenge because Bucci failed to file a Rule 35 motion in Superior Court.

This study compares group-based versus individualized brain parcellation methods for analyzing functional connectivity (FC) disruptions in early psychosis using HCP-EP data. The authors applied the Group Prior Individualized Parcellation (GPIP) algorithm to adjust group-based template borders according to individual FC patterns, testing whether accounting for interindividual variability in brain organization affects case-control FC differences.

Results showed that individualized parcellations reallocated over 40% of vertices on average and yielded higher functional homogeneity than group-based parcellations in both patients and controls. Group-based parcellations detected larger FC differences between patients and controls, with t-distributions shifted toward higher values. Network-Based Statistic analysis identified approximately 9% more dysconnected edges using group-based versus individualized parcellations, with 643 edges differing between methods. While specific edges and regions affected varied considerably between parcellation approaches, network-level inferences remained consistent, with the control network most impacted in both cases.

The findings indicate that group-based parcellations inflate estimates of FC differences in psychosis, suggesting that individualized approaches provide more conservative and refined maps of brain dysconnectivity, though coarse-grained network-level conclusions are robust to parcellation choice.

The professor reviews numerical methods covered in the course, starting with linear systems (Ax=b) solvable via Matlab's backslash in O(n³) operations, noting issues with ill-conditioning. For nonlinear systems, Newton-Raphson requires multiple iterations each costing O(n³), with convergence depending on initial guesses. Root-finding and minimization problems are coupled through methods like fsolve and fmincon, with practical costs often dominated by Jacobian formation at O(n²) rather than O(n³).

Implicit ODE solvers require solving nonlinear systems at each timestep, with total effort scaling as (timesteps) × (iterations) × (cost per solve), potentially reaching 10¹⁰ operations for large problems—still manageable on modern computers.

The lecture introduces functionals (functions taking other functions as inputs), with density functional theory as a key application where molecular energy depends on electron density.

For numerical integration, methods like rectangle, trapezoid, and Simpson's rules work by fitting basis functions to sample points and integrating those approximations. Interpolation (k=n) forces exact fit at data points, while approximation (k<n) uses fewer parameters. Orthogonal basis functions prevent singular matrices in interpolation.

Polynomial basis functions are common but problematic: monomials yield exponentially ill-conditioned matrices, while Lagrange polynomials give coefficients directly as function values, and Newton polynomials allow incremental point addition without recomputing previous coefficients.

Gaussian quadrature optimally chooses weights and points to integrate polynomials up to order 2n-1 exactly, achieving higher accuracy (O(Δt⁶) for 3 points) than Simpson's rule. The 7-point Gauss and 15-point Kronrod combination provides error estimates.

Multidimensional integration suffers the "curse of dimensionality": effort scales as (points)^dimensions, making naive quadrature infeasible for high-dimensional integrals like 6D electronic structure calculations requiring 10¹² evaluations.

Hong Liu lectures on entanglement entropy in quantum systems, covering its definition, properties, and applications. He defines entanglement entropy as the von Neumann entropy of a reduced density matrix obtained by tracing out degrees of freedom in one subsystem. For pure states, this quantifies quantum entanglement between subsystems. Key properties include subadditivity and strong subadditivity conditions.

In many-body systems with local Hamiltonians, ground state entanglement entropy typically follows an area law: proportional to the boundary area divided by a short-distance cutoff. Liu discusses exceptions where subleading terms reveal important physics, including topological order in 2+1 dimensions (characterized by a constant term) and central charge in 1+1 dimensional CFTs (appearing as a logarithmic term).

The lecture culminates in the Ryu-Takayanagi holographic formula: entanglement entropy in a CFT equals the area of a minimal surface in the dual AdS geometry divided by 4G_N. Liu verifies this satisfies strong subadditivity and reproduces known CFT results, including the logarithmic scaling in 1+1 dimensions. The formula connects quantum information to spacetime geometry, unifying previously disparate fields.

This study examines software engineering challenges in integrating large language models (LLMs) into financial report analysis workflows through a Design Science Research approach conducted with Getinge AB. Two research questions guide the investigation: identifying primary software engineering challenges in domain-specific LLM integration (RQ1), and comparing open-source versus commercial LLMs regarding complexity, performance, and maintainability (RQ2).

The research develops and evaluates two prototypical solutions: a local multi-agent system using open-source models (LLaMA 3.1, Qwen 2.5) and a cloud-based implementation using OpenAI's GPT-4o. Both systems automate financial commentary generation for order intake and net sales analysis. The local solution employs a four-agent pipeline (Data Interpretation, Trend Analysis, Report Generation, Validation) to address hardware constraints and data sensitivity requirements, while the GPT-4o implementation uses structured prompting with role definition and few-shot examples.

Key findings reveal three primary engineering challenges: task specificity requiring strict formatting and conditional logic adherence; data preparation complexity due to heterogeneous sources and formats; and data sensitivity constraints limiting deployment options. The local LLM struggled with instruction following and hallucinations despite multi-agent architecture, while GPT-4o captured trends more reliably but exhibited rigid example-following and logical inconsistencies. Expert evaluation found both approaches suitable for draft generation but inadequate for finalized reporting without human validation, citing concerns about accuracy, structural consistency, and transparency.

The study concludes that LLM integration in precision-critical financial domains requires substantial engineering investment in verification mechanisms, prompt management as software assets, and architectural patterns for reliability. Trade-offs between local deployment (control, privacy) and commercial solutions (performance, ease of use) present significant implementation decisions for organizations.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. This study demonstrates that next-generation sequencing of saliva and plasma liquid biopsies can detect cancer gene mutations in Fanconi anemia (FA) patients before clinical diagnosis of oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). In this prospective 2-year study of 16 Spanish FA patients, mutations were found in 15 liquid biopsy samples from 9 patients, with TP53 being the most frequently mutated gene (95% of mutant samples). Six of seven patients who developed lesions or carcinomas had detectable mutations with lead times of 23-630 days (median 205 days) before clinical diagnosis. No mutations were found in five of seven patients free of lesions/tumors. The test showed 92% accuracy, 86% sensitivity, and 100% specificity for predicting oral lesion development. Saliva provided better sequencing performance than plasma due to higher DNA yield. These results suggest liquid biopsy mutation analysis can stratify FA patients into risk groups for enhanced surveillance.

This article explains football offensive line blocking terminology to clarify common confusion and increase appreciation for these players. It defines: Trap Block (leaving a defender unblocked then kicking him out with another lineman); Base Block (one-on-one blocks requiring inside leverage); Reach Block (establishing outside leverage with a 45-degree drop step); Down Block (angle block on inside defenders using favorable pre-snap leverage); Log Block (pulling and sealing a defender inside); Pull (blocker moving around another player to gain numbers or leverage advantage); Veer Block (drop step to climb to second level, used in triple option); Combo Block (two blockers working from first to second level); Drive Block (one-on-one run block driving defender off line); Double Team Block (first part of combo, overpowering one defender); Scoop Block (backside combo block gaining far-point leverage); Cut Block (diving at legs to ground defender); Crack Block (perimeter player blocking interior defender); and Kick Out Block (establishing inside leverage on edge defender from outside the tackle).

The paper presents a DFT+DMFT study of electronic spectra in strongly correlated itinerant magnets (α-iron, CrO₂, CrTe₂, and altermagnet CrSb) in the paramagnetic phase, incorporating non-local self-energy corrections beyond standard DMFT. The non-local self-energy includes contributions from charge and spin fluctuations through renormalized interactions and Hedin vertices.

For iron and CrO₂, which have d-state fillings far from half-filling, non-local spin fluctuations near the Curie temperature cause significant band splitting, making the paramagnetic spectral density resemble ferromagnetic DFT band structures. For CrTe₂ and CrSb, which are closer to half-filling, strong local correlations already produce substantial band splitting that persists over broader temperature ranges, with non-local effects being secondary. These split bands are dispersive, carry partial spectral weight, and are expected to be sensitive to magnetic fields, suggesting potential spintronics applications. The density-density approximation used overestimates magnetic transition temperatures; extension to SU(2)-symmetric Hund interaction is suggested for future work.

GEM is a novel framework for cryo-EM reconstruction that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to represent protein density explicitly. Unlike NeRF-based approaches that model density implicitly, GEM uses compact 3D Gaussians (11 parameters each) instantiated only at nonzero-density regions, enabling parallel rasterization and localized gradient computation. This eliminates the cubic memory and computation overhead of NeRF methods. AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) provides guidelines for optimal performance: use commands with 16+ pages (128 pages maximum), keep the command input queue ahead of engine processing, and request interrupts at sequence ends rather than per command. TMPM can interrupt on low-water marks to allow queue refilling. Certain data structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU memory structures, vIOMMU page tables, pinned backing storage, and ring buffers. The HV/OS must avoid issuing migration commands for these.

For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped using IOMMU host page tables, with only one table per physical page. The TMPM engine modifies IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically, requiring software to avoid concurrent modifications.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded when no operations are in flight, requiring the HV/OS to pause operations, tear down the ring buffer, and use the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol. PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits should be disabled during reload. The reload firmware must be same or greater version. EPYC Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major value 71.

The ring buffer allows asynchronous command processing. Software can send single commands by not advancing the Tail pointer more than one entry from Head, causing processing pause when the queue empties.

TMPM hardware only moves data between 4k-aligned pages. Commands use a separate ring buffer from SEV/SNP, with status returned in command memory. Ring buffer pages must be DEFAULT or HV_FIXED; argument pages can also be HV pages. Each command contains a parameter page with 1-128 Migration Entries. SPAs can be 46-bit or 52-bit depending on encryption; entries are sized for 52 bits with 4k alignment (8-byte for host page table entries).

Initialization requires checking ENGINE_READY, setting ring buffer SPA (4k-aligned, 1-255 contiguous pages), configuring queue behavior, and setting DRIVER_INITIALIZED. Shutdown requires waiting for pointers to equal or PAUSED status, clearing DRIVER_INITIALIZED, and waiting for DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE to clear.

Six interrupt sources share one x86 signal: RBWritePtr_Err (uncontrollable, invalid tail pointer), RBMem_Err (uncontrollable, read error), QfreeIntStat (queue empty), QthreshIntStat (low water mark), IntOnError (command error), and IntOnComplete (command completion). Software clears interrupts via CLEAR_INTS when queue empty or paused.

SPA encoding includes encryption bits when SMEE/SME-MK is enabled. Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (hypervisor pages, updates IOMMU PTEs), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (SNP guest pages), and PM_NOP. Status and sub-status fields report results, with errors for invalid addresses, page states, sizes, or RMP exclusivity.

This study computationally investigates C-C bond formation (2CH₂ → C₂H₄) on gold surfaces using DFT with 2D periodic boundary conditions, comparing monolayer and three-layer gold systems. The monolayer shows stronger adsorption of reactants and products due to more available surface electrons, with reactants oriented carbon-down and products lying flat. The three-layer system exhibits weaker adsorption, with opposite reactant orientation and perpendicular product orientation. The reaction on the monolayer proceeds with minimal activation energy (4.78 kJ mol⁻¹) via translational diffusion followed by association over a shared proton. On three layers, the path involves more rotational motion, less stable intermediates, and higher activation energy (52.10 kJ mol⁻¹). Overall reaction energies are -432.06 kJ mol⁻¹ (monolayer) versus -335.50 kJ mol⁻¹ (three layers). Findings highlight how surface morphology affects carbon upconversion reactions, with implications for dendritic gold nanostructures used in plasmonic photocatalysis.

On-Balance Volume (OBV) is a volume-based technical indicator created by Joseph Granville in 1963 that measures buying and selling pressure by adding volume on up days and subtracting volume on down days. A backtest using RSI on OBV for S&P 500 (SPY) with a 5-day RSI period and 30 buy threshold yielded 337 trades, 73% win rate, 0.55% average gain, 24% max drawdown, and 2.09 profit factor. The lecture transitions from linear algebra to solving systems of nonlinear equations and optimization. It recaps singular value decomposition and condition numbers defined via singular values. Two stopping criteria for iterative methods are introduced: step norm criteria (comparing successive iterations) and function norm criteria (examining residuals). Validation of numerical solutions through multiple methods, experiments, or analytical limits is emphasized.

Nonlinear systems f(x)=0 are presented, where solutions are called roots. Examples include chemical engineering equations of state and phase equilibria. Solutions may be locally unique (isolated by a ball containing no other solutions) or non-locally unique. The inverse function theorem states that if the Jacobian determinant at a root is non-zero, the solution is locally unique.

Linearization approximates nonlinear functions near roots using the Jacobian matrix. Iterative methods create maps where the root is a fixed point. Convergence rates are classified: linear (q=1, C<1), superlinear (q>1), or quadratic (q=2, doubling accurate digits per iteration).

The Newton-Raphson method uses linearization to iteratively improve solutions: x_{i+1} = x_i - J^{-1}f(x_i). It has local convergence and quadratic convergence near locally unique solutions, but fails when the Jacobian is singular or with poor initial guesses. An example demonstrates convergence to circle intersections, showing iteration counts vary by initial guess proximity to solutions.

The authors present iCVS (inferring Cardio-Vascular States), a dynamical mechanistic model designed to estimate hidden physiological states of critically-ill patients using only routinely available bedside measurements. The model addresses the clinical challenge of inferring internal cardiovascular parameters—such as cardiac output, vascular resistance, and filling pressures—from partial observations like blood pressure waveforms and heart rate.

iCVS consists of a one-chamber heart acting as a pump, arterial and venous compartments, and regulatory units including baroreflex and independent autonomic components, plus a non-autonomic vascular resistance modulation. The model uses fifteen hidden parameters and five observables (mean arterial and venous pressures, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure) extracted from high-frequency blood pressure waveforms. A novel feature exploits both slow and fast timescales of pressure traces to maximize information without increasing complexity.

The authors demonstrate iCVS on ten critically-ill children in a pediatric intensive care unit, showing the model correctly identifies hypovolemic shock (via negative intravascular volume change), distributive shock (via negative non-autonomic vascular resistance), and cardiogenic shock (via reduced contractility). The model requires only age, weight, and arterial and venous pressure waveforms as inputs, making it suitable for real-time bedside deployment across diverse patient sizes.

This study conducted a pragmatic adaptive randomized controlled trial comparing two acupuncture styles—auricular acupuncture (AA) and peripheral acupuncture (PA)—against usual care (UC) for acute musculoskeletal pain in an emergency department. From February 2020 to May 2021, 236 patients were randomized across three arms. Both AA+UC and PA+UC showed greater pain reduction at 1-hour post-treatment (2.1 and 1.6 points respectively) compared to UC alone (0.5 points), with no significant difference between the two acupuncture styles. Patient satisfaction was high (mean 4.4/5) for both interventions, and adverse events were minimal with no serious events reported. The study population was notably diverse, with over 50% Black participants and significant representation of low-income and uninsured patients. While fewer opioids were ordered or prescribed in acupuncture groups, this finding was not statistically significant. The trial demonstrated feasibility of delivering 20-30 minute acupuncture treatments in a busy ED setting. Limitations include single-site conduct, English-only enrollment, and inability to blind patients to treatment. The authors conclude that both acupuncture styles are feasible, acceptable, and effective for ED acute musculoskeletal pain and warrant broader implementation.

Closed cell foams are widely used for thermal insulation due to their low thermal conductivity, which arises primarily from their high volume fraction of gas (since gases conduct heat less than solids) and small cell size that reduces convection and radiation. Aerogels have even lower thermal conductivity but are extremely brittle. Thermal conductivity of foams (λ*) comprises four contributions: conduction through solid (λ*s), conduction through gas (λ*g), convection within cells (λ*c), and radiation (λ*r). Conduction through gas typically dominates; convection is negligible in most foams because cells are smaller than the ~20 mm threshold where Rayleigh number exceeds 1,000. Radiation contribution increases as relative density decreases, creating a trade-off where thermal conductivity reaches a minimum at intermediate densities. Foams share the same specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient as their parent solids. Foams exhibit superior thermal shock resistance compared to solids because their lower modulus reduces thermal stress generation, with critical temperature change for cracking being greater by a factor of 0.2/√(relative density).

This study analyzes emotional expression in corporate Twitter accounts of two Spanish companies (Acciona and Iberdrola) from the Ibex 35. The corpus comprises 798 tweets published between April-June 2016. Using discourse analysis and cognitive linguistics frameworks, the research identifies prevailing emotions, verbal units that conceptualize them, and metaphors used.

Results show that emotional tweets predominate (66.5% for Acciona, 73.6% for Iberdrola), with positive emotions prevailing. "Pride" is most frequent in both accounts (27-27.9%), followed by "interest," "joy," and "confidence." Negative emotions appear minimally (3.7-4.7%).

Metaphors for happiness/joy in Iberdrola draw primarily from "light" (energy, sun, warmth), aligned with the company's mission. Acciona uses "sustainability" as a source domain for pride and confidence. The study concludes that metaphorical mappings derive from each company's mission, vision, and values, reinforcing organizational identity.

A machine learning-based automatic imaging tool was developed to predict overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma (DMG) patients from MRI scans. The method was trained and validated on 53 internal patients from Children's National Hospital and tested on 16 external patients from Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The automatic segmentation achieved mean Dice scores of 0.91 for tumor core and 0.88 for whole tumor on the internal cohort, with comparable results for whole tumor segmentation on the external cohort. The tool aims to provide consistent, repeatable tumor evaluation for multi-institutional clinical trials and improved therapeutic management.

The "Pound Cake" offense attacks the Box & One defense by isolating the star player 1-on-1 in the post area, exploiting the chaser's weakness in post defense. Base screens involve curl, fade, back cut, and screen-and-roll reads based on defender positioning. Additional options include ball reversal with post flashes, screener pops, guard basket cuts, and double mid-screens ("Horns"). Success requires proper execution of on-ball and off-ball screens, double screens, and offensive rebounding, along with defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Game strategies include scouting opponents, educating players on anticipated reads, making in-game adjustments, varying alignments, and attacking weakest defenders. The Box & One defense employs four players in a box zone with one "Chaser" in full denial of the star player.

The Supreme Court will consider whether trial courts may bar criminal defense lawyers from discussing a client's ongoing testimony with them during overnight recesses. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murder after a Texas judge prohibited him from conferring with his attorneys about his testimony overnight while he remained on the stand. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals upheld this limited restriction, citing Supreme Court precedents: a 1976 case holding that blanket bans on overnight conferences violate the Sixth Amendment, and a 1989 case permitting prohibitions on contact during brief midday recesses. Villarreal argues that any restriction on overnight discussions about testimony violates his categorical right to counsel and is unworkable in practice. Texas contends that overnight recesses differ from brief recesses because lawyers and clients naturally discuss various matters, making targeted restrictions feasible. The United States supports Texas, arguing such orders protect trial truth-finding and align with Sixth Amendment history.

Early Offense consists of three phases: initial early push, continuous flow into early set, and continuity style of play. The initial push creates outnumbered situations and mismatches before defenses organize. If unsuccessful, teams move immediately to flow phase, then continuity as the shot clock winds down. Keys to success include countering defensive pressure, playing tenacious defense to create transition opportunities, rebounding with authority, executing outlet passes, pushing the ball quickly with wide lane runners, minimizing dribbles, attacking numbered advantages, and moving seamlessly between phases without allowing defensive setup. Transition begins with defense; teams must secure the ball, make quick outlet passes, fill lanes fast, and maintain physical conditioning.

Dennis Waldron, as administrator of his wife Eugenia's estate, appealed a Supreme Court order granting summary judgment to Ball Corporation. Waldron's wife died of granulocytic leukemia in 1992. Ball sought her medical records to defend a workers' compensation claim by William Hallaban, who had the same rare leukemia and worked the same job at Ball. After Waldron refused to authorize release of his wife's records, Ball and its insurer used a medical expense claim form Waldron had previously signed to obtain the records from two hospitals without his consent.

Waldron sued for intentional infliction of emotional distress, invasion of privacy, fraud, and conversion. The appellate court affirmed dismissal of all claims: conversion failed because Waldron had no possessory interest in medical records, which belong to doctors; fraud failed because Ball's statements to Waldron were not material misrepresentations and any misrepresentations to hospitals were not made to Waldron; intentional infliction of emotional distress failed because Ball's conduct, while improper, was not "outrageous" given its legitimate business purpose and prior compassionate support to Waldron; and invasion of privacy failed because New York recognizes only a statutory right protecting name, portrait, or picture for advertising purposes, and CPLR 4504 creates no private right of action.

This study employed a single-group posttest design to evaluate an eight-week activity-based guitar lesson plan for five beginner-level students aged 18-33 with no prior instruction. The curriculum covered scales, chords, and arpeggios through online one-on-one 50-minute lessons. Data collection involved expert-approved content, theoretical knowledge tests (40% weight), and performance tests (60% weight) evaluated by three experts using a 5-point Likert scale based on Albuz's (2001) criteria: pitch accuracy (40%), tempo (10%), technique (30%), and musicality (20%). Success levels ranged from 0-30 (Very Unsuccessful) to 81-100 (Very Good). The lesson plan followed a 3E model (introduction, development, evaluation) adapted from the 5E model. Students achieved theoretical knowledge test scores of 80-100 (mean 92) and overall chapter scores of 89.2-98.8 (class average 93.6), all attaining "very good" grades. Results indicate activity-based instruction effectively facilitated student learning in amateur guitar education during the Covid-19 pandemic, supporting prior research on enhanced listening skills, engagement, and academic achievement through activity-based methods.

A study found cannabis use among people with psychosis increased by nearly 10% five years after states legalized recreational marijuana, with the rise tied to commercialization in retail shops. The passage covers distributed system design patterns, beginning with single-node patterns like the ambassador (for request splitting/experimentation using IP hashing) and adapter (for standardizing interfaces like monitoring, logging, and health checks across heterogeneous applications). It then explores multi-node patterns including replicated load-balanced services (stateless with session tracking), sharded services (for stateful data too large for one machine), and scatter/gather (for parallel computation). The text details caching layers, SSL termination, and consistent hashing for shard management. Finally, it examines event-driven architectures and FaaS (Function-as-a-Service), discussing benefits (simplicity, auto-scaling), challenges (debugging complexity, decoupling overhead), and patterns like decorators for request transformation and event handlers for asynchronous processing.

The 'Gaia' hypothesis, proposed by James Lovelock in the 1970s, suggests Earth is a self-regulating system where living things interact with inorganic processes to maintain planetary health. Researchers from the University of Exeter now propose 'sequential selection' as the mechanism: unstable life-environment interactions are short-lived until stable situations emerge, which then persist and acquire additional stabilizing traits. This addresses the original hypothesis's central problem—how evolution via natural selection could produce planet-wide stabilizing properties over geologic timescales. The findings, published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution, may help estimate the probability of complex life elsewhere and understand Earth's response to climate change and extinction events.

Mob violence expands beyond its original targets, with most lynchings not being for rape and many victims being innocent. Southern governors and religious leaders warn that lynching undermines civilization and threatens all citizens. They argue that law-abiding Black citizens must assist in bringing criminals to justice, while white citizens must reject mob justice and treat individuals based on merit rather than race. The passage advocates for capital punishment for rape through proper legal channels, immediate but fair trials protecting victims, and warns that lynching morally corrupts communities and future generations.

The passage discusses time frames in trading, recommending daily bars as the best starting point for most traders due to simplicity in backtesting and ability to identify market inefficiencies. It emphasizes being agnostic about time frames and trading multiple time frames—from minutes to decades—as a diversification tool to spread risk, optimize capital use, and reduce drawdowns. Different trader types use varying time frames: day traders use short time frames, swing traders use daily bars, and investors use years or decades. The key is finding the sweet spot between generating enough signals and maintaining an edge.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021. The company reported total revenues of $10.389 billion, up from $5.985 billion in Q1 2020, with net income of $464 million compared to $68 million in the prior year period. Total assets were $52.972 billion, with cash and cash equivalents of $17.141 billion. The company has multiple legal proceedings ongoing, including litigation related to the SolarCity acquisition and the 2018 CEO Performance Award. Construction in progress of $2.435 billion primarily includes Gigafactory Berlin, Gigafactory Texas, and expansion of Gigafactory Shanghai. Total debt and finance leases were $10.872 billion, with $1.819 billion classified as current.

The federal judiciary will use non-appropriated funds, such as court fee balances, to continue paid operations through Oct. 17 during the government shutdown. Federal judges' salaries are Constitutionally protected and will be paid regardless. Most proceedings will continue with deadlines unaffected, though some hearings may be rescheduled if executive-branch attorneys are unavailable. At least 10 district courts have issued orders delaying civil cases involving the federal government, though some judges are refusing to pause such cases. When funds deplete, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act, potentially requiring some staff to work without pay while others are furloughed.

Gillespie noted increased Tamiflu use for flu treatment. He advised seeing a doctor for illness lasting more than a few days or fever over 102°F, and recommended preparing a "flu kit" containing hand sanitizers, optional surgical masks, decongestants, pain relievers, and water. Flu shots remain available at local pharmacies.

U.S. soybean farmers face financial pressure after China halted purchases of the autumn crop for the first time in over two decades due to trade tensions and tariffs. U.S. exports have fallen, prices have dropped, and farmers are storing harvests at a loss. The federal government plans to roll out a relief package, while trade officials seek alternative buyers in smaller markets across Asia and Africa, though these cannot replace Chinese demand. The situation exposes American agriculture's vulnerability to geopolitical disputes.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine discovered that brown fat contains a "backup heater" system involving peroxisomes—cellular structures that burn fuel and release heat through a protein called ACOX2. This alternative heat source activates when mitochondria's usual heat production slows down. Mice with higher ACOX2 levels showed better cold tolerance, improved insulin sensitivity, and weight control, while mice lacking ACOX2 struggled with cold and gained more weight. The finding suggests potential dietary or drug interventions targeting this pathway to boost metabolism and address obesity.

The passage compares the Chicago Blackhawks and Philadelphia Flyers, noting both teams rebuilt quickly from poor standings three years prior. Chicago built through drafting and adding free agents like Marian Hossa and Antti Niemi. Philadelphia kept drafted players like Claude Giroux and James van Riemsdyk but built its defense through trades and signings, acquiring Kimmo Timonen, Chris Pronger, Matt Carle, and Braydon Coburn. The speaker believes Chicago will return to the finals soon while Philadelphia faces more urgency. Hockey's popularity in Philadelphia has grown, though it remains below baseball. Danny Briere moved to center due to Jeff Carter's injury and has excelled, with Carter returning to wing. The Flyers' centers—Mike Richards, Briere, and Giroux—are key to their success. A matchup between Pronger and Byfuglien is anticipated. Jonathan Toews is praised as a dynamic player comparable to greats, with strong Olympic performance. The Flyers have a desperate, underdog mentality that serves them well, driven by past injuries and the difficulty of reaching the finals.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivers significant performance improvements for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads compared to the previous generation V100. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary), with TF32 providing 10x faster performance than V100 FP32 operations. The A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which can double throughput for deep learning networks by exploiting 2:4 structured sparsity patterns.

The GPU contains 108 SMs with 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 6912 FP32 CUDA Cores, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. It features a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x larger than V100) with residency controls and Compute Data Compression for improved bandwidth efficiency.

The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability allows partitioning a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, benefiting cloud service providers with improved utilization and quality of service. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (double V100), and PCIe Gen 4 support doubles interconnect bandwidth.

CUDA 11 introduces several optimizations including Task Graph Acceleration for reduced launch overhead, Asynchronous Copy for direct global-to-shared memory transfers, Asynchronous Barriers for improved synchronization, and L2 cache residency controls. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U form factor, designed for scalable AI infrastructure.

DineEquity's stock decline has raised investor concerns about goodwill impairments at Applebee's franchise unit. Analysis of valuation methods and comparison to 2009 conditions—when no impairment occurred despite worse operating and economic environments—suggests impairment is unlikely. The 2016 franchise profit of $178.2 million exceeds 2009's $149.1 million, while the discount rate is lower (4.277% vs. 7%). Even with assumed 8% same-store sales declines in 2017-2018, fair value should exceed 2009 levels. The "at risk" warning likely stems from new 2017 accounting principles.

Casual dining struggles stem from excessive supply, not millennial avoidance, per Darden's CEO. Applebee's issues include brand misdirection, higher prices, and inconsistent operations—problems being addressed by new president John Cywinski. With only 33 franchisees, turnaround actions should proceed quickly.

DineEquity's $1.28 billion debt carries 4.277% interest with legal maturity in 2044 and anticipated repayment in 2021. Covenant thresholds require over 50% sales decline or 60% cash flow reduction to breach. The 97-cent dividend is sustainable: worst-case 2017 free cash flow of $64 million nearly covers $70 million in dividends, with $112.3 million cash and $95 million available credit providing cushion.

Increased 2017 store closures (105-135 vs. 40-60) align supply with demand. Despite Applebee's 6-8% SSS decline, 2017 adjusted EPS of $3.9-$4.5 is expected. Fair value estimate: $63 (15x $4.20 EPS), offering 6.6% annual gain plus 6.2% dividend yield.

James Swan's MIT lecture covers numerical optimization methods. He advises students to focus on numerics rather than chemical engineering science when solving problems, and to pick definitions and proceed rather than getting stuck on details.

The lecture reviews steepest descent for unconstrained optimization, where steps follow the negative gradient direction. Optimal step sizes can be estimated using quadratic Taylor expansions. Swan illustrates how steepest descent paths run perpendicular to contours and may fail to converge if no minimum exists.

He introduces conjugate gradient methods for solving linear systems (Ax=b) by minimizing quadratic functionals, requiring symmetric positive definite matrices. Conjugate directions preserve minimization from previous steps, achieving convergence in n steps for n equations without storing the full matrix.

Newton-Raphson methods use Hessian information for quadratic convergence to critical points (not just minima), but face challenges with singular Hessians and may converge to saddle points or maxima when eigenvalues are negative.

Trust-region methods combine steepest descent and Newton-Raphson heuristically: using Newton-Raphson when the quadratic approximation is reliable (step within trust region and reduces function value), otherwise using steepest descent. The trust-region radius adapts based on whether actual improvements match predicted improvements. MATLAB's optimization tools use these strategies, including dogleg variants.

A Harvard study of 501 couples found that higher seafood consumption correlates with increased sexual activity and pregnancy rates. Couples eating fish and shellfish at least twice weekly had 92% pregnancy success within a year, while those eating seafood eight or more times monthly had 22% higher sexual activity. Researchers remain uncertain whether biological factors (like zinc) or behavioral factors (shared mealtime) explain the link. The passage also notes other food-sex connections: a 2016 survey found 54% of millennials rank food equal to sex; dating data shows guacamole mentions increase message responses; apples may improve female sexual function; and a 2011 study found men think about sex every 28 minutes versus women every 50 minutes, while food occupies thoughts every 38 minutes for men and 62 minutes for women.

Emily Andrea has partnered with Monkey Monkey for a children's eyewear summer awareness campaign. The junior doctor emphasized that 80% of lifetime UV exposure occurs before age 18, making protective sunglasses important for children. She noted the brand's products are affordable and stylish, and mentioned her own children wear them.

A hockey player reflects on his unexpected journey from the minors to the Stanley Cup Finals, All-Star Game, and Olympics. He dismisses media predictions of a sweep, emphasizing his team's underdog status and motivation to prove doubters wrong. He notes that facing Chris Osgood will be as tough as facing Dominik Hasek, and stresses that good goaltending is essential for playoff success. Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon on October 24, 2001, amid an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow ran that cost the company $35 million and triggered a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. The move came after Enron's stock fell 17% to $16.41 that day and had dropped approximately 50% since October 16. CEO Kenneth Lay stated the change was necessary to restore investor confidence, though he had defended Fastow just one day prior. McMahon, formerly Enron's treasurer, had reportedly raised concerns about Fastow's partnership role in 1999. Multiple analysts downgraded Enron's stock, with Prudential Securities issuing a rare "sell" recommendation citing concerns about undisclosed information. The SEC investigation and shareholder lawsuits followed disclosures about off-balance-sheet transactions with LJM partnerships that Fastow managed. Enron's stock decline also affected other energy-trading companies, including Dynegy Inc., which fell 13%. The company faced additional concerns about other partnerships potentially requiring asset sales or equity issuance.

Williams %R is an oscillating technical indicator developed by Larry Williams that fluctuates between 0 and -100, measuring the current close relative to the highest high for a given lookback period. It is primarily used as a mean reversion indicator. Backtesting on the S&P 500 (SPY) showed that a two-day lookback period produced the best results, with a CAGR of 11.9%, profit factor of 2.2, and risk-adjusted return of 52%. The strategy performed exceptionally well during market downturns in 2008-2009 and 2020. Williams %R did not work effectively for short positions. When compared to RSI using similar criteria, Williams %R outperformed with 11.9% CAGR versus 7.3%. A combined strategy using Williams %R with a second indicator on Nasdaq (QQQ) achieved 13.4% CAGR with 96% risk-adjusted return. The authors consider Williams %R an underappreciated indicator that performs slightly better than WilliamsVixFix and outperforms RSI and Stochastics in their tested strategies.

This study investigated the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage in 22 hypertensive patients and 19 normotensive controls using a 7 Tesla dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI protocol. No significant difference in BBB leakage was found between hypertensive and normotensive groups based on dichotomous status. However, higher systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial blood pressure were positively associated with increased BBB leakage in grey matter regions, particularly cortical grey matter, independent of cardiovascular risk factors and cerebral small vessel disease markers. Medically well-treated hypertensive patients showed less BBB leakage than those with uncontrolled hypertension. The study suggests that current blood pressure, rather than hypertension status alone, affects BBB integrity, and that effective antihypertensive medication may have a protective effect.

The passage describes SPI communication protocols for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W ADC devices. Valid write operations require a minimum of 32 SCLKs per data transfer frame. Data read protocols fall into three categories: legacy SPI-compatible with single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible with dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) protocol. Four legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S) are available, with SPI-00-S as the default on power-up or reset. To change protocols, program SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in SDI_CTL_REG (first write uses SPI-00-S), then set SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. The SDI_MODE selection determines protocols for both write and read operations. When using SPI-compatible protocols, the RVS output remains low throughout data transfer.

Andrew Lo's MIT lecture covers modern portfolio theory, focusing on the efficient frontier and the capital asset pricing model. He explains how combining uncorrelated securities creates a bullet-shaped risk-return curve, with rational investors preferring the upper "efficient frontier" branch. The tangency portfolio—where a line from the risk-free rate touches this frontier—represents the optimal mix of risky assets that all mean-variance optimizing investors should hold, combined with risk-free assets according to their risk tolerance.

Lo demonstrates that adding more securities improves the risk-return trade-off through diversification, with covariances mattering more than individual variances. The Sharpe ratio measures this trade-off as excess return per unit of risk. In equilibrium, if all investors hold the same tangency portfolio, it must equal the market portfolio weighted by capitalization. This leads to the CAPM: expected return equals the risk-free rate plus beta (covariance with market divided by market variance) times the market risk premium, providing the discount rate for capital budgeting decisions.

Belarus's out-of-school education system combines Soviet and EU influences, evolving through three historical stages: pre-USSR literacy programs, Soviet-era labor and talent development, and post-1991 integration with EU lifelong learning concepts. The 2011 Education Code legally defines out-of-school education as part of lifelong learning, mandating personal development, creative abilities, and equal access regardless of background. By 2021, Belarus operated 318 institutions—185 comprehensive and 133 specialized—with regional study tours (47%) and ecosystem protection (23%) dominating specialized offerings. State-run institutions remain preferred due to lower costs, qualified faculty, and their role in organizing academic competitions that guarantee university admission. Four key cultivation objectives guide the system: IT mastery, social personality development, multicultural competence, and lifelong learning. Notable institutions include Minsk State Children's Palace for technology training, the Belarusian Youth League for social development, and the Firefighters Association for safety and career education. Challenges include funding shortages, outdated equipment, limited advertising creating unequal access, and exclusion of disadvantaged students due to costs.

The President transmits to the Senate a convention between the United States and Great Britain, concluded April 19, 1850, to establish a commercial alliance protecting a contemplated ship canal through Nicaragua and other interoceanic routes. The treaty requires no public funds, offers equal protection to all routes, and aims to secure Central American independence from foreign aggression. The President opposes annexation of Central American territories, aligning with predecessors' views. He notes France and Russia may accede to the treaty, and requests Senate advice on ratification, noting potential amendments needed to conform with a separate Nicaragua treaty.

The article presents four overnight trading strategies for the S&P 500 that buy at the close and sell at the next day's open, featuring minimal drawdowns due to short holding periods. Strategy 1 yields 8.43% profit with 29% win rate, requiring the close above the 200-day moving average—without this, performance degrades significantly. Strategy 2 produces 12.69% profit with 14% win rate and profit factor of 2.6. Strategy 3 achieves profit factor of 3.8. Strategy 4 performs best when the market is short-term oversold; holding until close when SPY opens below -0.1% boosts returns, though recent years show holding until close even on up-opens has become profitable, unlike earlier periods. Short holding periods limit drawdowns, though overnight news risk remains.

This study examines dropout tendencies among 1,061 students at Turkish public universities using Tinto's Theoretical Dropout Model. Students showed moderate overall dropout tendency (mean 2.67). No gender differences were found, but significant variations emerged: third-year and above students, non-metropolitan students, working students, and those with close friends who dropped out showed higher tendencies. Negative correlations existed between dropout tendency and school attendance frequency, parental education, GPA, and family income, while number of siblings correlated positively. Health/wellbeing and institutional factors scored highest among subdimensions. The study recommends targeted retention strategies including mentoring, financial support, and mental health services, particularly for non-metropolitan institutions.

The 2018 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon is a limited-production drag racing-focused muscle car with a starting price of $86,090. It features a 6.2-liter supercharged V8 producing 808 hp on premium fuel or 840 hp with race gas, paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission with TransBrake technology. The Louisiana Supreme Court denied Joshua W. Curran's application for supervisory and/or remedial writs in case No. 2010-KH-0233 on February 4, 2011. On a "Jeopardy!" episode before Super Bowl 52, contestants avoided the "Football" category until last, then failed to answer any of five questions about football terms, Tom Landry, fair catches, offsetting penalties, and the Minnesota Vikings' defensive line. This study reports the synthesis and characterization of ZnSe-WSe₂ and ZnSe-MoSe₂ core-shell nanowires (NWs) through selenization of sputter-deposited oxide precursors on ZnSe NWs. ZnSe NWs were first grown via chemical vapor deposition using Au nanoparticle catalysts, then coated with MoO₃ (15 nm) or WO₃ (20 nm) by DC magnetron sputtering, followed by selenization in a three-zone furnace at optimized temperatures (600–650°C for MoSe₂, 700–750°C for WSe₂). Characterization by TEM, XRD, XPS, Raman, and photoluminescence spectroscopy confirmed successful formation of the core-shell structures. TEM revealed that lower selenization temperatures produced smooth, conformal shells (~2 nm thick), while higher temperatures caused discontinuous shells with protruding TMD crystals (20–50 nm), attributed to a shift from solid-state interfacial reaction to gas-phase deposition mechanisms. The authors suggest this temperature-dependent growth behavior may extend to other TMD and van der Waals material systems, with implications for tailoring structures toward optoelectronic or catalytic applications.

A Princeton-led study published in Nature reveals that ISWI chromatin remodelers use the nucleosome's "acidic patch"—a negatively charged surface formed by histone proteins H2A and H2B—to regulate chromatin remodeling. The research found this mechanism may be general to chromatin remodeling enzymes, and that chemical modifications near the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity. The findings, generated using high throughput screening technology, provide data for future studies on chromatin modification effects and potential cancer therapeutic targets, as acidic patch mutations occur in some human cancers.

Sill reports Japan's stated desire to help Korea achieve independence from Chinese suzerainty through reforms. Japanese representative K. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon warned at Italian Tech Week that stock markets will likely experience a "drawdown" within 12 to 24 months due to excessive AI-driven investment, comparing the current situation to the dotcom bubble. Scientists from the University of Oxford have confirmed that Uranus's clouds contain hydrogen sulphide, the gas that smells like rotten eggs, using infrared data from the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii. This marks the first proof of a long-held theory. Unlike Uranus, Jupiter and Saturn contain ammonia instead, offering insights into planetary formation based on temperature and location. Researchers noted that a human descending through Uranus's clouds would face suffocation and extreme cold of negative 200 degrees Celsius before noticing the smell.

The paper introduces EduVidQA, a dataset for educational video question answering addressing the lack of interaction in online lecture videos. A survey of 52 STEM students found 67.9% wanted to ask questions while watching videos, but only 17% actually did. The dataset contains 270 real-world QA pairs from YouTube comments with expert-verified answers and 4,982 synthetic QA pairs generated from lecture transcripts. A qualitative preference study with 10 students identified Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking (ECT), and Uses Pedagogical Techniques (UPT) as important answer qualities. The authors benchmarked 6 multimodal language models, finding that finetuning smaller open-source models (7B-13B parameters) on synthetic data achieved comparable or better performance than larger closed models like GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5, with mPLUG-Owl 3 8B showing highest Clarity scores and Llava-13B achieving best ECT/UPT correlation on real-world data.

Cameroon's government plans to restore 12 million hectares of deforested land by 2030, backed by local councils, NGOs, and businesses. Environment Minister Hele Pierre called it the largest such project in the Congo Basin. The initiative, part of the 2011 Bonn Challenge, will provide $820,000 annually to local councils and $115,000 to vulnerable chiefdoms for reforestation. However, environmental experts emphasize that protecting existing forests is more critical than restoration, as indigenous forests store more carbon and harbor greater biodiversity. Cameroon has lost 777,000 hectares of forest since 2001, with half occurring since 2012. The government is pursuing both protection and restoration strategies, with increased sanctions against deforestation, though with limited success.

The killing of Kim Jong Nam, half-brother of North Korea's leader, at a Malaysian airport has renewed interest in poison as a weapon. South Korean intelligence claims female North Korean agents sprayed a toxin in his face. Various poisons have been used throughout history: ricin from castor beans, thallium in rat poison, arsenic, strychnine, and cyanide—the fastest killer and easiest to detect through bright red blood post-mortem. Poisons are difficult to store and conceal due to residues, smells, or colors. Historical poisonings include Cleopatra, Alexander the Great, and Napoleon; Victorian British housewives using arsenic on husbands; Soviet assassinations including Georgy Markov killed by ricin-tipped umbrella in 1978 and Alexander Litvinenko poisoned by Polonium-210 in 2006; the 1995 Tokyo sarin gas attack; and Indonesian activist Munir Said Thalib poisoned in 2004.

President Ford addresses Congress on fighting inflation, outlining a 10-point program for joint executive and legislative action. This paper addresses memory management challenges in long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) AI agents, specifically memory inflation and contextual degradation caused by finite LLM context windows. The authors propose a hybrid memory system with three components: Working Memory (immediate context), Episodic Memory (time-indexed vector database of interactions), and Semantic Memory (consolidated knowledge base). The core innovation is an "Intelligent Decay" mechanism that assigns utility scores to memories based on recency, relevance to current tasks, and user-assigned importance, enabling proactive pruning and consolidation rather than passive truncation. A user-centric visualization interface allows non-technical "citizen developers" to directly influence memory retention through simple actions like pinning or striking through memories. Experiments on a 500-turn software project planning task showed the hybrid system achieved 92.5% task completion (vs. 65.2% for sliding window, 81.4% for basic RAG), reduced contradictions to 1.2% (vs. 18.1%), and maintained performance over time while the "All-Add" baseline exhibited self-degradation. Limitations include hyperparameter tuning requirements and dependence on user feedback quality.

The AP Creation NAE event enables SEV-SNP guests to create, destroy, or modify AP register states at specified VMPL levels, providing an alternate AP booting method. It supports creating vCPUs with immediate or deferred VMSA installation, and destroying vCPUs. VMPL specification requires the Multi-VMPL hypervisor feature.

The #HV doorbell page NAE event allows SEV-SNP guests to register a page for hypervisor notifications when Restricted Injection is enabled. Actions include GET_PREFERRED (request hypervisor-preferred GPA), SET (establish doorbell page), QUERY (check existing configuration), and CLEAR (remove assignment).

The #HV Send IPI NAE event enables SEV-SNP guests to send IPIs to other vCPUs when Restricted Injection is enabled, using SW_EXITINFO1 formatted like the x2APIC Interrupt Command Register.

The #HV Timer NAE event provides emulated APIC timer functionality when Restricted Injection is enabled, supporting SET and GET actions for timer registers (Timer LVT, Divide Configuration, Timer Initial Count, Timer Current Count).

The APIC ID List NAE event allows guests to request APIC IDs from the hypervisor, replacing broadcast INIT-SIPI discovery. Guests supply contiguous shared pages; the hypervisor returns APIC IDs in a 4-byte count followed by 4-byte entries.

The SNP Run VMPL NAE event enables switching vCPU VMPL levels by associating unique VMSAs with each level.

The SNP TIO Guest Request NAE event supports trusted device binding, requiring Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status. Data pages return measurements, certificates, and attestation reports identified by GUID-indexed tables.

The Secure AVIC feature manages guest-owned APIC state via private backing pages per vCPU, with REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions.

The termination request NAE event allows guest-initiated termination with 64-bit information in SW_EXITINFO2 and reason codes in SW_EXITINFO1.

SEV-ES guests identify support via CPUID: ECX[31]=hypervisor, EAX[1]=SEV support, EBX[5:0]=encryption bit, EBX[11:6]=physical address reduction.

SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP requires initial AP register values to remain unmodified after measurement. Methods include reset vector memory checks or predetermined CS/IP locations. APs use AP Reset Hold NAE events or MSR protocol for subsequent boots, transitioning to real mode at SIPI-supplied vectors.

The AP jump table (4K, encrypted, page-aligned) enables OS control of AP booting, set by UEFI via SET event and retrieved by OS via GET event from the SEV-SNP Secrets Page.

The SNP AP Creation feature (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013) enables vCPU hotplug by allowing VMSA-based AP state management without AP Reset Hold requirements.

NMI handling requires hypervisor #DB interception and guest "NMI Complete" messages. Debug register virtualization is supported via "DebugVirtualization" bit in SEV_FEATURES; otherwise DR7 intercepts are used with cached values.

SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported under SEV-ES/SNP.

SNP Restricted Injection limits host notification to #HV doorbell exceptions. The doorbell page contains PendingEvent (16-bit: NoFurtherSignal[15], virtual #MC[9], NMI[8], vector[7:0]) and NoEoiRequired (byte 2). Hosts present interrupts by writing vector numbers, setting NoFurtherSignal for non-maskable events, and managing NoEoiRequired for optimized EOIs. Guests acknowledge via atomic exchange and handle EOIs through atomic NoEoiRequired clearing or explicit MSR writes.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon was owned by multiple parties, with J. & W. R. Wing of New Bedford holding the largest share (twenty sixty-fourths), and was managed by Joseph Wing and William R. Wing. On September 10, 1892, ownership was divided among several individuals and estates, all native American citizens. The vessel had 30 crew members plus a captain, whose compensation was based on shares of voyage net proceeds. Built in Dartmouth, Massachusetts in 1854 for whaling, the 201.42-ton vessel was purchased by Joseph and William R. Wing in fall 1887. It was fitted out at San Francisco in December 1891 for a year-long whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas, with no equipment for sealing.

The author thanks family, mentors, and parents for support and learning opportunities. Modern applications require high availability, reliability, and instant scalability, making distributed systems necessary for nearly all software. Building distributed systems is challenging and often bespoke, similar to pre-object-oriented programming. Containers and container orchestrators now provide reusable components that simplify creating reliable distributed systems, paralleling how objects simplified software development.

Following its 2019 season, Formula 1 reported increased attendance (4.2 million, up 2%) and TV cumulative audience (1.9 billion, up 9%), though unique viewers declined 4% to 471 million. Under Liberty Media ownership since 2016, CEO Chase Carey, CCO Sean Bratches, and Managing Director Ross Brawn sought to transform F1 from a motorsport into a global entertainment brand after inheriting an organization with minimal digital infrastructure from Bernie Ecclestone.

The sport faced challenges including predictable competition dominated by three wealthy teams (Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull), difficulty overtaking due to aerodynamic fragility, and an aging fan base despite 41% being under 35. The 2021 Concorde Agreement introduced a $175 million budget cap and car design changes to enable closer racing.

Formula 1 operated four revenue units: promotion (30% of 2019 revenue), broadcast (38%), advertising/sponsorship (15%), and other including Paddock Club and streaming. The organization pursued five strategic pillars: improving sport health, upgrading events, engaging fans digitally, expanding brand reach, and broadening global footprint. Fan engagement initiatives included Esports, Netflix's "Drive to Survive," fan festivals, and personalized content through data exchange. The sport also committed to carbon neutrality by 2030, maintaining its role as automotive technology leader.

The Pennsylvania Superior Court affirmed the judgment of sentence in Commonwealth v. Zeid, directing the appellant-defendant to appear in the lower court to be committed until he complies with the sentence or any unperformed part thereof, based on President Judge Griffith's opinion reported at 36 Pa. D. & C. 2d 101.

A hockey player reflects on winning the Stanley Cup for a second consecutive year, noting the team was able to relax and enjoy the experience more this time. He mentions the absence of defenseman Vladimir Konstantinov due to injury, expressing pride that the team won without him and one of their other best defensemen. He describes how the team never exploited Konstantinov's accident for motivation but followed his and Sergei Fedorov's recoveries closely. The player emphasizes the team's closeness as key to their success, noting they genuinely enjoy being together. He recounts the emotional moment of learning Konstantinov would be present for the Cup presentation and giving him the trophy on the ice, calling it significant given that a year prior Konstantinov was not expected to survive. The player, in his th season, expresses desire to play five more years, citing this as the most fun he's had in his career. He describes the exhausting schedule including the Olympics and playoffs. He notes the team's young core aged - will keep them competitive for years, identifying specific players as the backbone. He expresses pride in having his name on the Stanley Cup trophy. He analyzes the playoffs, stating the four-game sweep was deceiving as the Capitals series was difficult, with Dallas being physically the toughest. He credits the team's success to strong defense, four-line depth, size, and speed. He hopes coach Scotty Bowman returns, praising him as the "fire" who keeps players motivated and prevents complacency.

Carroll County's school board is requesting reconsideration of a decision to move the school system's Central Office from Westminster to the former North Carroll High School in Hampstead, despite $6 million being allocated in the county budget. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie and board members cite concerns about the non-central location, projecting 50% more miles driven and 30% more travel time for staff visiting schools, resulting in increased operating costs. The Board of Education had previously opposed the move in April, when commissioners approved it 4-1. Board member Marsha Herbert recused herself due to her teaching history at North Carroll. County Commissioners President Richard Weaver defended the budget decision, stating the school system is "just one piece of the puzzle." The board plans to send commissioners a letter detailing specific additional annual costs.

Turing GPUs improve encoding quality over Pascal and software encoders, enabling 4K streaming with lower CPU utilization. They support USB Type-C and VirtualLink for simplified VR headset connectivity through a single connector. NVLink replaces MIO/PCIe for SLI, providing higher bandwidth for advanced display topologies. Turing introduces real-time ray tracing via RT Cores, enabling physically correct lighting effects through hybrid rendering combining ray tracing and rasterization. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, making ray tracing 10x faster than Pascal. NGX provides AI-based graphics enhancement including DLSS for improved image quality and performance, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading eliminates CPU draw call bottlenecks, while Variable Rate Shading enables dynamic shading rate control for performance optimization. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal's SMP to support up to four views per pass. Turing GPUs include TU102, TU104, and TU106 variants with different configurations of CUDA Cores, Tensor Cores, and RT Cores.

This study examines Peru's structural and policy-related obstacles to medical oxygen access through a political economy analysis using qualitative interviews with 13 stakeholders and reviews of academic literature, grey literature, and policies. Peru's fragmented health system—comprising public, social security (EsSalud), and private subsystems across 24 decentralized regions—limited coordinated responses to oxygen needs. A regulatory "policy trap" requiring >99% oxygen purity concentrated market control among six large suppliers, preventing smaller providers from entering. COVID-19 exposed severe shortages, particularly in rural Andean and jungle regions, exacerbated by bureaucratic delays in lowering purity standards to 93%, lack of centralized procurement, and absence of national oxygen demand data. Civil society and private sector donations provided 496 oxygen plants, but many fell into disrepair due to lack of maintenance plans, legal clearance delays, and inadequate training. Post-pandemic, nearly 200 plants remain unused, with health establishments reverting to purchasing from primary suppliers. Interviewees emphasized the need for a National Oxygen System with supply chain management, maintenance funding, trained personnel, and equitable distribution to ensure preparedness for future health crises.

The Board increased the share repurchase authorization by $50 billion on April 30, 2020.

Cash-in-transit heists in South Africa reached record levels in 2018, with over 159 reported incidents. Three trucks were attacked within hours on Tuesday in Mthatha and Bloemfontein. The industry suffered R1.1–R1.4 million in vehicle losses within six months. In one incident, suspects failed to bomb a Fidelity truck. ARS scientists recommend that cotton farmers in the southeastern U.S. control Palmer amaranth by conventionally tilling infested fields for one year, then returning to conservation tillage for two years. This approach balances weed management with soil conservation and profitability. Research by economist Leah M. Duzy found that while conventional tillage in year one provides financial advantages due to heavy weed pressure, net returns in years two and three are similar between systems. Farmers save approximately $25.57 per acre annually by returning to conservation tillage, totaling $15,342 yearly for a typical 600-acre Alabama cotton farm. Farmers should use high-residue cover crops when plowing and resume conservation practices afterward.

White House press secretary Sean Spicer stated on April 17, 2017, that President Trump would not release his 2016 tax returns because he is under audit, despite the IRS having previously said audits do not prevent such releases. Spicer declined to say whether Trump would never release his returns, stating "We'll have to get back to you on that." The briefing followed weekend protests across the U.S. demanding Trump release his returns, a practice presidential candidates have followed for decades.

The speaker addresses a religious council, arguing that government depends on religion for moral foundations and cannot alone solve societal problems. Modern life's complexity has multiplied opportunities for crime and wrongdoing, while post-war periods typically see increased lawlessness. Government's role is limited to maintaining order and administering justice; it cannot create the moral determination to obey law, which comes from religion. Education helps but requires moral growth alongside intellectual development. American government rests on religious principles—freedom, equality, and self-government derive from belief in divine fatherhood. Historical examples show clergy shaped education and governance. True reform requires addressing moral roots, not just symptoms. The speaker concludes that despite current challenges, evidence suggests American religious faith remains strong, and emphasizes that only through religion can the nation's moral and spiritual life be enlarged and improved.

This scoping review examined methods for measuring socioeconomic status (SES) in sub-Saharan African health research. The study identified 65 articles from 22 countries, with South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana most represented. Cross-sectional designs predominated (52%), and maternal/child health was the most common theme (31%). Eleven SES categories with 41 distinct measures were identified. The asset-based Wealth Index was most frequently used (61.9%), particularly variations like the standard Wealth Index (28.6%). Principal Component Analysis was the predominant calculation method (57.7% independent use). Other measures included indices based on education/health/living standards (16.7%), and occupation/income/education (4.8%). The review found publication increases between 2020-2022, likely pandemic-related. Authors recommend standardizing SES measurement methods while allowing local contextual adjustments to improve health equity policies and interventions.

Researchers confirmed through 3D modeling and field experiments that Rapa Nui's moai statues were transported upright using a rocking, zig-zag motion with ropes and few people. The study by Carl Lipo and colleagues identified design features like forward-leaning posture and D-shaped bases that enabled movement, supported by concave roads across the island. A 4.35-ton replica was moved 100 meters in 40 minutes by 18 people, validating the physics-based approach.
