Sudan, the last male northern white rhinoceros, died in Kenya at age 45 after a severe leg infection, leaving only two females of the subspecies. Captured in 1975 and moved from a Czech zoo to Kenya's Ol Pejeta Conservancy in 2009, Sudan never reproduced despite breeding efforts. Scientists collected his sperm before his death and plan to attempt egg retrieval from the remaining females for implantation in a southern white rhino surrogate, though this procedure has never been done and carries extinction risks. The subspecies declined from 2,000 in 1960 to functional extinction due to war and poaching.

This study developed and tested maternal vulnerability segmentation tools (MVST) to identify pregnant women at risk of low utilization of essential maternal services in Oromia, Ethiopia. Using baseline data from 1,189 pregnant women, researchers created a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and information/service access dimensions. Through exploratory factor analysis, they validated four-item (urban-rural) and six-item (rural) tools with acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha ≥0.60). Higher vulnerability scores correlated with lower health facility delivery and antenatal care utilization (p<0.001). The tools enable community health workers to classify pregnant women by vulnerability level for targeted interventions, though further validation across contexts is needed.

Castle Gardens is a purpose-built care home in Invergordon offering dementia, nursing, residential and end of life care. It features en suite bedrooms with wheelchair access, TV points and nurse call systems, plus GP services, a mobile hairdresser, and pet-friendly policy. Activities include arts and crafts, baking, quizzes, animal visits, music, church services and minibus trips. The property has a mature garden, greenhouse and potting shed. The provider advises checking suitability for individual circumstances and notes that facility descriptions are supplied by the care home without responsibility for inaccuracies.

Changing global lifestyles and food habits are driving growth in the cheese snacks market, which is expected to rise at a 5.2% CAGR from 2017 to 2025 according to a Persistence Market Research report. Sedentary and hectic lifestyles have increased demand for convenient, easy-to-eat foods, with savory snacks like extruded snacks and salted chips being most popular. Westernization and altered taste preferences have expanded cheese snack consumption beyond North America and Europe worldwide. Health-conscious consumers increasingly prefer baked over fried options, and recent research highlighting cheese's nutritional benefits has boosted sales. Leading market players include Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE SA, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC Limited, and General Mills.

Soumya Swaminathan, a pediatrician and current Director General of India's ICMR, will become WHO's Deputy Director General (programmes) in late November—the first Indian to hold this position. Her priorities align with WHO Director General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus's vision: universal health coverage, epidemic response, non-communicable diseases, and access to diagnostics and drugs. She identifies preventive and promotive healthcare as a key gap in India, emphasizing health and wellness centres. Her father, Dr. M.S. Swaminathan (father of India's green revolution), noted that international exposure provides valuable perspective from his experience at the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines.

This document outlines the statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial comparing dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo in patients with diabetes. Statistical analyses will use summary tables, listings, and figures with ICH numbering conventions. Testing will be 2-sided at 0.05 significance level. Three analysis sets are defined: safety analysis set (all randomized patients who received at least one dose), full analysis set (FAS, same as safety set but with randomized treatment assignment), and per protocol set (PPS, FAS patients without relevant protocol deviations). The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods with stratified log-rank test comparing dasiglucagon versus placebo. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, analyzed using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests. Pharmacokinetic parameters will be calculated using non-compartmental analysis. Safety analyses include adverse events, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity assessments. All analyses use SAS version 9.4 or higher, with Phoenix WinNonlin for PK/PD analyses. The document also includes detailed programming specifications and quality control requirements for SAS validation.

The share of young Americans without college degrees who are disconnected from the workforce—neither working nor seeking employment—has risen significantly, reaching roughly 12% of 18- to 24-year-olds as of May 2024, higher than any year between 1989 and 2009. While some are unable to work due to disability or illness, experts cite multiple factors for the trend: young people perceiving available jobs as undesirable or insufficient to support independent living; cultural stigma against blue-collar work; mental health challenges including depression; longer periods of family financial support enabling non-work; and potential undercounting of gig workers. Proposed solutions include expanding education models with apprenticeships and reducing stigma around non-degree career paths, though experts note helping those already in their mid-to-late twenties will be difficult.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2 motion offense with no post player, requiring all five players to have passing and ball-handling skills. The continuity involves basic cuts where O1 passes to O2 and cuts to the basket, O2 passes to O3 in the middle and basket cuts, and O3 passes to O5 or O4. Players clear to corners if passes aren't received. Overplay counters include immediate back cuts when denied, with O3 back cutting when denied the middle and O2 back cutting when denied the wing. Dribble penetration is allowed when defenders overplay passing lanes, with kick-out passes if help defense sags. The back door option involves corners breaking to the middle when wings are overplayed or the shot clock is low, with O1 feeding O5 on the left and O2 feeding O4 on the right.

Deepa Das Acevedo, a legal anthropologist at Emory University, argues that political attacks on tenure address a problem that "didn't need fixing in the first place." In her book responding to the "war on tenure," she traces two decades of state legislation and university policies weakening tenure protections, noting these attacks are strategic rather than accidental. She maintains that tenure's core justifications remain valid: employment security compensates for lower academic salaries and promotes academic freedom. Contrary to critics, empirical data does not support claims that tenure de-incentivizes productivity; most professors remain committed post-tenure. Tenure does not prevent termination for just cause, including misconduct, though institutions vary in enforcement. Recent rapid dismissals of tenured faculty over social media posts demonstrate that tenure's practical protections depend entirely on institutional willingness to follow established processes, which universities increasingly disregard.

Research from Ben-Gurion University found that using smiley face emojis in work emails decreases perceptions of competence without increasing warmth, unlike face-to-face smiles. A study of 549 participants from 29 countries showed that emails without smileys received more detailed responses, and smiley use led to assumptions that the sender was female. Researchers recommend avoiding emojis in initial workplace interactions.

Regional teaching programmes are common in UK postgraduate medical education but lack guidance. A deanery covering five hospital trusts with approximately 50 Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees had no regional teaching programme and low GMC survey scores. A quality improvement project was launched, including qualitative interviews with six trainees and eight trainers using thematic analysis.

Key findings identified challenges: the new three-year Stage 1 curriculum created uncertainty; trainees faced high demands including the primary FRCA examination; trainees were heterogeneous in needs; hospitals operated in silos with variable teaching quality; and implementation faced logistical barriers including location, funding, rota organisation, and quality control. However, participants saw benefits including fairness, better exam preparation, social networking, and easier organisation for smaller hospitals. Both groups supported developing a regional programme, with trainers willing to collaborate and trainees offering suggestions for sustainability. The study informed specific QIP actions including a trainee survey and engagement with hospital education leaders. Limitations included small trainee sample size and potential interviewer bias.

This study presents the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) of neonatal jaundice, analyzing nearly 30,000 parent-offspring trios from Norway. Researchers identified two genome-wide significant loci: a missense variant in UGT1A4 (rs6755571) with a five-fold protective effect, and a variant near CHRDL1 on the X chromosome. The UGT1A4 variant showed colocalization with UGT1A1 expression in colon but not liver, suggesting intestinal rather than hepatic bilirubin conjugation may be primary in neonates. Maternal GWAS revealed ABO blood group incompatibility effects. Notably, adult bilirubin level variants, including the top UGT1A1*28 variant and SLCO1B1, showed minimal association with neonatal jaundice, indicating context-specific genetic mechanisms. The study demonstrates substantial differences between neonatal and adult bilirubin genetics, with polygenic scores for adult bilirubin levels losing predictive power when excluding the UGT1A region.

U.S. Border Patrol agent Larry O'Neal, 44, of Houlton faces federal child pornography charges after being indicted Feb. 15 for possession of sexually explicit images of children on his personal computer. Homeland Security agents traced a downloaded file to his IP address in January, searched his home on Jan. 19, and found child and adult pornography on his computer and external drive. O'Neal pleaded not guilty Feb. 22 and admitted to downloading the material using search terms including "young," "rape," and "teen hardcore." No evidence was found on his work computer. He was released on bail and faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted.

This patent application describes a hard-sided, collapsible shelter or camper that provides rigid protection while remaining highly portable. The shelter features bi-fold or multi-fold wall panels, a roof section, and a floor section that transition between an expanded configuration for occupancy and a collapsed configuration for transport. In the expanded configuration, the shelter forms a weather-tight, lockable enclosure with standing height; in the collapsed configuration, it becomes a low-profile case suitable for roof rack mounting, truck bed storage, or towing by various vehicles including bicycles. The design includes options for climate control, solar panels, batteries, plumbing, kitchenettes, bathrooms, and a movable bed platform. Wall panels fold parallel to the floor and roof when collapsed, with staggered hinge points allowing panels to nest. The shelter addresses the trade-off between portability and protection in existing camping shelters by combining rigid construction with compact storage.

The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1), data sheet (Exhibit 99.2), and supplemental materials (Exhibit 99.3). The information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 unless expressly referenced. Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, signed the report.

The article examines pivot points trading strategies through backtesting on S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF markets from 2010 to present. Pivot points are calculated from the previous day's high, low, and close average, with derived support and resistance levels. Six strategies were tested on 1-minute futures data, with only the first strategy showing modest results in Nasdaq (62% win rate, 0.16% average gain). The authors conclude that pivot points are largely ineffective as standalone strategies, though some day trading ideas warrant further research. Lewis Borsellino, a prominent 1980s-90s pit trader, used pivot points but provided no specifics. Pros include objectivity and versatility; cons include lagging price and low win ratios. Pivot points were invented by floor traders and are less relevant in modern electronic markets.

RWE Supply & Trading may double or triple its LNG derivatives trades this year from 2017's 1.5 million tonnes, driven by Asia's shift from oil-linked prices and risk management needs for physical cargoes. The company traded 6 million tonnes of physical LNG in 2017, up from 4.5 million tonnes in 2016. New Asian buyers and fragmented demand are increasing short-term trading. RWE has traded 7-10 physical cargoes on the JKM index this year, matching its 2017 total. JKM LNG swaps volumes quadrupled in 2017 to 50,266 lots.

The lecture begins with administrative announcements, including delaying the next problem set to Tuesday. The instructor recaps the number four-vector \(N\), describing particle number density and flux for dust, and its covariant conservation law (vanishing spacetime divergence).

The main topic is the stress-energy tensor \(T^{\alpha\beta}\). For dust, it is defined as the tensor product of the number four-vector and four-momentum, yielding \(T^{\alpha\beta} = \rho_0 u^\alpha u^\beta\), where \(\rho_0\) is rest energy density and \(u\) is four-velocity. Physically, \(T^{\alpha\beta}\) represents the flux of momentum component \(\alpha\) in direction \(\beta\): \(T^{00}\) is energy density, \(T^{0i}\) is energy flux (equivalent to momentum density), and \(T^{ij}\) is momentum flux or stress. The tensor is symmetric (\(T^{\alpha\beta} = T^{\beta\alpha}\)), motivated by the requirement that torque on an infinitesimal fluid element must vanish to prevent unphysical infinite angular acceleration.

Conservation of energy and momentum is expressed covariantly as the vanishing spacetime divergence \(\nabla_\alpha T^{\alpha\beta} = 0\). In a specific reference frame, this separates into distinct conservation equations for energy and momentum.

Examples include:
- **Perfect fluid**: In its rest frame, \(T^{\alpha\beta} = \text{diag}(\rho, p, p, p)\), with covariant form \(T^{\alpha\beta} = (\rho+p)u^\alpha u^\beta + p g^{\alpha\beta}\). Dust is a perfect fluid with zero pressure.
- **Point particle**: Described using Dirac delta functions localized on the worldline.
- **Electromagnetic fields**: Components include energy density \((E^2+B^2)/8\pi\), the Poynting vector for energy flux, and spatial stresses representing anisotropic pressure.

The lecture transitions to mathematical preliminaries for gravity, introducing flat spacetime in curvilinear coordinates (e.g., polar coordinates). In a coordinate basis, the basis vector \(e_\phi\) has dimensions of length and is not normalized. Transformation matrices \(L^\alpha_{\bar{\mu}} = \partial x^\alpha / \partial x^{\bar{\mu}}\) between coordinate systems mix dimensions, resulting in a non-constant metric.

Art teacher Kenneth Hobbs unveiled the second panel of a 22-foot Wolverine mural at Lawton High School's cafeteria. The new 10-foot by three-foot section, funded by the class of 2014, depicts the school's front and south side, a "Hanta Yo!" sign, and a Wolverine breaking out of a pixilated frame. It connects to the first panel, funded by the class of 2006 and unveiled in May 2010, which shows three historical school buildings and a timeline of athletic championships. The second panel adds the 1993 National Wrestling Champions and their coaches to the timeline, joining the 1927 National Women's Basketball Team already depicted on the first panel.

The passage discusses research contradicting the common belief that racial, ethnic, and language-minority children are overrepresented in U.S. special education. Federal policies have been enacted to reduce this perceived disproportionate representation, requiring local agencies to report overrepresentation and allocate funds accordingly. However, the cited study found that after adjusting for confounding factors like socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavioral functioning, minority children are actually significantly underidentified for disabilities compared to similar White children. Black children were 23-77% less likely to be identified with various disabilities, while Hispanic children were 29-73% less likely. The author questions who loses when minority children who might benefit from special education are mainstreamed instead, given that current federal efforts aim to reduce their representation despite evidence of underidentification based on actual need.
The speaker disagrees with Curtis on limiting opponents' puck possession in the team's defensive zone against Mike and Joe Nieuwendyk, and notes Brett's potential absence would help.

Minnesota nonprofits provide specialized mental health services in public schools, complementing existing school-based care. Know the Truth offers peer substance use support, employing recovery specialists like Tiffany White who share personal experiences with students. Restoration for All provides culturally specific mental health services for African immigrant and refugee youth, addressing gaps in cultural understanding among school staff. Both programs rely on grants and contracts, with recent federal funding cuts affecting some services.

South Korea's spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, half-brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Monday. U.S. sources also believe North Korean assassins murdered him. South Korean intelligence believes he was poisoned, and that Kim Jong Un had issued a standing order for his assassination following a failed 2012 attempt. Kim Jong Nam had lived in Macau under Chinese protection and publicly opposed his family's dynastic rule. Malaysian police confirmed a woman was involved in the attack seen on CCTV, though the cause of death remains under investigation. South Korea's acting president condemned the regime's brutality. Malaysia, which maintains close relations with North Korea, is conducting an autopsy.

A Salvadoran woman who fled to the U.S. after losing two children to gang violence was deported back to El Salvador under the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy, joining thousands of Central Americans fleeing violence who were caught and returned. Despite Trump's claims about gang members "infesting" the U.S., only 0.09% of 2017 Border Patrol detentions involved Central American gang members; most were violence refugees. El Salvador faces severe gang control by MS-13 and Barrio 18, with extortion, forced prostitution, and killings common. Police and military contribute to 10-15% of violence. An estimated 90% of deportees attempt re-migration within days due to lack of safe alternatives in the small country.

Thames Centre councillor Kelly Elliot is advocating for the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a policy requiring automated external defibrillators (AEDs) in all schools. A student at West Nissouri Public School fundraised for an AED after a local child's death, but the board declined installation. Elliot notes TVDSB is Ontario's only school board without such a policy, while the London District Catholic School Board has AEDs in every school maintained by Middlesex County EMS. Despite raised funds and a $2,000 maintenance donation, the board continues to resist. The board has not commented.

The Washington Court of Appeals, Division Two, affirmed on March 18, 1991, a September 18, 1989 Superior Court judgment in favor of Kitsap County in a case brought by Tom Belcher and others. The unpublished opinion by Chief Judge Worswick, concurred in by Judges Alexander and Morgan, was later published at 60 Wn. App. 949.

Miami Hurricanes guard Adrienne Motley passed Octavia Blue to become No. 7 on the school's all-time scoring list during an 81-57 victory over Clemson. The game also celebrated the women's athletic program and honored late coach Kay Yow through the annual Play4Kay event. Teammate Jessica Thomas reached 1,200 career points, and Miami led for over 36 minutes, outscoring Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. The Hurricanes (19-6, 8-5 ACC) next face No. 14 Duke.

Eric Bass forwarded a Dallas Morning News "Inside UT Football" newsletter from October 12, 2000, to several Enron colleagues. The newsletter, written by Chip Brown, covers Texas Longhorns football topics including: the upcoming do-or-die game against Colorado (where a loss would likely eliminate UT from Big 12 title contention); Major Applewhite being named sole starting quarterback over Chris Simms for the Colorado game; promotions for freshmen receivers Roy Williams and B.J. Johnson to starting positions; and increased playing time for running back Kenny Hayter. The Q&A section addresses fan questions about the quarterback rotation, offensive play-calling, defensive struggles, recruiting, and coaching decisions following the Oklahoma loss.

Weiss Realty. At 204 Glen Cove Road in Carle Place, Jersey Mike's Subs leased 2,250 square feet, Hand and Stone Massage leased 3,000 square feet, and Fortunoff Bedding leased 4,500 square feet in the Plaza 200 shopping center, with Greg Batista, Joann Argent, and David Lucas/Fred Feinblum representing the respective tenants, and Christopher Wierzbicki representing landlord Pliskin Realty & Development. Weiss Realty. U.S. stocks rose Wednesday, with banks, energy companies, and smaller companies leading gains, as investors hoped Italy would avoid new elections. The S&P 500 gained 1.3% to 2,724.01, the Dow rose 1.3% to 24,667.78, the Nasdaq added 0.9% to 7,462.45, and the Russell 2000 jumped 1.5% to 1,647.99. For the week, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were up slightly while the Dow declined. Year-to-date, the Nasdaq and Russell 2000 posted strong gains of 8.1% and 7.3% respectively, the S&P 500 rose 1.9%, and the Dow fell 0.2%.

A Valencia man wounded in the Las Vegas mass shooting has filed a lawsuit against gunman Stephen Paddock's estate. Travis Phippen, whose father John was killed in the attack, filed the suit in Nevada District Court through attorney Rick Patterson of Owen, Patterson & Owen. The lawsuit seeks control of Paddock's assets, including bank accounts, safe deposit boxes, and real property. At least 59 people were killed and 527 wounded when Paddock fired from Mandalay Bay during the Route 91 Harvest festival. Three other Santa Clarita Valley residents remain hospitalized.

Scale AI billionaire Alexandr Wang, 28, advises 13-year-olds to spend all their time "vibe-coding"—using AI to generate software through natural language prompts—arguing that 10,000 hours of practice with AI coding tools will create a career-defining advantage, similar to how early computer use benefited Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg. Wang, who became the youngest self-made billionaire in 2022 and now leads Meta's AI superintelligence team, believes AI automation is shrinking traditional tech jobs, making early, deep engagement with AI tools urgent for aspiring tech workers.

A petition to save Gresford Health Centre from closure has attracted over 600 signatures. Alyn Family Doctors plans to shut the Gresford branch and amalgamate patients with surgeries in Llay and Rossett due to staffing shortages. Patients fear travel difficulties and increased pressure on remaining surgeries, especially with proposed housing developments in Llay and Rossett. The health board is supporting feedback collection from patients on the proposal.

When a penalty kick is awarded during normal play, defending players must position themselves at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the mark, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. Once the ball is kicked and moves forward, it is live and defenders must react immediately to secure rebounds, box out attackers, and clear the ball. Defenders should hold their ground if they reach position first, or stand beside attackers if beaten to a spot. They must remember the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player has touched it. After securing or clearing the ball, defenders should transition quickly to attack. Coaches should practice positioning and reaction drills, including defending against rare "tap" penalty kicks where a teammate rushes in to shoot after a tap. These rules do not apply to penalty shoot-outs, which follow different procedures with no follow-up allowed.

This patent application describes a gaming machine that synchronizes event display timing with background music (BGM) beats. The machine includes a display, speaker, storage device storing BGM tempo data and sound data, and a controller. The controller determines event display timing based on BGM tempo data, dynamically configures animation data accordingly, and displays it. This synchronization applies to player-operated events, randomly determined events, and multiple events following rhythm patterns. Specific implementations include slot machine reel stops and bonus games, where animations are timed to match BGM beats using frame counts derived from tempo data. The system can also synchronize event sounds and illumination with the BGM.

The speaker expresses gratitude for being elected to high office and acknowledges the weight of responsibility. They review the success of American self-government over 40 years, noting prosperity, expanded territory, protected rights, and successful navigation of foreign wars. The speaker identifies the people's virtue and intelligence as the foundation of this success, warning that corruption and ignorance pose the greatest internal threat. External dangers require military preparedness through fortifications, standing forces, and especially a well-organized militia. Other priorities include internal improvements like roads and canals, support for domestic manufactures, fair treatment of Indian tribes, maintenance of national credit, and strict accountability in public finance. The speaker emphasizes preserving peace, fostering national harmony, and maintaining the Constitution's principles through an enlightened and virtuous citizenry.

This study explores barriers and facilitators to implementing metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnostics through qualitative interviews with ten UK stakeholders. Five themes emerged: diagnostic choice (cost, speed, and toolkit integration), infrastructure (training gaps, accreditation challenges, digitalization needs), open data sharing (privacy concerns versus surveillance benefits), COVID-19's proof-of-concept value, and communication gaps within hospitals, between hospitals, and with commercial sectors. Key barriers include high costs, slow turnaround times, lack of bioinformatics training, research-only reagents, inadequate data storage systems, and siloed hospital departments. Participants viewed mNGS as complementary to existing tools rather than a replacement, emphasizing need for local infrastructure, equitable funding distribution, and improved stakeholder collaboration. COVID-19 demonstrated mNGS utility and increased manufacturing capacity, though centralised UK models delay results. The study concludes that addressing infrastructure, cost-effectiveness evidence, and communication could advance routine clinical adoption.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs)—porous molecular structures that can trap gases, water, and chemicals. Robson created the first such structure in the late 1980s by combining copper ions with organic compounds. Kitagawa later developed MOFs that could absorb gases like methane, nitrogen, and oxygen. Yaghi created an extremely porous MOF in 1999 with surface area equivalent to a soccer field in just a few grams. Applications include water harvesting from air, capturing greenhouse gases, and extracting PFAS chemicals. The three share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

NHS workers at Sandwell Hospital recreated a 1927 photograph of nursing staff to mark the NHS's 70th anniversary. The original image was discovered in a broom cupboard earlier this year. Fourteen staff members participated in the recreation at the same location nearly 90 years later. The photographs will be displayed during an NHS anniversary tea party at the hospital.

Professor Andrew Lo discusses an auction demonstration where a smaller package (an iPod) sold for $45 while a larger package (his hedge fund book, retailing at $45) sold for $60, illustrating how information asymmetry affects valuation. He then transitions to current events, explaining the federal government's takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac—government-sponsored entities that purchase mortgages from regional banks to make credit more available. These institutions had grown too large to fail, and their potential default threatened major international investors including sovereign wealth funds. The Treasury backed their obligations to prevent market panic, though this creates inflation risks and burdens taxpayers. Lo notes shareholders face near-total losses while counterparties holding their debt are protected.

He then begins the core lecture on present value, defining an asset as a sequence of current and future cashflows (not past ones). Using currency exchange as an analogy, he explains that cashflows at different times are like different currencies requiring conversion rates. The value operator V converts cashflow sequences to numbers, with one implementation being market price. Under perfect certainty, net present value equals the sum of cashflows multiplied by discount factors (exchange rates between time periods), which are obtained from markets. These discount factors relate to an interest rate r, where $1 in year T equals $1/(1+r)^T in today's dollars. This framework allows valuation of any certain cashflow sequence, reducing management decisions to simple questions about whether positive NPV projects should be accepted.

VentureWire's November 7, 2000 issue covers private company business news including Broadcom's $2 billion acquisition of SiByte, Alta Partners raising $300 million for Fund III, Furniture.com shutting down, and eStellarNet's $30 million first round. The issue details numerous funding rounds across sectors including IT equipment, e-commerce, fiber-optics, wireless, and real estate technology. Notable funding includes Dotcast's $60 million third round, Stellcom's $50 million Series B, and Centric Software's $30 million Series D. M&A activity includes Sonus acquiring Telecom Technologies for over $451 million and InfoSpace acquiring Locus Dialogue for $128 million. The issue also reports layoffs at Divine interVentures, company name changes, new executive appointments, and venture capital fund news including Westbridge's $140 million Indian technology fund and Osprey Ventures' planned $100 million second fund.

Sergio Romero visits the Avontuur, a 97-year-old sailing schooner, at Puerto Cortés in northern Honduras. Unlike modern cargo ships that use bunker fuel, the wind-powered vessel transports small cargo between Europe and the Caribbean with a minimal crew.

This report examines Title IX staffing trends in higher education from 2019-20 to 2023-24, finding that dedicated Title IX positions grew 38% but 56% of institutions still lack full-time staff. Most Title IX offices reside in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs (28%). Three positions are tracked: heads of compliance (31% of institutions), investigators (16%), and deputy heads (12%). Doctoral institutions have the most positions (64%), while associate's colleges have the fewest (19%). Women hold 77% of Title IX positions, with Black women notably overrepresented at 13% versus 6% in professional roles overall. Unlike broader higher education trends, Title IX staff show pay equity, with women and people of color earning comparable or higher median salaries than White men. The report recommends institutions reassess Title IX officer responsibilities, increase dedicated staffing, and prepare for potential regulatory changes under the Trump administration.

A speaker acknowledges team effort but criticizes lack of unity in recent play, emphasizing that talk must translate to action during a crucial time. They note that childhood dreams and limited injury excuses should motivate performance. They suggest prior experience with key injuries has prepared other players to step up if "griz and z" remain unavailable.

Berkshire Hathaway sold its 10.6 million share stake in General Electric in Q2 2017, ending a $3 billion crisis-era investment that generated over $1 billion in profit. The sale coincided with GE's leadership change and 20% stock decline. Berkshire also bought shares in Synchrony Financial and added to Bank of New York Mellon and Apple positions. Other investors' Q2 moves included David Tepper selling his entire SPDR S&P 500 ETF stake, George Soros purchasing over $1 billion in PowerShares QQQ Trust, and Viking Global buying 12.3 million Wells Fargo shares worth about $680 million.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, a convicted sex offender from Cottage Hills, was arrested Thursday in Grafton and charged with a Class 4 felony for loitering within 500 feet of a park. Darnell approached children near a river offering fishing equipment, prompting a concerned adult to contact police. His sex offender status stems from a 2003 or 2004 conviction for sexually assaulting a one-year-old child. Jersey County State's Attorney Ben Goetten stated his office will seek maximum penalties if convicted.

His Majesty seeks formal diplomatic recognition from the United States as a sovereign and independent state, citing previous informal acknowledgments through consular appointments and naval commanders' dealings. He emphasizes rapid modernization over 23 years: development of a written language, establishment of schools, creation of a constitutional monarchy with representative government, enactment of civil and criminal codes, and establishment of jury-based courts. Foreigners have used these courts for significant property disputes. His Majesty argues that his kingdom provides essential services to global whaling fleets and serves as a critical Pacific waystation for vessels traveling between the Americas and Asia, offering superior repair facilities and supplies.

This study examines kindergarten teachers' views on visual arts in early childhood education in Piraeus, Greece. The literature review establishes that visual arts promote children's expression, communication, skills development, self-esteem, and cultural literacy. Research shows arts support emotional development, socialization, cooperation, problem-solving, and inclusion, particularly for children with disabilities and non-native speakers.

The study surveyed 65 teachers (81.5% women, mostly aged 23-42 with 1-5 years experience, 89.2% without visual arts training). Results indicate 87.7% strongly agree or agree that visual arts are crucial in early childhood education. Teachers observed benefits including imagination and creativity development (89.2%), self-confidence and social skills (21.5%), and motor skills (16.9%). Most (87.7%) consider visual arts important for intellectual development, and 81.5% believe art activities promote social interaction.

Regarding teaching approaches, 41.5% strongly agree that visual arts are well-integrated into the curriculum. The most effective strategies reported were free approach (33.1%), experimentation with various materials and tools (30.7%), group teaching (15.3%), and guided approach (13.8%). Positive feedback was considered important by 87.7% of teachers. Children's interest in art activities was rated high or very high by 76.9%.

The main challenges identified were classroom management (86.1%), followed by external factors like time constraints and lack of resources (10.7%). Solutions included individualized instruction, patience, demonstrating techniques, rewarding achievements, and providing diverse materials.

The study found demographic factors did not significantly influence teachers' perceptions of visual arts usefulness. Teachers emphasized the need for professional development programs, adequate resources, and dedicated art spaces to overcome implementation barriers. Limitations included the electronic survey format and lack of qualitative depth from interviews.

A Spring ISD middle school teacher at Dueitt Middle School is on administrative leave after allegedly calling African American students "cotton pickers" on Wednesday. Parent Roshonda Davis reported the incident to the superintendent after her daughter informed her. Other students confirmed hearing the slur, leading to the teacher's removal. The district stated it takes such reports seriously, and Davis expressed satisfaction with the district's response. The investigation is ongoing.

The German Ambassador conveyed Germany's confidential peace terms, including willingness to restore Belgium (with Meuse travel rights), maintain Holland, Denmark, and Belgium as neutral buffer states, return French coastal territory and Russian territory, and properly treat Serbia and Romania. He noted British hesitation to state terms stemmed from allied disagreements over maximum demands versus minimum acceptable terms, and that American pressure might prompt England to confidentially reveal its terms. Separately, the Greek Chargé communicated his government's response to U.S. peace proposals, expressing appreciation for President Wilson's initiative while noting Greece's severe suffering as a neutral nation under blockade and foreign occupation. Greece stated readiness to join peace consolidation efforts when possible, though currently excluded from communication with one belligerent and awaiting resolution of difficulties with others.

This passage details defensive strategies for disrupting side screen/roll plays in basketball, focusing on "On Ball" switching scenarios above and below the free throw line. Below the free throw line, an aggressive trap is used with specific rotations through phases: hard double team, pass out of post trap, and final match-up positions, with variations for skip passes and passes to low post. Above the free throw line, an aggressive contact switch denies jump shots and middle penetrations through three phases: contact switch, snuggle pass denial, and smother position. The "All Out" disruption strategy involves trapping the point guard before any screen is set, forcing the offense into freelance play. This includes phases for double teaming, pass out of trap, and secondary trap on base roll, with all rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

Whitman Howard raised Produce Investments Ltd's price target from GBX 210 to GBX 240 and maintains a buy rating. Shore Capital and Numis Securities also have buy ratings, with Numis setting a GBX 286 target. Produce Investments shares traded at GBX 187.00, up 0.54%, with a market cap of GBX 50.52 million. The company declared a GBX 5.03 dividend payable December 5th, yielding 2.75%. Produce Investments PLC grows, sources, packs and markets potatoes, daffodil bulbs and flowers through fresh, processing and other segments.

Amazon.com, Inc. entered into a 364-day revolving credit agreement on November 18, 2022, with JPMorgan Chase Bank as administrative agent, providing up to $10 billion in unsecured borrowing capacity. The agreement carries an initial interest rate of Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 0.45% and a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts. Funds may be used for general corporate purposes including backstopping commercial paper. The agreement contains customary terms but no financial covenants.

Marines with Task-Force-Southwest practiced flying Instant-Eye drone technology at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, for surveillance in confined areas; the task force will deploy to Afghanistan in spring to train Afghan forces. Marines with 2nd Law Enforcement Battalion completed grenade-assault training February 9th at Camp Lejeune for an upcoming exercise in California. The Marine Corps awarded the Purple Heart to 91-year-old Lee Anderson on February 9th for injuries sustained at Iwo Jima 72 years prior.

Three University of Dayton female students reported separate incidents early Wednesday morning where a naked man entered their bedrooms. The first incident occurred around 3:15 a.m. on Woodland Ave., the second around 4 a.m. on Frericks Way where the suspect attempted to restrain the student, and a third about 15 minutes later on College Park. In all cases, the suspect—a white male in his mid-20s, approximately 5'10", medium build, with brown curly hair—entered through unsecured windows or a door and fled when confronted. University police are investigating.

President Washington addresses Congress on the prosperous state of the nation, noting progress in agriculture, manufacturing, commerce, and navigation. He reports on western frontier defense efforts, including treaties with friendly Indian tribes and military operations against hostile ones, while expressing hope for peaceful relations. He details implementation of the whiskey tax, establishment of the permanent capital district on the Potomac, completion of the census showing nearly four million inhabitants, and loans obtained in Holland. Washington submits two Indian treaties for Senate ratification, reports successful debt subscription funding, and urges attention to remaining matters including the militia, post office, mint, weights and measures, and sale of western lands.

Corey Perry is a young, experienced player who has succeeded at the major junior level with the London Knights and handled intense situations well. His participation in last year's playoffs provided valuable learning experience. He is described as an effective, "greasy" player with good hands who works well down low with the puck.

The team includes extra players in regular practices rather than separating them as "black aces" to support team building and educate them on lifestyle expectations in pressure situations.

A player's hand injury makes his return doubtful pending medical clearance.

The coach emphasizes starting strong, maintaining an even emotional keel through success and adversity, and focusing on the next game. The team has strong leadership committed to sacrifice and playing their system. Veterans remind younger players that Stanley Cup opportunities are rare, but preparation remains consistent: work hard, stay committed, and play the best game possible.

Hampton and Newport News Police apprehended a 15-year-old suspect following a January 31 robbery at a Tinee Giant convenience store. A witness followed the suspect's Ford SUV after the robbery, saw someone toss an object and fire shots from the vehicle, then provided information to police. Newport News Police later located the SUV on Newsome Drive and found the teen nearby with a handgun. He faces charges including possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and underage firearm possession, but no robbery charges have been filed.

Colleges face criticism for lacking viewpoint diversity, with faculty historically skewing left. However, definitions of viewpoint diversity vary widely: Heterodox Academy emphasizes socioeconomic, political, and cultural differences; Florida defines it as exposure to varied ideological perspectives; conservative critics and the Trump administration offer less clear definitions. The administration is now tying federal grant advantages to universities that adopt specific policies, including banning race and sex-based hiring, freezing tuition, capping international enrollment, requiring standardized tests, and maintaining a "vibrant marketplace of ideas." Education Secretary Linda McMahon also indicated "patriotic" education will factor into discretionary grants. Research shows students will pay higher tuition to attend colleges with fewer opposing political views, suggesting colleges may increasingly market viewpoint diversity to attract enrollment. Critics warn that conditioning federal funding on political compliance risks making higher education serve White House priorities rather than genuine intellectual diversity.

A Sarasota couple was arrested after accepting a package containing carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is 10,000 times more potent than morphine. The package was intercepted by Homeland Security and delivered under surveillance to Michael Bennett, 39, and Trisha Steffes, 36. They admitted knowing the package contained carfentanil. A search of their home found over 7 grams of fentanyl in a false electrical outlet and other drugs. Both face charges including delivery of carfentanil and possession of fentanyl with intent. Bennett was released on $15,500 bond; Steffes was also charged with oxycodone possession and released on $17,000 bond.

This patent application describes display devices with crack sensing circuits protected from static electricity. The display panel includes a display area with pixels, a pad area with input pads, and a circuit area with a crack sensing circuit. A crack sensing line extends around the display area with one end connected to an input pad. The crack sensing circuit includes static electricity discharge elements (capacitors) positioned at the center area of the circuit area, between switching elements that connect test data lines to pixel data lines. These capacitors store or discharge static electricity to prevent damage to switching elements and erroneous defect detection during testing. The display panel may include a bending area between the display and circuit areas, with voltage transmitting lines and crack sensing lines positioned at the same layer in the bending area. Multiple sub-capacitors may connect to sub-wires of test data lines.

Alexander Zverev defeated Dusan Lajovic in a five-set marathon at the French Open, advancing to the third round despite his history of struggling at grand slams. Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also overcame 2-1 set deficits in lengthy matches. Dominic Thiem's match against Stefanos Tsitsipas was suspended due to darkness. World No. 1 Simona Halep recovered from a slow start to beat Alison Riske. Novak Djokovic advanced after a tough match against Jaume Munar, continuing his comeback from elbow surgery. Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina won in straight sets.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 15, 2019, notifying participants in its 401(k) Plan of a temporary blackout period expected from January 2, 2020 to the week of January 12, 2020. The restriction on exchanges, loans, and withdrawals was necessary for transitioning recordkeeping to Fidelity Investments. The company also notified Section 16 officers and directors that they would be subject to trading restrictions during this period.

The Foreign Relations series editors have complete access to retired State Department records including central files, decentralized bureau/office files, Executive Secretariat files, and overseas diplomatic post files. State Department files from 1981–1989 will eventually transfer to the National Archives after declassification. Research for this subseries uses special access to restricted documents at the Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies; some printed material comes from still-classified documents. The Reagan Library preserves significant foreign affairs documentation from White House offices, State Department, NSC, CIA, Defense Department, and Joint Chiefs of Staff. Some research used RAC project scanned collections, though attachment status was sometimes unclear. Documents are presented chronologically by Washington time. Editorial methodology follows Office style guidelines, reproducing originals as exactly as possible with supplied headings, preserved spelling and punctuation (except silent correction of obvious errors), bracketed corrections and additions, italicized underlined text, preserved abbreviations, and detailed footnotes indicating sources, classifications, and reading by officials.

This patent application describes systems and methods for indicating wireless channel status in 5G New Radio communications, particularly for beam failure recovery scenarios. The disclosure addresses the need for mechanisms to handle quasi-co-located (QCL) relationships between reference signals and data/control channels after beam failure occurs in high-frequency millimeter wave systems.

Two main example embodiments are presented. In the first embodiment, after beam failure recovery, a user equipment (UE) assumes a QCL relationship exists between a newly selected beam and downlink reference signals for physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) or physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH) decoding, using the same spatial domain receive filter until updated QCL configuration is received. In the second embodiment, after beam failure recovery, the UE assumes no QCL configuration exists and uses only demodulation reference signals for detection or decoding until TCI states are updated.

The application details various sub-embodiments for handling TCI field presence or absence in downlink control information, including predetermined value settings, mapping updates between TCI states and DCI fields, and different decoding assumptions based on scheduling timing relative to threshold values. The described techniques aim to reduce signaling overhead and improve communications system performance during beam failure recovery periods.

Parents and caregivers can help children become better conversationalists and cultivate curiosity by using five strategies: asking specific, open-ended questions instead of rote ones; engaging with children's questions rather than dismissing them; modeling curiosity by asking their own questions; showing children how to find answers when they don't know something; and practicing active listening by repeating what was heard and avoiding multitasking. These approaches help children develop confidence in asking and answering questions while maintaining their natural wonder and enthusiasm for learning.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between physical activity and self-esteem among 225 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul, Turkey. Data were collected using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF) and Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (ROSE). Results showed that males had higher self-esteem and MET scores than females. Regular exercise was associated with higher self-esteem. A positive correlation was found between self-esteem and physical activity (MET scores), as well as between self-esteem and height, and self-esteem and self-reported school success. No significant relationship was found between BMI and self-esteem. The study notes limitations including its specific population of high-achieving students in a developed urban area and reliance on self-reported data.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

Canadian researchers studying blood samples from nearly 3,000 Toronto residents found celiac disease affects about one per cent of the population, with 90 per cent of cases undiagnosed. Professor Ahmed El-Sohemy of the University of Toronto led the study to understand potential nutritional deficiencies from the disease, which triggers immune reactions damaging the small intestine. The findings align with international data. Celiac disease has a strong genetic component, affecting those unable to fully digest wheat proteins. Diagnosis requires antibody blood tests and intestinal biopsy while patients consume gluten; many follow gluten-free diets without confirmed diagnosis, complicating detection. Gastroenterologists note symptoms like fatigue are common to other conditions. The study, published in BMJ Open, was funded by Canadian Institutes of Health Research; El-Sohemy founded a nutritional genetic testing company, creating potential conflict of interest.

U.S. stocks firmed on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised the fed-funds rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1%-1.25% and announced plans to gradually reduce its $4.5 trillion balance sheet "this year." The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 2,431, with consumer staples and utilities leading gains while materials and energy declined. The Dow Jones hit an intraday record but traded slightly lower, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.9%. Oil futures fell 3.7% to $44.73 per barrel on rising U.S. stockpiles. Treasury yields declined, with the 10-year yield at 2.128%, and gold rose 0.6%. Fed Chair Janet Yellen maintained inflation would hit 2% next year despite recent softness. Individual stock movements included Tesla rising 0.6% on a five-star safety rating for its Model X, H&R Block surging 9% on strong earnings, and oil-related stocks declining sharply.

This patent application describes a device and method for optimizing basal insulin delivery in Type 1 diabetes management using automated insulin delivery (AID) system data. The system calculates total insulin delivered (basal plus bolus) over a predetermined period, determines the proportion delivered as basal insulin, and compares it to a threshold (typically around 70%). If the threshold is exceeded, the system calculates a modified basal dosage that maintains an average basal rate within safe limits. The device includes a processor, memory, wireless communication, and an artificial pancreas application. The method can incorporate time-dependent segmentation using clustering algorithms to create hourly basal profiles, exclude insulin delivered near bolus times from calculations, and adjust recommendations based on hypoglycemia history. The system aims to provide accurate open-loop parameters for when AID is unavailable, addressing the problem of outdated manual settings in patients using automated systems.

In Hirsch v. Cummings, decided January 30, 1939, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit affirmed the dismissal of a suit by "alien enemies" seeking recovery of property seized during World War I under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The court held that Public Resolution No. 53 (1934), which postponed deliveries to Germany while it remained in arrears on certain obligations, validly suspended plaintiffs' right to recover. The court rejected plaintiffs' attempt to distinguish their case from Cummings v. Deutsche Bank und Discontogesellschaft, 300 U.S. 115 (1937), noting that the Supreme Court there held that the original grant of recovery rights to alien enemies "was made as a matter of grace and so was subject to withdrawal by Congress." The court found no merit in plaintiffs' claim that their property was illegally seized, as the resolution's broad terms made such prior lawlessness irrelevant.

Schneider Electric has introduced the Edge Module, a prefabricated data center solution designed for telco edge applications. The module addresses growing demands for edge computing driven by 5G, IoT, autonomous vehicles, and other technologies requiring high processing power close to end users. The turnkey solution integrates power, cooling, software, and IT components, offering flexible deployment options including single or three-phase power, N+1 cooling with free air options, and multiple rack configurations. It features remote monitoring and control through Schneider's EcoStruxure platform, enabling autonomous "lights out" operation, along with built-in security features. The module is specifically designed for cell tower sites with single-phase 208V power capability and scalability up to 48 KW.

The passage defines abbreviations for internal pull resistor states (IPD, IPU, DIS) and describes boot configuration terminal functions for a Texas Instruments device. It details how certain pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC peripheral functions, including: XIP (NOR) on GPMC configuration using BTMODE[10] to select pin muxing options; Ethernet PHY configuration using BTMODE[9:8] for EMAC PHY mode selection; reserved boot pins requiring external pulldown resistors; and ARM boot mode configuration bits (BTMODE[4:0]) that determine boot configuration. After reset, these pins function as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins. The passage references additional documentation in Sections 5.2, 5.2.6, 5.5.1, and 8.3.17, and the TMS320DM814x Technical Reference Manual.

Tail risk, or "fat tails," refers to increased probabilities of rare, extreme events compared to a normal distribution, with left tail risk representing significant losses. Nassim Taleb popularized this concept, arguing that financial markets experience extreme movements more frequently than standard models suggest. Six hedging strategies are presented: put options, foreign assets, cash, Cambria's TAIL ETF, Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio, and trend-following strategies. Put options act as insurance but require ongoing costs and rolling. Cash (5-10% allocation) provides stability during meltdowns. Foreign assets offer diversification. Trend-following strategies feature positively skewed distributions with many small losses but rare large gains. Cambria's TAIL ETF invests in out-of-the-money puts and Treasuries, producing negative returns in rising markets but positive returns during crises. Backtests show that allocating 10% to TAIL reduces drawdowns but lowers long-term returns. The All Weather Portfolio diversifies across asset classes including commodities. Tail risk hedging involves trade-offs: insurance costs reduce compounding but improve performance during crashes and help investors avoid behavioral mistakes like panic selling. The strategies are psychologically difficult due to consistent small losses before rare large payoffs.

Hong Liu's MIT lecture discusses the operator-field correspondence in AdS/CFT, focusing on how scaling dimensions of boundary operators relate to masses of bulk fields. The key result is the mass-dimension relation: for a scalar field of mass m in (d+1)-dimensional AdS, the dual operator has scaling dimension Δ = d/2 + √((d/2)² + m²R²). This emerges from analyzing the asymptotic behavior of bulk fields near the boundary (z→0), where solutions behave as φ ~ A z^(d-Δ) + B z^Δ. The non-normalizable mode (A) corresponds to adding a source term to the boundary theory, while the normalizable mode (B) corresponds to states/expectation values. The BF bound (m²R² ≥ -d²/4) ensures stability. Massless fields map to marginal operators (Δ = d), negative mass-squared to relevant operators (Δ < d), and positive mass-squared to irrelevant operators (Δ > d). Similar analysis applies to vector fields (dual to conserved currents with dimension d-1) and the metric (dual to the stress tensor with dimension d). The lecture concludes by showing how correlation functions can be computed from the gravity partition function with specified boundary conditions.

The passage discusses algorithms for computing Nash equilibrium in multiplayer imperfect-information games. For two-player zero-sum games, efficient methods exist including linear programming and approximation procedures like counterfactual regret minimization. For multiplayer games, computing Nash equilibrium is PPAD-hard, and iterative algorithms lack convergence guarantees. The Gambit software suite offers limited methods for extensive-form games, with only logit quantal response equilibrium (QRE) capable of solving 3-player Kuhn poker after dominated action removal, taking over 40 seconds.

The authors present a new approach formulating the problem as a nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) using sequence-form representation, modeled as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program solvable with recent nonconvex quadratic optimization advances. This guarantees exact Nash equilibrium computation.

Experiments on 3-player Kuhn poker show the new approach solves the reduced game in 2.47 seconds with deviation gain of 1.4 × 10−17, compared to logit QRE's 43 seconds and deviation gain of 1.67 × 10−5. However, the approach cannot solve the full game within 24 hours, while logit QRE solves it in several minutes. Removing dominated actions as preprocessing significantly improves performance.

For strategic-form games, the NCP approach outperforms mixed-integer bilinear programs, with speedups of 2.7x to 5x. The authors conclude their method is best for exact Nash equilibrium in small games, while logit QRE offers better scalability for moderate-sized games, and iterative self-play algorithms remain the only option for very large games without convergence guarantees.

Iron Sulfate Heptahydrate Market Summary

Iron Sulfate Heptahydrate [iron(II) Sulfate], also known as ferrous Sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is a water- and acid-soluble compound with octahedral molecular geometry. It is produced as a co-product during titanium dioxide manufacturing from ilmenite and through crystallization of hot Sulfate solutions. The product contains 18-20 weight% iron, up to 3 weight% free acid, and at least 4% free moisture, with crystals that tend to stick together and acidic liquid that can leach from storage containers.

Applications include medical treatment for iron deficiency (listed by WHO as an essential medicine), industrial uses, textile dye fixation, leather blackening, ink production, treatment of iron chlorosis in fruit cultivation, water purification through flocculation and phosphate removal, reduction of Cr6+ in cement production, and as an iron supplier in agriculture.

The professor discusses the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP) as a difficult but fundamental concept in information theory, explaining how typical sequences from discrete memoryless sources concentrate around probability 2^(-nH(X)) with the number of typical sequences approximately 2^(nH(X)). He then introduces Markov sources as models for sources with memory, describing them as labeled transitions on ergodic Markov chains where each output depends on the previous state. The lecture covers steady-state probabilities and conditional entropy H(X|S) as the fundamental limit for source coding. Finally, the professor presents the Lempel-Ziv universal compression algorithm (LZ77), which achieves asymptotic compression at rate H(X|S) without prior knowledge of source statistics by finding longest matches in a sliding window and encoding match length and position using unary-binary codes.

Coaches should prepare teams by studying Law 10, practicing kicks, ranking takers by composure, simulating shoot-out conditions, and analyzing opponents. President Nixon addresses Congress in his 1970 State of the Union, calling for reform of American institutions and programs. A swimming robot nicknamed "mini manbo" will investigate damage at Japan's Fukushima Dai-Ichi nuclear plant in July. This passage provides an overview of Nassim Nicholas Taleb's career, trading strategies, and key concepts from his books. Taleb, a statistician, mathematician, philosopher, trader, and investor, gained prominence through his Incerto book series: *Fooled by Randomness* (2001), *The Black Swan* (2007), *Antifragile* (2012), and *Skin in the Game* (2018). He emphasizes that markets are driven by unpredictable randomness and tail events rather than normal distributions.

Taleb made his fortune primarily through options strategies, particularly profiting from the 1987 crash. He later founded Empirica Capital with Mark Spitznagel, who subsequently established Universa Investments where Taleb serves as advisor. Universa employs barbell strategy principles, reportedly growing from $300 million in 2007 to over $11 billion by 2022, and made over 4000% during the 2020 COVID crash.

The barbell strategy structures portfolios with binary extremes: most assets in low-risk investments (cash, short-term Treasuries) and a small portion in high-risk, high-reward assets or strategies that profit from volatility. This approach loses money most of the time but generates substantial gains during tail events. Taleb distinguishes between Mediocristan (thin tails, contained risks) and Extremistan (fat tails, multiplicative risks).

Key concepts include antifragility (systems that benefit from shocks), skin in the game (having personal stakes in decisions), and critiques of forecasting, bureaucratic separation from consequences, and the confusion of luck with competence in trading.

Coach Vigneault expressed disappointment with his team's Stanley Cup Final loss, noting all three games went to overtime and praising his players' effort. The Malawi Health Equity Network (MHEN) has urged the government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils to improve public financial management. Gary Gensler's MIT lecture covers initial coin offerings (ICOs) as a new form of crowdfunding where startups sell crypto tokens to raise money before networks are functional. Evaluation criteria include assessing token use case viability, reading white papers, reviewing team credentials, checking venture capital involvement, measuring community engagement, examining monetary policy, and analyzing token distribution. Statistics show ICOs declined 78% in Q3 2018 to $1.8 billion, with 84% using Ethereum platform, 76% offering only ideas, and 1.7% having functional code. The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase II study evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Conducted between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units of high-titer convalescent plasma (326 patients) or control (163 patients). The primary endpoint—proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% vs. 84.1%). No statistically significant differences were observed for any secondary endpoints, including mortality or mechanical ventilation at Day 30. Safety profiles were similar between arms, with comparable rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal events. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6% of the intervention group. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter disease course in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Arthur Santiago and Cristiano Mattos, professors at Brazilian universities, developed a dialogic educational activity using the Discord platform during COVID-19 emergency remote teaching. The activity, grounded in Freire's critical pedagogy and analyzed through Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), aimed to foster student dialogue and autonomy in a non-formal education course for physics teacher education students.

The seven-stage activity focused on the contested issue of school reopening during the pandemic, engaging 19 students in researching, debating, and producing scientific communication materials. Discord's features—persistent text channels, voice channels, and student-managed access—enabled self-organized group work, asynchronous and synchronous collaboration, and increased student agency compared to traditional face-to-face settings.

Students identified their own difficulties with remote learning, researched reliable sources on COVID-19 and school reopening, and collaboratively produced an infographic for social media dissemination. The platform allowed students to move between groups independently, schedule additional meetings without teacher presence, and negotiate meanings through multiple communication modes.

The study found that Discord facilitated dialogic interactions and student autonomy by: leveraging students' prior familiarity with the gaming platform; enabling Freirean-inspired thematic organization around students' lived problems; and supporting collective product construction that connected personal and socio-political issues. The activity transformed students from passive recipients to active producers, developing critical consciousness of systemic contradictions through collaborative, self-regulated learning.

This patent application describes electronic gaming systems and methods featuring a stop-based bonus game where stop positions initially associated with lower-value second awards (e.g., credit prizes) can be upgraded to higher-value first awards (e.g., jackpot awards) after being selected. The bonus game uses constructs such as wheels, reels, dice, or grid-based treasure maps with multiple stop positions. When a player selects a stop position associated with a second award, that award is provided to the player, and the stop position is then re-associated with a first award for future play—increasing the odds of winning a jackpot over time. These upgraded associations can persist across player sessions. The system includes a processor, memory, displays, and input mechanisms for credit and player interaction. Various implementations describe secondary jackpot wheels, multiple jackpot tiers (GRAND, MAJOR, MINOR, MINI), and reset conditions when first awards are won.

This study investigates using generative AI in undergraduate physics education through a learning-by-teaching approach where students prompt, validate, and refine AI-generated simulations of physics phenomena. Conducted in spring 2025 at a large R1 university with 161 students in an introductory physics for life sciences course, the study compared three laboratory conditions: traditional physical equipment, pre-built AI-designed simulation, and student-AI collaborative simulation development, all focusing on electric potential and equipotential lines.

Results showed that students using both simulation methods (AI-engaged and pre-built) performed significantly better on immediate conceptual assessments than those using physical equipment (p<0.001, η²=0.359), with no significant difference between the two simulation groups. However, these differences did not persist on midterm or final exams. Student attitude surveys favored both simulation approaches over physical equipment, with the pre-built simulation rated slightly higher on one comparison measure. The AI-engaged approach additionally offered opportunities for developing scientific modeling and validation skills, as students had to verify both technical functionality and physical accuracy of their AI-generated simulations. The study concludes that generative AI can support conceptual learning without compromising traditional educational goals, while also preparing students for future professional use of emerging technologies.

This lecture explains electroweak unification, which combines weak and electromagnetic interactions. The strength difference between these interactions is addressed through heavy gauge bosons as mediators. The structural difference in coupling—vector for QED versus vector-axial for weak interaction—is mitigated by absorbing the 1 minus gamma 5 term into particle spinor definitions, projecting out left-handed components.

The weak current is rewritten using these redefined spinors, simplifying it to a vector current. For electromagnetic interactions, left-handed and right-handed components are projected and added, showing no mixed terms and explaining why helicity is unchanged in QED.

Building on strong isospin concepts from QCD, neutrinos and electrons are described as a doublet. The charged weak currents are expressed as left-handed components of these doublets using tau plus and tau minus matrices (combinations of Pauli matrices). The third component using tau 3 resembles a neutral current.

Using the Gell-Mann-Nishijima equation, electric charge connects to isospin and hypercharge. A hypercharge current is defined, revealing a new component coupling to right-handed particles—necessary since the initial neutral current lacked right-handed contributions.

Generalizing to all particles, isospin currents (coupling to the W1, W2, W3 triplet) and hypercharge currents (coupling to the singlet) are constructed. The W plus and W minus bosons emerge as linear combinations of W1 and W2. The photon and Z boson arise from mixing the third isospin component with the hypercharge singlet via the weak mixing angle theta W, with couplings satisfying g sine theta W equals g prime cosine theta W equals the electromagnetic coupling.

This study characterizes Alzheimer's disease (AD) plasma biomarkers in 1,067 elderly Amish individuals from Ohio and Indiana. Compared to cognitively unimpaired individuals, those with AD showed significantly higher plasma p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio. Plasma p-tau181 demonstrated significant association with AD among APOE ε4 carriers (OR=6.02, p<0.001), with APOE ε4 moderating this relationship. The Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio showed strong discriminative capability for AD (AUC=0.83) and cognitive preservation. Clustering analysis using Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified two subgroups: a low-risk cluster with elevated Aβ42/Aβ40 and reduced p-tau181, and a high-risk cluster with decreased Aβ42/Aβ40 and increased p-tau181. The high-risk cluster contained significantly more APOE ε4 carriers and AD individuals. Three-cluster refinement further separated individuals by Aβ and tau risk profiles. These findings demonstrate that plasma biomarkers, particularly p-tau181 and Aβ42/p-tau181, can distinguish AD and cognitive impairment in this genetically homogeneous population, supporting their potential for AD screening and risk stratification.

This patent application describes an automated cryogenic storage system for biological samples. The system includes one or more cryogenic storage vaults maintained at approximately −150°C, a sample handling module (SHM) with a robotic transfer arm, and external ports for docking portable cryogenic workstations. The SHM enables automated transfer of individual samples between vaults or to removable storage devices while maintaining samples below their glass transition temperature (e.g., −134°C) during brief transit through non-cryogenic environments. Key components include interleaved rotating shelf racks, vertical shuttle assemblies for tray elevation, specialized grippers with extendable insulating sleeves, and a controller managing sample tracking via barcode scanning. The system incorporates humidity control through cryogenic gas circulation and a cryotrap dehumidification system, along with multi-stage disaster recovery procedures for handling mechanical failures.

This patent application describes deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carboline compounds (Formulas I-IV) with improved metabolic stability compared to their non-deuterated analogs. The compounds contain trideuterated N-methyl and/or di-deuterated methylene groups that limit metabolism via N-dealkylation and alpha-oxidation pathways while maintaining pharmacological activity against 5-HT2A receptors, serotonin transporter (SERT), and dopamine D2/D3 receptors. The invention provides pharmaceutical compositions including depot formulations (using polymers like PLGA for sustained release over 14-180 days) and osmotic-controlled release oral delivery systems. Methods of use include treating central nervous system disorders such as schizophrenia (particularly residual symptoms), depression, sleep disorders, anxiety, PTSD, impulse control disorders, and Parkinson's disease. The deuterated compounds demonstrate significantly reduced formation of N-demethylated amide metabolites compared to non-deuterated compound Q in mouse, rat, and dog pharmacokinetic studies, with 55% decreased metabolism in rats and 72% higher parent drug exposure in dogs.

Michael Johnson, 61, has been named the first lay president of John Carroll University in its 131-year history, replacing Jesuit-affiliated predecessors who served without salary. This study systematically reviews empirical research evaluating ChatGPT's accuracy and validity in educational settings. ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, has evolved from GPT-1 (2018) to GPT-4 (2023), with rapid adoption in education—reaching 100 million users faster than major social platforms. The review analyzed 18 peer-reviewed empirical studies across disciplines including medicine, writing assignments, business, finance, chemistry, physics, and programming.

Findings indicate ChatGPT produces coherent, well-structured text and can pass many undergraduate exams, sometimes performing at Grade A level in business courses and exceeding high school students in essay writing. However, significant limitations exist: responses often lack depth, critical thinking, and argumentation; accuracy decreases with complex scientific and calculation problems (dropping to 12% for advanced finance problems); and outputs may contain hallucinations or false information stated with confidence. Performance varies by field—strong in humanities and social sciences, weaker in specialized medical contexts and chemistry problem-solving.

The study proposes an "ABCD framework" for educational adoption, recommending validation of ChatGPT responses, text-based prompt structuring, redesigned assessments targeting higher-order skills, authentic assessment design, institutional policy development, and student training for constructive use. The author suggests future cooperation between educational institutions and developers to create education-specific ChatGPT versions, noting ongoing rapid improvements including GPT-4's enhanced capabilities.

A cross-sectional study at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, assessed awareness and attitudes toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) among 230 third-trimester pregnant women. While 78% had heard of LEA, only 6.5% cited healthcare providers as their information source, and merely 14.3% were willing to use it. Main barriers were fears of side effects, cost concerns, and perceived interference with natural labor. A study by King's College London scientists analyzing data from 49 studies involving 266,939 people found that regular physical activity reduces depression risk across all age groups.
