The "Four Down" basketball offense is primarily used for final-period shots but works as a spread offense for teams with skilled ballhandlers. It is signaled by pointing four fingers downward and is also called "Four Low" or "Four Flat." The alignment places four non-ballhandlers along the baseline with shooters in corners, creating space for the ballhandler to operate one-on-one. Primary options include driving to the basket, pulling up for jumpers, or passing to open posts or corner shooters when defenders help. Under pressure, corners pop out for release passes and can assume the ballhandler role. Special plays include Mid Screen (O4/O5 set screens for O1), Triple Base Screen (O3/O4/O5 set staggered screens for O2 with O3 continuing for a shot), and Misdirection Double (O3/O5 set a weakside double screen for O4 after a dribble handoff between O1 and O2).

The 2-3 zone is the most commonly used zone defense in basketball, effective at protecting the basket and stopping dribble penetration, but vulnerable to outside shooting. It features two guards at the free throw line and three players inside, with the post defender staying between the ball and basket. Defenders shift positions based on ball location, with specific rotations for middle, wing, and corner positions. The defense offers variations including wing adjustments, 1-1-3 alignment, and trap options at the point, wing, and corner. Against dominant post players ("footers"), the 2-3 zone can employ double and triple teams through specific positioning adjustments.

The UC1825B-SP is a controller designed for 10-30 V input, supporting push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge topologies. Key design guidelines include: using a sense resistor with ~1 V CS pin threshold for current limiting; placing low-value ceramic input capacitors close to the VIN pin; running feedback traces away from inductors and noisy traces; keeping compensation components near the IC; making power traces short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per Ampere); employing ground planes with separate power and signal ground sections; and using low EMI inductors with ferrite closed cores. The device requires careful PCB layout due to 2-A peak output driver currents, with VCC and VREF bypassed using low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors. Test results show operation with 48-V input and 10-A output load.

This email from Steven Kean to Bernadette Hawkins, dated February 28, 2001, forwards a collection of news articles about California's electricity crisis compiled by Miyung Buster. The articles cover: Governor Gray Davis's focus on utility finances rather than summer power shortages; Western states' shared power problems and efforts to reduce California's dominance; stalled construction of "peaker" plants due to contract disputes; business concerns about California's climate; Davis's political response to the crisis; California's relatively efficient per-capita electricity use; falling spot power prices as plants return to service; and legislative obstacles to Davis's plan to buy utility transmission lines.

Community Board 7 of Manhattan sued the New York City Department of City Planning under the Freedom of Information Law to compel disclosure of documents related to the "Trump City" development proposal. The New York Court of Appeals reversed lower court decisions, holding that although the community board had standing, it lacked capacity to sue. The court distinguished capacity from standing, noting that governmental entities created by statute have no inherent right to sue and require express or implied statutory authorization. Despite the board's advisory role in land use review under the City Charter, the court found no legislative intent to grant community boards power to bring judicial actions for document disclosure, citing the Charter's failure to include recommended subpoena powers, specific document provisions in ULURP, and legislative history showing rejection of proposed lawsuit authority. The board's purely advisory function could be accomplished without FOIL enforcement power.

Cboe Global Markets' smooth launch of bitcoin futures could lead to additional cryptocurrency products like options and ETFs, according to CEO Ed Tilly. The Sunday debut saw nearly 3,700 contracts traded by 20 firms, with significant volatility including a 20% surge that triggered a trading halt. Cboe plans to wait for settlements on one-month contracts before introducing new crypto-derivatives. Three fund managers have reapplied to the SEC for bitcoin ETFs following the launch. Cboe has also appealed an SEC ruling blocking a bitcoin ETF from Gemini, which provides settlement prices for Cboe's futures. Tilly indicated futures for other cryptocurrencies may follow. The launch generated unprecedented interest, with Cboe's website briefly crashing due to traffic six times normal levels.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. It can be powered down via the PWDN pin or by writing to the PD_CH field in register bank 1. After power-up or reset, the device requires an initialization sequence of register writes with a free-running sampling clock connected. The device supports a speed-boost mode enabling up to 8MSPS sampling for a selected channel pair while other channels remain idle. Register access uses SPI with three register banks (0, 1, 2), where bank 0 is always accessible and banks 1-2 require selection via register 0x03. Multiple devices can be configured in daisy-chain topology by setting the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register, requiring N × 24 SCLKs for register writes across N devices. Key registers include 0x00 (SPI mode, read enable), 0x01 (daisy-chain length), 0x03 (bank selection), 0x04/0x92 (normal operation settings), 0x0D (data format, averaging), 0x13/0x18 (test patterns), 0x37 (speed-boost channel selection), 0xC0 (power-down, bandwidth), 0xC1 (reference, output lanes), and 0xC4/C5 (common-mode range). For ATE applications, the device achieves 0.0015% TUE at 25°C ±5°C post-calibration and offers wide-bandwidth mode (700kHz) for fast multiplexed signal settling to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. The device uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and requires careful PCB layout with proper decoupling capacitors and avoidance of digital-analog signal crossing.

Premium subscription features include the Lex column for daily corporate and financial commentary, Editor's Choice weekly newsletter from Lionel Barber, FT Newsmine Blog for macroeconomic data, and Martin Sandbu's Free Lunch for daily global economics analysis. Subscribers also receive EM Squared, daily FT ePaper, and exclusive weekly emails.

The device supports external reference mode by setting INTREF_DIS to logic 1, allowing a 4.096V external reference at REFIO with internal buffering. The REFCAP pin requires 10µF minimum capacitance to REFGND and 1µF for high-frequency decoupling. The internal buffer has 0.5ppm/°C typical drift (2ppm/°C maximum) across –40°C to +125°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar/unipolar ranges, outputting straight-binary format. The LSB size equals FSR/2^16.

Alarm features include input alarm (user-programmable thresholds with hysteresis) and AVDD alarm (fixed 4.7V low/5.3V high thresholds). Both alarms have active and tripped flags read via ALARM_REG, with ALARM output on a configurable multifunction pin.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI and source-synchronous protocols with single or dual SDO-x options. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge, requiring minimum 32 SCLK cycles for valid commands. Daisy-chain topology connects multiple devices with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK, chaining SDO-0 to SDI of next device.

Three operational states exist: RESET (RST low), ACQ (signal acquisition), and CONV (conversion initiated by CONVST/CS rising edge). RST pin configures as application reset (RSTn_APP=1) or power-on reset (RSTn_APP=0).

Nine configuration registers control device operation, including SDI_CTL_REG (SPI protocol), SDO_CTL_REG (output mode), DATAOUT_CTL_REG (output data flags), RANGE_SEL_REG (reference/input ranges), and alarm threshold registers. Write operations to RST_PWRCTL_REG require 69h unlock code at address 05h.

The device offers NAP and power-down modes for reduced power consumption, entered via RST_PWRCTL_REG bits with specific timing requirements for wake-up.

PPL Corporation (NYSE:PPL) saw net money outflow of $29.88 million on Wednesday despite shares rising $0.19 to close at $37.65. Analysts have mixed ratings: Zacks downgraded to "hold," while ValuEngine and Jefferies maintained "buy" ratings. The stock has a consensus "Hold" rating with $38.94 price target. PPL reported Q2 EPS of $0.52, beating estimates by $0.02, with revenue of $1.73 billion (down 3.4% year-over-year). The company has a $25.58 billion market cap, PE ratio of 15.61, and pays $1.58 annual dividend (4.24% yield). Insiders sold 47,163 shares worth $1.86 million in the last three months. Institutional investors own 71.01% of shares.

Europe faces ageing population challenges with varying approaches across EU member states. Current strategies often lack factual foundations and fail to progress beyond pilot stages. This paper examines digital wellness services for the "young elderly" (ages 60-75) delivered via mobile platforms to maintain health, activity, and independence before age 75+. Mobile technology enables scalable interventions that could reduce EU health and social care costs by tens of billions annually if adopted by millions.

The proposed three-step approach involves: proactive prevention targeting the 60-75 age group; smartphone intervention tools (with 60%+ EU smartphone penetration by 2020); and commercial ecosystems to sustain ICT-based services. The young elderly represent 18-23% of EU populations, projected at 97 million by 2020.

The BeWell research program (2014-2016) in Finland uses the Wellmo omnivore platform and Tieto cloud services to develop these services. Survey data from 101 young elderly respondents indicates high mobile app proficiency and positive attitudes toward wellness, supporting service viability. Key findings show intellectual wellness is particularly important, and compensatory relationships exist between wellness dimensions.

Service design requires user co-creation through action design research, with omnivore platforms enabling personalized wellness routines. The technology infrastructure must scale to hundreds of thousands of users, using advanced analytics for data fusion and personalized coaching.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 26, 2018, announcing its first quarter 2018 financial results. The filing includes two exhibits: a press release with the financial results announcement and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Chicago Blackhawks players Patrick Kane, Brent Seabrook, and Bryan Bickell discuss their Stanley Cup Final series. They mention evening the series, with Seabrook scoring an overtime winner. Bickell emphasizes physical play against opponents, while Kane notes the team's depth and contributions from various players. They express pride in the Blackhawks' history and logo. Seabrook discusses encouraging teammate Jonathan Toews to focus on scoring. The players highlight the importance of defensive play, getting pucks to the net, and creating traffic in front of opposing goalies. They describe the series as bizarre with close games and varying scores, feeling confident with two remaining games in Chicago.

FreeNAS has released version 11, based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE, following the failed version 10 "Corral" which was demoted to a tech preview due to bugs. New features include the bhyve hypervisor for virtual machines, AWS S3 compatibility, integration with messaging tools like Slack, selectable boot services, and a beta GUI built on Angular. Docker support from Corral has been deferred to a future release, while FreeBSD jails remain available. Forum feedback on version 11's release candidates has been positive.

This study analyzes the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam during 2021. Vietnam initially controlled COVID-19 through strict border restrictions, contact tracing, and quarantine measures, recording only 1,465 cases and 35 deaths in 2020. However, the Alpha variant (detected January-May 2021) and Delta variant (detected from April 2021) caused a nationwide outbreak with over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths by year-end.

Researchers sequenced 1,303 genomes from two tertiary hospitals, finding 93.8% Delta (predominantly AY.57 lineage), 5.7% Alpha, and minor other variants. Phylogenetic analysis revealed multiple Alpha introductions with limited sustained transmission due to containment measures. The Delta AY.57 lineage, first introduced to Vietnam's northeast region around March 14, 2021, became dominant from June onward. Phylogeographic analysis showed initial spread from northeast and Red River Delta regions to the southeast, followed by the southeast becoming the main source seeding other regions from July-December 2021.

The AY.57 lineage exhibited sharp genetic diversity increase between April-August 2021, coinciding with outbreak expansion in an immunologically naïve population. Viral dispersal between provinces remained limited, likely due to strict travel restrictions. The study found weak purifying selection driving AY.57 evolution, with an estimated evolutionary rate of 5.29×10⁻⁴ substitutions per site per year. The findings demonstrate how genomic surveillance informs pandemic response and how public health measures shaped viral evolution patterns in a previously low-transmission setting.

JPMorgan Chase reduced its DeVry Education Group holdings by 9.6% in Q3, selling 53,234 shares to retain 499,104 shares worth $11.5 million. Other institutional investors adjusted positions: UBS increased by 10.6%, M&T Bank acquired a new position, PNC increased by 637.7%, Retirement Systems of Alabama increased by 0.4%, and KBC Group increased by 82.6%. DeVry's stock traded at $31.20 with a $1.95 billion market cap. The company reported Q3 earnings of $0.39 per share, missing estimates by $0.02, with revenue of $449.9 million. Analysts predict $2.55 EPS for the fiscal year. DeVry paid a $0.18 semiannual dividend on December 22nd. Research ratings include one sell, seven hold, and four buy ratings, with a consensus "Hold" and average target price of $26.11. Major shareholder Value Advisers International sold 3,272 shares in November. Insiders own 5.61% of the company. DeVry Education Group operates as a global educational services provider in healthcare, technology, business, accounting, finance, and law.

Ostersunds will face Arsenal in the Europa League last 32, marking the Swedish club's first meeting with the English team. The tie will see Ostersunds manager Graham Potter return to his home country. Arsenal last played a Swedish side in Europe in 1999-2000. Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, Celtic and Napoli all dropped from the Champions League to the Europa League; they will face Atalanta, Copenhagen, Zenit and RB Leipzig respectively.

This systematic review examines the relationship between cannabis/marijuana use and gut microbiome alterations in humans. The authors searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases, ultimately including 9 studies (1 case-control, 6 cohorts, 2 clinical trials) with 2,526 participants from 1983-2021 across USA, Iran, Israel, and UK. Key findings indicate cannabis affects microbiota composition in various conditions: HIV patients showed increased Fusobacterium and Anaerotruncus but decreased Dorea; musculoskeletal pain patients exhibited elevated S. mutans and Lactobacilli; oral microbiome changes included reduced Capnocytophaga, Fusobacterium, and Porphyromonas but increased Rothia; and OEA supplementation increased A. muciniphila in obese participants. Cannabis use was associated with lower Prevotella:Bacteroides ratios and linked to cognitive deficits through microbiome and mitochondrial function alterations. The endocannabinoid system appears to mediate anti-inflammatory effects via gut-brain axis interactions and SCFA production. Adverse events included respiratory symptoms, drowsiness, and systemic aspergillosis. The review was limited by heterogeneous pathological conditions preventing meta-analysis, with most studies showing moderate to high risk of bias.

Chinese textile firms increasingly use North Korean factories for cheaper labor, with clothes labeled "Made in China" and exported globally. UN sanctions on North Korea exclude textile exports, allowing this practice to flourish through Dandong, the main border trade city. North Korean textiles totaled $752 million in 2016, the country's second-largest export. Manufacturers save up to 75% using North Korean factories, where state-owned facilities operate with workers paid significantly less than Chinese counterparts. North Korean workers in China earn about $300 monthly, keeping roughly one-third while the rest goes to government handlers. New UN sanctions ban increasing North Korean laborers abroad, though many already work in Chinese factories under restricted conditions.

Glenner Town Square, a 1950s-themed miniature village for Alzheimer's and dementia patients, opened in April 2018 in Chula Vista. The 8,500-square-foot facility features 13 interactive storefronts designed to stimulate long-term memories. The George G. Glenner organization also operates adult day-care centers in Hillcrest and Encinitas, with plans to convert them to Town Square projects. The passage lists additional licensed adult day programs for cognitively impaired individuals throughout San Diego County, including locations in Clairemont, Mira Mesa, Logan Heights, Bankers Hill, Rancho Bernardo, San Marcos, and Fallbrook, offering services such as medical care, therapy, meals, transportation, and structured activities.

A hockey player discusses reaching the Stanley Cup Finals for the third time with a third different team, expressing strong desire to win after previous losses. He notes the sold-out arena, enthusiastic fans, and Chicago's status as a true hockey town. He reflects on learning from past defeats, the team's hard work reaching the finals, and anticipates a tight series against the Philadelphia Flyers despite regular season standings.

President Reagan reports that America has improved significantly, with renewed energy and optimism. He notes bipartisan cooperation stopped economic decline, with inflation reduced from 12.4% to 3.2% and across-the-board tax cuts passed. He proposes four goals for the 1980s: ensure steady economic growth through deficit reduction and tax simplification; develop America's next frontier in space with a permanently manned space station; strengthen traditional values through education reform and crime reduction; and build meaningful peace through military strength and diplomacy. He emphasizes limiting government growth, pursuing arms reductions with the Soviet Union, and maintaining bipartisan cooperation.

Ben Rice was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, southeast of Boston, and grew up as a Yankees fan despite living in Red Sox territory. He attended Noble and Greenough School in Dedham, then played at Dartmouth College, where he had limited playing time due to the COVID-19 pandemic and Ivy League cancellations. The Yankees drafted him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft based on his summer league performance. After an inconsistent 2024 rookie season, Rice became a near full-time player in 2025, hitting 26 home runs over 138 games while splitting time between first base, catcher, and designated hitter. He will turn 27 on February 22 and is under team control until after the 2030 season.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the third consecutive quarter to a range between 1 percent and 1.25 percent, citing strong job growth and moderate economic growth while acknowledging weaker-than-expected inflation. Fed officials lowered their 2017 inflation forecast from 1.9 percent to 1.6 percent but maintained a 2 percent prediction for next year. Some officials now predict unemployment could fall below 4 percent.

This study develops a mathematical model to evaluate the effectiveness of screening-isolation strategies for epidemic control in semi-isolated communities without vaccines or medications. The authors modify the SEIR model to incorporate screening efficiency, time lags in isolation, and external influx of infection. Computer simulations with varying parameters (R0 values of 3, 6, and 8; screening efficiencies of 0.7 and 0.9; frequencies of once per 3 days or 7 days; and daily influx rates of 0.01, 0.1, and 1) demonstrate that daily screening with 90% efficiency effectively controls diseases with R0 up to 6, while screening every 3 days remains viable for R0=3. The study identifies critical constraints on time lags for successful control and shows that infection sizes scale proportionally with external influx, emphasizing the necessity of strict border control. The authors suggest PCR-based tests as promising candidates for future community-wide screening, noting that detectability prior to infectiousness (v=0) would optimize control outcomes.

Tom Brady's agent Don Yee confirmed the 40-year-old quarterback will return to play for the New England Patriots in 2018 and beyond, stating Brady intends to play into his mid-40s. Brady has two seasons remaining on his contract worth $14 million plus a $1 million roster bonus annually. Despite missing voluntary offseason workouts and retirement rumors, Brady remains focused on training. Patriots owner Robert Kraft indicated no contract issues exist and the team is not pursuing a new deal.

MultiChoice's DStv Premium subscriber numbers declined by 41,000 (from 1.962m to 1.921m) due to Netflix's popularity in South Africa, reducing average revenue per customer from R353 to R344 monthly. CEO Calvo Mawela cited Netflix's "unfair advantage" and noted that streaming service switchers rarely return to broadcast TV. MultiChoice is developing a standalone streaming service (separate from Showmax) and secured streaming rights for all DStv channels in late 2018. The company has appealed to ICASA against over-regulation, warning that excessive regulation could cause job losses to international streaming competitors.

CoreWeave's stock has risen due to AI deal wins with OpenAI ($22.4B) and Meta ($14.2B), diversifying its customer base though Microsoft remains a concentration risk. The company's aggressive capital expenditure and debt-funded growth raise sustainability concerns given its high valuation. Despite strong momentum, shares may face a cooling-off period as optimism appears fully priced in and risks remain elevated.

Joppatowne High School held its 45th commencement ceremony at Harford Community College, where over 130 seniors graduated. About 95% of the 138-member class will attend college, technical school, join the military, or enter law enforcement. Graduate Amya Hill, 17, will study nursing at Albany State University after overcoming early academic struggles. Zachary Wagmun, 17, plans to attend Harford Community College for an electrician's apprenticeship. Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson gave speeches; Stevenson shared three life lessons about trying new things, separating from negative influences, and focusing on the present. Several local officials also spoke, including state Sen. Robert Cassilly, who honored two fallen first responders.

A coach discusses his team's approach to an upcoming elimination game against Calgary, stating they will not analyze the previous game publicly but will focus on extending the series. He notes that pressure lies with Calgary, who are expected to win at home with the Stanley Cup present and national attention. He emphasizes that playoff success comes down to winning battles and making big plays at key moments. The team will stay in Calgary after the game for maximum rest before traveling. He acknowledges Calgary has strong players who deserve credit and expresses curiosity about how Calgary will handle the mental challenges of an elimination game at home. He admits his own team struggled with anticipation and nerves in their previous home game.

A fired assistant U.S. attorney, Michael Ben'Ary, left a letter accusing the Department of Justice leadership of prioritizing punishment of perceived Trump enemies over public safety. Ben'Ary was terminated during a terrorism prosecution related to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly falsely suggested on social media that he was an ally of former Biden official Lisa Monaco. The letter warned that removing career officials from U.S. attorney's offices and the FBI was making America less safe.

This manuscript identifies an intervalley superconducting phase in approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe₂ at hole filling νₕ = 3, appearing as an intermediate phase between a ferromagnetic Chern insulator and a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator. Using exact diagonalization of a continuum model with screened Coulomb interactions, the authors find that superconductivity emerges when short-range intervalley interactions are screened, producing time-reversal symmetric extended s-wave pairing. The superconducting state exhibits continuous connection to the fractional spin Hall insulator across the phase boundary, with topology and symmetry changing simultaneously. Key evidence includes negative binding energy, dominant pair density matrix eigenvalue, and finite superfluid stiffness maximized in the intermediate regime. Non-uniform quantum geometry is found crucial for stabilizing this phase, as it does not appear in ideal first Landau levels. The authors propose that tuning the effective screening length via gating or substrate engineering could realize this superconductivity experimentally.

The passage explains that over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves direct transactions between two parties without a centralized exchange, typically conducted electronically through dealer networks. OTC markets are decentralized, less regulated, and less transparent than formal exchanges, with trades occurring via market makers who quote buy and sell prices. These markets accommodate securities that don't meet exchange listing requirements, including small company stocks, corporate bonds, derivatives, and foreign stocks via ADRs. While offering flexibility for customized contracts and access to capital for smaller companies, OTC markets carry significant risks including counterparty default, market manipulation, pump-and-dump schemes, and poor liquidity. Studies cited show OTC stocks have average negative annual returns around 24%, with over 90% failing. The passage concludes that both long-term investment and short-term trading in OTC stocks are generally inadvisable due to high risks, low returns, and transaction costs from slippage.

"Brainsaver" classes are 12-week courses offered by OptumCare in three Valley locations, focusing on brain-healthy activities including physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, education, socialization, and nutrition. The program targets adults aged 50s to 80s and aims to reduce Alzheimer's risk through a holistic approach. Classes are held at Deer Valley, Goodyear, and Chandler locations on specified weekdays.

Vice President JD Vance said a federal government shutdown is likely after a White House meeting between President Trump and congressional leaders failed to resolve funding disputes. Democrats and Republicans remain far apart, with Democrats demanding that a stopgap funding bill include extensions of enhanced Obamacare tax credits, while Republicans want a "clean" resolution. Both sides blame each other for the potential shutdown, which would begin Wednesday without a deal.

Moina Shaiq created "Meet a Muslim" in Fremont, California, after placing a newspaper ad inviting questions about Islam. The program, which began at a coffee house and has expanded to dozens of venues across multiple states, aims to break down stereotypes by educating people about Muslim faith and culture. Similar initiatives emerged after 9/11 and have resurged amid rising anti-Muslim crimes. Shaiq discusses topics including hijab, Sunni-Shia differences, women's rights, and American Muslim identity, volunteering her own time and money. She has faced threats, including a death threat in Atlanta. While Muslim advocacy groups support such efforts as effective local responses to Islamophobia, some activists like Asha Noor argue they are ineffective and policy change should be prioritized instead.

This patent application describes methods for transmitting/receiving sounding reference signals (SRS) in wireless communication systems, specifically focusing on guard period configuration for antenna switching. The disclosure proposes configuring guard periods (Y symbols) between SRS and other uplink transmissions (PUCCH/PUSCH), with priority rules matching those between SRS and uplink channels. Guard periods can be configured via higher layer signaling, considering subcarrier spacing (typically 1-2 symbols). When guard periods overlap with PUCCH for beam failure recovery, both guard period and overlapping SRS resource may be dropped. The application details UE and base station operations for handling collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets, including dropping lower-priority transmissions, shifting SRS positions, or deferring transmission to subsequent slots.

Turing Tensor Cores are specialized execution units for deep learning matrix operations, enhanced for inferencing with new INT8 and INT4 precision modes. They bring AI capabilities to GeForce and Quadro systems, powering Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), which uses neural networks to construct high-quality images from fewer samples than traditional techniques like TAA.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was arrested after eight days on the run following his sentencing to 13 years in prison for violently shaking his four-month-old son. He had been found guilty of wounding with intent but failed to appear in court after being released on bail over a weekend. Police found him hiding in Litherland. At Liverpool Crown Court, Lakatos admitted breaching bail, claiming he "panicked" at the prospect of imprisonment, and received an additional 10-day consecutive sentence. His son, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered catastrophic brain injuries, four fractured ribs, a fractured shin bone, and retinal haemorrhaging from two shaking incidents in 2015, and will require lifelong nursing care and medication. Lakatos admitted both incidents but denied intent to cause serious harm, describing the second as "vigorously in a moment of frustration."

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 4, 2016, reporting that on January 3, 2016, it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was made under Items 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) and 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure), with the information furnished but not deemed "filed" for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel.

Coach Quenneville discusses coaching the Blackhawks, emphasizing consistency, accountability, and communication. He addresses goaltending decisions involving Corey Crawford and Scott Darling, noting healthy competition between them. He praises players' playoff improvements, particularly faceoff performance and shot mentality. He highlights Patrick Kane's evolution as a shooter and discusses line combinations and player trust based on defensive reliability. He commends a rookie's surprising development and injury recovery, and stresses playing each game as a must-win while adapting to opponents' speed as series progress.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defensive coverage in football with no safeties helping over the top, designed to maximize blitz pressure while covering all eligible receivers. It typically involves rushing 6 players and having all non-linemen cover offensive players man-to-man. Strengths include simplicity of assignments, effectiveness against motion and RPO offenses, strong run defense, and success against both short and long passing routes due to pressure and tight coverage. Weaknesses include vulnerability to big plays if coverage is beaten, susceptibility to draw plays and quarterback scrambles, vulnerability to pick plays, and leaving the middle of the field open with no deep safety help. Common variations include "Rat" coverage, where one rusher drops to cut crossing routes and watch for scrambles, and dropping hybrid defensive linemen into coverage.

Astronomers believe the first known interstellar visitor, the cigar-shaped asteroid Oumuamua, likely originated from a binary star system. University of Toronto's Alan Jackson reported that the asteroid was probably ejected during planet formation and has wandered interstellar space since. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the 1,300-foot red-tinged object is traveling away from Earth at over 16 miles per second. A Queen's University Belfast team found Oumuamua is tumbling through space, likely from a collision that ejected it from its home system. Scientists now agree it is an asteroid, not a comet, and hope it may reveal how planets form in other systems. Researchers suggest close binary star systems may be the source of most interstellar objects.

This study identifies four core dimensions of holistic education—empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry—through a systematic literature review of the LIBRE/EMC2 framework within Indian higher education. Drawing on Indian sage-thinkers including Tagore, Osho, Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo, the research validates these dimensions against contemporary policies like India's NEP 2020 and UN SDG 4.7. The twofold methodology combined comprehensive framework analysis with PRISMA-guided systematic review of Scopus and Semantic Scholar databases, yielding eight articles for thematic analysis. Results confirm alignment between ancient Indian educational philosophies emphasizing integrated spiritual-material development and modern holistic education frameworks. The study establishes empirical grounding for LIBRE/EMC2's four dimensions while highlighting the need for culturally sensitive assessment tools and curriculum development. Limitations include database restrictions excluding non-indexed sources, suggesting future expansion to regional journals and implementation studies across diverse educational settings.

Soybean May futures rose due to diminishing supplies and steady crushing demand from soy meal exports. Physical market supplies decreased in early April, with arrivals dropping to 97,040 tonnes from 164,286 tonnes in March. Prices are expected to rise further on crusher demand, while refined soy oil and CPO may see technical rebounds, though cheap imports could pressure prices. Good domestic demand may provide support.

A University of Maryland study found that young adults who regularly consume caffeinated energy drinks are at higher risk for alcohol use disorder and stimulant drug use (cocaine and non-medical prescription stimulants) by age 25. Researchers tracked 1,099 college students over time, identifying that 51.4% with sustained energy drink consumption showed significantly higher substance use risk, even after controlling for demographics, sensation-seeking, other caffeine use, and prior substance use. The study, published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence, is the first to examine how different patterns of energy drink consumption affect later substance use.

Consumer advocates reported glitches in HealthCare.gov during the final days of Obamacare enrollment, including incorrect messages that no plans were available in some areas. The Trump administration said the issue was resolved, though advocates reported it continued. Friday is the deadline for 39 states using the federal exchange, with Dec. 15 as the final day for most consumers. Hurricane-affected areas can get extensions to Dec. 31. Despite a shortened 45-day enrollment period and reduced advertising, consumer interest remained brisk. Many eligible for subsidies may see lower premiums in 2018 due to increased taxpayer subsidies. States running their own exchanges have later deadlines, with California and New York extending to Jan. 31.

President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed a state of war between the United States and Germany on April 6, 1917, pursuant to a congressional joint resolution and Section 4067 of the Revised Statutes. The proclamation directs U.S. officers to exercise vigilance in their duties and appeals to American citizens to support war measures. It establishes regulations for German males aged 14 and older within the U.S. who are not naturalized, designated as "alien enemies." These regulations prohibit possession of weapons, aircraft, wireless apparatus, cipher codes, and invisible writing; require peaceful conduct and compliance with U.S. laws; ban attacks against the government or military personnel; restrict access to military installations and designated prohibited areas; and subject violators to arrest, confinement, restraint, or removal from the country. Alien enemies must obtain permits to depart or enter the U.S., may be required to register, and can be relocated by executive order if deemed dangerous to public safety.

The Washington Nationals signed pitcher Jeremy Hellickson to a minor league contract, adding him to the competition for the fifth starter spot alongside A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde. Hellickson could receive a $2 million major league deal with up to $4 million in performance bonuses. The Nationals may leave Hellickson in extended spring training to build arm strength, using an opt-out clause that extends beyond the traditional pre-opening day deadline. General manager Mike Rizzo cited past experiences rushing players through camp as reasoning for the cautious approach. The team has scheduling flexibility to potentially skip the fifth starter initially. Cole pitched well recently and will make the team in either the rotation or bullpen, while Fedde likely heads to the minors. Manager Dave Martinez announced Max Scherzer as opening day starter, a decision made when he was hired. Hellickson, the 2011 AL Rookie of the Year, struggled with Baltimore last season but has worked on delivery adjustments. Shortstop Trea Turner left camp Monday for an ingrown toenail procedure and could return Tuesday.

Tesla announced new budget-friendly versions of its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles on Tuesday. The Model 3 Standard costs $36,990 and the Model Y Standard costs $39,990. Both models include fewer features than premium variants, lacking Autosteer, LED lightbars, adaptive high beams, and FM/AM radio. Buyers can save $5,500 on the Model 3 and $5,000 on the Model Y compared to Premium versions. Tesla's stock fell 4.45% following the announcement, with Wall Street apparently hoping for lower prices. The Model Y Standard will be available November-December, while the Model 3 Standard arrives December-January. New York residents may reduce prices further by $2,000 through state EV incentives. The announcement follows the end of the federal $7,500 EV tax credit. CEO Elon Musk previously promised a $25,000 EV by 2018 but later called such efforts "pointless," shifting focus to self-driving technology.

VentureWire, November 14, 2000, reports private company business news. Top stories: Apax Partners merges European and Israeli units, pledging $600 million for Israeli investments; DSL provider New Edge Networks lays off 135 employees; consulting firm KSolutions receives $50 million first-round funding; and Cisco acquires wireless chip firm Radiata for $295 million.

In a 1924 California assault case, defendant John Ortiz appealed his simple assault conviction after being charged with assault with a deadly weapon. Ortiz claimed self-defense, testifying he had no weapon when entering his home but pulled out a pocket-knife only after the victim, Albert Donaso, rushed at him with a knife. The appellate court affirmed the conviction, ruling that: (1) the district attorney properly cross-examined Ortiz by asking him to demonstrate how he retrieved and opened the knife; and (2) evidence about whether Ortiz had written threatening letters was properly excluded as a collateral issue, since the central question was self-defense, not whether the cutting occurred.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces neural shaders as the next evolution in graphics rendering, enabling AI-powered techniques like Ray Reconstruction (RR), Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA), RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (NTC), Neural Radiance Cache (NRC), RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These technologies use neural networks to approximate complex lighting calculations, compress textures efficiently, and generate realistic faces in real-time. The architecture includes enhanced Tensor Cores accessible through the Cooperative Vectors API and SER 2.0 scheduling optimizations.

The Blackwell GPU family comprises multiple chips: GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores) powers the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores) powers the RTX 5070.

A 6-year-old girl in Pennsylvania witnessed her mother, Devanna Cornitcher, being stabbed to death by her boyfriend, Alonzo Carter, in a Chester apartment. Carter, who was found covered in blood and smoking a cigarette near the body, allegedly confessed to the stabbing, claiming self-defense. Both children, including a 3-year-old son, were present during the incident. Carter was arrested on murder and related charges and is being held without bail at George Hill correctional facility.

District courts lack appellate jurisdiction under the organic act; only the supreme court possesses appellate powers. Appeals from justices of the peace to district courts are tried de novo as original proceedings, with transcripts serving only to verify proper origin and appeal. In this case, the district court correctly overruled a motion to dismiss and permitted filing of an account. The jury properly weighed discrepancies in witness testimony regarding dates and cattle numbers, and the verdict was not clearly against the weight of evidence. The court appropriately denied a new trial, and the judgment for defendant Miera is affirmed.

A hockey player discusses the challenges of early-game power plays and penalty kills when not fully warmed up, credits the crowd's energy as a season-long strength, acknowledges the opponent's talented goal scorers, notes frustration with recent efforts but expresses optimism about turning things around at home, and emphasizes the need to improve puck possession against strong opposing defensemen.

This study used machine learning to predict depressive symptom severity (DSS) based on sleep quality, anxiety, and brain gray matter volume across three independent cohorts (HCP-Young, HCP-Aging, eNKI). Poor sleep quality robustly predicted DSS across all cohorts, with anxiety improving prediction performance and mediating the sleep-depression link. Brain structure and function did not predict DSS or mediate associations. The reverse prediction (sleep quality from depressive symptoms) was less robust. Longitudinal data showed predictability of future DSS, with neurofeedback intervention affecting predictions. Findings suggest sleep and anxiety are critical factors for identifying depressive symptoms at the individual level, supporting precision psychiatry approaches.

The Base Cross Offense is a basketball strategy that uses a small player setting a baseline screen for a big player to create size mismatches. The offense begins with the point guard passing to a wing and cutting to the basket; if not open, the guard sets a baseline screen for the post player. Variations include Pass Entry, Dribble Entry, UCLA Entry, and Hawk Entry. Success depends on precise execution of screens and reads against defensive counters like trailing, switching, or fronting. If the base screen doesn't produce a shot, the offense flows into weakside down screens, mid screens, or side screens. Teaching requires breaking down components through drills and scrimmages, with emphasis on scouting opponents and adjusting alignments during games.

The passage criticizes the Carter administration's foreign policy failures in Iran and Nicaragua, where it replaced moderate autocrats friendly to U.S. interests with extremist, anti-American regimes. It argues that without a realistic policy for handling non-democratic governments threatened by Soviet subversion, similar disasters will recur elsewhere. The author contends that Carter officials, driven by progressive preferences for leftist over rightist forces, failed to recognize that traditional authoritarian governments are less repressive, more susceptible to liberalization, and more compatible with U.S. interests than revolutionary autocracies, which create rather than merely tolerate social inequities and generate refugees.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts, a Guyanese-born U.S. military veteran, resigned effective immediately after being arrested by ICE agents during a "targeted enforcement operation" on Friday. ICE stated Roberts had been given a final removal order in May 2024 and was in the country unlawfully since first arriving in 1999 on a student visa. His attorney, Alfredo Parrish, said Roberts believed his immigration case had been closed successfully and is filing a motion to reopen it. The Iowa Board of Educational Examiners revoked Roberts' license, and the school board had planned to discuss ending his contract. Questions arose about the district's vetting process, though officials said Roberts completed required I-9 verification. A conservative advocacy group criticized the background check firm for not performing I-9 verification. U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn called it "unacceptable" that someone under a final deportation order led Iowa's largest school system. Roberts is currently held at Woodbury County Jail, and his attorney filed a request for stay in Omaha federal immigration court.
