Since his promotion from Double-A, the 22-year-old has posted a 4.22 ERA and 1.32 WHIP in 11 starts, ranking third in the International League with 71 strikeouts. Brad Boxberger struck out three in a rehab appearance, while Wilson Ramos went 1-for-3 in his return from ACL injury and Shane Peterson drove in two runs.

President Nixon announces an accelerated withdrawal of American troops from Vietnam, with 100,000 additional troops to return between May 1 and December 1, 1971, bringing total withdrawals to 365,000—over two-thirds of forces present when he took office. He cites successful Vietnamization, including South Vietnamese effectiveness in the Laos operation and reduced American casualties, as justification. Nixon rejects setting a fixed withdrawal date, arguing it would aid the enemy and endanger remaining forces. He defends American soldiers against atrocity charges, praises their humanitarian efforts, and calls on Hanoi to negotiate seriously and release prisoners of war. He emphasizes ending the war honorably to redeem sacrifices, heal national divisions, and build lasting peace.

Scientists discovered a new genus and species of clingfish, named "duckbilled clingfish" (Nettorhamphos radula), from two preserved specimens found in a 1970s museum collection in Australia. The fish, described in the journal Copeia on April 14, has a broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800-2,300 teeth—ten times more than other known clingfish. Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University, and the Western Australian Museum used CT scanning and 3-D printing to analyze the specimens without dissection. The discovery highlights the value of museum collections and noninvasive imaging techniques in taxonomy.

Lattice Semiconductor shows early signs of revenue rebound driven by data center strength, though weak automotive and industrial markets offset this growth. Management highlights opportunities in high-end data center chips and emerging markets including robotics, vision systems, and security. Inventories are normalizing, financials remain solid with strong cash generation and no debt, and Q3 guidance suggests further growth. Despite raising the target price to $70, the author maintains a HOLD rating due to expensive valuation and thin margin of safety.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its 2015 Annual Report on Form 10-K with the SEC for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The company, incorporated in Delaware with principal offices in Palo Alto, California, is a large accelerated filer with 132,056,338 shares of common stock outstanding as of January 31, 2016.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures and sells high-performance fully electric vehicles and energy storage products. As of December 2015, the company produced and sold two vehicles: the Model S sedan (over 107,000 delivered since June 2012) and the Model X SUV (deliveries began Q3 2015). The company planned to unveil the lower-priced Model 3 in March 2016 for production in late 2017.

The company operates company-owned stores and galleries, with 208 total locations worldwide as of December 31, 2015, and 584 Supercharger stations. Tesla sells directly to consumers, bypassing traditional franchised dealers, which has created legal challenges in some states.

Tesla manufactures vehicles at facilities in Fremont and Lathrop, California, and Tilburg, Netherlands. The company is building the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada for battery cell and pack production, with Panasonic as a partner. The Gigafactory is expected to reach full production capacity in 2020.

The company offers a four-year/50,000-mile New Vehicle Limited Warranty and an eight-year/infinite mile battery and drive unit warranty. Tesla also provides resale value guarantees and leasing programs in certain markets.

Key risks include production delays, supplier dependence (particularly single-source suppliers), competition from established automakers, consumer adoption of electric vehicles, and international expansion challenges. The company had 13,058 full-time employees as of December 31, 2015.

Final exams at Lehigh University run December 12–20, with students studying across campus due to overcrowded libraries. After renovations reduced private spaces in Fairchild-Martindale Library, students have turned to academic buildings, cafes, and reserved study rooms. Extended building hours and online room reservations through the Center for Career and Professional Development help accommodate demand. Some students arrive early to secure spots, while others find library overcrowding distracting and prefer quieter locations like Maginnes Hall or STEPS.

This passage is a statistical analysis plan (SAP) for clinical trial ZP4207-17086, detailing procedures for electrocardiogram (ECG) and immunogenicity assessments, changes to protocol-specified analyses, and appendices covering data presentation standards, SAS programming QC requirements, and a comprehensive list of tables, figures, and listings.

ECG assessments will categorize patients by normal/abnormal findings and present descriptive measures by visit and treatment group, including categorical summaries of QTcF values (>450 ms, >480 ms, >500 ms) and changes from baseline (>30 ms, >60 ms). Immunogenicity will analyze anti-drug antibody (ADA) occurrence descriptively without statistical tests, counting treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA patients against evaluable patients.

Two changes to protocol-specified analyses were made: rewording of the primary efficacy parameter analysis with additional sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changing secondary efficacy variable terminology from "within" to "at" specific time intervals.

Appendices specify data presentation rules (formatting, decimal places, footnotes), SAS programming QC requirements (naming conventions, log review, output verification, dataset validation), and an extensive index of tables, figures, and listings organized by ICH E3 guidelines covering demographics, efficacy endpoints (time to plasma glucose recovery), adverse events, laboratory assessments, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analyses, and patient listings.

Scientists increasingly recognize ultraprocessed foods as potentially addictive, sharing characteristics with substances like alcohol, nicotine, and opioids. These foods—comprising over half of average American caloric intake—are engineered to trigger brain reward systems through combinations of salts, fats, and sugars, leading to cravings, loss of control, and tolerance. Research shows neurochemical changes similar to drug responses, with about 14% of adults meeting criteria for food addiction. Experts argue this addiction framework matters for policy, as individual willpower strategies fail when substances are designed to be irresistible. Some advocate for regulation approaches like Chile's warning labels and marketing restrictions, while noting tobacco companies historically helped disseminate hyperpalatable foods into the food supply.

The Trump administration announced a new nuclear policy through the 2018 Nuclear Posture Review, which aims to modernize the US nuclear arsenal by developing smaller atomic bombs and enhancing deterrence capabilities. President Trump stated the strategy addresses 21st-century threats while maintaining commitments to arms control and non-proliferation. Defence Secretary Jim Mattis highlighted concerns about Russia and China developing new nuclear capabilities and modernizing conventional forces, with Russia's military strategies particularly troubling due to their reliance on nuclear escalation. The policy includes expanding low-yield nuclear options, modifying submarine-launched ballistic missile warheads, and pursuing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile to counter Russian non-compliance with arms treaties. The report identifies North Korea and Iran as threats but does not mention Pakistan. US officials emphasized that the policy strengthens extended deterrence commitments to allies while remaining flexible against diverse threats, including nuclear terrorism.

The federal government agreed to give provinces and territories 75% of tax revenues from legalized marijuana sales, with a portion allocated to municipalities. Finance Minister Bill Morneau announced the two-year agreement after meeting with provincial and territorial counterparts. Ottawa will keep 25% up to $100 million annually, with excess going to provinces. Expected revenue is $400 million over two years. Ministers will reconvene in December 2018 to review the framework. The original 50-50 split was rejected by provinces. Provinces can add markups beyond taxation levels. The Federation of Canadian Municipalities requested one-third of revenues for administrative and policing costs, but distribution will be decided provincially. The federal government has committed over $1 billion over five years for legalization costs including policing and border security. Ministers also discussed equalization payments, Canada Pension Plan review, global economy, and corporate ownership information sharing to combat tax evasion and money laundering.

This inaugural address outlines the new administration's policies, emphasizing continuity with predecessor's reforms against corporate lawlessness while seeking lasting solutions through antitrust and interstate commerce law amendments. The speaker calls for immediate tariff revision to address revenue deficits, supports graduated inheritance taxes if needed, and defends necessary government expenditures including military preparedness, resource conservation, and Panama Canal completion. On monetary policy, banking law changes are sought for greater currency elasticity. The address advocates postal savings banks, expanded foreign trade, and federal jurisdiction over treaty rights for aliens. Regarding race relations, it acknowledges constitutional protections for African Americans while deferring to state electoral qualifications, expresses personal opposition to race prejudice, and cautions against appointments that might inflame racial tensions. On labor, the speaker supports injury compensation laws and safety regulations but opposes restricting federal injunction powers in labor disputes, though endorsing statutory limits on temporary restraining orders.

ANU and Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris researchers studied alumino-silicate glass, commonly used in mobile device screens, finding that sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium atoms form clusters and channels rather than distributing randomly at nanometre scales. This microscopic organization affects glass flexibility and fracture resistance, potentially enabling more shatter-proof phone screens. The research, combining experiments and computer modelling, may lead to collaborations with manufacturers. Current smartphones remain vulnerable to damage, with iPhone X and iPhone 8 featuring glass front and back panels, and Samsung's Note 8 failing drop tests. Samsung continues developing foldable screen technology, targeting a foldable Note device, while both Samsung and LG have displayed prototypes without commercial release.

South Africa is expected to retain its investment-grade credit rating from Moody's this week following Cyril Ramaphosa's assumption of power, according to a Bloomberg survey. The rand has strengthened and business confidence improved since Ramaphosa replaced Jacob Zuma. However, risks remain including potential budget shortfalls, weak economic growth, and the ANC's pursuit of land expropriation without compensation. A downgrade to junk status would remove South Africa from major bond indices and risk significant capital outflows. Moody's currently rates South Africa one step above speculative grade, with S&P and Fitch having already downgraded the country to junk last year.

Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) threatens global health, with traditional culture-based diagnostics taking 2-3 days and promoting resistance through broad-spectrum antibiotic use. Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) offers faster alternatives but faces computational challenges in translating genomic data into clinical predictions. Existing "gene hunting" methods are limited by known knowledge, while machine learning approaches like Random Forest and XGBoost treat genomes as unordered features, ignoring sequential context. Transformers require massive datasets unavailable for AMR prediction.

This paper presents AMR-EnsembleNet, a synergistic ensemble combining a lightweight 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that learns local SNP motifs with XGBoost that captures non-local feature interactions. Using the GieSSen dataset of 809 E. coli isolates with 60,936 SNP features across four antibiotics (CIP, CTX, CTZ, GEN), the ensemble outperformed individual models on imbalanced datasets, particularly improving recall for clinically relevant resistant cases. SHAP analysis validated that top predictive SNPs mapped to known AMR-associated genes (gyrB, marR, rpsL, parC, fusA, ampC, acrD, ftsI), confirming biological relevance. The framework provides an interpretable, computationally feasible solution for rapid AMR prediction from genomic data.

The dollar rose broadly on Monday as traders unwound bearish bets against the U.S. currency. The absence of further harsh rhetoric between U.S. President Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un over the weekend helped bring investors back to the dollar. The dollar index rose 0.3 percent, and the dollar was on pace for its largest one-day percentage gain against the Swiss franc since late July. Analysts noted that stretched positioning led to market reversal and unwinding of strong yen and Swiss franc positions. The dollar was also boosted by gains in U.S. stock markets, with the S&P 500 up 1.05 percent. Investors are awaiting U.S. retail sales data due Tuesday for clues on inflation.

Saskatoon city hall proposes a $1.2-million plan over two years to remove and replace approximately 1,000 black ash trees damaged by cottony ash psyllids, a European tree lice species. Insecticide treatments have only delayed tree decline. The psyllids first appeared in 2006, disappeared in 2009, and reappeared in 2015. This year, 121 trees have already been removed in business districts. Funding for the first year ($757,000) has been identified from reserve funds, but second-year funding ($423,000) is not yet secured. About 27% of Saskatoon's 105,000+ tree inventory are ash species, originally planted due to Dutch elm disease. The city also faces potential threat from the emerald ash borer, not yet detected locally. Calgary and Edmonton lost most susceptible trees to the same pest and no longer plant black ash. Residents can identify psyllids by white cotton on leaves and curled, discolored foliage.

This study investigates water-assisted capillary densification as a scalable method to enhance the mechanical performance of electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. The researchers developed a simple post-processing technique involving wetting yarns with ethanol and water, followed by drying, which harnesses capillary forces during evaporation to drive fibers into close-packed, highly aligned configurations. 

Four yarn types were prepared: as-spun, water-rolled, ethanol-rolled, and heat-treated (110°C for 5 hours after liquid rolling). Mechanical testing revealed that water-treated yarns exhibited higher average stresses than ethanol-treated counterparts due to slower evaporation kinetics enabling more effective compaction. Heat treatment further increased stiffness but reduced ductility through localized fiber fusion.

The study established strong correlations between microstructural parameters and mechanical performance: fiber alignment (R²=0.68) and packing density (R²=0.75) both predicted peak load, with their combination yielding R²=0.80. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model was developed incorporating distributed fiber recruitment, stochastic failure, orientation averaging, and post-failure load retention, successfully reproducing the five-regime stress-strain behavior observed experimentally. The model parameters ϕ (alignment) and ψ (packing efficiency) showed strong linear correlation with SEM-derived microstructure metrics.

Key findings demonstrate that yarns smaller than 10 μm diameter approach single nanofiber mechanical performance, and that capillary-driven densification effectively bridges the gap between intrinsic nanofiber properties and macroscopic yarn performance through enhanced interfiber adhesion and load transfer.

MIT finance professor Gary Gensler discusses financial system challenges and opportunities in a lecture covering: finance's role as intermediary for money and risk; key sectors including banking, insurance, asset management, and exchanges; primary versus secondary markets; the symbiotic relationship between finance, regulation, and technology; major risks including market, credit, liquidity, funding, and model/correlation risks; the 2008 financial crisis caused by weak underwriting, predatory lending, easy credit, derivatives leverage, and poor risk management; and blockchain's potential as a disruptive technology targeting legacy systems and economic rents in financial services.

Physicists developed a method to generate self-organizing liquid droplets that form predictable layered patterns, with potential applications for pharmaceuticals and consumer products. The technique, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, uses immiscible liquids (oil, water, and alcohol) that de-mix from the edges inward when confined in droplets or thin straws, creating tunable stripe patterns based on de-mixing speed. The research enables designed emulsions resembling nested structures with controlled, step-wise release of inner droplets. Co-authors include NYU researchers Jasna Brujić, Pepijn Moerman, Eric Vanden-Eijnden, and the late Pierre Hohenberg.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui's convictions and sentences for being a felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry. The court rejected his challenges to his 120-month sentences, which exceeded the advisory guideline range of 63-78 months, finding no abuse of discretion in the district court's upward departure and variance. The court also rejected his constitutional challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) as foreclosed by circuit precedent, which Verastegui raised solely to preserve for Supreme Court review.

OnePlus has released Android Nougat updates for the OnePlus 3 and OnePlus 3T, with global rollout beginning and wider availability expected within days. Both devices share identical software builds despite different specifications. The updates include Nougat features like redesigned notifications and settings menus, multi-window support, direct-reply notifications, and doze on the go, plus OxygenOS 4.0 tweaks. Users can manually check for updates in Settings > About > Software updates if not yet notified.

This lecture discusses the nuclear force, which is the residual interaction between quarks in different hadrons that binds nuclei together. Experimental understanding comes from nucleon-nucleon scattering, nuclear binding energies, and nuclear structure information. The nuclear force depends on distance (short-range, vanishing beyond ~2 femtometers and strongly repulsive below ~0.5 femtometers), spin, and angular momentum, but shows charge independence—it does not depend on whether nucleons are protons or neutrons. This charge independence allows study of mirror nuclei (where N and Z are swapped for the same A), enabling researchers to investigate properties of unstable radioactive nuclei by examining their stable mirror counterparts.

Enjifit, a workout partner app, launched on July 3, 2018 for iOS devices. The app connects users with nearby workout partners or personal trainers based on shared goals and interests. Features include filtering users by location, in-app messaging, workout reminders, and posting sessions for others to join. The app is free to download, with a PRO subscription for trainers and nutritionists to feature their services. Founded by 27-year-old Nicole Garcia and based in New York City, Enjifit celebrated its launch with an event on July 1, 2018. An Android version is planned.

Independent developer Milky Tea announced that HyperBrawl Tournament will come to Steam's Early Access in June 2017. The game is a combat sports arena title combining handball with PvP combat, featuring 10 warriors, 10 weapons, 6 arenas, 8 mini games, and 1-4 player local or online multiplayer in 1v1 or 2v2 formats.

Pepsi's No Shakin' Carry Go campaign will send 10 winners on a 3-day VVIP trip to the One Africa Music Fest in Dubai this November. The all-expense paid trip includes meeting Pepsi stars Wizkid, Tiwa Savage, Davido, and Tekno. The One Africa Music Fest is the world's biggest Afrobeats Festival, previously held in New York, London, and Houston. Entry details will be announced on Pepsi Nigeria's social media accounts: @pepsi_naija on Instagram and Twitter, and Pepsi Nigeria on Facebook.

This patent application describes a method for training and using a depth estimation model that generates depth maps from single color input images. The model is trained using monocular video data and/or stereoscopic image pairs with an input scale occlusion and motion aware loss function. The training process involves extracting depth maps and poses from images, generating synthetic frames through projection, and calculating photometric reconstruction errors to refine model parameters. The loss function addresses occlusion issues by using minimum photometric reconstruction errors between multiple synthetic frames, incorporates upsampled depth features to avoid artifacts, and masks static features to prevent inaccurate depth predictions. The trained model enables applications such as augmented reality in location-based parallel reality games, where virtual content is properly occluded and scaled based on real-world depth.

Tech megacaps lost $770 billion in value on Friday as the Nasdaq dropped 3.6%, its steepest decline since April. Nvidia, Amazon, and Tesla each fell about 5%. The sell-off followed President Trump's threat to impose a "massive increase of Tariffs" on Chinese imports, with later announcements of a 100% tariff on China and export controls on critical software effective November 1. Nvidia's market cap declined by nearly $229 billion, Microsoft's by $85 billion, and Amazon's by $121 billion. Tesla dropped $71 billion. The tech-heavy declines also pushed the S&P 500 down 2.7%.

A new Accenture study finds that investors across all ages and wealth levels prefer hybrid wealth management combining robo-advisers with human expertise, rather than choosing one over the other. The survey of 1,300 investors found that online tools once considered optional are now expected, and respondents ranked hybrid firms highest for offering low-cost robo access plus human guidance for complex situations. The findings contrast with recent industry moves: BlackRock cut portfolio managers for data-mining investments, while Betterment added human advisory services.

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan in Braselton, Georgia, finishing 1-under 863 for a one-shot victory over Lipscomb. The Owls, ranked No. 32 entering conference play, secured their seventh straight NCAA Regional spot. Jake Fendt and Pablo Rodriguez-Tabernero tied for second at 2 under. Lipscomb's Dawson Armstrong won the individual title at 6-under 210, becoming the Bison's first ASUN individual men's champion. Armstrong, ranked No. 37 nationally, earned his sixth college win and third of the 2016-17 season. Jacksonville's David Wicks, co-ASUN Player of the Year with Armstrong, tied for eighth at 1 over. Four ASUN teams—Kennesaw State, Lipscomb, Jacksonville, and North Florida—are likely to receive NCAA Regional bids.

Episode four of UFC 216 Embedded features Demetrious Johnson shopping for suits and studio equipment, Ray Borg training at the UFC Performance Institute, Derrick Lewis doing a mock weigh-in with Forrest Griffin, Tony Ferguson trying on fight night wardrobe, and Kevin Lee visiting a children's cancer center, culminating in media day interviews and faceoffs at T-Mobile ahead of UFC 216 on October 7.

On April 13, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of $12.5 billion in notes across seven series with maturity dates from 2024 to 2062, with interest rates ranging from 2.730% to 4.100%. The offering, underwritten by Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Morgan Stanley, had an aggregate public offering price of $12.719 billion and estimated net proceeds of approximately $12.692 billion. The notes were issued pursuant to a supplemental indenture naming Computershare Trust Company as successor trustee.

North Wales Police are appealing for witnesses after an attempted kidnapping of a woman in her 30s on Sisson Street in Rhyl at 8:25am. A man in his 40s of oriental appearance tried to force her into a silver vehicle, but she escaped unharmed. Initial reports suggesting a child was involved prompted Denbighshire council to alert head teachers and parents; police later confirmed no child was involved. DCI Neil Harrison stated the incident appears isolated with unknown motive. Police urge anyone with information to contact them via web chat, 101, or Crimestoppers quoting reference V151756.

Zimbabwean pupils appealed to President Mnangagwa to suspend November 2018 public examinations, citing inadequate preparation due to teachers being absent for Zimbabwe Electoral Commission duties. The request was made by Child Parliamentarians during a meeting with the President and was disclosed by Permanent Secretary Dr Sylvia Utete-Masango at a conference. As a remedy for lost teaching time, she suggested schools implement holiday lessons and noted the third term would open early on September 4. Schools were scheduled to close on July 26 for elections on July 30, cutting 10 working days from the second term. The President's response to the pupils' request was not revealed.

NASA's New Horizons spacecraft, which conducted the first Pluto flyby in July 2015, was extended to explore Kuiper Belt Objects. By January 1, 2019, it will reach 2014 MU69, nicknamed "Ultima Thule" through a public naming campaign hosted by the SETI Institute. This object, located 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto, will be the most primitive and farthest object ever observed by a spacecraft. Observations suggest it may be an extreme prolate spheroid or a close/contact binary. The name Ultima Thule, meaning "beyond the known world," was selected from 34,000 public nominations. A formal name will be submitted to the IAU after the flyby, depending on whether MU69 is a single body, binary pair, or multiple objects.

This study presents the largest genetic analysis of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) to date, using exome sequencing data from 454,803 UK Biobank and 173,585 Geisinger Health System participants. The researchers identified 27,331 CHIP mutation carriers in UKB (6% prevalence) and 12,877 in GHS (7.4% prevalence), with DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 being the most commonly mutated genes. Prevalence reached approximately 15% by age 75 and doubled every 9-12 years.

The genome-wide association study identified 27 loci (24 novel) associated with CHIP risk, with replication in the GHS cohort. Rare variant analyses revealed significant associations at SMC4 and CHEK2 loci, and gene burden testing implicated ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Gene-specific analyses showed that DNMT3A-CHIP had the most associated loci (23), with protective variants identified in PARP1 and LY75. Notably, variants at the TCL1A locus showed opposing effects—increasing DNMT3A-CHIP risk while decreasing TET2-CHIP and ASXL1-CHIP risk.

CHIP showed limited overlap with mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCA), though carriers were enriched for mCAs. Genetic correlation was observed between CHIP and mosaic loss of Y chromosome (mLOY). The study also identified novel rare variant associations with mCA phenotypes and telomere length.

Cross-sectional phenotypic analyses revealed expected associations with hematologic, cardiovascular, and oncologic traits, plus novel associations with obesity measures that varied by CHIP subtype. Longitudinal analyses confirmed elevated risks of blood cancer (HR=3.88), myeloid cancer (HR=7.10), lung cancer (HR=1.64), and all-cause mortality (HR=1.27) among high VAF CHIP carriers. TET2-CHIP drove cardiovascular disease risk, while DNMT3A-CHIP was not associated with lymphoid leukemia. A DNMT3A polygenic risk score predicted multiple CHIP subtypes and several cancers but not cardiovascular disease.

The study did not replicate previous findings of IL6R-mediated cardioprotection in CHIP carriers when extended to the full cohort. The authors conclude that CHIP represents heterogeneous subtypes with shared genetic etiology but distinct clinical risk profiles, identifying potential therapeutic targets including PARP1 and LY75 for DNMT3A-CHIP prevention.

Attacking runs in soccer are off-the-ball movements by offensive players into open space to receive passes from teammates. Key concepts include recognizing or creating open space, choosing appropriate run types (bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, wide), breaking away from defenders, timing runs to avoid offside, receiving optimal passes, and communicating with teammates. Effective runs require coordination between runner and passer regarding direction, speed, and timing. Coaching progression involves demonstration with cones, adding passes, introducing stationary then moving defenders, and advancing to full play scenarios.

This passage is a transcript of interviews with several NHL draft prospects, including James van Riemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby, and Karl Alzner. The interviewer asks questions about their backgrounds, college or professional plans, family influences, and hockey experiences. The prospects discuss their decisions about college hockey programs, their exposure to NHL teams and scouts, family members who played professionally, and their draft expectations. The event takes place in Columbus before a game, with the interviewer congratulating the players and wishing them luck with upcoming media interviews and the draft.

The "Clock" Offense is a 1-3-1 formation used to attack the Diamond & One defense by placing the "Star" player in the middle, creating open looks, lay-ups, and offensive putbacks while isolating the Star 1-on-1 against a chaser typically unprepared for post defense. The offense includes basic outside rotation with corner pass-and-cut sequences, post feeds, ball reversals, and post isolation options. Dribble clear actions allow wings to exchange roles with corners through back cuts. High post triangle action isolates the Star against the chaser with drop pass options for easy layups and kick-out passes for open shots. Offensive rebounding produces three-on-two advantages and back screen opportunities. Success requires execution of double screens, base screens, strong post ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Implementation involves scouting opponents, educating players on defensive reads and counters, using various alignments, and attacking weakest defenders. The Diamond & One defense uses four zone defenders with one player in strong pass denial against the opponent's top scorer, best deployed against odd or one-guard front offenses.

Education initiatives often fail not because of flawed ideas but because of poorly designed narratives. The sector invests heavily in program development but neglects how to communicate them, allowing public skepticism—rooted in past experiences of top-down mandates, data misuse, and technology fears—to dominate. Researchers Uncapher and Kendall-Taylor propose treating narrative as designable R&D: frame core ideas, test metaphors and values with audiences, iterate based on feedback, then scale through toolkits and training. Effective strategies include leading with shared values, using concrete metaphors, explaining mechanisms, centering human benefits, and transparently addressing risks. Trust is rebuilt when communities see themselves in the story and safeguards are visible.

The Texas Supreme Court issued a tentative opinion to remove the American Bar Association's authority over determining law school graduates' eligibility for the Texas bar exam. The move aligns with conservative criticism of the ABA's power but leaves unclear how oversight would function. The court stated it does not plan to add administrative burdens and may consider other multi-state accreditors later. Public comments are due by December 1, with changes potentially enacted in January. The ABA is reviewing the implications and will submit comments.

The Las Vegas Aces lead the Phoenix Mercury 3-0 in the 2025 WNBA Finals and can complete the first sweep since 2020 with a win in Game 4. The Aces have overcome early-season struggles and a 17-point deficit in Game 3, relying on coach Becky Hammon's defensive schemes, bench contributions from players like Jewell Loyd and A'ja Wilson's clutch performance. Wilson's last-second winner in Game 3 sealed the 90-88 victory. The Aces' core trio of Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, together for multiple seasons, has provided cohesion and consistency. Hammon has varied defensive strategies throughout the series, including zone defenses that disrupted Phoenix's rhythm. Mercury's Nyara Sabally is out for Game 4 with a concussion.
Akure-based lawyer Morakinyo Ogele issued a seven-day ultimatum to the EFCC to publicly apologize to Sun Newspaper for invading its premises and pay N1 billion compensation.

Police in Guilford and Milford, Connecticut are warning residents to lock their vehicles after a series of car break-ins and thefts along the shoreline. Thieves, described as groups of young adults or juveniles, have targeted dozens of vehicles nightly, stealing property and vehicles when keys are left inside. Officials express concern for public safety as suspects drive recklessly when fleeing. Milford police are also seeking two suspects who used stolen credit cards. Police advise residents to lock cars, keep outdoor lights on, and call 911 if they see suspicious activity.

A coach discusses his team's performance in a hockey game, noting that penalty kills changed the game's course and praising his players' effort despite the loss. He defends goaltender Pekka Rinne, calling him a "rock" and team backbone, while acknowledging the difficulty of five-on-three situations and unlucky deflections. He highlights a goal by inexperienced player Freddy and emphasizes respecting opponents' capabilities. The coach addresses defensive matchups, expressing trust in all defensemen including the less-heralded pair of Maty and Weby. He discusses Stanley Cup Final pressure, noting Rinne's big-game experience with his country, and states the team has gained valuable experience through past playoff runs despite lacking finals experience. He mentions maintaining consistent preparation routines and acknowledges the importance of speed against fast opponents like Pittsburgh. Finally, he praises Filip Forsberg as a mature leader who emerged through opportunity.

US stock indexes fell sharply after Trump threatened 100% tariffs on China starting November 1, with the S&P 500 dropping 2.36% last week and closing at its lowest level since early July. The index fell 3.33% over two days from a record high of 6,427.02 to 6,212.69. The VIX volatility index rose to 21.90, its highest since June 23. Crude oil declined 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% Monday after OPEC+ announced further production increases. Investor sentiment showed 40.3% bullish and 33.0% bearish in the latest AAII survey. Analysts warn of potential deeper correction amid trade uncertainty, weak economic data, and stretched valuations.

Output capacitance for converters is determined by two calculations: maximum allowable voltage deviation during load transients and output voltage ripple requirements, with the larger value selected. For the design example, at least 1.3 mF was required, but approximately 2.3 mF was used to account for radiation-induced single event transients in space-grade designs. An optional output filter with an additional inductor and ceramic capacitance can reduce output voltage ripple. The filter's resonant frequency should exceed the crossover frequency but remain below the switching frequency and ESR zero. A damping resistor may address high-frequency peaking. The converter's cycle-by-cycle current limiting activates at approximately 35 A, providing 45% margin above the 24.25 A peak inductor current, with primary-side current sensed through a 1:100 current sense transformer.

A report by the International Whaling Commission found that 122 pregnant female minke whales were among 333 killed during Japan's latest Antarctic hunt, with 114 whales not yet adults. Japan reduced its quota from 900 to 333 in 2014 after an International Court of Justice ruling against its "research whaling," but continues defending the program as necessary for population management and cultural tradition.

The speaker reports that Congress was able to convene in Philadelphia despite contagious sickness, and suggests amending the 1794 law to allow postponing congressional meetings. While peace in Europe has not been restored, the nation enjoys domestic tranquility, prosperous agriculture, and civil liberty. U.S. envoys to France have arrived in Holland and proceeded to Paris. The speaker recommends maintaining precautionary defense measures, emphasizing that commerce is essential to American prosperity and requires protection. Spanish troops remain on U.S. territory contrary to treaty obligations, and foreign agents are attempting to incite Indian hostilities. Various treaty commissions with Britain and Spain are proceeding on boundary disputes, debt claims, and captures. The United States must fulfill obligations to British subjects for losses, and consular expenses for captured seamen require reimbursement. The consular act needs revision regarding seamen's support and forged papers. The speaker urges the House to consider national debts and taxes, recommending immediate taxes over loans. The session opens during a critical period in European affairs requiring national unity.

This email from Ann Schmidt to Jeff Dasovich contains news summaries dated July 16-17, 2001, regarding Enron and energy industry developments. The passage details defensive strategies against the Power Offense in basketball, focusing on two primary approaches: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. Show & Recover involves defenders temporarily stepping out to impede shooters before quickly returning to their assignments, preventing switches that create mismatches. This method includes defending baseline crossings, down screens, and final matchup positioning. All Out SOS Disruption employs aggressive trapping tactics, including sideline pushes to prevent mid-penetration, inverting big defenders inside, contact switches on screens, and wing double teams to force offenses into unplanned situations. The system requires precise rotational positioning (Triangle "I" formations) when the ball is passed out of traps, with defenders adjusting based on offensive actions.

Quantum-correlated pairs are essential resources for quantum information science. While entangled photon pairs have been widely demonstrated, generating nonclassical phonon pairs via optical control remains challenging due to limited single-photon optomechanical coupling strength. This work presents a method to generate quantum-correlated phonon pairs from an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity using effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity, where Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions occur simultaneously in one pulse. The effective optomechanical spontaneous four-wave mixing process creates degenerate correlated phonon pairs, which are retrieved by a second pulse and verified using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

AMD's SFS (Secure Firmware Update) support is limited to priority runtime concerns affecting AMD-provided binary firmware components in AGESA releases. SFS updates are non-persistent and serve as interim steps between BIOS releases, allowing customers more time to validate new BIOS versions. Each SFS update package is designed for a specific PI release with defined base patch and firmware level requirements.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, using fixed frequency, peak current mode control with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. The devices support multiple converter topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, and require external gate drivers. A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices details component selection: 205 kΩ for RT, feedback resistors of 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ for 5V output, 20.5 kΩ resistors for 25 ns dead time, 49.9 kΩ for ~50 ns leading edge blank time, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, transformer with 2.5:1 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance, 170V GaN FETs for primary switches, 80V GaN FETs for synchronous rectifiers, 0.47 μH output inductor, and 2.3 mF output capacitance for radiation-induced transient mitigation. The controllers operate from 4V to 14V input with 0.1 µF minimum bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds, routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes, and placing bypass capacitors close to pins.

Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns contain crystallographic information used for symmetry determination, phase classification, and orientation determination. Direct electron detectors (DEDs) offer superior detection quantum efficiency and modulation transfer function compared to indirect detectors, though hybrid pixel detectors (HPDs) have larger pixel pitch that limits angular resolution. This study demonstrates a sub-pixel shift-and-add algorithm to create super-resolution EBSD patterns using a Timepix-based TruePix detector (256×256 pixels, 55 µm pitch). Multiple patterns collected with sub-pixel spatial offsets were registered and summed to improve resolution. Experiments on silicon single crystals showed the super-resolution method increased signal-to-noise ratio from 30 to 70, outperforming long-exposure single frames and frame integration methods. The technique requires no hardware modification and enables 10× up-sampling, revealing fine features including higher-order Laue zone rings and detailed band structure comparable to camera retraction and simulation methods. Applications include improved pattern indexing, strain measurement, and addressing pseudosymmetry challenges.

This report examines newcomer education in California, defining newcomers as recently arrived students with limited English proficiency, often from disadvantaged backgrounds and with trauma histories. In 2020–21, California had 151,996 Title III Immigrant Students (2.5% of K–12 enrollment), with 67% socioeconomically disadvantaged and significant language diversity. Newcomers face distinct challenges: they differ from typical English learners, lack dedicated support systems, and experience poor outcomes including high dropout rates. Federal court rulings guarantee their educational rights, but many districts may not meet legal standards due to resource constraints. California lacks comprehensive state data on newcomers and students with interrupted formal education (SIFE). Funding comes through the Local Control Funding Formula, CalNEW program ($5 million annually), Opportunities for Youth pilot ($9.7 million), and federal Title III funds, though only 22.4% of eligible newcomers received Title III Immigrant Student Program funding in 2022–23 due to enrollment decline requirements. Effective practices include specialized instruction, integrated language/content teaching, translanguaging, extended learning time, welcoming environments, robust intake processes, and community partnerships for legal, housing, food, and mental health services. Recommendations include building state leadership capacity, improving data systems, codifying the OFY initiative, adjusting funding formulas for late-arriving students, addressing newcomers in instructional frameworks, investing in open curricula, supporting research, and advocating for federal policy changes.

Red Same, Red Opposite, and Red Rover are SOS mid-court defensive scenarios used to disrupt opponents' half-court offense, change tempo, and create turnovers. All involve trapping the ballhandler near the sideline hash mark, with non-trapping defenders forming a Triangle I formation. The scenarios differ only in which defender initiates the trap: in Red Same, X3 traps with X1; in Red Opposite, X2 rotates to trap with X1; in Red Rover 4 and 5, designated defenders X4 or X5 trap with X1. When the trapped player passes out, defenders execute "Near Player" rotations to the nearest offensive player, with sprint releases to high post and SNUGGLE denials on perimeter players. All scenarios conclude in either "Base Go Red" or "Base Go I" based on the coach's predetermined decision, with standard SOS rules applying throughout.

Astronomers discovered exoplanet MOA-2016-BLG-227Lb using gravitational microlensing. The super-Jupiter mass planet (2.8 Jupiter masses) orbits an M or K dwarf star (0.29 solar masses) approximately 21,000 light years away in the galactic bulge at 1.67 AU. The microlensing event was detected May 5, 2016 by the MOA group using New Zealand's MOA-II telescope, with follow-up observations from telescopes in Hawaii, Chile, and Israel. The research team, led by Naoki Koshimoto of Osaka University, published findings April 6, 2017 on arXiv. The analysis combined lightcurve data with Keck adaptive optics imaging, employing Bayesian analysis considering various contamination scenarios for excess flux—a first for microlensing events. The authors recommend further study using Hubble, Keck AO, and future telescopes including JWST, GMT, TMT, and ELT.

Backtesting is the process of testing trading strategies against historical market data to evaluate their potential effectiveness, profitability, and risk before risking real capital. It relies on high-quality historical data that includes delisted assets to avoid survivorship bias, and factors in transaction costs and slippage for realistic results. Key metrics include the Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and win rate. To avoid overfitting, traders should use diverse datasets, out-of-sample testing, and sensitivity analysis. Backtesting cannot guarantee future success due to changing market conditions and psychological factors not captured in simulations. It is commonly applied across asset classes including forex, cryptocurrencies, futures, options, and CFDs, with each presenting unique challenges such as volatility, leverage, and data quality. Tools range from user-friendly platforms like TrendSpider to comprehensive systems like MetaTrader. Backtesting works best when integrated with forward testing, paper trading, and real-time market analysis, and requires continuous refinement based on feedback and changing market dynamics.

Organizer Jesse Tomlin, who has been in recovery for seven years, started the event to provide fellowship and support while addressing the local overdose epidemic, which claimed 37 lives in Carroll County in the first five months of 2018. Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah, after conservative commentators published past blog posts attributed to him that criticized President Trump during his first term. The posts, allegedly written while Rosenzweig was at a private law firm before joining the U.S. attorney's office in September 2020, called Trump "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist." He becomes one of dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump's Justice Department who were believed to be at odds with the president's political agenda. The Department of Justice has also fired three other prosecutors in the same district who previously worked with former special counsel Jack Smith.

The NVIDIA RTX Blackwell architecture introduces GDDR7 memory with built-in ECC and EDR technology, Fifth-Generation Tensor Cores supporting FP4/FP6/FP8 formats, and Fourth-Generation RT Cores with double ray-triangle intersection throughput. Key innovations include Mega Geometry for high-detail ray tracing with Cluster-level Acceleration Structures and Partitioned TLAS, Linear Swept Spheres for hair rendering, Shader Execution Reordering 2.0, and an AI Management Processor for GPU workload scheduling. Blackwell adds 4:2:2 video codec support, Ninth-Generation NVENC with AV1 UHQ mode, DisplayPort 2.1b with 80 Gbps bandwidth, and Max-Q power efficiency improvements including advanced power gating and accelerated frequency switching. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame and transformer-based AI models for improved image quality. The architecture enables neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API, supporting RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The flagship GB202 GPU powers the RTX 5090 with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA Cores, while GB203 powers the RTX 5080/5070 Ti with 45.6 billion transistors, and GB205 powers the RTX 5070 with 31 billion transistors.

In *William Skrainka et al. v. Gerard B. Allen* (1879), the Missouri court established four principles: creditors must be preferred over stockholders in corporate asset matters; stockholders who received second-mortgage bonds to compensate for excess calls remain liable to creditors for unpaid stock equal to bond sale proceeds; corporations cannot increase liabilities by issuing bonds without valuable consideration; and in statutory proceedings against stockholders, liability is determined by shares held at the date of motion after notice, not at execution return date. The court held Allen liable for bonus stock credits and bond sale proceeds, but reversed the lower court's calculation of his liability based on shares held at execution return rather than motion filing date.

A coach discusses a young player's development, emphasizing playing "the right way" through details like winning puck battles and wall play rather than focusing on scoring. The team reduced his minutes due to his first professional season demands. The coach praises Sidney Crosby's leadership in making young players comfortable, describes the team's balanced scoring lines and scrappy, resilient identity, and explains coaching strategies including video analysis, line adjustments, and encouraging players to trust their instincts on shooting decisions.

The 3-3-5 defense uses 3 defensive linemen, 3 linebackers, and 5 defensive backs, emphasizing speed and athleticism over size. It offers flexibility through disguised coverages like Cover 1 and Cover 3 from the same pre-snap shell, and can generate pressure from multiple positions. Vulnerabilities include edge running plays and seam routes in pass coverage. Common blitzes include the Sam Blitz and SAW Blitz. Joe Lee Dunn invented the scheme; notable users include Iowa State under Matt Campbell and high school coach Tim Racki, who won 8 state titles with it.

This patent application describes dry electrode films for energy storage devices incorporating microparticulate non-fibrillizable binders with particle sizes of 0.5–40 μm, particularly cellulose derivatives like carboxymethylcellulose (CMC). The invention addresses limitations in existing dry electrode fabrication methods by using jet-milled binders to achieve smaller, more uniform particle sizes that improve electrode film mechanical properties, reduce defects, and enhance electrochemical performance. The dry electrode films combine fibrillizable binders (e.g., PTFE) with microparticulate non-fibrillizable binders (e.g., CMC, PVDF) and active materials through solvent-free processes including high-shear jet milling and calendering. Example 1 demonstrates that jet-milled CMC with 10 μm particle size versus 70 μm commercial CMC increased first-cycle efficiency from 90.2% to 90.9%, improved cell-to-cell consistency, eliminated film defects, and increased tensile strength from 0.936 N to 1.74 N. The electrode films are self-supporting, free-standing, and suitable for lithium-ion batteries and other energy storage devices, with applications in electric vehicles and consumer electronics.

AMD shares rose following an AI chip deal with OpenAI. New York's early intervention providers have not received a substantive raise in 30 years, with reimbursement rates for many services lower today than in the 1990s. Providers, who include special education teachers and therapists with master's degrees, typically earn $50,000-$70,000 annually—far less than comparable positions in other settings. The stagnation has caused widespread provider attrition, leaving vulnerable children without critical developmental services. A 2024 state-authorized 5% rate increase remains pending federal approval, while a 2025 telehealth rate cut caused many virtual providers to quit. Similar pay crises affect early intervention programs in Texas, Rhode Island, Illinois, and other states. Research shows timely early intervention reduces future special education needs and improves life outcomes, but families increasingly face months-long delays or complete lack of access to services.
The defendant's appeal from a Supreme Court judgment was dismissed, with all five judges concurring.

Research indicates that dietary protein guidelines may need updating because not all protein sources are equal in quality. While U.S. adults consume 35-55% more protein than recommended, many—especially those over 70—may lack sufficient high-quality protein. Protein quality depends on essential amino acid composition and bioavailability; animal proteins generally outperform plant proteins. Studies show that under current guidelines, plant-based proteins like peanut butter and legumes require significantly larger quantities to match animal protein benefits. The Netherlands has adjusted guidelines for plant-based diets, recommending meat-eaters consume less meat while vegetarians and vegans eat more protein or animal products like dairy and eggs. Older adults face particular challenges due to reduced muscle protein synthesis efficiency and higher amino acid requirements. Strategies to improve protein quality include combining complementary plant proteins (such as beans and rice), processing methods like soaking and fermentation, and choosing softer animal protein preparations. Experts suggest personalized guidelines based on demographics and shifting focus from protein quantity to essential amino acid requirements.

This email from Sarah Palmer to herself dated January 14, 2002, contains a compilation of news articles about Enron. The articles cover: an Enron employee's August 2001 warning to CEO Kenneth Lay about accounting problems; the delayed release of details regarding the sale of Enron's trading unit to UBS Warburg, which would give Enron and creditors 33% of pretax profits for at least two years with no upfront cash; Rep. John Dingell's statement about "pretty strong evidence" of insider trading and false accounting; the Senate Banking Committee's scheduling of a February 12 hearing on Enron; former CEO Jeffrey Skilling's short sale of competitor AES Corp. stock after his resignation; the potential shutdown of Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company in India due to cash shortages; BG Group's ongoing negotiations to renegotiate a $388 million deal for Enron's Indian upstream assets; commentary on the Enron scandal reaching "a whole new level" with political implications; energy traders' efforts to address debt concerns following Enron's collapse; and a CNNfn segment discussing the UBS deal and broader market concerns.

New research shows the average Brit wakes up three times nightly, with one in 10 waking 7-10 times. A survey of 2,000 adults by Tweak Mattress identified 10 main causes: needing the toilet (47%), snoring (41%), partner occupying space (25%), discomfort (19%), bad dreams (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), phone use (10%), sleep talking (10%), anxiety (6%), and partners watching TV/reading (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart explained that sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene (pre-bed routines) and sleep cycles, noting that environmental factors like noise and discomfort disrupt the light REM stage where people most easily stir.

The author analyzes Apple's stock valuation through multiple metrics rather than comparing it to competitors. Using P/E, EV/EBITDA, EV/Operative FCF, and EV/FCF multiples correlated with their respective growth drivers, the author finds that Apple's current valuation exceeds projected levels across all models. The strongest correlation (R²=0.57) exists between EV/FCF and FCF growth rate. Based on this analysis, the author concludes Apple's shares are overvalued and buying at current prices is a poor investment decision. The author discloses no positions in Apple and no plans to initiate positions within 72 hours.

Anthropologist Donald Blakeslee discovered an interactive sacred shrine in a Kansas backyard—limestone boulders carved by Wichita Nation sculptors centuries ago. The shrine features holes, basins, and channels that direct water flow, reflecting Wichita religious beliefs about water moving between three layers of existence (sky, world, underground). Blakeslee demonstrated its functionality by pouring water through it. Nearby, another boulder contains depressions where women once prayed for successful pregnancies. Gary McAdams, a leader of the Wichita and Affiliated Tribes, explained that water was transformational in ancient Wichita culture, used for baptisms, preparation before important events, and cleansing after death.

Intel's drone light show at Travis Air Force Base in northern California was postponed from July 4th to July 5th due to 30 mph winds exceeding the drones' 18 mph limit. The 500-drone display, featuring patriotic imagery synchronized to music, is being considered as a safer alternative to fireworks in wildfire-prone areas. CalFire officials support the shift to drones for fire safety. Several western cities used drone shows this year due to fire dangers, including Arizona events by Firefly Drone Shows that proceeded as planned.

This article surveys theoretical results on transformer expressivity using logic, automata, and circuit complexity. Transformers are formalized as functions mapping strings to tokens, with variants including Unique Hard Attention Transformers (UHAT), Average Hard Attention Transformers (AHAT), and SoftMax Attention Transformers (SMAT). UHAT with positional encodings is strictly contained in AC⁰ and captures FO[Mon] (first-order logic with monadic numerical predicates), including all regular languages in AC⁰ and non-regular languages like Palindrome. AHAT extends to TC⁰ and expresses Counting LTL, with masked NoPE-AHAT equivalent to Kt[#] and NoPE-AHAT recognizing permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images. Verification of Masked UHAT is decidable (EXPSPACE-complete), while NoPE-AHAT verification is undecidable. Two key limitations are discussed: hard attention approximates soft attention imperfectly (though uniform AHAT layers better approximate SMAT), and expressibility differs from trainability—PARITY is expressible by SMAT but difficult to train, unlike MAJ. The article identifies open problems and aims to engage logic, automata, verification, and programming language researchers in the FLaNN community.

Some animal partnerships are unequal or exploitative. Pearlfish live in sea cucumbers' anuses for protection; some eat the cucumber's gonads. Pistol shrimp and gobies share burrows in a mutualistic relationship—gobies guard entrances while shrimp dig and clean parasites off the fish. Arid bronze azure butterfly larvae deceive bearded sugar ants by mimicking queen ants chemically, gaining entry to nurseries where they eat ant babies for nutrition.

Enron-related news from April 18-19, 2001 includes: Sycamore Networks faces declining sales as competitor Ciena wins business from its top customer Williams Communications; Enron India's Dabhol Power Co. will meet lenders April 23 in London regarding its disputed $2.4 billion Maharashtra power project, where MSEB owes 2.26 billion rupees and phase two may be scrapped; Enron-owned Azurix plans to break up and sell its water assets including Wessex Water; Enron Broadband fired 20% of staff due to weak bandwidth trading demand and cut capital spending from $750 million to $250 million; Nevada's PUC chairman asked the SEC to delay Sierra Pacific Resources' $3.1 billion purchase of Portland General Electric from Enron; and bandwidth trading struggles amid oversupply, with only about 10% of fiber capacity lit and prices falling sharply.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi campaigns for a liquor ban while a state government remains undecided, forming an 11-member committee to study the issue. The committee will visit six states—three with bans and three with state-run liquor shops—and submit recommendations in three months. Members of the Bahaniya Mukhti Vahini (BMV), an organization of women self-help groups and village representatives formed to address liquor-related abuse, have been included. The state currently operates 712 liquor shops, will not open new outlets, but will continue running unsold shops rather than closing them.

This lecture covers gender discrimination and identity in economics. The agenda includes: reasons to study gender differences (equality/fairness, efficiency, preference formation); the gender wage gap (20-30% remaining even for equal work, with gaps widening mid-career); technological solutions like blind auditions (which increased women in orchestras but had limitations); belief biases where women are punished more for failures and rewarded less for successes; gender identity norms such as men earning more than wives (creating a "missing mass" of couples near 50% income split); child penalties affecting women's long-term earnings; and non-promotable tasks where women volunteer more and are asked more due to higher compliance rates, amplifying gender disparities.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end and precision reference, featuring nine configuration registers and multiSPI interface supporting SPI-compatible and source-synchronous protocols. The device operates through ACQ and CONV states triggered by CONVST/CS edges, with conversion time varying between tconv_min and tconv_max. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge, using 32-bit optimal frames or short/long variants, with commands executed at rising edge. Programming supports byte and half-word read/write operations, with output data configurable to include device address, range flags, alarms, and parity. The multiSPI interface offers single/dual SDO modes and internal/external clock options for source-synchronous operation. Key registers control reset/power (RST_PWRCTL_REG), SPI protocols (SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG), data output formatting (DATAOUT_CTL_REG), input ranges (RANGE_SEL_REG), and programmable alarm thresholds with hysteresis (ALARM_H_TH_REG, ALARM_L_TH_REG). The device includes NAP and power-down modes for power saving, with specific unlock sequences required. Applications include industrial analog input modules for PLCs, with recommended PCB layout emphasizing analog/digital partitioning and proper decoupling capacitors for AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO pins.

This passage explains a momentum-based sector rotation strategy between SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (20-year Treasury bonds). The strategy involves monthly rebalancing by investing in whichever ETF performed better in the prior month. TLT typically acts as a safe haven during stock market weakness, though this failed in 2022 when both assets declined sharply. Backtesting from 2003 shows a 9.2% CAGR with dividends reinvested, with maximum drawdown reaching 41% in 2022 after previously staying around 22%. The strategy works best in tax-deferred accounts and assumes no slippage or commissions. Entries and exits occur at monthly closes. The article notes momentum strategies generally perform well on 1-12 month timeframes but carry risks of large drawdowns and survivorship bias.

This study used a co-produced, community-based active case finding approach to identify 23 people with probable but undiagnosed Long Covid in three English localities (Camden, Merton, Derbyshire). Semi-structured interviews revealed four key themes: uncertainty and lack of awareness about Long Covid; barriers to healthcare engagement including self-doubt, hesitancy, and multi-system symptom complexity; experiences of enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma including discrimination based on age, gender, and ethnicity; and use of non-NHS treatments and social support. Participants reported epistemic injustice—symptoms dismissed by healthcare professionals, difficulty conveying experiences, and layered stigma compounding marginalization. Desired improvements included easier primary care access, longer appointments, dedicated Long Covid services, and employment protections. The study highlights how stigma and systemic barriers prevent disadvantaged groups from receiving Long Covid care, potentially increasing health inequalities.

Moldova's economy grew 1.1% year-on-year in Q2 2025, reversing a 1.2% contraction in Q1, driven by construction, energy, and ICT sectors. The National Bank of Moldova cut its benchmark rate to 6% in August to stimulate lending. The EBRD forecasts 1.5% GDP growth for 2025 and 3.8% for 2026, contingent on reforms and international support. Challenges include inflation, fiscal constraints, and currency volatility. Sustaining growth depends on securing EU financing and diversifying beyond remittances.

Turing architecture introduces GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps, 20% more power efficient than GDDR5X), larger L2 caches (6 MB in TU102, double previous generation), and improved memory compression for 50% effective bandwidth gains over Pascal. The display engine supports 8K/60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2, HDR with tone mapping, and VirtualLink/USB-C for single-cable VR connectivity. NVLink replaces SLI bridges, providing 50-100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth. RT Cores enable real-time ray tracing (10x faster than Pascal software emulation), while Tensor Cores power AI features like DLSS for image reconstruction and NGX for neural graphics acceleration. Mesh Shading eliminates CPU draw call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading optimizes rendering efficiency, and Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per pass for improved VR performance.

New York City's school system spends $25,087 per student—40% more than in 2008-09 and the highest among the nation's 100 largest districts—yet student performance has stagnated or declined. Over half the budget goes to employee benefits (30.3%) and teacher salaries (23.4%), with pension costs rising sharply. Critics cite waste, including $350 million for unsatisfactory broadband, $100 million annually for 1,300 unplaced teachers, and a $784 million school renewal program with poor results. From 2009-2015, fourth-grade math and reading scores dropped, while eighth-graders remained below national averages. Though graduation rates reached 72.6% in 2016, only half of graduates were college- or career-ready.

The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals dismissed an appeal by Charles M. Rice et al. against C. Raymond Bradford et al. upon stipulation of counsel, with mandate issued immediately. The case was decided per curiam on October 5, 1936.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy is a mean reversion approach for the S&P 500 that enters trades after three consecutive down days, exiting at the next day's open. Originally published in 2013 and updated with out-of-sample data, the strategy shows a 65% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, and 0.13% average gain per trade across 661 trades since 1993. Modifying the exit to the next day's close increases average gains to 0.24% but reduces win rate to 61% and raises drawdown to 17%. A further improved version from March 2022 achieves 0.35% average gains with 60% win rate and 10% drawdown while reducing market exposure. The strategy also works for Nasdaq 100 and individual stocks, though less effectively than for S&P 500. In the 2022 bear market, it executed 35 trades with 0.3% average gains.

In 1886, Hawaii passed legislation for a $2,000,000 loan pledged against kingdom revenues, which the U.S. opposed under reciprocity treaty privileges. In early 1887, the U.S. declined to approve a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance. On December 23, 1887, Britain proposed that the U.S., Britain, and Germany jointly guarantee Hawaiian neutrality and equal port access, referencing the 1843 Anglo-French convention recognizing Hawaiian independence. Secretary of State Bayard declined in February 1888, citing existing U.S.-Hawaii treaties that already restricted Hawaiian territorial concessions without U.S. consent and ensured equal port accessibility. Meanwhile, the British commissioner at Honolulu formally protested the U.S. exclusive use of Pearl Harbor under a supplementary reciprocity convention, arguing it violated British treaty rights, though the U.S. maintained the arrangement did not cede territory or jurisdiction.

Index Markets Research offers a statistical analysis report on the Global Polyolefin (POF) Shrink Film Market, covering industry definition, applications, manufacturing technology, market drivers, segmentation, revenue forecasts, and key players including Harwal Group, Sealed Air Corporation, and Amcor Limited. A hockey player discusses the commitment and positioning required for penalty killing, emphasizing awareness, instinct, and reading teammates' reactions. He notes the emotional nature of playoff hockey, particularly the finals, and the need to stay level-headed after wins and losses. He mentions his experience in different power play roles, praises a teammate's steady defensive play and fitness dedication, and recalls taking faceoffs in Ottawa.
