UFC light heavyweight champion Jon Jones wants to fight former heavyweight champion Brock Lesnar instead of current champion Stipe Miocic, citing greater fan interest, a larger payday, and more impact on the sport. Jones acknowledges Miocic is more talented but believes he is relatively unknown to the general public. His trainer Mike Winklejohn supports this decision, agreeing Lesnar is a better matchup for now and stating Miocic presents a harder fight that requires additional preparation.

GA10x GPUs feature third-generation NVLink with 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, PCIe Gen 4 with up to 64 GB/sec peak bandwidth, and a GA102 architecture containing seven GPCs with 84 SMs total. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB L1/Shared Memory. ROPs are now integrated into GPCs rather than memory controllers, increasing total ROPs to 112. The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput compared to Turing by adding FP32 capability to both datapaths, and features 33% larger combined L1 data cache and shared memory with double the bandwidth. Ampere GPUs achieve up to 1.9x better power efficiency than Turing.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add hardware-accelerated motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering than Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32 and BF16 data types, implement Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x throughput on sparse matrices, and enable up to 2.7x higher tensor operation throughput than Turing.

GDDR6X memory uses PAM4 signaling to achieve up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, a 52% improvement over TU102. RTX IO provides GPU-based loading and decompression, accelerating I/O performance by up to 100x compared to traditional storage. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5x AI training throughput compared to Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB scalable to 96GB via NVLink. Display outputs include DisplayPort 1.4a supporting 8K60 with DSC, and HDMI 2.1 with 48 Gbps bandwidth. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode support, while seventh-generation NVENC provides high-quality encoding up to 8K HEVC.

The MSPM0 C-Series microcontrollers feature an independent watchdog timer (IWDT) with a 25-bit counter and system-independent power/clock source that generates a POR reset if not reset within programmed time; a windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) with eight selectable periods, sleep mode auto-stop, and interval timer mode; and an RTC_B real-time clock with 32kHz input, calendar counters, customizable alarms, interval wake-up options, and calibration/compensation up to ±240ppm. General-purpose timers (TIMGx) support 16-bit counting, QEI, and cross-trigger synchronization, while advanced timers (TIMAx) add clock doubling, repeat counters, asymmetric PWM with dead band, and fault handling. The devices include IOMUX for pin function selection, SWD debug interface with security features, DEBUGSS with mailbox communication, and factory constants for device identification. Typical applications require 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors, 47kΩ pullup with 1000pF pulldown on NRST, and external crystal capacitors where applicable.

The double-down trading strategy involves adding an equal position size to a losing trade to improve the average entry price and recover losses faster if the price reverses. Backtests on SPY (S&P 500 ETF) showed improved performance metrics with doubling down in mean reversion strategies, with average gains per trade increasing from 0.56% to 0.97%. However, backtests on HYG (junk bond ETF), a trending asset, showed worsening results, with average losses increasing from 0.19% to 0.22% per trade. The strategy differs from the Martingale strategy, which doubles position size after each loss and increases risk substantially more. It also differs from the repair strategy, which uses call options. The double-down strategy is rarely part of a rational trading plan and often reflects a trading bias focused on price rather than probability of success.

A persistent heat wave is affecting the Northern Hemisphere, breaking temperature records in Canada, the United States, Europe, and the Middle East. In Montreal, 11 heat-related deaths have been reported. Ottawa recorded its highest humidex at 47, while Montreal hit 37 C on July 2. A cold front is expected to bring relief to Eastern Canada by Friday. In the U.S., excessive heat warnings were issued in New York and New Jersey, with heat index values up to 41, and Denver tied its all-time high of 40 C. At least one heat-related death was reported in Pennsylvania. In Europe, Scotland recorded its highest temperature ever at 33.2 C, and southern Russia saw 37 C during FIFA World Cup matches. The Middle East also set a world record in Quriyat, Oman, where temperatures remained above 42.6 C for 51 consecutive hours. Climate scientists link the duration and intensity of these heat waves to climate change.

The passage contains a December 31, 1842 message from the U.S. President to Congress regarding diplomatic and commercial matters concerning the Hawaiian (Sandwich) Islands and China. It references treaties between Hawaii and Britain (1836, 1839) and France (1839), and discusses the strategic importance of Hawaii as a Pacific refueling station, particularly for American whaling vessels. The President recommends funding a consul in Hawaii to protect American interests while disclaiming any U.S. desire for exclusive control. Regarding China, the message notes the recent Opium War treaty opening four ports to British trade and suggests the U.S. should negotiate similar access.

The document describes a low-side current sensing circuit using an amplifier and high-speed comparator to detect over-current conditions by amplifying the voltage drop across a shunt resistor. Design requirements specify generating a logic high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. The circuit requires 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors placed directly between device supply and ground pins to prevent supply ringing, false triggers, and oscillations from fast output edges. The device supports split or single supply configurations, with input signals required to stay within recommended ranges. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing input-output coupling, placing series resistors close to the device, using controlled impedance traces for long distances, and maintaining stable, low-noise power supplies. Additional sections cover documentation update notifications, support resources, electrostatic discharge precautions, mechanical packaging specifications, and legal disclaimers.

The Oppo R15 launch provides design clues for the upcoming OnePlus 6, expected by June. Both phones, along with Vivo models, share similar designs under parent company BBK Electronics. The OnePlus 6 will likely feature an iPhone X-like notch, 19:9 aspect ratio display, and possibly an under-display fingerprint sensor following the Vivo X21 UD launch. While the Oppo R15 uses MediaTek or Snapdragon 660 processors, the OnePlus 6 is expected to use a Snapdragon 845.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%-28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes up to $600 cell phone protection. The card charges a 5% balance transfer fee ($5 minimum) and a 3% foreign transaction fee, with no ongoing rewards program. It was named Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025.

Changes to the FAFSA's financial aid eligibility formula, which now incorporates IRS data subject to stricter privacy rules, have created confusion for colleges about what student information they can share with scholarship providers. A January survey found only 58% of financial aid offices would share federal income tax data from the FAFSA with scholarship organizations even with student consent, while 22% would never share it. The Native Forward Scholars Fund and other providers have experienced delays in accessing needed financial data, forcing students to bear extra burdens requesting information and jeopardizing their ability to attend college. The Education Department issued guidance last week clarifying that colleges can share FAFSA data with scholarship providers with student consent, and that two designated organizations can receive tax information directly without consent, but questions remain about upcoming security standards and streamlined consent processes.

The passage argues that tariffs rarely create harmful monopolies, but supports removing the tariff on anthracite coal. It advocates for monetary system elasticity to equalize interest rates, with banks providing adequate regulated circulation convertible to gold, without full reconstruction. It calls for immigration legislation and addresses balancing fair treatment for labor and capital, supporting both corporate and labor federations while opposing abuses by either. It emphasizes harmony between organized capital and labor with public interests, adherence to law, individual freedom, and mutual understanding, rejecting class animosity in politics and judging individuals by merit rather than class.

Tens of thousands of volunteers annually count birds within 15-mile diameter circles for one day, compiling data into ornithology's longest-running database spanning over a century. The Sheridan count is December 14 (contact Julie Rieder at 702-468-0029 or julie.rieder@gmail.com); the Story-Big Horn count is December 23 (contact Jean Daly at 306-674-9728 or djdaly@fiberpipe.net). Open to all skill levels, participants should bring lunch, water, warm clothing and footwear; binoculars, field guides and spotting scopes are suggested.

On September 10, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. for the issuance and sale of €1,000,000,000 in 1.375% Notes due 2024 and €1,000,000,000 in 2.000% Notes due 2027. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013, with interest payable annually. The 2024 Notes mature January 17, 2024, with interest beginning January 17, 2016; the 2027 Notes mature September 17, 2027, with interest beginning September 17, 2016.

The passage examines how global ICT firms are transforming their business strategies in response to the Internet of Things (IoT) and a "new productivity paradox." While IoT promises significant economic benefits, high R&D-intensive firms face declining marginal productivity of ICT due to the Internet's characteristics of freebies, easy copying, and standardization that drive technology prices down. This creates "uncaptured GDP"—value providing utility and happiness that traditional GDP metrics cannot measure.

The analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005–2016 reveals bi-polarization: high R&D-intensive firms fall into a vicious cycle of declining marginal productivity, while low R&D-intensive firms enjoy a virtuous cycle. Leading firms counter this by activating "self-propagating functions" through digital business strategies that harness "soft innovation resources"—including sleeping resources, trust-based information, and untapped potential—to develop "supra-functionality" beyond economic value.

Seven leading firms (Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, Amazon) demonstrate this transformation by shifting from product-centric models to service-oriented, trust-based strategies that create uncaptured GDP. The paper concludes that successful IoT-era strategies require recognizing the trap of ICT advancement, embracing soft value addition, and developing trust-based disruptive business models with consolidated challenge to social demand.

This video discusses nuclear binding energies, starting with observed nuclear abundances in the solar system showing hydrogen dominance and iron excess. Binding energy is defined as the difference between the sum of constituent masses (protons, neutrons, electrons) and the actual nuclear mass. The average binding energy per nucleon remains fairly constant at 7.5-9 MeV for most elements, peaking at iron, which enables both fission (heavy nuclei splitting) and fusion (light nuclei combining) as energy-releasing processes.

The Weizsäcker formula (semi-empirical mass formula or liquid-drop model) parameterizes binding energy through five terms: (1) volume term (~16 MeV/nucleon) indicating short-range nuclear forces; (2) surface correction reducing binding for surface nucleons; (3) Coulomb repulsion between protons; (4) asymmetry term favoring equal proton and neutron numbers due to Pauli exclusion; and (5) pairing term favoring even numbers of protons or neutrons. The resulting curve shows maximum binding energy around iron.

On September 27, 1945, Colonel Alfred McCormack was appointed Special Assistant to the Secretary of State for Research and Intelligence. Executive Order 9630 terminated the Foreign Economic Administration, transferring its foreign economic functions to the Department of State and assigning it surplus property disposal responsibilities in foreign areas. The passage documents 1945 developments in Lend-Lease operations, including congressional statements, presidential communications, and quarterly reports. It covers international finance developments, including Bretton Woods proposals, Export-Import Bank policy, and the December 27 signing of agreements establishing the International Monetary Fund and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Trade policy developments include the Trade Agreements Act renewal recommendation and commodity agreement policy addresses.

Uber has the technical capability to secretly record iPhone users' screens due to a unique permission granted by Apple, according to research by Sudo Security Group. The "entitlement" was originally given to improve Apple Watch functionality for map rendering. Researcher Will Strafach noted this permission appears unprecedented for third-party developers. Uber has since voluntarily removed this capability from newer app versions, stating it is no longer connected to their current codebase. There is no evidence Uber used this technology improperly, though the discovery raises questions about Apple's decision to grant such extensive permissions to the company.

Australian medical professionals warn that consuming more than one glass of wine nightly may indicate chronic alcoholism, with 27% of Australians aged 55-64 in New South Wales drinking at risky levels. Health experts recommend at least a few alcohol-free days weekly and limiting intake to two standard drinks most days. Risks of daily drinking include pancreatitis, liver disease, obesity, and alcoholic dementia. Research indicates even minimal alcohol consumption increases cancer risk, as alcohol is a carcinogen. Older adults often underestimate safe drinking limits, and rising substance misuse among aging populations, combined with cheap supermarket alcohol, contributes to growing health problems. Most alcoholic beverages exceed one standard drink, and guidelines cannot be met through weekly averaging.

U.S. imports from China reached $9,000,000 in some years, while exports to China totaled $1,200,000 in 1841, though actual American produce reaching China was higher through indirect trade. China, with 300 million people, historically excluded foreigners but showed signs of opening through its treaty with England establishing equal diplomatic correspondence. President John Tyler recommended Congress appropriate funds for a commissioner to reside in China to protect American citizens and their interests. Separately, representatives of Hawaiian King Kamehameha III noted that an 1826 treaty with U.S. Commander Thomas ap Catesby Jones was never ratified by the United States, though Hawaii had followed its terms for sixteen years.

The overlap in soccer is an attacking tactic where a wing fullback sprints past a midfielder along the sideline to become an unmarked attacking option. If the overlapping player is marked, another attacker becomes free. The overlap requires space and a clear vertical lane, typically resulting in a cross from the end-line. An "underlap" is a variation where the fullback runs inside the midfielder toward the middle, usually resulting in a shot on goal. In both cases, the defender returns to position after the play. A coach's anecdote illustrates that adding overlaps to an already crowded attack can backfire.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed a judgment dismissing Ross Nelson's action for specific performance of an 1892 land contract with Puyallup Indians John and Chekudakai Salerhand. The court held that restrictions on alienation in the 1886 patent to Salerhand remained valid despite the 1887 Bland Act granting citizenship to Indians, and that the 1893 Congressional act removing restrictions did not take effect until ten years after its passage. Contracts for conveyance of allotted Indian lands made prior to removal of restrictions were void. The court rejected arguments that the restrictions were repugnant to the fee grant, were personally applicable only, or were impliedly repealed by citizenship legislation, noting that government policy treated Indians as wards requiring protection from alienation of their lands.

The US government has auctioned off the seized Russian superyacht Amadea, formerly owned by sanctioned oligarch Suleyman Kerimov. The 106-meter vessel was seized in Fiji in 2022 by the KleptoCapture task force and was valued at approximately $230 million. The sealed bid auction closed on September 10, though the new owner and price remain undisclosed. The yacht's ownership has been legally contested by Eduard Khudainatov, who claims to own it, but a judge ruled him a "straw owner." Khudainatov has appealed, creating potential legal risks for the new owner, who may need to keep the yacht in US waters.

This article analyzes an SEIR-like epidemiological model with a time-dependent transmission parameter for SARS-CoV-2. The model includes nine compartments: susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic infectious, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased. The authors establish mathematical properties including well-posedness, continuity, and differentiability of the parameter-to-solution map. They apply Tikhonov regularization to estimate the transmission parameter from reported daily infections, providing conditions for existence, stability, and convergence of solutions. The model accounts for varying severity levels and different transmission rates across infectious compartments, with most parameters obtained from literature while the transmission rate is estimated from observed incidence data.

Enron-related news from April 7-8, 2001 includes: a $600 million energy management agreement with J.C. Penney; plans to cut 250 jobs (20% of workforce) at its broadband unit due to completed fiber-optic network and slow streaming media demand; taking a dispute with India's Maharashtra state government to arbitration over a $20 million unpaid electricity bill; and requesting a one-month delay on a Pompano Beach City Commission vote regarding a power plant rezoning. Mohamed Salah scored twice and assisted two goals as Liverpool defeated Roma 5-2 in the Champions League semi-final first leg. The speaker welcomes attendees to the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, acknowledging foreign representatives from Canada, European colonies, Latin American republics, and the Caribbean. Expositions serve as timekeepers of progress, stimulating enterprise and friendly industrial rivalry while recording advancements in art, science, and manufacture.

Modern inventions including telegraphs, steamships, and railroads have eliminated distances between nations, enabling instantaneous communication and vast international trade. The speech contrasts historical slow communication methods with modern rapid transmission of news, noting that isolation is no longer possible.

Trade statistics indicate unprecedented American prosperity, with productive employment for millions. However, the nation requires expanded foreign markets through reciprocity treaties rather than exclusiveness or commercial warfare. The speaker advocates for increased steamship service, an Isthmian canal, a Pacific cable, and expanded American merchant marine to facilitate trade.

The exposition honors James G. Blaine, whose spirit animates the pan-American movement for commerce and fraternity among Western Hemisphere republics. The address concludes with hope that the gathering fosters mutual respect and peaceful relations among nations rather than conflict.

A player discusses an upcoming game, stating that home ice advantage is minimal since the opponent plays well on the road. They emphasize enjoying the playoff atmosphere while maintaining focus, noting the team's experience helps keep players balanced and prepared to play hard without expecting anything to be given to them.

The speaker's sole focus is winning the Stanley Cup for Buffalo over the next two weeks. RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC) uses neural networks to compress material textures more efficiently than traditional methods, achieving over 3x memory savings while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) reduces visual artifacts in texture sampling and runs fast on Blackwell GPU due to 2x point-sampled texture filtering rate improvements.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) uses neural shaders to cache and approximate radiance information, creating high-quality global illumination and dynamic lighting effects in real-time rendering. It improves performance by reducing GPU computational load and enhances indirect light quality through inference of path-traced rays after one bounce.

RTX Skin brings subsurface scattering technology from film rendering to real-time path tracing for games, enabling realistic translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to infer more natural-looking faces from simple rasterized input plus 3D pose data, trained from thousands of offline generated images.

The Blackwell GPU architecture includes multiple chips: GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores) powers the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores) powers the RTX 5070.

Kyocera International Inc. announced that its DuraForce PRO rugged smartphone received the iF Design Award in the 'Industry/Skilled Trades' category, selected by 58 judges. The award follows a CES Innovation Awards honor. The DuraForce PRO features a Super Wide View HD Action Camera, 13MP rear camera, 5MP front camera, and biometric fingerprint scanner. Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine discovered that brown fat contains a "backup heater" system involving peroxisomes and the protein ACOX2, which generates heat when mitochondrial function is impaired. Research in mice showed that ACOX2 metabolizes specific fatty acids to produce heat, and mice lacking this protein exhibited lower cold tolerance, poorer insulin sensitivity, and greater weight gain on high-fat diets, while mice with elevated ACOX2 displayed improved metabolic health. The fatty acids involved are found in dairy products, breast milk, and produced by gut microbes, suggesting potential dietary or pharmaceutical interventions to boost metabolism and address obesity.

The increase was driven by a 28.3% surge in the West, while sales fell in the Midwest and Northeast. Buyers face limited existing home inventory, pushing demand toward new construction despite higher prices—the median new home price reached $337,200, nearly $87,000 above existing homes. Sixty percent of new homes now sell above $300,000, up from 53% in 2016. Sales rose slightly in the South despite climbing mortgage rates.

An immigration judge in Baltimore rejected Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia's asylum request, leaving a 2019 removal order in place. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI), created in 2003, gives each of the 500 component stocks equal 0.2% weight at quarterly rebalances, unlike the traditional market-cap-weighted S&P 500 where larger companies have greater influence. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) tracks EWI, while SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) tracks the market-weighted index. Historically, RSP has outperformed SPY due to the small-cap effect—smaller companies tend to grow faster than large ones—though this reversed in the last decade. A $10,000 investment in RSP in 2004 grew to $60,000 over 18 years versus $55,000 for SPY, despite RSP's higher 0.2% expense ratio compared to SPY's 0.0945%. Equal-weighting provides more protection during downturns in large tech stocks, as smaller companies can offset losses.

Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are energetic cosmic phenomena linked to core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). When massive stars retain hydrogen-rich envelopes, relativistic jets may fail to escape, creating "choked GRBs" that produce high-energy neutrinos and shock breakout signatures but no gamma-ray emission. This study uses relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations with the PLUTO code to investigate jet propagation in Blue and Red Supergiant (BSG/RSG) progenitors. The authors develop density profiles for BSG and RSG stars, estimate breakout and choking times through numerical integration of 39,000 1D models, and implement a shock-finding algorithm identifying shock zones via converging flows, pressure jumps, temperature-density alignment, and relativistic Mach numbers. Preliminary results for a BSG star (50 solar radii, 15 solar masses) with a jet luminosity of 10^51 erg/s and 5-second engine time show the jet chokes approximately one minute after launch. The simulation reveals a double-shock structure: an external cocoon shock and a termination shock at the jet head, plus an internal collimation shock that dissipates after engine shutdown. Post-injection, only the accelerating cocoon shock remains as a dominant particle acceleration site. Future work will extend parameter studies to both BSG and RSG progenitors with varied luminosities and Lorentz factors to maximize detectability of neutrino emission from these hidden sources.

Turing GPUs feature optimized memory subsystems with GDDR6 and doubled L2 cache (6 MB in TU102 vs 3 MB in GP102), delivering 50% effective bandwidth improvements over Pascal. The display engine supports 8K@60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2, HDR with tone mapping per ITU-R BT.2100, and enhanced NVENC/NVDEC for 8K HEVC encoding and improved decoding. VirtualLink via USB-C simplifies VR headset connectivity. NVLink replaces SLI bridges in TU102/TU104, providing 50-100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth. RT Cores enable real-time ray tracing through hybrid rendering combining rasterization and ray tracing, with 10x performance over Pascal. Tensor Cores support NGX AI features including DLSS for image quality and performance gains, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading eliminates CPU bottlenecks via Task and Mesh Shaders. Variable Rate Shading enables Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering expands to four views per pass. Turing GPUs include TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000), and TU106 (RTX 2070), with RTX-OPS as a workload-based performance metric.

Iain Stewart discusses SCET (Soft-Collinear Effective Theory) applications for LHC physics, focusing on factorization theorems with two cutoff parameters (μ and ν) needed to handle rapidity divergences. He explains how renormalization group evolution occurs in a two-dimensional space, with hard, collinear, and soft modes living at different points (μ~q, ν~q for hard; μ~m, ν~q for collinear; μ~m, ν~m for soft). Path independence allows flexibility in choosing evaluation points.

He derives anomalous dimensions for the Sudakov form factor, showing μ-anomalous dimensions are standard while ν-anomalous dimensions arise from ν-dependence in the regulator. The evolution kernels take Sudakov-like exponential forms.

Stewart then applies this framework to Higgs production (gg→H) with measured pT, showing it involves SCET₂ with n, n̄, and soft modes, requiring transverse-momentum-dependent PDFs with rapidity divergences. He briefly mentions jet broadening in e⁺e⁻ as another SCET₂ example.

Finally, he examines Drell-Yan production (pp→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻X), describing four kinematic regimes: inclusive (τ~1), threshold (τ→1), isolated (constrained hemisphere momenta), and pT-measured. The isolated case introduces beam functions—matrix elements measuring both large and small momentum components—which factorize into perturbative matching coefficients and standard PDFs through SCET₁-to-SCET₂ matching.

The lecture discusses coding gain in digital communications, focusing on effective coding gain as a measure of performance improvement over baseline systems. In the power-limited regime, effective coding gain compares a signal set's performance to 2-PAM at a fixed bit error probability of 10^-5, calculated using the union bound estimate involving nominal coding gain and average nearest neighbors per bit. The nominal coding gain depends on minimum distance and energy per bit, while a rule of thumb adjusts for nearest neighbor effects: effective coding gain equals nominal coding gain minus 0.2 log₂(K_b) dB. Examples show 2-PAM and 4-QAM yield zero coding gain, while a four-point subset of a 3D cube achieves approximately 1 dB effective coding gain.

Orthogonal signal sets achieve arbitrarily large nominal coding gain as dimensions increase, but effective coding gain remains bounded due to increasing nearest neighbors; with mean subtraction (simplex sets), they approach the Shannon limit of -1.59 dB. However, orthogonal sets have poor spectral efficiency (approaching zero) and high decoding complexity (M log M operations), making them impractical compared to binary codes. Bi-orthogonal and simplex sets share similar asymptotic properties.

In the bandwidth-limited regime, analogous analysis applies with M-PAM as baseline, using normalized SNR and nearest neighbors per two dimensions. The lecture concludes by introducing binary block codes as the next topic, noting that separating coding and modulation is economical for binary signaling with minimal loss (at most 0.2 dB) compared to unconstrained signaling.

This study examined predictors of adherence to COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 Spanish adults during the first pandemic wave. Using data from the PSY-COVID study (May-June 2020), researchers analyzed behavioral, cognitive, social, affective, and sociodemographic variables. Results showed self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and general adherence were strongest predictors of post-confinement prevention behavior intention. Regional differences existed, with Canary Islands residents showing highest intention and Aragón/Balearic Islands lowest. Trust in scientists exceeded trust in government. Perceived severity moderated relationships between adherence to avoid infection and perceived vulnerability of others. Findings suggest public health strategies should enhance self-efficacy, ensure consistent messaging, and address regional disparities.

This paper proposes an optimized weighted expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for estimating transition probability matrices (TPMs) in Markov cohort-state-transition models when data limitations exist, such as unequal observation intervals and missing transitions. The method modifies Craig and Sendi's uniform weighting approach by using weights inversely proportional to variance to minimize output variance, validated through a 3-state toy example comparing a fictitious "SuperDrug" to placebo. Results showed a 15.2% reduction in ICER variance and 3-percentage point increase in cost-effectiveness probability. The authors recommend this method for similar data sources only, with stepwise validation including face validity checks, and note that further research with real-world clinical data is needed for robust statistical validation.

Cat tail movements indicate different emotional states: tapping while napping shows relaxed attention, whipping signals nervousness or aggression, straight up with curved tip means friendliness, and low or neutral positions indicate relaxation. Cat body language and leg movements also provide behavioral cues. "Zoomies"—sudden darting between rooms—result from accumulated arousal, frustration, fear, or pent-up energy, as indoor cats lack natural stimulation and store energy during daytime sleeping.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which extends SEV and SNP to facilitate page migration between memory tiers. TMPM enables migration of pages during concurrent DMA operations and migration of SNP-protected guest pages. Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for hypervisor state pages and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for guest pages. The system requires IOMMU enablement and uses a ring buffer command interface supporting up to 128 pages per command. A new Pre-Migration RMP state facilitates SNP guest page migration. Performance is optimized with 16+ pages per command, ideally 128. Certain structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU data structures and the ring buffer itself.

Aaron Rome delivered a hit that was not blindside but left Horton injured. The speaker supports Rome as an honest, important player while acknowledging Horton's injury is unfortunate. The team must move on during the finals. They need to improve special teams by moving players into position rather than just moving the puck to regain momentum.

The S&P 500 declined 2.36% last week, falling from a Thursday record high of 6,427.02 to close Friday at 6,212.69, its lowest level since early July. Wauwatosa East High School's Tosa East Players celebrated 77 years of theater with a ribbon-cutting for the newly-renovated Dale K. Hidde Theatre and the production "Encore! Encore!" Conceived by Jennifer Lato, Amanda Marquardt, and Kate Sarner, the show features music and dance from the program's history with full sets, costuming, and choreography. The euro rose 0.1 percent against the dollar on Wednesday, though currency moves were limited as investors awaited a July 6 deadline for U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and the Independence Day holiday kept trading subdued. The yuan gained 0.8 percent after China's central bank moved to stabilize the currency. The yen rose 0.2 percent as a safe haven, while the Australian dollar edged up on strong retail data. Blackwell introduces architectural improvements for neural shaders, which calculate light and color on the GPU. Shader technology evolved from fixed-function pipelines to programmable vertex (GeForce 3), pixel (HLSL), geometry (DX10), compute (DX11), and ray tracing (DX12) shaders. Blackwell's developer-created neural shaders support prior generation GPUs.

Emergency Medical Service (EMS) systems require optimal ambulance station locations to minimize response times. This study presents a multi-criteria integer programming model for the Ambulance Location Problem (ALP), formulated as a real-world case study in rural Southwest Germany (Rhineland-Palatinate) for two district councils needing to reopen obsolete stations. The model maximizes population coverage within two response time radii (r1=5 minutes and r2=10 minutes) simultaneously while ensuring all demand points are covered within the legally mandated maximum time (r3=15 minutes).

The model uses binary variables to select station locations and assign demand points (road segments weighted by population) to stations, subject to constraints ensuring coverage limits, travel time thresholds, and fixed existing stations. Applied to a study area with over 450,000 inhabitants, 70 municipalities, and 17 potential locations (from which 4 were selected), the optimization utilized detailed road network data with custom ambulance speed profiles. Using the ε-constraint method, 16 Pareto-optimal solutions were identified, revealing a fundamental trade-off: maximizing 5-minute coverage concentrates stations in urban centers, while maximizing 10-minute coverage distributes stations evenly into rural areas.

The analysis demonstrates that short response time goals systematically disadvantage rural areas, whereas longer response time criteria promote geographic equity. The static model served as a decision-support tool for preliminary site selection, with final decisions requiring further discrete event simulation analysis due to real-world ambulance availability constraints. A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock's price rises unexpectedly, forcing short sellers to buy back shares at higher prices to cover their positions, which further drives up the price. The opposite is a long squeeze, where price declines force short sellers to buy back shares. High short interest alone is not a reliable predictor of squeezes, and backtesting short squeeze strategies has proven impractical due to their random nature. Short selling carries unlimited loss potential, making short squeezes particularly painful for short sellers.

**Key Specifications:**

| GPU | CUDA Cores | Tensor Cores | RT Cores | Memory | Transistors |
|-----|-----------|--------------|----------|--------|-------------|
| TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti) | 4,608 | 576 | 72 | 11 GB GDDR6 | 18.6B |

The professor begins by stating he will not repeat material on discrete coding and invites questions. He announces the next problem set (problems 1-7, end of lectures 8-10, and problem 26) will be due October 14th.

The lecture then covers the difference between Riemann and Lebesgue integration. Riemann integration splits the horizontal axis into equal intervals and approximates the function within each. Lebesgue integration instead quantizes the vertical axis into slices and measures how much of the function lies in each slice using "measure theory." For well-behaved functions, both methods yield the same result, but Lebesgue integration handles "weird" functions that Riemann cannot, particularly important for communication theory and random processes.

The professor explains measure theory: the measure of an interval [a,b] is b-a; countable unions of disjoint intervals have measures equal to the sum of individual measures; and subsets of zero-measure sets also have zero measure. He demonstrates that rational numbers between 0 and 1 have measure zero despite being dense, and constructs an uncountable set with measure zero using ternary expansions excluding the digit 1.

A function is measurable if the set of times where the function lies in any interval is measurable. For non-negative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists (finite or infinite). The professor defines L1 functions (measurable with finite integral of absolute value) and L2 functions (measurable with finite integral of squared magnitude). For time-limited functions, L2 implies L1.

The lecture connects this to Fourier series: for L2 time-limited functions, all Fourier coefficients exist and are finite. The Fourier series converges "in the mean" (energy sense), meaning the energy of the difference between the function and partial sums approaches zero—not pointwise equality, which is less important for engineering applications. The professor introduces "l.i.m." (limit in the mean) notation for this convergence.

Finally, he describes segmenting arbitrary L2 functions into time intervals and expanding each segment into Fourier series, which forms the conceptual basis for voice compression algorithms. He contrasts this time-varying frequency view with the Fourier integral, where frequencies are "frozen in time," noting that the Fourier transform will be covered next lecture.

DNA origami is a technique using DNA base-pairing to create precise nanostructures. The researchers found that DNA origami assembly is robust across various conditions, but strand incorporation efficiency depends on target sequence position in the growing structure. Not all staple strands bind in every nanoparticle, suggesting nanomachine components should be added in excess with positions selected based on incorporation efficiency mapping. This paper studies modal extensions of lattice semantics, where the necessity operator is interpreted as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds. The authors define regular modal extensions where "necessity means true in all accessible worlds" and establish that for complete lattices, normal modal valuations produce unique regular extensions precisely when designated values form a filter closed under meets. They characterize lattice properties through modal validities: implicative filters correspond to the validity of (□φ ∨ □ψ) → □(φ ∨ ψ), while axiom K's validity depends on linearity outside the filter (for deductive implication) or anti-monotone, involutive negation with down-distribution (for standard implication). The framework is illustrated using twist algebras from Boolean algebras, showing that paraconsistent semantics satisfy K exactly when the filter contains all elements with first coordinate 1. The work aims to enable meaningful interpretation of truth values across different logics, with applications to computer systems where states operate under different algebraic properties.

Researchers developed an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning potential for YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋ₓ (YBCO) to study oxygen defect dynamics and the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal phase transition. The potential was trained on 1,368 DFT configurations including defects, achieving 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å root-mean-square errors for energies and forces. Unlike previous classical potentials, the ACE potential accurately reproduces the high-temperature structural transition at approximately 800 K (experimentally ~1000 K), capturing the entropy-driven mechanism where oxygen atoms migrate from CuO chains to interstitial sites. The transition is facilitated by decreasing oxygen Frenkel pair formation energies due to thermal expansion. The potential improves upon classical approaches in describing lattice parameters far from equilibrium and defect migration barriers within 20 meV of DFT. This work demonstrates machine learning potentials can capture complex defect physics in quaternary oxide superconductors, with applications for understanding radiation damage recovery and optimizing high-temperature superconducting devices.

This research examines how artificial intelligence impacts inclusive education through a non-empirical literature review conducted September 2023–March 2024 using PRISMA guidelines. Inclusive education upholds principles of acceptance, accessibility, and equal opportunity for all students regardless of disability, ethnicity, or background, yet faces barriers including inadequate educator training, incompatible digital materials, overcrowded classrooms, and insufficient infrastructure. AI benefits inclusive education through assistive features like text-to-speech and speech-to-text, adaptive learning, automated administrative tasks, and continuous student evaluation. This lecture covers ion traps, contrasting them with neutral atom traps. While neutral atoms rely on magnetic and optical forces with trap depths of millikelvin to kelvin, ions utilize Coulomb forces, enabling confinement strengths of 10,000 kelvin using electric fields. Both platforms are used for atomic clocks, quantum information processing, and quantum simulation.

Ions cannot be confined by static electric potentials because the divergence of the electric field is zero, requiring dynamic traps. The Penning trap uses a quadrupole electric field with a superimposed magnetic field, confining ions axially through electrostatic forces and radially through cyclotron motion. The RF or Paul trap alternates rapidly between confining and anti-confining potentials at radio frequencies. Net confinement arises from micromotion—rapid oscillations where the particle's driven motion rectifies the alternating field into a harmonic restoring potential (secular motion).

For quantum computation, single qubit operations employ Rabi oscillations. Two-qubit gates, such as the Cirac-Zoller gate, utilize the center-of-mass vibrational mode as a data bus. The procedure involves swapping the control ion's qubit state into the phonon state, performing a controlled phase operation on the target ion conditional on the bus state, then returning the information to the control ion. While foundational, this gate requires cooling to the motional ground state and faces scalability limitations due to the slow center-of-mass frequency; alternative gates avoid these constraints.

This study examined race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and cognitive decline in 2,284 older Black and White adults from three harmonized cohort studies. However, White adults with high BP declined faster than Black adults with high BP in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White adults with variable BP showed significantly faster decline than Black adults with variable BP across all cognitive domains. The authors suggest that chronic stress and allostatic load in Black individuals may lead to neuroadaptations that reduce cognitive vulnerability to BP-related physiological changes. Limitations include lack of medication adherence data and comprehensive medication history.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification defines a secure method for applying non-persistent runtime updates to AMD Security Processor (ASP) firmware without requiring BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS addresses priority runtime concerns in AMD-provided binary firmware components, excluding x86 code such as SMM, AGESA, and UEFI. Updates are temporary, do not persist across reboots, and serve as interim fixes between BIOS releases.

Security relies on AMD cryptographic signatures verified by the ASP, with optional customer co-signing allowing OEMs/ODMs to maintain root of trust for update by providing RSA public keys during early boot. Version tracking utilizes three levels: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL) for update packages (monotonically increasing), Security Patch Level (SPL) for individual firmware components, and System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code modifications. Packages must match specific firmware combinations and apply sequentially.

Deployment requires an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with the ASP via a TEE Extended Command Buffer interface, using commands such as GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO and UPDATE_FW. Packages require 2MB aligned memory buffers and follow the naming convention fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. In multi-socket systems, the first socket's ASP receives the patch.

The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated distance education, highlighting the need for alternative methods including artificial intelligence (AI). AI systems utilize machine learning, deep learning, and neural networks to perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence, with applications such as IBM's Watson and Google's autonomous vehicles demonstrating advanced capabilities. In education, AI enables Intelligent Education Systems (IES) comprising domain, pedagogy, and learner models, and supports three primary educational approaches: AI-assisted face-to-face instruction, face-to-face instruction with AI teachers (virtual robots or screens), and simulation-based education using virtual or augmented reality. These systems function through either supervised learning (human-controlled algorithms) or unsupervised deep learning (AI self-training). Potential benefits include increased efficiency, personalized instruction, cost reduction, and data-driven decision making. However, significant concerns exist regarding the loss of human social interaction, privacy and security risks, educator unemployment, psychological isolation, and the potential for AI to surpass human control. While computers have not yet achieved human-level mental capacity, advancing technology suggests that education may increasingly become machine-dependent, necessitating serious philosophical and practical preparation for this future.

El neuromarketing, definido como la aplicación de técnicas de neuroimagen para comprender la conducta del consumidor en relación con los mercados, se encuentra en una etapa emergente e incipiente en el sector audiovisual español. Aunque empresas internacionales ya utilizan estas técnicas para testear contenidos y publicidad, en España su adopción se concentra principalmente en los grupos mediáticos privados Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Mediaset emplea pulseras de actividad electrodérmica para testear ficción, mientras que Atresmedia utiliza EEG, EMG y sensores biométricos para bloques publicitarios, habiendo abandonado el test de contenidos por dificultades interpretativas. La investigación, basada en 18 entrevistas a consultoras, representantes del sector, neurocientíficos y académicos, confirma que estas técnicas son viables pero requieren equipos multidisciplinares y enfrentan barreras como el desconocimiento, la desconfianza, los costos y la complejidad para interpretar datos. Las productoras cinematográficas, aunque interesadas, no invierten por falta de recursos. La proyección futura es positiva, pero depende del desarrollo tecnológico, la reducción de costos y la demostración de retorno de inversión.

Research indicates that installing air filters and upgrading ventilation in schools significantly improves student outcomes at low cost. Benefits include direct cognitive gains from reduced particulate matter, improved health and attendance, and addressing inequalities for low-income students in polluted areas. The intervention requires minimal administrative burden—devices cost $50 to $100 per classroom annually and need only yearly filter changes. The author recommends schools reconnect existing devices, install new filters, pilot programs aiming for a Clean Air Delivery Rate of 30 cubic feet per minute per student, and monitor outcomes, while calling on philanthropy and advocates to support air quality standards and funding.

Australian ecosystems are experiencing sudden, potentially irreversible collapses due to combined gradual climate change and extreme weather events. Research published in Nature Climate Change documents six case studies of catastrophic shifts, including kelp forest loss, wildfire destruction of Gondwanan refugia, floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest conversion, arid zone boom-bust cycles, and mangrove dieback. Even near-pristine systems show limited resilience. Australia's temperature has risen 1°C since the 19th century, with more frequent heatwaves, fires, and droughts. This retrospective cohort study utilized the All of Us Research Program dataset (v7) to develop machine learning models predicting healthy aging among 99,935 participants aged 50 and older. Healthy aging was defined by a composite score of zero for comorbidities (modified Charlson Comorbidity Index), cognitive conditions, and mobility function. Three algorithms were trained—logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost—to predict outcomes using social determinants of health (SDOH) survey data and electronic health records. The XGBoost model with random oversampling demonstrated the best performance (AUROC 0.793 [95% CI: 0.788-0.796], F1 score 0.697) and achieved predictive parity across race and sex groups. Feature importance analysis using SHAP values identified health insurance type as the most predictive factor for healthy aging, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The study concludes that machine learning models can accurately predict healthy aging using SDOH data, highlighting health insurance as a critical determinant of long-term health outcomes in older adults.
