This study simulates the transition from internal combustion engine vehicles to battery electric vehicles using one year of real-world driving data from over 10,000 users in Asti, Italy. The research evaluates four BEV models with varying battery capacities and four charging policies, replicating exact user trips without modifying itineraries. Results show that current BEV technology suits part of the population but not all: with the most favorable charging policy (fast DC charging when battery is low) and largest battery vehicle (Audi A6 e-tron), 72% of users could complete 100% of trips without changing driving habits, while 5% remain unserved even under optimal conditions. Overnight charging provides the best balance of trip feasibility and battery state of charge after trips, while workplace-only charging proves inadequate for most users. The study advances prior research by using vehicle- and road-type-specific energy profiles, per-trip state-of-charge updates, and capturing seasonal variations. Limitations include assumptions about invariant energy consumption, constant charging power, universal charging infrastructure availability, and exclusion of cost analysis.

IES Holdings, Inc. has significantly outperformed infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks, with its share price nearly doubling year-to-date. Despite challenges in its largest residential division, data center projects are driving growth in its next two largest divisions. The company's backlog exceeds $2 billion, growing 20% year-over-year, with improved cash flow and record cash balances. However, the stock is considered overextended within the industrials sector, with sub-par free cash flow yield and increased insider sales. The 28-year-old company operates in 130+ U.S. locations, serving housing, data center, power, and industrial markets. The author holds no position in the company and has no plans to initiate one within 72 hours.

Institute manager Kevin Deery expressed frustration after his team's third consecutive draw, a 1-1 result against Larne at Drumahoe. Deery felt his side deserved to win, citing bad luck and poor finishing, with their last two goals being own goals. He criticized decision-making in both penalty areas, noting a defensive lapse on Larne's "freak" free-kick goal and missed chances by Ciaron Harkin, Gareth Brown, and Dean Curry. Despite the setbacks, Deery remains confident his team will improve, with 13 games remaining and a top-six position still intact.

The ACC Tournament concluded its two-year run at Barclays Center with Virginia's 71-63 championship win over North Carolina. Tournament organizers expressed interest in returning to the venue. Virginia, which began the season unranked and picked sixth in the ACC, completed an improbable run to the title. The tournament featured a Duke-North Carolina semifinal matchup, their third meeting of the season, with North Carolina winning. Duke's Marvin Bagley III showcased NBA draft potential. Clemson secured its first NCAA Tournament appearance in seven years.

This February 6, 2002, internal Enron email compiles news coverage of congressional investigations into the company's collapse. Former CEO Jeffrey Skilling is scheduled to testify February 7 before the House Energy and Commerce Committee without invoking the Fifth Amendment, while former CFO Andrew Fastow and former Chairman Kenneth Lay were subpoenaed after Lay canceled a voluntary appearance; Lay may invoke the Fifth.

Enron board member William Powers testified that the company knew by March 2001 that affiliated partnerships caused $500 million in losses but gave the Raptor partnership $800 million in shares to hide them, rendering over 70% of earnings from the prior 15 months false. He stated Lay knew of the financial troubles and that executives enriched themselves by tens of millions through self-dealing partnerships like LJM while threatening employees who resisted participation.

Arthur Andersen CEO Joseph Berardino testified that information was withheld from auditors. Labor Secretary Elaine Chao addressed retirement account protections following employee testimony about a three-week lockout that prevented stock sales as prices plummeted, costing workers like Deborah Perrotta $40,000 in savings. Whistleblower Sherron Watkins' memo warning Lay of impending accounting scandals was released.

Financially, Enron's debtor-in-possession financing dropped from $1.5 billion to $250–500 million; its broadband unit owes approximately $440,000 in back taxes; and the company is fighting the Houston Astros' attempt to terminate the Enron Field naming rights contract. Spain's energy regulator also announced an investigation into Enron's distribution operations.

Former Maui County Councilmember Mike Victorino, a 2018 mayoral candidate, hit two teenagers with his car on April 13 on West Papa Avenue. The Maui News reported on April 17 that Victorino was not speeding or under the influence, and both teens sustained nonlife-threatening injuries. Police stated the pedestrians were not in a crosswalk, though the mother of one teen claimed they were.

Linebackers are defensive players positioned 3-5 yards behind the defensive line who must possess toughness, athleticism, and intelligence. They relay play calls, stop both run and pass plays, and serve as the "Quarterback of the defense." The position name comes from their alignment behind the defensive line. Individual positions include Sam (strong side), Mike (middle), Will (weakside), and Jack (second middle linebacker in 3-4 fronts). Required skills include vision, agility, block shedding, tackling, and high motor, with typical body types being 5'10"-6'5" and 215-255 pounds. Notable linebackers include Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor, all Pro Football Hall of Famers. While the value of inside linebackers has declined due to offensive shifts toward passing, versatile linebackers who can rush, cover, and stop the run remain valuable for creating defensive mismatches.

The Bank of Canada and financial markets are exerting opposing pressures on the Canadian dollar, with markets currently pulling the loonie higher to nearly 75.50 U.S. cents. While Governor Stephen Poloz has signaled concerns about export challenges and a desire to prevent excessive strength, strong economic data and expectations of interest rate hikes are supporting the currency. CIBC now expects the Bank of Canada to raise rates in the fourth quarter rather than 2018, though low oil prices and the widening interest rate gap with the U.S. have recently pressured the loonie downward.

The Board of Governors received gameday feedback following two games at Colorado State University's on-campus stadium. ASCSU President Josh Silva noted challenges with student awareness of the tailgating lot and plans to rebrand and introduce pre-game programming. Athletics Director Joe Parker reported attendance of 37,583 for the first game and 27,038 for the second, with initial queuing and congestion issues improving by the second game. Transportation planning included identifying all campus parking, with 50 vehicles towed each game weekend from gameday lots and similar numbers from surrounding neighborhoods. Transit ridership exceeded predictions at 7,000 for the first game, and the MAX system was heavily utilized for post-game departure.

This study examined whether role-taking and literacy interventions could reduce demographic and appearance-based biases in social engineering contexts. Using a 4×2 mixed factorial online experiment with Arab participants (n=139), researchers compared four groups: Persuader (role-taking as manipulator), Persuadee (role-taking as target), Literacy (educational materials), and Control. Participants assessed trust and risk-taking regarding personas varying in age, gender, ethnicity, and attire before and after the intervention.

Results indicated no significant changes in trust or risk-taking behaviors across demographic factors post-intervention, with Bayes Factors supporting the null hypothesis that interventions did not reduce reliance on these cues. Only Issue of Involvement showed a significant decrease. The study concludes that while participants found the interventions engaging and awareness-raising, short-term interventions are insufficient to overcome deeply ingrained cognitive biases and heuristics. The authors suggest future research explore longer-term, immersive strategies such as virtual reality or gamified training to achieve lasting behavioral change.

The Great Southern Storm named a 45-player initial colts squad under new coach Glynn Verbruggen, replacing Phil Gilbert, ahead of the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin next month. The squad will train on June 4 and 11 at Railways, featuring State 16 players Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight among others. North Albany provides 12 players, Railways eight, and Albany and Royals seven each.

A district and sessions judge in Zhob awarded death sentence, imprisonments, and fines to four convicts in separate murder cases. Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced Shehzado to death plus Rs. 200,000 fine for stabbing a man. Brothers Ajab Khan and Fateh Khan received 25 years imprisonment each plus Rs. 200,000 fines. Dilbar Khan received 25 years imprisonment plus Rs. 105,000 fine. Advocate Samad Khan Mandokhail represented the victims' families.

Allen Iverson discussed his memoir "Misunderstood" on ESPN's "First Take," identifying his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner as his lowest point, which coincided with his NBA retirement. The 50-year-old described the split as self-inflicted and revealed the couple has since reconciled after he underwent deep self-reevaluation. Iverson addressed achieving sobriety, stating he realized alcohol was not helping him and was tired of fighting it. He also reflected on his influence over younger NBA players, noting he helped them feel comfortable expressing themselves.

The passage analyzes Germany's plan to dominate Central Europe by subjugating the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. While the United States does not oppose economic unification, it opposes imperialistic control by Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest. Current control rests on an alliance among ruling powers bound by shared interests in subjecting these peoples, maintaining German-Magyar ascendancy, and war debts. Key assets to counter this include the economic weapon of commercial exclusion, which threatens German post-war stability, and nationalist discontent within Austria-Hungary combined with the Emperor's desire to preserve the empire through a League of Nations. The recommended strategy involves stirring nationalist unrest while offering the ruling powers safety through international cooperation, thereby reducing resistance and accelerating independence from Berlin.

Texas teachers and parents express concerns that a new law replacing the STAAR standardized test may increase student stress and testing time rather than reduce it. The law replaces the single STAAR exam with three shorter tests administered throughout the school year, beginning in 2027-28, and bans practice tests. Critics worry that three tests will triple pressure while maintaining similar accountability rating weight for the end-of-year exam. The law also directs the Texas Education Agency to study reducing testing's impact on school accountability ratings, but that report isn't due until 2029-30 and implementation isn't required. Some administrators fear all three tests could follow strict STAAR protocols, while advocates hope districts can use existing assessments like MAP for the first two exams. Educators want more input on test creation and fewer restrictions on testing day to reduce student anxiety.

The passage introduces LAPIS, a compiler framework built on MLIR that bridges high-performance computational science and AI/ML by enabling automatic compilation of Python-based ML code to performance-portable Kokkos C++. LAPIS addresses three key challenges: creating an extensible compiler supporting performance, portability, and productivity; interfacing C++ scientific codes with Python ML frameworks; and developing a Kokkos dialect with hierarchical parallelism abstractions and memory models for accelerators. The framework includes lowering passes for linear algebra operations, a Kokkos-inspired memory reference model with DualView support, and a C++ emitter. Demonstrations show portable performance on AMD MI300A, NVIDIA H100, and Intel Granite Rapids for sparse/dense linear algebra kernels and coupled scientific ML use cases.

This work constructs strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the Quantum Haar Random Oracle Model (QHROM), establishing their existence with access to both the oracle and its inverse (Theorem 1.1). The construction, $G_U(1^\lambda, k) = X^{k_3} \cdot U_\lambda \cdot X^{k_2} \cdot U_\lambda \cdot X^{k_1}$, makes two queries to the $\lambda$-qubit Haar random oracle $U_\lambda$ and requires sampling $O(\log^{1+\epsilon}(n))$ bits of randomness to achieve security against polynomially many queries. The security proof employs Ma-Huang's path-recording framework, modeling the Haar oracle via isometries $V$ and $V^\dagger$ that record queries in databases. The authors define an approximate isometry $S$ that merges independent left and right databases while simulating keys, and use query-by-query analysis to prove this maps the real experiment close to the ideal one with two independent Haar unitaries.

Chipotle released a new queso dip on September 12 to boost sales, but customers have complained about its $2.95 price point and taste. A small chips and queso costs $3.95, while a large is $6.25. Social media posts criticized the price and quality, with one customer calling it "microwaved." Chipotle spokesman Chris Arnold stated that 63% of test market customers said the queso would increase visit frequency, and prices won't be reduced because it uses real, whole ingredients. In Sacramento, burritos start at $6.70, making the large chips and queso nearly as expensive as a full meal.

State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for May 23, 2001, containing case summaries across multiple practice areas including Bankruptcy, Civil Rights, Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Negligence & Intentional Tort, and Real Property. The publication includes Fields of Practice listings advertising attorneys in various specialties, classified advertisements for legal services, expert witnesses, office space, and employment opportunities. It also contains sections for News & Moves, Bar Events, and contact information for subscription and advertising services.

Peggy Mahoney forwarded an Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum email to Enron colleagues on August 28, 2000. The forum posed two questions: one on whether natural gas exploration on federal lands should be encouraged to meet future demand, and a previous question on whether California power generators were manipulating wholesale electricity markets and whether price caps should be imposed. The email included 25 selected responses to the California question from various industry professionals, offering diverse opinions on market manipulation, deregulation flaws, supply-demand imbalances, and the effectiveness of price caps.

CEMEX, a Mexican cement company, grew from a domestic firm to a global building materials leader through strategic acquisitions and a distinctive post-merger integration process called the "CEMEX Way." Between 1992 and 2007, CEMEX expanded from Mexico into Spain, Venezuela, Colombia, the Caribbean, Asia, and eventually acquired major companies including RMC (2005) and Rinker (2007), becoming one of the world's largest suppliers. The CEMEX Way involved standardizing business processes and technology across all operations while learning best practices from acquired companies and implementing them corporation-wide. This approach enabled rapid integration—reducing PMI duration from 25 months to under five months—and continuous improvement. Key to CEMEX's success was transferring operational capabilities from emerging markets to developed ones, using middle-level managers to identify and disseminate innovations, and maintaining operational flexibility at the local level. The company evolved through four internationalization stages: laying groundwork (pre-1992), stepping out (1992-1995), growing up (1996-1999), and stepping up (2000-2007), with each acquisition building on and enhancing core competencies developed in previous markets.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea manager after Bayern Munich granted permission for talks. The club made Carlo Ancelotti's assistant their top choice to replace Bob Bradley, who left after a 4-1 loss to West Ham. Clement will reportedly sign until 2019 with a £30 million transfer budget to help avoid relegation. Swansea currently sit 19th in the Premier League after conceding 44 goals in 19 games. Clement previously worked with Ancelotti at Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, winning the 2014 Champions League, and had a brief spell at Derby in 2015-16. Swansea player Neil Taylor expressed support for Clement's potential appointment.

The 1956 Hungarian revolt was a nationwide uprising against Soviet-backed Communist rule, triggered by economic failures, political repression, and hopes inspired by de-Stalinization and events in Poland. After initial Soviet concessions including troop withdrawal and Imre Nagy's reappointment as prime minister, the USSR used the Suez Crisis as cover to invade with 250,000 troops on November 4. Despite fierce resistance, Hungarian fighters were defeated by mid-November, with approximately 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers killed. The brutal suppression marked a turning point for both the Soviet Union and NATO.

A federal judge dismissed Drake's defamation lawsuit against Universal Music Group regarding Kendrick Lamar's 2024 song "Not Like Us," which called Drake a "certified pedophile." U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas ruled the lyrics were "nonactionable opinion" and "hyperbolic vituperations" made during a heated rap battle. The suit included claims for defamation, harassment, and deceptive acts. Drake plans to appeal.

A Springfield, Massachusetts police officer faces disciplinary action after posting "Hahahaha love this" on Facebook in response to a story about a car killing counter-protester Heather Heyer at a Charlottesville white supremacist rally. Officer Conrad Lariviere apologized, calling himself a "good man who made a stupid comment." Police Commissioner John Barbieri initiated an internal investigation and said the matter will go to the Community Police Hearings Board. Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the comments. Lariviere had also questioned whether the driver was a "nazi scumbag" and told a critic he deals with "real danger" while others "live in a fantasy land." He denied being racist.

The DAWN-PLASMA study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating high-titer convalescent plasma (≥1/160 neutralizing antibodies, 800-1000 mL in 4 doses, first dose within 12 hours of randomization) plus standard of care versus standard of care alone (2:1 allocation) in hospitalized COVID-19 patients aged ≥18 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, radiographic infiltrates or clinical evidence of rales with SpO2 ≤94%, who were not receiving mechanical ventilation. The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints include clinical severity assessments, time to sustained improvement, mortality at 30 and 90 days, and safety outcomes. The study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees and conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. Six patients were substituted after five withdrew consent and one failed screening.

Williams & Connolly confirmed hackers accessed a small number of attorney emails through a zero-day attack but found no evidence of broader IT system access or extraction of confidential client data. The firm attributed the attack to a nation-state actor linked to recent law firm and company breaches, and stated it has blocked the threat actor with no remaining unauthorized network traffic.

The passage describes video output data signals for different color modes. PINCNTL191 carries 8 MSBs of G/Y/YC data (green for RGB, Y for YUV444/Y/C, multiplexed Y/Cb/Cr for BT.656). PINCNTL184 carries 8 MSBs of B/CB/C data (blue for RGB, Cb for YUV444, multiplexed Cb/Cr for Y/C, unused for BT.656). A third signal carries 8 MSBs of R/CR data (red for RGB). The passage also defines pin state abbreviations (I, O, Z, S, GND, A, MM, DSIS, IPD, IPU, DIS) and notes that IPD/IPU/DIS represent default internal pull states after reset.

Coppin State University, a historically Black university in Maryland, has more than quadrupled out-of-state student enrollment over two years through its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU. In 2024, qualifying out-of-state students grew from 81 to 195; this fall, 416 of 1,000 incoming students came from those areas. Overall enrollment rose 26 percent. The university increased its visibility through high school visits, advertising, and transfer partnerships. Coppin is building a new dorm to accommodate growth. The strategy addresses declining high school graduates nationally and capitalizes on increased HBCU interest following the 2023 affirmative action ban.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. The controllers feature multiple enable methods through the EN pin, including direct connection to VLDO, external signals, or resistor-divider programming for undervoltage lockout with user-defined thresholds. An internal 1.23-V bandgap reference is divided to 0.613 V for error amplifier operation, with regulation within +0.7%/-1% across conditions. The transconductance error amplifier (1800 µA/V) compares VSENSE to the lower of SS pin voltage or internal reference, with frequency compensation between COMP and AVSS.

Output voltage is programmed via resistor divider to VSENSE. Soft-start timing is controlled by a capacitor on the SS pin, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when SS exceeds 1 V. Three switching frequency modes exist: internal oscillator (RT resistor to AVSS, 100 kHz–2 MHz), external synchronization (RT floating, SYNC input at 2× desired frequency), and primary-secondary (SYNC daisy-chain between devices). Primary-secondary mode creates 90° or 270° phase shift between controllers.

Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) provide ~150 mA peak current, requiring external gate drivers. Dead time (TDSP/TDPS) and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors on PS, SP, and LEB pins. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP < 0.3 V and previous duty cycle < 25%. Duty cycle limits are configurable: 50% (DCL to AVSS), 75% (DCL floating), or 100% (DCL to VLDO), with only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP supporting 50% mode with dual outputs.

Peak current mode control uses CS_ILIM pin with 150 mV offset, compared to COMP/2. Overcurrent protection triggers hiccup mode when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, with programmable delay and restart timing via CHICC capacitor. External fault protection is available through FAULT pin (>0.6 V triggers shutdown). Slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation, set via RSC resistor. Frequency compensation supports Type 2A or 2B networks. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart at 160°C.

The Democratic Party has gained control of the U.S. government, completing a shift that began two years ago with the House of Representatives and now includes the Senate, Presidency, and Vice-Presidency. This change reflects a national desire to address problems that have emerged alongside American prosperity: wastefulness, unmeasured human costs of industrialization, exploitation of natural resources, and government corruption. The speaker outlines needed reforms including tariff revision, banking and currency reform, industrial regulation, agricultural modernization, conservation of natural resources, and stronger protections for public health and labor conditions. The work ahead is framed not as partisan triumph but as restoration—cleansing evil without impairing good, humanizing processes without weakening them, and pursuing justice through measured, informed action rather than haste or destruction.

Indianapolis Public Schools (IPS) is holding its first public meeting on Tuesday at 6 p.m. at Thomas D. Gregg School 15 to discuss a proposal to close three high schools by 2018-2019. The Facilities Utilization Taskforce will present findings showing IPS enrollment has declined from 109,000 students in 1967 to 30,000 today, with all seven high schools under capacity—five less than half full. The report recommends operating three to four high schools. Additional public meetings are scheduled through May, with school closures to be identified by June and voted on in September.

This paper proposes LG-CD, a Language-Guided Change Detection model for remote sensing images that integrates visual and textual information. The model uses SAM2 as a shared visual feature extractor and CLIP for text feature extraction, with a text fusion attention module to align text with visual features and a visual-semantic fusion decoder to generate change detection masks. The approach addresses limitations of unimodal methods by leveraging natural language guidance to improve detection accuracy, semantic understanding, and generalization. Key contributions include: (1) novel integration of visual and textual information with natural language cues directing attention to target regions; (2) utilization of SAM2's generalization capabilities with multi-layer adapters for fine-tuning; and (3) design of text fusion attention module and visual-semantic fusion decoder for high-precision change mask generation.

The White House stated it was not defending Roseanne Barr's racist tweet that led to her show's cancellation, but President Trump and Press Secretary Sarah Sanders demanded an apology from ABC for negative on-air comments about the administration. Trump tweeted that Disney CEO Bob Iger apologized to Valerie Jarrett but never apologized to him for "HORRIBLE statements" about him on ABC. Sanders cited examples including ESPN's Jemele Hill calling Trump a white supremacist and Joy Behar comparing Christianity to mental illness, calling it a "double standard." She insisted Trump was focused on other matters while simultaneously defending his media criticism.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan discussed his team's final minicamp practice, noting balanced competition between offense and defense. He mentioned his father Mike Shanahan observes practices and provides feedback, though he is not staff. Shanahan said he plans to take time off in Mexico with family before training camp. He emphasized play-action's importance to his offensive philosophy for creating explosive plays while reducing pressure on players.

MIT OpenCourseWare lecture on poker strategy by Will Ma. Covers post-flop play including continuation betting, when opponents check to the preflop aggressor, and bet sizing (typically 50-100% of pot, increasing on later streets). Introduces the "Fundamental Theorem of Poker": bet best hands for value, bluff worst hands, check middle hands. Analyzes multiple hand examples comparing ace-queen, king-queen, pocket queens, and pocket sevens on a 9-8-2 flop. Discusses when to fold weak hands, when calling is reasonable (second pair, flush draws, gutshots with other equity), and when to raise (typically two-pair or better with deep stacks, but wider with shallow stacks). Covers leading into the preflop raiser on favorable boards, implied odds and reverse implied odds, set mining with pocket pairs, and bluffing with draws having high outs rather than weak hands with no equity. Emphasizes analyzing what hands your range represents when bluffing and giving up when board cards strengthen opponent's range.

Miyung Buster sent an email on July 18, 2001, to numerous Enron employees and external contacts regarding California energy issues. The email contained summaries of news articles covering: competing legislative proposals to prevent Southern California Edison's bankruptcy, including a $2.4 billion transmission line purchase plan and a "straight bailout" alternative; PG&E's lawsuit against California seeking compensation for energy contracts seized by Governor Gray Davis in January; criticism from consumer advocates about utility rescue plans; an editorial on distributing costs of California's power crisis; Contra Costa County's $1.7 million energy conservation building upgrades; and Duke Energy's 27% second-quarter earnings increase partly from California trading. The articles detailed legislative debates before summer recess, PG&E's $14.4 billion bankruptcy debt, and state power purchases being sold at losses due to reduced demand.

Prof. Cyril Dim of the University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus, explains that cervical cancer is a malignant condition of the cervix caused primarily by human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18. HPV is sexually transmitted, making cervical cancer a sexually transmitted disease. The condition progresses through pre-cancerous stages (detectable via Pap smear), early stage (curable), and late stage (incurable, only manageable). Symptoms include post-coital bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, and abnormal vaginal bleeding. Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and histology. In Nigeria, cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women but may cause the most deaths due to lack of structured screening programs. Approximately 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths occur annually in Nigeria. Treatment options include radical surgery and radiotherapy for early stages; late-stage treatment combines radiotherapy and chemotherapy to prolong life. HPV vaccines are available for prevention.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana "Nevermind" album cover depicting a naked baby underwater is not child pornography, dismissing Spencer Elden's 2021 lawsuit. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found that while Elden was nude in the image, no other factors indicated lasciviousness, comparing it to a family photo of a child bathing.
Precise estimation of m-qubit polynomial functionals underpins quantum information science, statistical mechanics, and many-body physics.

A coach discusses his team's performance after two games, acknowledging they haven't played to their potential but remain confident in their abilities. He addresses lineup decisions, noting Chris Neil is absent for the birth of his child. The coach analyzes their struggles with faceoffs, defensive positioning, and offensive zone pressure against Anaheim's structured system. He praises opposing players like Rob Niedermayer and acknowledges his own goaltender has kept them competitive. He plans adjustments for the home games, including increased fourth line usage, emphasizing better puck possession, patience, and attacking with speed rather than seeking stretch passes. He expects strong home crowd support and urges his team to avoid being overly emotional while elevating their play to previous levels shown in earlier rounds.

The passage discusses artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, noting its growing presence accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. AI aims to develop 21st-century skills through learning, self-correction, and reasoning principles. It transforms teaching-learning processes, research, organizational management, and external relationships. AI offers personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated grading, data analysis, and administrative streamlining, but faces challenges including equity, ethics, privacy, training needs, costs, and organizational resistance. Traditional pedagogical practices and psychological concerns among faculty impede integration. Developing AI literacy among all stakeholders and reshaping teacher roles through participatory, research-informed approaches are recommended to maximize benefits while preserving academic freedom.

A player expresses surprise and gratitude at being put back in the lineup after two weeks, praising teammates and coach Pat for keeping the team focused through a difficult season. The player describes being nervous, dropping his stick, and trying to contribute despite uncertainty about the coach's decision. The team won three championships in nine years, with the player noting Pat's no-nonsense approach and refusal to let the team become complacent, which had been missing in previous years.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff at BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found 92.45% went to Democrats in 2023-2024, up from a 6:1 ratio in 2017-2020 to roughly 12:1. The study by Notre Dame professor Derek Muller examined the top 100 grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms, finding about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups versus $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Most Democratic-leaning firms included Cleary Gottlieb (99.7%), Fried Frank (99.4%), and Mintz Levin (99.1%); least Democratic-leaning included Nelson Mullins (66.4%), Lewis Brisbois (77.3%), and Ogletree Deakins (81.5%).

The lecture covers discrete symmetries in quantum field theory and introduces path integrals for fermions. For complex scalar fields, parity (P), time reversal (T), and charge conjugation (C) are implemented by unitary operators with phases η_P, η_T, η_C constrained to ±1. Time reversal requires anti-unitary operators due to its anti-linear nature. For Dirac fields, parity involves a matrix D = η_Pγ⁰ acting on spinor space, while charge conjugation uses matrix C satisfying Cγ^μC⁻¹ = -γ^{μT}, and time reversal uses D_T with D_T^T = C⁻¹γ⁵. The lecture then introduces Grassmann variables for fermion path integrals, where Berezin defined integration rules: linearity, vanishing total derivatives, and ∫dθ θ = 1, making integration equivalent to differentiation for these anti-commuting objects.

U.S. stock index futures rose on April 20 as earnings season started strongly and oil prices rebounded, though geopolitical tensions and French election uncertainty kept investors cautious. Of 57 S&P 500 companies reporting, 75.4 percent beat expectations, with overall profits estimated up 10.8 percent. Visa and Mattel were scheduled to report Thursday. Oil prices recovered on signals OPEC may extend supply cuts. Qualcomm rose 2.6 percent after beating estimates, while eBay fell 1.9 percent on weak guidance. At 6:19 a.m. ET, Dow futures were up 41 points, S&P 500 up 6.5 points, and Nasdaq up 17.5 points.

This patent application describes systems and methods for synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras to improve sensor data fusion. The system includes a LIDAR sensor that rotates about an axis to scan an environment by emitting and detecting reflected light pulses, and one or more cameras with rows of sensing elements aligned parallel to the LIDAR's axis of rotation. The cameras operate in a rolling shutter mode, capturing image pixel rows sequentially with exposure times synchronized to the LIDAR's rotation. The controller obtains image pixels in an order matching the LIDAR's light beam emission pattern, enabling temporal and spatial alignment between camera images and LIDAR data. This synchronization improves the accuracy of combining sensor data to generate three-dimensional environmental representations, such as colored point clouds. The cameras may be arranged in a ring formation around the LIDAR's axis, with curved or flat image sensors, and the system adjusts timing parameters based on the LIDAR's rotation rate and pointing direction.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its position in Zoe's Kitchen, Inc. by 114.5% in Q2, owning 17,056 shares worth $203,000. Other institutional investors including FMR LLC, California Public Employees Retirement System, and Massachusetts Financial Services Co. also increased holdings in Q1. Director A Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares in August. Analysts have mixed ratings: two sell, seven hold, three buy, with consensus "Hold" and $17.55 target price. The stock opened at $12.39, with 50-day moving average of $12.85 and 200-day of $14.30. Q2 earnings were $0.06 EPS on $74.30 million revenue, beating EPS estimates but missing revenue estimates. Revenue increased 12.1% year-over-year. The company operates Mediterranean-inspired fast-casual restaurants.

The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division affirmed two judgments against defendant Bradford Washington: one from January 31, 2008, convicting him of second-degree murder, second-degree criminal weapon possession, first-degree reckless endangerment, and child endangerment by jury verdict; and another from February 11, 2009, convicting him of second-degree murder by guilty plea. The court rejected the defendant's claims that a detective's testimony about attempts to locate him was improper and that the jury charge on consciousness of guilt was improper, finding both unpreserved for review and without merit. The court also rejected the claim that the prosecutor changed theories during summation. The second judgment was affirmed based on the first judgment's affirmance.

Darren Osborne, 48, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 43 years at Woolwich Crown Court for driving a van into worshippers outside Finsbury Park Mosque in London last June, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. Osborne shouted "I want to kill all Muslims" after the attack and was found guilty of murder and attempted murder. The judge noted he targeted victims based on their appearance. Ali's family expressed relief at the verdict, describing him as peaceful and innocent. Prosecutors said Osborne was "brainwashed" into Islamophobia after watching a BBC drama, and he had also planned to attack London's mayor and Labour leader. Police released footage showing Osborne's planning in Wales before the attack. The Met's counterterrorism commander praised the community's unified response, stating Osborne failed to create divisions.

Several major hedge funds reduced healthcare holdings in Q2 2017 as the sector outperformed the broader market amid fading Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Jana Partners exited nine healthcare companies entirely, while Third Point trimmed stakes in Humana and Baxter International. Healthcare stocks in the S&P 500 rose 6.7% versus 2.6% for the index. Facebook is adding a "Trending News" section to its iOS and Android apps, accessible through the "Explore" tab. The feature aggregates and ranks news stories by how many publications share them. Users can tap stories to view headlines from multiple sources, videos, photos, and top Facebook posts. This patent application describes a coil-less atomizer for electronic cigarettes using woven fiber tubes with hollow interiors that function as both heating elements and wicking elements. The woven fiber tubes, made of materials such as carbon fiber, have electrically conductive heating sections connected to leads or electrical contacts, with end sections contacting a liquid supply. Liquid is transported to the heating section via capillary action through the hollow interior and porous fiber walls. The tubes can be formed in U, C, or L shapes, with single or multiple tubes of same or varying diameters arranged parallel or in contact. The design eliminates separate wicking elements, allowing miniaturization. Manufacturing involves masking and sputtering to create conductive sections with lower resistance than the heating section. The atomizer operates with airflow sensors or switches, using batteries of 3-5 volts, with total resistance typically 1-8 ohms.

This bankruptcy court decision addresses damages for Randall Fincke's violation of Massachusetts securities law (§ 410(a)(2)) and breaches of fiduciary duty to Access Cardiosystems, Inc. and its investors. The court previously found Fincke liable for a material misstatement in an October 2002 Business Plan falsely claiming Access received patent counsel advice that its defibrillator product infringed no patents.

The court denied Fincke's motion to reconsider the § 410(a)(2) liability finding, rejecting his argument that investors understood the "advice" as informal rather than formal. The court maintained its prior finding that no such advice—formal or informal—was actually given.

For damages under § 410(a)(2), the court rejected the investors' claim that all post-October 2002 investments were recoverable, finding their testimony of reliance on the Business Plan not credible. The court held that only securities sales made "by means of" the misstatement were recoverable, requiring a causal nexus between the misstatement and specific transactions. Based on objective analysis of proximity between the misstatement and investments, only Joseph Zimmel's October and November 2002 stock purchases ($1.5 million total) were deemed made "by means of" the Business Plan. Later investments, including the April 2003 transaction, were based on different documents and circumstances.

The court entered judgment for Zimmel of $1.5 million plus interest from May 25, 2007, and for Access of $281,534.62 plus interest from July 6, 2004, for Fincke's waived fiduciary duty breaches regarding improper loan repayments.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge digital library professionals and computational researchers to foster collaboration on innovative practical applications. Digital library experts possess deep collection knowledge but often lack technical resources, while computer science researchers have computational expertise but limited awareness of real-world library challenges. The workshop follows a "scientific speed-dating" format featuring a keynote, panel discussion, and breakout sessions rather than paper submissions. Goals include starting a workshop series, identifying common challenges, providing a forum for discussing ideas, producing a SIGIR Forum report, and continuing at future conferences. The full-day interactive schedule includes welcome introductions, keynote, scientific speed-dating, panel discussion, and guided breakout sessions on topics like LLMs, OCR, and interface evaluation. Target audience comprises practitioners and researchers interested in building research systems for digital libraries, with expected attendance of around 25 participants. Organizers are Christin Katharina Kreutz, a Tandem Professor for Data Science in the Humanities, and Hermann Kroll, a PostDoc focusing on effective access paths in digital libraries.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of Ohio Revised Code 3105.03's one-year durational residency requirement for divorce, rejecting arguments that it violated the constitutional right to travel. The court distinguished this case from *Shapiro v. Thompson* and *Dunn v. Blumstein*, noting that divorce is not a basic need like welfare or a fundamental right like voting, but rather a statutory privilege. The court found Ohio has a compelling interest in overseeing marriage and divorce laws for its residents, ensuring jurisdiction over marital relationships, preventing "quickie" divorces in states with no interest in the marriage, and encouraging reconciliation. The one-year requirement was deemed the least restrictive means to establish domiciliary intent, as subjective intent alone would require case-by-case judicial examination. The court also noted the statute exempts alimony-only actions from the residency requirement, addressing basic needs.

On August 17, 2022, Apple Inc.'s Compensation Committee approved the Apple Inc. The 1987 film *Wall Street* remains the definitive film about finance due to its combination of classic storytelling elements—the rags-to-riches narrative, the Hero's Journey, and fairy tale structure—along with its immersive depiction of 1980s excess. The film follows Bud Fox, a young broker who gains wealth and status through his association with Gordon Gekko, a charismatic corporate raider who became a cultural icon through Michael Douglas's Oscar-winning performance. Unlike more earnest or realistic financial films, *Wall Street* succeeds by making audiences question whether they are rooting for the villain, while capturing a specific era through its fashion, technology, and culture. Phrases like "Greed is good" have become enduring touchstones, and Gekko continues to inspire finance professionals despite being the film's ostensible antagonist.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its 2016 Annual Report on Form 10-K with the SEC, covering the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy's memoir, published October 14, covers his judicial philosophy and reflections on key cases. Kennedy emphasizes judicial humility and integrity, rejecting both originalism and pragmatism as unsatisfactory approaches to constitutional interpretation. He discusses controversial decisions including Citizens United, where he defended the ruling against campaign finance limits; Obergefell v. Hodges, where he authored the same-sex marriage decision and reconciled with Justice Scalia after a personal attack in Scalia's dissent; Bush v. Gore, where he focused on legal rather than political considerations; and Texas v. Johnson on flag burning. Kennedy disliked being called the "swing justice," stating "the cases swung, not me." Though personally opposed to abortion, he remained on the court to uphold his judicial oath. The memoir also recounts a "chilling" meeting with Vladimir Putin, opposition to cameras in the courtroom, a suspected Manson family-related break-in at his home, and his view that presidential deference to Supreme Court rulings is essential.

The Simons Observatory's Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) uses microwave frequency multiplexing with SLAC microresonator radio frequency (SMuRF) electronics to read out nearly 31,000 superconducting transition-edge sensor (TES) detectors. Unlike the small-aperture telescopes, the LAT's warm electronics are mounted directly to the receiver and exposed to diurnal temperature swings in the isothermal receiver cabin. This temperature variation causes phase drift in the RF transmission lines, which was measured using off-resonance "pilot" tones that pass through the system unperturbed by microwave resonators. Analysis of 290 off-resonance tones over 22.6 hours showed time delays of a few picoseconds correlated with ambient temperature. When converted to noise-equivalent current, this phase drift contributes minimally to on-sky detector noise and remains within the readout noise budget, indicating it will not significantly affect the telescope's mapping speed.

The passage discusses computational challenges in modeling electron-photon interactions in optical cavities using the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. Standard quantum chemistry methods are inadequate due to the non-local, weak but long-range electron-photon coupling term. The sinc basis set offers a solution as an orthonormal, systematically improvable basis for representing molecular orbitals on uniform real-space grids, though direct implementation scales as O(N⁴) for two-electron integrals. Sparse or low-rank approximations can mitigate this cost due to rapid decay of off-diagonal integral tensor elements. The sinc function's properties as a band-limited function and its natural emergence from Fourier transforms of confined particle eigenfunctions make it suitable for extended interactions. The passage ends mid-sentence describing the photon field Hamiltonian in cavity QED.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units of high-titer convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). The primary endpoint—proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% vs. 84.1%, p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for any secondary endpoints, including mortality or mechanical ventilation at Day 30. Safety outcomes were similar between groups, with comparable rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal events. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6% of the intervention group. The study concluded that early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter clinical outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

This study analyzed empirical dietary patterns among 32,498 US adults from 2009-2020 NHANES data, identifying four patterns: "American" (refined grains, meats, added sugars; lowest Healthy Eating Index score of 42.4), "Prudent" (vegetables, poultry, seafood; HEI 58.2), "Legume" (vegetables, legumes; HEI 55.0), and "Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy" (highest HEI 62.0). Adults with cardiovascular disease showed higher adherence to the American pattern (37.1% vs. 33.3%). Higher socioeconomic vulnerability scores and SNAP participation were associated with greater likelihood of following the American and Legume patterns, and lower likelihood of the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. Associations between social risk factors and dietary patterns varied significantly by race and ethnicity, with Hispanic individuals showing no link between vulnerability and the American pattern. Findings suggest that interventions to improve nutrition should account for naturally occurring dietary patterns and their variation across vulnerable subgroups.

A player with a stable personality, skill, size, and strength has performed well in pressure-filled playoff games, scoring big goals including an overtime winner without overcelebrating. The Wham play is a football running concept where a Tight End or Fullback pulls to kick out a Defensive Lineman, similar to Trap but with different personnel. Its main strength is creating favorable, unexpected blocking angles as a complementary change-up play. Its weaknesses include complex installation requiring precise identification of fronts and assignments, plus the need for a powerful blocker. The passage details specific assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, covering all offensive positions. Two variations are presented: Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the Fullback kicks out the Nose Tackle and the quarterback can throw based on box count; and Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses defensive reaction to pin-and-pull to widen running lanes for the trap block.

This study evaluated horizontal transmission of Hepatitis C virus (HCV) among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye district, Rwanda. Using a descriptive cross-sectional design with 148 participants from 30 families, researchers found a 10.8% HCV prevalence—higher than Rwanda's general 4% rate. Testing involved HCV Ab rapid screening with ELISA confirmation. Significant risk factors included HBV co-infection (p=0.001), HIV co-infection (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016), while blood transfusion showed no significant association (p=0.058). Awareness of HCV transmission was low (93.9% incorrect answers) and not significantly correlated with infection status (p=0.079). The study recommends early screening of household members, patient follow-up, and educational programs to support Rwanda's 2030 HCV elimination goal. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, which cannot determine infection origin.

This paper introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework, a formal model analyzing computational problems through three interconnected spaces: syntactic (formal definitions), semantic (configurations satisfying constraints), and logical (inferential outcomes). CDF captures both intensional (internal generative rules) and extensional (observable behavior) perspectives, using mappings αf (syntax→semantics), βf (semantics→logic), and γf (syntax→logic). The framework classifies problems as ComCDF (compositionally coherent, stable mappings) or ExpCDF (explosive, unstable mappings), aligning with the P/NP boundary. Applied to SAT problems, 2SAT exhibits local, decomposable binary clause structures enabling polynomial-time solutions, while 3SAT's non-local ternary clauses create exponential semantic explosion and computational intractability. The CDF framework thus reveals structural origins of complexity through the geometry and logic of problem construction rather than runtime bounds alone.

Patents grant inventors temporary monopolies; upon expiration, inventions become publicly available. Scott Crump's 1992 FDM patent enabled today's desktop 3D printers, while his company Stratasys produces industrial machines costing up to $400,000. Industrial 3D printers average $104,222 (metal printers: $566,570), while desktop machines average $1,094. Other 3D printing methods include stereolithography (now $3,500 for basic models, up to $990,000 for industrial systems) and powder bed fusion for metal parts. Manufacturers view additive manufacturing as a tool for production parts in a $12.8 trillion global business. Modern 3D printers use diverse materials including plastics, metals, ceramics, and biocompatible substances. The BAAM system produces parts up to 240″×90″×72″, while HP's Jet Fusion 4200 matches the output of 163 desktop printers. Applications include NASA propulsion components, GE aircraft engine parts (25% lighter, 5× longer lasting), and medical devices. Expiring patents enable entrepreneurs to democratize industrial processes. The Wohlers Report ($500) is the definitive annual resource on additive manufacturing.

China has emerged as a global leader in clean energy transition while other major economies have stalled on climate commitments. At the UN Climate Summit, President Xi Jinping pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions 7-10% by 2035, expand wind and solar capacity to 3,600 GW, make electric vehicles mainstream, and increase forests to 34 billion cubic meters. China invested $625 billion in clean energy last year—nearly one-third of global investment—and its large domestic market has driven down renewable technology prices worldwide. Though China's annual emission reduction pace of 1% lags behind industrialized nations, analysts suggest China may overdeliver on its commitments. The country benefits from policy continuity due to its political system and dominates green technology manufacturing, including battery production for major automotive brands.

A randomized controlled trial in Cambodia compared 3.5 mg/kg and 7.0 mg/kg total doses of primaquine over 14 days to prevent Plasmodium vivax recurrences. Among 156 enrolled patients, recurrence rates within 90 days were 81.4% with no primaquine, 24.4% with 3.5 mg/kg, and 4.7% with 7.0 mg/kg. The 7.0 mg/kg dose reduced recurrence risk 5.9 times compared to 3.5 mg/kg, with comparable safety and tolerability in G6PD-normal patients. Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated. The study recommends 7.0 mg/kg primaquine for P. vivax in Cambodia and Southeast Asia.

Paulo Dybala confirmed he is fit to play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-final return leg, telling TyC Sports he has been training with the team and will "probably play 100%." The Argentine forward also discussed his contract renewal until 2022, stating it was his choice to stay at Juventus, which he considers comparable to Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona. A Mississippi woman was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling approximately $266,600 from Pink Hearts Fund, a cancer charity. English local authorities will receive millions of pounds in refunds after being overcharged for council tax summons court fees since 2013-14 due to a Ministry of Justice administrative error. The Ministry discovered the error during a fees system review and is urgently reducing fees to correct levels. Details of reimbursement will follow soon. The error affects a fraction of 300 court fees, but will cost HM Courts and Tribunal Service £9 million in revenue this year. Council tax summons reached 3.5 million last year, with campaigners linking rising figures to the 2013 abolition of council tax benefit. Over 4,800 people faced court and prison threats for non-payment in 2016-17, up 11% since 2013, with at least 62 imprisoned.

The U.S. government has frozen approximately $18 billion in federal infrastructure funding for New York City projects, including the Second Avenue Subway extension and Hudson River Tunnel, citing potential unconstitutional DEI criteria in contract awards. The Department of Transportation has suspended a $300 million payment and is conducting audits under a new interim rule limiting race- or gender-based preferences. LG will release webOS-powered TVs this month, featuring integration with Sky TV's EPG from launch. Users can view Sky content through the webOS menu and control it with LG's Magic Remote. The "Today" menu aggregates viewing options from apps like Netflix, Sky Now TV, YouTube, and live TV. enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; he previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head of oncology clinical development.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC), representing seven accrediting agencies overseeing 3,000 institutions, endorsed using artificial intelligence to improve credit transfer processes. The statement aims to dispel myths that accreditation standards block innovation in credit evaluation. Credit transfer poses significant barriers to degree completion: 58% of adults who attempted to transfer credit in 2024 experienced some credit loss, with 20% repeating courses and 16% abandoning their degrees entirely. Manual evaluation is inconsistent and subject to bias, with white students more likely to have credits accepted than Black or Latino students. AI can analyze course descriptions, enrollment, and learning outcomes to identify equivalencies, with research suggesting faculty seek approximately 70% overlap in learning objectives. CRAC encourages a default position of accepting credits unless evidence shows learning outcomes aren't met, while maintaining human oversight through a "trust-but-verify" approach. A pilot program involving 59 institutions is currently testing AI-powered course equivalency analysis.

Cryotherapy, a wellness treatment using chambers cooled to -180°F, is gaining popularity in the U.S. after originating in 1970s Japan. Proponents claim benefits including muscle recovery, reduced inflammation, pain relief, improved circulation, mood elevation, immune support, and calorie burning. The treatment works by triggering survival mode, drawing blood to the core for hyper-oxygenation. Polar Brrr Cryo in Grand Rapids, Michigan—Southwest Michigan's only facility—serves clients ranging from professional athletes to office workers since opening February 4th. The FDA has not approved cryotherapy, warning of frostbite, burns, and eye injuries. Limited scientific evidence supports claimed benefits, and one death occurred in 2015 from unsupervised use. Sessions last three minutes with protective gear and supervision; medical clearance is required for heart conditions or hypertension. Introductory rates are $25 for one session or $90 for three, with regular pricing at $55 per session.

The Israel Antiquities Authority announced the discovery of a 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment engraved with "Hyrcanus" in Hebrew, found in 2015 under Jerusalem's Givati parking lot near a mikvah complex and the remains of the Akra fortress. The name matches two Hasmonean kings (140–37 B.C.) but was also common, making ownership uncertain. The fragment represents one of Jerusalem's earliest chalk vessels, used by Jews for ritual purity.

This passage provides a comprehensive guide to Bollinger Bands trading strategies, covering 12 specific approaches including the Squeeze, Breakouts, %B, Walks, Bounce, Double Band Trend-Following, Band Width, RSI Divergence, Pinch Play, Reversal, Volatility Contraction, and Triple strategies. Bollinger Bands consist of a 20-day simple moving average with upper and lower bands set at 2 standard deviations, though settings are adjustable. The tool measures volatility—bands widen during high volatility and contract during low volatility. Testing showed profitability as a breakout indicator in gold but limited success with stock indices. Key risk management involves using stop-loss orders and confirming signals with additional indicators like RSI or MACD. The bands were created by John Bollinger in the 1980s and work best when combined with other technical analysis tools rather than used alone.

The holiday effect in stock markets refers to seasonal patterns where stocks show increased returns around specific holidays. The article examines seven US holidays using S&P 500 data (SPY and ^GSPC), finding only three with tradeable effects: Independence Day (4th of July), Thanksgiving, and Christmas.

The 4th of July strategy (buying three days before, selling at close before holiday) showed a 1.01% average gain, 68% win ratio, and 2.97 profit factor. Thanksgiving (buying at Monday's close, selling at Wednesday's close) yielded 0.82% average gain with 65% win ratio. Christmas/end-of-year rally (buying after December 20th, selling first trading day of new year) produced 1% average gain with 67% win ratio and 4.8 profit factor.

Other holidays showed minimal or negative effects: Martin Luther King Jr. Day (-0.05% average), President's Day (-0.24%), Memorial Day (0.18%), and Labor Day (0.11%). The article also explores post-holiday effects, finding that the second day after holidays often shows better returns than holding through the holiday itself. Potential causes include lower liquidity creating price "vacuums," increased optimism, reduced macro news, and pre-holiday risk reduction selling.

Scottish councils are setting budgets and deciding whether to raise council tax by up to 3%, ending a long-running freeze policy. About 26% of households—those in bands E to H—will see bills rise regardless of local decisions due to multiplier changes passed last year, raising £100m annually. Areas with more higher-band properties like Edinburgh will be more affected. Council tax bands are based on 1991 property values, and studies suggest 57% of properties would change band in a revaluation, though the government opposes this due to cost and potential bill shocks. Councils rely mainly on government grants, with Glasgow raising only 17% from council tax. The Scottish government's budget includes disputed funding changes, with Labour claiming a £170m cut to core grants while Greens argue a deal makes allocations "just about good enough."

Amazon is developing an AI chip to improve Alexa's speed and performance. The company's "Alexa Loses Her Voice" Super Bowl commercial was the most-viewed ad on YouTube that day. At CES, Sony unveiled an updated Aibo robot dog, while Amazon secured partnerships with HP for Alexa integration. Amazon and Google engaged in aggressive holiday pricing for their smart speakers, likely selling at a loss. Amazon's Echo Dot drove record holiday sales with Prime member support. Apple's competing HomePod speaker faced shipping delays, missing the Christmas season. A malfunctioning Alexa device in Germany played loud music at 2 a.m. while its owner was away. Amazon announced Alexa will be integrated into Big Mouth Billy Bass, a talking fish novelty item.

This document is a legal agreement between AMD and recipients of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block Specification, governing use, confidentiality, feedback, warranties, liability limitations, export compliance, and governing law. The technical specification defines the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, including: GHCB establishment via MSR protocol and GPA registration; version negotiation between guest and hypervisor; hypervisor feature advertisement through a bitmap; NAE events for VMGEXIT handling including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, MMIO access, page state changes, SNP guest requests, AP creation, doorbell pages, IPI, timers, and termination; SMP booting mechanisms; and restricted injection for SNP guests. The GHCB is a 4KB shared memory area enabling encrypted guests to communicate with hypervisors while protecting register state, with specific protocols for CPUID requests, AP reset hold, and multi-VMPL support.

Enron faces severe financial crisis as its stock plummeted to near seven-year lows on October 29, 2001, following Moody's downgrade of its senior unsecured debt to Baa2 (two notches above junk status) and placement of its commercial paper rating on review for downgrade. The company, which lost over 50% of its market value in two weeks, is negotiating with banks for $1-2 billion in new credit after drawing down $3 billion last week to pay off commercial paper and boost liquidity. The crisis stems from a $638 million third-quarter loss, $1.2 billion in equity write-downs related to undisclosed partnerships managed by ousted CFO Andrew Fastow, and an ongoing SEC investigation. European energy companies have begun freezing dealings with Enron due to credit concerns, while U.S. trading partners remain cautious but continue transactions. Analysts view the credit drawdown as a sign of desperation, with potential for harsher loan terms and further rating cuts. Royal Dutch/Shell was reported as a possible takeover suitor. A report by economists Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty states that India's income inequality has risen rapidly since the 1980s, with the top 1% now holding 22% of national income—the highest level since 1922. This increase followed economic policy changes in 1983-84, including reduced public sector engagement and increased entrepreneurship and foreign investment. From the 1950s to 1970s, strong regulations and fiscal progressivity had reduced top income shares while bottom 50% and middle 40% incomes grew faster. The "Shining India" period benefited the top 10% rather than the middle class, with the middle 40% experiencing greater prosperity during 1951-1980. India shows one of the highest increases in top 1% income concentration globally over the past thirty years.

Russia has intensified its targeting of Ukrainian drone pilots, using missiles, bombs, and other weapons to strike suspected operator positions. Ukrainian soldiers and drone operators report that pilots have become "target No. 1" due to their critical role in combat, with casualty rates skyrocketing in recent years. Drones now cause approximately 70% of casualties on both sides of the war, serving as force multipliers for intelligence gathering and precision strikes at low cost. Both sides view enemy drone pilots as high-value targets, with Ukrainian forces also hunting Russian operators. Ukrainian pilots have responded by moving operations underground, building stronger shelters, and rotating positions frequently.

The NHS recommends 6-8 glasses (1.2 liters) of water daily, with some intake coming from food. Water intoxication, though rare, can occur from drinking 2-3 liters quickly after exercise, diluting blood salt levels. Research from Monash University suggests drinking according to thirst rather than rigid schedules. A 2010 study found drinking two cups of water before meals helped participants lose 15.5lbs over 12 weeks versus 11lbs for non-water drinkers, as it reduced calorie intake by 75-90 calories per meal. Athletes following excessive hydration recommendations have died from overconsumption.

The authors present Doublethink, a Bayesian model averaging method that enables simultaneous control of Bayesian false discovery rate and frequentist familywise error rate for identifying direct risk factors in biobank-scale data. Applied to 1,912 variables for COVID-19 hospitalization in UK Biobank (1,917 cases, 200,000 controls), the method identified nine individually significant variables and nine pre-defined groups including age, sex, and deprivation indices. Post-hoc grouping revealed additional signals including obesity and psychiatric history. Compared to 127 published studies, Doublethink confirmed common risk factors (age, sex, obesity, smoking) but found stronger evidence for rarely studied factors like dementia and infection, while finding no direct effect for commonly analyzed diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension. The method addresses limitations of candidate risk factor studies and machine learning approaches by accounting for model uncertainty and controlling confounding, though it is computationally intensive and limited to direct rather than total effects.

This passage provides a comprehensive overview of patterns in software development, tracing their evolution from algorithms (Knuth's 1962 work) through object-oriented programming patterns (the "gang of four" Design Patterns book in the 1990s) to distributed systems patterns enabled by containerization and open source software.

The text emphasizes three core single-node container patterns: the sidecar pattern (augmenting application containers with additional functionality like HTTPS, configuration management, or monitoring), the ambassador pattern (brokering external communications for sharding, service discovery, or request splitting), and the adapter pattern (standardizing interfaces for monitoring, logging, or health checks). These patterns enable modularity, reusability, and separation of concerns.

The passage then covers multi-node distributed patterns including replicated load-balanced services (stateless and session-tracked), caching layers with SSL termination, and sharded services for stateful data. Microservices architectures are discussed as enabling reliability, agility, and independent scaling, though with added complexity in debugging and design.

Throughout, the text stresses the value of patterns in providing shared vocabulary, enabling knowledge reuse, accelerating development without requiring direct experience, and facilitating community collaboration through open source software.

Basketball teams must prepare for three jump ball situations: defensive (opponent advantage), even (equal chance), and offensive (team advantage). Defensive strategies include early rotation, watching jumper cues, and specific alignments like Box, Diamond, and "Y" formations. Even jump balls emphasize boxing out, anticipation, and coordinated clockwise/counter-clockwise rotations. Offensive plays with height advantage include tip-forward strategies like Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, with designated players maintaining defensive balance.

The passage contains diplomatic communications from January 1942 regarding U.S.-Finnish relations during World War II. The first excerpt describes a conversation where the narrator showed Finnish official Mr. Toivola a Tokyo radio broadcast allegedly quoting the Finnish Legation calling Soviet-Finnish peace rumors "Anglo-American machinations," expressing doubt about its authenticity but warning it would be against Finnish interests if true. A hockey player reflects on winning the Stanley Cup, describing his excitement and conversations with teammate Fleury about past game-winning moments. Defending baseline out of bounds plays requires different strategies than standard half-court defense because the defense has a numerical advantage (5 on 4) and shooters move directly to the basket rather than away from it. Four effective defensive approaches are: (1) Jam—aggressive face-guarding without switching to disrupt plays and draw violations; (2) Jump Switch—aggressive switching to deny passing lanes, effective with under five seconds remaining; (3) Trap—double-teaming the inbounds pass receiver; and (4) Combination Defense—using box-and-one, diamond-and-one, or triangle-and-two alignments to catch offenses off guard. All strategies begin with sagging off to protect against lob passes and basket cuts for three seconds before executing the primary defensive action.

This study investigated the molecular signature of neuropathic pain using Morton's neuroma as a model system. Researchers analyzed 22 affected plantar digital nerves from patients with Morton's neuroma and 11 control nerves using RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry. Differential gene expression analysis identified over 3,349 differentially expressed genes, with upregulated genes related to immune and inflammatory responses and downregulated genes associated with nervous system development. Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis revealed modules correlated with paroxysmal pain, including defence response (positive correlation) and neurogenesis (negative correlation). Deconvolution analysis showed higher macrophage and Memory B cell proportions in Morton's neuroma, with macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain severity. A specific M(GC) macrophage subset signature (CD163+, MARCO+, STAB1+) was identified, with MARCO expression correlating with paroxysmal pain. Immunohistochemistry confirmed demyelination, increased intraneural T cells, and elevated CD163+MARCO+ macrophage densities in Morton's neuroma. The findings implicate persistent neuroinflammation, particularly M(GC) MARCO+ macrophages, in chronic neuropathic pain associated with focal nerve injury.

Overnight trading involves buying at the close and selling at the next day's open or close, exploiting the overnight edge in stock markets where average gains from open to close have been near zero for 30 years. Multiple strategies exist, including Turnaround Tuesday, holiday seasonality, end-of-month effects, weekday effects, mean reversion, and options expiration effects. A portfolio combining these uncorrelated strategies—across different asset classes, time frames, and types (mean-reverting, trend-following, momentum)—can improve risk-adjusted returns and reduce drawdowns. Backtests since 1993 show realistic results with low commissions and slippage, though execution requires automated or mechanical trading. The key principle is that many sub-optimal uncorrelated strategies outperform a few "perfect" ones, helping compound returns by avoiding severe bear market losses.

The passage describes sterilization systems and methods for analyte monitoring devices, such as continuous glucose monitors. Traditional two-piece architectures require separate sterilization processes—radiation for sensors and chemical for electronics—necessitating user assembly. The disclosed one-piece architecture employs a collimator to focus radiation sterilization (e.g., electron beam) on the sensor and sharp while shielding electronic components within the electronics housing from radiation damage. The system comprises a sensor applicator, a sensor control device including an electronics housing with a sensor and sharp extending from the bottom, a cap coupled to the applicator, and a collimator positioned within or adjacent to the cap defining a sterilization zone that receives the sensor and sharp. Seals at the interface between the sharp hub and the top of the electronics housing, and between the collimator and the bottom of the electronics housing, create a sealed sterile region encompassing the sterilization zone and a portion of the housing interior. The collimator, constructed from high-density materials such as polyethylene or metal, blocks radiation from penetrating to the electronics. Alternative embodiments utilize external collimators positioned adjacent the applicator during sterilization. Methods include loading the sensor control device into the applicator, securing the cap, and sterilizing the sensor and sharp with radiation while preventing radiation damage to the electronics using the collimator.

This patent application describes metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters based on cyclic platinum(II) and palladium(II) complexes employing benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues for use in OLEDs and lighting applications. The emitters exhibit both singlet and triplet excitons, enabling unity internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. The triplet state is localized on the benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine portion, while the singlet energy can be reduced by extending conjugation without significantly changing triplet energy, creating a small singlet-triplet gap that allows thermal promotion to the singlet state. General Formulas I-XVII describe various implementations including square planar Pt(II)/Pd(II) complexes (Formulas I-XIII) and octahedral Ir(III) complexes (Formulas XIV-XVII). The application details synthetic procedures for 46 example compounds, with emission spectra and device performance data provided for selected examples.

The lecture explains how to construct SNARGs (Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments) using two building blocks: BARGs (Batch Arguments) and somewhere extractable hash functions (also called somewhere statistically binding hash functions).

A BARG allows proving that many instances belong to an NP language with a proof size depending only polylogarithmically on the number of instances k, not linearly. The soundness property discussed is semi-adaptive: the adversary must commit to which position i they will cheat on before seeing the CRS, though they can choose the actual instances adaptively.

A somewhere extractable hash family consists of five algorithms (gen, eval, open, ver, extract) with properties including completeness, index hiding (the hash key conceals which position i is special), and somewhere statistical binding (at position i, even an all-powerful adversary cannot open to both 0 and 1). By repeating this construction l times, binding can be extended to l locations while keeping unrevealed indices hidden.

The SNARG construction works as follows: to prove C(x) = 1 for a circuit C, the prover computes all wire values, hashes them using a somewhere extractable hash binding on l wire positions, then provides a BARG proving that every gate is satisfied (valid openings exist for each gate's input and output wires respecting the gate's logic) and that the output wire is 1. The verifier simply checks the BARG.

The efficiency relies on the BARG's index language property—the instances x₁*...xₖ* have a succinct description (hash key, hash value, and gate index), so verification time depends only polylogarithmically on circuit size, not linearly.
