Yael Kalai introduces an advanced cryptography course focused on the evolution of proofs in computer science from the mid-1980s to present. The class covers interactive proofs, doubly efficient interactive proofs, the GKR protocol, PCP, MIP, and applications including reproving Shamir's IP equals PSPACE theorem. The course then explores using cryptography for succinct proofs, the Fiat-Shamir paradigm, batch proofs, and SNARGs. Requirements include scribing notes for most sessions and one problem set. Students are encouraged to complete pre-class reading, particularly a survey by Justin Taylor on proof systems.

The lecture begins with interactive proofs, contrasting them with classical NP proofs. Interactive proofs allow back-and-forth communication between a prover and verifier, with the verifier using randomization that the prover cannot predict. Without randomization, the model collapses to NP; without interaction but with randomization, the model becomes MA (Merlin-Arthur), which may be more powerful than NP though this remains unproven.

Kalai presents a randomized algorithm for verifying matrix multiplication in O(n²) time: choose random r in field F, construct vector x = (1, r, r², ..., r^(n-1)), and check if Cx = ABx. This works because two distinct degree-(n-1) polynomials agree on at most (n-1)/|F| points.

The sum-check protocol is introduced as a foundational interactive proof for verifying that Σ f(h₁,...,h_m) = β over all (h₁,...,h_m) ∈ H^m, where f is a degree-d polynomial in each variable. The protocol proceeds in m rounds: in round i, the prover sends a univariate polynomial g_i(x) = Σ f(t₁,...,t_{i-1}, x, h_{i+1},...,h_m) summed over remaining variables; the verifier checks g_i has degree ≤ d and sums to the previous claim, then sends random t_i. Soundness error is at most md/|F|. The protocol has O(m) rounds, O(md) communication, and verifier runtime O(md|H|).

Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy (SUDEP) is the leading cause of death in healthy young epilepsy patients, with highest risk in those with uncontrolled generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS). Approximately 70% of SUDEP occurs after nocturnal GTCS, with 87.6% of patients found in the prone position, which carries over 60-fold relative risk compared to non-prone positioning. Central apnea and autonomic instability are key risk factors, both potentially exacerbated by prone positioning. Intervention must occur within 25-180 seconds post-seizure, making autonomous systems critical.

Researchers developed Korus, an autonomous body repositioning mattress to prevent SUDEP. The twin XL-sized device contains an 8×4 array of inflatable cells expanding up to 14 inches, with pressure sensors (1,152 nodes) and machine learning algorithms (Random Forest Classifier) detecting four cardinal body positions. Testing with 10 normative controls demonstrated 100% success in achieving recovery position from prone in average 21.75 seconds, with 96.8% accuracy in prone position detection. No misidentification occurred between prone and supine positions. Long-term sleep recording showed 97.3% correct position detection with 2.3 false position changes per hour, never incorrectly detecting prone position.

Korus represents a first-in-class autonomous intervention system, potentially reducing SUDEP risk by over 50%, comparable to SIDS "back to sleep" campaigns. Future development includes improved mapping, computing optimization, biomechanical frameworks, and integrated seizure detection algorithms.

The PGA848 is a high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with eight binary-gain settings (0.5V/V to 100V/V). It features external access to its output-stage difference amplifier inputs (DA_IN– and DA_IN+) for noise-filtering, noise-shaping, and custom attenuating gains. The internal 6.67kΩ feedback resistors have 0.01% accuracy (enabling 80dB CMRR) but ±15% absolute variation. A typical application drives a 16-bit SAR ADC with three filter stages: input EMI/RFI filter, parallel capacitor feedback filter (318kHz nominal cutoff), and charge reservoir filter. The device operates with independent input (≥±4.5V) and output (≥±2.25V) supplies, with output supplies clamped to input levels. Layout guidelines emphasize symmetrical input paths, bypass capacitors, trace separation, and minimizing leakage/parasitic capacitance on DA_IN pins.

In 2013, the European Space Agency launched the Gaia space observatory to catalog astronomical objects and create a precise 3D map of the Milky Way. Using Gaia's initial data combined with information from the RAdial Velocity Experiment (RAVE), a University of Toronto team led by Jason Hunt calculated that the Sun orbits the Milky Way's center at 240 km/s. By analyzing the distribution of stellar velocities and triangulating with Sagittarius A*, they refined the distance from Earth to the galactic center to 7.6–8.2 kiloparsecs (approximately 24,788 to 26,745 light years), narrowing previous estimates of 7.2–8.8 kiloparsecs. Hunt anticipates that Gaia's 2017 final data release will further improve measurement precision.

Inclusive education for children with disabilities has become a global agenda since the 1994 Salamanca Declaration and 2006 Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. Myanmar ratified CRPD in 2011 and enacted disability rights laws, though inclusive education remains understudied. This research examines education for visually impaired children in Yangon, where a "limited inclusive education in phase" system operates: students receive primary education at special schools, then transition to regular schools for secondary education. Two special schools (one public, one NGO-run) and two connected regular schools were studied through interviews, focus groups, and observations. Findings show special schools provide essential Braille instruction, life skills training, supplementary study time, and psychological security, while regular schools offer social skill development and disability awareness for non-disabled students. However, limitations include poor communication between special and regular school teachers, regular school teachers' dependency on special school expertise, limited social integration between disabled and non-disabled students, and lack of public awareness about educational opportunities for children with disabilities. The study concludes that while this phased model effectively utilizes existing resources, improvements in teacher collaboration and student integration programs are needed. The authors suggest that low-income countries should develop context-appropriate inclusive education models rather than immediately adopting one-track systems.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end. The device uses SMPL_SYNC to simultaneously sample multiple ADCs, requires a positive pulse on SMPL_SYNC centered around SMPL_CLK's falling edge after power-up, reset, or sampling clock restart. It features an internal precision voltage reference with 10µF bypass capacitor on REFIO, or accepts external reference when internal reference is disabled via SPI or SDI/EXTREF pin.

The ADC supports 2-lane and 4-lane modes with SDR and DDR interfaces, outputting 20-bit results MSB-first in 24-bit packets. Data clock frequency depends on sampling clock, data rate, and lane count per provided equations. A data output randomizer XORs conversion results with LSB or PRBS bit to minimize ground bounce interference. Two averaging modes improve SNR: simple average (halves data rate) and moving average (preserves data rate).

Test patterns for debugging include fixed pattern, digital ramp, and alternating pattern for two channel groups. The device powers down via RESET pin (logic 0) or PWDN pin (logic 0), or through register writes. Initialization requires register sequence with free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode enables 8MSPS for one channel pair while idling others.

SPI configuration uses three register banks addressable via 8-bit addresses, with daisy-chain support for multiple devices. Key registers control interface modes, data format, averaging, test patterns, analog input ranges, bandwidth, and common-mode settings. For ATE applications, the device achieves 0.0015% TUE post-calibration at 25°C±5°C and offers wide-bandwidth mode (700kHz) for multiplexed signals settling to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. Three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) require proper decoupling without specific sequencing.

This patent application describes systems and methods for neuromuscular stimulation that decode neural activity to identify desired movements and deliver appropriate electrical stimulation to achieve those movements. The technology creates a "neural bridge" for patients with motor impairments from stroke, spinal cord injury, or other neural damage by measuring neural activity (via EEG, ECoG, or implanted electrode arrays), removing artifacts, extracting features, and using decoders to determine desired movements. The system employs a body state observer to dynamically adjust stimulation patterns, supports multiplexed signals for compound movements, and can control body limbs, prosthetics, wheelchairs, computers, exoskeletons, or robotic arms. Training involves machine learning techniques like support vector machines with visual cues and feedback. Experimental results demonstrated a quadriplegic participant achieving 77.4% accuracy in initiating, sustaining, and switching between rhythmic and discrete thumb movements using thought alone, with a virtual central pattern generator enabling rhythmic movements.

The speaker says time off before the series has allowed the team to focus and prepare. They emphasize looking forward to the upcoming game rather than past events, noting they will review video and make adjustments later. They acknowledge the opponent's strong shot-blocking ability and the importance of winning to avoid returning to Dallas at a disadvantage, stating the team is focused on playing their best.

This passage is a detailed table of contents from a diplomatic correspondence volume, documenting U.S. foreign relations during 1917. It covers two main sections: Part I addresses the continuation of World War I and peace efforts, including President Wilson's December 1916 peace proposal, responses from Allied and Central Powers, and U.S. intercession for Greece. Part II covers neutral rights issues, particularly German submarine warfare, the severance of U.S.-German relations in February 1917, the Zimmermann telegram revelation, U.S. entry into the war in April 1917, and Latin American countries' responses including severance of relations with Germany by Panama, Cuba, Brazil, Bolivia, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Haiti.

On August 1, 2016, Microsoft Corporation entered into an Underwriting Agreement with multiple underwriters for the issuance and sale of $19.75 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes across seven series with maturities ranging from 2019 to 2056. The notes will be issued under an indenture dated May 18, 2009, as supplemented by an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture dated August 8, 2016, with U.S. Bank National Association as trustee. Interest will be payable semi-annually on February 8 and August 8, beginning February 8, 2017. The company filed a prospectus supplement dated August 1, 2016, in connection with the offering. The report was signed on August 5, 2016, by Keith R. Dolliver, Associate General Counsel and Assistant Secretary.

This study uses verbal autopsy surveys to determine cause-specific mortality in India during 2018-2021, addressing limitations in official COVID-19 death reporting. Researchers conducted WHO-compliant electronic verbal autopsies on 20,453 decedents from the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey, with causes coded to ICD-10 standards by physician panels.

Findings indicate SARS-CoV-2 caused 17.93% of deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths during the pandemic period, with death rates peaking at 1.1% annualized in May 2021. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths declined. SARS-CoV-2 death rates were highest among those over 80, though most deaths occurred among ages 61-80 due to population distribution. Geographic variation showed lowest rates in the Gangetic plain and highest in Goa, Meghalaya, and Tripura.

The study employed statistical adjustments for under-inclusivity in death reporting and non-response to verbal autopsy surveys. Limitations include potential misclassification of vaping-related disorders as COVID-19 deaths, unvalidated modifications to verbal autopsy instruments for SARS-CoV-2 detection, and incomplete correction for delayed death reporting beyond 32 months.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture delivers significant performance improvements over Turing through second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, and GDDR6X memory. RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection rates and add motion blur acceleration via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, achieving up to 8x faster motion blur rendering. Tensor Cores introduce structured sparsity for 2x throughput gains and support new data types including TF32 and BF16, enabling up to 2.7x higher tensor operations. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to reach 936 GB/sec bandwidth, a 52% improvement. RTX IO offloads decompression from CPU to GPU, accelerating I/O up to 100x. The A40 data center GPU offers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and 5-10x AI throughput compared to RTX 6000. Display outputs support 8K60 and 4K120, with HDMI 2.1 and hardware AV1 decode. Seventh-generation NVENC enables high-quality encoding up to 8K HEVC.

The 3-4 defense, featuring 3 down linemen, 4 linebackers, and 4 defensive backs, has been used to win 16 major championships since 2005 by coaches Bill Belichick, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart. The defense employs bigger linemen using a "two gap" approach and hybrid outside linebackers who can rush or cover. Its strengths include versatile pressure packages and two-safety sets that confuse offenses, while weaknesses include vulnerability against spread formations that force linebackers into coverage, creating a light 5-man box. Common blitzes include the Weakside Edge Blitz and "Crossfire" Blitz, which show different pre- and post-snap looks. Common coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 2 Man. The defense originated with Bill Parcells and Belichick's New York Giants, with notable disciples including Matt Patricia, Romeo Crennel, Saban, and Smart.

The professor begins by discussing quiz results, noting the average was 78-79 with a wide spread, and mentions that solutions will be posted. He advises students to focus on understanding solution approaches rather than worrying about individual points, as grading considers multiple factors including participation and homework.

The lecture then covers full factorial design of experiments, extending to k factors. Key concepts include using contrasts to estimate effects, where the total effect of a factor is calculated as the difference between average outputs at high and low settings. For a 2³ design, this involves comparing planes of points on a hypercube. The professor explains how interaction columns are generated through multiplication of factor columns, and how these enable estimation of interaction effects.

The relationship between contrast and regression approaches is discussed, with coded values (-1 to +1) forming the x-matrix for regression. ANOVA is used to test significance of effects, comparing sum of squared deviations to noise estimates via F-tests.

An example using break forming data (punch depth and material type) illustrates the methodology. With 10 replicates at each of four combinations, the professor shows how to fit a linear model with interaction, check residuals for patterns, and assess significance. He notes that using only means allows direct inverse solution with zero residuals, while full data requires pseudo-inverse and provides error estimates.

To check for model adequacy (curvature), center points can be added, though this requires care with discrete factors. The professor demonstrates lack-of-fit testing by comparing deviation from linear model to replication variance.

Finally, blocking and confounding are introduced as methods to handle nuisance factors. By arranging runs so that nuisance effects align with higher-order interactions rather than main effects, their impact can be minimized. This leads to fractional factorial designs, where subsetting corner points reduces experimental runs when certain higher-order effects are deemed negligible.

The Neofoot study evaluated newborn foot length as a proxy measure to identify low birth weight (LBW) and preterm birth (PTB) in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where neonatal mortality rates are high and many births occur outside health facilities. The prospective diagnostic accuracy study enrolled 342 newborns in Madang Province, measuring foot length with a simple plastic ruler device within 72 hours of birth. Reference standards included birth weight measured with electronic scales and gestational age calculated from ultrasound scans and last menstrual period. The optimal foot length cut-off for identifying both LBW (<2.50 kg) and PTB (<37 weeks) was <7.7 cm, with sensitivity of 84.7% and 88.0% respectively. Among 123 babies with paired measurements, trained community volunteers showed acceptable agreement with researchers (mean difference 0.07 cm, 95% limits of agreement -0.55 to +0.70 cm). The study found foot length measurement feasible for identifying at-risk newborns in resource-limited settings, though implementation research is needed to address digit preference in measurements and assess health system impacts.

Iran's parliament gave initial approval to a bill increasing spending on the missile program and Revolutionary Guards in response to new US sanctions. The measure allocates over $260 million each to the ballistic missile program and the Quds Force, and requires strategies to counter US human rights violations and support sanctioned Iranian bodies. The government backed the bill, stating it avoids violating the 2015 nuclear deal. The bill requires a second parliamentary vote and clerical approval to become law.

MSPM0G MCUs feature five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with two power domains (PD1 for CPU/high-performance peripherals, PD0 for low-power peripherals) to optimize power consumption. The PMU generates core supplies with brown-out reset and dynamic voltage scaling. The clock module provides multiple oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, HFXT, SYSPLL) and distributed clocks including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, and various peripheral clocks. The DMA controller supports 12 channels with multiple transfer modes and data types, enabling data movement without CPU intervention. Peripherals include two 12-bit ADCs with 4Msps conversion, temperature sensor, VREF with 1.4V/2.5V references, three comparators, 12-bit DAC with FIFO, AES-128/256 accelerator with secure keystore (4 keys), CRC-16/32, MATHACL, multiple UART/I2C/SPI instances, CAN-FD, RTC with calendar functions, independent watchdog, windowed watchdog, general-purpose and advanced timers with PWM, up to 93 GPIOs with wake capability, and serial wire debug interface. The boot strap loader supports UART/I2C programming with password protection.

Blackwell introduces new clock gating capabilities that enable rapid shutdown of entire clock trees to save dynamic power, including during brief idle periods. Memory power management was a key focus, with the memory clock tree being gated for the first time using GDDR7's fast-wakeup architecture. A new separate voltage rail for GPU cores and memory enables independent voltage control per workload, boosting performance and allowing shutdown of unused chip portions to reduce leakage power. Rail-gated states can be entered at frame granularity, benefiting battery-powered gaming and content creation.

A Berliner Testament is a mutual will where spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and their children as final heirs, providing financial security to the surviving spouse. However, it has a strong binding effect that prevents unilateral changes, which can create problems if circumstances change, such as marital breakdown or new relationships. Clauses can be added to reduce this rigidity. Tax implications should also be considered, as sole inheritance may exceed tax allowances. Legal advice is recommended when drafting such a will.

Delta expects premium cabin revenue to overtake coach cabin sales next year. In the last quarter, premium ticket revenue rose 9% year-over-year to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. CEO Ed Bastian reported no signs of slowing premium demand. Delta's main cabin revenue share dropped from 60% in 2010 to 43% in 2024, while premium seats and loyalty programs now generate close to 60% of revenue. Airlines have added more premium seats to fleets, some with elaborate features that have delayed new plane production.

This study develops and evaluates population-level forecasting models to predict annual fatal opioid-related overdoses at the census tract level in Cook County, Illinois (2015-2022) and Massachusetts (2001-2021), aiming to inform geographically targeted public health interventions. The researchers compare multiple modeling approaches—including simple baselines (all zeroes, last year, historical average), statistical models (Poisson GLM, Gaussian Process, Bayesian spatiotemporal), and neural networks—using both traditional error-based metrics (RMSE, MAE) and a novel intervention-focused metric called "best possible reach" (%BPR), which measures how well a model identifies high-burden areas for limited-budget interventions.

Key findings indicate that simple historical average baselines with tuned look-back periods perform competitively with complex models across both locations and metrics. The study demonstrates that %BPR can yield different model rankings than error-based metrics, with potential to identify 15-18 additional annual fatal overdoses for intervention in the top 100 tracts. The Bayesian spatiotemporal model with Social Vulnerability Index covariates achieved the highest %BPR in Massachusetts (62.0%), while the Poisson GLM with SVI performed best in Cook County (79.4%). The authors recommend including tuned historical average baselines in future forecasting studies and using intervention-aware metrics like %BPR to better align model evaluation with public health decision-making needs. All software and the Cook County dataset are publicly available.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder in 1978, used to measure price gains or losses on a scale from 0 to 100. A Contract for Difference (CFD) is a financial contract allowing traders to speculate on asset price movements without owning the underlying assets. In CFD trading, RSI helps identify overbought conditions (typically above 70) and oversold conditions (typically below 30), enabling mean-reversion strategies. For day trading, shorter time frames with more extreme thresholds (15 for oversold, 85 for overbought) are often used. Effective RSI trading requires backtesting, combining multiple time frames, using other indicators, and prioritizing risk management. Three popular strategies include a basic two-day RSI approach, an enhanced version with a QS exit mechanism, and an RSI Momentum trend-following strategy.

Science is advancing efforts to "hack" the mind through multiple approaches. Researchers are developing a "memorization pill" by studying individuals with exceptional natural memory and sequencing their genomes for drug development; this team has already engineered fruit flies with photographic memories using CREB activators. Other scientists are working to identify intelligence-related genes for potential genetic enhancement. Additionally, experimental deep brain stimulation devices are being developed to both monitor brain activity and automatically correct abnormal patterns, such as those preceding panic attacks or depressive episodes.

This chapter covers host environment requirements for implementing BIOS interface mechanisms to access AGESA software. The host must establish a valid stack before calling AGESA procedures using module dispatchers. Entry point identifiers are in AMD.H. Bridge procedures locate binary image entry points and call the AMD dispatcher, with an example in AmdBridge32.asm.

The host must implement a call-out router function loaded in the standard header to route AGESA core call-outs. The router translates function numbers to execution addresses. Call-outs use 32-bit protected mode flat addressing.

UEFI BIOS has four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) across three modes. AGESA core files are arranged into three libraries, with four additional UEFI libraries. Build tools vary by phase: MASM 6.15 for 16-bit SEC, Microsoft tools for 32-bit and 64-bit phases.

Configuration options are described in Chapter 181, with platform-specific options in <plat>Option.c files. UEFI requires special handling for StdHeader content and PEI_Services handles.

The SEC phase establishes C environment and 32-bit execution mode using AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. Two PEIM modules support AGESA: AmdProcessorInitPeim (processor initialization, publishes AMD_PEI_INIT_RESET_PPI_GUID and AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI_GUID) and AmdMemoryInitPeim (memory initialization, publishes AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI_GUID). AmdResetPeim coordinates reset requests.

DXE drivers perform late initialization. AmdCpuDxeDriverInit calls AmdInitLate and publishes AGESA_DXE_PROTOCOL_GUID. AmdGpuVgaControlDxe monitors PciIo protocol for VGA resource decoding.

Reference files in \Addendum include Cpcar32.asm (Cache-As-Ram wrapper) and <Plat>Options.c (platform build options). UEFI control files include AgesaPei0Libs.inf, AgesaPei1Libs.inf, and AgesaDxe0Libs.inf.

Required environment variables are AGESA_ROOT (AGESA code directory), AGESA_OptsDir (platform build directory), and AGESA_Platform (target platform name). Integration steps include copying option files, setting environment variables, and enabling CAR before AmdInitReset.

Build methods include Binary Modules (indirect method with common entry point) and Source Integration (direct source integration). Stack procedures are provided as macros without segment declarations. AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT provides early silicon initialization. AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK establishes pre-memory stack with specified position in CAR zone.

Key procedures include: AmdCreateStruct (allocates parameter block storage), AmdGetDataEye (returns DIMM data eye results), AmdGetApicId (returns processor APIC address), AmdGetExeSize (returns available cache size), AmdGetPciAddress (returns processor PCI address), AmdIdentifyCore (identifies current processor), AmdIdentifyDimm (identifies DIMM from memory address), AmdAddMmioRegion (merges MMIO range), AmdReadEventLog (reads event log entries), and AmdReleaseStruct (releases allocated storage).

Entry procedures in order: AmdInitReset (minimal post-reset initialization), AmdInitEarly (full pre-memory initialization), AmdInitPost (memory initialization), AmdInitEnv (pre-PCI configuration), AmdInitMid (graphics display configuration), AmdInitLate (late boot table generation), AmdInitRtb (S3 suspend preparation), AmdInitResume (S3 resume silicon re-initialization), AmdS3LateRestore (post-PCI restore), and AmdS3FinalRestore (final S3 restore).

Required call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer (post-memory buffer allocation) and AgesaDeallocateBuffer (buffer de-allocation).

Former Langley City mayor Peter Fassbender, who served one term as a Liberal MLA, is considering running for mayor again and will decide by early August. Fassbender was mayor from 2005 to 2013 before becoming MLA for Surrey-Fleetwood and serving as Minister of Education and minister of Community, Sport and Cultural Development. Two incumbent Langley City councillors have already declared their mayoral candidacy.

The speaker expresses gratitude for being called to national service by a free and virtuous nation, acknowledging the heightened honor and responsibility of the current difficult period. The United States had achieved unprecedented prosperity through republican institutions and peace, evidenced by agricultural, commercial, and manufacturing growth, reduced public debt, and national development. This prosperity's end came not from American wrongdoing but from belligerent powers' unjust retaliation against American neutrality. The speaker outlines guiding principles for governance: cherishing peace with all nations, maintaining neutrality, preferring diplomacy to war, fostering independence, preserving state and individual rights, supporting the Constitution, protecting religious freedom and press freedom, observing economic restraint, maintaining limited military forces with strong militias, promoting commerce and science, and continuing benevolent policies toward Native Americans. The speaker draws confidence from predecessors' examples, particularly the immediate predecessor's service, and from fellow citizens' intelligence and virtue, ultimately trusting in divine guidance for the nation's future.

The Supreme Court granted review of a Texas man's case regarding the right to appeal despite a plea agreement waiver. Hunter pleaded guilty to aiding and abetting wire fraud in 2024 and was sentenced to 51 months in prison with a mandatory mental health medication condition. The 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal based on his waiver, but Hunter argued this conflicts with other circuits' rulings allowing constitutional challenges. The Court will hear arguments in early 2025.

In *Thuro v. Meredith* (1924), the Colorado Supreme Court affirmed a judgment for real estate brokers seeking commission from their principals. The court held that principals cannot defeat a broker's commission by refusing to sign a contract with a purchaser produced by the broker. The court rejected claims of fatal variance between pleading and proof, finding any variance immaterial and harmless where Mrs. Tallman was bound as purchaser and Mr. Tallman acted as one. The court also upheld the refusal of requested instructions on immaterial issues and found alleged errors in overruling motions to strike harmless.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler pitched eight scoreless innings with 12 strikeouts and no walks against the Red Sox in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card series, becoming the first MLB pitcher to achieve this feat. Yankees scout Matt Hyde, who first discovered Schlittler at Northeastern University, called the performance "unbelievable" and "surreal." Schlittler was drafted in the seventh round of 2022 and debuted in July 2024.

Montecito Union School District settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, now 65 and 68, who claimed a deceased principal molested them in the 1970s. The settlement equals about 40% of the 350-student district's annual budget. The case was filed under a 2019 California law that removed the statute of limitations for childhood sexual abuse claims against public agencies. The district admitted no liability and will manage costs through hiring freezes, staff reductions, and redirected capital funds. A third plaintiff had previously settled for $1 million. The settlement came weeks after state legislators failed to pass a bill that would have restored such time limits.

Plantar pressure mapping is essential for clinical diagnostics and sports science, but data quality issues like outliers from technical errors or procedural inconsistencies can compromise analysis accuracy. This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) against an explainable machine learning (ML) approach using a Convolutional Neural Network with SHAP explanations for detecting outliers in plantar pressure data.

Data were collected from 703 subjects across multiple centers using resistive and capacitive pressure plates under static and dynamic conditions. The dataset comprised 798 valid and 233 outlier samples, augmented with 2,000 synthetic outliers across four categories: General Acquisition Error, Double Foot Capture, Inverted Orientation, and Incorrect Side Annotation. The SPM approach used affine registration to a reference template followed by pixel-wise nonparametric hypothesis testing with cluster-based correction. The CNN classifier used three convolutional blocks with foot-side embedding and SHAP for explainability. Both approaches were evaluated using nested stratified cross-validation, with human-centered assessment via semantic differential survey by 16 experts.

Results showed the ML approach outperformed SPM (F1: 0.99 vs. 0.93; MCC: 0.96 vs. 0.78). SPM's lower performance stemmed from sensitivity to misalignment and difficulty handling pathological yet valid samples. Experts rated both approaches positively for clarity, correctness, and usefulness, with no significant differences between them. While SPM was descriptively rated as simpler, 43% of experts preferred the ML approach with SHAP explanations, versus 35% for SPM. The study concludes that ML-based outlier detection with explainable AI offers superior accuracy for automated quality control in plantar pressure analysis, though both approaches provide interpretable explanations suitable for clinical decision support.

The popular definitions of bear markets (20% decline) and bull markets (20% rally) lack rational basis or hard data supporting their significance. These percentage-based definitions fail to help investors manage risk or deploy capital meaningfully. The author proposes alternative definitions based on long-term economic trends and investor psychology regarding valuations. A secular bull market is a 10-20 year period driven by broad economic shifts with rising corporate revenues, decreasing volatility, and increasing willingness of investors to pay more for earnings. A secular bear market features increased volatility, cyclical rallies and retreats, and decreasing willingness to pay for earnings. The author argues that earnings multiple expansion or contraction drives returns more than rising profits, citing that three-quarters of the 1982-2000 bull market gains came from rising price-to-earnings ratios rather than earnings growth.

Pharma tariffs threatened by President Trump did not take effect as scheduled. The administration will now prepare tariffs on companies that don't build U.S. infrastructure or make drug pricing agreements, with no new timeline set. Pharmaceutical executives receive near-daily calls from White House staff and senior agency officials as part of efforts to strike deals ahead of 2026 midterms. The administration has asked Eli Lilly to increase insulin production, Pfizer to boost certain drug output, and AstraZeneca to consider a U.S. headquarters.

The High Post Split Offense involves a high post split followed by down screens. Defending it requires two main strategies: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption.

**Show & Recover** involves two phases. First, defenders sag off in front of the high post when the ball is passed there, with guards positioning one stride in front and wings in help position. The post defender drops off to protect against guard splits. When the high post faces the basket, the defender jams them toward their weak-hand corner. Second, on down screens, defenders "show" to force shooters wide, then recover to pass denial positions. If the high post passes to a wing, standard defensive principles apply, with options to front, trap, or play straight up in the low post.

**SOS Disruption** uses four phases. First, pressure the ballhandler early to push them away from the high post area while denying direct entry passes. Second, sag off on the high post split, switching when guards cut through and smothering the high post toward the corner. Third, use "contact" switches on down screens, physically blocking shooters and maintaining strong pass denial. Fourth, trap passes to the wing with a double team, rotating into triangle positions, with specific rotations for pass-outs and post traps.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8% stake in Dubai-based private equity firm Abraaj, which faces allegations of investor fund misuse. The sale has become more urgent amid Abraaj's disputes with investors including the Gates Foundation and the World Bank's IFC, and as Deutsche undergoes restructuring involving 7,000 job cuts. Deutsche considers the stake non-core and had previously sought a valuation two years ago. Abraaj, which managed $13.6 billion, is under investigation, has cut 15% of jobs, suspended new investments, and seen executives resign, while considering selling its investment business unit.

This study examines Turkish teachers' perspectives on metaverse integration in education. The metaverse, which evolved from science fiction to platforms like Second Life, Roblox, and Fortnite, offers immersive learning experiences, personalized instruction, and safe practice environments for students. However, limitations include monitoring difficulties, increased cognitive load, and infrastructure requirements.

A survey of 333 Turkish teachers found that while 78.1% had experienced virtual reality or 3D environments, most lacked true metaverse exposure. Teachers held positive attitudes toward educational metaverse use (6.23/9) and identified advantages including student engagement, practical application opportunities, and boundary elimination. Primary concerns involved technical problems, psychological issues like addiction, inequality of opportunity, data security, and teacher readiness. Teachers rated Information Technology, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics as most suitable for metaverse applications, and expressed strong willingness to participate in training (8.08/9). Most predicted effective metaverse implementation within 3-5 years.

The study concludes that successful integration requires infrastructure investment, teacher training, content development, and health considerations, recommending gradual implementation beginning with low-risk applications.

The "Flash/Back Door" offense attacks the Box & One defense by exploiting its middle vulnerability. A baseline post player flashes to the middle, creating matchup problems. If no shot is available, High/Low post action and wing back cuts follow. The offense can flow into Single/Double Screen continuity. Variations include using base screens for star players and point back door entries. Success requires execution of mid screens, base screens, strong post ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and timing. Implementation involves scouting opponents, educating players on defensive reads and counters, using various alignments, and attacking weakest defenders. The Box & One defense uses four players in a box zone with one "Chaser" denying a specific opponent the ball.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 11, 2015, announcing financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress (Exhibit 99.2), both furnished but not deemed "filed" under securities laws.

The speaker describes witnessing his baby's birth as an amazing, indescribable experience, praising his wife as a trooper. He then discusses hockey, expressing concern for a teammate injured by an elbow to the head, comparing it to a previous incident involving Patrick Eaves. He states the team regrouped and played harder to win for their injured teammate. He also addresses criticism about a Drury hit, noting that high-tempo games lead to incidents, and mentions the opposing player has a history of similar hits, expecting league review.

The speaker's MCL has healed and feels strong, though another injury will need surgery after the series. The brace helps and it's not painful. They recovered quickly from a previous MCL tear by working on motion immediately. They're ready to return to the game tomorrow after watching games on TV, which they discussed with Brett. They hope someone else heals quickly to return to the series.

H.B. Fuller Company VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares at $58.40 each on October 2nd, totaling $315,184.80. The specialty chemicals company reported Q3 EPS of $0.65, missing estimates by $0.02, with revenue of $562.87 million beating expectations. The firm has a $2.87 billion market cap, PE ratio of 25.96, and beta of 1.72. A $0.15 quarterly dividend will be paid November 2nd. Analysts hold mixed ratings: one buy, five hold, and two sell, with a consensus price target of $57.40. Institutional investors own 92.37% of shares, with BlackRock significantly increasing holdings by over 10,000% in Q1.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 the bail plea of 2008 Malegaon blast accused Lt Col Prasad Shrikant Purohit and a plea challenging bail granted to co-accused Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur. Purohit seeks bail after the Bombay High Court rejected his application, while Nisar Ahmed Haji Sayed Bilal, father of a blast victim, seeks cancellation of Thakur's bail citing her potential to influence witnesses. The High Court granted bail to Thakur on April 25 but rejected Purohit's plea. The NIA gave Thakur a clean chit but maintained serious charges against Purohit. Six people were killed in the September 29, 2008 blast in Malegaon, Maharashtra.

The authors present LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web-based tool built on R Shiny for identifying disease trajectories using electronic medical records (EMR) data. The tool follows a four-step process: disease filtering (using Cox regression with time-varying exposure), disease pair detection (binomial testing), disease pair validation (conditional logistic regression), and trajectory construction by concatenating validated pairs. LUKB DT was applied to UK Biobank ICD-10 diagnosis data to study COVID-19 disease trajectories, finding that COVID-19 primarily led to SARS-CoV-2-related conditions (viral agents, viral pneumonia, respiratory failure) and other medical care, but did not identify immune-related diseases possibly due to limitations in the hospital-based diagnosis data. The analysis of 183,386 individuals with 8,411 COVID-19 cases took 55 minutes using 8 computational cores. The authors note limitations including reliance on processed medical records and that constructed trajectories may not reflect real patient pathways, recommending the tool be used for investigating risk factors rather than patient clustering.

Children with language vulnerabilities require tailored support for language development. Speech-language therapists (SLTs) deliver interventions but face challenges when collaborating with educators to provide consistent linguistic modeling during everyday interactions. Game-based learning is common in therapy, yet generating diverse examples with specific morphological structures in real-time is demanding for professionals.

Robot-Assisted Language Learning (RALL) offers potential solutions, though earlier systems were limited by rigid programming and insufficient adaptability. The authors developed TalBot, integrating a large language model (LLM) with the Furhat conversational robot to lead word retrieval games with preschool children. TalBot manages turn-taking, provides feedback, interprets mispronunciations, and redirects off-topic conversations.

The LLM handles game management and dialogue generation while the robot manages physical interactions, speech synthesis, and non-verbal communication. This approach advances RALL by enabling adaptive responses without predefined structures, handling approximate rather than exact matches, and simplifying content updates.

Future development focuses on morphological learning through three mechanisms: generating unlimited grammatically correct material, providing consistent linguistic models without fatigue, and serving as a role model for educators. Implementation involves laboratory studies, field studies in preschools comparing robot and educator performance, and feasibility studies with children having clinically significant language vulnerabilities.

Key considerations include data protection regulations, ethical assessment of long-term effects, practical implementation challenges, and potential resistance from educational settings. The long-term goal is creating a robust LLM-based RALL application for teaching morphological structures across languages.

This passage documents AMD AGESA software integration requirements for UEFI BIOS environments. The PEI phase uses two modules: `AmdProcessorInitPeim` for processor initialization publishing `AmdInitEarlyPPI`, and `AmdMemoryInitPeim` for memory initialization publishing `AmdInitPostPPI` and `AmdMemoryInfoHOB`. The DXE driver performs late initialization via `AmdInitLate`, generating tables accessed through `AgesaDxeProtocol`. Additional services include data eye retrieval, APIC/PCI address determination, processor identification, memory address translation, MMIO management, and event logging. AARCH64 APUs with Platform Security Processor use different initialization paths without stack macros.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage using two deep safeties and five underneath players (two corners, three linebackers in a 4-3 defense) to defend short routes while protecting against deep passes. Strengths include balanced coverage against quick passes, hitch/slant routes, and wide receiver screens, plus run support from "hard" corners positioned near the line. Weaknesses include vulnerability to multiple deep routes (especially 4 verticals), trips formations, and certain run schemes that create numerical advantages or exploit the weak side. Cover 2 rules assign specific zones: corners cover flats, safeties cover deep halves, and linebackers cover hook/curl or middle hole zones. Variations include "Switch" (corners bail deep, safeties play flats) and disguised 1-high shells.

The 5-day low overnight trading strategy in the S&P 500 involves entering trades at the close when the market opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than its opening price, then exiting at the next day's open. This patent application describes an image processing method and apparatus for placing external objects, such as advertisements, in videos using computer vision technology. The method involves: obtaining a video with multiple frames; placing a target three-dimensional model (e.g., a cube) on a target plane in the first frame, with feature points of the model surface falling on that plane; determining 3D coordinates of feature points in a world coordinate system and their pixel coordinates on the first frame; calculating the camera pose for the first frame; tracking the target plane across subsequent frames to determine camera poses for remaining frames; and replacing the 3D model with a target model to generate a video with the placed object. The approach uses plane tracking rather than feature point calculation, enabling faster processing with lower computational requirements and applicability to videos without large parallax. The system can be implemented on electronic devices with processors and storage, and may utilize neural networks for plane detection and deep learning for camera calibration.

The offside trap is a defensive soccer maneuver where defenders move upfield in unison just before an opponent passes to a leading striker, placing that striker in an offside position. First used in the 1900s, the tactic became riskier after offside law changes and the rise of short-passing attacks. Success requires mature players, precise timing, unified movement, and a designated caller—usually a center-back. Defenders must maintain a straight line parallel to the halfway line, communicate constantly, and recognize when opponents will play forward. Signals may be verbal or non-verbal. The trap works best against through-ball teams and flat-back-four formations, but fails if any defender moves late or an attacker avoids involvement. Overuse increases risk of opponents adapting.

The Dividend Discount Model values stocks as the present value of expected future dividends discounted by risk-adjusted rates. The Gordon Growth Model simplifies this to P = D/(r-g) for constant growth, showing that stock prices depend on expected dividends, discount rates (inversely), and growth rates. This implies the discount rate r equals the dividend yield (D/P) plus the growth rate (g), demonstrating that growth opportunities add value beyond current cash flows. Accurate valuation requires estimating both future cash flows and appropriate risk-adjusted discount rates determined by market forces.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. Output voltage is set via resistor divider to 0.613 V reference. The controllers feature programmable soft-start, three oscillator modes (internal, external synchronization, primary-secondary), and configurable dead times. The controllers support buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies, with applications up to 2 MHz enabling GaN-based designs.

The Nobel Prize, established by Alfred Nobel in 1901, honors major scientific discoveries but recognizes only narrow fields—physics, chemistry, and physiology or medicine—leaving disciplines like ecology and geology unrecognized. Awards are limited to three recipients per prize, omitting hundreds of contributors to winning research. Selection focuses on discoveries rather than individuals and takes nearly a year. Winners are predominantly white men from wealthy regions such as the United States and Western Europe, as underrepresented groups face barriers accessing major research institutions. By 2023, only 13 women had won the physiology or medicine prize, and just one Black person had won any science Nobel. Despite these constraints, the prizes generate significant public interest in science.

The technology relates to systems and methods for splice site classification and aberrant splicing detection in genomic sequences using deep learning. It employs atrous convolutional neural networks (ACNNs), including architectures named SpliceNet (SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, SpliceNet10000), which use dilated convolutions to capture long-range contextual dependencies with large receptive fields. The networks are trained on datasets of donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, and non-splicing sites to classify nucleotides. For aberrant splicing detection, the system processes reference and variant sequences through the ACNN and compares splice site scores to identify pathogenic variants. Technical implementations include groups of residual blocks with varying convolution window sizes and non-exponential atrous rates, batch normalization layers, ReLU layers, skip connections, and global average pooling.

Kickers specialize in scoring via extra points and field goals while handling kickoffs and situational kicks. Expected to make approximately 90% of extra points and 80% of field goals from 25-60 yards, they also execute kickoffs for touchbacks or directional placement and serve as emergency punters. The term "placekicker" refers to kicks set by a holder or tee. Required skills include accuracy, lower body power, and flexibility, with typical builds of 5'10"-6'2" and 180-210 pounds. Notable examples include Justin Tucker (most accurate, longest field goal record), Morten Andersen (565 career field goals, Hall of Fame), and Adam Vinatieri (all-time leading scorer, consecutive field goal record). Kickers influence fourth-down decisions and game outcomes through scoring and field position management.

VentureWire newsletter from May 31, 2001, covering venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include Insight Capital closing its fourth fund at $740 million for software investments; Whitney & Co. spinning off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices after falling short of its $2 billion fundraising target; Rho Ventures closing Fund IV at $435 million, its first fund open to institutional investors; and Quake Technologies raising $30 million in Series B funding for optical networking chips. North Carolina regulators are discussing tests for GenX and related chemicals in backyard vegetables near The Chemours Co. plant near Fayetteville, following a Dutch study that found these chemicals in 40% of food samples near a similar plant. State waste management director Michael Scott said inter-agency talks haven't decided whether to test gardens or how. The discussions respond to residents' health concerns about plants, fish, and venison. Fish test results from waterways near both plants are expected within months. GenX, used since 2009 to replace PFOA in making Teflon, has shown toxic effects in animals but human effects are unknown. The EPA classifies it as an "emerging contaminant" with no federal health standards. A resident near the Fayetteville plant stopped eating his homegrown produce after finding GenX in his well water. The chemical was detected in drinking water for 200,000 people in Wilmington, 100 miles downstream.

High-κ materials are essential for advanced electronic devices, requiring both high dielectric constants and wide band gaps. Traditional materials like SiO₂ and perovskite oxides face limitations in achieving these properties simultaneously. HfO₂ offers better balance but still has trade-offs. Machine learning-based virtual screening has emerged as a promising approach to discover next-generation high-κ materials, though accurate prediction of ionic dielectric constants (εion) remains challenging.

This study develops a high-accuracy machine learning model for predicting εion by separately predicting Born effective charges (BECs) using an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) and phonon properties using a machine learning potential (SevenNet), then analytically combining them. The joint model achieves R² = 0.843 and RMSE = 0.129, significantly outperforming direct prediction approaches.

Using this framework, researchers virtually screened 8,717 oxides and identified 38 previously unknown high-κ candidates with figure of merit ≥ 350. Twelve exceed the best training oxide (KTaO₃). Most identified oxides contain transition metals with empty d-orbitals and oxygen octahedral networks. Ten have been experimentally synthesized, with five showing high experimental dielectric constants matching predictions.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend but indicates weak future short-term gains across markets. Backtesting on S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT) using a strategy of entering after two consecutive days with higher highs and higher lows and exiting after 1-10 bars showed poor short-term returns. S&P 500's two-week average gain was 0.23%, half of random gains. Gold showed similar poor performance at 0.37%. Treasuries showed negative short-term returns despite falling interest rates. Extending to three or four consecutive days did not improve results. The pattern acts as a short-term reversal pattern but is not powerful enough to use as a standalone trading signal for long or short strategies.

A coach discusses his team's preparation for an upcoming playoff game, emphasizing their relaxed yet focused mindset. He explains they had a simple practice after traveling to get loose for tomorrow's game. The team honored an injured player, Marc, by bringing his equipment and hanging his sweater in his stall; the player wanted to play despite his injury but doctors wouldn't allow it. The coach notes the importance of enjoying the moment while staying focused, creating a positive atmosphere in the dressing room, and learning from past experiences with elimination games. He praises a veteran player's leadership and hockey intelligence, noting he wants to win more for his teammates than himself. The team has already begun discussing adjustments needed for the next game.

Heading into "Dancing with the Stars" Season 34 Episode 3, 12 contestants remain including gymnast Jordan Chiles, the only remaining athlete, following Week 2's double elimination of Baron Davis and Corey Feldman. Episode 3 features a "TikTok night" theme. The competition scoring combines judges' scores (maximum 30 points) and public votes equally. Viewers may vote during live Eastern and Central time broadcasts via the ABC website, Disney+ app, or text message, casting up to 20 votes per celebrity weekly.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivers industry-leading performance for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting all deep learning data types (FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, binary), with TF32 providing 10x faster performance than V100 FP32 operations. The A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, enabling up to 2x throughput improvement by skipping zero values in 2:4 sparse matrix patterns.

The GPU contains 108 SMs with 6912 FP32 CUDA cores and 432 Tensor Cores, fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process. Memory architecture includes 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache—nearly 7x larger than V100. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology allows partitioning into up to seven isolated GPU Instances for improved utilization in multi-tenant environments.

Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (12 links at 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair), doubling V100's interconnect performance. PCIe Gen 4 support delivers 31.5 GB/sec bandwidth. New CUDA 11 features include asynchronous copy operations, hardware-accelerated barriers, task graph acceleration, and L2 cache residency controls.

The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, delivering 5 PFLOPS AI performance in a 6U form factor. It supports scaling from single-node deployments to thousands of nodes via Mellanox HDR InfiniBand and the Magnum IO SDK.

Medora Brown joined Sanergy, a Kenyan sanitation company, as communications manager in 2015 to develop a social media strategy. Sanergy, founded by MIT students in 2011, provides franchised hygienic toilets in Nairobi slums and converts waste into fertilizer and animal feed. Brown faced challenges allocating limited resources across diverse audiences—slum dwellers, farmers, and global investors—while demonstrating social media ROI.

Kenya's growing middle class and technology sector, dubbed "Silicon Savannah," offered opportunities: 55% internet penetration, 82% mobile phone ownership, and rising social media use, particularly Facebook. However, slum dwellers used social media sparingly for practical purposes, while farmers increasingly engaged through platforms like Facebook and WhatsApp.

Sanergy's three brands had different needs: Fresh Life required personal trust-building for franchise recruitment and consumer adoption; Farm Star sought consultative selling to demonstrate fertilizer benefits; and corporate fundraising relied on foundations and large donors rather than mass appeals. Brown aimed to create efficient content strategies, measure business impact, and determine which platforms best served each constituency's distinct requirements.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 genes linked to male pattern baldness in a study of over 52,000 men. The findings, published in PLoS Genetics, showed 40 genes on the X chromosome (inherited from mothers) and others scattered across the genome. A formula was developed to predict hair loss risk, though individual prediction remains inaccurate. The study found genetic patterns somewhat predictive: 14% of those with fewer baldness genes were bald versus 58% of those in the top 10% for baldness genes. Researchers noted male pattern baldness affects approximately 80% of men by age 80.

Mercy University School of Education has strengthened its mission through several grant-funded initiatives. The five-year, $2.8 million federal GRAD-PRO grant expands postbaccalaureate opportunities for Hispanic and underrepresented graduate students in health sciences, education, and business through faculty mentoring and scholarships. The three-year BRANCH-ED grant enhances teacher preparation quality and diversity through district partnerships and curriculum reviews, achieving 100% outcome success in its first year. The NSF-funded MISTI program, ongoing since 2013, prepares STEM teachers for high-need schools through intensive observations, coursework on social justice, student teaching placements, and multi-year mentorship. The NSF Master Teaching Fellowship (2019-2024) developed 14 STEM teacher leaders through graduate coursework and leadership projects. The $687,500 CR-ITI/ESOL grant (2023-2028) addresses English language teacher shortages in New York City through clinically rich preparation and mentorship. These grants collectively advance curricular innovation, mentoring, diversity initiatives, and school partnerships to prepare educators for diverse learners.

A goaltender credits his teammates' strong defensive play for winning two tight games. He highlights a key save on a bouncing puck late in the second period. The team has momentum heading to Anaheim, where they expect a challenge from an opponent eager to win at home.

A CORAF report on the largest System of Rice Intensification (SRI) project ever undertaken found that SRI increased rice yields and farmer incomes in West Africa. The three-year SRI-WAAPP project involved over 50,000 farmers across 13 countries, producing an additional 20,000 tons of milled rice valued at $10 million in 2015-2016. Independent evaluation found yield increases of 54-153% depending on system type, and 41% average income growth. The project used four adaptable principles rather than fixed techniques, enabling local adaptation. Authors noted that full SRI adoption in 2017 would have eliminated regional rice import needs. However, concerns exist about potential labor burdens on women, prompting adoption of labor-saving technologies. The project's regional scale facilitated cross-border collaboration and faster SRI dissemination.

Retired lawyer Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his McGill University law schoolbooks after 50+ years, reflecting on memorable cases like Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Company and The Wagon Mound while ultimately recycling most volumes, keeping only his tax law book as a reading stand.

Mailis Reps signed directive for two state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla opening September 1 next year. Hiring has begun. Construction proceeds with Novarc AS and Kamp architects for Viimsi, Salto architects for Rapla.

After five days investigating Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock, authorities remain unable to determine his motive for killing 58 people and wounding hundreds at a country music festival. Investigators have examined his politics, finances, potential radicalization, and social behavior with little result. They are exploring whether he met with a prostitute before the shooting, reviewing cruises he took (including one to the Middle East), and analyzing a cryptic note found in his hotel room. The FBI plans to erect billboards requesting public information. Paddock, a 64-year-old reclusive high-stakes gambler, meticulously planned the attack from his 32nd-floor hotel suite, stockpiling 23 guns and setting up surveillance cameras. He had also booked rooms overlooking other music festivals in Chicago and Las Vegas, suggesting he may have considered additional attacks. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, who was in the Philippines during the shooting, told investigators she noticed no warning signs of violence.

This systematic literature review examines 15 peer-reviewed articles on robotic coding in science education published between 2015-2022, sourced from Web of Science and Scopus databases. The study identifies three main research themes: cognitive skills (21st-century skills and computational thinking), applications in teaching (integration into science/engineering using Arduino and tablets), and affective variables (interest, motivation, and opinion). Key findings indicate robotic coding enhances problem-solving, scientific creativity, and algorithmic thinking, while increasing student motivation and interest through hands-on product creation. Study suggestions emphasize integrating robotic coding across STEM fields, expanding to different learning levels, and conducting large-scale research. The review reveals gaps in addressing psychomotor skills, curriculum development, and broader 21st-century competencies like innovation and leadership. Recommendations include diversifying tools beyond Arduino, examining additional affective characteristics, and providing teacher in-service training to support implementation.

System Management Arts Incorporated ("Smarts") moved to revise the court's previous opinion denying its motion for partial summary judgment against Avesta Technologies, Inc. and David Zager, based on newly-discovered evidence under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b). The court denied the motion.

The underlying dispute involved Smarts' claim that Avesta's "Trinity" program infringed Smarts' patents, while defendants argued that Morgan Stanley's "Delphi" program constituted prior art invalidating those patents. In the prior opinion ("Smarts I"), the court found a triable issue of fact regarding Delphi's status as prior art, relying partly on the "Klener Declaration" from Igor Klener, who stated he had obtained a general understanding of Delphi in 1993-1994.

New evidence from Klener's September 2000 deposition revealed that shortly before signing his declaration, Avesta had invited him to participate in a private stock placement before an anticipated IPO; his $225,000 investment later doubled in value. Klener was also friends with Avesta executives. Klener denied any quid pro quo.

The court held that the motion was timely and proper under Rule 54(b) because it was based on newly-discovered evidence. However, the court rejected Smarts' argument that Klener's alleged bias rendered his declaration insufficient as a matter of law to provide corroboration. Under Federal Circuit precedent, while corroboration is required for prior art defenses, there are no formalistic restrictions on its form; the "rule of reason" applies, and witness interest is merely one factor in assessing the adequacy of corroborating evidence. Credibility determinations, including assessments of bias, are jury functions. The newly-discovered evidence did not eliminate all genuine issues of material fact regarding patent invalidation.

The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York denied in part and granted in part a motion to dismiss appeals by the New York City Department of Finance and New York State Department of Taxation and Finance from a bankruptcy confirmation order. The appeals concerned whether certain transfers in 1515 Broadway Associates' Chapter 11 reorganization plan were subject to real property transfer tax and gains tax. The court held that the appeal regarding the reorganization of the general partner into a limited partnership was moot because the plan had been substantially consummated and effective relief could not be fashioned without disrupting the reorganization. However, the appeals regarding potential future foreclosure of the property and state tax issues were not moot because those transactions had not yet occurred and effective relief remained possible.

Machine translation has historically focused on "decoding" language rather than understanding it, as illustrated by Warren Weaver's 1947 letter comparing Russian to coded English. While tools like Google Translate have practical utility, the author questions whether high-quality translation is possible without genuine comprehension of meaning and language.

Software engineering ensures efficient software development and maintenance through systematic approaches, with requirements classified as functional (defining system services) and non-functional (defining system qualities and constraints). The paper reviews existing research on Domain Non-Functional Requirements generation, prioritization mechanisms, project size computation, interplay among NFRs, and knowledge reutilization. The proposed methodology identifies potential NFRs by clustering keywords extracted from functional requirements using semantic similarity measures to generate semantically coherent groups, then applies a decision tree classifier combined with an NFR matrix for classification. Tested on the IVR dataset for null and non-null function classification, this approach demonstrates higher accuracy and reduced execution time compared to existing methods using only the NFR matrix.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture introduces a Hybrid Rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Key innovations include dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing approximately 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. Turing also features Tensor Cores supporting NVIDIA NGX (Neural Graphics Acceleration), providing AI-based features including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for image reconstruction, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

The architecture introduces several advanced shading technologies: Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders eliminates CPU draw call bottlenecks for complex scenes; Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows dynamic shading rate adjustments per 16×16 pixel region for Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering; and Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space to enable temporal stability and reuse across stereo views. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands upon Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four views per pass for efficient VR and shadow rendering.

Turing is available in three GPU variants: TU102 (high-end), TU104 (RTX 2080/Tesla T4/Quadro RTX 5000 with 3072 CUDA cores, 48 RT Cores, and 368 Tensor Cores), and TU106 (RTX 2070 with 2304 CUDA cores, 36 RT Cores, and 288 Tensor Cores, lacking NVLink/SLI). The architecture introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-based performance metric weighting Tensor, CUDA, RT, and INT32 operations. Turing supports VR via USB-C/VirtualLink, hardware-accelerated ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and is compatible with Microsoft DXR, Vulkan RT, and NVIDIA RTX APIs.

Rana Tariq Khan announced water pump and furniture for a Lodhran government school, citing his late brother's vision. He urged civil society support. An official said Punjab provides free education, stipends and infrastructure.

Smoky River FCSS seeks parents with babies aged 2-4 months in October to participate in the Roots of Empathy Program for the 2017-2018 school year. The Canadian program, created by Mary Gordon in 1996, uses classroom visits by a baby to teach children empathy through guided observations. Schools report increased positive social behavior and decreased aggression. Interested families can contact Crystal at 780-837-2220 or youthsrfcss@live.com.

Sex-specific Mendelian randomization (MR) is limited by small sample sizes, particularly for females in the Million Veteran Program (MVP), causing weak instrumental variable (IV) bias. To address this, researchers developed a semi-empirical Bayesian framework with an Adaptive Posterior Mean (APM) estimator that borrows information across sex groups to calibrate variant-phenotype effect sizes. They performed sex-specific genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of five sleep phenotypes in MVP and conducted two-sample MR with six cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes from the All of Us (AoU) study. Simulations demonstrated that APM improves causal effect estimation efficiency and reduces mean squared error versus raw estimates. Using this approach, they identified sex-specific causal associations: insomnia increased chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk in females; long sleep increased hypertension risk in females; short sleep increased coronary artery disease risk in males; and obstructive sleep apnea showed significantly different causal effects on CKD between sexes. The method improves IV selection and causal inference in sex-stratified analyses.

He proposes a four-part plan: addressing urgent priorities, investing in the future, attacking the deficit, and maintaining no new taxes.
