This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP secure virtualization technologies. The GHCB is a 4KB shared memory area enabling encrypted guests to communicate with hypervisors during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), where guest register state is protected. The protocol defines version negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement via bitmap, and MSR-based communication for pre-GHCB setup. Key features include: page state change operations, SNP guest requests for firmware communication, AP creation for secure multiprocessor booting, restricted injection with doorbell pages for hypervisor notifications, and trusted I/O support. The document details NAE event handling, SMP booting challenges and solutions, NMI processing, and debug register virtualization. SEV-SNP introduces additional capabilities including VMPL levels, multi-certificate retrieval, and secure AVIC for guest-owned APIC state management.

The NFL enters its final three weeks with pivotal matchups ahead. Week 15 predictions include: Colts over Broncos 20-17, Lions over Bears 24-13, Chargers over Chiefs 21-20, Cardinals over Redskins 24-17, Jaguars over Texans 38-7, Ravens over Browns 20-10, Vikings over Bengals 34-10, Seahawks over Rams 24-23, Raiders over Cowboys 24-23, Falcons over Buccaneers 27-17, 49ers over Titans, Steelers over Patriots 24-23, Panthers over Packers 31-27 (if Rodgers plays), Saints over Jets 31-7, Eagles over Giants 24-10, and Bills over Dolphins 24-17. Several games lack betting lines due to uncertain quarterback situations involving Aaron Rodgers, Carson Wentz, Tyrod Taylor, and Bryce Petty.

LGBT activists attempted to mock Vice President Mike Pence during Savannah's St. Patrick's Day parade by displaying pride flags in his photos and through a satirical book making his family's pet rabbit gay. Conservative commentator Chad Felix Greene countered that Pence appeared unbothered and friendly throughout, arguing activists were misinformed about his positions and wasting effort on ineffective protests. One activist declined to debate Greene's cited article, citing disinterest despite claiming to read diverse sources.

Zeenews.india.com uses cookies and tracking technologies to store information on users' devices, identify users and their interests, remember preferences, track site usage, control content access, protect sites, and process requests. The site employs first-party cookies (placed by zeenews.india.com) and third-party cookies (from embedded content or social networks). Cookie types include persistent cookies (for improving experience), session cookies (temporary, deleted when browser closes), essential cookies (necessary for site functionality), analytical/performance cookies (for usage analysis), functionality cookies (remembering user choices), and advertising cookies (for targeted ads). Users can refuse or withdraw cookie consent through browser settings, though this may limit site access. Data is kept only as long as necessary unless explicit consent for removal is given. For questions, contact response@zeemedia.esselgroup.com.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended May 1, 2016 with the SEC. The company reported revenue of $1.305 billion, up 13% from $1.151 billion in the prior year quarter, with net income of $196 million ($0.33 per diluted share) compared to $134 million ($0.24 per diluted share) previously. Gross margin improved to 57.5% from 56.7%.

The GPU business generated $1.079 billion in revenue (up 15%), driven by strong growth in GeForce gaming GPUs and datacenter products for deep learning. The Tegra Processor business contributed $160 million (up 10%), primarily from automotive applications. Gaming platform revenue reached $687 million (up 17%), while datacenter revenue grew 63% to $143 million and automotive revenue increased 47% to $113 million.

Operating expenses totaled $506 million, up 6% year-over-year. The company returned $562 million to shareholders through a $500 million accelerated share repurchase agreement and $62 million in dividends. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities stood at $4.75 billion as of May 1, 2016. NVIDIA intends to return approximately $1.00 billion to shareholders in fiscal year 2017.

The company has $1.50 billion in 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018, which became convertible during the quarter. As of May 1, 2016, 534 million shares of common stock were outstanding.

This MIT lecture covers reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains, focusing on case studies of ReCellular and Whirlpool. The professor leads a class discussion analyzing ReCellular's business model of collecting, refurbishing, and reselling used cellphones. Students debate whether the company has a future, with arguments centering on shrinking margins due to rapid technology evolution, changing consumer behavior (from free phones to paid devices), and market saturation. Some students believe ReCellular can adapt by evolving with technology and serving price-sensitive laggard customers, while others argue single-product companies rarely survive disruptive technologies.

The discussion then shifts to Whirlpool's options for handling appliance recycling under extended producer responsibility regulations in Canada: joining an industry-funded organization (IFO), creating their own closed-loop system, or opposing regulation. Students calculate costs, estimating IFO expenses at $24-35 million annually (roughly $47-80 per unit) versus forward distribution costs of about $70 per unit. The professor explains network design challenges, noting that reverse logistics typically costs more due to unoptimized collection systems. Whirlpool ultimately chose a closed-loop approach despite higher costs, seeking customer connection and potential competitive advantage through their 48% market share, though the initial trial proved more expensive than anticipated. The lecture concludes with brief student project presentations on companies including Zara, Dell, Hewlett-Packard, BMW, and Philip Morris International, examining their environmental practices and carbon footprint strategies.

SDXC cards initialized with XPC=0 operate at up to 0.36W in Default Speed or SDR12 with Class 0 indicated if Speed Class is unsupported. Cards initialized with XPC=1 operate at up to 0.54W and support Speed Class. Re-initialization is required to change XPC selection. UHS-I hosts set S18R=1 in ACMD41 to request 1.8V signaling; UHS-I cards respond with S18A=1 if in 3.3V mode, allowing voltage switch. After switching, cards indicate S18A=0. UHS-II cards always indicate S18A=0. Fast Boot (Bit 29) is reserved for eSD.

A coach discusses several players' performances and team strategy during the playoffs. He praises Matt's mental makeup and ability to bounce back from setbacks, noting his strong body of work in the playoffs. He addresses Geno, an elite talented player, encouraging him to balance making plays with situational awareness and simple plays when opportunities aren't present. The coach notes that playoff hockey involves less penalty calling and emphasizes the importance of clean power play entries and established zone time. He commends the defensemen, particularly Brian Dumoulin, for stepping up in expanded roles, blocking shots, and contributing in all situations.

Individual soccer defending requires defenders to control opposing ball carriers through positioning and technique. Defenders must first get goal-side and assess teammates' positions before choosing between aggressive defending (cutting off passes, tackling, interposing) or attack stalling (delaying to allow defensive setup). Key defensive tactics include maintaining goal-side position, keeping proper stance and balance, not overreacting to fakes, denying passes/shots, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler's vision, jockeying, shepherding, and stealing the ball. Defenders must eventually stop retreating and either stand ground or tackle based on position relative to goal. Critical oral communication from teammates indicates whether to delay ("Contain," "Delay," "Jockey," "Stand him up") or tackle ("Challenge," "Tackle," "Take him"). If beaten, defenders must turn and chase immediately. Coaching requires progressive instruction on approach, stance, positioning, techniques, and communication terms.

Michigan State Police closed all lanes of I-696 in both directions on Tuesday morning after receiving a call around 1 a.m. about a man threatening suicide on a bridge. Officers organized 13 semi truck drivers to park under the bridge to shorten the potential fall distance. After several hours of negotiation involving multiple law enforcement agencies, the man walked off the bridge peacefully and was taken to Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak for evaluation. The incident was documented in a photo shared on Twitter by MSP Metro Detroit.

This patent application describes methods for controlling uplink data transmission in wireless communication systems when a device is in an enhanced coverage state to reduce power consumption. Enhanced coverage functionality extends cell coverage through repeated data transmissions but increases battery consumption, which is problematic for devices that cannot be frequently recharged.

Two main solutions are presented: Solution 1 involves an application querying a modem for radio coverage information and deciding whether to refrain from sending uplink data based on conditions such as coverage enhancement level, signal strength, data type, QoS, device movement, battery level, or power supply status. Solution 2 involves the application instructing the modem to conditionally transmit data based on similar parameters.

The application can receive coverage information through AT commands or other APIs, including coverage enhancement levels, modes, classes, repetition indicators, signal strength, or quality. Transmission restrictions can be applied based on various combinations of conditions, and the network can configure these parameters through downlink messages such as Attach Accept or RRC Connection Reconfiguration messages.

The described approaches are applicable to LTE, NB-IoT, EC-GSM-IoT, and other wireless technologies, with implementation details including new AT commands and information elements for configuration.

This study investigates whether depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) synergistically enhance their association with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) when coexisting, and whether this relationship relates to inflammatory status measured by C-reactive protein (CRP). Using 2007-2010 NHANES data from 4,136 adults (305 with RA), researchers found that RA prevalence increased when depression coexisted with obesity or HTG, with maximum effect at medium CRP levels (1-3 mg/L). Depression with obesity showed synergistic association across all CRP levels, while depression with HTG showed effect only at medium CRP. The study suggests these interactions could inform RA prediction models but notes limitations including cross-sectional design and self-reported RA diagnosis.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 26, 2020, announcing a strategic change in its retail operations, including closing Microsoft Store physical locations. The company furnished a press release as Exhibit 99.1, which is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

The speaker argues that age is irrelevant in modern hockey, emphasizing knowledge and team play over skill and speed. They express pride in joining a successful team, reference winning a Stanley Cup with Brett Hull despite past doubts, and prioritize team victory over personal achievements. They mention being physically able to play despite minor injuries, explain their late signing with Detroit due to Dallas's delays and budget issues, and describe feeling fortunate to join the team after facing uncertainty about where to play.

A hockey player discusses a leg injury sustained when another player fell on it, expressing hope to play in the upcoming Stanley Cup Finals game after receiving treatment. He notes teammates are resting, emphasizes controlling energy and avoiding overconfidence, and acknowledges Tampa Bay as a strong opponent. He mentions the excitement of playing in Calgary, where fans celebrate enthusiastically, and describes himself as a small part of the team while expressing pride in being a Flame.

British households added an average of £560 to their debt in Q1 2017, with single parents experiencing the highest increases at £930-£940. A survey by True Potential found 15% of people take on debt for necessities, rising to 20% among single parents. Other debt causes include career changes and parental leave. Couples without dependents had the lowest increase at £350. Average total debt stands at £1,797, with men owing more than women and 45-54 year-olds carrying the highest debt at £2,299. The North East has the highest regional debt at £2,664. True Potential's David Harrison called for greater financial education, noting personal debt is "the elephant in the room" as consumer confidence may be built on unsustainable borrowing.

Information Systems (IS) research has shifted from positivist, technologically deterministic approaches to focus on human and social factors. This paper examines two parallel developments: complexity science and User Experience (UX) approaches. Complexity theory, originating from evolutionary biology and chemistry, emphasizes self-organization, non-linearity, and irreversibility in far-from-equilibrium systems. Unlike complicated systems (like computers), complex systems (like information systems incorporating human usage) cannot be fully understood by analyzing individual components. UX has superseded traditional usability practice by addressing subjective concerns of personal experience rather than merely operational metrics. The author critiques existing IS complexity research for maintaining representational views that separate human and technological subsystems, arguing instead for recognizing IS as complex adaptive systems where humans are integral parts. A Knowledge Transfer Partnership with a UK UX company aims to explore how irreversibility and temporal dynamics impact design and success in practical settings.

This paper introduces OntoAligner, a framework that integrates Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs) into ontology alignment (OA). While modern OA techniques predominantly use large language models, KGEs remain underexplored despite their ability to encode semantic and structural information as low-dimensional vectors. The authors formulate OA as a link prediction task over merged source and target ontologies, implementing a three-stage pipeline (Parser, Encoder, Aligner) that unifies ontology triples, trains KGE models via PyKEEN, and computes alignments through cosine similarity. The framework integrates 17 KGE models—including TransE, DistMult, ComplEx, RotatE, and ConvE—selected for their diversity in modeling approaches and proven performance in knowledge graph tasks. This systematic integration into OntoAligner aims to advance OA through semantically grounded, computationally scalable KGE methodologies.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Conducted between May 2020 and January 2021, it randomized 489 patients (2:1) to standard of care plus convalescent plasma (n=326) or standard of care alone (n=163). The primary endpoint—percentage alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%, p=0.976). Patients received 800-1000 mL of convalescent plasma with high neutralizing antibody titers (≥1/160), with first dose administered within 12 hours of randomization. The study followed WHO master protocol guidelines and was approved by Independent Ethics Committees at each center. Six patients withdrew before intervention and were substituted. Analysis sets included Full Analysis Set (FAS) and Per Protocol Set (PPS), with 91.9% of plasma group patients receiving all 4 units.

The Match-up zone defense combines person-to-person and zone principles using specific defensive rules. Offensive alignments never split defenders, overloads are easier to defend, and opponents tend to get confused. Success depends on smart, knowledgeable players and communication. The defense is passive, reacting to offensive movement, but can include aggressive traps. It can dictate offensive alignment by showing different zones initially, then applying match-up rules.

Basic rules assign X1 as point guard, X2 as shooting guard, X3 as small forward, X4 as power forward, and X5 as post player, though assignments may adjust based on personnel. X1 takes the point with or without the ball; in a two-guard front, X1 takes the right-side player. X2 takes the first player left of X1, X3 takes the first player right of X1, X4 takes the second player left or right of X1 as baseline defender, and X5 takes the center or baseline player right of X1 if no post exists.

Application varies by offensive alignment: 2-3 (X1 right guard, X2 left guard, X3 right wing, X4 left wing, X5 post); 1-3-1 (X1 point, X2 left, X3 right, X4 second right, X5 post); 1-2-2 (X1 point, X2 left, X3 right, X4 second left, X5 right baseline); 1-4 (X1 point, X2 left, X3 right, X4 left post, X5 right post).

Defending cutters involves switching with weakside defenders or interchanging roles. Specific switching and interchange patterns are detailed for 1-3-1, 1-2-2, 2-3, and 1-4 alignments, including point cuts, wing cuts, post flashes, and high post rolls. Trapping can extend to full and half court when the ball enters primary trap zones like corners.

This passage introduces distributed systems design patterns, focusing first on single-node patterns using containers. It explains that containers establish resource boundaries, team ownership, and separation of concerns, motivating the division of single-machine applications into multiple containers. The sidecar pattern augments application containers with additional functionality like HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, and monitoring tools. The ambassador pattern brokers external communications, handling sharded service routing, service discovery, and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern standardizes interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks across heterogeneous applications. The passage then transitions to multi-node patterns, describing microservices architectures and replicated load-balanced services for stateless applications, including caching layers, SSL termination, and session tracking. Finally, it covers sharded services for stateful applications, explaining sharding functions, consistent hashing, and replicated sharded caches to improve reliability and performance.

Netflix stock fell after Elon Musk urged followers to cancel service. The US government shutdown continued following a failed GOP funding bill in the Senate. The S&P 500 closed above 6,700 on limited shutdown impact bets. Economic data showed weakness: ADP reported the biggest private payroll drop in 2.5 years with only 73K jobs gained in July, while May and June were revised down by 258K. The 12-month average hit pandemic lows, with gains concentrated in health care. Despite this, Q2 earnings have been strong: 15 of 17 mega-cap companies beat expectations, pushing S&P 500 earnings growth to 11.2% and sales growth to 5.6%. The S&P 500 hit its 9.1% average annual return mark, historically signaling seasonal volatility ahead as August-October typically shows weaker returns. The US dollar rallied to 2024 lows but was rejected following tariff announcements and weak data. The article notes AI has driven market gains this year, but warns of potential limits given high valuations and negative equity risk premium.

DomeShelter Australia's Container Mounted DomeShelter™ (CMDS) is a weather-resistant, relocatable industrial shelter designed to withstand Australian Wind Regions A to D. The steel-frame structure attaches to existing containers via welding, bolting, or Twistlock, and suits multiple industries: oil and gas, agriculture, events, and tourism. It provides rain and UV protection for goods, heat resistance for livestock, and translucent natural lighting for venues. The family-owned company manufactures in Australia and serves global markets.

This patent application describes systems and methods for providing customizable user interfaces to confirm whether users should review or take actions associated with untrusted emails, particularly phishing emails. Unlike anti-ransomware technologies that automatically remove threats without user input, this solution gives users autonomy by pausing suspicious actions and prompting users to confirm their decisions. Company administrators can dynamically customize notification content, structure, and appearance through an administrator console without requiring security awareness system administrator involvement. The system uses a driver to monitor application processes, injects a monitor library to detect untrusted domain access attempts, and pauses execution while querying a server to determine URL trustworthiness. Client and server setting hashes enable efficient synchronization of configuration updates. The system supports both standalone email clients and browser-based email through injected code or browser extensions, with a Browser Intermediary Application facilitating OS communication for extension-based implementations. User responses are recorded for training analysis and security improvement.

The passage describes a fluid flow measuring and control device for plumbing installations that addresses limitations of prior consumer-grade flow measurement devices. The device features a main flow channeling system with inlet and outlet connections, a parallel bypass channeling system containing a flowmeter with dual movement sensors to detect net flow including backflow, a solenoid valve for flow control, and upstream/downstream pressure sensors. A transceiver sends flowmeter data to a computer that stores pre-recorded fluid usage signatures for appliance identification, detects abnormal usage patterns, and controls the valve to shut off flow when leaks or breaks are detected. The bypass design isolates measurement components from the main flow path to avoid pressure reduction and debris accumulation. The system uses pattern recognition algorithms to identify specific appliances from their unique flow signatures, enabling per-appliance consumption tracking, leak detection through pressure differential analysis during valve closure, and notifications to user mobile devices.

Schools that excel in teaching math typically also excel in reading, and vice versa, according to an analysis of districts nationwide and Mississippi schools. The author compared schools to hotels rather than restaurants, arguing that elementary schools should provide consistently strong outcomes across all subjects rather than specializing. Analysis of 140 high-performing districts found most produced outstanding results across both subjects, while only 14 districts showed significant specialization—and 12 of those were strong in math but weak in reading. Mississippi 2025 test data showed a 0.87 correlation between school-level reading and math scores. Growth rate analysis confirmed this pattern: among the 50 schools with greatest reading gains, none were below average in math growth, and among the 50 lowest reading gain schools, only two reached average math growth. Florida data showed similar correlations. The author notes that while proficiency rates correlate with socioeconomic status, growth measures better isolate school impact, and strong performance across subjects remains the norm.

Crystal morphology significantly affects the sensitivity, performance, and safety of energetic materials like PETN, RDX, and β-HMX. Current prediction methods—BFDH, SE, and AE models—all deviate from experimental morphologies and fail to capture growth kinetics or edge/corner effects in small crystals. This work introduces a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation technique using intermolecular interaction parameters, implemented in the open-source Python package cgkmc, and applies it to PETN growth with results matching AE predictions and experiments. The model uses a colored graph with occupation numbers and interaction energies, calculates surface sites via coordination numbers, and employs harmonic transition state theory for evaporation rates with dynamically updated rate prefactors to maintain equilibrium at specified crystal sizes.

Soccer teams need a well-practiced corner kick defense plan implemented immediately when a corner is awarded. At professional levels, corner kick conversion rates can be as low as 2%, but this requires years of tactical development. Key defensive principles include: preventing corners when possible, assigning specific jobs by position, goalkeeper authority, quick reaction to positions, aggressive ball-winning, high/wide clearances, outlet positioning, fast-break transition, and basic defensive techniques.

Three main defensive strategies exist. Zone defense assigns players to cover specific areas; advantages include easy teaching and forward movement toward the ball, while disadvantages include zone flooding and hesitation. A basic zone setup places players at posts, on the six-yard line, in the penalty area, and one player 11 yards from the kicker.

Man-to-man marking assigns one defender per attacker; advantages include simplicity and preventing zone flooding, while disadvantages include backward running, scrambling to cover, and lost focus. Setup matches defenders to attackers from goal outward based on proximity.

Mixed/combination defense, shown by studies to be most effective, uses zone coverage for post players and six-yard line defenders while remaining defenders mark man-to-man. This includes an outlet player for fast breaks.

Coaching tips emphasize scouting opponents, modifying plans game-to-game, quick defensive movement upfield, goalkeeper positioning one step ahead of the goal line at a 45-degree angle, and the kicker-marking player acting as a "one-man wall" positioned 10 yards from the corner circle.

The Mid Screen Offense is widely used in professional basketball because its central positioning removes helpside defensive support. The basic action involves a point guard driving off a high post screen, with options including drives to the basket, pull-up jumpers, drop passes to the post, or kick-outs to wing shooters. Success requires coordinated reads and counters between the ballhandler and screener to respond to various defensive tactics such as fighting over screens, sagging, switching, trapping, or going under. Phase 2 involves ball reversal into continuities like motion, single/double, flex, inside triangle, or side screen offenses. Common variations include post pop, horns (double mid screens), 1-4 low alignment, post isolation, and two game. Proper execution demands defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience, best developed through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, recognizing defensive adjustments, and varying alignments to attack weak defenders.

NVIDIA's combined L1 data cache and shared memory architecture, introduced in Volta V100, improves performance and simplifies programming by merging both memory types into a single block. The A100 GPU increases this combined capacity to 192 KB/SM from V100's 128 KB/SM. This integration provides low latency, high bandwidth, and efficient handling of both streaming and frequently reused data.

A hockey player describes scoring a goal against Dallas after waiting for teammates to clear the zone, then discusses two-on-one plays in the second period including a powerplay situation. He emphasizes not dragging out the series, learning from Philadelphia's letdown when ahead, and taking advantage of Dallas being down. He mentions signing with the Devils to reach this point, having finals experience in Finland, and getting more comfortable against Dallas as the series progresses. He notes Dallas's speed, cycling, and media attention differences. He discusses line matching, defensive responsibilities, avoiding too many men penalties, and a veteran teammate's playoff performance.

Casey Mittelstadt's college season has ended, raising questions about his availability for the Rochester Amerks. He could sign an AHL contract or amateur tryout to play in the regular season and playoffs, though this may not be his best business decision. Seeking an NHL entry-level deal would burn the first year of his contract with just one game played for the Sabres, who have 11 games remaining. If signed to an NHL deal now, he could not be sent to Rochester. Buffalo's ideal scenario is an amateur tryout this season and an entry-level deal starting 2018-19, allowing him professional experience before next season. The 19-year-old must decide between staying in school or going pro, which would end his NCAA eligibility.

This document provides design requirements and component selection guidelines for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN power semiconductor devices and TPS7H5001-SP controllers. The converter operates at 500 kHz with a 5V output, using a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider resistors, 25 ns dead time with 20.5 kΩ resistors, 50 ns leading edge blank time with 49.9 kΩ RLEB, and 33 nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5 ms). The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance. Primary-side GaN FETs are rated at 170V, while synchronous rectifier FETs use 80V-rated devices with parallel Schottky diodes. The design includes RCD clamp, 0.47 μH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance for SET mitigation, 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, and Type 2A frequency compensation with 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noise coupling, separating analog and power grounds, and proper placement of bypass capacitors and sensitive traces.

BMW released a video explaining the Society of Automotive Engineers' five levels of self-driving capability. Level 1 offers basic cruise control; Level 2 adds automated steering, both requiring full driver attention. Level 3, expected in BMW's 2021 iNext, allows brief driver distraction but requires takeover within seconds. Many companies skip Level 3 for Level 4, which allows minutes to regain control and enables the car to stop safely if the driver doesn't respond. BMW anticipates Level 4 regulations and infrastructure by mid-next decade, though Waymo already operates limited Level 4 vehicles and plans a commercial taxi service in Phoenix. Level 5, fully driverless operation, likely won't arrive until decade's end.

This patent application describes systems and methods for detecting abnormal cardiac activity, particularly atrial fibrillation, using deep learning architectures with cardiac data (ECG/PPG) and motion data from wearable devices. The technology addresses limitations of existing ECG monitoring methods, which can be cumbersome, costly, and inefficient for detecting asymptomatic cases. The disclosed method involves receiving cardiac and motion data divided into windows, determining signal quality indices, extracting cardiovascular features, applying tensor transforms (such as wavelet transforms), and classifying activity using a deep learning architecture comprising a convolutional neural network, bidirectional recurrent neural network, and attention network. The system can incorporate subject contextual information (medical history, demographics) and generates reports classifying cardiac activity as normal or abnormal. Data is collected from wearable devices like smart watches containing cardiac sensors (PPG, ECG) and motion sensors (accelerometers). The attention network weights windows to identify specific periods of abnormal activity and calculate burden metrics.

This study examined the risk of incident hypertension within one year postpartum among 2,514 women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) at two southeastern U.S. academic health systems (2014-2017). Higher systolic blood pressure at 15-90 days postpartum (HR 1.70 for 140 vs. 120 mmHg), severe preeclampsia/eclampsia versus gestational hypertension (HR 1.49), and older maternal age (HR 1.46 for 35 vs. 25 years) were significantly associated with increased hypertension risk. Conversely, longer time to postpartum BP check was associated with lower hazard (HR 0.52 for 90 vs. 42 days). Only 32% of women had normal-range BP at the comprehensive visit, while 55% had Stage 1 or 2 hypertension-range readings. Notably, 40% of eligible women lacked any documented 15-90 day postpartum BP measurement despite guideline recommendations. The 12-month cumulative incidence of hypertension ranged from 4.7% for optimal BP (110/65 mmHg) to 13.0% for Stage 2-range BP (140/90 mmHg).

JPMorgan Chase is deploying AI across its global operations, investing roughly $18 billion in technology this year. The bank has rolled out its proprietary generative AI platform to all 200,000 employees, with over 175 active use cases spanning retail banking, wealth management, and institutional services. AI tools are automating customer support, generating research insights, and supporting credit assessments and fraud detection. The bank faces challenges in balancing innovation with compliance, transparency, and legacy system integration. Success could set a global standard for AI adoption in finance, though durability under market stress and tighter regulation remains untested.

iOS 11 drains iPhone batteries more than twice as fast as iOS 10, according to Wandera's analysis of 50,000 devices. Phones on iOS 10 last 240 minutes versus 96 minutes on iOS 11. While some users downgraded to iOS 10.3.3, Wandera advises against this due to security risks. Older iPhone models experience worse drain than newer ones. Apple's iOS 11.0.1 update improved battery life to 159 minutes. Users can extend battery life by limiting background app refresh, location services, or using low power mode.

Enron faced severe financial turmoil on October 29, 2001, with its stock plummeting to seven-year lows after Moody's downgraded its senior unsecured debt rating to Baa2, two notches above junk status. The company, which lost over 50% of its value in two weeks and shed $14 billion in market capitalization, announced it was negotiating with banks for $1-2 billion in additional credit after drawing $3.3 billion the previous week. Analysts viewed this as an act of desperation, predicting lenders would demand harsher terms and collateral. The crisis stemmed from SEC investigations into off-balance-sheet transactions with partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, which led to $1.2 billion in equity write-downs. European energy firms began freezing trades with Enron, while multiple shareholder lawsuits targeted company executives over alleged conflicts of interest. Moody's warned of further possible downgrades, and Standard & Poor's revised its outlook to negative.

The document lists silicon errata for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Revision A3. Issues 106-116 cover: AuxOutputFull bit incorrectly cleared on Port 60h reads affecting PS/2 emulation; tACK bits not affecting UDMA timing (fixed at 30 ns, no violation); ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRD addresses; LPC controller aborts transactions with certain SYNC patterns requiring PLD workaround; SMB NEGACK status bit clearing inconsistently requiring double-write workaround; GLPCI retry counter counting all PCI bus retries; GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers clearing non-selected bits after suspend requiring Read-Modify-Write; SMBus data hold time below 300 ns specification; LOWBAT_FLAG missing after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y failing to deassert when delay exceeds PM_SED requiring counter programming adjustment. The document includes standard AMD legal disclaimers and trademark notices.

Connaught Public School in Hintonburg attempted to break the world record for most students playing tunnel ball simultaneously on Wednesday, with over 250 students participating compared to the previous record of 120 set by an Australian school. The event, organized by fundraising coordinator Karen Monaghan for the school's yard renewal project, lasted nearly thirty minutes and involved the entire student body. The record remains pending verification by Guinness. The event also raised $10,000 through student pledges and business donations for planned yard improvements including a new kindergarten playground, basketball court, funnel ball net, soccer field grass, and additional trees.

A survey by ValueInsured found 71% of Washington homeowners worry about a housing bubble, though the sample size was small. Seattle's housing market is among the nation's hottest, with King County median prices rising 18.6% year-over-year to $658,000. However, experts like OB Jacobi of Windermere Real Estate say current conditions differ from 2008, citing high buyer credit scores, larger down payments, and high homeowner equity. NWMLS director George Moorhead predicts a market correction involving price and inventory stabilization rather than collapse. The article also lists income needed to buy homes in 25 U.S. cities, with San Francisco requiring $226,577 annually and Detroit $7,359.

Several billionaire CEOs reject the concept of work-life balance, viewing it as incompatible with achieving extraordinary success. Jeff Bezos prefers "work-life harmony," arguing work and personal life complement rather than trade off. Reid Hoffman considers seeking balance a sign of insufficient commitment to winning. Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman finds the idea of achieving greatness with 40-hour weeks "mind-boggling," while Scale AI cofounder Lucy Guo, who works 90-hour weeks, suggests those wanting balance are in the wrong job. Zoom's Eric Yuan acknowledges true balance is difficult, though he prioritizes family when conflicts arise. Alibaba's Jack Ma endorsed China's demanding "996" schedule as a "blessing."

American consumer confidence rebounded in April to 128.7, up from 127.0 in March, approaching the 18-year high of 130.0 reached in February. The Conference Board index measures current conditions and six-month outlook. Economists attribute the strength to a strong labor market with 17-year low unemployment, tax cuts affecting paychecks, reduced stock market volatility, and diminished trade war concerns. However, some analysts caution that sluggish real income growth may limit actual consumer spending despite high confidence levels.

NEC Corp established the "NEC Satellite Operation Center," becoming operational in April, to operate the ASNARO-2 radar satellite launched in January. The center uses NEC's GroundNEXTAR system and a high-security data center, with capability for simultaneous multi-satellite operations. GroundNEXTAR provides operational functions, 3D animation visualizations, and image distribution. NEC will market ASNARO-2 images with JEOSS starting September. The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and compatible with GaN power semiconductors. The devices use fixed frequency, peak current mode control and can be applied to buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

The controllers feature Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation using a transconductance error amplifier, with Type 2A including an additional high-frequency noise attenuation capacitor. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C and reinitiates at 160°C. Operating input voltage ranges from 4 V to 14 V.

A design example demonstrates a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter with 5 V output using GaN FETs. Key component selections include: 205 kΩ timing resistor, feedback resistors of 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ, 25 ns dead time with 20.5 kΩ resistors, 49.9 kΩ leading edge blank resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5:1 transformer turns ratio with 40 μH primary inductance, 170 V primary-side and 80 V secondary-side GaN FETs, 0.47 μH output inductor, and 2.3 mF output capacitance for radiation-induced transient mitigation. Frequency compensation components selected were 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF, with 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor.

Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt/dv loops, routing feedback traces away from noise sources, and placing bypass capacitors close to pins.

Software must ensure the halt command is last in the queue for precise halting, and use only one command at a time for precise error halting. Interrupt status bits are cleared by writing PM_RBCtl[CLEAR_INTS] to 1 when the ring buffer is empty or paused. In systems with SMEE or SME-MK, encryption information is encoded into SPAs passed to page migration firmware, with the C-bit indicating encrypted memory. Command status is returned in ring buffer entries and migration lists, with status and sub-status fields for error isolation. RMP_ENFORCE remains true if SNP was ever initialized. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO moves hypervisor-owned pages in SNP-enabled or non-SNP systems, updating IOMMU PTEs and requiring 2M pages to be smashed to 4K. Astronomers have discovered the most distant and energetic "odd radio circle" (ORC) ever detected—a massive double-ringed radio structure nearly 10 billion years old. Found by citizen scientists using the LOFAR radio telescope, the source RAD J131346.9+500320 challenges theories that ORCs are caused by black hole mergers, instead suggesting galactic superwinds as the cause. The discovery, published October 2 in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, marks the first ORC found through citizen science and with LOFAR. The RAD@home Astronomy Collaboratory also identified two other unusual cosmic giants with bent radio jets and rings, all located in massive galaxy clusters. Researchers believe interactions between relativistic plasma jets and hot thermal plasma may shape these rare structures.

This paper presents a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller (BHC) for budget pacing in real-time digital advertising auctions. The authors address limitations of existing proportional/integral feedback controllers that suffer from oscillations and require delicate tuning. Their approach discretizes error space into multiple bands with variable multiplicative steps, combining hysteresis control with proportional feedback. The BHC uses large steps for large errors to accelerate convergence and small steps for minor errors to preserve stability. The controller calculates normalized error between desired and observed spending rates, maps error magnitude into non-overlapping bands with associated gains, and updates the pacing multiplier accordingly. The authors validate their approach through real-world experiments, demonstrating significant improvements over legacy feedback-based pacing systems, particularly for small-budget campaigns.

The Horns Offense uses high post mid-screen action that can create easy layups if the on-ball defender gets caught on screens. NBA teams typically avoid switching since this creates post-up mismatches. Two main defensive approaches exist: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption.

Show & Recover involves three phases: the defender pushes the ballhandler to the sideline while the screener's defender shows and bumps; the on-ball defender recovers by going over the top; and final matchup positioning with help defenders dropping to cover the roll.

SOS Disruption initiates action before the first screen by trapping the point guard, forcing the offense into unplanned freelance play. This also uses three phases: initial double team on the first pass; rotations when the ball exits the trap following near-player principles; and final alignment with standard SOS defensive positioning, including potential "base go red" or "post trap" rotations on subsequent actions.

The Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator is a mean-reversion trading tool that measures the relative position of a closing price within a bar's high-low range using the formula (Close-Low)/(High-Low). However, IBS does not work effectively on commodities, gold, metal stocks, or indices in commodity-dependent economies like Norway and Australia. The strategy requires precise execution near market close, as delaying entry to the next open significantly reduces returns. While IBS can be enhanced with filters such as VIX levels or distance from the 200-day moving average, there is risk of curve fitting. The indicator's continued effectiveness may be challenged by widespread algorithmic use, though it showed strong performance in 2019-2020 after a weak 2017-2018 period.

This MIT lecture covers adaptive experimentation and robust design of engineering systems, building on traditional design of experiments. The speaker traces the history from Sir Edward John Russell's advocacy for simple experiments to R.A. Fisher's development of factorial designs at Rothamsted Experimental Station, where Fisher demonstrated that complex experiments could improve efficiency by a factor of 2 compared to single-factor approaches.

The lecture explains how full factorial designs become impractical with many factors, leading to fractional factorial designs that deliberately sacrifice information on certain effects. The speaker discusses robust parameter design—making systems less sensitive to uncontrolled noise factors—and critiques Taguchi's crossed array approach, noting that industry has largely entrenched these methods despite their limitations.

The core research presented shows that adaptive one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimentation often outperforms fractional factorial designs, especially when experimental error is substantial (around 25% of factor effects) or interactions are significant. Empirical studies across 66 systems demonstrated that adaptive OFAT provides comparable or better results with greater flexibility. The method works by sequentially changing one factor at a time, adopting changes that show improvement, and can exploit interactions even without explicitly estimating them.

For robust design specifically, the speaker recommends crossing adaptive procedures with factorial designs in noise factors—running full noise arrays, then changing one control factor at a time and selecting levels based on performance. Validation studies on sheet metal spinning and paper airplane experiments showed this approach outperforms traditional Taguchi methods, particularly with informed starting points. Ensemble methods running multiple OFATs from different starting points provide additional robustness to experimental error.

The lecture concludes with practical considerations: adaptive methods suit sequential experiments where learning is immediate and reusable, while factorial designs remain preferable when archival precision is needed or experiments must run in parallel. The speaker advocates for democratizing robust design—doing simpler experiments on more systems rather than expensive studies on few—since companies rarely know where their biggest quality problems lie with sufficient certainty.

This paper presents a complete phase diagram for the classical bilinear-biquadratic Heisenberg model on a partially anisotropic triangular lattice composed of isosceles triangles, using four interaction parameters (two bilinear: K and L; two biquadratic: A and B). Yael Kalai discusses the Fiat-Shamir paradigm's soundness in the random oracle model. She demonstrates that applying Fiat-Shamir to protocols with non-negligible soundness (like a 1/2-soundness zero-knowledge proof for Hamiltonian cycle) allows cheating: a prover can repeatedly query the random oracle until finding a favorable challenge, then present that as proof. This attack extends to protocols with negligible soundness achieved through sequential repetition, as the prover can build valid transcripts incrementally by backtracking and retrying individual rounds.

The Fiat-Shamir paradigm is sound in the random oracle model only for constant-round protocols with negligible soundness. For c-round protocols, a cheating prover's success probability degrades by a factor of q^c (where q is the number of queries), remaining non-negligible for constant c. The Kilian-Micali protocol satisfies these conditions (4 rounds, negligible error), making Fiat-Shamir sound for it in the random oracle model. However, this doesn't guarantee security with any explicit hash function—contrived hash functions can break even protocols secure in the random oracle model.

Kalai then connects this to parallel repetition of zero-knowledge protocols. Parallel repetition of the Hamiltonian cycle protocol destroys zero-knowledge because the simulation technique that enables cheating in the random oracle model becomes essential for simulation. A 2019 result showed this protocol is actually Fiat-Shamir sound (under standard assumptions), which implies it's not parallel zero-knowledge: if a simulator existed for a Fiat-Shamir-sound protocol, it could generate accepting transcripts for false statements, breaking soundness.

This white paper examines AI's transformative role in higher education, exploring institutional responses, pedagogical impacts, and future opportunities. AI applications include intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics, and adaptive learning technologies that personalize education. While 86% of students globally use AI tools, challenges persist: faculty resistance, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and infrastructure gaps in developing regions. China and the U.S. lead implementation, with Squirrel AI and Arizona State University demonstrating successful case studies. Institutions are responding through faculty training, curricular innovation incorporating AI literacy across disciplines, and policy interventions. AI enhances teaching through personalized learning and automated grading, accelerates research via data analysis tools, and improves administrative efficiency through predictive analytics and chatbots. Future opportunities include emotional recognition systems, VR/AR applications, and language translation for global collaboration. However, risks such as academic dishonesty, automation fears among educators, and ethical concerns require robust policy frameworks. The paper recommends prioritizing faculty training, establishing ethical guidelines, ensuring equitable access, fostering interdisciplinary research, and promoting collaborative human-AI teaching models to maximize benefits while addressing challenges.

The team maintained their game plan despite being down, staying composed and taking shots, which led to scoring goals against Belfour. Players expressed happiness about their situation despite the team being for sale by Dr. McMullen, noting they focus on playing hockey rather than business matters. The speaker also commented on the unpredictability of hockey and the difficulty of facing the same shooter twice.

The North Dakota Supreme Court reversed a district court's suppression of evidence in a DUI case against Denise Hahne, holding that law enforcement is not required as a matter of law to provide motorists with an opportunity to avoid temporary sobriety checkpoints. The district court had suppressed evidence after finding Hahne had no safe or legal way to avoid a checkpoint on a busy, curved 50 m.p.h. road where only a dangerous U-turn was available. The Supreme Court, applying the three-part balancing test from *Brown v. Texas* and *Michigan v. Sitz*, ruled that while checkpoint stops constitute Fourth Amendment seizures, they are constitutional if reasonable. The Court emphasized that under *Sitz*, the "subjective intrusion" analysis concerns fear and surprise to law-abiding motorists, not fear of detection by those violating the law. Avoidability is merely one factor in assessing intrusion on personal liberty, not a legal requirement. The case was remanded to apply the correct legal standard.

New Jersey ranked 25th in the 2018 Commonwealth Fund state healthcare scorecard, down two places from the previous year. The state performed well on access to care (14th), children's coverage (5th), and employee-based insurance payments (3rd), and had low infant mortality (7th) and healthy lives promotion (19th). However, it ranked below all other Northeast states and needs improvement in preventative care, elderly hospital readmissions, and medical costs. The infant mortality data did not account for racial disparities, though black babies in New Jersey die at more than three times the rate of white babies.

The OECD warns that trade tensions and rising oil prices threaten global economic growth, as threatened tariffs have begun affecting business confidence and could negatively impact investment and jobs. The Paris-based organization slightly lowered its 2018 world growth forecast to 3.8 percent, with 3.9 percent expected for 2019.

Alan A. Brister sued the United States for a tax refund after the IRS adjusted his 1985 and 1986 tax returns in 1993, reversing withholding credits and applying his 1989-1992 refunds against resulting liabilities. The government conceded the adjustment was untimely under the three-year limitations period but argued the time limit was waived because Brister filed false and fraudulent returns with intent to evade tax. The court found that Brister, Solar Roofing Inc.'s accountant, knowingly filed false W-2 forms claiming withholding taxes that were never paid by his financially troubled employer. For 1985, Brister filed a return claiming $10,435.50 in withholding after being told Solar Roofing would not cooperate and learning the company lacked funds to pay taxes. For 1986, he claimed $5,231.42 in withholding without employer authorization or confirmation of payment. Brister admitted using the IRS as a collection agency to recover personal loans. The court held the returns were knowingly false and, following *Scallen v. Commissioner*, that Brister's intent to obtain improper refunds constituted intent to evade tax regardless of whether he had sufficient legitimate withholdings to offset his liability. The government's 1993 adjustment was therefore timely, and judgment was entered for the defendant.

The 13/48 trading strategy uses exponential moving average crossovers to identify trading opportunities: a bullish signal when the 13-period EMA crosses above the 48-period EMA, and a bearish signal when it crosses below. The strategy is momentum-based and works best in trending markets, particularly stocks, but risks whipsaws in choppy conditions. Backtesting on the S&P 500 from 1960 to present shows a 5.1% annual return versus 7.2% for buy and hold, with 66% time invested. Despite a slightly better risk-adjusted return of 7.8%, attempts to improve the strategy with filters were unsuccessful. The strategy is a lagging indicator prone to false signals.

This study examines faculty members' and students' opinions on distance education's impact on equality and inequality of opportunity in education. Distance education, defined as audio-visual interaction between physically distant teachers and learners, offers flexibility and reduced costs but faces challenges from digital gaps and infrastructure limitations. The qualitative research involved 21 faculty members and 26 students using semi-structured interviews and content analysis.

Faculty members identified positive impacts including learning at personal pace and easy information access, while negative impacts involved technology access problems, internet connection issues, and unsuitable learning environments. Students similarly noted benefits like time flexibility and free access to sources, but cited financial limitations and internet problems as inequality causes.

Suggestions for improvement included determining learner characteristics, improving technology access and digital literacy, resolving internet infrastructure problems, state budgeting for technology access, and teacher consultancy services. The study concludes that while distance education can reduce educational inequality, persistent digital gaps and infrastructure deficiencies continue to threaten equality of opportunity, particularly for disadvantaged students.

This MIT lecture covers entangled photon states and their properties. Entanglement is defined as a quantum state that cannot be factorized into separate wave functions for subsystems a and b. The professor distinguishes between entangled modes (like single photons in superposition) and true entangled states, which require two physically separable systems that can be individually addressed and manipulated.

The four maximally entangled Bell states are introduced: ψ⁺, ψ⁻, φ⁺, and φ⁻. These states exhibit two key properties: non-local correlations between separated subsystems and fragility against decoherence.

Entanglement purification is explained as a method to convert weakly entangled states into maximally entangled Bell states through quantum operations and measurements. The success probability of purification relates to a quantitative measure of entanglement: the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix obtained by partial trace.

For creating atomic entanglement, two methods are discussed: photo-dissociation of diatomic molecules (theoretically simple but experimentally challenging) and a probabilistic "poor man's entangler" using light scattering and Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The Hong-Ou-Mandel effect causes identical bosons (photons) to bunch together at a 50-50 beam splitter, while fermions exhibit anti-bunching. This interference, combined with polarization scrambling through quarter-wave plates, enables entanglement of distant atoms through photon measurement.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on August 3, 2017, announcing its early adoption of new FASB accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases effective July 1, 2017. The revenue recognition standard, adopted using the full retrospective method, materially impacted consolidated income statements and balance sheets by changing timing of Windows 10 and certain commercial software license revenue recognition, with no impact to cash flows. The leases standard, adopted using a modified retrospective approach with practical expedients, materially impacted balance sheets through recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for operating leases, with no material impact to income statements or cash flows. Prior periods will be restated accordingly, with restated financial information for fiscal years 2016 and 2017 available in Exhibit 99.1.

In May 2007, Victor Reinoso, Deputy Mayor for Education under Washington DC Mayor Adrian Fenty, faced a 12-hour deadline to recommend a new chancellor for the DC Public Schools (DCPS). The recommendation came as DCPS was about to come under mayoral control per legislation passed in April 2007, following decades of failed reform attempts in a system plagued by patronage, high leadership turnover, bloated administration, and poor student performance despite high per-pupil spending.

Reinoso, a former school board member with an MBA from MIT Sloan and consulting experience turning around struggling businesses, had grown frustrated with the school board's consensus-driven culture that diluted difficult decisions. After Fenty's 2006 election, Reinoso helped draft the DC Public Education Reform Act of 2007, which established mayoral control, created a chancellor position, and stripped the school board of most powers.

During the transition, Reinoso built a flat organizational team, commissioned data showing DCPS ranked last in student achievement among 11 urban districts, and identified six persistent "Pain Points" including lack of accountability and operational inefficiencies. For chancellor, he sought an entrepreneurial leader willing to radically rethink public education without "sacred cows."

Candidates included Rudy Crew, an experienced African American superintendent known for aggressive reforms in New York and Miami-Dade, and Michelle Rhee, founder of The New Teacher Project with minimal administrative experience but strong views on teacher accountability. Reinoso also considered retaining incumbent superintendent Clifford Janey, whose cautious approach concerned him despite his reform ideas.

The search was complicated in early May when Reinoso took blame for copying portions of an education plan without attribution, causing temporary legislative delays. With his recommendation due, Reinoso needed to select someone who could transform DCPS without destabilizing it.

This paper develops quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods for efficiently estimating expectations of quantities of interest from nonlinear partial differential equation models of tumor growth. The authors consider a semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion PDE that models tumor invasion and proliferation, with uncertain diffusion and proliferation coefficients treated as random fields. The work extends QMC theory to nonlinear (specifically semi-linear) parabolic equations, providing rigorous error estimates for uniform random fields and numerical experiments for log-normal fields on complex domains. Key contributions include novel parametric regularity bounds for the nonlinear term u(1-u), which is non-monotone and requires new proof techniques. The analysis handles both space and time derivatives, making it significantly harder than elliptic cases. The paper establishes well-posedness, derives QMC error rates, and validates results numerically, with applications to computational oncology and glioma modeling.

This is a fantasy football email report from Commissioner.COM dated November 25, 2001, sent to Paul Lucci at Enron. The email contains promotional offers for sports merchandise and services, followed by NFL player news and fantasy football recommendations. Player updates include injury status and start/sit advice for Week 11, covering players such as Muhsin Muhammad (out with shoulder injury), Warrick Dunn (starting despite toe injury), Mark Brunell (expected to start), Terrell Davis (returning Dec. 2), and Olandis Gary (out for season with broken leg). The report also includes a fantasy matchup breakdown between "Luccis Losers" and "Team Chick."

The Mesh concept is a versatile short-to-intermediate passing play from the Air Raid Offense that has been widely adopted across football. It creates natural picks and confusion for defenses, working effectively against both man coverage (keeping receivers moving) and zone coverage (finding voids). The play struggles against zone blitzes and simulated pressure that rush five defenders. Key routes include shallow and deep drags, rail/flare routes from running backs, and a corner route. The quarterback's progression runs: flare, shallow drag, deep drag, then FB arrow route. Popular variations include the "mesh rail" with an RB as primary option on a vertical route, and adding a sit route at 8-10 yards as a stationary zone target. The concept can also be adapted to single wing offenses as a smash concept variation.

Culp, Inc. reported Q4 2017 earnings with net sales of $77.4 million and pretax income of $7 million. Full-year net sales were $309.5 million with record pretax income of $29.7 million. The mattress fabrics segment achieved record annual sales of $190.8 million, while upholstery fabrics sales declined 6% to $118.7 million due to soft retail conditions. The company announced a $0.21 special dividend and ended the year with $54.2 million in cash and investments. Culp expects Q1 fiscal 2018 sales comparable to prior year, with mattress fabric sales slightly lower and upholstery fabric sales slightly higher. The company is actively pursuing acquisitions in the hospitality market, which currently represents approximately 10% of upholstery fabric revenues and offers margins 50-75% higher than residential business.

Chris Lattner, creator of Apple's Swift programming language, has joined Google to work on Google Brain, the company's major artificial intelligence project. Lattner previously left Apple in January for Tesla, where he led the Autopilot program for about six months before departing due to conflicts with CEO Elon Musk. His move to Google brings significant qualifications and industry recognition that may help the company attract additional AI talent. Google is heavily investing in AI and machine learning technology, viewing it as key to competing with Amazon Web Services in the cloud computing market.

This document specifies the SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD processors. The GHCB enables secure communication between encrypted guests and hypervisors through a 4KB shared memory area, protecting guest register state from hypervisor access while allowing controlled information exchange during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE).

Key components include: GHCB protocol versions with hypervisor feature advertisement; MSR-based protocol for pre-GHCB communication; NAE events for CPUID, I/O, MSR access, MMIO, page state changes, AP management, and trusted I/O; SMP booting mechanisms including AP Jump Table and SNP AP Creation; Restricted Injection with #HV doorbell pages for secure interrupt delivery; and Secure AVIC for guest-managed APIC state. The specification details register state requirements, error handling, and version negotiation between guests and hypervisors.
Scotty will decide how much time to devote to hockey versus family, with sacrifices required in coaching. The speaker expects him back next year, noting his unmatched passion and energy for hockey.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon has called the broadcaster's 28.6% gender pay gap "unacceptable" and pledged to achieve 50:50 gender balance in its top 100 positions by 2023. The gap exceeds the national average of 17.4% and those at ITN (19.6%) and the BBC (10.7%). Mahon attributed the gap to women comprising 66% of lower-paid roles and only 34% of top positions. ITV and Channel 5 have not yet published pay gap figures. The issue gained prominence after BBC salary disclosures revealed significant disparities, including Chris Evans earning over £2 million compared to Claudia Winkleman's £450,000-£499,999. A PwC review found no gender bias in BBC pay decisions, though this was rejected by BBC Women, and former China editor Carrie Gracie resigned in protest.

This technology relates to sealing fluid flow passages in high-pressure oil and gas flow control devices, particularly valves and fluid ends. Conventional designs mount seals on components that seal against the device body, causing erosion of the body bore and requiring cumbersome repairs. The disclosed solution transfers erosion wear from the body to less complex, less expensive mating components by mounting seals in recesses formed in the body that intersect the bore, allowing seals to extend and seal against surfaces of the mating components. For plug valves, seals are mounted in the valve body bore to seal against inserts and retaining nuts. For fluid ends, endless grooves in the housing walls mount seals that seal against discharge plugs, suction plugs, valve seats, and stuffing box sleeves. This design increases operating life while reducing downtime and repair costs, as worn components can be replaced rather than repairing the body through weld build-up operations.

The passage introduces CTPNet (Channel, Trend and Period-wise representation learning Network), a deep learning framework for multivariate long-term time series forecasting. CTPNet addresses limitations of existing methods by simultaneously learning three complementary dependencies: inter-channel dependencies (interactions across variables), intra-subsequence dependencies (local temporal structures within subsequences), and inter-subsequence dependencies (global temporal dynamics across subsequences). The framework uses Temporal Query-based Multi-Head Attention for inter-channel dependencies, an efficient Transformer for intra-subsequence dependencies, and a similar network with transposed inputs for inter-subsequence dependencies. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.

A 34-year-old man from Mission was arrested Thursday after driving a black pickup truck recklessly through a Maple Ridge strip mall parking lot, causing multiple collisions. The driver backed into a vehicle, crashed through barricades, jumped a curb, and hit a bus stop, injuring a female pedestrian and her son. Both victims sustained non-life-threatening injuries. The man faces charges of impaired driving, hit and run, and dangerous driving causing bodily harm, and was released on a promise to appear in court.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 26, 2020, disclosing updated revenue guidance for its More Personal Computing segment for the quarter ending March 30, 2020. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and specifies that the information is furnished, not filed, under SEC rules. The company is incorporated in Washington, headquartered in Redmond, and trades on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT, with registered securities including common stock and notes due 2021, 2028, and 2033.

A hockey player discusses not scoring immediately after being brought in, staying positive by focusing on playing well in other areas, and believing goals would come with time. They emphasize that winning matters more than personal scoring.

Generative AI poses significant challenges to traditional higher education assessment methods, particularly essays and multiple-choice questions, due to its ability to produce sophisticated human-like text. While concerns about academic integrity and plagiarism detection persist, the paper argues for integrating AI into assessment design rather than attempting to eliminate or outrun it. A case study of a redesigned postgraduate immunology coursework assessment demonstrates practical AI integration: students used ChatGPT to generate draft essay outlines, participated in peer evaluation workshops, then completed final submissions independently. Survey results showed 57.9% of students had prior AI experience, with only 5% feeling very confident using these tools. Students valued AI for planning and structuring work but criticized its generic, superficial outputs and accuracy limitations. The study concludes that embedding AI literacy into curricula, training educators and students on ethical AI use, and designing authentic assessments that evaluate higher-order cognitive skills offer the most sustainable path forward for maintaining academic integrity while preparing students for an AI-driven workplace.

The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed Ray Jones Jr.'s first-degree murder conviction and life sentence for killing his infant son. The court rejected his two assignments of error: first, that his inculpatory statements to hospital staff and police were inadmissible due to Miranda violations, finding all three statements voluntary and not requiring warnings since they were not products of custodial interrogation; and second, that the trial judge improperly restricted cross-examination of a psychiatrist, finding no abuse of discretion in sustaining a relevancy objection. The court held any error regarding the police station statement was harmless given overwhelming evidence of guilt from two prior confessions and other testimony.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver confirmed the 2026 All-Star Game will remain at the Clippers' Intuit Dome in Los Angeles despite an ongoing league investigation into whether the team circumvented salary cap rules regarding Kawhi Leonard's $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC, a company that received investment from Clippers owner Steve Ballmer. The NBA can impose penalties including fines up to $7.5 million, voided contracts, and forfeited draft picks if violations are found. The All-Star Game will feature a new format with U.S. and international teams and will air on NBC on February 15, 2026.

Scotland's Abusive Behaviour and Sexual Harm Act will criminalize "revenge porn" from April 1, carrying a maximum five-year prison sentence for disclosing or threatening to disclose intimate photos or videos. The law covers images taken in private showing nudity, underwear, or sexual acts. Justice Secretary Michael Matheson stated the offence addresses technological changes and abusive behaviour, while acknowledging that legislation alone cannot eliminate such violence.

This patent application describes a system for active ground terrain mapping to control mobile agricultural machines. A pose detection sensor on the machine generates position and orientation signals at points along a route. A point cloud identification system uses these signals to identify points estimated to correspond to ground surface, and an elevation generation system creates elevation values for each point. A plane identification system may calculate a predictive plane for ground surface ahead of the machine. Control signals are generated based on elevation values to control controllable subsystems such as height actuators for booms or headers. The system uses weighting functions based on distance from the pose detector to assign confidence values to elevation estimates. The point cloud is virtually attached to the machine and moves with it, with elevation values aggregated into georeferenced map cells. Multiple map layers can store elevation data, confidence values, point counts, and variance data for improved ground following and crop volume estimation.

Micro-credentials are certifications assessing knowledge and skills from specific learning experiences, particularly in technology-enabled contexts. Defined variously by agencies like UNESCO and the OECD, they address the gap between traditional higher education and digital economy skills. Higher education institutions globally offer micro-credential programmes to enhance employability.

In Mauritius, research explored education and industry leaders' readiness to adopt micro-credentials and their recognition as alternative credentials. Through qualitative interviews with 10 educational leaders and four industry leaders, findings showed general familiarity with micro-credentials but varying interpretations, with confusion between micro-credentials, micro-credits, and badges. Most favoured a hybrid integration model with existing credit systems, though concerns existed about implementation ease. Respondents viewed micro-credentials as potentially disruptive innovations requiring incremental implementation, with recognition in the National Qualifications Framework seen as essential. Key challenges included establishing reliable assessment methods, ensuring quality, and adapting regulatory frameworks. The study recommends integrating micro-credentials into a unified national framework with competency-based approaches, credit mapping, and qualification pathways to support recognition by employers and academic institutions.

Matthew Shashy, 29, of Montgomery, was sentenced to four years of probation for discharging a firearm outside Maxwell Air Force Base. A federal jury found him guilty in August 2017 of impeding, intimidating, and interfering with Air Force personnel. In January 2017, Shashy fired a shotgun three times near the base entrance during morning rush hour after spray-painting anti-government graffiti at multiple locations. A civilian followed him, photographed his license plate, and rear-ended his truck after Shashy braked suddenly. Shashy fled but was later identified and surrendered after barricading himself in his residence, where additional firearms, ammunition, and anti-government literature were found. The Montgomery Police Department and FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force investigated the case.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP) presented at Brookfield's investor day, highlighting 20% annualized returns since 2008 and Adjusted AFFO growth from $352M to $926M since 2012. The company currently yields 4% with an AFFO yield of 5.84%, retaining 1.84% for growth. BIP targets 6-9% annual distribution increases, though the author considers this aggressive given low inflation in developed countries. Past same-store EBITDA growth averaged 5% on a constant currency basis. The current 4% yield is lower than historical levels (5.4% two years ago), benefiting existing shareholders through accretive unit issuances, though this growth method depends on maintaining unit prices. The author concludes that while past returns were exceptional, future total returns around 10% are more likely given current valuations. The author discloses a long position in BAM.

A Phase 2 clinical trial found that combining omalizumab with oral immunotherapy (OIT) significantly improved efficacy for children with multiple food allergies. After 36 weeks, 83% of children receiving omalizumab plus OIT could safely consume two-gram portions of at least two allergenic foods, compared with 33% receiving placebo plus OIT. The 48 participants aged 4-15 received omalizumab or placebo injections for 16 weeks, beginning OIT at week 8. Those receiving omalizumab also experienced fewer adverse events during weeks 8-16. The study was funded by NIAID and conducted by Stanford University researchers.

Archaeologists failed to find a rifle believed hidden in a gap at Dublin's City Hall since the 1916 Easter Rising. The search, financed by Dublin City Council, sought a weapon reportedly dropped by Irish Citizen Army rebel Willie Halpin to avoid British capture. While the rifle remained missing, excavations recovered other artefacts including roof fragments with bullet holes, 1930s milk bottles, and pottery. Consultant archaeologist Franc Myles suggested the rifle was likely removed shortly after the Rising by British forces. The project was supported by Halpin's family and Dublin Lord Mayor Nial Ring.

In 1874, Equifax began as a system where businesses tracked consumers' creditworthiness in little blue books, with people as the product and businesses as customers. Today, credit bureaus collect extensive financial data on individuals without their consent, making it difficult to opt out. Lawmakers have struggled to regulate these massive corporations for fifty years.

A $5.25 million donation from John Knight's estate to London Health Sciences Centre's ovarian cancer research team was announced on Valentine's Day, timed to honor his wife Mary, who died from the disease in 2008. The couple was married 34 years. The funds will hire researchers, purchase equipment, and enable global collaborations. Victoria Hospital's A-block lobby was named the Mary and John Knight atrium. Researchers Gabe DiMattia and Trevor Shepherd noted the challenge of early ovarian cancer detection and the need for specialized personnel and partnerships to advance their discovery work on how the cancer metastasizes.
