ETF Channel calculated the weighted average implied analyst target price for the Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth ETF (VOT) based on its underlying holdings, finding a target of $145.80 per unit compared to its recent trading price of $132.83, representing 9.77% upside. Three holdings with notable upside to analyst targets are Sensata Technologies Holding (ST) at 11.37%, Global Payments (GPN) at 10.34%, and Markel (MKL) at 10.26%. The passage questions whether analyst targets are justified or overly optimistic, noting that high targets may reflect future optimism or precede downgrades if outdated.

Tanzania's government launched the Tanzania Business Clinic (TBC) initiative to improve the country's business climate. Industry, Trade and Investment minister Charles Mwijage announced the platform, which will bring together business experts and public officials to provide solutions to business challenges and educate people on business practices and regulations. TBC follows the Cabinet's adoption of a blueprint for amending laws to improve the business environment, with implementation starting in the 2018/19 financial year. The initiatives target sectors including textiles, leather, fish, edible oil, medicines, food, and mining. Tanzania ranked 137th in the World Bank's 2018 Doing Business Report, performing poorly in starting businesses, construction permits, trading across borders, and property registration. The government aims to transform Tanzania into a middle-income economy through industrial development and job creation.

Former Facebook executives Chamath Palihapitiya and Sean Parker have expressed guilt and concern about social media's negative societal impact. Palihapitiya, former VP of user growth, stated that Facebook's dopamine-driven feedback loops are destroying social fabric globally, causing misinformation and eroding civil discourse. Parker, Facebook's founding president, noted social media changes relationships and may harm children's brains. Former product manager Antonio Garcia-Martinez accused Facebook of lying about its influence over users. Palihapitiya acknowledged Facebook's positive aspects but plans to use his earnings to support structural changes he can control.

Julia Banks, who won the federal electorate of Chisholm for the Liberals in 2016 after Labor held it for nearly 20 years, faced questions about potential dual Greek-Australian citizenship. Local voters in the multicultural Melbourne eastern suburbs electorate remained largely unaware of the issue on Friday. Some Liberal supporters, including swing voters, indicated they would likely vote Liberal again in a potential byelection, while one Labor voter welcomed damage to the Turnbull government. A Monash University politics lecturer predicted a byelection would likely favour Labor in the marginal seat, which the government holds by just over 1 per cent, noting that multiple candidates could splinter the vote. A senior Labor strategist expressed confidence in regaining the seat, citing housing affordability and renter security as likely campaign issues. Banks won Chisholm in 2016 with a 2.84 per cent swing, partly through a social media strategy targeting Chinese-background voters, defeating Labor's Stefanie Perri by 2154 votes.

Sam Altman defends GPT-5 against critics, stating the large language model was misunderstood and acknowledging his changed perspective on AGI, following a flawed product demo that generated inaccurate charts and disappointed users expecting revolutionary advancement.

Soccer players use numerous non-verbal communications during matches, primarily hand signals. These include arm movements indicating set pieces, openness for passes, desired run directions, and passing instructions; hand signals for substitutions, wall positioning, and goalkeeper directions; pointing for positioning, coverage assignments, and pass targets; and various other signals for throw-ins, corner kicks, and free kicks. Additional non-verbal cues involve head nods, ball handling, and pre-arranged team signals. Coaches may need to develop comprehensive non-verbal systems when crowd noise prevents verbal communication.

This passage details the UHS-I and UHS-II bus speed modes, initialization sequences, and command structures for SD Memory Cards. UHS-I operates in SD mode with 1.8V signaling for higher speeds (SDR50, DDR50, SDR104), entered via voltage switch sequence initiated by CMD11 after ACMD41 negotiation. UHS-II adds FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes with full/half duplex operation, initialized through PHY synchronization and enumeration. The document covers card identification mode (CMD0-CMD3), data transfer mode, lock/unlock functions including Card Ownership Protection (COP) with Force Erase Password (FEP), and command classes including CMD6 for function switching across six function groups (access mode, command system, driver strength, power limit).

President Ulysses S. Grant issued a proclamation on May 24, 1870, warning U.S. citizens against participating in illegal military expeditions being organized within the United States to attack Canada, a nation at peace with the U.S. Grant admonished citizens from aiding such activities, warned that participants would forfeit government protection, and directed federal officers to prevent these unlawful proceedings and arrest those involved.

An 11-year-old boy, Damian Sunderland, was attacked by a relative's dog on June 20 and faces months of surgery. He was treated at Children's Mercy Hospital and University of Kansas Hospital for threatening injuries, recently undergoing major surgery to graft skin to his face and recreate his lips. Dr. Brian Andrews, who sees about two serious dog bites annually, used skin grafts from Damian's arms and legs to match natural skin tones, with possible tattooing later. Damian's mother, DeAnn Tieman, said he was excited to hear he would have lips again. Updates on his recovery are available on his Facebook page.

The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a programmable RISC-V scheduler on NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU that offloads context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving gaming performance through Windows HAGS compatibility. Blackwell adds hardware support for 4:2:2 chroma sampling video, with the ninth-generation NVENC improving AV1/HEVC encoding quality by 5% and adding 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds over 50% generationally. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth for 8K@165Hz or 4K@480Hz displays.

Blackwell's Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating with faster state transitions, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and accelerated frequency switching 1000x faster than previous architectures. Low latency sleep states enter 10x faster than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings in workloads like small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, creating up to three additional frames per rendered frame using 40% faster AI models with 30% less VRAM, plus enhanced Flip Metering for smoother pacing. Transformer-based models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, and lighting quality while ingesting 2x more parameters.

Neural shaders enable AI-driven rendering techniques including: RTX Neural Materials for film-quality assets at game frame rates; Neural Texture Compression providing up to 7:1 VRAM savings; Neural Radiance Cache for efficient global illumination; RTX Skin for real-time subsurface scattering; and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI for realistic facial rendering.

Blackwell GPU specifications: GB202 (RTX 5090) has 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and 512-bit memory; GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti) has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and 256-bit memory; GB205 (RTX 5070) has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and 192-bit memory.

This VentureWire newsletter from May 22, 2001, reports on venture capital and technology industry news. Top stories include Kodiak Venture Partners closing a $290 million second fund, Mercury Interactive acquiring Freshwater Software for $147 million, Celetron raising $48 million in first-round funding, and TVM's first close on a new life science fund. The newsletter also covers numerous funding rounds, including CGtime ($7M Series A), Lawson Software ($40M first round), NetContinuum ($26M second round), and NuVasive ($29.3M Series D). Bad news includes staff cuts at AgWeb and Ironmax, and Rx.com ceasing operations. Merger and acquisition activity includes Blink.com acquiring BookmarksPlus and Everstream acquiring The MusicBooth for $10 million. Executive appointments include Ed Koepfler as president and CEO of Icarian, and Jan Knox promoted to president at Viator. VC fund news covers the University of Pittsburgh and Redleaf Group forming Oak Leaf Networks, while personnel changes include Baroness Sarah Hogg becoming 3i chair in January 2002.

This Phase 2/3 study evaluated SII-NVX-CoV2373, a COVID-19 vaccine manufactured by Serum Institute of India, in 920 Indian children and adolescents aged 2-17 years. Participants were randomized 3:1 to receive two vaccine doses or placebo. The vaccine demonstrated non-inferior immune responses compared to adults, with over 98% seroconversion for anti-S IgG and neutralizing antibodies after the second dose. Immune responses were actually higher in children than adolescents, and both groups exceeded adult responses. The vaccine showed robust immune responses against Delta, Omicron BA.1, and BA.5 variants. Safety results showed no vaccine-related serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest; most solicited adverse events were mild injection site pain, tenderness, headache, fatigue, and fever resolving within 1-2 days. The study concluded SII-NVX-CoV2373 is safe and highly immunogenic for pediatric COVID-19 vaccination.

Mud Bay, a Pacific Northwest pet store chain founded in 1988, implemented a "Good Jobs Vision" (GJV) from 2014-2017 to improve employee conditions while maintaining competitiveness. The initiative, developed through employee input, included five strategies: investing in staff (raising wages from $11.50 to $15.00/hour, expanding benefits, creating an ESOP), offering fewer products at everyday low prices, standardizing processes, improving efficiency through cross-training, and partnering with animal welfare organizations. Results included 70% sales growth, reduced employee turnover from 48% to 31%, and strong customer satisfaction, though net profit margins declined from 2.18% to 1.99%. By 2018, the company faced a decision about whether to close stores an hour earlier to reduce costs, with co-CEOs Marisa and Lars Wulff holding differing views on the potential customer impact.

This study examined experiences of 17 third-year B.Ed. distance learning students and 4 lecturers regarding Physical Education teacher training at North-West University, South Africa. Using qualitative methods including interviews and questionnaires, five themes emerged: positive student-lecturer interaction despite lack of physical contact; increased student competence and lecturer passion; obstacles including students' limited background knowledge, technological illiteracy, and assignment administration problems; benefits and challenges of video-based practical training; and positive influence of program content on participants' perceptions of Physical Education. Recommendations include more face-to-face contact, technological training, enhanced video use, improved learning management systems, and better administrative systems.

Document management affects all businesses, not just large corporations. Poor document management costs time, money, and customers through lost documents, limited accessibility, storage expenses, and security risks. Despite digital trends, 40% of business processes remain document-driven. Better document management improves workflow and productivity, with 81% of surveyed businesses planning improvements. Solutions include cloud scanning via Xerox ConnectKey technology, mobile connectivity, PIN-protected printing, color printing restrictions, and automated toner notifications.

U.S. passports are issued only to citizens under rules prescribed by the President. Applicants must establish citizenship, U.S. domicile, and intention to return. Expatriation—permanent abandonment of allegiance for foreign citizenship—disqualifies applicants, though temporary foreign residence for health, education, or business with intent to return does not constitute expatriation. Permanent foreign residents generally cannot receive passports, though circumstances like family/property ties, health reasons, or representing American enterprises may support issuance. Americans in countries with U.S. extraterritorial jurisdiction may receive indefinite protection, and their descendants may inherit citizenship rights despite fathers never residing in the U.S.

A city court reserved its order on Congress leader Shashi Tharoor's anticipatory bail plea for tomorrow in the case of his wife Sunanda Pushkar's death. Delhi Police opposed the plea, citing flight risk and potential witness influence, while Tharoor's counsel argued he had cooperated with the investigation. Tharoor, summoned as an accused for July 7, faces charges under IPC sections 498A and 306 for alleged cruelty and abetment of suicide. Pushkar was found dead in a hotel on January 17, 2014.

ITV cycling presenter Matt Barbet launches the "Home Roads" podcast on June 8, featuring conversations with professional cyclists and sports figures while riding bikes together. The podcast focuses on personal stories and local routes rather than famous race courses. Four initial episodes feature Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche, and David Millar, with additional episodes including Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram, and Philippa York to follow.

The 200-day moving average (200 DMA) is a widely used technical analysis indicator that calculates the average price of an asset over 200 trading days to identify trends and smooth short-term fluctuations. Traders use it as a trend-following tool: prices above the 200 DMA indicate an uptrend, while prices below suggest a downtrend. Notable investors like Paul Tudor Jones employ it primarily for defense—exiting positions before bear markets to prevent significant losses. Backtesting shows the strategy performs well during recessions and major downturns (e.g., 2007-09, 2020) by reducing drawdowns, but it underperforms buy-and-hold during prolonged bull markets due to whipsaws—false signals causing frequent trades with low win rates (as low as 28%). Variations exist, such as Jeremy Siegel's 1% buffer rule or combining the 200 DMA with other indicators like RSI. While simple and effective for risk management, the 200 DMA is not a guaranteed outperforming strategy, particularly when central bank interventions sustain rising markets.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU features significant memory and bandwidth improvements over V100, including 1.7x faster HBM2 memory (1555 GB/sec), 2.3x L2 cache read bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache nearly 7x larger. A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability, partitioning each GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with separate memory paths for multi-tenant use. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (2x V100), while PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth to 31.5 GB/sec. The architecture adds hardware-accelerated features including 5-core NVJPG JPEG decode, 5 NVDEC video decode units, an Optical Flow Accelerator, and 11x improved FP16 atomic throughput. CUDA 11 introduces Task Graphs for reduced launch overhead, asynchronous copy operations bypassing registers, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. A100 supports Compute Capability 8.0 with third-generation Tensor Cores enabling structured sparsity (2:4 fine-grained) for up to 2x speedup. The DGX A100 system delivers 5 PFLOPS in 6U, with eight A100 GPUs interconnected via NVSwitch, supporting MIG for up to 56 isolated GPU Instances.

This MIT lecture covers hinged dissections, starting with the lack of existing software for animating them despite available examples online, including Greg Frederickson's work on dissections from triangles to hexagons and pentagons. Frederickson has authored three books on dissections covering hinged, twist-hinged, and surface-hinged varieties. The professor suggests several project possibilities: creating general animation software, implementing slender adorned chain folding, designing new hinged dissections, and building physical hinged dissection furniture.

The lecture explains a 1999 method for hinged dissections of polyominoes, polyhexes, polyiamonds, and polyabolos using inductive proofs with cyclic hinged dissections of half-squares or similar pieces. This extends to 3D tetrahedra by cutting to centroids. Physical realizations include mesoscale chemically-actuated pieces and DNA origami at nanometer scales.

For continuous motions in 3D, ball-and-socket chain robots can fold into arbitrary shapes by feeding through tubular paths, with examples built at MIT's Center for Bits and Atoms. These offer advantages over reconfigurable robots requiring attachment/detachment mechanisms.

The lecture details pseudopolynomial bounds for hinged dissections using grid-based triangulation, chainification of triangles, and gadgets for moving hinges and converting between triangles while preserving hinges. This involves triangle-to-rectangle conversions, rectangle-to-rectangle transformations, and pseudocut overlays.

In 3D, dissections require matching volume and Dehn invariant (sum of edge lengths tensored with dihedral angles, modulo rational multiples of π), proven necessary by Dehn (1901) and sufficient by Sidler (1965). The 4D case is resolved, but 5D+ remains open. Decidability of Dehn invariant equality was proven in 2008, though efficient algorithms remain unknown.

A 2017 study by researchers at the Universities of York and St Andrews found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots learn about object properties through play, enabling them to select correct tools for tasks. The birds explored blocks and ropes before being tested on tool selection, showing improved performance without changing their exploration behavior after learning objects' usefulness. The research suggests this "latent learning" aids creative problem-solving and may apply to other species.

This document defines the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, specifying Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events that require VMGEXIT processing. NAE events trigger #VC exceptions; guests inspect error codes, copy register state to GHCB, invoke VMGEXIT, and resume after hypervisor processing. The protocol requires guests and hypervisors to set appropriate bits in GHCB VALID_BITMAP for state fields. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request. Each event specifies required GHCB fields and handling procedures. The document also covers SMP boot challenges under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, NMI handling with #DB interception, debug register virtualization, and SNP Restricted Injection with #HV doorbell page semantics for interrupt delivery.

A coach discusses his team's playoff win, noting they played with five defensemen for part of the game and praising his forwards' support and the third period performance. He highlights strong play from Max, Jannik, and Raffi, particularly Raffi's physicality and clutch hits. He contrasts the two teams' goaltending styles and says they need clarification on contact initiated by the opposing goalie. He praises Raffi's attitude and work ethic, accepting his outside-the-box play. He describes the game as intense with offense on both sides, comparing it to previous physical series against Nashville and San Jose. A player is day-to-day and not skating. The coach reflects on his limited playing potential leading to a coaching career that started at the Tier II level to give back, eventually reaching the Stanley Cup after nearly 30 years. He has kept his visiting group small to stay focused, with his two daughters and best friend attending. He expresses confidence in his players' big-game experience and expects a hard series against a balanced Boston team. He declines to discuss lineup possibilities, emphasizing a one-game-at-a-time philosophy. He praises a young player's upside, hockey sense, and playoff contributions. He believes the time off was used well through practices and skill work, seeing no problem with the layoff. He declines to comment on something he hasn't heard about, focusing only on his team and the Bruins.

Joan Jordan (45), an Irish software engineer diagnosed with MS in 2010, faced years of employment rejection due to her illness before securing part-time work with Eupati after eight years. She has written "huManS Multiple Sclerosis," a book she wishes she'd had at diagnosis, and seeks sponsorship to print more copies. On World MS Day, she is speaking at Trinity College for MS Ireland's launch of a report on improving MS research in Ireland, developed with Novartis. The report recommends establishing an MS Research Community, better data sharing, greater patient involvement, and improved dissemination of findings. Approximately 9,000 people live with MS in Ireland.

The Saskatchewan Roughriders are considering using return specialist Christion Jones as a defensive back, similar to how they've deployed receiver Duron Carter at cornerback. Jones, who practiced extensively with the defense this week as an "emergency DB," has experience at both receiver and defensive back from his time at Alabama. Head coach Chris Jones stated the team has limited Jones's offensive and defensive roles to protect his effectiveness as a returner, where he currently ranks third in the CFL in punt and kickoff return averages and leads in combined return yards.

This patent application describes address obfuscation techniques for memory devices to prevent reverse-engineering of wear-leveling functions by malicious actors. The system uses configurable mapping functions that translate logical addresses to physical addresses through selectable per-bit logic operations (such as inversion, XOR, XNOR, pass-through, or address swap). These mapping functions can vary across memory devices, dice, or arrays, and can change over time based on triggers like boot events, schedules, random numbers, or unique device identifiers. The large number of possible configurations (M^N for N-bit addresses with M operations per bit) makes reverse-engineering difficult, and even if one device is compromised, the knowledge cannot be applied to other devices or the same device at different times. The system includes selection components, mapping components with subcomponents for each bit, and interfaces for receiving logical addresses from host devices. A security key can enable direct memory addressing for manufacturer testing while keeping the obfuscation active for end users.

This manual provides safety instructions, cleaning tips, and operational guidance for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze MP3 player. Safety warnings include avoiding headphone use while driving, keeping volume at moderate levels to prevent hearing damage, and keeping the device away from moisture. The player features a 1.9" color screen, FM radio, voice recording, microSDHC expansion slot, and supports multiple audio/video formats. Battery life reaches 24 hours for audio or 5 hours for video. The device charges via USB or optional AC/car adapters. Users can transfer files via drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player, with video/photo conversion requiring Sansa Media Converter software. The manual covers playback controls, playlist creation, FM radio presets, voice recording, and system settings customization. Firmware updates are available through SanDisk's support website. The product carries a one-year limited warranty covering material defects, with technical support accessible by phone or online.
12,000-year-old camel engravings at Jebel Misma in the Nefud Desert indicate early human presence in what was once a lush landscape.

The passage argues that K-12 education's focus on "21st century skills"—such as critical thinking, collaboration, and communication—has come at the expense of teaching actual knowledge. The author contends that skills cannot be effectively deployed without foundational content knowledge, using examples from cricket terminology and string theory to demonstrate that comprehension requires prior learning. Research from multiple fields supports that knowledge acquisition enables complex thought. Evidence of declining knowledge emphasis includes rising GPAs alongside falling test scores, reduced graduation testing requirements, and indifference toward states and schools using content-rich curricula. The author advocates for high-quality instructional materials that build sequential knowledge, warns against AI's potential to dilute strong curricula, and concludes that knowledge is essential for human flourishing.

This study analyzed demographic factors associated with insecticide-treated net (ITN) usage among children under-5 and pregnant women in Nigeria using 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey data. Among 13,727 households, 56% owned at least one ITN, with higher ownership in rural areas, North West/North East regions, and lower wealth quintiles. Only 41.4% of children under-5 slept under ITNs, with usage higher among younger children, rural residents, North West/North East regions, and lower wealth quintiles. Among pregnant women, 49.6% used ITNs, with higher usage in North East/North West regions and lower wealth/education levels. ITN ownership declined from 69% in 2015 to 56% in 2021, attributed to COVID-19 disruptions. Current utilization remains below the 80% target set in Nigeria's National Malaria Strategic Plan.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended May 1, 2022. The company reported revenue of $8.29 billion, up 46% year-over-year, with net income of $1.62 billion ($0.64 per diluted share), down 15% from the prior year. The termination of the Arm acquisition resulted in a $1.35 billion charge. Revenue growth was driven by Data Center (up 83%) and Gaming (up 31%) segments. Operating expenses increased 113% year-over-year, including the acquisition termination cost. The company had $20.34 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. NVIDIA repurchased $2.0 billion in shares and paid $100 million in dividends during the quarter. The Board increased the share repurchase authorization to $15 billion through December 2023. The company faces supply constraints, demand estimation challenges from cryptocurrency mining volatility, and macroeconomic uncertainties including COVID-19 disruptions in China and the war in Ukraine.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali is taking a leave of absence from his businesses after Eater reported accusations of inappropriate misconduct by a female chef from 10 years ago and sexual misconduct by three former employees over two decades. Batali co-owns Tarry Lodge locations in Port Chester and Westport and Tarry Market in Port Chester. In a statement, he acknowledged the allegations "match up" with his past behavior, apologized, and took full responsibility. He has also been removed from ABC's "The Chew."

HMD Global, Nokia's exclusive manufacturer, has not released the kernel source code for the Nokia 8 despite Chief Product Officer Juho Sarvikas promising to share it 136 days ago on September 20, 2017. While HMD cited security reasons for not unlocking the bootloader, withholding kernel modifications violates the GNU General Public License version 2 (GPLv2), drawing criticism from developers including Francisco Franco. The article suggests HMD should follow Xiaomi's example with the Mi A1 and comply with licensing requirements.

Researchers have reclassified seafloor fossils from Newfoundland, once considered decomposed material, as one of Earth's earliest animals—a spongelike creature named after punk rocker Johnny Rotten due to its spiky appearance. The 560-million-year-old organism, described September 16 in a study led by paleontologist Christopher McKean, had fingerlike tubes and pores indicating it was a filter feeder. The name also references "jiggamint," a spiky fruit called gooseberry by the now-extinct Beothuk peoples. The discovery may help identify early animal ancestors of modern species.

A University of Queensland study found that Black Mamba, Western Green Mamba, and Jamesons Mamba venoms launch a dual neurological attack: first causing flaccid paralysis through postsynaptic neurotoxicity, then causing spastic paralysis through presynaptic toxicity once antivenom treatment begins. This explains why some patients initially improve with antivenom before developing painful spasms. The research also found venom function varies by geographic location, complicating treatment. Scientists call for specialized antivenoms to address these limitations.

This systematic review examines AI applications in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback. The study uses the TPACK theoretical framework to analyze 20 peer-reviewed articles from 2010-2023 sourced from five academic databases. Findings indicate AI enhances efficiency, scalability, and personalization in educational processes, with automated grading showing particular promise for STEM disciplines. AI-driven systems provide real-time, tailored feedback that supports self-regulated learning. However, challenges persist regarding algorithmic bias, data privacy, and AI's limitations in evaluating complex constructs like creativity and critical thinking. The review highlights global adoption patterns, with emerging implementation in African contexts including Zambia. Ethical considerations and the need for transparent, equitable AI deployment remain critical concerns. The study concludes that successful AI integration requires balancing technological capabilities with human pedagogical expertise, supported by ongoing professional development and interdisciplinary collaboration.

A speaker interprets fans' cheering as encouragement for an upcoming game in Detroit, emphasizing their readiness and support. They reject being labeled a defensive specialist, stating that games involve both gains and losses, with their team focused on gaining ground. They dismiss categorizing players by type, preferring to react to individual tendencies once play begins.

A hockey player describes an intense game where he felt good getting physically involved, scored by catching a deflected puck and passing to a teammate, and emphasizes his focus on helping the team win regardless of personal stats. He mentions his parents and brother attending Stanley Cup Finals games, and praises teammate Cory as highly skilled, underrated, and ideal to play with.

Birmingham City FC's top ten away days from the last decade include: a 1-0 survival-securing win at Bristol City in May 2017; a 2-1 Midlands derby victory at Wolves in February 2017; a 5-2 triumph at Fulham in November 2015; promotion-clinching 2-1 win at Reading in May 2009; a 3-0 rout at Derby in January 2016; a dramatic 2-1 Europa League victory at Club Brugge in October 2011 with 8,000 travelling fans; a 3-2 injury-time win at Tottenham in December 2007; a 4-0 demolition of Crystal Palace in March 2013; a 4-0 win at Shamrock Rovers in July 2013; and a dramatic 2-2 draw at Bolton in April 2014 that secured Championship survival with a last-minute equaliser.

Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher, and Randy Moss were first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees, while Terrell Owens was elected on his third ballot. Brian Dawkins was also voted in as part of an eight-person class that included Bobby Beathard, Jerry Kramer, and Robert Brazile. Lewis and Urlacher defined middle linebacker play in their era, with Lewis winning two AP Defensive Player of the Year awards and one Super Bowl MVP, and Urlacher winning one Defensive Player of the Year award. Moss and Owens were dynamic receivers who played for five teams each due to conflicts with teammates and coaches.

On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil rig—leased by BP from Transocean and working on BP's Macondo well in the Gulf of Mexico—exploded, killing 11 workers and injuring 17. The rig sank two days later, causing the largest marine oil spill in U.S. history, with nearly five million barrels released before the well was capped on July 15, 2010.

The case examines BP's organizational history, including its transformation from a state-owned company to a privatized entity focused on cost-cutting and growth through mergers. Under CEO Tony Hayward starting in 2007, BP reduced staff and management layers while aiming to become less risk-averse. The company's "asset federation" model gave site managers autonomy with compensation tied to performance, but created disincentives for sharing safety practices across sites.

BP had experienced prior safety failures, including a 2005 Texas City refinery explosion (15 killed) and a 2006 Alaska pipeline spill. The Baker Report on Texas City found BP had cut maintenance and safety costs, and that executives failed to communicate that process safety was a core value.

For the Macondo well, several decisions made in the days before the explosion prioritized cost and time over safety: using long string casing with fewer gas barriers instead of a safer liner/tieback option; using only six centralizers instead of the 21 recommended by Halliburton's modeling; skipping a cement bond log test; and conducting only partial mud circulation. The rig had known maintenance issues, and many decision-makers were new to their positions. Investigations suggested these choices, driven by cost pressures and organizational culture, contributed to the disaster.

The Acer Swift 16 AI laptop is $450 off at $800 during Best Buy's Techtober sales event. It features 16 GB RAM, 1 TB storage, a 16-inch OLED screen with 2,880 x 1,800 resolution and 120-Hz refresh rate, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V CPU with 13-hour battery life in testing. The laptop is 0.79 inches thick. An alternative is the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition at $900, which has a 15.3-inch screen but thinner 0.55-inch chassis. Techtober runs through October 12, coinciding with Amazon Prime Day.

This lecture covers limited attention in economic decision-making. The instructor reviews how attention fits into the broader study of preferences, beliefs, and learning. Three main topics are addressed: motivating evidence for attention limitations, a study by Chetty et al. on inattention to taxes, and a paper on "learning by noticing."

Evidence for limited attention comes from psychology experiments demonstrating change blindness (failing to notice when actors or objects change between scenes), the invisible gorilla test (missing unexpected events while focused on specific tasks), and dichotic listening experiments (remembering only attended messages). Factors affecting attention include physical environment, distractions, worries, sleep, and poverty.

The Chetty et al. study examines consumer inattention to sales taxes, which are added at the register rather than displayed on price tags. Using a field experiment where after-tax prices were made salient on tags, they found demand fell 8.8% when taxes were highlighted. Comparing this to price elasticity estimates, they calculate consumers react to sales tax changes only one-quarter as much as to equivalent price changes, indicating substantial inattention.

The "learning by noticing" paper addresses why people might miss important information even when attention is limited. Using seaweed farming in Indonesia, the study shows experienced farmers neglected pod size as a productivity factor simply because they didn't believe it mattered. Despite having data available, they never learned its importance because they didn't attend to it. Only when researchers explicitly directed attention to pod size through summarized experimental data did farmers change behavior, demonstrating that incorrect mental models can prevent learning from available information, potentially causing large persistent welfare losses.

This is Franklin D. Roosevelt's first inaugural address, delivered in 1933. Roosevelt acknowledges the severe economic crisis facing the nation, including shrunken values, rising taxes, unemployment, and frozen credit. He asserts that "the only thing we have to fear is fear itself" and criticizes financial leaders for their failed policies. He proposes immediate government action to put people to work through public projects, agricultural reform, foreclosure prevention, reduced government costs, unified relief efforts, and transportation and utility supervision. He calls for strict banking supervision and sound currency. Roosevelt emphasizes national interdependence, pledges "good neighbor" foreign policy, and requests broad executive power if Congress fails to act, concluding with a call for national unity and divine blessing.

U.S. officials exchanged dispatches regarding Korean political murders and rebellion in 1894. The State Department disapproved of Consul Allen's intervention in the Kim Ok-kiun murder case in Shanghai, noting U.S. jurisdiction extended only to American citizens. Minister Sill reported rebel forces defeating government troops and capturing Chon-ju, while Admiral Skerrett declined sending ships to Chemulpo due to Bering Sea duties. Sill warned of growing rebellion dangers to Americans in Seoul. Chargé Denby confirmed China sent 1,500–2,225 troops and three warships to Korea at the King's request, with Viceroy Li Hung-chang assuring Japan and Russia of immediate withdrawal after hostilities and inviting Japanese gunboats to protect their subjects.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

@ThingsExpo was named a top IoT and M2M media brand by Onalytica in 2015-2016 based on Twitter influence analysis. The passage covers various IoT-related topics including connected devices in homes (averaging 7.8 per US household), WebRTC identity management challenges, data monetization strategies, IoT back-end data platforms, and enterprise technology predictions for 2017. Other subjects include blockchain investment ($1.4B in 2016), Microsoft's changes under CEO Satya Nadella, data ownership concerns in IoT applications, and the 21st anniversary of Scrum.

The MACD and RSI strategy combines two momentum indicators for market analysis and trading. MACD analyzes trends using 12-period and 26-period EMAs, while RSI identifies overbought/oversold conditions on a 0-100 scale. A sample strategy incorporates both indicators plus a mean reversion filter, yielding 235 trades with 0.88% average gain and 73% win rate on SMH from 2001-present. Traders may use MACD for trend direction and RSI for price swings, or have one confirm the other. Some analysts argue combining two momentum indicators creates redundancy, while others find value in additional confirmation. Effectiveness depends on specific rules, parameters, and markets used; backtesting is essential to evaluate performance.

President Trump has shown willingness to reverse major policy positions, most recently declining to label China a currency manipulator despite campaign promises. Analyst Sean King hopes Trump will similarly reconsider his withdrawal from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), a trade deal that would have benefited Japan's auto sector with cheaper U.S. market access. Japan is proceeding with 10 other nations to revive TPP without the U.S., though its impact is questioned. King noted the treaty remains valid until February 2018 and suggested other members might offer concessions to bring the U.S. back, similar to South Korea's concessions for the U.S.-Korea free trade agreement.

The Flexbone Offense is a run-heavy system evolved from the Wishbone, featuring option plays and misdirection with three backs. It requires a decisive running quarterback, a powerful athletic fullback, quick slotbacks, blocking wide receivers, and athletic offensive linemen. Its strengths include uniqueness that forces defensive preparation, ball control, multiple running threats, and physical wear on opponents. Weaknesses include limited passing volume, difficulty coming from behind, extensive practice requirements, and struggles in bad weather. Common formations include Double Slot, Trips, and Receivers Over. Key running plays are Triple Option, Midline Option, and Rocket Toss. Pass plays include Play Action Wheel Route, Toss Boot, and 4 Verts. Traditionally used by service academies and Paul Johnson's teams, it remains prevalent at lower college levels and high schools.

The Indian equity market consolidated for another session on Tuesday, with Nifty50 gaining 29.65 points (0.28%). Short covering provided support after a quiet opening, with rollovers dominating trade. Wednesday, the penultimate session of the derivative expiry, is expected to see continued tepid trading with resistance at 10,650-10,695 and support at 10,585-10,510. Technical indicators (RSI at 65.4201, MACD bullish) remain positive, though Nifty has not achieved clear breakout from its trading range. Low India VIX and elevated PCR levels suggest upside remains capped, warranting cautious trading with profit protection at higher levels. Stocks showing good technical setup include GATI, Snowman Logistics, SBI, Canfin Homes, Bajaj Finserv, Godrej Properties, Reliance, ONGC, Bharat Financial, and RAYMOND.

Jeff Carter scored his first playoff overtime goal, giving his team a 2-0 series lead, calling it a huge moment for the team. He credited Drew Doughty for a great play and noted that teammate "Penns" screened goaltender Marty. Carter mentioned his familiarity with Marty from his time in Philadelphia and said a goal is a goal regardless of how it goes in. Drew Doughty emphasized the need to reset and refocus, treating the series as if it's just starting when returning to Los Angeles with home-ice advantage. Doughty described his own goal, skating with the puck and using a defenseman as a screen against Marty's quick glove. He anticipated the opponent would play desperate hockey in Los Angeles and acknowledged the growing fan excitement with increasingly loud crowds.

Mississippi State (8-0) will face its toughest non-conference opponent, Cincinnati (7-2), on Tuesday at 6 p.m. on ESPN2 at BB&T Arena in Newport, Kentucky. Cincinnati, ranked No. 25 in the AP poll, averages 13.2 offensive rebounds per game and struggles with turnovers, committing at least 18 in four of nine games. Mississippi State forces 17 turnovers per game and holds opponents to 37.5% shooting. The Bulldogs have greater depth with eight or nine rotation players compared to Cincinnati's seven-man rotation, and guard Eli Wright returns from suspension.

The Protestant church in Germany is using social media to attract followers amid declining attendance, exemplified by a Twitter service at Magdeburg's Walloon Reformed Church of St. Augustine where parishioners tweet during liturgy. Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann views this as an experiment to engage people who live online, drawing parallels to Martin Luther's use of pamphlets—16th century social media—to spread Reformation ideas. While some participants share prayers and encouragement, others find the format too hectic or exclusionary, such as 86-year-old Ingeborg Brunner, who prefers traditional hymn-singing services.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU features third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, FP16, BF16, and FP64 formats. TF32 provides up to 8x throughput over FP32 on A100, while FP16/BF16 mixed precision offers up to 16x throughput. FP64 performance reaches 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5x that of V100. The A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that doubles compute throughput by skipping zero values. Memory architecture includes 192 KB L1/shared memory per SM, 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100), and 40 GB HBM2 delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. The Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. CUDA 11 adds support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, asynchronous copy operations, and task graphs.

The Larry Swedroe Portfolio is a diversified investment strategy allocating 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds, designed for long-term growth with minimized risk. Based on evidence-based investing principles, it emphasizes small-cap value stocks, low-cost index funds or ETFs, and periodic rebalancing. The portfolio typically includes 15% small-cap value, 7.5% international small-cap value, 7.5% emerging markets, and 70% intermediate bonds. Swedroe advocates bottom-up value investing, focusing on companies with strong fundamentals, and advises against market timing and active management. A backtest from 2012 using VIOV as a proxy showed a 3.71% annual return, lower than historical averages, suggesting the strategy may be best suited for risk-averse investors or pensioners due to its heavy bond allocation.

Warren Buffett's 2011 shareholder letter emphasized buying back undervalued stock. Berkshire Hathaway initially set a 120% of book value repurchase limit in 2012, buying approximately $1.3 billion in shares that year, but made no repurchases from 2013-2016 despite the threshold being nearly reached multiple times. The author argues that 120% of book value has become more conservative over time because the gap between Berkshire's intrinsic value and book value has widened due to unrecorded gains in controlled companies. Despite Buffett frequently discussing repurchases, he maintained the 120% figure in his 2016 letter. The author suggests increasing this threshold slightly would still honor the intent of buying below intrinsic value, and that repurchases should be considered if the price-to-book ratio returns to the low-mid 120% range. The author discloses a long position in BRK.B.

European stocks are set for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, with the STOXX 600 down around 1.7-1.8 percent, driven by rising bond yields and a stronger euro. The German DAX has reversed sharply after starting 2018 at record highs, now down over 5 percent in eight sessions and negative year-to-date. Banking results disappointed, with Deutsche Bank shares falling 5 percent after posting a 497 million euro loss for 2017, while Spain's Caixabank and Sabadell also declined on underwhelming earnings. Bank of America Merrill-Lynch's "Bull & Bear" indicator hit a "Sell" signal during the fifth consecutive day of losses. Investors are watching U.S. payroll data and monitoring leverage risks as funding costs rise. Tech stocks face pressure after Apple reported lighter iPhone sales guidance, though Amazon's record profits may boost some European names.

The District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District, reversed a final summary judgment in favor of The Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. Danny Langston, injured as a passenger in a vehicle owned by George Johnson, Jr. and operated by Fred Johnson, sued for negligence. The trial court granted summary judgment based on Personal Service's argument that its Ohio-issued surety bond covered only George Johnson, Jr.'s personal acts, not Fred Johnson's operation of the vehicle. The appellate court held that under Florida's dangerous instrumentality doctrine, George Johnson, Jr. could be held personally liable for Fred Johnson's negligent operation. Under Ohio law governing the bond, Personal Service would be contractually liable for a judgment against George Johnson, Jr. for damages "resulting from the ownership...of a motor vehicle." The court distinguished prior Ohio cases and remanded for further proceedings.

This paper examines how an Australian university developed an "Arts Specialism" to address gaps in primary pre-service teachers' arts education competencies. Using Stephen J. Ball's policy sociology theory and critical discourse analysis, the study traces the development through three policy contexts: influence, text production, and practice. The Arts Specialism comprises four courses (totaling 600 hours) covering dance, drama, media arts, music, and visual arts, emphasizing experiential learning and school-based projects. Despite challenges including limited curriculum time, COVID-19 disruptions, and resource constraints, the initiative demonstrates progress in equipping generalist teachers with specialized arts knowledge and pedagogical skills. The paper identifies opportunities for expansion through enhanced policy support, industry collaboration, and further research tracking graduate outcomes and school-based implementation.

Historical accounts of children raised by animals, including Jean de Liège (1644), an Irish "sheep-boy" (1672), and a Texan "Wolf Girl" (early 1800s), describe humans exhibiting animal-like behaviors and physical traits, though many such tales are considered hoaxes or distortions. The author suggests keeping an open mind about whether such cases could still exist.

A free five-week chronic pain self-management course starts in Montrose in May, run by Pain Association Scotland for Angus Health and Social Care Partnership. The relaxed, interactive format allows participants to share experiences and learn coping strategies. Previous attendees reported better pain management, improved relationships, and enhanced quality of life. Contact 01307 474889 or achppatientcourses.tayside@nhs.net to book.

This passage details the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification, covering non-maskable interrupt handling, debug register virtualization, and the #HV doorbell mechanism for interrupt delivery. For NMIs, hypervisors must intercept #DB and use "NMI Complete" messages from guests as injection indicators. Debug register virtualization is supported via the "DebugVirtualization" bit in VMSA, with fallback to intercept-based handling. SMM is unsupported, and nested virtualization is prohibited under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP. The #HV doorbell page uses PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to align with APIC behavior, enabling optimized interrupt delivery and EOI processing without VM exits. Hosts must emulate APIC semantics faithfully, while guests must use atomic exchanges to acknowledge interrupts and handle EOIs appropriately.

iOS 10.3.1 offers multiple security features including data encryption via password, PIN, or thumbprint; two-factor authentication; automatic data erasure after failed login attempts; and iCloud backups. iOS devices have built-in anti-malware layers and constant updates, unlike Android which relies on third-party antivirus. The Find My Phone feature enables remote location, locking, and data erasure. iOS requires explicit user confirmation for app permissions, with fewer vulnerabilities than Android. Apple's hardware and software exclusivity allows easier security patching compared to Android's fragmented ecosystem across multiple manufacturers.

U.S. homebuilder optimism declined slightly in April, with the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo sentiment index falling to 68 from 71 in March. The reading missed analyst expectations of 70. Measures of current sales, future sales expectations, and buyer traffic all edged lower. Despite the decline, new home sales remain robust, supported by low mortgage rates and strong employment. February new home sales reached a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 592,000, up nearly 13% year-over-year. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate has fallen for four weeks to 4.08%, still low historically. The April index was based on 307 respondents, with current sales conditions at 74, buyer traffic at 52, and six-month sales outlook at 75.

This passage covers strategies and guidelines for executing last shot situations in basketball. It emphasizes that last shots require preparation, not just drawn-up plays, and explains why holding for the final shot of a period matters—potentially creating 4-6 point swings when combined with the first possession of the next period. Key elements include: getting the ball to your best player, reading defensive pressure, keeping plays simple, practicing various scenarios with game clocks, and maintaining physical conditioning. The passage details timing rules (automatically holding with under 30 seconds when leading or trailing by less than 8 points), specific second-by-second execution guidelines, required passing skills (skip passes, baseball passes), and comprehensive strategies for different situations based on time remaining (1-3, 3-6, 6-12 seconds) and court position (endline, sideline, baseline). It also covers timeout management, intentionally missed free throws, and maximum dribble allowances based on time remaining.

John Bishop, a Korean War veteran, doubts Canada could play a pivotal role in the Korean Peninsula again, citing U.S. President Trump's unpredictable behavior. Former Canadian diplomat Marius Grinius notes that Canada's "controlled engagement" policy under the previous Conservative government severed diplomatic ties with North Korea, costing Canada valuable ground-level intelligence. Despite booming Asian trade, cultural ties, and its legacy with the U.N. Korea command, Canada has inconsistently committed to regional security. North Korea conducted multiple nuclear and missile tests last year, defying U.N. resolutions. U.S. Vice-President Mike Pence warned during a Monday visit to the Demilitarized Zone that "the era of strategic patience is over," while North Korea accused the U.S. of creating a dangerous situation. Veteran Doug Finney argues Canada must act due to North Korean humanitarian suffering and to honor the legacy of 27,000 Canadians who served. Scholar Tina Park says Canada, as an architect of the "responsibility to protect" doctrine, should address crimes against humanity in North Korea.

This passage details the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, covering data transfer formats, write operations, block handling, CRC protection, erase operations, write protection mechanisms, and command structures.

Data transfer uses CRC checks with 1 or 4 bits parity. Block writes require 512-byte block length regardless of WRITE_BL_LEN settings. Write commands are rejected on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR. Multiple block writes use CMD25 rather than continuous single writes for faster operation.

Three erase operations exist: standard ERASE (CMD38), DISCARD (CMD38 with argument 00000001h), and FULE (CMD38 with argument 00000002h). DISCARD and FULE are supported only on SDHC/SDXC cards, not through SPI. DISCARD allows partial or complete de-allocation with "don't care" contents. FULE logically erases the entire user area.

Write protection includes mechanical switch (host responsibility), card internal protection, and password protection. Password protection uses 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers. Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds 128-bit FEP and 8-bit FEP_LEN registers, preventing card reuse without password knowledge. COP requires CMD42[1Fh] unlock when FEP is set.

CMD6 switches card functions across six function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit, and two reserved groups. Mode 0 checks supported functions; Mode 1 sets functions. Power Limit defaults to 0.72W with maximum 1.80W for UHS-II.

Command classes 0, 2, 4, 5, and 8 are mandatory for all cards. Class 7 (except CMD40) is mandatory for SDHC/SDXC. SDSC uses byte addressing; SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing.

CRC7 protects commands and responses (except R3) using generator polynomial G(x) = x⁷ + x³ + 1. CRC16 protects data blocks using G(x) = x¹⁶ + x¹² + x⁵ + 1.

Timeout values: 100ms minimum for read operations, 250ms for write operations (500ms for SDXC in specific scenarios), 250ms per DISCARD command, and 1 second per FULE command.

October 2025 features three major skywatching events: a supermoon on October 6, when the full moon appears up to 14% larger and 30% brighter due to its closest approach to Earth; the Draconid meteor shower peaking around October 8, originating from comet 21P Giacobini-Zinner near the constellation Draco with up to 10 meteors per hour; and the Orionid meteor shower peaking on October 21, producing about 20 meteors per hour from Halley's Comet debris, best viewed after midnight due to the dark new moon conditions.

MIT OpenCourseWare lecture on linear algebra. Professor James W. Swan begins by addressing a typo correction in homework 1, explaining that the corrected version is easier than solving with the hint. He notes two remaining lectures on linear algebra before moving to other topics, with today's focus on eigenvalue decomposition and singular value decomposition on Monday.

He reviews permutation matrices as a formal system for reordering equations, explaining they are unitary matrices (their transpose equals their inverse) that swap rows when multiplied on the left and columns when multiplied on the right. Reordering is essential for Gaussian elimination to minimize numerical error and fill-in, with an example of a 40 million equation system that becomes unsolvable without proper reordering.

The lecture introduces eigenvectors and eigenvalues through a Plinko game analogy, where a sparse matrix describes probability diffusion. Eigenvectors are special vectors that, when multiplied by a matrix, point in the same direction but are stretched by a scalar factor (the eigenvalue). For an N×N matrix, eigenvalues are found by solving det(A - λI) = 0, yielding the characteristic polynomial whose roots are the eigenvalues.

Key properties discussed: diagonal and triangular matrices have eigenvalues equal to their diagonal elements; real matrices have eigenvalues that are real or complex conjugate pairs; determinant equals product of eigenvalues; trace equals sum of eigenvalues. Algebraic multiplicity refers to repeated eigenvalues, while geometric multiplicity is the dimension of the null space of (A - λI), representing freely specifiable eigenvector components.

A matrix with complete eigenvectors can be diagonalized as A = WΛW⁻¹, where W contains eigenvectors and Λ is diagonal with eigenvalues. This eigendecomposition simplifies solving systems of equations and decouples systems of ODEs. For symmetric matrices, eigenvectors are orthogonal and W⁻¹ = Wᵀ. When complete eigenvectors don't exist, alternatives include Jordan normal form, Schur decomposition, and singular value decomposition (to be covered next lecture).

Taylor Swift has broken numerous records throughout her career. She became the youngest artist to write and perform a No. 1 song on the Hot Country Songs chart with "Our Song" in 2006, and the youngest entertainer of the year winner at the 2009 CMA Awards. At the 2010 Grammys, she became the youngest album of the year winner with "Fearless," later becoming the first woman to win the award twice (2016), three times (2021), and four times (2024). She holds the most American Music Awards (40), most No. 1 hits on Billboard's US Digital Song Sales chart (29), and most Grammy song of the year nominations. Her "All Too Well (10 Minute Version)" is the longest No. 1 song in history. She is the only artist to claim all top 10 entries on the Billboard Hot 100 in a single week, achieved with both "Midnights" and "The Tortured Poets Department." Her album "The Life of a Showgirl" and its lead single "The Fate of Ophelia" broke Spotify records for most-streamed album and song in a single day. The Eras Tour became the highest-grossing music tour ever at $2 billion, contributing to her $1.6 billion net worth as the world's richest female musician.

The article examines exponential moving average (EMA) trading strategies through backtests on the S&P 500 (SPY). Four strategies were tested: short-term mean-reversion (buying when price crosses below, selling when above) and long-term trend-following (buying when price crosses above, selling when below), plus two time-based exit variants. Results show mean-reversion works best with short EMA periods (5-day EMA yielded 7.41% CAGR), while trend-following performs better with longer periods (200-day EMA returned 7.84% CAGR with lower drawdown). The best overall result came from buying below the 50-day EMA and holding 200 days (10.17% per trade). The EMA differs from simple moving average by weighting recent prices more heavily, making it more responsive but still a lagging indicator. The formula is EMA = (K × (C − P)) + P, where K = 2/(n+1). Drawbacks include potential false signals and entry/exit delays. The article concludes EMA strategies work best at extremes—very short or very long periods—and are most useful as part of broader trading systems rather than standalone indicators.

This study presents a systematic literature review of 28 articles from leading Information Systems journals (2000-2017) examining digital transformation, digital business strategy, and organizational capabilities. Using Wolifswinkel's guidelines, the authors identified 12 dimensions of digital transformation, 6 dimensions of digital business strategy, and 10 dimensions of organizational capabilities. Key findings show publication activity increased from 2009, with research concentrated in automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors, primarily in the US and Europe. The analysis reveals overlapping dimensions across the three concepts, with "external collaboration of ecosystem of digital platforms" shared by all. The authors propose that digital transformation represents digital business strategy in action, and present a conceptual framework illustrating how organizational capabilities enable digital transformation. The study contributes theoretical frameworks for managers and IS researchers seeking to understand relationships between these concepts for successful electronic commerce implementation.

YouTube announced that April the giraffe's livestream is the second-most-watched live channel in company history, with over 232 million views. The stream, which began February 10 at Animal Adventure Park in Harpursville, New York, peaked at 1.2 million simultaneous viewers when April gave birth on Saturday. Only Riot Games' League of Legends eSports channel has more views. The animal park's channel reached 200 million views in 54 days, becoming the fifth-fastest to do so.

The Foreign Relations series editors have complete access to retired State Department records including central files, decentralized bureau/office files, Executive Secretariat files, and overseas diplomatic post files. Department files from 1981–1989 will eventually transfer to the National Archives after declassification. Research also uses restricted documents at the Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies. Some printed material comes from still-classified documents, and Reagan Library staff continue processing these. Presidential papers there include significant foreign affairs documentation from multiple federal agencies. Some research used records scanned for the Remote Archives Capture project, though not all records were scanned, creating occasional uncertainty about document attachments. Documents are presented chronologically by Washington DC time. Editorial methodology follows Office style guidelines, reproducing original documents as exactly as possible with supplied headings, preserved spelling and punctuation (except silent correction of obvious typos), bracketed corrections and additions, italicized underlining, and preserved abbreviations. Telegram numbers appear at text starts. Bracketed insertions indicate omitted unrelated or still-classified material, with notes on amount omitted. Entire withheld documents are listed chronologically. Original brackets are identified in footnotes; all ellipses are original.

This paper addresses the multi-period resource allocation problem with stochastic demands, proposing a sequential adaptive policy based on shrinking horizon optimization. The static formulation determines all allocations at the beginning using only marginal demand distributions, solvable via bisection on the dual variable. The proposed sequential approach re-solves the optimization at each time step for the remaining horizon, conditioning future demand distributions on observed history. For independent demands, both methods coincide; for correlated demands, simulations with jointly log-normal distributions demonstrate the sequential method's superiority over static and roll-forward baselines, achieving revenue close to the prescient oracle bound.

Research on 150+ firms across major industries found that digital transformation requires cultural changes, not just technology adoption. Digital leaders outperform laggards in revenue and enterprise value growth. Four key cultural themes differentiate data-driven companies: growth mindset toward risk and learning, data transparency for collaboration, empowerment of teams to examine data with realistic goals, and alignment through common targets and objective measurements.

Digital leaders encourage experimentation, long-term development, and view failures as learning opportunities. They prioritize training in critical thinking skills and create environments where data is widely shared, enabling good ideas from anywhere. They use detailed metrics to define success while granting teams autonomy in achieving goals. Data-driven objectives coordinate efforts across the organization with transparent methodologies.

Digital laggards optimize existing initiatives, discourage risk, restrict data access, and rely on "culture of genius" over data-driven decisions. They set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, leading to "best effort" approaches without real-time feedback. They struggle to connect goals with strategy and show misalignment between espoused values and actual behavior.

Organizations typically begin in one of four patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant. Success requires transforming core beliefs about people and capabilities, not just implementing systems.

Two teacher educators analyze how bans on Critical Race Theory (CRT) impact Native content instruction in teacher education at predominantly white institutions in Utah, Idaho, and Arizona. Using Tribal Critical Race Theory (TribalCrit) and ethnographic methods including personal stories, interviews, and observations, they identify three main impacts: continued silencing of Native perspectives, perpetuation of Native invisibility in public education, and refusal to learn culturally sustaining pedagogies. The authors document how anti-CRT legislation in these states—such as Idaho's HB 377—has emboldened school administrators to eliminate culturally responsive teaching and tribal history training, even in schools serving majority Native populations. They highlight how colonial unknowing, or willful ignorance of Native peoples and their sovereignty, remains deeply embedded in teacher education through predominantly white teacher workforces, lack of professional development on Native-centered teaching, and resistance from pre-service teachers who view diversity coursework as unnecessary indoctrination. The authors argue that accurate teaching of Native histories and sovereignty is essential for critical democratic education and mutual respect between Native and non-Native communities.

Lyla Carreyn, a 5-year-old who received a kidney from her 4K teacher Beth Battista, was discharged from the hospital Saturday night after being admitted since February 21. She experienced post-surgery complications including a difficult-to-treat infection. Lyla is now enjoying simple pleasures like wearing footie pajamas and drinking unlimited water, which were restricted during her treatment. She requires over 15 daily medications and lab work three times weekly, with risk of re-admission if infection or rejection occurs. Battista was tested as a donor after seeing a Facebook post about a student in need and was found to be a match after Lyla joined her class.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on September 8, 2020, reporting that on September 4, 2020, it completed the sale of $5.0 billion of common stock through its at-the-market offering program, with final settlement expected by September 9, 2020.

This study analyzes self-reported mask-wearing behavior across U.S. counties from September 2020 to May 2021 using data from the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey (CTIS). The authors address limitations in existing survey data—small sample sizes, unrepresentative samples, and biases including non-response and social desirability—by applying Bayesian binomial regression models, survey raking by age/sex/education, and bias correction using vaccination data as ground truth. Results show substantial spatial heterogeneity in masking behavior, with urban counties showing higher proportions than rural ones (median >0.8 vs. <0.6), and temporal variation peaking in January 2021 and declining sharply in May 2021. Community-reported masking levels closely approximated bias-corrected self-reported estimates. The findings highlight the need for fine-scale behavioral data and geographically-targeted public health policies rather than one-size-fits-all approaches.

Sven Henrich of NorthmanTrader.com analyzes a ratio chart comparing 10-year Treasury yields ($TNX) to the S&P 500 ($SPX), supporting Alan Greenspan's 2018 warning of simultaneous stock and bond market bubbles. The chart shows a precise correlation since 2008, with a trend line shifting from support to resistance after the 2016 U.S. election. Henrich identifies a potential multi-year head and shoulders pattern that, if confirmed by breaking its neckline, suggests the 2016-2018 rally may have been a blow-off top preceding a massive multi-year bear market. Current conditions—rising yields and falling stocks—are pushing the ratio downward, though bulls may find short-term hope as the ratio approaches critical support.

This MIT lecture on underactuated robotics covers limit cycles and walking robot dynamics. The instructor, Russ Tedrake, explains that walking robots present a fundamental control challenge, with two key technical hurdles: limit cycles (periodic motions) and impacts (hybrid dynamics). He introduces the Van der Pol oscillator as a simple example of stable limit cycle behavior, where trajectories converge to a periodic orbit but don't synchronize in time. To analyze limit cycle stability, he presents Poincaré maps, which convert continuous-time stability analysis into discrete-time fixed point stability by examining system states at a defined surface of section.

The lecture then covers historical developments in walking research, from Muybridge's photographic studies to McMahon's ballistic walker model and McGeer's passive dynamic walkers—machines that walk down slopes with no motors or controllers. The rimless wheel model is presented as the simplest walking system with fully understood dynamics: a massless-legged wheel on a slope where energy gained from gravity balances energy lost to inelastic collisions. This system exhibits a stable rolling limit cycle and a standing fixed point, with analytically derivable Poincaré maps. The compass gait model extends this by adding a hip joint, while kneed walkers add further complexity with knee collisions. The instructor notes that ground impact dominates walking energetics, and that these simple models capture essential walking dynamics despite their minimalism.

The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress (Exhibit 99.2), which was posted to the company's investor website.
