Lincoln's second inaugural address notes that little new can be said about the Civil War after four years of public declarations. He recalls how both sides sought to avoid war, yet one would make war to destroy the Union while the other accepted war to preserve it. He identifies slavery as the cause, with one-eighth of the population enslaved in the South. Both sides prayed to the same God, but their prayers could not both be answered. Lincoln suggests the war may be divine punishment for slavery, quoting scripture that offenses must come but woe to those through whom they come. He concludes with a call to finish the work, bind up the nation's wounds, care for veterans and their families, and achieve a just and lasting peace with malice toward none and charity for all.

Trend following strategies using moving averages can outperform buy-and-hold approaches in gold trading. A 12-month (250-day) simple moving average system—going long when price is above the average and holding cash when below—turned $100,000 into $10 million from 1971 to 2021, compared to $4 million for buy-and-hold. The system captured major upward moves while avoiding significant drawdowns after peaks in 1980 and 2012. Gold differs from stocks in lacking cash flows and utility, though it has historically served as an inflation hedge. Practical trading options include ETFs (GLD) or futures contracts.

This study investigates carbapenem resistance in 147 gram-negative bacterial isolates from Evercare Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh, using the Disk Potentiation Test (DPT) to detect KPC and MBL carbapenemases. All isolates showed 100% resistance to Imipenem, with highest prevalence in patients over 60 years and in ICU settings. Acinetobacter baumannii was the predominant carrier of both enzymes (30 strains), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Escherichia coli. Overall, 26.53% carried KPC, 44.89% carried MBL, and 24.49% carried both enzymes. The DPT method demonstrated efficacy for rapid identification of these carbapenemases to guide antibiotic selection and infection control.

This document is a technical datasheet for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. It provides detailed electrical characteristics, peripheral specifications, and operational guidelines for these ARM Cortex-M0+ based devices.

Key sections include ADC configuration requirements for internal/external voltage references, with specific register settings (VRSEL bit in MEMCTL) needed to achieve specified ENOB and offset error performance. The devices feature dual 12-bit ADCs with 4Msps conversion rates, multiple clock sources (LFOSC, SYSOSC, SYSPLL), and five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) across two power domains (PD0, PD1).

Peripheral coverage encompasses DMA with 12 channels, event management fabric, up to 128KB SRAM with ECC protection, dual-bank flash memory up to 512KB, GPIO with FastWake capability, and multiple communication interfaces including UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD (MSPM0G351x only). Analog peripherals include temperature sensor, VREF with 1.4V/2.5V options, comparators with integrated DAC references, and 12-bit DAC with FIFO and DMA support.

Security features comprise AES-128/256 accelerator with GCM/CCM modes, keystore for four keys, TRNG, CRC, and flexible firewalls. Development tools include LaunchPad evaluation kits, MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig GUI, and multiple IDE options (CCS, IAR, Keil).

A coach discusses team strategy, player performance, and mindset during a playoff series. He addresses power play improvements, managing defenseman minutes based on fatigue, and the positive veteran leadership Sean brought when returning to the team. He analyzes line deployment in overtime periods, noting increased ice time for Vasicek's line. He describes Roddy as low-maintenance, Eric Cole as mature beyond his rookie status, and Bates as consistently prepared. The coach emphasizes not deviating from the team's approach despite losses, being careful about introducing new tactics mid-series, and the difficulty of generating offense against Detroit's strong defensive play and puck movement. He acknowledges frustration building during scoreless stretches and the need to reset emotionally while examining technical adjustments, particularly regarding neutral zone play and forechecking effectiveness.

Kenneth Kaylor appealed a divorce judgment awarding Sharon Kaylor rehabilitative alimony, claiming it exceeded his ability to pay. The Florida District Court of Appeal agreed, reversing the financial aspects of the award. The court noted Kenneth's net monthly income of approximately $2,000 was reduced by $400 in alimony, $650 in child support, and $345 in house expenses, leaving insufficient funds for additional required payments. The award also gave Sharon $175 monthly more than her stated needs. The court cited that alimony must consider the recipient's needs and the payer's ability to pay, finding the judgment erroneously moved Kenneth from financial well-being to misfortune. The case was remanded for a revised award, with other judgment aspects affirmed.

This document describes AMD AGESA firmware procedures for processor initialization and memory management. Key procedures include: AMD_ENABLE_STACK, a stackless assembler routine that initializes processor and cache systems to establish pre-memory stack regions across processor cores, handling protected/real mode configurations and creating UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instances; and AMD_DISABLE_STACK, which returns processors to non-stack-enabled states when main memory becomes available, disabling CAR mode and flushing cache lines. Supporting functions include AmdCreateStruct for allocating and initializing parameter block structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost methods; AmdGetDataEye for retrieving DIMM data eye bitmaps; AmdGetApicId for obtaining processor core APIC addresses (x86-64 only); and AmdGetExeSize for determining available pre-memory execution cache sizes (x86-64 only). Most procedures require established stack environments and operational HyperTransport links, with specific register preservation rules and status code returns.

Literacy has evolved beyond reading and writing to include information access, critical thinking, and technology use. Curriculum literacy—the ability to understand, evaluate, and implement educational programs—has become essential for effective teaching. Research shows teachers' curriculum literacy levels are often inadequate due to insufficient training, time constraints, and frequent curriculum changes.

This study used thematic content analysis of 29 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus to examine curriculum literacy's role and development barriers. Findings show research increased significantly from 5 studies pre-2000 to 89 in 2020-2025, with focus shifting from social sciences to digital tools, artificial intelligence, and learning disabilities. Australia, the United States, and Turkey led research output. Social sciences dominated (24 studies), while other fields remained underexplored.

Key themes included: curriculum literacy's weak but positive relationship with digital literacy; its importance for preservice teacher development, critical reflection, and equitable education; and the need for flexible curricula aligned with individual student needs. The study recommends expanding curriculum literacy training in teacher education, supporting digital skill development, and pursuing interdisciplinary research beyond social sciences.

This paper examines the digitalization of Vietnamese higher education (HE), noting that government policy has driven transformation, with COVID-19 accelerating progress. Vietnam's HE system comprises 237 universities under multiple governing bodies, with MOET overseeing education-related activities. Before the pandemic, digitalization was slow and uneven; most institutions had only basic learning management systems, while distance learning platforms were limited to a few universities. Challenges included underfunding, fragmented governance, and lack of digital skills among staff and students.

Current policies include the 2020 National Digital Transformation Program and the 2022-2025 Project, which set targets for online learning platforms, digital materials, and data warehouses. Post-COVID-19, most HEIs have developed distance learning platforms and applied digital technologies to management and teaching. MOET now permits up to 30% online content for Bachelor programs, and national database systems operate nationwide. However, digitalization levels vary, with advanced institutions like Hanoi National University leading while newer participants face budget and preparation challenges.

The paper recommends: policy dissemination support through clear guidance and training; increased government funding for infrastructure and partnerships; leadership training on digital transformation; lecturer training in intellectual property, pedagogy, digital skills, personalized learning, and mentorship; and student support through digital skills training and paperless administrative procedures.

AMD stock surged 23.71% after announcing a deal with OpenAI that could give the AI company up to a 10% stake in AMD. OpenAI will deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs over multiple years, starting with 1 gigawatt in late 2026. AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares with vesting tied to deployment and share price milestones. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record highs. Nvidia shares fell 1% on the news. The deal marks AMD's emergence as a major AI chip supplier after years of trailing Nvidia.

Baseline characteristics were comparable between study groups. Median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, mean weight was 82.2 kg, and mean BMI was 28.7 kg/m². This passage provides a comprehensive FAQ about Nasdaq 100 E-mini futures, covering their definition, trading mechanics, specifications, and strategies. The E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures contract, launched June 21, 1999, is a derivative product based on the Nasdaq 100 index (100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies), trading electronically on CME Globex. Each contract equals the index value multiplied by $20, with a tick size of $5 for outright trading and minimum price fluctuation of 0.25 index points. Trading hours run Sunday 6:00 p.m. to Friday 5:00 p.m. ET with daily maintenance breaks. The contract expires quarterly (March, June, September, December) and is cash-settled. Key risks include leveraged losses from price movements. The all-time high was 16,676.50 (November 2021) and all-time low was 797.50 (October 3, 2002). Seasonality shows stronger performance in Spring and Fall. To trade, investors need a futures broker account with CME access. The passage also describes a volatility-based backtested strategy (F101) with specific entry/exit variables, though full rules are behind a paywall.

A hockey coach reflects on winning the Stanley Cup with the Washington Capitals, highlighting his bond with Alex Ovechkin and their shared journey. He describes conversations with Ovechkin about carrying more responsibility as the team changed, which Ovechkin answered by scoring seven goals in two games. The coach emphasizes the team's resilience, having come back in every playoff series. He expresses personal happiness for Ovechkin, his family, and mentors who supported his coaching career, including Jack Button, David Poile, and Wayne Fleming. He praises Evgeny Kuznetsov's playoff performance as Conn Smythe-worthy and discusses Braden Holtby's reset after losing the starting role, which refocused him for postseason success. The coach concludes by stating he is content in Washington and loves working with the team.

Tube UK provided audio systems for Manchester Day 2017, delivering equipment to five carnival floats and five music/compere stages across the city centre. The event, commissioned by Manchester City Council and produced by Walk the Plank, was managed by a nine-person Tube team led by Melvyn Coote. Four floats used battery-powered systems with Tannoy and D&B speakers, while Graham Massey's float used a 4.5 KVA generator with D&B Y7Ps and Q-Subs. A hockey player describes scoring a goal with assists from Kesler and Hansen, reflects on a difficult summer and his fortune to now compete for the Stanley Cup, praises teammates Jannik and Lappy for their performance, and credits Manny for providing consistent encouragement to play a simple north-south game with feet moving.

A 29-year-old man, Jonathan Rinderknecht, was charged with starting the Pacific Palisades fire that became the most destructive blaze in Los Angeles history. Federal officials allege he lit a fire on New Year's Day that smoldered underground before reigniting during high winds on January 7, killing 12 people and destroying over 6,000 homes. Rinderknecht was arrested in Florida and faces charges including malicious destruction by fire. Investigators found a lighter in his car matching one from his apartment, and noted he fled the scene, returned to film the fire, made 911 calls, and lied about his location during questioning.

Pets at Home in Burton has partnered with the National Autistic Society to host an autism hour on Sunday, October 8, an hour before opening. The store will dim lights, reduce sounds, and train staff to create a calmer environment for autistic customers who often experience sensory overload in public spaces. A bear trap is a bullish trading pattern in an uptrend where sellers are tricked into believing a reversal is occurring when a bearish candle breaks a significant low, only for price to reverse sharply upward. Market makers intentionally create these traps to trigger retail traders' stop-loss orders, which become buy orders that allow institutions to purchase at discounted prices. Retail traders fall victim due to FOMO and impulsive decision-making. Warning signs include divergence between price and indicators like RSI or MACD, and breaks of support levels without confirmation. Protection methods include holistic analysis, avoiding crowd-following, disciplined strategy adherence, and backtesting approaches. One backtested strategy exploiting bear traps on QQQ showed 80% win rate, 13% CAGR, and 20% max drawdown with 10% time-in-market.

The lecture reviews two theorems: a sequence converges to x if and only if the absolute value of xn minus x approaches 0, and the squeeze theorem. The binomial theorem is stated without proof. Three special limits are proven: 1/n^p approaches 0 for positive p; p^(1/n) approaches 1 for positive p; and n^(1/n) approaches 1. The proofs use elementary methods, the binomial theorem, and the squeeze theorem.

The lecture then introduces limsup and liminf for bounded sequences, defined as limits of suprema and infima of tail sequences. These sequences are shown to be monotone and bounded, hence convergent. Examples demonstrate that limsup equals liminf if and only if the original sequence converges. The Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem is proven: every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence, with subsequences converging to limsup and liminf.

This retrospective study from China compared tenecteplase and alteplase for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment, analyzing 120 tenecteplase patients (March-November 2023) and 144 alteplase patients (January 2022-February 2023). Tenecteplase demonstrated significantly faster treatment times: median door-to-needle time (36.5 vs. 50 minutes, P<0.001), door-to-puncture time (117 vs. 193 minutes, P=0.002), and higher rates achieving target times (DNT ≤45 min: 65.83% vs. 40.44%; DPT ≤120 min: 59.09% vs. 13.79%). Tenecteplase was an independent predictor of meeting these targets. Clinical outcomes showed higher 24-hour NIHSS improvement (64.17% vs. 50%, P=0.024) and shorter hospital stays (6 vs. 8 days, P<0.001), with no significant difference in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (3.33% vs. 4.86%) or any intracranial hemorrhage (13.3% vs. 15.28%). The authors attribute tenecteplase's advantages to its enhanced fibrin specificity, longer half-life enabling single bolus administration, and reduced need for infusion equipment. Limitations include single-center design, non-randomized treatment assignment, and early outcome assessment.

This study examines digitalization in education within private sector companies through semi-structured interviews with 20 expert-managers. Digitalization in education involves using digital technology for teaching, encompassing online platforms, hybrid learning, virtual reality, and gamification. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated this shift, necessitating remote working and distance education.

Participants identified key challenges: technological problems and financial constraints (63% of company-related issues), plus participant resistance, digital literacy gaps, and adaptation difficulties (37% of individual issues). To adapt, companies implemented online and hybrid training (65%), updated content (40%), and adopted digital platforms (20%).

Positive effects included time/location-independent access (70%), equal opportunity and increased reach (65%), and improved content accessibility (60%). Negative effects comprised participant indifference and concentration problems (70%), lack of face-to-face interaction (60%), and reduced training effectiveness (25%).

Participants defined digitalization primarily through technological opportunities (60%) and easy access (40%). The study concludes that while digitalization in education is inevitable and increasing, face-to-face education will not disappear entirely. Recommendations include developing VR-enhanced materials, applying gamification, and integrating private sector practices into national education systems.

Traditional materials discovery methods are costly and slow. Generative AI models, particularly diffusion-based frameworks, are gaining traction for inverse materials design. Superconductors with high critical temperatures (Tc) are a priority target. This study presents a guided diffusion framework (DiffCSP-based) that generates crystal structures conditioned on target Tc values. The model is pretrained on over 2 million structures from the Alexandria Database, then fine-tuned on 7,183 superconductors. Using classifier-free guidance, 200,000 structures were generated and filtered through a multi-stage screening process combining machine learning and DFT calculations. This yielded 773 novel candidates with DFT-calculated Tc > 5 K and thermodynamic stability (Ehull < 200 meV/atom), representing a ~135× improvement in hit rate over element-substitution baselines. Experimental synthesis of 18 selected candidates found 9 showed superconductivity above 4.2 K, though measured Tc values were lower than predicted and X-ray diffraction revealed most formed as disordered BCC solid solutions rather than the predicted ordered structures. The study highlights challenges in distinguishing true synthesizable novelty from artifacts of incomplete reference data in underexplored chemical spaces.

The paper introduces SynDoc, a hybrid framework for domain-specific Visually Rich Document Understanding (VRDU) that combines discriminative Vision-Language Pretrained Models (VLPMs) and generative Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). SynDoc addresses limitations of existing approaches: discriminative models require extensive fine-tuning and struggle with zero-shot scenarios, while generative MLLMs lack domain-specific knowledge and produce unreliable outputs.

The framework consists of four key components: (1) a Synthetic Data Generator that blends structural information extraction (OCR, PDF parsing) with multi-task inquiry generation and quality verification to create high-quality synthetic annotations; (2) a discriminative "warmer" model adaptively fine-tuned on synthetic datasets to extract domain-specific knowledge; (3) adaptive instruction tuning incorporating multimodal features with MLLM predictions; and (4) a recursive inferencing mechanism where discriminative and generative outputs undergo iterative refinement through cross-feeding.

Experiments on four datasets (FormNLU, CORD, Ephoie, FUNSD) demonstrate that SynDoc enhances zero-shot performance, with the warmer providing domain-specific guidance to improve MLLM accuracy. Results show that top-K retrieved entities and recursive inference substantially improve performance, though open-source models require more iterations than proprietary models like Gemini. The framework effectively mitigates hallucinations and imprecision in MLLM predictions while maintaining scalability for domain-specific document key information extraction.

This lecture introduces the construction of spacetime for compact spherical bodies in general relativity. The instructor defines a compact body as occupying a finite spatial region with a vacuum exterior, and assumes spherical symmetry and static conditions. The most general metric for such a spacetime uses Schwarzschild coordinates, where the radial coordinate represents areal radius (surface area = 4πr²), though this does not correspond to proper radial distance. Alternative isotropic coordinates are mentioned but not used extensively.

For the exterior vacuum region (r ≥ r*, where r* is the stellar surface), the stress-energy tensor vanishes, allowing simplification to Ricci = 0. Solving the field equations yields φ = -λ, and integrating gives φ(r) = ½ log(1 + a/r). Matching to the Newtonian weak-field limit determines a = -2GM, producing the Schwarzschild metric: ds² = -(1-2GM/r)dt² + (1-2GM/r)⁻¹dr² + r²dΩ².

The instructor recounts how Karl Schwarzschild derived this solution in early 1916 while serving as an artillery officer on the Eastern Front and recovering from a lung infection; he died weeks later. Birkhoff's theorem states that any spherically symmetric vacuum spacetime, even time-varying ones preserving spherical symmetry, is described by the Schwarzschild metric externally—no gravitational waves are produced from such variations.

For the interior, the body is modeled as a perfect fluid with ρ(r) and p(r). Defining e^(-2λ) ≡ 1 - 2Gm(r)/r, the tt Einstein equation yields m(r) = ∫₀ʳ 4πρ(r')r'²dr', representing gravitational mass (distinct from baryonic mass m_b due to binding energy). The rr component and stress-energy conservation combine to give the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation for hydrostatic equilibrium: dp/dr = -(ρ+p)[Gm(r)/r² + 4πGp r][1 - 2Gm(r)/r]⁻¹, coupled with dφ/dr = [Gm(r)/r² + 4πGp r][1 - 2Gm(r)/r]⁻¹. These three equations, with an equation of state and central density boundary condition, determine the interior spacetime.

This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 nasal spray as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) against COVID-19 in 1,634 healthy adult workers in Beijing, China, from November 26 to December 9, 2022, during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. Participants were randomized 3:1 to receive SA58 or placebo within 72 hours of exposure to SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals. SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95%CI 52.41%-92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95%CI 37.50%-76.69%). No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred. Adverse events were mild and similar between groups, with no serious adverse events reported. The intranasal administration offers advantages over intramuscular injections. Study limitations include healthy young participants, short follow-up duration, and early termination due to China's COVID-19 policy changes.

This study audited 74 TB mortality files at Kitwe Teaching Hospital in Zambia from June 2018 to June 2019. Most deaths occurred among males (67.6%), with mean age 39.2 years, and 81.1% were HIV-positive. Patients predominantly resided in high-density areas (83.8%). Common presenting symptoms included cough (41.9%), fever (40.5%), and diarrhea (29.7%). Laboratory findings showed anemia (39.2%), hypoalbuminemia (12.2%), and multi-organ dysfunction. The study identified male gender, age under 50, HIV co-infection, high-density residential areas, and unstable hemodynamics as key clinical presentation patterns. Limitations included retrospective design and missing data. The authors recommend prospective studies to identify mortality predictors and assess malignancy's role in TB/HIV deaths.

The Amazon's 2024 fire season was its most destructive in over two decades, releasing 791 million tons of carbon dioxide—equivalent to Germany's annual emissions and a sevenfold increase from the previous two-year average. For the first time, fire-driven degradation surpassed deforestation as the primary source of carbon emissions in the Amazon. The study, published October 8 in a European Geosciences Union journal, found that 3.3 million hectares were impacted by fires driven by extreme drought, forest fragmentation, and land-use mismanagement. Brazil recorded its highest emissions from forest degradation, while Bolivia lost over 9% of its intact forest cover. Researchers used advanced satellite systems and Monte Carlo simulations to achieve precise measurements. The study calls for immediate global action to reduce fire use, strengthen protection policies, and address forest degradation in climate finance mechanisms.

Dell Technologies will expand its use of Salesforce's cloud-based CRM platform to nearly 40,000 global sales staff under a new strategic agreement. This patent application describes a nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) generator with feedback control for cancer electrotherapy. The system generates high-voltage, short-duration pulses (0.1-1000 nanoseconds) that trigger apoptosis in tumor cells without substantially affecting surrounding normal tissue. The generator incorporates a controller, power supply, and pulse generator with feedback signals adjusting pulse characteristics including voltage, pulse width, frequency, and temperature. The pulse generator uses a Marx-switch stack hybrid circuit with MOSFET switches to achieve high output voltage with few stages, enabling high efficiency, low impedance, and variable pulse duration. Multiple generator circuits can be combined in parallel for increased current or in series for increased voltage. The system includes various electrodes for different tumor types and locations, with sensors measuring voltage, current, and temperature to maintain treatment parameters through feedback control loops.

This patent application describes mixed reality (MR) systems and techniques for orthopedic surgical procedures, particularly shoulder and ankle arthroplasty. The system enables virtual guidance for bone preparation, implant positioning, and surgical instrument tracking. Multiple users can simultaneously view and interact with surgical plans from same or different perspectives. The technology integrates with existing planning systems like BLUEPRINT™, supports range-of-motion simulation, and provides closed-loop tool control using depth cameras and tracking elements. Educational applications include remote collaboration between teachers and students with manipulatable virtual models.

The Uzbek sum has strengthened approximately 9 percent against the dollar on the black market over the past week amid signs of imminent full exchange rate liberalization. The black market rate moved from 8,100-8,200 to 7,400-7,500 per dollar. Uzbekistan previously required exporters to sell a quarter of revenue at the official rate of about 4,100 sums per dollar, while importers bought currency at roughly 8,000-9,000 on a separate bourse. Currency controls have been cited as a major obstacle to foreign investment.

The "Back Cut" Offense exploits weaknesses in the Diamond & One defense, which is vulnerable in corners and middle, by producing open looks, lay-ups, and offensive putbacks. The offense uses single/double baseline screens to free up a Star player and forces opponents out of this defensive alignment.

The offense includes multiple looks: First Look involves the ballhandler driving the gap while the post flashes middle, looking for a back cut or weakside back screen for the Star. Second Look features the ballhandler cutting to the corner, with the wing passing to the post who looks to feed the baseline back cut. Third Look uses Single/Double Action with base screens and fake crosses if defenders cheat.

Implementation requires execution, coordination, double screens, base screens, strong post ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Teaching uses the Whole-Part-Whole method with breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies include scouting opponents, educating players on defensive reads and counters, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weakest defenders.

The Diamond & One defense derives from Box & One, with four defenders zoning and one denying the opponent's top scorer, best used against odd or one-guard front offenses.

Scientists documented the first modern case of "river piracy" in northwest Canada, where meltwater from the Kaskawulsh glacier abruptly diverted from the Slims River to the Alsek River on May 26, 2016. The phenomenon, caused by a 30-metre canyon forming at the glacier's end due to retreat, transformed the deep, swift Slims River into a shallow waterway while increasing flow to the Alsek, which now drains into the Pacific Ocean instead of the Arctic's Bering Sea. Researchers calculate only a 1 in 200 chance this occurred without human-caused global warming.

Night trading involves holding positions from market close to next-day open, distinct from after-hours trading. Since 1993, all S&P 500 gains occurred overnight; daytime trading from open to close yielded zero returns. Similar overnight bias exists in gold (0.03% average gain) and gold miners (30% CAGR since 2007). This edge likely stems from inflation, earnings growth, and compensation for overnight risk. While the bias exists, profitable strategies require overcoming slippage and commissions. Published strategies include a 2014 approach using three consecutive down days, which showed 6% gains in 2020 with minimal market exposure. Alternative 24-hour strategies (close-to-close) combine for 950 trades averaging 0.33% gain. Overnight strategies are considered accessible opportunities for traders seeking moderate returns with reasonable risk.

Dengue, caused by four serotypes of dengue virus (DENV1–4), affects 100–400 million people yearly, with incidence increasing 30-fold globally over 50 years. No direct-acting antivirals exist; two licensed vaccines show imbalanced protection and low efficacy in young children. AT-752, an oral guanosine nucleotide prodrug inhibitor of DENV polymerase with pan-serotype activity, was evaluated in a Phase 1 study of 65 healthy subjects across single ascending dose (SAD) and multiple ascending dose (MAD) cohorts. AT-752 was well tolerated with no serious adverse events. Pharmacokinetics showed rapid metabolism to AT-273 (surrogate for active metabolite AT-9010), with long half-life (15–25 hours) and sustained intracellular exposure. No ethnic sensitivity was observed between Asian and non-Asian cohorts. Food decreased peak levels but not total exposure, allowing administration with or without food. In MAD cohorts, 750 mg three times daily achieved rapid plasma AT-273 levels exceeding the 90% effective concentration for DENV inhibition. Results support AT-752 as a promising antiviral candidate for dengue treatment.

Unlike current injectable GLP-1 medications that require refrigeration and needles, these daily pills offer easier manufacturing, distribution, and administration, potentially improving accessibility and reducing costs. Side effects were similar to other GLP-1 drugs (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation) without the liver toxicity seen in earlier small-molecule attempts. On March 11, 2011, a 9.0-magnitude earthquake and tsunami devastated Japan, suspending production at approximately 80% of Japanese automotive plants and reducing monthly industry production by nearly 60% in March and April 2011. Nissan Motor Company, which suffered damage to six production facilities and approximately 50 critical suppliers, utilized its established risk management frameworks to recover rapidly. The company's operational philosophy emphasized supply chain flexibility, decentralized regional structures with centralized crisis coordination, and a "crisis mentality" developed following its 1999 alliance with Renault. Nissan maintained dedicated risk management functions, conducted earthquake simulation training, and maintained an emergency-response plan prioritizing human life, disaster prevention, rapid recovery, and community support. Within 15 minutes of the earthquake, Nissan convened its Global Disaster Control Headquarters and implemented four key recovery practices: integrating global regions into information sharing by dispatching staff to Japan, allocating constrained components to highest-margin vehicles, managing production by slowing lines and leveraging in-transit inventory to secure alternative supplies, and empowering field-level decision-making. While Japanese automotive production declined 24.3% over six months across all manufacturers, Nissan recovered faster than competitors due to localization strategies initiated in 2008. In January 2012, Nissan announced plans to increase localized production in the Americas from approximately 70% to 90% by 2015, reduce Japanese-sourced components by 50% by fiscal 2013, and enhance business continuity planning beyond Tier 1 suppliers.

Thermoelectric materials convert heat to electricity and vice versa, with efficiency measured by the dimensionless figure of merit ZT. n-type Bi₂Te₃₋ₓSeₓ (BTS) lags behind p-type counterparts due to stronger crystallographic anisotropy and higher intrinsic point defects. This study demonstrates that a simple annealing strategy decouples carrier and phonon transport in Se-alloyed Bi₂Te₃, significantly improving thermoelectric properties. n-type BTS was synthesized via melting-hot pressing (MT-HP), with annealing tuning carrier density and mobility through cation vacancy formation while Te(Se) volatilization introduced atomic-scale defects that reduced lattice thermal conductivity. The Bi₂Te₂.₆Se₀.₄ sample annealed for 100 hours at 723 K achieved a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K and average ZT of 0.99 at 300–423 K, with high carrier mobility (295.97 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) and low lattice thermal conductivity (0.48 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹). This scalable MT-HP synthesis and annealing approach offers a practical route to high-performance n-type Bi₂Te₃-based thermoelectrics for cooling applications.

Mentalization—the capacity to understand one's own and others' mental states—plays a central role in personality disorders (PD), yet distinctions between self-oriented and other-oriented mentalizing remain understudied within the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders (AMPD). This study examined how these distinct mentalizing facets relate to Criterion A (personality functioning) and Criterion B (maladaptive traits), and whether they moderate the relationship between attachment insecurity and PD pathology.

In a sample of 109 participants (60 psychiatric inpatients and 49 community members), self-mentalizing was assessed via the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire, while other-mentalizing was measured using the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition. Personality pathology was evaluated using the Self and Interpersonal Functioning Scale (Criterion A) and the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 (Criterion B), and attachment was assessed with the Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised.

Regression analyses revealed that self-mentalizing deficits were the strongest and broadest predictor, significantly associated with both self and interpersonal functioning (Criterion A) and all five maladaptive trait domains (Criterion B), explaining over 50% of variance in self-functioning and Negative Affectivity. In contrast, correct other-mentalizing uniquely predicted only interpersonal functioning difficulties, and its predictive significance diminished when self-mentalizing was included. Hypermentalizing showed weaker associations with Antagonism and Psychoticism.

Moderation analyses demonstrated that mentalization buffers the effects of insecure attachment. Correct other-mentalizing moderated the relationship between anxious attachment and interpersonal functioning, while self-mentalizing moderated associations between anxious attachment and both Negative Affectivity and Detachment. Additionally, other-mentalizing facets moderated the link between avoidant attachment and Detachment.

These findings indicate that self-mentalizing serves as a general mechanism underlying diverse aspects of personality pathology, whereas other-mentalizing specifically influences interpersonal functioning. Clinically, interventions should prioritize self-mentalizing while also targeting other-mentalizing to address attachment-related interpersonal difficulties, particularly differentiating between anxious and avoidant attachment patterns. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small sample, and methodological differences between self- and other-mentalizing assessments.

This paper characterizes the thermal performance of Mod-Cam, a cryogenic testbed receiver for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) utilizing microwave kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs). Measurements of the 100 mK detector stage demonstrate an RMS temperature fluctuation of 3.2 × 10$^{-5}$ K. Thermal responsivity measurements for aluminum (Al) and titanium-nitride (TiN) KIDs yielded median values of 1.995 × 10$^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$ and −6.081 × 10$^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$, respectively. These results correspond to equivalent optical power fluctuations of 0.20 fW (Al) and 0.11 fW (TiN) under a 5 pW optical load, representing fractional noise contributions of merely 0.0040% and 0.0023%. The analysis confirms that cryogenic thermal fluctuations constitute a negligible contribution to the overall detector noise budget, validating the Mod-Cam thermal design and ensuring that the instrument will achieve background-limited sensitivity goals when deployed on FYST.

This lecture introduces MIT's 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, taught by Erik Demaine, covering topics including temporal structures, geometry, memory hierarchy, and succinct data structures. The course utilizes a pointer machine model, where data consists of nodes with a constant number of fields (pointers or data) accessed via a root node.

The lecture focuses on persistence, preserving all past versions of a data structure. Four levels are defined: partial persistence (updating only the latest version, yielding a linear history), full persistence (updating any past version, yielding a tree), confluent persistence (merging two versions, yielding a DAG), and functional persistence (nodes are immutable, only new nodes are created).

For partial persistence, any pointer machine data structure with constant in-degree can be transformed to be persistent with amortized constant time and space overhead. This is achieved by having nodes store back pointers and a log of modifications ("mods"). When a node's mod log fills (capacity 2p), a new node is created with changes applied; pointers to the old node are recursively updated to point to the new node.

For full persistence, versions form a tree that is linearized using an order maintenance data structure (supporting constant-time insert and order queries). Nodes store 2d+2p+1 mods. When a node fills, it splits into two nodes by partitioning the version subtree, redistributing mods, and updating pointers, again achieving amortized constant overhead.

Confluent persistence is significantly harder. Fiat and Kaplan (2003) demonstrated an algorithm with O(log u + effective depth) overhead, along with a lower bound related to effective depth. A 2011/12 result achieves logarithmic overhead specifically for the "disjoint case," where merged versions share no nodes. Functional data structures, such as balanced BSTs via path copying (O(log n)) and deques with concatenation (O(1)), are also discussed as examples of immutable alternatives.

Generative AI (GenAI) models used in computational screening workflows for scientific discovery frequently produce nonsensical or suboptimal candidates, wasting computational resources and risking model decay when iteratively retrained on poor-quality data. To address this, the authors propose a queue prioritization algorithm that integrates active learning (AL) with a custom acquisition function to rank candidates generated by a generative model before subjecting them to expensive simulation.

The approach was demonstrated on a workflow for discovering Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture. A generative diffusion model (DiffLinker) produces candidate linkers that are stored in a non-prioritized queue. An XGBoost surrogate model (MIS), trained to predict MOF stability (internal strain), provides property predictions and uncertainty estimates. An acquisition function combines these metrics (and optionally other properties like synthesizability or similarity to known structures) to reorder candidates into a prioritized queue, ensuring high-potential candidates are simulated first via molecular dynamics. The model retrains periodically as new data arrives.

Results showed the AL-enhanced workflow identified an average of 604 high-performing candidates out of 1000 generated, compared to 281 without AL, representing a doubling of viable candidates with less than 1% computational overhead. By filtering unreasonable candidates from the fine-tuning dataset, the method prevented generative model decay. The acquisition function effectively balanced exploration (prioritizing uncertain candidates) and exploitation (prioritizing high predicted performance) via upper confidence bound tuning; weak exploration (λ=0.1) simultaneously maximized stable MOF discovery and minimized prediction error. AL operations utilized approximately 0.6% of total CPU resources, demonstrating seamless integration into high-throughput screening workflows.

Professor Noelle Selin of MIT discusses the Minamata Convention on Mercury, the first global environmental treaty in over a decade, signed in October 2013. Mercury is a global problem because atmospheric emissions persist for 6-12 months, enabling worldwide transport. When deposited, mercury converts to methylmercury, a neurotoxin that bioaccumulates in food chains, affecting Arctic ecosystems and human health—particularly fetal neurological development and adult cardiovascular health.

Major emission sources include coal combustion (~25%), artisanal and small-scale gold mining (a recently recognized significant source), industrial processes, and waste disposal. The treaty emerged after 11 years of negotiations, with the US initially favoring voluntary partnerships before shifting to support binding regulation under the Obama administration, which had made mercury a priority issue.

The convention addresses mercury throughout its life cycle: emissions controls, product phase-outs (thermometers, batteries, fluorescent lamps, dental amalgam with exemptions), and waste management. For artisanal mining, the treaty emphasizes capacity building and formalization rather than elimination, recognizing livelihood dependencies. Product regulations use a "negative list" approach rather than blanket bans with exceptions, with phase-out dates like 2020 negotiated as compromises between regions.

The treaty connects to broader international frameworks including the Stockholm Convention, Rotterdam Convention, Basel Convention, and WHO guidelines. Implementation faces challenges of capacity limitations in developing countries, lack of enforcement mechanisms, and the need for continued scientific assessment. While the treaty likely prevents mercury increases rather than achieving reductions, it establishes important international norms and signaling effects for business decisions.

The passage describes container design patterns for building distributed systems, focusing on three single-node patterns and several multi-node patterns. This manuscript describes KaviKrishna's community-based participatory research (CBPR) approach to tuberculosis control in rural Assam, India, integrating Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) with modern molecular methods. In *People v. Vasquez and Perez* (1974), defendants were convicted of possession of burglar's tools but acquitted of attempted petit larceny and resisting arrest. Despite noting the troubling result where defendants who abandoned their criminal attempt were still convicted, the court found its statutory interpretation correct and denied the motion to set aside the verdict, suggesting legislative amendment if desired.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, featuring a multiSPI digital interface supporting various data transfer protocols. The device operates in three functional states (RESET, ACQ, CONV) controlled by CONVST/CS and RST signals. It supports single-device and daisy-chain topologies, with flexible output configurations including standard SPI, dual SDO, and source-synchronous modes. Nine configuration registers control device operation, including reset/power control, SPI protocol selection, data output formatting, input range selection, and programmable alarm thresholds with hysteresis. The device offers NAP and power-down modes for power savings, and includes safety features such as overvoltage protection and input/AVDD alarms. Applications include industrial analog input modules for PLCs and data acquisition systems, with support for standard industrial voltage and current ranges up to ±10V.

OSCAR is a one-shot multi-label causal discovery method for high-dimensional event sequences that uses two Transformers as density estimators to extract Markov Boundaries—minimal sets of causal events for each label. Unlike traditional methods that become computationally intractable with thousands of nodes, OSCAR scales to tens of thousands of event types through fully parallelized conditional mutual information testing. Validated on a vehicular dataset with 29,100 event types and 474 labels, OSCAR achieved 55% precision in 11.7 minutes where classical methods failed to complete within 3 days. The method provides quantified causal indicators showing directional influence between events and labels, enabling practical deployment for real-world sequential data analysis.

The lecture discusses iterative methods for solving large sparse linear systems, where direct elimination is too expensive. The professor introduces preconditioners (matrix P) to accelerate convergence, with simpler choices including Jacobi (diagonal of A), Gauss-Seidel (lower triangular part), SOR (successive overrelaxation), and incomplete LU (ILU). The error equation shows e_{k+1} = (I - P^{-1}A)e_k, where convergence depends on the spectral radius ρ(M) of the iteration matrix M = I - P^{-1}A being less than 1. For Jacobi applied to the 1D Laplacian matrix with eigenvalues 2-2cos(θ_j), the spectral radius is cos(π/(n+1)) ≈ 1 - O(1/n²), requiring O(n²) iterations. Weighted Jacobi with ω=2/3 improves high-frequency convergence but leaves low frequencies slow. Gauss-Seidel squares Jacobi's eigenvalues, giving ρ ≈ 1 - O(1/n), better but still requiring many iterations. Multigrid methods address this limitation by handling different frequencies on different grids.

This study examines 45 teacher candidates' views on a distance education special education course at a private university during 2022-2023. While 58% preferred traditional education for better interaction and understanding, 57.7% still recommended distance education overall. Participants emphasized mandatory attendance remains important for success. Key technical deficiencies identified include system development needs (66.6%), internet infrastructure improvements (13.3%), and insufficient technical support (11.1%).

Turing GPUs feature native HDR display processing with ITU-R BT.2100 tone mapping, enhanced NVENC encoding with 25% HEVC and 15% H.264 bitrate savings, and updated NVDEC decoding for HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR. This article explains the Reversal Day trading strategy, where a stock or market index changes direction after an extended trend. A Bullish Reversal Day occurs when a stock moves upward after a downtrend, closing above the previous day's high. A Bearish Reversal Day occurs when a stock declines after a rally, closing below the previous day's low. Reversals can be caused by changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, or technical analysis. Key indicators include trend direction changes, heavy trading volume, and technical indicators like RSI and moving averages. The article presents backtested trading rules for both bullish and bearish reversal strategies using gold (GLD), finding that the bullish reversal strategy showed positive average gains while the bearish version produced losses due to gold's upward overnight drift.

Cocoa futures are financial derivatives traded on ICE and CME Globex platforms, representing contracts to buy or sell 10 metric tons of cocoa at a pre-agreed price. Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December, with financial settlement on CME and physical delivery on ICE. Trading symbols are CC (ICE) and CJ (CME). Minimum price fluctuation is $1.00/metric ton ($10 per contract). Cocoa futures show seasonal patterns, performing better in summer and poorly in spring and fall. The all-time high was $5,379 in July 1977; the low since 1979 was $707 in December 2000. As of November 25, 2022, cocoa traded at $2,484 per metric ton. The iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB) offers ETF exposure. Key risks include adverse price movements due to leverage and lower liquidity compared to other commodities.

Behavioral economist Mitesh Patel notes that framing savings as avoiding losses (like 401(k) auto-enrollment) could increase participation. Research shows HSA users spend less on healthcare but visit emergency rooms more, particularly lower-income families. This cross-sectional study of 243 prison officers at Nsawam Medium Security Prison, Ghana, found a 9% burnout prevalence using the Maslach Burnout Inventory. While 42% reported high emotional exhaustion, 32.5% high depersonalization, and 68.7% low personal accomplishment, the composite burnout rate was 9%. Irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49%), and lack of training (47.7%) were perceived as primary causes. Female officers had significantly higher burnout odds than males (AOR 0.31), and diploma/certificate holders had lower odds than postgraduates. Junior officers showed higher depersonalization, and main shift workers reported higher emotional exhaustion. Coping strategies included talking to colleagues (62.5%), anticipating off-duty time (60.1%), and family support (54.3%). Despite 74% reporting pride in work, 56% perceived lack of supportive culture. The study recommends addressing shift irregularities, workload, and training to reduce burnout.

The sector's high volatility means few stocks remain top performers long-term, and technology strategies may correlate strongly with broader markets, offering limited diversification.

A debate has emerged over whether Morgan Tsvangirai, leader of Zimbabwe's MDC-T party, remains an asset or has become a liability to the opposition. While Tsvangirai historically strengthened the opposition—most notably by defeating Robert Mugabe in the first round of the 2008 presidential election—his devastating 2013 election loss, party splits, and current cancer diagnosis have raised concerns. The article argues that Tsvangirai should step aside to allow leadership renewal, taking a supporting role rather than leading, to preserve his legacy as a political great.

The SD Card Association releases a non-confidential Simplified Specification/Addendum as a subset of its complete SD Specification. Implementation may require licensing. The information is provided "AS-IS" without warranties, and the Association assumes no responsibility for damages or patent infringements resulting from its use. No patent licenses are granted by implication.

Stanford's Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR) is criticized for failing to teach academic writing skills effectively. The program uses overly broad course titles, offers vague instruction, and lacks rigor—evidenced by grade distributions where over 80% of students receive A grades. Critics note PWR's overt liberal political bias in course offerings and events, with no conservative alternatives. The authors oppose a proposed PWR minor, arguing resources should improve existing classes instead. They propose a standardized, source-based writing course designed by experienced humanities professors to replace the current program.

The Montecito Fire Protection District will teach fire safety to elementary school children during Fire Prevention Week, October 3-14. Fire engine companies will visit schools to teach 800 children emergency preparedness, including "Stop Drop and Roll" and "Crawl Low in Smoke" for preschool through second grade, and the "Fire Safety Trailer" for third and fourth grades covering hazard identification, 9-1-1 communication, and safe home exits. Activities for October 3-6 were canceled due to predicted inclement weather and will be rescheduled. Parents are encouraged to practice emergency plans with their families.

A prototype BMW M8 has been spotted with provisional headlights, standard brakes, and downgraded wheels rather than the full-LED systems and carbon-ceramic brakes expected on a $150,000 vehicle. BMW M has not released specifications, but the M8 is expected to use a CLAR platform from the 7 Series with a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 producing 600+ horsepower, standard all-wheel drive with rear-biased capability, and performance rivaling Ferrari and Lamborghini. The original 1980s-1990s 8 Series had a planned M8 version that never entered production, though its V12 engine later powered the McLaren F1. The new M8 will compete with the Mercedes S-Class Coupe and Cabriolet, while rumors suggest the 6 Series name may return on a 911-rivaling sports car.

Ottawa police are warning residents about a swarming incident where a woman faked car trouble to lure a man to her vehicle, where he was robbed by accomplices. The incident occurred Saturday around 5:30 p.m. on Innes Road near O'Toole Road. The victim drove the woman to her car, where two men confronted him; the trio attacked him and stole his wallet containing an undisclosed amount of cash. The victim was hospitalized for his injuries. Police provided descriptions of the female suspect (early thirties, Caucasian, thin to medium build, dirty blonde short spiky hair, mole on face, wearing white clothing) and one male accomplice (5'6", muscular build, brown hair, brown sleeveless shirt). The vehicle was described as a dark-coloured older model North American four-door sedan. Police are requesting information at 613-236-1222, ext. 5116, or anonymously through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-8477.

At a Code Conference panel, All Raise's Aileen Lee, shift7's Megan Smith, and Stubhub's Sukhinder Singh Cassidy discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee criticized how "good guys" often get opportunities based on likability while women and people of color face greater scrutiny, advocating for systematic bias removal in business processes. The panel addressed board-level diversity and pushback, including some firms limiting men-women one-on-one meetings, which Lee rejected. Smith noted women of color are most excluded, a point highlighted by the absence of black men and women at the conference despite some women of color being on stage.

StockX, founded in 2016, has expanded its streetwear category to include BAPE and PALACE, adding to its existing Supreme collection. The company, which operates as an authenticated marketplace for sneakers, watches, handbags and streetwear using stock market-style anonymity and transparency, appointed Scotty Newman as BAPE general manager and Kenny Locklier as PALACE general manager. At launch, StockX will offer over 4,000 BAPE products dating to 2010 and more than 3,000 PALACE products. BAPE, founded by NIGO in 1993 and acquired by I.T. Group in 2011, is a Japanese lifestyle brand. PALACE, launched by Lev Tanju in 2010, is a British skateboard brand with celebrity fans including A$AP Rocky, Jay-Z and Drake. StockX, co-founded by Josh Luber, Greg Schwartz and Dan Gilbert, has over 200 employees and exceeds $2 million in daily sales, with investors including Eminem, Mark Wahlberg and Scooter Braun.

Vertigo, an iOS app launched last month, has integrated with both Spotify Premium and Apple Music, becoming the first iOS app to enable cross-platform music-sharing. Users can import playlists from either service, find new music, and share songs in-app. The app also offers "live sessions" for live-streaming music with video, photos, real-time chat, and audio commentary. Vertigo obtained API access by ensuring only paid subscribers use the service and paying royalties to rights holders. The app may fill a social void for Apple Music, which has downplayed social features, while competing with Spotify's established social aspect.

Glen Campbell's family shared in a People magazine interview that music has become a comforting part of his life as he battles the final stages of Alzheimer's disease. His daughter Ashley Campbell noted that he sometimes smiles and sings along to songs in his heart. Campbell's final album "Adios," recorded in 2012 and released June 9, showcases his enduring love for music despite the disease.

This study presents a streamlined workflow for Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) data analysis in hematologic malignancies using VIA software. Ten myeloid neoplasm samples (9 AML, 1 MDS) were analyzed 5-6 times each by independent technologist-director teams to assess efficiency and reproducibility. The workflow incorporates automated variant analysis with decision-tree based filtering, custom views for variant curation, and tiered classification following international guidelines. Results showed complete concordance with standard of care (karyotype/FISH) for detected variants, with OGM additionally identifying novel findings in 5 of 6 positive cases including submicroscopic deletions and complex rearrangements. Technologist review times averaged 25-47 minutes depending on case complexity, representing approximately 50% time reduction compared to Bionano Access alone. The study demonstrates that OGM with VIA enables efficient, reproducible, high-resolution cytogenomic analysis that consolidates multiple legacy techniques into a single assay.

A reporter spent $560 on a 7-day Eurail pass in October 2022 to travel by train across Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland, taking eight rides between six cities. They preferred train travel to flying, citing greater comfort, affordability for first and business class, easier boarding without security checks, better scenery, no ear-popping or dehydration, and lower carbon footprint. The total cost was cheaper than the approximately $440 estimated for economy flights between the same cities.

Brazilian stocks rose on Thursday, led by Vale SA shares climbing up to 4.9% after reporting record first-quarter iron ore production. Steelmaker Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais also gained after posting a first-quarter profit. The Brazilian real fluctuated amid investor concerns over geopolitical tensions in North Korea and Syria, though polls showing Emmanuel Macron leading France's presidential race provided some relief. Latin American currencies and stock indexes showed mixed performance, with Venezuela's IBC up 50.43% year-to-date and Colombia's IGBC down 0.19%.

Rio Blanco County's 4-H senior livestock judging team concluded their 2018 season at Colorado's state contest. Macy Collins finished third overall individually and Marryn Shults placed seventh, with Collins ranking fifth in beef, third in swine, and fourth in sheep/goat, while Shults placed fourth in beef and fifth in sheep/goat. Collins made the All State team and will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full scholarship, having been part of RBC's first State Champion Team in 2015 and winning every major Colorado invitational contest. Jilly Bumguardner and Tatumn Kennedy gained experience for future competitions.

U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, as both leaders sought common ground on the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. Trump criticized the agreement as "terrible" and "insane" for not addressing ballistic missiles or regional conflicts, while Macron urged keeping the deal as the best option to constrain Tehran. A senior Iranian official stated Tehran might quit the non-proliferation treaty if Trump scraps the agreement. Macron's visit also addressed steel tariffs, the Paris climate accord, and maintaining U.S. troops in Syria. Trump and Macron indicated they were close to reaching an understanding on Iran.

A holder in football catches the snap and positions the ball precisely for the kicker on field goals and extra points, requiring soft hands, quick placement, and the ability to rotate the ball to keep laces away from the kicker. Often a secondary role filled by punters, backup quarterbacks, or receivers, holders operate with minimal recognition but are crucial to scoring success. They also participate in fake field goal plays. No official NFL stats track holding performance, and there is no consensus on the best holders historically.

The Daily Examiner is transitioning from a metered digital subscription model to a premium model where some stories will be subscriber-only. Non-subscribers will still access vital public safety information and some local stories. Subscriber-only content will be marked with a PLUS symbol. Existing subscribers retain unlimited access to all stories and other News Corp sites. Subscriptions include options for Saturday paper delivery or digital-only access, app access, daily newsletters, breaking news alerts, and unrestricted access to other News Corp products. Sign-up is available online or by phone.

Thailand's road deaths during Songkran dropped 11% to 390 following a junta campaign against drink driving using harsher penalties, vehicle seizures, and mortuary visits. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha remains unsatisfied. Drink driving caused 28% of accidents. Thailand has the world's second most dangerous roads per capita. Myanmar reported 285 deaths during the same period.

The European Union is pushing global development banks to prioritize climate action more aggressively, despite U.S. opposition. The proposal urges multilateral development banks like the World Bank to align financing with the Paris Agreement, redirect lending from fossil fuels to low-carbon initiatives, improve transparency, provide local currency financing, and de-risk climate investments. Led by Germany and France, the initiative will be featured at upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings. The EU argues climate finance is central to sustainable growth, while U.S. officials warn it could distract from core economic development missions. In 2024, MDBs channeled a record $137 billion into climate projects, but European leaders say this remains insufficient. The proposal could reshape international development finance and strengthen EU climate leadership, though U.S. opposition may block consensus.

The Supreme Court of Canada ruled 7-0 that records detailing abuse of former residential school students can be destroyed after 15 years. The decision upheld a lower court ruling, balancing victim privacy against historical documentation. The records were collected through a confidential assessment process for compensation claims under a 2006 settlement agreement. Over 37,000 claims were processed, with participants required to sign confidentiality agreements for private hearings. The court found settlement negotiators intended the process to be confidential, and both claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on these assurances.

Eric Thames hit a two-run home run in the fifth inning as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Minnesota Twins 2-0 on July 3, 2018. The homer, which just cleared the right-field fence, was Thames' third in six games and eighth of his 12 homers this season to put the Brewers on the board. Milwaukee starter Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings with two hits, three walks, and eight strikeouts. Josh Hader pitched three hitless innings in relief, and Corey Knebel earned his ninth save. Minnesota starter Jake Odorizzi gave up two runs and four hits in five innings with four walks and nine strikeouts. The Twins fell to 1-7 on their nine-game road trip. The Twins became the first team since 2012 whose first baseman played an entire game with no putouts or assists.

This McKinsey memorandum from December 6, 2000, provides an update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000. Governments globally are opening generation markets to foreign investors due to rising power demands and limited funds. State-owned utilities are increasingly unbundling, with competition introduced at wholesale and retail levels. Some international players have reduced investments in riskier markets, shifting focus to the U.S. or Europe. The EU Directive has spurred competition in Europe, while Asian economies are resuming restructuring plans. Latin American privatizations have restarted at a slower pace after currency devaluations caused investor exits.

The document details regional developments: Europe shows continued liberalization with varying progress across countries, including Austria's internal disputes over market opening, Denmark's full retail access by 2003, France's delayed but accelerating liberalization, Germany's complicated grid access conditions, and the UK's completed deregulation moving into consolidation. Central and Eastern European countries continue privatization efforts to attract capital, with Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, Russia, Slovak Republic, Turkey, and Ukraine pursuing various restructuring and privatization plans.

Asia-Pacific shows recovery-driven restructuring, with Australia phasing in full competition by 2003, China aiming for nationwide interconnection by 2010, India's ongoing reforms in select states, Japan's initial market opening for large customers, South Korea's major KEPCO breakup, and other countries including Indonesia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam advancing various stages of reform.

Latin America has postponed some privatizations due to economic instability, though major economies have largely completed distribution and generation privatization except Venezuela and Mexico. Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and other countries show mixed progress with transmission auctions, wholesale market development, and ongoing regulatory challenges.

Middle East and Africa are increasingly opening to foreign investment, primarily through IPPs, with five Sub-Saharan countries having privatized power systems. Regional transmission links are a notable trend, including the West African Power Pool and a Six-Country link. Algeria, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and UAE show various stages of reform, IPP development, and privatization consideration.

This 1941 inaugural address describes the evolving challenges facing American democracy, from nation-building under Washington to preservation under Lincoln, to the current threat of external disruption. The speaker argues that democracy has proven resilient through crisis, surviving by maintaining constitutional principles and the unhampered initiative of free citizens. The speech emphasizes that a nation's survival depends on its spirit and faith—embodied in America's democratic aspiration for freedom—more than material prosperity. This spirit, rooted in centuries of history and documents like the Mayflower Compact and Constitution, must be preserved against doubt and fear through active defense of democratic ideals.

Former CIA officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is on trial in Virginia for allegedly providing top-secret information to a Chinese spy for $25,000. Prosecutors say his scheme was uncovered after customs agents found undeclared cash at O'Hare Airport in April 2017, and that a secure phone revealed his communications with the Chinese recruiter. Defence claims Mallory was loyal and planned to expose Chinese intelligence operations. The trial is rare as espionage cases typically end in plea deals; Mallory faces possible life in prison.

Olean is applying for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant, with the Common Council unanimously authorizing Mayor Bill Aiello to submit the application. The program will award $100 million among 10 communities statewide. The proposed project area spans from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and from Franchot Park to Seventh Street. Planned projects include redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building, funding business incubators, expanding downtown theater options, improving pedestrian access to Lincoln Park, and creating a park across from Olean General Hospital. The city could also receive over $2 million through the Buffalo Billion initiative. John Sayegh of Jamestown Community College praised the effort and offered to collaborate on upgrading the underutilized Cutco Theater to help make Olean a destination.

This IDC white paper, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, examines how industrial simulation, modeling, and high-performance computing (HPC) drive digital transformation. Industrial enterprises face challenges including geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy costs, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, while digitalization fundamentally changes value creation processes. IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis, enabled by modern technologies including HPC and cloud solutions, optimize industrial processes and create innovation scope. Three-quarters of respondents prioritize increasing innovation through these tools, with deployment in product development, production planning, and quality management expected to rise to 90% within two years. However, data silos hinder optimal digital support, requiring integrated data sources and a "single source of truth." Key technologies include 3D displays (used by two-thirds of enterprises), digital twins, IoT sensor data, and high-performance data analytics (used by 42%). HPC enables complex calculations, improves quality, unlocks new usage scenarios, and increases agility. Currently, 8% identify high demand for HPC calculations, expected to rise to nearly half within two years. While 26% already use professional HPC infrastructures and 39% plan deployment, challenges include security concerns (72%), high energy consumption (58%), inadequate computing performance, and lack of expertise (42%). Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructures (87%) or colocation (74%) over on-premises solutions. Cloud-based HPC architectures offer scalability, flexibility, cost optimization through OPEX models, and access to cutting-edge methods. HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) enables global collaboration, supports new business models, and provides modernity through continuous innovation. IDC recommends establishing virtual product development, creating holistic data strategies, evaluating appropriate HPC operating models, considering scalability and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise for implementation.

Uber has rolled out a panic button nationwide that allows riders to dial 911 directly from the app's home screen. The feature, announced in April following alleged sexual assaults, displays real-time location in most cities. Seven cities in a pilot program automatically transmit location and vehicle details to emergency dispatchers, with Nashville joining soon.

A hockey player or coach discusses a loss to Scotty Bowman's Detroit Red Wings, noting the opponent's strong defensive play and left wing. The speaker admits their team failed to generate chances, particularly on the power play, and struggled with nerves after conceding the first goal. Despite playing evenly for most of the game except the first ten minutes, giving up a two-goal lead proved costly. The speaker acknowledges needing better individual performance and more contribution from the team.

In spring 1953, the free world weighs the chance for just peace, contrasting it with the failed hope of 1945. The United States and free nations chose cooperation, mutual respect, and disarmament, while the Soviet Union pursued force and domination, creating fear and arms races. The death of Stalin offers a new Soviet leadership an opportunity to change course. The U.S. proposes concrete steps: an honorable Korean armistice, Austrian treaty, German reunification, and broader European community. It offers disarmament agreements with U.N. inspection and commits to redirecting resources from arms to fighting poverty through world aid. The test of Soviet intentions requires deeds, not words: genuine peace in Asia, free choice for Eastern European governments, and effective disarmament.

This study examines how digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth affect sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image in Indonesian ICT companies. Digitalization is essential for modern business, particularly in supply chain activities, though companies face financial and technological challenges in implementation. The research proposes seven hypotheses: digital customer experience positively affects brand image; electronic word of mouth positively affects brand image; brand image positively affects supply chain image; supply chain image positively affects sustainable supply chain performance; and brand image mediates relationships between digital customer experience/electronic word of mouth and supply chain image, while supply chain image mediates between brand image and sustainable performance. Data was collected from 315 employees involved in supply chain activities across randomly selected Indonesian ICT companies, using structural equation modeling with partial least squares analysis. Results confirm all hypotheses, showing significant positive effects with t-values above 1.96. Digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth enhance brand image, which improves supply chain image, ultimately boosting sustainable supply chain performance. The model explains 82.3% of variance in sustainable supply chain performance. Indonesian ICT companies should implement e-commerce practices to strengthen digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth, thereby improving brand image and overall supply chain performance.

This patent application describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system for aircraft, specifically designed for improved efficiency during descent. The engine features a motor/generator connected to the low-speed spool, allowing the core to be shut down during descent while the fan windmills to generate electricity. This electricity powers aircraft systems and can be stored in an energy storage system. The engine is undersized relative to thrust requirements for takeoff and climb, with the motor providing supplemental power during those modes. During descent, the controller prevents core operation, switches aircraft systems to electric power, and optionally uses stored energy to drive the motor to overcome engine drag or provide minimal thrust.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on February 1, 2021, reporting the issuance and sale of $14 billion in senior unsecured notes on February 8, 2021. The notes include: $2.5 billion of 0.700% Notes due 2026, $2.5 billion of 1.200% Notes due 2028, $2.75 billion of 1.650% Notes due 2031, $1.5 billion of 2.375% Notes due 2041, $3 billion of 2.650% Notes due 2051, and $1.75 billion of 2.800% Notes due 2061. The offering was underwritten by Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Morgan Stanley. Interest will be paid semi-annually beginning August 8, 2021.

Cloud-based HPC offers modernity, flexibility, and access to cutting-edge technology, with 52% of respondents citing this as core to innovation. It enables faster calculations, deeper data analysis, and new digital products and business models. Bridgestone adopts a step-by-step cloud approach to overcome on-premises limitations. 81% of HPC users plan to implement cloud solutions. IDC identifies IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers for addressing disruptive changes, streamlining product development, and supporting digital transformation. Recommendations include establishing virtual development, creating holistic data strategies, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability and security, and leveraging external expertise. The study surveyed 200 decision-makers from industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland in December 2021.
