A federal judge dismissed a 2021 lawsuit by Spencer Elden, the man photographed as a naked baby on Nirvana's 1991 "Nevermind" album cover, ruling the image is not child pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found that while Elden was nude in the photo, no other factors met the legal standard for child pornography, comparing the image to a family photo of a bathing child.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for her role in the 2014 murder-for-hire plot against her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel. Despite her conviction after three hours of jury deliberation, Adelson maintained her innocence at sentencing, claiming no evidence linked her to the crime and that she would have stopped it if aware. Judge Stephen Everett interrupted her statement to warn he could consider her "utter lack of remorse." Her husband Harvey also asserted her innocence, shocking court observers. Prosecutors alleged the motive was relocating Adelson's daughter Wendi and her children to South Florida; Wendi Adelson was not charged. Co-conspirators Charlie Adelson, Katherine Magbanua, and one hit man were convicted of murder, while a second hit man pleaded guilty to second-degree murder.

Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, supports National Inquiry chief commissioner Marion Buller and would withdraw her family's story if the government reset the commission. LaPlante said families weren't consulted before the AFN's 48-15 vote calling for Buller's resignation. She agrees with extending the inquiry's deadline by two years, citing insufficient time to build proper structure and staff. However, some Saskatchewan families, including Lillian Ewenin, support Buller's resignation, citing disrespectful treatment during Saskatoon hearings and lack of communication. Danielle Ewenin said the commission ignored holistic approaches to community trauma.

Rising interest rates have pushed 30-year fixed-rate mortgage costs near 5 percent. Author Scott Sheldon outlines techniques to improve mortgage borrowing power: paying off debt to reduce debt-to-income ratio; obtaining a co-signer to supplement borrowing ability; switching loan programs such as from Freddie Mac to Fannie Mae or conventional to FHA; increasing down payments, though with less impact than debt reduction; and changing jobs within the same field before applying. Sheldon advises thorough research for individual circumstances and notes borrowers can refinance later without restrictions.

This article examines the evolution of special education and teacher preparation in Singapore. Before 2004, special education operated separately from mainstream education through voluntary welfare organizations, with students with disabilities primarily attending special schools. The watershed year of 2004 marked a shift toward inclusion when Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong envisioned Singapore as an inclusive society, leading to Enabling Masterplans and UNCRPD ratification in 2013.

Teacher preparation expanded significantly post-2004. The National Institute of Education (NIE) introduced training for Special Needs Officers (now SENOs) in 2005, the Certificate in Special Needs Support for mainstream teachers, and made special education coursework compulsory for all pre-service teachers. Special school teacher preparation evolved from the 1984 Certificate in Special Education to the current Diploma in Special Education (DISE), with pathways to Advanced Diploma, bachelor's, and master's degrees.

Key contextual factors include Singapore's tripartite governance structure between government, unions, and employers, and continuous PAP rule enabling long-term policy implementation. Current challenges include special schools remaining under social service agency rather than Ministry of Education purview, limited continuum of options for students with higher support needs, and less comprehensive preparation for special educators compared to mainstream teachers. The "Learn for Life" movement signals continued expansion toward holistic, inclusive education.

This email from Jean Munoz of McNally Temple dated July 31, 2001, distributes IEP News to a large distribution list including energy industry executives, lobbyists, and government affairs professionals from companies such as Enron, Duke Energy, Calpine, Williams, Dynegy, and Edison. The email contains summaries and full text of news articles covering California's energy crisis, including: (1) a Los Angeles Times op-ed by State Controller Kathleen Connell and UC Irvine Professor Peter Navarro criticizing Governor Gray Davis's $43 billion long-term power contracts as "stranded costs" that will burden California's economy for years; (2) an SEC preliminary inquiry into whether Davis energy advisors used inside information to trade power company stocks, requested by Republican Secretary of State Bill Jones, following the firing of five consultants for conflicts of interest; (3) a Salon.com article on Davis's efforts to bail out Southern California Edison, which contributed over $350,000 to his campaigns; (4) San Francisco Chronicle reports on ballot measures to create public power districts and Davis spokesman Steve Maviglio's purchase of $12,000 in Calpine stock; (5) Associated Press articles on reduced federal electricity refunds to California, Texas's deregulation pilot program, and ongoing developments in the energy crisis.

Sony released a firmware update for its A7Riii camera to fix a 'Set File Name' function issue and improve overall stability. Mac users running macOS High Sierra (10.13) cannot install the update, as Sony's software only supports Mac OS X 10.10–10.11 and macOS 10.12. This incompatibility stems from Apple's High Sierra rather than Sony's software. Workarounds include using an earlier Mac OS version or running Windows.

MIT Professor William Green discusses partial differential equations (PDEs) and introduces probability concepts in a chemical engineering lecture. For Homework 7, students must solve a drug diffusion problem using both COMSOL and finite volume methods, paying attention to convergence due to sharp concentration gradients caused by small characteristic lengths. Green explains finite volume methodology, emphasizing flux calculations across control volume boundaries and numerical stability advantages. He recommends starting with fixed meshes before attempting variable meshing, and suggests using sparse matrix solvers like backslash or BiCGSTAB for the linear system. He introduces the CFL number as a critical constraint for time-dependent PDEs, where the time step must be small enough relative to spatial discretization to maintain numerical stability. Transitioning to probability, Green argues that undergraduate chemical engineering problems present deterministic solutions unlike real-world measurements, which always contain noise and fluctuations. He explains fundamental probability concepts including joint probabilities, conditional probabilities, Bayes' theorem, and probability density functions, noting that even precise measurements yield distributions rather than single true values.

On Feb. 14, The New York Times reported U.S. agencies intercepted 2016 calls between Russian intelligence officials and Trump campaign members including Paul Manafort, but found no evidence of collusion. The FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn about his contacts with a Russian official after Trump's inauguration; Flynn resigned Monday amid trust concerns. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation and demanded Attorney General Jeff Sessions recuse himself. At least five Republican senators, including Rob Portman and John Thune, withheld support for labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder over his delayed tax payments on an unauthorized immigrant housekeeper. Linda McMahon was sworn in as Small Business Administration head after an 81-19 Senate vote, and David Shulkin was sworn in as Veterans Affairs secretary following a unanimous confirmation.

A 1968 study by Lew Goldberg found doctors highly inconsistent in diagnosing stomach ulcers from x-rays: they disagreed with each other and even contradicted themselves when shown duplicate images. Researchers then created a simple computer algorithm based on how doctors claimed they made diagnoses, and it outperformed even the best doctor. The author questions whether experts are still needed to create diagnostic rules when artificial intelligence and big data can now generate rules automatically.

Research from Which? indicates lenders have been slow to pass on interest rate rises to savers while quickly increasing mortgage costs for borrowers. Following the November base rate rise from 0.25% to 0.5%, Which? found that 48% of 327 variable instant access savings accounts saw no rate change, with only 21% passing on the full 0.25% rise and just 10% of 95 providers applying the full increase to all accounts. In contrast, 53% of providers increased standard variable rate mortgages for existing borrowers by year-end, and market averages for two-year, three-year and five-year fixed-rate deals all rose between October and December. UK Finance responded that banks balance borrowing costs with savings returns and that mortgage and savings rates depend on factors beyond the base rate.

The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch the Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, at 10:00 a.m. at the Mt. Carroll Township Public Library. The initiative, created by Dolly Parton in 1996, provides free books to children ages 0-5 to prepare them for kindergarten. The program has expanded to over 1,300 communities worldwide. The United Way partnered with the Morse Group and other supporters to bring it to Carroll County. Registration and sponsorship information is available at uwni.org/imaginationlibrary.

Hong Liu discusses D-branes in string theory, explaining their mass arises from vacuum energy of open strings living on them, calculable via Euclidean path integral over surfaces with boundaries. The D-brane tension scales as 1/g_s, making D-branes heavy at weak coupling. He introduces channel duality: gravitational interaction between D-branes via closed string exchange equals a one-loop open string vacuum diagram. The low-energy effective action for massless modes on D-branes is the Dirac-Born-Infeld action, generalizing Maxwell theory and Nambu-Goto action. When n D-branes coincide, the gauge symmetry enhances from U(1)^n to U(n), with open string excitations forming matrix-valued fields in the adjoint representation. Separating branes corresponds to the Higgs mechanism, giving mass to previously massless gauge bosons via scalar field expectation values.

A rare Asperitas cloud formation, the newest cloud type classified in over 50 years, was spotted over Bristol on Monday morning. The wave-like clouds were photographed by residents and an NPAS helicopter in Monmouthshire, Thornbury, and Filton. The Met Office confirmed the classification but noted the formation process remains uncertain, with theories linking them to post-thunderstorm conditions or wind direction changes.

The MSPM0 C-Series microcontroller datasheet describes multiple peripheral subsystems. The Low-Frequency Sub System (LFSS) combines peripherals clocked by a 32kHz low-frequency clock for timekeeping and low-power operation, including a Real Time Clock with prescaler extension and timestamp captures, and an asynchronous Independent Watchdog Timer (IWDT). The Voltage Reference module (VREF) provides configurable 1.4V or 2.5V internal references supporting ADC operation up to 515ksps, with external reference input capability. The Comparator (COMP) compares voltage levels with features including 6 blanking sources from timers, wakeup from low power modes, fault handling connection to advanced timers, and an 8-bit reference DAC output. Security features include flexible firewalls and CRC-16 with custom polynomial support. The CRC module supports 16-bit CRC16-CCITT with bit reversal. UART peripherals (UART0-2) provide standard asynchronous communication with programmable baud rates, LIN mode, FIFOs with DMA support, and loopback operation. I2C peripherals support 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, multiple controller/target modes, Standard-mode (100kbps), Fast-mode (400kbps), Fast-mode Plus (1Mbps), SMBus 3.0, and wakeup on address match. SPI peripherals support up to 16Mbits/s, controller/peripheral configuration, programmable frame sizes (4-16 bits), multiple formats (TI, Motorola, Microwire), and DMA-capable FIFOs. The IWDT in LFSS uses a 25-bit counter with closed/open window, driven from 32kHz LFOSC with programmable divider and eight selectable periods, generating POR reset on timeout. The Windowed Watchdog Timer (WWDT) offers eight selectable periods, automatic stop in sleep mode, and interval timer mode. RTC_B operates from 32kHz crystal providing calendar counters (seconds to year), customizable alarms, periodic interrupts at multiple frequencies, and calibration/compensation for crystal offset and temperature drift up to ±240ppm. This case examines the historical categorization of "unskilled" work in the United States from 1820 to 2021. The U.S. Census Bureau began collecting occupational data in 1820, and by 1917 Alba Edwards formalized a six-tier classification system where "skill" applied only to manual labor, distinguishing professional work by property ownership rather than skill level. In 1930, 28% of workers held "unskilled" jobs, with African Americans disproportionately represented in farm labor, factory work, domestic service, and other labor categories.

The four main "unskilled" occupational groups evolved differently. Farm labor, historically reliant on enslaved and then exploited African American workers, declined from over 50% of employment in 1870 to 1.3% by 2019, though remaining dependent on immigrant labor. Factory work grew through industrialization, with Ford's assembly line reducing production time dramatically, but manufacturing employment fell 67% between 1965 and 2020 due to automation and offshoring. Servant occupations transformed into the service industry, which became the dominant employer of non-college-educated workers by the 21st century, including retail, fast food, and healthcare aides. Other labor, including construction and mining, saw significant declines through mechanization.

Government regulations like the 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act established minimum wages and banned child labor but excluded agricultural and domestic workers. Labor organizing improved conditions through strikes and collective bargaining, though union membership fell from 34.8% in 1954 to 6.2% by 2020. Some employers adopted "Good Jobs Strategies" investing in workers through higher wages and training. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted that nearly 70% of essential workers held historically "unskilled" positions, earning low wages despite their critical economic importance.

Eric Hirsch, founding CEO of EdReports, will step down at the end of the school year. The Gann Fan is a technical analysis tool created by W.D. Gann that uses nine diagonal lines drawn from significant price points to identify potential support and resistance levels. The main 45-degree line (1:1) represents equal price and time movement, with other lines showing different time-to-price ratios. Cover 1 is a man-to-man defensive coverage with a free safety playing deep zone, allowing defenses to stop the run, blitz, or bracket receivers. Chemical engineer Arthur Potts warned Edmonton city council that declaring the road salting experiment a success is premature. Researchers have developed tiny, resealable synthetic packets tens to hundreds of nanometers across that release contents when exposed to specific light wavelengths. When illuminated, the linking molecules change shape, softening the glassy layer to release contents; when light turns off, the packet reseals. Potential applications include targeted drug delivery and environmental uses. Both polymers used—polyethylene oxide and polylactic acid—are biocompatible and already used in medical treatments. The research team, from the University of Chicago and University of Massachusetts, plans to explore other triggers like pressure or chemical cues. This study describes a Training of Trainers (TOT) intervention for maternal and newborn health (MNH) in Palghar District, Maharashtra, India (2019-2022), building on a pilot in Pune (2017-19). The 32 Palghar MTs (25 doctors, 7 nurses) trained 505 health providers, showing significant post-training improvements in clinical knowledge and skills (abdominal palpation, newborn resuscitation, eclampsia management). Palghar MTs reported gains in clinical competency, training confidence, and career recognition. The study highlights the need for systematic trainer selection, extended supervised practice, hybrid virtual/in-person platforms, and enabling health system conditions for sustainable workforce development.

T-Tamer is a theoretical framework for optimizing bi-objective trade-offs in cascaded inference systems. It formulates routing and termination decisions as a multi-stage costly exploration problem over directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), where nodes represent sub-models and edges encode precedence constraints and performance dependencies. The framework addresses limitations of existing heuristic-driven policies, which lack generalizability and provable efficiency guarantees.

The authors prove that no-recall strategies—where the final prediction must come from the last inspected model—cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to optimal utility, establishing fundamental limitations of confidence-based early-exit heuristics. For with-recall strategies, they develop a dynamic indexing policy that achieves online optimality by computing stop/continue thresholds based on current minimum loss and observed model outputs. This policy runs in O(n) time per input with O(n·|V|²T) preprocessing for directed lines and trees, and O(n²·|V|²T) for transitive closures of directed lines.

Experiments on vision (VGG) and NLP (BERT, GPT-2) early-exit workloads demonstrate that recall-based strategies deliver efficient accuracy–latency trade-offs, reducing latency by 45–90% with limited accuracy degradation.

Sector trading involves buying and selling securities within specific economic sectors, carrying higher risk than broad market investing. Based on JP Morgan research from 1980-2015 analyzing Russell 3000 components, the worst sectors to invest in are information technology, energy, utilities, and materials due to lowest median returns. The median stock produces negative lifetime returns while minority generate spectacular gains, illustrating the difficulty of stock picking and shorting. Inverse thinking—studying failures rather than winners—may improve investment outcomes. AMD's Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables runtime updates to AMD firmware, with the AMD Security Processor (ASP) serving as root of trust for detection. System designers (OEM/ODM) maintain root of trust for update, with optional co-signing of update packages. SFS requires runtime application, does not persist across reboots, and must be enabled via BIOS tokens. Updates require specific memory alignment and follow a defined process: ASP verifies signatures, loads and executes patches, then updates patch level information. SFS packages are versioned, sequentially applied, and must match system firmware combinations. The system boots unpatched, with customers applying patches as needed. Security features include AMD ROM Armor for write protection and attestation support. SEV/SNP updates have specific requirements, with SEV firmware automatically committing and preventing rollback.

This passage develops a theoretical framework for solving the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP), where unknown parameters governing complex systems are inferred from observations using computer models and probability theory. The key contributions include: (1) proving existence of a unique Bayesian posterior distribution with explicit density formula for nonparametric settings; (2) establishing continuity properties of posterior densities; (3) showing the uniform prior maximizes entropy; and (4) developing an asymptotically unbiased, strongly consistent numerical estimator based on importance sampling. The approach uses measure disintegration rather than Bayes' theorem, handling cases where the quantity-of-interest map is not one-to-one through generalized contours. The method differs from traditional Bayesian inverse problems and calibration by targeting distributions of physical parameters rather than point estimates or distributional parameters, with applications including epidemic forecasting, materials design, climate prediction, and gravitational wave analysis.

The Trump administration faces pressure to ensure a smooth end to Affordable Care Act enrollment season, with the deadline of Dec. 15 approaching for 39 states using HealthCare.gov. Research presented at the American Physiological Society's 2018 Experimental Biology meeting found that low "mental energy" affects walking patterns in older adults more than physical fatigue. Clarkson University researchers observed adults averaging 75 years old performing physical and cognitive tasks. While gait showed no change in the first 30 seconds after mental fatigue, walking speed and stride length decreased significantly later in the test for those reporting more cognitive fatigue, unlike physical energy levels which showed no such relationship. The study used LED sensors to capture gait data and the Pearson correlation coefficient to analyze results.

This article presents a method to reduce power consumption in HF-band RFID/NFC systems through dynamic magnetic field strength scaling. The proposed PTF-Determinator method determines the power transfer function during the card detection phase by approximating the physical relation factor (distance) between reader and transponder. The reader scales the magnetic field strength based on this information to avoid oversupplying the transponder. A case study of reading digital business cards demonstrates energy savings of up to 80% in simulation with modified hardware and 26% in real hardware measurements. When applied to a state-of-the-art smartphone, the method could reduce battery drain by approximately 13% during normal operation and 39% when the maximum transmission distance is exceeded.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana "Nevermind" album cover featuring a naked baby underwater is not child pornography, dismissing Spencer Elden's 2021 lawsuit. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found that while the image shows Elden nude at 4 months old, it lacks the lasciviousness required under federal law, comparing it to a family photo of a bathing child.

Jeane Kirkpatrick argued that continuous self-abasement toward the Third World and automatic support for U.S. enemies is unnecessary, and that liberal idealism should not preclude using military force to defend national interests. Singapore's Smart Nation vision, launched in 2014 by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, aims to enable meaningful lives through seamless technology. The World Bank raised China's 2025 GDP growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.5%, citing government stimulus, infrastructure spending, manufacturing support, and recovering exports. The Trump administration's "Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy" aims to increase U.S. breastfeeding rates through WIC and other policies, but experts say federal paid parental leave is critical. In January 1942, former Finnish Foreign Minister Erkko told U.S. Minister Schoenfeld that most Finns favored withdrawing from the war, but timing depended on favorable circumstances when Russia would benefit from Finland's exit and Germany would be indifferent due to successes elsewhere. The 4-2-5 defense combines elements of the 4-3 and 3-3-5 defenses, featuring 4 down linemen, 2 linebackers, and 5 defensive backs with a 6-man box. This study evaluated a brief, individually-tailored digital sleep psychoeducation intervention for 195 older adults with chronic health conditions and low health literacy. Participants, predominantly from minoritized groups with low socioeconomic status, completed a mobile app module covering sleep stages, health condition impacts, sleep hygiene, and sleep restriction strategies. Results showed statistically significant improvements in sleep quality (PSQI scores) with a small to medium effect size (d = 0.40), despite the intervention's brevity. Factors significantly associated with sleep quality included socioeconomic status, health literacy, and total health conditions. The findings suggest that accessible, personalized digital interventions may serve as useful initial components in stepped-care approaches for sleep problems in underserved populations, though more intensive interventions may yield greater clinical benefits.

Micro E-mini futures are 1/10th size futures contracts launched by CME Group in 2019 to make futures trading accessible to retail traders with smaller capital. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré patterns, particularly with Neural Texture Compression, and runs fast on Blackwell GPU due to 2x point-sampled texture filtering rate improvements. Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance information, improving global illumination and dynamic lighting effects in real-time rendering by inferring final lighting values from path-traced rays after one bounce. RTX Skin applies subsurface scattering for realistic translucent materials like skin in real-time path tracing. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to infer more natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data.

The Blackwell GPU architecture includes multiple chips: GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores) powers the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores) powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores) powers the RTX 5070. Fox regarding Alexander McLeod, imprisoned in New York for alleged involvement in the 1837 destruction of the steamboat Caroline. Kay Frazier, 50, died from a blood clot after surgery to remove it, an inquest heard. The Wigan grandmother married American prisoner Gary Frazier in 2012 after exchanging 12,000 letters and visiting him in a Nebraska jail. An international team of physicists from Leiden, Beijing, and Hangzhou used Bell's test to confirm that large quantum systems genuinely obey quantum mechanics. They tested Bell correlations in systems with up to 73 qubits, measuring energies 48 standard deviations below classical possibilities. The team also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations up to 24 qubits. This work demonstrates that quantum computers are becoming more authentically quantum, with applications for secure communication and stronger quantum algorithms.

Advanced attacking runs in soccer require players to anticipate opportunities three or more passes ahead. Individual runs include blind-side runs, drawing defenders out, inverted runs, overlap/underlap runs, third-man running, late runs, and deep-lying runs. Planned runs involve designed routes, runs to receive specific passes, and fast breaks. Key considerations include avoiding offside positions, proper timing, and unpredictability. Supporting runs maintain possession through back-pass options, square pass options, and swinging the ball. Effective attacking runs require successful passes, with only one runner receiving the ball at a time. Players should scout opponents to optimize runs.

A peer-to-peer interview study of 21 medical students identified four factors influencing decisions to report mistreatment: personal concerns about repercussions and sense of justice; situational factors including severity of incidents and bystander inaction; structural barriers like unclear reporting processes and perceived futility; and climate factors including expected hierarchy and normalized abuse. Only 12 of 34 described incidents were reported. Students cited fear of retaliation, ambiguous definitions of mistreatment, lack of confidence in institutional response, and belief that abuse is culturally expected as primary barriers. The study recommends improving reporting systems through transparency, anonymity protections, bystander training, and top-down cultural change.

A research paper in *Climate Change* argues that the 939–940 CE Eldgjá eruption, the largest lava flood eruption of the Common Era, may have encouraged Iceland's Christianization. The eruption caused devastating climate effects, blocking sunlight and harming agriculture. Iceland officially converted to Christianity in 999/1000 CE following a parliament at Þingvellir. Later traditions, including the 13th-century *Kristni saga*, also associated volcanic events with the conversion.

The authors examine border-crossing in language teacher education across English as a Second Language (ESL), World Languages (WL), and Bilingual Education (BE), applying Valdés' framework of language curricularization to analyze how theories, ideologies, policies, and contexts shape these fields. They trace the historical development of U.S. language education from English-only assimilationist policies through Cold War-era federal initiatives to contemporary program models, noting persistent inequities where minoritized emergent bilingual learners face subtractive schooling while English-speaking students receive enrichment through WL study.

The authors describe three phases of curricular innovation at their Chicago institution: Phase 1 redesigned ESL methods to emphasize translanguaging pedagogy and serve diverse candidates including WL teachers; Phase 2 created a combined ESL/WL methods course for Chinese language teachers, incorporating multilingual approaches and cross-program collaboration; Phase 3 (planned) will develop BE methods to train WL educators as bilingual educators through critical curricular analysis. Throughout, they utilize a heteroglossic vision acknowledging learners' dynamic linguistic repertoires rather than parallel monolingualisms.

Key priorities include documenting candidates' linguistic histories, building critical consciousness through drama-based pedagogy, and examining how ideologies shape program elements. The authors argue that regular curriculum review, cross-program collaboration, and explicit modeling of desired practices enhance teacher preparation, while acknowledging constraints from divergent program structures and enrollment patterns. They advocate for maintaining distinct field identities while fostering historical awareness and pedagogical flexibility across language teacher education.

Construction crews on the $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium project have exceeded minority hiring goals, with 54 percent of work hours completed by minorities, women and military veterans since November, surpassing the 38 percent target. The Community Benefits Oversight Committee received this update at its inaugural meeting Monday. Of $509 million in subcontracts, $91 million (18 percent) has gone to 32 small-business-enterprise companies, exceeding the 15 percent goal set in Senate Bill 1. The company operates through two main segment groups: Devices and Consumer (including Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, and Other) and Commercial (including Licensing and Other). MIT professor introduces 6.451, a course on coding for digital communications offered in alternate years. The class will be videotaped for OpenCourseWare. Four handouts are distributed: information sheet, personal data sheet, first problem set (due in one week), and chapters 1-3. Teaching assistant Ashish Khisti will guest lecture for sessions 2-4 while the professor is on vacation; his office hours are tentatively Tuesdays 5-7 PM in Building 32. The midterm is scheduled for March 16, the Wednesday before MIT's vacation week, and will run two hours.

The prerequisite 6.450 is enforced rigorously not for content but for mathematical sophistication. The course focuses on coding over the additive white Gaussian noise channel, covering algebraic block codes, convolutional codes, tail-biting codes, capacity-approaching codes, low-density parity-check codes, lattice codes, and trellis coded modulation with their decoding algorithms. No single textbook covers all material; the professor provides his own course notes.

Problem sets are weekly (except before exams and the final week), intended for learning rather than strict grading; they carry 15% weight primarily to ensure completion. The midterm counts 1/3 and the final 1/2 of the grade. This year, non-essential topics will be cut to allow more time for capacity-approaching codes and possibly codes for band-limited channels.

The professor reviews chapters 1-3 rapidly: chapter 1 introduces the additive white Gaussian noise channel with parameters power P, noise spectral density N₀, and bandwidth W, yielding signal-to-noise ratio P/(N₀W). The Shannon capacity formula is C = W log₂(1 + SNR) bits per second. Chapter 2 covers conversion from continuous-time to discrete-time channels via orthonormal PAM, showing equivalent SNR and spectral efficiency ρ = R/W bits/Hz (or ρ/2 bits per two dimensions in discrete time). Chapter 3 contains the capacity formula derivation, which students may read independently.

This article compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) and lump-sum investing strategies through backtests of S&P 500 returns from 2000-2019. Studies show lump-sum investing outperforms DCA most of the time, with Morningstar finding DCA beats lump-sum only 27.8% of the time over 10-month periods and 10% over 10-year periods. However, DCA helps mitigate behavioral biases and removes timing anxiety. The article demonstrates sequence of returns risk by reshuffling returns: when strong returns occurred early (while cash was high) and weak returns later (when fully invested), DCA's final value dropped from $173,949 to $87,396 and CAGR fell from 5.5% to 1.9%, while lump-sum results remained stable. The conclusion favors lump-sum investing when capital is available, noting that randomness affects DCA more than commonly assumed.

The passage reviews nine Vanguard ETFs for ultimate diversification: VTI (U.S. total stock market), VT (world stocks), VXUS (international stocks), VNQ (U.S. real estate), VNQI (global ex-U.S. real estate), VTC (U.S. corporate bonds), BND (U.S. total bond market), BNDX (international bonds), and BNDW (world bonds). Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference after presenters were ordered to remove terms including "DEI," "diversity," "equity," and "inclusion" from their slides due to state law HB 261. The conference, themed "Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship," was organized by the Student Access and Success division rather than an academic unit, making it subject to stricter rules. Associate professor Sarah Herrmann and other faculty withdrew rather than censor their research. The university acknowledged communication could have been clearer and is considering restructuring future conferences under Academic Affairs to exempt them from the law.

This address to Congress covers foreign and domestic affairs, including Indian treaty negotiations with the Creeks, implementation of treaties with Britain (receiving posts like Niagara and Detroit) and Spain (boundary commissions), arrangements with Algiers for prisoner release, and injuries to American trade from French cruisers in the West Indies. The speaker recommends creating a navy, encouraging manufactures (with exceptions for essential military supplies), promoting agriculture through public institutions, establishing a national university and military academy, revising officer compensation, improving militia efficiency, securing harbors, and accelerating public debt repayment. The address concludes by congratulating Congress on the success of the government experiment and offering supplications for its perpetuation.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated April 23, 2001, contains news summaries about Enron and energy-related developments. Key stories include: PG&E CEO Robert Glynn's miscalculations leading to Pacific Gas & Electric's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing; Tri-State Generation & Transmission's proposal for a $1.3 billion, 1,200-megawatt coal-fired plant in Colorado; Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi's planned meeting with U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to discuss oil prices; Enron's India unit Dabhol Power Company meeting lenders in London regarding payment defaults by Maharashtra State Electricity Board and seeking approval to potentially terminate the $3 billion project; Mangalore Power Company halving its project capacity to avoid a "Dabhol-like situation"; ONGC disputing Enron's claims about the Moon Prospect gas well at Tapti fields; and Spain's government planning electricity market reforms to increase competition against dominant utilities.

Eilish McCready, 25, founded Fearless Theatre School in Glasgow a year ago to provide inclusive drama classes focused on personal development rather than performances. The small classes welcome all children, including shy children and those with additional needs such as autism, using drama to build confidence and social skills without pressure. McCready was inspired by her own negative experience with performance pressure as a child. Lizanne Conway, whose three sons have autism, says the classes have helped her older boys' confidence and social skills, noting the staff are positive, caring and genuinely inclusive. Lisa Byrne says her shy daughter Rua has gained confidence, started a YouTube channel, and now performs in public after attending Fearless classes.

Enron faces financial turmoil as its stock price plummeted from over $80 to $19.79, with shares dropping more than 40% in one week. The company disclosed a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in write-offs, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity related to partnerships headed by CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC opened an informal inquiry into Fastow's transactions, prompting a conference call where CEO Kenneth Lay defended Fastow and claimed adequate liquidity, though analysts criticized Enron's lack of transparency. Enron may need to issue up to $1 billion in stock to cover $3.3 billion in notes from investment vehicles, though Treasurer Ben Glisan stated asset sales could raise $2.2 billion. This winter, offshore fishing will feature sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish. Anglers should head south and let the current carry them north, targeting 160' depth for sailfish off the Dodge Wall and 90' for kingfish. Live bait is essential and available from bait boats on VHF 68. Kite fishing will be prominent, though flat lining and deep rods also work; wire leaders are recommended for wahoo and kingfish. Inshore, the inlet will host schools of jack and tarpon along beaches and the ICW, requiring fish finders to locate them. Spawning sheepshead will be on channel bottoms, best caught with shrimp or clams.

A study published October 8 found that ChatGPT generates resumes for women that are on average younger and less experienced than those for men, then ranks female applicants as less qualified. Researchers analyzed 1.4 million online images and videos, finding coders consistently rated women as younger than men, especially in prestigious occupations. Text analysis confirmed this bias, linking younger females with less prestigious jobs and older males with more prestigious ones. An experiment with 450 people showed that viewing online images influenced age perceptions of workers. The study demonstrates how AI models trained on biased online content inherit and amplify gendered ageism, which may help explain why women face barriers to advancement despite diversity hiring efforts. Researchers note that addressing single biases like sexism or racism separately overlooks intersecting inequalities.

The SPY and XLU rotating system is a weekly rotation strategy between the S&P 500 (SPY) and Utilities (XLU) based on past performance, published by Michael Gayed in 2014. The strategy relies on utilities' sensitivity to interest rates—they outperform when rates fall and underperform when rates rise. While the strategy showed strong historical performance since 1926 (13.1% annual returns) and outperformed from 1999-2014 (6.7% vs. 4.6% buy-and-hold), it has lagged the market by over 5% annually since publication (5.1% vs. 10.4%) and failed to recover from the 2020 COVID crash. The underperformance may reflect strategy decay after publication, though the period may be too short to confirm the strategy no longer works.

Researchers are rebranding grape pomace as a renewable resource for health products, including antioxidants, grape oils, and dietary fibers. Grape waste, which causes environmental pollution and attracts pests, totals 14 million tons annually from global wine production. Changmou Xu's team is developing technologies to extract nutrients from pomace while removing pesticides, testing applications in food preservation, animal health, and reducing foodborne pathogens. They aim to replace artificial antioxidants like EDTA with natural phenolic compounds from pomace to meet consumer demand for clean label ingredients.

Game is selling an Xbox One S (500GB) bundle for £249.99, including Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. The individual items cost £297.10 on Amazon UK, offering a £47.11 saving. The Xbox One S received a 4/5 score for its small size, 4K upscaling, and value as a UHD Blu-ray player. All bundled games scored well: Forza Horizon 3 (5/5), Tekken 7 (4/5), Halo 5 (4/5), and Gears of War 4 (4.5/5).

This clinical study of BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA COVID-19 vaccines was conducted at 153 locations across 6 countries from April 29, 2020 to February 10, 2023. The study included healthy children and adults aged 12 years and older without prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Phase 1 involved 195 participants aged 19-82 years receiving two doses of BNT162b1, BNT162b2, or placebo. Phase 2/3 involved 46,406 participants aged 12-91 years receiving two doses of BNT162b2 or placebo, with 99% receiving at least one vaccine dose.

The study design began as observer-blinded, later becoming open-label for initial doses, with booster doses generally administered open-label. Participants remained in the study for up to 26 months.

BNT162b2 demonstrated 95% effectiveness in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 compared to placebo. Immune response measurements showed antibody levels after BNT162b2 booster doses were comparable to levels after the primary series, with BNT162b2SA showing similar immune responses against the Beta variant.

Safety results indicated the vaccines were generally well tolerated. Most injection site reactions and systemic events were mild or moderate, with pain at the injection site and tiredness/headache being most common. In Phase 2/3, less than 1% of participants in either vaccine or placebo groups left due to medical problems. Serious medical problems were rare, with researchers not believing they were related to the vaccine. No participant died in Phase 1; in Phase 2/3, deaths occurred across groups from various causes not attributed to the vaccine.

NASA's Cassini spacecraft completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn on August 14, 2017, skimming 1,010-1,060 miles above the clouds. The 20-year mission will end September 15 with Cassini becoming the first Saturn atmospheric probe. The team may adjust the second pass to 120 miles closer based on atmospheric density results. Instruments will gather data on cloud-top atmosphere, temperature, auroras, vortices, and chemical composition. Cassini will also attempt to determine Saturn's day length by examining magnetic field and axial tilt offset. The probe, low on fuel, was directed into Saturn to avoid contaminating Titan or Enceladus, potential life candidates. Titan altered Cassini's flight path throughout the mission and will trigger its final descent on September 11.

This patent application describes methods for characterizing states, functions, and tissue contact of ultrasonic surgical device end effectors by measuring and analyzing ultrasonic transducer impedance values. The system applies power to an ultrasonic transducer, measures impedance, compares it to reference values, classifies the impedance, and characterizes the end effector state or tissue type to adjust power levels accordingly. The application claims priority to numerous related patent applications spanning surgical network control, situational awareness, smart energy devices, and various surgical instrument technologies. The disclosed system includes a modular surgical hub with integrated generator, smoke evacuation, and suction/irrigation modules that communicate with cloud-based analytics, visualization systems, robotic systems, and handheld intelligent surgical instruments. The hub facilitates coordinated information flow between sterile and non-sterile field operators through multiple displays and enables real-time data processing for improved surgical outcomes.

This MIT lecture introduces plasma diagnostics, explaining that diagnostics allow indirect measurement of plasma properties like density, temperature, and velocity through physical effects, since direct observation is impossible. The course requires prior plasma physics knowledge (MIT 22.611) and draws from Francis Chen's textbook. The instructor emphasizes that diagnostics are essential for meaningful plasma experiments, illustrated by historical examples: the 1950s ZETA pinch's false fusion claims due to insufficient diagnostics, and how Thomson scattering development enabled verification of Russian tokamak temperature claims, transforming fusion research. Similarly, the National Ignition Facility's initial lack of diagnostics led to years of confusion before achieving ignition once proper measurements were implemented. The lecture identifies three audiences for diagnostics knowledge: experimentalists (to understand measurement uncertainty), computational researchers (for code validation), and theorists (to design testable predictions and evaluate experimental claims). Theoretical ideals like complete particle position and velocity data are impossible; practical diagnostics measure moments like density and average velocity, or magnetic fields, but face limitations including spatial/temporal sparsity, line integration (especially for light-based measurements), instrument filtering effects, and dependence on poorly understood physics like atomic data. The course focuses on enduring principles rather than changing implementations. The lecture concludes with an interactive exercise where students map their plasma research across 16 orders of magnitude in density (10^16–10^32 m^-3), temperature (0.1 eV–10+ keV), and magnetic field (0.01–100+ tesla), identifying diagnostics used in devices including tokamaks (DIII-D, ASDEX Upgrade, SPARC, CNT), inertial confinement fusion (NIF), pulsed power machines (Z, magLIF), and other configurations.

The Rams have requested permission from the Jaguars to interview Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy. Marrone went 1-1 as Jacksonville's interim coach after serving two seasons as their offensive line coach. He previously coached the Bills from 2013-2014, improving their record from 6-10 to 9-7 before opting out of his contract. The Jaguars may also remove Marrone's interim tag to make him their permanent head coach.

North America segment sales grew 24% to $13.4 billion with operating income of $517 million; International sales declined 2% to $7.7 billion with an operating loss of $76 million; AWS sales increased 49% to $1.6 billion with operating income of $265 million. Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $3.2 billion compared to $1.5 billion in the prior year period. The company changed its reportable segments beginning Q1 2015 to North America, International, and AWS. The filing discloses ongoing legal proceedings including patent infringement cases and tax disputes with the IRS and French Tax Administration.

This case study examines Tesla's financial situation in 2017-2018 as the company faced potential liquidity challenges while ramping up Model 3 production. Founded in 2003, Tesla grew into the world's leading EV manufacturer under Elon Musk's leadership, launching the Roadster (2008), Model S (2012), Model X (2015), and Model 3 (2017). Despite becoming the most valuable American automaker by market capitalization in April 2017, Tesla struggled with profitability and negative operating cash flow. The company repeatedly raised capital through equity and debt offerings, nearly doubling shares outstanding and accumulating over $10 billion in long-term debt between 2010-2017. Model 3 production delays and accelerated cash burn raised investor concerns about whether Tesla could raise additional needed capital, with one Goldman Sachs analyst predicting over $10 billion in required external financing by 2020. Musk's 2018 statement that Tesla would not need equity or debt raises that year echoed a similar 2012 claim, leaving the company's survival dependent on balancing capital needs with investor willingness to provide funding.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture introduces multiple advancements including GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% improved power efficiency over GDDR5X, redesigned memory interface circuits for speed and noise reduction, and doubled L2 cache (6 MB in TU102). Turing features RT Cores for real-time ray tracing acceleration, delivering 10+ Giga Rays/Sec compared to Pascal's 1.1 Giga Rays/Sec, and Tensor Cores for AI operations including DLSS for image quality improvement with reduced shading work. The architecture supports hybrid rendering combining ray tracing and rasterization, Variable Rate Shading for optimized shading rates, Texture Space Shading for decoupled visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering for up to four views per pass. Turing includes hardware support for USB-C and VirtualLink for simplified VR connectivity, an enhanced display engine supporting 8K at 60 Hz with DisplayPort 1.4a and DSC 1.2, and improved NVENC/NVDEC for video encoding/decoding. The architecture comes in three variants: TU102 (RTX 2080 Ti), TU104 (RTX 2080), and TU106 (RTX 2070), with TU102 and TU104 supporting NVLink for improved SLI bandwidth.

Hurricane Harvey may have damaged or destroyed up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast, including nesting sites and marshes home to threatened and endangered species. Aransas National Wildlife Refuge sustained damage to salt marshes where endangered whooping cranes feed, while Attwater Prairie Chicken National Wildlife Refuge saw endangered prairie chicken populations drop from about 60 to as few as 10. State and federal agencies are conducting initial damage assessments with more detailed monitoring to follow. Scientists are factoring climate change into wildlife sanctuary management due to increasing storm size and intensity. Some marine species like shrimp and crabs appear to have survived, though many oyster beds were lost, and bottlenose dolphins may have been injured by freshwater inflows.

This study introduces a method to analyze public transit hierarchy based on real passenger travel patterns using smart card data from Seoul. The ascending-descending method classifies trip stages by half of total travel distance to construct transfer rate matrices and quantify hierarchical differences between modes. Applied to 10.2 million trip chains from November 2019, results show consistent hierarchy (walking < community bus < urban bus < light rail < metro) within Seoul, with intercity bus ranking highest in interzonal trips. The method reveals regional variations in modal hierarchy, such as metro ranking higher in Seoul while intercity buses rank higher in Gyeonggi and Incheon, demonstrating that hierarchy varies by geographic context rather than being spatially homogeneous.

In a 1995 Louisiana Court of Appeal case, Jerry Wayne Hill sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury after his 15-year-old son Michael drowned when a car driven by an intoxicated teenager plunged into Bayou Bartholomew at an unmarked "T" intersection. The trial court found the police jury 20% at fault for inadequate warnings and the driver 80% at fault. The appellate court affirmed the finding of liability but amended the fault allocation to 35% for the police jury and 65% for the driver, noting the police jury knew of the intersection's danger and had failed to maintain a double arrow sign for three months prior to the accident. The $150,000 general damage award was affirmed.

This study assessed the potential of green open access (self-archiving) to increase discoverability of clinical trial results publications using automated tools. Analyzing 1,897 clinical trial publications from German university medical centers (2010–2020), researchers found 54% were openly accessible (gold, hybrid, bronze, or green OA), while 46% remained closed-access. Of the closed-access publications, 85% had publisher permissions to self-archive postprints in institutional repositories, typically after 12-month embargoes. However, only 16% of publications with self-archiving permissions were actually archived as green OA, indicating substantial unrealized potential. The study used Shareyourpaper to determine article-level self-archiving permissions and Unpaywall to assess OA status. Researchers noted that low self-archiving rates likely reflect lack of awareness, absence of institutional mandates in Germany, and researcher autonomy, contrasting with countries having stronger OA policies. The approach enables scalable identification of archivable publications to support institutional and broader interventions.

Natural gas prices held at $3.27/MMBtu, constrained within a descending wedge pattern since March. U.S. exports are rising due to Europe's LNG demand, but domestic oversupply and seasonal factors maintain price pressure and volatility.

Global stock markets rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen indicated potential interest rate increases as soon as March, signaling confidence in U.S. economic strength.
