Gary Gensler, Senior Lecturer at MIT Sloan and advisor at MIT Media Lab, introduces a course on blockchain and finance. He surveys students on cryptocurrency ownership and blockchain project experience, finding about 45% and 33% respectively. The course will examine whether blockchain might catalyze change in finance, focusing on blockchain fundamentals, economics, and financial sector use cases.

Gensler traces internet history from 1974 through TCP/IP, HTTP (1990), and early commercialization, noting PizzaNet's 1995 online ordering problem: inability to pay online. He explains cryptography as secure communication against adversaries, from ancient ciphers to MIT-developed public-key cryptography, which enables SSL/TLS securing modern internet commerce.

Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 Halloween email proposed "a new electronic cash system that's fully peer-to-peer with no trusted third party." Blockchain technology—time-stamped append-only logs secured by cryptography, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols—solved the "Byzantian Generals problem" of peer-to-peer value transfer without centralized intermediaries. The first Bitcoin transaction for goods occurred May 2010 when Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 Bitcoins (then ~$41, now ~$66 million) for two pizzas.

Blockchain verifiably moves data on decentralized networks through economics of verification and networking. It offers opportunities in finance—moving money and risk—where centralized intermediaries collect significant economic rents (7.5% of US GDP, $1.5 trillion). Challenges include performance/scalability (Bitcoin: ~7 transactions/second vs. Visa: 20,000-70,000), privacy, interoperability, and governance. Permissioned blockchains (controlled nodes) currently dominate financial sector interest over permissionless systems like Bitcoin.

The $200 billion crypto finance market remains modest against global capital markets ($300+ trillion). Public policy issues include illicit activity, financial stability, capital controls, and investor protection. The course emphasizes critical reasoning across technology, markets, law, and social norms, requiring class participation (30%), two individual write-ups, and a team project proposing a blockchain use case in finance.

Digital laggards tightly control data access, hoarding it as power and favoring "business judgment" over data-driven decisions, while digital leaders encourage transparent data access and measurement to learn. Digital leaders use standardized APIs (88% vs. 27%), embrace detailed metrics for flexible goal achievement, and align organizations through transparent, data-driven objectives developed via combined top-down and bottom-up processes. A retail case study shows how real-time sales reporting enabled nimble, data-driven decisions. Digital laggards set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, causing employees to avoid measurement and focus on process adherence rather than outcomes, stifling innovation. Data culture aligns organizations vertically (individual to company goals) and horizontally (cross-functional collaboration). Four organizational patterns emerge: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—each requiring targeted actions to build strong data culture.

Interest in psychedelic substances for therapeutic use has resurged, leading to drug-facilitated psychotherapy as a new psychiatric approach. A pooled analysis of six Phase II trials found 54% of PTSD patients no longer met diagnostic criteria after MDMA-assisted therapy. The FDA designated MDMA-assisted therapy as a breakthrough therapy for PTSD based on positive results showing significant, sustained symptom reduction and acceptable safety. A recent Phase 3 multisite study confirmed its safety and efficacy in severe PTSD, demonstrating significant attenuation in symptom severity compared to placebo with therapy.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 28, 2016, announcing its fourth quarter 2015 and year ended December 31, 2015 financial results. The filing includes two exhibits: a press release with the financial results announcement and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Ireland is highly exposed to exchange rate fluctuations, particularly involving the euro, dollar, and sterling. The weak euro against the dollar has attracted record numbers of American tourists, while weak sterling against the euro has reduced UK visitors. Sterling fell from 76 pence to 91 pence against the euro since the Brexit referendum, though the euro itself has strengthened against the dollar from $1.05 to $1.18 due to expectations of ending quantitative easing and rising eurozone interest rates. The author believes euro appreciation exceeds ECB preferences, as low rates support export-driven recovery. Historical euro mean was $1.35, which could mean euro-sterling parity. Tourism businesses cannot practically hedge currency exposure. UK importers benefit from cheap sterling and should hedge to lock in advantages. UK exporters face difficulties and need hedging strategies, such as incurring costs in the destination currency. Weak sterling also harms the car industry through cheap UK second-hand car imports.

Cleveland Browns coach Kevin Stefanski has not committed to naming rookie Shedeur Sanders as the backup quarterback following the trade of Joe Flacco to Cincinnati. Stefanski stated he will "let the week play out" before deciding on the QB2 role between Sanders and fellow rookie Will Zappe. Sanders, a fifth-round draft pick, has been inactive through five games as the emergency quarterback. The Browns traded Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick for a 2026 fifth-round pick, leaving only Sanders and Zappe on the active roster. Stefanski emphasized his focus on player development when making roster decisions. Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders for his professionalism. Deshaun Watson remains on the physically unable to perform list rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study found that 21% of women and 10% of men in their 50s and early 60s (Generation X and late Baby Boomers) meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, significantly higher than the 12% of women and 4% of men aged 65-80. Researchers attribute this disparity to this generation being the first to grow up surrounded by ultra-processed foods and to 1980s marketing of "diet" products like low-fat cookies targeted at women. Using the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 with over 2,000 participants, the study found addiction correlated with being overweight (women 11 times more likely, men 19 times more likely), poor physical or mental health, and social isolation. Experts warn that children today consume even higher proportions of ultra-processed foods, potentially leading to greater addiction rates in future generations.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note in circulation and issue the £10 polymer note as planned in September, despite concerns over traces of animal fats. The bank confirmed an "extremely small amount" of tallow was used in production but rejected alternatives as costly and compromising anti-counterfeit measures. Over 134,000 people signed a petition against the notes. The Bank has delayed supply contracts for the £20 note, due in 2020, to consider plant-based substitutes and will launch a public consultation, with a final decision expected by summer 2017.

Qarlinngua, meaning "like pants" in Inuktitut, is a 50+ metre tall sea arch located 80-90 km southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut, on Baffin Island's Brodeur Peninsula. First photographed publicly by hunter Max Kalluk in August, the formation was initially dismissed as fake online and by tourism officials before geologists confirmed its authenticity. Formed by erosion of Paleozoic sedimentary rock (250-600 million years old) as rising seas and open water wear away softer material while quartz-rich sections resist erosion, the arch is accessible only by boat during brief summer windows when sea ice breaks up. Arctic Bay Adventures is currently the sole tour operator visiting the site, which geologists estimate could collapse within decades to thousands of years. Nunavut's tourism department plans to promote Qarlinngua to high-income travellers despite limited accessibility and expensive travel costs.

This study examines career transitions of lecturers and education personnel in Indonesian higher education institutions using grounded theory. Research focuses on civil servants (PNS) who hold dual roles as both lecturers/functional staff and campus administrators. Pre-research indicates lecturers shifting to administrative roles experience declining performance in teaching, research, and community service (Tri Dharma). Education personnel face unclear career paths due to bureaucratic reforms eliminating certain structural positions.

The study applies Schlossberg's 4 S transition theory (situation, self, support, strategies) and finds four new dimensions: new tasks, strengths/weaknesses, organizational support, and reciprocal relationships between factors. Data was collected through snowball sampling of six key informants from three university types, using semi-structured interviews and NVIVO 12 Pro analysis through open, axial, and selective coding.

Findings reveal career transitions produce changes in behavior (burnout, motivation, competence, self-discipline, identity), roles (dual campus and social/family roles), learning (especially during COVID-19), and perception. Unlike Schein's single career anchor theory, informants use two anchors: competence and managerial. Limitations include narrow institutional focus, lack of generalizability, absence of demographic analysis, and potential researcher bias as an education staff member.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K Current Report dated September 10, 2019, disclosing that Bob Iger resigned from the company's Board of Directors on that date. The report was signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on September 13, 2019.

A hockey player discusses returning to play after a head injury, noting he felt comfortable despite taking a hit in his second shift. He mentions dehydration and cramping from recent travel for a CT scan in Denver. His doctor from Duke reviewed the scan and confirmed his risk level is similar to what it will be in September, three and a half months post-injury. He expresses gratitude for the opportunity to contribute to his team's success and emphasizes the importance of playing better and harder for a potential Stanley Cup win at home. He notes the supportive environment from family, medical staff, and management regarding his return.
The Mayor, etc., of the City of New York v. Collis P. Huntington: Appeal from judgment for plaintiff affirmed with costs, based on trial judge's opinion.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of mathematics anxiety research from 2013 to 2023 using Scopus database data analyzed with VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Publications increased annually, peaking at 56 documents in 2022, with research concentrated in social sciences (35.1%) and psychology (30.7%). Network visualization reveals seven clusters connecting mathematics anxiety to cognitive variables (performance, working memory, skills) and affective variables (emotion, motivation, self-efficacy, gender). Among 168 publishing journals, Frontiers in Psychology leads with 39 documents and 55,251 citations (Q2), alongside Q1 journals including the Journal of Educational Psychology. Analysis of 978 authors identifies Garcia-Santillan as most productive (10 publications, 143 citations), while Pekrun Reinhard has the highest citation count (985). Geographically, 78 countries contribute, with the United States leading in publications (62 documents) and international collaborations, followed by the United Kingdom (48) and Germany (32). The University of Barcelona is the most productive affiliate (23 documents). The study concludes that mathematics anxiety research has expanded significantly across disciplines, with strong international collaboration and publication in high-impact journals.

North Korea warned the US it is ready to retaliate with nuclear attacks during a military parade marking the 105th anniversary of Kim Il-sung's birth. The parade displayed new intercontinental and submarine-launched ballistic missiles. Senior official Choe Ryong-hae stated North Korea would respond to all-out war with all-out war. The event occurred amid speculation of a new nuclear test and rising tensions, with North Korea recently calling President Trump "foolish" and Trump responding that North Korea is "looking for trouble." China's Foreign Minister warned conflict could break out at any moment with no winners, and no Chinese representatives appeared at the parade.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2020 reports financial results including revenue of $3.87 billion (up 50% year-over-year), net income of $622 million, and diluted EPS of $0.99. The company completed its $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies on April 27, 2020, which contributed approximately 14% of total revenue. Operating segments were restructured to Graphics and Compute & Networking. The company issued $5 billion in notes in March 2020. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $10.98 billion. The report includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes covering business combinations, leases, stock-based compensation, debt, segment information, and legal proceedings including securities class action litigation.

This patent application describes a detection model training method and apparatus for medical imaging, particularly for colorectal polyp detection. The method addresses limitations in existing deep learning systems that require large amounts of labeled training data and suffer from accuracy reduction when deployed across different hospitals due to domain differences in image data.

The proposed solution uses an initial training model comprising an initial detection model and an adaptive model. The training sample includes source domain data (labeled images with target object presence indicators and domain identifiers) and target domain data (unlabeled images with only domain identifiers). The method involves: determining whether target objects are present in source domain images through the initial detection model; determining domain classifications for all images through the adaptive model; calculating loss function values based on detection results, domain classification results, and identifiers; and adjusting parameter values to obtain a final detection model.

The adaptive model may include a gradient inversion module that creates an adversarial relationship with the feature extraction module, enabling extraction of domain-invariant features. This approach allows unlabeled target domain data to be used for training, increasing sample size and improving model accuracy while reducing labeling costs. The method is implemented through a training apparatus with specialized units and can be deployed on terminal devices with processors and storage media.

This email from Ann Schmidt dated May 25, 2001, contains news clippings about Enron. The New York Times reports that Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay offered Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Curtis Hebert Jr. continued support in exchange for changing his views on electricity deregulation; Hebert refused. The article notes Enron's significant political influence, including Lay's role in recommending FERC candidates and access to Vice President Cheney's energy task force. Multiple sources report on the escalating dispute between Enron's Dabhol Power Co. and India's Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which canceled its power purchase agreement, claiming misrepresentation about plant capacity. Dabhol disputes this and had previously issued its own termination notice over $48-64 million in unpaid bills. The $3 billion project, India's largest foreign investment, faces potential $2 billion in government obligations if terminated. Bechtel threatened to withdraw from the project by May 31 if unpaid. Other articles cover California officials' harsh rhetoric against Enron, Australian firms' continued interest in India's power sector despite the controversy, and El Paso Corp. Chairman William Wise agreeing to testify in a federal hearing on California gas price manipulation allegations.

Teams must prepare for three jump ball situations. Defensive jump balls occur when opponents have height or jumping advantages, requiring early rotations, watching the jumper's eyes and hands for direction tells, and alignments like Box, Diamond, or "Y" with back defenders to prevent easy shots. Even jump balls provide equal chances, requiring boxing out, anticipation, and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations on predetermined signals. Offensive jump balls utilize 6-inch or greater height advantages through set plays including Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, generally tipping forward to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance.

Apple removed several ICE-tracking apps from its App Store in October following claims from US Attorney General Pam Bondi that such tools endanger ICE officers. Developers including Joshua Aaron of ICEBlock and Mark of Eyes Up are appealing the decisions and pursuing legal action. Apple justified DEICER's removal under guidelines prohibiting defamatory content toward targeted groups, while Google—which also removed similar apps—considers ICE officers a vulnerable group. Legal experts say the apps constitute protected First Amendment speech. The removals highlight concerns about centralized platform control, particularly Apple's closed ecosystem which lacks Android's sideloading alternative. Stanford researcher Riana Pfefferkorn criticized Apple's actions as "needless kowtowing" to the Trump administration.

NASA's Terra satellite captured images of Tropical Depression 02W's remnants in the South China Sea on April 17, 2017. The depression made landfall in the eastern Visayas on April 15 with 25-knot winds, weakened to a remnant low while crossing the Philippines, and exited into the South China Sea. By April 17, the remnant low was located 230 nautical miles west of Manila, moving west with a compact closed circulation. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center indicated wind shear and drier air would prevent re-intensification.

Alberta's education minister David Eggen indicated the province may allow parents to pay school bus fees despite Bill 1 eliminating such fees for students living 2.4+ km from school. Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million transportation shortfall affecting 24,000 students. The board surveyed parents on alternatives including longer commutes and changed bell times. Parents expressed willingness to pay previous fees. The shortfall stems from stagnant provincial grants, carbon levies, and Bill 1. The board's April 12 decision deadline may be extended following discussions with the Ministry of Education.

The Supreme Court considered whether the double jeopardy clause bars separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm to advance a violent crime or drug-trafficking offense, while Section 924(j) applies when such conduct causes death. The parties agreed that double jeopardy generally bars simultaneous convictions for lesser and greater included offenses, unless Congress clearly intended otherwise. Justices debated whether Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii)'s consecutive-sentencing language or the "in addition to" language in Section 924(c) provided clear congressional intent for cumulative punishment. The government argued Section 924(j) lacks language authorizing cumulative punishment with its predicate offense. Justice Gorsuch questioned the precedent requiring clear congressional indication for cumulative punishment, though this issue was not fully briefed.

This section provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for Texas Instruments devices, including status definitions, material types, RoHS values, lead finish options, MSL ratings, and part marking conventions. The data is subject to change without notice. TI provides all technical data and resources "as is" without warranties, and users are solely responsible for selecting appropriate products and ensuring their applications meet all applicable requirements. TI disclaims liability beyond the annual purchase price of affected parts.

This passage describes a study developing resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI-based classifiers for schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD). The research addresses four key challenges in biomarker development: accuracy, generalisability, across-session variability, and specificity. Using LASSO and voting machine learning algorithms on harmonized multi-site datasets (1,015 discovery, 683 validation participants), the classifiers achieved approximately 79.6% accuracy (AUC 0.876) in discovery and 77.3% accuracy (AUC 0.824) in validation. The study identified 47 important functional connections, with notable laterality effects in seven brain regions. Voting classifiers showed improved sensitivity over LASSO, particularly for early-stage patients. The research also explored whether diagnostic biomarkers could function as state and staging markers by examining relationships with symptom severity scales.

Amazon's mobile accessory kit enables Alexa integration in wireless earbuds and wearables. The Jabra Elite 65t ($170) are among the first earbuds using this kit, but Alexa functionality is limited compared to smart speakers. Key limitations include: no phone calls or music from popular streaming services (only Amazon Music works), Android-only support initially with iOS coming later, no reminders, limited navigation capabilities, and no text messaging. The earbuds do offer good call quality, multi-room audio control, access to 30,000+ Alexa skills, and superior voice shopping. Sound quality is excellent with effective noise isolation and a comfortable fit, featuring HearThrough for ambient sound. Battery life totals 15 hours (5 hours plus 10 in case), below competitors' 24 hours, and lacks a tracker feature if lost. Alexa performs adequately for basic tasks but requires phone interaction for many functions, undermining the hands-free purpose. Feature updates are planned, but full smart speaker parity remains unavailable.

Shohei Ohtani made his first postseason pitching start in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS between the Dodgers and Phillies on October 4 at Citizens Bank Park. Ohtani, who went 1-1 with a 2.87 ERA in 14 regular season appearances, faced Phillies ace Christopher Sanchez (13-5, 2.50 ERA). Manager Dave Roberts hoped Ohtani could pitch six-plus innings. Ohtani retired Trea Turner, Kyle Schwarber, and Bryce Harper in order in the first inning, then struck out in his first at-bat against Sanchez. The game aired on TBS and truTV and streamed on HBO Max.

After the Las Vegas mass shooting at a country music festival that killed 58 people and injured over 500, country musician Charlie Daniels called the attack an "anomaly" and warned against letting fear win. While many in the country music community debate gun control and the industry's ties to the NRA, Daniels supports regulating "bump stock" devices but opposes stricter gun laws, citing Chicago's strict regulations and high violence as evidence that such laws leave people defenseless. Daniels will perform at Cary's Booth Amphitheatre on October 21.

Digital leaders embrace risk-taking, experimentation, and long-term development to compete in rapidly changing environments. They view themselves as learning organizations that rely on data and continuous feedback to adapt and avoid obsolescence. While encouraging experimentation for its learning value, they also practice thoughtful planning to avoid excessively costly risks. Additionally, they prioritize long-term individual development through training in critical thinking skills like problem solving, statistics, and design thinking, recognizing that such investments may not yield immediate returns but can produce significant future impact.

Willis Eschenbach analyzed solar radiation data from Hawaii's Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO) to test his theory that clouds respond to changes in forcing to oppose them. He found that while volcanic eruptions (El Chichón and Pinatubo) reduced maximum solar radiation by about 25 W/m², clouds rearranged to allow more sunlight through during these periods, partially offsetting the volcanic aerosol effects. Surprisingly, despite this significant solar reduction lasting two years, temperature records from MLO and four other Hawaiian stations showed no cooling effect. Eschenbach notes this contradicts mainstream climate science assumptions and proposes that the climate system responds to restore equilibrium through multiple mechanisms, though he acknowledges no definitive explanation exists for the temperature stability.

A former player discusses Winnipeg's return to the NHL, praising the passionate fan base, strong organization led by Mr. Chipman, and the MTS Centre arena, while contrasting it with Atlanta's poor attendance. He recalls playing at the old Winnipeg Arena and fans chanting "we want the jets." He also describes learning to distinguish between identical twins Henrik and Daniel Seden by their faces and speaking styles, noting Henrik is more vocal and was always the captain. Finally, he explains his approach to facing goaltender Tim Thomas, emphasizing the need to vary shooting strategies including shots for rebounds, backdoor attempts, and exploiting corners.

Energy sector trading involves gaining exposure to energy stocks through ETFs like XLE or VDE, or by building individual stock portfolios. The S&P 500 energy sector includes oil and natural gas companies, with major holdings in Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger. The sector has outperformed the broader market, with XLE returning 52.81% versus the S&P 500's -9.28% as of July 2022. Two XLE trading strategies are mentioned: one with 198 trades, 0.61% average gain, 65% win rate, and 6.4% CAGR; another with 335 trades, 0.21% average gain, 59% win rate, and 3% annual return. The energy sector is difficult to trade due to commodity price volatility driven by macro factors, but offers valuable diversification benefits.

Canada's big five banks declined 4.6%-7.5% from February highs, while five small-cap lenders dropped 1.6%-28%. Using five criteria—beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history—MCAN Mortgage Corporation ranked first and Atrium Mortgage Investment Corporation third, with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce second. Small-cap financials offer higher dividend yields and lower volatility but have lower liquidity and less diversified business models. The author holds positions in AMIVF, CM, TD, and BNS.

The Hawk Offense features wing isolation, high post shuffle cuts, and weakside post-ups, similar to the UCLA Offense. Two defensive strategies counter it: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. Show & Recover involves defenders "showing" to disrupt cutters and dribble penetration, then recovering to their assignments without switching. SOS Disruption uses wing traps, contact switches, and rotations to totally disrupt the offense, exploiting the difficulty of reversing the ball when the off guard cuts low. Both require strong individual fundamentals and team coordination.

AMD has released two new high-end graphics cards, the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, to compete with Nvidia's GTX 1070 and 1080. The Vega 56 is priced $50 lower than the GTX 1070 in the US, though UK pricing may be less competitive. AMD's key advantage is FreeSync technology, which offers cheaper adaptive synchronization monitors than Nvidia's G-Sync. The company has also released Enhanced Sync to improve FreeSync performance and minimum frame rates. While the Vega 64 does not beat the GTX 1080 Ti, AMD's CrossFire supports up to three cards compared to Nvidia's two-way SLI limit, potentially offering better multi-GPU performance on AMD's X399 platform with Threadripper CPUs.

In *Madison Snap and William Francis v. The People* (1857), the Illinois Supreme Court affirmed the defendants' conviction and $50 fine for maliciously shooting a mare trespassing in their oat field. The court held that wounding trespassing livestock violates both statute and common law; while property owners may expel animals using necessary force without unnecessary harm or take them up damage feasant, they may not inflict injury in retaliation.

Old paper £10 notes will cease to be legal tender in the UK on 1 March. After this date, they will no longer be accepted in shops and restaurants, but can be exchanged for new polymer notes at banks, building societies, post offices, or the Bank of England, possibly requiring ID. The new polymer £10 notes, featuring Jane Austen, entered circulation on 14 September 2017. They last longer than paper notes and include enhanced security features and a tactile element for blind and partially-sighted people. The Bank of England will release a polymer £20 note in 2020, with no current plans to update the £50 note.

The safety position in football is a defensive back role serving as the last line of defense against big plays. There are two primary variations: the free safety, who typically roams deep with freedom to cover the middle of the field using speed, and the strong safety, who plays closer to the line focusing on run defense and tackling. Safeties require versatility including coverage skills, tackling ability, speed, athleticism, and communication. Notable players include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Ronnie Lott, Brian Dawkins, and Sean Taylor. The position is crucial for creating turnovers, limiting quarterback passing options, and providing defensive leadership and confidence.

Research published in Nature Geoscience shows Australia's Great Barrier Reef has recovered from near-extinction five times in the past 30,000 years by migrating seaward or landward to adapt to changing sea levels. However, lead author Jody Webster of the University of Sydney warns that the reef's historical migration rate of 20 cm to 1.5 metres per year may be insufficient to withstand current rapid changes in sea surface temperature and acidification caused by climate change. The study identified five "death events" caused by reef exposure to air during falling sea levels or sediment dumps during rising sea levels. While the reef would likely die naturally within thousands of years due to the next ice age, human-induced climate change may accelerate this timeline. The reef has recently suffered from mass coral bleaching, including a 2016 event that killed nearly a third of its coral.

Following the 2024 Arab Summit in Bahrain, the "Hope" initiative was launched to address education access for over 10 million out-of-school Arab children aged 5-15. This report, prepared by Ministry of Education officials Mr. Jaber Mustafa and Mr. Younis Bukhari, focuses on Syria as a case study of prolonged conflict affecting children's education.

The study examines how war disrupts education through displacement, school destruction, and psychological trauma. In Syria, approximately one-third of schools have been damaged or destroyed since 2011, with nearly 4,000 documented attacks. Over two million Syrian children remain out of school due to poverty, displacement, and infrastructure collapse. Research shows 60.5% of Syrian children affected by civil war meet criteria for psychological disorders.

Using triangulation methodology combining interviews, surveys, and a case study of a child named Ahmed in Alkhabor, Syria, the researchers identified key challenges: irregular attendance, resource scarcity, psychological barriers, and lack of safe learning environments.

The report proposes immediate solutions including emotional and academic support programs, alongside sustainable measures through the Hope Initiative—a permanent organization designed to maintain educational frameworks during conflicts. The initiative aims to combine psychological interventions, temporary learning facilities, and long-term educational infrastructure to protect children's development and support post-conflict recovery.
Primatologist Jane Goodall died on October 1 at age 91. Her legacy includes stories of living chimps and enduring skeletons.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, an indigenous community 18 kilometers from Mexico's Popocatépetl volcano, face heightened stress from simultaneous seismic and volcanic activity. Although they traditionally prefer eruptions to earthquakes, the September 19 quake—which heavily damaged the town—combined with recent increased volcanic activity and evacuation recommendations has caused anxiety. Recent eruptions produced ashfall in nearby municipalities.

Sean "Diddy" Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison for two Mann Act violations involving transporting sex workers across state lines for "freak offs." The 55-year-old music mogul was convicted by a jury but acquitted of more serious sex trafficking and racketeering charges. During the Manhattan sentencing, Combs apologized to victims and his family, calling his actions "disgusting, shameful, and sick," but Judge Arun Subramanian rejected defense arguments about his good works, stating they couldn't "wash away" his abuse of power over women. The sentence of 50 months plus a $500,000 fine was far below the 11 years prosecutors sought. Combs' legal team had requested 14 months, while prosecutors argued for at least 135 months, calling him "unrepentant." The case featured testimony from 34 government witnesses, including ex-girlfriend Cassie Ventura, though the jury found no coercion in the sexual activities. Combs faces additional civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault and other violence.

The passage analyzes trading strategies around futures expiration weeks for DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50. Both indices show positive performance during expiration weeks, with DAX 40 averaging 0.39% gains (57% win ratio) and Euro Stoxx 50 averaging 0.3% (54% win ratio). December is the strongest month for both. The week after DAX 40 futures expiration performs poorly overall (-0.1% average, 47% win ratio), with September being particularly weak. The backtest for post-expiration performance uses a 100% margin investment strategy rather than futures backtesting, with four annual trades held for one week after expiration Friday. High trading volume makes DAX 40 attractive to traders despite post-expiration weakness.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III's conviction and twenty-year sentence. The court rejected his claim that Judge McMahon should have recused herself, finding no abuse of discretion or appearance of partiality regarding duty station changes, docketing errors, or prior recusal from a related bankruptcy case. The court also upheld the sentence as reasonable, rejecting arguments concerning alleged judicial bias, medical needs, cooperation credit, and sentence length, noting the defendant's extensive criminal history and the massive amount of money involved.

The UC1825BEVM-CVAL uses an RCD clamp circuit with a resistor, capacitor, and diode to clamp the switch node voltage. Starting values for the resistor and capacitor can be calculated using Equation 30 (Vclamp = Kclamp × Nps × (Vout + VDiode), where Kclamp is recommended to be 1.5 for ~50% overshoot) and Equations 31-32, which require knowing the transformer's parasitic inductance and allowed clamp voltage variation over the switching cycle.

This patent application describes methods for producing elastomeric compositions containing dispersed carbon black particles from hydrophilic carbon black and curable hydrophobic silicone pre-polymers. The key innovation involves treating hydrophilic carbon black particles with silicone-based dispersants (amino-silicone, silicone-acrylate, or silicone-epoxy) that have carbon-black-affinic moieties, enabling stable dispersion in hydrophobic silicone matrices. The treated particles are mixed with curable silicone pre-polymers and cured via addition-curing or condensation-curing. The hydrophilic carbon black is characterized by specific properties including pH ≤5.0, volatile matter content ≥1.5%, oxygen content ≥1.0%, acid value ≥0.05 mmol/g, surface zeta potential ≤-15 mV, and specific Raman spectroscopy ratios. The dispersants feature branched siloxane-based structures with amino, acrylate, or epoxy functional groups. Resulting compositions achieve uniform particle dispersion with Dv90 sizes typically ≤5 μm, suitable for applications including intermediate transfer members in printing systems, where the dispersed carbon black provides mechanical reinforcement, thermal/electrical conductivity, and radiation absorption properties.

The passage details design requirements for driving the ADS8860 ADC with the PGA848, including supply voltages and three filter stages: an input EMI/RFI filter, a PGA feedback filter with 318kHz nominal cutoff (277kHz at high tolerance), and a charge reservoir filter at the ADC inputs. The PGA848 provides 318kHz bandwidth with -0.1dB flatness to 41kHz, using a 2.5V reference generated from a REF6250 through a precision divider and buffered by an OPA192 in dual-feedback configuration with 86° phase margin. Supply voltages above ±20V permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines emphasize symmetrical inputs, bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance, and thermal management. The document also covers simulation tools (TINA-TI, PSpice-for-TI), related documentation, ESD precautions, and mechanical packaging information.

The Supreme Court reversed the Eighth Circuit's decision in a veteran seniority case under the Railway Labor Act. The petitioner, a railroad apprentice machinist who served in the military, sought seniority credit at North Little Rock, Arkansas from November 3, 1955—the date he would have completed his apprenticeship but for his service. The District Court granted this relief, finding his promotion would have been automatic, but the Court of Appeals reversed, citing uncertainty about future job availability. The Supreme Court held that such speculative possibilities should not defeat veteran seniority rights, following its decision in Tilton v. Missouri Pac. R. Co., and remanded for proceedings consistent with this opinion.

Pan Finance is a global financial intelligence publication serving over 200,000 senior decision makers across 150 countries with coverage of economics and commerce. U.S. equities advanced despite looming government shutdown threats, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq rising on technology and semiconductor strength while the Dow edged higher; investors balanced risks of delayed economic data against expectations of modest Federal Reserve rate cuts. Other reported developments include SNB and ECB exploring linked instant payment systems, BRICS Bank preparing to issue its first Indian rupee bond by March, BBVA raising its Sabadell bid to €17 billion, Iran and Russia sealing a $25 billion nuclear power deal, and OpenAI introducing parental controls following a teen suicide case.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko, reported killed in Kiev, appeared alive at a news conference revealing his murder was staged by Ukrainian authorities to foil an alleged Kremlin assassination plot. Ukrainian Security Service head Vasyl Gritsak announced a Ukrainian citizen was detained, allegedly paid $40,000 by Russian security services to organize the hit, and was also tasked with procuring weapons and explosives for terror attacks in Ukraine. Babchenko, a Kremlin critic who fled Russia in 2017 after death threats, apologized to his wife and others who mourned him unaware of the plan. Ukrainian law enforcement had known of the contract on Babchenko for two months. Ukrainian prosecutor general Yuri Lutsenko criticized politicians and groups who had accused the government of allowing contract killings.

Americans spent over $100 billion on summer vacations last year. Travel offers health benefits but can be expensive. Tips for saving money include: creating a budget using tools like Excel, budgetyourtrip.com, or your bank account; using online travel sites like TripAdvisor, Priceline, and Yelp for bargains; choosing credit cards without foreign transaction fees and bringing a backup card; monitoring cell phone roaming charges; traveling during offseason and booking early; signing up for airline newsletters; and searching for local deals through information centers and newspapers.

A study found PortMiami is Florida's top money-making operation with over $41 billion in economic impact, up $12.8 billion. The port added 116,000 jobs since 2012, totaling 300,000, and contributed $288 million in taxes in 2016. Cargo increased by nearly 1 million tons in 2016, while cruise passengers reached a record 5.1 million. The Miami Herald questioned the study's accuracy, which the mayor defended. A new $247 million Royal Caribbean terminal is planned, projected to generate $500 million annually.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem provides master control of the device, handling configuration of subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It features ARMv7 ISA with Thumb2, JazelleX, and Media Extensions, an interrupt controller, and integrates the ARM Cortex-A8 processor. The processor uses Harvard architecture with NEON SIMD engine, enhanced VFPv3 floating-point coprocessor, separate L1 caches, and 128-bit interconnect. For debugging, it includes an Embedded Trace Module interface connected to a 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer, though the trace port is not externally pinned out.

National Weather Service forecast for extreme southwestern California issued 2:47 AM PDT July 4, 2018. A high surf advisory is in effect for coastal areas from 6 PM Wednesday through 9 PM Friday, while an excessive heat watch covers inland and desert regions from Friday morning through Saturday evening. Low clouds and fog will clear to mostly sunny skies Wednesday through Thursday, with temperatures warming. Friday and Saturday will bring dangerous heat, with inland highs reaching 99-117°F and desert areas 105-117°F; coastal highs will range from the 70s-90s. Sunday through Tuesday will be partly cloudy with gradually cooling temperatures. Light winds will increase to 15-25 mph with gusts to 25-35 mph in afternoons.

President James Madison, on July 9, 1812, proclaimed the third Thursday in August as a national day of public humiliation and prayer, following a congressional request. The proclamation called for Americans to worship God, acknowledge transgressions, seek forgiveness, and pray for divine protection and guidance during the War of 1812, including blessings on American arms, peace among nations, and conversion of enemies from violence.

Medical staff at the University of Virginia School of Medicine warn of increased natural hazards as spring approaches. The Blue Ridge Poison Control Center anticipates more calls and advises awareness of poisonous plants, mushrooms, black widow spiders in wood piles, and emerging snakes. The center warns against self-treatment methods like tourniquets and suction, which can cause more harm than good. Recommended precautions include wearing appropriate clothing, checking boots for spiders, and staying alert to surroundings.

ESPN, once Disney's cash cow through cable bundle fees from 100 million subscribers, faces declining revenue and rising costs as cable subscriptions dropped to 70 million by 2023. The company launched ESPN+ in 2018, reaching 25 million subscribers, and announced plans for a direct-to-consumer flagship service in 2025. In 2024, Disney partnered with Fox and Warner Bros. Discovery to create Venu Sports, a joint streaming venture. ESPN's evolution from a 1979 startup to a dominant sports media brand involved key growth drivers including NFL rights, satellite competition, and brand differentiation through campaigns like "This Is SportsCenter." The case examines ESPN's transition from B2B to B2C amid streaming disruption, analyzing competitive pressures from tech companies, shifting fan consumption habits, and financial challenges including approximately $10 billion in annual sports rights obligations.

IEX operates with conflicting identities: IEX One, a niche exchange gaming the SEC's National Market System (NMS) through its speed bump to benefit buy-side traders; and IEX Two, an unrealized vision to disrupt markets by serving all traders equally. The speed bump provides superior execution for large market orders but represents just another NMS subsidy rather than true innovation. With under 3% market share, IEX remains trapped within the SEC's flawed system. To achieve dominance, IEX must bypass the NMS entirely and restore balanced liquidity provision for both buy-side and sell-side interests, rather than merely manipulating existing regulatory frameworks.

U.S. employers added 200,000 jobs in January while unemployment remained at 4.1 percent, a 17-year low. Average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent from a year earlier, potentially signaling accelerating wage growth as the labor market tightens. Eighteen states increased minimum wages in January, affecting 4.5 million workers. Black unemployment rose to 7.7 percent from 6.8 percent in December, though it has declined steadily since 2010. Economists caution against drawing broad conclusions from single-month reports, noting that job growth under Trump has been similar to Obama's tenure, with 2.1 million jobs added in 2017 compared to 2.2 million in 2016. Jobs figures are subject to revision and have a margin of error of approximately 100,000.

IT Central Station reports that IT buyers frequently compare Oracle's Exadata and HPE's Vertica data warehouse systems. Exadata users praise its "smart scan" feature for offloading SQL workloads to storage servers, while Vertica users favor its columnar storage for faster access to "hot data." Users note weaknesses: Oracle needs improved patching, and Vertica's documentation requires improvement. IT Central Station offers a 68-page comparative report based on user reviews, available for download.

Coronation Street's sensitive portrayal of Aidan's suicide storyline has reopened discussion about suicide. The writer shares their own past suicide attempt during struggles with sexuality, and recounts friend Cheryl Fialka's 33-year experience of grief after her husband John killed himself at age 31 while working on a cruise ship in Alaska. Cheryl describes the shock, absence of warning signs, and enduring anger and sadness, questioning whether awareness of the devastation left behind might affect those considering suicide.

Competitive Capabilities International (CCi) and R&G Global Consultants partnered to develop Stable Operations TRACC, a data-driven continuous improvement solution that uses big data analytics to help manufacturers increase capacity by 15-20 percent within six months. Cargill was the first client to deploy the product. The solution addresses challenges including high capacity utilization, supply chain service delivery issues, and CAPEX avoidance through data analytics, the TRACC methodology, and blended learning modules. CCi, established in 1987, specializes in manufacturing and supply chain best practices including World Class Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, Lean, and Supply Chain Optimization.

This study examines barriers to women's education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu Kashmir using quantitative research methods. Pakistan's female literacy rate is 51.9% (73.3% for men), with rural areas at only 40.8%. Key obstacles identified through surveys of illiterate and literate women include: patriarchal cultural norms restricting women's mobility and education; poverty preventing school fees, books, and uniforms; early child marriages ending education; lack of educational infrastructure with few secondary schools and poor facilities; illiterate parents unaware of education's value; religious factors prioritizing only Quran study; and management problems like household workload and transport issues. Both groups viewed education as necessary despite challenges. The study recommends government legislation for compulsory education, monthly awareness seminars, media campaigns, and open distance learning to improve access.

The Pakistan Super League will allow franchises to draft new players if contracted international stars opt out of the March 5 final in Lahore due to security concerns. PSL chairman Najam Sethi announced a new draft on February 22 to determine which foreign players will participate. The decision follows a recent bombing in Lahore that killed 13 people, despite the Pakistan Cricket Board's promise of top-level security at Gaddafi Stadium. Pakistani army chief Gen. Qamar Javed Bajwa has extended full support to PSL organizers, who view the final as a showcase to bring international cricket back to Pakistan. The country has not hosted major test playing nations since the 2009 attack on the Sri Lanka team.

After her 20-year marriage ended, a woman who had been a stay-at-home mom with no knowledge of her family's finances worked with a financial planner to locate accounts, set budgets, and rebuild her career. Now 49, she has gained financial independence, secured steady employment with health insurance, and manages all major decisions herself, approaching retirement on her own terms.

Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke visited Maine's Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument to review its designation. The author, who moved to Maine 24 years ago, describes the state's outdoor heritage and argues that the monument—created through an 87,000-acre private land donation with a $40 million endowment—benefits rural Maine's economy without taxpayer cost. The author criticizes Governor Paul LePage's opposition to the monument as inconsistent with conservative principles and expresses hope that Zinke, who grew up near Glacier National Park, will recognize the monument's cultural and economic value and preserve its designation.

This paper presents the LifeCLEF 2014 plant identification task, which evaluated content-based image retrieval for botanical species identification. The dataset contained 60,962 images of 500 European plant species across 7 view types (entire plant, branch, leaf, flower, fruit, stem, leaf scan), collected by 1,608 contributors through citizen science. The task used multi-image queries from single plant observations and introduced user quality ratings and metadata. Ten research groups submitted runs using various methods including Fisher vectors, convolutional neural networks, bag-of-visual-words, and matching approaches. IBM AU achieved the best results (score 0.471) with Fisher vector encoding combined with CNN and segmentation. Results showed substantial improvement when combining multiple images from the same observation, with LeafScan and Flower categories performing best. The paper concludes that scaling to thousands of species remains challenging, with a possible 2015 expansion to 5,000 French flora species.

This passage provides detailed technical documentation for the TMS320DM814x/TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processors, covering memory addressing, pin assignments, and boot configuration. The TILER subsystem includes a 4-GB extended addressing range enabled by a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame buffer access, accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can access single views through a 512-MB region. Terminal function tables document pin multiplexing, signal names, ball numbers, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown states, supply voltages, and peripheral functions. Boot configuration is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset, with BTMODE[15:11] controlling GPMC CS0 settings, BTMODE[4:0] selecting boot mode order, and BTMODE[9:8] configuring Ethernet PHY mode when EMAC boot is selected. The document details pin functions for multiple peripherals including DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers, EMAC interfaces in MII/GMII/RGMII/RMII modes, general-purpose I/O (GP0-GP3), GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SD/MMC, SPI, timers, UART, USB, and video input/output. Pin multiplexing is controlled via PINCNTL1-PINCNTL270 registers, with most pins defaulting to tri-state (MUXMODE=0x0). Internal pullup/pulldown resistors are provided on most pins, with external resistors recommended for boot configuration pins and when internal resistors don't match desired states.

The CAG 2015/16 report identifies significant weaknesses in Tanzania's public procurement process, causing substantial government losses. Prof Mussa Assad found non-compliance with procurement laws, including eight contracts worth Sh63 billion and $1 billion poorly managed, and Sh23.98 billion in irregular procurements without competitive quotations. Ten public entities procured Sh11.253 billion worth of goods and services without valid contracts. Specific cases include the Ministry of Water's Sh491 million contract and the Registrar of Political Parties' Sh668 million procurement, both unvetted by the Attorney General. The report also notes persistent poor asset management, with 37 dilapidated buildings across 12 embassies and ten undeveloped embassy plots abroad.

Offensive switches in soccer are position exchanges between two attacking teammates used to beat defenders. They may be "called" (using oral communication) or "natural" (without verbal cues), and can occur with or without the ball. The basic offensive switch, also called a "crossover run" or "lateral/horizontal switch," involves two teammates running diagonally forward in opposite directions to form an "X" pattern, exchanging duties until returning to their original positions. A "vertical switch" involves players exchanging positions from back-to-front or front-to-back toward opposite goal lines. Both types aim to free runners for passes by causing defenders to hesitate or choose whom to cover. Switches are typically performed in the opponents' half, with lateral switches particularly effective against offside traps. Players should verbally communicate "Switch back" when returning to original positions.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on September 25, 2022, reporting that Joseph Gebbia was appointed to its Board of Directors effective September 25, 2022. Gebbia waived cash compensation until further notice and joined other directors in waiving equity compensation until July 2023. No related party transactions requiring disclosure exist between Tesla and Gebbia. The Board has not assigned him to any committees. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on September 28, 2022.

The paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark of 4,800 questions across 8 nanomaterial synthesis subdomains, to evaluate LLMs' ability to hypothesize physicochemical principles. The benchmark was created by curating ~17,000 academic papers, using Claude-3.5-Sonnet with multi-agent roundtable discussions to generate questions, and conducting human evaluation with a 5-point Likert scale. The authors also release MatterDB, a dataset of 31,735 papers with extracted synthesis mechanisms. Fourteen LLMs were evaluated using text-infilling (TIF) and multiple-choice question (MCQ) metrics. Key findings: LLMs excel at logical reasoning but struggle with conceptual understanding and principle-based reasoning; larger models and principle-guided prompting improve performance; reasoning-focused models show strong MCQ performance but weaker TIF results, indicating a trade-off between reasoning and precise knowledge reproduction. The benchmark reveals critical gaps in LLMs' comprehension of materials synthesis mechanisms that must be addressed for reliable scientific hypothesis generation.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on May 20, 2015, reporting results from its 2015 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. Three proposals were adopted: (1) election of twelve directors for one-year terms, with each director receiving substantial majority support; (2) advisory approval of named executive officer compensation with approximately 392.5 million shares for and 5.4 million against; and (3) ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered accounting firm with approximately 458.7 million shares for and 1.8 million against. The report was signed on May 26, 2015, by Rebecca Peters, Vice President, Corporate Affairs and Assistant Secretary.

Tropical Storm Nate is strengthening in the western Caribbean and moving toward the southeastern United States, potentially bringing heavy rain to West Tennessee over the weekend. Friday evening will remain mild and dry with temperatures in the 70s, cooling to upper 60s by 10 p.m. and bottoming out in the middle to upper 60s by Saturday sunrise. While severe weather risk is low, significant rain is expected between Saturday evening and Sunday morning. The storm's path has shifted farther east from previous forecasts.

Dr. Edith Mbagwu, a primary care physician at Ochsner Health Center, recommends using the SMART goal-setting framework to help people maintain weight loss resolutions. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, and Time-based. For weight loss, this means defining clear exercise and nutrition plans, tracking progress through preferred metrics, ensuring goals are achievable with available resources, setting smaller milestones for larger targets, and scheduling dedicated time for health priorities. Dr. Mbagwu suggests motivation strategies like training for events or targeting health benchmarks to maintain commitment.

An EF-0 tornado touched down near the Prince William County line on Friday, August 11, at 6:08 p.m., lasting two minutes with 75 mph winds. It cut a mile-long, 100-yard-wide path of damage at Broad Run in Fauquier County. Doppler radar detected rotation at 6:02 p.m., prompting a tornado warning. This study examines difficulties in foreign language education during the COVID-19 pandemic transition to distance education. Researchers surveyed 294 undergraduate and graduate students studying German or English at a Turkish university in 2020-2021, using a 53-item "distance education problems scale" with 6 subscales.

Key findings indicate that students view distance education as unsuccessful for foreign language teaching. The highest reported problems were internet and computer-related issues (µ=0.473), particularly connection interruptions/freezing (µ=0.707). Student-related problems ranked second (µ=0.396), with lack of motivation (µ=0.694) and low active participation (µ=0.639) as top concerns. Problems with course content/acquirements (µ=0.252) centered on insufficient mutual communication (µ=0.544). Teacher-related problems were lowest (µ=0.147).

Statistical analysis revealed male students perceived more student-related problems than females. Students lacking training in distance education programs, those without dedicated study rooms, and those without reliable home internet connections reported significantly more problems across all dimensions. No significant differences emerged between German and English language students.

The study concludes that face-to-face education remains more effective for foreign language instruction, citing insufficient materials, problematic assessment processes, inadequate teacher preparation, and low student engagement. Recommendations include self-discipline and technical training for students, professional development for teachers in virtual classroom management and assessment, and implementation of hybrid education models.

Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen testified to the Senate Banking Committee on the U.S. economy and monetary policy. She stated that the FOMC expects moderate economic expansion, further job market strengthening, and inflation rising to 2 percent. The Committee will evaluate whether to adjust the federal funds rate at upcoming meetings. Yellen cited uncertainty from fiscal policy changes, productivity growth, and international developments. She warned that delaying rate increases could require rapid future hikes, risking market disruption and recession. Yellen noted the unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent in January, wage growth has increased, and business investment improved late last year. Market-based inflation compensation measures have risen from 2015-2016 lows, while longer-term inflation expectations remain stable.

Dereck James Harrison, 23, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder during kidnapping and kidnapping in the May killing of Utah train worker Kay Porter Ricks, 63, avoiding the death penalty. Prosecutors agreed not to seek capital punishment in exchange for his plea; sentencing is set for May 17. Harrison claimed his father, Flint Harrison—who later killed himself in jail—actually killed Ricks by cutting his throat and hitting him with a metal rod. The Harrisons kidnapped Ricks from a Salt Lake City TRAX stop, drove his truck to rural Wyoming, and killed him during a five-day manhunt following their earlier kidnapping of a woman and her four daughters. Two of four charges were dropped in the plea deal.

Hong Liu discusses the quantization of Dirac theory, explaining that standard commutation relations lead to an unbounded Hamiltonian and bosonic symmetry, so anticommutators are used instead. The anticommutation relation {ψ_α(x), ψ_β†(x')} = δ_{αβ}δ³(x-x') is self-consistent and yields a positive-definite Hamiltonian. Field expansion gives creation/annihilation operators with {a_k^r, a_k'^s†} = {c_k^r, c_k'^s†} = (2π)³δ³(k-k')δ^{rs}, all others zero. Each fermionic oscillator can only be excited once (Pauli principle), with ground state energy -½ω_k opposite to bosons. Single-particle states |k,s⟩ = a_k^s†|0⟩ and |k,s̄⟩ = c_k^s†|0⟩ have momentum k, polarization s/s̄, and spin-½. The spin-statistics theorem states half-integer spins use anticommutators (Fermi-Dirac), integer spins use commutators (Bose-Einstein). The U(1) Noether charge Q = ∫d³x ψ†ψ = ∑_s∫d³k/(2π)³(a_k^s†a_k^s - c_k^s†c_k^s) shows particles and antiparticles have opposite charge ±1. Correlation functions relate to scalar ones via D^{±,r,F}_{αβ}(x-y) = (i∂̸_x + m)_{αβ}D^{±,r,F}(x-y), with Feynman propagator S_F(k) = i(k̸ + m)/(k² - m² + iε) = i/(k̸ - m + iε).

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, reference, and multiSPI interface. Data transfer frames begin at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end at the subsequent rising edge. The device supports SPI-compatible protocols for configuration and offers single/dual SDO-x modes and source-synchronous protocols for data read operations. Nine configuration registers control device operation, including reset/power control, SPI protocol selection, data output formatting, input range selection, and alarm thresholds. The device features programmable input alarms with hysteresis, NAP and power-down modes for power savings, and requires proper PCB layout with analog/digital signal separation and supply decoupling.

This study investigated interactions between a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS) and lifestyle/environmental factors on age at onset (AAO) in 486 LRRK2-PD and 9,259 idiopathic PD (iPD) patients from three cohorts (AMP-PD, Fox Insight, Tunisian). The MGS, derived from 14 SNPs related to mitochondrial function, was inversely associated with AAO in LRRK2-PD (higher MGS = earlier onset by ~1 month per 1% increase), with stronger effects in European versus Tunisian Arab-Berber populations. No MGS-AAO association was found in iPD. Gene-environment interactions were identified: in LRRK2-PD, MGS interacted with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption (high MGS + consumption = 6-11 years earlier median AAO); in iPD, MGS interacted with caffeinated soda and work-related pesticide exposure. Smoking, black tea, and green tea showed no interactions with MGS. The study highlights population-specific effects of polygenic scores and the importance of including lifestyle/environmental factors in genetic association studies.

Enron Corp. secured the remaining $450 million of a $1 billion credit line and obtained an extension until mid-December on a $690 million note due November 27, 2001. The company is in active discussions to restructure its debt and reaffirmed its commitment to a merger with Dynegy Inc. Enron shares fell sharply amid liquidity concerns, dropping 28-33 percent on November 21, 2001, following a 23 percent decline the previous day. Goldman Sachs downgraded both Enron and Dynegy to "market perform," citing major liquidity issues and concerns about Enron's ability to recover lost business. Dynegy CEO Chuck Watson stated the company is continuing confirmatory due diligence on the merger, while ChevronTexaco reiterated confidence in Dynegy's management approach.

This patent application describes systems and methods for periodic beam failure measurements in 5G NR communications. The disclosure addresses beam failure detection (BFD) in high-frequency millimeter wave systems where beam blockage can cause connection failures. The core innovation involves user equipment (UE) determining measurement period durations based only on periodic BFD reference signals (RSs) that have a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship with demodulation RSs (DMRSs) of physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) receptions monitored by the UE, rather than all BFD RSs in a set. This ensures at least one assessed BFD RS is present in each measurement period, preventing missed beam failure detections and counter resets. The UE monitors these BFD RSs during each measurement period, reports beam failure instances when all monitored BFD RSs fail to meet specified thresholds (signal quality or block error rate), and declares beam failure after consecutive instances. The application also covers handling measurement periods where no BFD RS is transmitted—either ignoring such periods or treating them as beam failure instances—to maintain accurate failure tracking.

U.S. stocks closed slightly lower on Tuesday but recovered from deeper intraday losses as geopolitical tensions involving Russia, Syria, and North Korea drove investors toward safe-haven assets and pushed the VIX volatility index above 15 for the first time since Election Day. Investors are preparing for the start of corporate earnings season, with analysts expecting 10 percent first-quarter earnings growth for S&P 500 companies. The Dow fell 0.03 percent, the S&P 500 lost 0.14 percent, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.24 percent. Technology and financial sectors were the worst performers. United Continental shares declined 1.1 percent following a passenger incident controversy. Trading volume was below the 20-day average, and advancing issues outnumbered decliners on both major exchanges.

The passage introduces MOTO (Multi-Objective Three-layer Optimization), a framework for mapping local transition-state networks in complex physicochemical systems. The three-layer workflow comprises: (i) a multi-objective explorer generating diverse initial guesses using NSGA-II with objectives for diversity, feasibility, and minimum-mode separability; (ii) a bilayer minimum-mode kernel using HVP-based Lanczos/LOBPCG for direction optimization and minimum-mode-force ascent to locate index-1 saddles; and (iii) deterministic bidirectional saddle descent to certify connectivity.

Benchmarked on atomistic spin systems, MOTO scales to 10⁶ spins with <1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 s wall time, reducing memory to ~0.01% of explicit-Hessian approaches with 10× speedup on a 70×70 spin system. The framework demonstrates generality across a Bloch-type spin model, DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111), and a Ni(111) heptamer Cartesian system. For Pd/Fe/Ir(111), MOTO identified 12 transition states enabling 32 pathways between skyrmion states, revealing meron/antimeron-mediated mechanisms including skyrmion duplication and chiral droplet formation. The Ni benchmark recovered canonical surface-diffusion rearrangements without algorithmic modification. Limitations include sensitivity to hyperparameters and mask design; future directions target automation and integration with path solvers.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended April 30, 2017. The company reported revenue of $1.937 billion, up 48% year-over-year, with net income of $507 million ($0.79 per diluted share), up 144% from the prior year. GPU business revenue increased 45% to $1.562 billion, driven by gaming and datacenter growth, while Tegra Processor revenue rose 108% to $332 million. Gross margin was 59.4%. The company held $6.21 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. During the quarter, NVIDIA paid $82 million in dividends, settled $605 million of convertible notes, and withheld 2 million shares for tax obligations. The company faces patent litigation from Polaris Innovations Limited and is constructing a new headquarters under a $380 million operating lease arrangement.

Google fired engineer James Damore for circulating a memo arguing that biological differences make women and men suitable for different roles. The memo claimed women have greater interest in people than things and higher neuroticism, while men have greater status drive. However, recent neuroscience challenges these assumptions: brains are "plastic" and change with experience, male and female brains exist as mosaics rather than distinct categories, and many alleged sex differences exist on spectrums rather than as fixed traits. Research shows spatial cognition gaps can be eliminated through training and vary across cultures. "Stereotype threat"—anxiety about confirming negative group stereotypes—affects performance and brain activity. Empowerment techniques can alter brain activity and overcome these effects, suggesting that observed differences may stem from environmental factors rather than innate biology.

The Department of Labor and Employment in Western Visayas is preparing aid for an estimated 17,000 Boracay workers who may be displaced by a proposed island closure. Plans include organizing two job fairs with the Department of Tourism and local governments, partnering with TESDA for skills upgrading, and deploying a quick response team to profile affected workers.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter of a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. The severity remains undetermined, but reports suggest he could miss 2-3 weeks, with Week 5 against Houston unlikely and Week 6 against the Rams in doubt. Jackson did not practice Wednesday or Thursday of Week 5, and coach John Harbaugh stated Jackson couldn't have returned to the game. One source indicated Jackson may not return until after Baltimore's Week 7 bye week.

Hospital at home programs across the U.S. are shutting down as a Medicare waiver that enables them expires September 30, tied to a potential government shutdown. Hundreds of hospitals, including UMass Memorial, Hackensack Meridian Health, ChristianaCare, and Mass General Brigham, have stopped admitting patients or fully discharged their home hospital census. The programs, which provide inpatient-level care in patients' homes and help alleviate emergency department crowding, serve approximately 1,000 beds nationwide. Hospital leaders express concern that the temporary nature of the waivers—extended multiple times since 2020—has limited investment in the model. A bipartisan bill to extend the program for five years is under consideration.

This study examines EFL pre-service teachers' and teacher educators' perceptions of ICT and CALL integration in Vietnamese tertiary initial teacher education. Using Hong's (2010) theoretical framework and a convergent mixed-methods design with 67 pre-service teachers and 3 educators, findings show high perceived opportunity to learn CALL-related knowledge (M=3.05), particularly in digital media competences and ICT pedagogies (M=3.33). Key factors impacting ICT integration include: individual educator obstacles (skills, confidence, fear of change), infrastructure limitations (unstable internet, poor equipment, slow technical support), pre-service teacher-related obstacles (attitudes, engagement), and inconsistent CALL integration policies. The study highlights the absence of official institutional requirements for ICT use, with educators relying on personal initiative. Results align with prior research on opportunity to learn and TPACK framework while emphasizing the need for explicit policies, improved infrastructure, and continuing professional development for educators. Limitations include small sample size and single-site focus in southern Vietnam.

This Pennsylvania Supreme Court case, decided November 28, 1932, addressed whether life beneficiaries of Senator William Flinn's estate were entitled to undistributed earnings from stocks accrued from the date of death or from when the trustee received them. The court held that intact value is generally fixed as of the date of death, rejecting arguments that the testator's five-year administration period postponed trust creation. The court affirmed that life tenants were entitled to earnings from death, finding later dates would violate Pennsylvania's 1853 Act against illegal income accumulation. However, for stock held by Booth & Flinn Company (a separate entity) that passed to executors via dividend in January 1925, intact value was fixed at receipt date, not death. The court also upheld averaging yearly earnings on a per diem basis to determine undistributed earnings on Gulf Oil stock, as no better method was proposed. The lower court's decree was affirmed as modified.

Global citizenship education has developed extensively but lacks sufficient guidance on understanding international conflict and peaceful cooperation. The authors argue that recent geopolitical developments—particularly tensions with China and the Russia-Ukraine war—expose limitations in existing global citizenship education models. While global citizenship education emphasizes advocacy issues like environmentalism, human rights, and multiculturalism, it inadequately addresses national security, economic cooperation, and why states engage in violent conflict.

The article proposes supplementing global citizenship education with three theories from international politics: realism, which emphasizes power and security in an anarchic international system; regionalism, which explains how economic integration can contain conflicts; and institutionalism, which examines how international organizations facilitate cooperation. These perspectives help explain why conflicts arise, how states relate internationally, and conditions for peaceful cooperation.

International cooperation depends on state interests and issue characteristics, including provision of global public goods and coordination of standards. Citizen engagement should expand beyond NGOs and digital activism to include influencing national foreign policy, which employs negotiation, information, economic measures, and military means to pursue security, economic welfare, status, and values. The authors conclude that global citizenship education should incorporate international politics theories, historical analysis, and critical media literacy while broadening its agenda to include state positioning in a conflictual world.

The passage contains diplomatic telegrams and documents from November-December 1918 regarding the World War I armistice. This study explored integrating music software (Sibelius) into a general music education course at a Caribbean university for 24 pre-service teachers in early childhood and primary education programs. Using mixed methods with a phenomenological approach, researchers examined whether technology could be integrated, if students comprehended music concepts, how performance was impacted, and whether use was motivating. Results showed 90% assignment accuracy, majority affirmation that software enhanced understanding, and 67% support for continued technology use, though participants were largely neutral on motivation and preferred traditional approaches. Recommendations include continued software use, progressive training, technology-integrated practicum assessments, and technology-inclusive final assessments. The study aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (quality education) and addresses post-COVID needs for digital teaching competencies.
The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, affirmed the dismissal of a writ of habeas corpus and remand of John Gracy, with five justices concurring and one justice dissenting.

The author thanks readers for feedback on report timing, maintaining a 1pm deadline. They discuss becoming self-employed in 2002 due to unsuitable conventional work hours.
