The James Webb Space Telescope captured the clearest view ever of a dying red supergiant star just before it exploded as supernova SN2025pht in galaxy NGC 1637, 40 million light-years away. The Northwestern University-led team identified the progenitor in mid-infrared light for the first time, revealing it was hidden by unusually thick, carbon-rich dust that made it appear over 100 times dimmer in visible light. This finding explains why astronomers rarely see red supergiants explode despite predictions they should account for most core-collapse supernovae—they are often obscured by dust clouds that JWST's infrared vision can penetrate. The star was the reddest, dustiest supergiant progenitor ever observed, with unexpected carbon-rich dust suggesting powerful convection dredged up material from its core. This marks JWST's first confirmed detection of a supernova progenitor, opening opportunities to study how massive stars live and die.

This study introduces the "Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model," a novel framework for understanding ventricular repolarisation and T-wave morphologies on ECGs. The model conceptualises the heart as an egg-shaped mass with Wilson's Central Terminal at its centre, where repolarisation signals expand outward like ripples. Signals moving toward an ECG lead produce positive deflections, while those moving away produce negative deflections. The asymmetrical "T-zone" of the egg shape generates the characteristic T-wave hump. The model explains ST elevation and depression, various T-wave abnormalities (peaked, inverted, flattened, biphasic), and clarifies the QT interval. The study proposes measuring the QTp interval (Q-wave start to T-wave peak) as more reliable than the conventional QTc interval, which ends when repolarisation exits the T-zone. The model challenges the view that repolarisation begins only after the S-wave, instead suggesting it starts with the Q-wave as a continuous process. Clinical implications include improved localisation of myocardial issues and better assessment of arrhythmia risk and medication effects on QT intervals.

The passage describes methods and systems for creating virtual game environments from real-world scenes using physical objects. The process involves: selecting physical objects with predetermined properties (shape, color, dimensions), arranging them into a physical model, scanning with a 3D capturing device to obtain a digital representation, converting this into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual construction elements, and defining game-controlling elements based on the physical properties. The system recognizes known objects from a library and creates themed virtual environments accordingly. A computationally efficient voxelization method maps surface elements to voxels by defining points within surface elements and mapping them to corresponding voxels. The system supports cyclic gameplay where physical model changes initiate new game cycles, and includes physical playable characters with tool models that unlock corresponding virtual abilities.

This article examines the experiences of undergraduate education-related programme leaders in further education (FE) colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours's (2009) four-level lifelong learning ecology framework. The macro layer traces how education-related undergraduate provision evolved from 1990s-2000s workforce training initiatives and post-Dearing report expansion, with education studies degrees developing distinct from teacher training through HE-FE partnerships. The exo layer covers local institutional relationships with employers and HEI validation/franchising arrangements. The meso layer positions programme leaders as "keystone species" providing personalized student support and nurturing learner identities. The micro layer addresses diverse, non-traditional student populations and the stewardship-style leadership required.

A 2020-2021 British Education Studies Association-funded study surveyed 70 programme leaders (20% FE-based) and interviewed 11. Findings show FE programme leaders often arrived through informal routes rather than open application, typically held master's degrees (fewer doctorates than HE counterparts), and had diverse career backgrounds. They managed smaller teams with higher line management responsibilities, facing poorly defined roles spanning administrative demands, academic support, and pastoral care. Key challenges included balancing HE-specific needs with FE institutional policies, limited time for scholarly activity, and tensions between internal demands and external engagement. The article concludes that programme leaders need enhanced "sightlines"—opportunities for research, scholarly networks, and partnerships beyond their institutions—to better fulfill their keystone role in supporting student success and widening participation.

The UAE announced the Mars 2117 Project on February 14 to build the first human settlement on Mars by 2117. Unveiled by Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum at the World Government Summit, the project will partner with international research institutions to develop faster Mars travel. It begins with an Emirati scientific team before expanding internationally. The UAE previously announced a Mars Probe mission in 2015, aiming to send the Arab world's first spacecraft to Mars by 2021. The announcement coincided with Elon Musk's attendance at the summit; his SpaceX company plans to colonize Mars and reduce trip costs from $10 billion to $200,000 using reusable transportation systems.

Nigerian couple Gbenga Ogundele (aka Benson Ogundele), 58, and wife Mojisola Popoola, 42, of Laurel, Maryland, were sentenced to 234 and 18 months respectively in federal prison for an online dating fraud scheme that defrauded victims of millions of dollars from January 2011 to May 2015. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft and ordered to forfeit $2.2 million; Popoola was ordered to forfeit $165,000 and pay $34,100 restitution. Co-conspirators included Victor Oyewumi Oloyede (234 months), Babatunde Emmanuel Popoola (12 years, $465,170 restitution), and Olusegun Charles Ogunseye, Olufemi Wilfred Williams, and Adeyinka Olubunmi Awolaja Jr., who pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy. Funmilayo Joyce Shodeke received 13 months probation for unlicensed money transmitting. The group used fake romantic relationships and false stories to convince victims to send money to "drop accounts."

This patent application describes a novel compound represented by Chemical Formula 1 for use in organic light emitting devices. The compound features a triazine-based core structure with specific substituents including aryl groups, heterocyclic groups, and various linking groups. The application details the chemical structure, synthesis methods, and incorporation into organic light emitting devices as electron transport layers. Experimental results demonstrate that devices using these compounds exhibit lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime compared to comparative compounds. The compounds are particularly effective when Ar3 comprises heterocyclic groups rather than fused aryl groups or pyridine/quinoline linkages. Thirty-two specific compounds were synthesized and tested in device configurations, with Examples 1-15 showing superior performance to Comparative Examples 1-7.

A woman with multiple sclerosis says Delta Air Lines employees tied her to a wheelchair with a dirty blanket during a flight from Atlanta to Amsterdam on April 1 because the airline didn't have a proper wheelchair with straps she needed. Maria Saliagas, who travels annually to Europe with her husband, normally receives accommodations from Delta for her condition. Her son said the blanket was tied forcefully, causing bruises and making her cry. Delta expressed regret and stated they reached out to resolve concerns and ensure the family's return flight exceeds expectations. The family, returning April 30, rejected an offer of 20,000 SkyMiles and is seeking policy changes for how Delta handles passengers with disabilities.

Martyn Waghorn credits former Sunderland youth coach Kevin Ball with teaching him "what football is about" after nearly being released at age 15, but will face his former club with Ipswich Town on Saturday. The 28-year-old striker from South Shields, who has scored 87 goals across seven clubs since leaving Sunderland in 2010 without scoring, says Ball helped him focus on fundamentals and change position, leading to improved form. Ball now serves as an ambassador at the Stadium of Light, where several academy graduates including Josh Maja, Joel Asoro, George Honeyman, Ethan Robson and Lynden Gooch may feature for Sunderland.

GPS technology has led to a significant increase in truck traffic through Ponca, Arkansas, a small town in the Ozark Mountains near the Buffalo National River. Truck wrecks on Arkansas 43 have risen dramatically, with seven accidents in 2½ years on a steep 2-mile stretch featuring a 1,300-foot elevation drop and sharp curves that GPS systems fail to adequately represent. Drivers following GPS routes from Springfield, Missouri to Clarksville often don't realize the terrain's difficulty until their brakes fail. The Arkansas Highway and Transportation Department plans to install warning signs within one to two months. Local residents and business owners express safety concerns for tourists and pedestrians, noting that Wal-Mart-bound independent truckers frequently use the route.

This protocol describes a register-based cohort study examining trends in revision surgery types for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) in Denmark from 1995-2022. The study will analyze data from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register to compare three surgical approaches: debridement with implant retention (DAIR), one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange. The primary outcomes are trends in revision types over time and risk of second revision following each approach. The study includes all adult patients undergoing primary THA, with follow-up up to 28 years. Strengths include comprehensive data spanning nearly three decades; limitations include potential misclassification of PJI diagnoses and incomplete data from some private clinics.

This patent application describes a floor cleaner with a vacuum source, supply tank for cleaning fluid, distribution nozzle, suction inlet, and recovery tank. The recovery tank includes a tank body with lower end wall, upwardly extending sidewall, and inlet duct; a movable strainer with perforated body and handle; a shutoff float that closes the suction air outlet when fluid exceeds a desired level; and a removable cover with filter. The floor cleaner features a steerable base with brushroll, hydrophobic textile cleaning medium, removable brushroll cover with dual opposed actuators, lights illuminating the spray pattern, first and second squeegees, and optimized center of gravity positioning for balance. The battery is positioned for gravity-assisted replacement when upright.

The Philippines-Australia FIBA World Cup qualifier on July 2, 2018, ended in a brawl after the Philippine team was losing 79-48 with four minutes left in the third quarter. The article argues that the Philippines was primarily at fault for the escalation, despite Australian player Daniel Kickert's actions during warm-ups and his decking of RR Pogoy after Pogoy's initial shove. The Philippine team threw punches, chairs, and water bottles, and took a group selfie after the incident. The Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas apologized for breaching "traditional Filipino hospitality," while coach Chot Reyes and player Terrence Romeo defended the team's actions. The author suggests the brawl revealed the Philippines' unreadiness for global basketball respect and that further accountability measures are needed beyond the apology.

The "Give & Go" isolation offense uses two ball handlers in a 2-1-2 spread alignment with the post on the weakside. Basic continuity involves O1 passing to O2 and cutting to the basket; if unavailable, O2 dribbles out and the action repeats with reversed roles. Back cuts occur when defenders deny passing lanes. Dribble penetration options include turning the corner or using spin/behind-the-back moves. Post help provides a pressure release when cutters are unavailable, with O5 returning the pass to continue the Give & Go. Weakside help involves O1 passing to O3 for a return pass. Weakside exchanges (position swaps, down screens, back screens) keep defenders occupied when they sag to help.

Leam Richardson dismissed the tunnel incident between Wigan Athletic and Fleetwood as minor compared to the Manchester United-Manchester City "Milkgate" controversy. He described the clash between Ivan Toney and Nathan Pond as brief and harmless, with players laughing about it afterward. Richardson avoided involvement, heading toward the referee instead. Toney may start in Tuesday's FA Cup replay against AFC Fylde, with Paul Cook planning to field a strong side to secure a third-round trip to Bournemouth. Richardson emphasized the importance of winning to advance to the Premier League fixture.

This study examines Turkish teachers' opinions on culturally responsive education using Q methodology with 21 participants from diverse ethnic backgrounds. Three factors emerged: "Unification" (8 participants), emphasizing bringing cultures together and global citizenship; "Student Support" (6 participants), focusing on equality and cultural competence development; and "Teacher Support" (3 participants), highlighting teacher training and curriculum development. Teachers generally agreed that cultural diversity is valued and inequalities exist, but showed disagreement on whether discrimination measures are implemented and whether different cultures are seen as threats. The study found consensus on presenting life practices for general culture, while the most disagreement concerned anti-discrimination measures. Teachers refrained from explaining extreme positions, suggesting sensitivity around multicultural issues in Turkey. The Turkish education system is viewed as acknowledging diversity but lacking full implementation of culturally responsive practices, particularly in curriculum and teacher support. Recommendations include mandatory pre-service diversity training, culturally responsive professional development, and creating more inclusive educational environments.

This patent application describes electronic devices with enhanced touch sensor and display structures. The devices feature enclosures with transparent and opaque wall portions, where display layers are mounted under transparent portions and touch sensor layers extend under both transparent and opaque portions. The design enables touch input on multiple surfaces including front walls, sidewalls, and rear walls, with configurations including curved sidewalls and foldable devices with flexible hinge regions. Touch sensors may be implemented as attached layers, deposited coatings, or integrated structures, using capacitive or other technologies with transparent or opaque electrodes. Display layers may use LCD, OLED, or other pixel technologies on rigid or flexible substrates. Fabrication methods include lamination, deposition, patterning, and bending processes to conform layers to planar and curved surfaces.

Progressive (PGR), the fourth largest U.S. auto insurer, reported strong February 2018 results with an 87.8% combined ratio and 19% premium growth. The company raised $1.08 billion through debt and preferred share offerings, expanded Uber commercial coverage, and recognized $70 million in additional premiums. Despite improved underwriting margins across all business lines and expectations for higher 2018 earnings due to lower corporate tax rates, the author maintains that Progressive remains overvalued with an intrinsic value estimate of $48-$54 per share. The author projects 10%+ book value growth and FY2018 EPS in the upper range of $2.50-$4.30, with estimated dividends between $0.76-$1.85. Existing investors are advised to hold positions.

The dual momentum trading strategy by Gary Antonacci selects assets that outperform peers over a given period while also showing positive returns. It combines absolute momentum (an asset's own percentage price change) and relative momentum (performance compared to other assets). The strategy involves calculating momentum by dividing current price by past price, comparing assets with positive absolute momentum to find the strongest relative performer for buying, and in short-enabled markets, identifying the weakest among assets with negative absolute momentum for shorting. Originating from Jagadeesh and Titman's 1993 research on relative momentum, Antonacci extended this in 2012 by adding absolute momentum to reduce volatility. Academic research supports momentum effects for short-term periods of 1-12 months. Implementation works best with ETFs tracking diversified equity indexes, using monthly rebalancing. Backtesting from 1950-2018 showed the Global Equities Momentum model outperformed traditional allocations with lower drawdowns, though it underperforms during strong bull markets. Benefits include better risk-adjusted returns than buy-and-hold and reduced volatility.

The Break, a longtime restaurant and billiards hall in Birmingham's Five Points South, will be demolished for high-rise apartments. Some residents welcome the change, hoping to revive the area's declining nightlife, while others criticize the focus on luxury housing amid rising rents and call for more affordable options. No closure date has been set.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis for trash talking without professional MMA experience. Gracie offered to fight Danis at Bellator 180, but Danis declined to compete at a preliminary spot, choosing to attend the IBJJF World Championship instead. Gracie will now face Dave Marfone at the June 24 event at Madison Square Garden. Gracie called Danis an amateur who needs to fight before talking, stating he would accept the fight anytime once Danis gains professional experience.

US researchers found that higher temperatures correlate with lower exam scores, with a 0.5°C rise causing a 1% drop in results. The study of 10 million students over 13 years suggests UK students may be more affected due to lack of air conditioning in schools. June, when most UK exams occur, is when temperatures typically exceed 21°C—the threshold for negative effects. While proposals to change the academic year or move exams online exist, the current system's synchronized testing allows for grade boundaries to adjust annually, potentially offsetting heat-related disadvantages.

The advance-decline indicator, also known as the AD line, is a market breadth indicator that plots the cumulative difference between advancing and declining stocks. It confirms stock index trends and predicts potential reversals through divergences. The article explains related concepts including advance/decline issues, distribution, and volume. A backtest of the NYSE advance-decline indicator on the S&P 500 (SPY ETF) showed poor performance with a profit factor of 1.55, below the 1.75 threshold. The authors conclude the indicator is likely not useful for profitable trading strategies and recommend alternatives like RSI, Williams %R, or IBS.

Dive operators disagree on whether tourism will be affected by the ex-HMAS Tobruk landing on its side when scuttled. Glenn Bowman of Dive Hervey Bay believes projected income could drop 50% as the starboard side is inaccessible to most divers. Ed Gibson of Hervey Bay Dive Centre disagrees, stating the wreck remains accessible and dive tourism will thrive. Both agree the dive will be spectacular. The Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service confirmed the wreck is in the correct location and safety inspections are underway, with the government engaging four commercial tour operators on dive experience opportunities.

The rapid advancement of large language models and generative AI creates legal and ethical challenges including misinformation, deepfakes, and amplified biases, while raising questions about whether existing regulatory frameworks suffice. The EU, US, and China have introduced AI regulations, and companies like Microsoft have published AI principles and established industry forums. However, gaps persist between technology industries and governments in understanding AI risks and benefits, and countries lack consensus on regulation, increasing compliance difficulties and innovation costs. Additionally, the complex nature of LLMs means certain risks may only emerge during real-world use rather than testing. To address these challenges, the authors recommend fostering partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers; creating forward-looking regulations; and implementing both top-down and bottom-up governance approaches where developers and users report issues through effective channels for prompt regulatory updates.

The article examines wealthy female celebrities and heiresses who launched business ventures, most of which failed financially. Millie Mackintosh's fashion line lost £182,833 and was liquidated with £548,000 in debts. Ella Mills' deli business lost £723,811 and closed two of three locations, though her separate snack company remains profitable. Trinny Woodall's makeup company initially profited then lost £70,089, but received £2.7 million from investors. Sadie Frost's lingerie company amassed £4.2 million in debts before dissolving in 2017.

A speaker discusses needing more offensive aggression and net presence against Detroit's defensive strategy of blocking lanes and pressuring high. Both teams' goaltenders and defenses are playing well, making it difficult to score. The speaker notes Ron Francis nearly scored, hitting the post. They praise their home arena as the loudest in the NHL, with enthusiastic fans who energize the team.

Global Ferronickel Holdings' subsidiary Platinum Group Metals Corp. renewed its supply contract with Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel Industry to supply 1.5 million wet metric tons of medium grade nickel ore for the 2018 mining season at market prices. PGMC has supplied the Chinese company since 2014 from its Cagdianao mine in Surigao del Norte. Global Ferronickel targets six million WMT shipments for PGMC this year. The company's 2017 income rose over 20 times to P779.7 million on 54% higher revenues of P5.8 billion, driven by better prices and foreign exchange impacts. Shares fell 2.70% to P2.52 on Monday.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson's investiture ceremony occurred in 2022, though she began serving three months prior. Federal courts may curtail operations during a government shutdown, but the Supreme Court would remain largely unaffected due to permanent funds. Chief Justice John Roberts marked 20 years leading the court, which faces major cases on elections, free speech, and executive authority. Nearly half of state attorneys general called for challenging a 2008 Supreme Court decision barring death penalty for child rape. Former Michigan athletes plan to appeal a dismissed NIL lawsuit. Venezuelan citizens sought Supreme Court intervention to prevent ending their protected status. The justices held their "long conference" to address cert petitions, with grants expected soon. The 2025-26 term begins October 6. Historical analysis notes Chief Justice Warren Burger's recorded conversations with President Nixon while still ruling against him in United States v. Nixon. The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to end birthright citizenship and was allowed to withhold foreign-aid funding. Justice Barrett discussed public scrutiny at a SCOTUSblog Summit. A Federal Reserve governor sought Supreme Court protection from removal by Trump.

The U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian released an ebook edition of Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1942 Volume II Europe on May 28, 2018. The FRUS series, established in 1861, documents official U.S. foreign policy records. The ebook edition provides full content with search, bookmarking, and offline access capabilities. Document numbers are recommended for citations rather than page numbers. The compilation follows Department of State Regulation 045, requiring historical objectivity, no text alteration without indication, and no omission of major facts. E.R. Perkins directed the Foreign Relations staff, with specific compilers assigned to different country sections: Rogers P. Churchill for Finland, Francis C. Prescott for France/North Africa, Prescott and Herbert A. Fine for Greece, and N.O. Sappington for the remainder. The Division of Publishing Services, under Norris E. Drew, handled editing, proofreading, and indexing through the Foreign Relations Editing Branch led by Elizabeth A. Vary and Ouida J. Ward.

Salem, Oregon residents are driving to other cities like Woodburn to find bottled water after officials announced Tuesday that the city's drinking water supply is contaminated with cyanotoxins from an algae bloom in Detroit Lake. Neither the city nor the Oregon Office of Emergency Management plan to coordinate water distribution, and grocery stores across Salem are reporting shortages. Children under 6, people with compromised immune systems, those receiving dialysis, people with liver conditions, pets, pregnant women, and nursing mothers should not drink tap water. Major retailers expect water shipments but timing is uncertain. Reports of price-gauging emerged Wednesday. The city expects fresh test results Thursday. The contamination also affects Detroit, Gates, Idanha, Jefferson, Lyons, Mehama, Mill City, Stayton, and Turner.

Eurozone stock markets fell on Friday as the euro pressured the US dollar and traders awaited US jobs data. Germany's DAX dropped 1.7 percent, with Deutsche Bank shares falling 6.21 percent after reporting losses due to US tax reforms. France's CAC 40 lost 1.6 percent, and the STOXX 600 fell 1.4 percent. London's FTSE 100 declined 0.6 percent. Analysts noted European markets bore the brunt of global equity selling, with attention focused on US nonfarm payrolls data expected to support continued interest rate rises.

This paper introduces Bolt, a new tool for learning Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf) formulas from positive and negative traces. The key innovation is treating Boolean operators separately from temporal operators through a novel approach called Boolean Set Cover. After enumerating LTLf formulas up to a fixed size using an optimized VFB algorithm (combining combinatorial search, fast evaluation via characteristic tables, and observational equivalence), Bolt switches to solving Boolean Set Cover by combining these formulas with ∧ and ∨ operators. The Boolean Set Cover problem is solved using beam search with domination-based pruning and a divide-and-conquer meta-algorithm. Experiments on a consolidated benchmark suite of over 15,000 tasks show Bolt significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art CPU tool Scarlet, solving more tasks with faster wall-clock times and smaller formula sizes. Bolt is competitive with a 2024 GPU-accelerated algorithm while running on CPU. An ablation study confirms that Boolean Set Cover enables solving harder tasks that pure enumeration cannot handle.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 9, 2017, announcing its financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress (Exhibit 99.2), which was posted to the company's investor website. The materials were furnished but not deemed "filed" under securities regulations.

This article explains offensive football positions for new viewers. The quarterback leads the offense, touches the ball every play, makes throwing decisions, and can call audibles to change plays. Running backs primarily carry the ball but also catch passes and block. Tight ends combine receiver and lineman duties, with "attached" types lining up on the line and "sniffer" or H-back types playing off the line. The offensive line—consisting of two tackles, two guards, and a center—blocks for runs and passes; left tackles protect right-handed quarterbacks' blind sides. Guards perform double teams and pulling blocks. Centers snap the ball and direct line adjustments. Wide receivers catch passes and block, with three main types: Split End/X (big, physical, on the line), Flanker/Z (fast, off the line), and Slot (small, quick, inside).

End job interviews promptly without lingering or groveling. Successful candidates show confidence, focus on the opportunity rather than themselves, and avoid asking about decision timelines. Simply stand, shake hands, and thank the interviewer.

Cornell professor Adam Anderson's research published in Psychological Science shows that humans interpret emotions by analyzing eye expressions, a process that evolved from universal environmental reactions to communication. Narrowed eyes, which enhance visual discrimination, were associated with emotions like disgust and suspicion, while open eyes, which expand vision, were linked to sensitivity emotions like fear and awe. Study participants accurately identified six basic emotions from eyes alone, with eye openness being the most important feature for reading mental states. The eyes provided more robust emotional indicators than other facial areas. The findings support Darwin's theory that expressions originated for sensory function before becoming social communication tools.

The Karnataka education department has cancelled its annual summer camp for government school students due to funding shortages and teacher unavailability. The "Swalpa odu, swalpa moju" programme, running since 2017-18, provided five weeks of Mathematics, Science, and extra-curricular activities for students who completed classes 5 and 6. Last year, 7,049 schools participated, primarily in drought-hit areas with 150+ students. The camps were initiated based on a 2016 Pratham report showing over half of rural Karnataka's elementary school completers struggled with basic division and English reading.

A commissioned study warns that relocating Vegreville's federal immigration processing centre to Edmonton would cause permanent population decline, lower property values, and higher unemployment. The town could lose 7.3% of its population and 130 students, with home prices dropping 30%. The centre, opened in 1994, employs 236 people and is one of Vegreville's largest employers. The union representing workers argues the closure is unnecessary for Edmonton expansion.

Brendon Naidoo, boyfriend of DJ Zinhle, was granted R50,000 bail at Alexandra Magistrate Court on fraud charges related to a foreign-exchange trading scheme. He must report to Sandton Police station twice weekly. Naidoo was arrested on April 8 and held at Johannesburg Central Prison. His next court appearance is scheduled for May 5.

This study investigated antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in wastewater during the COVID-19 pandemic in Western Uttar Pradesh, India. Researchers collected 150 wastewater samples from metropolitan and non-metropolitan cities between 2020-2021, isolating Enterobacteriaceae bacteria. Of 150 isolates, 62% were E. coli, 24% K. pneumoniae, 8% other Enterobacteriaceae, and 6% mixed populations. Results showed 74% resistance to one or more antibiotics, with 79.3% identified as ESBL producers. E. coli showed 57.14% multidrug resistance (MDR), while K. pneumoniae showed 28.57% MDR. Zone 1 (metropolitan areas) had highest MDR prevalence. Carbapenem resistance ranged 37-59%, and colistin resistance was detected in some isolates. The study found comparable AMR levels in metropolitan and non-metropolitan cities, attributing this to indiscriminate antibiotic use and inadequate wastewater treatment. Researchers concluded that approximately 80% of isolates were MDR, including resistance to last-resort antibiotics, indicating AMR in Indian wastewater is increasing and poses global health risks.

Three U.S.-affiliated academics—John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis—won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting electric circuits, demonstrating quantum properties at a macroscopic scale. They will share nearly $1.2 million.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine convictions of Anthony Davis and Eric Simmons, rejecting their arguments that insufficient evidence supported the convictions and that the jury rendered inconsistent verdicts. The court held that the State could aggregate the weight of two separate cocaine sales to Lampkin (1.61 grams and 1.51 grams) to meet the three-gram threshold for Class A felony enhancement, finding sufficient evidence of an agreement among the defendants. The court also rejected Davis's Blakely challenge to his enhanced forty-year sentence, concluding that any error in considering improper aggravators was harmless given his extensive criminal history.

Construction began on Fort Buford on June 15, 1866, at the confluence of the Missouri and Yellowstone Rivers near Williston. The military post operated until 1881, when Sitting Bull surrendered there. Soldiers faced poor food conditions, with self-provided meals causing scurvy and Surgeon J.V.D. Middleton criticizing the rotating cooking duty system. Supply lines via steamboat were cut off when the Missouri River froze. Other issues included boredom, alcohol abuse, and self-inflicted wounds. A January 1876 report described mental illness cases and library resources. The fort was abandoned but partially restored, with a museum opening in the headquarters building on June 15, 1963.

Flippy, a burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun working as a grill cook at Caliburger's Pasadena restaurant. The robot can grill 150 burgers per hour and uses AI to improve its technique over time. Caliburger has exclusive rights to use Flippy for six months before other vendors can purchase it. Nokia, Deutsche Telekom, and Hamburg Port Authority are testing 5G across an 8,000-hectare port area, with use cases including traffic light management, sensor data processing, and virtual reality monitoring. An antenna installed on Hamburg's television tower provides connectivity. The trial will test multiple network slices under live industrial conditions for the first time in Germany, allowing the network to adapt to varying application requirements. Deutsche Telekom aims to gain practical experience for adapting networks to customer needs, particularly for production and logistics sectors.

Apple Inc. filed its Q3 2021 Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 26, 2021. Total net sales increased 36% year-over-year to $81.4 billion, with Products revenue at $63.9 billion and Services revenue at $17.5 billion. Net income was $21.7 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $1.30. The company repurchased $22.5 billion of common stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends. Prosecutors dismissed four serious charges, including attempted murder, against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer, who was accused of plotting a school shooting in Vermont, following a state Supreme Court ruling that "preparation alone" did not justify the charges. Kennedy will proceed with lesser charges of criminal threatening and carrying a dangerous weapon. Sawyer, who pleaded not guilty, had his bail set at $100,000 with conditions including 24-hour home curfew and no contact with school personnel. The case prompted Republican Gov. Phil Scott to sign bills raising firearm purchase age, banning high-capacity magazines, and enabling easier gun removal from threatening individuals—the first significant gun restrictions in Vermont history.

Only 12 albums have spent 10 or more weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 since 2000. Taylor Swift and Morgan Wallen each have three albums on this list, while Adele has two. Notable entries include Adele's "21" with 24 weeks at No. 1, Morgan Wallen's "One Thing at a Time" with 19 weeks, and Taylor Swift's "The Tortured Poets Department" with 17 weeks. On October 22, 2001, Enron Corp. announced that the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron shares plunged 21% to $20.65, hitting a 52-week low. The partnerships LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, created in 1999, engaged in transactions with Enron that resulted in a $35 million charge and reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. The Secretary and Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin discussed arms control negotiations, with the US preferring Geneva talks for INF and START while leaving open future Shultz-Gromyko discussions. Dobrynin proposed inventorying bilateral agreements by status, which the Secretary agreed to discuss in late February. Dobrynin suggested additional security talks on radiological weapons, chemical weapons, conventional arms transfers, and Indian Ocean deployments; the Secretary was noncommittal. Clio, a legal technology company, acquired global legal research platform vLex for $1 billion in June 2024, giving it near start-to-finish capabilities for legal practice and law firm management. Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated knee with likely multiple ligament tears during a Week 4 game against the Jets. The injury, which occurred when his legs got wrapped up by cornerback Malachi Moore after a catch, was severe enough that Hill was carted off and taken to a hospital for imaging. Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel confirmed the dislocated knee diagnosis and stated Hill will miss the remainder of the 2025 season. Recovery timeline depends on the extent of ligament damage and whether surgery is required.

This study examines the relationship between science education and citizenship education in Turkey through curriculum analysis and interviews with eight science teachers. While citizenship education evolved from national identity formation to democratic global citizenship, science education shifted toward the Science-Technology-Society-Environment (STSE) approach. The 2018 Turkish science curriculum emphasizes scientific literacy, environmental awareness, and sustainable development—concepts linked to citizenship education. Teachers identified scientific literacy, environmental issues, and socio-scientific topics as primary connections between science and citizenship, noting that science education develops critical thinking, inquiry, and problem-solving skills essential for active citizenship. However, they reported that exam-focused pressures, inadequate infrastructure, and overcrowded classrooms hinder practical implementation of citizenship goals. The study concludes that despite theoretical alignment between science and citizenship education, explicit policy support and teacher training are needed to strengthen this integration.

UFC 216 takes place Saturday in Las Vegas, featuring Demetrious Johnson attempting a record 11th title defense and an interim lightweight title fight between Tony Ferguson and Kevin Lee that could determine Conor McGregor's next opponent. AI literacy has become a central topic in digital literacy research for education. The study examines how future preschool and primary school teachers perceive robots and their pedagogical implications using the Draw-And-Answer-Test (DAAT), a mixed-methods approach combining drawings and open-ended responses. From an initial sample of 143 students, 22 with misconceptions were excluded, leaving 121 participants (75 future preschool teachers, 46 future primary school teachers) from the Faculty of Education, University of Belgrade.

Results showed that 121 participants accurately depicted robots, while 22 held misconceptions—primarily depicting robots as electronic appliances (68.18%), with fewer showing humanoid figures, virtual reality components, or avatars. Most respondents perceived robots as animal-shaped (47.1%, especially Bee Bot), followed by typical robot appearance (24.8%), mechanical objects (24%), and humanoid forms (4.1%). The dominant functions identified were educational (52.9%) and assistive (31.4%). Most participants gained experience at the Faculty of Education. Future preschool teachers prioritized the cognitive domain in their conceptions, while future primary school teachers showed less consistency across cognitive, affective, and behavioral domains.

The study concludes that while misconceptions were minimal, curriculum improvements are needed to enhance digital competencies and algorithmic thinking development in teacher education.

The Green Bay Packers signed veteran tackle Byron Bell, who announced the deal on Instagram. Bell, 29, previously played for Carolina (2011-2014), Tennessee (2015), and Dallas (2017). He adds competition to a Packers offensive line with uncertainty at right tackle, where Bryan Bulaga is recovering from a torn ACL. Other options include Jason Spriggs and Kyle Murphy, both coming off injuries. Bell's signing suggests the team isn't fully comfortable with its current roster, and he could potentially become the starting right tackle.

Out of bounds situations are critical in basketball, requiring teams to be prepared to inbound from baseline, sideline, and full court. The primary objective is to successfully inbound the ball to the best players for high-percentage shots. Plays should be simple, practiced, and involve proper cuts, screens, and passes. Players must know rules including the 5-second count, inbounder restrictions, and automatic reads like "Give & Go" and lob passes when defenders position poorly. Scouting opponents helps anticipate defensive reads. Key rules include: inbounders cannot be changed once designated, cannot touch the ball until another player does, and after made shots can run the baseline. Technical fouls occur if defenders reach over the out-of-bounds plane to touch the ball.

The passage discusses Education 4.0 in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), emphasizing the need for educational reform to develop critical thinking, adaptability, and higher-order skills. It highlights digital games as an innovative pedagogical tool for teaching-learning and assessment, particularly through Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) and Stealth Assessment (SA). This MIT lecture covers experimental studies of neutrino oscillations. Neutrino sources include supernovae, Big Bang relics, cosmic ray showers, the sun, accelerator beams, and nuclear reactors. Key experimental parameters are length, energy, and mass sensitivity ranges. Solar neutrinos (meV scale, fixed Earth-sun distance) showed initial deficits in experiments like Davis's chlorine tank (Homestake), but the SNO experiment confirmed oscillations by measuring total neutrino counts via neutral scattering. Atmospheric neutrinos from cosmic ray interactions showed muon neutrino disappearance varying with zenith angle. Accelerator experiments at CERN, Fermilab (NuMI), and Japan use near and far detectors to study appearance/disappearance, with major progress since the 2000s. Reactor experiments measure anti-electron neutrino disappearance via inverse beta decay, with facilities in France, Japan, and China.

The Medina City School District has a 5.2-mill substitute levy on the May 8 ballot to replace the expiring 5.9-mill operating levy. A court in Kochi convicted migrant labourer Muhammed Ameerul Islam from Assam for the 2016 rape and murder of a 30-year-old Dalit law student in Perumbavoor, Kerala. Ernakulam Principal Sessions Court judge N Anil Kumar found him guilty under IPC sections 302 (murder), 376 (rape), and 376(A), but not guilty under section 201 or SC/ST Act provisions. The judge will pronounce punishment on Wednesday. The crime occurred on April 28, 2016; Islam was arrested 50 days later in Tamil Nadu. The trial, which began in April 2017, examined 100 witnesses. The passage argues that AI policy is becoming critical for AI developers due to increasing government regulation, yet CS curricula largely lack AI policy content. It synthesizes US and EU AI regulatory developments: the US lacks comprehensive federal legislation and exhibits partisan polarization between safety-focused Democratic policies and dominance-focused Republican policies, while the EU's AI Act establishes risk-based regulations with transparency requirements for high-risk systems and general-purpose AI models. Three themes emerge: policy volatility requiring adaptive developers, the challenge of translating abstract policy into technical specifications, and cross-border regulatory effects like the "Brussels Effect." The authors propose a framework integrating AI policy into CS courses through three perspectives (socio-political, translational, technical) and three dimensions (scope, power, agency), with guiding questions to help students bridge policy principles and technical implementation.

During a penalty kick in soccer, attacking teammates must be positioned at least 10 yards behind the penalty mark, inside the field but outside the penalty area, and must react immediately when the ball is kicked since play is live. Players should hold their ground if positioned first, or stand beside opponents if arriving second. All attacking players must follow up on rebounds or blocked shots, with the kicker able to touch the ball again only after another player has touched it. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, attackers must immediately transition to defense. Violations result in retaken kicks or indirect free kicks.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end including a programmable gain amplifier (PGA), second-order low-pass filter, ADC driver, and precision voltage reference. The PGA converts single-ended or differential inputs to drive the internal SAR ADC, with gain adjustable via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits. A 500kHz antialiasing LPF mitigates noise, while the integrated ADC driver ensures stable sampling. The device supports internal (4.096V, default) or external reference modes, selected via INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference requires a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor and is factory-trimmed for accuracy, though thermal stress from soldering can cause shifts. Temperature compensation maintains stability from –40°C to +125°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar/unipolar ranges, outputting straight-binary format. Alarm features include programmable input thresholds (high/low with hysteresis) and fixed AVDD thresholds (4.7V low, 5.3V high), with active and tripped flags readable via ALARM_REG or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI and source-synchronous protocols, with configurable single/dual SDO modes. Daisy-chain topology allows multiple devices with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK, requiring 32×N SCLK cycles. Operational states include RESET (application or power-on), ACQ (acquisition with optional NAP mode), and CONV (conversion using internal clock).

Nine configuration registers control device operation, including SDI/SDO protocols, data output flags, range selection, and alarm thresholds. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge, with 32 SCLK cycles optimal for commands. Write operations require unlocking with 69h to address 05h for certain registers.

Power supplies AVDD (analog) and DVDD (digital) operate independently. Decoupling requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors per supply. NAP mode reduces power between conversions when CONVST/CS is held high; power-down mode disables analog blocks while retaining registers and interface. PCB layout should separate analog and digital sections, with capacitors placed close to pins without vias.

Researchers developed a unified multiscale model linking atomic-scale energetics to macroscopic GaN growth kinetics. Using machine learning interatomic potential-based molecular dynamics and metadynamics simulations, they identified ordered liquid Ga layers at GaN-Ga melt interfaces that create a "Ga lubrication" mechanism, reducing N adatom migration barriers compared to clean surfaces. These calculated energy barriers were integrated into kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, revealing diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer growth under molecular-beam epitaxy conditions. A continuous diffusion model derived from Fick's law with chemical potential gradients predicted facet-dependent growth rates without fitted parameters. Experimental validation through MBE growth and transmission electron microscopy confirmed predicted rates of 0.01-0.04 nm/s and facet trends, including faster prismatic m-plane growth than basal planes in wurtzite GaN. The framework establishes that for systems with low element solubility like N in Ga, interfacial free energy profiles determine growth kinetics, providing a transferable predictive tool for III-nitride epitaxy design.

In soccer, the second defender provides "individual support in defense" by positioning behind and to the inside of the first defender, forcing the dribbler toward the sideline. Communication is essential: announcing arrival with phrases like "support" or "you have help," and signaling when to tackle with "take him" or "tackle." The support defender may also direct the first defender to delay or contain the attacker. Training progresses from stationary positioning through half-speed with communication to full-speed play. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender takes over, potentially executing a "Defensive Switch."

This study compared air-conduction (AC) and bone-conduction (BC) auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in 64 infants aged 0-6 months with normal hearing (NH) and conductive hearing loss (CHL). ABR remains the gold standard for infant hearing assessment in early hearing detection and intervention (EHDI) programs. The study found that AC ABR and ASSR thresholds were significantly higher in CHL infants than NH infants, while BC thresholds did not differ between groups. Air-bone gaps (ABGs) were significantly larger in CHL infants for both ABR (36 dB) and ASSR (21 dB) compared to NH infants (ABR: 15 dB; ASSR: 12 dB), though ABR ABGs showed better separation between groups. Minimum intensities for ASSR were higher than ABR minimum intensities. Sensitivity and specificity analyses showed ABR outperformed ASSR in detecting mild CHL. The authors conclude that ASSR requires more research before clinical implementation and that ABR should remain the primary diagnostic tool in EHDI programs, as ASSR threshold variability was too great to reliably separate NH from mild CHL using the tested parameters.

Enron's Dabhol Power Company in India stopped generating electricity after its sole customer, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), ceased purchasing power on May 29, 2001. MSEB rejected the proposal and rescinded the 1995 Power Purchase Agreement. The plant remains operationally ready but without dispatch instructions.

Turing GPUs feature dedicated RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling real-time ray tracing in games and applications through a hybrid rendering model that combines ray tracing with rasterization. RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, delivering 10x faster ray tracing performance than Pascal GPUs. Turing also introduces Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics enhancement through NVIDIA NGX, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for improved image quality and performance. Additional features include Mesh Shading for eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for optimized shading rates, Texture Space Shading for decoupled visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering for efficient stereo and multi-viewport rendering. The architecture includes three GPU variants: TU102, TU104, and TU106, with specifications ranging from 10.8 to 18.6 billion transistors. Turing supports multiple ray tracing APIs including NVIDIA RTX, Microsoft DXR, and Vulkan ray tracing.

This study examines the awareness of educational leaders in Addis Ababa's inclusive education resource centers regarding global, regional, and national legal frameworks for inclusive education. Using a qualitative case study design with 15 participants, including Ministry of Education experts, school principals, itinerant teachers, and teachers, the research found that while favorable policies exist—including the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, African Union protocols, and Ethiopia's Education and Training Policy and Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy—awareness varies significantly among leaders. Ministry of Education experts and itinerant teachers demonstrated relatively better understanding due to specialized training, while school principals and teachers showed limited knowledge of specific legal frameworks. The study concludes that increased policy awareness among educational leaders is essential for successful inclusive education implementation and recommends professional development programs, curriculum reforms, and enhanced monitoring of policy awareness at all levels.

The passage introduces a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approach to bridge quantum and classical descriptions of light-matter interactions on the nanoscale. Classical Maxwell solvers cannot capture quantum phenomena like photon correlations and entanglement, while exact quantum descriptions become computationally prohibitive for large systems. Existing methods including phase-space representations, quantum trajectory methods, and quantum Langevin equations have limitations. The authors propose an SDE approach without wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, or operator-valued noise, validated through the Mollow spectrum of a driven two-level system. The method uses a stochastic Bloch-vector approach that can handle non-symmetric diffusion matrices, addressing asymmetric noise correlations from non-commuting quantum operators that conventional symmetric treatments exclude.

This document specifies the SEV-ES (Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Encrypted State) and SEV-SNP (Secure Nested Paging) Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD processors. It standardizes communication between encrypted guests and hypervisors through a 4KB shared memory area, defining Automatic Exits (AE) and Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) events. The GHCB mirrors VMCB save state format and supports version negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement via bitmap, and various NAE events including CPUID requests, MSR access, MMIO operations, page state changes, AP creation, and SNP-specific features like restricted injection with doorbell pages. Key protocols include GHCB MSR-based communication for pre-establishment scenarios, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, secure AVIC, and SEV-TIO for trusted devices. The document details SMP booting challenges, NMI handling, debug register support, and specifies that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

NASA Glenn researchers in Cleveland are using the GEER chamber, the largest and most accurate planetary simulator, to replicate Venus's harsh surface conditions—extreme heat, pressure, and acidic atmosphere. The facility has enabled breakthroughs including an 80-day simulation and electronics surviving 21 days, overcoming previous limitations for Venus missions. Scientists are testing rock survival rates and developing durable technology, while also studying Venus's upper atmosphere where floating missions might one day explore. Researcher Geoffrey Landis notes that understanding Venus, Earth's "evil twin" that suffered runaway greenhouse effects, helps predict Earth's climatic future.

Machine learning potentials (MLPs) combine computational efficiency with predictive accuracy but face limitations due to scarce training datasets for surface systems. Universal Interatomic Potentials (UIPs) trained on bulk data systematically underestimate surface energies. This study evaluates three strategies for predicting surface properties: training from scratch (TS), zero-shot pre-trained models (ZS), and fine-tuning (FT), plus multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT) to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.

Using MACE as the foundation model, the study examined unary (Au), binary (RuO₂), and ternary (BiVO₄) surface systems. Results showed FT consistently outperformed TS, achieving comparable accuracy with 40–200 configurations versus 2,000 for TS. FT models also produced physically realistic diatomic potentials, while TS models exhibited unphysical behaviors at short and long ranges. For BiVO₄, FT reduced force prediction outliers from 13 (TS) to 3.

MHFT, which trains concurrently on bulk and surface data, addressed FT's limitation of degraded out-of-domain performance. Testing on Ag, Cu, Pt, and Ir surfaces after gold fine-tuning, MHFT achieved RMSE of 16 meV/Å² versus 27 for ZS and 88 for FT, with only minor accuracy loss on gold surfaces. The study concludes that FT and MHFT significantly enhance surface predictions with limited data, with MHFT preferred when preserving original model capabilities is essential.

Drawing on SAMHSA's six-part framework for trauma-informed practice, the article emphasizes creating safe, inclusive spaces that empower learners as survivors rather than victims, moving them from apathy toward advocacy while minimizing secondary trauma risks for all participants.

This paper investigates whether textual content in earnings press releases predicts stock returns on announcement days. Using 138,000 press releases from 2005–2023, the authors compare NLP techniques including LDA topic modeling and BERT-family models (particularly FinBERT) against earnings surprises. Findings show soft information from press releases explains return variation comparable to hard information, with FinBERT achieving highest predictive power (R² ~4%) but LDA offering better interpretability. Market efficiency tests demonstrate no profitable trading opportunities at market open, though advance access to both earnings surprises and press release content enables 56% accuracy in identifying top 10 performing stocks. Topic analysis reveals managerial self-serving bias: positive results emphasize internal financial factors, while negative results highlight external sector conditions.

The Federal Reserve's fourth interest rate hike in 18 months will increase costs for credit card holders, those with adjustable-rate mortgages, and home equity lines of credit, with a $5,000 credit card balance costing an extra $700 over the loan's life. A UCLA study found that meat-based pet food and waste from America's 163 million dogs and cats generate about 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually, equivalent to 13.6 million cars. This email from Steven Kean to Maureen McVicker contains three Enron-related news articles from October 16, 2000. Amsterdam's Buiksloterham district is pursuing an experimental docklands regeneration focused on localization, sustainability, and circular economy principles. Kilauea's eruption, ongoing for 27 days, has sent volcanic haze 4,000 miles to Guam, prompting health warnings for residents with respiratory issues. On Hawaii's Big Island, conditions have worsened with multiple geologic phenomena including fast-moving lava threatening Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens at 600 yards per hour, lava fountains exceeding 200 feet, and "Pele's hair" volcanic glass fibers falling from the sky. The RSI indicator works on Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies as a momentum indicator but not as a mean reversion indicator. Backtesting from January 2015 to September 2021 found that buying low RSI readings and selling high readings generated weak results with few trades on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin. However, RSI momentum strategies—such as entering when a short-term RSI crosses above a threshold and exiting when it crosses below—produced better returns than buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns. Unlike stocks, where mean reversion RSI strategies work and momentum strategies fail, crypto markets show the opposite pattern.

The US Supreme Court is considering an appeal after the Arkansas Supreme Court stayed two executions. The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals overturned a federal judge's ruling that had temporarily halted all eight executions, finding that the state's lethal injection method using midazolam did not create undue severe pain.

This manuscript illustrates the value of critical approaches to quantitative research in education, targeting scholars who use quantitative methods and/or critical perspectives. The authors argue that quantitative research has never been objective, emphasizing the importance of researchers articulating their positionalities. Jay, a white cisgender researcher, focuses on supporting queer and trans students through quantitative methods, while Jimmy, a Vietnamese-Chinese American, addresses data aggregation issues affecting Asian American communities and promotes critical reflection in institutional research.

Quantitative criticalism combines quantitative methods with critical epistemologies to challenge existing policies and advocate for social justice. Researchers must engage in justice-driven scholarship throughout all research stages, from question development to result interpretation. The authors identify tensions in this approach, including white supremacist foundations in statistics, unclear thresholds of criticality, challenges in operationalizing identity variables, limitations in statistical power for intersectional analyses, and conflicts between generalizability goals and community-specific needs.

Four example studies demonstrate quantitative criticalism applications: Sablan's (2019) QuantCrit study using community cultural wealth; Garvey's (2017) queer theory-based examination of sexual identity classifications; and two intersectionality studies by Szymanski and Lewis (2016) and Wilson and Urick (2022) using different analytical approaches. The authors conclude with implications encouraging educators to incorporate epistemology in methods curricula and offering reflective questions about intentions, historical method limitations, and criticality thresholds.

SpinGPT is an LLM-based poker agent for the Spin & Go format, trained through supervised fine-tuning on 320,000 professional decisions and reinforcement learning with 270,000 solver-generated hands. The supervised model (SpinGPT-SFT) achieved 80% exact accuracy in imitating professional play and won 13.4 BB/100 against the Slumbot benchmark after a heuristic patch. The final SpinGPT model, refined with ORPO offline RL, achieved 72% exact accuracy on solver data and defeated SpinGPT-SFT by 13.2 BB/100. The system is based on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with LoRA fine-tuning, using structured text prompts encoding game states. Limitations include format mismatch with benchmarks, potential LLM hallucinations, and lack of evaluation against human opponents or Spin & Go specialists.

A global learning crisis, worsened by pandemic closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs $129 billion annually. Youth unemployment nears 30% in lower-income countries, with 20% of global youth not in employment, education or training—two-thirds being young women. Nearly 40% of employers report skills shortages, with 39% of current job skills expected to transform by 2030. In lower-income countries, two-thirds of young adult workers face educational mismatch, primarily from being undereducated.

The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) addresses this by supporting partner countries through policy dialogue, financing and public-private partnerships to build education systems that teach foundational skills and 21st century competencies including creativity, problem solving and collaboration. Examples include Lesotho's Chamber of Commerce participating in education dialogue and securing matched funding, Ghana's $40 million consortium investment in foundational learning, Kenya's competency-based curriculum with the LEGO Foundation and World Bank, and El Salvador's teacher training on socio-emotional skills. In 2024, 20 GPE grants focused on employment-ready skills.

The passage lists 17 common mistakes that sabotage weight-loss efforts: drinking from plastic bottles (BPA leaching), eliminating sweets entirely, perfectionism, emotional eating, consuming store-bought protein bars and energy drinks, eating sweets randomly, surrounding yourself with unsupportive people, relying on scales for success, using meal-replacement supplements, eliminating all carbs, eating only fat-free products, insufficient sleep, extreme calorie restriction with excessive exercise, repetitive workout routines, drinking calories instead of eating them, being too strict too soon, and copying someone else's weight-loss routine. The MACD-histogram trading strategy is a mean-reversion system that identifies momentum changes and reversal points. Tested on 77 ETFs, it generated 6,669 trades with long positions outperforming short positions. Entry occurs on the close; exit occurs on the first day when the close exceeds the previous day's close. A backtest on QLD (2x Nasdaq 100) from 2007 onward showed 85 trades, 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, and 19% max drawdown while invested only 5% of the time. The MACD histogram visually represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line; bars above zero indicate bullish momentum, below indicates bearish momentum. The crossover strategy triggers buy signals when the histogram crosses above zero and sell signals when crossing below.

Turing GPUs feature a new display engine supporting 8K resolution at 60 Hz, HDR, and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2. They include enhanced NVENC for H.265 8K encoding and updated NVDEC for HEVC and VP9 decoding. Turing introduces hardware support for USB-C and VirtualLink, enabling single-cable VR connectivity. RT Cores enable real-time ray tracing, with hybrid rendering combining ray tracing and rasterization. Tensor Cores support NGX AI features including DLSS for image enhancement, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading eliminates CPU draw call bottlenecks, while Variable Rate Shading and Texture Space Shading optimize rendering performance. Multi-View Rendering expands simultaneous viewpoint processing from two to four.

Onesmo Rupil, 23, began using drugs at age 17, leading to his dismissal from the University of Dodoma in 2013 due to poor academic performance from substance abuse. Now recovered, he manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House in Mwanza, housing 30 young people in rehabilitation. Most clients use marijuana, which Onesmo notes is widely produced and trafficked locally. He attributes his own drug use partly to limited parental care from early boarding school attendance. Dr. Kassian Nyandindi of Muhimbili National Hospital reports 550,000 people affected by drug abuse in Tanzania as of 2014, with only 3,500 of 25,000 addicts receiving treatment. This study developed and validated an automated system for monitoring clinical practice guideline adherence in intensive care units by combining FHIR-encoded guidelines with OMOP CDM-standardized patient data. The system was deployed across five university hospitals to evaluate adherence to six COVID-19 and ARDS-related recommendations across 82,015 intensive care episodes. In validation against ground truth established by experienced supervising physicians, the system achieved 97.0% accuracy, significantly outperforming human reviewers (86.6%; p < 0.001), while processing over 2,000 patient days per second compared to approximately 30 seconds per patient-day for manual review. Most discrepancies (over 80%) were due to human error, often from overlooking data in complex clinical information system interfaces or inconsistent interpretation of imprecisely formulated recommendations. System errors primarily stemmed from unstructured free-text data not captured in ETL pipelines. The study found adherence rates of 10-60% for most recommendations, influenced by factors including pandemic timing, documentation completeness, and strict evaluation criteria. The authors recommend that guidelines explicitly define tolerance ranges, adherence frequency requirements, permissible deviation limits, and relevant time intervals to enable reproducible automated monitoring.

He dismisses fatigue concerns, emphasizes containing New Jersey's balanced, chemistry-driven lines, and trusts the coaching staff to find right matchups. He expresses confidence in his team's ability to respond to the challenge and play with urgency in the upcoming important game.

A 2018 paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry published in the Journal of Climate estimates that future global warming will be 30-45% lower than IPCC projections. Using observed temperature data from 1869-2016, the study derives median equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) estimates of 1.50-1.66°C and transient climate response (TCR) of 1.20-1.33°C, compared to 3.1°C ECS and 1.9°C TCR in 31 CMIP5 climate models. The authors address criticisms of their methodology, finding that potential biases from time-varying climate feedbacks, forcing efficacy, and temperature estimation issues are minor when using globally-complete data. The study concludes that high climate sensitivity values from most computer models are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850.

This document is a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for clinical trial ZP4207-17086, detailing planned analyses for plasma glucose concentration, pharmacodynamic metrics, and safety endpoints. Safety analyses cover extent of exposure (insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion), local tolerability, adverse events (TEAEs, SAEs, AESIs, injection site reactions, drug-related events), laboratory parameters (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy and alcohol tests), vital signs, ECG (including QTc categorical analysis), and immunogenicity (ADA occurrence). The SAP includes changes from protocol-specified analyses, references, appendices with programming specifications, QC requirements, and a comprehensive list of tables, figures, and listings with detailed specifications for each output.

Former Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said higher interest rates are needed to prevent the U.S. economy from overheating, but the pace must allow inflation to reach the Fed's 2 percent goal. She stated that monthly job growth of 90,000 to 120,000 is sustainable, and that tightening too slowly risks overheating while tightening too quickly could prevent inflation from reaching target. Yellen, who left the Fed last month after President Trump appointed Jerome Powell as chair, oversaw unemployment falling from 6.7 percent to 4.1 percent during her tenure. Powell is expected to continue gradual rate increases, with another hike anticipated this week.

Arizona has led U.S. school choice for decades, becoming the first state to enact universal Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers in 2022 despite voter rejection of a capped expansion in 2018. The state now provides over $1 billion annually in private education subsidies. The Grand Canyon Institute (GCI) finds that universal ESA vouchers cost the state general fund a net $330-350 million annually because most participants never attended public schools. While ESA vouchers primarily enroll children from higher-income zip codes, this gap has declined. GCI estimates that under 40% of ESA students use funds for private school tuition, with many using them for homeschooling or extracurricular activities. By FY2024, $360 million had accumulated in unspent ESA accounts. Religious schools, particularly Evangelical Christian and Catholic institutions, received 86% of religious school ESA expenditures in FY2023. Charter schools are disproportionately losing students to ESA vouchers despite enrolling only one-fourth as many students as district schools.

Mega Geometry is an RTX technology that increases geometric detail in ray-traced applications by enabling game engines like Unreal Engine 5 with Nanite to ray trace at full fidelity without low-resolution proxies. It addresses two main challenges: cluster-based LOD updates through Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) that reduce BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude, and high object counts through Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) that update only changed partitions. Mega Geometry also brings displaced subdivision surfaces to real-time ray tracing and is supported on all RTX GPUs from Turing onward via DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0.

Blackwell's 4th generation RT Cores add hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for efficient hair/fur rendering, offering 2x speed and 5x less VRAM than DOTS. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 improves GPU thread organization with twice as efficient reorder logic. The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a RISC-V-based scheduler that offloads GPU context management from the CPU, reducing latency and improving frame rates.

Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video, with the 9th-gen NVENC improving AV1/HEVC quality by 5% and adding AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. DisplayPort 2.1b support enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating with faster state transitions, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and 10x faster sleep state entry.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to 3 additional frames per rendered frame) using transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, offering better temporal stability and detail. Neural shaders enable techniques like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM savings), Neural Radiance Cache for global illumination, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces for realistic facial rendering.

The Blackwell GPU family includes: GB202 (flagship, 92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores) for RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6B transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores) for RTX 5080/5070 Ti; and GB205 (31B transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores) for RTX 5070.

This research examines pre-service teachers' opinions on Turkey's Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (grades 5-8) across four dimensions: achievements, content, learning-teaching processes, and measurement-evaluation practices. Using a quantitative survey with 100 students from Bayburt University's Faculty of Sports Sciences, the study found generally positive views toward program achievements, with 43% agreeing outcomes match student levels and 70% finding them understandable. However, 37% were undecided about scientific accuracy in outcomes. Regarding content, 80% agreed it was meaningfully ordered, though many were undecided about scientific errors, age-appropriateness, and international compatibility. For teaching processes, 56% agreed activities were enriching and 61% noted concrete materials usage, yet 60% disagreed that diverse methods were employed. In assessment-evaluation, 43% agreed different forms were used, but 34% were undecided about evaluation methods. The study concludes that pre-service teachers lack sufficient knowledge about program content, international comparisons, and scientific foundations, recommending increased research, informative seminars, and curriculum review courses in teacher training programs.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 5, 2016 correcting an error in footnote 1B of its Second Quarter 2016 Update. The corrected amounts for "Net increase in operating lease vehicles as result of lease accounting" are $241,253 thousand and $600,351 thousand for the three and six months ended June 30, 2016, respectively. The error did not impact cost of revenues or GAAP to Non-GAAP reconciliation.

This patent application describes methods for forming 3-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays. The invention uses damascene local vertical bit lines and avoids ribboning (stress-induced deformation of microscopic features) by etching local word lines in two steps, reducing aspect ratio and improving structural stability of word line stacks. The method addresses alignment issues from this two-step etching process. Memory structures are built on conductive global interconnect lines with multi-layers of silicon nitride and silicon oxide. Fabrication involves creating trenches, forming word line stacks, removing silicon nitride layers to create cavities, filling with metal to form word line strips, and depositing tunneling dielectric, charge storage, blocking dielectric, channel, and sacrificial layers in vias. Source and drain semiconductor regions are formed to create vertical NOR-type memory strings. The lecture discusses effective field theory (EFT) with fine tuning in the context of two-nucleon scattering. The professor explains that fine tuning occurs when an operator appears irrelevant under dimensional power counting but becomes relevant in actual calculations, indicating that naive dimensional counting is incorrect.

The theory involves non-relativistic nucleons with contact interactions and derivatives of contact interactions. For elastic scattering, the amplitude relates to the phase shift through the S-matrix, and the effective range expansion shows that P cotangent delta can be expressed as a Taylor series in momentum.

The Lagrangian includes kinetic terms and contact interactions with Wilson coefficients C_{2M} for operators with 2M derivatives. Feynman rules are simple: -iC_0 for no derivatives and -iC_2P^2 for two derivatives. Loop calculations require keeping both time and spatial derivative terms in the kinetic energy to avoid pinch singularities.

Power counting reveals that C_{2M} scales as 1/M. The complete amplitude forms a geometric series that can be summed, yielding P cotangent delta as a sum over coefficients. For S-waves, this gives the effective range expansion: -1/a + (r_0/2)P^2 + ..., where a is the scattering length and r_0 is the effective range.

Experimentally, scattering lengths are large (23 fm for 1S0, 5 fm for 3S1), indicating fine tuning. This requires treating C_0 as relevant rather than irrelevant. Two renormalization schemes achieve this: offshell momentum subtraction and power divergence subtraction (PDS). Both track power law divergences that dimensional regularization with MS-bar misses.

The beta function for C_0 shows three fixed points: a=0 (non-interacting) and a=±∞ (interacting). Nature's large scattering lengths correspond to being near the interacting fixed points, where the theory becomes scale invariant and conformal. The renormalization group equations propagate the fine tuning enhancement to higher operators: C_0 ~ 1/μ, C_2 ~ 1/(μ^2Λ), C_4 with mixed scaling, etc.

The amplitude with this power counting sums all orders of C_0 and expands in C_2 and higher operators, making explicit the independence from the renormalization scale μ.

This document describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine for AMD EPYC processors, which facilitates migrating memory pages between physical tiers while maintaining guest physical addresses. Firmware can be reloaded via BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol with version checking. Performance is optimized with 128-page batches and minimized interrupts.
