This paper presents an experimental study on using large language models (LLMs) to autoformalize physics problems for cyber-physical systems (CPS) in differential game logic (dGL). This study explores using large language models (LLMs) combined with linguistic and acoustic features to identify digital biomarkers for depression and anxiety disorders. Results demonstrate that LLM-extracted objective cues combined with behavioral markers can differentiate diagnostic groups and identify symptom disclosure, potentially enhancing psychiatric diagnosis efficiency and effectiveness.

Cover Zero is an aggressive, all-out pressure defense where every non-blitzing player covers an offensive skill player in man-to-man coverage. Examples include mirrored slants from Ole Miss, an Oregon RB seam gadget, Michigan's trips bunch jerk route, Wake Forest's slant-rub, and Jerry Rice motion slant-flat concepts.

COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, is detected in wastewater through RNA monitoring. Traditional virus concentration methods require centrifuges capable of handling 50-250 mL samples, limiting use in resource-limited settings. Three sampling methods exist: grab, composite, and passive sampling, with Moore swabs used for passive collection. This study evaluates parameters affecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection in wastewater and compares automated versus manual Nanotrap methods, as well as Nanotrap versus traditional membrane filtration and skim milk methods, to enable scalable, resource-appropriate wastewater surveillance.

This patent application describes a data intake and query system for processing machine-generated data from modern data centers. The system collects, indexes, and searches unstructured machine data (events) using a late-binding schema that applies extraction rules at search time rather than ingestion time. Key components include forwarders that receive and forward data, indexers that parse and index events with timestamps, and search heads that process queries. The system supports cloud-based deployments and can search external data systems through External Result Provider (ERP) processes. Indexers store events in time-series buckets with inverted indexes for efficient keyword and field-value searching. In this 2004 federal court case, plaintiff Melissa Jennings sued the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, soccer coach Anson Dorrance, and other university officials, claiming sexual harassment, invasion of privacy, and related claims. This literature review examines Information Technology (IT) integration in Indonesian language education within the Education 4.0 framework. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digital transformation, introducing alternatives such as Online Learning Platforms, Mobile Learning, Blended Learning, and AI-assisted tools. Research indicates IT improves language learning outcomes, with studies showing technology-based learning enhances language strategy use and engagement.

Key challenges include teachers' technological proficiency, maintaining student engagement in virtual environments, resource availability, and remote assessment difficulties—particularly for speaking and listening skills. The digital divide affects students globally, with unreliable internet and inadequate devices limiting participation.

Technological innovations analyzed include Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Learning Management Systems, gamification, and Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), which provides real-time pronunciation feedback and supports vocabulary acquisition through task-based and game-based learning.

Effective management strategies encompass digital platform integration, teacher professional development, AI-based language support tools, global virtual exchange programs, cloud infrastructure investment, mobile learning solutions, data-driven decision-making, and inclusive IT policies ensuring equitable access.

Student attitudes toward IT in language education are generally positive, similar to STEM fields, though resistance exists due to digital literacy gaps and concerns about replacing face-to-face interaction. Equitable resource access and teacher facilitation remain critical for successful implementation.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 nasal spray as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) against COVID-19 in 1,222 healthy adult workers in Beijing, China, during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95%CI 52.41%-92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95%CI 37.50%-76.69%). No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred. Adverse events were mild and similar between groups, with no serious adverse events reported. The intranasal administration offers advantages over intramuscular injections. This passage describes a medical system for assisting rescuers with intubation procedures, particularly rapid sequence intubation (RSI). The system uses multiple sensors—including airflow sensors, capnography sensors, impedance sensors, and acoustic sensors—to monitor gas parameters (oxygen, CO2, flow rate), physiological parameters (oxygen saturation, ETCO2, ECG, transthoracic impedance, blood pressure), and positioning parameters. A patient monitoring device with processors analyzes this data to automatically detect which step of the intubation procedure is being performed, verify proper endotracheal tube placement, and provide context-sensitive feedback through displays, wrist-worn devices, or other output devices. The system initiates timers upon detecting airflow, establishes physiological baselines for ongoing tube placement verification, and alerts users to improper placement or patient deterioration. The system may include defibrillators, portable computing devices, and connectivity to central facilities for additional patient information.

The long-short equity strategy involves taking long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline, aiming to minimize risk while maximizing profits from both rising and falling prices. Popular among hedge funds, this strategy often employs a long bias (such as 130/30) due to the market's upward trend. It requires identifying underpriced and overpriced stocks, frequently across different sectors to avoid correlation. The Medallion Fund and Edward Thorp's Princeton Newport Partners exemplify successful use of this approach. A backtest example using Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola showed a 3.8% annual return with 11% max drawdown. The strategy typically requires leverage and diversified pairs to be worthwhile, making it more suitable for institutional than retail investors.

Researchers developed an AI-assisted inverse design workflow to discover new 2D Dion-Jacobson (DJ) perovskites with targeted electronic properties. The approach uses a 12-digit invertible fingerprint representation of diammonium organic spacers, enabling two-way conversion between molecular structure and property prediction. Starting from 21 reported spacers, they generated approximately 4 million hypothetical candidates through molecular morphing, then used high-throughput DFT calculations and machine learning (LASSO regression) to predict energy level alignments. A two-step synthesis feasibility screening assessed PubChem availability and structural formability. The workflow identified 56 promising candidates with rarely explored type Ib, IIa, and IIb energy level alignments—8 type IIa and 44 type IIb validated by DFT, plus 2 type Ib found through inverse design in higher generations. Key design rules emerged: type Ib requires acene-based backbones with 5+ rings, type IIa needs extended conjugation, and type IIb benefits from pyridine-type nitrogen substitution. The method addresses limitations of forward design approaches by enabling targeted property-based material discovery rather than exhaustive chemical space searches.

This patent application describes systems and methods for improving occlusion rendering in passthrough visualizations for head-mounted devices (HMDs). Passthrough allows HMD users to see their physical surroundings via front-facing cameras, with images re-rendered from a 3D model to account for camera-eye misalignment and provide parallax. However, imprecise 3D models at object edges cause incorrect occlusion boundaries when virtual objects are placed near passthrough objects. The disclosed solution uses instance segmentation masks (e.g., for persons, pets) with computed depth measurements based on the 3D model, assigning significantly farther depth values to outer mask edges to create sufficient contrast. The rendering system samples these mask-assigned depth values to determine occlusion, improving passthrough visualization appearance. The application also describes optimized depth estimation techniques using video encoders and motion vectors for resource-limited devices, generating sparse point clouds and deformed 3D meshes to represent environmental contours.

A study in southern Zambia's low-transmission Choma District found rising prevalence of the Pfk13 P441L mutation, a WHO-candidate marker for artemisinin partial resistance (ArtR), increasing from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023. The passage describes methods and apparatus for improving user experience with three-dimensional (3D) binaural sound localization. Key challenges addressed include difficulties in localizing near-field sounds (less than one meter) and misalignment between perceived sound origin and visual sources. Solutions involve convolving sound to locations behind or near sound sources using far-field head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) rather than near-field HRTFs, enabling listeners to perceive sound as originating from visible sources even when actual convolution coordinates differ. Techniques include positioning sound on line-of-sight paths, adjusting volume to match visual distance, and selecting HRTFs based on listener distance. The system detects device actions (rotation, facial detection, sensor blockage, distance changes) to switch between binaural and mono/stereo sound. The professor discusses orthonormal expansions, contrasting finite and infinite dimensional spaces, and explains that projections onto orthonormal vectors converge to the original vector. The lecture then transitions to communication systems, describing the standard process of converting sources to binary data, then to symbols, and finally to waveforms for transmission. The professor explains the separation of discrete encoding and modulation, noting that modern systems often combine these functions. He discusses Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM), where symbols are mapped to real-valued signals and then to waveforms through filtering.

The Nyquist criterion for avoiding intersymbol interference is presented: a filter g(t) is ideal Nyquist with period T if g(0)=1 and g(kT)=0 for all non-zero integers k. This condition ensures that received samples equal transmitted symbols. The professor explains that while the sinc function satisfies this criterion, it has impractical delay characteristics. The raised cosine filter is introduced as a practical solution that provides faster decay while maintaining the Nyquist property through band edge symmetry.

Rutile RuO₂ has been proposed as an altermagnetic (AM) candidate due to reports of sublattice magnetic moments and high band splitting, but debate persists about whether it intrinsically hosts altermagnetism. Recent measurements and calculations report no sublattice moment in bulk RuO₂, suggesting thin-film observations may arise from extrinsic effects like strain, doping, or surface states. Exchange bias (EB) in RuO₂/ferromagnetic (FM) heterostructures has been cited as evidence for antiferromagnetism, but its origin remains unclear.

This study investigates EB in incoherent RuO₂/Fe/Ru heterostructures using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR), polarized neutron diffraction (PND), atom probe tomography (APT), HRTEM, and EELS. PND found no antiferromagnetic ordering in RuO₂ thin films. PNR revealed uncompensated, canted moments at the RuO₂/Fe interface that are sensitive to field history. APT, HRTEM, and EELS showed the interface contains mainly iron oxide with detectable magnetite (Fe₃O₄), known to produce EB through a low-temperature transition. EB was absent in RuO₂/Ni heterostructures, which have different oxidation potentials and stable compounds at the interface.

The results establish that EB in RuO₂/Fe-based heterostructures does not arise from intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic ordering in RuO₂, but from a magnetically active interlayer stabilized by Fe's high oxidation potential relative to Ru. This finding indicates EB and related magnetotransport behaviors should not alone be considered evidence of altermagnetism in RuO₂.

This paper explores applying Bayesian methods to relevance-theoretic pragmatics, specifically modeling implicature comprehension. It distinguishes between explicatures (propositions derived from contextual enrichment of logical forms) and implicatures (implicit premises and conclusions not resulting from logical form development). The authors develop a probabilistic model in ProbLog that captures relevance theory's comprehension heuristic: accessing interpretive hypotheses in order of accessibility and accepting the first that satisfies relevance expectations. The model uses Kullback-Leibler divergence to measure how utterances change probability distributions over propositions, with processing effort estimated via Herbrand base size. Five interpretive hypotheses are evaluated, demonstrating how the optimization model selects optimally relevant interpretations by eliminating hypotheses that fail relevance expectations, preferring those with highest divergence when effort is equal, and favoring smaller knowledge bases when divergence is equal.

Cybersecurity researchers at Georgia Institute of Technology developed ransomware that can control simulated water treatment plants, manipulating valves, chlorine levels, and readings. Researchers from the University of St Andrews developed deep neural networks to classify hyper-scale multi-modal medical imaging datasets. They combined 102 datasets to create a collection of 4.5 million images across four modalities: CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray. Three CNN architectures—ResNet-50, ResNet-18, and VGG16—were trained to classify images by modality. The best performing model, ResNet-18, achieved 96% classification accuracy and 86% balanced accuracy on unseen test data. The study demonstrates that CNNs can be trained on hyper-scale multimodal medical imaging datasets for accurate modality classification, with potential applications in medical imaging repositories and national healthcare institutions. X-ray classification performance was lower for bone X-rays compared to chest X-rays, indicating need for more diverse X-ray training data. Future work aims to extend classification to 3D scan modalities.

Chinese and Japanese troops entered Korea in response to a southern rebellion. Korean forces suppressed the rebellion themselves. The passage argues that mass formal schooling systems cause significant systemic harm to students through structural, objective, and symbolic mechanisms, including authoritarian control, preparation for capitalist subordination, and normalization of power imbalances. Educational pacifism rejects this harm as morally unjust because it treats innocent students merely as means to ends, violating Kantian ethical principles. Maria Montessori's philosophy aligns with educational pacifism through her critique of coercive schooling, emphasis on freedom and harmonious activity, and vision of education as creating intrapersonal and interpersonal peace. Contemporary Montessori education should embrace educational pacifism by rejecting harmful practices like testing, timetabling, and paternalism, while maintaining non-coercive structure and guidance. The author urges Montessorians to form a vanguard against educational harm and ensure authentic implementation of peace-centered pedagogy.

This MIT lecture introduces underactuated robotics, defining it as systems where control inputs cannot accelerate the system in every direction. The instructor contrasts conservative, high-gain robots like ASIMO—which uses 20 times more energy than humans when walking—with passive dynamic walkers that exploit natural dynamics. Examples from nature (birds, fish, albatrosses) demonstrate efficient, agile movement through clever use of dynamics rather than overpowering them with actuation. The lecture defines fully actuated systems (where F2 is full rank, enabling feedback linearization) versus underactuated systems (where rank of F2 is less than dimension of q). Using a two-link robotic arm example, the instructor derives equations of motion via Lagrangian mechanics, showing how the manipulator equations (Hq̈ + Cq̇ + G = Bu) reveal system structure. Removing the shoulder motor creates an underactuated Acrobot system. The course will cover optimal control, numerical methods, policy search, motion planning, and machine learning approaches to handle underactuated systems with uncertainty and unknown models.

Nick Mathewson, co-developer of Tor, discusses the anonymity network in an MIT lecture. Tor consists of approximately 6,000 volunteer-operated servers serving hundreds of thousands to millions of users. Mathewson explains that anonymity enables honest communication by protecting users from social consequences, with legitimate users including researchers, companies, law enforcement, and regular citizens seeking privacy for searches, political engagement, or sensitive health research.

He defines anonymity technically as preventing observers from linking participants to actions, distinguishing it from related concepts like unobservability and unlinkability. The lecture covers Tor's design evolution from onion routing, using multiple relays with layered encryption to prevent any single party from correlating traffic. Mathewson emphasizes that anonymity requires large user bases—"anonymity loves company"—making shared public systems preferable to private ones.

The talk addresses node discovery challenges, leading to a consensus-based directory authority system, and discusses abuse issues including IP-based blocking and hidden services. Future work includes key blinding to prevent enumeration attacks, cryptographic updates, improved path selection, congestion control, and scaling to larger networks. Mathewson notes that while criminals use Tor, effective security systems must work for all users, and deploying practical systems helps establish their social necessity despite imperfect solutions.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate health professions education (occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medicine) to inform occupational therapy education. From 202 identified studies, 9 met inclusion criteria. Qualitative content analysis revealed three themes contributing to both barriers and facilitators: environment (physical space and institutional culture/climate), relationships (faculty-to-student and peer-to-peer), and personal factors (student perceptions of belonging, academic ability, and identity). Students from historically minoritized identities face particular barriers including belonging uncertainty, discrimination, and microaggressions. The review recommends occupational therapy programs create welcoming spaces, build strong faculty-student and peer relationships, provide mentorship opportunities, implement bias training, and support affinity groups to foster belonging for all students.

This study proposes a world model framework using reinforcement learning for autonomous navigation in mechanical thrombectomy (MT). The authors implemented TD-MPC2 and SAC algorithms to perform multiple endovascular navigation tasks across ten patient-specific vasculatures in simulation. Single-task training with SAC achieved 82-100% success rates for individual phases. For multi-task learning across all phases, TD-MPC2 significantly outperformed SAC, achieving 65% mean success rate versus 37% (p < 0.001), with notable improvements in tasks A2R, A3L, and A3R. However, TD-MPC2 required longer procedure times. The study represents the largest dataset examined for autonomous MT and demonstrates TD-MPC2's superior generalization capabilities, though clinical deployment requires further optimization.

This lecture introduces graph limits, a relatively new subject in graph theory that provides an analytic framework for studying sequences of graphs. The speaker motivates the topic through an analogy: just as real numbers complete the rationals, allowing minimization problems to have single-number solutions rather than cumbersome sequences, graph limits provide single objects (called graphons) to represent limits of graph sequences.

A graphon is defined as a symmetric, measurable function W from [0,1]² to [0,1]. Examples include: converting a finite graph's adjacency matrix into a pixelated black-and-white image (a step function graphon); the limit of half graphs as n→∞, which becomes the function W(x,y) = 1 if x+y ≥ 1, 0 otherwise; and constant graphons representing quasirandom graphs.

The lecture defines homomorphism densities t(H,G) for graphs and extends this to graphons through integrals. A sequence of graphs converges if all homomorphism densities converge. Three main theorems are stated: (1) convergence in homomorphism densities is equivalent to being Cauchy in cut distance; (2) every convergent sequence has a limit graphon; and (3) the space of graphons is compact. The cut distance between graphons involves optimizing over measure-preserving transformations, generalizing vertex permutations. The speaker notes connections to Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma and quasirandomness.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) in Chile’s Atacama Desert for sub-millimeter observations beginning in 2026. The collaboration is assembling two instruments: Mod-Cam, a cryogenic testbed receiver with a 280 GHz camera, and Prime-Cam, a seven-module science instrument housing approximately 100,000 kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs). Both instruments employ flexible stripline circuits to connect cryogenic detector arrays to warm readout electronics across temperature stages from 4 K to 300 K.

This work characterizes the thermal and electrical performance of the stripline assemblies. Residual resistance ratio (RRR) measurements of the copper traces yielded approximately 120, consistent with high-purity OFHC copper. Direct thermal conductivity measurements agree with theoretical predictions. Thermal loading estimates demonstrate that Prime-Cam’s redesigned stripline (featuring reduced copper thickness and extended length between stages) will exhibit lower thermal loading at 4 K than Mod-Cam’s configuration despite having three times as many striplines.

Investigations into elevated crosstalk observed during Mod-Cam testing isolated the source to the SMP-SMA transition printed circuit boards (PCBs) rather than the stripline itself. The transition PCBs have been redesigned using impedance-matched vias to bury signal traces between ground planes, with simulations predicting approximately 20 dB improvement in crosstalk levels. These results validate the stripline approach as a scalable solution for reading out large KID arrays.

The author presents three options-based strategies to participate in AMD's potential upward movement before its Q1 2018 earnings announcement on April 25, 2018, without immediately purchasing shares at ~$10. First, buying a $10 strike call for $0.60 limits risk to $60 versus $1,000 for 100 shares. Second, a call spread—buying the $10 call and selling the $12 call—reduces net cost to $0.50, capping profits at $12 but lowering risk to $0.50. Third, selling a cash-covered $10 put for $0.56 reduces cost basis to $9.44 if assigned; combined with the call spread, this yields a net $0.06 credit. The author believes AMD's earnings will be positive, citing product improvements, processor demand, and a large short position (181.9 million shares) that could fuel a squeeze. Risks include capped profits, total loss of option premiums if AMD falls below $10, and forced share assignment if the put expires in-the-money. The author discloses long positions in AMD, INTC, and NVDA.
Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 2, 2015, furnishing a press release dated that day under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The report was signed by General Counsel Todd A. Maron.

A felon armed with a slungshot forced his way into a southeast Portland apartment Thursday night. Police responded to Stark Street Villa Apartments after witnesses reported a man threatening to kill people while attempting to break into apartments. Officers forced entry into an apartment, found a frightened woman, and took 37-year-old Jason A. Clifford into custody. A slungshot—a rope-like item with a hard object at the end—was recovered. Clifford was booked on charges including first-degree burglary, felon in possession of a restricted weapon, menacing, coercion, and first-degree theft. Two others in the apartment, Dustin L. Baker and Lindsey M. Walker, were arrested on outstanding warrants but are not believed involved in Clifford's actions.

WIRED reviews white noise and sound machines for better sleep. The article explains that "white noise" refers to a mix of all audible frequencies, while pink and brown noise use lower frequencies that many find more soothing. Tested products include the LectroFan Classic ($50), which offers fan sounds and colored noise with an 85-decibel maximum and 60-minute timer; the Snooz, which uses a real fan for simple operation; the Hatch 3 and Hatch Rest 2nd Gen, which combine sound machines with sunrise clocks and night-lights but require subscriptions for full features; the Babelio mini for pets; Yogasleep's Dohm, a 1962 design still used today; Momcozy's portable option with Bluetooth; the ErgoPouch with pebble-like aesthetics; a compact Amazon Basics model; and smart speakers like Google Nest and Amazon Echo, which can play ambient sounds via voice commands. The article notes safety guidelines for infants—keep machines under 50 decibels and more than 6.5 feet from cribs.

The Inverted Hammer is a bullish reversal candlestick pattern forming at the bottom of downtrends, characterized by a small body at the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow. It indicates buyers gaining momentum against sellers and potential upward price movement, but requires confirmation from other technical indicators such as trendlines, support levels, moving averages, and momentum oscillators. Backtests indicate a 70% win rate and an average gain of 0.36% per trade on the S&P 500, with the pattern occurring more frequently in overbought (58%) than oversold (42%) conditions. Traders utilize it for swing trading and mean reversion strategies, ideally within uptrends to signal the end of pullbacks, while employing risk management techniques including stop-loss orders and position sizing.

President Trump will order an investigation into Chinese trade practices requiring U.S. firms to surrender intellectual property. The move, which could lead to tariffs, comes as Trump seeks China's cooperation on North Korea. Administration officials insist the trade probe and North Korea diplomacy are unrelated. The investigation, under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, could take a year and may bypass WTO procedures. Trump had postponed the announcement earlier to seek China's help on North Korea. The EU, Japan, Germany, and Canada have also raised concerns about Chinese intellectual property theft.

Violet Brown, a 117-year-old Jamaican woman, is believed to have become the world's oldest living person following Emma Morano's death. Born March 10, 1900, Brown worked as a sugarcane farmer and attributes her longevity to hard work and Christian faith. She has credible birth documentation verified by researchers, though Guinness World Records has not yet officially confirmed her title. Brown lives with her 97-year-old son, can sit and walk short distances, and remains mentally sharp despite hearing difficulties.

A UC Davis study published in Annals of Epidemiology found California gun deaths declined from 2000-2015, driven by reduced gang violence and decreased homicides among black men. Firearm homicides dropped from 4.19 to 3.13 per 100,000 people, with black male gun homicides falling 32% from their 2005 peak and Hispanic male homicides declining 38%. White and Asian male rates remained steady. The research comes as California and private foundations increase gun violence study funding after federal restrictions.

Digital laggards set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and adopt unguided "best effort" approaches focused on process adherence rather than outcomes. Digital leaders create structured, transparent goals with clear metrics aligned to strategy, using data-driven objectives to coordinate across organizational levels while maintaining flexibility. They emphasize data culture as central to aligning beliefs, values, and actions. Data culture enables both vertical alignment (individuals to company goals) and horizontal alignment (cross-team collaboration). Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant, each with distinct strengths and improvement areas for building strong data culture.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, delivers significant performance improvements over previous generations for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, binary), fine-grained structured sparsity for up to 2x throughput gains, and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology enabling secure partitioning into up to seven independent GPU instances. The A100 provides 40GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, 40MB L2 cache, and third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s total bandwidth. Manufactured on TSMC's 7nm process with 54.2 billion transistors, the A100 achieves up to 20x speedups for specific operations compared to V100. CUDA 11 introduces new features including asynchronous copy operations, task graph acceleration, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch and Mellanox networking, delivering 5 petaFLOPS performance in a 6U form factor.

This study presents a handheld ISFET Lab-on-Chip device for point-of-care detection of circulating nucleic acid biomarkers in prostate cancer patients. The device uses RT-pHLAMP assays to detect YAP1 nucleic acid and AR-FL/AR-V7 mRNA from blood plasma within 15 minutes after RNA extraction. Testing in 14 PCa patients showed 100% concordance between benchtop and LoC detection for YAP1 and AR-FL. YAP1 nucleic acid presence correlated with advanced cancer staging (p=0.043) and higher initial PSA levels (p=0.035). AR-FL mRNA and AR-V7 mRNA were detected only in high-risk or metastatic patients. The authors note this is the first ISFET-based biosensor capable of detecting endogenous circulating nucleic acids from cancer patients and the first handheld device for PCa circulating mRNA detection.

Mark Schroeder emailed Steven Kean on December 8, 2000, providing feedback on an EU power sector summary document forwarded by Kean from McKinsey. Schroeder noted three errors: the Spanish pool is not mandatory (generation owners can bypass it), Denmark has more than two generators due to municipal ownership, and the Netherlands' "transitional" anti-competitive arrangements were omitted. He also observed that Poland was interestingly excluded from Central and Eastern Europe discussion despite being the most progressive former Communist country.

The forwarded McKinsey document, dated December 6, 2000, by Carol B White and Pru Sheppard, provides a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June-November 2000. It covers developments across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and Middle East/Africa, with country-specific details on market liberalization, unbundling, privatization, and competition status in approximately 50 countries.

European shares rallied on Monday, recovering from their worst weekly losses of the year caused by U.S.-North Korea tensions. The STOXX 600 rose 0.7 percent, with banking stocks leading gains. RWE jumped 3 percent after raising its profit outlook, while Danone gained 2 percent on takeover speculation. Ladbrokes Coral fell 2.7 percent after a Credit Suisse downgrade. Standard Life Aberdeen rose 2.7 percent on its trading debut, and Fiat Chrysler led auto stocks up 3.5 percent. Energy and basic materials sectors outperformed in quarterly results, while consumer cyclical and industrial companies missed expectations.

This case study examines Compass Minerals International on the eve of its December 12, 2003 IPO, led by CEO Michael Ducey. The company, acquired by Apollo Management from IMC Global in 2001, was the third-largest U.S. salt producer through its North American Salt subsidiary.

The salt industry has ancient origins with three main production methods: rock salt mining, mechanical evaporation, and solar evaporation. U.S. salt production grew substantially throughout the 20th century, driven primarily by highway deicing demand, which constituted about one-third of consumption. The industry consolidated significantly from 268 establishments in 1880 to 66 establishments owned by 29 firms by the early 2000s.

Compass Minerals faced emerging environmental challenges as road salt caused freshwater salinization, with chloride concentrations in some Northeastern streams reaching 25% of seawater levels during winters. Research indicated these impacts would worsen with continued development, potentially leading to future regulation.

The company's operations included rock salt mines in Louisiana and Ontario, solar evaporation in Utah, and mechanical evaporation in Kansas and other locations. General trade salt represented over 50% of North American Salt's revenue, with highway deicing at about 40%. Ducey sought to position the company to investors while navigating regulatory threats and identifying growth opportunities in new salt mine applications such as document storage and nuclear waste disposal.

In his final State of the Union address, President Lyndon B. Johnson reviews national challenges and achievements from his five years in office. He notes persistent problems including urban unrest, poverty, welfare pressures, education, law enforcement, Middle East tensions, Vietnam, nuclear dangers, and Communist relations, while emphasizing continuing national strengths: the economy, democratic system, exploration spirit, and public judgment. Major accomplishments include Medicare, voting rights, federal education assistance, Head Start, college aid, environmental preservation, and job training for five million Americans, with unemployment at 3.3 percent. Johnson urges continued funding for commitments including model cities, 500,000 homes for needy families, an urban development bank, 13 percent Social Security increase, maternal and child healthcare, poverty programs, and $3.5 billion for job training. He supports extending the Voting Rights Act, full funding for the Safe Streets Act, postal reorganization, and a random draft selection system. The 1969 budget shows a $2.4 billion surplus, with a projected $3.4 billion surplus for 1970, anticipating continued surtax with President-elect Nixon's support. Johnson discusses arms limitation treaties, aid to developing nations, European unity, Vietnam peace prospects, Middle East stability, and expresses personal gratitude to congressional leaders while urging support for the incoming administration.

A study by Rand Corporation, Harvard Medical School, and UCLA found that one in five American workers experience a hostile or threatening workplace environment. The 2015 survey of 3,066 workers revealed that most Americans work at high speeds under tight deadlines, with one in four feeling they lack sufficient time. Over half reported exposure to unpleasant or hazardous conditions. Women reported unwanted sexual attention, while young men reported verbal abuse. However, four in five found their jobs meaningful, and over half described their bosses as supportive.

This paper studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single expiring item to strategic buyers with stochastic arrivals, modeled as a Stackelberg game. The seller commits to a pricing schedule while buyers, characterized by private valuation and arrival time, decide when to purchase. The authors develop a Value-Based Threshold strategy framework that decouples these two dimensions, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions to prove equilibrium existence and uniqueness in continuous valuation settings—addressing a limitation of prior discrete-type work. For thin markets with infrequent arrivals, the optimal policy is constant pricing to eliminate buyer incentives to delay. For thick markets with frequent arrivals, linear discounting is optimal as competition makes buyers behave myopically. Numerical simulations validate these policies and reveal transitions based on seller time sensitivity: end-loaded pricing for patient sellers, flat pricing for moderately sensitive sellers, and front-loaded discounts for impatient sellers. The model uniquely assigns time-dependent disutility only to the seller, better capturing online marketplace dynamics for expiring items like event tickets.

The toss play is a widespread outside run in football where the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back aiming to reach the edge of the defense. Its strengths include simplicity in teaching and installation, efficiency in getting the ball to the perimeter, and consistent yardage gains with proper personnel. Its weaknesses include ineffectiveness without a fast running back and susceptibility to edge pressure. The passage details blocking assignments for the toss play from the I Formation against 3-4 and 4-3 defenses, specifying roles for each offensive position. Two variations are described: Flexbone Toss (or "Rocket Toss"), which uses motion to get the ball outside faster, and Single Back Toss G Pull, which uses a pulling guard as the lead blocker instead of a fullback.

The speaker notes the opposing team is playing a different neutral zone strategy with forwards coming back hard, limiting their opportunities. They plan to try something different to get back in the series, acknowledging their power play has been scoring but needs correction after the last game. They express frustration about being down in the series but remain hopeful they can tie it by returning to their previous playoff form.

Microsoft Corporation held its 2019 Annual Shareholders Meeting on December 4, 2019. Shareholders elected thirteen directors, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers, and ratified the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2020. Shareholders rejected two proposals concerning a report on employee representation on the Board of Directors and a report on gender pay gap. Of 7,632,138,696 shares entitled to vote, 6,610,123,128 were voted.

Diane David appeals a trial court's dissolution of marriage order, challenging the award of the marital residence to Joseph (the noncustodial parent), the unequal property division, and failure to consider tax consequences of liquidating her retirement funds. The Missouri Court of Appeals found no error on the briefed issues but remanded for reconsideration due to a mathematical error in calculating Diane's assets ($62,781 vs. correct $59,182). The court upheld awarding the farm to Joseph, noting statutory factors don't require giving the marital residence to the custodial parent. Regarding the unequal division, the court found no abuse of discretion in considering Diane's $27,130 teacher retirement account as separate property, distinguishing precedent where retirement accounts materially impacted distribution. The tax consequences claim was denied as raised for the first time on appeal. On remand, the trial court must recalculate the property distribution.

Tesla, Inc.'s 2016 annual report (Form 10-K) covers its business as a vertically integrated energy company designing, manufacturing, and selling electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar energy products. The company produces the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, with Model 3 planned for mass-market production in late 2017. Following its November 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, Tesla offers end-to-end clean energy solutions including generation, storage, and consumption. Key products include the 14 kWh Powerwall 2 and 200 kWh Powerpack 2 energy storage systems, plus solar roof tiles expected in 2017. Manufacturing occurs primarily in California, Nevada, and through Gigafactory partnerships with Panasonic. The company sells directly to consumers through company-owned stores and service centers, operates 790 Supercharger stations globally, and faces risks including production delays, supplier dependencies, competition, and regulatory challenges. Tesla had 17,782 employees as of December 31, 2016, with SolarCity adding 12,243.

A speaker discusses playoff hockey strategy, emphasizing discipline, defensive improvement, and focusing on one game at a time. They mention reducing penalties, wearing down opponents, and building confidence from previous series. The speaker also touches on media entertainment value, traffic in front of the net, and briefly jokes about rulebook questions regarding puck possession.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana is appealing for government and public support to obtain ambulances, stating they have personnel ready to assist traditional health providers. National Operations Director Dr. Eric Asamoah Darko explained on the Citi Breakfast Show that their only ambulance, donated by the Chinese Red Cross, broke down due to engine problems, and they are seeking alternative engines. He noted the World Bank funded nine first aid posts on accident-prone highways. Ghana, with 29 million people, has only 55 functioning ambulances out of 155 total, with 100 broken down. Vice President Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia announced plans to procure 275 ambulances for the National Ambulance Service.

This passage is a technical data manual for the Texas Instruments TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor, detailing its hardware specifications, pin configurations, and peripheral interfaces. The document describes the device's C674x DSP core with 32KB L1 program/data memory and 256KB L2 RAM, ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem with NEON SIMD engine, system MMU for memory protection, and various peripherals including HDVICP2 video codec accelerator, face detection module, spinlock and mailbox modules for inter-processor communication. Extensive pin multiplexing tables cover boot configuration, camera interfaces, DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers, Ethernet MAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP audio, PCIe, SD/MMC, SPI, timers, UART, USB, and video input/output. The manual includes revision history from SPRS712A through SPRS712C, updating operating points, power sequences, clock specifications, and timing requirements.

A hockey player discusses preparing for the Stanley Cup Finals, emphasizing the need for discipline, avoiding penalties, and improving their power play. He notes the team's excitement after a long wait, praises his linemates Krejci and Lucic, and acknowledges facing a skilled opponent. He stresses playing hard every game, staying patient, and avoiding turnovers against a talented team.

VentureWire newsletter dated May 22, 2001, sent to jdasovic@enron.com, covering venture capital news including: Kodiak Venture Partners closing a $290M Fund II; Mercury Interactive acquiring Freshwater Software for $147M; Celetron securing $48M in first-round funding; and TVM's first close on a $61M life science fund. The issue also reports on 22 additional funding rounds ranging from $400K to $40M, three companies cutting staff (AgWeb, Ironmax, Rx.com), two product launches, four acquisitions, two new board appointments, seven executive changes, one new VC fund partnership between University of Pittsburgh and Redleaf Group, and three VC personnel moves.

An email from Mark Palmer at Enron forwards a class action lawsuit filed November 27, 2000, against electricity generators including Reliant Energy, Southern Company, Dynegy, NRG Energy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy. The suit, brought by San Diego resident Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of SDG&E customers, alleges defendants conspired to manipulate California's wholesale electricity market from May 2000 onward by improperly sharing confidential real-time data through the Western Systems Coordinating Council to withhold capacity, export power to create artificial shortages, and inflate prices. The complaint cites violations of California's Cartwright Act, Unfair Trade Practices Act, and Consumer Legal Remedies Act, seeking treble damages, restitution, and injunctive relief. FERC and California regulators found prices "unjust and unreasonable," with estimated overcharges exceeding $4 billion. Palmer notes Enron's suit will look similar.

Three members of George Washington University's Alpha Phi sorority face expulsion after a racist Snapchat post circulated showing two members with a banana peel and a caption reading "[Name]: 'I'm 1/16 black.'" The sorority apologized on Facebook, acknowledging issues with privilege and lack of diversity. Student Imani Ross tweeted the photo, prompting university investigation. The incident occurred at the start of Black History Month, shortly after the sorority attended diversity training. University Provost Forrest Maltzman called the post disturbing and hurtful. The GW Black Student Union noted similar racially charged incidents involving bananas have occurred at other campuses.

Vladimir Putin's fourth term as Russian president will further entrench his power and escalate tensions with the West. A key but overlooked goal is developing a post-Soviet ideology to enhance Russia's stature and provide an alternative to Western liberal democracy. This addresses Russia's identity crisis, where the country has become hostage to Putin's persona. As economic prosperity promises ring hollow, his government will work to codify a worldview offering domestic legitimacy and patriotic mission. The West should recognize this vision's hollowness rather than accept it, and can prevail by maintaining a more positive alternative vision despite internal political challenges.

Create Sheffield is a new partnership bringing together education, arts, culture and voluntary sector organisations to ensure all children and young people up to age 25 in Sheffield experience and participate in arts and culture. The initiative aims to improve school attainment and develop skills for creative careers, addressing concerns that arts subjects are being squeezed out by academic pressures. It proposes creating a list of cultural experiences and developing young makers, while also offering creative career education, family arts access, and Artsmark support for schools. Membership fees ranging from £125 to £5,000 annually will begin in September.

Oregon public schools have among the lowest graduation rates nationally, with one in four students failing to graduate in four years. The state also requires fewer instructional days—about 165 compared to the national average of 180—prompting debate about whether the two are linked. Oregon Board of Education member Kim Sordyl argues there is a clear correlation and criticizes state leadership for inaction. Other factors cited include high class sizes, poverty, and budget deficits. State Representative Diego Hernandez counters that quality matters more than quantity, and no legislative studies have examined the correlation. One parent moved to Washington, where students receive 15 more instructional days annually—equating to an extra year of schooling over 12 years. Tualatin High School, with graduation rates near 95%, emphasizes attendance and instructional time, with its principal supporting more school days.

The speaker acknowledges their team hasn't played their successful playoff style, crediting the Devils' strong defense while noting their own poor puck management. They express confidence after rest and reflection, emphasizing the need to win at home in Anaheim. They praise the Devils' goaltender and anticipate loud home crowd support, noting advantages like line matchups and last change. They deny any lack of respect for New Jersey, reject frustration-fighting as uncharacteristic, and stress the importance of generating offensive chances through better neutral zone play and puck possession. They focus only on the next game, note all playoff opponents are defensively strong, and highlight the organization's turnaround. They conclude that physical play requires first gaining puck control through the neutral zone against New Jersey's trap system.

Tropical Storm Nate may erode 70 percent of sandy beaches from Florida Panhandle to southeast Louisiana and destroy half of protective sand dunes, according to a U.S. Geological Survey study. The National Hurricane Center predicts Nate will make landfall as a Category 1 hurricane with 74-95 mph winds. Over 90 percent of Louisiana beaches face likely erosion, with the Chandeleur Islands particularly vulnerable to overwash. Sand movement could block roadways. While the study focused on beach erosion, major hurricanes have historically accelerated wetland erosion. Louisiana's coastal erosion slowed to a football field every 100 minutes between 2010-2016, partly due to fewer major hurricanes.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Q2 FY2017 Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2016. Revenue was $1.428 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with net income of $253 million ($0.40 per diluted share), up 873% from $26 million ($0.05 per share) in Q2 FY2016. Gross margin improved to 57.9% from 55.0%.

GPU business revenue increased 25% to $1.196 billion, driven by gaming (GeForce up 20%), datacenter (Tesla/GRID up 110%), and professional visualization (Quadro up 22%). Tegra Processor revenue rose 30% to $166 million, led by automotive systems (up 68%). Operating expenses declined 9% to $509 million due to absence of prior-year restructuring charges.

The company had $4.88 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. During the first half of FY2017, NVIDIA returned $633 million to shareholders through $509 million in share repurchases (including a $500 million ASR agreement) and $124 million in dividends. The $1.5 billion 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018 remained convertible as of July 31, 2016, with $229 million in conversion notices received and an additional $200 million notice subsequent to quarter-end.

Intellectual property litigation with Samsung and Qualcomm was resolved through a binding memorandum of understanding, with all pending litigation dismissed. The effective tax rate was 20.3% for Q2 FY2017, down from 64.0% in the prior year period, primarily due to absence of tax-related restructuring charges and the U.S. federal research tax credit.

Copper is frequently cited as a leading indicator for stocks due to its widespread use across industrial sectors, with rising prices signaling economic growth and falling prices indicating slowdown. However, backtesting a simple trading strategy—buying SPY when copper's four-week return is positive, otherwise holding cash—found no strong correlation between copper and subsequent stock returns, particularly during 2011-2016 when copper fell over 50% while stocks rose. While the strategy showed decent returns with manageable drawdowns, the performance may reflect luck rather than predictive power. The article concludes copper is not a reliable leading indicator for stocks, though it may help predict broader business cycles.

EON Resources Inc. held a special conference call to discuss $45.5 million in funding and a related Farmout Agreement. Participants included President and CEO Dante Caravaggio, CFO Mitchell Trotter, VP of Operations Jesse Allen, and VP David Smith. Host Michael Porter opened with forward-looking statements disclosures before turning the call over to Caravaggio, who noted this was approximately the seventh or eighth such call and apologized for airport background noise.

The passage reports serious medical problems in clinical trials of BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA vaccines across multiple phases. In Phase 1, 2 of 48 BNT162b2 participants had serious problems (inflamed appendix and nerves), deemed unrelated to the vaccine. In Phase 2/3, few serious problems occurred with no single problem affecting ≥1% of participants; among 16+ year-olds who received BNT162b2, 3 had temporarily lasting problems possibly related to the vaccine, and 3 placebo-then-BNT162b2 participants had problems possibly related to the vaccine. For BNT162b2SA, 4 of 324 participants (1%) had serious problems deemed unrelated. In Phase 3 boosters, few serious problems occurred with no single problem affecting more than 1 participant, all deemed unrelated to the vaccine. For lower-dose boosters (5-10 µg), 1 participant had a serious problem deemed unrelated. For 30 µg boosters in Phase 2/3, 65 of 22,470 participants (<1%) had serious problems, with 2 in the 16+ age group possibly related to the vaccine. For additional boosters (Dose 4 or 5), 1 participant had a serious problem deemed unrelated.

Coach Quenneville discussed his team's performance in a hockey game, noting they had a strong start but lost momentum by standing around and allowing counterattacks. He praised his goalie's performance in keeping them in the game during overtime. Quenneville commented on line rotations, player conditioning, and the need to maintain momentum through the finals. He emphasized playing to their strengths, staying even-keeled emotionally, and taking each game as it comes without predicting outcomes. He also acknowledged the challenge of facing an experienced Boston team.

The President communicates to Congress dispatches regarding a border dispute between Maine and New Brunswick. Lawless men from British Provinces trespassed into disputed territory claimed by Maine, cutting timber. Maine's land agent was arrested by trespassers while attempting to consult with New Brunswick's land agent. Maine authorized an armed posse to arrest trespassers and protect property. British officials demanded recall of Maine's forces, claiming exclusive British jurisdiction, but the U.S. denies such agreement exists. The President states Maine has right to arrest depredations but not to militarily occupy territory, proposes arbitration if needed, and will aid Maine if New Brunswick invades. He expects release of arrested agents and peaceful resolution, noting the dispute endangers U.S.-British peace.

The S&P 500 spends only 8.3% of trading days at all-time highs, averaging about 21 per year since 1950. An All-Time High trading strategy involves buying when the index is within 5% of its peak and selling when it drops more than 5% below. Backtesting showed a 3.20% CAGR with 43.2% market exposure and 33.75% maximum drawdown. The strategy's profitability depends on earning returns on cash during non-all-time high periods, such as through conservative investments yielding 3% annually.

This patent document describes a respiratory mask system for delivering respiratory therapy, including CPAP and non-invasive ventilation. The system comprises a mask interface with a frame and seal, and a headgear assembly with a yoke. The frame features a gas inlet angled 10-45° from vertical, an outlet vent, and a channel for receiving the yoke. The yoke has a variable width design with narrower middle portion and wider side portions, and may include textile covering, alignment surfaces, and various attachment features such as hooks, posts, magnets, or snap-fit mechanisms. The seal assembly may include inner and outer clips with hooked flanges forming a seal channel, and a diffuser may be located within the outlet vent. The system incorporates features for automatic headgear adjustment with filament collectors and directional locks. A nasal seal configuration includes nasal prongs with a shallow bridge portion having depth less than half the overall seal depth. Various attachment mechanisms between yoke and frame are described, including retention bumps and notches, anti-rotation grooves and tongues, and protrusion-recess arrangements.

This article presents three free mean reversion trading strategies for ETFs (XLP, FXI, and S&P 500), along with their historical backtesting results. Mean reversion, originally a statistical term coined by Francis Galton, describes how asset prices gravitate toward a moving average over time, with abnormal rises reverting down and vice versa. The article explains that mean reversion strategies typically feature high win ratios with many small winners and occasional big losers, opposite to trend-following strategies. Mean reversion works best in stocks rather than commodities, particularly during bear markets due to increased volatility and explosive bear-market rallies. The three strategies include: a deviation-from-recent-high strategy for XLP (consumer staples), an IBS short strategy for FXI (Chinese ETF), and a 5-day low strategy for the S&P 500. The article provides equity curves and performance data for each strategy, noting that mean reversion in stocks became more effective after the 1990s due to futures trading and arbitrage. Code for the strategies is available for Amibroker or Tradestation.

The Nigerian government will release N750 billion this week to MDAs for 2017 Budget capital projects, bringing total releases to N1.2 trillion. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun announced this in Abuja while receiving a delegation of 30 French firms interested in investing in Nigeria's banking, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture and youth empowerment sectors. Delegation head Philippe Labonne stated the investment interest follows French government directives and that firms would form partnerships with Nigerian counterparts due to improved foreign exchange market stability.

The passage describes high-speed data communications networks for buildings, particularly those incorporating optically switchable windows such as electrochromic windows. These networks use trunk line segments (coaxial cables or twisted pairs) connected by passive circuits like bias T's or directional couplers to deliver signals exceeding 1 Gbps to devices including windows, IoT devices, sensors, antennas, and controllers. The systems enable integrated environmental monitoring and control through digital architectural elements (DAEs) containing sensors, processors, and network interfaces, which can be installed in building structural elements like mullions during construction. These networks support functions including window tint control, HVAC management, security, acoustic monitoring, and wireless communications, with machine learning algorithms optimizing building operations based on collected sensor data.

Finnish Foreign Minister Witting discussed failed 1940 Finnish-Swedish defense talks, Soviet objections, and growing Finnish dependence on Germany. He noted Soviet military buildup led to Finnish-German transit agreements. Witting stated Finland's military actions were defensive responses to Soviet offensives, not expansionist aims. Finland's near-total reliance on German imports limited its autonomy. The Finnish position was geographically determined, similar to Sweden or the U.S. Finns hoped to avoid actions interfering with Allied supplies to Russia but expected military necessity might force continued German cooperation. The Swedish minister believed no Finnish-Soviet understanding was currently possible, citing lack of leadership among peace advocates and Finnish government emphasis on German dependence and territorial annexation policy.

Kimbho, a real-time messaging app launched by Ramdev's Patanjali on Wednesday as a "Swadeshi" challenge to WhatsApp, is no longer available on Google Play Store but remains on iOS App Store. The app, which had approximately 5,000 installations and user-reported issues, allows messaging, group chats, video calling, and media sharing. "Kimbho" is Sanskrit for "How are you? What's new?" The launch follows Patanjali's introduction of Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards with BSNL, offering 10% discounts on Patanjali products. Patanjali Ayurved operates nearly 5,000 retail outlets and has expanded into e-commerce, private security, and diverse product categories including food, cosmetics, and apparel.

A study published in Nature Astronomy confirms that Uranus's atmosphere contains hydrogen sulfide, the gas responsible for the smell of rotten eggs. Scientists from Caltech, Oxford, and Leicester used the Gemini North telescope to detect the gas in the planet's cloud tops. While the smell would be unpleasant, a human descending through the clouds would die from suffocation and exposure to -200°C temperatures before noticing it. The discovery helps explain how and when Uranus formed.

A player expressed excitement about teammate Manny's return, praising his leadership and contributions both on and off the ice. He emphasized staying level-headed through playoff wins and losses, noting the need to focus on the upcoming game in Boston rather than celebrating. He mentioned his positive personal history playing in Boston, including his first NHL game, first win, and first shutout against the Bruins. He also described being prepared during a game moment against a player who frequently tries to score on him in practice.

This study investigated long-term effects of unintended pregnancy on children's psychosocial problems using data from 7,784 participants in the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development birth cohort. Pregnancy intentions were measured as three dimensions: mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness. Children's psychosocial problems were assessed at preschool age (5-6 years), early adolescence (11-12 years), and middle adolescence (15-16 years) using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, with maternal mental health and bonding examined as potential mediators.

Results showed that pregnancy mistiming and unwantedness predicted more internalizing and externalizing problems at preschool age, with small effect sizes. These associations were largely mediated by maternal bonding problems and, for mistiming, maternal psychosocial distress. However, no significant associations between unintended pregnancy dimensions and children's psychosocial problems were found in adolescence after controlling for co-occurring risk factors. The authors suggest that in contexts with liberal abortion policies, highly unwanted pregnancies may be terminated, leaving a sample with less severe unintendedness. They conclude that maternal mental health and bonding are more important factors for children's psychosocial outcomes than pregnancy unintendedness itself.

The Cincinnati Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for draft picks, with Cincinnati receiving a sixth-round pick and sending a fifth-round pick to Cleveland. The Bengals, who have lost three straight games with Jake Browning throwing eight interceptions in four games, hope the 40-year-old Flacco can stabilize the position while Joe Burrow recovers from toe surgery. Flacco was named 2023 Comeback Player of the Year after a productive stretch with Cleveland. To make room for Flacco, the Bengals released quarterback Logan Woodside. The trade may allow Browns rookie Shedeur Sanders to move up to the No. 2 quarterback spot behind Dillon Gabriel.

This patent application describes a display device with a through portion (through hole) surrounded by pixels. The device includes a substrate with first and second surfaces, a pixel array with pixels surrounding the through portion, scan lines extending in a first direction, and data lines extending in a second direction crossing the first direction. The data lines adjacent the through portion are at different layers and curved along the through portion's perimeter, with first and second data lines not overlapping. The substrate has a display area with pixels and non-display areas including a first non-display area surrounding the through portion and a second non-display area surrounding the display area. The device features a thin film encapsulation layer with inorganic and organic layers, a dam adjacent the through portion, and various configurations for the curved data lines to reduce the first non-display area while maintaining sealing performance. Multiple embodiments describe different layer arrangements for the data lines, including configurations where data line portions are at different layers connected via contacts, or where data lines share materials with other device components to reduce manufacturing masks. The display device can be implemented in mobile phones, smart watches, and vehicle dashboards.

President Johnson delivered a 1964 commencement address at the University of Michigan outlining his vision for the "Great Society." He identified three key areas for national improvement: rebuilding American cities to combat decay and preserve community values; protecting the countryside from pollution and environmental destruction; and reforming education to ensure universal access and quality. Johnson emphasized that achieving this vision required cooperation between federal and local governments, and called upon graduates to join in addressing poverty, racial injustice, and the pursuit of a society where material progress serves spiritual and moral enrichment.

A coach analyzes his team's overtime loss to Buffalo, noting they played two strong periods but became conservative in the third, allowing Buffalo to rally. He emphasizes that both teams contest critical areas like blue lines and front of nets equally well, and that Buffalo's goalie Hasek kept them in the game until their skilled players capitalized. The coach states his team needs to generate more second and third scoring chances rather than relying on first shots, control contested areas for a full game, and maintain their intensity longer. He mentions potential lineup changes to add offensive depth and fresh legs, acknowledges the emotional toll of previous series, and expresses admiration for his team's resilience and togetherness through adversity.

VentureWire People, dated May 17, 2001, is a daily newsletter sent to jdasovic@enron.com reporting executive changes at venture-backed firms. The issue includes a publisher's note from Brian O'Connell welcoming the recipient and providing links to cancel subscriptions, advertise, or provide feedback.

The newsletter lists executive appointments across multiple categories: SmartBargains named Carl S. Rosendorf (former Barnes&Noble.com EVP) as CEO; Creative Planet promoted CFO Kelyn Brannon to president; CyLex Systems appointed Bill E. Newell as president and CEO; Zone Labs named Irfan Salim as first president and COO; PrivateExpress appointed Richard W. Ormond as president and CEO; and EVLogix appointed founder Andreas Kozma as president and CEO.

Marketing and sales appointments include Jeremy Goulding as VP of international sales at Artisan Software, Brent Wells as sales VP at Ockham Technologies, Jeff House as sales executive at ePartners, William E. The "Box and One" is a combination defense where four players form a box zone while one "Chaser" denies passes to an opponent's star player. Baseline defenders (X4, X5) use 1-2-2 zone shifts, while outside defenders (X1, X2) use 2-3 zone shifts. Against even and odd front offenses, the on-ball defender pushes the ball handler away from the chaser's side, with other defenders rotating to cover areas and protect the basket. The chaser maintains pass denial throughout, with support from teammates if their opponent receives the ball. The defense aims to disrupt the opponent's set plays by keeping the ball from their top scorer.

This article demonstrates how to backtest a trading strategy in Python using pandas, yfinance, and matplotlib libraries. The strategy uses simple and exponential moving averages to generate trading signals for SPY stock data downloaded from Yahoo Finance. The process involves importing libraries, downloading historical data, calculating moving averages, generating signals when the close price exceeds both averages, calculating returns only during invested periods, and plotting results. The backtest showed the strategy returned 804.82% versus 1505.31% for buy-and-hold, indicating underperformance. The article emphasizes that Python is intuitive and accessible for financial analysis without requiring specialized degrees.

The SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE command requires customers to provide their RSA public key for SFS package verification during early boot before BOOT_DONE, with no updates permitted afterward. The x86 passes a pointer to an MBOX_BUFFER_HEADER structure, followed by a ReqBuffer containing KeySize and OemCoSignKey in RSA_TOKEN_FORMAT. Customers generate 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA key pairs and sign packages using RSA-PSS schemes. SFS update packages check system patch levels for applicability, can patch registers, firmware images, or components, and are non-persistent across reboots. SEV updates auto-commit preventing rollback, and SNP-enabled systems require HV-FIXED pages. Attestation data is provided to OS or management software. Update packages verify firmware versions before application to maintain synchronization. Commands require 2MB-aligned memory, with specific buffer arrangements for GET_FW_VERSIONS and UPDATE_FW. The process involves creating a TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, appending co-signing headers and signatures if used, and communicating via the TEE mailbox interface. ASP verifies signatures, loads patches, and updates patch levels. GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO returns firmware and patch level information. UPDATE_FW validates entire packages before application. Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run parallel to x86/DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though SEV/ES VMs require stop/restart for SEV firmware updates.

Surfer Dane Gudauskas describes paddling into a massive wave during an XXL swell at Cloudbreak, Fiji, calling it the most intense surf experience of his life. Despite challenging wind and rain conditions, he decided to paddle rather than tow after seeing the size of the waves. He rode an 8'6" Channel Islands board but broke it during the wipeout, noting he would have preferred something over 9 feet. The experience left him with delayed-onset soreness and an adrenaline comedown he plans to recover from by longboarding at San Onofre.
