He advocates for intrusive advising to help students persist.

Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, Dean of Campus Life at New York Institute of Technology (10,000 students), visited September 12. A first-generation college student from Detroit, she emphasizes mentorship, adaptable student-centered approaches, building community, and using social media to share Radford's story.

Both candidates are experienced professionals excited about the opportunity.

Five MMA analysts predict Beneil Dariush will defeat Evan Dunham at UFC 216, with four picking a unanimous decision and one predicting a second-round submission. Analysts cite Dariush's superior all-around skills, particularly his underrated ground game, while acknowledging Dunham's durability and recent momentum after three straight losses.

Jacob Allen sued Richard Knight and his wife Hannah (executrix of her former husband Hope Allen's estate) for withholding approximately £64 left to him by his father's will. The jury ruled for Allen, ordering payment of his proportionate share of the estate plus 41 shillings and 5 pence in court costs.

Nick Kyrgios defeated Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 to level Australia's Davis Cup tie with Germany at 1-1. Earlier, Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur in a five-set marathon. The tie continues Saturday with doubles, followed by Sunday's reverse singles between Kyrgios and Zverev.

Tensions between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un over nuclear threats caused a global market sell-off and increased volatility. Raymond James strategist Jeffrey Saut warned of technical market damage and advised trimming positions, though he believes war is unlikely and maintains a long-term bullish outlook. He noted potential conflict could drive oil to $150 per barrel. Chantico Global CEO Gina Sanchez predicted volatility levels not seen since the financial crisis.

U.S. higher education institutions increasingly prioritize global competencies, yet only about one percent of students participate in study abroad programs. This gap between institutional intent and participation has prompted development of alternative strategies including virtual exchanges and collaborative global learning, though immersive travel experiences remain valuable for fostering intercultural understanding, leadership skills, and personal growth. Financial barriers persist as the primary obstacle to scaling education abroad programs.

This article presents a structured methodology for building sustainable business models for faculty-led education abroad programs, drawing on over two decades of experience across six continents. The framework addresses three interdependent drivers: curricular logistics (learning outcomes, credit structures, assessment, strategic alignment, competitive landscape, locational efficacy, engagement modalities, and program duration); operational logistics (risk management, program leadership, travel timing and organization, flights, lodging, partner coordination, local transport, communication, meals, entertainment, emergency preparation, student preparation, wellbeing, and problem support); and financial logistics (expenses for faculty, operational support, external parties, projects, and coordination; income from tuition and fees; and internal/external funding sources).

The article identifies twelve business model types across three categories: external party-led programs (private/nonprofit companies managing logistics for student fees), faculty-led programs (semester or short-term with student payment-driven, revenue-driven, corporate donation-driven, or grant-driven models), and student-led programs (typically non-credit club-based activities funded by donations and activity fees). Key principles for sustainability include leveraging community engagement revenue or corporate sponsorships, utilizing dedicated staff support, and delegating appropriate responsibilities to students.

A UCLA study found that black tea may promote weight loss and good health through a gut microbiome mechanism, increasing bacteria associated with lean body mass and decreasing obesity-related microbes. While green tea polyphenols are more effectively absorbed into blood and tissue, black tea works specifically in the gut. Researchers suggest combining both teas may be most beneficial, as green tea also affects the liver and both offer multiple health benefits.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 8, 2021, announcing the redemption of all outstanding 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021, with a principal amount of €1,750,000,000, on September 6, 2021. The redemption price will equal the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. The filing includes a press release dated July 8, 2021, as an exhibit.

A 19-year-old New Hampshire man, Parker Hogan, was arraigned on charges of causing or aiding in his roommate Michael Buskey's suicide. Police said Hogan brought a gun, notebook and pen to the scene, instructed Buskey on holding the gun correctly, practiced shooting methods with him in the woods, waited for the gunshot, confirmed Buskey's death, removed a phone from his pocket, and took the gun and a note. Hogan told police he helped plan the suicide because Buskey faced a court date and feared jail. Hogan pleaded not guilty to charges including falsifying evidence, posted bail, and is scheduled to appear in court in July.

A hockey player discusses adjustments made during a game, including dealing with a larger opponent on the power play and positioning to see shots better from the side. He praises a teammate's overtime goal and emphasizes the importance of fundamentals and hard practice to stay sharp. He notes the series is four out of seven, they're pleased with the win, and will focus on the next game without distraction.

This study examines how advanced technologies affect management processes in distance education. Using a qualitative case study approach, researchers interviewed four experienced academics at Anadolu University about artificial intelligence, blockchain, metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips.

Findings indicate these technologies will transform educational processes through adaptive learning, synthetic content creation, virtual environments, and AI-powered assistants. Management will shift from hierarchical to horizontal structures with reduced human resources but increased efficiency. While initial investment costs are high, long-term economic benefits include reduced labor costs and increased productivity. However, experts noted concerns about unemployment for those lacking technological literacy, potential psychological impacts from virtual addiction, and the emergence of "meta-culture" requiring new ethical and legal frameworks. The study recommends developing AI management systems, blockchain certification applications, and further research on brain-computer interfaces in education.

Officials marked the completion of the 179 megawatt Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 Solar Projects near Las Vegas on December 11, 2017. The utility-scale solar arrays, located in the Dry Lake Solar Energy Zone at Apex Industrial Park, will power commercial data centers for Switch in Reno and Las Vegas. The projects were developed by EDF Renewable Energy and built by First Solar Inc., with attendance by former Senator Harry Reid, federal land managers, and local officials. An NV Energy executive noted these bring Nevada's total solar plants to 16.

The telegram from Ambassador Hartman in Moscow analyzes the Andropov regime's foreign policy, concluding it shows no significant departure from Brezhnev's hardline approach, though Andropov appears more vigorous and intelligent. Hartman argues that U.S.-Soviet relations should prioritize security and arms control, particularly INF negotiations, noting that the current "zero-zero" position is becoming unsustainable. He warns that Soviet propaganda is successfully shifting European public opinion against perceived U.S. rigidity, and recommends adjusting the INF negotiating position to preserve deployment schedules and alliance credibility.

Apple Watch Series 3 will include LTE-capable cellular models in 38mm and 42mm sizes, according to KGI Securities analyst Ming-chi Kuo. The modems will support only LTE, not 3G, potentially limiting availability in markets like India. Kuo estimates 17.5-18 million Apple Watch sales over the next year, with at least half being Series 3 units. LTE models are projected at 2.8-3.6 million units (35-40% of forecast). Sales may begin this fall alongside new iPhones.

This patent document describes systems, devices, and methods for neural modulation using target multipoles to create linear electric fields. The technology involves electrodes on leads positioned to modulate neural tissue, a neural modulation generator to deliver energy, and a programming system to determine electrode fractionalizations based on target multipoles with at least three poles that progressively stack fractionalizations to provide linear electric fields. The target multipoles include center points with multiple anodes and cathodes on opposing sides, where fractionalization percentages increase with distance from the center. The system allows user control of field angle, focus, and spread, and can automatically determine target multipoles based on user-drawn anatomical regions or identified pain areas. The linear field design maximizes electric field for dorsal horn and dorsal root modulation while minimizing dorsal column activation, enabling sub-perception pain therapy.

A Senate committee criticized the Supreme Court of Canada's Jordan ruling, which set 18-month and 30-month deadlines for criminal trials, calling it "out of step with reality." The committee's report, released Wednesday, includes 50 recommendations and argues for a complete system rethink rather than rigid timelines. Senators George Baker and Bob Runciman warned that tens of thousands of charges risk being dismissed, stating the Court lacked sufficient data before imposing the deadlines.

Inmate John Bryant filed a pro se § 1983 lawsuit against the New York State Department of Correctional Services (DOCS), Sing Sing Correctional Facility, and Officer Hanser Hernandez, alleging constitutional violations during a 20-day "Code Blue" lockdown triggered by a false report of ammunition found at the prison. Bryant claimed inmates were denied showers, recreation, legal mail privacy, medical care, religious services, and adequate compensation for prison work. The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York granted DOCS's motion to dismiss, ruling that DOCS and Sing Sing were entitled to Eleventh Amendment immunity as arms of the state and could not be sued under § 1983 absent state consent or congressional abrogation. The court dismissed claims against Sing Sing sua sponte and allowed potential claims against Officer Hernandez to proceed if properly served.

The UK Government is consulting on new powers to protect staff and suppliers affected by large-scale insolvencies following corporate failures like Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies, and strengthening the Insolvency Service. Business Secretary Greg Clark stated the reforms will hold irresponsible directors accountable. Frank Field welcomed moves to increase individual accountability, while Shadow business secretary Rebecca Long-Bailey criticized the Government for delayed action.

The Grand River Conservation Authority is undertaking a $1.8-million project to create digital floodplain maps using LiDAR technology for the Speed, Conestogo, and Grand rivers over five years. This will replace outdated hard-copy maps from the 1970s and enable real-time flood forecasting when combined with new software from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The technology creates detailed 3D models of riverbeds and surrounding land, allowing the authority to predict flooding impacts and notify at-risk properties more effectively. The project was not prompted by a June flood event that caused significant local damage.

Engineers developed a novel optical technique using femto and pico-second lasers for rapid screening of protein structural properties, including inside living bacteria. The method, called time-domain thermo-transmission, enables millisecond-scale screening without heating samples or killing cells. Researchers are studying natural proteins like squid ring teeth proteins, which function in water, and synthetic variants for potential manufacturing and medical applications. The work, published in Analyst, received Army Research Office support and a DURIP grant for equipment to scale up the process. Collaborators include Penn State, University of Virginia, and Washington University researchers.

A speaker discusses hockey players enjoying time with kids on the ice, acknowledges an upcoming must-win playoff game, emphasizes focusing on process over consequences, mentions a teammate's arrival, expresses the team's shared desire to win the Stanley Cup, notes defensive adjustments being reviewed, identifies board play as needing improvement, and states that matchups against Detroit are difficult to predict.

This paper proposes a methodology for e-commerce risk analysis in digital business ecosystems, where a "trusting agent" evaluates potential interactions with "trusted agents." The authors introduce "FailureLevel" (FL) to quantify interaction failure probability on a scale from -1 to 5, distinguishing between "Previous FailureLevel" (PFL) from past performance and "Future FailureLevel" (FFL) for predicted risk. The methodology divides analysis into pre-interaction and post-interaction time phases, using time slots within a defined time space. PFL is determined through past interactions or recommendations, weighted by trustworthiness, timing, and criteria relevance. FFL is predicted using Gaussian distribution based on historical PFL values, calculating probability distributions across failure levels rather than crisp values. An example demonstrates comparing two logistic providers using three weeks of pre-interaction data to predict failure probabilities for a one-week transaction, enabling informed agent selection.

Iowa State, ranked 14th, lost 38-30 to Cincinnati in week 6, ending their unbeaten season and opening up the Big 12 Conference race. Cincinnati built a 31-7 halftime lead that Iowa State couldn't overcome. The article compares this to last season's chaotic Big 12, where unexpected teams like BYU and Arizona State tied for the regular season title while traditional powers struggled.

This study evaluates education for students with disabilities within inclusive education frameworks during distance education in Kazakhstan. Amidst the country's State Programme targets for inclusive education and the COVID-19 pandemic's forced transition to online learning, researchers employed a qualitative case study design using semi-structured interviews with ten special education teachers, analyzed thematically. Findings indicate that the majority of teachers prefer formal education over distance education, viewing the latter as insufficient for meeting students' individual learning needs. Significant challenges identified include high levels of family anxiety, inadequate technological access, insufficient communication, and weak or unqualified teacher-student and peer interactions. The study recommends diversifying technology-based learning methods, developing individualized learning content, organizing online seminars to enhance family participation, and implementing regular social activities to strengthen interpersonal connections.

A memorial football match will be held Sunday at Stark's Park in Kirkcaldy for Aidan Sutherland, a 20-year-old footballer who died from diabetes complications in July. Organized by friend Ben Graham, the event will raise awareness about diabetes and donate to the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Activities include a pipe band, stalls, face painting, and a match featuring Aidan's friends, former teammates, and professionals including Colin Cameron and Darren Dods. Kick-off is at 1pm with events beginning at noon. Family and organizers emphasize the importance of recognizing diabetes symptoms and acting quickly.

The speaker discusses team communication and learning from mistakes, describing a six-on-five hockey situation where they positioned themselves in front of the net. They mention excitement about returning home to play in front of sold-out crowds, emphasizing the need for emotional control and discipline. They note that playoff teams typically use all four lines and six defensemen, with different players contributing at different times. The team has dealt with injuries throughout the season, with players like "Fabbs" stepping up and performing well when called upon.

This study analyzed high-throughput transcriptomic data from three Alzheimer's disease (AD) cohorts (Knight ADRC, MSBB, and ROSMAP) to examine the relationship between epilepsy-causing genes and a severe cognitive subtype of AD characterized by synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD). Analysis revealed that 16 epilepsy-associated genes were significantly dysregulated across all three cohorts, with 15 consistently downregulated and one (CERS1) upregulated. Nine of these genes were synaptic genes highly expressed in neurons, including GABA receptor subunits (GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2), glutamate receptors (GRIN2A), and voltage-gated sodium channels (SCN1A, SCN8A). Pathway enrichment analysis identified epilepsy-related pathways including glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapses, as well as ion channel activity pathways. Dysregulation of these genes was observed at both early and late AD stages, with effect sizes more pronounced at later stages. These findings support a bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and AD, suggesting shared genetic vulnerabilities and pathophysiological mechanisms involving synaptic dysfunction. The results indicate that epilepsy-causing genes may play a role in AD onset and progression, potentially offering shared therapeutic targets.

Uranium prices show positive momentum despite recent corrections, with analysts forecasting 6% annual demand growth through 2020 and prices potentially reaching $65/pound by 2019. The World Nuclear Association reports 440 operating nuclear reactors globally, with 160 planned and 300 proposed—representing over 100% potential increase. Negative sentiment from the 2011 Fukushima disaster has created a disconnect from supply-demand fundamentals, though energy security and climate concerns are reviving nuclear power interest. The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) shows seasonal patterns with March lows and July highs, with technical indicators suggesting possible near-term weakness but potential support around $14.40. Retail sentiment has dipped, short positions have fallen 15%, and risk management suggests monitoring April lows as first support level.

President Eisenhower delivers his farewell address after eight years in office, expressing gratitude for congressional cooperation and wishing his successor well. He warns against three major threats to American democracy: the military-industrial complex's potential for misplaced power, the danger of public policy becoming captive to a scientific-technological elite, and the temptation to mortgage future generations' resources for present convenience. He emphasizes the need for balance in national programs and calls for disarmament through mutual trust rather than arms, acknowledging disappointment at not achieving lasting peace while noting war has been avoided. He concludes with a prayer for global peace, justice, and human betterment.

The Tax Court held that noncharitable gifts by check are complete for Federal gift and estate tax purposes when the checks are paid by the bank, not when delivered to donees. Elizabeth C. Dillingham delivered six checks totaling $18,000 to family members on December 24, 1980, and six additional $3,000 checks on January 28, 1981; all were paid on January 28, 1981. The Court declined to extend the "relation back doctrine" (which applies to charitable gifts) to noncharitable gifts, finding petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery. Under Oklahoma law, a check does not constitute a completed gift until payment because the donor retains dominion and control, including the power to stop payment. Consequently, the $36,000 in gifts were complete in 1981, not 1980, affecting annual exclusion eligibility and estate tax limitations periods.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture introduces several key technologies: Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity enables 2x data compression and doubled math throughput via 2-out-of-4 non-zero patterns without accuracy loss. Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) uses Tensor Cores for AI-powered upscaling, with third-generation Tensor Cores enabling 8K/60fps gaming. GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, achieves over 900 GB/sec bandwidth using PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding. NVIDIA RTX IO accelerates asset loading by up to 100x through GPU-based decompression, offloading CPU work. The A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing, and 5-10x AI performance versus Turing. Ampere supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, and includes fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode and seventh-generation NVENC. The RTX 3090 features 24GB GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 matches RTX 2080 Ti performance. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology enables safer memory overclocking. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU offers 48GB GDDR6, NVLink support for 96GB, and significant performance gains in rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads.

WIRED highlights discounted toys available before Amazon Prime Day ends, including Squishmallows plush toys at 50%+ off (20-inch Diane Peach Bigfoot for $24, 20-inch Caedyn Cream Cow for $24, 5-inch Austin Avocado for $5, 12-inch Maui Pineapple for $9), Magna-Tiles 32-piece set reduced from $50 to $35, retired Lego Icons Dried Flower Centerpiece, Play-Doh 36-pack, Lego Halloween Skeleton, Plus-Plus 60-piece building set, blind boxes, Melissa & Doug Wooden Ice Cream Counter for $36, Crayola Color Wonder Magic Light Brush Station for $16, and Blue Marble National Geographic Rock Tumbler Kit for $52.

This study investigated genetic biomarkers for cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM), a common vascular malformation affecting 0.5%–1% of the population. The researchers analyzed 103 CCM patients, evaluating single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A genes, along with plasma inflammatory cytokines.

Key findings include: PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC genotypes were more frequent in asymptomatic patients, suggesting protective roles. A diagnostic biomarker combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF plasma levels showed moderate accuracy (AUC 0.663) for distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic patients, with better performance in familial forms and infratentorial lesions. The FCGR2Ars1801274 GG genotype demonstrated high accuracy (AUC 0.796–0.875) as a prognostic biomarker for predicting symptomatic events during 4-year follow-up. VDR variants correlated with symptom timing: VDRrs731236 AA associated with later symptom onset, while VDRrs11568820 CC associated with earlier onset.

The study proposes an "aggressive behavior" paradigm for CCM incorporating both hemorrhage and epilepsy, and suggests immune-mediated mechanisms may drive disease progression.

Methane gas bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments pose environmental and stability risks. These bubbles, primarily CH4 from microbial decomposition, grow through elastic expansion and localized fracturing described by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM). A mechanical-reaction-transport model integrates methane diffusion with LEFM to simulate bubble growth from a penny-shaped seed to a mature "inverted tear drop" configuration. The model uses COMSOL Multiphysics, implementing solute conservation, solid mechanics with Kelvin-Voigt behavior, and fracture propagation via stress intensity factors and strain energy density criteria. Validation against analytical solutions shows good agreement for bubble shapes and sizes across varying fracture toughness. The model applies to individual bubbles and serves as foundation for upscaling to gassy mud properties.

This study developed and implemented a teacher education program integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to enhance teacher education students' (TESs) diagnostic and instructional design capabilities. The program involved 22 TESs across four cycles of collaborative lesson preparation, teaching practice with panoramic camera observation, and post-lesson discussion. Results showed significant improvement in TESs' diagnostic abilities, with observation report scores increasing from 0.47 to 1.88 out of 2. Pre- and post-test comparisons using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests revealed statistically significant enhancements in perceived capabilities for lesson preparation (Z=-4.025), linking student learning with teaching practice (Z=-3.535), and adjusting lesson plans based on discussion (Z=-3.536), all p<0.05. The panoramic cameras provided concrete evidence of student behaviors, enabling more effective collaborative reflection than traditional observation methods.

Amazon has patented a system for delivery drones to self-dismantle during emergencies. The "directed fragmentation" technology uses a constantly updated sequence considering flight conditions and terrain to release components in a controlled manner, altering the drone's descent trajectory to direct parts toward safer locations like water or fields while avoiding populated areas. The system responds to malfunctions, severe weather, or component failures, using latches, springs, or explosive charges to jettison parts based on factors including replacement cost and weight. While the patent was granted, implementation is not guaranteed.

The President addresses Congress celebrating sixty years of stable government and the success of free institutions. He reports amicable relations with foreign nations, including Great Britain regarding reciprocal navigation terms, France where diplomatic ties have been restored, and various European and American states, while maintaining strict neutrality in foreign conflicts. He details interventions to uphold neutral obligations, including halting assistance to a German vessel during the Schleswig-Holstein war and suppressing a filibustering expedition against Cuba, and notes ongoing claims against Portugal and Mexico. The address emphasizes the importance of inter-oceanic canals across Nicaragua, Panama, and Tehuantepec, and a transcontinental railroad, recommending surveys and protection for private enterprises undertaking these works without direct government funding. He reports that California has formed a state constitution and will apply for admission, with New Mexico expected to follow, urging favorable congressional consideration while avoiding sectional controversy. Financially, he notes deficits from the Mexican War and recommends borrowing authority, tariff revision for revenue and domestic industry protection, and strict economy. Other recommendations include establishing an agricultural bureau, a California mint, commissions to examine land titles in new territories, increased military forces for the extended frontier, naval reorganization, postal rate reductions, and preparations for the Seventh Census. He concludes with a defense of constitutional separation of powers, limited use of the presidential veto, and a strong affirmation of the necessity of preserving the Union.

Social media platforms use AI to moderate content, but the technology has significant limitations. AI can recognize offensive language and images through natural language processing and image recognition, yet struggles with context, evolving word meanings, and intent. AI systems inherit biases from human-created training data, which spreads across multiple programs and proves difficult to correct. AI cannot determine intent, leading to errors like removing educational historical content or posts condemning hate symbols. While AI helps prioritize content for human review and has aided emergency interventions, platforms like Facebook continue expanding human moderation teams. Experts note that AI works best assisting human moderators rather than operating independently, and ethical development lags behind technological advancement.

Connecticut municipal lobbyists requested state assistance to reduce administrative burdens and implement cost-control reforms amid the state's financial crisis. The Council of Small Towns and Connecticut Conference of Municipalities seek changes to the municipal retirement system, easier arbitration for collective bargaining, and retention of higher land-transfer fees. Governor Dannel P. Malloy called the meeting productive, acknowledging that budget uncertainty makes governing harder. Senate President Martin M. Looney disputed claims that towns weren't seeking protection from state aid cuts. Small towns specifically want relief from state mandates like binding arbitration and adjustments to prevailing wage thresholds unchanged since 1991. Municipal groups also want employee retirement contributions removed from state law to allow collective bargaining.

SanDisk warranty service requires contacting support, returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging with prepaid freight and tracking, after which SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product. Replaced products carry the remaining warranty period. SanDisk excludes liability for lost data and prohibits use in life support systems.

The End User License Agreement grants a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license for personal use of the Software solely with SanDisk products on a single device. Users may not modify, reverse engineer, or redistribute the Software. The Software is provided "as is" without warranties, and SanDisk disclaims liability for indirect, consequential, or other damages, including from use in high risk activities. The agreement is governed by California law and subject to U.S. export regulations.

The passage describes a method and system for manufacturing orthodontic appliances through automated digital treatment planning. The process involves measuring patient tooth positions and malocclusion elements (including openbite, molar and canine class relationships, overjet, and bi-protrusion), generating multiple branched treatment plans with interim final positions based on tooth movement constraints, modifying positions to correct identified malocclusions, and selecting a final plan. Branching creates treatment variations including bicuspid extraction versus non-extraction options and specific correction protocols for Class II/III malocclusions. The system utilizes a processor executing instructions to generate appliance models and output fabrication instructions for appliances produced via direct additive manufacturing or indirect thermoforming methods.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended September 30, 2018 with the SEC. The company reported total revenues of $6.8 billion for Q3 2018 and $14.2 billion for the nine-month period, compared to $3.0 billion and $8.5 billion in the prior year periods. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million for Q3 2018, compared to a net loss of $619.4 million in Q3 2017. For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, Tesla reported a net loss of $1.1 billion compared to $1.3 billion in the prior year period.

Total assets were $29.3 billion as of September 30, 2018, up from $28.7 billion at December 31, 2017. Cash and cash equivalents were $3.0 billion, down from $3.4 billion at year-end. Total debt was $10.9 billion, with $1.8 billion classified as current. Tesla adopted ASC 606, the new revenue recognition standard, on January 1, 2018 using the modified retrospective method, which changed the timing of revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees.

The company operates in two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Automotive revenues totaled $6.1 billion for Q3 2018, while energy generation and storage contributed $399.3 million. Tesla had 171.7 million shares of common stock outstanding as of October 26, 2018.

This study evaluated COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) transfusion in 112 patients with hematological malignancies hospitalized for severe COVID-19 between May 2020 and April 2021 in France. The cohort included 83 patients with B-lymphoid neoplasms, 19 with multiple myeloma, and 10 with myeloid neoplasms. Patients received four ABO-compatible CCP units with high anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody titers.

Results showed 90-day overall survival of 64.9% for the entire cohort: 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasms, 36.8% for plasma cell neoplasms, and 20% for myeloid neoplasms. CCP transfusion was associated with decreased inflammatory markers and improved PCR cycle threshold values at day 7. Multivariable analysis identified age over 70, high blood pressure, and COVID-19 severity as risk factors for mortality, while prior anti-CD20/CD19 monoclonal antibody therapy was associated with better survival.

A propensity score analysis compared 81 CCP-treated B-cell neoplasm patients to 120 untreated patients, using inverse probability of treatment weighting to control for bias. In the main analysis of anti-CD20 pre-exposed patients alive at day 16, CCP was associated with a 63% reduction in mortality risk. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent benefits ranging from 40-63% mortality reduction.

The authors conclude CCP is particularly beneficial for B-cell lymphoid malignancy patients pre-treated with anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies, who often cannot mount adequate vaccine responses and may develop viral escape variants. Limitations include the observational design, lack of data on viral variants, and changing treatment landscape with vaccines and anti-spike monoclonal antibodies becoming available.

This document lists errata for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, containing numbered hardware issues with brief descriptions. Issues include: PMC Sleep_Clock control side effects, GLIU Error MSR failures, UART register access problems during DMA, 8237 DMA memory write failures, system hangs on I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher, PIC failures with processed interrupts, UDMA write CRC corruption, ATAC SSMI issues during DMA, GLIU clock domain wake failures, ACPI register access hangs, PMC register write corruption, KEL status reporting errors, PCI memory read failures, UART clock gating failures in CEIR mode, timing violations on IRDY# and DEVSEL#, SSMI synchronization issues, PIO access failures with active UDMA, wake event input failures from S3 state, LPC I/O failures during legacy DMA, USB controller clock gating failures, ATAPI packet command failures, KEL AuxOutputfull bit errors, UDMA timing issues, ATAC hangs on unaligned PRD addresses, LPC aborts on sync errors, SMB controller NEGACK status bit errors, GLPCI retry counter issues, GPIO register write failures after suspend, missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, and Sleep_X deassertion timing issues. Three detailed errata describe PIT deviations from industry standards (counter latch command cancellation), debug port system hangs, and PIT mode 3 count value loading problems. Additional issues cover XPIC IRR clearing delays causing duplicate interrupts with AEOI, and DMA rotating priority mode failures. A thermal alarm issue prevents PMC self-recovery from Faulted Standby because the thermal alarm resides in the Work domain rather than the Standby domain, blocking alarm detection during standby. The Sleep Clock must be enabled if any sleep-related options are used, with a workaround to disable it at GPIO while enabling it in PMC registers if the Sleep Clock itself is not desired.

On September 12, 2017, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of $5 billion in senior unsecured notes through four tranches: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027, and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. Steve Yzerman and Coach Cooper outlined the Tampa Bay Lightning's rebuilding philosophy, emphasizing patience and developing home-grown talent through the draft rather than relying solely on free agency. They highlighted drafting foundational players like Steven Stamkos and Victor Hedman, then developing later selections including Nikita Kucherov, Ondrej Palat, and Tyler Johnson through the AHL system. The organization focused on allowing young players time to mature physically and mentally while maintaining draft assets. They discussed Stamkos's evolution from a scorer to a complete player and leader who prioritizes team success, enabling other players to step up. The team applied lessons from previous playoff failures, particularly a first-round sweep the prior year, developing resilience to overcome deficits in the current postseason. Cooper noted that coaching many current players in the minors built trust and accelerated their development. The organization emphasizes recruiting high-character players, creating a winning culture, and using strategic free agency signings to fill specific roster needs while maintaining opportunities for developing talent.

The Bittle tree, planted over 100 years ago by Roanoke College's first President Dr. David Bittle, was removed due to storm damage and repurposed into the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for the College's 175th anniversary. Created by Reverend Chris Bowen and George Arthur for Antrim Chapel, the cross symbolizes the College's rooted foundation and extending future.

Two women with personal experience of child sexual abuse, May Baxter-Thornton and Emma Lewis, have been appointed to the victims and survivors panel of the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (IICSA) to advise on reaching and listening to Welsh victims. Baxter-Thornton, who was abused in the late 1970s and early 1980s, has 16 years of experience working with abuse victims. Lewis, who entered care at age 10 and disclosed abuse at 12, supports young people transitioning from care. Both pledged to ensure Welsh victims' voices are heard in the inquiry's recommendations. The IICSA opened in Wales in November 2016 and has since engaged with victims, survivors, and experts across multiple locations.
The Louisiana Supreme Court granted a writ of review in Robert Daniel Chappuis v. Sears Roebuck & Co., ordering the Court of Appeal to send up the record and notifying counsel for both parties.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) is used to transport vapor and liquids like petroleum and gas under various pressure requirements. ERW differs from ordinary welded pipe and seamless steel pipe, offering high production efficiency, low cost, and material savings. It is widely used in aviation, energy, electricity, automotive, and light industry sectors. Modern ERW production has achieved satisfactory seaming quality, with inner burr removal controlled to 0.2–0.5 mm. ERW steel pipe uses hot-rolled coil with wall thickness controlled to ±0.2mm, following API or GB/T9711.1 standards. It has become widely used in urban gas network engineering.

A playback device receives digital data representing audio content, sends at least a portion to an identification system configured to identify the content, receives associated information (such as metadata or identifiers), sends the information to a control device configured to control the playback device, and plays the audio via wired speakers. The control device may command the playback device to retrieve such information and display representations of the received information or metadata from a metadata curating device. The disclosure also describes media playback system environments including networked playback devices, control devices, playback zones, and audio content sources, and methods for extracting data from different positions in an audio pipeline and detecting discontinuities in digital data.

The passage contains two letters to the editor. The first, by Beth Utton of Longmont, argues that health care is a right, not a commodity, criticizing Rep. Ken Buck's statement to the contrary. Utton advocates for Medicare for all, noting that Medicare's goal is providing care rather than profit, making it less costly than private insurance. The second letter, by Bonnie New of Greeley, criticizes a Tribune headline about Denver paying nearly $1 million to the family of a teen killed by police. New argues the headline should have mentioned the teen was committing a crime (driving a stolen car toward an officer), defends the officer's actions as self-defense, and expresses shock that any settlement was paid.

This disclosure relates to directional illumination apparatus for display devices, particularly privacy displays using imaging directional backlights with waveguides and switchable retarders. The apparatus includes a directional backlight with an illuminator array and waveguide having first and second light guiding surfaces, a transmissive spatial light modulator, input and output polarisers, at least one additional polariser, and at least one retarder arranged between the additional polariser and either the input or output polariser. The retarder may comprise crossed A-plates, C-plates, O-plates, or switchable liquid crystal retarders to reduce off-axis luminance for improved privacy while maintaining head-on luminance. The display can switch between wide angle and privacy modes by controlling the backlight illumination profile and applied voltage across switchable retarders. Applications include autostereoscopic displays, multi-viewer displays, and automotive displays with reduced visibility to snoopers.

Consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles has risen significantly, with only 49% now viewing them as unsafe compared to 73% last year, according to Deloitte research. Trust in traditional car manufacturers (51%) exceeds trust in tech companies (21%), and 53% of consumers cite brand confidence as a reason to ride in autonomous vehicles. Meanwhile, 73% prefer engine-powered vehicles over electric, citing driving range, price, and charging infrastructure as concerns, though 37% would consider electric vehicles for lower ongoing costs. Customer service remains important for 71% of car buyers. The UK government is still conducting a safety inquiry ahead of expected rollout.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory, developed by Yale Hirsch and documented in the Stock Trader's Almanac, suggests U.S. stock market performance follows a predictable four-year pattern tied to presidential terms. Historical data indicates the first two years of a term typically underperform the last two years, with midterm election years showing weak performance until the fourth quarter. Pre-election years rank best for returns, followed by election years, with S&P 500 averages of 12.5% when incumbents run versus 6.7% in all election years and -1.5% in open-field elections. Sector-specific impacts occur in healthcare and energy due to policy differences between parties, while trade policy effects depend on congressional control. Despite election-related volatility, analysts recommend staying invested and rebalancing portfolios rather than making dramatic changes based on election outcomes.

Intel CPUs contain a microcontroller called the Management Engine (ME) that remains active even when computers are powered off, with network and storage access. Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy presented a local exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on the ME, which runs the Minix operating system. While physical access is currently required, concerns exist about potential remote exploits. Mitigation options include firmware updates from System76 to disable the ME, Dell's Latitude 14 with disabled ME by default, Intel's detection tool, and the me_cleaner tool that tricks the ME into inactivity. However, completely disabling the ME is impossible without causing shutdown after 30 minutes, and methods vary by motherboard manufacturer. The ME originated from Trusted Platform Modules in the early 2000s and evolved with added hardware components, with some parts included at NSA request. Intel's closed-source approach previously prevented security auditing of the ME.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening legal protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing family involvement in their care. The bill was proposed after Stephen Komninos died in a Haddonfield group home in 2007. The law allows state inspectors unannounced visits twice yearly, requires notification of parents or guardians within two-to-eight hours of patient injuries, and mandates biannual family meetings. The Department of Human Services may hire additional staff to implement the inspection requirement.

This paper examines Mortimer J. Adler's philosophy of perennialism and its application to Christian education and global education management. Adler emphasized eternal values, continuity in education, and holistic learner development through reasoning and universal truth. The study explores posthumanist perspectives on education, analyzing how technology and human-machine relationships challenge traditional humanist frameworks. Key concepts include docility as an enduring educational virtue—characterized by postponing judgment, perseverance, and submission to authoritative knowledge—and the integration of democracy with education. The research reviews multiple studies on Christian-based education management across family, health, cross-cultural, and business contexts globally. The authors critique Adler's failure to address gender inequality in education and conclude that just education requires empowering women, eliminating pressure on children to become job-ready adults, and recognizing that educational failures stem from systemic issues rather than student deficiencies. Adler's framework ultimately calls for educational management that prioritizes timeless perennialist values over instant achievement, extending beyond administrative functions to deeper engagement with learners' intellectual and moral development.

The Cleveland Browns have not ruled out selecting Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield with the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft, according to an ESPN report. The MSPM0C1105/1106 microcontrollers feature an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU (up to 32MHz) with pre-fetch/cache, SysTick timer, and NVIC with 4 priority levels. Five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) optimize power consumption across two power domains (PD1 for CPU/high-performance peripherals, PD0 for low-power peripherals). The PMU provides brown-out reset and core regulation. Clock sources include internal 32kHz/32MHz oscillators and external crystal options, generating MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, and HFCLK/HSCLK. Peripherals include DMA with 3 channels, event manager, 32KB flash (100K cycles), SRAM with retention in most modes, up to 45 GPIOs with wake capability, 12-bit ADC (1.6Msps), temperature sensor, RTC, VREF (1.4V/2.5V), comparator, CRC-16, three UARTs, I2C (up to 1Mbps), SPI (up to 16Mbps), independent/watchdog timers, and advanced/general-purpose timers with PWM and QEI support. Venezuelan citizens with Temporary Protected Status (TPS) asked the Supreme Court to uphold a federal judge's order blocking the Trump administration from ending their protected status. The TPS program, created in 1990, allows foreign nationals to remain in the U.S. when unsafe conditions prevent their return home. In 2021 and 2023, DHS designated Venezuela for TPS, with an extension through October 2026. In 2025, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem terminated Venezuela's TPS designation and extension. Challengers sued, arguing Noem lacked authority and acted with racial animus. Judge Edward Chen initially blocked the termination, but the Supreme Court stayed that order in May 2025. Chen later issued a final ruling that Noem acted unlawfully; the 9th Circuit declined to stay this ruling. The government returned to the Supreme Court seeking intervention, while challengers argued the prior stay didn't preclude final judgment on the merits.

Ed Sachse, 56, is president of property services for Kennedy Wilson, overseeing 21 million square feet of U.S. properties. He began as a teen window-washer in Detroit, learning entrepreneurship. After studying accounting at Michigan State University, he worked for Arthur Andersen before moving to Los Angeles in the 1980s. He became CFO at Camden Financial, then a broker at Coldwell Banker, where he sold an empty school to the Simon Wiesenthal Center. He started his own property management company in 1993. Diagnosed with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma in 2001, he battled the disease for six years while running his business. The Great Recession devastated his company, but a 2009 meeting with Kennedy Wilson led to its acquisition of his firm. Sachse lives in Pacific Palisades with his wife Julie, has two grown children, and plays guitar in a garage band.

The invention provides an optical waveguide display apparatus and method that enhances field of view (FOV) by coating external waveguide surfaces with a material, preferably a meta-material, having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than 1.0. Prior art waveguides suffer from limited FOV dictated by total internal reflection (TIR) constraints, with different wavelengths experiencing different FOV limitations when diffracted by input Bragg gratings. The low-index coating reduces the critical angle for TIR according to Snell's law, allowing light from wider input angles to propagate along the waveguide, thereby expanding the total field of view and enabling operation across broader wavelength ranges for multi-color displays. The meta-material comprises a periodic array of unit cells containing magnetic resonators (e.g., alumina sandwiched between conductive plates) centered between opposing conductive meshes (e.g., silver), with structural parameters optimizable to achieve real refractive index values between 0.0 and 1.0. The apparatus includes input and output diffractive parts (preferably conjugated Bragg gratings to reduce chromatic dispersion) and may employ multi-layered slab waveguide structures wherein component waveguides are separated by intermediate meta-material layers, optionally covered by protective outer layers.

The lecture covers renewal theory and countable-state Markov chains. Three major renewal theorems are discussed: the strong law for renewals (sample path time average), the elementary renewal theorem (expected value of renewals over time), and Blackwell's theorem (limiting behavior of expected renewals). Blackwell's theorem addresses arithmetic versus non-arithmetic renewal processes, showing that for arithmetic processes with span λ, the probability of renewal at time mλ approaches λ/x̄.

The professor then examines age and duration at a given time t for arithmetic renewal processes. The joint probability of age z(t)=i and duration x̃(t)=k equals q_{t-i}·p_X(k) where k>i, with q_j being the probability of arrival at time j. Asymptotically, q_i approaches 1/x̄. This yields the marginal distribution for duration: p_{x̃}(k) = k·p_X(k)/x̄, with expected duration E[x̃] = E[X²]/E[X] and expected age E[z] = E[X²]/(2E[X]).

For countable-state Markov chains, the lecture distinguishes recurrence types. A state is recurrent if return probability equals 1. First passage time probabilities f_{ij}(n) are defined recursively. The key lemma states four equivalent conditions for recurrence: infinite returns with probability 1, infinite expected returns, infinite sum of return probabilities, and infinite sum of n-step transition probabilities. States in the same class share recurrence status. Null recurrence occurs when expected return time is infinite (steady-state probability zero), versus positive recurrence with finite expected return time.

A 2015 Christmas visit to Glasgow nearly ended fatally for the author after a hand scratch from a garden gate nail led to sepsis, putting them in a three-month coma. Sepsis affects 30 million people annually worldwide, killing 6 million, with 40% of survivors experiencing lasting post-sepsis syndrome. Triggered by infection, the condition causes uncontrolled immune response and organ failure. Symptoms include pale mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, lack of urination, and nausea. Research links vitamin D deficiency to higher risk. While no specific cure exists, promising treatments include metformin and gene therapy targeting NF-kB protein. Global awareness remains critically low—only 40% in Australia, 14% in Brazil, though over 60% in the UK and Germany—making education the most immediate life-saving tool.

Intelligent education systems using AI have transformed scientific experiment learning through personalized platforms and virtual/augmented reality environments. Privacy concerns have emerged regarding student data, particularly video recordings of experiments that capture faces alongside crucial operational details. Current face anonymization methods—multi-object tracking, clustering algorithms, and GAN-based approaches—adequately protect privacy in general contexts but fail to address the unique requirements of scientific education, where instruments and hand movements must remain visible for assessment while faces are anonymized.

The authors propose a specialized facial blurring algorithm built on a modified YOLOv8 architecture called Multi-Scale Feature Fusion YOLOv8 (MSFF-YOLOv8). Their system incorporates Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR), a dilation module that prevents misclassification of experimental instruments as facial pixels. They introduce two evaluation metrics: SOBA (Sensitivity of Blur Accuracy) and OBR (Over Blurred Rate). The system achieves real-time processing at 22.67 fps with 96% accuracy, maintaining low instrument mis-blur rates (0.02) across physics, biology, and chemistry experiments.

The authors created a specialized dataset from 51 experiment videos with 7,590 face labels and 5,240 instrument labels. Comparative testing against SAM, Edge-SAM, and original YOLOv8 demonstrated that MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR processing outperformed alternatives in both speed and accuracy, particularly for heavily occluded scenarios. The optimal configuration used 1920×1080 resolution with CAOR preprocessing, achieving 96.02% SOBA and 0.0159 OBR. Future research directions include developing real-time edge classification refinement.

Sam Altman says intellectual property is trickier for AI video than images because video feels "much more real and lifelike" with stronger emotional resonance. OpenAI's Sora app has generated viral unauthorized videos featuring characters like SpongeBob and Pikachu. Scientific research on human memories is advancing, with experts expecting to soon fully understand and potentially manipulate them. Key developments include: adaptation of "face cells" discovery (neurons active when thinking of specific faces), identification of CREB protein's role in memory formation, and the ability to activate neuron groups to specify memory storage locations. MIT researchers led by Dr. Susumu Tonegawa demonstrated precise memory implantation by creating artificial associations between benign situations and fear responses, and later reversed negative reactions into positive ones. This progress raises ethical questions about future applications.

The speaker emphasizes their team doesn't care about outside perceptions, having earned their place in the Stanley Cup finals by beating three strong teams.
