Ogba, an electrical engineer with no criminal record or gang affiliation, was shot from behind by two men while walking to his car on March 15 after visiting friends. The suspects fled in a waiting SUV, believed to be a newer model Nissan Rogue. Police believe the assailants, who came from another area, sought random vengeance against the neighbourhood rather than targeting Ogba specifically. Investigators have released security footage showing grainy images of the suspects and vehicle, requesting community cooperation to identify them.

A coach discusses his team's upcoming game, confirming a player who fell into the boards is fine to play. He critiques their powerplay performance, noting passing issues under pressure but praising their penalty killing. He emphasizes discipline, avoiding retaliation penalties, and maintaining focus. He acknowledges missing player Forsberg but states the team must not use his absence as an excuse. He analyzes the previous game as evenly matched with limited scoring chances due to strong defense, and mentions two uncalled high-sticking incidents. He concludes by expressing confidence for upcoming games in New Jersey.

The paper introduces ABXLAB, a framework for studying how large language model (LLM) agents make decisions in realistic web environments. The authors test 17 state-of-the-art models across over 80,000 experiments, manipulating product attributes (ratings, prices) and choice architecture nudges (authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, incentives). Results show LLM agents exhibit strong systematic biases, with effect sizes 3-10× greater than human baselines. Agents show pronounced sensitivity to ratings (30-80pp increases), prices (up to 93pp preference for cheaper options when ratings are matched), order effects (up to 90pp for first-listed items), and nudges (10-60pp shifts). User profiles act as categorical switches that dominate decision-making. The findings suggest current agents rely on brittle heuristics and are highly manipulable by superficial cues, raising concerns about their reliability for autonomous decision-making.

This is a presidential message to Congress covering foreign relations, domestic affairs, and departmental operations. The past year saw a financial crisis, diminished political partisanship, and the capture of the American vessel Virginius by Spain, which is being satisfactorily resolved. Relations with most foreign powers remain friendly. The U.S. participated in the Vienna exposition, receiving numerous awards, and sent a representative to a conference on patent protection. The Emperor of China received Western diplomats, and slight progress was made against the Chinese coolie trade. The Geneva arbitration award from Britain was paid and used to redeem public debt. The northwest water boundary with Britain was determined per the German Emperor's award, with about 350 miles of northern boundary remaining to survey. The mixed commission under the Treaty of Washington awarded $1,929,819 to Britain and dismissed other claims. Santo Domingo requested U.S. protection. Several treaties were proclaimed, including with Denmark, Mexico, the Orange Free State, and Ecuador. The President recommends legislation on expatriation, including defining when citizenship may be relinquished and addressing status of children born abroad to American parents. Regarding Spain, the President notes liberal measures in Puerto Rico and Cuba but continued slavery in Cuba, and demands reparation for the Virginius incident including restoration of the vessel, surrender of survivors, salute to the flag, and punishment of guilty parties. He recommends constitutional amendments for partial veto power and restricted legislative scope in extra sessions. Treasury receipts exceeded expenditures by over $43 million, but revenues are declining due to financial panic. He recommends economy in appropriations, currency elasticity through modified national banking laws, and eventual specie resumption. Shipbuilding has increased 3 percent. He suggests federal maintenance of waterways connected to state canals and exploration of the Amazon. The War Department needs proper coastal armament and staff corps promotions. The Navy has been prepared for potential conflict with Spain. Postal revenues increased but expenditures rose more, with recommendations for postal savings banks and telegraphs. Utah requires legislation on jury selection and limitation of probate court powers. The bankruptcy act should be amended to eliminate involuntary bankruptcy provisions. Claims against the government require attention to prevent fraud. Indian policy continues toward reservation consolidation and civilization. Land office operations increased, with over 13 million acres disposed of. Pension expenditures decreased slightly but rolls grew to over 238,000. Civil service reform requires binding rules. Colorado statehood is recommended, along with an irrigation canal from the Rocky Mountains. General amnesty and improved civil rights legislation are suggested.

First Solar, a thin-film cadmium telluride solar panel manufacturer, faced significant challenges in 2011 after years of dominance as the industry's lowest-cost producer. The company recorded its first net operating loss in seven years ($39 million) as revenue growth slowed dramatically from 66% in 2009 to 8% in 2011. Chinese competitors, subsidized by their government, flooded the market with low-price crystalline-silicon panels, while European solar subsidies shrank following the 2008-2009 financial crisis. First Solar responded by vertically integrating into systems business through acquisitions, expanding from 5% to 25% of sales between 2009-2011, and diversifying into non-subsidy reliant markets. The company maintained a conservative financial strategy with lower debt than competitors. By 2011, First Solar controlled approximately 41% of the U.S. market but operated at only 68% capacity due to competitive pressures, prompting senior executive Tymen deJong to question whether the company's competitive advantages remained sustainable.

The passage describes viral qPCR procedures for the DAWn-plasma study: nasopharyngeal swabs are sent to hospital laboratories for routine analysis, with remaining material stored at 4°C for ≤24 hours, then at -80°C or -20°C until batch transport to Leuven for later quantitative PCR analysis. It also contains bibliographic references to DAWn-plasma trial publications and a list of figures and tables from a clinical trial report, including outcome measures, biomarkers, antibody titers, and adverse event classifications.

Week 6 of the 2025 college football season featured major upsets that reshaped conference and College Football Playoff races. UCLA defeated Penn State 42-37, marking the first time since 1985 that a team with a 0-4 or worse record beat a top-10 opponent. Florida also upset Texas 29-21, damaging both teams' CFP hopes as they were the preseason AP poll's top two teams. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava rushed for 150 yards and three touchdowns, while Penn State's defense allowed 430+ yards for only the sixth time since 2022. Florida's DJ Lagway outplayed Texas' Arch Manning, completing 21 of 28 passes for 298 yards and two scores. Alabama held off Vanderbilt 20-14 despite red zone struggles, while Miami defeated Florida State 36-14 after FSU's offense committed three turnovers. Cincinnati beat Iowa State 34-25 to enter the Big 12 title race, and Texas Tech remained undefeated with a dominant win over Houston. SP+ rankings saw Penn State drop from 4th to 16th, while UCLA rose from 65th to 50th. Miami took the top spot in CFP projections.

Alan Oppenheim demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and discrete-time linear systems using a programmable digital filter. The system converts continuous-time signals to sequences via sampling and back via D/A conversion with low-pass filtering. When the digital filter acts as an identity system, the setup demonstrates aliasing: as input frequency increases past half the sampling frequency, output frequency decreases due to spectral overlap. Non-ideal low-pass filters cause beating effects near the Nyquist frequency. With a low-pass digital filter inserted, the overall system becomes a continuous-time filter with frequency response rescaled by the sampling period—specifically, the digital cutoff frequency π/5 maps to π/(5T) in continuous time. Demonstrations show the impulse response, frequency response sweeps, and how changing sampling rate adjusts the effective analog cutoff frequency proportionally, illustrated with both sinusoidal inputs and live audio.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 29, 2019, announcing that Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja intends to retire after serving since 2008 (with a 14-month gap). Ahuja will continue briefly as CFO, then serve as an advisor. Tesla intends to appoint Zachary Kirkhorn, Vice President of Finance since March 2010, as his replacement. Kirkhorn led cost reduction for the Roadster and played key roles in Gigafactory 1, Model X, and Model 3 launches. Elon Musk praised both executives, while Ahuja cited Tesla's improved profitability and cash flow as reasons for his confidence in the transition. Kirkhorn emphasized continued focus on cost management and operational efficiency.

A Derby Chinese takeaway, Sun Waa, received a one-star food hygiene rating after inspectors found cooked rice left at room temperature for six hours, a blocked wash basin, food debris buildup, and other hygiene issues including cross-contamination risks and use of bleach on surfaces. The business has since been revisited and significantly improved, with a full re-score expected in March. The November 2017 inspection report was released following a Freedom of Information request.

Tarren Joseph Titus, 23, received three months of house arrest and a year's probation after pleading guilty to possessing hydromorphone and violating probation. Police found him attempting to escape through a bedroom window during a June 2017 raid where drugs and paraphernalia were discovered. Justice Deborah Austin praised his "outstanding" transformation, noting his eight months of daily sobriety meetings and counseling. The only house arrest restriction is a curfew. Defence lawyer Robert McFadden stated Titus was exposed to drug culture from a young age, which contributed to mental health issues. Federal prosecutor Michael Robb, who had sought six months of house arrest, expressed impressed by Titus's progress.

Hockey players Jonathan Toews, Brad Richards, and Kris Versteeg discuss their team's approach to a potential Stanley Cup-clinching game. They emphasize that winning at home or on the road makes no difference to experienced players, and they focus on blocking out distractions to concentrate on their jobs. Toews reflects on how quickly playoff runs pass and the unique togetherness of postseason hockey. The players note their families experience more nervousness watching than the players feel playing. They credit coach Joel Quenneville for making strategic adjustments and enabling players to perform their best. The team believes they improve as series progress and play their best in meaningful games. They acknowledge Tampa Bay as a skilled opponent requiring patience and smart play. Richards praises teammate Marian Hossa as a complete two-way player and leader. The players stress the importance of preparation, body maintenance, and staying ready for opportunities, drawing on their collective experience of previous championship runs.

Research by NYU's Michelle Munson and University of Houston's Sarah Narendorf shows that understanding "mental health narratives"—how marginalized young adults perceive and make sense of their conditions—is critical to improving mental health treatment engagement and outcomes. Their studies, published in the American Journal of Orthopsychiatry and forthcoming in the Journal of the Society for Social Work and Research, found that young adults' interpretations of their symptoms, feelings about them, and perceptions of help sources strongly influence treatment engagement. Unlike physical illness narratives, mental health narratives often involve greater emotional dimensions like fear and shame due to stigma and discrimination. The researchers define "marginalized" youth as those facing added challenges including poverty, disabilities, and involvement with safety-net systems. They recommend training providers to use cultural humility and collaborative approaches that respect young adults' own understandings of their conditions, rather than relying solely on expert diagnosis. Current projects include technology-based interventions with the Jed Foundation and an NIMH study examining whether narrative types generalize across populations and change over time.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who immigrated from Uzbekistan to the U.S. in 2010, recently toured NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener connected him with his brother, a NASA research astronomer. Murad, who became a U.S. citizen in January, has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since age three. During the tour, astrophysicist Jeremy Schnittman showed Murad and his mother the facility's clean room, cryo-vac chamber, acoustic chamber, and laser lab. Murad, now on an accelerated academic track, hopes to attend Cal Tech and lead a Mars mission. He plans to watch the upcoming total solar eclipse from his home in Kansas City, which lies in the path of totality.

Anita Anand, presenter of BBC Radio 4's Any Answers since 2012, was removed from presenting the show less than 24 hours before broadcast because the edition was to discuss the BBC's gender pay dispute. Anand had publicly supported equal pay on social media. The programme was presented by Julian Worricker instead. Critics accused the BBC of implying women journalists could not be impartial on the issue. The BBC cited impartiality rules preventing presenters who have campaigned on topics from interviewing people on those subjects. Dame Jenni Murray had similarly been required to step down from presenting a Woman's Hour discussion on the pay dispute after signing a letter about it. The BBC stated that while staff may hold opinions, editors decide case-by-case whether presenters can interview on subjects they have publicly campaigned on.

The NRA claimed YETI coolers cut ties with the organization, prompting boycott calls and protests where supporters destroyed YETI products. YETI responded that it only eliminated outdated discount programs and offered an alternative customization program to the NRA Foundation, calling the NRA's statement inaccurate. The dispute follows other companies distancing from the NRA after recent shootings. YETI maintains it supports the Second Amendment.

This study benchmarks 15 summary-level Mendelian Randomization (MR) methods—including IVW (fixed and random), Egger, RAPS, Weighted-median, Weighted-mode, MR-PRESSO, MRMix, cML-MA, MR-Robust, MR-Lasso, MR-CUE, CAUSE, MR-APSS, and MR-ConMix—using real-world genetic datasets to evaluate type I error control, estimation accuracy, and replicability. Assessing over one thousand negative control trait pairs across three confounding scenarios (population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounders), the analysis found that MR-APSS, Egger, and Weighted-mode consistently controlled type I error, while most other methods exhibited inflated error rates, particularly under looser instrument variable (IV) selection thresholds. MR-APSS provided the most accurate causal effect estimates and was robust to weak IV and selection bias, whereas other methods showed bias toward null effects with weaker instruments. In a replicability case study of LDL-C and coronary artery disease, CAUSE and MR-APSS demonstrated high consistency across datasets, though CAUSE produced deflated p-values. The study recommends employing negative controls, multiple IV thresholds, and independent data sources to enhance reliability, while acknowledging limitations regarding the isolation of confounders and the exclusion of individual-level MR methods.

The passage lists 11 foods rich in folate (vitamin B9): asparagus (33% daily value per cup), broccoli (14%), citrus fruits like oranges (50 mcg), legumes, avocado (110 mcg, 28%), lady's finger (103 mcg per half cup), nuts and seeds, cauliflower (55 mcg, 14%), beetroot (14%), carrots (5%), and corn (34 mcg per cup). It notes preparation methods and additional nutritional benefits for several items.

Female Hungarian winemakers Zita Kovács, Zsófi Laposa, Krisztina Csetvei, and Andi Gere discuss their experiences in the traditionally male-dominated profession. Kovács notes early prejudices have shifted to respect for women winemakers. Laposa credits technological advances for opening the field to women, bringing "gentleness and uniqueness" to the community. Csetvei balances winemaking with raising her young daughter, who accompanies her to tastings and harvests. Gere works alongside her father, noting that feminine influence has refined her family's wine style with elegance.

This patent application describes structurally-colored articles and methods for making them. Structural color is produced through physical light interactions (scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, diffraction) rather than dyes or pigments, offering environmental benefits. The articles use optical elements—single or multilayer reflectors/filters—optionally combined with textured surfaces and/or primer layers to impart color. These can be applied to footwear (uppers, soles, cushioning elements), apparel, and sporting equipment. The optical elements contain 2-20 layers with different refractive indices, made from materials like silicon dioxide, titanium dioxide, and zinc sulfide, deposited via vapor deposition or wet chemistry techniques. Color properties are defined using CIE 1976 (L*a*b*) and CIELCH color spaces, with structural color varying from single-hue angle-independent to iridescent multi-hued. The primer layer can include paints, inks, metals, or oxides, often dark-colored, applied through various printing or deposition methods. The textured surface features micro/nanoscale profile features (10 nm–500 μm) that affect optical properties through their shape, dimensions, and arrangement.

New merger deals suggest junior mining acquisitions, particularly in gold, may be increasing after slow months. Hecla Mining proposed a US$462 million acquisition of Klondex Mines, while Alio Gold announced a $128 million deal for Rye Patch Gold. Canada has seen only six metals and mining mergers in 2018 versus 19 at this time in 2017. Hecla's CEO stated the Klondex deal was unrelated to gold prices. If completed, Hecla's annual gold production would rise to approximately 370,000 ounces. Klondex shares increased 61 percent following the announcement. An analyst noted traditional silver producers are adding gold assets. A third Monday deal involved Anaconda Mining's proposed acquisition of Maritime Resources. Industry executives anticipate further consolidation as junior miners seek risk diversification.

A hockey player discusses facing Detroit, noting their strong offense and goaltending. He emphasizes playing tough but clean to avoid penalties, as officials are calling infractions strictly. He criticizes embellishment on calls and expresses old-school views on officiating. He praises Detroit's line centered by Kris Draper and acknowledges the need for better faceoff performance against their skilled centers. He highlights Nicklas Lidström as the league's best defenseman due to his positional smarts. He mentions his team's loud home arena, the need to focus amid distractions, and jokes about his growing playoff beard.

MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs operating up to 32MHz, with 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM. They feature extended temperature range (-40°C to 125°C), supply voltages of 1.62V-3.6V, and integrated high-speed oscillator. Key peripherals include 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, 12-bit ADC, comparator with DAC, temperature sensor, advanced timers, and communication interfaces (UART, SPI, I2C) supporting multiple protocols. The MSPM0 platform enables performance improvements with reduced energy consumption. Development support includes LaunchPad kits, free MSP SDK, Code Composer Studio IDE, MSP Academy training, and TI E2E forums.

A 63-year-old politician died, survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter. He was an All India Congress Committee member who served as Nagaland Minister for Veterinary and Animal Husbandry (1998-1999) and Roads and Bridges (2000-2003), and was a Nagaland Assembly opposition member for two terms (2003-2013). He first won as an independent in 1993 before joining Congress in 1998. His funeral was held at his private residence, with burial at Viswema village. State governors, chief ministers, and other officials condoled his death and attended the service.

India's 21 state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in fiscal year 2017/18, with 19 of 21 banks reporting losses in the March quarter after the Reserve Bank of India withdrew loan restructuring schemes. Fourth-quarter losses alone reached 626.81 billion rupees ($9.30 billion). Gross non-performing loans rose 15% to 8.96 trillion rupees ($133 billion), with IDBI Bank showing the highest bad-loan ratio at 27.95%. The losses occurred despite a government 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan, with concerns that banks may lack funds for growth after meeting Basel III capital requirements by March 2019.

A 2018 Zillow analysis found homes with air conditioning sold for 2.5% more (nearly $5,500) than homes without it, with premiums highest in San Antonio (5.8%), Cincinnati (5.7%), Detroit, Indianapolis, and Las Vegas (5% each). Air conditioning was required by 62% of buyers versus 48% requiring private outdoor space. Nationally, 66.1% of sold homes had AC, with 99.1% in Las Vegas and 97.9% in Phoenix. Rentals with central AC commanded 2.8% more ($40/month), with highest rent premiums in New York, Las Vegas, and Phoenix metros. Seattle was the only market where AC decreased home values.

Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options contracts. Call options grant the right to buy shares at an agreed-upon price, while put options grant the right to sell shares. Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts based on price predictions, selling covered calls, and buying protective puts. Risks include total investment loss and unlimited risk for short calls. Risk management involves stop-loss orders, position limits, and diversification. Requirements include being at least 18, having a valid address, sufficient funds, and typically a margin account. Minimum account balances vary by broker, generally around $2,000. Investors should allocate no more than 10% of their portfolio to options trading, conduct thorough research, use technical indicators, and backtest strategies before committing funds.

Governor Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program to train school administrators in security. Participants in schools without resource officers may keep firearms in secured storage after completing training and obtaining approval from local superintendents, school boards, and county sheriffs. School sentries or their boards must provide weapons, ammunition, and bullet-proof vests. Alabama Secretary of Law Enforcement Hal Taylor and Superintendent Dr. Eric Mackey supported the program as a no-cost security measure to protect students until additional School Resource Officers can be added.

This patent application describes systems and methods for blockchain transaction risk management using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The technology addresses challenges in tracing cryptocurrency transactions due to blockchain's decentralized nature, which enables money laundering and terrorism financing. The solution includes components for: receiving blockchain transaction data and intelligence labels; selecting transaction flows between source, intermediate, and destination addresses; applying AI graph search algorithms with configurable trace parameters (direction, constraints, filters); generating reports with suspicious address identification; and triggering actions like alerts or transaction suspension. The system employs AutoML for model training, behavior-based classification using statistical, topological, temporal, linkage, derived, and sequential features, and risk scoring regression with time decay factors. It supports automated tracing of digital asset flows and interactive journey boards for investigation, enabling compliance with Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Terrorism Financing regulations across multiple blockchain types including Bitcoin and Ethereum.

The Bank of England warns that artificial intelligence stock valuations may constitute an unsustainable bubble resembling the dot-com era, with concentration in U.S. tech giants creating systemic vulnerabilities and potential infrastructure bottlenecks in power, semiconductors, and data. The central bank cautioned that a market correction could trigger global volatility and expose the UK to shocks from U.S. equity markets, echoing concerns from the International Monetary Fund. The passage also lists various financial news headlines, including gold prices exceeding $4,000 on Federal Reserve easing expectations, Fifth Third Bank's acquisition of Comerica for $10.9 billion, and Germany's antitrust investigation into Temu. The source publication, Pan Finance, is described as a global financial intelligence journal and news website with offices in London, Barcelona, Lagos, Miami, and Sharjah, serving over 200,000 readers across 150 countries.

Plum School District officials will begin 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday to avoid a third consecutive tax increase amid $4 million in debt. The district plans to recruit Chinese tuition students for 2018-19, and the agenda includes elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting, and initiating the closure of Regency Park Elementary School. The workshop follows a special voting meeting on personnel matters.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals by Infosys Finacle found over 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020, with more than half of financial institutions investing or planning to invest this year. Average investment is expected to be about $1 million. Half of banks are working with fintech startups or technology companies on blockchain capabilities. Priority use cases include cross-border payments, digital identity management, clearing and settlement, letter of credit process, and loan syndication. Private blockchains were preferred by 69% of banks, hybrid or consortium blockchains by 20%, and public blockchains by only 10%.

Pump and dump schemes involve promoters artificially inflating stock prices through false information, then selling to latecomers who suffer losses when prices collapse. These scams primarily target penny stocks in OTC markets and unregulated crypto markets due to low volume and limited supply enabling dramatic price swings. A 2002-2015 German study found 6% of investors participated in such schemes, with average returns of -28% and €1.2 million in annual losses. While eradicated from major exchanges through SEC enforcement, pump and dumps persist in crypto markets via digital platforms like Telegram. They remain illegal in regulated markets and immoral regardless of legality, with promoters profiting while most participants lose capital.

This patent application describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for transmitting paging information in new generation wireless communication systems using high-frequency bands with beamforming techniques. The disclosure addresses the challenge of implementing discontinuous reception (DRX) mechanisms for paging when beam directions vary across subframes or timeslots, making it difficult for idle user equipment to predict scheduling.

The solution defines a paging occasion (PO) as a group of paging resources corresponding to one or more preset beams or ports, such as a complete synchronous signal burst set or sweeping resources, rather than a single subframe. Both the first communication node (base station) and second communication node (terminal) calculate the PO's time domain position using parameters including DRX cycle, paging transmission interval, number of transmissions, device identifier, and PO offset. The base station transmits paging information (downlink control information and/or paging message) within this calculated PO across all beam directions. Quasi-co-location relationship information may also be configured or indicated to assist the terminal in determining receive resources.

Argus Research upgraded Orbital ATK (NYSE: OA) to buy with a $120 price target following the company's Q2 2017 earnings report. Orbital reported $1.12 billion in sales (up 3% year-over-year) and adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share, beating expectations by $0.13, though GAAP profits fell 3% to $1.51 per share and free cash flow turned negative at $55.8 million. Management raised full-year guidance to $4.6-$4.65 billion in sales and $5.95-$6.25 per share in earnings, citing a strong book-to-bill ratio of 1.45 and 10% backlog growth. Despite Argus's optimism about second-half cash flow and defense spending, the author considers the stock overvalued at 22 times trailing earnings and an EV/FCF ratio exceeding 40, with projected 10% annual profit growth insufficient to justify current prices.

This case study documents the transformation of Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) under Director Jill Medvedow from 1998 to 2010. When Medvedow arrived, the ICA operated from a converted police station with 25,000 annual visitors, minimal funding, no permanent collection, and limited programming. She stabilized and reinvented the institution through disciplined leadership, risk-taking, and strategic vision.

Medvedow secured a waterfront location on Fan Pier's Parcel J after winning a competitive bid in 1999, despite the ICA's weak financial position. She built political support through direct engagement with local leaders and launched an unconventional $62 million capital campaign with limited initial funding. She assembled a new board of business leaders and hired Paul Bessire as Director of External Relations.

For the building design, Medvedow selected Diller + Scofidio, a New York firm with no U.S. building experience, through a non-traditional selection process that included public presentations. The $51 million building opened in December 2006 after navigating numerous approvals, the sale of surrounding Pritzker family land, and construction delays. The ICA exceeded projections with 280,000 visitors in its first year and sustained strong attendance through 2009, including 130,000 visitors for a 2009 Shepard Fairey exhibition.
The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals dismissed Pink C. Jenkins's appeal against the United States on April 10, 1937, following a motion by the appellee and consent of the appellant.

This study proposes "whole human pedagogy," a decolonial framework for education abroad centered on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. Drawing on hooks (1994), Thompson (2016), and decolonial theory, the framework critiques Euro-U.S. epistemological dominance and advocates for including bodily, emotional, relational, and transformative knowledge in academic spaces. The qualitative study interviewed 17 education abroad practitioners in Fall 2023, finding they understood approaching students as whole human beings as central to their work. Participants described embodiment through physical immersion and sensory learning; emotions through culture shock processing and reflection; belonging through non-hierarchical relationships and learning communities; and becoming through transformative self-development. The framework offers applications for program development, professional development, and future research, representing a rebellion against dehumanization and a method for embracing repressed knowledge types toward individual, communal, and global liberation.

Sean "Diddy" Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for violating the Mann Act by transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. Having already served one year, he faces approximately three more years in prison. He was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges. The case involved years of drug-fueled "freak-offs" with sex workers. During sentencing, Combs apologized for his actions and requested leniency to reunite with his family, while six of his seven children addressed the court pleading for mercy. Judge Arun Subramanian noted Combs used his power and resources to evade capture for years.

Amazon announced new Echo devices with Alexa+ integration, including the Echo Dot Max and Echo Studio with improved audio and AZ3 chips. Three new Kindle Scribe tablets were unveiled, featuring the first color-screen model (Colorsoft), faster performance, and new AI features like Story So Far and Ask This Book. New Fire TVs and a $40 Fire TV Stick 4K Select run on the new Vega operating system. Ring introduced Retinal 2K and 4K cameras with Familiar Faces, Alexa+ Greetings, and Search Party for finding lost pets. Blink launched a 2K video doorbell and Arc accessory for 180-degree coverage.

The passage describes container design patterns for building distributed systems. The sidecar pattern augments applications by adding functionality like HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, and monitoring tools without modifying the original application. The ambassador pattern brokers communications between applications and external services, handling tasks like sharding, service discovery, and request splitting. The adapter pattern standardizes interfaces for heterogeneous applications, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, and health checks. For multi-node systems, the replicated load-balanced pattern provides horizontal scaling for stateless services, while sharded services partition data across machines when state exceeds single-machine capacity. The scatter/gather pattern enables parallel processing by distributing computation across multiple nodes. Each pattern emphasizes modularity, reusability, and separation of concerns through container composition.

Confidential 1892 dispatches from U.S. Minister Stevens reported Hawaiian revolutionary plans and growing annexation sentiment amid political deadlock and public dissatisfaction with the Queen. Stevens recommended annexation or a customs union including Pearl Harbor cession. Navy reports corroborated these accounts until January 1893, when peaceful revolution dethroned the Queen. The document states U.S. policy from 1820 to 1893 emphasized friendship and protection, consistently opposing foreign intervention, with annexation previously contemplated under President Pierce. Submitted by Andrew H. Allen.

Seven months after significant staff and funding cuts at the U.S. Department of Education, researchers express cautious optimism about rebuilding federal education research. The department plans to reinstate 20 of 100+ terminated research contracts and temporarily preserve 10 federally funded regional education labs. It is also seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES), with researcher Amber Northern advising on reforms through December. New hiring has begun for assessment positions at the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), though severe staff shortages persist—NCES was reduced from 100 employees to three. While some researchers view these developments as encouraging, concerns remain about data quality, reduced reporting capabilities, and competing priorities such as a new executive order requiring extensive data collection on college admissions. The administration acknowledges early "chaos" and aims to shift toward results-focused spending, though experts warn that rebuilding will be challenging given the scale of cuts and ongoing resource constraints.

Theratechnologies Inc. (TSX:TH) announced an agreement with underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to issue US$50 million in convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30, 2023, with an over-allotment option of US$7.5 million. The notes bear 5.75% annual interest, payable semi-annually, and are convertible at US$14.85 per share. They are non-redeemable before June 30, 2021, after which redemption is possible if share prices exceed 130% of the conversion price. Proceeds will fund payments under the EMD Serono Termination Agreement, Trogarzo™ commercialization, and general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close around June 19, 2018, subject to regulatory approvals. The notes will be offered via short form prospectus in Canada and private placement in the U.S., where they are not registered under U.S. securities laws.

NGC 5949 is a dwarf galaxy located approximately 44 million light-years from Earth, discovered by William Herschel in 1801. Despite having about one-hundredth the mass of the Milky Way, it is considered relatively large for a dwarf galaxy. It is classified as a barred spiral due to its loosely-bound spiral arms, visible in Hubble imagery as a bright, ill-defined pinwheel. Its proximity makes it a valuable target for studying dwarf galaxies, though astronomers face challenges explaining dark matter distribution within such galaxies and reconciling their observed numbers with cosmological simulations.

The Ultimate Oscillator (UO) is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 that measures price momentum across three timeframes (7, 14, and 28 periods) using weighted averages to reduce volatility and false signals common in single-timeframe oscillators. It calculates buying pressure and true range, combining averages in a 4:2:1 ratio to produce values from 0-100, with levels below 30 considered oversold and above 70 overbought. Trading signals require divergence between price and indicator: buy signals need bullish divergence from oversold territory with the oscillator rising above the divergence high, while sell signals require bearish divergence. Backtests show strong performance across settings, with optimized strategies achieving profit factors above 2.5, win rates around 78%, and consistent results as a mean reversion indicator.

The Supreme Court dismissed Varun Thakur's plea to cancel interim bail for the Pinto family, owners of Ryan International School, in connection with his son Pradyuman's murder. The Punjab and Haryana High Court had granted anticipatory bail to the Pintos on November 21, barring them from leaving India without permission. Pradyuman, 7, was found murdered in the school on September 8. Initially, bus conductor Ashok was arrested by Gurugram Police, but the CBI later cleared him and charged a class 11 student instead. Pradyuman's family alleges the Pinto family's complicity.

Automation threatens millions of jobs, particularly truck driving, with industry giants investing heavily in autonomous vehicles. The World Economic Forum predicts over five million jobs will be eliminated in five years. In response, some propose human augmentation through technologies like neural laces—brain-integrated electronic meshes to enhance cognitive abilities—and exoskeletons to amplify physical strength while reducing injury risk. Researchers at Harvard and companies like SuitX are actively developing these technologies. However, experts like Tom Davenport note that immediate solutions involve workers developing non-automatable skills such as creativity and machine literacy, though physical laborers face greater challenges than knowledge workers in adapting to this transition.
President Trump denied a New York Times report on his television habits. The Times cited 60 sources defending the article. Trump had criticized media "fake news."

A lava flow from Hawaii's Kilauea volcano crossed Highway 132, destroying power lines and equipment, cutting power to Vacationland and Kapoho Beach Lots neighborhoods. The Hawaii County Civil Defense Agency confirmed 71 homes destroyed, with additional structures like outhouses and sheds also lost. The lava from Fissure 8 advanced 800 yards in 80 minutes before slowing. Over 400 utility poles have been destroyed. Authorities ordered evacuations in the Kapoho area as lava approached. One person was rescued after being trapped by molten rock. The eruption, ongoing since May 3, has opened 24 fissures, displaced thousands of residents, and produced volcanic glass, gases, and ash up to 15,000 feet. Lava covered two wells at a geothermal plant, which officials said remain stable with no dangerous gas releases.

Meb Faber's Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach using market timing across five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. The strategy allocates 20% to each position, entering and exiting based on signals rather than remaining fully invested. Implementation uses five diversified index ETFs without selecting individual securities. Backtesting over 16 years showed a maximum drawdown of -13.24%, significantly lower than passive strategies. The model is universal and applicable to various portfolios. Meb Faber is co-founder and CIO of Cambria Investment Management, author of five books, and holds degrees in engineering and biology from the University of Virginia.

Richard Berg appeals a trial court decision increasing his child support obligation from $145 to $258 per child per month. Richard Mosse's photography project "Heat Maps" documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East using a military-grade thermal camera mounted on a robotic arm that detects radiation from distances up to 50 kilometers away. The technology renders human flesh as translucent grey and eye sockets as blackened, creating images that strip refugees of individual identity to reflect how Western governments view them as statistics rather than humans. The large-scale panoramas, constructed from grids of nearly 1,000 frames, depict camp conditions as grim and dehumanizing. Mosse deliberately employs surveillance technology designed for weapons targeting to subvert its original military purpose, utilizing the Brechtian "distancing effect" to force viewers to engage with the crisis unfamiliarly. The three-year project involved navigating complex border logistics and access restrictions. The work is currently displayed at New York's Jack Shainman Gallery until March 11.

President Donald Trump announced the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports starting November 1, 2025, plus export controls on "any and all critical software," in retaliation for China's new export controls on rare earth minerals. The double bottom chart pattern is a bullish reversal formation consisting of two swing lows at approximately the same level with a swing high between them, typically appearing in downtrends. The pattern establishes a support level at the swing lows and a resistance level called the neckline at the swing high. Traders consider the pattern complete only when price breaks above the neckline. Trading approaches vary: aggressive traders enter at the second low using reversal signals, while conservative traders wait for confirmed neckline breakouts with volume increases. Profit targets are estimated by projecting the pattern's size upward from the neckline, with stop losses typically placed mid-pattern for 2:1 reward/risk ratios. Research by Thomas Bulkowski indicates 68% of formations reach their target, though his study has limitations including potential survivorship bias, manual pattern selection, and a bull market timeframe. The authors prefer fully quantified rules over Bulkowski's statistics due to reliance on human interpretation.

UDMA write CRC corruption occurs when a preceding UDMA read operation with host termination leaves a corrupted state residue (host_pio_term set). During UDMA write device termination, the ATAC passes correct CRC for the first termination but fails to restart CRC for subsequent portions, causing errors. UDMA writes become generally unusable due to these CRC errors. The resolution uses the UDMA I/O blocking feature via bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of an antitrust suit brought by Innofood and Sea Breeze against Mitsubishi entities and ESSA, a Mexican government-owned salt producer. The court held that the act of state doctrine barred the claims because the case challenged Mexico's sovereign decision to distribute its natural resources exclusively through Mitsubishi. ESSA, 51% government-owned, constituted an instrumentality of the Mexican government, and its policy regarding salt distribution—covering 90% of Mexico's salt exports—was a quintessentially sovereign act. Relief would require invalidating Mexico's official decisions about exploiting its natural resources. The court rejected plaintiffs' arguments that ESSA's conduct constituted merely commercial activity, finding that decisions about natural resource exploitation are powers peculiar to sovereigns. The Sabbatino factors also supported application of the doctrine: no international consensus condemns such sovereign arrangements, the case implicates significant foreign relations concerns, and the Mexican government remains in existence. The court noted it need not decide whether a commercial exception to the act of state doctrine exists, as any such exception would not apply here.

The passage describes interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry as a method to resolve antiparallel domains and assess crystalline quality in chemical vapor deposition (CVD)-grown hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). hBN's lower threefold rotational symmetry allows two antiparallel orientations to nucleate on sixfold symmetric metal surfaces, forming grain boundaries that compromise properties. Conventional techniques like TEM, STM, and LEED are limited in sampling area or cannot distinguish antiparallel domains, while Raman spectroscopy cannot directly resolve orientational polarity.

SHG signals are coherent and sensitive to antiparallel domains: intensity vanishes at boundaries between antiparallel domains and depends on relative population when multiple domains exist within the focal spot. Interferometric detection measures phase differences between antiparallel domains. CVD-grown hBN samples showed SHG intensity variations up to three orders of magnitude compared to mechanically exfoliated references, while Raman intensity varied only fourfold. Dual-polarization SHG imaging mapped crystallographic orientation, revealing distinctive domain distributions across growth methods. Numerical simulations confirmed that reduced SHG intensity arises from destructive interference among antiparallel domains. The method provides scalable structural assessment for hBN and other non-centrosymmetric 2D crystals.

This study used untargeted metabolomics to analyze blood samples from 22 cirrhotic patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement to identify metabolite changes associated with hepatic encephalopathy (HE) development. The analysis revealed that bile acids decreased immediately post-TIPS but recovered by discharge, with greater decreases observed in patients who developed severe HE. Participants with less intrahepatic shunting prior to TIPS—indicated by greater metabolome dissimilarity between pre- and post-TIPS hepatic vein samples—were more likely to develop HE. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids showed inverse correlation with HE severity, suggesting a protective role. Chemical proportionality analysis identified fluctuations in glycerophosphocholines and bilirubins, particularly biliverdin reduction, as associated with HE development. The findings suggest that pre-existing intrahepatic shunting may protect against post-TIPS HE by allowing prior acclimatization to portal toxins, and that specific bile acids may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for HE prevention.

This document lists 116 errata for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, detailing hardware bugs and their workarounds. Key issues include: UART register access conflicts with DMA cycles; 8237 software DMA memory writes from LPC failing; I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher causing system hangs; USB over-voltage protection non-compliance; LBARs allowing illegal I/O base addresses; PIC failures with edge-configured interrupts when clock gating is enabled; ATAC and ACC prefetch errors with misaligned PRD tables; UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination; ATAC SSMI during DMA not blocking I/O; main GLIU clock domain not awakening from statistics counter ASMIs; ACPI register byte access hangs; PMC register corruption from WORD/BYTE writes; KEL emulation and snoop mode issues; PCI memory read failures on back-to-back fetches; unsupported 8259 PIC polling mode; UART clock gating failure in CEIR mode; PCI timing violations on IRDY#/DEVSEL#; unreliable SSMIs with concurrent IRQs; UDMA failures when bus master is enabled before PIO commands; most wake events non-functional from ACPI S3 state; RTC CMOS RAM access errors; LPC I/O failures during block/demand mode DMA; USB controller clock gating failures; ATAPI packet command failures; KEL AuxOutputFull bit errors; fixed UDMA tACK timing; ATAC hangs with non-DWORD aligned PRDs; LPC aborts on sync patterns; SMB controller NEGACK bit issues; GLPCI retry counter inaccuracies; GPIO High Bank register corruption after suspend; SMBus hold time violations; missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby; and SLEEP_X/Y deassertion failures when delays exceed PM_SED.

The passage describes distributed system design patterns for containerized applications, focusing on the adapter pattern, replicated load-balanced services, sharded services, scatter/gather patterns, and function-as-a-service (FaaS) architectures.

The adapter pattern enables containers to expose compatible interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks without modifying the original application container. Examples include using Prometheus exporters for Redis monitoring, Fluentd for log normalization, and custom adapters for database health checks.

Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy and horizontal scaling for stateless applications. The pattern uses multiple identical replicas behind a load balancer, with readiness probes ensuring traffic only routes to initialized instances. Session tracking can ensure user requests consistently map to specific replicas.

Sharded services partition data across multiple machines when state exceeds single-node capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization by storing unique data per shard rather than replicating all data. Consistent hashing minimizes rebalancing during scaling, while replicated shards within each shard provide fault tolerance.

Scatter/gather patterns parallelize computation across multiple nodes, with a root distributing requests to leaves that return partial results for aggregation. This enables faster processing but introduces overhead and straggler problems where slowest nodes determine total latency.

FaaS and event-driven architectures suit stateless, asynchronous processing like request transformation, event handling, and pipeline workflows. Benefits include simplified deployment and automatic scaling, while challenges include operational complexity, debugging difficulties, and unsuitability for long-running processes or memory-intensive applications.

The President transmits to Congress a letter from the Governor of Texas claiming jurisdiction over four counties east of the Rio Grande, including Santa Fe, which Texas's legislature may attempt to enforce by force. The President explains his constitutional duty to execute federal laws and treaties, citing acts of 1795 and 1807 that authorize him to use military force when laws are obstructed by combinations too powerful for civil authorities. He argues that the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo made New Mexico a U.S. territory with defined boundaries, and that its ninth article protects inhabitants' liberty, property, and religion. Texas's authority cannot extend beyond its boundaries; any Texan force entering New Mexico would be trespassing, and obstruction of federal treaty obligations would require presidential intervention. The executive cannot determine the boundary—that requires congressional action with Texas's assent or legal adjudication—but must protect established inhabitants pending such resolution. The President urges immediate congressional settlement of the boundary question, suggesting direct legislation with possible indemnity to Texas rather than slower judicial or commission processes, to prevent potential violence and restore national harmony.

James D. Rone, employed by Dan Raymond Construction Company, was injured at a sewer construction site in Hobart, Indiana while working for a joint venture between Raymond and Boncar Construction Company. Rone lost fingers when a cable moved while he was descending from a back hoe gantry after lifting telephone wires. The back hoe was operated by Robert Crank, a Boncar employee. Rone sued Boncar for negligence under Indiana law and for violating the Illinois Structural Work Act. The trial court struck the Illinois Structural Work Act count, and a jury returned a verdict for Boncar on the negligence count. On appeal, the court held that: (1) Rone waived his right to appeal the dismissal of the Illinois Structural Work Act count by failing to perfect a timely appeal; (2) questions of negligence and contributory negligence were properly submitted to the jury since conflicting inferences could be drawn from undisputed facts; (3) the Indiana Employers Liability Act did not apply because Rone was not suing his employer; and (4) the trial court did not err in refusing two proposed jury instructions. The judgment was affirmed.

The AEGEAN study evaluated apixaban adherence in atrial fibrillation patients across multiple groups: Primary SOC, Additional Educational Program, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Educational Program. Time to apixaban initiation averaged 1.6-1.8 days across groups. Total drug exposure and interruptions were comparable at 24 weeks (157-160 days exposure, 1.4-1.8 days interruption). At 48 weeks, exposure ranged from 301-328 days with interruptions of 2.2-4.8 days. Most subjects received 5 mg BID dosing (86-88%), with minimal dose modifications (2.3-4.1%). Treatment compliance exceeded 95% at Week 24 and 94% at Week 48 across all groups.

Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.6-91.9% with no significant difference between groups (p=0.8117). Adherence declined significantly from Week 12-24 compared to baseline-Week 12 in both groups (p<0.0001). At 48 weeks, adherence was 87.5-88.4% from Week 24-48, with overall adherence from first dose to Week 48 at 89.5-90.9%. Persistence at 24 weeks was 91.3-91.7%, and 85.2-87.8% at 48 weeks, with no significant differences. Fully adherent subjects declined from 26.5-28.1% at 24 weeks to 14.5-14.9% at 48 weeks.

Predictive factors for non-adherence included alcohol consumption, technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, and lower MMSE scores in the Primary SOC group; age and VKA-naïve status at 48 weeks. Subgroup analyses showed significant interactions for atrial fibrillation type and sex from Week 24-48.

Safety outcomes were similar across groups. At 24 weeks, 51.2-52.0% reported adverse events (AEs), 7.3-8.9% had related AEs, 12.4-14.7% had serious AEs, and 3.9-5.5% discontinued due to AEs. Bleeding events occurred in 6.5-9.0%, with major bleeding in 0.7-1.1%. From Week 24-48, 33.8-40.8% reported AEs, with 3.2-4.1% experiencing bleeding events and 0.3-0.7% major bleeding. Twenty-four deaths occurred total. No pregnancies were reported. Laboratory data showed no concerning signals.

The study concluded that adherence and persistence remained high through 48 weeks, with no additional benefit from the educational program.
