Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies, popularized by Tony Crabel's 1990 book, have become less effective over time. Backtests on S&P 500 futures showed minimal average gains (0.04% per trade) and low win rates for basic strategies, with similar poor results for Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil futures. The market has changed due to false breakouts, overnight session gains, and increased algorithmic trading. However, adding daily filters based on longer timeframes can improve results—one live strategy achieved 0.27% average gain with 65% win rate and profit factor of 2. While ORB strategies remain less relevant for major indices, individual stocks may offer better opportunities. Traders should use strategy optimization carefully to avoid curve fitting.

The "Amoeba" defense, developed by Jerry Tarkanian at UNLV, contributed to their 1990 NCAA Championship. It is an aggressive, trapping match-up zone defense run from a 1-1-3 alignment designed to disrupt opponents. The defense features extreme ball pressure with four defenders zoning, requiring quick guards for outside rotations to generate steals and transition baskets. Key alignments include point guard pressure at midcourt, free throw line protection, wing positioning between the free throw line and baseline, and post defense at the basket. Specific scenarios cover wing pass entries, corner passes with trap options, post/wing exchanges, skip passes, ball reversals, guard/wing interchanges, cross court passes, two-guard front matchups, triple teams on the high post, and wing pass matchups with optional double teams.

A hockey player discusses recovering from an injury that kept him out of recent playoff games, expressing readiness to return. He reflects on the difficulty of watching from the sidelines, the value of playoff experience for his team, and the depth that has allowed players like Helm, Filppula, Samuelsson, Cleary, and Franzen to step up. He notes similarities with their opponent's depth, acknowledges pre-game nerves as helpful for focus, and mentions using teammates' lack of championship wins as motivation. He dismisses fatigue concerns for the finals, emphasizing excitement and energy from the opportunity, while praising rookie Jonathan Ericsson's mature playoff performance despite limited experience.

Anti-police brutality groups in Utah are outraged after a prosecutor ruled police were legally justified in fatally shooting Patrick Harmon, a 50-year-old black man, in August. Body camera footage shows Harmon running from officers before being shot; a slowed-down version indicates he pivoted toward police with a knife, though the knife isn't clearly visible in the video. Officer Clinton Fox claimed Harmon threatened to stab him. Black Lives Matter organizer Lex Scott called the shooting murder and demanded the district attorney resign. The shooting occurred after Harmon was stopped for lacking a bicycle tail light; officers discovered felony warrants. About 50 protesters had previously demanded the footage's release. The case comes amid national debate on race and policing. Salt Lake NAACP president Jeanetta Williams said she didn't see a knife in the video and the group will seek more information before deciding on action.

The passage describes patent drawings of a gaming machine design, including front perspective, front elevation, rear elevation, right and left side elevation, top plan, and bottom plan views. Dashed broken lines indicate portions not part of the claimed design.

Retired Toronto lawyer Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his 50-year-old McGill law schoolbooks, reflecting on memorable cases like Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. and The Moorcock before recycling most volumes. He kept only his tax law textbook, now used as a reading stand.

This study examined the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and suicide attempts or self-directed violence among US Veterans using data from the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Researchers analyzed 199,474 infected Veterans matched with 992,036 uninfected comparators, utilizing electronic health records and emulated trial design. Results showed infected Veterans had significantly higher risk of suicide attempts (hazard ratio 2.54 in first 30 days, 1.41 over one year) and self-directed violence (hazard ratio 1.94 in first 30 days, 1.38 over one year) compared to uninfected controls. Risk was highest in the first 30 days post-infection but persisted for at least one year. No significant difference in unverified suicide deaths was found between groups. The study highlights the importance of early suicide prevention efforts following COVID-19 infection among Veterans.

Momentum investing involves buying stocks with the best historical performance over 3-12 months and periodically rebalancing to maintain holdings in the highest momentum stocks. Research by Eric Crittenden found that approximately 20% of stocks drive all market returns while 80% produce zero returns, making stock selection difficult. A backtested S&P 500 momentum strategy using monthly bars and simple moving average crossovers from 1960-2023 produced a 6.6% annual return versus 7% for buy-and-hold, but with only 69% market exposure and 26% drawdowns versus 55%. The risk-adjusted return was 9.5%, substantially higher than buy-and-hold. The S&P 500 Momentum Index (SP500MUP) measures relative strength performance across all markets.

The ADP National Employment Report showed 32,000 private nonfarm jobs lost in September 2024, the largest decline since June 2020. The six-month moving average fell to 23,000, its lowest level since the post-pandemic period. Education & Health Services gained 33,000 jobs, while Leisure & Hospitality lost 19,000. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly jobs report is typically the most anticipated economic news of the first week of each month.

Kiran Rana, a digital and social media editor at The Globe and Mail, discusses her love-hate relationship with social media in the weekly Amplify newsletter. She notes that social media has transformed news consumption, with growing numbers of Canadians and Americans getting news first on platforms like Facebook. Recent trending topics include Ontario PC party political disarray and #MeToo movement developments in Canadian politics. While social media enables information access and social change, Rana highlights its negative aspects: undermining democracy, creating echo chambers, and facilitating online harassment, citing personal attacks against columnist Denise Balkissoon. She also references The New York Times' investigation into fake Twitter followers and profiles Veena Dwivedi, an Indo-Canadian neuroscience professor who overcame racism and sexism in STEM to run her own lab while supporting young women in the field.

LifeShare Community Blood Services is seeking blood donors to address winter shortages in northeast Ohio, where donations have dropped due to snow, cold temperatures, and flu outbreaks. Type O blood is most critically needed, though all types are welcome. Eligible donors must be at least 16 (with parental consent), weigh 110+ pounds, and be in good health. Upcoming mobile drives are scheduled February 3-4 in Avon Lake, Amherst, Elyria, and Grafton.

Overbought refers to when stock markets have risen significantly over a defined period, indicating weaker short-term returns ahead. It is bearish for trading, suggesting potential price correction. Mean-reversion explains that strong deviations from trends tend to reverse direction over time. Media can amplify overbought conditions through positive coverage creating FOMO, or worsen downturns with negative articles. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is one tool to identify overbought conditions—such as when 2-day RSI exceeds 95. Backtesting shows returns in the first days after overbought conditions are significantly lower than long-term averages, though returns eventually revert to mean. Overbought conditions predict short-term, not long-term, results.

The passage describes distributed system design patterns, focusing on container-based architectures. It covers the adapter pattern for normalizing logging formats and adding health checks without modifying main containers, using Fluentd and custom adapters. It then discusses microservices versus monolithic architectures, highlighting benefits like independent scaling and team autonomy. The text details replicated load-balanced services, including stateless services, session tracking, and caching layers with Varnish and nginx for SSL termination. It explains sharded services for stateful data, sharding functions, consistent hashing, and hot sharding. The scatter/gather pattern enables parallel request processing across multiple nodes. Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) patterns include decorators for request transformation, event handling for asynchronous tasks like two-factor authentication, and event-driven pipelines. Finally, it addresses distributed ownership and master election for reliable task assignment across replicated services.

European officials are nearing completion on the largest pharmaceutical policy overhaul in decades, addressing drug shortages, antimicrobial resistance, environmental impact, and hospital drug compounding, with potential deal expected by year-end. Telehealth has evolved from patient access tool to drug marketing channel, with companies now selling medications for conditions ranging from erectile dysfunction to weight loss through direct-to-consumer advertising, often using unapproved compounded drugs. Colorado became the first state to limit health plan payments for an expensive arthritis treatment. The Trump administration withdrew threatened 100% pharmaceutical tariffs originally set for October 1.

A top-level Pakistani delegation led by Foreign Secretary Tehmina Janjua arrived in Kabul for the first Pakistan-Afghanistan Joint Working Group meeting. Pakistan proposed five working groups focused on counter-terrorism, intelligence sharing, military cooperation, economic engagement, refugee repatriation, and connectivity. Pakistan maintains there is no military solution to the Afghan conflict and supports an Afghan-led peace process. The visit follows a high-level Afghan delegation's trip to Pakistan earlier in the week. Pakistan's Ambassador to the U.S., Aizaz Ahmad Chaudhry, denied Pakistani responsibility for Afghan violence and stated Pakistan would benefit from Afghan peace.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. The controllers feature three oscillator modes: internal oscillator (RT resistor sets frequency, SYNC outputs 2× clock), external synchronization (RT floating, external clock applied to SYNC), and primary-secondary mode (two controllers synchronized via SYNC). Output configurations vary by device: TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP have dual primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and support 50% duty cycle; TPS7H5001-SP uniquely includes dual synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB). Dead time (TDSP/TDPS) and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors for most devices. The controllers implement peak current mode control with slope compensation, hiccup mode overcurrent protection, external fault protection, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. Applications include buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies, with design examples provided for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices.

This patent application describes systems, methods, and devices for wireless communication of analyte data using a diabetes management partner interface. The disclosure addresses challenges in integrating analyte sensor systems with multiple partner devices—particularly automatic or manual insulin delivery devices from different manufacturers—by enabling configurable wireless communication parameters. The analyte sensor system uses the interface to receive authorization and input from partner devices to modify configuration parameters including wireless connectivity settings, access control parameters, and analyte data parameters according to specific system requirements. The system supports multiple operating modes tailored to different device configurations, manages whitelists and advertisement structures, handles intermittent or continuous connection models, and can restore previous configurations when transitioning between modes. The interface facilitates communication between display device applications and partner device applications, enabling unified alert management and monitoring of medicament delivery device operability status.

Israel and Myanmar signed an education cooperation agreement to teach Myanmar students about the Holocaust, anti-Semitism, and xenophobia, while allowing each state to edit passages about their own history in the other's textbooks. The agreement includes mutual textbook verification and corrections, development of Israeli/Jewish studies in Myanmar and Myanmar studies in Israel, and academic cooperation from pre-school to postgraduate levels. The deal occurs amid international criticism: Israel for killing over 100 Palestinian protesters in Gaza, and Myanmar for alleged ethnic cleansing against Rohingya Muslims. Myanmar supported the US embassy move to Jerusalem; Israel continued arms sales to Myanmar despite UN accusations. The US Holocaust Memorial Museum revoked an award from Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi over Rohingya killings. Social media users criticized the agreement as history revisionism between "two ethnic cleansers."

William C. Smith, 42, of Trotwood, was arraigned in Miami County Municipal Court on Monday on a murder charge for the death of Willard Higgins Jr., 40, of Troy. Smith pleaded not guilty and received a $500,000 bond. Higgins died at Kettering Hospital following a physical altercation with Smith on Walnut Street around 12:30 p.m. Friday. Smith was detained Friday evening by Washington Courthouse police on drug charges before transfer to Miami County. Higgins had difficulty breathing after the altercation, was transported to Upper Valley Medical Center, suffered a heart attack and brain bleed, and was flown to Kettering Hospital where he died. Witnesses said Smith allegedly commented about Higgins' girlfriend, sparking the fight. An autopsy is underway at Montgomery County Crime Lab, with a pre-trial hearing set for December 19.

A 2015 survey by Professor Yvonne Sadovy and Fiji's Ministry of Fisheries found that 70% of known kawakawa and donu breeding sites in Fiji have declined or disappeared, with 18% labelled dead and 9% healthy. Grouper catches also declined 70%. The 4FJ Campaign, founded by cChange Fiji director Scott Radway, seeks to protect these species by asking people to pledge not to eat, buy or sell them during peak breeding months (June-September). A survey in Suva found 95% of respondents willing to give up eating these fish during breeding season. The campaign has wide support from private sector, research institutions, government, NGOs and communities.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on July 22, 2020, reporting the release of its Second Quarter 2020 financial results via an update posted on its website. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

VentureWire's November 15, 2000 issue reports on private company business news. Top stories include Advanced Technology Ventures raising an $800 million fund, Qualcomm forming a $500 million venture arm, IP Communications securing $312 million in funding, and Foodbuy.com cutting 22% of its workforce while ending California operations. The issue covers numerous funding rounds across sectors including mobile technology, optical networking, e-commerce, and broadband. Notable raises include FreeRein ($15M), PacketLight Networks ($18M), NetCarrier ($28M), Autodaq ($33M), Video Networks ($66M), and RichFX ($33M). Bad news includes Drinks.com laying off half its staff and WebTaggers shutting down. The issue also reports mergers, executive appointments, and venture capital firm developments including Portview Communications closing a $61 million fund and Cambrian Ventures raising a seed fund from individuals.

Blackwell's RT Core introduces Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for ray intersection testing, offering 2x faster rendering and 5x less VRAM usage for hair compared to DOTS. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 improves GPU thread reorganization with twice the efficiency. The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a RISC-V-based scheduler that offloads GPU context management from the CPU, reducing latency and improving multitasking.

Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video, balancing color accuracy and file size. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% and adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding, with AV1 Ultra High Quality mode providing an additional 5% improvement. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds by over 50% gen-over-gen. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth for high-resolution, high-refresh displays.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating with faster state transitions, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and low latency sleep (10x faster than Ada), enabling up to 50% power savings in workloads like small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to 3 additional frames per rendered frame) with 40% faster AI models and 30% less VRAM, plus transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, detail in motion, and image quality. Neural shaders enable AI-based techniques including Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM savings), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI face rendering).

Blackwell GPU variants include: GB202 (92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 512-bit memory) for RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6B transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 256-bit memory) for RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205 (31B transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 192-bit memory) for RTX 5070.

The Supreme Court's order granting defendants' motion for a further bill of particulars was reversed on appeal. Plaintiff Jane Kursa had failed to furnish a bill of particulars, resulting in a conditional order of preclusion, then submitted one defendants deemed insufficient. The appellate court found defendants failed to move within the required 10-day period under CPLR 3042(d) without alleging special circumstances for delay. Despite plaintiff's own dilatory conduct, strict statutory compliance was required, and the motion was denied.

The Imperial Russian Government acknowledged the unjustifiable seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon but rejected the principal claim for loss of services during detention. In January 1899, the U.S. offered $42,000 as compromise settlement, explicitly preserving claimants' rights to full recovery if refused. Russia rejected this offer in March 1899, proposing only $2,500 indemnity. The claimants argue the Okhotsk Sea cannot be effectively controlled by any nation, citing treaties of 1824 and 1825 with the U.S. and Great Britain that guaranteed freedom of navigation and fishing in Pacific waters, and noting Russia never asserted control beyond ordinary jurisdictional waters. The Russian commander's claim that the Okhotsk Sea was "closed" contradicts established international law and treaty obligations.

The lecture discusses collective (coherent) Thomson scattering in plasmas, where the scattering wavelength exceeds the Debye length, sampling collective plasma motion. The speaker derives the scattered power spectrum using the Klimontovich distribution function and test particle treatment, accounting for interference effects from particles at different positions. The spectral density function S(k,ω) is expressed in terms of electron density fluctuations, with contributions from both electron and ion terms. Peaks in the spectrum occur when the plasma permittivity ε approaches zero, corresponding to normal plasma modes like ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibilities involve the plasma dispersion function (W function), which can be tabulated for computational purposes. The derivation includes incoherent scattering as a limiting case.

Blue Bird (BLBD) reported record Q3 sales with strong margins driven by bus volumes, higher pricing, and resilient demand despite tariffs. The company maintains a robust backlog of 3,900 units supporting growth into FY25, though near-term orders face uncertainty. Investments in facilities, product innovation, and federal EV funding position BLBD for long-term growth. The author maintains a Buy rating based on attractive valuation, healthy demand, margin expansion, and positive long-term outlook despite short-term EV risks, and may initiate a long position in BLBD within 72 hours.

On Friday, the stock market experienced its biggest single-day decline since Brexit and largest weekly drop in two years, with the Dow falling over 600 points and major indices declining about 2 percent each. The widespread sell-off was triggered by a jobs report showing the largest monthly wage increase since 2009, sparking investor panic that higher inflation could prompt faster Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Despite the sharp correction, most analysts view it as a return to normal market volatility rather than broader economic trouble.

This document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP secure virtualization technologies. The GHCB enables encrypted guests to communicate with hypervisors through a standardized 4KB shared memory area without exposing sensitive register state. The protocol defines Automatic Exits (AE) and Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), with NAE events requiring guest-controlled state sharing via the GHCB. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement through a bitmap mechanism, SEV-SNP support, and various enhancements including page state changes, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL execution, and trusted I/O. The GHCB MSR protocol provides pre-establishment communication using 12-bit function codes for version negotiation, CPUID requests, AP management, and page state changes. SEV-SNP guests must register GHCB guest physical addresses before use and can utilize extended features like SNP Guest Requests for firmware communication, certificate retrieval, and confidential computing blob configuration through EFI protocols.

Massachusetts General Hospital's Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA) faced chronic inefficiencies and long patient wait times despite two years of improvement efforts. In June 2009, a patient complaint letter prompted Dr. Jeanine Wiener-Kronish, chief of anesthesia, to convene the PATA Task Force to urgently address these problems.

PATA conducted pre-surgical assessments for 43% of surgical patients—outpatients requiring clearance before anesthesia. The clinic had 12 exam rooms and typically saw 55 patients daily, with appointments averaging 2.5 hours and many exceeding 4 hours, though only 80-90 minutes involved actual provider contact. Limited capacity meant only 65% of outpatients could be seen in PATA; healthier patients received same-day OR assessments, causing surgical delays and lost productivity.

The task force, led by DACCPM Executive Director Susan Moss, explored solutions requiring internal changes only, as previous proposals for additional resources were rejected. An MIT Sloan MBA intern conducted a time study revealing patients spent more time waiting than with providers. The June 2009 meeting generated conflicting proposals: extending hours, adding resources, or improving efficiency without additional resources. The team agreed to analyze data-driven scenarios and challenge existing assumptions at their next meeting.

A 4-year follow-up study of the ePOD-methylphenidate RCT found no evidence for long-lasting age-dependent effects of stimulant treatment on dopamine system development in ADHD patients. Using pharmacological MRI, researchers assessed 32 adolescents and 24 adults who were stimulant-naive at baseline. While initial RCT results showed short-term age-dependent effects of methylphenidate on dopamine-reactivity, these did not persist long-term. However, age-dependent associations emerged between extent of stimulant use and brain measures: adults with higher thalamic resting cerebral blood flow received less medication, while adolescents with lower medial prefrontal cortex dopamine-reactivity received more. These baseline associations predicted subsequent medication use patterns. Whole-brain analysis revealed CBF-response correlated with noradrenaline transporter distribution, not dopamine receptors. The findings suggest neuroplasticity may account for lack of long-term imprinting effects, though the age-dependent associations may have predictive value for treatment optimization.

The speaker expresses excitement about advancing to play another game and aims to succeed on Saturday night. The team is healthy, confident, rested, and energetic, despite Dwayne's injury. They value a player who brings physicality and offense through forechecking. The team will maintain their approach, execute their game plan, and believe playing well will produce desired results.

This cross-sectional study of 7,264 Chinese schoolteachers found that 56.9% had inadequate or problematic personal health literacy, with significant sociodemographic variations by age, marital status, school type, and teaching subject. Teachers with inadequate health literacy had higher odds of poor health status (OR=5.79), health-compromising behaviours (OR=2.90), health service use (OR=2.73), and healthcare costs (OR=2.51). Similarly, teachers in non-supportive school health literacy environments showed higher odds of negative health outcomes. The study highlights the need for targeted interventions addressing both personal health literacy and organizational school environments to improve teacher health outcomes.

Linguistics expert Martin O'Leary researched etymology to reveal how seemingly unrelated words share Proto-Indo-European (PIE) roots. PIE, spoken 4,500–2,500 BC on steppes north of the Caspian Sea, is the "mother tongue" of over 440 modern languages including English, French, Spanish, German, Russian, and Persian. Examples include "architect" and "dachshund" (from "teks," meaning "to weave"), "science" and "sh*t" (from "sek"), and "blue," "phlegm," and "flamingo" (from "bhel," meaning "to shine"). Words sharing common derivation are called cognates. O'Leary's Twitter charts showing these connections received thousands of retweets.

Webster Elementary School dedicated two recycled "buddy benches" and planted a tree in memory of former music teacher Robert Pickell, who died in July after falling through his roof. Over 100 people attended the Friday ceremony where students shared personal tributes. Pickell's wife noted his love of recycling. Current music teacher Tricia Witmen, who knew Pickell since 6th grade, said the benches embody his spirit of friendship. A plaque will be added to the tree when it grows large enough.

Vert Rotors, an Edinburgh-based engineering firm, has developed the VERT.500, a scaled-up version of its patented small compressor for industrial use. Developed with the Advanced Manufacturing and Automation Centre, the oil-free device offers clean air, energy efficiency, and low noise, addressing limitations of standard oil-free compressors. Founder Olly Dmitriev stated it will save hospitals and businesses thousands in noise protection costs while reducing electricity bills and CO2 emissions. The company, established in 2013, previously focused on ultra-compact compressors and recently announced a "super-compressor" for Scotland's space industry.

The speaker notes that while outcomes can't always be controlled, putting forth maximum effort is essential. A specific individual is mentioned who remains involved with the team despite being unable to play, attending skates and offering perspective from an observer's viewpoint, having made a sacrifice for the team's benefit.

Interfacial mobility, a key parameter controlling microstructural evolution in materials, is typically extracted from molecular dynamics simulations using equilibrium fluctuations or linear response methods. Both approaches assume Markovian, memory-free motion, but recent research shows that memory effects persist due to hierarchical relaxation processes, particularly at low temperatures or with solute interactions. These non-Markovian effects manifest as transient sub-diffusion, challenging conventional mobility extraction. The authors adapt generalized approaches from biochemistry to address memory effects, using a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model of interface migration with interacting solute to demonstrate inconsistencies with the capillary fluctuation method and present alternative extraction techniques including a time convolutionless propagator approach.

Intel may release a 40th anniversary edition Core i7-8086K processor with 5GHz maximum clock speed, six cores, and 12 threads. The specifications match the existing Core i7-8700K but with 300MHz higher speed. As a K-series CPU, it will be overclockable and likely cherry-picked for better overclocking potential. Retailers already sell pre-binned Core i7-8700K CPUs at higher prices. The 8086 processor launched in 1978, establishing x86 architecture. Intel previously released an anniversary edition Pentium G3258 in 2014. The Core i7-8086K is expected to retail around $480, approximately $100 more than the Core i7-8700K.

Dr. Kellie Leitch sparked debate about Canadian values, particularly regarding female genital mutilation (FGM). While some deny FGM occurs in North America, a Detroit doctor faces charges for allegedly performing it on two seven-year-old girls. The Ontario Human Rights Commission indicates FGM is practised in Canada, with some families sending daughters abroad for the procedure. FGM is an ancient cultural practice, not religious, occurring globally especially in Africa. In Canada, women who underwent infibulation sometimes request reinfibulation after childbirth, often at husbands' request. Medical professionals argue against performing any non-clinically necessary genital mutilation, rejecting "cultural accommodation" as moral cowardice. The author concludes FGM is not a Canadian value and supports screening would-be citizens accordingly.

Walter Lippmann's memorandum analyzes the political context of the Inquiry organization. He predicts the war will not end suddenly, with demobilization following rather than preceding peace negotiations. Lippmann describes an expected German peace propaganda campaign designed to divide Allied nations by appealing to left-wing groups with minimal concessions. He notes this strategy has already created tensions between Russia and Western Allies and weakened liberal support for the war. The German government maintains Central European unity while exploiting Allied divisions. Two counter-strategies exist: coercive suppression of dissenting opinions, which risks deepening class divisions and corrupting war spirit; and unifying the Allies through broadly acceptable purposes, as demonstrated in President Wilson's reply to the Pope. European Allies' silence on this reply reflects tense domestic political situations. Lippmann argues that focusing on territorial peace terms now would undermine morale by substituting narrow nationalistic ambitions for the greater purpose of defeating German militarism and would risk splitting the coalition.

A player emphasizes the need for veterans to remind teammates to stay focused for one more tough game in Calgary, noting the team battles hard, plays well on the road, and must stick to their game plan. He praises Olie's performance, mentions refocusing tomorrow, and expresses confidence in the team's unity.

This study develops an agent-based epidemiological framework to evaluate COVID-19 interventions in the Netherlands, using rich data on demography, mobility, mixing, hospitalization, and seroprevalence. The model simulates 170,721 agents across 380 municipalities at 1:100 population scale, with hourly resolution from February 27 to June 1, 2020. Four intervention phases are analyzed: unchecked transmission, minor interventions, strict national lockdown, and gradual lifting.

Key findings show mobility reductions contributed most to epidemic control (without them, hospital admissions would have doubled), while behavioral changes had moderate impact and school closures had little effect due to late implementation. The study evaluates subnational interventions triggered by local infection thresholds (3%, 1%, 0.33%, 0.1%). A 0.33% threshold allowed 167 municipalities to delay interventions with only 410 additional hospital admissions (3.4% increase), and 18 municipalities remained intervention-free for over five weeks. Lower thresholds reduce hospital admissions but increase societal burden; higher thresholds (3%) caused 157% more admissions. The framework demonstrates that with adequate local infection monitoring, subnational strategies can substantially reduce societal intervention burden while maintaining comparable epidemic control, even in small, densely populated, highly mobile countries like the Netherlands.

On February 7, 2013, the leadership team of MIT Sloan's Sloan Women in Management (SWIM) club faced a critical decision regarding their third annual conference scheduled for the next day. Despite 11 months of planning, a major winter storm threatened Boston with snowfall predictions ranging from 3 to 50 inches. The five-person leadership team—three co-presidents (Rachel, Lea, and Tarini serving as CFO, COO, and CMO) and two conference directors (Janet and Merrill)—gathered at 2:00pm with SLO Associate Director Marco Esquandolas to decide whether to cancel, modify, or proceed with the sold-out 500-person event.

The conference planning had been fraught with challenges: tension between co-presidents and directors over decision-making authority; Merrill's departure from MIT Sloan in August 2012 to join a startup while attempting to continue directing remotely; speaker recruitment difficulties that left the agenda unfinalized until December; a keynote cancellation in January 2013; and marketing struggles without confirmed speakers. By February 4, however, all elements appeared resolved—15 speakers confirmed, 500 tickets sold, $38,000 in sponsorships raised, and operations scheduled.

By February 7, weather reports indicated snow would begin Friday afternoon, though forecasts varied significantly. All 15 speakers remained committed to attending, with some already en route. The team identified three options: cancel before 2:00pm to avoid vendor setup costs; hold a half-day conference with concurrent sessions; or delay the decision until Thursday evening. Rescheduling was deemed impossible due to venue unavailability and impending graduation. The team weighed financial risks, speaker and attendee safety, sponsor relations, and organizational legacy in their deliberations.

Scientists found that some dogs exhibit "addictive-like play behavior" toward toys, sharing features with human behavioral addictions. In a study of 105 dogs, 33 showed intense signs including distress when toys were inaccessible and choosing toys over food. The behavior was more common in terriers and shepherds, likely because these traits are valued in working dogs. Researchers estimate about 3% of dogs may show this behavior. The drive appears to be for play itself rather than the toy, and experts emphasize the importance of play for dog-human relationships.

Baking powder and baking soda are not interchangeable despite both helping batters and doughs rise. Baking soda is a base that bubbles when mixed with acids, while baking powder contains baking soda plus a dry acid. Substitution is possible: use 2-3 tsp baking powder for 1 tsp baking soda, or 1/2 tsp baking soda plus 1 tsp vinegar or lemon juice for 1 tsp baking powder. Baking powder lasts 3-12 months (shorter in humid climates) and can be tested with water; baking soda lasts indefinitely if sealed and cool, and can be tested with vinegar.

Federal Reserve officials in September were divided on interest rate cuts, with a 10-9 majority expecting two more quarter-point reductions by year-end, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday. The committee voted 11-1 to cut rates by 25 basis points to 4%-4.25%, with Governor Stephen Miran dissenting in favor of a half-point cut. Officials expressed concern over weakening labor market conditions while expecting inflation to ease toward the 2% target. They also discussed tariffs, generally viewing them as not causing lasting inflation. A government shutdown now threatens to leave policymakers without key economic data before their October 28-29 meeting.

This paper introduces LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method that identifies distinguishing reasoning features between large reasoning models (LRMs) by comparing their outputs. LOT operates in three stages: an LLM compares reasoning traces and highlights distinguishing traits, annotates these features in other traces to create feature vectors, and trains a logistic classifier to predict source models. When classification fails, LOT proposes new features from failed samples, iteratively building an open taxonomy.

The authors apply LOT to classify reasoning traces from 12 LRMs across diverse scales, base families, and domains. LOT achieves 80-100% accuracy when models differ substantially along these axes, outperforming few-shot prompting (by 23.8%), VML (by 19.6%), and human-defined taxonomies (by 11.7%). Key findings include: smaller models exhibit more circular reasoning; code-specialized models occasionally use Python for math problems; and models from the same base family show similar reasoning patterns. A case study on Qwen3 models demonstrates that reasoning differences have causal links to performance gaps—aligning smaller models' reasoning styles to the largest Qwen3 improves accuracy by 3.3-5.7% on GPQA-Diamond.

This lecture covers policy with behavioral agents, focusing on paternalism and government intervention. It distinguishes between traditional neoclassical reasons for policy (externalities, equity, market failures like monopolies and public goods) and behavioral reasons called "internalities"—where people don't fully internalize costs/benefits to their future selves.

Paternalism is defined as influencing conduct for people's own good. Hard paternalism forces choices through mandates, bans, or significant price changes. Soft paternalism includes libertarian paternalism (Thaler and Sunstein)—nudges that preserve freedom of choice—and asymmetric paternalism (Camerer et al.)—helping those who make mistakes while minimally interfering with optimal behavior.

Arguments against paternalism include government incompetence, lack of information about individual preferences, heterogeneity across people, regulatory capture, corruption, and freedom of choice having intrinsic value. Arguments for include people making mistakes, choice being costly, and soft paternalism allowing opt-outs.

Popular paternalism includes Social Security, Medicare, mandatory education, and cigarette taxes. Unpopular forms include helmet/seatbelt laws, junk food taxes, and drug prohibition. The Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) plan exemplifies successful libertarian paternalism: voluntary enrollment, automatic contribution increases timed with pay raises, and easy opt-out—leveraging present bias and loss aversion.

Markets often fail to solve behavioral problems because firms simultaneously exploit naive consumers while other firms struggle to sell help to those same consumers. The lecture also covers "sludges"—deliberate obstacles that harm people—and emphasizes that eliminating sludges can be as important as implementing nudges.

The course concludes by stressing that psychological considerations matter in economic choices, small changes can make big differences, and designing with behavioral insights in mind is valuable for personal decisions, helping others, and product design.

A new study funded by Boeing and published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences suggests that sitting in a window seat and not moving during a flight reduces the risk of catching cold or flu germs on airplanes. Researchers observed 10 flights, tested for 18 viruses, and found that 80% of aisle seat passengers moved during flights compared to 43% of window seat passengers. The study concluded that on average only one person per 150-passenger flight would be infected by a hypothetical sick passenger in an aisle seat. However, researchers observed only one coughing passenger and found no viruses, and outside experts noted the small sample size limits general conclusions. The study found that the 11 people closest to an infected passenger face the highest risk.

New research co-authored by a University of Calgary professor found that dinosaurs took significantly longer to hatch than previously thought. By studying fossilized embryos of Protoceratops and Hypacrosaurus, researchers determined incubation periods of nearly three months and six months respectively—much longer than birds' 11-85 days. This indicates dinosaur incubation resembled primitive reptiles rather than modern birds, suggesting birds evolved rapid incubation after diverging from other dinosaurs. The prolonged incubation exposed eggs and parents to extended risks from predators, starvation, and environmental disruptions. Combined with dinosaurs' slow maturation and high resource requirements, this disadvantage may help explain why non-avian dinosaurs went extinct while birds survived the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event. The study was conducted by Gregory Erickson, Darla Zelenitsky, Mark Norell, and David Kay.

The case follows a winding path: Trump issued the order on January 20, federal courts blocked it, and the administration first sought Supreme Court intervention in March only regarding universal injunctions. Andrew Sabo appealed his conviction for cocaine possession with intent to deliver and felon in possession of a firearm, arguing that evidence from a search warrant should be suppressed because the supporting affidavit lacked probable cause. He also sought a Franks-Mann hearing for alleged false statements in the affidavit and disclosure of the informant's identity. The Wisconsin Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's decisions, finding that the citizen informant's detailed observations about drug activity and firearms were sufficiently corroborated by police investigation to establish reliability and probable cause, that Sabo failed to make the required preliminary showing for a Franks-Mann hearing, and that the trial court properly exercised its discretion in denying disclosure of the informant's identity.

This application describes techniques for enhanced overlay network-based transport of IPsec traffic to and from customer branch office locations using an Internet-based overlay routing infrastructure. The method involves selecting an optimal ingress edge region through a multi-step DNS and IKEv2 redirect process. A customer router's DNS resolver queries an authoritative DNS to map a service hostname to an initial IKEv2 destination. Upon establishing an outer IPsec tunnel, the first overlay network edge performs a secondary DNS lookup to verify if it is the optimal ingress region. If not, it issues an IKEv2 redirect to a second, more appropriate edge region. Additional periodic lookups allow edges to drop liveness probes when they are no longer optimal, triggering routers to initiate new hostname lookups. This approach enables enterprises to utilize Internet links as an optimized, low-cost WAN alternative to expensive MPLS leased lines, providing built-in security and global reach for connecting branches, data centers, and mobile users to cloud applications.

The professor discusses exact solutions to nonlinear PDEs, focusing on Burgers' equation and the Korteweg-de Vries (KDV) equation. For the inviscid Burgers' equation with a delta function initial condition, the solution consists of a fan (where u = x/t) followed by a shock. The shock position is found to be X = √(2t) by conserving total mass, and this solution satisfies both the jump condition and entropy condition. The professor then presents a general exact solution formula involving minimization and explains its derivation from the viscous Burgers' equation via the Cole-Hopf transformation, which converts it to the heat equation. Taking the viscosity to zero yields the inviscid solution through a stationary phase argument. Finally, the KDV equation is discussed as an example of a completely integrable nonlinear PDE, where solitons emerge unchanged after interaction, leading to discoveries of other integrable equations including the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers may corrupt other PMC register writes due to a shadow register technique that updates registers at 32-bit granularity regardless of write size. The inactive byte lane retains previous data, enabling two corruption types: local (same register) and cross (unrelated register). ACPI allows WORD and BYTE accesses to PM1_STS, PM1_EN, PM1_CNT, and PM2_CNT, but these cause corruption; non-ACPI registers require DWORD-only access. Resolution involves setting up an SMI I/O trap for ACPI registers to control and prevent problematic accesses.

Astronomers observed a rogue planet, Cha 1170-7626, undergoing the fastest growth rate ever recorded for any planet. This paper presents NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end framework for reconstructing visual stimuli from fMRI data by directly conditioning latent diffusion models on brain activity, bypassing intermediate embedding spaces used in prior two-stage approaches. The Colorado Supreme Court reversed a trial court's denial of a protective order in a personal injury case, remanding for reconsideration under a proper balancing test. The Bond family sued YMCA after a child was injured, seeking damages including mental suffering and psychiatric expenses. YMCA sought discovery of the family's mental health therapy notes and records. The trial court denied the protective order, finding the defendants needed full access to defend against the damage claims. The Supreme Court held that while the plaintiffs waived physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges by placing their mental condition at issue, the trial court abused its discretion by failing to balance the plaintiffs' interest in confidentiality against YMCA's discovery needs under C.R.C.P. 26(c). The Court emphasized the compelling public policy protecting therapist-patient confidentiality to ensure effective mental health treatment, noting that disclosure could seriously undermine the plaintiffs' therapy. The Court directed the trial court on remand to utilize flexible protective order procedures, such as in camera review, to accommodate both parties' interests.

Earth's total solar eclipses occur due to a cosmic coincidence: the moon's diameter is about 400 times smaller than the sun's, but it is also about 400 times closer to Earth, making them appear the same size. This alignment allows the moon to completely block the sun and reveal its corona. In the past, the moon was closer and appeared larger; it is now moving away about 1.5 inches per year. In approximately 600 million years, the moon will be too small to fully cover the sun, ending total solar eclipses on Earth.

The Put-Call ratio is a sentiment indicator that divides put volume or open interest by call volume or open interest to gauge market trends. Backtests show the Put-Call ratio is not among the best sentiment indicators, with the VIX indicator performing better. The ratio is available on most trading platforms and exchange websites, though free downloadable sources are limited. This passage describes AI-based image encoding and decoding systems that use deep neural networks (DNNs) to achieve low bitrates. The AI decoding apparatus determines whether to perform AI up-scaling based on AI data verification and second DNN availability, outputting either the third image (after AI up-scaling) or the second image (potentially with legacy up-scaling). Hong Liu discusses the large N expansion of gauge theory and its mathematical correspondence with string theory scattering amplitudes, where 1/N corresponds to the string coupling. Feynman diagrams of genus-h can be viewed as triangulations of surfaces, suggesting gauge theory could be equivalent to string theory if diagram weights match a string action. However, this identification is difficult because Feynman diagrams are discrete and only resemble smooth surfaces at strong coupling, where calculations become intractable. Simpler systems like matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics admit explicit string theory descriptions, as shown in work from the late 1980s and early 1990s.

The lecture then explores why QCD cannot be described by a four-dimensional string theory: string theory requires 26 or 10 dimensions for consistency, and compactifying extra dimensions introduces unwanted massless spin-2 particles violating the Weinberg-Witten theorem. Holographic principle hints and string theory consistency suggest a five-dimensional description instead. For scale-invariant theories (CFTs), symmetry requirements fix the metric to anti-de Sitter (AdS) form, leading to the conclusion that a D-dimensional CFT corresponds to string theory in AdS_{D+1}.

The historical development is traced from 't Hooft's 1974 large N expansion, through Wilson's lattice QCD showing quark confinement via strings, 't Hooft's 1993 holographic principle, to Maldacena's 1997 discovery of explicit AdS/CFT correspondences using D-branes, with Witten later connecting this to holography.

This patent application describes methods and systems for driving light sources in near-eye displays (such as VR/AR/MR headsets) to improve power efficiency while maintaining user experience. The technique involves determining a maximum luminance location based on the user's field of view (typically at the center or foveal region), then driving light sources at varying luminance levels depending on their distance from this maximum luminance location. Light sources closer to the maximum luminance location emit at higher luminance levels, while those farther away emit at lower levels, since human eyes are less sensitive to peripheral vision. The system uses eye-tracking to dynamically adjust the maximum luminance location as the user's gaze changes. Different display zones can have different relationships between input display values and luminance levels, with the central zone having a larger luminance range. The light sources may include OLEDs or micro-LEDs, and power reductions of 5-40% may be achieved with minimal noticeable impact to users.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted Wednesday on rape and criminal sex act charges in Manhattan, marking the first criminal case from sexual misconduct allegations against the former film producer. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus R. Vance Jr. stated the indictment advances accountability. Weinstein's lawyers said he declined to testify before the grand jury due to insufficient preparation time and "political pressure" making indictment unavoidable. This manual provides instructions for installing a SanDisk SSD in notebook and desktop computers. For desktops: power off and disconnect power, open case, unplug SATA cables from existing HDD, remove drive, install SSD into 3.5-inch mounting adapter if needed, connect SATA cables, close case, and power on. The Leapfrog Hospital Safety Grade reports significant improvements in patient safety, with five hospitals improving from "F" to "A" grades this spring and 46 achieving "A" grades for the first time since the program began six years ago. States including Rhode Island, Hawaii, Wisconsin, and Idaho have moved from near-bottom rankings to top ten in percentage of "A" hospitals. The PGA848 has a linear operating input voltage range within 3V of either power supply with excellent common-mode rejection. A typical application involves driving a 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC (ADS8860) using ±15V input supplies and 5.3V output supply, with the REF pin set to 2.5V midscale using a precision voltage divider and OPA192 buffer. The circuit includes three filters: an input EMI/RFI filter, a 318kHz feedback filter (CFB = 75pF), and a charge reservoir filter at the ADC inputs. Layout guidelines emphasize symmetrical input paths, bypass capacitors, trace separation, and minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance. Supply voltages exceeding ±20V permanently damage the device.

Steven Kean forwarded news articles to John Hardy on March 7, 2001, regarding Enron's involvement in lobbying efforts to protect the Export-Import Bank from proposed 25% budget cuts by the Bush administration. Major exporters including Enron, Boeing, Caterpillar, and Halliburton launched an aggressive Capitol Hill campaign, planning to mobilize 100,000 smaller suppliers to create congressional support. The articles also covered: Century Development's new Houston office tower with Reliant Resources; growing Dutch gas competition and Enron Europe's trading activity; delays in California's power deals and lawsuits involving Enron Wind; Sierra Pacific's doubts about SEC approval for its $3.1 billion acquisition of Enron's Portland General Electric; and falling U.S. natural gas prices with completion of work on Enron's Transwestern pipeline.

This study examined the impact of BCHE-K carrier status on age-at-diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) in APOE4 carriers among 45 patients aged 50-74 with CSF biomarker-confirmed mild AD. In APOE4 carriers (N=33), BCHE-K carriers (n=11) had a mean age-at-diagnosis 6.4 years earlier than noncarriers (n=22, P<.001). No similar effect was observed in APOE4 noncarriers. BCHE-K carriers showed slightly higher amyloid and tau accumulations despite younger age-at-baseline. APOE4 homozygotes with BCHE-K exhibited a predominant amyloid, limited tau pathophysiology, and limbic-amnestic phenotype. Multiple regression analyses showed amyloid accumulation associated with APOE4 carrier status, larger ventricle volume, less synaptic injury, and less tau, while tau pathophysiology associated with more neuroaxonal damage, synaptic injury, and glial activation. The authors conclude that in mild AD patients under 75, BCHE-K reduces age-at-diagnosis by over 6 years in APOE4 carriers, with functional glial activation explaining much of the phenotypic effects.

In 2017, British exam board OCR confused the Capulet and Montague families in a Romeo and Juliet exam question given to over 14,000 students. The error, which asked how Tybalt's hatred of the Capulets influenced the play's outcome when he actually hated the Montagues, led Britain's exam regulator Ofqual to fine OCR a record £175,000. Ofqual stated the mistake made the exam "not fit for purpose" and harmed public confidence in qualifications. Nearly 2,735 students received grades based on other exam sections, and OCR is not expected to contest the penalty.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture focuses on structures for implementing finite impulse response (FIR) digital filters. The instructor reviews that FIR systems have impulse responses with finite nonzero samples and difference equations corresponding to convolution sums. Standard structures like direct form, transposed form, and cascade form apply to FIR systems, though parallel form structures are generally not possible due to the absence of poles.

The lecture then covers two FIR-specific structures. First, linear phase FIR systems exploit symmetry in their impulse responses (h[n] = h[N-1-n]) to reduce multiplications by half. For even-length systems, this combines delayed input pairs before multiplication by coefficients. Second, frequency sampling structures implement FIR systems using DFT coefficients H[k] as multipliers in a parallel bank of first-order sections with poles that cancel zeros from a common 1-z^(-N) term. This offers advantages when many frequency samples are zero and enables hardware sharing across filter banks.

The lecture concludes by comparing filter structures based on delays, multiplications, modularity, and finite register length effects. Coefficient quantization sensitivity increases with polynomial order, making direct forms most sensitive and cascade/parallel forms preferable. For second-order sections, direct form quantizes r² and 2r cos θ, while coupled form quantizes r cos θ and r sin θ, yielding different realizable pole position grids.

A bronze sculpture titled "The Last Three" has been unveiled in New York City as a memorial to Africa's last three Northern White Rhinos. The 5m-high artwork depicts the closely-related zoo survivors moved to Kenya's Ol Pejeta sanctuary in 2009 in a failed effort to save the sub-species, now extinct in the wild. Art critic Jerry Saltz called it a "kitsch monstrosity," sparking social media debate, while others defended the artists' awareness-raising goals. The Northern White Rhino once lived across central Africa but was wiped out by poachers by 2012.

This document contains legal and public notices for Smith County, Tennessee, dated May 31, 2018. Notices include: two vehicle possession announcements (2000 Chevy Silverado, 1999 Suzuki); two estate land sales (Alfred Gene Stewart Jr. estate—2.67 acres auctioned June 23, 2018; Betty Rose Drake estate—1.8 acres at 72 Riddleton Circle auctioned June 9, 2018); three notices to creditors (estates of Leon Dewayne Barnes, Nellie Belle Hunter, and Sarah Kaye Stallings); two trustee's sales for defaulted properties (217 College Avenue East on June 13, 2018; 9 Hills Dale Lane East on June 21, 2018); a court order for service by publication in an adoption/termination of parental rights case regarding Jason Rodgers; and a notice to Danny Lee Brown regarding a dependency and neglect petition. The document also references links to the Town of Gordonsville budget and South Side Utility District water reports for three districts.

Ultralight backpacking, defined as a base weight of 10 pounds or less, originated from Mark Jenkins' 1994 article about traveling through Europe and Africa with minimal gear. The movement began with DIY gear but has grown mainstream. To achieve ultralight weight, hikers should first eliminate unnecessary items by evaluating whether each item is truly needed for warmth, comfort, food, or safety. The three heaviest gear categories are shelter, sleep system, and backpack. Experimentation helps identify personal needs, such as using quilts instead of sleeping bags or cowboy camping. Ultralight backpacking is ultimately a philosophy of minimizing obstacles to enjoying the backcountry experience rather than strictly meeting a weight limit.

This study analyzed US vital statistics data from 2014-2020 to examine the relationship between cancer and COVID-19 mortality. While observational studies have produced conflicting results on cancer as a COVID-19 risk factor, this population-level analysis found only modest excess cancer mortality during the pandemic. Nationally, multiple-cause cancer mortality increased by 2% (12,000 excess deaths), with hematological cancers showing the largest increase at 5%. In contrast, diabetes and Alzheimer's showed much larger elevations (39% and 31% respectively). The authors developed a demographic model projecting excess mortality under the null hypothesis that cancer itself is not a risk factor, finding that age distribution, population size, and baseline mortality risk largely explain observed patterns. The modest cancer mortality elevation reflects competing risks—patients with deadly cancers like pancreatic and lung cancer face high baseline mortality that predominates over COVID-19 risk. The study rules out the "immune incompetence rescue hypothesis," as hematological cancers showed the highest excess mortality rather than protection. The authors conclude that lack of excess cancer mortality reflects competing mortality risks rather than immunosuppression protection, and suggest future research focus on hospitalizations, Long COVID, and screening changes rather than mortality alone.

A study of 105 RSV specimens from Massachusetts General Hospital found that the severe autumn 2022 RSV surge in the United States was driven by multiple pre-existing viral lineages of RSV-A (91%) and RSV-B (9%), with many lineages shared between Massachusetts and Washington state. Genomic analysis showed no evidence of a single highly transmissible variant; instead, RSV-A genomes belonged to at least 10 distinct lineages with common ancestors dating to 2014-2017, and RSV-B genomes to approximately 2019. The genetic divergence rates were consistent with historical patterns, unlike the accelerated evolution seen in SARS-CoV-2 variants. The findings suggest non-viral factors, such as altered population immunity from pandemic-related suppression of RSV circulation, may explain the surge.

The Cape Horn Pigeon, an American whaling vessel, was seized by Russian authorities in 1893 while on the high seas 125 miles from Russian territory. Though Russia claimed the vessel had entered territorial waters, no evidence supported this finding, and Russia ultimately acknowledged the seizure resulted from a misunderstanding, returning the vessel without confiscation. The owners claimed $45,000 in damages for lost whaling profits, calculated by averaging previous voyages' catches. International law supports compensation for such unlawful seizures, as established in precedents including the 1795 Neptune case and the British detention of the American vessel Betsey.

Ben Affleck was seen looking upbeat at what is believed to be an outpatient treatment centre in LA, seven months after announcing he sought help for alcohol addiction. The 45-year-old actor, who completed a rehab stint in March, was photographed smiling while wearing grey sweatpants, a tee and black hoodie. An onlooker described him as "happy" and "refreshed." In his March statement, Affleck called rehab "the first of many steps" and expressed gratitude for support from family, friends, and ex-wife Jennifer Garner, with whom he shares three children.

Environmental education (EE) is an interdisciplinary approach fostering environmental awareness, values, and responsible behavior. Originating in 1947 and formalized through UNESCO's 1975 Belgrade Charter, EE aims to develop knowledge, skills, attitudes, and participation to prevent and solve environmental problems. Key principles include lifelong learning, interdisciplinary approaches, and global perspectives with regional considerations. EE objectives encompass awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, participation, and evaluation ability.

The environment comprises natural (biotic and abiotic) and human-made (physical and social) elements with seven distinctive properties: uniqueness, interdependence, dependence on other elements, ecosystem integration, chain reactions, varied resilience, and temporal changes. Environmental knowledge is categorized into natural resources, social environment, environmental technology, and waste/pollution.

Sustainable development, defined by the 1987 Brundtland Report as meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own needs, requires balancing economic growth, fair income distribution, and quality of life. The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals emphasize environmental sustainability as foundational to social and economic stability.

Achieving sustainable environmental development requires reducing energy consumption, minimizing waste, conserving natural resources, and utilizing clean technologies. Environmental management employs scientific principles and tools like ISO 14000 standards. Successful examples include Mahidol University's Collaborative Learning Project and Thailand's Huai Sai Royal Initiative Project, demonstrating how EE transforms individual and community behavior toward sustainable outcomes.

Interdisciplinary music education integrates music with fields like mathematics, language, psychology, and cognitive sciences to enhance learning. Research shows benefits for cognitive development, problem-solving, language acquisition, and emotional-social skills. The study uses a qualitative case study approach, interviewing one social studies teacher in a Fine Arts Faculty music department. Findings reveal insufficient basic music education at primary levels in Turkey and recommend preparatory classes, practical courses (creative drama, material design, speech training), and instruments like guitar and ukulele. The participant noted professors assume prior knowledge, inadequate presentation work, and lack of workshop spaces. Suggestions include micro-teaching, learning style assessments, and interdisciplinary curricula connecting music with history, geography, and technology through STEAM approaches.

Russia has cultivated relationships with Western far-right activists since Soviet times, a practice examined in Anton Shekhovtsov's book "Tango Noir: Russia and the Western Far Right." The Kremlin uses these activists to promote narratives of Western chaos and Russian power through three main tactics: "nudge propaganda" using fringe figures, "narrative laundering" of fake news, and selective sourcing. This strategy intensified after 2008 when Russia adopted full-scale information warfare following its Georgia invasion. Shekhovtsov identifies six "operator" nodes in Putin's power structure that coordinate these efforts, including foreign sympathizers, think tanks, oligarchs, and diplomatic missions. While Kremlin interventions in France backfired, Russia saw some success in Germany. Despite evolving tactics, Russia remains globally unpopular with sanctions intact and US relations unimproved. The author warns of emerging Russian paramilitary support for European far-right violence as a potentially more potent disruptive weapon.

Foreigners entered a military bivouac despite warnings from sentinels and Lieutenant Gato, behaving heedlessly until led out by a guide. K. Otori, Japanese minister, wrote to British Consul-General C.T. Gardner demanding contradiction of a telegram claiming Otori demanded dismissal of naval instructor Mr. Collwell from Korea, expressing regret at Gardner's hasty action without consultation. Gardner replied that Otori should apply through usual channels for information. The U.S. Government, through Mr. Gresham, received requests from Korea's minister for intervention to protect Korean independence threatened by Japanese and Chinese troops. Despite Korea's appeals for U.S. mediation and a conference of neutral powers, the U.S. maintained impartial neutrality, declining joint intervention while offering only friendly influence with Japan.

This study explored the readiness, expertise, and needs of 124 students in the Faculty of Industrial Education regarding educational multimedia creation. Using a descriptive research design with surveys and interviews, researchers found students had high overall expertise (mean 3.51) but expressed highest need for learning materials (mean 4.62). Students showed high expertise in presentation and infographic creation but low need for additional training in these areas. Conversely, they demonstrated low expertise in copyright and metaverse creation with high need for learning materials in these topics. The most commonly used devices were notebooks (93.3%) and smartphones (88.9%). Findings indicate students require targeted support in emerging technologies and legal aspects of multimedia, while being more confident in traditional content creation. Limitations include small sample size and limited population diversity.
