Nabors Industries' divestment of Quail Tools is paying off: the sale exceeded the purchase price and proceeds will reduce debt by 25%. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia, Nabors' key markets, appear to be at cyclical troughs. Nabors' stock has risen 70% from recent lows but remains below historical valuations. The author, a financial blogger bullish on oil and gas, may initiate a long position in Nabors within 72 hours.

This passage describes two native assembler procedures for processor initialization. The first procedure, AMD_ENABLE_STACK, initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region before main memory is available. It divides the stack among processor cores, maps them to global address space, sets MTRRs, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. It handles both protected mode and real mode configurations, destroys specific registers, and returns status codes indicating success, warning (stack reentry), or fatal error (unknown processor family). The second procedure, AMD_DISABLE_STACK, removes the pre-memory stack and returns the system to a non-stack-enabled state when main memory becomes available, disabling CAR mode without modifying MTRR settings. Both procedures must run on all processor cores and use register passing models.

Florida International University reopened March 19, 2018, four days after a pedestrian bridge collapse killed six people. The university held a moment of silence at 1:47 p.m. marking when the bridge fell. President Mark B. Rosenberg named the victims, including student Alexa Duran, and said the school is cooperating with investigators. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue extracted a fourth car Saturday night; five bodies were removed from the scene and one victim died at the hospital. National Transportation Safety Board investigators remained on site. Southwest Eighth Street was closed indefinitely. The student government planned a Wednesday vigil for the victims.

Caroline Hope, a 37-year-old English teacher who contracted E.coli during surgery for advanced colon cancer in Turkey, has died at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital in Glasgow. She had been living in Turkey for four years and was medically evacuated back to the UK last month after her family raised over £31,000 through crowdfunding, as strict repatriation rules prevented standard medical evacuation. Her mother confirmed the death and thanked donors and hospital staff.

The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) awards diamond certification to songs that have sold at least 10 million equivalent units through sales and streaming, a status established in 1999. As of September 2025, 179 songs have received this certification. Elton John's "Something About The Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind" was the first diamond-certified song in 1997. Drake holds the record for most diamond singles with 10, followed by Post Malone with nine. Rihanna leads female artists with seven diamond singles. Other artists with multiple diamond certifications include The Weeknd, Bruno Mars, Katy Perry, and Eminem. The most recent song to receive diamond certification is "A Bar Song (Tipsy)" by Shaboozey in September 2025.

Shaun Dion Hamilton first noticed Christian Kirk at The Opening in 2013, when Kirk was a rising junior and already one of their team's best players. Now Kirk is arguably Texas A&M's best player and a major challenge for Alabama, which enters Saturday's game as a 26 1/2-point favorite. Nick Saban has called Kirk probably the best all-purpose player in the SEC, dangerous as both a wide receiver and returner. In two games against Alabama, Kirk has 16 catches for 148 yards and a touchdown, plus a 68-yard punt return touchdown in 2015 and a 25-yard touchdown catch in 2016. This season, Kirk is tied for the SEC lead with four touchdown catches and has returned a kickoff for a touchdown. Alabama players emphasize the need to know where Kirk is on the field and make tackles, as he creates explosive plays by making defenders miss.

North Carolina's Department of Health and Human Services set a health goal of 140 parts per trillion for GenX in water supplies, representing the concentration at which no adverse non-cancer health effects are anticipated. According to toxicologist Dr. Susanne Brander of UNC-Wilmington, these non-cancer effects include endocrine disruption, thyroid disease, and reproductive effects. Limited research exists on cancer associations. A GenX forum featuring Erin Brockovich and Robert Bowcock will be held August 16th at 6:30 PM at UNCW's Lumina Theater.

Hong Kong and Singapore have become popular destinations for initial coin offerings (ICOs) following bans in China and South Korea. Neither city currently has specific ICO regulations, attracting companies seeking favorable environments. After China's September 2017 ban defined ICOs as illegal fundraising, many Chinese issuers relocated to these cities. South Korea's simultaneous ban also drove local companies to seek alternatives through overseas subsidiaries. Bithumb, a major South Korean exchange, plans to launch its ICO through a Singaporean corporation. Industry experts note significant growth in ICO activity in both locations since September 2017.

The Trump administration has cut services for multilingual learners in K-12 schools, including professional development, newcomer centers, and English learner teacher hiring. The Education Department's Office of English Language Acquisition has been reduced to three staff members, and the 2026 budget proposes eliminating all funding for these programs. Oklahoma faces losing $6.4 million and Virginia $17.5 million, affecting tutoring, translation services, and family engagement. Teachers report students avoiding services due to fear of deportation, with some declining to answer questions about their backgrounds. Newcomer center enrollment has dropped sharply; one Texas district consolidated nine centers into one, reassigning most teachers. Educators note reduced professional development opportunities and suspended adult ESL classes. Harvard professor Gabrielle Oliveira states that program cuts and staff losses represent lost opportunities for immigrant children, while advocates warn that reduced federal oversight leaves states to self-monitor legal obligations to educate these students.

Apple Inc. filed its Q1 2020 Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The company reported total net sales of $91.819 billion, up 9% from $84.310 billion in Q1 2019, with net income of $22.236 billion compared to $19.965 billion. Products sales were $79.104 billion and Services sales were $12.715 billion. iPhone sales increased 8% to $55.957 billion, while Mac sales decreased 3% to $7.160 billion and iPad sales decreased 11% to $5.977 billion. Wearables, Home and Accessories sales grew 37% to $10.010 billion, and Services sales grew 17% to $12.715 billion.

Geographically, Americas net sales increased 12% to $41.367 billion, Europe increased 14% to $23.273 billion, Greater China increased 3% to $13.578 billion, Japan decreased 10% to $6.223 billion, and Rest of Asia Pacific increased 6% to $7.378 billion. Gross margin was $35.217 billion (38.4% of net sales), up from $32.031 billion (38.0%) in Q1 2019.

Total assets were $340.618 billion, with cash and cash equivalents of $39.771 billion and marketable securities of $167.290 billion. Total liabilities were $251.087 billion, including $103.302 billion in term debt. Shareholders' equity was $89.531 billion. The company repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.5 billion in dividends during the quarter.

The company adopted new accounting standards for leases (ASU 2016-02) and hedging (ASU 2017-12), recording $7.5 billion in right-of-use assets and $8.1 billion in lease liabilities. The European Commission's State Aid Decision required Ireland to recover €12.9 billion plus interest from Apple, which remains in escrow pending appeals.

A record-setting 8-hour-13-minute Russian spacewalk ended with a communications antenna positioned 180 degrees from its intended orientation outside the International Space Station on Friday. Commander Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov had replaced an electronics box to upgrade the antenna, but it became hung up and required manual pushing and remote commanding to partially extend. NASA confirmed the antenna remained functional despite the misalignment, while Russian officials convened to assess further action. The spacewalk surpassed the previous Russian record of 8 hours 7 minutes set in 2013. Misurkin discarded the 60-pound obsolete electronics box, launched in 2000, which will burn up in the atmosphere. Misurkin is scheduled to return to Earth at month's end.

This manual provides instructions for installing a SanDisk SSD. If the SSD isn't recognized, remove other USB devices. The cloning process involves running data cloning software, selecting the source drive (usually "IDE") and destination drive, then beginning the cloning. For notebook installation: power off, disconnect power and remove battery, remove brackets from the old HDD and attach to the SSD, align connector pins with the SATA connector, replace the drive bay, then reconnect battery and power. For desktop installation: power off and disconnect, open the case, unplug SATA cables from the existing HDD, install the SSD into a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if needed, connect SATA cables, then close the case and power on. The old HDD can be kept as a backup.

Bills quarterback Josh Allen praised running back James Cook as an "all-time teammate" after Cook signed a $48 million contract. Cook has 401 rushing yards and five touchdowns through four games, with 100+ yards in his last three games. Allen believes the new contract freed Cook to play more loosely. The 4-0 Bills host the Patriots in Week 5, seeking a 3-0 division record.

New research from Yale's Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no evidence of "discernible disruption" to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT's launch in November 2022, with occupational shifts largely beginning before 2021. While entry-level workers face hiring challenges, researchers attribute this to broader labor market dynamics rather than direct AI effects. Some companies like Shopify and Cloudflare are increasing intern hiring, viewing AI as augmenting rather than replacing junior roles. However, 72% of S&P 500 companies now disclose AI-related risks, up from 12% in 2023, with reputational and cybersecurity concerns leading. Meta announced it will use AI chatbot conversations to personalize ads starting December 2025, without opt-out options. OpenAI launched Sora 2, a video generation model requiring copyright holders to opt out of training data. Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker, a tool for custom AI model creation, while new startup Periodic Labs raised $300 million to build AI for scientific discovery.

The passage details six SOS defensive strategies for disrupting low post offenses in basketball. Post Fronting is the primary method, where the defender positions themselves between the post player and the ball to deflect passes. Base Go is the main double-team option, triggered when the post is moved off the block or on a coach's call. Go Top is a secondary trap used when posts turn to the middle for shots. Go Wing deploys when the wing is a poor outside shooter. Hold prevents open three-pointers by having four defenders stay home on kick-out passes. Yo-Yo allows a defender to sag off a non-shooting wing to double-team the post while teammates deny passes. Each strategy includes specific player rotations for lob passes, pass-outs, skip passes, and final matchups, with all rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

The Gold Overnight Trading Strategy involves buying gold futures, GLD, or gold miners ETFs (GDX/GDXJ) at market close and selling at the next open to capture overnight price movements driven by global market changes. Backtests show GDX averages 0.12% daily gains overnight versus 0.09% losses intraday, while GLD shows 8.4% annual returns from overnight trading versus minimal intraday gains. The strategy carries high risk due to gold's volatility and sensitivity to economic and geopolitical factors. The authors note commodities are harder to trade than stocks, with strategies often degrading over time. They are testing refined versions including one long strategy with 0.17% average gain (0.11% since 2012) and a short strategy with 0.7% average gain. Successful implementation requires disciplined risk management, psychological control, and clear entry/exit plans.

This 1894 Foreign Relations of the United States volume contains presidential messages and State Department correspondence regarding U.S.-Hawaiian relations. Document 1 (February 6, 1893) transmits a draft of an uncompleted 1854 treaty with Hawaii. Document 2 (February 16, 1893) transmits a report covering U.S.-Hawaiian relations from September 1820 to January 1893, prepared by Andrew H. Allen of the State Department's Bureau of Rolls and Library.

Email dated November 5, 2001, containing news articles about Enron's financial troubles, including: a $35 million March 2001 transaction between Enron and Chewco Investments LP run by former executive Michael Kopper; SEC investigation into off-balance-sheet partnerships involving CFO Andrew Fastow; short seller James Chanos identifying red flags in Enron's financial reports; Arthur Andersen facing scrutiny over audit clarity; AFL-CIO and union funds demanding corporate governance reforms; potential asset sales to address credit crunch; and disputes over Enron's India and Korea operations.

The passage details U.S.-Hawaiian diplomatic relations from 1881-1892, including Secretary Blaine's 1881 instructions regarding treaty violations and American interests in Hawaiian neutrality; the 1883 U.S. refusal to join Hawaiian protests against British and French expansion in Polynesia; the 1884 reciprocity treaty renewal granting the U.S. exclusive rights to Pearl Harbor as a coaling station, ratified in 1887; General Schofield's 1873 recommendation for acquiring Pearl Harbor; and cable connection proposals between Hawaii, Australia, and North America, including a British-protested 1884 Hawaiian subsidy act and an 1891-92 U.S. survey.

The American Stroke Association developed the FAST acronym to identify stroke symptoms and urge rapid action. F stands for Face drooping (one side sagging or numb), A for Arm weakness (inability to raise both arms), S for Speech difficulty (slurred or hard to understand), and T for Time to call 911. A similar mnemonic, STR, uses Smile, Talk, and Raise both arms. Symptoms require immediate emergency response even if temporary.

Sara Zaske's daughter Sophia only wanted a phone after moving from Germany to California, where she became the only fourth-grader without a smartphone. In Germany, only 51% of children 6-13 own mobile phones, with most having basic flip phones. Across Europe, 46% of children 9-16 own smartphones, with usage varying by country and economic factors. US children receive phones earlier: 45% of 10-12 year-olds have smartphones with service plans, and 42% of children 8 and under own tablets. In South Korea, 72% of 11-12 year-olds own smartphones, while in Taiwan usage rises from 45% at age 11 to 71% at age 15. Turkey shows no parental consensus on optimal phone age. South Africa has 81% mobile phone access among secondary students, while Ghana and Malawi show lower ownership with gender disparities. Australian children typically receive phones at median age 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics states no "right" age exists, recommending limited screen time for young children and parental monitoring regardless of age.

The author, who previously made a film about cryonics with skepticism, discusses the recent cryopreservation of a British teenager and the history of cryonics since Robert Ettinger's 1964 theory. Despite 2,000 people paying for the service and celebrity interest, the author argues no scientist believes revival is possible, calling cryonics firms "morbid confidence tricksters" who exploit death fears and rob death of dignity.

The passage identifies the top five best-performing stock markets since 1900 as Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, and Denmark, based on Credit Suisse data. Australia's ASX leads with over 6.5% annual real returns in USD, attributed to dividends (53% of gains), commodity exports, strong banking, low corruption, and minimal WWII damage. The U.S. market delivered 6.5% real annualized returns, with $1 invested in 1900 growing to $3,806 by 2019. South Africa averaged 7.2% returns (6.4% in USD), benefiting from natural resources and economic diversification. New Zealand achieved 6.4% annualized returns. Denmark ranked fifth despite an 80-year bear market (1898-1980), with strong performance only in the last 35 years. Globally, stocks outperformed bonds (5.2% vs. 2% real returns) and Treasury bills (0.8%) from 1900-2019. Key advantages of stock investing include inflation protection, dividend income, ownership, liquidity, diversification, and accessibility. However, past performance doesn't guarantee future results, as demonstrated by markets like Russia (closed 1917-1991) and Germany (devastated by wars and inflation). A 2017 study found that only a small fraction of stocks drive overall market gains, making stock picking difficult.

In South Louisiana, Beignet the Nutria serves as a local alternative to Punxsutawney Phil for weather predictions on February 2, which is both Groundhog Day and World Wetlands Day. Jonathan Foret, Executive Director of the South Louisiana Wetlands Discovery Center, raised the wild nutria from infancy and obtained a special permit to keep him as an educational mascot about invasive species. This year, Beignet did not see his shadow, predicting a mild hurricane season with no hurricanes, while Punxsutawney Phil predicted six more weeks of winter.

Robin Chase, co-founder of Zipcar, discovered in October 2000 that her car-sharing company's revenue was half of projections, with car utilization at 22% rather than the estimated 40%. Despite positive press and growing membership since its June 2000 launch, the business model was failing. Chase, who had developed quantitative skills at MIT Sloan and built Zipcar using Internet and wireless technology to differentiate it from failed predecessors, faced a critical decision three weeks before closing $1.3 million in funding and two weeks before moving to official offices. After analyzing the data, she determined that daily rates needed to increase 20% to break even, though this risked customer backlash and violated pricing promises to early members who had already paid deposits and sold their cars.

The passage outlines U.S. policy positions on post-World War I territorial settlements. Regarding Alsace-Lorraine, the U.S. supports France's recovery of the provinces as essential to French recovery and German demilitarization, but will not fight longer than France is willing. For Italy, the U.S. supports boundary rectifications based on defensive and nationalist considerations, commercial freedom for Trieste, and cultural autonomy for its inhabitants, while rejecting Italian ambitions on the eastern Adriatic. For the Balkans, the U.S. rejects the Treaty of Bucharest, calls for evacuation by Central Powers, restoration of Serbia and Montenegro, and settlements based on balanced nationalistic and economic considerations through impartial inquiry, with specific territorial recommendations including return of Dobrudja to Bulgaria and Aegean coast access for Bulgaria. For Poland, the U.S. supports an independent democratic state with sea access, though complete unification is impractical; boundaries should balance national and economic factors, with democratic governance essential to prevent internal friction among Poles, Ruthenians, and Jews.

Montreal has been named the world's best city for students in the QS Best Student Cities 2017 rankings, displacing Paris which held the top spot for four years. The ranking considers factors including university quality, affordability, desirability, and safety. Canada is gaining popularity as an alternative to traditional study destinations like the US and UK, with Montreal, Vancouver (10th), and Toronto (11th) all ranking highly. London rose to third place despite Brexit concerns, while Paris dropped to second due to cost and desirability factors. Germany is the only other country besides Canada with two cities in the top 10 (Berlin and Munich), benefiting from free tuition. Asian cities are increasingly attractive, with Seoul ranking fourth and five Asian cities in the top 20. The international student market is lucrative, contributing an estimated $36 billion annually to the US economy alone.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air Lines headquarters over suspected embezzlement and breach of trust by the owning family, Yonhap reported. The investigation follows increased scrutiny of the family after Cho Hyun-min allegedly threw water at a meeting attendee in April; her sister Heather Cho was jailed in 2014 for a plane return incident over nut service. The Seoul Southern District Prosecutors' Office is investigating Chairman Cho Yang-ho and family members for tax evasion, embezzlement, and breach of trust, including potential unpaid taxes on inherited overseas assets and suspicious money flows. Chairman Cho recently stepped down as co-CEO of affiliate Jin Air amid public pressure.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers use a transconductance error amplifier with 1800 µA/V transconductance and 10,000 V/V DC gain, comparing VSENSE to the lower of SS pin voltage or 0.613-V reference. Output voltage is set via resistor divider to 0.613 V. Soft-start uses a capacitor to gradually increase output voltage until SS exceeds VREF, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating at 1 V.

Three switching frequency modes exist: internal oscillator (RT resistor, 100 kHz–2 MHz), external synchronization (floating RT, 200 kHz–4 MHz clock at SYNC), and primary-secondary (two controllers synchronized via SYNC). Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) have ~150 mA peak current capability.

Dead times (TDSP/TDPS) are programmable via PS/SP resistors (10–300 kΩ), with 8 ns minimum if floating. Leading edge blank time is programmable via LEB resistor (10–300 kΩ minimum). Pulse skipping occurs when COMP < 0.3 V and previous duty cycle < 25%. Duty cycle limits are 50% (DCL to AVSS), 75% (floating), or 100% (DCL to VLDO), with only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP supporting 50%.

Peak current mode control uses CS_ILIM with 1.05 V overcurrent threshold, triggering hiccup mode with programmable delay via CHICC capacitor. External fault protection triggers at 0.6 V with 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width. Slope compensation is set via RSC resistor to prevent subharmonic oscillation. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks at COMP pin. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C, resuming at 160°C.

The controllers operate from 4–14 V input with 0.1 µF minimum bypass capacitance. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt loops, and routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes.

Between 62% and 82% of retail CFD traders lose money, according to broker statistics. The high failure rate stems from factors including lack of trading plans, insufficient knowledge, illiquidity, hidden fees, leverage risks, and the zero-sum nature of CFDs. While some disciplined traders profit through risk management and proven strategies, most retail traders face stacked odds due to amplified losses from leverage, widening spreads during volatility, and undercapitalization. Professional traders rarely use CFDs, and the majority of retail participants lack proper planning and market understanding.

This patent application describes systems and methods for change block tracking (CBT) to enable incremental and differential backups in cloud computing environments that do not natively support CBT functionality. The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/721,644, filed December 19, 2019.

The background explains that businesses need reliable data protection while minimizing productivity impact, with challenges including rapidly expanding data volumes and frequent data modifications requiring frequent backups. Traditional incremental backup by comparing all disk blocks is processor and time intensive.

The summary identifies that certain cloud architectures like OpenStack lack native CBT support or API functionality to enable CBT, preventing efficient incremental/differential backups. The disclosed solution enables CBT in such environments by generating virtual machine disk images at different times, comparing them to identify changed blocks, creating a map of changed block locations, and using this map at a virtual server agent to extract and back up only changed blocks. This allows differential or incremental backups in cloud systems without native CBT support and provides data in formats compatible with the information management system rather than hypervisor-specific formats.

The detailed description covers an information management system architecture including storage managers, data agents, media agents, primary and secondary storage devices, and various information management operations such as backup, archive, snapshot, replication, deduplication, and hierarchical storage management.

This study analyzes SARS-CoV-2 genomic evolution in Rio Grande do Sul (RS), Brazil. Twelve respiratory samples collected from Esteio between April-June 2021 were sequenced, revealing 68 nucleotide substitutions, with 10 belonging to P.1 lineage and 2 to P.1.17 sublineage (Gamma variant). Analysis of 4,706 RS sequences from March 2020-May 2022 showed lineage succession: B.1.1.33 dominated 2020, followed by Zeta, then Gamma (57.1% of 2021 sequences), Delta (32.3%), and Omicron (>90% from January-April 2022). Phylogenomic analysis confirmed monophyletic groups for Alpha, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron. Molecular evolution analysis of structural proteins E, M, and N found no positive selection in E protein, 2 adaptive sites in M protein, and 14 in N protein. Stability analysis using DynaMut2 showed most M protein mutations stabilized structure, while N protein mutations mostly destabilized it. The study highlights the importance of E, M, and N proteins in viral assembly and pathogenesis beyond spike protein characterization.

This study protocol describes a three-arm randomized controlled trial examining the effectiveness of a digital mindfulness psychoeducation programme (Digital-MindCAN) for cancer survivors in Singapore. The programme combines cancer-specific knowledge with mindfulness principles and practice, delivered via real-time videotelephony. Eligible participants are adults aged 21-65 who completed curative cancer treatments 2 weeks to 2 years prior. The 150 participants will be randomly assigned to: Digital-MindCAN with standard care, Palouse Mindfulness (general MBSR) with standard care, or wait-list control. Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress; secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, perceived relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety. Data collection involves self-administered questionnaires, physiological measures (skin temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation), and focus group interviews. Quantitative analysis will use ANCOVA and repeated measures ANOVA; qualitative analysis will employ realist evaluation. The study addresses gaps in existing mindfulness interventions by incorporating cancer-specific content, using objective stress measures, and including qualitative assessment. Positive findings could inform clinical practice by supporting Digital-MindCAN as part of standard care for cancer survivors.

This study examines preschool teachers' views on sensory education and classroom practices using phenomenological design with 20 teachers selected through maximum diversity sampling. Three main themes emerged: importance of sensory education, relationship with preschool education program, and difficulties/limitations. All teachers emphasized sensory education's importance for child development across all developmental areas, though most only identified five senses rather than seven. Teachers reported sensory education is insufficiently addressed in the 2013 preschool program, despite being implicitly present in outcomes and indicators. Classroom practices included visual, auditory, tactile, music-rhythm, art, and experiment activities, evaluated through observation and development forms. Family involvement occurred through seminars, interviews, and home activities. Major limitations included inadequate physical facilities, insufficient materials, and teachers' need for training. Teachers expressed confusion between "sense" and "emotion" and desired professional development in sensory integration. Recommendations include in-service training, interdisciplinary occupational therapist support, improved classroom materials, enhanced undergraduate education, and collaborative activity development.

Stanford researchers developed "biofilm lithography," a technique using light and genetically engineered E. coli bacteria to create intricate bacterial community patterns with 25-micrometer resolution. The bacteria secrete sticky proteins in response to blue light, allowing researchers to shape biofilm growth into designs like polka dots, stripes, and circuits. The method offers advantages over existing techniques in speed, simplicity, and compatibility with various surfaces including microfluidic devices. Applications include studying biofilm dynamics, developing novel biomaterials, creating conductive biofilm circuits, and understanding antibiotic resistance sharing in bacterial communities. The research was published March 19 in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The passage examines Russian higher education projects (HEPs) established in exile following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, analyzing how these initiatives conceptualize themselves and their relationship to their homeland. Drawing on "education in emergencies" frameworks, the study explores four HEPs varying in institutionalization—from informal online courses to accredited degree programs—through interviews with organizers and discourse analysis of promotional materials.

The research identifies three key narratives in HEPs' self-conceptualization. First, they serve as "safe havens" providing infrastructure and sanctuary for fleeing scholars and students, addressing gaps in international education frameworks for displaced academics. Second, they engage in "preservation and reconceptualisation," maintaining academic heritage and Russian-language scholarship while attempting limited reformulation of educational approaches, particularly through liberal arts models emphasizing critical thinking and democratic citizenship. Third, they practice "hope-making praxis," transforming passive anticipation of return into active engagement through concrete educational activities aimed at shaping Russia's future, despite uncertain prospects.

The study finds that while HEPs pragmatically focus on present possibilities rather than awaiting return, their reconceptualization of preserved practices remains incomplete, with some perpetuating hierarchical teaching methods and insufficiently examining colonial biases. The conclusion suggests further research on practice continuity, international influence, gaps between declared missions and everyday teaching, changing self-conceptualization over time, and HEPs' broader impact on international education landscapes.

This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of a nutritional supplementation intervention modeled on the RATIONS trial for reducing tuberculosis incidence and mortality among household contacts of persons with TB in India. Using a Markov state transition model with data from over 10,000 participants in eastern India, researchers compared usual care against an intervention providing macronutrient and micronutrient support costing $13 monthly for six months. The analysis projected that per 100,000 household contacts, the RATIONS intervention would reduce lifetime TB incidence from 7,718 to 6,749 cases and TB mortality from 1,529 to 906 deaths, averting 13,775 DALYs. From a healthcare perspective, the intervention cost $229 per DALY averted; from a societal perspective, $184 per DALY averted—both below India's willingness-to-pay threshold of $550. Sensitivity analyses showed the intervention remained cost-effective across wide parameter ranges, including when supplementation costs nearly doubled. The authors conclude that nutritional support is highly cost-effective for TB prevention in undernourished populations and suggest India could leverage existing food distribution infrastructure for implementation.

This MIT lecture introduces dynamic optimality in binary search trees (BSTs), asking whether one BST can perform as well as all others for any access sequence. The professor defines the BST model of computation, which allows walking pointers (left, right, parent) and rotations, with search cost measured by nodes touched.

Key properties discussed include: sequential access (constant amortized time for in-order access), dynamic finger (log k time where k is key distance from previous access), entropy (based on access frequency), working set (log of distinct keys accessed since last access to an item), and unified property (combining spatial and temporal locality). While splay trees satisfy most properties, their dynamic optimality remains unproven.

The lecture presents a geometric view of BST execution: access sequences map to points (time × key), and valid executions correspond to "arborally satisfied" point sets where every axis-aligned rectangle contains another point. This transforms the optimization problem into finding minimum satisfied supersets.

The greedy algorithm adds points row-by-row to satisfy empty rectangles, which appears offline in tree terms but online geometrically. Using split trees, this can be made truly online with O(log log n) competitiveness, the best known bound. Whether constant competitiveness (true dynamic optimality) is achievable remains open.

The lecture discusses finite temperature CFT on a sphere and its gravity dual description. Unlike flat space CFT where temperature provides the only scale, a sphere introduces a radius R, creating a dimensionless parameter RT that distinguishes low and high temperature physics.

For global AdS with spherical boundary, three Euclidean solutions exist: thermal AdS (thermal gas), small black hole, and big black hole. The small black hole behaves like flat space Schwarzschild black holes with negative specific heat and is never stable. The big black hole has positive specific heat. Thermal AdS has zero classical action (same as pure AdS), while black holes have actions proportional to N².

A first-order phase transition called the Hawking-Page transition occurs at critical temperature Tc = (d-1)/(2πR). Below Tc, thermal AdS dominates; above Tc, the big black hole dominates. The transition happens when black hole size equals AdS radius.

The field theory interpretation uses a toy model of N² free harmonic oscillators with SU(N) singlet constraint. Low energy states (order N⁰) have density of states independent of N, while high energy states (order N²) have exponentially large degeneracy (exp(N²)). At low temperature, only low energy states contribute; at high temperature, entropy overwhelms thermal suppression, causing the phase transition. This large N mechanism explains the Hawking-Page transition generically.

Dale Capstick of Coxheath, Cape Breton, has experienced nightly visits from approximately three dozen giant house spiders (Eratigena atrica) since August. HPE introduced the Edgeline Services Platform and two related apps at its Discover 2017 conference to help customers manage growing IoT device inventories by integrating IT systems with Operational Technology functions. ESA inaugurated a new 35-meter deep space antenna at its New Norcia station in Western Australia on October 4, 2025. Entering service in 2026, it will support missions including Juice, BepiColombo, Solar Orbiter, and future missions like Plato and Vigil. The antenna strengthens ESA's Estrack network, enables international collaboration with agencies like NASA and JAXA, and reinforces Europe-Australia space partnership.

Researchers from UCL and Imperial College London have revealed how polymyxin antibiotics kill bacteria by forcing active cells to overproduce and shed their protective outer armor, creating gaps that allow the drug to enter. Using atomic force microscopy, they showed this process only occurs in metabolically active bacteria, leaving dormant cells unaffected. This discovery explains why infections can recur when bacteria enter dormant states, and suggests combining polymyxins with treatments that wake dormant bacteria or stimulate armor production could improve effectiveness. The findings indicate antibiotic effectiveness assessments must account for bacterial metabolic state.

This passage details the SD Memory Card initialization, identification, and operational procedures from the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. After bus activation, the host initiates card initialization using ACMD41 with HCS (Host Capacity Support) bit to indicate SDHC/SDXC support. The busy bit in OCR indicates initialization completion, which must finish within 1 second. CMD8 expands ACMD41 functionality, enabling CCS (Card Capacity Status) in the response to distinguish SDSC (CCS=0) from SDHC/SDXC (CCS=1). The host then obtains each card's CID via CMD2 and assigns RCA via CMD3.

For UHS-I initialization, the host sets S18R=1 in ACMD41 to request 1.8V signaling; cards respond with S18A=1 if supported, followed by CMD11 voltage switch. UHS-I cards require driver strength selection (CMD6 Function Group 3) and mode selection (CMD6 Function Group 1), with optional CMD19 tuning for SDR50/SDR104 modes.

Data transfer operations include: block read (CMD17/CMD18), block write (CMD24/CMD25), erase (CMD32/CMD33/CMD38), DISCARD, and FULE. SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing, while SDSC uses byte addressing with variable block lengths. Write protection includes mechanical, internal, and password-based methods. Card Ownership Protection (COP) enables Force Erase Password (FEP) functionality, requiring COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) when FEP is set.

CMD6 switches functions across four groups: Access Mode (bus speed), Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. Application commands require CMD55 prefix. Lock/unlock operations use CMD42 with specific data block structures, with different behaviors for Type 1, 2, and 3 (COP) cards.

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals held that terminating at-will employees for refusing to take a polygraph test violated public policy, affirming the circuit court's ruling. The majority opinion, authored by Chief Justice McHugh, determined that public policy questions are matters of law for courts, not juries, and that West Virginia recognizes a protected interest in privacy that grounds this public policy. The court cited precedent establishing that at-will employees may recover for discharge contravening substantial public policy principles, and referenced privacy protections in prior state cases. Two justices dissented: Justice Miller argued no public policy against polygraph testing existed at the time of termination, noting the relevant statute took effect nine months later, and that privacy tort cases cited by the majority did not apply. Justice Neely joined this dissent and separately objected on ex post facto grounds, arguing the legislature had already addressed the issue prospectively and retroactive application was unjustified.

Austin Police Chief Brian Manley made a televised plea Sunday for the perpetrator of an 11-day bombing campaign to contact authorities before more people are harmed. Three package bombings killed two people—17-year-old Draylen Mason and 39-year-old Anthony Stephan House—and injured two others, with all victims being black or Hispanic. Police are investigating the attacks as a possible hate crime. The reward for information has been increased to $115,000 combined. The investigation has involved approximately 500 federal agents, 735 reported suspicious packages, 236 interviews, and 435 leads. Manley emphasized that public assistance is critical to solving the case and that laboratory analysis has improved understanding of the bomb construction.

UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves has declined to rule out tax increases ahead of November's budget, citing geopolitical instability, U.S. tariffs, and rising borrowing costs as factors reshaping the economic landscape. While she confirmed avoiding VAT increases remains policy for now, she refused explicit guarantees, with Chief Secretary Darren Jones also not dismissing potential manifesto tax cap breaches. Market forecasts suggest a fiscal shortfall of up to £30 billion may necessitate tax rises, though this risks alienating voters expecting growth without additional household burdens. Analysts indicate Reeves is preserving flexibility for economic developments, leaving businesses and households uncertain while signaling market credibility and discipline as priorities.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 29, 2020, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2019. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and states that the information is furnished, not filed, under the Securities Exchange Act. The company is incorporated in Washington, trades on NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT, and has registered common stock and three series of notes due in 2021, 2028, and 2033. Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer, signed the report.

May 9, 2001 news compilation: Questia Media laid off half its workforce (139 jobs) due to difficulty raising investment capital, slowing book digitization; the company backed by Enron's Ken Lay had over 5,000 paying subscribers. U.S. markets mixed with Dow down 51.66 points, Nasdaq up 25.20. Enron criticized Japan's deregulated power market as unfair to newcomers, calling for an independent regulator. Enron relocated families of Dabhol Power Company executives from India to Singapore amid contract disputes with Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), which denied federal government pressure to maintain the agreement and appointed an arbitrator for London-based dispute resolution. MSEB stated plans to increase power from its Uran plant were unviable due to high fuel costs. Hindu nationalist group SJM demanded judicial probe into the Enron deal. Dabhol lenders indicated willingness to back PPA termination by May 15 deadline. Prize Petroleum sought to acquire Enron's 30% stake in Panna, Mukta and Tapti oil and gas fields for approximately Rs 600 crore.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, supporting single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar/unipolar ranges. Output is straight-binary format. The device features alarm functionality (input and AVDD monitoring with programmable/fixed thresholds), multiSPI interface with various data transfer protocols (SPI-compatible and source-synchronous), and nine configuration registers. It supports RESET, ACQ, and CONV operational states, with low-power NAP and power-down modes. Applications include industrial analog input modules for PLCs, with fast settling time under 5µs and safety features like overvoltage protection.

A mother appealed a California court's decision awarding custody of her 6-year-old son Edward to his father. The mother had left Edward with his father in 1946 when she moved to Nevada and obtained a divorce, then refused to return Edward after a 1949 visit. The appellate court affirmed the lower court's ruling, holding that despite Civil Code section 138's preference for mothers of children of "tender years," the trial court properly considered Edward's stability and established home environment with his father from age 2 to 6, finding that "other things were not equal" and custody with the father served Edward's best interests.

Professor William Green introduces ordinary differential equation initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), explaining that ODEs involve derivatives with respect to one variable and IVPs specify all initial conditions at a single point. He demonstrates converting higher-order equations to first-order systems using a particle motion example with position, velocity, and time as state variables.

The lecture covers numerical solution methods, starting with Forward Euler: y_new = y_old + Δt·f(y_old). Green explains that Forward Euler, analogous to the rectangle rule, has O(Δt) total error, making it inefficient—halving step size doubles computation but only halves error. Better methods like trapezoid and midpoint rules achieve O(Δt²) error by estimating average f values.

For ODEs where f depends on y (not just t), explicit Taylor expansions become expensive due to Jacobian computations. Runge-Kutta methods, particularly RK2 (midpoint with Forward Euler estimate) and RK45 in MATLAB, provide efficient alternatives by using multiple function evaluations per step to estimate intermediate values.

Green emphasizes numerical stability concerns: errors propagate through iterations via a matrix (I + Δt·dg/dy). If this matrix's norm exceeds 1, errors amplify exponentially. Even stable physical systems (negative eigenvalues in df/dy) can produce unstable numerical solutions with poor method choices. Forward Euler on dy/dt = -2y with Δt = 1 demonstrates this, producing oscillating, exploding solutions rather than the true decaying exponential.

The lecture concludes with upcoming schedule changes, homework assignments requiring custom ODE solver implementation, and preview of implicit solvers for the next session.

The passage discusses representing and validating digital business processes in extended enterprise (EE) scenarios, where organizations share common goals across boundaries. It presents a Model Driven Architecture (MDA)-based approach with three components: a static domain model (entities and relations), a workflow model (process activities), and a value model (value exchanges between parties).

For static modeling, the authors use controlled natural languages like Attempto Controlled English (ACE) and OMG's Semantics of Business Vocabulary and Business Rules (SBVR), which translate to logic-based formalisms. They address the challenge of hybrid reasoning combining closed-world assumption (CWA) for complete internal data and open-world assumption (OWA) for incomplete external knowledge, using Description Logics (OWL DL) and Horn rules (SWRL). Business rules may express alethic (necessary) or deontic (obligatory) modalities.

For workflow modeling, graphical notations like BPMN and UML Activity Diagrams are used, with underlying formalisms including Petri nets, π-calculus, and temporal logics (LTL, CTL) for verification. Declarative representations enable consistency checking, data exportation, and annotation.

For value modeling, techniques like e3-value and REA model profitability through value transfers between actors, with both graphical and logic-based (Prolog-style) representations.

The three models relate through consistency checking: static consistency aligns value exchanges with business objects, semi-dynamic consistency checks forecast achievability, and dynamic consistency monitors execution against expectations via log files. Open issues include critical areas detection and representing pragmatics (stakeholder motivations).

Education is a fundamental human right essential for national development, yet Africa faces significant challenges in providing quality education, with sub-Saharan enrollment rates at only 6%. This study examines digital storytelling (DST) as a tool for modernizing African higher education and teacher training. DST combines traditional narrative with digital media to create personal stories, promoting skills including digital literacy, critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and collaboration. The research analyzes 15 qualitative studies from 2000-present across African contexts, finding that DST enhances student engagement, identity expression, cultural preservation, and community building. Applications include geography education, pre-service teacher training, oral proficiency development, and postgraduate research monitoring. Benefits encompass empowerment of marginalized groups, transformation of evaluation methods, and fostering higher-order thinking. Challenges include resource shortages, infrastructure limitations, time constraints, and technological proficiency gaps. The studies demonstrate DST's effectiveness in diverse academic settings, though researchers emphasize focusing on narrative content rather than technology itself. DST serves as both an educational tool and means of cultural preservation, bridging traditional knowledge transmission with modern technology while giving voice to underrepresented populations.

Steve Wynn settled with a second woman over sexual misconduct allegations in 2006, his attorneys revealed in court documents. The casino mogul recently reported her to the FBI, accusing her of attempted extortion for threatening to publicize settlement details. The woman, a former Playboy Bunny at the Palms casino-hotel, contacted Wynn's attorney after a January Wall Street Journal report about other harassment allegations against Wynn. Her attorney denies extortion, stating she only wanted to speak and sought no money. The FBI declined to confirm an investigation. This follows Wynn's resignation as Wynn Resorts chairman and CEO last month after multiple women accused him of harassment or assault.

Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who styles himself as an environmentalist and criticizes air pollution, uses a government-provided diesel Ford Galaxy that emits 189g of CO2 and averages 36mpg. The vehicle waited on double yellow lines outside his Islington home for 40 minutes on January 30, with a traffic warden recognizing the car and not issuing a ticket. Islington Council, where Corbyn lives and serves as MP, has proposed banning diesel cars with £130 fines for violations. The car qualifies for London's Ultra Low Emission Zone charge from April 2019. Corbyn, a cyclist who does not own a car, accepted the chauffeur-driven vehicle in 2015 for security reasons despite living near a Tube station. Tory MP Andrew Bridgen accused Corbyn of "breathtaking hypocrisy," comparing him to Soviet leaders. Corbyn has frequently tweeted about air pollution and Labour has pledged a Clean Air Act with "clean air zones."

This MIT lecture introduces AMO (Atomic, Molecular, and Optical) physics, defining it as what AMO researchers do, built from atoms, molecules, photons, and electromagnetic fields. The field has evolved from studying individual gas-phase particles and collisions to few-body and many-body physics, including entanglement and quantum information, with significant overlap with condensed matter physics.

A key development is the shift from merely observing nature to controlling it—first internal states through optical pumping, then external motion via laser cooling, and finally single quantum systems. Technology drives these advances, particularly lasers (now cheaper and more numerous), ultrashort pulses, frequency combs, and high-finesse cavities.

The course (8.422) covers QED, light-atom interactions, open systems, mechanical forces of light, single photon physics, quantum information basics, and many-body physics of quantum gases, while excluding high-energy physics, advanced atomic structure, and high-intensity lasers. Prerequisites include quantum mechanics and perturbation theory.

The professor uses optical lattices as a unifying example: standing waves create periodic potentials for atoms, enabling applications from atomic clocks (using "magic wavelengths" to decouple internal and motion states) to condensed matter physics (Mott insulators). Pulsed lattices function as beam splitters for atom interferometry or probes of dynamic structure factors in many-body systems, illustrating how AMO physics combines precision control with complex quantum phenomena.

Brazil's largest private power company CPFL Energia launched Envo, a new firm offering solar power services for homes, including equipment, installation, and grid connection assistance. The company, acquired by China's State Grid Corp in 2016, aims to capture growing demand as Brazil diversifies from hydroelectric power. Solar grid connections rose from 7,500 in late 2016 to 10,000 by April 2017. CPFL declined to disclose investment amounts or confirm equipment sourcing from China, stating only that panels would be purchased wherever cheapest. Banco Santander Brasil will provide financing for Envo clients.

HBO Max offers numerous acclaimed TV shows across genres, including crime dramas like "The White Lotus" and "The Rehearsal," superhero series such as "Peacemaker" and "The Penguin," true crime documentaries covering cases like Ruby Franke and the Austin yogurt shop murders, period dramas including "The Gilded Age," comedies like "Hacks" and "The Righteous Gemstones," and international productions such as "Dune: Prophecy" and "Like Water for Chocolate." The platform features both ongoing series with multiple seasons and completed limited series, with several shows having recently concluded or been canceled while others have upcoming seasons confirmed.

Hong Kong's indie toy culture inspired Labubu, a designer toy that became 2025's biggest Gen-Z trend through a complex global supply chain: manufactured by a Chinese company in Vietnamese factories, designed by a Dutch artist in Belgium, and popularized by a Thai K-pop star.

University of Utah scientists mapped the near-surface geology around Old Faithful using portable seismometers and new seismic analysis techniques, revealing a 200-meter diameter reservoir holding approximately 300,000 cubic meters of heated water. The study, published in Geophysical Research Letters with Sin-Mei Wu as first author, found that eruptions occur at the end of seismic tremor periods, caused by collapsing pressurized bubbles. The research team used 133 small, low-cost seismometers deployed in 2015 to capture ambient seismic signals without disturbing the environment. They determined that seismic waves from Old Faithful do not reach the western boardwalk, indicating an underground feature affecting wave propagation. The team plans continued seismic surveys to study air temperature effects on subsurface structures, earthquake wave propagation, and similar analysis in Norris Geyser Basin.

Secretary Stettinius urged flexible, informal approaches to international negotiations to allow for modifications. He sought to ensure Latin American "associated nations" declared war to qualify for initial United Nations participation. He prepared policy guidance memoranda for President Roosevelt's Big-Three meeting, hoping to resolve voting procedure issues and quickly convene a United Nations Conference. The British accepted a compromise voting formula, though Roosevelt had moved toward Russian views on unanimity. Stettinius noted his first invitation to a chiefs of state meeting at Yalta and kept his Crimea notes secured.

In this 1979 habeas corpus appeal, the First Circuit affirmed the district court's ruling that Ronald L. Johnson's confession was voluntary. Johnson was convicted in 1964 of first-degree murder and armed robbery for a 1963 liquor store robbery where he killed a Boston police officer. His confession was given 8.5 hours after arrest following a car chase and crash, during which he was injured. The court applied the pre-Escobedo/Miranda standard from Procunier v. Atchley, examining whether Johnson's will was overborne under the totality of circumstances. Despite factors including Johnson's low intelligence (IQ 86), sixth-grade education, injuries, lack of sleep, and absence of Miranda warnings, the court found the confession voluntary because Johnson had prior police experience, demonstrated belligerence and resistance throughout custody, questioned lineup witnesses, and showed no indication of being intimidated by police presence. The court declined to rule on whether Lego v. Twomey's burden-of-proof standard applied retroactively, finding the confession voluntary even under that stricter standard.

Eighteen climate scientists, including 13 based in the U.S., received French President Emmanuel Macron's "Make Our Planet Great Again" grants. Winners Camille Parmesan and Benjamin Sanderson cited difficulty obtaining U.S. research funding under President Trump and psychological strain from his climate skepticism as motivations for accepting the all-expenses-paid positions in France. Macron congratulated recipients at a Paris ceremony ahead of a climate summit. Parmesan, a University of Texas scientist, will work in the Pyrenees; Sanderson, formerly at the National Center for Atmospheric Research in Colorado, will work in Toulouse.

This study describes the Healthy Davis Together/Healthy Yolo Together (HDT/HYT) COVID-19 asymptomatic testing program in Yolo County, California, which conducted 770,165 tests among 89,924 residents from November 2020 to June 2022. The program reached 41.1% of Yolo County and 78.4% of Davis residents, with testing coverage highest in Davis where the program originated. Analysis across four variant periods (Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, Post-Omicron) found that daily testing peaked during Omicron (895 per 100,000 population), which also had the highest number of positive cases (5,865, 50.8% of all cases) and frequent testers (39.7%). Women (59%), individuals aged 19-34 (39.8%), and White participants (52.2%) were consistently the most frequent testers across all periods. Testing participation declined significantly after Omicron, likely due to pandemic fatigue, vaccine availability, and increased use of at-home tests. The study highlights how demographic factors and pandemic dynamics influenced testing adherence, offering insights for future public health surveillance strategies.

Worcester city employees earned over $11 million in overtime pay in 2017, with police department employees receiving $4.4 million. Police Chief Steven Sargent attributed overtime costs to late calls, special projects, parades, protests, training, and grant-funded work rather than understaffing. Lieutenant John Towns received the most police overtime at $59,577. Police detail pay totaled $9.3 million, with Officer George Kelly earning $100,384 in details—exceeding his $75,508 base salary. The Department of Public Works and Fire Department also earned millions in overtime. The city had 7,287 employees on payroll, with 223 earning over $100,000 in regular pay. City Manager Edward Augustus Jr. was the highest paid employee, and only two women ranked among the top 50 earners.

Flu season in Indiana has resulted in 278 deaths and can last until mid-April. Respiratory pathogens like flu virus can survive on surfaces for about a day, while norovirus can remain viable for days or weeks. A handwashing experiment at IU Health Pathology Lab found 15 bacteria types on hands before and after washing, with no significant difference, indicating insufficient washing technique. A cell phone test found 10 bacteria types consistent with normal flora. IU Health recommends washing hands with regular soap for 20-30 seconds, scrubbing all hand surfaces, and washing after bathroom use, diaper changes, caring for sick individuals, and before eating. Proper handwashing prevents self-inoculation and disease spread.

Walking is a sensory act shaped by place and environment that can become an aesthetic experience through art-based practices. This study examined how walking transformed into aesthetic experience for seven prospective teachers in a 10-week undergraduate program conducted online following the 2023 earthquake in Türkiye. Using art-based methodology and aesthetic inquiry, participants created visual diaries, photographed their surroundings, analyzed artworks including Francis Alÿs' "The Collector," and produced their own art works. The study found that walking fostered environmental awareness, developed multiple perspectives, and connected daily life with art and pedagogy. Participants moved from conceptual to sensory understanding, using walking to explore themes of freedom, urban rhythm, social problems, and personal identity. The research demonstrated that everyday walking, when approached through critical art-based methods, can become a tool for aesthetic experience, visual literacy, and social engagement in teacher education.

India's Supreme Court ruled that parties cannot seek votes based on religion, caste, creed, community, or language. The author argues this order is problematic: it misunderstands how identity-based politics has helped marginalized groups challenge hierarchies through democratic organization; judicial fiat cannot address communalism when stronger rule of law implementation is needed; and the order is unimplementable given how identity factors pervade elections at all levels. The author suggests electoral democracy should evolve naturally rather than through artificial bans.

Apple Inc. filed its Q3 2023 Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2023. The company reported total net sales of $81.797 billion for the quarter (down 1% year-over-year) and $293.787 billion for the nine-month period (down 3%). Net income was $19.881 billion for the quarter and $74.039 billion for nine months. Key product performance: iPhone sales declined 2% to $39.669 billion, Mac sales fell 7% to $6.840 billion, iPad dropped 20% to $5.791 billion, while Services grew 8% to $21.213 billion. The company repurchased $18.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends during Q3. Total assets were $335.038 billion, with $28.408 billion in cash and cash equivalents. The company had $105.287 billion in term debt outstanding. Apple announced new products including 15-inch MacBook Air, Mac Studio, Mac Pro, and Apple Vision Pro. The European Commission state aid case remains under appeal, with an ECJ decision expected in 2024.

Abraaj, a $13.6 billion private equity firm focused on developing economies, faced investor scrutiny over its $1 billion health care fund after investors discovered over $200 million in uninvested cash. Founder Arif Naqvi returned more than $100 million to investors in December 2016 following demands for proof the money wasn't used for Abraaj's operations. The fund, which aimed to buy hospitals in Nigeria, Pakistan, and India, had invested about half its capital, including a struggling $145 million purchase of CARE hospitals in India. Major investors include the World Bank's IFC ($300 million total, $100 million in health care), the Gates Foundation ($100 million), and U.S. government-backed OPIC ($150 million loan). World Bank President Jim Yong Kim had praised Naqvi and Abraaj as a model for private sector investment in developing markets. Despite the controversy, Naqvi was pursuing a new $6 billion fund for society-improving investments.

The company's ATR-14 is 0.48, with weekly volatility at 3.70% and monthly at 4.85%. Its RSI is 45.3. Extreme Networks has a market capitalization of $1.25 billion with 115.06 million outstanding shares, and average daily trading volume of approximately 2.6 million shares.

This is Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-Q quarterly report for the period ended September 30, 2018, filed with the SEC. The document contains consolidated financial statements including cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets, along with detailed notes on accounting policies, revenue recognition, acquisitions, debt, stockholders' equity, income taxes, and segment information. The company operates in three segments: North America, International, and AWS. For Q3 2018, net sales were $56.6 billion (up 29% year-over-year), with net income of $2.9 billion compared to $256 million in Q3 2017. Nine-month net sales reached $160.5 billion with net income of $7.0 billion. The report details significant acquisitions including Ring Inc. ($839 million) and PillPack ($753 million), debt obligations totaling $24.8 billion face value, and various legal and tax contingencies including a $1.5 billion IRS dispute and European Commission state aid investigation. The company adopted new revenue recognition and financial instruments accounting standards in 2018, and will adopt new lease accounting standards in 2019.

The speaker discusses their team's preparation, including video review to understand positioning and strategy. They emphasize getting shots through to the net rather than taking time for big slap shots, as blocked shots have been an issue. They also highlight the importance of driving to the net, creating screens, and staying for rebounds against quality goaltenders, without unnecessary physical play.

The #MeToo movement arrived abruptly in Canadian politics, prompting rapid resignations: Nova Scotia PC leader Jamie Baillie, Ontario PC leader Patrick Brown, and Liberal MP Kent Hehr all stepped down following misconduct allegations within 48 hours. This sparked debate about due process, with some comparing the movement to McCarthyism. The passage argues that political figures should resign when allegations become too distracting, that parties should hold leaders to high standards, and that believing accusers while maintaining fairness—through a presumption of truth-telling rather than disbelief—expands rather than upends justice principles. The surge in accusations reflects women finally being believed, not opportunism, and fairness requires un-stacking a deck historically weighted against victims.

Indiana is implementing outcomes-based contracting to address middle school reading struggles, hiring private tutoring companies with pay tied to student improvement results. The approach, already tested in states like Texas, Florida, and Arkansas, makes at least 40% of contracts dependent on clearly-defined student gains. While research remains limited, Stanford researchers found "promising" results in districts using pandemic-relief funds for high-dosage tutoring, noting improved collaboration and data tracking. However, vendors face financial risks when student attendance or participation is low. Indiana's program targets 6th and 7th graders with poor reading scores, with state education secretary Katie Jenner seeking donations and grants to fund contracts while finalizing structure details.
